title: Not As Bad As the Critics Are Saying
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice (2016)

** 1/2 (out of 4)

Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) fears that Superman (Henry Cavill) and his wars on Earth are causing innocent people their lives so he plans to take him out. What he doesn't know is that Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) has his own plans for destruction.

BATMAN V SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE isn't the worst film ever made like some critics would lead you to believe. While I didn't hate the movie I must say that it's certainly a disappointment for the most part because of the missed opportunities throughout the picture. There are some solid performances, some dazzling special effects and the final forty-minutes are terrific but everything leading up to the finale is just downright slow, boring and for an "action" movie these early scenes are quite forgetful.

I'm going to place the majority of the blame on the screenplay because so much of the early stuff simply wasn't needed. THE AVENGERS showed how this type of film could be made and while I don't blame this film for being dark, at the same time it looks like some fun could leak through at some point. What really hurt the movie is the fact that it's just so boring and this here is the biggest problem. I was rather shocked but I was really falling asleep throughout the early portions of the film and I constantly had to keep moving around in my chair to stay awake.

As I said, the final forty or so minutes finally picked up the pace and we actually got some terrific action scenes as Batman and Superman finally have to team up. The biggest question going in was how would Affleck do. Well, I thought he was just fine in the role, although certainly not on the same level as Bale. I thought the actor pulled off the Wayne aspect as well as Batman. I'm not the biggest fan of Cavill's Superman and I honestly didn't think too much of Eisenberg. Amy Adams does what she can in her supporting role and Diane Lane, Jeremy Irons, Holly Hunter and Laurence Fishburn are fun.

I've never really cared too much for Zach Snyder as a director and needless to say, his work here isn't going to have me hoping he's behind the camera on future films. I thought he finally got the crazy finale going in the right direction but he did very little with the earlier, smaller action scenes nor did he do anything with the dialogue and drama. In fact, some of the dialogue was downright embarrassing.

BATMAN V SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE is obviously just an introduction to future films so hopefully they use this as what not to do going forward.

title: What it is/isn't
review:
I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. Ben Affleck surprised me in the role as Bruce Wayne/Batman. I was not prepared to like him at all, and ultimately thought he was perfect. Can't wait to see the stand- alone, especially if it's penned by Geoff Johns (according to some rumors I read).

I think where a lot of reviews have gone wrong is that they mistook what this movie is. This is NOT a stand-alone movie, but is a first episode. Not only that, it is a first episode in a series of movies about familiar characters that we have loved and admired for decades. (I consider Man of Steel to be prologue.)

As a First Episode, Batman v Superman did a great job of introducing lots of characters that we will get to know much better later on. It set many things in motion that we will witness in full in later movies.

Furthermore, I felt that this was a film written very much for fans, especially fans of some of the darker story lines. Many nods to classic moments in DC comic history provided enjoyment throughout the film. There are some story lines that have NEVER been remotely covered in film (except some average cartoon representations), and this film tackled them tastefully and enjoyably.

There is more to the DC mythos than origin stories, and I'm glad to see the studio attempt them. Can't wait to see all of the upcoming films. I truly believe that as those films are released, Batman v Superman will be vindicated in hindsight and appreciated for the solid cinematic work it is.

title: Very good, solid superhero action/ thriller
review:
A modern, slick homage to superheros.

The plot is rather straight forward - Batman and Superman think that each other are causing more havoc than security to the world and fight out their differences.

The first hour is rather uneventful in terms of action, but explores Batman's origins and Superman's fame as a sort of a combating God-sent angel with powers and maximum strength.

The second hour consists of events occurring within a short period of time - the confrontation and fight between Batman and Superman, and the threat of destruction arising from unknown sources.

This film may not be Oscar material, but it's a cinema treat and definitely lives up to the hype.

title: The goal of movies is to be entertained
review: I want to start off by saying that the purpose of watching movies is to be entertained, and I believe Batman VS Superman fulfilled it's purpose. The first thing I want to make note of is my appreciation of Zach Synders directing, he brought this film into a new and dark realm and made characters that many though would fail into good heroes. Christopher Nolans The Dark Knight redefined the super hero genre of movies making it a serious competitor in the movie industry. I believe this movie set the bar so high that all other super hero movies will fall short, but that does not mean they are bad movies. BvsS is a good film and Zach took it to new levels of darkness and complexity. I honestly think this movie was too dark for some viewers, and because of it many will not like it. I have read many people talking about how batman seems like a villain and he is a brutish idiot that is fueled by revenge and murder. Honestly I think that was exactly what Synder was trying to make batman look like. Ben Afflecks Batman is willing to go against society to do what is right, and I think that is exactly what our world is missing today. Too many people are worried about what is political correct and what is good for everybody, but the world does not alway work like that. It needs hard men that are willing to do what is right and necessary. Going into this I though Ben would do a terrible job, but he actually surprised me. In way did he pass up Bale but he was still enjoyable. This movie is far from perfect the plot although easy to understand is blotchy and the film is flat out way to long. The last 40 minutes are spectacular but it takes awhile to get there, but I think in some ways that is the point, the movie builds up significant tension. For me I honestly can not decide if Jesse Eisenburgh's performance as Lex Luthor was utterly annoying or just crazy enough, and it may just be me but I hate Amy Adams as Louis Lane and think her scenes on screen were terrible and too long. she was forced to be in this movie and it did not fit. Overall this was a good film and shouldn't be compared to other Batman or super hero movies as it is completely its own movie. The biggest thing overall is that the superhero genre is in dire need of a break from cinema.

title: Don't trust the critics
review: Go judge it for yourselves. I liked it and I can confidently say most casual moviegoers and casual superhero enthusiasts will find it enjoyable, if they watch it with an open mind and grounded expectations. And if you're a hardcore comic book fan, you'll definitely like it, unless you're an irrational Marvel fan. Some people could find the first half of the movie a little confusing. They tried to fit a lot of information in a very short time. But it wasn't a big issue for me. Acting was top notch. Special mention to Eisenberg. I believe looking the part and acting the part are two entirely different things. Eisenberg doesn't look the part, but he certainly acted it well. To those critics who say the movie is not funny, they are too thick to understand the wit and humour of this movie. To them funny probably means Bruce Banner falling face first on Natasha's boobs or a stereotyped Latino as comic relief. I am not a conspiracy believer, but if a reviewer goes to a superhero movie with a predetermined idea of what a superhero movie should be like, then I have a problem with it. Superhero genre is becoming too big to be contained in one formulated type. The movie played out way differently than what we thought from the trailers, and I loved it. My rating is 8.5. Go watch it!

title: Batman V Superman , man of steel #2
review:
I have been awaiting this film release for 3 years, With each trailer I have got more and more hyped. Maybe that's the downside to the movie itself. Why set up something in one direction, to go in another? As I drove to the cinema I was recalling some of the negative reviews about it. I decided to forget all the trailers and judge the movie for what it is. Not my own opinion either being reassured or let down by the experience.

Man of steel for me set up the beginning of super mans journey to become the 'superman that every one knows'. The way they reference the future of krypton being part of the human race, his genetics being the seed. B v S continues to tell his story ( albeit at a pace some dislike), he is doubting himself and at one point becomes who he is destined to be ( telling Louis he loves her) his sacrifice (and rebirth) makes the world and the meta humans realise no statues are needed, HOPE is part of who they are, and what he stands for is humanity. Justice league part 1 will continue the superman story, the world will react to him differently. Heroes will want to support him. Yes B V S is a please all and open up the DC universe. But there is subtle story lines that continue to thread. Leaving the film it took me a good day to digest it. I will watch it again. Not every film is made to be a complete package, just leave preconceptions at the door and enjoy it for what it is.

title: Battle Royale (w/Cheese); Gadot's WW is the show-stopper worthy of her own film (no fear; it's in the works!)
review: BATMAN v SUPERMAN : DAWN OF JUSTICE (2016) *** Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg, Laurence Fishburne, Jeremy Irons, Holly Hunter, Diane Lane, Gal Gadot, Harry Lennix, Scoot McNairy, Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Lauren Cohan. (cameos: Michael Shannon, Kevin Costner; Voice of Patrick Wilson) Director Zack Snyder's follow-up to the ill-advised reboot of Superman in MAN OF STEEL does a better job (not saying much) of this grudge match between The Caped Crusader (a forlorn Affleck better as Bruce Wayne than the Batman) and Supe (Cavill the Pill) as Gotham's hero finds himself tasked in taking down Metropolis' alien 'savior' with gusto and reserves at the ready. While the bloated screenplay by Chris Terio & David S. Goyer goes on to much with some sequences (um, yeah we all know how Bruce's parents died already; get on with it!) Snyder wisely employs producer Christopher Nolan's colleague Hans Zimmer to score the epic bitch slapping fest with gusto and brio. While the Battle Royale of billionaire vigilante with an arsenal of Kyrptonitic weapons and taciturn Kal-El brings it for the most part it is about twenty minutes too long but saving grace is comely Gadot as Diana Prince, AKA WonderWoman who steals the show and wakens things up in the climactic fiendish plot by Lex Luthor (annoying tic-fest Eisenberg who overacts beyond words) to create Doomsday (an ungodly blob of goo) to destroy the Dynamic Trio. If you see it, by all means do so on an IMAX screen (at the very least to take in an 80 foot giantess, the aforementioned WW).

title: Why critics think the movie is bad.
review:
I've seen Batman v Superman (obviously) and decided to mull it over before simply adding a comment.

I can't say that it blew my mind, although that is exactly what i wanted it to do. However as a film entitled "Dawn of Justice", it was exactly that, THE DAWN OF JUSTICE. I think people went into this film expecting Man of Steel 2,when it's a prequel to the Justice League.

I have read critics complain about the film being "muddled" and over exerting the "sub plots", But on seeing it for myself I can honestly say that all those were needed. Not as a film on its own but as an introduction For what is to come.

Even the politics are justified if we try to understand why humanity admires Superman as a true saviour. The Christ connotations are strong, but not as bad as those in the dread awful Superman Returns. The appearance of the Reverse Flash really brought home the complexity of the impact he can have in the future. This can't be seen as a mere superhero film about Batman fighting Superman,but the evolution of a species and their saviours.

BTW....Ben Affleck was awesome!!

There is a reason Superman and Batman are some of the most collosal icons in comic folklore. That. is resinated in this film. We see the different aspects of each character and what makes them who they are.

If this film is to set the stage for the expansion of the DC universe then it has done it well.

This was not Man of Steel the sequel but rather the confusing, intriguing, complex origin story of the Justice League.

title: Regards the origin of the characters
review: Great movie! It's a superhero film in the literal sense of the word, deals with issues of justice, honor, greatness without making jokes. It is a film that respects the reader of comic books. It is noticed that the director Zack Snyder studied very well the details of the characters in the magazines and also was inspired by other elements such as video games "Injustice: Gods Among Us" and Batman games "Arkham Series" The film is very capricious, I really liked this movie, worth seeing at the cinema. I liked the neurotic Bruce Wayne and the crazy Lex Luthor. And the time that the Wonder Woman appears! Uhul!!! Rate: 9,8 #BatmanvsSuperman

title: Subtle poetry at it's finest
review:
I read somewhere that Batman v Superman was an indicator on the decline of superhero movies. I can't even fathom how someone could write this. The movie is a cornucopia of subtle poetry, great craftsmanship, great script and great actors. The subtle greatness of this movie can be identified as naive, but should in any case be accepted for what it is – a powerful ingredient in the modern movie genres. Zack Snyder and the rest of the cast deserve an audience who actually pays attention to the greatness of the movie. Instead of just tagging along the negative vibe. To see, you need to look.

Batman v Superman is an indicator on the continued growth and increase of the superhero movies and sets the bar pretty high.

title: Worst movie ever made.
review:
Got to see an early preview of this movie at a VIP showing, I was truly enthused.

No spoilers here, other than to say this is the worst movie I've ever seen. Truly a wonder this kind of junk can be made. And trust me when I say I'm being kind...

The acting was terrible, the effects were garbage, honestly, in 2016, oh man...absolutely terrible.

And lastly, the story is perhaps the worst 'non-story' I've ever seen. How anyone approved this is beyond me.

Avoid.

title: Like the old saying goes, "You get more with less!"
review:
I was so looking forward to watch this movie, but only to find out that it was a waste of my time.

The movie for me was me-eh!

I just think that, they tried too hard by overloading this movie with 3 different story lines and because of it, it really lost that WOW factor, well for me it did anyways.

Maybe should take notes like how MARVEL did their movies. Made a single movie per character to explain the superheros life story/background.

To me i couldn't help stop thinking that the only reason for this movie, was to see how could we put 3 well known superheros together, just to confuse the heck out of people, because i was.

To me the movie was too cluttered, rushed and kept jumping around a lot, from one character story line to the next.

If you ever wanted to watch 3 movies into one, now's your chance.

After watching "Man Of Steel" i had actually thought this would of been a pretty good movie, but boy was i wrong.

I would probably wait for it to come on DVD and don't waste your $$$ going to the cinemas's to watch it, very bad idea.

title: Great movie, could be better
review: Well, I saw it two times and I can't wait for the R rated version. This movie is most definitely not for people unfamiliar with the DC comic universe. A lot of people in the cinema didn't know what the heck is going on, when the nightmare sequence began, while I only needed the Omega symbol to connect the dots. I completely ignored the critical reviews, because come on - Sharknadoo has a better critic's score? Give me a break. Critics shouldn't review superhero movies in my opinion, simply because superhero movies aren't meant to have a plot any different than "good guys win". Now someone will say "Oh yeah? What about Suicide Squad?" well, they are super-villains. Anyway, to conclude, I liked the movie, but I have my fair share of DC universe knowledge. If you are not familiar with the comics, you may have a problem liking it.

title: A Great, Misunderstood Superhero Movie
review:
It seems as if I'm caught in another Deadpool situation. While many others really loved this movies others have trashed it and hated it. I ignored both sides and cleared my head before watching this movie. I set my expectations at 0. I wasn't expecting a masterpiece or a piece of crap. I was middle ground and after being burned with a recent rewatch of Man of Steel which really was a jar of Granny Smith's Peaches I didn't know what to expect from this movie. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice was really great. I liked it a lot and it had some great moments but a few missteps. It's things that may make or break the film for others but didn't bother me in the long run.

First let's start with the good. Ben Affleck as Batman was awesome. I thought I'd always think of Ben Affleck being Ben Affleck in this film but I sincerely believed him as Batman. He was epic, scary, dark, tormented, sassy and many other adjectives. The way they introduced him was excellent. I also didn't mind that he killed people. I could honestly care less about Batman killing people. But enough Batfleck talk, let's talk about the main character himself, Superman. Henry Cavill was great in the film, especially near the middle and the end. He actually portrayed emotion and empathy for humans which was lacking in Man of Steel. Everyone else was great but the 2 performances I got to mention in this review are Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman and Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. They were both great. I don't get why people said Eisenberg was annoying because he did a phenomenal job as Lex Luthor Jr. When I first heard the casting I was skeptical but after finding out he was playing Lex Luthor's son I was okay with him having Eisenberg tendencies throughout the film. He can off as menacing and fun. He isn't as annoying as other people have said he is. Gadot did a great job and had a excellent take on her. I like the cockiness of the character and how awesome she was. It also shouldn't go without saying how great the rest of the cast is. It seems as if Snyder finally brought life to the lifeless characters from Man of Steel because I was so happy with how Fishburne played Perry White and Amy Adams as Lois Lane and especially Jeremy Irons as Alfred. Phenomenonal job from a great cast that never disappoints.

But I can't blame Zack Snyder for Man of Steel because I completely blame David S. Goyer's script. It was extremely weak and had some pretty terrible dialogue scenes and poorly written scenarios. It didn't come as a surprise to me when they added Chris Terrio to the screenplay. It seems he took control over all of the screen writing because this movie is written very well. Sadly it seems Goyer did get a crack at how this film should be structured because that's something that fell flat in this film. The story structures its events in a Goyer way where they'll constantly keep moving back and forth, back and forth, back and forth and made the film stagger at points. But it didn't stop from some great scenes in the movie and some awesome dialogue from Affleck and Cavill. Honestly Snyder isn't the problem with the DCCU. The problem is Goyer. If anyone needs to be taken out of this franchise it's Goyer who needs the boot.

Snyder's direction is fantastic on this film. He's able to direct these shots that seem to come out of a Malick film. There also seemed to be a lot of Malick influence in the film, especially in the amazing opening. Snyder really knows how to open a film. It's breathtakingly beautiful and was very nice to watch the intense, stylized and different. That's the biggest compliment I can give Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is that it isn't the typical Marvel film. This is a bold and visionary superhero film from DC that goes against the grain like these films should instead of feeling the same.

As I've already mentioned the biggest problem with Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is its structure. It breaks the flow of the film at points and gets really annoying. Another problem was one shot of CGI at the beginning. It's in an ocean scene and I honestly was stunned that this made the final cut for how shitty it looked. Luckily the CGI improved as the film progressed.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice gives Superman the redemption needed after Man of Steel and shows us what we wanted as an intro to a larger DC Cinematic Universe. The cast was great, the direction was great, the writing was sloppy at points but was also great, and the fight scenes were amazing. Definitely see this film. It's not for everyone but for someone who loves comics and film in general this was a treat.

title: All Hail Zack Snyder
review:
I saw this yesterday and man, did this movie blow away my expectations. I wasn't sure about Ben Affleck as Batman. I remembered Daredevil but then I remembered Argo. Suffice to say that Batfleck is awesome. He absolutely nails this Frank Miller version of Batman, and his is the performance that carries the audience through the movie.

Gal Gadot is amazing as Wonder Woman, and her character can stand toe-to-toe with the other two in their respective areas of expertise. She out-sneaks Batman in one scene, and outfights Superman in another. She's a quietly intelligent warrior and, in one scene where she finds out she's outclassed, smiles like Thor and jumps at the challenge. Perfect!

All the supports are bang-on. Jeremy Irons' Alfred, Laurence Fishburne's Perry White, Dianne Lane's Martha Kent and Amy Adams' Lois Lane.

Now... Lex. Yeeech. Ghastly. Cringe-worthy. I hated every second this guy was on screen. If it wasn't for this most abhorrent of all film Lexes (And really, only Spacey's was any good) the movie would be pretty close to a ten.

A few choice morsels for long-term fans, and definitely the most satisfying screen realisation of The Dark Knight Returns. The way they've introduced the DC Universe is very cleverly done, and different to the way Marvel set up The Avengers. Which is great!

Thank you Zack Snyder.

title: Finally - A REAL Comic Book Movie.
review:
Make no mistake. People dissing this movie are doing so for one of three reasons.

1) They don't understand what the movie is trying to do. 2) They just want the reason to fail (because people like a bloodbath). 3) Because its not a 'Marvel movie'.

The movie plays like a Geoff Johns comic book. It doesn't spoon feed you information... you need to use your head a little bit (something comic book movie fans aren't used to these days).

The choppy story telling which has had certain simple minded critics spitting feathers with rage is common place in modern comic book narrative and bringing this style to the big screen is something Zack Synder should be commended for. He has defied the cookie- cutter style of the modern super-hero movie and given us something that people will be mentally chewing over for decades.

Make no mistake people, this is REAL ART. Keep this in mind when you watch it.

And for those of you lost by it... don't blame the movie for your own shortcomings.

title: Phenomenal intelligent movie! Must see more than twice!
review: First off I just wanna say that DC and everyone involved with this amazing film should take everyone's criticism as a huge compliment because Marvel nor anyone elses standards are expected to be higher! The hyper criticism has shocked me. Some of the youtubers I've followed, their remarks have blown me away even to the point of unsubscribing. This movie definitely does not appeal to the 21st century short attention span, and I love that! There's a lot that goes down in this movie and a lot of info the viewer needs to take in. Was something else expected? Why don't movies like Lord of the Rings or Age of Ultron get put under the same microscope?! Age of Ultron tossed together a few technology terms to bring their story together but nobody lost their mind over that. It's because DC is expected to be perfect and that's OK. This movie is not perfect but it sure as hell isn't a 30%! Everyone did a phenomenal job acting! Wonder Woman is amazing in this, Ben Affleck equals best Batman as I predicted and Cavill did an even better job as the humble and determined Kryptonian! The action is second to none and so is the storytelling and characterization! Zach Snyder quite frankly has balls for how he uniquely put this film together not following any super hero trends in film but instead builds a story, does a great job quickly developing Batman and Lex as well as setting up the Justice League perfectly! I loved it! But then again I am a true DC fan and I also realize that the comic books have a great many different interpretations of all these characters so to say this film doesn't stay true to any of the characters makes no sense! No one cared Bane had no venom nor did he tower over Batman in The Dark Knight Rises. That's like 90% of who he is right there!!!lol I really am grateful to be ALIVE to have seen it, and have already enjoyed it 4 times!! Lol Looking forward to my 5th tomorrow.

title: Great Movie (may contain spoilers)
review: Batman v Superman is an amazing movie a great comeback for DC after a dry-spell it has a good story, tension between the two superheros, great fight scenes, and a good set up for the movies to come. Ben Affleck's Batman was impressive he surpassed my expectations, Affleck kept to Batman's dark and gritty character while still standing up for justice. Henry Cavill reprising his roll as Superman was good as well he shows the power of Superman his ideas of justice and his disapproval of Batman. Finally this was one of Jesse Eisenberg best performances by far, portraying the villain, Lex Luthor as psychotic yet at the same time a genius, truly a great performance. As a personal opinion I think it's on par with Marvel's Avengers.

title: Sets up the DCEU perfectly
review:
Ill make this quick for you :

  • Although this movie does have its faults (as all films do) this film's negatives are completely overshadowed by its positives.


  • First off, Ben Affleck as batman was PHENOMENAL. The tension and emotion Ben brought to the character is unheard of in a superhero movie and I 100% believe he is the best batman portrayal ever.


  • Zack Snyder once again displayed his tremendous skills in fight scenes, visuals and effects


  • It sounded AWESOME


  • Movie will make you feel all kinds of emotions


  • Gal Gadot kills it as wonder woman, very excited for her movie next year.


-Jeremy Irons as Alfred was another great choice

  • Jesse Eisenberg wasn't a traditional Lex Luthor so I didn't view him as one, If you see this character as completely new and original villain you will LOVE him.


Best scenes:

  • Flash reaching out to Bruce by using the speed force and telling him of the future


  • The Knightmare sequence


  • The batman & lex confrontation at the end


  • The trinity's battle with doomsday


  • THE BATMAN V SUPERMAN FIGHT SCENE = PRICE OF ADMISSION


All in all 9/10 there was some pacing issues and a lot of the movie focused on Lois which I found to be quite boring but this doesn't effect the movie as a whole on any scale. The critics are bashing this movie because they cant accept this dark tone in a superhero movie. Final statement : Very faithful to comics (except maybe for batman's possible killings and the appearance of some Justice league members) and set up the Justice League perfectly and very differently to Marvel. Great Film and cant wait for the directors cut.

title: Great movie worth a watch
review: I've seen reviews but over an under an 8. This Movie was great. Only complaint I've got was With doomsday and the last act. Jesse eisenberg as lex really was good and stole some scenes. Great cast. Not overcrowded. If you like Comic book Movies or Movies in general then you should watch this one. Bruce Wayne's parent deaths was done fast in the intro as they should. title: A positive mess

It have some great moments and bad moments. Furthermore this movie more to adults than kids because they will get bored on this movie plus don't have a clue what going on( weird choice since majorities of moviegoers that bring money are family )but overall I give you my honest opinion it wasn't terrible as those critic mention. This review is coming from a casual moviegoers not some DC or Marvel fan-boy.

title: Messy, Pretentious and Miscast
review:
"Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" is a film with a messy and pretentious screenplay and absolutely miscast. The story is confused, with segments and ellipsis; actually it works only in the end. The reason for Batman and Superman fight each other is ridiculous. Lex Luthor is a genius but Jesse Eisenberg, who is totally miscast, transforms the great villain in a clone of The Joker with stupid lines and attitudes. The red-haired Amy Adams performing Lois Lane that is brunet and Laurence Fishburne performing Perry White that is Caucasian are jokes with the characters from the comics. Ben Affleck uses two facial expressions, one for Bruce Wayne and the other for Batman along the whole movie. Henry Cavill with his expressionless face is the worst Superman of the cinema history. Further, both heroes are non-charismatic (actually both are hateful). Jeremy Irons, Diane Lane and Gal Gadot save the cast. Indeed the plot is only pretext for the excessive use of CGI. My vote is six,

title: Best Superman movie with Batman and Wonder Woman on it
review: I can say that I am more of regular movie fan. I was a child when I first saw Reeve's Superman and now I am around 30s. I love Actions,fantasy , science fictions and war movies. title: Zack Snyder failed to Deliver
review:
if you are going to watch this movie please lower your expectations as it did not deliver on so many aspects. The plot, screenplay, story etc were all awful.

Batman and SuperMan, two of the best DC superheroes appearing on a Big Screen for the very first time, How can you go this wrong?.

title: Bad, but not through lack of trying
review:
Let me start off by saying that this movie is very poor indeed. The plot is nonsensical and barely even present, the action scenes are few and far between and every character lacks depth and development. That being said, Ben Affleck puts in a very good performance as a slightly cocky yet troubled Bruce Wayne/Batman. He is one of the few actors to portray both egos of a superhero character well and has definitely come along way since Daredevil (2003). Jeremy Irons also has a solid portrayal of Alfred and manages to do it without copying the fantastic work of Michael Cane in the Dark Knight Trilogy. My problem with this movie is not with Batman, I would still very much like to see a solo Batman movie starring Ben Affleck. My problem with this movie is not even with Superman or Wonder Woman despite the fact that both characters lack all discernible traits and are essentially just generic hero #1 and generic heroine #1.

My real problem with this movie is the writing. The reason for the feud between Batman and Superman is nonexistent and is only really held together by pointless (albeit visually impressive) dream sequences that are never truly explained. It also doesn't help that teasers for upcoming DC movies Wonder Woman, The Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg are so painfully shoehorned in.

While I am a fan of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and how they intertwine their movies I am not a fan of this dire attempt at it by DC. Not every movie has to be filler until the next one, I thought we had learned that from Iron Man 2.

If the next movie in this universe is to improve on this, it has to be a movie. That means it can't just be a set up for the sequels as this so clearly is. Develop characters. Develop the plot. Make something that can be enjoyed on it's own, something that isn't just there to keep fans busy until the next one.

In conclusion, I think this movie had potential that was wasted in trying to set up a franchise. Learn from your mistakes DC, nobody was expected Citizen Kane but we were definitely expecting better than this. If Green Lantern (2011) didn't exist then this would be the biggest misstep DC have ever made.

title: Zach Snyder is Dr. Frankenstein and this is his monster.
review: This is by far one of the most chopped up movies I've ever seen...by "chopped" up I mean the movie just goes scene to scene without transitions or clear context. The only redeeming factor was Batman, quite frankly he's the only character that's actually likable. Superman just comes off as an angry teenager type. title: The worst DC movie ever
review:

Perhaps it's the writers, or the directors, or perhaps the casting, but nothing in this movie is worth getting excited about much less praising. It's time for DC to reboot the creative arm of the film franchise and focus more on stories that flow with characters the audience can relate to the comics. Save your money and time on this one and go watch mildew grow in the shower, it will be far more entertaining.

title: Most superhero movies are fun, but not this one
review:
I always believed the point of superhero movies was to send a message of hope. The great importance of the heroes isn't only what they do, but what they stand for. They present the idea that one person really can make a difference, that goodness can exist in the world if we all do our part. We don't all have to be Superman or Batman, but we all need to follow their example to stand for what is right. We all need to stand for good.

I didn't feel any of that after watching Batman vs. Superman. I felt the opposite—hopeless. The movie robbed me of my optimism. The movie darkened my outlook on life. It was bleak. But before I delve into that too much and depress myself all over again I want to present something else I took away from the movie Batman vs. Superman illustrates the dangers of millionaire millennial geniuses and their unpredictable, uncontainable exploits. This is one off the wall thought that I considered momentarily before laughing and dismissing entirely. I do not imagine that is what Zack Snyder had in mind. Whether he intended this or not, the movie is undeniably promotive of funerals. As other film watchers have already noted, it also places an emphasis on coffins. It's a very pro coffin film. The story begins and ends at different funerals with different coffins. Where there is death, there are funerals and coffins. Snyder clearly wants to endorse the coffins. Don't argue with me on this. I'm right.

The rest of the movie (i.e. the parts between the funerals) doesn't change much in tone. It's gloom and doom. It's Zack Snyder doing Zack Snyder stuff. Batman vs Superman is essentially exactly what you expect it to be. If that's your taste, cut off a slice and chow down. You'll love it. If you're one that prefers movies that offer a little sprinkle of a spice called fun, you may want to steer clear. Personally my tongue and I fall into the latter camp.

How can I like a movie that gave me absolutely no joy? It's ponderous. It's dull. The characters wore me out like JJ Watt wears out blockers (note to anyone living in a bubble containing only comic book material: JJ Watt is football player from a league called the NFL). Through its 2.5 hour run time, the movie somehow manages to feel rushed, yet laggy and littered with empty scenes. It's almost impressive if you think about it.

In a more personal realm of analysis, the movie failed to connect with me on a level of preference. I disagreed with oh so many choices: Batman is psychotic killer who tries to kill Superman even though his only reason for doing so is flimsier than a car antenna. Bundy had better reasons for killing, or at least more interesting reasons. (Batman was afraid, that's why he tried to kill him. Yes, really, that's it. I know, it's lame, right?). Then suddenly in the moment before the murder, Batman changes his mind because their moms happened to have the same name? Get real. I rolled my eyes so hard the force nearly knocked me out of my chair.

Moving on, I cannot comprehend the rationale behind the forced and inappropriately timed romance scenes. If my friends and I and everyone in the city were all in imminent danger of being brutally killed by a giant monster, I wouldn't stop to smooch and chat with my girlfriend. I didn't understand why Superman did that. I also didn't quite understand Lex Luthor, but maybe that was sort of the point. He's complex and zany. I can live with that one.

I don't want to present the notion that I hated the entire movie. Not true. Certain moments reeled me in. My favorite element of movie, by far, was Wonderwoman.

Wonderwoman rocks. Even her theme music, which is so absurdly disparate from the rest of the music that it's laughable, somehow still worked for me. Probably because the sound let me have fun for a second.

The girl was totally badass. She was battling for her life against this abominable beast and she stopped to smile. Then I smiled. She had fun in that scene so I did too. She also managed to be likable as a person and as Wonderwoman, a critical foundation to establish in anticipation of her solo movie. In her own movie she needs audiences to care about both Wonderwoman and Diana Prince. I see now that shouldn't be a problem.

That's the silver lining of this whole experience. Even if you didn't care for this particular movie, you know there will be others, and the others look ripe with potential. Aquaman looks like a mysterious beast with an intriguing backstory. Flash and Cyborg look equally intriguing, even if they're slightly less beastly. And I've already mentioned the enchanting Wonderwoman.

I'm looking forward to the future of D.C. comic movies. Hope is restored.

title: Where the only super is superficial.
review:
A film with both Batman and Superman in it should be superb... and yet this film isn't. Even if you are willing to overlook Ben Affleck's raspy voice and his lumpy, squished face when squeezed into the Batman helmet, or the lack of humorous riposte between Alfred and Batman...this film's super is superficial. Which probably has more to do with the film's overall surmise that Batman and Superman could, or would be arch enemies based on a dislike for the collateral damage of one another's heroic actions. Unless of course you believe that both Superman and Batman suffer such self loathing that when shown a mirror both would rather fight to the death than accept its reality.

There is however one big flaw with this theory. Both Batman and Superman are on the same side (good) and suffer no shortage of evil to fight. Yes, Batman may be dark and brooding, but if he can accept the loss of numerous Robins and most everyone he loves (acception being Alfred) I think he can cope with the inevitable killing of a few innocents if one is defending the planet from aliens intent on destroying every human being on it. As for Superman, the blue boy scout, he doesn't intentionally kill, full stop.

So the story line is flawed and some of the acting is dubious, but thankfully Lex Luthor is deliciously evil and creepy! Louis Lane is not the 'most galactically stupid woman in history' and there is one funny line when Wonder Woman appears towards the end of the film. Does this save the film from a fate of ultimate blandness...no. Are you left pining for some humour...any humour, yes, sob...oh please... yes.

title: A masterpiece. You may just not know it yet.
review: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, contrary to what many, many critics have said, may just be Snyder's tour de force. The love invested in the project is quite palpable. Snyder himself has said that he is "a comic book guy" and that he has "made the movie as much as (he) could based on that aesthetic". He has, therefore, intended to translate such a medium, that of the graphic novel, to film to the best of his abilities. And he has delivered: other comic book films are just that, films based or inspired in comic book films; this is something quite different and special. It is, very much, a comic book come to life. It is visually brilliant and almost operatic. The editing, which has been absolutely panned by the critics, even lends itself to the translation Snyder has set off to achieve, and, at least for me, is no mistake. It catches the feeling a reader has when reading a comic, and moving his eyes from one vignette to the other. And this is achieved without any special effect; it is just how the editing is done and the scenes are ordered, which is indeed remarkable. The script is also very well written; one should remember this are comics, not Shakespeare. And yet, it has a heft that most superheroes lack. Down the road, lighter, more frivolous forays into superhero films (the majority of those that have come before) will loose their shine and be promptly forgotten, while this one may become more appreciated and better stand the test of time. For my part, I sincerely wish Snyder does not stray from this path, for he is not merely interested in making a buck, nor in pleasing a crowd for an afternoon, but in comics films as art. Mr. Snyder, from me, you get a standing ovation.

title: A dizzying mess
review:
My partner and I saw this film on a whim last week while on vacation, as we saw it was playing at the local IMAX theater. That right there should tell you that we're not fanboys who were anticipating the release of the film for months, unlike some of the other (both positive and negative) reviewers. I have however seen many of the modern-era (1978+) live-action Superman and Batman films, but not, notably, Man of Steel.

Do *NOT* see this film without having first watched Man of Steel. I was completely bewildered for the first half-hour at least. I ended up watching Man of Steel a week later just to get a better understanding of what the hell was going on in the opening. I came away feeling the prior film was a much better movie, but seeing it did not improve my assessment of Batman v Superman at all; if anything, it made it seem even worse in comparison.

This film was almost nonstop action, which I am not a fan of even in movies that have comprehensible plots and solid characters. This film had neither, so I felt like I was strapped into a roller coaster ride without my prior knowledge or consent for two and a half hours. The Hans Zimmer score was good, but the directing and editing made the film nearly unwatchable, independent of the visual effects.

Besides the music, the only redeeming factors of the film for me were the casting of Affleck and Eisenberg as Batman and Luthor, respectively. Since I'm not a fanboy I had not read any prior criticism of the casting of either of these actors, both of whom I'd enjoyed in other films. I thought they did just fine here, given the limitations of how their characters were written.

My partner, who is much more inclined to like action films, couldn't stand the directing or editing either. We spent the whole half-hour walk back to our hotel talking about how bad it was. Unless there are drastic changes down the line, I doubt I'll watch any further films in the Justice League series.

title: The main features of the film
review:

title: The Disclaimer is right in the title!
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. DAWN. OF. JUSTICE.

Some people have made complaints about, well... the abundance of content contained in this movie. A fair amount of people, for example, have been complaining about the runtime, as well as the content itself, and I felt like I should address this. I don't feel like either criticism is very well founded, and here is why:

The amount of content needed to tell a story of this scope, and from various angles and points of view, more than warranted the runtime. It would be very hard, if not impossible, to introduce proper character development as well as the cultivation of the narrative itself and have them both effectively coexist, otherwise. In an age where we are all used to watching 12 or 13 hours of a television show per season, I really don't think two and a half hours is too much to tell a story this grandiose.

And I've heard people complaining about the fact that the film was messy or even convoluted, That it spent too much time on court hearings, politics or public opinion. I could not disagree more. These scenes were not mere filler, but rather provided much-needed context to shine a light on where these characters were and what they were going through; being forced to navigate the complex world we live in adds a refreshing touch and it is this dynamic of gritty realism that more and more modern superhero films are incorporating (thankfully!) into their respective universes.

Zack Snyder... you did good.

title: Loved it
review:
I was excited from day 1. When the reviews started coming in my heart sank a little bit. But ignore them! the film may not be a masterpiece but my god it was amazing. I don't want to do a long review so here are some notes 1) The opening is beautifully done that pays homage to the comics.

2) fantastic soundtrack done by Hans and Junkie XL... they never disappoint. The music is heart pounding-ly good, it uses tracks from man of steel and creates an awesome theme for wonder woman.

3) Affleck nails the role of Batman... his fighting style is amazing, the suits look brilliant on the big screen and the story arc and development around him is well done. Alfred is also more hands-on and more sassy then ever!

4) Wonder Woman certainly knows how to make an entrance

5) The build up to the Justice League was well executed... we had just the right amount I think. It wasn't too much but we got a good look.

6) Zack knows his comic books. There are many references from other stories and the film pays homage to some classic stories (mainly the dark knight returns)

7) Doomsday... I don't know what to say... I loved him! he was scary and strong. It was an interesting take on the villain that follows the comic books and creates something new which I think is a positive thing. Adding new (not massive) elements to characters should be encouraged, it's risky but why not?.

8) I was incredibly nervous about Jesse Eisenberg as Lex but I can confidently say that he did an amazing job at reinventing Lex Luthor Jr. There was a bit of Joker in him which people may dislike but he is cunning and ruthless unlike the other Lex's we've seen on screen. He may not be what the comics offered but he was an immensely interesting character, that was fun but also rather terrifying.

9) special effects- I love special effects so I was hooked from the start

10) The politics and consequences surrounding MOS were covered heavily in this film. It may not be your typical superhero film but the political and psychological battle was engaging.

11) Armored Batman = jaw drop

12) It was really good to see the MOS cast again including Jenny and that nerdy internet blogger.

There was a lot to take in... some may see that as a bad thing but I paid attention and I got most of it, I have a few unanswered questions but I'm sure they will be covered in the future. I believe this film deserves a lot more credit. It was creative, clever, action packed and very enjoyable. Of course! like every film... there are aspects that I did not enjoy, however they are minute compared to the things that I loved! I'm a DC and Marvel fan, it's idiotic to compare them like some people have been doing and I think BvS is up there with the greats (my greats anyway). Sure there might be story issues, movie mistakes or inconsistencies that go against the comics but I honestly see it as a good thing. The cast and crew have taken the DC universe in a new direction which offers new things for the audience whilst acknowledging the material that birthed these superheroes. I salute the cast and crew!

title: Satisfaction at it's best that lived up my hyped after 3 years of waiting.
review:

title: Massively entertaining with a thin plot
review:
Zack Snyder did an incredible job with the fight scenes and action sequences and I suspect that he devoted majority of his time composing those aspects. That being said, the movie isn't a bad one. I have read user reviews where people complain that the movie was very long with a run time of 2 hours and 33 mins, but i barely felt that it was long as the experience was quite engaging. If you are one of those people who are discouraged by the reviews, don't lose heart, the movie is well worth the time and it will leave you wanting more.

The movie introduces some key characters and sets up the scene for the upcoming Justice League titles. One of the reasons why I felt the plot was thin was because of the focus on the Bat. Snyder was so fixated in establishing a new Bat that it almost seemed like a Bat movie. I think Ben Affleck looked the part but in terms of portraying a broken Batman, I had my reservations about the story line. The Batman doesn't seem to be broken, he seemed confused. One moment he is out to show Supes who is boss and then just one dialogue later he is making a promise to him? some ground work was missing. Viewers were not allowed to see the story in full (not that we don't know who martha is but is the name enough to convince him to change his mind instantaneously?) If he is searching for what superman stands for then it would have made some sense to me but his agenda was entirely something else. He wanted to show superman that he is not a God, that men can stand up to him and then when he beats supes, he just forgets all of that? That's a pivotal point in the movie as that's when they join together, hence it should have been better thought out.

I watched the movie in IMAX 3D and it was thrilling.

title: The epic showdown between Batman and Superman has to be this frustrating to endure.
review:
Back when I was a kid, I truly wished for DC Comics' prime superheroes, Superman and Batman, to clash together. I got the cartoon but I truly wanted for them to meet in real life. And as we finally get a titanic clash of two of the greatest superheroes, what I get...is a mixed bag.

Okay, to be honest, it is a noble task for "300" director Zack Snyder to set up a cinematic universe from the divisive "Man of Steel". Of a flawed telling of Superman's origins, there needs to be corrections be done to justify a setup for a "Justice League" movie. Too bad the same mistakes are done in this effort, from its dark and gritty tone to its plot excesses. However, you can forgive them as they tend to highlight the epic showdown between DC's greatest properties; if not too much.

As for the plot, there are times that it feels forced or designed to set up DC's other properties. For it is easy to tell a growing rift between the Son of Krypton and the Bat of Gotham, it is baffling that the execution is flawed. The best storyline comes from Bruce Wayne/Batman. Ben Affleck does an impressive performance as Wayne and his alter ego, with Jeremy Irons' Alfred Pennyworth in full support. And although I commend Affleck for impressively embodying Batman, his performance is tad too similar from his predecessors and his motivation goes south.

The supposed backbone of the movie, Superman's subplot, fails to fulfill the personality missing from "Man of Steel". As both Clark Kent and Superman, Henry Cavill was able to pull off a fine act but he was given no room to develop more for both identities. And his storyline feels a little constrained to learn of his character journey to justify "Man of Steel". At least Amy Adams' Lois Lane is given further credit, more than she was previously.

The true breakout and delightful surprise comes from Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman/Diana Prince. While the Amazon warrior princess feels phoned in, she makes a striking impression from her limited screen time. Gadot is impressive, making me wish for more room for her to shine.

While I can post more compliments, I cannot but feel frustrated as to how disappointingly this "Justice League" setup was staged. Some scenes are thrown in like pies. The action scenes were hard to follow. The pacing is flagging. The main villain, Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, is a balance between witty and exasperating. The Easter eggs end up too visible like billboards. The introductions to other DC characters are too much forced. And the showdown that the movie truly sells isokay. And expecting an okay reaction from a showdown between Batman and Superman is not okay.

After a preview, I heartbreakingly realized that a trailer for "The Lego Batman Movie" made a better impression than the actual movie itself, making this one of the most frustrating movies I could ever review. All the while, I was still hyped to see where Snyder and company will go from this one. And I hope it is not surely a recollection of what the movie was. Now, we can all lay our hopesto the "Suicide Squad".

title: I walked into the movie worried due to critics, but I ended up not being disappointed and enjoying it.
review:
*SPOILERS FOR ANYONE WHO HASN'T SEEN IT* I don't know where to start, but I'll start with what I didn't like. I would have liked at least a little, more, character development with Batman and Superman in the movie before Superman was ultimately killed by Doomsday. I was worried about this film having too much action and destruction like before. Essentially Batman and Superman have one scene together which is the main fight. That was the most we got out of their time together on screen. I thought there would be more fights. The fight was a little slow, which I thought it should have been fast- paced at some points, rather than the slow punches.

Lex Luthor's motivations were evil and plausible. I liked that. I also welcomed Jesse Eisenberg's performance. I was very skeptical of him at first but I came to buy his performance as Lex Luthor and thought he did a good job. But I hope he evolves and grows darker and less silly.

I liked Man of Steel but had mixed feelings about it. For one, the dark and gritty tone and two, the lack of humor. I was worried about Batman v Superman being straight-up serious and anti-humor and jokes...but I actually bought the serious tone for the first time, and found myself engaged. A DC movie deserves such treatment anyways and Superman deserves to be taken seriously, but not so far to the extent that it has to be dark. It was leading to somewhere great, but didn't have a satisfying outcome. I found myself enjoying this film more than a Marvel film. I was suddenly more hyped about this I was for Captain America: Civil War.

What I'm saying is prior to this, I was confident about Captain America 3 being a fun movie, but serious with occasional humor, no people getting killed, etc. I don't know how to put it, but Batman v Superman nailed it. The serious tone worked for the first time without jokes. I'm not against jokes in movies, that is not to say there wasn't any humor in Batman v Superman, there was, but for the first time I did not feel bored without humor or jokes. The serious tone worked.

The only factor the film lacked was Superman. Yes, he was in the movie. But doing the Doomsday story already? I was disappointed. I wanted to see Superman develop and also see his friendship with Batman develop.

Affleck as Bruce Wayne and Batman, nailed it. Amy Adams played an important role in this, and she was very good. Although I'll say that her Lois still seems more like an every- woman rather than Lois...she is not sassy or funny enough like she usually is. That was the only problem. I was happy with Superman's first rescue scene but thought it was too short....did Superman kill that guy or did he just get injured? Also...rescuing that girl from a fire...it would have nice to get a full-length scene of Superman rescuing people rather than just showing a montage of him saving various people.

At least we got Superman interacting with Lex Luthor twice, saving Lois 3 times and briefly fighting Doomsday. He was active as Clark Kent. Superman could have spoken more for God's sake. In the hearing, not a goddamn word...that one scene with Martha...not one word...that scene with Jonathan...pretty quiet. I did not want Doomsday to get involved so soon, but as he was planned to be in this story anyways, I would have expected a longer fight scene between Doomsday and Superman, but now that story is over...and we can't get a full-length and proper Death and Return of Superman story anymore because they did it so soon and rushed it.

Lawrence Fishburne played a damn good Perry White. Loved the Justice League cameos. Barry Allen...is he homeless?

The most interesting moral dilemma in the movie was "Must there be a Superman?" and that played a pretty good role in this movie. This film put Superman through a lot of conflict which was good. I liked that.

Having said all this, it was a great movie, despite Superman having less screen time, and in and of that itself, he had great scenes but ending the movie with the Death of Superman was wrong. I know he is coming back but this is only after 2 movies, we get Justice League. I don't want to count Suicide Squad since it does not involve Superman nor center on the DC heroes. And how are they going to start Justice League? Superman shows up by the end of the movie? Well what kind of movie is that? What about the Reign of the Supermen, and the black Superman suit/mullet hair Superman...is that going to happen? I don't see it happening. People could be less excited for Justice League now as it sounds like it won't be the ultimate superhero team up we are expecting. First half or more without Superman.

I don't know what rating to give it because I am still processing this and need to see it again, so a 7 or 8 out of 10 for me. An improvement over Man of Steel. Better balance. Better editing. Less action, consequently though, not enough. Superman could have kicked more of Batman's ass...the trinity versus Doomsday could have been a little bit longer. That's my review.

title: A serious and gorgeous Comic Book film, that really needs multiple viewings in order to fully understand and appreciate
review:
First let's address some of the more controversial aspects of the film: 1. - Lex's plan and motivation didn't make sense. First lets star off with his motivation on why he hates Superman, it's very subtle but it's there when he tries to give a speech at the his house-party where he got flustered. He showed visible contempt at the idea of having total knowledge but no power. This is Luthor in the face of the Superman. He's a genius. He's unparalleled. And here comes a being who makes him look pathetic and feel powerless despite his knowledge. He needs to bring god down low - god will obey Luthor, and Luthor will have knowledge and power.

Now let's move onto Lex's plan on tricking Superman and Batman to fight each other, well not so much in tricking them, but in pushing them over the edge, Lex already knows that Batman hates Superman for the events that happened at the end of Man of Steel, so by blowing up the senate while Superman is there, he pushes Batman over the edge, and by kidnapping Superman's mother and forcing him to fight Batman, he hopes that at least one of them will end up dying, because both of them are a hindrance to him.

2. - Batman kills people. Batman kills because he's hopeless at this point in his life. That was the point of his first interaction with Alfred, the "...turns good men cruel" exchange. Alfred tells him something has changed, a fact Bruce denies. Superman's sacrifice is what he needed to get his hope in humanity back, evidenced by him deciding to punch the wall instead of branding Luthor.

Batman killing was kind of simple to justify for me, seeing as how many of the deaths he fired warning shots beforehand. Especially in the batwing. To me, the core difference here was that although he gave time for characters to get out of the way, he was willing to cross the line if it came to it. For example in the warehouse fight he grabbed a machine gun and fired a spray to get everyone to duck. If they hadn't, he was going to shoot them, but he gave time for them to react. Same with the Batwing, he started way off the mark and gave them time to move, but they didn't. But he HAD to get rid of those trucks to infiltrate the building like he needed to, and he was on a time table so he couldn't do it more tactically. His relationship with the Joker seems to be Joker was simply able to escape Batman and that's why he's still around. Which makes sense to me, Joker gets away in large explosions and similar physic defying logic in the animated series all the time.

Another thing was I felt that batman's fight against Supes was very justified and explained. The "You let your family die" scenes, and then right after that the guy who supposedly sent them back died in front of him on TV and Affleck portrayal of anger there really came across to me as "okay, no more play time I need to stop this guy NOW".

Now let's discuss on why I say with the title of my review that this is a film that needs multiple viewings so that you can truly appreciate it, on my first viewing the first hour felt a bit off with some of the editing, like you may say that some of the scenes pop-out right out of nowhere, but when I came back from a second viewing those scenes that seem to pop up out of nowhere actually don't, at all. There's something weird about this film. I feel the first time you watch it you're absorbing so much info that you get lost and it feels like you're dropped in the middle of a scene but you're not. With a second viewing you already know how the movie is going to go and things you missed will pop up so much and it'll make the movie so much better. The Knightmare scene pops up because Bruce is decrypting Lex's files and you see it's going to take a long time because the percentage moves very slowly. Then the Knightmare scene pops up, we see what we see, and then Bruce wakes up, still in front of the bat computer where we left him and we get the cameo and then Bruce wakes up again in the same spot. During the first viewing it made no sense, but when u see it a second time it does, and the flow isn't bad at all. The setup of scenes is there, sadly it takes multiple viewings to catch em.

And a lot of the character motivations and actions can be better appreciated and understood with a second viewing, like the way Batman decides to help Superman after learning that his mother was kidnapped, he didn't stop just because his mother has the same name as his, he stopped because he realized that Superman isn't just some all-powerful alien, he's also a man with humanity in him, and after realizing this he doesn't want him to end up feeling the same pain he has experienced of losing his mother, that's where the future Flash's warning comes into place, because you really don't want to see an angry Superman that has lost his mother all because Batman didn't listen.

This is truly a remarkable film that is getting a lot of hate that it doesn't deserve, this is a film that challenges its audience by making them think and infer on a lot of things, and with a second viewing it just gets better, because you catch a lot of things that you may have missed on a first viewing, I truly like this film and I recommend that you give it a chance.

title: A truly sobering, uneven film
review:
You would think a film involving two of the most iconic superheroes of all time, Superman and Batman, would encompass the very best of the genre. Alas, the film ultimately finds a way to upend any such outcome. Where to begin?

Things I liked:

Despite their characters being horribly mishandled, Henry Cavill and Ben Affleck manage to hold their own mostly. Henry, despite having to play an overly stoic and low-temperament hero, manages to come across looking well as the Last Son of Krypton. Ben carries a certain suave look as Bruce Wayne, definitely giving previous actors of the role a run for their money. His Batman isn't too shabby either, looking the part pretty well. If only that were enough.

Jeremy Irons holds his own as Alfred Pennyworth, though he is horribly underused. Gal Godot also falls into the same category as Wonder Woman, if for the fact that we don't really get much insight as to why a photograph is so important to her. Also, despite the death of Bruce Wayne's parents being very overdone and stale, the film does serve to bring emotion into such a depiction through the use of visuals and frame shots in a way that I have to say was very well done.

Things I didn't like:

The script of this film was poorly written. Many scenes bog down the narrative, to the point where it can be difficult to follow the main plot of the story as well as break down the connections between events of the film. Those not well-versed in comic-book lore will find it harder to follow along (even then, didn't make it all that more enjoyable). From numerous dream sequences to irrelevant references (hey guys, there is going to be a Justice League movie!), this movie has it all...and suffers as a result.

The titular characters are also terribly handled. Batman kills people, as well as branding people with Bat-marks. He dreams of using guns to solve problems. He aims to kill Superman simply due to there possibly being "a 1% chance" of him doing bad things (with that logic, why not lock up/kill everyone, Brucie?). He shows little to no amount of deductive reasoning befitting of the nickname "The World's Greatest Detective", falling for one of the most pathetic attempts at blackmail conceived.

Superman is overly dull, brooding, and stoic to the point of being soulless. He gives up protecting humanity at the drop of a hat...only to return to it a few seconds later. He puts heavy emphasis on saving Lois Lane, to the exclusion of all else (sorry, Jimmy). He also shows little to no care for anything other than brute strength and force to solve his problems...from flying a terrorist through a brick wall at high speed without a second thought, no doubt killing him, to initially contemplate burning Lex Luthor to a crisp with his heat vision when hearing that he kidnapped his mother. And despite showing a scene where he was somehow able to contemplate Lois falling off a building from a huge distance...and could have possibly used similar skills to find his mother, Superman instead sits by while Lex monologues his questionable plot involving blackmail...showcasing that Superman will be helpless when the plot requires him to be rather than any internal consistency.

Speaking of Lex Luthor, this has to be without a doubt the worst version of this character yet. Lex Luthor is supposed to be a cunning, charismatic, and intelligent businessman. Instead, Jesse Eisenberg (whether through himself or possibly Mr. Synder's direction) gave an impression that almost seemed like a cross between Mark Zuckerberg and the Joker...which is totally the opposite of what the character is. His motivations are inadequately developed, and also come across as having little basis in logic. Having the two superheroes fight for...reasons? Create a super-powered beastie (Doomsday) of which you can't be certain as to it's capabilities and limitations as backup? Sounds like the plans of a madman like the Joker, not a smart businessman.

The titular fight, while decent, takes a while to actually take place...and in the end, it has nothing to do with their so-called "different philosophies" (which might have meant something if they were given weight beyond mere mentions in passing) but rather simply being duped through blackmail....how deep. And all in the end to finish with the two becoming fast buddies due to quite possibly the biggest cop-out reason in recent memory. Who knew that having the same name for parents could be so important? The final fight might be slightly better (Wonder Woman appears!), but besides the botched use of Doomsday...all it serves is to lead to one of the most pointless deaths in recent cinema history. Perhaps the death of Superman proves to be a fitting metaphor for this film in it's treatment of the characters, but otherwise it is a moment without much meaning.

Couple all this without much in the way of levity, and you have a truly sobering and uneven film that attempts to have more importance than it really does. Superman and Batman are big icons, and will no doubt survive a mess like this like they have in the past...but this definitely is a low-point in the DC library of media. Truly unfortunate.

title: Snyder's true vision is an epic slow-burn thriller that pits two incompatible philosophies of fear and hope against a backdrop of plausible real-world political dynamics
review:
Zack Snyder is an incredibly divisive filmmaker, having outputs such as 300 and Watchmen. The idea that his films are an acquired taste is very much true. Watchmen, a film adaption of the graphic novel of the same name, continues to be debated for its unnecessary length and lack of emotional drama, unlike its source which is universally considered one of the greatest works in the medium. Visually, Snyder is lauded for his stylized action and violence but criticized for poor narrative. Expectations of Batman and Superman meeting for the first time in cinema are stupidly difficult to realize, but mostly the two heroes are expected to be friendly and cordial, not cutthroat. Studio interference also led to negative receptions of the incoherent theatrical cut. Ben Affleck as a grizzled batman caused further controversy because it gives less room for future Batman stories and his characterization as a jaded crime fighter, breaking his famous no-kill rule. Man of Steel is just as divisive as his other films. Nevertheless, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice Ultimate Edition, Snyder's true vision, is an epic slow-burn thriller that pits two incompatible philosophies of fear and hope against a backdrop of plausible real-world political dynamics. The Ultimate Edition is what Warner Bros. should have released and Watchmen been.

Batman v Superman stars Ben Affleck as Batman, a 20-year crime-fighting veteran who realizes his decades work in Gotham hangs in the balance when Superman, an alien with literal superpowers, becomes the figure of hope and peace, putting his immense physical abilities for humanity's greater good. Superman, played by Henry Cavill, lives normally in his true self as Clark Kent, a Daily Planet news reporter. Two years after his destructive battle with fellow Kryptonian General Zod in Metropolis, Superman has to grapple with a skeptical public divided between people who view him as an ordinary man who does good acts and those that treat him as a rogue figure, unbounded by law.

The plot follows alternatively between both characters including Lex Luthor and Lois Lane. Batman is secretly doing detective work to locate a hidden figure who plans to bring a dirty bomb to Gotham. Following an ambush in a war-torn part of Africa, Superman finds himself at controversy when he is wrongly accused of the resulting deaths. Lois Lane, Clark Kent's partner, has to uncover the truth behind the ambush. Lex Luthor, a wealthy industrialist, openly influences Sen. June Finch to allow access inside the crashed Kryptonian ship and importation of a xenomaterial, capable of weakening Kryptonian physiology. The two main characters view each other on opposite lenses. Batman sees Superman as a threat who must be eliminated, while Superman views Batman as a lawless vigilante who decides unilaterally who lives or dies. Batman is the embodiment of fear, while Superman is the personification of hope.

Ben Affleck nails the grumpy attitude of the character in the comic book miniseries The Dark Knight Returns, including the physicality. Unlike previous versions, this Batman is a hulking behemoth who prefers to overpower foes instead of using agility. Similar to the Burton films, Batman is willing to kill and does so in significant numbers. Taking liberties and deviations can often lead to poor characterization, but not in this. His willingness to kill is given proper motivation, thus as executed in the story Batman's characterization works. Henry Cavill is much improved from his first outing as Superman in Man of Steel. None of the forced emotions and bad delivery of lines such as "You're a monster Zod..." Cavill convincingly plays the inner conflict of doing good, while getting flacked. Differentiating himself from Christopher Reeve, this Superman doesn't have the traditional boy scout persona commonly found in the comics and is more contemplative, even brooding. In the theatrical cut, Cavill looks bad because a majority of the 30-min deleted scenes were his as Clark Kent doing investigative journalistic work about Batman's recent violent outings. Reinserting those scenes in the Ultimate Edition gives the character more humanity, thus better overall acting. Amy Adams, like Cavill, is given more material in the Ultimate Edition. The biggest and most criticized acting decision is of Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. Fans expect Luthor to be gentlemanly and smooth, not manic. Eisenberg is another casualty of the theatrical cut that makes his performance and role look bad. Luthor has additional scenes in the Ultimate Edition that give him proper motivation, unlike in the theatrical cut where he comes off truly insane. The additional 30-minutes gives everyone more breathing room that enhances the acting.

As a political thriller, Batman v Superman digs deep into deconstructing the characters to their basics. Driven by the death of his parents, Bruce Wayne crusades as Batman to fight crime, a motivation consistently referenced throughout the film. 20 years as Batman, accompanied by the death of Robin, drags Bruce Wayne to mental lows, losing his humanity and empathy, further motivated by a sense of hopelessness and failure. Events unfold that reveals his detective work was a ruse to locate Kryptonite, a xenomineral capable of killing Superman. Unlike Bruce Wayne, Clark Kent does not have the same family tragedy and still has his mother to lean on. A figure with god-like powers, Superman ushers in political debates as to the necessity of his existence and whether he should be confined to government-sanctioned actions. Someone with such powers will court controversy, regardless of intentions. Superman is also shown to be more human and grounded than Batman. Lex Luthor manipulates both characters' inherent antagonism by blowing up Capitol Hill, abducting Martha Kent, building hatred for Superman through affected Wayne employees and importing Kryptonite which he intended for Batman to use against Superman. After an epic match, and before he could kill Superman, Batman finds his lost humanity when Superman says his mother's name, the same name of Batman's mother Martha Wayne. Two formerly opposite characters cast their differences to fight a common threat. Batman v Superman also introduces Wonder Woman, played by Gal Gadot, and the concept of metahumans.

Superhero films are big on spectacle and action. Snyder delivers the best fighting sequences in the genre. The Batman and Superman fight is brutal. Superman isn't depowered to make him a fair adversary. Batman is a tank, taking on armed goons singlehandedly. Wonder Woman is electric, taking center stage in the final fight against Doomsday. Doomsday is a Frankenstein monster with nearly limitless powers. The presentation of each hero and villain does justice to the characters. Batman v Superman is criticized for its bleak and dour tone, but for the film's subject material it is the appropriate direction. Even if the colors are greatly saturated, the film remains a beauty to look at. The cinematography, visual effects, production design, and score are all fantastic. Snyder is at the top of his artistic career.

A genuine critic that can be leveled against this film is it undoes Superman's death by implying he may be alive. Building all that drama only to discard the payoff is not a good cliffhanger. Elements of his boy scout persona should have been presented in the beginning and then gradually becoming more emotionally distant. Superman is the beacon of hope and comics' greatest superhero, and despite the film's strengths narratively this version feels a bit distant. Overall, the film is still widely epic. Warner Bros. should be ashamed of butchering a great, elseworlds tale.

9/10

review:
