title: Ben Affleck Proves Doubters Wrong
review:
As a huge Superman fan I really wanted to like this movie. For me there has not been a GREAT Superman movie since Superman 2.

Superman 3 was more of a Richard Pryor comedy featuring Superman, than an actual Superman movie, the less said about Superman IV: The Quest For Peace the better. Whilst Superman Returns had its heart in the right place, it was let down. I did however like the enjoyable Man Of Steel, but I found it good rather than great. Anyway on to this movie

Plot In A Paragraph: Fearing the actions of Superman are left unchecked, Batman takes on the man of steel.

I can see why fans of Superman are upset, as his character is truly thrown under the bus!! He is A, being reduced to a punching bag for The Dark Night (and not just because his morals won't allow him to kill a human in an unfair fight!! He is soundly beaten!!) and B, he is basically a supporting character in his own movie!! Somebody on here said they thought the makers of the movie liked Batman more than Superman, and I can see why they think that.

The plot was an absolute mess, story lines are put in place, then are just dropped all together. A prime example is Clark Kents Super hearing ability allowed him to hear Alfred talking in Bruce Wayne's ear at Lex Luthors party, he knew he was up to something, and chose to pursue it before being distracted. He never again checked up on what Bruce Wayne was doing. Characters have knowledge of things, without you finding out how they obtained this information. As for Lois Lane she is not going to last 5 minutes in a world without Superman!! She just seems to be a device to make Superman go somewhere or do something to move the story along!! The first time we see her she is took (with a bag over her head) to meet a terrorist who has granted her an interview!! This terrorist is so stringent with his affairs he did not know he had granted an interview to a woman!! Really?? Either he is the world's most incompetent terrorist or it was an excuse to utter lame dialogue like "I'm not a woman. I'm a reporter"

The full movie is littered with awful dialogue!! And I mean soap opera style bad!! It's more apparent during the opening 45 mins or so. A few plot holes are here and there, and it is clearly Step A, to setting up Justice League movie. It's a pity they didn't concentrate on making this one great instead.

Now on to the fight, somebody said it was as one sided as Sly Stallone V Van Damme in Expendables 2!! My eldest son compared it to Clubber Langs destruction of Rocky in Rocky 3, either way it was lame!! And the way Superman managed to stop Batman long enough for Lois Lane to save him, was by saying his mother's name!! (Their mothers share a name) Was pathetic as Batman stood there for a couple of minutes demanding to know why he said that name!! Now since their mothers share a name, The Dark Knight decides to be friends with a guy he has spent almost an entire movie plotting how to kill!! Lame.

And now finally on to the death of Superman/Clark Kent. As a fan of Superman, I should have been crushed!! Yet it did nothing for me, I wasn't even close to being moved. Now compare that to Terminator Genysis, when Arnie said "Kyle Reece..... Protect my Sarah" and Emilia Clarke's reaction gave me a chill as Arnie made the ultimate sacrifice, here I felt nothing!! Now since we all know Superman will not stay dead, due to the very last second of the movie, why did they kill Kent off?? He went AWOL after a lecture from editor Perry White, lots of people walk out of jobs every day!! That could have been it!! Then after he is resurrected, he apologies for walking out, and he has his job back!! Silly to kill Clark Kent off!!

I sound like I'm hating on the movie, I'm not as there were things I did like!!

Henry Cavill delivers again as Superman and Ben Affleck totally proved the doubters wrong. He was convincing as both Bruce Wayne and The Dark Night, and he was a lot better than Bale for me!! I don't hate Affleck like some do, but do think he is a better director, than he is an actor. However I loved his performance here!! Jeremy Irons isn't given as much to do as one would hope (but considering what happened to Supermans character, what hope did Alfred have??) as he is is solid. Gal Gadot looks good as Wonder Woman. And I never tire of seeing one my childhood crushes, Diane Lane on screen.

And I liked the beginning showing what Bruce Wayne was doing whilst Superman was battling General Zod.

Now what I loved. Kevin Costner returned as Pa Kent. For me he was the best thing in Man Of Steel, and he brought the heart to the movie!! And again here he is the best thing in it, I went to the first showing I could, and was still tipped off that he was in it, what I didn't know was it was a totally new scene!! And again he brings real heart to it, as he talks about whilst he helped saved his family's farm and he was called a hero, rewarded with a hero cake, he inadvertently caused destruction at the neighbouring Lang farm. My favourite scene in the movie.

I'm still waiting for another great Superman movie, and I think of this as a Batman movie, that has Superman in it.

title: Best DC experience so far, Ben and Gadot, well done!

title: A promising future for the DC Cinematic Universe, for me this movie is beyond awesome.
review:
*** No spoilers ***

I will start with a peculiar phenomena when constructing opinions, they are expressed like the referred subject is per se good, bad, wrong, right, and so on. An example in movies: If a person thinks that a movie is good, bad, best or worse, then he/she automatically generalizes thinking that the movie is good, bad, best or worse itself, which it is impossible to establish as all expressions of art are a subjective topic. Psychological cognitive biases are the background of this phenomena stating "my opinion is the true, so my self-esteem is protected".

Looks like this movie is being loved for general audiences and hated by "specialized" movie critics. I quoted "specialized" because those critics are persons like you and me expressing their opinions for earning a living, and then their opinions are assumed as a kind of law or the true for the movie. Nothing more wrong.

I love this movie, dark, emotive, fast, full of action, reflexive, sad. Let's review their components:

* Henry Cavill as Kal-El / Clark Kent : Delivers a more mature being like Superman, with human weaknesses and internal conflicts as revealed during the movie. Now there is a real connection from audiences with the character. A really good performance progress for Mr. Cavill.

* Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne: What a triumph! For me, this is the definitive Batman. Detective, genius, dark, depressed, implacable, a higher level in the development level on the character, that, I think, will be a standard for future representations of the Batman. Additionally Affleck's contribution for the scripting is outstanding. I never had a problem with Mr. Affleck's acting, and this time is really great. Besides his good attitude to the fans during the premiere in Mexico talking in Spanish most of the time. Great Mr. Affleck.

* Gal Gadot as Diana Prince: It is revelation as Wonder Woman. What a presentation during her scenes and the fight! All the questions about her performance of the character are now cleared and I cannot wait for her solo movie. Good work Ms Gadot.

* Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor: My weak link in the movie, not for his performance skills, which are remarkably good, but the character is like a second representation of The Joker in "Batman" (1989) mixed with The Riddler in "Batman Forever" (1995). Hopefully, the character could be evolved to the evil leader we know.

* Jeremy Irons as Alfred: A sidekick for Bruce Wayne, helping and warning him the risks for his actions. As always, a good actor.

* Amy Adams as Louis Lane: My second, and last, weak link. I like her performance, but I feel that her character could be more developed.

* It is no secret that The Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg are here. They are presented in very interesting ways.

* Action scenes. including the batmobile, the batwing and fights: Awesome! Zack Snyder always has mastered this characteristic. In this movie, he manages to deliver a solid piece in the whole running time, including the opening scene which takes place when the terraforming process occurs in "Man of Steel" (2013), now from the eyes of Bruce Wayne. Dramatic.

* Music: What more can be said about Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL? Masterpieces for helping the development of the story.

It has been said, that the movie has plot holes and inconsistencies. I still really did not find them, but tell me, which fictional story has no inconsistencies, even when it is partially based in real life which sometimes we cannot fully explain to ourselves?

As I stated above, this is my positive opinion and my personal perception of the movie. Do not let this influences your judgment. Criticizing movies is not an issue about who is right in opinions and preferences. Go see, feel and experience the movie with open mind. Each movie has something to offer to our experience as human beings and this has a lot for offering.

DC Comics: many people are awaiting your next movies. Keep this dream alive.

title: Masterful: A Lot of Catch-Up Done Well
review:
The DC Movie Universe had a lot of catching up to do in order to set up the Justice League to Compete with an already well-established Marvel Film Franchise, and to redeem its recent track record of poor movies--besides The Dark Knight Trilogy and possibly the Man of Steel. That being said, the edgy casting decisions paid off, and the writing and directing was exceptional.

Critics and certain members of the general audience will say that there was too much going on at once, and it was hard to follow the evolution of the story. This may be true for some--especially those unfamiliar with the DC Universe--because there are multiple story-lines happening in the film. However, I would encourage you to familiarize yourself with the characters and story-lines this movie is supposed to re-envision before watching it--you'll be glad you did, because you'll appreciate the film much more. Snyder is clearly a comic book fan, and he paid respects to the comic books in many aspects of the cinematography and directing, but he did an excellent job of adapting the story for the big screen.

I laughed. I cried. I was on the edge of my seat. I would call this a SMASHING SUCCESS.

title: Confused, muddled mess.
review:
For a while I've been treating this film like religion, if it works for you great, I don't want to take your joy. Seeing so much praise for this film, and obviously bitter fans crapping all over Civil War has forced me to say my piece.

I wanted to LOVE it. These are 3 characters that matter to me. On a surface level there are cool scenes, and cool images. Enough bombast and use of religious/mythological touchstones to overwhelm the senses. If you were to take a shot every time someone referenced gods/God/Angels, etc. you'd die of alcohol poisoning.

Batfleck was great, though this was a decidedly brutal version of Bats, that should work as a great contrast to the optimism of the Big Blue Boyscout. Except that character was nowhere to be found (a smile is hard to be found in this film), which is sad because Cavil is a perfect choice for Kal-El. At least we get Batman, Wonder Woman, and Superman (I guess) on film together for the first time right? Except, strangely I don't think Superman and Wonder Woman ever talk to each other, in a movie that's more than 2 and a half hours long!

Those are personal gripes, but from a story/filmmaking standpoint the film is weak, and doesn't stand up to modest scrutiny. It confuses complicated with complex, and has plot lines that could be pulled out entirely without changing the story one bit. It relies on the fact that these characters exist in our minds as whole concepts. You know them even if you've never read a comic in your life, and you don't even realize we've gotten 2 movies now with Super Sadman. It does troubling things with these characters and it doesn't have the deftness to pull off the grim depths it was plumbing. Wonder Woman was great, in the few moments we got of her. This movie was ambitious, I'll give it that. It swung for the fences. But in doing so it whiffed hard and tossed the bat into the stands knocking out a fan. Also it was juicing and got a 10 game suspension.

title: So Much Potential Wasted
review: Batman v Superman Had so much much potential. It had so much potential for many reasons. However, this is where it gets sad, the film has many many faults. For example, the film is called Batman v Superman there is literally ten minutes of fighting between Batman and Superman until they eventually join forces and work together. Us fans didn't want to see them work together we wanted to watch them destroy each other so that we could finally prove to our friends that one of them is the best superhero. Overall this is very disappointing film. I do not recommend it. Although if you're reading this you have probably already been disappointed

title: Red Dawn
review:
Murderiffic sequel to Man of Steel and the second in Zack Snyder's murderverse series about angst-driven superheroes, light on the hero part. Batman's the main killer this time around, probably because Snyder got his hand slapped so much for turning Superman into a killer in the first movie. Don't worry, Superkiller fans, Snyder manages to sneak in some Superman slaughter in one of the movie's irritating dream sequences. Yeah, that's right. In the first hour, anytime it appears something interesting is happening, it turns out to be a dream. Great storytelling. The first half of this movie is dull beyond belief and doubles down on the bleak, dour, and depressing tone of Man of Steel. We can add "angry" to the mix this time, as a lot of characters are just so angry they're frothing at the mouth. Chief among these whiners is Batman, who is mad as hell and not going to take it anymore and never stops reminding us of this fact in every single scene. The script is disjointed and dumb, giving the appearance of dealing with weighty ideas while never coming close to actually doing it. For example, the main theme running throughout the first hour and change of the movie is just dropped once the fighting starts and the movie never returns to it. I hate that. If you're going to act like you're more grown-up than the average superhero movie, then follow through with it. Don't just cop out and leave it dangling while you devote the final hour to your hyperviolent action scenes and CGI monster.

The second half of the film is the mindless action and destruction that we got so much of in Man of Steel. Hack Snyder has quickly become the superhero film's own Michael Bay. The best parts of the movie, to me, were the Clark Kent parts. No, not Superman. The Clark parts, with Lois and Perry and his parents (yes, parents plural as Pa Kent shows up in a hallucination or something). These are the only times the movie has any real heart or human connection. The rest of the time it's someone whining, killing, or whining about killing. Unfortunately, the Clark parts are very brief and make up a fraction of the movie in total. For their parts, Henry Cavill and Amy Adams again do well and come out of the movie smelling better than most of their co-stars. Although I really don't get what the point was of that business where Adams' Lois throws a spear into a pool of water only to have to retrieve it two minutes later. Honestly, though, there's quite a bit about this mess that needs explaining and that's pretty low on the list.

Much of the focus in this one is spent on propping up Batman and introducing him as part of the murderverse. On that note, I've seen a lot of praise directed towards Ben Affleck for his performance and I must admit I don't get that at all. He's not bad but he's not particularly good either. The script doesn't give him a chance to show what he can do besides growl and destroy things every chance he gets. He never rises above the material so I can't get behind any praise parties thrown in his honor. Jesse Eisenberg is the film's villain and he is just the worst. Absolutely terrible! I refuse to call his character Lex Luthor since he is only that in name, certainly not in any characteristic that I recognize of Lex's. Basically Eisenberg is trying to do Heath Ledger's Joker here and failing miserably. He's annoying in every single scene and by the end you find yourself wondering why he is spared of the murderousness that the DC heroes have shown themselves to possess in these two movies. If you're going to kill bad guys, why leave the worst one alive?

Wonder Woman is also here. That's basically all I can say about that. She doesn't speak much and it's taken for granted the audience is full of fanboys who know all about why she's there so no explanations are given. She's peppered throughout the movie as a Catwoman stand-in (sexy thief that flirts with Batman), to then show up in all her costumed glory (darkened colors, of course) to help in the big fight against the CGI Doomsday at the end. She's got a sword, because that's a thing now and it will undoubtedly help her with murdering in her own film, since she doesn't get to murder anyone here. We also get teases of Aquaman, Flash, and Cyborg. No explanations, just teases. Again, if you aren't a fan following all the information for these movies that comes out, you will be lost about half of this stuff. Which is just terrible storytelling but I am to the point of giving up on trying to understand the rationale behind those making the decisions on DC's films. There's a lot of reasons that Marvel is succeeding while DC flounders and, if you don't get those reasons by now, you probably never will.

All I can say is that if you really loved Man of Steel's tone and thought that was the perfect direction to take a series of superhero movies, then you'll probably love this one. I did not love Man of Steel, although I tried so very hard to find positives about it since I have been a lifelong Superman fan. But my patience and good will has been exhausted and, from now on, I will be meeting every DC film with a very critical eye. This film is overlong, pretentious, unnecessarily grim, and just plain not fun to watch. There's not a single moment from this that put a smile on my face. Not one. How can you make a movie teaming up the two most recognizable superheroes ever and have it be so damn depressing?

title: Dreadful film-making with no understanding of original characters
review:
This movie was probably the most awful superhero movie since Green Lantern. It's very hard to find a point to begin with, what makes this wannabe homage to iconic comic books such a dreadful experience. Maybe we can start with the absurd and weird dream sequences, which are very hard to distinguish from scenes in the "real world". They made no sense whatsoever and seemed completely out of place in this movie.

What bothers me the most is, that Zac Snyder doesn't seem to understand the characters he is dealing with. The Batman in this movie is completely overwritten in his anger, hate and dreadfulness. Though the opening scene is handled OKish, I found it quite hard to understand, why Wayne would feel such rage against Superman. At least, Superman has done good stuff, as we are shown throughout the movie. Why Batman/Bruce Wayne wouldn't try to talk to Superman in the first place is beyond me. Instead he wants to outright murder him, which is not something Batman would do. Despite being cruel and quite vengeful, he still feels himself bound to justice. That's a very important part of his character, Snyder isn't able to grasp. And by the way: The whole opening premise collapses like one of the many buildings in this movie during the final fight, which is so ludicrous, even Wonder Woman cannot make it look exciting.

On the other hand there is Superman/Clark Kent. Both roles are severely underwritten. Clark Kent has - in contrast to Bruce Wayne - basically nothing to do and remains a blank sheet throughout the hole movie. Unfortunately, Superman doesn't show to be a richer persona, as well. His lines of dialogue must fit on paper napkin, the meaningful ones should find enough space on a post-it-note. The biggest problem of Snyder is, that he doesn't find many "Supermany" things to do for Superman. His unique abilities are, much like in Man of Steel", not really put to use. Instead, Superman ends up being thrown into and flying out of buildings a lot of the time. There is some punching, some eye-beams, then some throwing again. It's so tedious.

In the end, Superman and Batman should find themselves on the same side, arguing about the means to reach their goal of bringing justice to people. It's this conflict, that makes Frank Miller's iconic graphic novel "The Dark Knight" so gripping. This movie is anything but.

title: Very much a disappointment
review:
DC makes great animated features. The Justice League series and independent DTV movies are very solidly entertaining. Same for the various animated Batman series as well. Even their live- action TV shows have been mostly compelling (well, except for Supergirl...). Yet somehow, most of their attempts to bring Superheroes to the Big Screen just fail to deliver. I except the first two Chris Reeve movies.

Man of Steel wasn't perfect, but held promise for something greater. That promise was broken in BvS. The casting, the convoluted plot, the apparent choice to not adequately light scenes so we could see what the heck was going on, etc. completely detract from the story they might have been trying to tell. It's very telling when so many reviewers even admit they're giving this substandard film a 10 "just to offset the negative ratings".

On a positive note, this has given me very low expectations for any future Justice League films; maybe I'll enjoy them more as a consequence. Ideally, they'll get their act together by then, but I'm not optimistic.

title: An overblown, disjointed start of a franchise
review:
This movie has been something of a milestone in my life in that it has been the first time I've intently followed a film's development and then seen it fall flat. It's honestly a bit jarring to see something with so much hype and so much good material as its basis crash and burn so badly with so many problems.

Continuing the story that began in "Man of Steel", "Batman v Superman" shows a changed world. Superman (Henry Cavill), a god among men, is treated as much with reverence as he is with suspicion. And among those who wants him destroyed is Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg), for vaguely defined reasons I couldn't remember with a gun to my head. Meanwhile, in Gotham, Batman is waging a personal war on crime, leaving branded criminals and terrified bystanders in his wake. His violent approach catches the attention of Superman, who tries to tackle him as a civilian through his job at the Daily Planet. Bruce Wayne, on the other hand, witnessed the destruction of Metropolis during Superman's fight with Zod and is concerned that Superman will turn against the world and rule it.

Just to get to the casting you've probably been wondering about: Ben Affleck wasn't at all bad as Bruce Wayne and Gal Gadot was good as Wonder Woman, even if her part in the movie was a bit small and I didn't care for the way Batman was written here. Sure, he has a cool look and good fight scenes and a background faithful to the original story we all know, but he is ridiculously brutal, even by Batman standards. Between his use of firearms during fights and the fact that his Batwing has more heavy weaponry than a fighter jet, plus he actually means to kill Superman, not capture him, he is such a departure from the principled Batman of the comics.

I had very mixed feelings about Eisenberg as Luthor. On the one hand, he gives a very entertaining performance that captures the comic book Luthor's planet-sized ego and contempt of Superman and he adds some humor to many Superman-related scenes that would have been mind-numbingly bleak without it. Unfortunately, Eisenberg's Luthor has a seriously psychotic streak that makes it hard to see him as the head of a major corporation; instead, he comes off as more of a highly funded, slightly saner Joker. While Bryan Cranston, whom many wanted for the role, would probably have been great as the comic Luthor, Eisenberg makes a good fit for whoever the hell the guy in this movie is.

While there were some other acting performances here that I enjoyed, such as Laurence Fishburne as a no-nonsense, tough-talking Perry White, Jeremy Irons as Bruce Wayne's snarky, yet caring butler Alfred, the movie as a whole is a total mess. Many of the scenes are fine on their own, sometimes even good, but they have no real flow when they are played together. It's like Snyder just put effort into a bunch of cool scenes, shot additional scenes based around them and then just patched everything together like a quilt. The scene where Batman takes on a warehouse full of armed thugs, for example, was completely mind blowing. It was intense, it looked amazing, it was elegantly edited and was the kind of action I like to see in a Batman movie. Unfortunately, this scene is clumsily inserted into the middle of the climax, while the big final battle is happening elsewhere. While Batman is fighting for something vital to the plot in the warehouse, that bit could and should have been placed somewhere else in the movie, such as the introduction scenes.

The visuals of the movie also fail on several levels. While I mostly like Zack Snyder's sense of visual aesthetics and some of the more low-key fight scenes, like the warehouse fight scene described above, are pretty good, the bigger ones during the climax are a pure assault on the senses. They are loud, flashy and run more on the sight of buildings being destroyed and violent close-quarter fighting than conflict. The climax basically boils down to lots of flashy blasts and explosions and not much else.

In case you haven't before seen the possible pitfalls of a superhero movie that's setting up way too many sequels (looking at you, "Age of Ultron"), this movie stomps into all of them. In case the subtitle didn't hint it, "Batman v Superman" gives us a first look at the new cinematic Justice League, but it does so in the clumsiest and most ham-fisted way imaginable. For starters, there's the visions that Bruce Wayne has, such as the one of a future where Superman is a tyrant, that obviously teases the future Justice League movie. Then there's the way we are first introduced to the new Justice League members: putting the plot on pause and having Wonder Woman watch a bunch of video clips of the future members. Because what's more fun to see in a superhero movie than a character watching video clips? With its questionable writing and overblown, effect-driven action scenes, "Batman v Superman" is enough to not just make me worry about the future of DC Comics on celluloid, but worry about filmmaking today. The film is everything that's bugging moviegoers and film critics alike about big movie franchises; planning ahead for countless future entries at the expense of the current one, relying on special effects rather than storytelling, and banking on the high profiles of the characters it adapts without concern for what fans actually like about them. If you're still interested, "Batman v Superman" makes for a passable few hours in a movie theater, but not much else.

title: Urgh just horrible
review:
This film is just horrible. What's wrong? Listing all the points would involve too many spoilers, and take several pages, so let me try to generalise. Or maybe I won't. Please don't read this if you plan on seeing the movie, although personally I would urge you not to, so as not to encourage or finance any more garbage like this to be made.

The movie is too long. Waaay too long. You could feel (and in several cases) hear the audience urging the film to end as we entered the last self-indulgent 15 minutes. I think we had maybe 3 or 4 endings one after another.

Early in the film Superman is demonised on very flimsy evidence and the (American) public come to hate him. He should have moved to Mexico where it's clear that he is still loved. The logic goes that because Superman is all-powerful the best thing to do is to destroy him before he destroys us. I felt that was a stretch to create a story that never really held water, was never believable in any way (yes yes I know it's a superhero movie). And even if the senate committee and general public felt that way, surely Batman wouldn't?

Around the same time that everyone is hating on Superman, Superman himself starts hating on Batman and his literal branding of criminals. So we're nicely set up for these two to battle it out, egged on (and manipulated) by Alex Luthor (son of Lex).

Ben Affleck turned in a decent performance as Batman but Henry Cavill was better. Really I shouldn't single out any of the cast as I have no quibble with the all-round good performances that were turned in by the strong cast. Although I wasn't keen on Jesse Eisenberg as Luthor but that's probably just me.

Back to the awfulness itself (having exonerated the cast I suppose I have to blame the director and writers). I think the movie didn't really flow and on the second occasion that a dramatic scene turned out to be Bruce Wayne daydreaming, I was ready for the inevitable BOO! JUMP OUT YOUR SEAT moment. Zzzz what a tired and lazy film technique.

Later on, a Lord of the Rings troll appears and a LotR "fire whip" too. Then we have a Harry Potter vs. Voldemort moment as Superman battles the troll, helped by Batman as they have since reconciled in a way that seemed absolutely as unbelievable as their contrived enmity.

Finally Wonder Woman shows up to save the day. I felt bad for her character and the actress: she should have got her own movie and not be tagged on to this one as what felt like an afterthought.

The dramatic final battle is a stunning waste of amazing CGI because by this time I don't think anybody cared who won. Well of course we all knew that good would triumph. But our journey with the characters had been such a long and boring one that I (and my companions) just wished it would hurry up and end.

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice (2016) is the biggest letdown of 21st century!
review:
I feel like I have wasted precious 151 minutes of my life watching this movie. Believe me when I say this, I wanted to like it, a lot, and I am sorry to say this, but I hated it. Here is why...

Zack Snyder tried stuffing too many plots into a single movie, and he failed to deliver on many levels. The script is bad, jumping between plots is confusing, almost all the characters failed to develop any kind of connection with the audience, the use of flashbacks is way too much, and the story is just simply lame. The only good thing about the film has to be Wonder Woman played by Gal Gadot and you have seen almost all of her screen-on-times on the trailers already. I really wish DC would have kicked-off its extended universe with a little bit more quality than this piece of absolute crap.

Who am I kidding? You're still going to go and watch this movie, after all its Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman for Christ sake! Just don't keep your hopes up, you are going to get severely disappointed, as I was.

title: Rest in peace DC
review: This movie could not have went in a worse direction. With too many side-plots and plot holes, the "story" is practically impossible to be invested in. Too many writers had too many vastly separate ideas, and as a result will leave you shaking your head in confusion. Also, this movie is not "Batman VS Superman". The two battle for about 5 minutes before returning to the unapologetically poor story. The movie is basically a sequel to "Man Of Steel" featuring Batman, Except at least in "Man Of Steel" the characters had motives for their actions. Simply put, Batman, Superman, and Lex Luthor have no legitimate reason for their actions throughout the entirety of the film. One may argue that their motives were simply led by pure paranoia, but this is never explained. Therefore, there is no real rhyme or reason for anything in this movie to happen. Finally, Batman/Bruce Wayne is the worst character in this movie, which is saying a lot. Batman amounts simply to a hot tempered whiny bitch throughout the whole film, and it left me wondering why they didn't just make a justice league movie and leave him out. In fact, why even continue the "Man Of Steel" story? There was no need for such a convoluted plot,the premise is already kinda silly in perspective. However, I did like the concept of a world that views Superman as a controversial figure. If only it wasn't a concept ripped from "The Incredibles". Don't even get me started on the "young Bruce bat levitation" scene >.<

title: "All that is powerful can't be good"
review:
Proceed with caution.

"All that is powerful can't be good. And all that is good can't be powerful". Deep. Dark. A logical paradox. Impressed? So was I...but not for long. What started off as a promise of a big bang ends with fluttering flare put out by an incoherent and weak plot. It's Batman Vs Superman. But what we get is a rouge Batman and a distracted Superman settling their petty squabbles with a brief fist fight that ends before it even starts.

Without any comparison to the standards set by The Dark Knight - a dark and gritty take of a hero battling his own demons to outwit another demon, Batman Vs Superman plays upon the concept of dark and gritty excessively that the plot crumbles in its own weight and gets lost. You get disconnected as an audience. A superhero movie with great potential turns out to be a big emotional and psychological noise.

Batman has a purpose. He knows what he is doing. He doesn't have pretentious thoughts or notion about anyone. He is smart. He is meticulous. But here we see a sloppy batman, haunted by nightmares, whose motive to start a vengeance against Superman makes no sense at all.

And Superman, well let's not go there. How his will can be broken so easily is beyond me. And Doomsday? Felt more like a finale from a Power Ranger movie.

Henry Cavil is as charming as ever. A perfect Superman. Ben Affleck's chest had more expression than his face. But then again, an aging batman can't be the excuse, or can it?

Yes the effects were good. Yes the cinematography blended in with the actions like poetry, were good. But that is all you are going to get. After waiting for 3 years, a movie that promised to leave you wanting for more ends up in a sad afterthought, "that's it?" Maybe the movie is right after all...

"All that is powerful can't be good. And all that are good can't be powerful".

title: Batman v Superman was a really fun true fan movie.
review: This movie was epic on every level. The fights, the cameos, and the visuals were just beautiful to watch. If you are a DC or true superhero fan you will utterly enjoy most of this movie. Batman was no doubt the best part of the movie. Ben Affleck is no doubt now the definitive Bruce Wayne/Batman. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman stole every scene she was in. This was really essentially because now more casual movie-goers will be anticipating and more accepting to her movie next year. Henry Cavill's superman was underplayed or so it felt like, however, when he was in action the Synder visuals were breathtaking. The only problem I had with this movie was that straight away after Batman and Superman fought they were calling each other friends. I don't think their relationship was fleshed out enough to make them two friends. They could've worked together to stop Doomsday and then work on being friends in the Justice League movie. The overall pacing of the film also felt a bit rushed and the extra 30-minute director's cut will now be very anticipated by fans that want to see the story evolve. Other than that everything about this movie was amazing. Thank you very much Mr Zach Synder, although we pressured you so much but you came through like a true hero!

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice Review: You know you've sunk to a new low when last year's Fantastic Four is no longer the most boring superhero movie ever
review:
Reviewed by: Dare Devil Kid (DDK)

Rating: 1/5 stars

"Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" derails a potentially powerful story along with some of the most iconic heroes of comic folklore for an obsession with dark tones and darker themes that are all just a poor excuse for mimicking Christopher Nolan's "Dark Knight Trilogy" masterpiece. While that trilogy was by far the darkest of all superhero movies, it was also extremely engrossing, thoroughly entertaining, and overall fun to watch, with even a bit of humor strewn here and there - elements that Director Zack Snyder and writer completely forgot were intrinsic to a superhero film's success. They all don't have to provide as much fun and humor as Marvel's movies (though "Captain America: Winter Soldier" showed that Marvel can even find a much darker tone amidst their staple fun times), but in aiming for everything dark and grimy under the night sky, things certainly don't need to get lifeless and morose.

"Dawn of Justice" is plainly and simply a shockingly joyless and overtly prolonged affair that presents its two beacons of justice as angry, cranky, melancholic, gullible men-in-tights. As far as the acting goes: Irons and Adams aren't given any scope to showcase their superlative acting chops; Affleck looks the part but can't act the part; for some inexplicable reason Snyder is still adamant about not allowing Cavill to act when he's proved that he most certainly can; and Eisenberg desperately needs a new acting style. Add to that the big, loud, bloated nature of the film, with everything transpiring within it feeling vacuous, and you end with a profoundly dissatisfying movie- watching experience that's ugly, incoherent, and unmitigatedly boring in every sense.

I mean, when Alfred couldn't care less about what his beloved Master Bruce does anymore, or if Wonder Woman has better things to do than save the world, we should probably take a cue and leave this hot, steaming pile of dump in the doldrums where it belongs.

title: Another Underrated Snyder Film
review:
I personally love Zack Snyder and believe that he's The Most Underrated Director in the business. I'm a big fan of his work with 300, Dawn of The Dead and especially Man of Steel which still has a couple problems but overall pretty solid. I anticipated BvS for about 3 years since it was announced and that movie did not disappoint.

Critics seem to have a gripe against Zack Snyder overall (300-60% Rt, Watchmen 50% and MoS 50%). Clearly the critics continue to bash the talented director giving the film 41% on RT. Just like MoS, the film has split the media right down the middle.

I must've seen a different film to the idiotic critics as they state complaints that contradict, not only the supporters but other complainers. Say, perhaps a critic had said that Ben Aleck was terrible and boring however another critic with similar gripes would say he's the best part of the movie.

Unsurprisingly, I cannot see the flaws the critics say at all. Though i loved lex, i can understand why some people don't. However, the main complaints seems to be that the structure and storytelling parts aren't strong at all. My experience with the film is that it was almost perfect and the lead up was well served. In my opinion, I just see that critics are just complaining about the minor,minor,minor,minor, issues with the film and making them seem like they stick out like a sore thumb since it was so anticipated. The film has very minimal flaws. Just because it was slightly different to your expectation, it doesn't mean that it's terrible.

I won't sugarcoat my opinion in this review and I will get somewhat nasty in some points, but believe me when I say that these words pain no one more than me, because I wanted to love this film with all my heart. Yet this is a real disappointment. It is everything I feared it would be, but prayed for it no to be. This is actually one of the most frustrating films I have seen in a long time, because for every reason you are given to enjoy and admire it, you are handed another two to get turned off, and this gets worse the more and more the film goes on.

Unfortunately, there are no two ways around it, this is Zack Snyder all over again and his difficulty in storytelling which we find once again here. It definitely helps that the screenplay is actually solid and probably what saves this movie from the disaster it could have been. Yet, Snyder, does not manage to make this into an organic film. Now, of course there is some blame to be given to the studio for overloading this film to the point where it would seem impossible to make it coherent, but I have to admit that this is not the central problem the film has, even if it could have done with something less.

The problem is simply the chaotic and boring story we are handed and even worse, how some of the characters fit into it. There is so much that is unclear, left unexplored, but even more so, character motivations that shift uncontrollably and leave you scratching your head repeatedly. Moreover, there is a collection of the worst superhero film clichés all tied together into one sweet package that by the end of the film almost got me to the point where I felt insulted in my intelligence. The whole last hour is a preposterous third act mess that really screws up what up until then was a quite decent film, even if it lacked momentum and most importantly the struggle of the two title characters which is repeatedly sidelined in favor of subplots and intrigue that frequently result aimless. Not to mention the whole ending which goes on for eternity with an emotional dryness. Basically the film does not flow and ends up being a mess.

There is some insight to what the film is trying to put forward, some of the thematic undertones manage to emerge occasionally and put forward a collection of scenes that actually carry some gravitas. But unfortunately that is undermined firstly by the fact that the movie never, ever delivers on its title promise, but even more so by the fact that any storytelling or emotional momentum is overwhelmed by bad character development, a little too much spoon feeding to the audience and worst of all a CGI orgy that gets worse and worse to the point where the screen is exploding and you have absolutely zero investment in what is going on. Not even some of the usual visual goods Snyder brings to his movies manage to truly emerge here because of the mess that is constantly going on in at least one of the various filmaking components.

There are still things that can be enjoyed, Zimmer and Junkie Xl really do something special here. It might be a little too much of what we expected, but still there is no denying how much their music elevates a lot of stuff. Henry Cavil remains a great Superman ad Ben Affleck is inspired casting. Gal Gadot is surprisingly good for what she has to do. And overall the first hour of the film actually had something going on, the point is that as soon as it starts stretching and overstating its welcome, other than not delivering much emotional beats or pay off, you start to phase out more and more and the film never picks up again, instead getting worst.

I know that everyone on the planet will go see this film and I am not saying people shouldn't do that. I felt personally that the film really let me down and was an indicator of many things wrong with the genre.

title: Can't believe this is a big budget movie
review:
There is a show that has a good script despite mediocre directing and vise versa. There is also a show that can be saved by a good directing despite mediocre writing.

This show have none of that..

But after all, if you don't know how to tell a story, It must be writing a script is not your thing, and I suggest you better find alternative job you good at. Because create an incoherent script is the same as making the whole production suffered.

This show is a prime example about a big budget movie goes wrong in all aspect from directing, writing, and acting. The directing is just plain awful, just look at the first half of the show, the dramatic tension is all over the place without flowing well. Well your actor might be confused and going on "what am I supposed feel because your awful script and directing" mode (well your character is just carricature, I'm sure your actor knows it). Can't believe this show get a good rating.

title: A train wreck. Worst superhero movie since Green Lantern.
review:
This movie is a train wreck. Slow paced, horrible script and bad directing. It has many pieces that could have worked if they had focused in on it but sadly it never does. title: Bat-boring, super-disappointing non-delivery
review:
Just as with people who liked the retread that was The Force Awakens, I just cannot comprehend at all that so many fan boys are trying to convince themselves that BvS is a good (or God forbid, great) movie. It is a *terrible* movie, shock-full of absurd shortcomings. You never feel anything at all for any of the characters; the storytelling is completely horrid and unconvincingly self-important. All characters besides the two mains feel like they're only there as brief vignettes; there is zero sense of their being part of an actual, on-going narrative. And I'm saying this as a long-time comic book reader and collector; as a big superhero fan. Here's just a few of the movie's many problems (and yes, there are a few spoilers here):

  • Was Batman's stealing the kryptonite a part of Luthor's plan? It didn't seem to be, yet it played a key part in Luthor's plan to pit Batman against Superman. So, huh? I call that a plot hole.


  • How did Luthor learn Superman's secret identity? This wasn't explained.


  • How did Batman find Martha Kent in the undisclosed location? Not explained.


  • So many story elements were just included as throw-aways, incl. the big thing at the end. That's completely meaningless. And speaking of the final fight, Superman should not have been able to carry that spear. He was vulnerable to it; there were two other major characters who could have carried it without being affected by it; it's more logical that one of them would have done it. Only, if they had, we wouldn't have gotten that nonsensical shock-value throw-away ending.


Almost nothing worked in this movie. Mindless action, no characterization, ridiculous pacing, overwrought stylism with no substance. Who the hell likes this sort of stuff? I liked about two things about this movie. I liked the early sequence with the flash- back to Metropolis being destroyed by Zod's people in the first movie; it was visually spectacular in a way that worked. The other thing I liked was Luthor's overall character arc. He pits the two mains against each other (thus providing a proper explanation for why they fight, which really needed one!) and he's aware of the more cosmic implications of what's going on, unlike the other characters. However, I didn't particularly like Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of him. I don't have anything against Eisenberg (I loved him in The Social Network), but the way he played Luthor as some kind of insecure, twitchy psycho just seemed stilted and artificial to me. Neither he nor any of the other characters, except Wonder Woman, felt anywhere near real or relatable. The romance between Clark and Lois also fell flat; we are introduced to it in the beginning of the movie, but apart from two kisses along the way, there is no feeling whatsoever in the course of the movie that these two are in a relationship. All the characters just feel dead.

It's a shame. I was hoping to like this movie. I wasn't overly fond of Man of Steel, but I didn't hate it, either; I rated it a 7 out of 10. BvS is much worse and can garner only a 2. This DC Murderverse movie is just incredibly terrible. I never thought we would get a movie compared with which Man of Steel looks like a wholesome, competent, better story, but that is what we have gotten. Most people will agree with this appraisal in the fullness of time, no doubt.

title: Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Debacle
review:
Spoiler dodging will make this harder, so be warned I might drop one or two, but if you have any sense you'll hunt down the spoilers and avoid the movie.

Okay, so where did they go wrong?

They tried to fit so much story into the movie that none of it was realised. Introducing a new take on Lex Luthor, this time as a smart crazy teen, while also introducing a new Batman (Ben Affleck) at a later stage in his life and changing the core aspect of Batman's history, while introducing Wonder Woman, while putting in hints for the next movie while having Superman lose the trust of the people; I can see why the extended cut is over 3 hours long, but:

1. The characters got no development. Batman was two dimensional and the writers seemed to be relying on prior knowledge of the DC Universe to fill the character out (all the characters, really)but then made so many inappropriate changes that anyone who did know the universe would have been put off by the concept. For audience members that had no prior knowledge, the lack of character development would leave those poor souls guessing.

2. While I was concerned about Ben Affleck being cast as Batman I will be fair and objective; there was so little in the script that in any way 'read' like Batman, and there was so very little for Affleck (or any of the actors) to work with in the script, that it is impossible to judge his performance. His performance did seem somewhat wooden, but when the script is a metaphorical plank, perhaps wooden is all you can give.

3.Wonder Woman was unidentifiable as Wonder Woman unless you knew either a) that she was going to be in the movie or b) you had the prior universe knowledge I mentioned earlier, and most likely c) both of these factors. And I can't speak too much about the casting, but I think they said, "get me a brunette with an accent or who can do an accent." She may be a good actor (I haven't seen her in anything else so I don't know), but not for this role. Her two dimensional performance can once again be put down to the one dimensional script (congrats to all the actors for finding a second dimension in that morass).

4. Lex Luthor came across more like the Joker. A rich, spoiled, childish brat of a Joker. Imagine everything Luthor is supposed to be then throw away everything except 'smart'. Not a genius, just 'smart'.

5. Because of the convoluted, rushed, weak, and ill-conceived nature of the story, the concept and the script, Jeremy Irons was wasted. Enough said.

Ultimately, I got the feeling from this movie that Warner Brothers were trying desperately to play catch-up with Marvel. What Marvel did over five movies in the lead up to 'Avengers', Warner Brothers tried to do in one. It could have been done over three movies (on top of 'Man of Steel') or perhaps even two if they decided not muck about and used Grant Gustin as Flash and Stephen Amell as the Green Arrow. Or they could have decided to play it smart, do it over five movies, like Marvel, but giving it a uniquely DC look, instead of leaving the DC look out of it, as they did here.

I was going to wax poetic about the screenwriters, but as I write this review I find myself thinking that they probably had every producer, accountant and executive at WB in their offices every other day, telling them how to do their jobs.

Good points? Amy Adams and her portrayal of Lois Lane. She had the only character that was even slightly accurate, and she managed to realise her character effectively. The only other positive I can think of is the closing credits – they rolled, just three and a half hours too late.

title: Loud, inane, violent, crude garbage that spits in the faces of fans
review:
Spoilers in general tone and a few details that you already know if you've seen the trailers; just not taking any chances after that warning up top.

----

The Batman character portrayed here might as well be the love child of Donald Trump and Dick Cheney, on bad meth. And that's probably the kindest thing anyone can say about him.

This IS NOT a dig against Ben Affleck, who spends well over two hours utterly convincing us of the way Batman sees himself, the world, and particularly one Superman, revealed in time to be Clark Kent. Henry Cavill's Kent/Superman feels very familiar to his fans; if you could see the character you grew up with while watching Cavill in Man of Steel, then you'll have few qualms about his portrayal here. He's the quintessential straight arrow who's learned the hard way that not everybody always plays by the rules, even the "good guys", but he's not letting that stop him.

Batman, on the other handwhere to start? The old Batman, up to and generally including the Christopher Nolan epic cycle, is all about bringing the Bad Folks (Guys and Gals) to lawful justice. It's REALLY hard to do that if they're dead. Yes, he's deeply shaken by losing people in the attack of General Zod on Gotham City, which chillingly, and in the mind of this survivor gratuitously, evokes detailed comparison to the effects of the 9/11 attacks on New York. The new Bruce Wayne is different than the Bruce Wayne of old in other important ways as well; he takes an explicitly vengeful, hysterical response to the childhood death of his parents, leading him to say things like "if there's the merest shadow of a chance this guy (Superman) could do that (destroy everyone on Earth with his superpowers), then I HAVE to TAKE HIM OUT!" The fan mind quails at trying to place those words in the mouth of Christian Bale's/Christopher Nolan's Batman, and utterly fails.

The violence is uniformly, lethally, over-the-top; Batman's stealth, cunning, and inventiveness in crafting effective yet non-lethal weapons has been jettisoned in favour of Shock And Awe At All Costs. And, like the Americans' military version of same, it comes to have severe, almost terminal blowback — which he grudgingly acknowledges at the very end of the film, far too late to do anything about it save through the Magic of Hollywood.

Because, underlying everything, this is what it is: a cynical, exploitative, crude commercial cash grab. There are, or will be, games on your computer and online. There are, or will be, theme park attractions calculated to sell lots of extra-price admission tickets, souvenirs, and other merchandising tie-ins. There will be sequels for as long as there is money to make them.

Not all is gloom and doom. Laurence Fishburne as Perry White will delight and motivate fans of Fishburne in the scant few minutes his very human Perry White is on screen. Diane Lane as Martha Kent isn't given any great lines, but she does her considerable best to add a third dimension to what was clearly written as a near-cardboard character, despite having been defined so clearly for so long. Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman is someone I'll be keeping an eye out for any other opportunities I have to watch her work; she gets better lines than Diana Lane does, and action as well, and she makes the awesome look nearly effortless; you soon stop seeing the actress rather than the character.

And it was absolutely delicious to see Jesse Eisenberg, an actor whom I had grown to generally loathe, taking on the role of Lex Luthor and playing him the way he always should have been played — as a spoiled brat of a megalomaniac who just HAS to control everything he can think of — and he has a depressingly amazing imagination. Mr Eisenberg, your agent has no doubt been telling you for years that you'd do much better as the unsympathetic Bad Guy cartoon character. This role should have taught you not only that he (your agent) is a very wise man, but that playing these roles is several hells of a lot more fun than, say, Mark Zuckerberg.or J Daniel Atlas. You're also that much better at them.

Should you see it? If you're a strong, traditional Batman fan, the answer is an emphatic "NO; run away; run screaming away". If you're in love with any incarnation of Superman from 1933 to 2013, the answer is a qualified "maybe, but you're going to have to see this AND THE NEXT MOVIE to see Your Guy look good". Those hoping to see the Justice League form, way too early in this timeline, will be tantalised but ultimately disappointed. Above all, the superpower most on display is the one that empties your wallet and your aspirations.

title: Overstuffed
review:
1. Batman v Superman feels like one of those films your friend made and you want so badly to ignore all the bad stuff and point out the good with compliment sandwiches.

2. Ben Affleck is a badass Batman. I wish there had been more of him. He is just not around enough. He's fine as Bruce Wayne but I wanted to see more of them. The best scene in the movie is where he's throwing down against those Russian henchmen in the vein of Arkham Asylum. Just goes to show, dark and gritty always goes well with Batman.

3. There is way too much going on in this movie. There's Batman hating Superman. There's a Congressional inquiry. There's crazy Lex Jr. There's Diana Prince. There's the bullet subplot. There's Wally, played by Scoot McNairy. And they still manage to chuck in the Batman origin story in the opening credits. The problem with such an enormous cast is that you need everyone to be doing things at all times. Amy Adams is shunted into the bullet subplot because she's Amy Adams and you can't have a Superman movie without Lois Lane. Holly Hunter's Senator Finch has a lot of promise, but she becomes an antagonist to Luthor for some strange reason. There's a half-baked explanation as to why Wally is antagonistic to Wayne. While we're trying to keep track of a dozen plot lines, important hints relating to the actual fight are lost.

4. The titular fight does not go on nearly long enough. Their initial clash during the high- speed Batmobile chase was tantilising but the fight itself was over like *that*. We all knew they'd end up being pals but boy does it just feel like a giant middle finger. The fight with Doomsday ends up being pretty cool (especially with the intervention of Wonder Woman, who kicks ass), even though Batman is predictably dumped on the sidelines for lack of power.

5. I'd love to give Chris Terrio (Oscar winner for Argo) credit for the good moments in the screenplay (some awesome lines, great political subtext, etc) and then forgive him for the overstuffed mess by the fact that Snyder was trying to cram an entire Phase One into this one movie. I went nuts for that "Martha" connection. The best written moment in the movie happens in Superman's Congressional hearing, and it devastates me that they weren't brave enough to follow through with it completely, but it was still hugely powerful and the clues were spread like Chris MacQuarrie. The worst moments are the dream sequences, which make absolutely no sense and ultimately play like Thor's lightning bath fantasy in Age of Ultron.

6. Henry Cavill is flat as Superman. Lord help us if he ends up as James Bond. Amy Adams tries her best but suffers from underwriting. There's only so much a talented actress can do with "be damsel in distress". She sees horrifying executions at the start of the film and kinda gets over it. Laurence Fishburne and Jeremy Irons get barely anything to do but provide a few bits of humour. Eisenberg gave a great performance, as long as you don't get bogged down trying to reconcile him with the role of Lex Luthor.

7. I love Callan Mulvey and was thrilled to see him get a good role in this movie, but his allegiances are so confusing. I have no idea what was going on at the start of the movie with him in the desert.

8. It amused me how much Snyder just kinda did his thing all over again. Everyone smashes up buildings and have those long distance punches. But what amused me were the occasional shoe-ins like "good thing this part of town is deserted" and "that island is uninhabited!" Someone needs to smash his slow-motion button, especially when he just uses it on people walking towards graves.

9. The stakes always feel high in this movie, which I give credit to Chris Terrio. The opening stuff from Man of Steel feels like it could have come from a 9/11 documentary. The scene where Batman lures Doomsday away I felt like I was watching as a helpless spectator.

10. That music was beast! I loved the guitar riff.

There's too much going on in this movie for me to love it or even like it. But the bits I loved I LOVED, and I'm thrilled to see a Batman reboot under Ben Affleck's control.

title: Unbalanced effort at combining two superhero giants
review: First off, I share no allegiance to Marvel movies or DC movies. I am simply a movie fan, but you have to state that since many folks on this site appear to think that this film is hated out of spite. But the problems in this movie are glaring and plentiful. As a kid you could show me a film with some explosive action and I would love it, but as an adult I need to be invested in the story first to care about the action. This film fails to do that, but instead of it just being packed with action to make up for that fact, it is full of spliced together character development. The story jumps around without explanations and a once intelligent Bruce Wayne turns into a revenge thirsty thug. I agree with Snyder on the aspect of superheroes killing folks to give them more depth, however I don't think you should execute that idea by having Batman shooting guns at people. Secondly Jesse Eisenberg, he is a talented actor but he was not right for this movie. Upon seeing the first trailers I thought he was out of place, but I also thought that maybe Snyder had a trick up his sleeve and Eisenberg would blow me away. There is no trick up the sleeve, he was just as terrible for this role as he first appeared to be. The redeeming quality of this movie ends up being Wonder Woman, out of all the faults this movie contains, Snyder handled her introduction perfectly. Some of the action is well done, other times it disintegrates into CGI almost to the point of looking cartoonish. Overall this film failed, I wanted it to work so bad but it was a mess. If they continue to make new Batman movies I just hope they remove Snyder from the project.

title: Zack Snyder doesn't get 'Good' heroes
review:
Why would BVS open with Batman's origin? Have there not been enough Batman movies so far? This movie was intended to set up the idea of the Justice League. Lex Luther (groan), is a genius billionaire on par with Batman, but not in this portrayal. Here he's someone who can't even address a room full of people without regressing to a babbling infant. This Lex is more of a re-skinned Joker.

Zack Snyder doesn't understand heroes, heroic heroes. Oh, he gets the broody, psychopathic, anti-hero (batman, watchmen) but not superman. Superman doesn't threaten someone and tell them to consider it mercy. Superman is good. He had a normal childhood (by superhero origin standards), raised by loving parents in a small Midwest town. He's a well adjusted man with a moral compass that points due north. He fights for truth, justice and the American way. He's kind, humble and self-controlled. He pulls his punches most of the time to avoid turning his opponents into a greasy stain. Other justice Leaguers refer to him as the blue boyscout.

Zack Snyder doesn't seem to understand that kind of hero. I think Zack inwardly hates Superman. In this movie, the public mistrust superman and are putting him on trial. We see a man defacing superman's statue and it's portrayed in a way to makes us side with the vandal against superman. The writer of this movie identifies with Lex. He's got a grudge against God and verbalizes it through Lex to Superman.

I don't fault the acting. It was at least adequate. It could've been better if the roles were better written. DC it appears is rapidly losing ground to Marvel. In my opinion, the best Justice League was the 2006 cartoon series. Jack Kirby and Bob Kane understand heroes. They can make them in depth and real. They tell good stories while staying true to the character.

I love these characters, but what DC is doing with them brings back back memories of a second star wars trilogy. I just can't go through that again.

title: This is not really a batman v superman film
review:
After what Zack Snyder did with 'Man of Steel', i had no plans of actually going to the cinema to see this film, but fate has it, i ended up seeing it anyways, and that was because i bought the wrong tickets, i was actually going to see 'Captain America : Civil War'. But anyways, now i have seen BvS, and can say it was slightly better than i expected.

The film actually builds up nicely, it gives Bruce Wayne and Batman some backstory, we already had that from the Batman Trilogy from Christopher Noland, but probably doesn't hurt to get it served one more time, just in case we forgot something. Anyways, superman however isn't given any more depth, at all. That is a shame, because 'Man of Steel' failed really bad to picture what goes through superman's head.

This is because Zack Snyder is more of a visual artist, he focuses a lot on the special effects and the stylish presentation of the films he makes, he is not a very good director when it comes to character work.

So we have a good build up, a movie that for a long time felt like a 8/10 for me, it was suspenseful and engaging, for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, or so. problem is, this film is 2 hours and 30 minutes long, so that meant there was 1 hour to go. So what did we get in that hour?

Well you don't need to be much of a rocket scientist to figure it out, you get action scenes. One stacked upon the other. Batman is what pulls this film off at this part, as we have been given a lot of time to see his motives, and his reasons, we believe in his cause. Superman's cause is vague and difficult to understand.

But the real problem arrive when this movie turns, and is no longer about batman v superman, but turns into batman, superman & wonderwoman vs doomsday, that's where most of it went wrong.

It was unnecessary to involve this into this movie, they could have spared doomsday for the next film. Doomsday is one of the most powerful characters in any of the comics, it would fit better to see him fight the entire justice league, than just these three.

They of course involved this, because Zack Snyder want to show off his skills, and the movie studio want as much explosions as possible to show the kids, i get that. But you could have made an full movie with superman fighting batman, and made it fantastic, all the ingredients was in place. Instead in this film it ends with batman not killing superman, because their mothers have the same name.... oh my god...

Who writes this stuff?

And on top of that, why on earth would you use Lex Luthor's son? Is this suppose to be clever and creative?. It isn't. If you take your time to retell batman's story, and superman's story in 'man of steel' at least use Lex Luthor in this reboot you have created.

With "Lex Jr" into the mix, with doomsday, and with wonder woman, it gets crowded, and since Zack must please the kids, we run out of story building on the 1 hour mark, and from there, we go supersonic to the finish line.

Wonderwoman for example does not have much screen time in this film, but i think Gal Gadot plays her nicely, though little is told about the character, but she gets to show of some of her awesome moves at least.

The music in this film is sadly average. Hans Zimmer builds on the sound he created for 'Man of Steel' and it feels like ambient music all the time. Hans Zimmer should have rewrote the music for this film. In interviews Zimmer gave for 'Man of Steel' he told people he was nervous writing the score, because John Williams score was so epic, and so well known. It shows too, in what he wrote, because 'Man of Steel' is some if Zimmer's worst work, ever. It's not bad, but it's average. And a superhero movie must have more than that, it needs the epic sound.

There are of course plenty of "epicness" elsewhere in this film. The CGI are very good for the most part, though it is mostly filmed in the dark, the sound effects are good, the sound mixing are pretty good, the editing is not that bad, the cinematography is actually quite good.

And the best acting comes from Ben Affleck and Jeremy Irons. They are the duo that save the film.

But this film did the same mistake that 'Spiderman 3' did, you try to serve to much on one plate.

I wanted to see more of batman's fighting, that was truly awesome, and was maybe the best thing in the entire film. Nicely choreographed fighting scenes that almost felt to brutal to be allowed to be seen by kids. If only batman and superman could have been the main event of the entire film, all the ways these two legendary comic heroes could outsmart one another, we could have gotten one of the best superhero films of all time. Instead they overdid it, again.

6/10 - OK film, nothing special

title: Why did you say that name?!?!
review: Director Zack Snyder has proved to be the Kryptonite of this new DC universe. Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice is classic Snyder: visually adept yet narratively and thematically senseless. With two of the most compelling and popular characters in the world, numerous questions about purpose and responsibility are aimlessly wasted. Throw in resplendent amounts of religious and political imagery, and way too many dream sequences, what we're left with is a sad mishandling of what should be a powerful and (ahem) entertaining film. The opening is fantastic, as we watch Bruce Wayne and others reel from the disasters perpetrated by Superman in Man of Steel. Unfortunately from there, things go downhill fairly quickly, as story clichés (Kryptonite) and lame coincidences (Bruce and Clark's mom have the same name! Wow!) fill a convoluted plot. Worst yet, this "action" film is overstuffed with unending amounts of ethical speeches and monologues in place of actual character connections. DC's desperation to right their own wrongs in the destruction in Man of Steel becomes embarrassing ("Luckily that island was deserted"). Even when we aren't being lazily spoken at or having our emotions ineffectively manipulated, the set-pieces are largely insipid and boring. As for the pluses, Affleck is great as Batman, giving a unique turn as a sloppier, older, and angrier Dark Knight. Also, for the very little we see of Gadot's Wonder Woman, it creates an excited eagerness for her stand-alone film. However, BvS as a whole has less in common with its positives than with Eisenberg's poorly-casted Lex Luthor: frantic, ill-thought, desperate, and truly awful.

title: This movie is about as good as Ben Afflecks chubby face in the Batman suit
review: There was excitement in the air upon hearing that a fully fledged movie would be created based on the DC animated movie "Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Part 2", in which Batman has the ultimate fight with Superman. Upon seeing this film, I realized why some movies go straight to DVD over others, because they're garbage. Director Zach Snyder left no stone unturned for a horrible rendition of a classic DC animated movie, sure change things a little, not the entire plot. Zach has worked on other movies such as Dawn of the Dead, Watchmen and I'm guessing had some input on those infomercials late at night. Ben Afflecks portrayal as Batman was comedic, his face at times was spilling out of the Batman mask, not to mention the stubble mustache that materializes itself during the most critical scene in the movie. Batman also uses a "robotic" voice in order to speak, this isn't revealed as to why but it just is. Maybe they couldn't live up to the voice that Christian Bale used. Jesse Eisenbergs first appearance in the film had me asking what sort of role he was going to play, as time went on I kept telling myself "this must be Lex Luthors son?", no, Jesse Eisenberg plays the joker! Wait, hold on a second, he's Lex Luthor? With a full lock of hair. Lastly, Wonder Woman swings into action with a European accent. Wonder Woman is meant to portray all things American and she practically comes into the film speaking fluent Espanyol. Amy Adams is the only real positive to this movie, not particularly for her acting but you could say everyone came down to her level for it, so it felt OK? The story line is absolutely botched and follows the animated films plot line for around all of 20 minutes and then branches off into some ridiculous Micheal Bay themed ending. When I say ridiculous, I mean, this is utterly stupid and makes no sense. I feel like the director watched the animated film and thought "how can I ruin this completely". The story ends up being the complete opposite to the animated film and then some. It seems the film is only created in order to depict a larger DC universe that is sure to expand onto the big screen over the next decade, however, if these films are also built around a timely classic to gain the audiences attention, only to take a tangent off into a storyline the director forms in his head in a matter of days in order to make his mark on the franchise, I think I'll wait for the VHS version of them. Do they still make those anymore?

title: Haphazard arrangement of scenes, lack of flow and unimaginative use of CGI
review:
The title pretty much summarizes the entire movie. Whilst comic fans feared that Ben Affleck's Batman would ruin the movie, Zack Snyder took it upon himself to ruin the movie.

The random selection of scenes and their placement will leave you scratching your head throughout the movie if at all you manage to keep yourself from falling asleep. Each scene is probably shot and and sequenced to complete a checklist of information to be dished out to lay the foundation for the future movies in the DC Universe. Hell they even screwed with the intros of the rest of the Justice League characters.

And as per the mandate of each Superman Movie made till date, the last half an hour of the movie is a long charade about how everyone thinks Superman is dead (thats new !).

Not only are the action sequences unimaginative but they are also illogical. (I mean is it really necessary for Superman to toss the villain through half the skyscrapers in the city !? And how stupid did Batman have to be to lead Doomsday from an uninhabited island to the city hes supposed to protect.)

Thoroughly unimaginative action sequences and a CGI budget that the director probably blew off on the repetitive shock waves shot on by doomsday.

All in all it was a poor choice for the studio to have Snyder direct this one.

title: A disappointing mess
review: Contrary to most people I actually enjoyed Man of Steel. While I objected to certain option the filmmakers took, I found it to be a thorughly enjoyable super hero movie. My positive reaction to "Man of Steel" gave me some hope for this oddly titled semi-sequel, despite the involvement of the likes of David S.Goyer and Zack Snyder. Sadly I found the movie to be a sprawiling, poorly scripted and paced mess that took itself too seriously - it's dudes in capes, not Nietzsche. The attempts at philosofy and depth were laughable, but nonetheless approached by the Director as if the script was intelligently written, which certainly was not. The action (of which there was very little until the dumb mess at the end) was poorly constructed, excessively CGI'd and very unexciting. A movie featuring such iconic characters of popular America culture should have been carefully and efficiently planned out. Such a massive gathering of iconic DC comics characters could have been, if handled right (as it has been before in comic books and animated movies and TV series),been something truly special. Instead we have this mess of a movie that does not deliver in any counts. Such a wasted opportunity. I regret deeply having awarded the people involved in this mess with the price of a theater ticket - they'll actually think they have done a good job and make a equally awful semi-sequel.I haven't been this disappointed with a movie in a long time.

title: Crap movie, partial character development spoilers and a few spoilers about scenes, so don't read if you haven't seen the film yet
review: I gave this a 5 out of a 10 for the good special effects (minus the crappy looking CGI at the end) and also for the way Batman and Wonder woman look on screen, but everything else was average at best. Overall I found this movie to be boring and emotionless, especially the first 90 minutes of the film, a lot of it was not needed. They could have spent time building Lex Luthor and the other characters instead. However, there is no character build up, so when things happen you don't feel any emotion for any of the characters or their decisions. It all feels like it's just jumbled together. The opening scene was not needed and doesn't fit the rest of the movie, that would have been fine if it were a batman movie, but how many times do we need to replay the same story? We know Batman's origins already. The scenes felt very choppy and there was no flow in this film whatsoever. It really just felt like a slide show of photos. Just when you think something might happen, it just went right back down to more talking and scene switching. Eisenberg is horrible as Lex Luthor, and there is no explanation as to what he's doing or why. If they expect everyone to be aware of who he is just from the comics or past movies, then that was a mistake as well. He's not scary, he isn't a threat, he's a joke on screen. I don't see how people can view this as a good movie, it's not a good movie at all. Biased fans will say it's great, but that is because they are there to support DC, and not give a realistic view about the movie. For any fan of DC, Marvel, or any type of film about superheroes, you will be very disappointed with this film, just like I was. Maybe Marvel set the bar too high for movies now, but this is not even close to being comparable to one of the Marvel films. They are so much better. I also felt that The Man of Steel was a much better film than this one. At least that movie had some cohesion from scene to scene, and you felt emotion for the characters. I also have no interest in watching this movie a 2nd time, no replay value at all. Maybe the extended cut will be better, but I doubt a half hour can save this movie. As for the future, if someone other than Snyder directs the justice league, then it likely will be better. However, I don't see any hope of success for solo movies involving Cyborg or Aquaman. Wonderwoman and Batman are the only hopes for DC going forward. I hope this review helps.
