title: Batman v Superman is a mess...but an enjoyable one.
review:
Batman v Superman is perhaps the perfect microcosm of both Zack Snyder as a director and also the Warner Bros. vision for Superhero movies as a whole. The movie itself is a glorious mess. The pacing is all over the place, lagging for large portions of the movie, to a degree that threatens to lull the audience to sleep, and then suddenly ramping up to a speed that moves too fast for the plot in many places. There is little to no narrative flow as this movie more or less strings along unrelated scenes, end-to-end, which takes an already murky plot and throws it into near-indecipherable territory. This seems to be the biggest point of consternation for critics and is honestly a decent reason for Warner Bros. to consider asking Zack Snyder to take a step back from the director's chair, as these are all career-long vices of his (Watchmen, Man of Steel being past evidence of this).

And yet, despite all those fundamental mistakes, there's a lot to like here. Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot both proved to near perfect castings, despite early internet outrage directed toward both. If there's one major take away from this movie, it's that both character's solo movies in the DCEU have the ground work in place to be outstanding. Both Jeremy Irons and Laurence Fishburne were great too and hopefully as the DC Universe unfolds, we get even more of these ancillary characters. Also, as has become standard fare for Zack Snyder films, the film is beautiful. For everything he lacks as a story teller, the dude does some absolute magic with camera work.

Condensed down into the most generalized version, this film is being crucified to an unnecessary degree. Sure, the film whiffs on many fundamental check lists but at the same time, the good largely outweighs the bad. It's by no means perfect (particularly if you're not the type to jump out of your seat at tiny little easter eggs embedded specifically to tease Justice League). That being said, there's enough here to not only watch this movie, but also be optimistic about DC's cinematic universe going forward.

title: A Masterpiece that sets up the DCCU in a Epic way!
review: Although the pacing in ACT 1 of the movie definitely seems very out of whack the first time you watch it, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a visual, action packed masterpiece and serves off as a great launch pad of the DCCU. This movie set out to accomplished everything it wanted to do. First of all, Warner Bros establishes Ben Affleck's Batman extremely well and Ben's performance as the Dark Knight is definitely first class. I think after watching this movie Ben Affleck will without a doubt be recognized as the greatest Batman adaptation ever. Second, Henry Cavill knocks it out of the park with his take on The Man of Steel. We all know that Christopher Reeves was a great Superman, but Cavill's take on the iconic character is straight out of the Comics and he is able to make the switch from Clark Kent to Kal-El with ease. Third, DC brings the Amazonian Princess to the silver screen for the first time and she is indeed wonderful! Wonder Woman is not all the focal point of the movie, but with the small amount of time she has she is able to steal every scene she's in and leave you wanting more, but this is Batman v Superman so you will have to wait another year for her. Fourth and probably the most important thing, Warner Brothers introduces you to the other members of the Justice League, while still keeping the focal point on the conflict between Batman and Superman. Fifth, The threat that is supposed to be big enough to bring the two greatest super heroes of all time together is established in the form of Doomsday, with Lex Luthor being the power behind the conflict of these two titans. Realizing that they need each other to bring down this unstoppable threat or their world will be destroyed, the World's Finest finally come together on the Silver Screen along with Wonder Woman to finally unite the DC Trinity. I could go on and on why this movie is so great even though it obviously has it flaws as I stated before. Bottom line is true comic book movie fans will walk away from this film wanting more as the story paints a great picture of the coming doom for these characters. If you appreciate great comic movies and the Batman v Superman will quickly have you wanting to get back in the ticket line and watch it again and again. Take it from me I've already scene it 4 times. And will be better every time you watch it.

title: People fear what they don't understand
review:
Following the events of 'Man of Steel', Superman has announced himself to the world, which has caused a divide in humanity: some see him as a saviour, whilst others see him as the ultimate threat to earth. Siding with those who see Superman as a threat, Gotham City-based vigilante Batman travels to Metropolis to combat Superman. However, a much graver threat looks to endanger humanity.

After many years of development, excitement, anticipation and scepticism, two of the biggest characters in all of fiction, come face to face together for the first time in a live-action movie. There's not just the pressure of the two icons first live-action met though, but also the pressure of establishing the 'DC extended universe', a new cinematic universe featuring DC comics' line up of characters, set to the rival the successful 'Marvel Cinematic Universe'. I'm pleased to say that it is successful on both fronts.

Despite all that needed to be achieved in the film with all the threads that it has: setting up new characters, character arcs, back story, plot and just overall world-building, the film is fairly well balanced and structured, with good character development, interesting and emotional themes and moves at a breezy pace, even though the runtime is 2 and a half hours, thanks to writer Chris Terrio's solid script. The dark tone continues from 'Man of Steel', but the film does have humour in it with great witty one-liners and comments, some of the best coming from Jeremy Irons' Alfred. The humour isn't over the top though and there's just the right amount there. The mature tone gives the film tension and weight, allowing you to invest in the characters and the situation.

Of the many scepticism of the film, casting has probably been the main one, in particular the choice of Ben Affleck for Bruce Wayne/Batman. Affleck however has been cast well in the role, bringing grit and gravitas. His interpretation is one that has not been seen on screen before. Affleck's Wayne is like a war veteran, who has been fighting for 20 years and has lost so much along the way and it has taken its total on him. He is more ruthless and hardened, losing his way and boarding on a villain at times. A lot is implied and a solo Batman film with Affleck will be something interesting to watch in the future.

Much anxiety surrounded the casting of Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman as well, but again, they have chosen right. When she appears on screen, particularly when she is in action, you really believe she is Wonder Woman. She is a supporting player in this, so we don't see her as much as the title characters, but she has enough of a presence to be established and spark interest for her upcoming solo film out next year.

The third and final piece of controversial casting came in the form of Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. Here Eisenberg gives a performance of the character, like with Affleck's Batman, that we have not seen on screen before. This didn't work for me, all i saw was an OCD version of Jessie Eisenberg and i understand that he is playing lex luthor Jr not Sr but i would've much preferred the lex luthor we all know and mostly love, just imagine watching Bryan Cranston sharing scenes with Ben Affleck and Henry Cavil. Jessie Eisenberg is a good actor but he wasn't right for the role.

Henry Cavill gives another great performance as Clark Kent/Superman. He once again portrays a more complicated and humanised Superman, one that's more interesting to watch than previous film versions and much more in line with the comics. His arc ties in nicely with Batman's, as they both experience something of an existential crisis.

There's not as much action as you might think with a film like this, which is not a criticism, but an observation. When there is action though, it's really exciting too watch and every scene is well choreographed, with some ambitious set pieces. It never feels like an attack on the senses, like a lot of its contemporaries and it feeds into the character arcs and the story, like all great action should.

Hans Zimmer returns to provide the music for the film, with the addition of Junkie XL, fresh off last years successful 'Mad Max: Fury Road'. It does what all great music should in a film, heightening the experience and often making the hairs raise on the back of the neck. However, it is great and at times epic, but it does not reach the heights of previous work, in particular, Hans Zimmer's.

The pressure was on, but Snyder and his team have delivered a film that we not only deserve, but one we need right now. It's dark, emotional, witty, ambitious, epic and the dawn of an exciting new franchise.

title: An absolutely fantastic re-imagining of the stories that have already been told.
review:

Critics talking poorly about this film are obviously not familiar with the comic book story line, nor can I be convinced that they are fans of the actual series...

If they were, they'd know what's coming, and all of the "plot gaps" they're complaining about would make a lot more sense.

This film was an incredible re-envisioning of the stories that have already been told. It's really a shame that every troll with an internet connection (and a blog) thought they could just watch the movie and know what they're talking about as they picked it apart.

Mark my words.

By the time this series wraps up... It'll be one of the best super hero franchises ever created by Hollywood.

Don't buy into the negative hype... Just enjoy the ride, and know that without a doubt, this story is far from over.

Regarding what's already been done?

But really, if you're a fan, this is going to be a must see now.

I personally didn't want to wait regardless of the impending BluRay. I'm glad I didn't.

title: Bold, Brave, Brilliant...Divisive
review:
Lets get one thing straight. If you didn't like MoS, its very, very unlikely that you will not like this. Its that world, it is that Superman, its a direct continuation (and I can't honestly understand why people thought it would be any different). If you are one of the many that did like MoS, its VERY likely you will like this.

Before watching it last night I was worried. The divisive nature of the reviews from critics and fans made me sceptical. Talk of Batman not being Batman, who kills remorsely and sleeps with women not for his playboy attitude but because that's him now...it sounded wrong. And it is wrong as that is simply not true. Some of the reviews I have read are astounding in their inaccuracy. Even those on here.

Its a complicated film. The first hour can either be described as a mess of film directing or a plethora of ideas that are never fully explored but are new, are interesting, and pertinent. If anything, there is too much going on, no one strand is fully explored to its potential, no one investigation is fully seen through to a conclusion. Interspersed through this are confusing (and abstract) dream scenes and premonitions that also have little explanation or build up. There is little action in that first hour other than the opening scene. Its an introduction to this new world, a deconstruction of us, of Superman of Batman, and in a small part, of Wonder Woman.

Yet when it clicks, a little over an hour, the film moves up a layer. Synder's dedication to detail and his love of comic books is laid on its fullest. This is a film for the geek in all of us and it holds nothing back - it explains little that perhaps it should (You've seen all you are going to see of Robin in the trailer). You either take it as a love letter to the comic book fan in all of us, or you criticise it. Too me, what it did well, it did so damn well, none of the problems it has effect the overall film.

Superman's story is one of redemption and it pays off. His whole struggle is littered with divine imagery, as was MoS. its a continuation of that story. His relationship with Lois is believable and important. His interaction with Batman is superb. Their contrast is almost pitch perfect and exactly what I wanted to see.

Batman...well, what can I say. Probably the best Batman I have ever seen on film. The reports of him being too dark are way off. He's no darker here than he was in Rises. We get the best ever Batman on screen, no argument. We get the best Bruce on screen.

Lex is superb. A completely different take that is more layered than you have seen in the trailers.

And as for Wonder Woman - well, this is something I do agree with on the critics - she steals the show.

The film is nowhere near perfect - if anything there is the potential within it to be one of the greatest films ever made. It needed either expanding or trimming of some of that first hour (hopefully the directors cut will give us that film) but as it stands, its a fan triumph if not a critical one. The end fight with trinity was an event to watch only on the big screen. I don't think a smile left my face from about an hour in. Its just sheer entertainment.

Yes it has plot holes all over the place (what Superhero film doesn't) but it dares to be different. It goes to places I never thought it would. The scale and depictions of the main characters raise it above the mediocre and into the lower levels of greatness. It will be interesting to see where this ends up box office wise as coming out of the cinema, there were very few people who were not happy with what they saw.

title: Good to see again--friction between helpfulness and helplessness
review:
Well, after seeing some of the reviews I felt a certain trepidation at going to see this movie, though enjoying Snyders previous works. I went with a friend and we both loved it. The question for both of us is—will we be seeing this movie again? And the answer is a resounding yes. Speaking for myself, I have lost track of the number of times I have seen the hero films that really move me—John Carter, Battleship, Raimi's Spiderman trilogy, Captain America's The Winter Soldier, Indiana Jones, Star Trek, Thor, Avengers Age Of Ultron, 300 and Man Of Steel. I love Man Of Steel with every viewing and I think Batman v Superman is great too.

The actors were all great. I have liked Henry Cavill since the Count Of Monte Cristo and The Immortals, and find his Superman / Clark Kent the best yet, much closer in essence to the wily and smart Superman of the comics from the 1950's and 60's, and the animated shows from the 90's. And it's refreshing to see his portrayal of Clark Kent as a confident journalist trying to integrate integrity into his work. Ben Affleck was equally good as Batman, again a little closer to the sharp Holmes-like detective of earlier comics. It was a nice touch to see him gritting his teeth in the heavy armor. I always wondered why Iron Man wasn't completely punch drunk. Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg, Fishburne, Irons, Lane, Costner, Gadot and the other supporting cast were all excellent. Lane did well, as it is not always easy to draw out sympathy from an audience through tears and screams. Eisenberg's characterization of Lex Luthor, in which he interleaves restrained petulance, envy, anger and murderous manipulation, was the first that didn't make me reach for the fast forward on the remote, not that I could have in the cinema.

I cannot agree with other reviewers who feel that there are too many plot points in the film, with a little concentration it was not too difficult to keep up. In fact I think it made the film a great psychological ride, and it is Luthor, hidden in the background, who is continually fueling and stoking the fire of hate. Alfred knows who the real enemy is but bats are blind. As other reviewers have pointed out, much of the film exhibits the friction of power and powerlessness, helpfulness and helplessness. For all of his power, Superman is compelled to fight Batman knowing that to refuse would result in the immediate death of his mother, Martha Kent, and that to save her he must turn for help to the one he has already warned off and is about to face in battle, Batman. Batman, as a child, witnesses helplessly the violent death of his mother at the hands of street power. And having conquered Superman with the help of poisonous kryptonite, Batman finally hears in that moment Superman's weak cry of help, for Martha, and comes suddenly to the realization that in saving Clark Kent's mother, he may redeem himself for not having had the strength to save his own mother, Martha Wayne.

Perhaps the film is dark, I do not know. What with Batman, Kryptonite, the GM creature Doomsday, and self-doubts about whether the world even wants him, Superman undoubtedly takes a mean beating in this film. And yet in spite of it all, I was so inspired by his love for Lois Lane, and his uncompromising principle of self-sacrifice for the world, even after being fired upon by all around him.

title: Exactly how this movie should've been!

title: Wrong things at wrong times
review:
Film makers should understand that every viewer that enters the theater to watch a film comes with a clean slate. They don't have back stories to support a back-story of a character, nor all the viewers read all comics with enthusiasm.

That's what Batman V Superman exactly does not do. It just 'puts it out there', as though we hold a PhD degree in DC comics. That's where everything started to get messed up. The reason why Batman is so adamant to go against Superman itself does not hold a strong ground. Rest of the movie is just a Krypnonian (if you understand the metaphor) error of it all.

George Clooney can now finally breathe his sigh of relief. He isn't the only one who has messed up Batman's personification in live action. Kudos, Ben Affleck, you have surpassed Mr. Clooney. Gal Gadot is a miscast, I put a rest to that.

Jesse Eisenberg, however, showed some promise in the character. But comic book fans will have a bad taste. Lex Luthor is supposed to be menacing, calculative, and manipulative. Here in BVS, Eisenberg is trying to rip off Heath Ledger (acting all crazy all the time does not win you an Academy Award Mr. Eisenberg).

And for an action film, the film lacks the concept of it genre too. It's an 'action' film with all the right actions missing! Did not expect that from the man who made 300 and Watchmen. All the wrong things done at wrong times! Eat and chew Mr. Snyder, don't try to swallow it a whole. This is DEC, not MCU.

title: Critics?? Meh. This is pure entertainment, pure blockbuster, pure epic. (No Spoilers)
review:
Ignore the critics. Nobody is expecting this to receive an Oscar for Best Picture. It is, however, the epitome of a blockbuster. A modern epic. An all-out action, entertaining and enjoyable film. With amazing visuals, loud (but great) music, an ensemble cast, scene-stealing acting performances, a good plot, put in a few twists, sprinkle in a bit of humor, and you got yourself a recipe for a modern-day, 21st-century, all-out action superhero ensemble blockbuster. Evidently, Snyder makes no apology for that. Also, seeing these iconic and legendary comic book characters come to life on screen will make the little boy in everyone jump in excitement.

PROS.

1. Amazing cast and great acting.

Ben Affleck brings an all-new interpretation of the on-screen Batman and boy, did he do it with aplomb.

Henry Cavill- for me a very underrated performance, and he is now to me the definitive on-screen Superman.

Gal Gadot had limited screen time but stole every scene she was in.

Jesse Eisenberg was the one I was initially skeptical of, but he nailed it as the quirky, nerdy, IT billionaire Lex Luthor.

Amy Adams and Jeremy Irons did well, while Diane Lane and Lawrence Fishburne had small but eye-catching roles.

2. Cinematography.

Visually dark yet beautifully crafted. Several scenes took my breath away. See it in the biggest screen that you can.I can't wait to see it a few more times.

3. Music.

Great.

4. Action.

There is enough in there to satisfy the masses and comic book fan boys.

5.The FIGHT.

You know which fight I'm talking about. I isolated this on purpose as that is what it deserves. You will get back the price of your ticket by this scene alone. So far the best fight scene of all time in superhero movies. Civil war and Apocalypse will come out later but I doubt they can top this.

CONS.

1.Editing.

This is my biggest gripe not because it is the worst but because I feel that it is something that can easily be corrected. Certain scenes changed too abruptly with no transition whatsoever. For me this movie is an 8 but better editing would make it a 9.

2. "Preview" scenes.

Justice League will be out next year and it would be hard to resist including some scenes as a preview to what is to come. However just- like Avengers 2, they stick out like a sore thumb. Does not add anything to the film yet take away its flow.

3. Love scenes.

Both Cavill and Adams gave great performances individually. But when both are on-screen together something just feels amiss- the lack of chemistry was apparent.

4. CGI. Although the cinematography was amazing, there were 2 scenes in which the CGI was atrocious- one involving a car chase and the ending involving Doomsday. A small blot on a 150-minute film, though.

SUMMARY.

An entertaining film and superhero epic. It is Watchmen on steroids and I mean it in a very good way as I'm a fan of the Watchmen film. Overall it has much more hits than misses and it's a pity as the flaws for me are minor. Perhaps if Ben Affleck, with his Oscar-winning film- making skills, had more say in the making of it it could be taken to a higher level??

title: Just got back from a 12:35 am showing.....
review:
And I was blown away. The fight scenes alone are worth the cost of admission. It's a visual spectacle. As a Batman fan I was excited to see him really fight in live action. Affleck did an excellent Bat and Bruce. He had a very The Animated Series vibe. As did Alfred. Most of the levity came from Alfred as a result. Very sarcastic. Wonder Woman was excellent as everyone has said, pretty much. You see the joy in her face when she is fighting. Superman/Clark does Superman things. Saving people and stopping disasters. I loved the way Eisenberg played Lex. He's the intelligent and manipulative Lex we expect. Lois was well used. She's the intrepid reporter and pivotal to the story.

I went into the movie having read a lot of the negative reviews, so I was looking for the problems I'd read about. I had no issues with the pacing. I thought it moved along fine and despite its length, and the late hour, I never lost interest. Though to be fair I love the universe. The editing problems I read about were again overblown in my opinion. I had no issues with the transitions, but perhaps the extended cut will smooth that out for those who had a problem with it.

Overall, I genuinely enjoyed it. Really, really, really enjoyed it. I really don't get the heavy negative criticism it's gotten. It reminded me a lot of the current Justice League animated movies. Judging by the turnout and general fan response it seems audiences liked it while critics panned it. While critics are fans as well as critics they have an inherent bias regarding how they feel a comic book universe movie should be made. And that way seems to be the Marvel method. This certainly isn't that type of movie and critics seemed to dislike the tone. If you watch it without a hard notion of what a comic book movie should be and go into it with an open mind I think you'll enjoy it. Maybe a lot.

title: It could have been a masterpiece!
review:
I have just watched it and I still can't shake off the feeling that something isn't right with the film. It wasn't quite a disappointment. This film actually had the potential to be a masterpiece. Yet, the directing and the editing weren't the best. I think Snyder got a bit too enthusiastic with the plot and made it quite confusing. I felt like I was watching several different films into one with no essence. He should have stuck to one idea and built the entire film around it without offering too many Easter eggs. Yet, I do appreciate the cameos and all the parts which offer a slight idea about what the future films will be like.

I really enjoyed the performances of Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot and I believe they are definitely the right choice to play Batman and Wonder Woman. To be frank, I expected the worst, yet I was proved wrong. I really cannot imagine a better Wonder Woman and this Batman is one of my top 3 now.

Another aspect worth praising is Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Lex Luthor. It was unexpected and exciting to watch him.

Overall, the film is not a perfect 10, yet, it is one worth watching. It can surprise you.

I am really looking forward to the next ones. :D

title: Really Good Movie That's Getting a Bad Rep.
review:
First of all, go see it. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a great starting point for what's to come. It does have its flaws, but all in all...good. I've notice that it does seem to be getting a lot of bad press. People really need to think about three things before sitting down in a theater and watching it.

1. Man of Steel got so much flack for the destruction at the end that director Zac Snyder spent to a lot of time in this movie trying to respond to fans and critics, which is why half of the world is against Superman. If Snyder didn't feel it was necessary to do this, then the film might have been able to spend more time with our heroes.

2. This is not a Marvel movie. Don't try comparing it, or you'll get up and walk out. Marvel has not only set the bar high for the modern superhero movie, they created a whole new bar. They have done something that is hard to follow. Disney owning Marvel always needs to focus on adults as well as children. Dawn of Justice is not the colorful Avengers.

3. This is not Chris Nolan's Batman. As great as The Dark Knight trilogy is, it was more or less based in the real world. And it worked so well. Nolan once again turned Batman into a household name. Dawn of Justice is not that. It is a comic book movie. Things happen in this new universe that cannot and should not be explained. Leave Nolan's Batman at home.

That being said, Batman v Superman does have its down points. Mixing two huge series together was a bit much. SPOILERS!!! The Dark Knight Returns and The Death of Superman can come together in the same time line, but not in the same movie. Also, Wonder Woman defiantly needed more screen time. She, in a lot of ways, steels the show. But we don't see her as Wonder Woman until the final battle. I will admit, Ben Affleck's performance does allow the audience to forgive the whole Daredevil thing that happened years ago. Affleck almost seems perfect for Bruce Wayne and Batman. Jeremy Irons as Alfred was a bit questionable for me. I didn't get an "Alfred" feel from him. This may have to do with lake of screen time and development of the character. With a standalone Batman film down the road, I'm sure that can easily be corrected. Hennery Cavell's Superman is probably the dullest of all the characters. Again, sharing the screen with so many people doesn't help. He spends most of the movie doubting himself, we still never got the real Superman out of him yet. Louis Lane eats up a lot of the screen. At times, a little too much. But she does bring everyone together in the end. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luther, I though brought an excellent, new take to the villain. There are places when it's a bit over the top, but for the most part...very enjoyable. All in all, a wonderful movie to spend money to see. I will be seeing it again this weekend. Don't let what the big critics say shy you away and form your own opinion.

title: A Fantastic Movie
review: Yes, many people will not like this movie, and here are all of the reasons why I can understand that: -Batman kills -Doomsday looks like a ninja turtle and never actually comes to look like the Doomsday from the comics -Introduction of other superheroes is sloppy -Several plots all happening in one movie that do not have enough individual focus -Some very sloppy absolutely crummy CGI during Doomsday fight regarding Wonder Woman -Gotham and Metropolis are right next to each other. review: I'm not sure what my expectations were but I was excited at the prospect of my two favourite comic book characters appearing in the same film.This is a very grown up film which deals with some astonishing issues in a very serious way. title: Martha!
review:
Picking up 18 months after the disastrous events of the disaster of a film MAN OF STEEL, Batman (Affleck) fears future collateral damage from Superman (Cavill), and sets out to stop him. Disappointing for the Superman fans, since this outing focuses more on Batman (with Affleck given top billing); and disappointing for the Batman fans for the lost opportunity of THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS. There are some noteworthy ideas, but they're few and far between; for example, Batman's voice-changer is an excellent addition that would've saved Christian Bale some throat scratching. But never once is the viewer rooting for or against anyone; what with this gumbo of several important characters all being crammed into one film leaves everyone underdeveloped and the audience apathetic—there is no beat for us to cheer for the introduction of Batman or his batmobile, nor the reintroduction of Superman or Lois Lane. Aside from flashbacks of Bruce Wayne's childhood (which is only necessary because the history was rewritten for the sake of a cheep plot device), there is very little development or interaction from our stars (besides fighting) and it is all just go, go, go, CGI mess everywhere for almost two-and-a-half hours. Worst yet is the immature common ground Batman and Superman find to set their differences aside.

★½ (out of four)

title: What a disappointment and missed opportunity
review: Take out the only actual real fight sequence (which you pretty much saw most of via the trailers), whats left is a narration of two so-so written stories about who Batman is how he came about and then what happened to public opinion on Superman after his Zod fight in Man of Steel and the viewpoint of Batman on all of this. Quite frankly this was barely a movie in its own right, and more of extended piece of glue that is an attempt to gluing together Man Of Steel and the forthcoming Justice League. But even if that is all you expect from this movie and nothing more, it is still a mediocre 7 or very generous 8. title: This is a movie that takes itself seriously, it doesn't interpret comic book as a book filled with levity and not-so-funny running jokes like "language!"
review:
This is not the movie we deserve, but the one we need right now. This movie is not perfect. But only because it had to set up the next movies to come in the franchise. Yet it still has all the elements we loved in the Nolan trilogy. It is dark, visually spectacular and has the audience on the edge of their seats.

It does more than just acknowledging its prequel – man of steel. It builds on it, promising that the DC universe, we all have been waiting for is not going to be a collection of secluded islands. And as such it should not be viewed as a standalone movie, but rather as a pilot episode in a series.

Ben Affleck brings a seasoned Bruce Wayne, whose experiences have made him a cynic. Jeremy Irons takes over from Michael Caine as Alfred and Henry Cavil reprises his role as Superman/Clark Kent.

The action sequences are tense, foreboding and visually stunning. I managed to go to the movie without seeing a single trailer, and I was completely satisfied with the overall experience. Snyder could cut off the final showdown with Doomsday and I still would have been satisfied.

This is a movie that takes itself seriously, it doesn't interpret comic book as a book filled with levity and not-so-funny running jokes like "language!"

Get over it! Batman is not the most popular superhero because he runs around making light of situations, but because he operates in the night and is steadfast in his resolve to stand against what he thinks is unjust!

By the end of what can only be described as a mash up of cut-scenes that take themselves far too seriously, everyone around me was checking their phones eager to make the pain end. title: A brutal battle from two of the biggest heroes on the planet.
review: I'm torn between two of my favourite Super heroes in Zac Snyders' latest flick: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. I didn't know who to root for while they tore down Metropolis and Gotham City in the process making themselves even more popular with the locals than the Avengers. I own Superman and Batman shoes, t-shirts, paintings, model cars even luggage so at times it was easier to back the villain Doomsday. This movie lacked coherency with more stop start than a modern car engine. It also lacked a sense of humour. Sure you have the occasional laugh, but this is a brutal movie that throws in everything for the fan boys and girls including the kitchen sink. (literally) Ben Affleck has done it all now including TV Superman, Dare Devil and now the Caped Crusader with even cooler toys and Bat Tunnel. He's ably assisted by wisecracking butler Jeremy Irons as Alfred (sorry no Robin) while Amy Adams steps up as Louis Lane to the mild mannered Henry Cavill as Clark Kent/Superman. The poor mans Samuel L, Laurence Fishburne, is the worst newspaper editor on the Daily Planet as Perry White. Wait till you hear his headlines...they elevate the Gold Coast Bulletin to Pulitzer prize winners. Jesse Eisenberg is mixing up Facebook founder with the Joker to give us his hairy rendition of Lex Luthor. What evil is brewing at Lex Corp? (cool logo though) If the creators had taken out the useless origin stories, flashbacks and trippy dream sequences this could have been so much better and shorter...(2 hours 31 minutes). It incorporated too many story lines with the last hour worth the price of admission in an otherwise fatuous telling of this great story arc. Thank goodness for Wonder Woman i'll root for her.

title: The first half is twice as long as it should be and way too dry, but the payoff is worth it.
review:
Without spoilers: the main consistent criticism of the movie is that it's too long, which I agree with, the first half or so of the movie should be half as long as it is, because it's pretty dry, but the payoff is worth it imho. And I actually found Jesse Eisenberg to be a decent Lex Luthor, he does the eccentric, narcissistic asshole, that Lex Luthor should be, well. If you thought that Gene Hackman and Kevin Spacey were good as Luthor, then I think that Eisenberg was on par too. Other than that, the story is decent, there aren't any more plot holes than in other movies, although it's really working hard on setting up the JL movie. Other than that, the rest of the cast is good and it's a really good looking movie.

So the tl;dr version is, if you can get through the first half without falling asleep from the dryness, it's a decent superhero flick. Let's hope the directorial staff will get reworked for the future movies in the DCCU though. But if you ask me there were movies as "bad" as this in the MCU too, so I don't really get this uproar from the critics.

title: The Passion of Kal-El
review:
(Contains spoilers.)

Saw a screener for free in IMAX. I am not a DC fan but know the basics.

The good points of this movie:

-Glad they addressed the massive innocent body count of the last Superman movie.

-Cameos by future Justice League members were fun.

-Wonder Woman was awesome.

The bad:

-Fight to the death literally stops because Batman and Superman's mommies have the same first name and the one that isn't in dead is in trouble.

-Blatant, in-your-face Christ allegories. This is basically an Easter movie with superheroes.

-Amy Adams continues to be wasted talent as a Lois that doesn't do much besides get into peril repeatedly and need to be rescued. This gets pretty old.

-Several scenes that make little sense when you think about them too hard.

-If you've seen one Zack Snyder movie, you've seen them all, pretty much. You could cut out paper dolls of Supe and Bats and tape them to either side of your computer/TV screen and just re-watch Watchmen. I've read there's already a 3 hour directors' cut of this movie, because of course there is, because this is Zack Snyder.

-If you've ever read a Superman comic where he goes against Doomsday than nothing that happens is a shock.

-Way too many scenes "torn from the headlines" to make the world more "gritty and real" and instead come across as weird cultural callbacks: 9/11 towers falling in a plume of white dust, journalist captured and executed by terrorists in the desert (Daniel Pearl, et all), Hurricane Katrina, Boston bombings' iconic double leg amputee... those are just the ones I can think of off the top of my head. Way too much reality in my superhero fantasy, thanks.

-Batfleck doesn't give a hoot and has basically no moral code whatsoever. It makes for an interesting anti-hero aspect but is jarring in the wake of three Nolan movies where he was unquestionably the hero. (Different universe, I know.) The feel of this Bats is too similar to Nolan's in styling and mood/theme: a lot of the just Batman footage feels like it was found on the cutting room floor of The Dark Knight Rises.

Wait for the rental.

review: Well, it's been awhile since 'BVS' came out, and as expected, ben affleck did not do the job.Some fans liked him as the 'Dark Knight', most...did not!Batman has always had a line he wouldn't cross, and he was clearly always working to make sure he didn't become what he hated.THIS version apparently lacks the moral compass that makes 'Batman' the character we love to watch.The conflicted nature, the moral center, and the absolute surety he will not become just another thug vigilante.Affleck fails in this at every level, and from the majority of fan response so far, was one of the weakest links in this movie.Too bad the other actors had to suffer because of afflecks' ego, he just had to play this part, everyone knew it was awful casting, and after 'Man of Steel' was so perfect at bringing back the character, and after it was so perfectly played, 'BVS' not only trashed the 'Dark Knight', which will now have to be resurrected...AGAIN...for the 2nd or 3rd time, it made it harder for the other characters to keep their fans.Warner bros. is freaking out, the 'Justice League' movies are now in question, and here's the best part:even after 'BVS' got the reviews it got, by the fans, not even the critics, affeck had already finished a tentative script for his own 'Batman' movies, to which warner bros. is saying, 'Well...let's just wait a minute on that...'I have to say, I might have underestimated afflecks' ability to stink it up:He may have single handedly brought the current series of 'Justice League' movies to a grinding halt, he DEFINITELY grounded the 'Batman' franchise, and fans will not go running to the next movies involving 'Wonder Woman', etc.Still, he rejects all claims about bad casting, and carries on as if he deserves an Oscar.What a d-bag.I will just refer you to 'sad affleck', and say that may be the only time you see affleck admit, if only by facial expression, he totally screwed this up!﻿

title: Terrible...simply awful.
review: I truly believe that Warner Bros paid people to fluff up the reviews for this movie. If you dislike MoS you will hate this movie. There have only been two times where I have wanted to walk out of a movie theater in my 20 plus years of watching movies. The first was M. Knight's The Last Airbender and the second time was this movie. I literally don't think I could hate this movie anymore than I already do. *Spoiler Alert: Potential Spoilers Ahead* The pacing is terrible, the movie cuts away before any character can even be slightly developed. The script is hackneyed and has more holes in it than a whack-a-mole game. They've created an incarnation of Luthor that has never been seen in any adaption comic book, movie, or TV series: He's been reduced to some psychotic trust fund brat punk kid, with no cunning or wit about him (This is not a criticism of Jesse Eisenberg its the script's and director's fault). You don't get your first legit fight scene till probably 30 minutes into the movie. The movie tries so hard to be the Dark Knight but falls so incredibly short its almost laughable. Which is ironic because you'll probably laugh once in the entire movie. The use of colors is ridiculous, it was as if Snyder said "I want everything to have a gray overtone, EVERYTHING!!!!." The movie's logic suffers and the choices made by our main heroes are so out of character that one must ask did they even view the source material. By far the worst superhero movie I have ever seen(yes I'm including Superman 3 and 4). If you just want to see your 3 favorite heroes on screen and don't care about anything else then watch it. If you appreciate good cinema, quality character development, and strong plot elements then avoid this thing like the plague, don't do it to yourself. Wonder Woman is probably the only good quality about this movie, her moments in the movie were probably the only thing I enjoyed. Superman is as plastic as he was in MoS and probably had like 25-30 lines in the entire movie. BatAffleck was OK (nothing extraordinary but not bad either). I did admittedly like his fighting style in this one more than I did The Dark Knight's. It very much so resembles the Arkham Games. Nonetheless if I haven't iterated it enough I'll say it one more time, this movie is one of the biggest crocks of cinematic crap I have ever had the displeasure of viewing. Second only to The Last Airbender and Dragon Ball Evolution.

title: Reality that no one cares !!!
review: It's not a recommendable movie. I just loved the film because my taste is of a different type. Generally, no one keeps a huge focus on film story unless they are a film critic or some other professionals. This movie has plot holes but I liked the deep meaning which it has (or at least I think it has even if the director did have no idea of it). title: Excellent movie
review:
You hear so many people that didn't like this movie. That's because they came into the movie with expectations. They came into it thinking of what it should be. They all wanted it to either be like Marvel or Dark Knight. Well DC isn't giving you either. It's darker than Marvel and this Batman has no problem with killing. Batman will kill people. Lex Luthor isn't the almost comical Gene Hackman. He's a maniacal villain that I think Lex Luthor should be. A villain that wants to kill Superman. Not in the silly and quirky way like Gene Hackman. He's doing it in a way it would take for someone like him to kill Superman.

The best part of this movie is Doomsday. I could watch his fight scene a hundred times. I'm probably getting close at this point. I heard people say they should have saved him for later. I don't get why that matters. It's not like he was going to have a bigger role. The guy isn't holding much of a conversation. That was the best fight scene I've ever seen in a movie.

If you come into this movie with an open mind you will love it. It's an amazing movie. Tons of fun. Admittedly they did try to put a lot of content into the movie, but it's still great. Too many dopes come to see this movie expecting to see exact characters they have built in their minds and if those characters aren't on the screen then they hate the movie. If you see the movie for what it is, you allow yourself to see what DC should really be. These are the best versions of Batman, Superman, and Lex Luthor. Forget about what you know about any of these characters going into the movie. Just watch it and you'll love it. It's when people want it to be what it's not is when it gets bad reviews. It's not Marvel and it's not Dark Knight. It's DC and it's incredible.

title: Woeful - in every department - woeful
review:
When Ben Afleck isn't the worst thing in the movie, you know you're in trouble. So let's list what doesn't work: The set-up to pit Batman vs Superman is unconvincing - and several times either character could just say 'hey, this is what's happening', and they'd reconcile and work together. That they don't feels contrived.

Lex is ridiculous. There's no back-story to establish his 'evil' or genius, only this guy who in any other reality would be put in a jacket and locked up for his own safety.

Monologue-a-philia. Honestly - SOOOooo many speeches, when one bullet / laser eyed stare could finish it all.

The FX and some fights are BIG - yet weightless - I didn't care who won - and (SPOILER) did a single person in the world think Superman would stay dead? - or not laugh at the ludicrous way he was cured? (SPOILER END) Ships that have power after decades, computers & fluids of awesome power magically as yet undiscovered, scenes that simply begin and end with no fluidity and some dreadful edits... on that budget I could've produced something a damn site more entertaining and bought everyone a beer afterwards.

Perhaps sewn back together with all the deleted scenes the film may have worked - but who cares. Captain America Civil War was great. The 'war' also felt a little forced, but the whole film had a sense of glee and the script some wit. That's how it's done folks, in well under 3 hours (the Uncut BvS).

Lets celebrate the good - some of the fights were great, and some of the set-design was wonderful. For sheer scale it was right up there. But it still wasn't enough for me to care.

I don't know why, but while Marvel have the magic, DC don't. Aside from Batman (with it's own occasional misfires) it never seems to get it right.

If you haven't seen this abortive drivel yet, trust me, don't lose the time from your life - you'll only regret it.

title: Must have been tripping..
review:
Plot spoilers.. Starts with some faux-profound schmaltzy voice-over- "what falls is fallen etc." Ooh thought provoking! You can extrapolate your own verbs like this at a dinner party "what dies is dead, what breaks is broken" and so on. It isn't difficult. May have carried more weight if spoken by Morgan Freeman but sorry everyone, he's gone. His character has been amalgamated with Alfred who is now a scientific genius inbetween fetching muesli for Batman.

Batman isn't as we knew him either. Watching too much Ironman probably. New bulky suit with flashing eyes and east German border guard boots. The bottom half of Afflecks face protrudes from the mask to finish the ensemble.

Not just the suit and Alfred have changed, Batman has gone full psycho. He shoots guns now and brands criminals with a burning bat badge with the intention that they can be easily identified and finished off in prison. He excuses this behaviour with something like "bad things make good people bad" or some such. Speak for yourself Batman!

On with the story, Batters was miffed that Superman damaged buildings and people died during the big set to with Zod. Batman decides to change tactics and advocate genocide. In relation to Superman.. "if there is even a one percent chance he is bad he absolutely must be destroyed". Applying that logic to the general population- nobody would be left alive. Batman wanted to kill Superman, okay that's fine, but the only reason Superman wanted to fight Batman was because Lex Luthor blackmailed him by kidnapping his mom and told him to fight Batman or his mom would die(which, Luthor should have known what happened to the last person who tried to threaten his mom, ha ha) . title: Would someone please fire Zack Snyder
review:
Now I don't lay all the blame on the director, but a good portion of it should be directed at Snyder and the film's writers. They've taken what could have been the best superhero movie of all time, and turned it into an attempt to compete with the Marvel machine. And DC has failed miserably.

The acting from the male leads was pretty standard (still on the fence about Affleck as Batman). Eisenberg's Luthor is a little tough to swallow at first, I mean the guy is known for playing weird characters. The real scene stealer is Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. Best casting decision ever as far as the DC movie universe goes. Makes me even more anxious for the standalone film next year.

But back to this movie. It definitely doesn't help DC fanboys and girls. The entire movie is basically about two grown men making angry faces and trying to kill each other. The movie simply doesn't live up to expectations. Granted the film is visually spot on, but technical prowess alone can't save this movie. Half the problem lies in the writing. And that's something wrong with almost all of Snyder's films. It's as if he values the "look" of a film over the quality of story and characters.

Take Man of Steel for example. The movie's production was exactly how we'd want a superhero movie to be. Clean, sharp, with some great effects. But the story was so generic, and had so many holes it was hard to enjoy anything. Same problem with Batman V Superman. You have the 2 most iconic superheroes in the comic book industry, the stage set for an epic showdown, and then go and write a story that even a middle school English teacher would give a D.

And the most upsetting thing about the film, for me, is that it's like no one read the actual comics. It's obvious most of the story came from the limited run series "The Dark Knight Returns" (the government puts pressure on Superman to apprehend the aging Bat). But the majority of the film to Batman and Superman punching and kicking.

Long story short, this movie doesn't offer much of anything. It's great for someone who just wants to watch two guys in capes fight (i.e. little boys), but in the wake of the successful string of Marvel movies, this doesn't stand a chance. And if you go as far as to compare it to Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy, this film is even more of a let down.

I'm hoping and praying the studio reconsiders letting Snyder direct another installment of the DCEU. Let someone with more experience handle the film. Snyder's movies have a track record for being more visually interesting than having any real narratives. And for making poor casting decisions (thinking Bryan Cranston would have been the better choice for Luthor).

At least we have Suicide Squad to look forward to.

title: Disappointed
review:
Spoiler Warning: If you haven't seen this movie yet you may want to skip this review because it contains spoilers.

Batman and Superman are arguably the two most iconic comic book heroes ever. As a lover of comics (both DC and Marvel), Zack Snyder's Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice was perhaps one of the most anticipated films of 2016 for me. Sadly,I walked out of the theater mostly disappointed and shaking my head.

In this film, Superman and Batman are essentially meeting each other for the first time. The main premise of the film is that Batman ( played by Ben Affleck) does not trust Superman (played by Henry Cavill) due to the collateral damage caused to Metropolis in Superman's battle with Zod in the previous film, Man Of Steel. To be quite honest, it feels as if certain scenes of this movie are missing or just not explained very well. For example, how did Lex Luthor (he is played by Jesse Eisenberg) know Batman was waiting to fight Superman in Gotham? Are we to assume they made a deal with each other? How was Lex sending him those messages about how he "let his family die" (in reference to one of Bruce Wayne's employees who was injured in the damage caused in Superman's fight during Man of Steel)? Does this mean he knows Bruce Wayne is Batman? There is no time to get invested in a scene either. While you're trying to process what is going on you find yourself in another scene completely. There is not enough real substance between the fight scenes and explosions and it felt like they were just playing with these characters rather than treating them properly to tell a story. By the way, the reason they give for trying to turn Batman and Superman into friends just after a scene where Batman was literally about to stab Superman to death with a kryptonite spear was incredibly weak. Just because their mothers are both named Martha, really? Oh and of course we get some pointless dream sequences and pretentious dialogue.

I do think there were some positive elements in the movie. While I did not appreciate the fact that this Batman was killing people, I do think Ben Affleck does an excellent job for what he was given to work with. His fight scenes are intense and there are certain scenes where it feels like there is a great Batman just waiting to come out and it's hindered by this script. Jeremy Irons is wonderful as Alfred and his banter with Bruce was fantastic and really left the impression that they have known each other for many years. Laurence Fishburne as Perry White was also solid and I enjoyed his moments with Clark and Lois. I enjoyed seeing Wonder Woman (played by Gal Gadot) make an appearance here as well. She seemed charming in her cameos leading up to the final battle and when she entered the fight it was exhilarating just seeing her go toe to toe with Doomsday. Plus, the music that plays when she is on screen was awesome.

Overall I think this movie had some good elements but the problems outweigh the positives. This movie clearly draws the Batman v Superman elements from The Dark Knight Returns storyline and Doomsday as well as Superman's death from The Death Of Superman storyline and frankly I just don't think mixing these things together works. The Batman in The Dark Knight Returns lived in a much different universe than the one in this movie does. The negative response to the film doesn't seem to have made an impact on Warner Brothers releasing a Wonder Woman movie starring Gal Gadot and a Batman movie with Ben Affleck, so hopefully DC can turn things around. I'm also hoping to see how Marvel handles a similar premise in Captain America: Civil War.

title: Overblown, Hyper Technical, Underdeveloped Head Scratcher
review:
Batman vs. Superman had the potential to deliver more than the standard, high-special effects blockbusters that we've come to expect the Hollywood system will churn out, year after year --- like money-grabbing eye candy simply designed not to liberate your mind, but more so your hard earned cash from your wallet. It had the potential to be more than the typical "hero meets hero, fights hero, teams with hero, fights badguy with hero(es)" comic book films which seem to saturate the genre. And it had the potential to deliver a lot more than its solo progenitors (eg Man of Steel) had given us. Yet for all it's potential, for having a great team, for being technically superior, and perhaps most significantly - for having a relatively superior cast of actors - the viewer is left feeling like they've just been shoveled a mass of hot, steaming lava -- brilliant and hot to the touch, but noxious and blinding at the same time.

One of the film's biggest flaws is its attempts at intertextuality, all of which fall flat. While making reference to prior events that are neither explained, nor sufficiently fleshed out, the viewer is left feeling confused at best -- and at worst, wondering if the cutting room floor somehow yielded a trove of scenes that likely should have been in the film, for no other reason than to make sense of what was going on.

Pacing was fairly lacklustre as well. While never boring - and with some exciting (albeit too fast, and 'blockbuster conventional' in their explosion-per second way) scenes, the film's script never finds any kind of balance between the dramatic and the action. Character relationships appear more or less tacked on to give Ben Affleck and the other big players some professional screen time, and the shift to the action scenes is less exciting than it is jarring and unnerving.

Overall - if you're looking for anything dramatic and gripping in the sense of the Dark Knight, it would be best to avoid this -- a movie which is definitely on the action-only side of the Super Hero genre. On the other hand, going to this movie after having a few beers, with a full box of oh-so-buttery popcorn in hand and a good sense of humor, this is guaranteed to be entertaining. The Citizen Kane of superhero movies was likely achieved in the Batman Series - but as Hero-genre answer to Vin Diesel's XXX, this little number works just fine. Just make sure you've got plenty of beer and popcorn in you - plenty.

title: One Of My Favorite Comic Book Movies Ever
review:
Batman v Superman is, in many ways, the comic book film I have always wanted: one that treats me like an adult, who doesn't need to be patronized about what the world is really like. It is a world where the heroes are given flesh, blood, and proper back stories; where you feel like decisions and battles have consequences; and which hits the themes of the best tradition of epic mythology.

I would recommend it to anyone who wants to see heroes in a fully realized world like our own, dealing with meaningful problems, and uniting against foes and villains you care about and actually fear might win. It is also a worthy introduction to the coming Justice League films.

title: Crushing disappointment
review:
Three long years we have waited for this film. Finally a movie that pits some of the most iconic superheros of all time against each other. Since its announce three years back, the hype has been real. Then the trailers happened, and everyone realized what kind of film this could be. Especially when the second trailer they released spoiled literally the entire movie. But that is a two minute teaser. It can't capture everything this two and half hour movie has to offer right? Well, for the most part, it unfortunately does. If for some reason you haven't seen this infamous trailer count yourself lucky, as many of us where not so lucky.But that's just a trailer, I won't hold terrible marketing against the film as a whole, that's just something to think on. However, 'Dawn of Justice' may not be the movie you think it is. It isn't really a Batman vs Superman kind of movie, it's actually more of a 'Man of Steel' sequel.

It majorly follows the man of steel as he is being put on trial for rigidity wrecking metropolis in the previous film. While that is happening Batman is whining and moping around, angry at Superman for destroying one of his buildings. A building that was chalk full of people that ended up losing their lives in this crap storm.

Going into this movie there was a few things that I knew for sure that I would like. And all of which I ended up loving just as I thought I would. The biggest one was the action. Just like '300' and 'Watchmen' 'Dawn of Justice' is an absolute beauty to look at. Zack Snyder is one of the best in the business as integrating stylish choreography with exquisite VFX. Even if the effects get to be a bit heavy handed at times, there is no denying how great this film looks.

Another thing that I liked about this movie was the idea of consequences. So many superhero movies these days leave large scale destruction in their wake with little to no repercussions. So, the idea of Superman being rejected because of how much damage he caused, despite the countless lives he saved, was an idea that I was way on board with. It seems that another film this year has kind of the same idea. Marvels 'Civil War' seems to be operating very similarly to this movie.

But the one thing that is apparently separating these two movies is that both parties in 'Civil War' stand by ideals that we can get behind. The major problem with 'Dawn of Justice' is that it doesn't offer this. Superman is the only real good guy between the two. "Well Rendan, Batman is a good guy too." Not in this movie he's not. The best part about Batman and his villains is his refusal to kill people, even villains. And the villains are constantly trying to make him do it, to sink to their level.

But in 'Dawn of Justice' he is a murderous lunatic that probably deserves more to be locked up than Lex Luthor does. He kills countless people and brands others. The movie takes his best quality, his moral dilemma, and throws it out the window. In doing this it becomes impossible to route for him in this movie. He is ultimately the villain, until he suddenly has a change of heart for virtually no reason.

It's actually difficult to talk about this movie because of how nonsensical it is. So much of the film is spent trying to set up other movies that it forgets basic storytelling. Very few scenes make sense and even fewer feel like they actually belong. It jumps aimlessly from scene to scene with so little flow that each scene almost feels like it is restarting the movie.

Characters do dumb things, people know stuff that they definitely shouldn't, and the action in the first half is completely non existent. And no, the dream sequences don't count. Why? Because they don't even matter to anything. Who cares if Batman kills a bunch of people, it isn't even happening. How can the film makers expect you care about what is happening if all of it is a characters head?

There is many other positives and negatives that this film had like the great performances or the fact that the music is virtually ripped straight from 'Man of Steel' but these points where the most blaring. I wanted to like this movie, I really did. I loved the concept behind it, it had some excellent action scenes and set pieces but it was ultimately forgettable. The script is incredibly lazy, forcing in sequel set up where ever it could and in the process, it forgot to just be a good singular movie.

title: Could have been so much worse, could have been better too.
review:
I did not expect too much from this film after hearing some bad reviews, but it was a watchable film that has moments of what could be great content but gets let down a moment later. There are some masterful shots in this movie that look simply amazing. The CGI is very good with only 2 seconds of Doomsday footage looking a little fake, other than that, no complaints about the look of the visuals.

Ben Affleck is a very good Batman and is also pretty good as Bruce, which has not been done since Keaton in 'Batman'. Henry Cavil is still looking good as Superman, and acts well considering the sloppy script/story which I will come to later. Gal Gadot was surprisingly good as Wonder Woman. I was not a fan of the decision to cast her when first announced but she made the role her own and I have high hopes for her solo film.

As a core to the film, these actors rescue the film from a deluge of problems that could have destroyed any chance the movie had of being good. Eisenberg's Lex Luthor is frankly the worst part of the film. Every time he starts to build a sinister presence, it is ruined by a silly childish line or action. The plot is all over the place, with unnecessary dream sequences, shoehorned in cameos and supporting roles and plot holes and character inconsistencies that make no sense.

I read comics, lots of them, and I was expecting some changes to the characters so I was not too bothered by the changes that were made. What I was annoyed by is the huge inconsistencies in Superman and his powers. Now I understand that without toning his powers down we would not get a very good movie, but how can he react fast enough to catch a bullet yet not react fast enough to avoid gas spaying out of said projectile. Then he gets suckered in to the same thing again 2 minutes later. He seemed to forget that he has x-ray vision in 80% of the film, never used his speed for any real advantage and they also seem to have written out his freeze breath. I also have no idea why a nuclear blast would even bother Superman let alone virtually kill him.

All in all, this is one Superman fan who wanted so much more than Batman promotional material and an hour of set up for the justice league film. 6/10.

title: Batman v Superman
review:
Much like my adolescent years, this film had me waiting way too long for some action. I found myself an hour and 40 mins into the film without experiencing a second of excitement.

Zack Snyder has made something that I can only describe as an anti film. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor is often annoying and in parts as cringe worthy as a bad best man's speech. Superman becomes a conflicted character in the worst possible sense, his character almost as confused as the direction of the film.

Ben Affleck as Batman was perhaps one of the few positives to come out of the film as well as Gal Gadot's appearance as wonder woman. however the casting as a whole is woeful, Jeremy Irons performance as Alfred not fit to follow Michael Caine's.

Ultimately DC have hit a new low with this shambles of a film, let's hope suicide squad gives Ben Affleck a platform to make his mark in a film we can remember for the right reasons.

title: The long wait is over
review:
Films rarely get bigger then Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice, seeing two titans of the comic facing off against each other for the first time on the big screen. Despite it weak critical reception Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice has proved to be box office success, making $468.6 Million in its opening weekend, shattering a record. But is it deserving of its box-office or the critical reception.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is set two years after the events of Man of Steel. Superman (Henry Cavill) has divided opinion, some see him as a saviour, others a threat. The US Senate are running an investigation into Superman and his actions around the world. Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) saw the destruction of Metropolis and prepares to face the Last Son of Krypton while also investigating a human trafficker in Gotham. But as Superman and Batman prepare for battle the industrialist Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) is coming up with his own sinister plans, gaining access to General Zod's Earth Engines and Zod's body to achieve this.

Batman v Superman is a very problematic film, it's writing is all over the place, director Zack Snyder believed that being dark is being violent and Warner Brothers are rushing to set up their own explained universe so they can catch up to Marvel. But the film is not without fun - Batman v Superman much more like a Zack Snyder film, he is not trying so much to emulate the realistic style and look of the Christopher Nolan Batman series. The Man of Steel sequel felt more like Snyder's adaption of Watchmen, showing the wider impact of a man with the powers of a god descending upon Earth, resulting in shifts in society and politics. This is when the film is at its most interesting. It's not like this material has been untouched by superhero films, the MCU and X-Men films have looked at similar issues, yet Batman v Superman does it well, even if Senate Committees are not exactly the most thrilling thing to watch but it does set out a world that has changed. There is a mix of people being in awe at Superman and others in revulsion.

When Ben Affleck was cast as Bruce Wayne/Batman it was met with distain because of his role in Daredevil 13 years prior. Following Christian Bale was a tough act to follow but Affleck was able to pull it off. He had the physique for the role, being in great shape and he brought a darkness to the role. His Bruce Wayne was an older than previous incantations and an even more lonely figure, yet still willing to fight and as Bruce investigate, being perfectly suave. He is also more violent and sadistic then previous Batmans, which is disloyal to the character, but that is the fault of the writing, not Affleck. Affleck did prove the doubters wrong. He was the more interesting hero out of the duo, sidelining the Man of Steel.

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was the other major addition and he is without a doubt the worst portrayal of the character ever. He was just a hype brat that had no menace to him. All he did was speak quickly and asked like he was child on sugar rush. Eisenberg was just unbearable.

Gal Gadot as Diane Prince, AKA Wonder Woman was also someone that fans were keen to see, being the first cinematic iteration of the most famous female superhero. Gadot role as Wonder Woman was really just a teaser but she did well in the action scenes and it does whet the appetite for her first solo film.

The writing is where the film suffers greatly. There were reports that the screenplay was troubled and Argo writer Chris Terrio was brought in to do re-writes. When the film starts it tries to set up numerous plot threads that it is surprisingly difficult to keep track. The film throws in too many characters investigating too many things when a more straight forward approach would have worked. The writers were mandated to set up the upcoming DC Cinematic Universe so had to throw in references to other characters for the Justice League film. The dream sequences could easily have been cut, even if the post-apocalyptic Batman fight was one of the best action sequences in the film, feeling like an action scene from Watchmen or Sucker Punch.

Snyder's long time cinematographer Larry Fong works on Batman v Superman, replacing Amir Mokri from Man of Steel. And Fong's inclusion lead to a huge improvement to the action - Man of Steel suffered from having too much shaky cam and sudden zooms that made it hard to follow what was going on at times. The action in Batman v Superman was much more fluid, from when Batman goes into action to Superman's first proper appearance. When Batman was in action it felt very similar to the fight scenes in Watchmen.

Also Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL do deliver with the music, just like they did with Man of Steel. There are some beautiful tracks in the film. Zimmer said recently that Batman v Superman would be his last superhero score and he at least goes out with a good one. It would be great to see what Junkie XL can on his own, seeing he has done good work on 300: Rise of an Empire and Mad Max: Fury Road.

Batman vs Superman is nowhere near as bad as the critical response has suggested it is. It does deliver on action and builds on the foundations that Man of Steel set out. It was a tough to try and set up the DCEU and all its characters in one film and a few lighter moments wouldn't have gone a miss - even The Dark Knight Trilogy had occasional jokes.

Ben Affleck (his best superhero depiction was in Daredevil, a movie hundred times more fun than this one) acts with a handbrake, Henry Cavill is a "sleep man walking", Jeremy Irons is underused and Jesse Eisenberg looks like an evil version of Mark Zuckerberg from The Social Network. BvS, in my opinion, is an unoriginal, dull movie, that will be fast forgotten after you leave the movie theater.

Disclosure, this is my first IMDb review. Mostly because I can't understand why it's getting such negative reviews, other than people were expecting Marvel (and thank God it wasn't). Maybe the best Super Hero movie. So why a 10/10?

1. The acting. Holy Kryptonite, Wonder Woman! Everyone was spot on. Affleck, which I called, nailed it. Maybe the best Batman yet. 4. Fight scene. Have you watched the animated, "The Dark Knight Returns"? Well, same idea. Really smart way of taking something good and making it their own.

The negative reviews are from people that I really think just weren't ready for this movie. That is, they were looking for the Avengers (which is way off base) or maybe something closer like the Dark Knight (but this WASN'T A BATMAN MOVIE, you can't compare).

All in all, watch it. Movie was incredible. Don't listen to the reviews and form your own opinion.

title: A very mixed bag - some of it is disturbing. Not for children.
review:
This is the very first time I have ever posted a movie review on any Internet forum. B v S impressed me deeply, mostly negatively, to the point that I am writing a review as a form of catharsis. First the big picture: I think it is no coincidence that this movie opened Easter weekend - Superman has always been the messiah figure, and in this movie he actually "dies" to save humanity. Snyder frames his "death" scene like a late medieval or Renaissance painting, with a shaft of light on Superman's body and cross-shaped ruins in a murky background. Martha and Lois are the grieving women at his funeral; it is only the last of several obvious religious references. And yet we are only given the tiniest hint of the Resurrection at the very last moment of the movie. It is as if Snyder thought he was just too cool to give us the kind of joyous payoff (humanity saved, Batman back to his principles, Superman triumphant) that would have redeemed the previous two and a half hours of unrelenting gloom. I guess optimism and happy endings are passé'...

This is a movie at war with itself - it clearly intends to give us a darker, more "adult" take on two pop culture icons, but in so doing it does violence to everything those icons have stood for for the better part of a century. Gone is Batman's "no guns, no killing" rule, along with Superman's buoyant optimism and moral certitude. Both of our "heroes" have few qualms about killing (the African warlord Superman drives through two walls at near supersonic speed surely didn't survive the impact). Plot holes abound - how is Luthor able to create Doomsday so easily? Why did people think Superman was responsible for the deaths of the African villagers when they had obviously been shot? Since when does Superman need to shoot anybody? Come to think of it, why is Superman blamed for the explosion at the Capitol? Would he plant a bomb if he wanted to kill people? And why does he just stand there looking sad after the explosion instead of rushing around to look for survivors who might need his help?

Bruce's visions open another Pandora's box of confusing hints: if his nightmare about Superman turning evil is just that, a nightmare, then why do we see Darkseid's Omega sign? If it is a premonition, on the other hand,then all of Bruce's paranoia about Superman is justified - but the Superman we see in the rest of the movie gives no indication that he might turn to the dark side, and we are supposed to think that Bruce's paranoia is unjustified or at least grossly out of proportion.

Like many comic book geeks, Snyder wants to have his cake and eat it, too. On the one hand he wants to make an IMPORTANT MOVIE that asks THE BIG QUESTIONS about the proper use and limits of power, while on the other he has an adolescent's infatuation with firepower, explosions and preposterous muscles. The Pa Kent speech is borderline nihilistic - is it meant to imply that heroism is futile? But then we are (I assume) supposed to admire Superman's self-sacrifice. Ma Kent's speech ("You don't owe them a thing") isn't much better - no wonder this Superman appears uncertain and conflicted. For all of his power, he comes across as a sad, ambivalent figure, psychologically brutalized by Luthor and physically brutalized by both Batman and Doomsday. Maybe he is supposed to represent our national ambivalence towards the use of power. In keeping with geek culture's current fascination with "darkandgritty", Batman is a more fully developed character, even though his brutality and sadism are off-putting.

Now for the good: there are some stunning visuals, and Wonder Woman is excellent, even though we don't see much of her until the end of the movie. Her physical grace and foreign accent mark her as a creature not quite of this world. Batman's physicality is truly frightening - this is a man who has earned his muscles the hard way and fights with brutal efficiency. His training montage featuring huge, rusty weights and giant truck tires (as opposed to martial arts and state of the art exercise equipment) is emblematic of his brute force approach, but once again we don't get to see much of the martial arts grace and skill that have historically been an integral part of his repertoire. His fight with the Russian thugs looks painfully realistic, except for when he gets shot in the head at point-blank range. Even with his armored cowl, the impact alone should have knocked him out.

In summary, B v S left me with a similar taste to the one I got from Daniel Craig's outings as 007: a beloved character which was also an aspirational figure has been turned into something sad and angsty, on which it is very hard to project our aspirations. Our world needs heroes to look up to, and Zack Snyder has failed to provide them.

Henry Cavill - Though the movies are better than before, I have to say what I don't want to, Brandon Routh is better. Henry is unable to get the emotions on his face. Everything is a poker face.

Zack Snyder - I was expecting him to work his magic after the beginning of the film, but oh dear, was I disappointed. Ben Affleck - Worst Batman ever. Okay, maybe not worst. We did have Clooney. But worst Bruce Wayne ever as well. This guy can't act worth crap in this movie. Although I liked how Batman was more comic book-like in this compared to the trilogy. Ryan Reynolds redeemed himself this year. Sadly the same cannot be said for Ben. Christian Bale remains the best Batman and Bruce Wayne we've ever had.

Amy Adams - She was trying so hard. So very hard.
