Rating - 5 Because comic book like movie. Some good fight sequences. Some really bad ones. Snyder and the editing team are awful. So is most of the cast, especially Affleck. I am very lenient with giving out stars so this is it. But it doesn't deserve it. A must watch for 12 year olds though.

title: Convoluted Mess
review:
I was really excited for this film until I saw that one trailer that pretty much revealed the whole plot of the movie and I hoped that I was wrong and the movie would surprise me. But I wasn't, the trailer spoiled the entire movie for me and that really isn't a negative for the movie itself but I just wanted to mention the worst marketing campaign ever.

Now about the movie, there were things I loved and things I hated. Let's talk about the things I loved, first. I thought Ben Affleck was great, not only as Batman but I think he was a great Bruce Wayne too. There were some things I disliked about the character as well but more about that later. Jeremy Irons is fantastic as Alfred and he actually has a lot to do in this movie. I'm one of those guys who likes Henry Cavill and he's good in the movie as well. One performance that surprised me was Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, she was pretty good too. I liked the opening of the movie and the first maybe 30 minutes I thought were pretty solid, although kind of convoluted and way too much stuff was going on and the editing and transitioning from scene to scene was all over the place. Still, I enjoyed the first part of the film and most of the action and visuals are pretty solid throughout.

OK so there are many reasons why I mostly disliked the film and a lot of people are saying "well it's cause you're not a fan of the comics" or "you just want to seem smart because critics didn't like it." Truth is I didn't like Batman v Superman because the movie is a mess. I'm just gonna list the things I disliked about it without any particular order.

The movie tries too hard to set up its own universe with the Justice League and its characters that it forgets to be its own good film. It's happened before with The Amazing Spider-Man 2 and now we get this. I really mean it when I say I wanted to love this movie, but I just can't. The editing is all over the place, scenes happen that do not need to be in the movie and the pacing is just off. Everything feels rushed and out of place. Jesse Eisenberg is a good actor, but he sucks as Lex Luthor. He's terrible, he could have been a much better Joker than Lex and it's not because he's a bad actor, but he is just a miscast for the role. Also, his motivations are pretty unclear. Lois Lane has absolutely nothing to do in the movie so they just send her off on these little tasks so she is kind of relevant. Luthor creating Doomsday out of a conveniently placed genetic chamber in the Kryptonian ship was so stupid and it felt rushed and shoe-horned into the movie, kind of like Venom in Spider-Man 3. Batman was good, for the most part. He is one of my favorite characters of all time and one of the things that intrigues me so much about him is his moral code. Well, not anymore apparently because Batman is a murderer in this movie. He's just killing people left and right. And when he decides he wants to kill Superman he just lets him live because their moms have the same name. Like, really? Also, why the hell does Superman suddenly decide that he wants the Batman to stop operating, for some reason? Why does Wonder Woman need to be in the movie? Gal Gadot was pretty good but the movie really should have been a lot more focused on Batman v Superman and that's it. Throw away Lex and Wonder Woman and everything else that does not matter, because your movie is about these two guys fighting each other. Also, this movie could have easily been 90 minutes long if it just focused on that. The pacing is all off and scenes that have absolutely nothing to do with each other suddenly transition into one another. That dream sequence with Batman killing guys in the desert with the flying thing had nothing to do with the plot of the film. Also, how the hell is a non-comic book reader gonna know that it was Flash who conveniently came back and said Lois is the key or something? How bad were those Justice League introductions anyway? Wonder Woman learns about them through an e-mail that conveniently already had the logos to their characters placed on the videos to them. Someone took the time to do that, really? So Superman dies at the end. That must have taken a lot of ball, right? Not really, because he's not really dead at the end. Saying Hans Zimmer's score is disappointing is an understatement, it's mostly loud noises all over the place.

I didn't know what was going on most of the time. The real reason this movie is getting panned by critics isn't the small details, it's the fact that it's a big convoluted mess of a movie that tries harder to set up a universe of movies than be a good movie on its own.

review: I have never been so disgusted with critics in my life. I went into this movie with the lowest of expectations after the onslaught of negative reviews nearly killing my excitement and by the end of the movie I was in awe. I loved it and my entire audience clapped through out. I am not saying it was a perfect "film". There were pacing issues at times, but all the acting, especially Affleck and Eisenberg was excellent. It may have been dark, but it was definitely fun, emotional and crowd pleasing. If you are a fan it was a dream come true at times. I am not going to turn this into a Marvel/DC thing as I think that is both childish and stupid, but I really think Marvel's success has warped some people's and critics perception of what you can do with comic movies. Marvel does a great job at what they do, but this dared to be different, serious and more adult and it should be applauded for that and not ridiculed. I see this sitting at 31% on RT and it is absurd. I can name 20 comic movies with higher ratings that aren't even close to this movie in quality. My advice to anyone that is a fan of these characters it to ignore the critics completely and just enjoy it. It is a great movie and everyone I saw it with loved it.

Ben Affleck as Batman... I thought he did the role justice and am looking forward to seeing more of him in this role. I thought the character he portrayed was brilliant. I might even go as far as saying he is my favourite Batman so far...

Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman... OMG she was fabulous. I was excited about seeing the Amazonian warrior come to the big screen ever since the teaser clip in the trailer and she did not disappoint. fantastic actress and performance.

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor has got to be the best casting I have ever seen! He was absolutely fantastic! I am a fan of Jesse as an actor but he outdid himself this time. By far my favourite character of the film. He just just kept it alive for me.

All in all a great movie. Go and see it!

title: No no no. Why Zack why
review: Do you know what you done ‪#‎zacksnyder‬? You have taken 2 epic story lines from the ‪#‎dc‬ universe and have ruined it for all the generations that saw the horror of a movie ‪#‎batmanvsuperman‬. What were you thinking? Was this movie for the general public? No, it was way too long with very bad screenplay, OK cinematography (just plain dark as well), too much content, too many things crammed into a single movie, very short character developments. The list goes on. Was it for the fan-boys? No. Our expectations were crushed. The usual filmy conveniences, the ex machina moments, incoherent and very bad adaptations of two great comic arcs. In the fight to catch up with ‪#‎marvel‬, you over reached and fell short by a mile. Granted, the movie had its moments and that the ‪#‎justiceleague‬ will happen. But we were hoping that the disgruntled fans after your ‪#‎manofsteel‬ would be won over by seeing how you tied the events back to this movie and created a nice platform to launch the next phase of dc movies. We were wrong. So wrong. At this point, the very well setup marvel universe is light years ahead of the dc movie universe. Inspite of dc having all the very well known big guns. I just can't understand why you are messing it up so much. ---------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------Spoiler alert -------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------- The dark Knight returns and the death of Superman storyline are both epic. Each could have been made into 2 wonderful separate movies. Go watch the animated movie adaptations and judge for yourself. Not only did you club both these but you also had the justice league assemble storyline added to it. What a waste. Doomsday was sooooo shoe horned into this movie. He is the guy who killed Superman. The biggest dc villain along with darkseid. And he gets what, the last 20 mins to show his badassory? Please don't direct any more dc movies.

title: Outstanding Movie, must see no question !
review:
For those super-hero movies fans, this is absolutely a required film in your archives. As many movie lovers, my expectation for this one was not as high, mainly because been a saga or "Man of steel" that had some good things, but the abuse of visual effects was obvious to complete a lack of argument story, and overall achievement was not reached.

That been said, this film is an instant master-piece!

The argument is terrific, the performance of Jesse Eisemberg, Henry Cavill, Ben Afflec and Jeremy Irons are up to the challenge, all the batman-tech is mind blowing. The sound, visual effects and the soundtrack absolutely blend to deliver an incredible film experience. Can wait to see it one or two times more in cinema, and can wait to buy the blue ray to store in my doomsday shell. Thanks to Zack Snyder and the studios.

title: Masterpiece
review: This is the best of the team Superheroes movies by far..Very emotional,great music,nice story,good characters,the best Batman ever portrayed in movies.Affleck was excellent and want to see him in a solo Bat movie soon.To understand the movie,you have to be a big fan of Supes and Bats comic..They had take pieces from Dark Knight Returns,from superman doomsday,from Flash Paradox,from the game and later comic,injustice gods amongst us...If you never read any of this,i think you will find the movie a mess..So i suggest you too read them and fast. And then you will love the Movie...Everythink was excellent,except that doomsday dies very soon..I hope he didn't and we will see him again..

title: Good movie
review: First of this has no spoilers. I have been mellow these past few days and had the opportunity to see this twice. First off the movies introductory scene is a work of art. It is a visually stunning movie. I was extremely impressed with Affleck's Bruce Wayne he had a certain fire about him that was obvious from the get go. The problem with this movie is bad storytelling and to a larger extent the Editing. The transition suffers and it affects the whole movie. It wasn't a bad movie. It was an OK movie a little bit too okay for my liking. This movie made me feel for superman. An alien who wants to help but is misunderstood at every turn and although Lois lane was supposed to be the films conscience. I think she didn't adequately portray that feeling on screen. It felt like to me that superman could do no good. Very minor adjustments to this film would have made it a great movie. I feel like the movie was originally longer but it was cut at different places. Some of the transitions are so quick you have to be looking at your screen every time. It was indeed very bad storytelling. gal Gadot was good although felt wooden at times. The movie does justice to the characters but doesn't translate those characters to the screen responsibly. Its still a good movie. Id pick it over fantastic four and that very dreadful age of Ultron

title: Thank You Foolish Critics!!!...
review:
...Because of so many of you and your horrible reviews I went into BvS with extremely low expectations. Instead, I was pleasantly rewarded with quite possibly the best Superhero movie I've seen and perhaps one of my favorite movies...period! As some of you reading this may have already noticed, BvS has not received rave reviews. Matter of fact, most of the so-called critics are trashing this movie; however, after the movie was finished, myself and everyone sitting around me were left asking: "Why?" We were all freaking out and pumped from the DC Trinity extravaganza we all just witnessed.

BvS was a glorious experience that had not only myself, but everyone (I noticed) around me completely enthralled and joyously entertained! I was giddy as a schoolgirl with excitement, particularly because this Superman fanboy not only loved me some Man of Steel, but was absolutely floored by the Batfleck...like that bad guy that was face-planted by Bats in the movie...you know the one. Yes, Mr. Affleck's masterpiece portrayal of the Dark Knight is by far the best Batman ever!...sorry Mr. Bale, but it ain't even close.

This is The Batman I loved from the comics! This is The Batman I loved from Batman: The Animated Series! This is the Batman that is the genius tactician that you could believe is finally capable of living up to the moniker of World's Greatest Detective! In addition, Wonder Woman kicks some serious ass and her appearance definitely received the biggest applause of the movie.

I could go into more detail about what makes this movie great for me, I could go on and on and give you an overly analytical rant as to why I feel the way I do about this film, but let's face it, who am I to suggest what you may like?...which is the same reason why you shouldn't put to much weight in the critics' reviews either.

Is the movie perfect in every way? Perhaps not. The best advice I can give in regards to BvS, is that if you are not already a fan of Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, DC Comics or the superhero genre, you may not like the film (or perhaps become a fan yourself). However, if you are already a fan of those things I mentioned, then the movie is definitely worth the price of admission! And furthermore, even though I had already seen all of the trailers, I was still given enough to chew on in this film to feel like I hadn't already seen it all.

Go see this movie with an open mind and remember that it's a piece to a bigger puzzle rather than a standalone movie. If you do that, then hopefully your experience, like mine, will be a BLAST! BvS is everything an action blockbuster of this type should be: being thoroughly entertained to the point where you and complete strangers around you in the theater, can't help but cheer and celebrate together at what you just saw on screen!

I know I'll be going to see it a couple more times before it leaves the theater!

title: Bold and Beautiful for Superheros
review:
Batman v Superman was like the Bold and beautiful for Superhero's. If you want to watch to grown men in skin tight suits sob for one hour in a customized toy bat mobile or Superman flex his triceps with a ship for no good reason...and show up at his girlfriends house without her permission..Or batman tell random people their shoes are nice this movie is for you.

This is the first time I've walked out of a cinema hall after having waited for a year and a half for this movie. This is a marketing scam the type that Mba textbooks don't talk about. Save yourself. Your bank accounts and buy Iron man t shirts and chant marvel is love marvel is life. Forget it being the worst superhero movie..this is the worst movie in general.

I heard there is a major cliff hanger - But what do you do when three out of four people watching the movie with you are snoring ? past the first 20 minutes. I am a huge dc fan & Batman Fan and this was beyond horrible - I couldn't sit through the first half. Poor cgi. Poor Acting - you need a flash light and a phone with internet so that you can keep yourself busy and watch the movie at the same time. If you go without backup entertainment you will leave like i did in the first half.

title: This movie broke me
review:
This movie is jut a jumbled mess, filled to the brim with empty content.

I had low expectations, and even then they weren't succeeded.

But now that the clickbaity things are out of the way what about the actual content of the movie?

I hated the fact that there is just so much empty things going on in the movie. Characters are inexplicably changing. Batman isn't even like Batman anymore. Lois and Clark have no chemistry.

There are good scenes, heck there are some great scenes. But those scenes are overshadowed and blended with tasteless lazy writing. I was getting interested in the movie until a particular scene in which the movie took a complete 180. From then on out it just kept disappointing me. There's only one really good action scene, and even that leaves a bad taste in your mouth because it shouldn't work that way.

If you're a superfan or a batboy you'd enjoy it. If you have been skeptical about the movie, and you saw that one trailer, you know exactly what you're in for. And that can be good or bad.

title: awful premise
review:
The whole premise of this movie is just ridiculous. Batman and Superman hate each other for no good reason. Since the superheros were invented decades ago both of them have always been portrayed as good people who are here for the greater good, to serve mankind and to help the innocents. But in this movie they are so hell bent on killing each other and blinded by arrogance that neither of them give a second thought to killing innocent civilians.

****SPOILERS****

In the end the only thing that stops them is that they discover that their mother has the same name, and just like that they become the best of pals.

Jesse Eisenberg belongs in tacky teenage comedies and they could not have picked a more unsuitable actor to play Lex Luthor. He is simply irritating throughout the whole movie.

I managed to stick it out to the end but regretted doing this once they threw in another "bad guy" in to the mix in the shape of an orc or orakei from lord of the rings, and wonderwoman for good measure.

Don't waste your time with this movie.

title: Bat-thug v. Man of Sour--Are you kidding me?
review:
Maybe I should start reading comics again. When did Batman--I saw this film a little over two months ago and still have yet to get over the caped crusader handling a gun to kill people and branding criminals. I can't decide which I was taken aback with most. When did he stop being a detective? Some one tell me where other than finding the picture of Wonder Woman that his investigative actions weren't driven by his wanting to killing or maim someone. Lois Lane was doing the detection things Batman should've been doing. Instead I get Bat-thug!!!!

And O-M-G Superman is even worse--With his powers he could have saved people dying in the congress hearing scene. Hearing and/or X-ray vision and super-speed found the bomb and carried it away as quick as one could snap their fingers. But wait, was Lois in the room during the hearing? I don't remember seeing him fly away with her in his arms. I saw it too many times. I do remember every time she was in jeopardy he stopped anything in his tracks to rescue her. Hello, uh, other people in the world. There's only two scenes where he helps someone who's not close to him and only one of those two were touching. This Superman other than his looks didn't like him at all--Too boring, brooding, less than caring for strangers, and worst of all doesn't take the time to try to make others see his reasons he did the things he did. The hearing which he comes no speech about the destruction in the first film and the battle in Africa that happens earlier. Superman's speech in "Quest for Peace" for me now is his 2nd best the first being the one he makes at the end of Superman II.

Watch this super dark, super confusing, humorless piece of crap on those devices where the viewing can be speed it up. Get to all the itsy-bitsy parts with Wonder Woman. She was the ONLY super heroine that engaged my interest. I sat upright in my chair thanking God I didn't walk out (and I so wanted to 3 times) when I saw her using her lasso. Thing I think that made her stand out was that action-wise she was transported to the big screen with little to no tampering with her character or fighting style. Can't wait to see her film.

In closing, I will state I won't mention the other characters as I want to spare you the reader from long, long tirade regarding Alex Luthor Joker Poser, forgettable Flash, forgettable Cyborg and biker gang man stereotype lookalike that was Aquaman.

title: and i'm generous. Movie's quite predictable and disappointing, and I wasn't familiar with the story.
review: For starters, I don't hate the movie. I think that Gal Gadot was greatin the very few minutes she got on screen. She is no doubt a great Wonder Woman. Plus, Jesse Eisenberg NAILED his part, being the creepy genius that wants everyone dead. Another thing that was great, is the angles in the 5-7 first minutes of the film. Very special and artistic. Putting these pros aside, Ben Affleck makes a SHITTY Batman. He's not at all dark and mysterious, and his face expressions didn't really made me believe that he knows what he's doing. Most of the film, he either looked quite bad in the suit (she made his chin look really wired), or looked like he was trying to remember what he's supposed to do (while the face expression was supposed to show that he's mysterious or something). I mean, i like Ben Affleck, but it was just quite funnyinstead of dramatic. And for Superman, it was way too emotional. Lots of tears in very not-so-emotional situations. The movie was funny, the end was predictable. I was sitting on my chair and I was like, "man, i just know that the sand on the grave will go high, no way they're focusing on some stupid sand for 5 minutes and nothing will happen". I was right. To sum up, It's funny and Gal Gadot is great. not sure they were aiming for funny, though.

title: Boredom v Cringing
review:
The Justice League may pre-date The Avengers in comic book version but they trail way behind on the big screen.

I assume the aim was to make this film as 'dark' as The Dark Knight trilogy, and aim not met. The film fails to hold the interest like Batman Begins, The Dark Knight, and The Dark Knight Rises and doesn't have a patch of the storyline of these films.

It took years for Batman to become 'cool' thanks to Christian Bale's portrayal of the character. The appalling 60's TV series and a series of equally awful films starring the likes of Michael Keaton, Jack Nicholson, Val Kilmer and George Clooney made Batman as big a joke as Superman and Wonder Woman.

Ben Affleck has had to take over from Bale, a massive ask made more difficult in a terrible film with little in the way of a plot and playing opposite two of comic books daftest creations. If it wasn't for this Affleck would make a good Batman.

Superman has been a joke character since the awful films of the 1970's and 80's. Man of Steel was an attempt to make him a series character, it only produced a boring film about an alien in blue spandex, this time without his underpants over his clothes.

Wonder Woman is a shockingly poor character in any shape or form and this film doesn't change that.

Jeremy Irons takes over from Michael Caine in the role of 'Alfred' and is awful in every scene he ruins. He is now Bruce Wayne's technical adviser.

The casting and performances were generally terrible. The script was horrendous with a lot pointless, and meaningless, chatter. Lex Luther was practically incoherent all the way through the movie, as well as the most cringe-worthy part of the whole film.

The fight scenes were difficult to see. They moved too fast and the camera jerked about so they were hard to follow. The fight between Batman and Superman, in which Batman is the victor, was the only highlight surrounded by tedium.

Most worryingly was the time taken to hint at the next few films in the franchise to be released over the next few years. All ones to avoid. It didn't mention Suicide Squad, released later this year, which is apparently part of the franchise and may be the only bright spark among them.

What parts of the film I wasn't bored through I spent cringing.

It's a terrible film.

title: This Movie is Terrible
review:
I don't know where to start.The performances are pretty bad with the exception of Ben Affleck who was average and Jesse Eisenberg who was fine.(I thought his performance was hilarious). I honestly don't know whether Henry Cavill is a terrible actor or not since haven't seen him in anything else. (I would like to think it was Zack Snyder's poor direction).

The movie has little to no establishing shots and when there are they way too tight, for example the bat-cave establishing shot only showed like half the room. Jeremy Irons is criminally underused as Alfred, his character is also poorly written, in fact every character is poorly written. Lois Lane is my least favorite character in the whole movie because her subplot is stupid.

The movie is extremely boring, I sat in that theater for 150 minutes yet it felt like 200 minutes. This is because of an extremely convoluted plot that tries to do as much as possible and failing in every way. The Dialogue was terrible.

The fight between Batman and Superman is too short. The only good fight is the one with Batman in the warehouse, that actually showed potential for what this movie could have been.

In conclusion, I think you shouldn't see this movie because it is poorly written, terribly directed, terribly shot, poorly acted and is just overall garbage.

title: Bad
review: This film was ridiculous, it made no sense whatsoever. Batman wants to kill superman for no apparent reason. Then changes his mind on a whim. An extraordinary amount of time was spent on setting up sequels and spin off's they obviously have planned. It takes you right out of the story when they do this so blatantly. They may as well have a scene where Batman sips a Coke, holds it up to the camera and exclaims "Ahhh so refreshing!" Wonder Woman appears for no other reason than to set up a sequel. Aquaman? Cyborg? Sequels coming soon...Batman turns to WW and says "there are more like us...we must find them... ( and make a film about it ) Lex Luther says several times 'this is only the beginning! ' They kept promising more and more to come and introduced characters and side stories and yet were barley half way through this film. The films storyline was scattered and jumped from scene to scene barely holding a thread together...we jump from the desert, to the city, to space, to a factory, to an office, to a court house, then into a dream and a mountain in Colarado... with no real connection or relevance to each jump, making it almost impossible to follow. I lost count of the amount of times I rolled my eyes at the childish drama and I turned to look at my girlfriend next to me who had almost rolled her eyes into the back of her head. Its a film safe for children ages 10 - 14 to watch but no one else could possibly enjoy it.

title: So many confusing sub-plots
review:
Disappointing. I took a group of teens to the movie, and for the hour ride home, we tried to rationalize what we saw. Reading the plot synopsis on IMDb is like reading a script for Sharknado: "during a vision of a dystopian future where Batman leads a band of rebels to kill Superman, Bruce Wayne receives a message from a time traveler warning him that Lois Lane is the key." Really? There are not enough weird coincidences in this movie, that we now need to have a time traveler interrupt a dystopian vision sequence? Batman fighting Superman should have plenty of plot material. Instead, the film also feels compelled to develop sub-plots around Lex Luthor's wish to rid the world of dangerous aliens, the rise of Wonder Woman, the discovery of Aquaman / Flash/ Cyborg / Green Lantern, General Zod's body somehow turning into a genetic hybrid, Superman versus the US Senate, African rebels, Batman's turn to the dark side by branding criminals, and others.

Sad too, because the action scenes are well choreographed and the sets / costumes are outstanding. Well-shot. Well-costumed. Poorly written. Worse directed.

Boo.

title: DC Universe Takes Leap Forward
review:
People are down on this movie, but I think they are being too hard on it. There seems to be much speculation of Lex's intentions. First off, I think this movie maybe should be called Lex Luther: Rise of the Villains. The movie title itself is a misdirect. Lex is playing 3 steps ahead of Batman & Superman. He has been for some time and knows who they are really Bruce & Clark. Hmmm...Bruce conveniently gets invited to a Lex Luthor party right as a time that he needs to steal some information from their computers. Well that's convenient. Lex was dropping breadcrumbs so that Batman would get the kryptonite. Lex is a billionaire and certainly controls media outlet, so he pushes forward stories related to distrust of the powerful and sets up our heroes and citizens to distrust each other. Why does he want to do all this? What was Luthor's end game in the comics? He wants immortality and power. He views Superman as a god and wants to control that god.

I enjoyed it and think it took a big step forward in the universe. Maybe people expected too much or maybe they didn't pick up on Lex manipulating them from the start. I don't know, but I really liked it.

In other DC news, Flash crossing over to Supergirl was a smart idea. Supergirl is awful, but it sets up the ground work of the multiverse. Any past D.C. film or TV show can be part of canon if it belongs from a different universe. Then in theory you could have any of these universes cross over.

title: in a word --- LAME ---
review:
I am so very disappointed in DC. Every new title that comes out is worse than the one before... Not only was the theater dead silent the entire movie, there was nothing good enough about any scene to cause any kind of emotional response. I sat through the entire movie wondering when it was going to get good, or better yet, something would at least be funny.

So Aqua-Man is in the movie for like maybe 5 seconds. Flash kind of makes an appearance in some vague nonsensical "dream" that "Bruce Wayne" has... Worst Bruce Wayne EVER BTW

WORST LEX LUTHOR EVER... Jesse Eisenberg... has OBVIOUSLY NEVER experienced any kind of real trauma in his life, worst performance I have ever seen. You can't act like you are mentally insane and provide a convincing performance. You have to "be the ball" and without ever experiencing any real trauma you'll never put on a convincing performance.

In short someone needs to fire all the people that are writing this junk... to include --- Arrow, The Flash, DC Heroes, Supergirl, Gotham ---

Get some real writers, Get some good actors...

The good news Henry Cavill --- really is a good pick for Superman, Poorly written script. Amy Adams --- Works as Lois but her part is written so poorly. Gal Gadot --- Great pick for Wonder Woman character, again poor writing.

For those who would like to see a GOOD Superman Vs. Batman movie watch BATMAN The Dark Knight Returns http://www.imdb.com/title/tt2313197/?ref_=fn_tt_tt_27 Many aspects/elements of that movie were STOLEN for this waste of time...

If you've seen Batman the Dark Knight Returns and Superman Doomsday then you've basically seen ALL of this movie only better...

short version.. I wasted $8.50 and I want my 2.5hrs back...

title: Boring, thx God they still have the action in last 20 minutes
review: Oke, for me, the movie is overrated. or maybe my expectation for this movie was too high. When I'm watched the trailer and the title, I'm so excited for a great fight and story between Superman n Batman. Yes they give us the story, but not the action. And trust me, the story has too many new character with their story. in Simple word, that other character's story make the movie more complicated and boring.The duration is 2 and half hour, it made some of my friends almost got slept, thanks to the last 20 minutes, at least I saw some action when they fought the Zod monster. My conclusion, there'll be sequel and new "avenger" in the sequel. My advice, just don't expect too much action, watch the Man of Steel (Superman 1) and make sure you have a good stamina to watch this movie so you would not fall in sleep.

title: A mess from start to finish (spoiler-free)
review: I went into this movie with low expectations, since I already knew it was getting bad reviews. But even with expectations very low, this movie managed to surprise in it awfulness. The plot was non- existent. It was a sequence of unrelated events in a specific order. The coherency of this movie is a joke. Performances were mostly good, but the actors didn't have to do anything hard, just look very serious. The script seemed like it was written by a five year old. The second act was missing from the movie. Even the action was disappointing. I expected that at the very least the fight between Batman and Superman would be memorable, but no. It was a visually uninteresting fight with little to no drama and a resolution that was so incredibly dumb, convenient, coincidental and non-sensical that I wanted to walk away from the theater. Everyone seems to be praising at least Batman and Wonder Woman. I don't get why. Batman was a psychopathic maniac, going around killing people left, right and center, tying down criminals and branding them. Wonder Woman looked cool, but her character wasn't just bad, it was none existent. Lex Luthor was a joke, with terrible character motivations and a convoluted plan that didn't make any sense. The world building in this movie was more forced then Iron Man 2 or Amazing Spiderman 2. In the end, this movie was a complete mess, with no redeeming value, and I strongly recommend you not to waste money on it.

title: Not worth going to cinema
review:
Not really spoilers if you have seen any of the trailers but you never know!!!

If I saw this on sky, Netflix or even amazon prime, it may have been worth watching, however I would not recommend anyone going to see this at the cinema.

Firstly the first part of the film nothing happens, it is supposed to introduce the theory that superman is a danger to mankind if he chooses to be. So what!!!!!!!!!!!! blah blah blah.

Didn't really get most of the batman stuff not sure why joker defaced the possible robin suit does not explain in any way, does not give much of a back story into batman so I guess we are following the Christian Bale story arc???? I will give this movie some points for the visuals (except Doomsday) it looks good is quite dark. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was the biggest fail in movie history seriously how he gets any work is beyond me, he actually seems like a bigger dick in real life than he does in this movie, which shows how bad he acts.

The good points Ben Affleck is not bad as batman which surprised me apart from his Bale voice in the show down (why oh why). He gives a good performance and actually does a good mix between Bruce Wayne and Batman (I am a little biased as I am a Michael Keaton fan) but he could well be the best batman yet. Henry Cavill is OK as superman not quite on the same level Christopher Reeve but still a solid performance. Gal Gadot seems like she will be decent as Wonderwoman but not really on screen that much.

The story is terrible flimsy plot, too many sub plots and Doomsday WTF why do all directors ruin movies with CGI is beyond me.

Anyway in summary most of the effects are good, Ben Afleck is surprisingly good, its not got a lot of action except two scenes within minutes of each other, the story is awful and the CGI for Doomsday but my overall summary is that Jessie Eisenberg is the worst thing to happen to Batman vs Superman.

title: Who thinks up this rubbish!!!
review: My whole family went to see this - 5 of us. My wife walked out after an hour, the rest of us stayed and we all thought it was pretty dreadful. The film's title is misleading: it's not really Batman V Superman. It's Lex Luther / Doomsday (a monster borne from a large plastic bag and VERY angry) vs Batman, Superman and Wonderwoman. The story is badly told, I didn't really get why Batman was so against Superman, except that he'd destroyed his building (but he did that saving the Earth I think in MoS) and after all the arguing and just as Batman was about to kill Superman, they suddenly became buddies because their Mums had the same first name ... eh? really? Jesse Eisenberg plays Lex Luther and is just really annoying, and unintentionally gave me the one scene that made me laugh when he was in jail at the end and talking about bells ringing and then the scene fades with him going 'ding ding ding ... ding ding ding ...'. He's clearly not fit to be CEO of LexCorp so why haven't the board thrown him out :-)?. This is 150 minutes of completely humourless dross. The big battle at the end, was just too much - too many crashes, bangs, electrical storms, fire, destruction etc .. I couldn't see what was going on - except Doomsday was even angrier. Henry Cavill ... usual Superman performance - a little bit like he was in U.N.C.L.E, but Ben Affleck, who was so good in Argo, must be wondering why on earth he did this film. Anyway the final 30 minutes is the big fight during which Superman sacrifices himself killing Doomsday with a spear made of Kryptonite, so not only does it kill Doomsday it also fatally weakens Superman allowing Doomsday to deal a fatal blow. Superman is dead ... we see everyone crying (he's dead) , we see the funeral (he's dead) we see more unhappy people (he's dead), we see his coffin (he's dead) then in the last shot we see Lois Lane drop some earth on his coffin in the grave (he's dead) and then the soil moves - what a surprise!!! HE'S NOT DEAD!!! I suppose Doomsday isn't dead either. Quite liked the Dark Knight Rises, quite liked Man of Steel. Hated this.

title: Not as good as you think it'll be
review:
Honestly I wasn't expecting much for the movie, but I still had a little hope since it's bout Batman and Superman. HOWEVER It sucked, really, I would consider to be only a little better than Fantastic 4 but not a lot better. For those of you who haven't watched it yet, don't look forward to it because it would make you feel better when you are watching it. The storyline doesn't fit the quality of movies in 2016 it is too bald and too straight forward. It honestly didn't surprise me or made me curious, the only reason i stayed was because of the effects and the explosions. The acting wasn't really any good, the actors and actress didn't feel comfortable acting their characters, it doesn't give you the sense of feeling that these actors and actress cannot be replaceable like Robert Downey Jr is and has to be the one and only Ironman. Amy Adams did good, Ben Affleck could really be a lot better. Jesse Eisenberg though, really need to stop copy Heath Ledger and just bring your own acting and feelings into this movie.

Good points: Not very commercialised, only a little compare to other big films this year like Creed. Batman equipment are much more advanced. I liked how the movie is like a trailer for future movies in DC, but they really tried a bit too hard....

Few points before going in: Learn some DC stuff, otherwise you wouldn't know what's going on while watching it. If your bf force u to watch it, say no, it's gonna be the worse times of your life. Drink a red bull otherwise u will fall asleep. Good day.

title: While visually appealing the story and characters leave much to be desired.
review: While the movie was visually appealing it ultimately is burdened by a messy plot and shaky character development/motivation. With DC and Warner Brothers trying to make this movie the bedrock of a franchise, one can't help but feel that it places its successors on less than stable ground. Zach Snyder borrows heavily from about 3-4 different comic story lines/alternate universes and tries to squish them together in this thematic follow up to Man of Steel. Imagine those were all fruits to make a smoothie. He peeled them and put the bitter skin in the blender to make the smoothie instead of the meat of the fruit that makes them good. He threw that stuff away and while you could technically say that he stayed true to the idea of a fruity drink, in practice it doesn't taste as good.

title: Fails to live up to the hype
review: I had no expectations going into this movie, I expected it to be a mediocre film and it was. The DC based movie franchise really struggles to lay down the ground work before introducing new characters and then maintain some continuity. Even though the Batman story has been told over and over again I felt like it would have served them better to continue Batman's story from where the Dark Knight trilogy left off (something they could have done even with a new actor donning the uniform) rather then rushing through the Batman back story and making everyone watch the Wayne's being murdered AGAIN!!! Alfred even made a comment that Batman had been fighting crime for 20 years and that he (Bruce) was getting old. So they made us watch the Wayne's get killed again then just skipped over the rest like his struggles against all the other villains was insignificant. I bring up this one point because the whole film felt this way, like it was rushed and disjointed. Henry Cavill is a great Superman but it's not even worth my time learning the actors name who played Lex Luthor because his performance was so bad and Ben Affleck as Batman was terrible as I believe most people expected it would be. Ignore the reviews that rave about this film and Ben Afflecks amazing performance because those reviews have obviously be written by the films marketing and PR team he really was as bad in this film as he was in Dare Devil. The fight between Batman and Superman was boring and it took way to long to get to that point with a rushed ending. Could have been so much better.

title: 153 minutes too long
review:
No juice at all. The dialogs are monologues and basically the film is just the fight between those two. No brains are needed to watch this movie. The best actor was Jeremy Irons, other than that, the flashbacks, the dreams, the nightmares are way too long and interrupts for no reason. The director trademark is dark images, fast pace action, and fantastic imagery. That's it. He should watch some Kubrick or Chaplin. No fun to watch.

The actors are stiff, the MARTHA!!!! Please, come on, there are other more creative ways to untangle a climax.

No more Zack Snyder films for me.

title: A let down (but not because of the acting)
review:
I was hyped for this but ultimately it was a let down. But not for the sake of the acting, but more the lack of well thought-out script, no major highpoints in the movie and general overuse of CGI and lackluster fight scenes.

First and foremost the actors did a good job, it was not really their performances that made this movie boring, it was more the script and complete lack of generally interesting scenes done by poor scripting and directing. There was nothing left to the imagination with the trailer, no real humor in the film, and the beginning & ending were way too drawn out.

Lex could have had more screen time. Something about watching an indestructible man and a guy who's got a suit that literally can't even be penetrated by bullets get thrown through massive bricks then stand up time and time again left me feeling like the stakes of the fight just weren't really there. Its hard to feel pulled in when the guys fighting aren't even really at risk.

title: A very disappointing start to the DC Universe
review:
Extremely disappointed with how this movie turned out. It was boring, full of dull scenes that moved a boring, inconsequential plot forward. Batman v Superman did not deliver on the promise of the title and subtitle Dawn of Justice played out on video clips on a computer so it was not something interesting to watch on a big screen. This movie was not visually dazzling or at all entertaining, it was a poor attempt to mimic Marvel's success and failed miserably.

I am a fan and anticipated this movie since they first announced it. I prepared by looking back. I didn't cringe too much as details emerged of bad casting and alternating release dates. Even as I watched the movie I held out hope that the tie would turn and the second half would be worth the first half wait, but alas no. This movie didn't even match up to its immediate predecessor in Man of Steel and was the worst version of Batman yet, maybe a little better than George Clooney but equally silly.

Check out more of this review and others at swilliky.com

title: I can't imagine a fan getting out of the theater disappointed.
review: I understand why the film would divide people but for me it is a personal favorite. Definitely among the top five of the best superhero films, maybe second to the Dark Knight. First of all, this is a beautiful film. The visuals are out of this world. The performances are ALL on point. Ben Affleck is amazing as Batman,Cavill does a much better job than in MOS and i even liked Jesse Eisenberg. Yes, this version of Luthor is a bit over the top but Jesse did a good job anyway. I've heard reviewers going about the film running lots of parallel stories together and not focusing on one storyline. And it is true that the movie is trying to set up a lot of things at once but i think it does it successfully; or as successfully as possible considering the difficulty of the task. There were so many scenes that i loved. Others because they were cool (f.e. the BvS scene AMAZING and Wonder Woman in action also SLAYING) and others because they were so emotionally overwhelming they send goosebumps all over my body. I also like that Lois Lane was not just a stand-by love interest or the means to some plot point. She was relevant, she was badass and one of the very few superhero romantic interests done right(i am having a hard time thinking of another one RN). The score was also very fitting and the ending I LOVED. In general, it is a dark film but it doesn't leave you in a grim mood. Quite the opposite. The ending note is quite hopeful; even though in a bittersweet way. As i said at the beginning i understand why this film wouldn't be for everyone but i'm quite certain that people who've been looking forward to this will not be let down.

title: Huge, huge disappointment
review:
So I went to the Premier of "Batman vs Superman Dawn of Justice" yesterday and was hype as all hell, through all of the marketing and expectation for this movie. I'm sad to say that I am really disappointed after seeing this movie. I'm going to count up all the bad and good points of this movie (in my opinion)

The Bad:

The plot was all over the place. There were huge plot holes, like apparently Superman can hear Lois Lane screaming while he's hiking somewhere in the mountains and is still able to save her, but for some reason can't hear his mother's screams while she's being abducted by Lex Luthor's men. Or the huge convenience that the Krypton ship was speaking English and not krypton. One of the things I hated the most about this film is that Batman breaks his one moral code that he never, NEVER breaks, that's his one rule, but apparently the writers of this film didn't care and just let batman mowing down people, literally shooting people with rifles, without any explanation given throughout the whole movie. Something that is also never explained is Lex Luthor's motivation for wanting Superman dead. I found Lois Lane to be of no use in this film either, her whole plot of finding the special bullet and tracing it back to Lexcorp finds no conclusion and was quite boring anyway, since Lex Luthor was behind much more devastating things anyway (like blowing up the Senate) The birth of Doomsday is weird too, why would the DNA mixture of General Zod and Lex Luthor create a 9 foot tall, huge green monster that can blast out shock waves? The fight between Batman and Superman was too short (8 mins ca.) and the whole reason for the fight was ridiculous anyway. Why didn't Superman fly down to Batman and quickly shout "Lex has my mother and is playing both of us" instead talking as slowly and as unconventionally as possible? The Justice League cameos were forced as well and for people that don't know DC's characters very well their appearance was very confusing. (for my friends at least) The last thing I didn't like about this movie was Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Lex Luthor. Watching him actually made me laugh on several occasions, because I couldn't take him seriously at all.

The Good

I loved the fight with the trinity against Doomsday at the end and was so hype when it happened (especially with the booming score) I thought the score was good by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL although I did find it to be overly bombastic with not enough memorable melodies, but instead constant loud drums, that after a while stopped driving the film (because of the heavy use of them, it numbed their effect) and were just sort of "there". I liked Gal Gadot's performance & look of Wonder Woman even though it seemed like she had a bit of a confused, middle eastern accent at times I thought Henry Cavill was decent as Superman, but nothing special I liked Ben Affleck's portrayal as Bruce Wayne a bit more than his performance as Batman, in which I still would prefer Bale. I liked the Batman action sequence (apart from the killing) And lastly I liked the actual fight between Batman and Superman, I didn't think it was particularly special but actually seeing it was still pretty awesome.

All in all a mixed bag that for me was very disappointing. The film was so concerned with setting up the JL that it completely forgot to be a good movie and tried to push in too many story lines in an already really full movie. I hope DC fires Zack Snyder and the writers of this movie and keep all of the cast except Jesse Eisenberg for JL. 4/10

title: Dawn of Justice - neither Batman nor Superman.
review:
You know the feeling? when we watched Alien Vs Predator long time ago, that's what i was feeling after watching this movie! It's no where near to Dark Knight or Man of Steel,

In my head all i was asking, why merge the 2 fantastic movies into one and mess it all up? then comes the wonder woman! Her intro. and incorporation are awkward and artificial, she was just there for 15 or 20 minutes,

Remember Avengers? there was plenty of post credit scenes, Easter eggs & Years of settings from Iron Man to Captain America-TFA then we were introduced into Avengers universe, in other hand we have Dawn of Justice, which serves no real purpose beyond helping to jump start Justice League.

title: Wait for shortened TV-version, if any
review:
I watched this movie at opening night with about 15 other people in theater that holds 300. It is difficult to review since there isn't really anything flat out wrong and the movie isn't that boring. There is too much repetition though and the origin story of Batman could have been left out. I think we all know the basic story by now.

Affleck as batman was OK but he is built like a tank and is not very agile which shows in the fight scenes. He suffers from the same flaw as the whole cast which is the total lack of personality in the characters. No-one really shines in any scene and they are there to deliver the lines they were told to. This movie was pointlessly long and several scenes could have been cut out or their message delivered otherwise. Special effects stole the end of the movie and was out of control. Most of the new characters weren't explained at all which can confuse regular viewers like me. I do know something but I was really surprised that they didn't even try to explain anything. Things just happened.

I would advice to avoid this title no matter how much of a fan. There really isn't anything to see.

By the way I and 3 others sat through the entire credits hoping to see something extra. There isn't any.

title: This movie is a huge problem
review:
This movie is a huge problem, as when it comes to superhero ensemble films, chemistry is the most important thing, what they didn't have. Joss Whedon did this very well with the different kinds of heroes in 'The Avengers' (2012), bringing in different heroes with different backgrounds, but their chemistry felt real, you can tell the actors got along.

Bryan Singer also achieved this in the "X-Men" movies, bringing in different mutants with different abilities and how they team up seamlessly to fight their enemies.

The "Dawn of justice" are supposed to be close friends from the get- go, but the fact that these actors could only make small talk with each other is problematic, you don't believe in their "friendship" because they don't seem to care, and neither should you.

Clichés, weak actors, artificial effects, script with many holes, we need a reboot.

title: Greatest superhero movie since Dark Knight
review: Batman v Superman... definitely an improvement from MOS,(which I loved), in the sense that it shows so much and completes this new cinematic universe DC/WB has to offer. The story is great, dark, fun at times and action packed without leaving behind some great dialogue and themes like power, religion, politics, justice, discrimination, revenge, society and a big etc. The actors do their part properly and zach snyder knows his comics and how to please fans, because every image is iconic and taken directly from the source material in a poetic aesthetically incredible dreamy way. Ben Affleck is Batman, period. The most comic accurate and brutal. His Bruce is exceptional. Henry Cavill reprises his role as Superman, but unlike in MOS (where he was a rookie), he is now in control of his powers, knows what he has to do as Clark and supes, and is much closer to the fully grown character we all love, shouting all the haters and leaving a great impression, he is Superman. Amy Adams is a great Lois, this time proving she is a natural journalist and very professional. Jessie Isenberg is a strange choice for luthor, but it works!, he is psychotic, evil and controlling and of course taken directly from the source. Gal Gadot steals the show.... Her Wonder Woman is epic, sure of herself, sarcastic and a fearsome warrior. A great surprise. Every one else serves for the story, and the acting is awesome. BELIEVE ME, THIS MOVIE IS EPIC. The action is on another scale/level. See it in the cinemas, if possible in a big big screen, with loud sound/sub-woofers, because the experience is sometimes scary as the scale is like you are experiencing the action, whats happening like you are witnessing it (specially the kryptonian invasion from Bruce's point of view). Can't say anything else because of spoilers, but I will say this: There's a big universe out there, and it is clearly implied in the movie. What's to come is only getting better.

review:

And after plenty of trite dialogue they become friends again because they have mothers named Martha in common. Just when you thought that conflict was resolved Lex Luther unleashes the Kraken or the equivalent of the Pillsbury Doughboy.

With so much Kryptonite floating around the smart money is betting on Batman. Actually the smart money belongs to those who pass on this overblown over hyped movie. Even if you see it for free, you'll never get that two and a half hours back.

The film in question is beyond dull at a whopping 153 minutes, depressingly juvenile yet self- important with little or no originality.The special effects are undeniably impressive at times yet always accompanied by an utterly uninspired score. I'd talk of characterization but there's little point. Amy Adams is wasted in this as are most of the cast. I would take some comfort in the idea of the superhero movie juggernaut coming to a halt but no doubt this extended trailer of a movie will make a ton of cash leading to a never ending series of sequels side-projects and whatever other money making opportunities can be milked from this dead horse. These film are made to take your cash and keep you dumb. WAKE UP.

title: Worst movie ever!
review: I normally do not like extreme ratings, too high or too low. Modesty in everything, I usually say. But when a movie is as blatantly deceptive as this one is, then to me the extremely bad rating is deserved. This was supposed to be a superhero movie, I thought. It wasn't. Coming out on the Christian's Easter weekend (spoiler alert!), this movie is a very, very tricky way of getting people into church for Easter without them knowing it. There are references to God and the devil throughout, so that you come to see Superman as God's representative and Lex Luthor (an obvious atheist representative) and the reincarnated Zod as the devil. Superman is crucified on a spear, dying as a sacrifice to save the world from the devil. Batman is his apostle Paul who at first opposes him, then sings his praises. Predictably, the last scene is the casket of superman getting ready to come back to life. What a disappointment! Everything was predictable. They made sure to get in all the usual necessary tricks to draw in everyone's emotions - the male muscles, the girl (Amy Adams), the action, the great CGI scenery. But there was nothing worthy in the story. It was nothing more than a Christian ploy to tell the Easter story through Superman. Really, really poor taste, in my opinion.

title: Yes, it's dark, but that's a good thing
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is one of the most polarizing if not THE most polarizing movie to come out in recent years.

I believe this is one of those movies that will be reevaluated and re-appreciated in years to come when the current trend has been abandoned and people will be able to appreciate for what it is and not for how it compares to other movies to come out around the same time.

It seems that most complaints and negative reviews towards this movie have one main criticism: it's dark tone and lack of "fun".

So basically what is really happening is that critics are comparing this movie to every superhero-themed flick to have been released in the last decade and since said movies were full of jokes and (occasionally cheesy) one-liners Batman v Superman is getting criticized for having none of that

Well, then good news are: this movie is NOT supposed to be funny, it is NOT supposed to have cheesy one-liners and it was NOT created exclusively for the delight of impressionable children who will eventually outgrow the light-hearted, zero-thought-needed superhero movies that have become associated with Marvel Studios and it's owner, Disney.

This movie is aimed at the audiences who want to see what it is like to have super powered individuals in a real world-like setting where saving people cause's political backlashes and the existence a vigilante is directly related to deep issues with society.

Having comic-relief in this movie would be out of place and even somewhat absurd so it is not something to be criticized.

With that said...is this movie perfect? Well, no. It has some very awkward moments and even though the way how it tried to build up the foundations of a sequel ended up in an amazing dystopian sequence, it also ended up with another separate scene which feels truly out of place and includes a memorable moment of not-so-good acting and special effects. Add to this the constant intercalation between too many plot points and it is inevitable to end up creating some flaws.

However, in the end, this movie IS VERY GOOD, possibly the best experience I have ever had in a theater, a cinematic accomplishment in terms of atmosphere and a spectacle for any fan of the titular characters, who both receive some of their best (in Batman's case, possibly THE best) big screen characterizations ever.

Keep also an eye for the big screen debut of the World's premiere super heroine and icon for female empowerment, Wonder Woman.

title: Unworthy of Your Worship
review:
Does the world really need Superman? Why would the world feel a need for Batman?

I will have to say for myself that I am in no support for the blessed Man of Steel. I see little appeal in his uninspired character and ability, and he has played a small role in my years growing up. As for the Dark Knight, he led a much greater influence on my childhood, as he showed great persistence and strategic planning to maintain social order. Does Zack Snyder's new interpretation do justice to developing the images of either of these idols of citizen worship? In truth, Mr. Snyder has zero sense of what to communicate about our matters of worship in a single deity, no matter how intentional his attempts.

It's unbelievable how little he hides Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice's symbolic ties with the Holy Scriptures. He starts it up with a dramatically overdone opening of Bruce Wayne as a child fleeing from his parents' funeral while flashing back to their deaths. He falls into a pit in a forest where hundreds of bats either carry him out or help him to float out, a scene I'm guessing is meant to be open to interpretation. The very next event we see of Bruce's life is ironically where Man of Steel had ended: right in the battle between Superman and General Zod. It takes you through Bruce's perspective of the destruction, and how he rescues a little girl whose mother was just killed in the mayhem. It's a savior figure of September 11th proportions, but the screenwriters Chris Terrio (Argo) and David S. Goyer (The Dark Knight) had no sense of structure to plot Bruce's growth into Batman emotionally right.

Then Lois Lane goes to Africa to track a crime organization, a racially insensitive and unnecessary subplot if anything. Then Lex Luthor investigates the remains of Krypton through explorations in the Indian Ocean, in order to gain world domination as the devil overthrowing Metropolis' god. Then Clark Kent looks upon Metropolis' criticism toward him, all questioning if he deserves the honor as he has let several people die. I will admit, their responses are shockingly realistic to how the world would react to a Superman, but when aligned with the film's three other subplots, this philosophy lacks its intended purpose.

Although an excellent dose of reality is added by the various people who come out to declare against the Man of Steel's actions towards humanity. You will see a legless man working under Bruce Wayne who defaces the Superman statue. You will see Neil DeGrasse Tyson speak on CNN about the hero's controversial actions. The people had looked up to Superman as their god, and they felt let down. So who other than Lex would come to force god to bow to him?

Batman has also failed as a messiah for the people, yet in a different level of failure as he never even earns your respect and empathy to begin with. He always burns his bat emblem to the criminals he stops, and shoots soldiers dead in the broad daylight of Africa like some killer. Definitely not the Batman we've come to hope for. But eventually, he and Superman had to meet through Lex Luthor's dinner party, forming a connection as they were both assumedly responsible for the deaths of their families. Then Lex tests Superman's godliness by forcing him to kill the Batman in order to save the life of his mother. This battle between god and man sounds promising as you've just read in the film's title, yet the promised battle composes of the same blasting through walls and heavy punches that was mindlessly tossed around in Man of Steel, except now with no Ihop to complete the consumerist picture.

Eventually, you just have to ask, when will Wonder Woman come in already?!

It may not all be director Zack Snyder's fault for creating a jumbled mess of a social message, another part goes to the superfluous 3D cinematography by Larry Fong (300, Watchmen) that overuses its high contrast, underexposed low-key lighting, and painfully bright flames. But the greatest blame of the tremendous lack of passion belongs to the atrocious miscasting. Ben Affleck is a sheer bore as Batman, backed with no motivation nor grief. Jesse Eisenberg is the last one I would want to play the nemesis who seeks world domination. He looks more threatened than threatening with his amateurish, high pitched speech of a college know-it-all who's trying to act like a jock. There's also several random uncomfortable moments of actors Henry Cavill and Amy Adams appearing semi-nude on screen for the sake of it, but it's ultimately Mr. Eisenberg who will make you feel most embarrassed.

Just take a look at our religiously unstable time, and you'll see how we're all susceptible to worshiping whatever god fills our immediate need, be it an iPhone or a significant other or a political figure, none of which saves us from when all hell breaks loose. I fail to see how Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice helps us to flee from those unfulfilling gods, nor deliver us to the greater saving power. I don't see any hope either that the future Justice League or Wonder Woman movies will continue what Zack Snyder is supposedly starting. Mr. Snyder, I hope you are reading this right now, because it's time you listened good: I understand your proper motives to attempt a message of belief in a false deity through these famous figures of American culture, but you also ought to listen to what the people of your Metropolis are saying about Batman and Superman's lack of heroism. They're in the proper mind. It's time you listened to the people.

Overall Grade: D-

title: A Train Wreck!
review:
Don't get me wrong, I am a fan of most ALL super hero movies, but this one was so ill-conceived and poorly "Pieced Together" it often times becomes Mixed up within its own story line, and that's putting it kindly.

title: Rushed, messy and lacking any real fun
review:
Im sad to say that this was a fatal blow to DC's cinematic universe before it had time to really get started. Man of Steel wasn't amazing but was decent and I had hopes for DC's future in movies. Clearly looking to emulate the success of Marvel's cinematic universe DC however decided not to take it's time to introduce us to it's characters and lead us to an eventual crossover. Instead it's chosen to give it all to Zack Snyder and force it out ASAP and now we have this under cooked mess. While Batman v Superman isn't awful or even that bad it is a far cry from what could have been and spells nothing but disaster for what's to come. Zack Snyder was a terrible choice from day one as while he is certainly talented at visual filmmaking he is terrible at telling a cohesive story with enjoyable characters unless he copies it right from a comic or graphic novel. This film tries to be several comic book stories in one and manages to do justice to none of them.

Firstly the film is completely joyless which some fans defend claiming it to be "dark and mature" well forgive me for expecting a film called BATMAN V SUPERMAN to be fun. When two men is silly outfits are fighting on screen there's only so much you can take seriously and while it's true that superhero stories can be mature they also need to remember what they are. Henry Cavill is dull and lifeless as Clark Kent/Superman and barely even speaks instead just looking glum 90% of the time. Ben Affleck does a decent job as Bruce Wayne and Batman and does fit the darker tone far better than his more brightly dressed opponent. I found Batman's story to be far more engaging although it's clear how confused the writers were in telling this ludicrous story which is more a 3 hour long teaser trailer for the Justice League as there are incredibly forced dream sequences to try and fit in these references to things to come. That's a huge problem with this movie, it's so busy trying to excite you for the next film it forgets to be a good movie on it's own. Batman and Superman's fight, the main point of the film has no reason to even happen and is purely fan service.

As for the villain we have Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor and he was utterly laughable as this diabolical mastermind. Jesse is great when playing characters like Mark Zuckerberg but here he is horribly miscast. Amy Adams' Lois Lane was a strong enjoyable character and a highlight of Man of Steel but here she is nothing more than a waste of run time as her utterly meaningless quest throughout the film is there for no reason other than to keep her occupied until the climax. However an unexpected highlight of the film was Gal Gadot's surprising and excellent portrayal of Wonder Woman. She was by far the best part of the film for me in the limited time she gets and for nothing else her and Batman are the only things to look forward to in the future of the cinematic universe.

The film has some exciting action and in fact the first 20 minutes are excellent with heavy drama and great visual storytelling. It's a shame then that the rest of the film falls flat. In conclusion I hope DC can learn from this mistake and take greater care in future. There is potential that I don't want to see go to waste. Step 1: GET RID OF ZACK SNYDER.

title: Warner Bros had to choose between wonder woman's bathing suit or a script writer. They obviously went with Wonder Woman.
review:
Batman vs Superman was supposed to be a superhero extravaganza, but it wasn't. BVS was just a bad movie, and people just cant accept that, not as bad as fan4stic but still pretty bad, it just felt unfinished containing not enough but too much at the same time.

Things just suddenly happened like the batman car chase with no exposition leading up to it and the explanation for things happening was really convoluted. Some scenes were just ridiculous like the scene with Superman's dad and others were pointless such as the very clichéd i love you scene before Superman's death. Which again is so pathetic. They had his damn funeral for about the same amount of time.

Only one of the five or six fight sequences was decent the others felt like going in and out of constant hyper-drive, the star wars kind.

The script was probably written by a deranged high six year old while the plot was literally an episode of any superhero cartoon. Some of the lines were just, ugh, so out of character. The imbecilic Bruce Wayne still irritates me. Even Lois lane figured out that it was Lex before he did and she is only a Pulitzer prize winning reporter and not the worlds greatest detective.

Batfleck might have been a good batman but other than the very first scene, his performance as Bruce Wayne was terrible. Wonderwoman's existence relied on basically nothing. And character motivations were flawed, the fact that superman fought batman because his mom was kidnapped, just insulted the ideological battle which was the climax of the epic dark knight returns. Im not saying that it should be a copy of a comic book but if you are planning on taking scene by scene visual inspiration from a comic please match those honestly beautiful visuals, not talking about the effects, with a story worthy of such a comic.

WB is right now is solely putting as many characters on screen as marvel i.e playing a vain game of catch up. Nothing in this movie other than some poster worthy shots actually clicked. The Martha scene has been insulted to death and I support that insult.

title: Batman vs. Superman? You must be kidding!
review:
The problem with "BVS: Dawn of Justice" is the built up tension between the two men and their motivations against each other to defeat. Years, but years ago, when Freddy vs. Jason was released, with no expectation, I saw and liked the movie at home theater. The spin-off showdown was executed pretty well and it was fun. However, "Batman v Superman" cannot give us goosebumps or even little excitement.

Ben Affleck is great, Bruce Wayne is great, as for Batman, he looks dark and intimidating and the best hand to hand combat in Batman franchise is here, but thanks to some cheesy visual effects, that also the movie itself suffers from, ruins the experience! In some scenes, Batman looks like a computer generated character from a PC game and it really bothered me!

There is something wrong with the way of storytelling in this movie. We don't care about the "gladiator" fight between the two, maybe because the tone of the movie is cold? In contrast with Zack Snyder's masterpiece "Watchmen", "Batman v Superman" is pretty heartless and soulless. The opening sequence of the movie is amazing!

The connection between the destruction in "Man of Steel" and Bruce Wayne's anger against Superman considering the casualties is very smart. However, the very beginning of the movie was not that impressive, because I know Mr. Snyder can do much better.

I think, the movie is not too dark as claimed by some people, the problem is not being too dark, it is the editing, the storytelling, the motivations, the clichés, the visual effects and so on.. Also, the movie has not a comic book tone or atmosphere which is an unforgivable mistake! Visually, the movie was just flat and at times, it was dull which is very surprising.

The purpose of this movie should have been focusing on the showdown between two of the greatest super heroes on earth, but instead, the purpose of this movie is to make a way for the upcoming Justice League movies. You make an almost three hour long movie, but you fill that movie with lots of other stories and characters. The expected fight between the two is a pure disappointment. It has a few priceless moments, but in the end, it was too short and not extraordinary, unforgettable or magnificent as it should be. Mr. Snyder didn't do "justice" to it!

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor wasn't bad, but annoying. His evil plans felt like we were watching a "Pinky and The Brain" episode. Doomsday? Ohh, man! Producers must abandon the idea of releasing a big monster in every big budget action movie! Therefore, this "monster movie" mood stabs the film even more. In the last half, the movie speeds up and again we see lots of destruction, explosion and mayhem! Batmobile is great, but in some action moments, the visual effects ruin everything again.

Gal Gadot is the second star of this movie after Ben Affleck's success! She is amazing, hot and strong! However, I prefer daily Wonder Woman who is more interesting than most of the "Bond girls" in James Bond flicks! The relationship between her and Bruce Wayne is very similar with classic spy movies. She was convincing as the character that made me want more of her in the movie.

The long first half of the movie is slow paced, then things hot up and then the movie speeds up like crazy! If you ask me, I prefer the slow first half over the action packed second half, especially because of some terrible CGI moments, clichés and rushed feeling. And the suddenly revealing humor between characters change the mood of the film in a bad way.

There are two parts in the movie which you can watch with awe. The dream sequence of Bruce Wayne is creepy, surreal and the second best part of the movie, but the best part of the movie is definitely the hand to hand combat sequence following an attack.

Henry Cavill as Superman is always perfect and he is the same here, nothing less and nothing more, but in this cold and soulless film, we cannot feel anything about a character in a real way. By the way, I want to mention again that Ben Affleck really delivers as Bruce Wayne and Batman and even if my personal favorite is Michael Keaton, I loved how Affleck portrays the character and having no problem with it. As a Batman fan, also my favorite super hero, I appreciate Mr. Affleck.

What this film succeeds in is to question what is wrong and what is right, to question the ethics of being a superhero, to question the decision of super heroes and reactions against them by the public and the government. By the way, the most interesting and intense character in the whole movie was Holly Hunter's Senator Finch! Lovely and beautiful actress Holly Hunter is remarkable in this story. And, Jeremy Irons was cool as Alfred!

title: Batman Vs. Superman - Really???
review:
Wow!!!

I felt like I wasted my time watching this movie. Here's why:

1. Superman Vs. Batman - Come on, we all know Superman could kick Batman's #ss any-day of the week and twice on Sunday. It's a no-brainer. Superfreak vs. freak in a mask. What good does Batman's bat-star do against superman who can withstand bullets.
