10. Oh yeah...this movie sucks!

title: I do not understand
review:
Only in a world where the ultimate crap that Jurassic World was that movie receives praise and standing ovation and BvS receive the amount of hate and backlash it got. It makes me sad. I went into BvS with high expectations and a reasonable amount of fear that they going to screw this up and I - an ultimate Batman fan - will hate the guts of the film. Instead, I turned out to be loving it.

I liked Henry Cavill in MOS so I knew what to expect, and I absolutely LOVED Batfleck. And while Michael Keaton will be my favorite Batman probably until the day I die, Affleck comes in a close second. HE IS AMAZING. He is taking this character so seriously and represents it with such passion it just blew me away. The only thing I'm still uncertain about is Eisenberg's Luthor. Even though I have seen the movie twice already I'm still convinced that he is a wrong casting choice for the character. Besides both heroes are in their mid-thirties-forties and then Luthor is a teenage kid? No, that is not okay. At least for me. Anyway, I could bore you much more with my rumbling but I won't do that as I try to keep this brief.

In short, I loved this film and this is the superhero movie I wanted to see. It is not perfect, and some stuff remains unexplained I do feel that the truth behind the incredible backlash is that Batman and Superman are just too iconic characters for their own good. Everybody have their own perceptions and know how these characters should be when it comes to creating them. I'm convinced that no matter who directed this movie, or what they managed to achieve plays no part in how people see this film. Besides, we are spoiled now when it comes to superhero films. People can nitpick way too much. I think it is an excellent movie and people should watch it, disregard all the criticism, and make up their own minds. The hate the movie gets is unreasonable. I also feel that the psychology behind that people seem to unable to relate to Superman's character is because we live in a disillusioned world with full of fear. People don't care about good/pure characters anymore. This is actually represented in the film quite clearly. Anyway, give it a shot and let's see if you like it!

title: The superheroes are the reviewers who lead us to believe this movie deserves 4 stars at most! CRAP MOVIE!
review:
I went out to the lobby to check and make sure that this was the same movie that actually got ratings higher than a 5. How do people get away with saying how much they were disappointed by the movie, but still rate it a ten? Are they giving it a "Sympathy" vote because it is a DC comic attempt at a movie, rather than a Marvel movie? It almost became "Me vs The Cinema", as I was going to ask for a refund of my ticket price! I can honestly say that I have felt like walking out of a few movies, but was ready to run out on this one... HORRIBLE, GARBAGE, and if I were to be given a DVD of this title I would use it as an ice scraper in my car. How much farther can Superman and Batman movies sink? ... not much farther than this one folks.

What kind of valid rating can be constructed of reviewers who agree that this movie was not the best, yet give it a ten star vote on the rating system? Are you trying not to hurt anyone's feelings, or damage the self esteem of the people responsible for putting this crap on the screen? Review after review relates that this is not the best movie, yet they rate it 10 stars? This is like observing an Olympic diver bounce off the board and perform a "bellyflop", and give a 10 score for the height of the splash! Where do these votes come from? Someone please pay me a few bucks so that I can throw a few bogus reviews out there. I can write things such as:

"IT IS AN OVERLY LONG, BORING PIECE OF WORK WITH NO REAL STORY, BUT IT WAS JUST WHAT I NEEDED TO GET SOME SLEEP IN A PUBLIC THEATER! 10 STARS"

"IT WASN'T AS GOOD AS MOS 5X, BUT SO MUCH BETTER THAN WD40! 9 STARS!"

"THE HEAT IN THE THEATER FELT GREAT, AS IT WAS BELOW ZERO TEMPERATURE OUTSIDE! 10 STARS!"

"I REALLY ENJOYED THE PREVIEWS OF COMING ATTRACTIONS! 10 STARS!"

How does this crap get produced? A great deal of special effects, but they forgot to add a decent cohesive story. My friends tell me "You must be a fan of both universes to understand the movie" I say "Bulldinky!!" All the buildup and publicity, the secret chatter about the production... What a load of horse crap that was. THIS FILM IS A TOTAL WASTE OF 2 1/2 HOURS!!! I would have liked it better if it were 1 1/2 hour long, because I feel that I would not have wasted the extra hour that I did waiting for the movie to suddenly "Get Better..." before it ended. I read both Superman and Batman comics as a kid, and let me tell you, if the comics back then were half as bad as this movie is now I never would have bought another DC Comic. If there is a comparison of DC and Marvel these days it is that DC Comics has a problem telling a story if it isn't referenced in a book as an inside joke known only to the select few people who read the small print.. Waste of time, talent , money, effort, and blank film. Steer clear of this piece of crap movie, and wait until something better comes along like King Kong vs Curious George, because you will never recover the time you spend trying to stay awake for this gem...

title: Meh! Mediocre movie where you can get lost easily
review:
Honestly, I didn't think too much about this movie to begin with and I have to say, I wasn't disappointed.

At some point I was sitting in the movie theater and I was asking myself: When is it going to end? Now I'm no expert, but that's not a good thing to be thinking about while watching a movie.

I am not an overly huge Ben Affleck fan, just given his past performances in some movies. Here he actually delivered and showed some good acting. So did Cavill. But for me, the best thing about this whole movie was Jesse Eisenberg. He really made me enjoy the few moments he was on screen. Now he is the "bad guy" here, but he kinda made me root for him after the first few scenes with him. It was just an astonishing performance as Luthor. In some way, he reminded me of the Joker from the earlier Batman movies. He really gave Luthor a new twist and I totally bought it.

As for the rest of the movie, it was kinda a see-saw of scenes. At one second you're in this scene and without any connection, it cuts to a totally different scene and then cuts to another scene after that. You can easily get lost in all of these scenes, that you don't know what you're actually watching.

And finally the big thing between Batman and Superman. The dispute between them seems a bit too forced, but (I don't want to spoil the movie) it ends too quickly and with a stupid reason in my opinion.

All in all, it is a movie. But not a movie that I would recommend to my friends or any other movie lover. If you're interested to watch this anyway, I would wait for the Blu-Ray.

title: Most horrendously edited movie i've seen in a good ten years.
review: This was the most horrendously edited movie i've seen in a good ten years. Almost every single scene was haphazardly put together, thus creating plot holes big and small that made me cringe throughout the movie. As a result of this the actions of the characters are nonsensical to the point that it feels like they know plot points that they shouldn't know. Also Zack snyders attempts at shoving in his philosophy of superheroes was painful to watch. He is clearly way in over his head. This movie wasn't a failure because it was too dark, or too intense. By all means it set the tone perfectly. It's a failure because it was just plain poorly made. Snyders cockiness and horrendous editing made what could have been one of the best superhero movies ever into a pile of dog sh*t.

title: A typical superhero-movie with good action
review:
I watched the movie without reading any Reviews before. That helped me a lot, because a lot of Reviews and Ratings about this movie are saying, it's awful. In my opinion it is not! And here comes why.

Zack Snyder is one of the greatest Directors of all time. Yes, he has directed "Man of Steel", a superhero movie which isn't great. We all know he does good movies though. And BvS is definitely one of them. With Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams,... the movie already has a great cast. The "new" Batman (Ben Affleck) is, of course, different to Bale's Batman from the Nolan Trilogy. But he is not worse than him, just different. I think he's doing his job better than great. His interpretation of the character is interesting, fascinating and so worth to watch. Even Jeremy Irons as Alfred is far better in his role than Michael Caine. Henry Cavill, who we already saw playing Superman in "Man of Steel", is good again. He brings Superman alive, and nobody else. One of the most magnificent parts of the movie were these, with the side characters. Gal Gadot, as well as Laurence Fishburne are giving us excellent performances. As mentioned Gadot, who plays Wonder Woman, she is just awesome. I agree with the issue, that Wonder Woman was a little bit unnecessary in this movie, although she was one of the coolest characters in it. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor... Many people hate him, I love him. He is totally different as from the comic books, but his performance is just amazing. I think, that when people say, they don't like Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, they just don't like Lex Luthor (or this specific version of him). This is a Luthor we never saw before. He looks different, acts different, and is also different in his way to ... be. There's just the question if you like him that way or not. For me, who loves it, it is only even greater that Eisenberg gives us such a good performance. So far with the cast. The story isn't good, I admit. It feels a little bit boring and uncreative. But it keeps up the movie, so the action can have his full appearance. Action. A big issue for Zack Snyder. But not as in a lot of his other movies, the see a bunch of random CGI explosions, we see more controlled and good used CGI explosions. At all, the action and fights are really good. The fight choreography is great as well and fun to watch. It doesn't feel like the characters go down under the huge amount of action, they fit perfectly in it. Probably they don't have to concentrate on the story...

My conclusion is, that the movie was pretty good, and they better than my expectations. It has great actors, good action, but not such a great screenplay. It makes still very much fun to watch, and without spoilers, I can't wait for the next upcoming movies from the DC Comics Universe!

title: Just bad
review: Only thing that got it the 2 stars was Ben Affleck played the Batman part very well, with the darker Batman, nicely done Ben.He seems to have grown as an actor over the years. Superman was lacking and Wonder Woman promising but seemed to be lost in the plot. Lex was pathetic not even convincing, didn't seem at all like a super intelligent arch villain. You just feel at times his biggest crime was not shutting up. As for the whole plot of it just didn't measure up. I gave it the benefit of the doubt and went to see it, after all how bad could a movie with both Batman and Superman and hey Wonder Woman be. They proved me wrong. Is it really necessary to see Batman's parents being shot for the 12th time in a motion picture and the whole sequence of events in the next 2 minutes after that bats and all. That needed to be edited out, trust me by now people know lets get on with it. Yawn.

title: ugh!! (IMDB won't let me use caps)
review:
This will be a very concise review based upon a few, limited topics. This is the best that DC could do with their first team-up is to waste perhaps the most significant story arc in their history: The Death of Superman??? No wonder DC remains light years behind Marvel in putting teams on the big screen.

Batman's whole motivation is to reject guns because a gun killed his parents, but apparently that's out the window because both the Batmobile and the Batplane have Gatling guns.

And how is it that after a monumental battle and having declared Superman his sworn enemy based upon a "1% chance" that Supes may be bad or a risk, he then becomes Superman's friend after Superman merely utters the word "Martha"?? Also Batman's apparent trust of other "metahumans" completely contradicts his approach to Superman.

The casting of Affleck and Gadot both proved to be good choices. However, some homage to Frank Miller would have been appropriate. Gadot was convincing but outside of one grainy, black and white you keep Wonder Woman under wraps until the last half hour of the flick? Poor choice in my mind, there were lots of opportunities to develop her character in a progressive manner. If you were not familiar with Wonder Woman, you had no idea of what her powers were or what that shiny string was that she looped around Doomsday.

Overall, a poor effort. Poor plot and character development and a difficult to harmonize story line.

title: You had one job and you couldn't even get that right
review:
The most anticipated movie of the year has currently turned into one of the worst movie of the year for me. I wasn't really expecting much from a movie called "Batman V Superman" but I was expecting something.

The biggest problem I have is the plot. The plot doesn't know when to stick with something or when it should drop something. It feels like I'm watching multiple episodes of a Superman TV show with the odd cut to Batman. I literally couldn't keep a straight face while watching this movie, I was laughing through it. I kept on thinking of the Room when I was watching this because there are so many scenes that go nowhere. The movie is 2 hours 30 mins and for about 2 hours it's trying to get us to understand this story and get immersed in it and they only got me immersed in this plot line was in the 1 hour 50 mins mark. I was only starting to get immersed in it as they were busy cutting it off. I'm still questioning a few of the scenes that were in this movie as well. There's a scene when Superman is talking to Lois while she's in the bathtub for some reason. There's this whole story where it's supposed to show that the public are starting to fear Superman because they're not sure how they can control a God but that didn't seem to go anywhere and it was also cut off around the point I was getting immersed in it and for the rest of the movie, it felt like it had been completely forgotten. So the majority of the film feels like it was a complete waste of time and felt like it went nowhere or if it was intending to go somewhere, I fail to see where it was going. However, I have a different opinion of the last 40 mins of the film. This is where I'm going to get into spoiler territory. The actual fight between Batman and Superman only lasts 5 mins and it happens as the film is nearing it's 2 hour mark. The fight was well staged however and it was well thought out. Batman defeats Superman by using kryptonite weapons to bring Superman down to Batman's ability and Batman brings him down from there. That was an intelligent way for that fight to go. However just as Batman is about to kill Superman, he finds out Superman's mother has the same first name as his so they decide to work together to bring down Lex Luthor. Yes that's the actual reason Batman and Superman team up. Their mother has the same first name. I'm not joking. It isn't the same mother or anything, it's just that their mother has the same first name. That's one of the stupidest reasons I've heard for someone wanting to be my friend. "Hey, we have the same amount of armpit hair, want to be friends?" Then they go on this mission to stop Lex Luthor and save Superman's mother. They save the mother successfully however, Lex Luthor has unleashed Doomsday upon Batman and Superman and they learn he can only be stopped by kryptonite. The only kryptonite weapon Batman has left is a spear, which left in Gotham. Superman goes back to Gotham, saves Louis again (because obviously we haven't see that enough times), takes the kryptonite spear stabs Doomsday killing Doomsday and then Superman dies. I wasn't entirely sure why Superman died. He wasn't hit by the kryptonite (Batman scraped him across the cheek with it and he didn't die then) he was just near it. Superman has a funeral and obviously they had to leave it open for a sequel so Batman says to Wonder Woman "Get the others ready" Wonder woman responds with "how do you know something else will happen?" Batman says "I have a feeling." That segment of dialogue gets my "dreaming of the money" award, when a writer was too busy thinking of the amount of money he was going to be paid for something, he forgot he still had to write a piece of dialogue that was good.

That was me just explaining the last half hour of this movie and it's the most exhausting thing I've ever had to type up. It was like that for the whole 2 hours and 30 mins and I can't think of any better way to explain it than to type up a segment of the film, which I've just done.

If you're going there to see action then you aren't going to be disappointed, but for people like me that aren't satisfied with just seeing action and want something more from the films you see, this is definitely a skip.

title: Greatest gladiator match delivers!
review: Batman v superman dawn of justice is a film that delivers in superhero action the only way we all expect a Zack Snyder directed film to do so...epically. Ben Affleck is the best Batman we've ever seen on screen, brooding and violent, yet you feel his pain and understand his purpose. Henry Cavill is back as Superman and elevates his performance from Man of Steel. Gal Gadot is stunning as Wonder Woman. Gadot's take on the most recognizable female heroine is terrific and well received. Amy Adams did a great job as Lois Lane and is an unsung hero in the epic climax.Jesse Eisenberg gives us a completely different take on Lex Luthor that is believable and complimentary to the protagonists of the film. The supporting cast led by Lawrence Fishburn as Perry White help connect the dots on a complex story that goes beyond the realm of a typical comic book movie. All in all this film is terrific yet undeniably divisive. Perhaps the expectation of seeing a battle between the two most important characters in the comic book world surprised those who not only got the epic fight but were treated to a much deeper plot and a well placed introduction of other future Justice League characters. Great film that challenges the way comic book movies could or should be made moving forward. The majority of critics are dead wrong, Batman v Superman is excellence yet to be appreciated but ready to be explored.

title: The film that I thought would never be done.
review:
I watched yesterday. And i walked out the movie theater very pleased, even grateful to have had this opportunity.

This is one movie I always imagined but never thought they would do. I'm a fan since the time of Christopher Reeve movies and read DC comics throughout my childhood and adolescence, it must be why I got goose bumps in various scenes. It was a dream come true for a fan who grew up consuming Dc material.

That said. The film is very beautiful, have sensational fights, and because of that, marks an evolution in superhero films. Right now what we need is new ideas, otherwise, not even jokes can save it, because just gets boring.

There are important flaws in the script , but for me it was clear that were the cuts to adjust the screen time. Maybe too much deep information that could make things harder for newcomers. (I highly recommend it at least to watch Man of Steel first). Another problem is that exactly because the volume of informations, some important scenes just got accelerated.

I'm sure this movie will be the subject for a long time. As for the negative critics. Somewhat exaggerated, giving too much importance to negative things, but not considering the whole package.

PS: I've watched twice, in Imax 3D and a regular movie theater in 2D. The Imax screen size and sound make a great difference. I do recommend it.

title: I told you so
review:
I firmly believed Batman V Superman Dawn of Justice would be rubbish throughout the last couple of years. And I was right. Rather than trying to be a good superhero movie, this is pretty much an extended trailer for the DC Cinematic Universe. Hollywood evidently hasn't learnt anything at all from The Amazing Spider-Man 2 or Iron Man 2. In this movie, Batman takes on Superman as he disagrees with his actions, while Lex Luthor is also involved with some complicated scheme. Oh, and Wonder Woman's in there as well. She doesn't add anything to the movie to be honest. To be fair to BVS, it's not a complete disaster. The opening scene is pretty good, Ben Affleck proves the whole Batfleck controversy was a wildly unnecessary backlash with a mature, suitably understated performance and as can be expected from Zack Snyder it looks amazing. While admittedly the film does start to feel artificial at times, it does at least look amazing. In terms of acting, Jeremy Irons steals the show as Alfred. The trouble is, BVS is a mess of titanic proportions. Multiple underdeveloped, rushed elements clash together like a hyperactive prison riot and as a result the narrative is largely incoherent. The story is poorly structured, boring, makes no sense and most of the film was given away in the trailers. This is one painfully superficial movie, since it has so much going on there just isn't any depth. It may think it's serious, dark and powerful but sadly BVS is about as sophisticated and powerful as a Flash Beat 'em Up game and makes a mess out of a killer premise. Still, that's what I was expecting from the start.

4/10

title: Not everything is rainbows and sunshine all the time
review:
I was nervous going into this movie because of the bad reviews I had seen, but I was pleasantly surprised. Upon seeing it the second time yesterday, I officially have a new favorite super hero movie. I love the cast, everyone did an incredible job (especially Ben Affleck!)I love the story, I love the dark and serious tone of the film, the cinematography is beautiful, I love the score from Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL, and I love the risks they took with that ending! This movie is dark and violent and emotional, and it's everything I could have ever asked for in a Batman film! So it pains me to see people being so harsh on this movie.

The tone is a big thing I've seen criticized, but I don't know what people expect. This isn't a cartoon, and it's definitely not a children's movie. It doesn't need "more jokes." It's a realistic look at what a world with superheroes would be. It felt very much like The Dark Knight trilogy to me, but with an even better Bruce Wayne.

To be fair, if you're not a big DC fan, I can see how some people might get lost in the story. I followed it just fine, but I think a previous knowledge of DC lore is necessary to enjoy the film in its entirety. A certain "dream" sequence and cameo will probably confuse casual viewers who aren't familiar with all the characters.

(Spoilers below) One thing a lot of people seem to take issue with is the fact that Batman kills people in this movie. First off, Batman killing is not a new thing. Michael Keaton's Batman killed and many of the comic book versions have as well. But that aside, this is an older Bruce Wayne, he's been fighting crime for 20-30 years now, and in events we'll hopefully get to see in the solo movie, he's lost his way. He has lost his faith in humanity, and it takes Superman's sacrifice for Bruce to find his faith in mankind again. "Men are still good," he tells Diana. And the death of Superman! A++! I commend Zach Snyder for having the guts to kill Clark Kent. That was a powerful moment and I think the movie wouldn't have been as great without it. His sacrifice was necessary. And of course he'll be back, he always comes back. Don't fret.

title: More Dusk than Dawn of Justice
review:
This movie has been a must-see for DC Comics fans since it was announced 2-3 years ago. Despite the controversial title, many fans will know that there is precedent set in the DC Comics world for a show down between Batman and Superman.

Expectations have run high following the heady heights achieved by Christopher Nolan's Batman trilogy and the excellent Man of Steel reboot. So does Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice live up to its billing? ...Alas, not quite. I'll try to give you an honest view without giving away any spoilers.

Let's deal with the good things first. One of the main question marks hanging over the movie was whether Ben Affleck could pull off Batman after Christian Bale's definitive performance as The Dark Knight. The answer is yes; he is older, darker, far less moral and for me stole the show somewhat from Henry Cavill's Superman. In fact the acting performances and characters were, in the main, effective – as you would expect of such a strong cast. Zack Snyder has also maintained the darker atmosphere and more serious story lines of the DC Comics movies, which sets them apart from the more tongue-in- cheek (but highly effective) Marvel movies. However, Batman v Superman does take itself a little too seriously with an almost complete lack of humour of any kind.

So why did I not enjoy the movie? The answer is straight forward; the story simply wasn't good enough. It was disjointed, confused with some of the better concepts being poorly executed. Zack Snyder failed to hold on to the flowing and more plausible story line which he achieved in Man of Steel by trying to cram a little bit too much in. The end result is a two and half hour movie that feels very long because too many scenes drag on without adding enough to the story. You will even find yourself scratching your head at times and asking "what was the point of that?" Sadly these moments happen a little too often in a movie that just isn't engaging enough.

What about the action sequences? Well as you would expect of a superhero flick, there is a good deal of explosive CGI fueled mayhem, with our heroes and villains leveling as many homes and office blocks as possible. Some of the scenes are great and engaging...but, strangely, some just fizzle out and overall the action scenes just aren't enough to lift and carry the movie. Surprisingly even Hans Zimmer's music score was something of a let down.

For fans of Batman and Superman this is a must-see movie, but don't go in with high expectations. I can only hope that the inevitable follow up to Dawn of Justice can breathe life back in to the Justice League concept.

title: Why does Warner have so much trouble making a good superhero movie?
review:
I'm certain there must be some senior managers at Warner Bros who look at the success of the Marvel movies and wonder why they can't match it. And so they should - in Batman and Superman, DC have characters with more worldwide brand recognition than anyone in the Marvel Universe, including Spiderman. Part of the reason is that they don't seem to work at it - they don't seem to have anyone who is overseeing the whole franchise and guiding its direction. They do with the DC Universe TV shows, and they are doing a great job of universe building, but that is apparently a completely separate continuity.

This isn't a complete failure - it is better than Dark Knight Rises and Man of Steel, but there is still a lot wrong with it. Wonder Woman is great, and should have featured more prominently in the film - I assume she will be a major player in the Justice League movies. Lex Luthor wasn't bad, but channelled the Joker a bit too much at times. Henry Cavill is much better as Superman than he was in Man of Steel.

The film is way too long - it could have been 45 mins shorter and still told the story. The first hour and a half meanders and drops in and out of dream sequences without warning. And there are many plot points that don't make sense. Batman wants to kill Superman because he is too powerful and can just kill people if he feels like it, yet Batman kills dozens of people during the movie without any regrets. As other reviewers have pointed out, Lex gives Superman an hour to kill Batman or Martha Kent will die - that is more than enough time for Superman to scour both Metropolis and Gothan with his X-Ray vision to find where she is being held.

Superman is supposed to be super-intelligent as well as his other powers, yet it never occurred to him to give the kryptonite spear to the other super-powered person there - Wonder Woman? And it didn't occur to Wonder Woman to toss Superman's body back into space where it could get the full effect of solar radiation? After all, he recovered from a nuclear explosion as soon as he was exposed to sunlight.

And finally, the death of Clark Kent. It's not going to be hard to explain Superman coming back from the dead, and in the comics Clark was buried under rubble and presumed dead, so his resurrection was explainable. But in this film, Clark's body is on display and he has a very public funeral. I'm not sure how they will plausibly bring Clark back for the Justice League movie.

title: Meh
review:
Not as bad as some have made it out to be, but this film certainly has problems. I found it quite cerebral, but in a "trying too hard" sort of way. There are confusing and unnecessary scenes, particularly certain dream sequences that do little to enhance the plot, and the first hour moves very slowly. It does use this time to cover important plot points but it's delivered in a drab and dull manner for the most part.

Ben Affleck is excellent (possibly best batman ever?), as is Gal Gadot and most of the supporting cast, and I understand Henry Cavil is also in this movie, though he seems more like a CGI version of himself.

Despite being rated as PG-13, it's too subtle and high-minded for kids I suspect, and quite dark in places too. Still, it ends quite well (why couldn't it have been like that for the entire last hour!) and I don't hate it. It just wasn't all it could have been.

title: A movie with little respect for movie fans, original creators of Batman, Superman
review:
As a defiance against hyper-ventilating movie critics, I watched Batman v Superman Dawn of Justice yesterday evening. I like well-made superhero movies, and well-told stories of great sacrifices made for a greater cause like the Avengers, Captain America, Iron Man et all series.

Before I bought my movie ticket, I thought the critics panning the movie were crazy. Surely it cannot be that bad, I thought. But while I walked out after watching the movie in a near empty INOX theater, I had to stop myself telling the next lot of people (very few) waiting for the next show: "Don't waste your time." I even thought of sending back my movie ticket to the film makers and telling them: "Look, apparently you made $400 million already from this piece of work and so would you kindly refund my ticket money?" I felt cheated.

The first half of Batman v Superman was okay... I even thought I might like to come again and see the movie again. The second half is a disaster of epic proportions. It descended into a clumsy, confusing,annoying experience made worse with perhaps the most irritating, ridiculous chief movie villain in the history of big budget Hollywood movies. The fellow who played Lex Luthor and the fellow who directed him should not be allowed to continuing cheating paying movie goers.

The ending of the movie is even more ridiculous, exasperating - and I could a sense the few people in the cinema hall almost feeling confused, dazed while the credits started rolling: "what the hell is this movie about, or trying to say?"

Batman v Superman is a monster creation that is a murderous insult to the original creators of the characters Batman and Superman, to faithful comic book fans who cherished those iconic figures, and a slap in the face to those who think most movie critics are nuts.

Better to have let the guy who directed the Turkish Airlines 'Gotham City' advertisement to direct this movie. He would have done a better job.

title: It's not perfect, but what is?
review:
The first set of reviews that came out for Dawn of Justice (I'm refusing to call it Batman v Superman, cause it's anything but a versus movie, that title may as well be click-bait) were extremely positive, some calling it the greatest superhero movie ever made and "the bar" that every other superhero movie will be judged on. Then pretty much every major critic in the world... slated it.

I went to see it at midnight after reading both sets of reviews not sure what to expect and to be honest, I was satisfied. Granted, it isn't an amazing film and you can sort of see where the critics are coming from in certain aspects, but it's by no means a bad film.

We got some things we didn't need (ANOTHER Batman origin story and about 7 dream sequences too many) but I was happy with what I'd seen walking out. Ben Affleck was amazing as both Bruce Wayne and Batman, Jesse Eisenberg gave a fun and unpredictable portrayal of Lex Luthor, Jeremy Irons was brilliant as Alfred, and the rest of the cast (Cavill as Superman, Adams as Lois Lane, Gadot as Wonder Woman to name the highlights) all got at least a B- in my book.

The score was fine, not Zimmer's best work, but Junkie XL's inclusion seemed to slow him down slightly. Zack Snyder will (to some degree) deservedly get some stick for this movie, but at the same time there are many amazing shots in Dawn of Justice and whilst he's no Christopher Nolan, I didn't think he did too bad of a job. There's a lot of plot to follow and it can get hard at times to do so, but for every bad point this movie has, there's an equally good point to balance it out on the scale of determining whether this is a good or bad movie.

Advice to people about to go watch the movie: Don't let the reviews influence your opinion. Go into it with your own expectations and make of it what you will. If you dislike it, fair enough, but don't just dislike it to be part of the "Let's all hate Dawn of Justice" bandwagon.

title: LOVED IT - Will be Seeing it Multiple times...
review:
Let me begin by saying that I don't understand in the LEAST why the critics don't like this film because I not only love it but think it's one of the best superhero films.

One of the nice things about this film and a surprise given the genre, was the attention that was paid to the characterizations and how well these were executed. The actors were all in fine form. Ben Affleck does a great job as an older Batman. He is perfect as the surly, haunted, super vigilante who not only fights criminals but also exacts justice and inspires fear in anyone who crosses his path. Henry Cavill is terrific as a Superman who is committed to doing "good" in the world but that has to grapple with the realities of the collateral damage his confrontations sometimes cause and with a world in which some see him as a god, some as a hero and some as a dangerous alien. One thing that has disappointed me about the more modern crop of super hero films is how the movies tend to go from one action sequence to another with very few scenes showing the characters in their day to day lives or interacting with regular people – the type of scenes that allow a character to move beyond a caricature. This movie is long precisely because it incorporates scenes like these. We see Clark in scenes with Lois and his mother, talking about the issues he's grappling with – we see him arguing with Perry about what journalism should be. We see Bruce discussing with Alfred the path he's decided on with regards to Superman – we see him haunted by nightmares. We get to know these two characters not only as superheroes but as men who both want the same thing but take different approaches to get there.

The supporting characters are nicely fleshed out. Jesse Eisenberg has possibly more screen time than our heroes as he beautifully brings to life a Lex Luthor that is brilliant but deeply scarred and committed to destroying a Superman he perhaps sees as a surrogate for another powerful man he knew in his life, his father. Jeremy Irons as Alfred acts not only as Bruce's sounding board but also his behind-the-scenes partner and frequently, his conscience. Amy Adams is as usual, terrific, reprising her role as Lois Lane and thankfully participating in the story almost as much as the title characters. In MAN OF STEEL I didn't "feel" a lot of the chemistry between Lois and Superman. In BvsS, their relationship is arguably one of the best things in the film. The relationship is more mature now. They have known each other for a while now and you totally get the feeling that these two people know each other well, respect one another absolutely and have a love that has become bone deep. The sweetest and most touching moments in the film come from the interaction between these two.

Holly Hunter is back also as Senator Finch and she also elevates her character beyond a supportive role, giving us a gutsy, smart legislator who is committed to doing right by the people she represents. Laurence Fishburne, Diane Lane and Kevin Costner also reprise their roles as Perry and Clark's parents. Though they only have a few, short scenes, these are some of the better scenes in the film, allowing for that character development in Superman/Clark that makes for a much better film than what we usually get in the superhero genre.

And let me now get to one of the best things in the film – Wonder Woman! Wow. I am SOOOO looking forward to the WW film. Apart from being absolutely stunning, Gal has this exotic, Mediterranean look that makes her perfect for the role of a superhero born as an ancient Greek Amazon. The scene with the three of them standing side by side as they prepare to battle Doomsday is just absolutely EPIC. One thing which I personally appreciated is that though the action scenes/CGI are MASSIVE and will blow your mind, they are also – believable and staged in a way that honors the best of these characters without undermining them in any way. I have always been more of a Superman fan than a Batman fan and one thing I found myself fearing when I heard about the concept for this film is that I figured they were going to have to make Superman seem somewhat inept or weak in some way in order to make a confrontation between him and a human believable, gadgets and armor notwithstanding. Batman's suit of armor is cool but sorry, against a being that can move mountains and shoot fire from his eyes and can blow things to pieces, it just seemed a stretch for that to be what allows Batman to survive. Fortunately, I was very impressed with how the big fight between them was staged. It wasn't really the suit of armor that allows the fight to happen, it's Batman's strategic use of Kryptonite and this was very well done. The moment when the relationship goes from enemies to allies and Batman finally sees the hero behind the alien in Superman is one of the best in superhero films, wonderfully combining a moment of climactic action with one of climactic emotion and it's a terrific thing that it is Clark and Lois' relationship that makes this possible and the simple love the two men had for their mothers.

The ending is "super" emotional and it reminded me a LOT of another film I grew up loving – STAR TREK WRATH OF KHAN with that unforgettable moment of sacrifice when Spock says goodbye to Kirk and the crew of the Enterprise. The next installment in the series should be INCREDIBLE.

Don't let others dissuade you from giving this movie a shot.

title: Pleasantly surprised given the volume of negative reviews
review:
I really don't get the amount of negativity around this film. After 4 days of reading lots of reviews, I eventually managed to get to the cinema and was expecting to be as disappointed as many were describing. I am pleased to say that was not the case!

Admittedly, while the movie does have some faults I really enjoyed it and felt that most of the performances were really decent - Ben Affleck being a stand-out. It did jump about a bit from scene to scene but I didn't find it confusing or convoluted as some are describing and followed the story quite easily.

I wonder if some people are being negative because its the 'trendy' thing but for a movie about a fight between a flying all-powerful alien and a rich guy who dresses as a bat, I found it very entertaining.

title: Best superhero movie to date! No question
review:
Most people that go to see this exceptional movie, expect to see an marvel-esque action movie, with bright and funny characters. They expected a family movie. These people walk away disappointed, telling everyone how "bad and illogical" the movies plot is. Oh, the unknowing.

After seeing this movie 2 times, I was AMAZED by how Zack Snyder handled the storyline. Things happening off-screen, that people have to figure out for themselves for the plot to make sense. You have to listen to everything the characters say to catch all there is to know about the story. And there is A TON to discover.

For example: in this movie Batman actually murders bad guys! Many people were shocked, including me at first. But, after seeing the whole movie and thinking it over after wards, I had an idea why he did. The only clue we got is Robin's suit and one of Batman's lines. And it was enough for a comic-book fan to understand. And to be amazed.

The acting choices for the main characters are great: Ben Affleck not only redeemed himself after DD, but became my favorite batman of them all. Henry Caville as Superman: great. Gal Gadot: even more so.

I personally enjoyed the serious tone Snyder set for his movies. They don't feel like kids stories or anything. It feels mature, grim, engrossing. Just brilliant. Action scenes - that's what Snyder does better that anyone out there. Marvelous, pun intended.

My only complaint would be how Batman, the greatest detective, didn't see through Luthor's scheme. That was the only thing I didn't get on board with. Other than that - great movie for DC fans, good movie for anyone with a thinking brain. Anyone else can go home and re-watch Marvel's simpler comedic popcorn family films.

9 out of 10! A Must see!

title: Good only in pieces
review:
So I have finally seen Batman V Superman , the film which I was anticipating but was not having too much expectation.

So first the good part, Wonder Woman and Batman were awesome. Gal Gadot and Ben Affleck were awesome. Gal is a scene stealer , the real power house that Super Man could not be. The story is good.

Conclusion:

title: Better than any PG-13 movie Marvel has put out thus far
review:

title: Very fun, but it could have been better.
review:
***SPOILERS***

Batman v Superman: dawn of justice review:

title: Zack Snyder is shameful and 12 things that don't make sense in this nonsensical movie
review:
I want to start off by saying Ben Affleck did a fantastic job! It's a bad movie, to call it otherwise is an insult to the intelligence of the viewer and I love superman movies. Labeling the truth as criticism won't allow the future movies to get any better.

1) Bruce Wayne has a hallucination where he falls into a well and begins levitating while bats fly around him during one of his many hallucination. Batman kept having frequent hallucinations which was unnecessary and never explained.

2) Superman arrives in Africa to save Lois. Then people blame Superman for the terrorist in Africa shooting each other with bullets. I mention bullets here because why would Superman be blamed for thugs in the desert shooting each other but of course Zack Snyder doesn't use common sense and just adds random nonsense into this movie.

3) Jesse Eisenberg is a dork in this movie. I noticed he was wearing a suit jacket with a gorilla on his shirt. Why was he cast to be Lex Luthor. Throughout the movie I kept thinking he reminds me of the Joker. He came across as trying too hard to sound intelligent and just being an all around geek/dork/nerd. The last time we saw Lex Luthor in a Superman film, he was being played by Kevin Spacey. How can you go from a guy who plays Frank Underwood to Jessie Eisenberg.

4) I noticed both in Man of Steel and in this movie that Zack Snyder has an odd obsession with heaven, hell and God and devil which is stupid. In Man of Steel, Superman visits a church to receive guidance on whether or not to save the Earth from General Zod. Fast forward to this movie and Zack Snyder goes even further and compares Superman to God from heaven and then says Doomsday is the devil.

5) Superman saves a girl from a burning building, tugs an overturned boat, saves a family in a flooded home and Lois Lane in Africa. He flies above the US Capital building for a few seconds. Fights Batman for a few minutes and Doomsday for even less time. That's all we see of his power. WTF why is this a 2.5 hour movie and that is all we see of Superman flying or doing anything super at all! Why did you do this Zack Snyder? Why are you so bad at producing Superman movies?!

6) Perry White plays the token angry black man throughout the movie for absolutely no reason. I just could not understand why Laurence Fishburne would allow Zack Snyder to make him look like the stereotype angry black man throughout the entire movie. He reminded me of Samuel L. Jackson every time anyone (Clark Kent or Lois Lane) asked him even the most basic questions having to do with journalism or pursuing any story that seemed newsworthy.

7) Bruce Wayne/Batman falls asleep and has another hallucination with Superman, Superman troopers and something that looked like flying gargoyles from Darkseid. This is another bizarre and unexplained part of the movie that just feeds into Batman's unusual and pointless paranoia with Superman. Again why is Zack Snyder allowed to make this trash.

8) The Flash shows up at the end of another Batman hallucination to say "I'm too soon and you have to find us and that you've always been right about him (Superman)". I can only guess this has to do with a future Justice League movie but this is a guess because it's never explained or anything. What kind of movie has several scenes in it that are hallucinations and never explains or advances the plot at all.

9) Its 1 hour and 15 minutes into the movie and I look around the theatre and notice that nothing important has happened. I could have walked to the snack bar and would miss nothing at all. You can show up to this movie 1 hour late and you wouldn't be missing anything important at all! How can Zack Snyder sleep at night knowing he made this trash.

10) The fact that Superman gets beaten twice in the same movie is an abomination and blasphemous. I mean you're telling me that Batman and Doomsday both beat the hell out of Superman. Why is this happening to Superman. Henry Cavill, do you like being on your back and getting being beaten up that much? This is just atrocious. Everyone is kicking his ass. I mean I was suspicious of this in Man of Steel when Faora was beating on Superman but then in this movie both Batman and Doomsday treated Superman like a novice fighter. This film is just a disappointment to anyone who enjoys watching Superman triumph, you will not see that in this movie.

11) Superman getting shot with one kryptonite gas bomb from Batman was what I considered luck but then Batman shoots him twice with the same weapon and Superman stands there like a fool waiting for the Kryptonite gas to land in his face and smack him again. This was just too much to swallow for me. Zack Snyder is a fool and I mean this in every way imaginable. Zack Snyder should never be allowed anywhere or with anything involving Superman.

12) Lois Lane is the damsel in distress so many times in this movie it's absurd. Amy Adams played her girl needs guy to save her from everything stereotype to the max. It was just embarrassing and Amy Adams should have spoke up for herself. I've never seen a woman so helpless throughout a 2.5 hour movie before but what do you expect with a Zack Snyder movie. I'm done with this review, every time I think of this film it puts me in a bad mood!

title: simply the best comics book movie in a long time.
review:
When i read some of the negatives critics of this movie i sometime wonder if we've been watching the same movie, either they didn't understand the movie or were trying to nitpick details they didn't like because you know: the superman's cry at the end of MoS.

I can understand some comics fans not liking the realistic / philosophical approach to comics books character , some god-like but i for one wanted a realistic approach to a world with superpowered beings for a long time and this movie does it.

So simply put if you want to see the DC universe put in a reality check situation this is it, a comic book movie for Adult, a movie with fictional character that make you believe they could exists.

and even then, for a running time of 2h33 i did not once felt bored, it kept me entertained from start to end.

thumbs up Zack ! and everyone's involved.

title: Loved it !
review: I spent most of my childhood reading comic books and Batman V Superman where my two favourites , so when they announced they would feature together in a movie together for the first time my excitement, then on Thursday came the reviews along with a sense of dread that this film could possibly be a 2016 version of Batman and Robin I have never seen a film so tore apart by the critics so with a sense of trepidation I took my seat in the IMAX with my wife and friends none of whom are massive comic book fans and I have to say we all absolutely loved it !! The first third of the movie is a slow build but still has a few highlights esp our first introduction to the bat! This is the batman I know from the comics , Synder has captured the spirit of the batman perfectly in this film , there are a few scenes that could have been left out and made the film feel bloated a bit such as the batman origin story of his parents which we have seen done a million times but the positives far outweigh the negatives ,Henry Cavil has been slated as Superman for not being smiley or positive but I guess when your a super powered alien being and the world doesn't trust you it might affect your mood ! He is the perfect choice to play Superman looks wise and has a certain aura that you believe he is the man of steel.The fight scenes are amazing when batman and superman throw down it feels and looks straight out of Frank Millers Dark Knight and when they team up along with Wonder Woman it gets even better ! I wanted to to take note of audience reaction during the film and the whole audience was captivated by this film from start to finish as we all went through an exciting and sometimes emotional ride together.I always believe the sign of a good film is it stays with you after the credits roll and you discuss it analyse certain scenes and this movie has certainly done that to me my wife and friends , I don't know what the critics expected it from it and why they hate it so much but all I can say is my childhood heroes I feel for the first time have been portrayed the way I imagined them as a boy as I read through my comic books , and I am excited for Justice League and the rest of the DC universe to be fully realised on the silver screen ! Don't listen to the critics go and see it yourself.

title: Awesome with some silly issues
review:
I loved this movie! I loved this movie regardless of the plot and editing problems. Ben Affleck was an awesome surprise! I can't wait for that solo bat flick he directs. I sure do wish a better creative team was brought in to assist with the BvS screen play though, Yikes! This movie could have easily been perfect, but silly decisions derailed it.

How about Lex Luthor? I wasn't a huge fan of Eisenberg as Lex, but I still have hope for him. Instead of Lex making Doomsday, I wish that Lex turning the ship on triggered the ship to go into a damage control mode. The ship is totally wrecked right? Krypton is gone! Imagine if Doomsday was in some kind of Krypton prison pod floating around in the Phantom Zone. The PZ is so huge with cool different versions in the comics. The possibilities! Batman was even trapped there by the White Martians once. Doomsday has a cool story as well and was actually killed by The Radiant in the comics. His body was wrapped and shackled to prevent his spirit from escaping and he was shot into space because the murders he committed made him unworthy of a burial. Eventually, his casket crashed on Earth, but imagine if Lex turning on the ship forced him here. The ship doesn't know it's on Earth because it's all bashed up and protocol is to account for prisoners, especially when a non-Kryptonian is trying to access the ship. Of course Zod and his followers were freed from The PZ after Kryoton blew up, but Doomsday was kept under different conditions. The ship also shouldn't accept Lex trying to take control. The pod is brought to the ships location and ends up crashing near it and cracks. Lex flees and solar energy brings back Doomsday and he's mad....and is wearing his tattered pants....and not totally pants less.

How about the Superman v Batman fight? Have them fight without any outside instigation. Batman wants to kill Superman and Superman wants to stop Batman from what he's doing. They explained Batmans reasons very well in the movie, but Supermans reasons faded away and Lex was shoehorned in. The fight should end when they hear Doomsday stomping around. They need to come to a truce and fight the monster. He needs Batman to use the Kryptonite gas and spear. Superman shouldn't be able to go near anything Kryptonite. There should be a truce and no definite winner.

How about Doomsday? I think Batman should be more involved with using the Kryptonite against Doomsday. The fight ends with Superman taking Doomsday into space and not coming back. Doomsday even tore off Superman's cape while fighting him and that's the cliffhanger. Batman picking up Superman's cape and talking to Wonder Woman about assembling the Justice League. Wonder Woman was awesome in this, but I didn't like her saving Batman from Doomsday's face rays. It shouldn't have happened.

What about Martha Kent? I did not like this part with Superman's mom. It was the worst part for me. Superman cares so much for his mom, but risks letting Batman go save her. He's faster than a speeding bullet and saved Lois out of no where like three times in this movie. He would definitely go himself. I wish instead of this, Lex found out that Batman is Bruce Wayne after Batman took the big Kryptonite rock (which should have been filmed) and instead sends his goons to try to take Alfred. This could be happening when Batman is going back to get more Kryptonite weapons after the truce with Superman. In this scenario, we can see Alfred beat up a few goons, highlighting his awesomeness. Alfred can hide in some bat cave hiding place while still communicated with Batman as Batman runs over furious. We can still get that awesome fight scene, but relate to Batman better, because it's Alfred.

I still loved it!

8/10

title: A very average movie, battle of gladiators is stale.
review:
Superhero movies are usually fun to watch. The whole notion of hero being is:- Superpower/Super-will, morality issues, mindset for acting as vigilante.

This movie is never clear at least on latter two points. Bit confusing and the dream sequences are too often. Problem with the movie is that it tries too hard to be a serious movie. Zack Snyder is good with visual parts of movie but the execution of story is laggard. All the tantrums while reaching to that climax of battle between two heroes produces very appalling result when the showdown actually takes place audience already seems bored. title: There are a LOT of things to say about this movie...

I felt that part really forced and unnecessary, besides, I don't dislike the new flash but I don't know how this will work out since he is a different actor than Grant Gustin. -Lois Lane. Most. -Alfred. I loved Alfred.

There are more points that I liked/disliked about this movie, but this is all I can point out without spoilers.

Finally, I just want to add that this is the second DC movie that I've ever watched and I can see myself watching more of DC movies!

title: An excellent movie that elevates the superhero genre.
review:
Batman v Superman might not be for the casual moviegoer. It might not even be for all the fans, and it is obviously not for the critics. Personally, I loved this movie though. It is a new approach to several of the DC Comics characters, while still remaining true to their core. As an avid DC reader I can appreciate the new take on all of these characters. There is plenty of foreshadowing for things to come within this universe.

The plot is fairly simple but the story behind it is quite complex and thought-provoking. It deals with the morality, politics, spirituality, and acceptance of superheroes in the modern age. Zach Snyder has crafted a film that offers a revealing look at how our world might react to a seemingly all powerful being as well as a brutal vigilante.

The acting in the movie is brilliant. Jesse Eisenberg makes for a wonderful, if non-traditional, Lex Luthor. Ben Affleck is the best Batman ever seen on film, which is saying something because my favorite movie is The Dark Knight. He plays Bruce Wayne exceedingly well also. Henry Cavill does an excellent job portraying Clark and Superman and Amy Adams really shines as Lois Lane. Laurence Fishburne makes an excellent Perry White and Jeremy Irons is an outstanding Alfred. The one actor who truly steals the show though is Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman/Diana Prince. Charming and Mysterious is the name of the game when it comes to her. All in all a wonderful cast.

Now let's talk filmography. Snyder is truly a wizard at the visual aspect of a film. The film is a complete visual spectacle to be sure. The action sequences are intense, well-choreographed, lengthy, and very well filmed. You really believe that a man can fly and another can take on an army. The scenes that aren't action packed are beautifully filmed, especially one near the very beginning. If you enjoyed the introduction in The Dark Knight, then you're in for a treat at this movie.

Overall, the movie surpassed every expectation I had, which I had built up over two and a half years of anticipation. This is easily one of my top five favorite films of all time. That is not to say that it isn't without its faults. But the story is amazing, the character development is wonderful, and the ending is beautiful. It truly elevates the superhero genre and Zach Snyder and his cast and crew should be highly praised for the masterpiece they have unveiled.

title: Batman V Superman Dawn of Justice AKA superhero movie of the year (in my opinion)
review: Right. So. Let's get into this. Honestly. This is the best superhero movie I've ever seen. That is my honest opinion. I don't understand the hate this movie is getting ,I mean, WTF rotten tomatoes 29%!? THIS MOVIE WAS FANTASTIC! Watch the movie, everything is good.

title: Ben ~ The Definitive Batman - Just Ignore Critics
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a step up which would eventually lead to Justice League. Seeing the iconic trinity of DC sharing the silver screen itself was worth the wait. Keeping the tone of the story grim & dark, Zack Snyder has made it very similar to his earlier take on Alan Moore's legendary graphic novel Watchmen. Christopher Nolan's Batman trilogy has been one of the best on screen adaptation of superhero eccentric but it was not entirely faithful to comic book genre. Much of the story was reformed for grounding it to realism so that main stream audience could relate under the pretext of modern day extremism.

Plot: The new chapter in this story arc introduces us to the legacy of Bruce Wayne's origin as Batman in a quick snippet. Fast track eighteen months from the aftermath of Man of Steel, we see a world with divided opinions on the existence of Superman; while some sees him as a savior others question his very presence, leading to countless debates at political & social circuits. As the world tries to cope in understanding what sort of hero it truly needs, LexCorp's business magnate Lex Luthor manipulates Superman by pitting him against Gotham's very own vigilante Batman for nefarious reasons.

This movie sets the premise for the upcoming Justice League, though at times it felt that it could have been addressed more coherently. General audience not familiar with the source material may have some issues as too many ester eggs & reference to league has been laid down. Some shortcomings in the story is however rewarded with startling visuals. Snyder's hallmark is evident in some of the scenes which are simply awe inspiring. The plot has its genesis from two of the iconic graphic novels ever written The Dark Knight Returns & The Death of Superman. Hans Zimmer & Junkie XL soundtrack composition has a different feel, something which we are not used to. It nets well with the movie however, as a standalone track there is crave for more lucid touch.

Castings bring forth some fresh faces to the existing troupe, Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman, Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. With new rules set in this DC Extended Universe, Ben Affleck not only excels as Bruce Wayne but he is righteously the definitive Batman ever to put up on big screen. Even with less screen time, Gal Gadot shines as the Amazon Warrior Wonder Woman during her climactic battle with Doomsday. Jesse Eisenberg's take on narcissistic Lex Luthor was quite different than what we have read in comic books, though the reason for his psychotic obsession for destroying Superman was kept fuzzy, I hope when the ultimate extended R version gets released for home it would give some more insight behind his motivation.

Final Verdict: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a pure comic book movie; it's not chef-d'oeuvre but a commendable boost to accelerate the much awaited Justice League. Watch this to institute your own opinion.

Way to go DC!!

title: Modern Age Depiction of the World's Finest Superheroes
review: This movie was probably the most polarizing superhero movie of this decade. Forget Marvel vs. DC fanboys, even DC loyalists are finding it hard to ascertain the level of the movie. Bear in mind, I personally enjoyed this movie very much and this might not be the case with other viewers as everyone has their own perspective of the MOST legendary superheroes of all time. Obviously, not everyone will be satisfied. Right from the start, we get thrown in the action as the movie continues right off where Man Of Steel ended. And since a batman movie is not complete without a little homage to his childhood tragedy, we get a rebooted taste of that as well. Not even one moment is of slow pace and the audience will be just glued to the edge of their seats (guaranteed). Oh the acting. You will rarely find the caliber of performances this movie comprises. Special points go to Henry Cavill, who was definitely faced with a challenge with role of donning the capes. His facial expressions are extremely well played. The looks of shock and despair are done excellently by him (If you don't believe it, notice his expressions of betrayal and confusion when the Courtroom explodes or how he is surprised when Batman blocks his attack for the 1st time) It boasted in the trailers and it delivered. Eventually the long-awaited fight ensues. Zack Snyder has delivered the best (bar none) 1 on 1 superhero clash. He goes all-out and delivers the best fight of the year hands down. Eventually the villain turns out to be, you guessed it (yes YOU), Lexy-boy-Luthor. Overall, the final boss is revealed and a great power struggle ensues. The fight is one of the best cinematic experiences of the decade. If you went and expected shallow fights with mindless destruction, weak and characterless enemies, with innumerable tired jokes & one-liners (Im referring to you, AVENGERS!!!), you will be thoroughly disappointed. The movie is way too serious and outright destroys any Avengers film made so far. Oh and the league is soon to be founded.

title: Could've been better
review:
So, I just got the opportunity to watch the movie Batman v superman, and i must say, i was a wee bit disappointed, because, when the movie was announced three years ago, i imploded with excitement. It built such a huge hype around it that it couldn't live up to the hype. Let's talk about the plot, it was a little here and there, but on the whole not the worst plot for a movie, and despite being a tad too long, i enjoyed the movie.

Let us talk about the performances of the actors, Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman was amazing. Batman was brutal, strong, scary. everything he was supposed to be. Although my favorite Batman will always be Bale, Affleck was amazing.

Henry Cavil as superman was pretty good too.

Gal Gadot as wonder woman literally made me scream. i loved every scene she was in! Jeremy Irons as Alfred was something new; as i was pretty used to Michael cane. but he did a wonderful job.

All in all, BvS was a pretty good movie; but was it good enough??

title: Potential for great follow ups!!
review: Well at least they got the whole Doomsday character thing out of the way. There will be no more queries as to why Superman cannot be killed. He was! But we all know, like Arnold, he'll be back!! Jessie Eisenberg is amazing as Lex Luthor. Hopefully in the follow ups we can see the Justice League take on Lex, with the Joker. A very fun film from beginning to end. Ben's Batman is very unique as opposed to previous portrayals. He actually brands the baddies. I've read a lot of negative reviews on this film, but it was, IMO very entertaining and it sets up some very intriguing sequels. Suicide Squad will introduce us to the new Joker as well as a host of other villains the Justice League can tackle.

title: Absolutely fantastic movie!
review:
I rated this film ten. I realize that may be a little bit high because I only watched it once and I may have a different opinion upon the second viewing but considering I went in expecting to be disappointed, I'm saying that I really loved it.

The more I think about it, and I've had quite a bit of time to think of it, while I was working last night I was thinking about it, and I can honestly say that the more I do think about it, the more I come to the realization that it was an awesome movie.

A film like this has the potential to literally sink the Titanic. (yes that was a reference to the movie which to my knowledge is still the number one box office grossing film of all time) The reason I say this is because it's the first live action film to portray two of the most popular superheroes of all time. Even if the movie was bad it had high potential and it no doubt would have still been a success, just because of that.

But I was just happy it was a great movie. I was skeptical about Jesse Eisenberg at first as Lex Luthor, and the trailers really sucked for the movie, but after watching the full product I can honestly say I loved it. Naturally I might change my mind later, as it really all depends if the movie is something I'd watch several times or not. But anyway, I want to see it again, and I loved Ben Affleck as Batman. I'm totally pro-Batfleck. Also, Superman is much more of a superhero now, and Lois, who was somewhat one dimensional in "Man of Steel," is actually very interesting in this film. And of course you already knew Doomsday was in it if you saw the trailer. When he and Superman fight to the death it is one of the most epic scenes in a superhero film. I also thought the same of the scene where Superman begs Batman to save Martha, which coincidentally is also Bruce Wayne's mother's name.

Check it out, it rocks, I could go on forever, but I'm cutting off right there. Oh yeah, and I loved Alfred in this too. Check it out, like I said, I thought I'd be disappointed with all the negative reviews, just don't listen to them. I really don't understand the negative reviews, because the film just rocked to me. I'll have to watch it again though, and I hope I still love it after that.

title: Don't Be Influenced by Negative Press Reviews
review:
I recently watched this film on a late night showing; so late in-fact that I had the center-cinema-sweet-spot with nobody surrounding me.

Waiting for this films release; the mere concept of a Batman/Superman shake-up was but a comic book fanboy dream; yet there I was waiting through what seemed to be 30 minutes of ad-trailers.

I left the cinema slowly nodding my head, corner lips aimed down with a fixated certainty in my eye; 'that was a damn good film'.

That doesn't mean to say I didn't have issues with it, because I did - at the end of the day anyone familiar with the universe and Graphic Novels or Animation universe - this film didn't stick to a predetermined script. However we knew this, coming out of Man of Steel with the early introduction of General Zod and his death.

Moving on to the issues then (minor plot spoilers ahead); - Batman The Detective; not so much when watching this film, the genius that knows everything about his enemy, missed key facts about our red-capped friend... Even I know who Martha is...

  • Superman/Doomsday; I won't overly expand on this for those who are yet to see. This was summarised in 30 minutes when in actual fact this story line should have stretched out at least one full standalone Superman film.


  • Batman/Murderer; is seen killing and snapping necks in one scene. Now this was only really brought to my attention after the film (possibly due to me floating in a DC Universe bubble). The closest I thought Batman went to killing was the Bat-branding we saw in this film which I thought added a dark story behind this old seasoned Batman. Unless circumstances changed when he was tasked with saving Martha Kent... Does this fit in with what happened after the 'Flash'back? - Death of Clark Kent; Need I say more? Not sure what a Superman looks like without his alter-ego. This can be corrected but it won't be in a conventional DC Universe style - slight uncertainty here.


Some positive/exciting notes; - 'Flash'back. The sequence that saw the Flash breaking through time and space to message Batman, 'Protect Lois, she is the key'. Very 'Injustice: Gods Among Us' right!? - Elseworlds-type approach?. Injustice: Gods Among Us showed a completely different story that got us all pretty gripped; the idea of Superman being bad was an interesting concept but never quite looked at in this brutal light. The glimpse of this in Batman v Superman was nice to see, I also think this explains the direction of the DC Cinematic Universe. Content from some of the best stories are being pulled into one - the Doomsday Summary, Death of Clark Kent, Introduction of the JLA (Characters) and the 'Flash'back. I would love to see a Flashpoint Paradox that incorporated the scene we saw in this film, could it be that a different inter-dimensional Batman was part of the plan to correct the future turn-out of events? Could a JLA Flashpoint Paradox film show what 'could have happened?'.

This film throws a lot of content at you; there's a lot of detail and a lot of questions to be answered. If these questions are answered in the other individual JLA films then some could be missing the point in this film...

We have just jumped into the future without a saddle and find ourselves unsure of what we're looking at.

Solid film; worth a watch but don't rock up thinking you're going to see what you've read in a book as we're being thrown a slightly different take; much like Injustice: Gods Among Us.

It's worth noting that Affleck's performance was very good. Y'know haters gonna hate!

One of the most endearing qualities about Clark Kent is how nerdy and salt of the earth that he is and Superman as the romantic idea of a hero with few flaws, someone we would all aspire to be - he was never "one of us" in the best of ways. What is interesting about stripping this beloved character of the qualities that make him who he is and make him a (physically) nearly invulnerable version of the most pathetic of us? We already have Hancock for that and at least he was funny.

The only character this movie got (maybe 80%) right was Batman and Affleck made a good Batman, hopefully he'll be given power to influence the next few films as he is an excellent writer, storyteller and director.

I hope Jesse Eisenberg quits acting so we can get a good Lex Luther in the reboots - his take on Lex was basically an evil Mark Zuckerberg and LexCorp was basically evil Google.

Gal Gadot did an acceptable job with Diana Prince and her Wonder Woman was pretty good, much better than I expected.

There was not one single thread that could be called coherent or consistent in this garbage of a movie. After Snyder and Goyer completely mangled the Jonathan Kent character in MoS with him teaching a young Clark to basically be a selfish prick that should never help anyone as to not expose who he was, taking it to the point of making Clark watch him die from the easily salvable tornado riding - but for some reason in this movie, Superman says he is doing what his Pa'Kent would have wanted him to do. What? We then have Batman spend the entire movie figuring out how to kill Supes and making the weapons to do so only to just suddenly change his mind in the middle of the fight because... reasons.

A glimmer of hope (pipe dream actually):

Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Lauren Cohen are Thomas and Martha Wayne. There's also a (probably not) dream sequence where The Flash warns Bruce Wayne of something that is never made clear. This could set up a live action version of the Flashpoint Paradox animated film which I think Snyder could actually pull off as that adaptation is as dark and "gritty" as he's trying to make the DCFU.Morgan would make a wonderful older Thomas Wayne/Batman for that story and I would love to see Lauren Cohen take a crack at that alternate reality's version of Joker.

Do not trust any review on here that even alludes to this being a "good" movie. No one with a shred of honesty would call this anything better than mediocre.

title: A modern comic book as film; not a film reflecting a comic book
review:
It is very true to the DC comics of the last 20 to 30 years on almost everything, mainly the storytelling style and elements. I can understand why the critics didn't like it, most didn't understand why certain things were happening because the movie didn't waste time with exposition (a really good example probably being Doomsday and how he works). Some probably wouldn't even enjoy the comics this pulls from, and that is fine. I think it is also very obvious that some of the elements used for the dream sequences are going to actually be event plot points in future movies to tie them closely together, in the same way comic books do.

So sure, as a film for someone that doesn't care about the comics or just doesn't know them well, they could hate watching the movie and be left very confused. That's fine. The studio let Synder make a movie for the fans of the comics, which is what he has been saying he wanted to do all along. It certainly wasn't made in the Hollywood style so many critics seem to be asking for with all the cheap jokes and a tightly packaged happy ending for everyone involved. This isn't the 1978 Superman, and it certainly isn't the 1989 Batman. I understood what I was watching and enjoyed it. It is a modern comic book as film, not a film reflecting a comic book franchise's characters.

title: Amazing action and great iconic moments all pulled together with a solid story and bad storytelling (SPOILERS)
review: This movie was good. It is not terrible and it is not amazing. I will just start by saying that Ben Affleck as batman was the best thing in the movie. He was brutal, very dark, and almost scary. It is hard to tell in some parts but I'm pretty sure he killed some people. Henry Cavill was great as superman. Probably better than he was in Man of steel. Gal Gadot was amazing. She was the perfect pick for wonder women. Even though she did not show up much in the movie it was awesome when she did. Jeramy Irons as Alfred and pretty much every other supporting cast member was good. Jessie Eisenburg as Lex Luther was my main fear and he was just really weird and didn't fit Lex Luther. The story was overall good except at the beginning it was sloppy and confusing. Pacing was also a little weird and it seemed pretty rushed. Some people say this movie was overlong but it really was not. It was just packed with stuff way too much so it made it hard to follow the story. It should have been split into 2 movies. One movie being actual batman fighting superman. The other being the doomsday part and setting up for the justice league. Some of the storytelling was really terrible and there are a couple bad plot holes and random side-plots that lead to nowhere. There a couple parts where I think its going in a direction and it changes course quickly. One other problem was some things would get really confusing if you were not a DC fan. People are hating on the actual batman v superman fight being too short and the name being false marketing but what do you expect like a 2 hour long fight. I think 8 minutes is a decently long fight and the lead-up to the fight was amazing. This movie had some of the best action I have ever seen in a superhero movie. The actual batman v superman fight was amazing and some batman scenes left your jaw dropping. Also the fight with doomsday and wonder women was personally the best superhero movie fight scene ever made. People and critics are also complaining about the movie being too dark. I think it is good that it is not like the Avengers, it is much darker and more violent. Marvel fan-boys are just complaining that not all superhero movies are fun. Usually the comics were very dark also so I like how Zack Snyder stayed true to the comics. People were also complaining about the overuse of CGI but I think it worked well because the CGI was never bad and how do you expect someone to make doomsday without using CGI. Its just not possible. The soundtrack was also amazing. Each of the main characters(Batman, superman, Lex Luther, Wonder Women) had their own theme which I liked. The film was also very emotional at parts and very sad. People also have problems with too many dream sequences but I think it is a perfect way of showing Bruce Wayne being mentally unstable and venturing into his dark mind. It also tied in with Man of steel perfectly and set up the Justice league perfectly. In conclusion I have no idea why this movie is getting such bad reviews. Don't listen to the critics because this movie was very good. It is definitely a lot to take in and it has its problems but as a whole it is a epic blockbuster that you will want to see on a huge screen and just not pay attention to the story. I am also looking foreword to the rest of the DC cinematic universe.

title: given the gravity of the occasion it should've been a lot more fun
review: Second installment in the new 'DCEU' is the long anticipated matchup between comic goliaths Clark Kent, aka Superman, and Bruce Wayne, aka Batman.
