Dark, grim comic book adaptation succeeds at bringing the two iconic superheroes to the big screen, but strips away all traces of humor and humanity, can't seem to decide which story it wants to tell, and ends in anticlimactic fashion. Not only that, but the action scenes are presented with such bombastic overkill that they fail to generate any real tension or excitement. Affleck and Cavill carry their weight admirably, but there isn't much in the way of character arc or development, and a woefully miscast Eisenberg certainly can't fill the shoes of Hackman or Spacey as Lex Luthor. Delivers on its promise, but a showdown of this proportion deserved a much better script. **

title: Made for the fans
review: After marinating on it for a night, I think I can finally write a review for Batman v Superman. Let me preface by talking about the one major problem I had with the movie, Batman killing. At first this annoyed me because the Batman I grew up with would never directly take a life, but after giving it some thought, I've come to terms with it. Why would criminals who deal in extremes respond to anything less than extreme measures? If Batman kills then the best case scenario for a criminal in his sights is to be hospitalized, and that's scary. Get in his way and you might just lose your life. Anyways enough on that one aspect of one character, let's move on. The acting in the film was superb. Cavill is the definitive Superman. Gadot was exceptional in her limited screen time. Eisenberg's Luther was very much the string pulling, mad scientist who becomes obsessed with Superman, and his long-winded speeches were quite enjoyable. Irons might just be my favorite on-screen Alfred, and while I've covered an aspect of Batman, Affleck's portrayal overall was phenomenal. There are other fantastic performances from the rest of the supporting cast, but I'll suffice to say that all performances range from good to fantastic. The acting was not the only highlight of the film though. Arguably the two greatest elements in the film are the cinematography and the score. The score was exactly what you'd expect from a collaboration between Hans Zimmer (The Dark Knight Trilogy, The Lion King, Interstellar) and JunkieXL (Mad Max: Fury Road): epic. It was operatic, emotional, and bombastic. Every piece of music has become an instant favorite of mine, and this is the only soundtrack that I can and have listened to all the way through multiple times. The cinematography in the film is equally as beautiful. Every shot from the cold opening (now my new favorite from any film) to the Trinity preparing for battle was a work of art. Many of the shots were ripped straight from the comics, and the fight sequences will go down as some of the greatest ever brought to the silver screen. Now it may seem like I don't have any negatives, but I do have a gripe. That gripe would be the editing. Some of the choices just felt a bit strange. For example, a scene might cut away abruptly, one might be where it probably shouldn't, and there was at least one instance where it felt a scene was missing. However due to the fact that a director's cut has already been announced and that Snyder's director's cuts are very good, I'm sure most of these issues will be fixed. For now though, they are flaws. Now onto the writing. Overall the writing was solid. The dialogue felt crisp and you can definitely tell that Terrio reworked a lot of it for the better when he took over. A surprising amount of humor was present (though it never felt out of place like many Marvel films) and it worked quite well. I can't remember a single joke that didn't land. Another huge positive was that many lines were straight from The Dark Knight Returns. I couldn't help but mouth those lines (with a huge smile on my face) with the movie every time one was used. Another element of the movie that borrowed from the comics was the plot. Two comics to be precise: The Dark Knight Returns and another equally famous story. For the sake of limiting the spoilers in this review I won't mention the second. The movie balances both of these stories well and the transition to the second, while bashed by many critics, I thought was done well. Ultimately the movie spends most of the first half building up to the climax of both of these stories, and then letting both play out one after the other in one epic third act. The build up and philosophical speeches of the first half may be too slow for some, and the massively epic conclusion might be too bombastic for others, but ultimately it worked out perfectly for me. I'm probably a bit biased in my opinion on this film, but that's because of how important it has been to me. It isn't just the first ever film featuring my two favorite characters, or the first film to feature the Trinity. It was announced back in my Freshman year of high school, and I've been following it ever since. It was delayed multiple times, had many strange casting decisions, and many thought it would never come out. Now that it has, I couldn't be happier with it. Ultimately though, I'd highly recommend that everyone sees this film. The critics might not like it, but those are also the same people who gave Sharknado almost a 90%. Form your own opinion, and don't just rely on the opinions of others.

title: A darker, more mature era for comic book films. A must see.
review:
In 2007 "I am legend" had an Easter egg, a batman/superman logo on a billboard, ever since that tease I've had a thirst to see those 2 on the big screen in an epic adventure... that thirst has been quenched.

BVS surpassed its predecessor "Man of steel" in every way imaginable. The acting was superb, the fighting scenes were intense, hardcore and choreographed as well as you'd expect from a Zack Snyder film (which is to say amazing). The story drew itself out a bit but still manages to keep you entertained or at the very least intrigued. This is no surprise to anyone who has seen Snyder's previous films, "Watchmen" in particular. It's similar to watchmen, bringing in politics and different point of views on super heroes from the perspective of us normal folk, the government, other super heroes and of course the villain.

BVS takes itself serious, it has a few laughs but to be absolutely clear it is far from Disney's MCU. If you walk in looking forward to the stereotypical action-comedy adventure, predictable, fun, bright and optimistic comic book movie you're going to be disappointed. Prepare yourselves before you walk in, this is a action-drama adventure, its dark, gritty and as violent as a PG-13 rating allows. It paves the way for WB's DCU, and they're new take on a more mature comic book movie-verse, and it does it wonderfully. Showing their JLA team members with out diverting itself from the story and also getting us comic fans excited about the next step of this universe.

As for the members that were in the spotlight, they were fantastic. Ben Affleck as an older, war-weary Bruce Wayne aka Batman was (to my surprise) amazing. This Batman fought, not just using his elbows (looking at you Christian Bale) but every inch of his bulked up, batman-like body. Before when i mentioned the intense fighting scenes i was referring to him. Henry Cavill, a confused by internal conflicts Clark Kent aka Superman does his part as well as he did in MOS, also my favorite Superman. Gal Gadot's performance as the mysterious wonder woman truly was one of the best parts of this movie. Not much time on screen as wonder woman which is fine since the movie isn't called BVSVW, but when she finally showed up the crowed applauded. Jesse Eisenber did a good part playing an eccentric Lex Luthor who's motives weren't completely revealed but seeing as how he's crazy that's OK. Not my favorite depiction of Lex but Jesse did his part and came through acting wise (another surprise). Jeremy irons plays Alfred just as good as Micheal Caine though its a different depiction of him.

The plot does a good job of introducing all of these characters and an even better job and pitting these 2 heroes against each other, and any critic who says otherwise must've missed the first half hour of the movie or was simply A.D.Ding his way through this 2 and half hour film. As for the Batman vs Superman actual duel it was awesome to see these 2 iconic characters go head to head and hold nothing back, brawn vs brains, god vs man, dark vs light.

Overall i'd say this is a must see, 8.8/10. Even the slow parts kept me intrigued, great acting and action and it managed to pave the way for DCU perfectly. I cant wait for the next Zack Snyders DC film JLA!!!

title: Don't expect too much out of the plot, just appreciate that Batman and Superman fought
review: I'd like to start off by saying I'm no professional critic so please excuse my writing skills. Batman is my #1 hero, and I admit that this movie has a lot of flaws, however, I don't think the super low scores that websites like rotten tomatoes gave this movie is very deserving (mind you, rotten tomato is a website that gave Arrow season 3 100% and Sharknado an 82%). The general consensus amongst critics of this movie is the plot/story and I totally agree, the subplot of the first half of the movie seems kind of wasted and is never really addressed again once the action starts rolling, the pacing was decent, the story seems to struggle with trying to make Louis Lane relevant later on, and trying to cram in the introduction of the Justice League members. A lot of people don't like Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor but I didn't mind him that much, he fulfilled his purpose in the story and for that I can look past the goofy/insane Luthor character. Since I'm a Batman fan, I was very pleased with Ben Affleck, hell, I think he did a phenomenal job playing Bruce Wayne, and finally seeing Batman fight like the Arkham games was just heaven. I feel like Superman didn't change much from Man of Steel, his morals are still the same, but Wonder Woman and her heroine entrance was complete work of art, the whole theater cheered when she appeared. The fight batman v superman fight was amazing and do was the doomsday fight (yeah sucks that the trailer spoiled him as a surprise but hey, it was good nonetheless). Despite the flaws of this movie, I still had one hell of an experience seeing the DC Trinity on the big screen for the first time. This movie did not surpass my hype but it did not let me down either. That's what you have to keep in mind when reading these reviews from "professional" critics, because they try their best to not be biased and analyze everything objectively down to the smallest details. They pick apart what little they can find and they don't take into consideration the hard work that was put into the movie and that perhaps movies like these are catered towards a certain audience, they always write their reviews with the mindset that everybody watching this movie is the same as they are. For me, Batman v Superman was fan service and a lengthy set up towards the justice league, hell, it's right in the title. That's why I can overlook these flaws in the story and appreciate the fact that Batman and Superman fought and Wonder Woman finally have a good cinematic debut.

title: Don't listen to the critics

You will be disappointed if you were expecting a full-on brawl, but if you go in with an open mind, you're in for a really good time. Only reason I'm not giving it a 10 is because it was pretty predictable.

title: Don't listen to critics! I had a blast and I'm sure most fans did too!
review: I gotta admit I was blown away by the movie and Seeing Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman on the big screen was great! Ben Affleck is the best Batman in a live-action film! This was filled with many Easter Eggs for the fans! It's a great introduction to the DC Cinematic Universe! It wasn't perfect, but heck... how often is a movie ever perfect? It was an amazing experience that I've waited so long for! I'm looking forward to what's next for the DCCU. I loved all the dream sequences and it shows what we really could be getting. The Cameos had me on the edge of my seat (Especially the Flash Cameo). I will admit that some teases of a Justice League were felt forced and not necessary. I loved the final fight between Bats, Supes and Wonder Woman vs. Doomsday! I was not impressed by his appearance to begin with but he actually evolved like he was supposed to and I'm 100% sure he isn't dead. (Meaning he will become immune to Kryptonite) Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice was overall a fresh start to the DCCU and I have a feeling it will only get better!

title: Like the animated series brought to life!!!
review:
Anybody who's knows what they are talking about when it comes to the DC Universe knows that the Animated Universe got it right. This film steps toward that direction.

Most obviously the Multiverse scenes were some of the films most unique visually and perfectly mysterious. Clearly Darkseid is what is coming! Which is good considering Thanos, the Darkseid ripoff looks more like Josh Brolin, and not in a good way, so let's hope they get him right, which knowing Zach Snyder, he'll get that visual correct. Because he pays attention!

Onto the film. I'm going to say this. As a 'film', it is jumpy. And if you don't know anything about the DCU, you are absolutely going to be confused sometimes. But that's not all bad, there's decades worth of fulfilling comics and animated cartoons waiting for you to read and watch. This one is for the fans. Long overdue if you ask me!

Ben Affleck is Batman. There, I said it. I read an amazing review on how the animated Batman was the best because of the fact that he was a detective, and actually maneuvered in the suit as there were no restrictions. Well those days are over. Affleck is the detective, and the Batman we've seen in the comics and the series. Next question.

Superman. Just yes. He flicked Batman through a friggin wall. Talk about satisfying! The main complaint I always hear is that he's too powerful. Well someone's got to be at the top of the pyramid, and you all got your wish. He's dead. Or is he? I never liked Doomsday until this. This was a perfect adaption of that arc.

If you missed all the visual tributes, you are just blind. So much Frank Miller and original Superman shots. Stuff I never thought I'd see on the big screen. Also Clark getting in the tub with Lois to, you know. That was a nice realistic touch.

Wonder Woman. Only thought here is, why did she not fly? Otherwise, just thank you.

Lex. Yes again! Jesse did a great job at being evil Jesse. He was purely maniacal!

Complaints. I have just 3. First, the senator, and the guy with no legs had too many scenes that went literally kaboom! Second was that there were too many shaky cam moments and close ups. Not enough atmospheric shots. Third the Flash and Aquaman parts just should've had better moments. Cyborg was on par.

All and all, as a DC fan, you really couldn't ask for more. As a film fan, just ignore the bad reviews, they aren't supposed to 'get it', they have Disney for that. Thank you sincerely for making turning shitty year around for me! You all give me hope!

I just hope they can bring Young Justice back now too!!

title: B v S Dawn of Justice...EPIC, exceeding expectations!!!
review:
This movie was much better than expected. Great actors, Great story...kept you wanting more to the very last moment.

The movie trailers had only touched upon some of the movie highlights, but there is so much more to this well thought out, well written and produced movie! Each of the actors were on their game throughout the entire movie. The storyline was intense and extremely entertaining...much more please! Will certainly see this movie more than once...looking forward to the 3D Bluray release!

That being said, this movie had great moments that took me through many phases of emotions from happy, sad, excited, worried, angry and joyous! The casting gelled and was able to create a movie about Herod and villains that captured my imagination and never let go! The action was intense as expected, but it was the private moments and intelligent storyline that satisfied and kept me wanting to see more. Hats off to HC, BA GG and the supporting cast for the creation of an epic movie that will continue to entertain for many years to come!!! Bring on many more DC movies similar to this quality and entertainment level and I'll be very happy!!

title: This isn't Marvel. Don't expect it and you'll be fine.
review:
I don't really understand most of the reviews. Was the movie perfect? No. But I found it very enjoyable, worth the money, and I would see it again. Some of the critics are complaining about the level of destruction, but if you look at their reviews for Age of Ultron (which has a whole city flying into the stratosphere) you will find that they don't seem to mind it in Marvel movies.

DC is going in a different direction. Their tone is much more in line with Marvel's Netflix shows than their movies. People love Marvel's movies, the way the dialogue is written, the humor. This movie has none of that, and I think people are disappointed because they wanted that kind of writing for this movie.

The DC Movieverse is built on the reality that thousands, perhaps tens of thousands, of people died during the events of Man of Steel, something that the MCU hasn't completely acknowledged outside of their Netflix shows.

It's hard to write Tony Stark making a Spider-Man underwear joke when you just moments before talked about all the dead people.

So, this is what I will say. If you love Marvel movies because of their style and humor, be well aware that you will find none of that here. But if you go into this flick without preconceptions based on other franchises, you may walk out with your new favorite comic book movie, or at least one you are damn happy you saw.

title: A Little Sloppy at Times, but One of the Greatest Ensemble Superhero Movies Ever Made
review:
NON SPOILER: Beautiful cinematography, some of the best fight sequences in the business, and a surprising amount of heartfelt moments.

Ben Affleck's Batman is perfect. The truest version of the character ever projected on the silver screen.

Henry Cavill's Superman has improved, but still has some room to grow.

Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman is mesmerizing. I thought she was going to be the weakest character in this movie. I am so glad I was wrong.

Jesse Eisenberg is a little odd at first, but really grows into Lex Luthor.

You might think you have seen the entire movie if you've watched all the trailers. You haven't. While the marketing team could have played their hand a little better, this is still an amazing movie.

If you find you're having a lot of issues with this film, know that it is a comic book before it is a movie and as such it suffers some of the same problems comics do. This is truly refreshing though, to see a film that is not pandering to the lowest common denominator, but making sure lifetime fans of these characters can walk away satisfied.

Stories that could have sprawled out and been expanded in to 4 different movies that would just drag on and try and milk you dry and take every penny they can from you, are fit into this one movie. They fit together pretty decently too . Dawn of Justice brings some of DC Comics most iconic characters together on one screen and it is a beautiful spectacle to behold.

SPOILERS:

Batman, Superman, and Wonder Woman unite for the first time ever in cinematic history. You may think the plot uniting them was a little sloppy, but now that they are together, we are just a small step away from the Justice League film(s).

Don't want to watch six movies while being teased for a decade that eventually we'll see every hero united against one force? This is the movie for you.

BRING ON THE JUSTICE LEAGUE BECAUSE DARKIED IS COMING!

1)Bruce has visions of a world branded with the omega symbol and inhabited by parademons. His rationale to Diana about uniting metahumans to fight is simply "Just a feeling I've got"

2) We see Cyborg's rebirth through his merging with a mother box (The very tool used by the inhabitants of Apokolips to travel between dimensions.) Clearly someone from Apokolips visited and left one behind.

3) Lex's final words. "He's coming. You can't stop him." Like Bruce, Lex has seen visions too.

Get hyped people, the Justice League movie is not far away!

title: Don't Listen to the Critics or Comic Purists
review: It was a really good movie, very entertaining. If you really want to listen to the critics and comic book purists who are moaning & groaning about straying off canon and other such differences; then do yourself a favor...stay home and read the comics. But if you like good movies and want to be entertained, then go out and enjoy this film. There was a lot packed into it, and yeah, there where a few disjointed bits and pieces here and there, but nothing so distracting that it ruins the flow of the movie. Henry Cavill, Ben Affleck, and Jessie Eisenberg do a great job with their characters, and Gal Gadot introduces her character in amazing fashion. "Batman v Superman" is well worth a night out at the movies!!

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is glorious
review:
(I will try to avoid spoilers, but I will discuss characterization choices. If that's spoilery then this is your warning.) Right off the Bat (see what I did there?) I don't have any idea what movie the reviewers saw, because this film doesn't match ANY of the nasty reviews I've read. Is it because of Zack Snyder? Does his name just evoke that much disdain? It must be, because this movie is one of the finest comic book films I have ever had the pleasure of watching. Or, perhaps, the problem is that it isn't a Disney movie. If that's it then they can go to hell. This movie doesn't follow the Disney model, it charts it's own course and it, and we, are all the better for it.

The Actors: I was on the "let's hate Affleck" bandwagon when he was announced as Batman. I was wrong. I am sorry. Affleck owned the part of Batman/Bruce Wayne better than ANY actor previously. I was stunned by how pitch perfect he was in this movie and I am now eagerly awaiting his stand alone Batman movies.

I was on the "let's hate Eisenberg" bandwagon when he was announced as Lex Luthor. I was wrong. I am sorry. The previews show us a Lex that appears to be merrily dancing around and being playful... Those previews are very misleading. Eisenberg's Lex is a dangerously psychotic man with unlimited resources. This is, mostly, a new take on Luthor and I applaud it. It was, again, a pitch perfect choice for this movie.

I was not a fan of Man of Steel. I didn't hate it, but I didn't like that Henry Cavil seemed to have no on screen charisma. Nor did I like the long journey from emo teen to emo Superman. Cavil's charisma and talent is all here and his journey to being the Superman we know finally becomes complete. All of the principals from Man of Steel are better in this film; Amy Adams as Lois and Lawrence Fishbourne as Perry White are both excellent.

The best for last; Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. I was NOT on the "let's hate Gadot" bandwagon when she was announced as Wonder Woman. I said from the start that she was a great choice and I was right. Gadot is the true standout among these fine performances. She gives life to the character of Wonder Woman and completely sells you on the near immortal, demi-god, warrior woman. After taking a hit during one battle she looks up and smiles and you just know she's about go all medieval on someone's ass. I absolutely cannot wait for her stand alone film. I have no doubt it will be epic. Sorry Linda Carter, I still love you, but there's a new Wonder Woman in town.

The Story: I need to tread carefully here because the plot of the movie was NOT spoiled by the trailers as many complained. There is PLENTY going on that you have to see to believe. So let me say this; the reviewers have complained that the story is a "mess," "overstuffed," or "muddled." I have to wonder if, perhaps, they spent too much time scribbling clever little bon mots in their notebooks that they failed to notice the amazing chess game that was taking place on screen. Moves and counter moves from all the principals, gaining ground in some areas only to lose it elsewhere. It was masterfully done, and when the checkmate is finally revealed you will be shocked to see how far ahead our players were planning.

Briefly I want to go back to Man of Steel. All the issues about destruction and disregard for human life that fans raised are addressed here and Batman V Superman retroactively makes Man of Steel a better film because of it. Witnessing the destruction of Metropolis through Bruce Wayne's eyes is truly terrifying and one can completely sympathize with his distrust and paranoia regarding this embodiment of a Greek God. His reactionary response, while extreme, is understandable and perfectly fitting with Batman's nature. I would love to watch Man of Steel and Batman v Superman back to back. It would be a glorious one-two punch.

Length: At 2 and a half hours I can, at least, sympathize with the length issue. But I do NOT agree with it. For me this movie FLEW by.

The Justice League: Great intros for Wonder Woman, Flash, Cyborg, and Aquaman. I can't say more about this without getting spoilery.

Overview: I loved The Dark Knight, I loved The Watchmen, I loved the X-Men films (mostly), and I've loved the Captain America movies. Batman v Superman is an equal of, if not better than, those films. At this point I consider it better. This movie has so many deep cuts into the DC universe even true comic fans will need multiple viewings to catch them all...

...And perhaps that is the real reason the critics have been complaining; Batman v Superman is a comic book movie that hasn't been dumbed down or softened for the movies. It contains deep symbolism, heavy metaphors, mythological allegories, and some dark commentary on our society. Could it be that Batman V Superman is too smart for the professional reviewer? Go see it and decide for yourself.

title: Ignore the critics - excellent movie !!!!!!!!! :)
review: Ignore the critics, I've seen this movie twice, just to be sure of my feelings towards it. title: Some good moments but shares Man of Steel's pacing problems
review:
This movie had some very neat visuals, a few of them ripped right from the pages of some of Batman's most memorable comics, and the dynamic between Superman and Lois was great to watch. However, I kept waiting for the story to start. For all its explosions, this movie had me checking my watch.

For a movie that is explicitly about Superman and Batman fighting, it skimps on foundation for why they would fight. The source material has plenty.

While this is an improvement over Man of Steel (no weird birth scenes) I found myself comparing it to Superman Returns, which, for all its flaws, really felt like a Superman movie. The question of what gives Superman the right to interfere in human affairs, which is a major issue in Batman vs Superman, is there answered very simply--because people keep asking him to.

Although Wonder Woman held her own, I would have liked to have seen more of her character and less sexy posing in skimpy costumes.

If you have more than two dream sequences, you need a rewrite.

title: Totally better than Nolan's trilogy!
review: (Tried to keep it spoiler free) The movie is great and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. title: Glorious even if not perfect
review:
One of the best of the genre in a style that, by 2016, was already not really appreciated by the masses (or/and the media, influencing the masses). With an elite script (except for the too fancy Martha thing), with perfect acting, Nolanistic "realism", psychologically developed deep and real characters, metaphorical, philosophical and socially charged themes and story plots, and the often perfect visual spectacle typical of Zack Snyder (granted, only possible because of the budget).

This is not a light movie, with characters with little to no motivations for doing what they do, except maybe the lazy ones "my loved ones are in danger" crap. There are jokes, but not to cut tension and not to transform all in a dumb comedy after all. And that's good. The rejection for this movie made it one of the last to approach this genre with any intention to comunicate something, emotional, philosophical, social. That makes it more unique. In the future, for those wanting for something like that, with more weight and brain, it would be up there with the Nolan's Batman movies, Man of Steel, X-Men First Class, Winter Soldier, Infinity War, Logan, Joker).

For the rest, they would have plenty to see while watching their cellphones and turning they brain off.

title: Ignore the Hate!
review:
While it is better than "Man of Steel" (but only slightly), this movie is not without problems of its own. The plot doesn't flow very well, and the film is a bit hard to follow as a consequence of that. I wasn't quite sure what the film was trying to be. And some of the characters' portrayals in this movie feel odd. Lex Luthor feels more like The Joker. However, the action sequences in this movie were impressive. Also, it knew just when to give us mindless action. and when to pause to give us plot. Another thing that made this stand out was they still tell Batman's origin story for those who may not be familiar with it, but it's done in 2 minutes over the opening credits. (Take notes, upcoming Marvel Spider-Man reboot. This is how you should tell the origin.) They also knew when to tease us just enough to get us hyped for the rest of the DC Cinematic Universe films. How, you may ask? No, spoilers. You'll have to see for yourself, but believe me, it's fanservice at its best. Overall, the film doesn't deliver much in terms of plot, but more than delivers on what fans really want to see: Mindless action scenes, and Batman and Superman fighting each other (with some teases for the fans to get them excited for the upcoming films)

Grade: B 8/10 3.5/5 stars

title: Far underrated movie that is very enjoyable if you answer the questions this film asks.
review: This movie, while not perfect is far underrated and misunderstood. The characters have clear motives that drive them if you simply care enough to listen to their dialogue and the world the movie takes place in is realistic and immersive. These characters have real consequences to their actions and they are forced to deal with issues that are very prevalent in modern society. It offers a gritter feel that requires a person to think about the events and not just simply watch for entertainment. While it is not Marvel it has a dark charm of its own. This movie also does a great job of humanizing Superman as we see him face problems he would face in a realistic modern society as opposed to seeing his typical perfect boy scout persona. Snyder does a great job of showing the Dark Knight morally shaded Batman and a side of Superman we don't usually get to see while he is on his way to becoming the comic character we all love. Terrio and Goyer do a great job of subtly revealing characters true intentions and motives while not force feeding us information. It's darker tone is a nice break from most superhero films and provides a realism not easily found in this kind of movie. While not on the humorous side the movie does have its share of comedic moments while providing a very intense and entertaining dark version of Batman. Some of the moments in the movie are a little too dark and it moves a little slowly but the plot progression was well worth the wait. You know why these heroes are fighting and contrary to most beliefs you know the reason they reconcile in the end. Batman has trouble accepting this otherworldly god like figure and doesn't see him as a hero to man until he is humanized. The ultimate edition of this movie is much better and the addition of the cutscenes flow together much better than the version that was released. The plot was so immersive once i stopped thinking about what everyone else thought of the movie and created my own opinion I forgot Doomsday looks like a rejected ninja turtle/ slimy green marshmallow. This is a fairly good movie that was butchered out of some of its potential by the studio. My advice would be to not go into the movie thinking you're going to get a Marvel movie because that's not what this is. Instead go in expecting to see a story about 2 heroes who are both struggling to accept the other in a world where what's different is feared and it is rare to see an act of kindness without personal gain. This is a film that asks controversial and challenging questions and doesn't play it safe. I personally enjoyed the film and the different take on society it provides.

title: Misunderstood
review:

The bad : Doomsday design and purpose Slooowly phased. Too many stories that doesn't get the space they deserve. Released before its time.

This movie is great. Even with the Martha scene and I'll tell you why. Batman IS a f upped character. I'm not saying that. But this is not the average superhero movie. Just like batman, drop the killrage. See this film again, (ultimate edition) and try to actually understand it. title: As real as it could be.
review: I have never seen ever, a superhero movie that deep since Watchmen. Details on the plot were outstanding. Man of Steel couldn't have asked for a better sequel than this. The Ultimate cut was way way better than the theatrical one. A perfect setup for Justice League. As Henry Cavill's Superman continues to find his place in the world of strangers. His existence becomes a conspiracy theory. Normal beings on earth having mixed reviews about whether their should be a Superman or not? Or whether he should answer to anyone? A Rigid Broken Man who got hurt in the events of Man of Steel takes things in his own hands. As he thinks he is the only person planet who could fight this probable threat to Human kind. Batman's Portrayal as Batman is beyond perfection. He doesn't just portray the Pain of Bruce Wayne but also his rage and rigidity. The balance Ben's Batman and Bruce had in BvS with limited screentime which was shared with Superman and Wonderwoman in a Superman centred plot, was tremendous. Ben was clear about being Batman and using Bruce Wayne as a maskup and a perfect one. He was likeable and inspiring as Bruce Wayne for his employees. As Batman he was serving his mission well without any second thoughts. He was not searching for an escape even after a 20 year reign of crime fighting. I think as a whole, Batman/Bruce was perfectly written and portrayed in BvS. This completel and concrete portrayal of Bruce/Batman's character was missing even in Nolan Trilogy. Gal's Wonderwoman was inspiring as she had a cameo, still she managed to make fans around the planet. Cinematography of this Superhero flick is out of the park. Zack Snyder delivered the punch again. The Score was on point. Hans Zimmer's and Junkie XL's genius written all over it. Plot was spread wisely and provided every necessary detail. Dialogues were written well, executed well. It kept the Dark and gritty tone as well as the Heart of the characters from DC Comics. Its a delight for a true Movie lover.

title: This is why I gave up on DC....
review:
I bought this movie based on DC's reputation. I figured there is no way they could ruin the start of the justice league. They were just given the avengers example a few years prior and have had a lot of time for casting, script writing, and plot construction. This seemed like a perfect time for them to take advantage of the superhero hype!

What I didn't know is that DC is trying to simply get their money and leave. The DCU is capable of great animated movies.... exceptions are there but their live action movie give me diarrhea. Suicide squad... made me want to commit suicide. Batman vs Superman was throw up in a blender. They casted the last people anyone would have casted. CAN ANYONE TELL ME WHY LEX LUTHER WAS PLAYED BY THE SAME GUY AS MARK ZUCKERBERG?! Lex Luthor is a cold, calculated, yet charismatic evil genius from a Latin decent(not to mention a athletic dude)..... Instead we get another overly done, "inspired by heath ledger's joker", whacky villain.... what's worse is that he's played by a pitifully inconsistent little dude who I'm guessing would not ever have been cast had they planned to use his role for anything more than a bug-eyed bed-wetter...

Lastly I can't believe they attempted the plot this movie tries to take on. They tried to knock out like nine different comics with this one movie. The death of Superman, the dawn of the justice league, Batman vs Superman, etc, etc. This is simply due to the lack of patience that is required to make happen what the marvel universe has so delicately constructed. They simply tried to mash as much content into the movie as possible which distracts from the lack of building material, character interactions, backstory, cgi physics.....

title: Watch the Ultimate Edition
review:
This is a review of the Utlimate Edition, and which I rate is as 10 out of 10. For me, BvS Ultimate joins Dark Knight, DK Rises and Logan as among the comic-movies I give the perfect score to; just so you know my sensibilities. However, I feel that a very real argument can be made that BvS Ultimate Edition is in its own league as being THE sole super-hero movie ever made.

My premise is that it has reaction to the Superman - the fantastically alien, ubermensch or God - as its main text. Simply put, no other film does this as its main subject and theme as BvS does. And the Ultimate Edition (i.e. Zack Snyder's full three hour+ artistic treatment) is a brilliant exploration of the theme.

It is the Ultimate Edition which is great. If you've only seen the theatrical cut, then you miss out on the storytelling which acts to balance the movie. Essentially, Bruce is given pathos and pity in his perspective in the UE's longer opening that provides such a balance. Luthor can be seen as more masterfully manipulative of both Bruce and Clark, and Bruce's real pathos and pity gives way to tragedy. Meanwhile Superman remains himself and is the subjected acted upon not only by Luthor's evasive deceptions but also thematic conversations of where and if the superman fits, and is 'good'.

Importantly, the UE also includes a Lois Lane investigative reporting thread that uncovers Luthor's manipulations but she just cannot reach the self-doubting Superman. The tragedy plays itself out, and Luthor remains out of the clutches of The Fourth Estate, and ahead of the branches of Government that serves to define the 'good' (relisten to Holly Hunter's speech for that note).

In all, the humans - Bruce, Lois, the pluralist branches of Government, and even the contemplative/uncertain side of Clark - are shown to have agency in UE, and Luthor manipulates them ALL. Masterful. And then plunge into tragedy, based particularly on Batman's pathos. I have thought since film riffs on The Dark Knight in a big way, if someone was present to 'But Luthor cannot win...'

The first half of Snyder's UE present all of these swirling agencies that focuses into what ultimately happens. I love this movie and I consider it THE only real super-hero to have ever been made. Please watch the Ultimate Edition before judging this movie. Also please sign the petition for a full Zack Snyder extended cut of Justice League, godwilling.

title: Son of Krypton vs. Bat of Gotham!
review: The biggest Gladiator fight comes to life! To understand the storyline in this movie you would have to watch Man of Steel. Overall I loved this movie from beginning to end. I actually found it hard to believe that many were disappointed. Ben Affleck was a better choice for Batman than what I actually thought. Also this movie paved a path for Wonder Woman and the Justice League. Once you understand the story you would appreciate this movie.

title: Awesome Movie
review:
Batman vs Superman is the first time in history that we have two iconic characters go head to head on the big screen. The movie is basically a sequel of Man of Steel with some in society blaming Superman for the collateral damage when he fought General Zod. Among his detractors is Bruce Wayne who does not trust an alien. Clark Kent on the other hand is concerned that Batman has a license to kill in Gotham City and wants things done by the book. Lex Luthor plays into this animosity be egging each side on.

BvS is an awesome movie. I highly recommend the Director's Cut as it explains more and is a bit darker. The acting and the action scenes are praiseworthy and the dramatic ending sets this movie apart from the majority of Marvel movies. Some did not understand the movie and hence gave the film a low score but for those who are paying attention and willing to reflect on the movie it is an awesome spectacle. This is not a simple movie, as it requires one to think and put the pieces in place. If you are willing to do that then the movie will be a fantastic experience for you.

Jackal

title: "People fear what they don't understand"
review:
Ultimate edition review

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a cinematic masterpiece. It's artistic and bold take on the superhero genre paves a path seeded with deeper meanings for comic book movies. This part political thriller, part superhero action epic takes a hard look at reality and delivers a hyper-stylized clash between iconic characters that is truly ground breaking.

The story is many things melded into a clever and engaging epic. The film tells a story from the point of view of not only Batman and Superman, but also the world. It is dense, but every scene is executed so well and feels important. From the very opening scene, this film is a stunning reinvention and introduction to this new version of Batman. It also connects so well the the universe as a whole, leaving breadcrumbs for more to come. I truly cannot talk about this film without the depth that it deserves without delving deep into spoilers so I'll just say this: The whole story is magnificent and congregates in an intense and gripping third act. But it also leaves some loose threads that hint at the expanding universe. This film connects so intimately to the previous installment Man of Steel, and I think that is one of its strengths. I really felt like these movies are all one big story.

This version of Batman is the 2nd best one yet. Ben Affleck gives a performance that makes the Bruce Wayne/Batman character feel new, but still honours the core of the character that most previous performances captured so well. His Bruce Wayne is charming, snarky and really damn sexy. His delivery of each and every line feels as though Bruce Wayne is real and exists. But Affleck's Batman is even better. This Batman is brutal, muscular and more broody than ever. It is incredible to watch. Every time Ben Affleck is on screen, with the costume on, he is scary. A good scary. Watching him felt like I was a guilty crook stuck in a dark alleyway. This older, brutal and more stylized version of Batman is compelling to watch. His arc of redemption throughout the film is misunderstood by many, but it truly is so amazing. You really get to feel much more with this version of Batman than any other. His journey throughout is such an enjoyable watch.

Henry Cavill continues his role as Superman and is fantastic. This film explores the Clark Kent reporter side much more and Cavill plays it perfectly. This Clark Kent is smart, determined and charmingly nerdy. I think there is much less of a difference between the two personas of Kal-El, but I feel it's more realistic. His Superman performance is just as great as it was in Man of Steel . In this film we get to see more of how Superman is seen by the public and how he reacts to it. Cavill expresses such powerful emotions when dealing with the way Clark reacts to his public image. It is so genuine and you feel a more emotional impact with Superman's actions. But the essence of Superman is still kept, because even through all the hardships and doubt he faces throughout this film, he still does the right thing. He is still good. This universe is definitely set in a darker, more harsh world, which reflects that of own. But there is a visible light and this film works its way towards that.

The action sequences in this film are gorgeous. Every shot is absolutely breathtaking and courtesy of cinematographer Larry Fong. The use of color perfectly reflects the tone of the film and delivers beautifully in epic action sequences. As this is a very visual film, the cinematography plays a significant part in telling the story. Each shot has so much detail that just enhances what is going on in the plot. Incredible thought and work has gone in to create a world in which this story is integrated in.

Hans Zimmer and Tom Holkenberg created the score for this film and it truly shines. The music is just fantastic and has a very orchestral, epic theme to it. Each track is crafted well for each scene, but where the score really shines is the character themes. The themes for Batman, Superman and Lex Luthor were all so well done. They fit with the characters and are so memorable. But the absolute stand out theme was Wonder Woman's. The electric cello that bursts into your ears with an epic riff is just heaven. I found myself listening to that track the most.

This is such a beautiful film. It totally deconstructs what a superhero comic book movie is and turns it into a deeply philosophical commentary on the world today. Using two iconic characters and putting them in the premise of this film worked so well. Although there are some minor scenes that were unnecessary and moments that could have been executed better, this film was so enjoyable to watch. It is on such an epic scale and is so different from the regular bunch of comic book movies, it is such a breath of fresh air. I could not recommend this movie enough, it is incredible.

title: Superman vs Godzilla
review:
I promised myself after watching Man Of Steel (all being well) to steel myself and see just one more Dark Crap film and this was it, the 3 hour Dawn Of Justice Ultimate Edition. Is there a Coherent Edition out there too? I wasn't disappointed – as I expected I didn't enjoy it; I'll probably stick with light-hearted Marvel from now on for this kind of entertainment, because ultimately Time's running out.

Batman has a lifelong violent grudge against Superman for being responsible for his parents' deaths and machinates to kill him for the first 150 minutes. Then, upon the utterance of a single word by Superman to the grunted astonishment of Batman all sins are forgiven for the final half hour and they become allies in attempting to defeat Evil. Unbelievable, they're living in a fantasy world if they expect us to swallow that! Then, the film nosedived from being mildly incoherent and boring into intensely incoherent and laughable. I thought the tinny music for the relentless multi-coloured patterns on the screen which were supposed to represent a cgi conflagration suited the Godzilla/Hobbit monster perfectly though – no doubt Warners owed any Asian backers something. There seemed to be more newspapers and TV news telling the "story" than usual – but do kids nowadays remember those antiquated types of news outlets? The film started and ended with gloomy grimy graveyards with much grunting and griping; there has to be an overarching moral there somewhere. And don't expect any light-bulb moments in here! Carnage is wreaked and Death would be stalking the Land for weeks afterwards but none of the twerps protecting the planet cared a fig about that. Affleck was fascinating with his ridiculous grunting, Cavill was a thoughtless sulky yob, Gadot should have been with someone else, I felt sorry for Amy Adams in yet another hopeless film.

I grew up with the nonsensical 1960's Batman, but unfortunately these particular superheroes have been allowed to grow up superselfish and superfluous.

title: wtf...
review:
My wife pretty much summed this movie up for me. She of course didn't pay attention and asked "Why are Batman and Superman fighting...aren't they both good?"

(Spoilerish) (not really more than a trailer) Initially I tried to actually answer the question, "Well if you were paying attention, Lex Luthor manipulated Batman into stealing some Kryptonite so he'd be able to kill Superman who has to fight him because...ugh...it's really damn stupid...but it's cool to see Batman and Superman fight..." (/Spoilerish)

Overall I could have given this a five, but then I had to subtract 10 for egregious use of Samsung Note shaky cam footage. Seriously...you couldn't afford real cameras? I can't fathom how a AAA budget allowed this kind of cinematography. It hurts...actual eye strain on a home projector. IMDb made me round up to a one.

Even more useless review crud:

Honestly the fight isn't great. It's OK. He could have been great as an old bitter "Dark Knight Returns" Batman, but they just missed.

Wonder woman is rather attractive. Maybe DC will redeem themselves and make the first decent superwoman movie...that's kind of a big deal nowadays right...girl power!

title: No justice here
review:
Overstuffed and consequently undercooked, Snyder's ponderous and joy free launch of DC's Justice League saga moves with the élan of a race car with square wheels. Plot points are introduced with no setup and others with no payoff. Framed by an ugly, over-pixilated cacophony of mind numbing action it tries to beat you into submission rather than win your heart.

The best part of the movie--and I can't even believe I'm saying this--is Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman. As the slapdash "narrative" zipped around like a fly at a picnic, all I kept thinking was "I wish this were simply a Batman movie.".

title: Depressing First half destroys the whole movie.
review:
It was a total bullshit movie. There was nothing new in the story. No great punchline. Plot was completely directionless. They tried to create a sense of grandiose by merely adding more and more characters.

Story was so bad that Story writer, somehow, managed to create a total detachment from the characters. Other than stupid dreams of Batman (which were pretty dumb) there was nothing to develop a character. In the end, Characters just felt too artificial.

When Climax approached, I felt Emotionless towards all the superheroes. Only character I could empathize with was Ancient Cryptonian who was angry at everyone in the movie and wanted to destroy them.

In a nutshell, this movie was an absolute waste of the resources. This movies had everything but a story.

title: Just bad - what a mess
review:
OK.. That's not what I was hopping to see...

Very poor story with almost no imagination... The casting really is very bad too... I mean there is good actors but they just don't fit the roles... title: Not good enough DC
review:
I wouldn't say it was bad, but personally it didn't fill my expectations.

What disappoints me the most is the flow of the movie. There are just too many uninteresting fillers with way too much runtime, which caused the action scenes to run short. For example, Bat vs Supes scenes ended way too abruptly with nonsensical reason (Martha), and Bats vs Goons was awesome but again it falls short. In my opinion, what makes this movie bad is both the plot and the script.

As for the characters, Henry Cavill is improving by margin as he brought his own version of Superman. Gal is a very beautiful incarnation of Wonder Woman; elegant and tough at the same time, she's got very little dialogue and scenes so I couldn't picture her yet as our lasting WW. Affleck though, I can say he is the best Batman so far, he outshines everyone in the movie with his character even with the crappy script. I wouldn't say Bale was bad, I mean he got his own movies for three times, but Affleck was just a level higher.

The supporting characters: Lois (Amy) got too much runtime and let's face it her story is not interesting at all. I'm so used to seeing and believing Lex Luthor is a firm and non-humorous character, and his life is always about ruling the world but in this movie he is too laid back and too focused on humiliating Supes instead of trying to control it all. Weirdly by seeing Jesse's performance in this movie, I pictured him as the Joker, but I don't know maybe I just have to get use to this new Lex.

But despite all this, I can't wait for Justice League and as much as it pains me to say this; Zack Snyder you didn't do a job good enough in directing this movie.

title: Murder man vs Barely any dialogue man: Dawn of rushing to get to the Justice League
review: No...just...just no. Thanks a lot Mr Snyder, you are now officially the Michael Bay of comic book movies. The action looked great though and I'm sold on Bat fleck as Murder man FOREVER. It's just literally everything else with the film, OK lets start from the beginning; or more accurately just playing the opening to Batman Begins which is pretty much what the opening to THIS film is, but shot very nicely. Then we have a sequence in the desert where Superman is framed for killing the native soldiers there...with bullets...wait what? Yes the entire squad of soldiers who were OBVIOUSLY gunned down by other mercenaries,(Who are working for Lex Luthor) They put all the blame on Superman, yeah makes sense right? And then a few minutes later Clark and Lois have a very deep conversation about the ramifications Superman's presence could bring onto the world...nah JK he say's "don't care" and jumps in the bathtub for some wet and wild fun, yay? And now we arrive the main event, oh not the epic superhero battle royale no no no I mean the outstandingly bloody GOOFY performance of Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, we have yet to hear an apology from Jesse to this day, alas I shall have to soldier on. So basically Lex finds Kryptonite from the world engine and then ask's some senator man to gain access to General Zod's ship in exchange for the shiny green stuff. So Luthor sticks some cherry sweets into the senator man's mouth and that seals the deal...OK then?(God his performance is so awkward) Anyway coming back to the main real issue of this film, Batman and Superman have barely any reason to fight each other, Batman wants to kill Superman cause he's responsible for a ton of death(Hypocrite he kills now) and Superman dislikes Batman because he's a vigilante who works outside the law?(Hypocrite Superman is a vigilante and has never worked with the law) Oh yeah and thats not even the reason he fights him anyway, Luthor kidnaps Clarks mother and tells him to kill Batman. Oh but its okay cause both Superman and Batman's mothers names is Martha, so they're best friends now...whoop de doo, oh and Wonder Woman's in the movie and so is Flash and Aquaman and Cyborg...sorry has Justice League already come out or something??? Ugh this film isn't terrible, its average, disappointing mainly the story and character motivations are WEAK, still excited for Suicide Squad though. But I swear if that film is anything like this one or worse? I'm officially done with DC films, guys just go out and watch Civil War like 5 times in a row or hell wait for X-Men Apocalypse to come out and watch THAT 5 times in a row, yeah i know "Marvel bias" but screw you they actually make good movies.

title: If you are not a big fan of Batman and superman series, don't buy the tickets
review:
I watched the movie the first day it went public in Japan, hoping it marks a beginning of a new era of hero movie series like Avengers. But I was kind of disappointed. Let me share how I fell after watching it: 1. This movie is not for rookies. By rookie, I mean those who doesn't have a long history watching Batman/Superman movies/episodes. I won't call myself an "elite enthusiast", but I have been following every superhero movie in the recent 8 years (and I actually bought the game "Injustice: God among us ultimate edition" at Steam, which tells a full story about the parallel world and the evil version of superman). Even I couldn't fully understand the movie (like the scene where Luther is talking about the evil coming from the sky, instead of the ground). 2. The fight scene is terrific. Especially the last battle between superman+batman+wonder woman and doomsday. Don't know why but I like to watch batman running around dodging doomsday's laser (Yeah, money is not so powerful in this circumstance, right).

In conclusion, the movies does give you good fightings, but you might have to do some homework to fully understand the story told in this movie.

title: Wonder Woman saved the day
review: I am a big fan of superheroes, so I went to see this movie with high expectations and came back disappointed. There are too many incoherent points in the plot. This made the movie were hard to see and hard to follow. It was like expecting the best and get a lesser result. The conflict between these heroes is absurd. How Batman beats Superman so easily is not believable. How Superman seems to have forgotten the destruction he caused in the previous movie is also not believable. Other elements that added to this A lot of narrative nonsense, a poor Lex Luthor, how easy you can get "Kryptonite" and a terrible villain. The rumbling soundtrack was also not good. Then came Wonder Woman and saved the day. Without Wonder Woman this movie would have been a complete disaster.

title: Not what you would expect
review:
I wanted to like this movie simply because it was a DC universe title with a mash up with batman, and superman together in one feature length film, but that unfortunately couldn't change the amount of scene shuffling going on.. as if the editor who edited the film had tourette's syndrome.

The pacing was uncanny, and hard to follow as each new scene would just jump wildly ahead taking time to adjust to new dialogue, and scenery. Making any attempt to follow the seemingly awful story the writers conceived for this epic showdown a waste of time.

What really killed the movie for me was when batman realized he was doing what had happened to him when he was a child, and that superman's mothers name was also Martha.. which concluded that batman.. and superman would become instant best friends instead of batman killing superman... truly the worst script writing I'v seen in recent years.

At least Ben Affleck played a pretty decent Batman in the film unlike his last Daredevil debut.

title: Love it , hate it.
review:
I watched this movie yesterday and went to see it with an open mind. Some of my friends told me it was " absolute garbage" and that " it was just the interpretation of PC correct writers and corporate film studio makers". However I didn't have that feeling at all; nor did my girlfriend who is a huge DC fan.

pro: -great fight scenes -a more realistic way of doing superheroes movies. How will people react to them. -The "darkness" of the film was just right. Batman is not a little schoolboy, pointing his finger at some villain saying " i will thee with the batman's wings of awesomeness". Batman's character is dark, superman's character is, well he is an alien and if we look at how we people treat other people (us versus them mentality) -Wonder-woman is kicking butskies! -Epic fights.

Con: -a bit too much of CGI for my taste. - one of the main villains was a bit of a miss cast or either he got a tad bit of a bad script.

Conclusion: A worthwhile movie that you should see, despite the criticisms. You should always make up you own mind and do not be swayed by others ( except if its your girlfriend or your partner in crime haha).

the only other thing that both my girlfriend and I felt, was that all the heroes got a bit of a rush rush job in their story line ( some call it origin story). However this is a personal feeling we had after the movie. Some viewers might not have had that same feeling as we did.

7/10 Great movie and a must see in the theaters.

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice. The title is just as bad as this movie itself! Why WB?
review:
Quick spoiler free review!

So I walked into this movie with fair expectations that i would be satisfied with what i was about to see on the big screen, hell something that i have dreamed of seeing on the big screen!!

The first ten minutes of the film was engaging had me at the edge of my seat screaming for more! Then the movie starts crumbling apart very quickly! Just shoving plot and sub plots into your face and down your throat! This movie to me felt like changing the channels on your TV but the only thing on every channel was just adds! Because that's all this movie is, a messy rushed unneeded set up for the DC universe!

There was so many times during the film i just thought "WHY THE F&%$ DID YOU PUT THIS IN!" especially with the many plot holes this movie has!

I wasn't even satisfied with the actual Batman V Superman fight, get through two and a half hours of screen time just to watch testosterone boil over! It could have been done exceptionally better!

The things I did like about the film was Ben as the bat he played an amazing roll i just wanted more of batman on screen "murdering" people! Jeremy Irons was cast really well, best alfred yet in my opinion! Most of the visual effects looked incredible on screen and was lovely eye candy until a particular troll shows up! Some of the action scenes actually had me cringing but with a great big smile! Wonder Woman looks great and can kick a ton of ass (but i feel like her role wasn't needed in this movie)

And everything else I just couldn't get behind!

In the end this movie had no real heart and really needed it! Its a tragic huge pile of crap with a few gold pieces tossed amongst the batch! DC is going to have to deliver far greater titles than this to keep me invested in their movieverse! I can see what they're trying to achieve and I'm afraid they will fail!

I guess we will find out once suicide squad drops!

title: Breaking News: "Superman and Batman defeated by Captain Ennui!"
review:
On behalf of good storytelling and suspense, we, everyone who expected the long awaited confrontation of two of the most iconic superheroes ever, to be a thrilling masterpiece, declare this poorly scripted advertisement for a potentially bigger sequel to come, an epic fail!

Rarely I have been so desperately looking for some relevance and emotional depth like it was the case while watching this muddled mess of a movie and it's so sad because it had everything a good action movie needs and yet the end result is boring for the most part.

Zack Snyder made one of my favorite movies of all times which is "Watchmen", however, he also did "Sucker Punch" which despite it's visual abundance and sex-appeal bored me to hell, and "Batman v. Superman" is somewhere between those two.

I still hold high regards for Zack Snyder as director for his ability to create powerful imagery that sticks to your mind, but he seems not to care much for his characters and plot development, it all looks so cool and the action is bombastic, but in the end it all feels so shallow and redundant.

Ben Affleck proved all the haters whiny naggers, he was superb as Batman! The other cast was fine too, although I consider Eisenberg's interpretation of Lex Luthor as too nerdy and psychotic which doesn't live up to the charismatic image of Luthor I got from the cartoons and comics. Amy Adams is again miscast for Lois Lane and Gal Gadot is a hot Wonder Woman but feels completely misplaced in this movie lacking any sort of background story, another example of how they introduce story arcs to leave them open for further installments to continue them, with the consequences that "Batman v. Superman" feels unfinished, incomplete, a sole introduction to a "cinematic Universe" yet to enter the screens, in other words, it's an overlong advertisement for the franchise rather than being a movie, a story on it's own.

I'm really disappointed.

title: Cartoony Script
review:
If you are any sort of fan of comics or super hero movies, you'd watch this anyways, so there's no reason to dissuade you. But if you're not, then I have absolutely NO REASON TO RECOMMEND YOU to watch this movie.

The movie sacrificed pacing, character building, and plot, for "comics fan-service." If you're a fan of well-written movies with engrossing plot and intriguing characters, this movie has nothing for you. Arguably very few super-hero movies have memorable plot, but this one has nearly a unlikeable plot. (very minor spoiler): Batman hates Superman until a point he just changes his mind. (spoiler ends)

If you've ever watched one of those Justice League cartoon/animated movies when you're younger, BvS is EXACTLY what it felt like: I had fun watching heroes in action, but who cares why they're doing it? It's a carton!! -That's pretty much the expectation you should have for BvS.

title: Potentially good, but fell down.
review:
I feel this was a decent film, although it could have been made better, there was the opportunity here for a solid storyline and character development, it touched on it a number of times throughout the film but didn't manage to hold it, I felt.

The film was moving at a steady pace right up until near the end, at the last 20 minutes, where I feel everything was turned to overdrive. The big climax came and then vanished, at least for me, anyways.

I felt Ben Affleck done a good job at portraying Batman, but Henry Cavill didn't quite come across as emotional as I would have liked. Jesse Eisenberg done well as Lex Luther, I really felt he done a good job at winning the hate of the viewers.

I felt overall that less would have been more, here. I enjoyed Man of Steel but this felt like it was too much, trying to squeeze characters and plot from both into one film.

title: Yet Another Superhero Movie !
review: It is far from summer and the new avalanche of superhero movie's has begun tiresomely to roll yet again. I went to see Batman v Superman today and had to sit through trailers for 4 more superhero coming attractions. I can no longer remember my reboot from my sequel or now a captain America from an avenger or stay awake during a X men trailer. Every superhero is in every film it such a muddle.As for this new Batman/Superman flick well i did doze of briefly early on dew to to much brooding, now superman is getting dark, oh do stop pulling my leg.Yet this movie was in the end much more entertaining for me than the average superhero movie.Though Lex Luther was a massive flop, a villain needs to be good but Lex Luther was a rambling bore. Happily Ben Affleck made a more than decent batman while good old superman was rather well fleshed out i thought by Henry Cavill, joining Lex Luther on my cutting room floor was wonder women, very poorly cast for a start and this inclusion seemed to serve just no point.It seems two superhero's are no longer near enough there must be scores.How much longer can Hollywood's obsession with superhero movies continue surely saturation point must come, surely audiences must eventually tire of the same old same old.I for one long for a super villain to come to my rescue and blast some of these endless superhero's into outer space. One last thought back in 1979 when the Chris Reeve superman film came out the slogan was "you'll believe a man can fly" now superman sort of zooms flash and you have missed him, a flying man is kind of amazing but we get barely a glimpse of superman in flight, nor does he seem to enjoy all his powers very much.These superhero movies, fantasy's after all just need to lighten up.

title: Like watching a car-accident, you can't look away
review:
Lex Luthor and Alfred was the only things that made this movie watchable. Everything else is a jumbled mess, a series of scenes just mashed together. Sure Batfleck does a good job but Batman is poorly written as hell, and it clearly shows that the writers and Snyder don't give a shite about Superman, so they just decide to bash him both mentally and physically, as clearly they feel thats the only way to right the many wrongs made in MoS. Lex is not Lex, but he at least made me laugh, intentionally or not, specially when Superman growls "Where is sheee?". That reply he has made me laugh out loud. Wonder woman totally overrated, Doomsday just another cgi-mess, Supermans death had no impact whatsoever. Terribly pretentious and "dark", stupid slow-motion scenes allover, strange narrative from Batfleck, to many dream-sequences. "Martha"!!. This movie even turns my review into a mess ;)

Bottomline is i did't care about any of the characters or their motivations. Basically all characters are dumb selfish assholes. But still, more entertaining than MoS, in a morbid "can't help looking at the car-accident"-way.

What grinds my gears is that this movie seems to think it's smart and profound. No it's not, it tries to be, but fails miserably.

One extra star for the soundtrack, which can be good at times. Superman theme and WW theme is great. Zimmers soundtrack deserves a better movie, just like with MOS. Only thing DC has over Marvel imo.

title: One of the best movies ever
review: I will get straight to to the point. If a person wants to go to the cinema to watch this epic film, kindly leave all the thoughts of the cartoon series, comics and even the previous batman series. If a person goes to watch this film with high expectations to get the complete package of the above mentioned things then they will be sorely disappointed. However If you go with an open mind then you will be blown away. That how awesome this movie is. There were times when my mind just went blank from this awesomeness.
