So don't listen to all the critics downplaying this movie. Just go and enjoy it to the fullest. You will not be disappointed.

title: BATMAN v EVERY OTHER aspect of the film
review:
DUE to the overwhelming amount of user reviews for this movie, I am quite sure only a few people will ever read this, and for that reason I am going to keep this very brief. I will only list a few points that need to be addressed even though this review could easily run for pages and pages.

-Batman will definitely be the the best part of the film for most moviegoers. However he does not feel like batman, but rather a hybrid of Batman, Punisher, and an unintelligent emotion-driven, walking contradiction.

-Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman is fine, but any female that is attractive could have played her part, as much of her fighting was CGI, and most of her lines were very underwhelming. People love her only because of WONDER WOMAN and not because of her performance, which is backwards film making.

-This film has so many plot holes and they are so massive that they should be called "BLACK plot HOLES" because nothing and nobody should be able to ignore or escape them. For example- Superman can save Lois so often (which is already another problem, but that's another story) by being able to hear/sense/feel she is in danger. However, the most important person to him besides Lois (his mom) is easily, and I mean EASILY, kidnapped and "tortured" without him even knowing.

-Superman dying was literally laughable. It was so unnecessary it can be compared to a horror movie where the characters are so dumb that they basically seal their own fate by acting out in the least plausible way.

-The reason for the BATMAN v SUPERMAN brawl (or rather quick scuffle) coming to an end, is literally on par with Starlord (Guardians of the Galaxy) starting a dance-off with Ronan to save the world they were on. HOWEVER, in that movie it worked because it was so comical in tone. This was NOT MEANT TO BE A JOKE, and there may be only one or two other "attempted" jokes in this entire film.

-Lex Luthor is almost unbearable. Possibly could have worked in another film, but NOT in this one.

-So many easter eggs were included, and almost all of them were detrimental to the film.

-The WHOLE INTRODUCTION of the JUSTICE LEAGUE characters was a JOKE. Literally, this film could have had a high school film department submit little "teases" to these characters and it would have been less corny than this whole scene.

-The ONLY BELIEVABLE lines in the whole film are given to Superman when he tells Lois that he "Loves Her" and that "She is his world." I literally teared up because it was so believable, and such a contrast to the rest of the films dialogue.

-Jeremy Irons is the best performer in the film, which is not a good thing, but he is great.

-Overall this movie is being blown out of proportion by many DC fan boys, whether they are "undercover" or not. I do not feel sorry for them though because they are not learning any lessons from this film, but rather defending it because of their loyalty to DC. If you liked it than that is completely fine, but do not try to argue that this is a quality film, because then you just look dull. If you FANBOYS wanted to do what is smart, you would also critique the films weak points and try to get those POINTS ACROSS TO WARNER BROS AND DC in hopes that they better their future films. All this defending will do is ALLOW movies like this to prosper financially, like the Transformers franchise, all while being only a mere shadow of what they could become.

title: Bat-Crazy Man Vs Super-Serious Man: Yawn of Justice is super disappointing. Still, I did enjoyed this superhero movie. I just wish, it could had been better.
review: From director Zack Snyder comes Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, the first big-screen meeting between DC's (Detective Comics) greatest superheroes. For the most part, the movie was entertaining, due to the intense action scenes & the quality of the visuals effects. However, I just wish the movie was a little more light-hearted and fun, than over-serious and dark. It doesn't even seem like a kid's movie with several of DC characters brooding, philosophical talking, and doing extreme violent acts in an over complicated plot about Meta-humans being left unchecked and turning out to be wolves in sheep's clothing. Like, really why would believe and blamed Superman for the massacre in Africa when he never used a gun? I get that, Detective Comics wants to continue to the adult-driven tone that director Christopher Nolan has done with the Dark Knight trilogy (2005-2012) and 2013's Men of Steel, but gees, this movie was a little bit off-putting with how messy, they treat Superman and the rebooting of Batman. Don't get me wrong, I like Ben Affleck's portrayal of Bruce Wayne/ Batman and his Frank Miller style of costume. After all, Affleck is by far, the best performance in the film, but I just didn't like all the screen time, it took to establish, his already known backstory. It took away, all of screen-time needed to establish Clark Kent/Superman's problems (Henry Cavill). For Superman, I really don't have a problem with Henry Cavill. He looks and acts the part. I just didn't like, how he became a secondary character in his own movie. After all, isn't this originally supposed to be, Superman's sequel? In my opinion, Batman should had been establish first in his own movie rather than pair up, out of the blue with Superman, without much establishment. Second off, the whole 'dream' story structure within the first 2 acts was really annoying with Batman. I hate, how it's cut to something, very vague and random like a hint to the comic book 'Crisis On Infinite Earths', until the main plot picks up, again. About Batman killing people, as much as I would love, that he had a moral code, I'm willing to accept this change, with a grain of salt. After all, Batman did kill people, throughout the comic book world, many times over, before. I just wish, the movie show a better reason, why Batman dislike Superman, rather than the fact, that Superman accidentally murder people, once in a while. It's very hypocritical, when you think about it, since Batman does that every night. I also hate, the fact, that the weak conflict got resolve, way too quickly. It's really odd, to consider them, being good friends after one night of battle with some very invasive music playing in the background. Another thing, about that night of battle is how they rushed and changed, much of the Doomsday and Superman storyline from the comics. This version of Doomsday's appearance toward the end of the film felt very offensive to fans of the 'Death of Superman" comic-books. I didn't like it, Doomsday should had been save for the oncoming Justice League movie, like the other random cameos of Justice League. Members like Arthur Curry/Aquaman (Jason Momoa), Barry Allen/The Flash (Ezra Miller) & Victor Stone/Cyborg (Ray Fisher) felt like a tease. One big character, that wasn't really needed for this movie is Diana Prince/Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot). She really comes out of nowhere, with no backstory at all and has little to do with the main plot. The actress does work as a strong female lead, however, her presence in this film was a little jarring. Since the meta-humans program, doesn't really come into play. One character, I didn't like, from the movie is actor, Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luther. He was horrible with his hammy joker-style humor. His reasons for hating Superman is also very inconsistent. I get that, they wanted him to be suffering from psychological disorder rather than just being greedy, evil, or driven by ego I still don't know, what his main goals were. How does he know about the character of Darkseid? Plus, his scenes with Senator Finch (Holly Hunter) were too-sexual awkward. Does he has feeling for her? Is she, his mother? We will never know. I just felt dirty, for watching it. It's also a sad attempt, by Warner Bros to change his character from Lex Luther Senior to Lex Luther Jr. as a lame way, to draw away the backlash of Eisenberg's casting in this film. Plus, to leave it, open for their originally choice, Tom Hanks to come in, and play the senior role. Another character, that bug me, is Lois Lane (Amy Adams). While Amy Adams brings her usual warmth, humanity, and mix of moxie and vulnerability to the Daily Planet's most intrepid reporter. I just hate, how much, the movie makes her, into a dumb damsel in distress burden for Superman. She really does way too any stupid stuff in the film like throwing away the spear. Overall: This movie never fully transcends into being an awesome viewing experience and yet is also too competently made to be anywhere near the disaster, its haters probably wanted. With that said, if you've already made up your mind about seeing this movie, then the actual film itself won't do much to change your mind one way or another. You're going to love it or hate it. For me, I found this superhero escapism movie to be very disappointing.

title: I figured out way back if God is all-powerful, He cannot be all good.
review:
Ah, the most controversial movie in ages as superhero movies go. Well, since MoS back in 2013. But whereas that film divided the critics 50-50, this film was hit hard with a 41% rating which has currently dipped to 28%. And a lot of people I have talked to about the movie have either: 1.) haven't seen because of said negative publicity or 2.) or hated for several arbitrary reasons or 3.) give it a pleasant rating anywhere from 7/10 to 10/10. So as quickly as possible I will lay out the pros and cons of this movie. Quite frankly I loved it but I can see why some people may not have liked it. Here are flaws that irked me:

1.The Knightmare scene where Batman has a nightmare and/or vision concerning Superman becoming an authoritarian ruler of Earth. This scene is great but then you see the minions of Darkseid raining down from the sky as well. Problem isaudiences (unless comic book fans or even simply a fan of the 90s and early 2000s DC animated shows) have no idea what these creatures are. For a fan, seeing this is awesome. For a casual moviegoer this is probably downright confusing. Although it still begs the question as to why Darkseid's forces are linked to Superman. BUT, if you watched the animated (awesome) show from the 90s, you know it's not entirely impossible for Superman and Darkseid to have joined forces.

2. Right after this already very mind-boggling scene, we are treated to what we assume is The Flash coming from either the future (or maybe another universe?) to warn Bruce about Superman, though it is a tad vague. These two scenes back-to-back were leaving a comic book nerds like me hooked and anxious for the sequel, but I will admit that they are just too much for casual audiences. Perhaps they should've been excluded from the theatrical version, which would have trimmed down the movie and maybe even pleased those who said the story was a mess in their eyes. At the same time it's great for the die-hard fans who in all honesty this film was made for. Moving away from this, the only other thing that bothered me was Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor. His introduction felt off from what I usually expect from Luthor who as far as I'm concerned has always been comedic when represented on film. That being said, as the movie went on I actually came to embrace this version of Lex. He actually encompasses every bit of the inferiority complex-having, power hungry, intellectual showboat that Lex is. He is in my opinion the most sinister version of Lex put on the big screen and he has some of the best lines in the movie. Still, at times he comes off as a bit too quirky and socially awkward but there is more good than bad here. Now to what I liked.

Visually, the movie is breathtaking. Every set looks great, the look of each hero or villain is fantastic, and the cinematography is jaw-dropping. In short, the movie is gorgeous. The performance of every actor and actress in the movie was phenomenal. Ben Affleck really nailed Batman in this movie. He is definitely on par with the greats like Keaton and Bale. As for the whole 'no-killing' thing, I'm just bored to death of this trope. Half the people who gripe about heroes killing bad guys here or there need to actually pick up a comic. Not only that, for goodness' sake the only reason why this became a facet of Batman is because the original writers needed an excuse for Batman to face his enemies in future story lines. I highly appreciate the role of this rule in films like The Dark Knight where the whole point was to test Batman's resolve. However, this film is about a broken and disillusioned Batman so his morals are obviously going to be different. Besides, Batman has killed in previous films (both Nolan and Burton) it never stopped me from enjoying those movies. Cavill was great at portraying the weight on his character's shoulders. All the warnings of Costner's Kent from MoS came to fruition, and all this tension came together perfectly because of the performances and visuals. Gadot really did steal the show at times and I cannot wait to see more of her on the big screen sword in hand. Amy Adams, Diane Lane, Laurence Fishburne, Jeremy Irons, and Holly Hunter all delivered in this movie. The acting really brought his movie to life. And the score by Hans Zimmer was one of the best soundtracks I have EVER had the pleasure of listening to.

This film hints at many popular DC comics story lines, but by far the most used is The Dark Knight Returns by Frank Miller. The themes really carry over very well and it really adds to the motives of the main characters. Yes, this movie is dark and thought-provoking, but unlike a lot of what people have been saying it has touches of humor mixed in as well. More so than MoS admittedly. All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed this movie on many levels and I believe there is something in there that every superhero or action lover can see in it. The critics have said their word, but it's really up for you as a viewer to decide for yourself. After all, the word of critics does not always hold up as I'm sure we've all seen on numerous occasions.

title: Batman v Superman: Do it Justice
review:
In an attempted to replicate the success of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Warner Brothers gave us the Man of Steel 3 years ago to layout the foundation of their multi-verse. It did a decent job of reintroducing Superman in the modern world although not on the same level as "Batman Begins" as many of us were expecting. The ending remains controversial today nonetheless I was genuinely looking forward to the sequel.

When they officially announced the title Batman v Superman, l was speechless and worried at the same time. To witness the two most iconic heroes battling one another is almost the biggest thing that could happen in the comic book cinematic history besides Marvel's Avengers, however when a franchise is moving towards something vs something, you know something is not right. Take a look at Jason vs Freddy or King Kong vs Godzilla, OK not exactly a good example but you get the point. Let's dissect the film:

Spoilers ahead

The film started off with the death of Thomas & Martha Wayne again. I am sure even for casual moviegoer, they are all well aware of Batman's origin by now, how many times do you think we need to see that on screen again? Studios never learn do they? Look what happened to the Spiderman reboot We were then given a whole ten minutes of the ending of Man of Steel in Bruce Wayne/Batman's angle. In short, Superman accidentally killed those who worked for Bruce Wayne and Lex Luthor who tricks Batman (by the way the greatest detective/ hero in the DC universe) into hating Superman by framing him in Africa and suicide bombing at the congressional hearing which Superman should have heard the bomb..

Then Superman is fighting Batman because Luthor captured his mom, setting him up against Batman who by this time still doesn't realize he's being manipulated. The situation gets worse, Superman actually told Batman that he's fighting because his mom has been captured. Batman came so close in killing him until he finds out their mothers share the same first name and they suddenly become best friend. There is no weight and resolution to their fight.

Don't even get me started with the creation of Doomsday which was spoiled for us in the 2nd trailer, it is so obviously that it is somehow linked to General Zod but how did Luthor gain access and control to the genesis chamber and come to know about the Krytonite? It's just lying there in India Ocean for 2 years for random divers to pick it upCountless of script convenience and plot holes..

This film is supposed to weigh on the consequence of Man of steel and yet the ending is pretty much the same as previous film with half of the city being leveled again. I might not be a die-hard comic book fans but this film failed to highlight what Batman & Superman stand for and what made them great. On top of these, it spent too much time re-establishing Batman in this universe I honestly think they should go for a Batman Solo film before this and stop having so many dream sequences (the cameos are pushing it)!

Hey suddenly Iron Man 2 isn't that bad. What do you guys think? I will be watching Justice League regardless, I mean why not?

PS: Batman is the only reason I am giving this film a 5

title: Amazing Movie, love it.
review:
This movie is great. I am a big superman and batman fan and I love this movie. Can't understand why it is getting such a poor response. Amazing looking scenes. Zack Snyder did a great job.The fight scenes were great, however they are a bit short. Too much is going at some points though.

Ben Affleck as Batman was an amazing choice. He is possibly the best Batman/ Bruce Wayne so far. Henry Cavvil does a good job as the superman. the DC Expanded universe has made. Wonder woman was amazing, Gal Gadot did a great job. Jesse Eisenberg plays the Lex Luthor this movie created well, however, this is a very different Lex Luthor to the one from the comics or past movies.

The movie had a very dark approach to everything. It is quite intense and is almost like a thriller. This movie has got me exited for the upcoming DC movies in the coming years, especially the 2017 Wonder Woman movie with Gal Gadot. The soundtrack for this movie is great. Hanz Zimmer has done a great job as usual. Wonder Woman's theme is especially good and is the most memorable. Lex Luthor's theme is almost cliché, however it works well with the character and makes you feel uncomfortable, making you fear Luthor more.

In conclusion I enjoyed the movie very much, the casting was excellent and the scenes were amazing.

title: Highly entertaining
review: From the first minute to the last I was throughly entertained by this movie and totally engaged. Some people have complained about the editing and plot and they may have a point, but in my opinion it doesn't spoil the overall experience. The action is great which is to be expected from Zack Snyder, the man is a genius when it comes to visuals. The characters are interesting and I was pleasantly by Jesse Eisenbergs Lex. Ben Afflecks Batman is fantastic, he totally steals every scene he's in, I can't believe so many people were against his casting, he's absolutely brilliant! The film moves at a good pace and attempts to juggle various plot points involving characters like Lois Lane who is as heavily involved here as she was was in Man Of Steel. I would have like more emphasis placed on motives for the conflicts that occur and a bit more reasoning behind why some of the characters have a dislike for each other but again this doesn't spoil the experience. All in all this was a great movie going experience I was never bored and the 2 hours 31 minutes run time flew by.

title: Batman V Superman - A View of the Film and a Review of the Reaction
review:
My commentary regarding Batman v Superman is as much about the reaction to the movie as the movie itself. The movie is excellent. I hold a lifelong affection for DC and thought the film was excellent. My wife holds affection for me and hence came to the opening but couldn't care less about DC and thought the film was excellent.

If you love DC comics you are likely to really enjoy this film. Zack Snyder has presented something that is faithful to the comics, almost reverent at times. He is no cynic, far from it. Much of DC, especially latter years, is dark and the film has this edge. I followed the film easily, I thought perhaps because I know so much about the DC universe. I didn't find it negative or humorless. But you know what, my wife did not find the film confusing or disorganized. It wasn't. She didn't find disturbing or excessively dark. It wasn't. Yet these are two major criticisms that have been repeated over and over within reviews of the film.

The acting was very good. Particularly Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot. However, there were not any cringe worthy portrayals and I believe that both Henry Cavill and Jesse Eisenberg hit the mark they aimed for and that these criticisms have also been extreme.

So the critics. What to think?

Well, there was definitely a siege mentality. It was excessive. I think that the movie will gravitate over time to a much better place, critically speaking. I already note a softening from some critics in subsequent articles. There is too much difference between the critics and the viewing audience for there to have not been something behind this.

My theory? It is Marvel, or should I say Disney. I think that the phenomena of Comic Book films is still one which we are reckoning with and that the conservative formula that Disney has used to date has hit a mark not only with audiences but critics. It is safe. I think that DC, or should I say Warner Bros, has not abided by the rules written so far. The Marvel films with relatively strong critical approval are nowhere near proportionally that much better than the Man of Steel or Batman v Superman films. Critics are unhappy with Warner Bros not following the formula, seemingly attempting to elevate Comic Book films to a loftier or at least a different place than Disney has taken their films. One major critic seemed most perturbed he couldn't take his young daughter to the film because to him and many others that is what these movies should be about. No more, no less.

I am not sure that another film will find that place that the Dark Knight found between the entertainment of a comic book and the quality of an exceptional film but DC is trying and in particular, Zack Snyder, is trying. I am pleased that, to date, the viewing audience has seemingly been influenced little by this critical reaction. There is room for different approaches. In fact, it is great that, just like in the comics, Marvel and DC are different. I just don't remember so many people being so angry about it when I was a kid.

title: Not the first time the general critic population and I have been in different worlds
review:
I heard it said over and over that this movie is hard to follow if you're not in the know with the DC Universe, and I can see some of that from inside-looking-out, but I have to believe there's something for everyone here. It has timeless elements of storytelling; the much heard "God vs. Man", as well as Light vs. Dark; just lots of Yin and Yang. I LOVE how they show Batman's struggles, as well as Superman's struggles, and how their ideals end up in conflict. I had heard some reviews say that during the big Bats/Supes Smack \down there's hardly any verbal exchange between the two. After watching the movie I wondered if they put on earplugs for that scene. The clash of ideals is very much at play here.

Ben Affleck's Batman? The man hasn't had the kind of career so praised for bringing the kind of gravitas that Christian Bale (whose Batman I still back to the hilt) has in various roles, but he's got solid acting chops, and that combined with his lifelong love of Batman gave us a Batman IN SPADES!!!! I shirk not to say he's now my all-time favorite Batman. He defied all previous conventions of what kind of physique can be expected from an actor, and how well he can throw his weight around with it. He awesomely played the public facade for Bruce Wayne, brooding private Bruce Wayne, and tough-as-nails/don't-trifle-with Batman.

Henry Cavill once again delivered beautifully as Clark Kent/Superman, and his wanting to help people, along with hurt that no one will accept him runs deep to where you have to cry for the man. The man deserves a place alongside Christopher Reeve in Man of Steel honors.

There was a universal fear that Gal Gadot would become the Sarah Palin of the DCEU, and I would say not even close. The movie makes limited use of her, in such a way that would be expected in a movie that leaves her name out of the title. I say she positively adds to the movie whenever she shows up. Jesse Eisenberg as Luthor? You do get just that, a Jesse Eisenberg Lex Luthor, and I understand if that doesn't work for some, but for me it worked in spades.

I read about the plot being too crammed. Not to me. It has become quite clear that I can be entertained by setup of future related movies if it's handled right. For all the understanding of other DC heroes being included, they don't clog up the movie by any means. One thing I will understand when it comes to those uninitiated in the deeper DC universe that is akin to Thor's hallucination in "Avengers: Age of Ultron", just know you could easily get the idea with a simple Google search.

In the end it's about personal struggles, reconciliation and redemption; and BRILLIANTLY depicted. I wholly adore this movie

title: Great movie and that's it what it is!
review:
Nothing will ever be perfect for everyone, but there's really not much, if not nothing, to criticize about this movie! It's a very good movie, don't pay any attention to those who try to diminish it as if they had to show how much they allegedly know about movie-making by destroying such a good works! A movie's main purpose is to entertain the viewers in such a way that they get to sucked in into the story, and that's something this one made effortlessly! And that's something the so called critics seem to have forgotten! I truly and honestly don't understand the hate of some of them! It's as if they were luring in the shadows, just waiting to jump out and criticize, because that's what it's expected from them, not because they actually have anything bad to say! So instead of being creative ourselves, why not be destructive, it's much easier! Just silly! Great story, great plot, even greater acting (by all of the actors! For all of the characters!) and also a believable take for a superhero movie, something which comes directly from the pages of comics and thus fantasy! And still... you can identify yourself with the any of the main characters! You feel the tiredness, the angst, the doubt, the rage, the fear,...

I read somewhere that Affleck was Batman and I must agree! Affleck is Wayne, Cavill is Kent! After Bale for Batman and specially after the iconic Reeve for Superman these two guys had no easy task to master, but guess what, they did it! They pulled it off! These 2 are just as legitimate as any other before them! Very interesting to see what happens during such fights from our human perspective! Somehow unsettling but also so real! I would truly give this film an 8.5 or a 9 (as nothing would ever get a 10 and there's always a little something one would like a bit more if it had been made as it was in one's head), but since I've seen some people trolling around and giving it 1 or 2 just to drag it down, well... that's not fair and I'd like to try to oppose it! So badly that I even created my account just to be able to review this film and vote for it! Eisenberg delivers an interesting Luthor, not the kind you would be used to or expecting, but not less legitimate nor believable! Gadot marks a new era, a more than welcome one, for such an important DC character as Wonder Woman, with such a refreshing but strong presence. All of the rest of the cast did a great job! Directing was awesome! The pace! Two and half hours which didn't feel as such! Just the right combination of depth and action, darkness and hope...

Doomsday and his origin story, yes, somehow different than in the comics, but in its essence, just as terrible, just as discomforting and unsettling! They did a great job honoring the source material and also the looks, being respectful towards it, but at the same time trying to create something new enough to not be too predictable and setting the first stone for a new storytelling! People tend to forget that these two characters have been around for over 75 years, being thought a and redefined over this time in countless comics and other media over and over again, changes have been made so often, so many different creative teams, so many stories, so many different artists, drawers, writers, sometimes even quite opposite and contradictory between them... what do those so called critics want in 2.5 hours?! What kind of miracle are they expecting?! How would anyone truly expect to have every single aspect of every single story in one film?!

Marvel has been building up a scaffold, a framework for it's story over the last 8 years! This one's just the second one of hopefully a whole bunch to come to tell a complete story! Don't get me wrong, I'm a huge Marvel fan, maybe even bigger than a DC one, but I do know how to appreciate their differences and the other kind of storytelling! I'm looking forward to see more of it and I hope this movie and all of the involved get the recognition they deserve for doing such a great work! Affleck was great! I always believed in him as Batman! I'm sure he'll make even better (should that even be possible?!) in his next solo movie! Irons, well, what do you think?! Of course he's good! A different kind of Alfred, but a very likable and appealing one! Cavill is the new Superman! Adams is Lane (I didn't buy it that much in Man of Steel, but now I have no doubt!). Eisenberg is the new Luthor and will turn to be the one people would have been waiting! Great movie! Don't let anyone tell you otherwise! Don't let it pass you by!

PS1 I went with a friend of mine who usually has very high expectations and who was somehow skeptical (although he committed himself to stay open and to not have any kind of actual expectation) as for him Batman was Bale and no one else, and other than Nolan's was quite difficult to imagine, and ha was surprised and excited about the movie! He said that's a movie to buy as soon as it comes out for home media!

PS2 Maybe the only problem the movie has was not in the movie itself, but in the second theatrical trailer as Doomsday was shown! As a bit too much of the plot was revealed beforehand! Less trailer would have meant more movie! And I think that might have been part of the problem with some!

title: Would have been better if it was not so long.
review:
From the moment the movie starts, you get the feeling that this is going to be a long two and a half hours.

Batman v Superman is filled with a lot of cool scenes that were so unnecessary. It was filled with flashbacks and dream sequences that just seem to over bloat the blockbuster. It works for a comic book,but not as well for a comic book movie.

Speaking of which, as a fan of the comics, and equally a fan of movies, I'm caught in a huge dilemma. The inaccuracy of the characters sometimes got in the way of my movie pleasure. That should not be a big deal and you might say they have to change a lot of things to fit a comic to a movie. Not in this day and era, and not with these two guys who have been movie stars (especially Bats) for more than 30 years.

The story being told about Batman targeting superman for being a threat to the globe is a great one and told interesting, but this film dumbed down Batman and made Superman too dark, something I forgive director Zack Snyder for in Man of Steel but now he's butchering two comic book (and movie) Icons.

And The Third Icon in the movie, Wonder Woman. She was a big help to the film in my book. Would have rather seen her in her own movie first, but there is an action scene in the film that makes up for it.

The film is not as bad as the faults I pointed out. For those who doubted Ben Affleck's capability to play the Dark Knight, you're going to have to eat crow on this one. Batfleck was amazing. He was holding the movie on his shoulders. Good thing he got real jack up for the role, his shoulders were ridiculous, and the battle scenes when Batman is doing hand to hand combat were thrilling. He's a devoted actor who completely respected the character and brought it like Christian Bale did for Nolan.

I also loved Jeremy Irons as Alfred. Makes me wish he had more scenes.

Also thought Jesse Eisenberg could have been a better Lex Luther, but it feels like they were more adjusting Lex Luther to Jesse Eisenberg rather than the other way around. Big mistake.

The action scenes in the movie was magnificent. This is something that I always like about Zack Snyder's style. He's just real good at making CGI look real good. When the superheroes fight, there is a lot of style to the movement that works for the overall picture, and it never feels that CGI is being used for a gimmick.

As much as I like all the action and the story, and watching these two iconic characters go at, the movie's biggest issue was that it did not need to be so long. Just a lot of things going on that do not push the movie forward. You know how all those Marvel movies have those after credit scenes that make you cheer in excitement? Batman v Superman had those scenes within the movie and it did not make me cheer.

It's always a bad sign when all I can think about is going to the bathroom during the film (it's like they are trying to evolve the human race to have bigger bladders with these comic book films). If the movie was really that good I would be only focus on it.

Good, not great and could have been better. C minus.

title: Some Injustice
review:
Batman v Superman is a very average movie. DC has been lagging far behind Marvel in the presentation of it's superheroes. Batman (Christian Bale) was the only modern DC movie that was good, the rest have been average to below average and BVS is the same.

Ben Affleck is alright as Batman. He is not good enough to propel the movie to it's potential, but he is not bad enough to destroy the project. He is just there.

Henry Cavill is at least decent as Superman. He will never make anyone forget Christopher Reeves, but he is better than any Superman actor since Reeves.

The movie is long and it is boring. There is so many extra scenes just to get a HUGE cast time on film. They have to fit in Amy Adams (who is as average as Affleck in the film), Diane Lane, flashback scenes for Wayne's parents (we all know the story - it does not have to be seen in every film that has Batman), visions of Kevin Costner, and time for Laurence Fishburne. We then also have to make time for Gal Gadot and the Wonder Woman character and show previews (in the film) of Aquaman (GAG), The Flash and Cyborg as promotional material for Justice League.

The script, the direction and the timing are tedious. It felt like a long movie. But the biggest flaw was Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luther. He was beyond bad - he was an injustice to the character and it was so evident he was not the right choice for the role. Every scene he is in brings the film down.

The movie would have gotten an 8 for the effects and the action, but I am giving it a 7 overall because of the acting and the script. Eisenberg could have made me rethink the grade and made it a 5/6 because he is that bad.

title: Its not a Marvel film so stop comparing it to one. A DC triumph (spoilers probably)
review:
Short answer: It is not a Marvel film so stop trying to make it one or compare it to one. its 2 and a half hours because DC is trying to set up a universe in one movie instead of 4 independent back story movies. The story line is dark and broody, like the topic they discuss, its long but not too drawn out, and the fight scenes are both very well choreographed and easy and enjoyable to follow. PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD STOP COMPARING IT TO THE NOLAN TRILOGY BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE SAME UNIVERSE, CONFLICTS OR STYLE.

Long Answer: The more I read critics and other reviews I keep seeing a trend of people asking why the movie was not funny, or comical, or why is it so long or dark.

First, its a DC film and if anyone knows the comics and back stories of superman and batman they are not exactly joking or comical characters, they are very serious.

two, Zack Snyder is a very purist director when it comes to the source material. See Watchmen, and 300 for example. This movie takes from two of the biggest superman/batman comics out there: Death of Superman and The Dark Knight Returns. So before you judge the film realize that is source material is dark and serious so too will be the film. Fight scenes are darker and filled with rain to add to the ambiance of the fight and create another dimension to it.

But back to the major issue, I feel that more and more people are comparing this to the avengers movies and their like standalone films. This is wrong because it is, once again, a completely different universe with different struggles and characters. Marvel decided to take their's on a much different approach then DC. Marvel focused on people without powers but heroic desire and builds them into the marvel universe. (even the xmen are very vulnerable despite their powers). Marvel characters always fight someone bigger then them or stronger but only the hulk is completely understandable and they still downplay that tremendously.

DC on the other hand came out with Man of Steel about Superman. Who is unkillable, bullet proof and unstoppable. This off the bat makes a universe completely different since reality now has to be bent to house such a character. As such Batman Vs Superman tries and succeeds in doing just that. This film should mark the first successful instance of a true superpower fight since Man of Steel. Where supersonic punches and earth shattering explosions fit the universe and do not feel like Michael Bay is just trying to blow 5 grand.

Go see the film if you wish but please just do research before seeing a film. Not every film is going to be a perfect story lines that neatly ends like the Marvel films. Superheros do not all fit one typecast.

title: Nobody does it better...than....
review:
Marvel. Period.

I've had a problem with the writing of various DC properties, but this has to be something like a new low for WB/DC, with almost every plot device being shown as explicitly shoehorned-in, and completely inorganic.

But hey, the good things first.

Refreshing, how this one, and its predecessor, deal with death, and the impact of superhero smack-downs in the real world around us. From that perspective, there's more meat on the bones here, than in Marvel's theatrical works. Thanks to Frank Miller?

The movie looks (Larry Fong, reuniting with director Snyder after Amir Mokri shot 'Man of Steel', and he's worked with his director on 300, Watchmen and Sucker Punch, among others), and sounds great too (Junkie 'Fury Road' XL supporting Hans 'Cymbals' Zimmer, and quite a few great sound designers). What they end up doing, following the character's dark arc with one of the superheroes' nemeses, was also a bold move, in spite of the end cop-out, which, to be fair, there was/is no escaping.

Cavill makes for a good Superman, Affleck for a great Batman (almost go DKR on him with some great mano-a-mano sequences given to him, that he bravely shoulders), Fishburne for a great Perry White (wish he'd had more scenes), Callan Mulvey (300: Rise of an empire, Captain America:Winter soldier!!!) and Gal Gadot, shoehorned-in, though not as badly as a few others, makes for a surprisingly great Un-Amazonian Wonder Woman.

Holly Hunter and Jeremy Irons are also given good parts, and their presence, as well as performances, elevate the rather shoddy material everyone is forced to work with.

SPOILERS, SPOILERS, SPOILERS.....(but not for people following the development of these properties online)in addn to the main warning before the review.

Jason Momoa and Chris Pine look to be cast well in the photographs they appear in (and the standalone upcoming flicks). Tao 'The Wolverine' Okamoto is lovely, and deserved more scenes and better characterization.

Why did they not have Grant Gustin instead, since one cannot even see Ezra Miller playing the same character, since he has nothing but a blink-n-u-miss-it gone-in-a-Flash kinda thankless role anyway? Snyder has spoken about it, but his explanation makes no sense to me, given the shoehorned-in context within this flick. Smacks of a big deal being made outta nothing.

Now, I will not be watching this again, in any format, like I usually try doing so for those movies I feel I enjoyed, or need to understand more. I do not regret watching this one, its like a juggernaut that's inescapable, and I will be checking out the standalone movies plus both the upcoming JLA flicks - they're inevitable viewing. And yeah, I was waiting for the movie to end. And I've watched longer movies than this one, patiently.

The writing sucks, and I'm kinda wanting to pin it on David S Goyer (not Terrio, who has only a few credits, including the Batffleck connection, Argo), due to wildly inconsistent work (contrast Dark City/Blade I and II/Dark Knight/Flashfwd/Da Vinci's demons to the likes of Blade:Trinity/Dark Knight Rises/Ghost Rider:Spirit of vengeance/Unborn/Jumper). It sucks when Batman has 10 minutes to do something, and its something to do with the complete inconsistency of (all things) his suit (not just that, but...).

Jesse Eisenberg. One of the worst performances, and characterizations, ever. The campy Gene Hackman made for a better Luthor, while Spacey's chrn./perf. will remain the best, even though it was in a middling Superman movie.

The redcapes are coming, the redcapes are coming... The bell has been rung (ergo, you cannot unring it, ergo...) Ding ding ding ding ding ding ding....

All the stupid dream sequences. Could have all been completely edited out.

The stupid characterization of Scoot McNairy, not just wasting this underrated actor's talents, like they do that of Hunter, but also trying to make 1 character stand for so many things, all at once, all in the same place, and in the same context.

Doomsday: the birth. Doomsday=Hulk?

Martha? Really? Seriously? And bring me the head of ..... 2016, folks!

Diane Lane and her diner TV-viewing, and all of her meaningless/impactless platitudes. Even the Kevin Costner dream- banter sequence (randomly/unnecessarily/gratuitously inserted) was better than when the camera was on her, and this is like the complete opposite of how it was in 'Man of steel'.

Lois Lane. Sigh. Why Amy why? Not sure the money's that good, but I honestly wouldn't know that it might be.

And why's Morgan Freeman not on-hand when you need him? Not kidding. He was always the conscience in the Nolan trilogy, albeit impotent, but a great sounding-board of sorts. Nolan executive producing this one, to me, did not seem to bring anything at all to the table this time around, unlike his blessings on 'Man of steel'.

Snyder's not a bad filmmaker by any stretch, and his rendering of Alan Moore and Dave Gibbon's 'Watchmen', especially the director's cut, is one of my favorite movies of all time, and that edit is 3 hours and 40 minutes long! He also made a great Zombie movie, 'Dawn of the dead'. '300' was alright, and 'Man of steel' just about passed muster. Sucker Punch, imo, had some great moments, but ended up leaving a largely bad taste, but has to be appreciated for being an original attempt at whatever it was going for, no matter that they PG13'd something that would be more comfy in R/NC17 territory. This, to me, regardless of whose fault it actually was, is Snyder's absolute worst movie to- date, and I am disappointed, since it had many, many things going for it, including Snyder himself.

review:
Finally a superhero movie that wasn't all about joking the whole time when things were being blown up or people were dying. BvS is a great comic book movie. Like watchman it can be taken right from a graphic novel. Now what I mean is BvS is kinda shot like a comic book plays out if you actually read them. A lot gets thrown in action and story alike. Also if you did read them Zach did great at sticking w the comic book mythology but adding his own twists (great visuals too). Now I am a true Batman fan and I can truly say Ben Affleck Batman/Bruce is the best ever portrayed In acting, look, and combat. Still Bale was perfect for the Dark Knight trilogy but Batfleck is perfect for this one.Henry was great as he was in MOS. Those of you who disagree w Man of Steel or BvS is probably because you like the cheesy Marvel style in general. I like marvel too but If you really look Marvel is all pretty repetitive, childish, & cheesy besides Deadpool, and Dawn of Justice was something new (that's my only marvel bash). Wonder women was great and I'm glad she wasn't in it a lot,just enough. Now as for Jesse as Lex I was least Optimistic about at first,but this was a different type of Luther that you start to like as the film progresses and by the end he actually sold me. The story between the 2 icons and their feud was well done and compelling. All around I see what people are saying about the plot being packed and A LOT going on (why is that a problem?). But also DC has a lot of catching up to do and I really think they attempted that w this movie and the cameos (not to excessive and still very entertaining). Its a 2 and a half hour movie and it seems shorter to me the way it is edited because it keeps you interested instead of playing a scene out for too long. I mean yes there is a short scene that tells us about future justice league, but don't forget the movie is called "Dawn of Justice" and of course they're will be something to introduce some connection in the Justice League/DC Universe. Hell Nick Fury and marvels little end credit scenes did that in literally every marvel movie. I loved how dark, gritty, and serious it was which probably most Marvel fans or children wouldn't like, but again it is something way different then anything we have seen in superhero movies and a different kind of plot finally(OK that was it w marvel knocks)

The Action was amazing especially the big fight between The Dark Knight & Man of Steel. EPIC! The second time around I caught a lot more that I didn't catch the first time. If there is one little thing I can say that annoyed me a little it was Lois Lane. Amy Adams is a great Lois lane but she is involved a little too much and plays damsel in distress a little to much, but not enough to make me freak out. Again my friends that have all seen this movie and as I can see many other audience members agree this is a great movie. I still don't know why all the hate by some of these critics. they don't change my opinion. I can say a lot more but I don't want to spoil anything. So just see it for yourself. You wont regret it.

title: Near perfect film adaptation of the DC Comics Universe!
review: Been a DC Comics fan my whole life, and have waited 30 years to see Batman and Superman on the big screen together. What can I say other than this movie is fantastic! They really nailed the tone of the DC Universe. Not cheesy at all, which is a huge accomplishment. I feel like the hardest thing to do on the DC side is to bring all these characters into a believable reality, and this film is incredibly well grounded. I also feel like it's difficult to have none of these characters feel hokey or campy, but this film accomplished that 1000%. Top shelf performances by cast and crew all around! Is it dark? Yes, as it absolutely should be. Is it fun? Hell yes! I can't remember the last time a dark film felt like this much of a good time. It is not moody or brooding, as countless critics have said. In fact, quite the opposite. This is a film that gets right down to business, and despite the long runtime, goes by so fast you'll wish it was even longer. This is a film I want to see over and over again!

title: Classic moral story about power and it's corruptive consequences
review:
Superman vs Batman is an amazing film and although some will take issue with what I am about to say, I feel it is the best Superman film ever made. Which brings me to the topic of why this film is so hated by many. Watching it tonight for the second time, the first being at the theater on opening day months ago, my initial feelings are confirmed. The storyline of this film is unlike any other of DC's superhero films I have seen. This film has an adult theme, moral, message to the story. It isn't another dumb kid comic book action film.

This film covers the repercussions of absolute power. How absolute power corrupts. How nefarious interests seek to manipulate power to bring about its own interest into realization. The film also covers self-sacrifice for the better good of humanity.

Oh heck, by the end of the film, it borrows the story of the crucifixion and self-sacrifice of Christ into a DC superhero adaption of the Christian Paschal mystery. It even has powerful symbolisms of the crucifixion when they lower Superman's body from the top of the rock. In that scene, the upper left-hand corner of the frame you have several telephone/power poles that resemble crosses while superman's body is lowered. Two women take possession of Superman's body. Sound familiar? And the symbolism of the dirt from on top of Superman's casket rising up from the lid and the grave. The hologram of the demonic creature Lex Luther made inside the ship after they destroyed Doomsday. The post-apocalyptic world in batman's dream with fire and destruction. Lex Luther even states, "The devils don't come from hell beneath us." Then a reporter on the televised newscast states, "What we've done is we project ourselves onto him. The fact is maybe he's not some sort of devil or Jesus character. Maybe he's just a guy trying to do the right thing." Then later in the film, Lex Luther says, "So, if a man won't kill god the devil will do it!" What does Lex do in this film? He throws the world into chaos through the use of manipulation and lies. Bringing the good of the world into conflict with each other to bring about destruction. Lex=Devil?

How could the critics not see the symbolism used in this film? I personally found the story coherent, clear with a strong message. Superman vs Batman, even though it's a DC Superhero movie, has adult themes embedded in the story and requires some critical thinking to understand the story. Look past the tights, spandex, capes, and explosions and you will see the underlying moral of the story in this film.

Nope, not getting religious on anyone. I don't care if the viewer is religious or an atheist, but it's no denying this film as a strong moral theme relevant to any time in history despite what the "critics" have stated about it. If you are going to watch this film, go into it with an open mind. It's not about Christianity, but about good and bad that is universal regardless of whatever belief system you may subscribe to or don't subscribe to. For this reason, I would rate this film a 9/10. I often get a much better understanding of films when I see them at home than when I see them in the theater. Sometimes I wonder why I even bother going to the theater at all.﻿

title: A better title would have been 'How Lex Lost His Hair'
review:
Spoiler alert: I did not see Man of Steel, on the other hand, I don't remember getting any indication that this was the spiritual successor to that.

Would seeing the prequel have saved the movie? That would be miraculous. Because mostly the plot just does not make sense. It's like they tried to make a 10 hour movie and cut it down to 2.5 hours, while making it still feel like you were sitting there for 4 hours.

You sit there for the entire time going 'where is this going?' with no real aha moment even though you feel like in the end some grand master plan all came together. But from the first 5 minutes of the film, when the bats lift Wayne up, I feel like the movie jumped the shark and it still went downhill from there.

And really, whats with all the prophetic dreams that don't play out in this film and turn out to be teasing a sequel?? I mean most people that like Superman and/or Batman don't read the comics and have no clue what the film could be alluding to and so they're just like, what was that?? (and the subplots you thought you were going to see rise from that just make it feel like a longer movie with more boredom and confusion)

Sorry this review seems so disjointed but I'm trying to make some sparse points that I feel need emphasis without giving away any of the movie.

Two final things I left the movie with - It seems to scapegoat the Russians as the bad guys a bit too much. Just 2 instances but as their prime minister has just declared a resumption of the cold war, Russian audiences would easily point to this as subtle US propaganda (or worse, a reflection that we really do see them as the enemy).

And secondly, why train and prep so hard when you can just make your new armor with a coating of kryptonite? That's what I would have done. That's what I thought he did (because honestly, did he really think thicker metal was going to protect him from Superman?)

But really, this review reads like the movie itself. Disjointed with minor good parts but mostly it just seems to go on and on with no point. And it doesn't even elaborate on some key points that would have made the whole thing a lot more coherent!

title: Great movie for the fans
review:
In a world of extraordinary humans and the God like Kryptonians, Power can not be innocent.

With its high octane action drama, extraordinary visuals, and great cast, Batman vs Superman won't disappoint the DC fan-boys, but it requires a patient yet enjoyable viewing from rest of the audience.

Zack Snyder's saga goes a step beyond the conventional Superhero movies and gives us a visual delight, adding a different tone to the superhero genre by exploring into the beliefs, uncertainties, dreams, nightmares, ego and pride.

The film as a whole is evenly paced, intense yet enjoyable. The characters are dark and grim. Ben Affleck is amazing as the Batman, it won't be justified to compare his Batman with that of Bale, as both the roles explore a different perspective of the character, as imagined by Snyder and Nolan. Jeremy Irons is good as Alfred,though he has a limited role. Wonder Woman will surprise many and Gal Gadot makes us believe she owns the character and now we have even higher expectations from the Justice league. Henry Cavill carries forward from Man of Steel and beyond any doubt is the most convincing Superman ever. People who remember Jesse Eisenberg from The Social Network would be amazed to see a very different role from the actor.

The CGI is pretty good most of the times. the nightmare scenes specially stand out. The Batman Superman face-off lives to the expectations, but ends in a rather weak way. Doomsday sequence appears flat and clichéd, only to be saved by the awesome Gal Gadot. Background score by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL is mind blowing throughout the movie, specially the electric guitar theme which follows the Wonder Woman will send down chills.

Zack Snyder's visual style of action sequences is impressive, supported by great cinematography and background scores, making him one of the greatest director in action genre.

Overall, a good movie, which would be cheered a lot by DC fans and draw mixed reviews from the rest.

title: Brilliant!
review:
I've been waiting for this film for over a year and prior to watching this I did a Batman and Superman film marathon leading up to watching this one.

I'm glad I watched Man of Steel a few days before watching this one as this film takes place during and after the events of this film. At the start we see Bruce Wayne's view of the Superman v General Zod fight and the destruction to Metropolis which sets the scene nicely that Superman may cause more damage, and can an alien be trusted?.

I knew Ben Affleck would be great as an older Batman as he was DareDevil many moons ago so for him it was playing a hero again, and he nailed it as Batman. I'm looking forward to what he brings to the character in future Batman films and exploring this character more, especially with the scene of him looking at the Robin suit. I also thought the chemistry between Batman and Alfred was great.

Also great casting was Gal Gadet as Wonder Woman, she was amazing and stole the show. I can't wait for the WW film out soon to explore her character better too.

Why am I not giving this film a 10? Lex Luthor - not the best choice of casting, and I couldn't get past that stupid hair. He brought a different side to Lex (a more psychotic side) which was good, but would have better had it been done by the Joker teaming up with Lex. With an older Batman I think it should have been an older Lex Luthor and for me the best actor to have ever played this character was Kevin Spacey (Superman Returns).

The other funny thing I find funny when reading other peoples reviews is that people moan that Lex Luthor wouldn't have had the logos for the other meta humans (Flash, Cyborg, Wonder Woman). Yes I agree that he wouldn't have created these logos BUT I think this was a little something the producers did just to get us excited about the upcoming Justice League film...and yes I am excited. Roll on 2017!!!

Overall, a great film with lots of action with some great acting. I'm looking forward to the other DC related films out in the years to come starting with Suicide Squad at the end of 2016 and Justice League next year.

review:
Lex Luthor is pitting Batman against Superman, disgracing him, hoping one will kill the other, leaving Luthor free to... do ... things, one supposes. It isn't really explained.

Really? 2 hours build up to that??? Come on... that's it... and all of the sudden Lex has a back-up plan, he had another kryptionian bastard on ice, and added some gene manipulation making it the ultimate monster. And they both fight the monster... I won't spoil who gets killed in the end, besides the monster, but the world is in agony, and they spend 20 minutes of the bloody movie showing us... Really, watch it on DVD/blu ray some time, when you are really bored.. but only if you are really, really bored.

title: It's A Dawn of Justice, alright!
review:
Warning: HERE BE SPOILERS!

The huge gap between aggregated RT meter and audience score really reflects how out of tune with the reality the critics are when facing with DC's movies, especially one coming from "Snyderverse". It feels like there's a kind of anti-Snyder movement.

On the movie itself, I think people knows by this point that I REALLY LIKE THIS MOVIE. It's superhero movie for the grown up. Snyder is doing away with the introductions. Everybody knows about Superman and Batman. Wonder Woman is slightly changed, but it's mostly show, not tell. And the introduction of her background is done in one of the most efficient in-movie advertisement for the next movie ever. Her appearance in the movie is also organic. Back to Superman: he is a distraught persona, but as Clark Kent and Superman. Clark Kent is facing a Perry White who doesn't believe in the power of paper to uncover darkness anymore. Superman is facing both adoration and accusations from people.

Accusations that is distilled in the form of a paranoid Batman. Bruce Wayne is matured person, a beloved boss who loves his employees, and a respected public figure. Batman is a devilish presence in the dark corners of Gotham. Both shows vehemence toward Superman. This is balanced somewhat with an Alfred that is loyal to his master but also not afraid to mock him openly. The loyal guardian also support this his master's crusade to find a weapon that can kill Superman, all the way until they cross path with Lex Luthor.

A truly manipulative, blackmailing, ego maniacal Luthor unlike we have ever seen before. Literally. He has fabulous hair. He also has tapped into the power of surveillance in order to accumulate information and knowledge he can use. "Knowledge is power" is subverted in the hands of Lex Luthor. Which leads us to the event unfolding in the movie. You see, it all boils down to Lex Luthor seeking to deface God. His scheme involves smearing the name of Superman, agitating people into hating him, and dragging Batman to fight him.

All the while Luthor himself descends into literal and figurative madness. Creating monsters on all sides: minion monster, manipulated monster, and a literal monster of deformity born of man's hubris. The scheme explodes in the sequence of fighting that actually feels strange in this movie. It feels it has to be there simply because this is a superhero movie. But its presence is truly, truly welcome. After all, we got to see Wonder Woman in action for the first time in big screen; sword, shield, and lasso in a cacophony of big punches, laser beams, and explosions. Explosions of the magnitude by which no Marvel movies has done before.

And the finale of that fight, man, that finale. It truly gives a drive for the heroes to seek others like them.

They need them, those whose presence is known, in order to face the darkness that is about to come.

It is, after all, a Dawn of Justice.

title: Batman vs Superman....Dawn of Tedium
review:
Its amazing how much money can be shelled out to make a boring action movie. Batman vs Superman reasserts this notion, in mind numbing style.

Whats really absent from this action movie is action. Instead, you get a lot of half baked introspection and hackneyed,undergraduate philosophy about the injustices of the world.

The actual action, such as it is, is squeezed into the latter half of the movie, much like Ben Affleck's Batman in his ridiculous, mechanical super hero suit. Even then, what we get is uninspiring action sequences that fizzle out before they ever get off the ground.

Simply put, there's not a lot to like here. My advice, give this one a pass. Three out of ten from me.

title: A DC Cinematic Crisis? I don't think so.
review:
I'm surprised at how I actually liked the movie despite all the negative reviews it seems to be having all over the internet. More often than not I've found myself in agreement with the consensus.

I was skeptical of this movie at first, to the point that I set my mind that I'll only give this movie the time of day if not for how Batman is going to be portrayed this time around. After watching it, I'm glad that I got more than just that.

You see, I wasn't impressed much by Man of Steel but I didn't hate it either. And as far as Zack Snyder's body of work goes, none of it has really impressed me as well, but I did enjoy them all immensely. From Dawn of the Dead to this latest outing, oh I enjoyed them all, yes indeed.

I once described Zach Snyder's directorial abilities by comparing him to a certain type of rock song - the kind that has lots of guitar solos, shifting time signatures, and over-the-top drum fills, but no catchy CHORUS to sing along to. He's all technicality and virtuosity that comes so naturally, but when it finally comes to a part when you need to put some heart in order for it to have some semblance of a song, the execution is left a tad bit forced. Oh but it's there. My experience on this movie is pretty much the same, which is why I'm giving it the 8 stars. I anticipated this movie as a test of how much Zach Snyder's story-telling capabilities have evolved this time around, and judging from what I saw, meh, still not by much, which is why most critics and wannabe-critics hated it. I can look past all of that though. I enjoyed this movie immensely, and one big factor for me in considering that a movie is good is if I was immersed in it during the viewing. I look at the repeat viewing possibility, and for this movie I consider it pretty high for myself. I'd definitely watch it again when given the opportunity.

One thing I loved about it (which is weird I guess), is I felt that Zach Snyder really, really, REALLY, really wanted to make a Batman movie all his life. I could see signs of this as early as his take on The Watchmen. He seemed really eager and excited. It's just too bad that when the opportunity finally came for him, Warner Bros. had different plans. The big company wanted a piece of the cinematic universe cake and so Zach was caught between juggling his chance to finally direct his Batman piece, and at the same time sowing the seeds for a much demanded Justice League silver screen debut. Oh and there's the little blue & red guy's story that he has to continue as well. It was an unfair challenge, but the business demands and so you gotta have something.

It is a testament to Marvel's success in recent years that their work have become the benchmark of a superhero movie's entertainment value, at least as far as the general movie-going audience is concerned. So when the same group views a DC movie, the reactions are often divided. The fans though, oh they will definitely get this movie, yes they will, hardcore DC fans especially. The rest however? The critics? The general movie-going audience? Let them be divided. Let them suffer the loss of such simple pleasures. It may be a riot, yes, just like what's happening all over the internet right now, where opinions are as polarized as north and south poles on a really bad solar storm. DC's still gonna rake in the cash on this one despite the negative press, and their cinematic universe is underway either way, with or without you (queue U2 song into...).

The thing with DC is that they have always done it their own way, and that means just basically putting their content out there and letting people be the judge, and they've been living by this approach for the past two decades. Just look at the huge body of work they've accumulated with animated features and shows which has become highly respected along with their never ending supply of TV shows. They can do this because they know that their characters are more popular and have been household names far longer than Marvel's or any other comic book company's. The burden of introduction is not so heavy with DC, unlike with Marvel where a lot of time and careful thought goes into setting the background and managing possible perceptions of the target viewers/audience before committing a character or storyline to a live action adaptation.

I know I may be in the minority on how I feel about this movie. Again, it's probably because I didn't really expect a lot from it. There were a lot of flaws. Maybe it was because I didn't have the wife with me when I watched it, just our 8 year old, who was obviously bored on the exposition parts but was very much alive during the beatdowns obviously. Maybe it's really just the Batman fan in me, and seeing him finally realized in those action sequences that I've so long been waiting for is more than enough reason for me to rewatch this movie. The way I see it, I got a good Batman movie with commercials of other Justice League members on the side, with Wonder Woman being the main feature trailer.

If my reception to DC's cinematic universe may have been lackluster before, I'm definitely more excited now.

title: Wasted Production
review:
The movie is messy, loud, and needs a tub of glue to bring the disparate story lines together. This movie needs to be edited more as some parts like the dream sequences were completely irrelevant to the movie. The monster at the end is so generic that it is laughable. What a waste of 250 million dollars! What i found distracting was the soundtrack - which is consistently amplified at 10/10 with no build up - its far too loud at all times, even when it is not necessary.

At the center of this mess, is a script that does not make sense. If you're used to watching the second trilogy of the Batman movies, you will see a big drop in the quality of script and coherence (and intelligence) of this movie. The movie is more a CGI centered production than a carefully plotted, character driven movie. I hope this is not the sign of the subsequent movies from the DC comics franchise.

Please have another director and script writer helm the sequel to this movie ! There are so many interesting approaches to make this movie - the approach taken to this one is out of sync with the fine movie making of the Batman movies.

title: The Worst Superhero Movie Ever Made
review:
The Plot

Following his titanic struggle against General Zod, Metropolis has been razed to the ground and Superman is the most controversial figure in the world.

While for many he is still an emblem of hope, a growing number of people consider him a threat to humanity, seeking justice for the chaos he has brought to Earth.

As far as Bruce Wayne is concerned, Superman is clearly a danger to society. He fears for the future of the world with such a reckless power left ungoverned, and so he dons his mask and cape to right Superman's wrongs.

The rivalry between them is furious, fueled by bitterness and vengeance, and nothing can dissuade them from waging this war. However, a dark new threat arises in the form of a third man: one who has a power greater than either of them to endanger the world and cause total destruction!

The guy picks up the phone and we can see through the window behind him the entire city of Metropolis coming down. Building are falling, fire everywhere and Wayne says "I want you to get everyone out of the building now.' Really? On the first fireball I'd be running. It's stupid.

Who Affleck blew to get this role would be something to discover.

The movie drones on and on and feels like it's 12 hours long. It's boring beyond belief. And did i say Affleck can't act?

Alfred looks younger than him. And is totally miscast as well (Jeremy Irons).

And who cast Lex Luthor? OMG. It's like they just wanted to throw sh!t to the fan.

The movie sucks.

And did i say Affleck cannot act?

Please. I implore you. Go out in the fresh air. Don't waste your money or time on this garbage.

title: What fans have been wanting to see for 30 years
review: First let me start off by stating that there are no spoilers here and that I am a fan of both Marvel and DC so there is no biased opinion here. I walked in the theater with a level head I tried not to get all wrapped up in all the hype or all the bashing and bad talk about the movie. The movie is called Batman versus Superman and that's what I was expecting to see Batman fighting Superman but man was I in for a surprise because this movie delivers so much more and then some. Even if you are not a fan of the whole superhero genre movies you can still respect this movie for what it is and that is a great film. Visually it is stunning I would recommend you see it in IMAX that is the best possible experience in my opinion, the fight scenes down to the editing everything looked crisp and clean and very professionally done and just looks amazing on the big screen. The performances in this movie are outstanding Ben affleck as Batman kills it!!! The best Batman adaptation we have seen on screen, sorry Christian Bale. This Batman is not like any other Batman we have seen before this is the closest thing to comic book Batman we have ever gotten. Henry cavil reprising his role as Superman still does a very good job and is very believable as Superman as his portrayal of the character but it's Gal Gadot wonder women that steals the movie. She's not in the movie for very long but when she is man does she have big screen presence and it is very satisfying to see a very strong independent empowered woman character holding their own with two of the most iconic male superheroes in the history of comic books. Now let's get down to the movie itself the movie is rather long but it does not feel long the movie does a very good job of placing you in this story that they are trying to tell that time flies by. There are so many Easter eggs and references to things that are related to DC Comics in the DC universe and that was very satisfying to see as a fan. The movie does have some pacing issues and gets a bit off track in places here and there but overall the dialogue down to the performances and the action to the visuals it was a very satisfying film I will definitely be going to see it again numerous of times repeat visits

title: The most underrated movie of all time
review:
It maybe wrong to say that this movie is a masterpiece, but it is far worse to say that it wasn't worth the hype. A Batman movie through and through, it tugs at our nostalgia as Thomas and Martha die (again). But the beautifully constructed Superman (read Cavill) lacks the human part that makes him Clark Kent.

Kudos to Zack Snyder for continuing to awe us with his beautiful green room visuals. From 300, to Watchmen to BvS, Snyder has refined his story telling method. This movie draws inspiration from a lot of iconic DC comics like "The Dark Knight Returns", "Death of Superman", and many others. But all of this is apparent only to those who have any knowledge about these works.

The music, though iconic in its own sense, drowns out the dialogues, emotions and other necessary parts of the movie. But these are all of little importance as compared to the real problem with this movie. Jesse Eisenberg.

Mr. Eisenberg is a lovely actor who is known for bringing a layered persona out of a flat character. He is one of the only actors who can ever make Mark Zuckerberg seem like a nice guy. But when it comes down to playing the arch nemesis of Superman, Lex Luthor, he misses. As compared to the Titanic presence of Gene Hackman and later Kevin Spacey, he seems like a goat standing in the big leagues. Though he comes out as a beautiful tactician, intelligent and a man with a vendetta against Superman, he breaks the Tough shell that makes Lex Luthor iconic.

Affleck's portrayal of Batman is the best one yet, and yes it is better that Bale. Let me tell you why; Bale's Batman, iconic as he was was confined to his own universe fighting human problems in a human way. Affleck takes his Batman and stands toe-to-toe with Gods. He shows us what Bruce Wayne is really capable of, and that the loss of Robin has affected him in such a way that now he sees no difference between criminals and heroes. The paranoia is evident o his face, and Irons tries to play the psychiatrist multiple times.

This is one movie that you should not dream up before watching, but its importance in pop-culture will always hold. This is the best Batman movie ever, and it's flaws can be turned into winners if the comparisons to Marvel stop. For one thing is certain, If Marvel is science then DC is religion. We cannot survive without either, and no they are not the same. In short, Batman would not ask Diana if she would like a Shawarma, in the same way that Iron Man won't really put his mind to defeating Captain.

In short, stop comparing, grab some popcorn, and enjoy the movie. Its always easier to criticize.
