title: Safe & decent effort, way better than what critiques said.
review: Not simply a follow up story of MAN OF STEEL (2013), BvS: DOJ is more of a DC's formal first take to introduce its cinematic universe in a desperate attempt against the continuing huge success of MARVEL's establishments so far. And like Rome, MCU also wasn't built in a day. So, it was a huge task for Snyder & his team to live up to the expectations of finally bringing DCs 2 most beloved & 'World's finest' superheroes together on the screen for the very first time. The stake was high but the wait was long due The movie kicks off with Bruce Wayne's perspective on the destructive battle between Superman & General Zod and his ideology as well as different popular opinions regarding whether our world is ready to deal with such a super powerful & independent man from another planet which have been destroyed already. From that point the whole first half was all about this introduction & build up of all the major characters & the basic plot line of the story. The approach & execution in response to that plan wasn't perfect but at least they didn't rush to show & introduce so many things all together at a time.The second half comes with the most anticipated & "the greatest gladiator match in history"and that's the best part of the movie, IMO (though they stupidly already gave away most of those scenes in the clips, teasers & trailers officially released online). This was a much better 2nd half than MOS; liked the way they put & justified Lex Luthor's plan behind all this along with his back up plan of introducing a common threat where Gal Gabot as Wonder Woman mostly steals the show. But yeahthere were some aspects that I like to point out as the disappointments or failures. First of all, I didn't get why Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor strangely borrowed elements or character attributes from Batman's pivotal nemesis "Joker"?! At times it was indeed felt like watching a character blend of Luthor & Joker. Luthor is not only Superman's one of the major villains in the comic book stories who as 'a smart ass evil genius' often carefully team up with other popular & alien bad guys to fight against even the Justice Leaguehis characterization doesn't need to look like smarter or more devilish than what he already is in the comics or animated series. Eisenberg tried too hard here, I guess the responsibility for making him like a "Lex-Joker-Luthor" mostly goes to the writers. My 2nd disappointment was about the major elements of the popular DC Batman & Superman stories that they borrowed or get influenced by here. Not only the title itself, director Snyder even admitted in numerous interviews while making this movie that Frank Miller's epic THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS would play a major influential role in this movie, which was more than fine enough to digest & enjoy in this very first encounters between the Batsy & the Sup. But the thing that surprised me here when there was another very popular story arc emerges at the very end & heavily impacted the story & the ending. Definitely it wasn't necessary to borrow elements from 2 very fan favorite stories & then blend them together in this very first film of DCCU & the prequel story of JUSTICE LEAGUE; as if DC is running out of time to tell all the great stories at once & catch up with the MARVEL(!). As a whole, the ending was too much off beat & comes so early in the series. Lastly, the way Luthor as 'Frankenstein' launched Doomday herewas merely convincing even for the die hard DC fans! It was like one of those 60s & 70s Hammer's Dracula & Frankenstein story arcswhere sometime a drop of blood was enough for a resurrection! The screenplay was alright but sometime their frantic effort to make every single line sounded like an epic play was evident. Last but not the least, though I was one of those Batfleck haters but kudos to Ben Affleck for giving his best efforts to portray a passable Bruce Wayne & Batman here, as I still think there are much better actors out there to play this most iconic comic book action hero of all time. Loved Jeremy Irons' portrayal of Alfred also, as at times some of his style of dialog delivery & voice work highly reminded me of the greatest horror movie icons of all timeSir Boris Karloff! Overall, Snyder's BvS was a safe & decent effort, nothing much spectacular but at least he didn't ruined it this time like the heavy chaotic ending of MAN OF STEEL; surely it could have been a pure epic extravaganza but still & at least it was better than what I anticipated after all the recent negative reviews from the movie critiques.

title: Truth, Justice, Hope.
review:
First things first. This is a great movie. Go watch it now. I'm not kidding,NOW!

I'll wait.

Did you watch it? Cool, now we can talk about it. Yes, by far this is not a perfect movie and reviewers have been having a jolly good time pointing out what is wrong with it. I will do that myself a few paragraphs down. But all things considered, the final product is everything you could expect from the first live action movie featuring DC's Trinity. The action is intense, the stakes are high and the characters are iconic.

Hands down the winner of the Batman V Superman romp is Wonder Woman. She is the one with the least screen time, yet she manages to steal the show in those brief moments. I am really excited about what they can do with her character in her solo movie and in the Justice League movies. I was not sure about the casting of Gal Gadot as Diana, but man what a delight she is. She brings charm, exoticism and blood-lust for battle to the role. Just perfect. She is the true hero here.

From the point of view of the filmmakers, the star of the show is Batman, and boy, do they deliver. I never had a problem with the casting of Ben Affleck, but I was not prepared for the darkness he was going to bring to the role. Finally we get see on film that part of the Batman myth, the borderline psychopath whose obsession and paranoia can get the best of him. But they are also smart enough, and Affleck is an actor good enough, to portray the frailty, the humanity that make Batman the greatest comic book hero.

Superman on the other hand gets the short end of the stick here in basically every way. Which is a shame really, because Henry Cavill gets and embodies the character perfectly and he could do so much with it if they gave him the right material. Don't get me wrong, the arc for Supernan from Man of Steel to this movie makes perfect sense and seems pretty faithful for those of us comic book fans that got invested in the character post-Crisis. Is just that you can see that they could explore the Superman mythos for the modern world in much more depth, they could explore Clark and Lois' relationship in much more depth and they have such talented actors to do it, so the fact the we only get such broad strokes can be frustrating. On the other hand there is always the hope of better things to come.

Zack Snyder gets most of the vitriol from reviewers and commenters and I absolutely get it. However, I think the expectations that people had from him are wildly unfair. You can't compare Zack Snyder to Chris Nolan in the same way that you can't compare James Cameron to Ridley Scott. Each director has their unique style and passions and their work will reflect them, even if they are based on the same characters. In a way that is what makes film great. Nevertheless, it is undeniable that there is a certain narrowness of vision and color blindness to Snyder's body of work, and this movie suffers for it.

Maybe the shortcomings of Batman V Superman seem more palpable to me because Mad Max: Fury Road is so fresh in my memory. That film with such a dark and gritty story, set up in such a stark wasteland, still manages to be colorful and uplifting. And it does not help at all the thought that George Miller could have been at the helm of Justice League. But if we compare any film of the past five years with Fury Road, let's face it, they all are going to come up short.

So let's not waste time nitpicking and pondering what could have been. Enjoy Batman V Superman for what is is: a great thrill ride of a movie and the goddamn Dawn of Justice!

title: Dawn of Injustice To the fans
review:
I really tried my hardest to love this movie, but I simply just cant,

The first couple of the minutes of the movie are fine, then you begin to wonder when the pace will pick up. And you will still be wondering that 2/3 into the movie. Then when things becomes interesting we then OUT OF THE BLUE have a justice league setup part which is so badly placed in the movie.

That's the biggest problem with this movie, the narrative structure of the whole thing is broken. Batman and Superman don't even fight until near the end and when they do its just what the trailer showed us. Nothing much else happened in that fight. Did I mention the fight lasted like only 3 minutes? It wasn't even a good fight in my opinion, the trailers ruined it for me. Its just what the trailer showed us.

Afflecks Batman isn't the problem, Cavills superman isn't the problem, Gadots wonder woman not the problem, hell its not even Eisenbergs Luthor that's the problem. Its Zack Snyders way of structuring this movie is what let it down. Its a constant bore for about 2 hours and the fights are quite underwhelming and your most of the time left wondering "What just happened?", "Why did that just happen?"

The narrative structure is so weak, the music by Hans for the first time is not great and its basically a Justice League setup shoehorned to what otherwise could've been a great movie.

3/10 Too much Dawn of justice, Not enough Batman v Superman.

title: Very misunderstood, but it's not without it's flaws.
review: Boy did the critics strike out with this one, there are problems without a doubt, but is every film perfect? Where to begin, first of all this movie was no where near as bad as everyone is saying it is, there are far worse comic book films being released right now(looking at you Fantastic Four). If you're familiar with Zack Snyder's work than you obviously know what to expect from him in terms of style and visuals, there are some moments in the film where I instantly recognized the prints of Zackie boy for better or worse, introducing Batman's past was obviously not necessary but of course Zack has to now show you his version of Batman's origin. Small nitpick, but aside from that Snyder's vision for action in this film is top notch and in my opinion way more organized than Man of Steel. The timing of each action set piece felt right and I didn't feel quite as overwhelmed as I did during the climax of Superman's first outing. This is most likely due to the involvement of Argo writer Chris Terrio who believe me, really added that much more to the film. He clearly understands the levels of this world and the ideas of it's heroes. He helps pace the film along nicely for the most part, the first half can be slow for some but once the ball starts rolling it really starts rolling. You're probably asking everyone, "well how's so and so as this person". I'm happy to confirm that Ben Affleck is the best Batman I've seen on film yet, this is a brutal and bitter Batman that is not afraid to go off the edge, and if you know the Dark Knight Returns than you will not be disappointed here. Gal Gadot has definitely proved me wrong as Wonder Woman and people are telling the truth about her entrance because wow, she was awesome absolutely. Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, and other reoccurring characters from Man of Steel are sadly not given a lot of time to develop more here, Superman is OK however I do believe Cavill is starting to embody the that hero you wanna root for more by the end of this film. This has been a mixed opinion with reviewers but I will be honest and say Jesse Esienberg as Lex Luthor just did not do it for me, he played the bad guy which was fine, but I just could not take him seriously. He's way too goofy and Joker like from the Lex Luthor I pictured as a kid. As it is a universe building these days in Hollywood you can probably guess what easter eggs and hints throughout the film are directing towards for the future of this franchise. As a DC fan since I was pretty much a child, this was all eye candy for me to witness, while it may leave general viewers in the dark and confused, it will definitely lead to interesting conversation when you get to answer people's questions about this movie because believe me, there is a lot going on in this movie. WB/DC have no time to build their franchise that Marvel had given themselves so you'd expect for a lot of references and foreshadowing throughout the film, for the most part I think it was handled very well. Unfortunately though if you have seen that second trailer from Christmas you will pretty much know how the story will go down, I really hope WB markets the future films more carefully and really surprise us with their reveals. It didn't hurt the film for me but I definitely would've been more positive if they had just kept some things under wraps. So again, is it perfect? Not at all, I have my problems with it, but overall it was a nice trip down memory lane and I was happy I gave it a chance(If you can see it in IMAX go, absolutely remarkable in the IMAX). To see Batman and Superman share the silver screen together was worth the ticket alone and I'm proud of WB for finally letting a project of this size to finally come together. This is a different tone, direction, and story so I'm ready for some diversity in this genre, Marvel can do their films and DC can do theirs, don't limit yourself why not enjoy both?

title: Great Movie with Tons of Untapped Potential, However Just One Major Flaw
review:
I honestly enjoyed the movie. I thought that the story was compelling and that the characters were well portrayed. By far, the best aspect of this movie was Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman. Phenomenal. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was also very well done. Henry Cavill returns once again, and his take on Superman was well done as well. Eisenberg's Luthor may be divisive for some people, but I took it for what it was and it turned out to also be great. So in retrospect, the cast was great and practically flawless.

Moving on to the action of the movie, it was also great. Snyder is well known for his visual aesthetics, and he delivers once again on that aspect. Great action, exhilarating, exciting, and well choreographed. Another note, if you are a fan, then these action sequences will probably be the best thing for you. For everyone else, it should be pretty satisfying and fun to watch.

Now, while many aspects of this movie are great, there is one major flaw in this movie that can be expected of most Snyder films at this point. This flaw is the pacing/coherency of the story. A lot of the film felt...messy, in a way. Things were haphazardly placed in this film, or so it seems. This really took away from the movie at times, and was really the only real complaint I could find. The rest of the film, given its editorial mistakes, was actually really fun and enjoyable, and was also thought provoking.

I realize I may be the few people who actually think that this movie deserves a good grade, and sure, whatever. Your opinion is your own, but I recommend this movie to everybody. At least watch it once, in my opinion, even if its for the sake of just seeing some of the most well known characters on the big screen. Its worth the watch, and the flaws that it has are easily overshadowed by the good.

title: Dawn of Justice
review:
Let me just start by saying this; I'm in the minority writing this because I really loved it. I know a lot of people don't like it, I respect that, just respect mine.

I'll start with the beginning of the film, another Batman parents origin but I don't mind seeing it again, and this time it was done really well, Bruce in the cave with the bats does remind me of Batman Begins.

Then it shows the end of MoS but from Bruce Wayne's perspective and it's clear what starts his dissent towards, Superman.

Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman is now the best on-screen portrayal of the character we have seen; he was fantastic, Henry Cavill as Superman was better than in MoS and had more depth and as Clark Kent, I thought he did a good job, Jesse Eisenberg as Lex I thought was the low point of all the acting but I still liked him as the character, very plotting but humorous, Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was great, she isn't the best actress I've ever seen so the lines she had were good but the action side of WW was amazing, great to see on the screen, the audience cheered at our screening, again when you saw the trinity, finally from the main cast, Jeremy Irons as Alfred was superb, a hands-on, witty Alfred is fun, stirring Bruce, I loved it.

The rest of the cast all did a good job, Amy Adams is good whatever she's in, Holly Hunter was good and the one scene with Granny's Peach Tea in the senate, the way it made her lose her focus, brilliant, Laurence Fishburne I thought was hilarious at times but also serious.

This Batman might also be the most vicious and brutal one we've seen, this is a murderous, Batman and it will cause divide but I liked it, it's a nice change, especially since you can tell he hates the world after losing, Robin. Which made me excited for the fight scene between Batman and Superman, and boy was it fun, gave me goosebumps to see these heroes I've grown up with fighting, I was rooting for Batman as its my favorite hero but by the end, I wanted them to stop, "like, no, you are friends, stop, please stop" but I did enjoy Batman winning.

They both got there punches in so good to see that as well which leaves me to Doomsday, besides his look, I was happy with how violent and dangerous he was, so to see the Trinity team up to take him down was amazing; WW with her lasso, Batman hitting him with kryptonite gas and Superman taking him down with the spear but dying in the process.

The funeral I thought was handles fantastically but we all know he isn't dead, so I look forward to this DCU which is set up well with the introduction of the Justice League; Cyborg, was the lowest point of the reveal, Ezra Miller as Barry Allen/The Flash was different then I'm used to and Jason Momoa as Aquaman was amazing, I look forward to seeing more of him.

I'll end with the soundtrack and Hans Zimmer has created a great one, as I walked out and even now, I have the music in my head, I will buy the soundtrack, so besides a few moments in the film, a few scenes with the way it was edited was jarring but overall, I loved it.

9/10

title: Great movie. Satisfying to comic book movie fans be it DC or Marvel, doesn't matter. Also appeals to general movie audiences. A must see.
review: I am in India and as we are 13 hours ahead of the U.S. I have already watched the Thursday preview in a packed cinema hall. I admit it is a long movie and it gets boring at some points, but it is a superb entertainer and will surely satisfy fan boys as well as casual movie-goers who don't come to the cinema with any type of bias. The action is great. Ben Affleck totally nails as Batman. After watching Wonder Woman in action I was simply speechless. Henry Cavill has significantly improved as Superman. The one character for whom I had high hopes for but was disappointed was Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. He is not the real Lex but his son Alexander. He doesn't have the attitude or personality like Lex Luthor from the comics.He feels more like Metropolis' Joker. Jeremy Irons' role feels like he is used as a comic relief. His immense talent is underused. He could have been given more screen time. Doomsday is not that great but the climatic fight with Doomsday when the Holy Trinity of DC Comics unites is simply epic. The movie is brimming with easter eggs. The Darkseid symbol in one of the bat-dreams and the cameos of Ezra Miller's Flash, Jason Momoa's Aquaman and Ray Fisher's Cyborg literally had the audiences on their feet. The titular fight is great. It is long enough and will satisfy greatly. Overall it is a movie that is made for the audience and not the critics, so don't be disappointed by the critic reviews and go watch this movie. It is not the best comic book movie out there but is surely one of the best and is definitely a much needed boost for the DC Extended Universe.

title: Beautiful with some flaws
review: Did the movie have flaws? Yes, of course. Does it deserve the malicious reviews it's getting from critics? Not even close. This movie started off slowly. There were scenes in the first half that could have been cut out for the sake of pacing. I brought my sister to the film and she knows nothing about comic books and she didn't get the dream sequences. The second half of the movie was just dynamite! You can totally see the $200 million budget of the movie in the second half and it does not disappoint. The audience cheered when Wonder Woman joined the battle, it was that good. I was one of the Ben Affleck haters when it was announced he'd be playing Batman, but really, he did a good job. Very believable as the caped crusader, and more than that, his fight scenes are the best I've ever seen in a Batman movie. That warehouse scene was just flawless! And as for Superman, well... his storyline was the heart of the film. The critics are just destroying this film and unfairly if you ask me. "Dawn of Rubbish" one critic said. Well, he and I didn't watch the same movie. Because this is a movie I'd gladly see again and pay even more in IMAX. See it for yourselves and decide for yourselves.

title: Definitely worth a watch.
review:
This movie is about right on part with what I was expecting... Not the greatest superhero flick, but pretty damn good. The tone, cinematography, and music all flowed very well for most of the film. Setting it apart from most Marvel movies; it feels like it's a drama first, and a superhero movie second. And Ben Affleck did a fantastic job portraying Batman. He makes it believable to the audience that he's been Batman for a long time, and that he still has something to prove.

There were a few things I didn't like that brought my score down to an 8/10. (In no particular order):

1. Jesse Eisenberg's version of Lex was kind of off-putting. With the theme of a grounded and dark film, he was a little too quirky at times. He did great as an actor, but I would have preferred a different version of the character.

2. The continuity was scattered at times. It seemed like the 2nd act got a little lost in itself. There were a couple of scenes that could have been taken out, and it feels like it wasn't edited properly with the story. But once the 3rd act kicks in, the movie gets right back on track.

3. It's a minor detail, but I wish the actual battle between Batman and Superman lasted longer. It was a great scene, but there could have been more to it. But I understand they probably kept it to a certain time because the final fight scene immediately followed..

It's a movie that I might see again in theaters. But I'll definitely buy the Blu-ray and watch it a few times a year.

title: Great setup for the Justice League
review:
Critics are giving this a poor review and I could care less. I watched it anyway and it was in my opinion a great movie for setting up the Justice league. I think the main problem critics and people that don't like it are having is that everything may feel rushed and it may cause some confusion for people not familiar with the Justice League comics. It's still a pretty great movie and here's why I think so.

Ben does a great job of playing this version of Batman. He's gritty and his fighting scenes are just amazing. It's the Batman fights you want to see with him zipping and flipping around. He pulls off not only Batman but the caped crusader with great ability.

Superman as always is well, Superman and you can truly see his power and how much he really has. It's great.

Wonder woman was played so so very well. She's so cool and I never really cared for her and I was watching thinking "wow she's awesome!"

Lex Luther. .. all I have to say is I love the way he is portrayed. You get the sense that this is definitely the criminal mastermind behind the Legion of doom.

All in all I suppose if your going in expecting it to be like the Marvel universe.. it's not I'm sorry. I love the Marvel universe and the avengers but this is the DC universe and it plays out as such. It's a new universe and it's an amazing one leaving me very excited to watch the Justice League movie.

title: The best COMIC BOOK movie ever made(even though very flawed critically)
review: Now yes Batman v Superman isn't close a perfect movie and yes it is flawed. From a critical point of view this movie would be rating at around a 7/10. Batman v Superman is a story, action and visually spectacular movie, which deserves a 10/10 and deserves a 10/10 for best COMIC BOOK movie ever made!

title: It's a different kind of superhero movie
review: First of all, I should say this: if people are expecting action-packed-no-consequence-movie, like The Avengers and Die Hard, or villain-like-Ledger's-Joker-movie, you will be disappointed. Zack Snyder and WB wanted to set a separate bar for the superhero movies, and they have succeeded in doing that in BvS. The story-line, though made to sound simple by the negative reviews, was more complex, which can easily fit any political drama: how a man seeking vengeance and trying to wash away the moment of helplessness becomes brutal in his work, how an alien being from a small village tries to keep faith in the fact that someone can be good all the time, how a megalomaniac realises that he has no control over things happening around him and makes situation worse by trying to take matters in his hands. BvS has a feeling of Snyder's Watchmen, but with a lighter shade. There is more exploration on the motives, events, and plots, with the fight sequences lending decent time. Affleck's Batman was believable: he was able to portray emotions very well, whether as a millionaire, company-owner, vigilante, or a vengeful man. Gadot fits the bill of WW: she does not look out of place. All her fight scenes were good, though she did not get much of screen-time(which was expected: it's a batman vs superman movie, not a JL movie). Jesse brought a new dimension to the too-beaten-up role of Lex Luthor. His switching between a mastermind, genius, madman, and scared human was done artfully, perhaps too much to be missed out by most of the audience. I pitied Cavill: it was supposed to be his movie, but his reduced screen time, coupled with more energy in Batfleck, overshadowed his own good storyline and acting. All the raw emotions, surprisingly comes from his Superman than Batfleck's Batman. Adam's and Fishburne's roles looked forced into the story, though the former had her own moments. Effects could have been better: Doomsday looks exactly like in the trailer, and WB didn't bother to improve him after the backlash it received. Zack's direction was better in this movie than in MoS, though the beginning was slightly disjointed, jumping too much between scenes than required. However, it became smoother as the movie progressed. BvS is a movie worth watching for its storytelling and acting. It complements the tome of MoS, and is rooted more into logical and real-world consequences. After all, this movie is not supposed to be about a bunch of heroes cracking too-smart-ass comments in the middle of destruction.

title: Cornier than the 60s Batman TV show
review:
BvS seems like it was written by a teenager who was trying to be edgy. It was so comically melodramatic, I couldn't stop laughing and rolling my eyes. It's a total cornball from the beginning scene where Bruce Wayne is saving people from the MoS end battle, to Batman and Superman deciding to team up because their mothers both have the same name, to the Superman funeral at the end (like he won't be back for the JLA movie).

Oh, and there's nothing in it for the hardcore DC fans, either. The characters are all totally off. Batman brands bad guys and kills several by shooting them and blowing them up, Superman is feared and hated, Wonder Woman looks scrawny and frail, and Lex Luthor is as goofy and jokey as we all thought Jesse Eisenberg was going to make him.

Wait to watch this one at home if you have to see it.

title: Why so serious?
review:
really had no high hopes for this because from the umpteenth trailer only a fool wouldn't be able to unspool the entire plot. That's alright, sometimes a movie can still come up with surprises and the journey is worth it. Unfortunately, BvS failed us (but it may not fail you).

My expectations are really low going in and it should by all means take little to buoy them up, but no, BvS lumbers along with no buoyancy, no purpose, and no clarity. Why does it kill it to add some levity to the narrative, instead of drowning us in self-importance and morose characters for 2h 31min. This is 151min which I totally feel every single minute of its passage, a skull-numbing and hollow def-con-one-yet-again experience. Why so serious?

There are so many things that didn't work for me and the missus (and also the idiot who was on his phone the whole time sitting next to me). Right on top of the heap is a Lex Luthor who got the short end of the stick. His motivations are drawn without clarity and his portrayal grating on my nerves. Next comes the narrative that tries to juggle so many threads and characters, and for me didn't get anything done satisfyingly right. This is equivalent to someone so scared that his dart won't hit the bullseye, and so he throws a whole bunch of darts at the same time but lo and behold, nothing lands up on the board let alone the bullseye.

This is a major disappointment. Sorry if I ruffled some feathers, I am just being honest and saying as it is for me.

title: Worse than Man of Steel, and possibly the worst DC film to date.
review: If this film were only a disappointment in the face of too much hype, it would've been another good film that undone by the need to temper expectations. After all, one can't be blamed for possibly expecting unrealistic standards for this film, and the temptation to hold it to impossible, unfair standards that it can't possible meet. This was a problem that happened with The Hobbit Trilogy (Peter Jackson 2012- 2014) and Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (George Lucas, 1999), which weren't great films but got overly criticized due to unrealistic expectations for them. But this film is so poorly told that it's hard to imagine anyone watching it and feeling intellectually, emotionally, or viscerally satisfied. Many of the issues that plagued Man of Steel (Zack Synder, 2013) are present here. The lackluster acting where people are either too shallow to be engaging or giving a performance that clashes with the rest of the film (Jesse Eisenberg). The weak narrative structure with plot threads that feel superfluous (an interesting complaint considering Synder's proposed "real version" needing to be three hours long). The cinematography is just as bad as before, with highly distracting hand held camera work, a muted dull color palette, and an over emphasis on slow motion to indicate important moments that almost feel like parody. The score is just as lifeless, feeling so much like every other uninspired score Hans Zimmer has cranked out over the past eight years. Synder and Goyer seem to still have a fundamental misunderstanding of how these characters work, to the point where you almost begin to wonder if they truly care about these characters at all or are just here for the paycheck. What makes this film worse is how portentous and pretentious it is, exploiting hot button issues and buzzwords to make it seem more thoughtful and important without any exploration of these ideas. It wants to tell the audience how interested it is in their ideas but anytime it seems to be about to explore the issue it does so in an insipid manner or is distracted by a poorly executed action scene. Further, a movie that questions from time to time how it's characters should use their power doesn't actually seem to actually care about how they use it as long as it looks cool, which might be defensible if it were but everything that is done in this film is either poorly executed or embarrassingly lifted from better films. As a film goes, I am upset by just how badly this film performs as both a philosophically charged action film and as a science fiction drama. But as someone who loves this genre and these characters in particular, the lack of an emotional core or clear appreciation for these character turns this from a bad film to a terrible film. This film is so bad that it retroactively taints Synder and Goyer's good work, as well as makes you actively uninterested in seeing any other films under this current DC administration. So, yes, "it's not fun" would be an excellent way to describe this film.

title: A new take on the superhero genre
review:
This is very different to your usual comic book movie. It ignores the usual formula and is actually much closer to Snyders other venture in to comic book law Watchmen. Gone are the laugh a minute huge set pieces of the marvel films, and instead we get a rather harsh look at how our world would react to these Gods suddenly appearing on our planet and going about their business with little regard to us as a species, or so it would appear.

What Snyder does here is put Superman through the grinder – having previously saved the entire planet in Man of Steel, there is a huge divide in public opinion of him and how involved he should be in human events. This is even more harrowing for Superman because he considers himself one of us, this is his planet and he is only trying to do what he thinks is the right thing. Now usually in the genre, it's pretty obvious what the right thing is – stop the bad guys, save the good guys. But in this world it is impossible to say who the bad guys and good guys are, and the notion that an Alien should be making that decision is the source of the main conflict in the film. The question of "should there be a Superman" is one that is asked throughout the film, and where the villain of the piece, Lex Luthor, firmly plants his flag.

Lex is an obviously hyper intelligent man. He was dedicated his life to the pursuit of human endeavour, and when this alien appears, essentially making all of his work pointless and obsolete, Lex decides that he needs to be dealt with or risk the human race becoming reliant on their God to carry them to greatness instead of pushing themselves towards greatness. This sets in motion a chain of events that leads us to the titular battle. Jesse Eisenberg gives a great performance as Lex, full of nuance and a massive amount of energy. There's a bubbling rage here, plastered over with a smugness and arrogance that only begins to show cracks when his own potential is questioned by the arrival of Superman.

Cavill plays his Superman with the same self-doubt and uncertainty as he does in Man of Steel. And so he should. This poor guy gets very little love for trying to be a good person. Even as Clark Kent, his editor has little interest in him trying to give a voice to the poor and disenfranchised people of Gotham. Long gone are the days where "doing the right thing" was the only moral code that a superhero needed to follow, and the way in that Snyder has deconstructed that idea along with the character gives me great hope that we will eventually see a more contemporary interpretation of the character in the Justice League films.

Now, the important stuff – Batman! The opening scene of the film is incredible. Its shows the death of the Wayne's in a way that we've not really seen before. Previously, the Wayne's murder had been about Bruce's father and the impact that had on him, whereas here his mother, Martha, is very much the focus of the scene (lots of nods to the comics here too!). The music here is pretty much perfect and really helps to expand on what is already a very emotional scene. This is inter cut with a young Bruce running into the woods at his parents funeral. He falls through a hole in the ground where he is attacked by thousands of bats who "lift him up towards the light" - a "beautiful lie" according to Bruce (an interpretation of a dream, so don't worry batfans, no flying batman here!). This whole scene perfectly sums up where Bruce is as a character- the moment his parents died he ran into the woods, not looking back, where he found the Batman - an ideology that convinced him he could find peace with the death of his parents by seeking justice for those who could not seek it themselves. This is the "beautiful lie" that Bruce is referring to in the scene with the bats. He has since realised this and become completely jaded with the world, to the point that he has pretty much abandoned the idea of differentiating himself from the criminals he seeks to bring to Justice (he's still lost in the woods). It feels like a continuation of where Frank Miller took the character (there are scenes lifted straight from The Dark Knight Returns) and while its not something that sits that well with me, I understand why they have done it, and I see how his interactions with Superman can influence him to be a better Batman (or bring him out of the woods). Hopefully that's where they take it in Justice League, and there's every indication that they will.

Finally, the world building they are doing seems massive – we get introduced to an Atlantean King, a man who can travel so fast he can skip time and dimensions (please god let Justice League open with the scene that leads to Flash's appearance to Bruce in his "dream") and an Amazonian Princess. Speaking of Wonder Woman – Gadot plays her with the grace and strength required for such an iconic character and I can't wait to see more of her. Her music was also one of the many highlights of the films score.

Overall, I loved this film. It's so different to the rest of the genre and feels like they're opening up a much greater universe than those which we have previously been exposed to. Everybody plays their part well and it's a fill that is filled with real stakes and genuine questions being asked of us as a species that we can't always give an answer to.

title: Another good day for the glaziers of Metropolis and Gotham.
review:
I went into the hugely hyped "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" with VERY low expectations, but came out with those expectations mildly exceeded.

The film picks up at the finale of "Man of Steel" with the glass-shattering fight between Kal-El and General Zod in Metropolis. Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) clearly has a branch in Metropolis (never explained) and is caught up in the carnage at a very personal level, setting up a grudge with Superman that is set to fester for 2 years. Also with a grudge (there was apparently only these two connected individuals!) is security guard Wallace Keefe (Scoot McNairy) who ends up legless after the attack.

Whilst most of the world still see Superman as a hero, there is growing discontent that he has great power without political accountability. Looking at this issue is US Senator Finch (Holly Hunter) with her committee and stirring the pot is 'one-bat-short-of-a-roost' industrial giant Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg). Meanwhile back in Gotham, Bruce Wayne is continuing his grudge campaign against the bad guys of the Gotham docks area, ably supported by his trusted manservant (here played by Jeremy Irons). Meanwhile (meanwhile) a mysterious and beautiful brunette (Gal Gadot) appears on the scene and pays a particular interest in Wayne and Luthor's business.

Phew! As you might conclude from this 'brief' introduction to the plot, there a several films shoehorned into this two and a quarter hours. Unfortunately, this is its downfall in that the story is an incoherent mess. As a viewer you are constantly grasping for the motivation for the characters doing what they are doing: surely in the next scene it will all become clear? But all too often you are left grasping at air!

This malaise can be demonstrated with a couple of examples: - the only rationale for Lex Luthor's story arc is that he is either a) 100% certifiable or b) omnipotent in knowing the events of future films before they have been made! - a dramatic change of heart by a lead character happens so quickly - and irrationally - that there may indeed by hope for the Middle East conflict! (For a comedic sketch on this topic see the full review at bob-the-movie-man.com!)

Frustratingly, amongst the ludicrously convoluted story (by Chris Terrio ("Argo") and David Goyer ("Man of Steel", "The Dark Knight")) there is a good film struggling to get out. The cinematography by Larry Wong ("Super 8") oozes quality and some of the individual scenes in the film are beautifully crafted. Some top moments:

  • The death of the elder Wayne's (again!!);


  • Wonder Woman's dramatic arrival (with a great musical motif by - presumably - Hans Zimmer)


  • Each of Jeremy Iron's well-crafted lines.


Also impressive is Ben Affleck's Batman - after all the fan-boy brouhaha at his announcement, he is really convincing in the role.

But with $250 million of budget (TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY!) you can afford to craft beautiful moments. It's not enough and director Zack Snyder really should have done better. Just to put that into perspective, you could make over 16 "Ex Machina's" for that!!

Given the volume of special effects, you can see where much of that money has been spent. It's never a good sign where each of multiple SF company's staff in the end credits need to be titled alphabetically. While the over-heavy CGI is very well done, we've seen it all so many times before, and that's just tiresome. (There must have been dozens of staff assigned to filming the bath scene with Amy Adams, which at first sight seems to manage to show absolutely nothing but will no doubt give hours of fun to fan-boys with their Bluray pause button in future months!)

title: If you don't like it you probably weren't paying attention
review: *Major Spoilers* I've read almost every review I can both good and bad trying to figure out why a lot of people didn't like it. I would like to take the time to address the issues most people have with this film and explain why they weren't "stupid." 1. "Batman kills people!" This Batman unlike the one we've seen in Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy (which I love) has been batman for over 20 years. He's much more "seasoned" than our Nolan counterpart and it has certainly taken it's toll on him! He's been through a lot more than any Batman we've seen on film to date. The death of Robin for example. He's broken. After everything criminals have done to him in the past it makes perfect sense he doesn't value their lives anymore. 2. "Superman says "Martha" and now they're friends!?" People please you have to understand it's not the fact that Batman and Superman's moms both have the same name that changed Batman's heart toward Superman. This is all about the psychology of Bruce Wayne and how his parent's death has haunted him his whole life. If there was anything he could have done to save them he would have. Superman yells "Save Martha!" Their moms having the same name was just the tip of the iceberg. When Lois explains that's his mother's name Batman being as intelligent as he is realizes that Superman's mom is a part of a plot to pit them against each other. Not only that but he can help save her life the way he couldn't save His own mother. 3. "Too many subplots. A jumbled mess." This one is all a matter of opinion. If you like one continuous story I could see how this could be annoying. I personally enjoyed the whole thing and can't wait for the 3 hour R rated cut! 4. "A bunch of CGI crap!" It's an action packed comic book film. What were you expecting? 5. "Superman Died!" If you've read the comics and knew Doomsday was in this movie like me you probably already deduced that that would happen. Hopefully how they resurrect him in Justice League isn't as dumb as it was in the comic book though. This is the very first review I've ever written and I felt it was necessary to defend this title given the very unintelligent reasons for bad reviews. I loved Batman V Superman!

title: Batman and Superman Winners
review: Just like the critics and fans, Batman and Superman duke it out for supremacy in the DC Universe. Despite its flaws, the Dawn of Justice does justice to the two heroes. Batman is on a vendetta against Kal-El/Clark/Superman. The collateral damage from the most recent Superman has cost many lives, many of whom were close to Bruce Wayne/Batman. He now worries about the unchecked power of Superman. So does the United States. When Superman has to save Lois (big shock, right?), some more collateral damage happens somewhere in Africa. Now the U.S. Congress wants to meet with Superman and discuss this immense power, since they think with great power comes great ... wait ... wrong franchise. Still, you get the idea. As Batman investigates some strange activities of Lex Corp and its founder, Lex Luthor, he meets the reporter, Clark Kent. Of course, he has his own agenda, wishing to investigate the Bat Vigilante who operates outside the law. In fact, when Wayne and Kent meet, the young reporter is already on to him. Also, a new casual observer is growing curious, as well as stirring up curiosity: a meta human who will be known as Wonder Woman. Finally, we have a Lex Luthor who has created an elaborate plot to pit the two against each other. We have a battle, a team-up, and the defeat of a bigger threat known as Doomsday. Fresh from the genes of General Zod, it wreaks havoc in Metropolis, so only the two heroes, I mean three, stop him. First, I want to get my gripes out of the way. First, the trailer for the movie pretty much gave away the whole plot - so thanks a ton, Warner Brothers. Second, Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luthor will have people considering him for a prestigious award: a Razzie. While Gene Hackman went with camp and humor, and Kevin Spacey went with more sinister, Eisenberg gives us a loopy Lex Luthor who has Tourette's Syndrome. There is also some lazy writing within the screenplay, as they could not execute the story as well Marvel writers have. Instead of focusing on our three superheroes, they pull some tricks out of left field to introduce Flash, Aquaman, and another hero I am unfamiliar with. However, it has a lot going for it. The most controversial casting decision, Ben Affleck as Batman, was the best choice. He owned that role, playing it to perfection. It even rivaled Christian Bale's take on the role. Henry Cavill as Superman is no Christopher Reeve, but he plays the role more for complexity and not so much as comical. Clark and Superman are much closer to each other. Moreover, unlike Brandon Routh and Kate Bosworth, Cavill and Adams have a good chemistry as Lois and Clark/Superman. Another good aspect was the fights and the action. While Doomsday went a little over the top, at least it was entertaining and fun to watch. And the fights between the two leads are both entertaining and done with a much greater level of believability than the Doomsday fight. The movie was drawn out a little long, especially the ending that will still pique the audience's attention. So that part did work for me. I just wish the writers could have found a way to shorten the path. Overall, despite these mistakes, Batman v Superman is one to watch for the ages. I look forward to the next one.

title: It Was Better Than What Critics Are Making Of
review: I was originally going to title this review as I quote the same way that Batman said to Superman "Tell me, Critics, do you bleed? You will?" Instead, I went with the one that you are reading. So far on Rotten Tomatoes, the audience score is at seventy-one percent, and critics are at twenty-nine percent. I understand that everyone has an opinion, and we should all respect that. However, at the same time, critics can go too far with it. I did go see this last week on Saturday, and I thought it was better than what critics are making of. I won't spoil it for you, because you have to see this movie. The premise of the movie picks up after the events of "Man of Steel," where Bruce Wayne witnesses the destruction of Metropolis as he notices Superman fighting General Zod and this makes him want to take him down for he had done. Superman receives a lot of mixed words of mouth by the world, and our two beloved superheros start to have a showdown. Heck, when everyone saw "Man of Steel" they complain about Superman fighting Zod in Metropolis, and couldn't take the fight to anywhere else. So the movie really does address the issues that everyone had as you seen the trailers or read articles about the movie on the internet. By getting to the point, here are the positives that I had with this movie. I thought the story is what it is by having a conflict between Batman and Superman so no need to go into detail about it, and certainly don't want to spoil the movie as what I said previously. The action in this movie is pretty darn good, as the fight between Batman and Superman really does make it worth awhile. The music by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL is really good, while introducing the Batman and Superman theme were all good. The cinematography is beautifully well-filmed, and it is visually stunning. Zack Snyder does a heck of a job to bring this movie to life on the big screen, and making this more of a comic book movie. The movie does feature some nod to Frank Miller's graphic novel "The Dark Knight Returns," which I thought that was neat. I do like the costumes for Wonder Woman and Batman, which I thought they were great. Even Superman's. For the cast, Henry Cavill is still, and will always be giving such a great performance as Superman, as well as Amy Adams for playing Lois Lane. Jeremy Irons does a great job as Alfred, which I don't have too much to say about but still he was great. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor had always got everyone concern about him whether he is good or bad for the role. To me, yes, he is over the top, but at the same time he can also be menacing. So, I say that Eisenberg made a good Lex Luthor. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman is in the movie in a brief role, but I thought she really knocks it out of the park. She really succeeds the role perfectly, and I think fans who read Wonder Woman comic books are going to pleased. Now for Ben Affleck, which had everyone the same way they feel about Michael Keaton as Batman, and thinking he can make this role the weakest link of the movie. Thankfully, he wasn't and he really puts the negative comments to rest. I thought he does an amazing job for his take on Bruce Wayne and Batman, and his Batman is so brutal because his fighting style is like one of those "Batman: Arkham Asylum" video games. If you like those games, then you will love how he fights in this movie. He is now one of my favorites along side with Michael Keaton, Kevin Conroy and Christian Bale as Batman. The movie is very well paced, and never I find it too long. Now, is it better than or on par with "Man of Steel?" No. The movie does have some flaws like characterization, which the movie has some but could've used a bit more. Also, I notice parts that may have been edited out because Snyder said that he is going to release his R rated director's cut for the movie. I hope that version is better than what the PG-13 had to offer. So, that is all I can say about this movie. By the way, do yourself one big favor. Don't let those negative reviews get in your way, just go see it with an open mind and then you can judge it on what you have seen. With "Suicide Squad" on the way, I am sure critics are going to enjoy that film because the movie will have some fun moments. To me, I don't have problem with this movie being dark, and I don't think this universe needs to be like what the Marvel Cinematic Universe did. The DC Extended Universe can be what they want to be, and so will Marvel as they be their own. I really had a fun time with "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice," and now it all leads up to the "Justice League" movie in two parts. I give this movie a 9 out of 10.

title: Well Worth the Wait & the Watch
review:
Don't go expecting The Dark Knight Returns by Frank Miller. They use some material from it, but that's not what this movie is. If it was it would be called TDKR. Given the book's popularity and acclaim DC would be stupid not to use it as the title were that what DOJ really was. This Batman is in his early 40's, and a far cry from the 55 year old Batman we see in TDKR. I think the comparison to the TDKR is born from seeing Batman fighting Superman in a mechanical suit. Again, they borrowed some ideas from TDKR, but this isn't that same story. I also see no indication in the film that Batman has been on hiatus. Sure he's older than we're used to seeing him, but there's no implication that he ever stopped being Batman. I don't know where people are getting their info, but this is not a continuation of the last three Batman films; this is a reboot. It just happens to pick up where Batman is by no means new to the cowl. Batman was Batman before there was a Superman, and the events of Man of Steel are dropped into that world. So, this isn't TDKR, and if that's what you are expecting you'll be disappointed. One day maybe they'll make that film, but its the kind of thing you can only do once, and if its done right it could very well be the first film with a comic origin that gets an Oscar nomination or even several.

Affleck delivers like no one before him. He's got the goods as Bruce Wayne & Batman. The fighting style is a lot more like what we see in the comics. Cavil continues to impress as Superman & Kent, and the supporting cast is amazing, reading like a wish list.

Does Batman kill people? In this film I think you can make that argument, but does that somehow ruin him? No, rather it makes him realistic. You can't always stop someone trying to kill you or someone else without killing them. The Punisher he's not. If he kills its due to a lack of options or through his tactics, which are and have always been pretty brutal. He's a beloved comic character, but fans need to treat this iteration like any other Elseworld or Earth One (Two, etc.) tale. It may not be 100% the Batman you're used to, but give it a chance.

I also think the concerns over the choppiness in the beginning will be rectified with the extended cut when the BlueRay comes out, so that's less a concern to me. You can follow it, and a lot may also be laying groundwork for the other upcoming films.

All in, its a great watch. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and look forward to the upcoming DC films.

title: This movie is iconic for the comic fans, and hit or miss for the average movie goer
review:
This movie ranks among one of the best movies (not just super hero) ever made. I think any advanced reader/movie goer who wanted to see the depth of how far a writer/director could take these characters will get an absolute treat. Anyone else who wanted to see a generic Marvel film filled with one-liners, less character building, and a lot more action will be thoroughly disappointed. . Zac Snyder managed to incorporate some of the best parts of the DC/Marvel classics in this film - from ideas incorporated in Mark Waid's Kingdom Come and Marvels, and Dan Jurgens' run on Superman. Blend those with the exploration of metaphysical ideas of dark vs light, personal responsibility vs identity, 20th century ideals of justice vs 21st century public relations, and you have what I believe is a masterful movie in the comic book genre.

What many critics fail to understand it's up to the writer and artist to take the character where they want the characters to go. Many non-comic book readers don't understand that with a passing of the torch from one writer to the next, there's also a slight identity shift of their favorite characters. Some writers take the Dark Knight to a much darker place just like Zac Snyder did, some don't, and end up giving you (entertaining) characters with much less depth.

The artistic choice to make Batman darker was in part to contrast Superman's 1950's ideals and simplistic forms of justice. What most people did not realize is that the transition from Nolan's more idealistic Dark Knight to this more lethal and pragmatic version of Batman comes from two events - 1. Joker kills Robin - which is spotlighted by the costume in the Bat cave with the words, "Hahaha, the joke's on you." and 2. Bruce Wayne witness to a 9-11-type cataclysmic event and the destruction of a Wayne building. There were many hints of how Batman became who he is, but Zac played this out for the well-versed comic book readers, and didn't breastfeed it to the average fan. In many ways, Christopher Nolan's Two-Face foretold the fall of the Bat, "You either die a hero or you live long enough to see yourself become a villain." To the well-versed comic fan, the transition was foreseeable, to the average fan – I can understand their confusion.

Moreover, critics failed to realize one of the major themes that resonated throughout the film – the dichotomy of the human race and the Meta-human race. In the comic book universe, (Kingdom Come) the US government became very skeptical of the destructive powers of the Meta-humans. As the Specture observes in Kingdom Come, "Long have these mortals suspected they are no longer the captains of humanity's destiny." Both Batman and Lex Luther symbolized the fear and as Alfred puts it - "the feeling of powerlessness that turned good men cruel." Congress tried to wrestle away Superman's political power by holding him accountable, and the president tried to take away Superman's actual power by nuking him in the sky. Lex and Batman both tried to take away Superman's destructive potential via kryptonite. Luther serves as catalyst to bring about the human vs Meta-human war so that humans can reclaim the reigns of power.

Many critics also didn't comprehend the philosophy of Lex Luther and how Jesse Eisenberg justifies killing Superman in his frenzied, Zuckerberg 2.0 manner. To me, Luther's iconoclasm is all over the script - "God is all powerful but he cannot be all good. Or he can be all good, but not all powerful. They need to see the fraud you are." "The oldest lie in America is that power can be innocent." The logic of Lex is simple – Superman is a false God, and much like how Joker tried to push Batman to the brink of darkness (and later succeeded), Luther was set out to antagonize Superman the same manner. In many ways, Lex represents the metaphysical loophole in the 1950's ideology of justice – there is right and wrong, but what if you are forced to do one wrong (kill the Batman) in order to do a right (save your mother) – are your actions just?

Moreover, numerous critics also fail to realize the significance of the title "Dawn of Justice." While it hints at the Dawn of Justice League of America, Zac Synder also uses the title to symbolize the justice served by post-Robin-Batman. Batman's branding perhaps equated a dusk of Christopher Nolan's idealized version of Batman, it takes Superman's heroism in order to reawaken Batman to his own dawn. "I failed him in life, but I cannot fail him in death." Bat's transformation is shown in the final encounter with Lex Luther, Batman could have branded him, but struck a wall instead to symbolize his awakening.

As Mark Waid writes in Kingdom Come – "Here before you is a clash of good against evil, of course, but more than that. There are clashes of judgment, clashes among different interpretations of what is good and what is justice, and clashes over who is to suffer the wages of the evil born of our best intentions."

For an advanced movie goer - this movie was iconic. For the average movie goer, it's hit or miss.In many ways for me, Zac Snyder took what could have been a generic film and made it profound, his inquiry into the meaning of justice, the depth of his characters,the sociological impact of Meta-humans, advances comic book story telling more than any Marvel film to date. The fact he would dare even attempt this mature way of storytelling gives me faith that other future creators can take what Zac left them with and take it even further, even against the opinions of the critics.

title: Excellent. Welcome to the DC Movie Universe!
review:
Please, if you haven't seen this film, don't read below. It contains spoilers (lots of them). You have been warned!

Headline Points.

As I write this review, I'm listening to the soundtrack on Spotify. So good! I have already pre- ordered the movie on iTunes. And I am going to see it again on Monday. So, yeah, I really loved it.

An Uncertain World.

Firstly, I genuinely can't see why people don't like this movie. For people to say it isn't funny or it's too dark, well that's not the point. It never promised to be anything other than hard-hitting (just like the comics it is based on). Having scoured the Internet to get a gauge, it is clear that there are two camps that have chosen not to like this movie. Critics and Marvel fans. I honestly believe that on the basis of some reviews, they haven't even watched the movie. Yes, trolls. They spoil it for everyone. What is clear is that this movie and this universe is made for the comic fans and for that I thank you, Mr. Synder, because, you have created something spectacular. The DC universe is a grown up, dark, troubled world where it's heroes are not even sure they are heroic. And there is a darker future to come. It is perfect.

Who's the Real Threat?

Affleck nails both Batman (a Batman that has been around for 20 years) and Bruce Wayne. Cavill is still the man to play Clark and Superman. It's their show and they both play it really well. Batman sees Superman as a threat. Superman sees Batman as someone that can't be trusted. Luther (Eisenberg does a great crazy Lex) plays them against each other. There are some scenes where you feel that you are right inside a comic (perfect). They are beautifully created and expertly thought out. A few times I caught myself thinking, 'epic' is just not a big enough word to describe this.

Welcome to the DC Universe!

We get glimpses of Aquaman, Flash, Cyborg and Wonder Woman. None of them get much screen time, with Synder, instead opting to give them brief cameos before they get their own film or appear in the Justice League movie. Wonder Woman is the exception and whilst she turns up at the end, I did feel that she is going to be the hardest character to get right in any DC film. That is not a reflection of Gal Gadot, who definitely looked the part and played the character like the comics. I just think that in an aggressive, male-dominated world, it is hard to depict her as anything as powerful as Superman. I hope I'm proved wrong on this.

Frank Miller's Batman.

The comic influences are wide, but The Dark Knight Returns is the biggest story to inspire this film. It is Frank Miller's Batman that appears in this movie. He sees it as his responsibility to take down the Superman. The fight scene between Batman and Superman has been covered in some of the trailers, but it doesn't prepare you for a scene that is truly epic. Since first reading Dark Knight I wondered what this would look like on the big screen and it does not disappoint.

It's been Emotional.

Whilst it is a dark and angry world, there are some fantastic scenes where Synder pulls on your emotional heart strings. The latter part of the film is played out really well and the Kevin Costner cameo is really well done. The music, courtesy of Hans Zimmer, has many of the same themes as Man of Steel, so there are some really nice, touching moments, that many wouldn't have expected.

Darkseid is Coming.

There are two scenes involving Affleck that are just screaming, 'here is a clue to the premise of the next movie and the future of the DC universe.' He has two dreams (nightmares) or hallucinations (unexplained at this point) that nod to Darkseid or some other alien invader coming to earth. There is also the suggestion that the Flash can time travel and that Superman's heroic future may be in question. We see Batman, presumably in a future apocalyptic earth, fighting Superman soldiers. We also see Parademons, which, for comic fans, is the stuff made of dreams. Whilst these scenes may be confusing for the uninitiated, they leave questions for the rest of us to debate over a pint for the next film.

Negatives.

I don't have many issues to highlight. I could really nitpick, but it is such an operatic effort, that crams a lot of content and introduces us to a new universe, that it would be unfair to untie it. If this was made into two movies or a trilogy, it would just get criticised for overdoing it. It can't win! My biggest issue is the fact that the Doomsday fight scene went on for too long but that just seems to be the way with action sequences these days.

Conclusion.

This is a film for the DC fans. And for that I am thankful. The little things, like Affleck's Batman voice and the Batmobile, were excellent. The apocalyptic future is pure DC and the ending What about the ending? I am definitely sold on seeing the rest of this DC movie universe. Can't wait to see it again! 9/10

title: Every comic book fans' Ultimate Fantasy Movie
review:
BATMAN v SUPERMAN An honest and insightful review by Navin Nambiar (Spoilers are highlighted. Skip those points if you haven't watched the movie)

Firstly, I have watched almost every single Batman, Superman, Justice league & Justice League Unlimited cartoon series and animated movie (Probably the only one I've not watched is Batman vs Dracula) leading up to this. I have also read most of the major comic books for both characters over the years.

Here are some of the animated movies and comics that have influenced the current Batman v Superman film (I may have missed out on a couple of others)-

Batman: The Dark Knight Returns Part 1 Batman: The Dark Knight Returns Part 2 Batman Beyond: Return of the Joker Justice League: Crisis on Two Earths The Death of Superman

Now let's come to the average viewer. Probably watched 1-2 Christopher Reeve Superman Movies, Superman Returns, and The Dark Knight Trilogy perhaps? Now these people (most of the critics included), who are used to laughing while watching the Avengers (Remember the Hulk bashing Loki scene where everyone was laughing away in the cinema including the kids so adorable) suddenly have to deal with a sense of realism. A darker take on these fun loving, family oriented superhero films made for the masses. Batman v Superman is not one of those films. Arms will get chopped off, necks snapped and limbs sliced off. Get where I'm going here?

This film, is a comic book brought to life. It is a combination of the coolest scenes from the above-mentioned animated movies & cartoons + a couple of comics. Now it's not the directors' fault if you're not familiar with these movies and comics is it? Is he supposed to show you the full lead up to how this is done or how that came about? The answer is a simple, No. The movie is titled Batman v Superman. If you're not familiar with the characters or the story plots, don't go bashing the film. Simply, don't watch the movie. It really is very simple.

Let me explain the level of detail involved here-

The scene where the two cops are after Batman at the warehouse. Batman defies gravity by hiding at the top of the wall and creeps away with almost spider like abilities- That's from "The Dark Knight Returns Part 2"

The scene where Superman is hit by the nuclear bomb - "The Dark Knight Returns Part 2"

Pretty much the entire Batman v Superman fight scene including Batman' - "The Dark Knight Returns Part 2"

Batman's Dream of the Flash- Justice League: Crisis on two earths (If I'm not mistaken)

SPOILER ALERT: The funeral scene at the end of the movie (roles reversed) - "The Dark Knight Returns Part 2", The Death of Superman Comic Book

Batman's fight scenes-

SPOILER ALERT: When he saves Superman's mum – Action sequences and moves are copied from the Batman games. The sequences where he grapples away from Doomsday can also be attributed by how he does so in the games.

I can go on and on. The Joker's identity, the way the Justice league movie will probably end, blah blah blah.

Now that I've listed the above-mentioned points, I think its fair to say that the average Joe probably hasn't watched these TV serials, movies and played any of the relevant video games. Here is where the fault (If you can call it a fault) of the movie, in my opinion, lies. The general audience is not aware.

So here in lies the question, is it the director's fault or yours? The movie is called Batman v Superman. Not Batman loves Superman or The Hulk is sad or Ironman's Girlfriend Saves the day. No one is forcing you to watch the movie. No one is asking you to write reviews on Facebook. Calm down and wait for the next X-Men or Avengers movie. Watch Ironman 3 again? Bring the kids along and have a fun time.

For me, Batman v Superman was AWESOME. It was Every comic book fans' Ultimate Fantasy Movie. And I'm super appreciative that my wife loved it too. After all, she did watch the animated movies leading up to this together with me ☺

Lastly, Ben Affleck please take a bow. I was one of those haters who was absolutely disgusted when they casted you as Batman. I was wrong. You Sir, are a Dark Knight.

title: Men of Tomorrow
review:
The Ultimate Experience BATMAN v SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE – ULTIMATE EDITION (★★★★★/5 Stars.) Just a quick recap of what I experienced the night of the BluRay released: biased or not, this was the best extended cut film I've ever seen.

While Aliens remains as one of my all-time favorite movies, the Director's Cut added scenes that were pretty good and enhanced the characters. Was it 100% necessary to the overall experience? No. It's safe to watch either cut and enjoy both.

I'll probably never see the theatre cut of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice again. And this is coming from someone that gave that version ★★★★½/5 Stars and is my current favorite movie of 2016.

This 'Ultimate Edition' cut boosts the theatre cut tenfold, without a shadow of a doubt. Characters were enormously fleshed out, emotions merely touched on before are thoroughly explained and an incredible amount of needed tension/investigations helped the viewing.

I saw the original three times in the theatre so it was easy for me to see the difference of larger character arcs, brand new scenes and even a simple one line of dialogue that added to the character interactions. This is not to say the theatre version didn't deliver. On the contrary, I still stand behind my four and a half star rating. These additions (or cuts?) simply made the experience better than I could've predicted.

Though I wish they had released this instead, I can fully understand why they didn't. Maybe, like Jonathan Kent in Man of Steel would say: the world isn't ready for this, they thought the risk too high. Perhaps. But, at least we all have it now on home video to enjoy dozens of more times.

***

Final thoughts: Like I stood behind my theatre cut review rating, I stand behind this five out of five star enthusiasm. BUT there was one thing I did NOT like. The comical fact they added the words "Ultimate Edition" to the opening credit's title. Seriously? That was unnecessary.

Mercifully, I got over that instantaneously when this version flew past my expectations.

(The following is my original review of the theatre cut back on 3/24/16)

When I was young, Chris Reeve's "perfect hero" Superman was my world. I idolized him and tried to be the good person he was had he been real. I even rejected any variation I saw of him not being so high on a pedestal.

Well, I just grew up.

Batman v Superman, or BvS, was so radically different (for both Supe and the Bat) it even completely shifted gears from its "new" origin story film, Man of Steel. This version of the superheroes and villain was so, ah-hem, alien to me, I loved it. I loved how it was made as both real and comic bookish at the same time. I also loved how there was so much here, so many details and plot directions, it demands a second and third viewing which I will gleefully comply with.

It would be completely hard to give away a synopsis without ruining all the twists and turns, but suffice to say, it begins where Man of Steel left off, only, from Bruce Wayne's point of view. And from his angle, it's not hard to understand he's wildly concerned about Superman's great powers.

As his suspicions increase, Superman has his own direction on how the "real" world might view him and his place here. And of course, it wouldn't be a based-on-comic-book movie without someone in the background cooking up their own plot.

Honestly, that's as vague as I can be to be fair to everyone else reading. Not to mention, I do need to see it again for my own sake of figuring everything out as there was just so much in this movie I know I missed.

I enjoyed the hell out of this. I loved the changes. I loved the new Bat. I loved how Superman/Clark was both updated but with so much of the spirit of the old. Heck, I even loved the new Lex's persona I've never seen before.

Even though, in this DC take on the Marvel trend of universes, Man of Steel was first and set some of the foundation, this is the one that is really going expand the DC universe to many more movies that I am going to welcome with open arms.

This is just my quick take on this movie. I have a feeling this initial great feeling I had here isn't going to wane; if anything, I think I will even rate it higher with additional viewings as I believe Director Snyder really had deeper meaning I was too blissfully overwhelmed to catch.

If you have an imagination to expand on your expectations or preservation of your past, I believe you, too, might love this new direction.

***

Final thoughts: While the world loves Marvel more – to each their own, I love the fact we didn't have to wait 5-6 movies to get many of the great DC Superheroes to meet. Though I know we have a couple of stand-alone Superhero movies following before the Justice League movie, I am appreciative DC didn't try my patience as Marvel did to get to their group hero film.

title: A decent movie that doesn't live up to the expectations
review:
This movie was weird. I really liked Snyder's visual direction, I liked the cinematography, the music, and boy oh boy did I like Ben Affleck's Batman. I liked Lex Luthor, it was a fresh take on an established character, and I liked Wonder Woman.

However, the movie's story and pacing is very awkward. The first hour is long, slow and full of weird "dream" sequences that shouldn't have been there. The presentation of future Justice League characters was out of place - you can actually pinpoint a few moments in the movie where a studio exec said "OK, this is where we'll insert something about JL", disregarding the actual script. This made it feel weird.

This could have been a great movie, if not for the semi-coherent storyline. It's not a bad movie per se, but what should have been the great foundation on which the JL universe is built, is now a "nice" movie at best that's way too long for its story and feels way longer than it is. It delivers on its promise, in that it's what its title says it is: it's Batman fighting Superman, also working as an intro to the Justice League.

title: Not without it's faults but still enjoyable
review:
I caught a screening of the film on Monday and enjoyed the heck out of it. This is my first time posting a review on IMDb and I do so because I am an unapologetic DC and Batman fan. These are my favorite characters and I want to continue to see them brought to life on the big screen. With that being said, like my headline indicates, this movie DOES have it's faults.

The bad: Eisenberg's Lex Luthor left me a bit annoyed. He pulls off the character as written very well; I'm just not sure I liked the way it was written. Perhaps his character will become less twitchy as the series continues? The editing felt a little choppy in a few spots but nothing too terrible. Batman kills. Although, I wonder again if that is part of his battle-weary, angry Batman that revisits his morals by the events of the end of the movie.

The good: Everything else! Jeremy Irons is a wonderful Alfred. Gal Gadot nails Wonder Woman. Ben Affleck IS The Batman. And Henry Cavill continues to bring us the ever-hopeful (albeit naive) Superman. I've seen reviews that are upset about the retelling of the Wayne murders, but it IS necessary as it sets up a key scene during Batman and Superman's battle. It was a surprise connection I never considered but a poignant one. Laurence Fishburne brings along some levity in a great performance as Perry White. The Justice League cameos felt more like an after-credits kind of scene but it worked in the overall subplot addressing the presence of meta-humans. And it was an awesome tease to see them on screen and excites my inner fanboy for their eventual inclusion in later films. Others have put down the ending as a "downer". But when one considers this is the second act of this story it makes sense. For me, it was a powerful and emotional ending that leaves me anticipating the Justice League movie.

There are so many other aspects of this movie that left me excited but that's all I can honestly think of right now. I'll be in the theater at least two more times this weekend to try and take it all in!
