title: BvS is a masterpiece
review:
"I'm sure by now everyone knows how the fight between Batman and Superman ends even if you didn't see the movie yet, but just in case... POTENTIAL SPOILERS BELOW!!! . . . . . . . . . . . I wanted to address this because I think nits getting too much online hate. Some people just didn't seem to grasp the metaphor that was in that scene.

Let's first discuss the first 2 opening scenes, because I believe they play a huge part in the fight scene. The opening credits that show the dream Bruce having of the death of the Waynes and Bruce falling into a cave shows him feeling helpless in the world. His rise out of the cave by the bats in the dream was symbolic of him rising above his fear to become Batman. Now he's been Batman for 18 years when the battle of Metropolis happens in Man of Steel. Bruce watching his building fall while on the phone with one of his top guys inside the building and seeing Superman and Zod in the sky brought him back to when he was a helpless 10 year old boy and since Superman is the lone survivor of the battle, he gets compared to Joe Chill in Bruce's eyes. This is the first time in nearly two decades that Bruce Wayne has felt truly helpless, aside from having a Robin die 10 years before BvS.

Flash forward to the fight scene between Batman and Superman. Batman utilizes Krypronite very well and actually defeats Superman. As he stands over Superman with the Krypronite spear ready to kill him and Superman says, "You're letting him kill her" and, "Save Martha", once he realizes what that means after Lois reveals that Martha is his Superman's mom's name, he's already connected that name with his own past, and now he's connected it with Superman having a family. He can't let that go. He sees himself now as Joe Chill standing over Superman as a helpless Thomas Wayne calling out for "Martha". This is a powerful moment in the movie that some people just didn't understand the symbolism of it all." ☆Slade

This guy speaks truth. A pat on the back for the people who got it while watching the movie, you're reason why this movie is doing great at the box office. I applaud you 🏻

I m 100% sure after 5/6years later people will consider BvS as a masterpiece.Try to watch this movie at least 3/4 times then you will find many awesome things in BvS.

title: What a film, absolute, rip roaring success.
review: What a symphony of scorched earth heroics, a two and a half hour maelstrom of thundering action, introspective gloom and very current vibes of apocalyptic dread. Zach Snyder should be proud of this achievement, for in the face of both ruthless odds and rabid fans who would make any one of us urinate down our legs at the thought of 'getting it right', he has mounted a titanic epic of a superhero flick, hitting all the right notes and fuelling both casual moviegoers and salivating super fans with a rekindled love for comic book films. We begin with a visually arresting opening credit sequence, which Snyder previously perfected to hair raising brilliance in Watchmen, a ten minute opus set to Bob Dylan. Here he inter cuts shots of young Bruce Wayne, both discovering the prophetic swarm of bats and on the fateful night of his parents murder, a sequence done over a thousand times in film, but never quite with the inventive flair used here. We then arrive with adult Bruce (Ben Affleck) in Metropolis right as it's being ripped to shreds by the Def Jam smackdown match of Superman (Henry Cavill) and Zod (Michael Shannon). There's eerie shades of 9/11 as Bruce darts through the ashen rubble, attempting to save the employees in one of his towers. One senses the fear and rage in Wayne right off the bat (pun intended). He glowers in seething fury at the man of steel, primally threatened and haunted all over again by loved ones he couldn't save a second time around. This film addresses the ludicrous amount of destruction that Superman wrought upon Metropolis in several ways. Political nerve endings are fried as Senate and State alike get hostile towards the god in the red cape. No one is more aggressive than Batman, though. This brings me to Affleck as Batman. Without a doubt my favourite cinematic incarnation of the caped crusader, and his debonair counterpart to date. Yes, even more so than Bale. Nolan's The Dark Knight is still tops for me, but the portrayal of Batman by Bale didn't strike as harmonious a chord with me as Affleck. It just didn't feel like pure Batman, it was real world Batman. Affleck feels much more rooted in the comics, and God damn it all if he isn't the most savage, violent Bats to come our way, well... ever. I've always been bothered by the nagging fact that Batman refuses to kill. Even in in a beatdown he could easily inadvertently cause death, so why bother trying? Here, he doesn't go out of his way to deliberately kill, but he sure has no problem brutally breaking bones and stabbing his adversaries without an iota of faux-noble hesitation. That's the kind of Batman I want to see. Fuming, fired up and full of rage demons that erupt into fantastic action scenes. One sequence involving a room full of thugs is just jaw dropping and probably my favourite sequence of the film, even over the titular smackdown with Superman. There's an earthy, simplistic take to him as well, with a modest suit that gives nods to Frank Miller and even Batman: The Animated Series. He is by far the elemental force that the character should be, and the part of the film that I connected with most. I hope he gets his standalone film real soon. Henry Cavill has grace and intuition as Superman, and a surprisingly earthly aura as Clark Kent, in a fit about Batman's vigilante tactics. He's the outsider here, an orphaned deity truly trying to do his best in a world that often shuns him in fear. He was never my favourite superhero, or even on the list, but Cavill combined with Snyder make him a force to be reckoned with, and a hero I can get behind. The two eventually meet in a remarkably choreographed clash of the titans, a duel that really only lasts a few minutes and isn't central theme, which raises questions in my head about the first part of that title. Their fight is composed of Batman's hard hitting, blunt force physicality pitted against Superman's fluid, elegent invincibility which is satisfyingly put to the test by the appearance of a certain green mineral we all know about. The combat feels urgent, from the gut and roars into action perfectly. Of course, that isn't where the fireworks stop, but I ain't sayin any more than that. Gal Gadot is truly wonderful as Wonder Woman, I also can't wait for her solo outing, and wish she'd been in the film more. Her much talked about entrance is the definition of crowd pleasing, and will make you cheer in approval, which I did out loud. She's endlessly gorgeous, and has the toughness to go along with it, a great casting decision by anyone's tally. My one concern with the film was a dream sequence midway through concerning Batman, and anyone who's seen the film knows what I'm talking about. I'm sure comic book fans have some point of reference or context regarding it, but the casual viewer doesn't, and a little more explaining would have been nice. I will say though it showcases Batman in an entirely new light which took me off guard nicely. This is what a superhero movie should be, plain and simple. Big, bold, audacious, stirring and full of high flying action, dastardly villains, conflicted heroes clashing like the ocean tides and a sense of pure adventure. Forget what the critics are saying, this one comes up aces in all categories and is a perfectly wonderful start to the stories of a group of characters that I look forward to seeing in many a film to come. Especially Affleck's Batman.

title: Good movie, entertaining, but...
review:
It is a very good film, especially from a special effects, musical and artistic perspective. The actors are excellent, the universe is very grim and the director captured the dark side of batman very well. Batman kills people (not a spoiler don't worry) as does superman which is rather surprising as it goes against the traditional batman style. The negatives are rather small, the film is long (I don't mind that) but it needs to be longer, one feels as if the story line is rushed at times, there are too many subplots to fit in, clearly this film is preparing us for others. The director really likes to link Superman to Jesus Christ, with many visual and audio references during the film, which can be slightly offensive and inappropriate, it would have been better to compare him to a Greek mythological god, but the director did a good job at it from a purely artistic perspective.

What this movie excels at is that you can just sit back and enjoy a very pleasant visual treat with an excellent soundtrack. It entertains, which is what a movie should do.

title: Very Action Packed and Entertaining along with being a mess
review:
Going into this film, I did not have high expectations or anything, all I was expecting was an awesome fight between Batman and Superman.

First of all Ben Affleck killed it in the role of Bruce Wayne/Batman you could understand why he wanted Superman taken out. In the end, he was such a relatable character. Gal Gadot was brilliant as well as Henry Cavill.

Lex Luthor and Jesse Eisenberg is this film, just didn't do it for me. He was too over the top and just did not fit the role.

A 2 hour and 30 minute film is a long time, but when I came out it only felt like an hour because I was entertained for the whole way through!

The action was great, the CGI was fantastic. When you think about it there was 3 villains, one what was Superman in Batfleck's eyes, Lex Luthor, and one at the end which has a plot twist. Which I will not spoil! But it has the same mistakes as what Spider-Man 3 and The Amazing Spider-Man 2 did, there is too many villains and it's crammed into a 2 hour movie. And it just turned into a mess.

Some cheesy scenes which did not need to be there, entertaining for the most part, very creative script, great action, fantastic acting for the most part, Zack Snyder is a very creative director and has a lot of potential for the future.

I will give Batman Vs Superman an 8.2 out of 10

title: A great movie.

title: A flawed masterpiece
review: I confess I am a huge fan of Frank Millers's seminal 1986 work "The Dark Knight Returns", which is just as well as the film, in its early sequences, borrows heavily from the book to the extent of recreating exact scenes from the comic (note Martha Wayne's exploding pearls in the opening sequences, to name but one). In this sense and this "interpretation" the film reflects the moral ambiguity that made Dark Knight so compelling. It brings a reality to the Superhero film that is often lacking (When Superman throws someone/thing through a building what happens to the people in that building?) and reflects that just because you think that you are doing right it doesn't mean that everyone thinks you are doing right. Ben Afleck as Batman is superb and brings real grit to the role, so much so that I was almost moved to tears at one point, and his beef against Superman is logical. Henry Cavill too brings the power and virtue of Superman to the screen in a way that feels grounded and real. Amy Adams also deserves an honourable mention as Lois Lane and Gal Gadot, in her brief appearances, as Wonder Woman certainly make the character worthy of further study. Even Jesse Eisenberg in his early scenes as Lex Luthor lends a logical argument to his desire to stop Superman. Set pieces are stunning and the film raises interesting questions on what it would be like to have very powerful beings roaming the planet, in a way that Avengers doesn't (not that I don't like Avengers films, I like them for wholly different reasons). So what goes wrong? Doing a Dark Knight returns film is a great idea and in so many ways this is a Dark Knight returns film. BUT! Dark Knight Returns was an endgame, a portrayal of Batman at the end of his time and how he faces that, while this is a beginning, Dawn of Justice and all that. Which means that some run-of-the-mill action film plotting has been shoehorned onto a classic story. So while the action sequences are superb they arrive at the expense of the plot. This includes the way in which Batman and Superman are persuaded to fight. In DKR it is logical and easy, Superman is a lackey of the government brought in to bring Batman down. However in a film where Superman isn't a lackey of the government the method is more contrived and ultimately weaker. Superman takes some scenes which were originally Batman's in DKR and if this WERE an endgame film would still have great power and resonance. However we know that this is just the start of a series so it renders the impact null and void. Nevertheless go and see this film for yourself, where it is good it is very good and will probably be the best film adaptation of DKR that we are likely to see.

title: Legendary superheroes wasted on a messy mediocre script with over the top effects
review:
Last night it was finally time for it. In the words of Lex Luthor "The greatest gladiator match in the history of the world". I don't think an aggressive meeting between the two probably most famous superheroes of all time, can be described in any other way. So what did I expect from this film? I wanted a deep film about how Batman and Superman's paths cross and explode into a fantastic fight. Then they have to unite against a common enemy and form the foundation of Justice League. Henry Cavill returns as the man of steel and Ben Affleck takes on the part of the dark knight. Jessie Eisneberg plays the mad millionaire Lex Luthor, who's main goal has always been to destroy Superman.

The truth is that Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is one big mess. My expectations about a deep fight between Batman and Superman went quickly down the toilet when a lot of other stuff took up space. It was Wonder Woman, Lois Lane the damsel in need, some sort of senator and of course a couple of weird dreams about the future, or was it the past? I didn't quite get that. Already there is an obvious lack of focus in the script. How hard can it be? Batman vs Superman and one enemy to fight. If you try anything else with more characters, you better know what you are doing because very few succeed when they try. Even Christopher Nolan didn't succeed in his last Batman film The Dark Knight Rises.

In Batman V Superman it always feels as if they know that they are building it all up for the next great film with more heroes and greater conflicts. The result is that this film takes a beat, becomes unfocused and because of that, even worse. It contains a lot of small details that just went wrong. Tiny details usually shouldn't do that much harm to a film, but when we don't even know why Superman is angry with Batman or why Wonder Woman doesn't do anything besides stealing technical stuff from Batman, you are approaching deep water and playing with huge parts of the plot that because of that doesn't work.

Lex Luthor is a good enemy. He is young, smart, a millionaire, a little sick in the head and not a strong man. Yet he can do so much harm and be very disturbing. The film scrapes on the shell of this character but we never understand why he is the way he is, or why he does certain things. Why does he hate Superman? Beats me. The film has strong parts that at times, lift it. Jeremy Irons as Alfred, stabs and quarrel quite humorously with Batman. I also personally as a journalist student, think that it is incredibly fun to watch Laurence Fishbourne as a crazy newspaper editor obsessed with coming up with good headlines for his stories. Very entertaining.

Well to summarize, I will admit that it is a superhero film and it shouldn't be taken too seriously and most of all not immediately be compared to Nolan's Batman films. It is an entertaining film with nice computer effects and great acting. Perhaps at times too much computer effects, but I can look past it because after all it is Superman. However, I still feel that a more clear and simple idea back in the process of writing the screenplay, would have given the film a more deep focus and the result of that would have been us understanding the characters and their actions. There are more to wish for, come on Warner Bros.

David Lindahl www.filmografen.se

title: Bad...
review:
It seems as if Zack Snyder's 'Batman vs Superman' has been hanging over the heads of geek media for almost three years now. It almost seems as if the internet has discussed this thing to the point to where it has no marrow anymore. The controversial Snyder and Affleck have hung with dread over this film. Now that it is finally here the question is "Is it bad?" Oh hell yeah. Is it a cinematic abortion? Probably not. It's just a boring movie that goes through way too many story threads without choosing one to fully develop. It's boring and pretentious and doesn't have a voice of it's own. It's Snyder trying his hardest to be Christopher Nolan and Frank Miller. The result is just uneven although it does have one great strength.

To it's credit 'Batman vs Superman' does have about twenty really solid minutes and they can be attributed to the most controversial element of the film.The one thing that really stops me from condemning it fully is Affleck. While not the best Bruce Wayne/Batman he does embody all the best elements of the character. He has that dark brooding presence. The scenes where he trains in the Bat cave for his fateful encounter with Superman are just the right mix of pulp with grittiness that doesn't feel contrived. I like that he is the oldest and most cynical Batman. There are about two exchanges between Affleck's Batman and Jeremy Iron's Alfred that feel original and organic. I think Affleck and Jeremy Irons have a good Batman movie in them. If Affleck were to direct it and not have any input from David Goyer than I think we might have the first solid entry in the DC Cinematic Universe. Unfortunately when the story gets bigger and more convoluted Affleck isn't able to salvage his scenes.

There are just so many plot points and would be story arcs that just spin in circles with no resolutions and thus no stakes until the fight sequences that come out of nowhere. If the movie had picked the plot of Batman wanting to save the world from Superman after the events of 'Man of Steel' and stuck with it the movie might have worked. I don't really care about anything else. The congressional hearings, Lex Luthor bits, and yes even the hints of the Justice League don't work because they aren't developed. They just add pretentious mood.

It also has no visual or thematic personality. There are montages where we can tell Snyder is trying his hardest to invoke the vastly superior Christopher Nolan. There's large crowd scenes of protesters and police regalia and it really serves no purpose. 'Batman vs Superman' isn't clever enough to say anything. He tries to emulate Nolan do in keeping the film so darkly lit that really it becomes an ugly film to even look at.

If it's any consolation to this films rabid fans I'll be honest and say I probably thought 'Avengers: Age of Ultron' was a worse movie. It doesn't bode well for the future of comic book films though. I think Batman and Superman need a break or at the very leas to be divorced from Snyder and Goyer.

title: Visceral, Spectacular Mess
review:
I am a very big fan of Superman, but this movie was a let down despite the hype.

Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman was not bad. Except for one problem; his version of Batman was written to be a rather irrational one. Batman in the comic books as well as in games and animations have always been known to be a brilliant detective and a mastermind strategist. Ben Affleck's Batman however, blindly hates Superman and was completely unaware of Lex Luthor's manipulations or his criminal activities until the third act. His is a far cry of the character we know as fans. Also, unnecessary repeat of his parents' death. We've seen it more times than Spiderman's Uncle Ben.

Lex Luthor came across as a discount Joker, more than a cunning power hungry capitalist. His is an evil Mark Zuckerberg slash Jack Nicholson's Joker. Jesse Eissenberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor was in short, disastrous. Lex Luthor has always been known to be eloquent, intellectual, conniving and most of all, a man to be feared. Most of all, Jesse Eissenberg's immense animosity for Superman came across as baffling. In fact, there wasn't any known motivation nor a strong reason to begin with.

The pacing of the film and story were confusing and sloppy right from the get go, jumping from scene to scene without clear connections, as though it was all put together hastily. As a result, you'd actually be left scratching your head from confusion and frustration if you weren't a comic book fan.

Zack Synder also decided to kill off Jimmy Olsen in such poor manner, it's as though he decided to insult the fans. Most of all, none of the audiences would even know who Jimmy Olsen is, until you read about it online.

Doomsday looked a lot more like some monster from The Lord of the Rings or a Frankenstein Ninja Turtle. In fact, inserting Doomsday into the story is really a poor choice, despite the awesomeness of the entire fight scene. I loved how Zack Synder's Doomsday actually has Solar Flare, but such a famous villain could have been utilized for another installment. However, I understand that the writers and Zack Synder wants to have Superman go through a journey similar to Jesus Christ, to make Superman sacrifice his life for the greater good in order for mankind to truly appreciate him and then eventually resurrect him ala' bible style, elevating him to hero status, somewhat similar to Christopher Nolan's Batman.

Speaking of which, Superman's death scene was very disappointing. If they had truly displayed his battle with Doomsday with respects to the source material, I would have applauded.

Warner Bros and DC could have done better, but in a desperate bid to catch up to Marvel, they decided to just smash everything together and squeeze out whatever they can instead of setting a steady pace. The entire movie would have done better if the story had focused on the differences between Batman and Superman's ideologies without bringing in unnecessary elements to accelerate Justice League. They should have explored Superman's identity as Clark Kent, but the filmmakers instead turned Clark Kent into a sloppy reporter. A complete insult to his character and personality. Amy Adam's Lois Lane was underused and underrated.

I will however, praise the filmmakers' vision of Superman and the exploration of themes close to our hearts. They've set the superheroes in a modern world under the threat of terrorism and power abuse, where every action has real consequences and effects. I appreciate how they decide to make Superman a character who is still struggling with his role in society and finding out what really makes a hero. Henry Cavill's Superman may seem to be dark and brooding, but Superman in the comics also had his pit falls and moral dilemmas. He wasn't always Superman.

A few other good things about this film is their clever nod to Frank Miller's, "The Dark Knight Returns". Superman catching the bullet only to release the weaponized Kryptonite, Batman's armor, the sonic cannon and most of all, Superman's revival from a shriveled corpse after a nuclear strike.

Overall, Batman v Superman is a watchable mess. Will not even spend a cent buying the DVD release.

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a masterpiece
review:
Let's get straight to the point. The much anticipated Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is easily the most daring attempt on telling a very adult-oriented superhero story in cinema while at the same time serving as a vehicle to quickly expand the DC Extended Universe that Warner Bros. and its creative team have been developing. Is it any good? I can boldly say it is a great film.

Set 18 months after the end of Man of Steel, Batman v Superman shows how much the world has changed and continues to struggle with Superman's presence. Along the way Bruce Wayne/Batman has been doing lots of detective work to get to Superman whom he blames for the collapse of his business building (and deaths of his employees) during the destruction of Metropolis in the previous film. Meanwhile eccentric business tycoon Lex Luthor has been planning something big against Superman and this involves talking with government officials in order to obtain very important things he needs.

With regard to storytelling, the movie really felt like a very cinematic comic book which has Superman as the central figure while switching to the views of Batman, Luthor and Wonder Woman (in a small role). The first half of the movie was focused on story and character development with some action sequences that help prevent the movie from boring the viewer. The second half of the film is where the pace really goes into overdrive leading to a very heavy action and special effects bonanza from director Zack Snyder and team.

At the same time the so-called "heavy spoilers" from the movie trailers did not really spoil the movie at all as there were literally tons of surprises and other forms of cinematic spectacle that not only amazed me but also intrigued me. Going back to the storytelling, Batman v Superman's presentation is clearly geared towards young adults and adult viewers as it contains mature elements like terrorism, torture, some sensuality and even horror jump scares. It's a PG-13 rated movie that bordered on R-rating territory.

In terms of performance, Ben Affleck is very outstanding as Bruce Wayne/Batman and is also the best cinematic portrayal of the icon. With Batman serving as a crucial viewpoint of the audience, Affleck successfully portrayed the Dark Knight as having been fighting crime for decades who lost lots of sleep because he was so driven with detective work and his view of the world changed because of Superman. The translation of the icon from literature to cinema was flawless and Affleck nailed it.

As I expected, Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor is a combination of pre- Crisis and post-Crisis Luthor with a notable touch of eccentricity which led to a few funny moments (perhaps Warner Bros.' way of countering the Marvel Studios-style humor without going overboard). Gal Gadot meanwhile successfully portrayed Wonder Woman respectfully and already I'm excited to see more of her in the 2017 standalone movie of the queen of superheroes.

With regard to weaknesses, Batman v Superman's narrative suffers somewhat when the film tries hard to emphasize world-building related to expanding the DC Extended Universe. You will see short but notable visuals confirming the existence of the other members of the soon-to-be-formed Justice League. Another weakness is Henry Cavill as Superman who had a noticeable reduction of screen time.

Overall Batman v Superman is a truly great movie that is worth waiting years for (or decades in the case of DC Comics fans). It delivered its big promise on showcasing the DC trinity of Wonder Woman, Superman and Batman on the big screen which essentially established a strong foundation of expanding the DC Extended Universe. The big battle between Superman and Batman lived up to its promise too. The movie's dark tone, gritty and adult-oriented approach to presentation clearly sets it apart from the superhero flicks that have been released since the year 2000. Even though it is not a Justice League movie, I enjoyed Batman v Superman a lot more than 2012's The Avengers (which was a very great and magical film to watch). At this stage the future looks very bright for DC Comics movies.

title: Mixed Mess
review:
One of the most anticipated movies is finally here and the ultimate question about it now is "is it any good?". Well if you check the reviews it's either the best movie ever or the worst movie ever. While that's the most usual bipartisan, polarizing way internet works, it's either Yes or No, either 0 or 1, the truth is as usual somewhere in the middle.

For the uninitiated DC viewers that watched only Man of Steel and are not particularly invested in Superman lore, Dawn of Justice will probably be a incomprehensible cool mess. For DC fans it's almost the same but they can at least understand some plot points. The main point is that it's a mess.

There is really not enough space to inspect all the highs and lows of this movie, because there are so much of either. If anything, it's polarizing af. So I am going to break down just some of the basics.

There's a lot of stuff to like and a lot to hate here. Story is mostly in that other camp. While there are 52 different plots and subplots going on from scene to scene the gist of the story is - Superman is a threat, Batman doesn't like it, Lex doesn't like either of them. Also, Wonder Woman is in it.

Probably the worst part of the movie is that the plot hole ridden story goes in hand with incoherent editing. From scene to scene movie goes all over the place. Batman chases bad guys in a truck with kryptonite, and after 5 minutes of that, Superman blocks him hard, scene ends, Batman goes empty handed. Shortly after, Batman gets kryptonite in a scene we didn't see. It's basically a setup with no payoff in chase scene and then matter resolves anyway without us witnessing it. It's hard to describe editing and pacing of this movie because it's so all thrown together.

If you know your DC stuff, main plots are basically Death of Superman/Injustice/Darkseid/Dark Knight Returns mashed together in not so compatible way.

Characters are also wildly mixed bag of everything. Let's go with the best - Batman is awesome. Yeah, he kills people here and there, but more as a collateral and not a murderous intent. And that's OK, because Batman is ultimately malleable character and you can do a lot with him and still make him great. While some of the decisions he makes here are just dumb, he's still the best part of the movie. Ben Affleck also is great as Batman and Bruce Wayne. Henry Cavill and Superman are like, OK I guess, just like in the Man of Steel. Really nothing to add there. Wonder Woman is kinda tacked on here, and while Gal Gadot is passable as WW I couldn't shake the feeling while watching that' she's actually horribly casted. I'm prepared to let Wonder Woman standalone movie reassure me though.

All the others were fine, Jeremy Irons is OK as Alfred. But except Affleck, Cavill and Eisenberg, others really don't have much of a screen time anyway. And then we come to Lex Luthor. Wow, just wow. Eisenberg does what he does and that's being Jessie Eisenberg. While I'm always open for different versions of popular characters, this was just a bad idea from the start. From casting to Luthor being an aspergerated maniac that behaves really, really weird. That scene with candy and senator, what the hell was that? It was so super awkward.

And then there's Flash/Cyborg/Aquaman shoehorned introduction with all the names, logos and all, in a dramatically formatted email from Batman. It was unintentionally hilarious as all hell.

Script also needs a brief mention, because there are a lot some really dumb stuff coming from characters mouths in this. If there isn't mention of a "god" at least billion times in the movie then there's at least one jar of urine as a punchline to some of the most dumb, own fart smelling, written parts of a dialogue I ever saw in a movie.

Oh yeah, and Superman dies. That was kinda unnecessary, especially if they are just going to bring him back in the next movie, even more so if they bring him back without some really palpable consequences. At least we can all hope for Supermullet.

In a nutshell, a lot of unnecessary characters, scenes and subplots with a lot of explosions, incomprehensible action, no jokes whatsoever (ok, there's one with Batman and Martha Kent), awesome Batman stuff.

They had almost 3 years to actively make this movie more coherent but they didn't. And as much as I would like to lay all the blame on Snyder, one man can't make a movie like this - although he is probably the most responsible for the worse parts of it and that's editing and nonsensical direction. Someone had to green light this to theaters, to edit it, write it, act it, bankroll it. Someone could just say "wait, this is insane, back to the drawing board." but didn't. A lot of dumb things happen for no reason except "next plot point needs to happen".

When things get dumb in BvS, they get really dumb, when they get awesome though, they get really awesome. Only thing I can say for the end - WB/DC, do better! Can Snyder, get coherent stories and directors. It's not that hard, Disney can do it. While I do appreciate the one thing DC always does, and that's doing something different and alternative story wise, and a lot of times it just works (Injustice, DKR, Earth One, Arkham games, Nolan movies, all Batman TV animated outings), and they also do it here, but it just seems like it doesn't click for some (well, a lot of) reason. Then it's probably time to tweak this formula a little bit.

Zack Snyder has definitely redeemed himself with this movie; I truly believe in his vision and think he is actually a worthwhile director. Whoever said that if you liked MOS you would like this one more was right. Apparently people are calling this movie dark; I did not find it dark rather I found it realistic. Let me try to put mythoughts into something coherent at least a little I apologize if Istart to ramble again:

1. Zack outdid himself...he truly is the man for this job and be delivered a masterpiece; this is now my new favorite CBM. 2. Ben Affleck as Batman/Bruce: I admit that I found him to be the weakest character of the 3 (Supes, WW, Bats) but he still did a good job; it was just I was more impressed with the characters of Clark and Diana and I kind of felt that Batman was just shoe horned in because he is Batman. I kind of understand what they were trying to do but much like tornadocide from MOS it wasn't delivered well; but unlike tornadocide this time I wasn't left wanting "to strangle someone 2. Henry Cavill is Superman for me! Yeah I know Christopher was and always will be great but I will watch Henry in this role until he is 50 he is that good; like when he saves Lois after Lex pushed her off the roof, the look on his face after the senate explodes. Speaking of which one thing that really was meaningful to me was the exchanged between he and the senator a second before the explosion. People say that these movies have no human connection but I disagree and that scene was done superbly. I really like the story WB/DC/Snyder/Terrio are trying to tell here,Superman doesn't like to be seen as a god by humans yet at the same time he himself blames himself for everything like he is omniscient or omnipresent. I recall in MOS when Superman told Swan that he (and the military) would never be able to control him...and Superman in turn needs to understand that he will never be able to control other peoples actions or stop people from dying. This is turning into a manuscript so I will try to finish this up quick. 3. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman PERFECT 10, I see no one else who could have done this role. OMG and the scene when she first appeared in costume and that freakin guitar! 4. Ihave always been against Amy Adams as Lois Lane and I feel that I might have been wrong. 5. Jesse asLex Luthor....I get what they were trying to do but it is with him thatI feel was the weakest link of the movie. The worse thing about his Lex was his creation of Doomsday which just came off as creepy and kind of disgusting; someone needs a girlfriend bad. 6. SPEAKING OF DOOMSDAY (I swear I'm almost done) holy crap as someone who never read the comic books that boss was freaking amazing, I loved the effects they used with him and how he pulled in and pushed out electric energy. title: A Music Video That Isn't Even Cool
review:
OK, I'm going to say at the outset, this is just so badly written and directed. It's a confusing mess of a billion things happening, none of them interesting, with zero desire to care for any characters, events, or happenings.

So, yeah it's tremendously bad, possibly worse than MoS.

Nothing matters, stuff is just happening ... constantly. There's zero character development which therefore means that there's no reason to care about anyone or anything. You can pretty much sleep through most of it, as it does get old fast, people speaking in snapshots, no real conversation or life (barring one bath scene), and it really doesn't have a middle at all. In fact there's very little start to this film, either, just a whole heap of end ... End ......EEEEENNNNNNDDDDDD.

There was an ongoing thing a long while back whereby a lot of film viewers were saying that 'what we really need is a film where superman gets to hit things a lot. Yes, that will definitely make a good supes film' ........ Oh ... kay ... now you've had two of those, with zero hope, light, and love for the man, nothing. He's a flying fist (with the characterisation that goes with that) and somehow that fist scowls more than Bruce Wayne at someone's parent's Silver Anniversary.

This has all the scripting of YouTube 'versus fight' with figurines (except those have more than one -bad- joke).

The animated DCs aren't the most amazing cartoons these days (come on, guys, get it back on track with a bit of world building there) but at least they develop character, build story, and push you to care. Perhaps look over there for some talent, rather than the comic side of thing (which aren't going great).

I'll tell you now, I actually fell asleep during bits of this music video.

This is not a good film, and it's a shame, because there's so much to work with. I really hope that the awfulness of this film will actually propel the Suicide Squad, Wonder Woman, and Flash, films to greater acceptance. But only if the latter two (the first is about bad guys) actually have some real light in them. Spoiler alert there's only two seconds of sunlight in this one.

title: The blatant story issues outweigh the fun action and characters.
review: I despise when people hate for the sake of hating. I want to make it clear, this is not a movie I have a vendetta against, but a movie that legitimately left me frustrated even though I even liked Man of Steel. The biggest problem is that there were four movies crammed into one. At first it was set up as a Batman film with Superman as the villain, but two minutes later Superman is the hero and Lex Luthor is the villain. Then, we see the press' view of Superman. This is a big issue from a story stand point. They pit two conflicting stories with two vastly different tones. This made it so hard to be invested any one side. None had a full arc. Any one of those would be a good movie but it doesn't commit on any. It commits on the least interesting story; that is Doomsday. The story rotated every five minutes had had no focus. They set up Superman as hating the "bat vigilante" which was well done, but they didn't have time to commit so Perry says to stop. For whatever reason, Superman listens making the BvS fight way less interesting. The scene I looked most forward to was the press scene. They asked several good, deep questions and so I was excited to see Superman answer those giving a counter argument but they ended up the meeting before it got interesting!!!! This movie had so many themes I couldn't keep track (I don't think the writers could either) and the one opportunity to wrap them all together, they ruined. By the end they had so many themes introduced I couldn't even tell what each character was fighting for. The worst is, I really, really enjoyed most of this movie but the clunky story telling made it hard to concentrate on what was going on. This is more of a preference, but Zach Snyder's editing doesn't work for me. He lingers on shots for too long, has awkward slow motion and also overuse of flashing CGI making it hard to watch. At the end, something emotional happens, but the way it was shot was so vague it's impossible to feel what's going on. Lastly, there are so many stories branching off and none had real closure. This made the whole movie feel so unsatisfying and anticlimactic. Overall, the things I like were so outweighed by the- not large in quantity-blatant story issues. There is some good fan service so go see it for the fun of seeing all it go down.

review:

I think what many dislike of this film is the lack of comedy act. Here, you won't have 1 hour of comedy skit, 1 hour of war against robots and 30 minutes of romance... no it's a pure superhero against superhero hate with lots of flashback (that were needed) and cool villain.

THE CAMEOS... Aquaman, Flash, Cyborg... they all look good and will have their single movies as well if they don't screw up productions... the way Wonder Woman discovered them was fascinating. Like some detective film.

The Score... the very intelligent score by Hans Zimmer (Dark Knight Trilogy) and Junkie XL (Deadpool). i have been listening to the score before and after seeing the film, and it's even better after. My favourite themes are ''Is She with you'' aka Wonder Woman theme... ''This is my World'' that is also used a little bit in Man of Steel. ''Men are still good (Batman Suite)'' is also pretty good listening.

I saw the film in Ultra AVX D-Box 3D... yup it cost me over 20$ for the ticket. I would never never experience a film as complete as this one. The 3D is pretty cool, i'm not a fan of 3D films but in the first 10 minutes of the film, i already say to my friends ''Hey proper use of the3D, huh!'' which they respond ''F*** yeah !!!''

The running time of the film may seem to be long, 155 minutes, but i would have taken 180 anytime with that kind of directing.

title: Marvel's schadenfreude
review:
Welcome to 2016 - the year where NO HEROES CAN BE FRIENDS. And here, amidst the releases of Daredevil vs. Punisher, Captain America vs. Iron Man (+ Marvel entourages), and X-Men vs. Other X-Men (sort of), comes DC comics' massive, go- for-broke tent-pole for its own super-franchise, too serious, even, for the conventional "vs": Batman v. Superman Colon Dawn of Justice - the (self- declared) "greatest gladiator match in the history of the world". But, after the dust settled, and my ears stopped ringing from the Hans Zimmer sledgehammering, we reflect on the adjective choice. Greatest? Nah. Surliest? Messiest? Unintentionally silliest? Better. But seriously (for being serious is about all it does) - the film is so hallucinogenically, histrionically mishandled that it almost defies belief. Visual pizazz aside, we're closer to Batman & Robin than Batman Begins (yup, I went there); more Breaking Dawn than Dawn of Justice.

You'd expect BvS to be excessively grim and mopey, with an overinflated sense of self-importance (all of which are true). What you don't expect is how downright strange it is. Amidst its two-and-a-half hour running time, there is more time devoted to Batman hallucinating abduction by alien bug monsters than actually battling Superman. Characters spout dialogue so utterly odd (Jeremy Irons' wry Alfred - a momentary highlight - blathers similes about "Mozart on the harpsichord"; Holly Hunter's scowling senator spits allusions like "rasslin' a pig" and "p*ss in a jar") it's more jaw-dropping than the film's action. And everything is so drenched in half-cocked discussions about Gods and morality it plays like a drunk football player puked in a theology textbook. And then it hits us: Zack Snyder, unsatisfied with delivering the pugilistics fans so desperately crave, is striving for artistry. For profundity. The problem? Snyder, while gifted at conjuring undeniably stunning, albeit showy, cinematic tableaux (though his best here are pilfered from Frank Miller, natch), has all the profundity of a popsicle stick. Seeing him sprinkle in dopey fantasy/dream interludes with such delirious abandon is so unintentionally amusing you almost feel guilty for jeering.

This batsh*t (ha) solemnity seeps into the plot as well. Initially, focalizing the plot around the criticisms of Man of Steel's collateral damage is clever, but Snyder's head is too much in the clouds to know where to take it from there. At least twice, characters pause, extensively, midway through cumbersome, meandering monologues, as if even they're literally forgotten what they're talking about, and it's the most honest the film ever is. Hands up if you came to a movie titled Batman v. Superman eager for nearly two hours of nonsensical, stalling subplots about African arms dealers, corporate subterfuge and computer hacking, Scoot McNairy's screeching amputee defacing Superman statues with the words "False God" (yawn), and Lawrence Fishburne's Perry White griping about travel expenses? How about the beloved (not) Marvel-derivative 'universe building' tie-ins to other future Justice League members so gratuitous it's gleefully disgraceful? Yeah, I thought not.

But plot schmott - let them fight. Problem here? Snyder's internalized Man of Steel's critiques so much that even he seems to despise Superman, regulating him to a supporting character, bereft of development, and more destructive narrative prop than character - a fate not helped by Henry Cavill's unfathomably surly, charmless performance. So: Batfleck, then? Not so much. Affleck looks the part (and his batsuit/armour do look spectacular), but, despite hints of promise in his haggard rage, his brooding mostly comes across as sleepiness. Moreover, he's besieged by the script's violently uneven misreading of the character, plaguing him with so much vacant staring we genuinely worry for his mental wellbeing. Hell, it would explain his impulse that Superman's inability to prevent collateral damage warrants being viciously stabbed to death as a preventative measure (listen for Christian "I have one rule" Bale weeping at the back of the theatre). So, the two heroes sneer and posture at each other redundantly, and we can't help but despite them both, let alone give a damn who wins.

And when they do - FINALLY - trade blows? They don't so much fight as take turns pummelling each other while the other lays there, stunned, crashing around a deserted building, as Hans Zimmer bwomps away in the background. It's impossible to imagine a more underwhelming, less cathartic, imaginative, and thrilling bout - and its resolution, where Batman flips from attempted murder to being bosom buddies with Superman, is so abrupt and for so ludicrously inane a reason, it plays like an SNL parody, and is just as deliciously hilarious. Thankfully, the climactic showdown with completely unsurprising twist villain Doomsday does - FINALLY - perk things up a bit, providing both a more mobile foe and the introduction of Gal Godot's Wonder Woman (who is introduced by an 80s hair metal guitar riff, of all things), though it still plays as an overcooked remake of The Incredible Hulk's Harlem brawl. Otherwise, there's really perilously little redemption to be found here. Jesse "Mmm!" Eisenberg's Luthor, even more unmotivated than Batman, is a squeaky, gibbering mess of tics, like a high school student doing an impression of Heath Ledger's Joker, while Amy Adams' Lois is such a whiny damsel it's genuinely embarrassing. Even Wonder Woman has her undeniably cool entrance marred by cameras lingering on her chest and crotch like a 90s video game. Classy.

The thing is, so many of BvS' innumerable flaws could be tolerated - stupid plot, dubious writing, and even boring fights - if it were fun. But Snyder's odyssey of awfulness is so drab, grim, and odiously self-satisfied that fun is like a long-lost mythical concept, with only shards remaining, deeply buried, like elusive kryptonite. The film's most worthwhile attribute has been an interview of Affleck confronted by early critical panning. A sea of disappointment dances across his face, calling the bluff of the colossal, shameful dud he's staked his recent reputation to. Batfleck is now Sadfleck. Now that's justice.

-4/10

title: Much better than I thought it would be
review:
Early reviews before opening were not kind to this movie, but I did not find much of the commentary correct, and I found Affleck well cast. It was quite entertaining, well made, very well acted. Plus, I was surprised to see some valid plot reasons to pit these two characters against each other, something I couldn't really fathom in advance.

Some plot connectivity seemed a bit weak, and I would have thought, considering how long it is, that would have been corrected. Still, very enjoyable for action movie fans, and my parting advice is: watch the final 2 seconds very closely. Worth the ticket price, although I did not find the 3D worthwhile.

title: Much better than I expected
review: I was not looking forward to this movie for so many reasons. I thought the Dark Knight movies nailed Batman's character unlike the previous versions. I didn't want a new version. I grew up a DC fan and have collected the comics forever. Believe me when I say that this is the first time every character (except Lex Luthor) played their roles exactly like they were portrayed in the comics. Ben Affleck had and amazing, gritty portrayal of Batman that honestly is how he is supposed to be played.I also enjoyed Superman much more this time around.

But this movie tries to put way too much story lines into this movie. Just so you know how many story lines they put I will list them out Death of Superman, Batman vs Superman, Justice League Origin, Darkseid or Apocalypse origin, and hinting at The Killing Joke. This movie tries to do entirely too much but that being said THEY HAVE TOO!!! People do not seem to understand this but DC has about 2 to 3 years to catch up to Marvel before it becomes impossible. They have to kick things off fast. They do not have the same amount of time that Marvel does. DC kicked things off amazingly with this movie though.

Finally I want to add that Marvel and DC are not the same comic books. Stop comparing them now or you will just be disappointed. DC is much more gritty and dark than Marvel and people need to accept that.

title: I like the movie but I somehow can not love the movie
review:
Okay..this is my first time I write a review. I'm a huge Superman and DC fan. I'm so desperately wanting to love this movie but somehow I can't. Seeing it for the fourth time kinda self explanatory. I can't feel connected to the way Snyder, Goyer and Terrio presented this movie. I do understand they take this movie with the dark and gritty tone to become a jumping point to the whole DCEU.

I was so hyped before seeing this movie for the first time. I mean it's the two most iconic characters ever brought together to the silver screen. I like the movie very much but I don't love it. I enjoyed the movie more the second time I saw it than the first time and I started to love it a little. Seeing it the third time really bummed me out cause I could saw more flaws than before. After seeing it the fourth time, I could definitely tell that I don't love this movie. But I still like it a lot.

Everything in this movie is so amazingly taken. Except for the first 20-30 minutes of the movie. It was felt rushed as subplots and kinda all over the place. They also need to build the characters better so that we, as audience, could connect to and care more about them. Nevertheless, it's a great movie but with many flaws. Although not perfect, but the way the scenes were taken is awesome. It was a very beautiful movie. Snyder is a great director when it comes to visual and action scenes. But I don't think he is a great storyteller. I do really like the score by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL. Makes me appreciate the album more. I also love how every character has their own theme. Furthermore, there were so many easter eggs in this movie, which I like by the way.

Eisenberg Lex was A-mazing! I love how Luthor is portrayed in this film. It was genuinely new and fresh. You really don't wanna mess with this evil-psychotic genius bastard. Batflex really sold me out!! Kudos to that. By far he is the best Batman ever. Gal Gadot was hot and badass though her acting seemed a little bit wooden in one scene. Her score was really dope. I can't wait to see her solo movie. Henry Cavill's performance was better than in Man of Steel but he was overshadowed by the above three. Ezra Miller's scene totally blew me away. Jeremy Irons was fantastic. I like the Alfred here. Amy Adams was okay. This Lois was doing a better reporting job than in MoS. I don't really like Jason Momoa here. He's a little bit awkward I think.

However, this movie supposed to have the title Dawn of Justice instead. The ending should have gone with a different direction. Too soon to kill an important character here. The fight scene and final act should have longer duration. Also, this movie is probably hard to digest for a non hardcore DC fan.

I think everyone should watch this movie at least once. It's a great movie with cool action scenes and awesome music. It's not perfect, it could've been better but it's still epic. Finally, I really looking forward to see the 3 hrs R-rated version of this movie.

title: Tried to do too much. Average.
review: Definitely better than Man of Steel, and definitely better than some Marvel movies out there. I knew entering the cinema this movie would be average, but was still very excited to see it. As soon as the movie started it plunged into Batman's perspective on Superman, and beautifully showed his growing hate towards him. Loved the idea of Superman being a figure of controversy, and loved the dialogue surrounding this. Loved Jesse Eisenberg's (Lex Luthor) acting, and loved his role as the puppeteer in the movie. Also loved the action between Batman and Superman. However, I was not a fan of everything else that happened. The movie moved into the justice league arc, and foreshadowed the later movies to come (expressed through visions Batman had). This was random and felt forced, leaving viewers with little knowledge of this world, wondering what the hell was going on. It tried too hard to fit Wonderwoman in, when she could well have stayed out of the movie. The sudden alliance between Batman and Superman was very unconvincing and was far too sudden (especially since the movie did not give an origin story to Batman or expressed the pain of his parents death), leaving the first half of the movie fairly redundant. I would have liked to see Batman and Superman's fight get more screen time. As the movie tried to fit all these extra parts in (such as Doomsday, Wonderwoman, Superman morality crisis, Justice League), their fight was very quick with Batman defeating Superman fairly quickly. This was disappointing for me as the movie was called "Batman vs. Superman" and I wanted to see that.

title: Just Beautiful
review:
Over the past 3 years, I've had so much hype for this movie, and it exceeded all my expectations.

One reason I believe the critics and general public did not like BvS was because they could not follow the first half the movie. There were a lot of different cuts shifting back and forth among Bruce Wayne's point of view, Superman's, Lois Lane's, Lex, etc. I was able to follow along with each character's point of view and felt that it flowed fairly well.

Eisenberg was a great Lex Luthor. Luthor is a maniac, and he is portrayed perfectly in this movie. A deceptive maniac who is so manipulative and puts people against each other. People complain about how this Lex just reminds them of Joker or a Riddler. Who cares? Snyder took Luthor in a new direction, one that a lot of people aren't used to. It's refreshing to see Snyder's influence from the comics but also taking a new approach and changing things up.

Gal Gadot is a gem. So beautiful and her role as Wonder Woman was amazing. She was fierce, strong, calm, all the virtues of Wonder Woman. Perfect casting choice.

Ben Affleck did a great job as Batman. One major fight scene where Batman takes down a bunch of henchmen (seen in the trailers) was incredible from start to finish. It was terrifying to see how merciless Batman was, but so needed. This Batman (in the movies) has been in the game for 20 years, so he's going to do whatever it takes to save people.

I really enjoyed the subtle jokes throughout the movie. Jeremy Irons as Alfred was well done (super witty and funny).

Cinematography was amazing, music by Hans Zimmer never ceases to amaze me. My favorite soundtrack of all time, with the Dark Knight trilogy right behind it.

There's a lot to take in, but I'd advise watching it a second time to get a better understanding if there are questions that are left unanswered. This movie opened up the DC universe and now DC has so many directions to go with the solo films. The cameos of Flash, Cyborg, Aquaman put a huge smile on my face. This movie was everything I've wanted and more.

title: Great Saturday Fun
review:
I spent two days reading negative reviews of this movie before I actually saw it in the theater. I think I got lucky, because the film the critics describe is nothing like the one I viewed.

I wasn't bored at all, and the movie has a nice build to the climax. I see it as essentially a Lex Luthor origin story underneath the hood, with most of the film focused on Superman and Batman. I thought I would be irritated by Eisenberg's Lex, but quite the opposite. I think his character is going to be great in upcoming movies and BvS left me wanting to see more of him.

Wonder Woman is a fantastic mystery. Who is she? Where does she come from? She has that smartest-person-in-the-room feel about her and her superpowers are awesome to watch.

There were a lot of fill-in-the-blanks moments, but I like that. I don't need everything spoon fed to me like Lex shoving a Jolly Rancher into someone's mouth. I still am not sure why Superman's mom works in a diner, but hey, it's a comic book movie! There is a lot of ridiculous nonsense in comics, which is a big part of their charm. The foreshadowing at the end of the film is excellent and I am looking forward to what comes next in the DC Universe.

title: Excellent Comic Book Movie
review:
In terms of comic book movies, I've only liked Watchmen, The Dark Knight trilogy, Punisher, and the Wolverine movies because I felt they were more serious, mature, dark, and more R-rated.

I never liked the other comic book movies such as X-Men, Spider-Man, Ant-Man, Avengers, Iron-Man, Captain America, or Thor because I thought they were too light and fluffy and too PG-rated.

Just like in the 2nd season of Marvel's Daredevil, I loved it when The Punisher and Elektra were on screen and didn't really care for Daredevil because he's too much of a Boy Scout. I mean seriously, who would fight sword-wielding ninjas with sticks?

When villains come at this new Batman with a gun, he doesn't respond with a slingshot. When people come at this new Batman with a knife, he doesn't respond with a stick. When people fire machine guns at this Batman, he answers with his own machine guns.

BvS doesn't try to lecture politics or preach good vs evil. It makes no apologies for its uninhibited realism. It immerses the audience in this dark and dire DC universe. And I thank Zack Snider for this. Thank you for Watchen, 300, and now BvS. I forgive you for Man of Steel.

No comic book movie is ever perfect. Watchmen came the closest IMO. And BvS came a close second.

I think the people (both users and critics) who disliked BvS just didn't understand this movie, especially the ending of the movie.

Overall, I truly enjoyed this movie and I look forward to watching Wonder Woman and the Justice League movies (Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, The Flash, Aquaman, and Cyborg).

title: A Superhero Punchup
review:
I later found out that this film was universally panned by the critics, but then again what do the critic's really know – sometimes I wonder if they really know how to enjoy a good movie, but then again they probably watch so many movies that they have actually forgotten the art of simply going to the cinema to enjoy a good movie. Okay, I will have to admit that the best part of the movie was right at the beginning when one of the audience members screamed out 'go Batman!'. I have to admit, especially since Nolan's trilogy, I've always had a soft spot for the Dark Night, and never been a huge fan of The Man of Steel.

Anyway, I think the problem is that Snyder is simply trying to do too much in this film. It is clear, from the title no less, that this is a lead up to a Justice League movie (no doubt an attempt to cash in on the popularity of the Avengers movies), however since it is slated for release in 2017 he is limited in what he can do. We've also just come out of a very successful Batman franchise so Synder was somewhat restrained in how he could bring Batman into the universe, and he does so through a direct sequel to Man of Steel.

At the beginning of the film Superman is fighting General Zod and Bruce Wayne, who is actually quite old at this time, is somewhat angered at the fact that during the battle 1000s of people (including a number of his employees when one of his buildings collapsed) were killed, and lays the blame directly at Superman's feet. In fact he has developed an intense distrust of Superman, namely because he is incredibly powerful, is not of this world, and doesn't seem to answer to anybody. Okay, Batman may be a vigilante, but in Bruce Wayne's mind this is okay because he has been doing it for years – Superman's the new kid on the block. However, it is clear that all of his villainous counterparts are dead and Gotham seems to be just as crime ridden today as it was when his parents were killed.

If there is one thing that I didn't particularly like and that was Lex Luther, but then again I've never liked Lex Luther. It feels that he simply gets overused, to the point that he seems to be the villain in every piece. It was one of the things I didn't like about the original films, because Lex Luther simply always seemed to come back with another nefarious way to destroy Superman. Okay, in this film he was somewhat crazier than the calculated villain that you usually encounter, however he is still a pain in the neck. Also, while trying not to give too much away, when he gets arrested at the end of the film I'm sort of wandering what happens to his company. Okay, we will probably find out down the track, but I hope it is dismantled and sold off. Doing the type of things that Luther does in the film is most likely going to result in the US Government confiscating all of his assets and selling them off to the highest bidder.

title: Loved it. One of the greatest superhero movies ever made...
review:
...right up there with "The Dark Knight" Trilogy and the first "Avengers," IMHO. I don't agree with a single critique from the legions of haters. The script was imaginative, philosophical, tight and witty - yes, it had some great humor, so it was not the relentlessly downbeat bummer you might expect, based on inexplicably negative reviews - in fact, I found the camaraderie and chemistry between the main protagonists quite inspirational. The politics were timely, the morality was compelling debated, the special effects and dreamlike cinematography were stunning, and the lead characters were all suitably complex, emotionally and psychologically.

For my money (literally), this movie fired on all cylinders, from casting to pacing to tone to interwoven story arcs to spectacular (and sensible) set-up for "The Justice League." It wasn't nearly as "dark" and much more fun than I was led to believe - moody and atmospheric, yes, but hardly nihilistic. The Nolan Bat-films were far more violent and brutal (and way less kid-friendly), though this latest incarnation should satisfy Bat-fans all of all generations, from Bob Kane and Bill Finger (finally given his due screen credit!!) to Frank Miller, borrowing elements from each era, forming the most faithful live action version of the character yet (though Adam West will always have a soft, sentimental place in my heart, and he was the ideal "camp" doppelganger, totally true to the comics of his time).

Ben Affleck absolutely nails the role, in and out of the costume, which is also the best yet - doesn't look like melted down tires for a change (sorry, Christian Bale - you know I still love you, affected deep gravelly voice and all). Batfleck's triumphant acting here reminded me of the backlash against Daniel Craig when he was first announced as Bond - and then he went ahead and proved he was more than worthy of that storied, beloved legacy. In fact, this is my favorite big screen portrayal of both Batman and Superman to date, and while no one can ever replace Lynda Carter in my heart, Gal Gadot kicked serious ass on every level, adding a uniquely exotic, intriguingly mysterious, mystical, mythical allure to the character. I am now even more anxious to see her solo "Wonder Woman" next year. I hope Affleck does a solo Batman soon too, since this movie perfectly balanced screen time between him and Superman, so despite the length, which literally flew by without a dull moment, it just left me wanting more. Batman's action sequences and fight scenes were brilliantly choreographed and executed.

Cavill really steps up his game here as well. This movie plays successfully as both a far superior sequel to "Man of Steel" and an ingenious followup to the Nolan trilogy. Superman here is brooding and conflicted, but also soulful and heroic - much like Batman, qualities which ultimately bond them. The depictions of both icons were both refreshingly original and canonically correct, as opposed to pointlessly revisionist. Initially I was most skeptical about the casting of Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, but by the end, he was an entertainingly offbeat yet ultimately definitive take on that legendary super-villain. Casting-wise, Zack Snyder's instincts were right on the money.

When this project was first announced, I was hoping for another cinematic comic book on the level of "Watchmen" and he did not disappoint (me, anyway). Contrary to some reports, there were only a couple of (extremely interesting) "dream sequences" that did not interrupt the flow of the narrative whatsoever, Basically, I don't understand any of the vitriol aimed at this neo-noir pulp epic - which totally winds up feeling like an issue of "World's Finest" or an episode of "Super Friends" during the finale, which was a bit too CGI-heavy for my tastes, but so are all of these blockbusters nowadays. In short, this was just further evidence of why I always ignore mainstream film critics and reserve judgment until I've seen the object of raging fan boy controversy myself. Cheers.

title: They learned from the Man of Steel and delivered a great movie!
review:
I just saw BVS (not Buffy the Vampire Slayer.... I am talking about Batman vs Superman) and here are my thoughts

SPOILER ALTERT

I score it 9/10

I loved Batman vs Superman! I loved the mature mythological line of thought, I actually liked Ben Afflick as Batman/Bruce Wayne. And Wonder Woman? It was interesting and cool (even though you can see some Xena elements, but then we saw Wonder Woman elements in Xena, so I guess the circle is complete). I want to see now the Wonder Woman movie.

She showed up in the right moment and convinced us she is a powerful warrior capable of fighting a kryptonian monster.

I found very interesting the comparisons with god, false gods and false messiah, and the way they portrayed Superman's vulnerability, which is not kryptonite, but his humanity, his feelings. How, in the middle of the battle he can just fly away to rescue Lois or his mother, instead of focusing on the real threat.

Bruce Waynes nightmares, and Flash's warning, prove this could be very important and dangerous in the future. And that Lex Luthor figure it out right away and used them against him.

Lex Luthor new take was refreshing. Not the Lex we are used to, but very modern, and has lots of potential.

I loved the grown up Bruce Wayne.

The movie kept my attention every second. I didn't look at my watch once, and couldn't find a minute that I could spare to go to the bathroom.

I would have loved to see more of the Clark/Lois relationship. And of course more Superman. But the movie revolved around the Superman effect in the world after the events of Man of Steel, and Bruce Wayne reaction to it.

The people that made this movie learned from the Man of Steel, and limited the fights and violence length to what is necessary and avoided long and boring battle scenes and excessive destruction.

My only complaint, and it is a very minor complain, is regarding Doomsday and the Death of Superman. I think Doomsday should have been an entire movie, not just the final 10 minutes.

But since we know Superman will come back to life, maybe we will see Doomsday comeback in another movie and make more damage.

I like it that DC is differentiating themselves from Marvel by making mature movies, while Marvel make lighter movies. I like them both. There is space for both. And Deadpool proved that there is space for adult superhero movies too.

What I expect for the future?

Well, I would love to see a Man of Steel solo movie before the Batman solo movie, since they stole a sequel from us with BvS.

There is a Justice League movie coming up, so maybe they could flirt with a relationship between Superman and Wonder Woman.

This movie opens the door to many things. I hope they make them great!

NEW ENTRY

OK. I just saw BvS for the third time. I still like it, but now I am scoring it around 7. The reason? Superman never speaks! I mean whats the point of having Lois Lane as your girlfriend if you are not going to give her an exclusive interview explaining what happened? That would have been so easy! I was expecting a more vocal Superman.

title: Great film...even better if you are a DC fan
review: This film was a great movie but it had a few problems. The pros do ,however, outweigh the cons. Story- personally for me, I really enjoyed the story because you had to fit it together yourself and wasn't really obvious. This movie did require you to think and although the core storyline was there you had to fit things you heard earlier in order for any of the motivations to make sense. Action- The movie has action throughout the movie and has nice story driven moments in between. I would say that about 40% of the film was action. When action did occur, it was absolutely amazing and what else would you expect from Zack Snyder. Notable fights include: batman's nightmare, batmobile Chase, batman v superman fight, doomsday fight finale. Wonder woman- I loved wonder women in this movie as she delivers all her lines with terrorising accent that makes you feel as though she is Amazonian. Her fight scene at the end with doomsday was amazing. She uses her sword, gauntlets, shield and lasso in the fight and it flows together nicely. Batman- one of the best characters in the movie. Hellbent on taking down superman. He is actually extremely creepy as batman and is almost James bond-esque in his Bruce Wayne scenes. Finally we see batman using detective skills and all of his gadgets. Batman is simply brilliant and wonder woman and him make this movie deserve at least 5 stars. Lex luthor- this character is extremely interesting because he is not the lex we know and yet he is at the same time. He is quirky, weird, awkward and also extremely terrifying. The moment he enters a room, it just makes things tense. Edditing- the first twenty minutes is very jumpy but after lex's party it all comes into focus.This would be my only problem with the film. Doomsday- although he looked crap in the trailer, he looks a lot better in the film. He also has an amazing fight with the trinity. One of the best parts of the movie. The military activation was all there. Batman v Superman- although the fight happened a lot later than expected it fit perfectly with the story and as you watch superman try to convince batman that lex has played them both you really feel bad for superman. This fight was good and straight out of the graphic novel. There was also some interesting stuff involving their parents in the fight. Over all verdict - statement - my favourite comic book film since iron man 1.

title: Batman v Superman goes in a different direction to other superhero movies - And that's a good thing! (NO SPOILERS)

title: Not bad but could have been better for sure...
review:
What is this movie? It is sequel to man of steel+flight from dark knight returns+superman doomsday+ bits of Injustice gods among us+ bits of batman superman public enemies+ bit of flashpoint paradox

Woah, that's too much to fit in 2.5 hrs, isn't it? and that's what the problem is with the movie. DC wanted to start their universe in a bit different manner than Marvel and I really appreciate that but historically (in The Dark Knight Returns) Batman and Superman fight at end of their careers! which is even after Justice League is disbanded so what makes them fight here is a weak manipulation plot which doesn't look that convincing. Historically whenever Batman was at low - Dark Knight Returns came in, when Superman was low - Death of Superman came in and that's exactly what Snyder and Terrio try to do here making it a big giant trailer for Justice League.

There are many plot holes/questions available online. Some of them are completed edited out ( May be like Watchmen, the director's cut of BvS will be better than theatrical release ) and for some of them you need to have knowledge about DC comics(para-demons, Darkseid, Injustice, knightmares).

Acting? Ben affleck nails it as Bruce and Batman, I want to see more of him, may be in Justice League or solo Batman movie. Those who have problems in digesting this brutal, darker Batman should read Dark Knight Returns, this is still a toned down version than Dark Knight Returns. Cavill? brings out emotional side of superman very strongly. Gadot? very small screen time but makes us want more of Wonderwoman. Amy Adams has much longer role than I expected. Ezra Miller's Flash looks promising. Jesse Eisenberg plays Jesse Eisenberg and we have to accept him as Luthor. Not bad but a different more psychotic take on Luthor. May be he will become the good old serious Luthor once he comes out of Jail. Doomsday? perhaps he was not even required in movie.

Well with so much hype, media campaigns and publicity, this surely won't fail in bringing lot of capital amount Warner Bros needs for next films but better, shorter and sensible plot would have helped restoring my trust on DC in making a successful franchise.

Why 10 stars because I still have a bit of hope that upcoming DC movies will be better than this one. 7 stars for this one being overall entertaining and 3 for the hope.
