title: Almost Perfect....
review:
Eighteen months after the destructive battle in Metropolis (Man of Steel), Superman has become a controversial figure. Billionaire Bruce Wayne, who has covertly operated in Gotham City as vigilante "Batman" for nearly two decades, blames Superman for the mass casualties that resulted from his fight with General Zod. Superman, in his public identity as Daily Planet journalist Clark Kent, sees Batman as dangerous and seeks to expose him. LexCorp's mogul Lex Luthor also sees Superman as a threat and convinces Senator June Finch to help him recover kryptonite from Zod's failed terraforming attempt from the Indian Ocean. Finch later stonewalls Lex's efforts to use Zod's DNA and the Kryptonian scout ship recovered from the battle to create a biological weapon.

Wayne infiltrates a fundraiser promoted by Luthor to retrieve data from LexCorp's mainframe, but his drive is stolen by mysterious antiques dealer Diana Prince, who learns that Luthor has files on herself, as well as individuals with superhuman speed (Flash), a cybernetic body (Cyborg), and a man that lives underwater (Aquaman). Wayne later receives the drive back from her after she copies it. He learns not only of Luthor's experiments with kryptonite, but also his ongoing investigation about metahumans including Prince herself, who is an immortal warrior. Batman attempts to retrieve Luthor's kryptonite, but is intercepted by Superman, who orders him to cease his activities. Later, Finch summons Superman to a Congressional hearing at the U.S. Capitol to debate the validity of his actions, where Luthor masterminds a bombing that kills dozens of people, including Finch. The public blames the bombing on Superman, who goes into self-imposed exile.

Batman retrieves the kryptonite and prepares to launch a strike against Superman; building a powerful exoskeleton and kryptonite- powered arsenal. With Batman now having the kryptonite, Luthor activates the Genesis Chamber aboard the scout ship and splices his own DNA and Zod's. Luthor endangers Superman's love interest Lois Lane to lure him to LexCorp Tower, where he reveals that he has been aware of Superman's secrets for some time. Lex blackmails Superman into confronting Batman by holding his adoptive mother, Martha Kent, hostage at an undisclosed location, anticipating that Batman would kill Superman with his kryptonite. Superman tries to reason with Batman, revealing that he knows his secrets, but leading to a fight in which Batman nearly kills Superman with a kryptonite spear. Superman pleads for Batman to "save Martha", which was also the latter's late mother's name, causing him to come to his senses and realize Superman is not a threat. Upon learning of Luthor's plan, Batman leaves to rescue Martha while Superman confronts Luthor, who unleashes a monstrous artificially bred creature (Doomsday) made with Kryptonian technology on the crashed ship. Superman and Batman join forces to fight him and are aided by an arriving Prince in her Amazonian attire, but are outmatched due to the creature's ability to absorb and redirect energy. Realizing that their shared Kryptonian DNA results in shared vulnerabilities, Superman retrieves the kryptonite spear and sacrifices himself to impale the creature with it, while the creature stabs Superman with his bone protrusions, seemingly killing him.

Luthor is arrested after Lane exposes his numerous crimes; when he is visited by Batman in prison, he gloats that Superman's death has made the world vulnerable to powerful threats, of which he was taught about while manipulating the Kryptonian ship's technology. Batman threatens Lex, and promises that he will always be watching Luthor. A memorial is held for Superman in Metropolis, and as Clark is also declared dead, Wayne, Lane, Martha, and Prince attend a private ceremony in Smallville. Martha passes an envelope to Lois, which contains an engagement ring from Clark to Lois. After the funeral, Wayne reveals to Prince that he plans to form a team (Justice League) from Luthor's file subjects to protect the world in Superman's absence. Later, a faint heartbeat begins echoing from Superman's grave and the dirt around it begins to levitate.

You should really watch this movie especially if you're a big fan of batman because Ben Affleck was so bad-ass.Henry Cavill (superman) was also good in this movie

9/10.

title: Really promising movie squandered by Justice League set-up and embarrassing finale.
review: What started so promisingly with a superb Batman and political back-story was totally ruined by a finale battle with a throwaway CGI monster that left me with my head in my hands... and a migraine. Too many subplots were juggled and it ultimately fell apart. I would have been delighted with a straight-up MoS sequel dealing with the previous film's fallout, or one that focused solely on the two heroes' conflict, or best of all - a Batfleck solo movie. In the end, we got a bloated film with excess Justice League baggage that didn't improve on Man of Steel's flaws - it was as if Zack Snyder ignored the criticisms and worsened them. It was even bleaker, with less humour, and even greater gratuitous collateral damage. Which brings me to the ending, and spoilers follow. The title fight barely lives up to the hype - it's short and one-sided - and then a completely unnecessary half hour is tacked on, featuring a large mutant creature created by Lex Luthor. Cue a series of incomprehensible nuclear-level explosions, as people are punched and blown up and buildings levelled. For no reason. I was embarrassed to be sitting there watching it. What makes that so disappointing is due to the promise of what came before; it's not a disaster of a movie. Their conflict is justified and established well, in an intriguing political context. Ben Affleck conveys the pain and the rage of a tortured Bruce Wayne/Batman like none before him, and thoroughly impresses, as does his compatriot Jeremy Irons, who delivers in spades. However, it says a lot that the only other stand out was Laurence Fishburne as the newspaper editor. ("Crime wave sweeps Gotham. In other news: 'Water. Wet.''') It's not that Henry Cavill and Amy Adams are bad, it's just that the characters are given so little by way of range. The first hour is thoroughly decent, but what the film lacks is focus - it ultimately feels like a contrived attempt to hurriedly set up the Justice League, and should have focused on the titular battle, and certainly could do without the last 30 minutes.

title: A Brilliant, Exciting Kickstart To The DC Cinematic Universe
review:
I struggle to understand the severity of critics towards this movie. Personally, I think it was absolutely amazing. Granted, it has its flaws, but the highs of this movie far outrank the lows.

The plot itself was fantastic and well-executed. Where I worried Zach Snyder was going to dwell too long on back story, he laid it out in an efficient, need-to-know basis and saved most of the movie's time for the main plot. Where I likewise worried the conflict between Batman and Superman would feel too forced, I walked out of the theater feeling as if the animosity made sense and came naturally.

Ben Affleck and Henry Cavill knocked it out of the park with their roles. Ben's role as Batman was very Nolan-esque; being a fan of Dark Knight trilogy, I appreciated the respect to the style. Henry Cavill does a good Superman and brings out more of what made him good in Man of Steel. Of course, Gal Gadot did a good job as Wonder Woman. (SPOILER) Though the story mainly rested on Batman and Superman, she did a good job of playing her role against Doomsday and more than proved her potential for a Wonder Woman movie.

Granted, there's a lot of conflict over Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, but personally I think he is my favorite super villain in the cinematic superhero universes we have all seen thus far. His over-the-top personality and abrasiveness were fantastic and his poetic, philanthropic nature helped establish his motives. Even in his (SPOILER) terrible speech at a public event, he hints at grander motives and busied thoughts all leading up to a greater scheme. Though many would have preferred a more toned down Lex as in the comics, I beg to differ. Jesse's was an enjoyable take.

The (SPOILER) fight scenes could have gone a little longer, the (SPOILER) Batmobile chase should have been a little more spread out, and I'm not sure Lois Lane in the bathtub was really necessary (actually, I thought that scene with Clark Kent was a little creepy) but that's really just me trying to find something wrong with the movie. In a nutshell, Batman v Superman is a must watch. Not perfect, but definitely groundbreaking and promising for the future of the DC Cinematic Universe.

(SPOILER) There is no end credit scene. My friends and I sat in the theater waiting for one and no scene showed, although I don't mind too much. The whole "let's tease future events in the credits" gimmick got a little old after a while, so props to Zach Snyder for eschewing that old trick.

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice Reviews
review:
BATMAN V SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE is an incredibly fun movie. There are a handful of moments that frustrated the living hell out of me, but I was able to surpass them the more I continued watching the film, and I'm glad I did. Just like MAN OF STEEL, the film is split towards the middle with fans and critics. It's a love/hate film. It's not for everyone I must say.

Let's start with the negatives. I hated when they killed off characters that have a significance to the lore of the DC Universe. I won't say who, but to those who have seen it, you know what I'm talking about. Another thing that I had a problem with was the pacing of the film and that it was a bit all over the place deciding whether it wants to be a Batman vs. Superman movie or a Justice League prequel. Another topic that is similar to that is that it is too focused on world building, which was one of the main problems with IRON MAN 2 and THE AMAZING SPIDER-MAN 2. Not to say that I hate those movies, but one of the main problems is that it's too concerned with creating this world and forgetting that they're making a movie. One element that aggravated me was some of the choices some of the characters make in the film.

Now, on with the stuff that I loved. The best part about the movie is the Trinity itself. Henry Cavill remains to be a fantastic Superman, But the real scene stealer's are Ben Affleck as Batman and Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. Every scene Batman was in were some of the best parts of the film, and when Wonder Woman appeared on screen in costume, the crowd cheered. After seeing her, now I'm even more pumped to see her solo movie. Another actor who I thought did a phenomenal acting job was Jeremy Irons as Alfred. There was something about him that made me think "Yes! THAT is Alfred!" and I honestly have to say that he might be my favorite Alfred in general. The action sequences are absolutely gorgeous. There's a reason why Zack Snyder is one of my favorite visionary directors of all time, and this film goes to show why. And when the fight goes down, it is glorious! It's Frank Miller's BATMAN: THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS graphic novel come to life, and I wouldn't have it any other way.

Now, I'd like to talk about an element of the film that I felt very mixed about, and that is Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. When I first heard about this casting, I was 100% on board because of his performance in THE SOCIAL NETWORK. I thought to myself "If he plays Lex like this, it will be perfect." Well, I was in for quite a treat. Eisenberg's performance reminded me too much of Jim Carry as the Riddler. In fact, if I was told that Jesse Eisenberg was cast as the Riddler, I would have been more on board for that. However, the upside to that is Eisenberg is having a blast with this role and owns it as his own. He didn't seem too much like himself, which is a good thing. There were a few moments where he came off as a threat, but there were too many moments where he came off creepy or laughable. Hopefully, he'll evolve in the future.

Overall, BATMAN V SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE is a solid superhero film with a handful of flaws that people will notice but forgive, or be unforgivable depending on who that person is. It's not the greatest superhero film, but then again, it's not the worst. I'm looking forward to seeing Wonder Woman, Aquaman, Flash, Cyborg and many other characters get there own solo films after viewing this. I know that there is too much world building in this film, but at least it's a world that I'm looking forward to, especially with a Justice League movie coming out next year.

title: A Masterpiece
review:
My gf and I, both in our mid-30s, saw it this afternoon. I'm a huge DC fan. Overall a big comicbook fan, but mostly DC. I ABSOLUTELY LOVED IT! My girlfriend, who simply followed me, and who knows nothing about Superman & Batman other than seeing TDK trilogy and MoS once, loved it also.

Not one second were we bored. The movie was gripping from beginning to end. I had read all the bad reviews before going. And all throughout the film, I tried, and I mean, I really tried, to find the flaws the critics "found" that made it deserve a 1/10. My girlfriend had no clue of the reviews. I only told her after the movie to gauge her reaction. She was in shock. She thought it was one of the best comicbook movies ever, on par with the TDKs.

Again, I'm speechless on why this bombed critically. No humor?? Well I'm sorry, this was never, nor was it ever advertised as "The Avengers 3: Enter The Goofy DC Guys", nor "Transformers 7: The Revenge of the Humans". From the start, we knew that the destruction of Metropolis in MoS was going to be the main catalyst of the darkness in the sequel. I guess nothing spells the reaction to the destruction of half of a giant city, thousands of lives lost like Robert Downey's smart wit humor. I remember we were having a laugh after 9/11, right?

Pacing issues?? Have they seen Iron Man 2 & 3? Age of Ultron? ASM? Every scene in the movie had purpose. They managed to include tons of valuable material with minimal editing issues. We both felt the flow worked as perfectly as it could. You simply had to pay attention. I know it's hard nowadays to not be spoon-fed the material in brain- dead fashion, but for the life of all things decent, try it once in a while! Keep your eyes on the screen, focus, and maybe, JUST MAYBE, you might actually understand what's going on.

Character development?? For Christ's Sake, the first 40 minutes were ALL character development. How much more do you want?? Yet another full length Batman origin solo movie, this time with slapstick comedy specially tailored for kids who see their parents murdered in front of their eyes? Because, come on, what can possibly spell more comedy than the brutal death of your parents, or a psychotic serial killer clown... I remember laughing my ass off watching Seven. Now that was a great comedy we all had fun watching!

The Justice League elements were a distraction? Uhm, wha... what?? I'm not even going to get into this. They couldn't have made a more perfect introduction. I guess they meant just like Samuel L. Jackson was a distraction in all the non-Avengers Marvel movies... oh wait, apparently, he wasn't.

Batman too violent?? WTF, again, his actions made sense IN THE MOMENT. He NEVER went into the fight TRYING to kill. The "alleged" killing, if it even actually happened, was collateral damage. Nothing he did classified as murder.

The fight scenes? The best comicbook fights ever put on screen. And please, don't mention Deadpool... Not the same universe at all. It's like comparing the Raid 2 and Star Wars... It's just not comparable.

So overall, you might think I'm a crazy fanboy, call me names and whatnot. But I give it a 10/10. In all honesty, I did not find a flaw. If you twist my arm and hold my parents hostage just to squeeze one out of me, I would say there was too much character development. But I don't see how this could possibly be a reason to trash on the movie. It's usually the biggest critical aspect of CBMs. We finally go in-depth, and it's too much. F*** me.

I pray for WB to stick with the game plan and not change a thing. If the darkness is what the critics and jaded moviegoers are criticizing the most, then it's going to get lighter going forward. Terrio even said it. The darkness is at an all time high in BvS, for a purpose. The JL movies will have a lighter mood, just because the natural progression of the established story will lead it there.

I was not the biggest fan of Snyder after Sucker Punch. But I like Man of Steel (had flaws, did not love it, but like it). However, it's inhuman to trash on the man because you simply hate his previous projects. He created a comicbook masterpiece with BvS. I give him all the praise. And I hope WB continues the work already laid out.

title: "People hate what they don't understand"
review:
It's almost been 3 years since this film was announced at Comic-Con and after waiting for patiently for this long, I can safely say this film delivered. However, I've got to address the elephant in the room immediately. This film has been bashed and received unfair criticism from every minute detail- from Ben Affleck's casting as Batman to even Gal Gadot's looks; both of which were ridiculous. Point being, it's unsurprising to see the response it's received from "critics" because people had already formed preconceived ideas and opinions before it had even come out. Anyone can make an account of IMDb or Rotten Tomatoes, regardless of whether they had seen the film or not. This is a film that warrants a viewing before you judge it, because otherwise you'd be missing out on this gem.

The narrative revolves around Batman and Superman having clashing ideologies and conflicting perceptions of one another. Henry Cavil's Superman believes Ben Affleck's Batman to be a dangerous vigilante who needs to be stopped. Batman meanwhile, after the events of Man of Steel, believes Superman is a threat to this world because theoretically, he could destroy everything the world stands for if he so pleased-luckily enough for him, Superman just isn't that kind of character. Chris Terrio is the Ying to Zack Synder's Yang (if that made any sense!). The two blended nicely with each other, with Terrio providing the substance and heart this film needed. It is a dark film, both aesthetically and thematically, but an enjoyable one nonetheless. Oh, and those who didn't somehow couldn't comprehend the destruction of the concluding battle of Man of Steel, don't worry, it's addressed in this film!

The film in my opinion has a great, rewarding build up to the frantic and eventful third act. The tensions are made clear early on and while the characters don't necessarily share their disputes with one another, we understand their agendas. I just wish there was slightly more time spent on the two characters talking directly to one another, but I guess actions speak louder than words.

I've been reading a lot of critic's reviews that state that the film is "incoherent" or calling it a mess editing wise. It's far from it in my opinion and I believe the editing was rather unique for a comic book film. It's difficult to describe without seeing it, but I felt it had the connotations of a comic book itself, and the transitions and changes of time felt as if you were physically turning a page. It's something I felt immediately, and I'm sure it's something not a lot of people will pick up on. The films run time of 2 hours and 33 minutes was nice as the pace built up nicely to the climatic battle. It was enough time to hint at other stories and characters of the wider DC extended universe, and there are a few surprises for comic fans. I'm talking about the awesome cameos and references of course here.There a moments, where I just geeked out,something I haven't experienced in film in a long time.

Aesthetically, this film was an absolute delight. Linking with the comments above, there are numerous homages to comics such as the Dark Knight Returns and overall fans of the comics will be very pleased. Zack Snyder and cinematographer Larry Fong have done a wonderful job of framing this world. I would wholeheartedly recommend watching this film in IMAX if possible; it makes it even more of an event.

Hanz Zimmer's soundtrack for Man of Steel was impeccable, and Junkie Xl and Hanz Zimmer have created an electrifying score. I personally can't get enough of Superman's emotive theme. They have also merged the soundtrack of Man of Steel into this score, and it works nicely. This score sounds much better in film than it does outside.

Now performance wise, I have to say I was impressed. Ben Affleck captures the brooding and brutal manner of Batman, whilst also exploring the detective and playboy side of both his persona and Bruce Wayne. I loved it; the detective and technical aspects of Batman's character were something that were missing in Christopher Nolan's grounded films, but are nicely addressed here. Henry Cavill's Superman is enjoyable to watch because he is a character that should have everything going for him as he has been given these god-like abilities. Yet despite this, these powers he has been given act as a burden and prevent him from living life to it's fullest. It's his morals that define him, and he provides a nice contrast to Batman's 'take-no-crap' attitude. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor demands your attention. It's a completely different take on the character. He's very agitated and most likely has psychological issues, all of which combine to make him very imposing threat (even if he does lack the physical strength that the titular heroes possess). He's a mastermind, with a cunning persona and seeks power at any cost. Gal Gadot's, role is short but sweet and enough to make me really, really excited for her solo adventure and the Justice League film next year.

All in all, Batman v Superman is one hell of a film. It's a different take on the superhero genre, one that comic book fans will most definitely appreciate more than the average audience viewer Regardless, it's most definitely worth a watch, after all, it's the son of Krypton vs the Bat of Gotham fighting for the first time on the big screen-how could you not want to see it!

title: Batman V Superman - Dawn of Justice
review:
OK, from where shall I begin this review? Hmmm... it's a bit difficult to me because I'm a huge fan of superhero movies etc. All I can say is that I had a few scruples when I first heard about the casting choice of Batman. I always thought that Ben Affleck was a decent actor but I wasn't so sure if he could actually pull it through. And all I can say is that he did a very good job fleshing out the Bruce Wayne/Batman persona.

So, by making that point clear let's talk about the movie. Dawn of Justice... well it was a decent movie but it wasn't that good. It had its strong and well written moments but it had also its flaws. I understand that it was a movie that it sets up the DCEU but they could have found another way to do it. Dawn of Justice is like 3 to 5 movies put together in a 2.30 big mash up. I believe that they wanted to reach the point where MCU is. But they didn't think that Marvel, before doing an Avengers film or The Civil War film, had already established its characters with 5 to 7 movies. But OK I'm not here to talk about Marvel. I'm just doing this comparison to point the idea of making small & steady steps and not just big and unsure jumps. I would preferred if they had established their characters with more movies than one movie which is a set up to an enormous idea.

With that been said let's move to the things I liked most about this movie. Well I believe that they established a more brutal and dark Batman. I think that it's the best portrayal of this character until now and I truly hope that critics and fans will give him a chance to prove himself more. Ben Affleck did a fantastic job with the character. He embraced the role and made him his. With only one exception... they trampled the "no killing rule". It fitted in the movie and the way that Batman's character grows in this universe. But I believe that it wasn't needed. If Batman kills then maybe he's not different from the Joker or any other from his rogue gallery.

If you liked Man of Steel then you won't have problem with Henry's Superman. And the rest of the cast was a big deal. I liked a lot Jeremy Irons' Alfred, Amy Adams' Lois Lane and of course Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman. She's awesome and that briefly appearance of her at the big battle was great. They made me want to see her solo film right now. Jesse' Lex was interesting but I couldn't connect with the villain. He gave everything to make Lex a crazy, megalomaniac mastermind but in the end it was a bit hollow. A kid with clearly daddy issues.

OK now the big fight. Batman v Superman. It was good. I liked how Bruce was prepared for the fight all of his gadgets and of course his skills... ohhh he's so brutal, he's too strong.But it ended quickly. I just wanted to see more of it. And then here comes Doomsday. The big reveal from the 2nd trailer that drove people crazy and mad about this movie and the way WB do their promotion. If there's another thing that I didn't like that much about this movie.. it's the extreme use of CGI. In a way it was frustrating to see. For me it's not that big deal for me but it was a bit tedious at some times.

All and all I believe that BvS was good movie. As I said above it had its moments and of course its flaws. But I can't ignore that they're just setting things up for something bigger... something better. And i truly hope they can achieve it. The trinity was great and they managed to establish at least these new characters and they gave us some sneak peeks about the Flash, Aquaman & Cyborg. For me it's an 8 out of 10 for all the reasons above.

title: This movie is not perfect, but it is one hell of a ride.
review:
Batman v Superman is an awesome action flick and an intense drama. Bringing these hero's to life is no easy task and Snyder is able to really bring human reactions to meta-human presence. I love the way the story developed but I did feel the story itself got a bit crushed under its own weight. In an attempt to cram 10 different stories into one blockbuster of a movie it is easy for the viewer to get lost in the script. The pacing is a bit questionable in some areas. The movie speeds past things I wanted to see more of, and draws out areas I wanted to end. *spoilers* * * Batman's fatal acts against criminals is questionable but understandable once you take into account the state in life this man is in. He has lost everyone and really couldn't care less about the villains at this point in his life. Superman's fate is justified in the sense that it is the only way that this world will ever accept him as being a true savior. Wonder Woman was used perfectly and I feel as though her role will be written down as the best part of this flick. Jesse did his part as a strange and maniacal villain but nothing like classic Lex. I am not saying whether or not that is good or bad, just strange.

Over all I highly recommend this movie. It has ups and downs but left me satisfied and wanting more from this new universe. I can't wait to see what else Snyder and other directors are going to do with the material!

title: An above average but ultimately disappointing film
review: This is one of the most anticipated films of all time and 3 years after it was announced I have now finally seen this film and it is pretty disappointing. The premise sees after the events of man of steel, Bruce Wayne believes that he has to take down superman to save the world so he suits up as batman and clashes with superman. Now everybody was worried when Ben Affleck was cast as Bruce Wayne/batman but he is easily the best part of this film. He truly delivers on the dual personalities of Wayne and batman so well and brings allot to his performance. He is also great in the action scenes with this being the most hard hitting version of batman ever. Henry cavill is back as superman and he does a good job in the role. He understands the character of superman and does a good job of bringing superman to the big screen. Gal gadot plays wonder woman in this film even though she isn't in the film that much I thought she did a great job while on screen. Jeremy irons is the new Alfred and he is brilliant in the role, he adds allot of depth to the character and his interactions with Affleck are great. Unfortunately, Amy Adams Lois lane wasn't given anything interesting to do in this film. Her character wasn't very interesting which didn't help. Also Jesse eisenberg is lex luthor in this film and I couldn't stand him in the role because he had nothing in common with lex luthor. He was just an awkward guy like eisenberg is in most of his films. The story has some decent drama in it, it does a good job of seeing both Batman's and Superman's point of view. However, the films plot is a bit of a mess with there clearly being forced tie ins to other characters and just twists that come out of nowhere and make very little sense. The script does really well in the dramatic department. But just like man of steel it is a very sombre film with no well done humour. Plus all the tie ins bog down the film. The style has some really good actions involved especially the main batman v superman fight. But towards the end of the film a lot of cgi gets added to the mix and it just doesn't really work and is quite hard to follow. Overall this is an alright film that if your a fan of comic book films will see but just go in with lower expectations.

title: True to life superheroes.
review: Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice. The movie DC Comics fans all over the world has been waiting for years. Now, I may be biased, because I am a Batman fanatic, and a DC Comics fan overall. No worries though, because I will admit that there are Marvel I believe are great movies, and I'm really looking forward to seeing Captain America: Civil War. How did BvS fair in my opinion? Put it this way, SCREW THE CRITICS! The movie was unbelievably great! Also, let me state that the trailers will not prepare you for this movie. They did not show too much! From the moment the movie started, my emotions were elevated. The music had a lot to do with that, as it was incredible. Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL really understood how to set the tone of each scene with one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard. Let's move onto Batman, which is played by Ben Affleck. This is my favorite superhero of all time. I was never a fan of Ben, because none of his performances were anything spectacular. In fact some of them were quite embarrassing to watch. It was hard to picture him as the Caped Crusader. Then tonight happened. BEN AFFLECK IS THE DEFINITIVE BATMAN/BRUCE WAYNE! Ben nailed the role. I've never seen a Batman so close to the comics. The other title hero, Superman. Henry Cavill returns to the role that he played in Man of Steel. Cavill is a great Superman/Clark Kent. Superman is carrying the weight of the world, and Henry conveys that to the viewer very well. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman/Diana Prince. Unreal. Gal is gorgeous, so maybe it's making it easier for me to love her in her role, but when she first shows up as Wonder Woman, the whole audience applauded. She was a joy to watch on screen. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was an awesome, yet different take on the role. He was quite comedic and goofy, but instead of making me laugh, I saw the genius psychopath coming out. It was more scary than funny. It was definitely a twist on the character, but he fit the role extremely well, and I was quite surprised anyone can pull off such a complex role. A controversial aspect of this movie is the tone. Most critics have stated that the tone is too dark, grim, and not fun. Again, I think Marvel has some great movies, but I don't think I can handle a lot of family oriented, fun, and comedic superhero movies all the time. I love to see a superhero movie that makes you think, and is not all fun and games. DC has it right, in my honest opinion. It's dark, scary, and these heroes have to deal with the consequences of their actions, whether it's good or bad. Seeing a superhero overcome the challenges of being who they are is sometimes the most heroic thing about them, and to see that, you have to see them go through some harsh times. The movie is very dark, and quite scary at times, but that's what it's about. Look at how bad everything is, and push through that to save humanity. Now I have been saying a lot of positives about the movie, but I mostly have mention the actors and main characters they are portraying, and about the tone of the movie in general. Are there any flaws in the movie by my opinion? Yes. Not many, but they are there, and the ones that are there are not too big. I wasn't exactly super thrilled about the origins of Doomsday, because it did fall off the comics a bit. Batman's morals aren't set to the really high standards you see in the comics, but I also have to remember that this is an aged Batman that has seen a lot in his time, and may have been affected by earlier events in his life that have changed his moral standards. So with a couple of flaws stated, how was the story altogether? Well, I will say this, if you're not a comic book fan, or you like the characters but never really took the time to learn them well, the story will seemed jumbled, crazy and full of holes, which seems to be the issue with many critics of this movie. Luckily, I'm not just a regular moviegoer. I've researched my stuff, and I've watched many DC comic book adaptations with their animated movies, I've read a few comics, and I'm always discussing these stories with people who know much more than me, making me another DC Comics nerd. I'm not here to spoil anything, but let's just say there are many references, influences, and easter eggs from many famous DC Comics stories. While Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns is the graphic novel that most influences BvS, you will see many inspirations from The Flashpoint Paradox, Justice League: War, Injustice, Superman: Doomsday, and so on. If you really study up on these, and some other stories in the DC Universe, the story in BvS becomes clear and easily understandable. With that said, I thought the story was really, really great! It kept me "nerding" out throughout the whole movie. Again, I'm not here to spoil anything, but let me mention the cameos. There are 3 cameos in BvS, and each one is bad ass. In no particular order, you will see Aquaman, Cyborg, and the Flash. The most interesting one will be the Flash, played by Ezra Miller (which I am still skeptical about, but I trust that he is the right fit as the Flash), because he has 2 cameos in it, and one of them will be of extreme importance in the DCEU! This movie is really what I've been craving for years in a superhero movie. It has great characters, a great story, and it references the comics it has been inspired by with having very few flaws.

review:
OK look lets be real its not the godfather but it no way deserves the critic bashing its getting I feel that the review embargo has something to do with the harsh reviews its been getting or they are being paid to do so - it is what it is a fantastic popcorn movie - excellent score everything fits so please go and see the movie use your own minds and enjoy it for what it is - i give it a strong 8 but due to the critics being cretins i gave it a big fat ten.

batman amazing ben nailed it superman again very good wonder women also very good lex luthor excellent

title: How can this film be considered anything but OUTSTANDING and SUPERB!
review: What a great film! The initial scenes are stunning, giving a very different perspective from what has gone before in Man of Steel. Snyder doesn't play it safe, he is creative with his story telling, the film moves at pace, and all the actors deliver. The cinematography is fantastic, and as I saw the film in 3D at a IMAX cinema, I can highly recommend this. Although I had doubts about the casting of Eisenberg as Lex Luther, he delivers a great performance. When comparing Ben Affleck's Batman to Bale's, Affleck action scenes are better than Bale's, but Bale's Bruce Wayne was a little more refined. This is a Super Hero movie with a seriousness about it, death and destruction are serious things. The movie makes the DC universe very believable and brings it right into the modern world, the action scenes are brutal and Batman's fight scenes are the best to date. The film also touches on the question of being all powerful, Superman's God like Power. This isn't new, with the analogy between Christ and Superman has been part of the Superman story as long as I know. Super Hero films don't have to be looking for laughs, they can be serious, and Superman v Batmans is a fantastic tense, action thriller. I've read criticisms of the film being incoherent, or disjointed. I disagree. The story and plot work and was clear to me. I believe the test of time will show this film to be one of the Great Super Hero films, and look forward to the next instalment....

title: Excellent, best super Hero Movie to date.
review: Anyone giving this movie anything below 5 is obviously trolling. I went to watch this movie with high expectations, and I loved it. This movie had to meet 2 major challenges: 1. Be the first Batman movie after Nolan's acclaimed trilogy. 2. Be the first DC's universe team-of-super-heroes movie after the popular Avengers movies from Marvel. And it excels at fulfilling both. It is hard to say this is a bad movie taking into consideration: -I didn't miss Nolan's Batman at all. Hell, Affleck nailed it as the new Batman. Of course Nolan's Batman belongs to a more sober universe than Snyder's. Alien super heroes like Superman and Wonderwoman wouldn't fit in Nolan's universe. So, comparing both Batmans is unproductive. Nonetheless, this movie remains more sober and dark than any of Marvel's movies. The cast of this movie is superb. Being Affleck and Eisenberg (playing Lex Luthor) the higher points. Hans Zimmer delivers another superb soundtrack we haven't seen in any Marvel's movie. The special effects are nothing fancy but are at the height of the movie. Anyone claiming that Doomsday CGI is awful needs to go Watch Hulk in any of the Avenger's movies. Overall, Bat vs Sup is a great movie, if you're a super hero fan boy (i'm not even one!) you will love it.

title: Just a watch it
review: There will always be batman movies and Superman movies and hero movies, and they will always be different, stories will be different and that is the fun part of it, enjoy how someone else has produced/directed it and who knows, it might be more then you could've imagined it. But watch the movie with an open mind, let me remind you if your not up to date with how the DC universe works you might get a little lost/confused so go with your comic book friend to help you understand. Other then that it was an enjoyable movie, but please see it in imax. And to all the marvel fans, yes, this movie is dark. So don't expect any cheesy lines and nonsense. I enjoyed the grim sad angry protagonists in the film, shows how someone would really struggle in their situations.

title: Dawn of the DC Universe
review: Batman vs., Superman: Dawn of Justice is the setup of DC Comic book universe that will ultimately lead into the Justice League. Henry Cavill reprises his role as Superman, the man from Krypton who saved Planet Earth from the evil General Zod. Ben Affleck joins the cast as Bruce Wayne and Wayne's alter ego Batman. Also joining the cast Gal Gadot as Diana Prince aka Wonder Woman. The movie begins where Man of Steel left off. Bruce Wayne witnesses the destruction of Metropolis because of the epic battle between General Zod and Superman. Wayne immediately distrusts the Man of Steel, he believes Superman's actions are irresponsible and his alien powers are not to be trusted as Wayne believes he can be easily corrupted. The film moves forward 18 months and we meet the main protagonist of the film Lex Luther, Superman's arch-nemesis played by Jesse Eisenberg. Luther's master plan is to discredit Superman and tarnish his savior image and pitting Superman vs. Batman in the process. A lot worked for this film. Gal Gadot stole the show. Her portrayal of Wonder Woman was awesome. After watching her embrace this role, I cannot wait for her stand alone film. 2017 cannot come too soon. Surprisingly Ben Affleck was awesome. I was completely worried when they announced he would be playing the role of Batman. I remember his Daredevil film and how disappointed I was with the film. I did not expect him able to carry another superhero role let alone Batman. The tone of the film is a plus as well. The film is dark and gritty, a grownup superhero film, not one where a guy flies around calling people names of characters of other big films because they look like them or constant silly jokes. Doomsday was also pretty cool; he was created different than in the comics but looked perfect for the part. There are a couple things that do not work. The story at times drags a little but not too much where you will be bored with the film. Also, some characters are a tad underdeveloped like Holly Hunter as Senator Finch. At times she seems like she wants to be good and there times she wants to be bad, she can't decide. Lex Luther was off. He seemed more like The Joker than Luther as he was portrayed as a psychopath not a sociopath. Eisenberg's portrayal was at times over the top, but not overly annoying. I found myself OK with him and at times frustrated with him. Overall I enjoyed Batman vs. Superman. Is the film perfect? No, no film is no matter what anyone says. Is this the best superhero film, no it is not the best. Fans of Frank Miller's Dark Knight and The Death of Superman will appreciate this film. Marvel fans will pick this part just to find ways to hate this. Everything they criticized the film to me, they praised about The Avengers. Am I a DC fan boy that hates Marvel? No I am not. Guardians of the Galaxy, Deadpool, Captain America: Winter's Solider, X-Men: First Class, and X-Men: Days of Future Past are some of my favorite films. I tell everybody, see the film for yourself as everyone has different tastes.

title: meh
review:
For a movie like this I normally ignore the very first reviews as there are too many "10"s many of whom I assume are connected to it one way or another. Its definitely not a 10. Pros - The CGI is pretty good but nothing really cool that wasn't in the trailers. Ben Affleck did a good job as Batman. Gal Gadot was good in the action scenes. title: Everything a comic fan could have asked for and more
review: To do my best to give a spoiler review the film is everything a comic fan could have asked for. They delve into plot lines that will appeal to you if you have a true interest in comics rather than just a interest in films loosely based on comics. They even touch on lesser known, unpopular, or even infamous story arcs. if there is any flaw it is some of the pace at the beginning but otherwise that is corrected throughout the rest of the film. FYI This is nothing like the comic movies you or your parents grew up with. When and if you go to see this don't go in it trying to compare it to anything because it deserves its own respect. This isn't Adam West's Batman, or anything like the Burton universe or the Timm universe superhero stories, this is its own thing. Those of you who will go in thinking that the Nolan verse is the paradigm of superhero movies will be sadly mistaken this movie is closer to the comics than the Nolan verse dreamed of being. Now that being said to the comic fan there are certain aspects about the characters that even you have to disregard going into this movie even though Snyder did a good job of keeping with the source material he takes his own twists to the characters and does good work with it. Even the cast and character choices were brilliant the story keeps you guessing throughout the whole show and is honestly breathtaking how not only accurate this is but how well done it is.

title: It's good, but there are some problems...There may be spoilers here!
review:
I just got back from seeing this. I've waited 3 years to see this movie and I can safely say it was worth the wait.

This isn't a hokey and trite superhero movie. You know the kind where they deliver terrible one-liners every 5 minutes that you half expect the heroes to look at the camera, break the 4th wall and say, "Hey look at us, aren't we being cute?" It's unfortunate that the general public has come to expect this from the superhero genre.

The good:

Ben Affleck-he made a great Batman. I was one of those who wasn't sure he could pull it off, but yes he did and terrifically if you ask me.

Gal Gadot/Wonder Woman-She was for me, one of the movie's greatest strengths. Every time she was in a scene, I couldn't take my eyes off of her and I wanted to know what she (Wonder Woman) was up to in this movie. She left me wanting to know more about her. And I'm twice as excited to see the Wonder Woman movie coming out next year!

Henry Cavill-I think he already made Superman his own. I don't really have much to say about him other than you really got to see that this guy can act in that final moments of this movie.

Jesse Eisenber-Loved him as Lex Luthor. You could tell the guy was menacing and unstable from the first time he's on the scene.

The Final battle of the movie-Great stuff, loved Superman realizing that he needed Batman's help and how the story evolved in this part of the movie.

The Bad:

The movie suffers from some editing problems. The first part of it is quite messy because it's small scene after small scene all clustered together. It becomes somewhat incoherent at times and difficult to follow.

Batman's motivation in the final battle. He clearly wants to kill Superman. I don't believe Batman should ever be that dark.

It also appears, according to the movie that Batman has been around for awhile but yet the public knows next to nothing about him. This is evident when we see the police shooting at him in a scene where he has chained up the bad guy who is guilty of human trafficking.

Finally, it is quite clear that Warner Bros/DC didn't quite know how to handle this type of story. Part of the movie feels like a sequel to Man of Steel, the other part feels like it's a reboot of Batman. It's a shame that Warner didn't take the time to give us both of those and tie both of those movies together. It made have made for smoother storytelling and less messiness that I spoke of at the beginning of the movie.

My rating is 8/10...simply because the final act of the movie was a true adventure and left me wanting more.

review: Be it the breathtaking dark theme, or the way the whole atmosphere was created to show batman's rage, Zack Snyder has truly shown what a great story teller he is. The movie is a bit slow but definitely you are not going to get bored if you love the characters. Wonderfully casted epic, where in the first half you will enjoy the theme, i.e how it all started, and then the next half is filled with chilling action sequences. title: An epic in the trailers but just okay in the theatre
review: The movie was okay at best. The movie never reached its potential in the end that it obviously had in the movie. What held it back so much was the awful editing which most of the time took you out of the moment. It was definitely not the Epic we were promised. It had a couple cool moments like the fights scenes and all. Other than that the moments that took away from everything were the Bruce Wayne dream sequences which made absolutely no sense what so ever and the set up for Justice League was just so boring and dull. The movie felt like it was basically two movies in one as since it follows the Batman series The Dark Knight Returns and then it switches gears and becomes The Death of Superman story with Doomsday. Wonder Woman just felt like she was forced to be in the movie purely for the whole set up for the future films. The final parts of the films when it finally became Batman V Superman it didn't give me the fight that was promised. It was literally just a 5 minute fight so if anything this movie should've been called Batman and Superman because there was definitely not enough fighting to be called Batman V Superman. Over all this movie was just Okay. DC fanboys and fangirls will like this movie but people like me who go for the fun and be entertained will be let down severely especially with the fact that we were promised this entire huge fight between the two titans and we got a 5 minute spat between the two and that was all.

title: True to it's source, but not the best comic book movie of the year
review:
Overall i think it was a good movie, and as comic book movies go it ranks up with the top (but not the best).

The opening of the film was good; it opens up the character of Batman the way it always happens and in good style and acknowledges it source material with "The Mask of Zorro" which was what the Wayne's saw before Thomas and Martha were killed. it introduces Bruce to the world he lives in, but it doesn't go into huge detail like it has in previous movies, which i like because there is no need to delve into his story when we've seen it often and enough and it was an appropriate decision as this movie was not a Batman solo movie. It should have been slightly more obvious that it was a dream as it was misleading. What happened after the movies opening was okay, we get to see superman, he rescues Lois, beats the bad guys, but why did he have to go through the walls? It wasn't necessary. After that we get to see the ongoing love life between Lois and Clark, but it wasn't good to see them having fun in a tub that's just stupid. They perfectly justified an developed at from the opening of the film. Luther's attempts to metaphorically kill superman in front of the world was smart and cleaver, the shooting at the start and the bombing at the hearing are good examples. The way doomsday was brought into the movie was not terrible, but it wasn't good either, I thought his final appearance was good and when he killed superman was (in my opinion) great, but it would have been better if it was in a superman solo movie.

Seeing Batman kill people wasn't good at all because in the comics and his other films Batman is strictly against killing anyone. Overall Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman was absolutely perfect. Seeing a new Lex Luther was a good move for the character, but their are areas for improvement with the new Lex. The fact that Lex was made to look quite mad was a bad move. Overall I think Jessie Eisenberg's performance of Lex Luther was good. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was amazing, a great opening to the character and shows the good qualities of Wonder Woman.

When it comes to it's source material it shows it pretty good, notable examples include Bruce having a nightmare of a giant bat, Batman coming back and causing trouble with the law, superman in a nuclear explosion and needed to be rejuvenated, Doomsday killing superman (but that could have been done better). The way these are executed in the film are good and make it a good film, but if some were done better then it would've made the film better. The bets part was during Batman and superman's fight when he was getting the upper hand in the fight. The sound wave machines and Batman's kryptonite gas gun were used well which is a good adaptation of the comics, but the best thing about it in my opinion was when Batman was standing on superman's throat.

What made the film not as good as expected was just little things really.The biggest problem tho had to be doomsday. Doomsday is a prehistoric kryptonian monster, and this film made him a deformed resurrected version of Zod. It was also completely stupid how hes creates explosions when he changes his form. Other things that let the film down was part of Lex Luther. The way how he lost his hair was stupid the fact that at time he just found things funny when they were not even funny and the tune he was singing at the end. When we see other members of the justice league they introduced the characters to the rest of the DCEU, and i know we can't see a lot of them because it opens up the justice league but it would have been better if we had seen a little more Cyborg.

title: Don't let critics and nitpicky fans fool you
review:
I went into Batman VS. Suoerman with somewhat high expectations because, unlike most fans, I loved Man of Steel. It was refreshing to finally watch a film that brought superhero-style action to the big screen as its intended to be; a no-holds-barred battle of Gods. For too long have we watched superheroes on the silver screen limiting themselves. Only fighting crime under the cover of night, or fistfights where the hero seems to not be able to hold his own against common thugs until the very end of the fight. To finally see actual superheroes, characters with unmatched strength flying through buildings and leaving trails of destruction in their wake, in broad daylight, was just what the genre needed. I'll agree, the film had its flaws, but overall, I got what I wanted. A full blown Superman film that righted all the wrongs of its predecessor, Superman Returns.

Now, this is not a review of Man of Steel, but the preface is necessary , as it sets the stage for BvS. BvS fixes any issue anyone may have had with Man of Steel in this dark, tension building sequel (this is not an Avengers film. After watching, there is no doubt in my mind it received an R rating prior to heavy editing. Even after editing, this is a hard PG-13. Bones are broken in graphic detail, on screen, Thugs and henchmen are killed with no remorse. There's blood, dark dream sequences, some jump scares, and, yes, more neck breaking is to be expected.

Bruce Wayne is older in this film. Weathered and scarred after twenty years of fighting crime as the Dark Knight. You won't find the questions in morality that was seen with Christian Bale in the Nolan trilogy. Affleck's Batman has already seen the darker side. He has already come to terms with the fact that his one rule is meaningless. There are some villains who will not be held back by prison bars. I will not say much more, as the subtle hints are what makes most of the first half of the film so engaging.

Then we reach Cavill's performance. Similar to his performance in Man of Steel, except we see a little more depth in his Clark Kent/Superman persona, as well as a bit of dabbling into his relationship with Lois Lane here. Not much can be said here that was not shown in Man of Steel except maybe that there was just some added dimension to his character.

And then we get to Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. I gave Eisenberg the benefit of the doubt, and even then he greatly exceeded my expectations. Now, some may argue that Eisenberg did not stay true to the character, Lex normally being a suave, smooth talker who eventually runs for President. While this holds true, Eisenberg brings something interesting to the table. Luthor's original "daddy warbucks" character is no longer the embodiment of success in this day and age. When superman was first released, a bald kingpin in a fancy suit was the archetypal image of a man with power. These days, the most successful beings tend to be young, awkward twenty or thirty-somethings who are tech-savvy, highly intelligent, and, at times very socially awkward. Eisnberg's portrayal of Lex as a young, rich man wearing converse with his suit, who is extremely intelligent yet can not properly formulate a sentence when standing in front of a crowd, and at times allowing his insanity to escape his own head before catching himself, is, in my opinion, the perfect way to thrust an otherwise obsolete villain into the 21st century in a realistic way without making the character too over the top.

Finally, we reach the second half of the film, which is what the entire first half teased while developing all these characters to such great depth (comments such as "No on wants to see Clark Kent take on Bruce Wayne" at the Daily Planet were a huge tease). I was on the edge of my seat the entire film, and Snyder, being Snyder, knew this. A film that builds tension through the entire first act, making you feel the tension rise within yourself as the story goes onto the final act, is a key element of great storytelling ability. As soon as the first punch is thrown, it's nothing but an uphill climb. The BvS fight was extremely well choreographed, but even that was just a tease for what was to come.

Enter Doomsday.

Here is the high-octane, action-packed sequence that leads to the birth of the Justice League. We see Superman in action once again, we see Batman enter a style of combat we have never seen on the big screen. No longer is he relying on stealth or ingenuity to escape from a situation. Here we see him use the batclaw to jump out of the path of an explosion and immediately leap onto another building. We see Wonder Woman arrive in the grandest cinema entrance I've seen in a while. We see the Justice League's first moments, and can only be left wanting more, yet not lacking satisfaction.

All in all, this is a film that can stand on its own as a great movie, but will also leave you aching for more. It is a film for fans of anything superhero, fans of the dramatic and theatrical, and for anyone who simply enjoys a good film. Check this movie out, preferably in IMAX for full impact. 10/10

title: No Spoilers: Batman V Superman - Dawn Of Justice.
review:
I loved it. The movie, in my opinion, perfectly lifts the tone right from the pages of modern DC Comics and turns it into live action.

Affleck does Batman justice. His version is the most comic accurate portrayal of the character compared to previous movie versions. And thank goodness we didn't have Christian Bale's Batlaryngitivoice.

Cavill's Superman is starting to evolve into the highly moral and selfless character we know him as. Gal Gadot was a great casting and Wonder Woman's entrance is memorable. I'm excited for her movie next year.

I guess my only criticism is that despite its length, the movie's plot moves a little fast because of the editing. The director's cut on the DVD is longer, so that could change. It's not a big problem for me. I'm definitely going to see this a few more times.

title: A Disappointment!
review:
This movie felt more like a filler or a prequel for the Justice League, without substance or anything worthy that gives credence to the hype that was created. The movie felt rushed and it was difficult to follow a lot of scenes and how things were done and why! A waste of time and complete disappointment :(

Batman was extremely bitter and wanted vengeance on Superman, which disappeared in no time once Martha's name was mentioned! I understand the connection but doesn't make sense to forget everything in a jiffy, does it?

I don't understand why Superwoman had to come from nowhere suddenly except to lay down the foundation for the sequel ... and even then, nothing good comes out of it as Superman is shown as dead after the final fight! Yep, there are rumbles later that hint he will come back ...

I expected more than this, I guess!

title: Batman V Superman is pretty great!!
review:
So I saw batman v Superman at an IMAX showing midnight, and beforehand, reading reviews, I was a bit cautious. I am a big comic book fan, and a massive DC fan and loved Man of Steel, so I was a bit worried about some of the critic reviews.

let me say, the critics were definitely being harsh. Does this film have faults? yes. Is it perfect? no. But I went to watch a film where Batman and Superman fight, and I wanted to see superhero action and I definitely got it.As well as action, the film also dealt with relevant, interesting themes, like the concept of power, corruption etc and I really loved this, and how the ideologies of Batman and Superman, as well as Lex were represented.

The fight scenes were spectacular, especially Batman's. I don't want to say too much, but simply put, they look like the Arkham games put on the big screen. Wonderwoman also had an amazing fight scene as well, and Superman's powers were well demonstrated.

The soundtrack, cinematography and script all looked and sounded good, and Ben Affleck was amazing as Batman. Henry cavill was also great, as was Gal Gadot. jesse Eisenberg's lex luthor is an either you love him or hate him portrayal, but I really enjoyed it.

There are criticisms however. The film is packed with a lot and as a result can get complicated and slightly confusing, and certain scenes jump quickly, which can be a bit jarring. Also, for people who are not well read in the comics, certain things which happen might be confusing and a bit random, yet for fans they are amazing and tease the wider DC universe.

Overall Batman V Superman was amazing in my opinion, yes, it was not perfect, but I enjoyed it and I reckon if you are a comic book fan you will too. It might leave general audiences a bit puzzled however. But i do definitely recommend it!!!

title: This movie provided something new to the battleground of the hero movies
review:
This movie is worth to watch. Honestly I should vote it a 7 but eventually I give it a 8 out of 10 because I look forwards to the sequel of this movie. Positive feedback is needed and I recommended users to do the same for the "first" movie of this series.

Wonder Women is definitely one of the spotlights in this movie. She is powerful, sexy and the actress is really a good fit to the WW role.

I know that there are lot of critics to the Batman/Ben Affleck. However, to me his performance is well above average in this movie. Some critics simply emerge because fans just cannot stop but compare his role to the previous Batman trilogy. Undoubtedly, the batman trilogy is one of the best series of hero movie and it is from Christopher Nolon! The same would happen if you compare Marvel movies to the Batman trilogy. To treat this movie fairly, we need to use another perspective to enjoy the actor and the movie. I doubt if DC at this moment, will decide to shoot an individual Batman movie but I do want to see more Ben's acting in the coming series.

Besides, as I said we can have something new from this movie. On the other hand new thing is not easily accepted but to me is a good try. Below are the examples:

1, Batman seemingly is not a rightful character per our traditional understanding/impression

2, The revelation of other heroes during the movie but not as a bonus scene (flash & Aquaman)

3, More attempts to describe the dark side of the heroes, like Superman will kill innocent if his beloved girlfriend or mother are under threat

For improvements, definitely DC would like to add as much DC universe contents as possible in this movie. However, as a single movie you always have constraint on time to tell the story to the audiences. The trade off is audiences without the DC universe background like me may get a little bit lost during the movie. Some of these audiences will simply turn to critic. Some like me will do background research after the movie and the unexplained scene will make more sense afterwards. (the scene flash coming from future) The firm makers need to pay more attention to this area.

Besides, some scene like Batman, a second ago, want to kill Superman but just because Superman like shouting his mother's name and suddenly Batman become more lenient and befriend with Superman. I understand the confusion of Batman thinking about her mother and Superman shouting his mother name will add extra confusion to Batman and that why such a weird reaction of Batman could be justified. However, I believe average audience will find it kind of difficult to get the meaning like this.

All in all, I love this movie and this movie provides something new to me and others as well. The film maker has room to do more on the side of storytelling and the inside world of hero's mind. I am so excited about the coming released Suicide Squad (Cara Delevingne) and Wonder Women (Gal) movies.

title: Dark, Gritty, and Spectacular.
review:
If you are going into this movie to see some brightly dressed action heroes fight together and crack some comedic lines to ease the tension, you'll be disappointed. THIS IS A COMIC BOOK MOVIE FOR ADULTS. The stakes in this story are overwhelming massive compared to any other superhero films that have come before it. Serious plot devices are incorporated and the violence of combat is NOT glorified or glossed over. Actions have consequences.

The fight scenes, alone, are worth going to see this film on the big screen. The choreography is fluid, hypnotizing, and brutal. The way each action scene is filmed and cut together also propels them into being draw dropping experiences. However, each of the fights have massive amounts of motivation behind them, so you'll never feel like characters are fighting just for the sake of it. The intensity of the world is established along with the costs of violence are established early on.

The story is brilliant and takes unexpected twists and turns. I will not spoil anything here, but it implements certain plot points from glorified comic books as well as new and exciting plot points to make the movie unique and unpredictable in its own right.

Cinematography and music are exceptional. If director Zack Snyder is known for one thing, it is his amazing talent of organizing and framing shots in order to tell a truly visual and breath-taking story. He succeeds in this once again with flying colors. Music by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL also offer very memorable tunes that will allow you to feel the energy or emotional of any scene.

Finally, Ben Affleck is the most intense, brutal, and emotionally tormented batman ever put to screen. Gal Gadot offers an interesting look into Wonder Woman, although, thankfully, she is only used when she is needed to the story. Henry Cavill offers a similar performance for Superman as we saw of him in Man of Steel, however this particular film offers a far greater deal of emotional struggles for him to really sink his teeth into and impress. The other supporting characters give solid performances, however one might be shocked or disappointed if they are expecting "copied and pasted" versions of the characters from the comic books to be in the film. For example Lex Luthor has been completely reinvented as the villain, but is used very effectively in the story. You'll love to hate him, which is good.

My final thoughts for anyone who is thinking about seeing the film...GO SEE IT AND FORM YOUR OWN OPINION. Most critic's criticisms spawn from the dark and "boring" nature of the story told. It is not boring. It is a dark story, but critics should know that a dark story doesn't mean the film can't be enjoyed. It's unique and still a spectacle of cinema that doesn't come around very often. You've never seen a comic book movie like this, trust me. Go see it if you're interested!!!

title: Well, this was worse than I ever imagined
review:
I have been a comic book fan for the better part of two decades now. At that, I've been mostly a supporter of DC Comics, the publisher who's properties were the first to hit it big on film, specifically Superman in 1978 and later Batman in 1989. Both movies were absolute hits and greatly contributed with making the comic book movie genre a force to be reckoned, so of course, seeing the two title characters together on the big screen has been something that fans like me thought was way over due.

It finally happened in the spring of 2016 after 6 Superman movies and 7 Batman ones. While the Man of Tomorrow has faced a rocky road when it comes to film adaptations ever since the second entry in 1980, the Caped Crusader brought to life by Christopher Nolan in the 21st century is close to universally loved. Many, myself included, were hoping that he could carry on such a fantastic job over to Superman but being justifiably more interested in his own creative projects, he assumed a producer role and chose Zack Snyder as director for Man of Steel and now the Batman-Superman encounter that we have been clamoring since pretty much 1989.

And that's where I found the problem to begin with. In my personal opinion, Snyder is a gimmick director who cannot handle story telling. Of course, there are exceptions to the rule as I think Watchmen is a fun enough adaptation of a source material that was near unfilmable, but Man of Steel was no exception to the rule that are works like Sucker Punch. Thus, I was hardly excited for this movie and every trailer only fueled my apathy. Deep down however, I wanted to be wrong. Of course I wanted to be wrong, it's the two most iconic characters in the history of comic books, why would I want it to be bad?

Sadly, I was mostly right in my negativity. Mostly right rather than completely since this was worse than even I imagined. Not only was Snyder's direction misguided in that it once again focused much more on visuals over substance but David Goyer and Chris Terrio's script had some terribly dull dialogue. Add to that some very lackluster fight choreography, over use of damsel in distress and dream sequences, uninspired score from Hans Zimmer (My biggest let down) and Junkie XL, lifeless acting from the protagonists, this was just a big wreck. A wreck that appeared much more preoccupied with establishing a rushed universe of heroes than with putting out a good film.

As positives, Gal Cadot was a good Wonder Woman but she was hardly enough in the movie to add anything to it. Eisenberg as a baddie was somewhat entertaining if at times exaggerated and not very Luthor like. Like I said above, Snyder is a one trick pony and that trick is stunning visuals so you can add that to things the movie did OK.

Had they been any other characters instead of Batman and Superman, I seriously think I would have walked out. This isn't even laughably bad, it's all around boring. I'm left angry and hoping that Warner Brothers realizes that while the characters have a strong fan base, this type of crap can kill any franchise. They should know better, after all, they have been killed badly in the past.

title: All the pieces of a great film, just hastily put together
review:
This was my #1 most anticipated film of 2016 because I love DC and I loved Man of Steel, but after reading a lot of disappointed reviews my expectations dropped and I got a little depressed from all the negativity. That might have helped me enjoy the film more than I expected. This is not as good as Man of Steel, but I enjoyed it very much. I was not bored once, even though there is a big chunk of the film that is slowly paced, I was invested in every character and the story. I was fine with all the casting, Jesse Eisenberg was not my ideal Lex Luthor, but he wasn't terrible either. There were scenes that gave me goosebumps, scenes that were jaw dropping and scenes that were heavily emotional.

To put this film in a metaphor, I would say it is a giant beautiful puzzle that was 2/3s finished and then someone hastily tried to finish it, in doing so a few pieces were shoved in the wrong spots and some pieces from a different puzzle got accidentally mixed in it and some pieces got left out. I am hoping the extended R rated cut fixes some of these mistakes and adds the missing pieces. Even though it has many flaws it still made me really excited for all the future DC films, hopefully they don't have to worry about setting up for future films and can focus more on finishing the puzzle properly.
