title: Lose lose situation
review:
This films has been absolutely getting demolished by critics. It's one of the most polarizing films I've ever seen It's gotten so bad to the point that if you like this film you're labelled a fanboy or dumb. If you dislike this film you're labelled a shill. This film is sure to be talked about for years so I may as well let my insignificant little opinion be known. I am more than content to be labelled a fanboy and let you know, I absolutely loved this film. To start, it's gorgeous, DP Larry Fong is at his A game and with Snyder flair for visual storytelling you'd be hard pressed to find a nice looking superhero movie.

But the real present this films gives us is great performances by everyone. Henry Cavill is endearing and conflicted as Superman/Clark Kent and provides nuances that just weren't available in Man of Steel. Gal Gadot, while not in the film for any great length was sexy and smart and a joy to watch. Even Jesse Eisenberg, although sure to be controversial, managed to give a great performance as the unstable Lex. Both Amy Adams and Diane Lane also provide memorable and endearing characters. But the most amazing thing this film gives is Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman, conflicted and tough, this Batman may be the best he's ever been on screen. Although Affleck was at first met with disdain and hatred, he has managed to maybe be the definitive live action portrayal of the Dark Knight.

If you liked Man of Steel you'll probably like this one. If not, probably not for you but either way I'd say give it a fair and honest chance. This world deserves quality superhero films and I feel this is one of them.

title: Batman Vs Superman
review:
Batman Vs Superman: Dawn Of Justice review here we go.

THE FIGHT I'm not gonna beat around the bush on this one. It made me feel nothing. Given if you watched the movie you'll understand why. I knew no one was gonna kill anyone and it was gonna end in them making up and fighting doomsday. ( The fight doesn't even occur until about an hour and a half into the film, it only last for about 15 minutes.) Why Superman didn't just take Batman's armor off is a mystery to me. Even so before the fight Kent pleads Wayne to listen to him and mutters something about Lex Luthor. Batman throws the first punches and Superman is doing his best not to fight but at one point it seems like superman is just angrily throwing Batman around for nothing.

PLOT

Hahahaha. "Plot" I found the movie playing less like a movie and more like a weird Terrence Mellick's Knight Of Cups movie. The editing was off and I didn't understand what the heck was happening until like 40 minutes in. It seemed like the style was more show don't tell approach. Did it work? I'm not sure but I understood for the most part. The trailers sure did ruin parts of the movie which is completely why I hate them. Once is enough for me. The whole Doomsday introduction could've been huge if it wasn't spoiled as it was in the trailers. Doomsday was cool and I thought it was neat how he grew more powerful throughout the scene but like I said still could've been better introduced.

CHARACTERS

Let's talk about batman. Batman has been in this business for about 20 years. He's as far as we see in the DC's universe we get as a veteran. Yes he used a gun in a scene or two but that's okay. This isn't a Nolan movie and we already established he's not a hero nor is he a villain. He's batman. Meaning he doesn't care. Affleck does the role justice. ( I appreciate a good pun)The suit was pretty legit and it fit the movie well. They clearly reveal his reasons for opposing superman and it's well in reason.

Superman Henry Cavil is back. Man of Steel dealt with Superman's growth into well Superman. It seems like in BVS, Superman is still sloppy as a hero leaving people dead as collateral damage. Not gonna focus too much here without spoiling stuff but his character could've done so much more.

Wonder Women

What do I say? She was fantastic. Gal Gadot had much elegance throughout her scenes and even towards the ending with the fight against Doomsday, her smirks as she's thrown out show she's done this before and it's not her first rodeo. Solid character with the amount of time she's given in the film and definitely exited to see her in her standalone film.

Lex Luthor

Having Jesse Einsberg cast as Lex was odd to me but after watching the movie I guess it wasn't too bad. Luthor is shown as a Zuckerburg character which makes total sense considering today's modern society. At times however it seems like Luthor has a zero Understanding of personal space to the point where he feeds someone a hard candy. Talk about a creep. His whole motive behind stopping Superman is well non existent. There's literally no reason given as too why he's so set on stopping and destroying the man of steel. How he created doomsday? I have no clue. For a dude who just practically crash coursed the entire Kryptonian history he sure knew what he was doing.

OVERALL

The movie suffers in the first 40 minutes but still it's interesting enough to keep you interested. The last hour is where the movie really does pick up with the nonstop action you expect from this film. The tease for the justice league was kinda forcefully put in there and held pretty much zero importance in the story ( but heck I got excited when I saw that) Overall the lack of story makes it hard to appreciate the film as whole but of course the action covers it up. There are some major plot holes that hurt the character's development thus hurting the story. There's of course a bit more to this story but since this review of mine is spoiler free I'll avoid discussing all that. Note: The movie was still pretty cool if you ask me. Watch it before having any judgments then make your decision. Rating : Solid 6 to a light 7.

title: Why did I give a 10/10 rating?
review:
See for superhero fans like me it doesn't really matter what people say about a movie of the above mentioned genre. Most people don't know anything about Bruce Wayne's past or as a matter of fact anyone else's. They don't know what those two dreams meant. What a giant omega and erupting hellfire means. So it doesn't matter if they say "Dude what were those two guys up to? It was boring". But I think these movies are basically made for crazy fans like me. And when they are disappointed then you can say that, yeah the movie has gone south. So when really fans get disappointed? People, Batman doesn't fatally wound or kill!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!?!? Seriously? Who can survive 1.) The crushing and towing of that car 2.) The gunning and blasting of those other vehicles. When I first saw the trailer, I thought that maybe there is a copycat Batman who is running around and branding people although I knew that there is no time for all those things in a 150 minutes movie. So if you guys mess with the virtue, moral and principles of Batman, then it's something unbearable for a fan. If Lois hadn't showed up would he have really killed Superman?????? What is your excuse? Is it " come on cut him some slack. He is new to the crime fighting business, he hasn't made his principles yet"????!!!!

So why am I giving it a 10/10 rating? The reasons are as follows:- 1.) I am really looking forward for the future Justice league and other DC movies (As if my rating matters). 2.) The Flash appearing like that has sparked the hope that sooner or later "INJUSTICE: GODS AMONG US" may follow. Which is the best comics storyline ever.

If someone says the story was terrible, then I would say "it's okay, plot can be a little subtle sometime, but regardless you should watch the movie and let them have their profits so that they make those other movies they promised about. Moreover it's the start of something big so it's acceptable and all those proverbs about importance of a good start doesn't matter ". But what let me down was Batman. But Ben Affleck as Batman did very nice. Everyone is arguing about Christian Bale as Batman but they thought a bigger and badder Batman was required, although the latter adjective doesn't apply to him at all.

title: Minor Pacing Issues, Still Entertaining
review:
I'll get my one complaint out of the way early, and that is pacing. This movie in a weird way is an origin story, not of a character but the Justice League and in a way the whole DC Universe. I half expected the movie to suffer from this just from what I saw in the trailers and while the film did drag at a few points, I view it as a necessary evil.

A lot of reviews also took shots at Jessie Eisenberg for his chaotic performance as Lex Luthor. I at first had a few doubts about this but he did win me over by the end of the movie.

Once you get past these two gripes I found the movie very entertaining and enjoyed the dark tone of the film. There were also a few surprising jokes that kind of came out of nowhere and got solid laughs from the audience.

Affleck I thought was surprisingly good, even on par with Bale's Batman/Bruce Wayne which I didn't think I would have said prior to seeing this movie.

I'm not going to put this on the same level as Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy, mostly because it's not a pure Batman movie. The reviews saying its better I would guess are written by Warner Bros. publicity people just like the people comparing it to Green Lantern are probably Marvel people. The truth is somewhere in the middle.

I have a hard time believing anyone going into this would have a bad experience as I found it to be entertaining and visually impressive. I gave the movie 7/10 although I think that score will go up once the full franchise come out. Fingers crossed.

title: Uncle Zack's bootleg Batman and Superman figures! Batteries not included.
review:
Sigh...

I can't get over how weird and nightmarish this movie is. It reminds me of the Tom & Jerry cartoons by Gene Deitch. Sure, the characters on the screen look like Tom & Jerry, but they don't act like them. It's like that time when your uncle gave you one of those cheap bootleg Batman figures (Bat-Cop, Bat Detective etc) for Christmas. It just felt wrong.

Batman is based on the grumpy old sadist from Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns (how original), only more violent. He makes Keaton's Batman look like Gandhi. He also looks unintentionally hilarious with the huge, fake muscles on the suit. A more expensive version of the ones little boys wear when they play Batman. I bet there's a deleted scene out there where he glues fake hair on his chest and puts socks in his underpants too.

And Superman...I can't even remember any of Superman's lines. The only thing I remember is Henry Cavill standing there looking tired and annoyed. He's just there to be killed off by Doomsday.

BvS feels more like a horror film than a superhero film. Dark, disturbing, nihilistic...I don't think superhero films should make people depressed. They even have the overrated Neil DeGrasse Tyson show up and tell us how meaningless life is and how worthless we (humans) are.

I feel especially bad for all the kids who saw it. I heard one boy say to his mother: "I think it's scary". I wonder what they thought when they saw the parademons? "Why did the scary ninja cockroach kick Batman's butt?"

Skip this crap and watch a real superhero movie instead, like Superman 1978 or Spider- Man 2.

title: Batman Vs Superman and the Dreadful Plot Holes
review:
"Batman Vs Superman: Dawn Of Justice" This should be a great film. Heck, it probably wanted to be, but the butchered script and incoherent mess of a tale that is inside of it prevented it from actually being a good film.

Ages after the destruction of Metropolis in 'Man of Steel', which is being directly addressed here, this is actually one good front for the film as one of the biggest issues that people had with the last film was the overly loud amounts of violence that had occurred, Batman (played by Ben Affleck) is out to get Superman after his destructive rampage on the city that killed many innocents.

Okay, this is the motivation that Batman has for fighting Superman. But what is Superman's reasoning? He thinks that Batman is a vigilante. But Superman is also one. He answers to no high authority either, at least, not in this or the last film. Huh? So, the main reason for the actual fight in this film makes no sense. That's a good start.

Diana Prince/Wonder Woman (Played by Gal Gadot) is also on the scene, she is trying to steal some interesting equipment that holds info on Superman and even begins looking into Lex Luthor. This sub-plot is given very little screen-time and might as well have just been throw in at the last moment when the script was written. There are sop many other plots and ideas running around in this film that it makes this slightly important one look even more pointless. The inclusion of WW is more than enough and I can't see why they need to involve her in the convolution that is this movie.

Lex Luthor (Played horrendously by Jessie Eisenburg) is getting up to his wacky adventures and proves that this casting choice was the worst idea since George Clooney as Batman in "Batman and Robin". His delivery is OTT and the dialogue is overly annoying and far too cartoony. His motivations even make no sense, he wants Superman and Batman dead because their superheroes and yet he goes and makes one later on. He tries to get Superman killed, but he puts him up against Batman for.... reasons. No solid explanations are given for what he wants to achieve and his hypocrisy is beyond agitating.

Jeremy Irons as Alfred is actually a pretty darn good casting choice and his speeches and big moments are the highlights of the film, but he isn't given a whole lot to work with. No wonder he was displeased with how the film came out.

Lois Lane does..... nothing worth talking about. She tries to prove that Luthor is the bad guy, but we all know that he is from the moment he steps on screen. She just gets captured a lot and.... that's it.

Every other character is either pointless or forgettable throughout the movie and that show just how poorly thought this whole project was.

Batman and Superman only actually fight for about 5 minutes and it's an okay fight, but it could've been so much better. The final fight with Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman up against Doomsday is actually an okay fight, but WW is the highlight of the fight and Gal Gadot proves that she can kick some ass in the costume. The plot and motivations of the characters are slapdash and make no sense. Superman is a broody idiot throughout and acts like nothing that is remotely in keeping with the character. He lets all innocent people die around him, despite that being the focal point of the last film. He blows more things up than Batman and his hypocrisy rivals that of Luthor.

The WW theme song is awesome, but that's the only music that I liked. Gal shows promise as the eponymous heroine and I look forward to Wonder Woman next year than I ever did this film and I hope it has an easy plot and story. Ben Affleck is actually really cool as Batman, but he is just a broody jerk throughout, not given anything worth getting into. Henry Cavill looks bored beyond belief in every scene he is in, a real step down from his performance in 'Man of Steel', which was mediocre at best.

Overall, a real mess that has to be seen to be believed.

title: Dark and Light a Beautiful Lie – The film we Deserved and Needed
review:
I have no loyalty to anything other than to a high standard, and what I want out of a film, I have seen everything from DC and Marvel starting with Batman in 1989. I saw this film twice just to take it all in and even to scrutinize further, to be as critical as I could about it. I had gone in with all the bad reviews looming over the experience, much like I did recently with Marvel's Civil War and all of its praise. I am probably one of the few who prefers this film to the Marvel critical success.

The beginning sets the theme and tone for the whole film through a familiar, but different opening dream sequence we revisit Bruce Wayne's childhood trauma, when the ideas of dark and light are first presented. This narrative carries us through the events to follow surrounding the aftermath of General Zod's attack, and the battle to stop him. This gives us everyone's perspective from Batman, Superman, Luthor, Lois, all the way to U.S. Senators and the public. Where everyone sits, their frame of mind and how they arrived at that point are all established by the time the conflict begins. It builds organically, naturally and was never boring, but enthralling.

Every angle is meticulous and masterfully shot to immerse you in this world, propel the story and action while being perfectly in sync with the memorable bombastic soundtrack which only adds to the mood, and intensity of the drama. It's done in Zack Snyder style where it is visually just as important in telling the story as any other aspect, much like the very comics from which these characters are adapted. It's very cohesive and as long as you are paying attention you will never get lost whether it be in dreams, or the creation of the "abomination" doomsday creature, it's called depth and I'm glad if it at all challenges the standards of critics and general audiences (they definitely need more of That).

Lex Luthor portrayed as a eccentric genius manipulator who's also human and tortured is as equally worthy of praise as Affleck's brooding physically fluid Batman, or Gal Gadot's alluring, briefly teasing but undeniably strong Diana/Wonder Woman. You can see the conflict and burden within Cavill's Superman as he carries the weight of his and Zod's actions upon his back, reasonably willing to answer for what he's done. I enjoy the specific, likely intentional, fact that Eisenberg's Luthor is written in such contrast to his usual portrayal, it also makes him the visual physical antithesis of his nemesis who is all muscle. He is able to carefully align everything in his favor and take advantage of the overall situation, and the two heroes emotions with his mental prowess. This to me only adds to the whole dynamic of the ongoing dark vs light, good vs evil, human vs alien, Bat of Gotham vs Son of Krypton narrative throughout that echoes in the public's outcry.

What Batman and Superman come to realize beyond the fact that their Mother's shared the name Martha is that they are two sides of the same coin, one is the boy scout in a flashy suit appealing to the public operating in the sunlight, while the other is more visceral operating at night in the shadows in a dark suit. However, they want the same thing, their perspectives are in fact not irreconcilable and this ends the conflict. Logically as soon as everyone's aware of the manipulation, they are on the same page and they can then concentrate their effort where it is necessary aligning themselves together. This is not so obvious to someone like Tony Stark or the Avengers in a very similar situation in Civil War.

This is sensationalized reality in epic comic book style at its best, rewarding the deeper analytical viewer and those who appreciate a darker more symbolic and psychological approach which scratches at the surface, emphasizing questioning ourselves, our beliefs, our perspective, our humanity, and our reality with great analogical religious parallels. While Civil War feeds us another easily digestible dose of colorful, one-liners, and fun packaged in what we've all come to expect from Marvel films, which is good. Batman V Superman challenges established norms, and further invites us to delve into humanities dark psyche, all while being visually more arresting, which is better. Seeing these character's, the conflicts and the narrative all brought to life is nothing short of immersing and fun up to and after the main 'event'. Personally I will always prefer and find art more relevant when it challenges established thinking, aesthetics and power structures, versus those that mirror or reinforce them. I look forward to DC's and Snyder's future efforts.

title: A jumble of interesting and creative ideas with potential, but poorly structured and fails to garner any interest
review: My curiosity drove me to see this a second time, and much to my surprise it actually got worse. Those few good scenes I held on to in the first viewing were ultimately bogged down by a unnecessarily depressing and serious jumbled mess that lacks purpose and structure. Any character that exists within the movie is given such a paper thin motivations that whenever something supposedly suspenseful or emotional happens, I lack any interest in the outcome of the horrifically bland events that unfold. I don't recall any of the actors or actresses being this bad, and maybe it's due to the horribly paced and forced writing, but every line of dialogue feels almost tortuous to try and sit through. And don't even get me started on how ridiculously this movie tries to force itself into have a shared universe, by cramming down our throats pointless scenes of character building for heroes we won't even see for the next two years. Hopefully Suicide Squad holds more hope for the DCU than this monster.

title: Overblown, overdrawn, and depressing
review:
Quite simply, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is as cumbersome a film as is the title. At two and a half hours, it could easily have been an hour shorter for the amount of plot or character development that took place. It lacks anything approaching energy, edge, humor or the "cool" factor that seems to define so many of the Marvel superhero films.

It even lacks the visual hook that people seem to love in other Zack Snyder films (myself included). There is just so much about this lumbering clunker to criticize, it seems almost unfair to start for fear I'll leave things out.

Credit where it's due - Ben Affleck does an outstanding job as Bruce Wayne/Batman. After that. well, things fall off quickly. Amy Adams spends most of the film watching Superman fly away from her, Henry Cavill is still woefully lacking in charisma, and the usually- likable Jesse Eisenberg is so caught up with Lex Luthor's tics and affectations he forgets to make him imposing or scary in any way.

Combine that with tacked-on villains, watching Gal Godot (who also feels like a throw-in) go through YouTube videos of her future Justice League teammates in what has to be the most ham-fisted segue to future films ever, and a final act that never seems to end, and you've got yourself one hot mess of a movie.

Batman v Superman needed to be epic for the DCU to take proper shape. It fails in almost every possible way.

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of An Underwhelming Series

Jesse Eisenberg was about terrible as Lex but not nearly as bad as I was expecting. He didn't bring down the movie, but they still should have gotten another actor.

The highlight of the film was Jeremy Irons as Alfred, however. He was perfect and I wouldn't change a thing about his character.

All-in-all, not a terrible movie but still not perfect. Needed a better editor to get rid of scenes that just were not necessary and cut the runtime a bit. Either that or we need the 3 hour version to help smooth the editing a bit. It's hard to say what would truly make this movie better other than getting rid of that third act.

Not as horrible as some had said but not nearly as good as others make it out to be.

title: Batman V. Superman Pre-Review Opinions and Speculations
review:
This is my Pre-Review prior to seeing the movie. I have not seen the film, though I will begin by stating my pre-opinions about the film and critics. So far the film is receiving aid by die-hard comic fans, but serious blows by critics on Rotten Tomatoes. A major abyss has divided said fans and critics apart, seen in the IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes Reviews. IMDb, with a current 8.9/10 stars, compared to Rotten Tomatoes, with a current 39%, has caused severe turmoil between the two websites. While the fans have nothing but good things to say, with the exception of a few, critics are destroying what we so rightfully built up. The hype was real, and still is very real for me, though some part of me is ACTUALLY hurt. The gap is evident and can be seen by just typing in "Batman V. Superman".

My speculation is that most critics saw this movie without seeing a lick of Man of Steel, while others went to see the movie without knowledge of ANY comics. I'm not saying that their opinions don't matter, but when the exact same statements arise such as "Confusing plot, slow start, not enough action, and bad acting" sprout through reviews from critics all across the globe, not only does it make me a bit suspicious of the truth, but what exactly went wrong if all of this is true? My expectations will be soaring high heading into the theaters, and I know I won't be disappointed. The vast majority of critics are weighing heavily upon this film, not just with low scores, but with unnecessary judgement. The concern over the gap has really got me thinking. Many comic book fans and movie fans say that it was one of the best if not THE best superhero movie of all time. I won't go that far until I see it, but my detective in me knows that critics are being harsh and unnecessary JUST TO tick us off. Likewise, I do believe some are heartfelt and true, but the vast majority are there to bring you down. Again, I know not whether critics are just stone cold and liars, or truthful people. We are all entitled to our own opinions, but when gaps that big spread from fans to critics, the honesty in said critics has me a bit on edge.

title: Brilliant cat and mouse game between four characters
review: Before going into the movie, there were multiple issues for the writers and Zack Snyder to contend with. First, the large-scale destruction in MoS (an inconsequential issue raised by some people). Second, the attempt in bringing a fresh outlook to Batman, without redoing the whole origin story again. Third, the need to setup a proper pathway to the justice league movies. I think they addressed all these issues along with a riveting story-line, at least till the last 30 minutes where it became slightly predictable. This is probably Snyder's best work since Watchmen. The allegiance to comic book style storytelling was very much apparent. The story made sense and it did not appear to be rushed. This movie will be loved by DC comics readers. The character of Lex Luthor has been written very well particularly. The story is basically a cat and mouse game between four characters - Batman, Superman, Lex and Wonder Woman. Cinematography is top-notch with perfect lighting and good use of camera angles. The background score deserves special credit. The new themes of Batman, Lex and Wonder Woman are outstanding. Batman theme accurately shows the transition of mood from despair to rage. Superman's character in this movie is something similar to how Batman was treated in Nolan's Dark Knight. The character was made to suffer, repent and stay grim all through the movie. But, the characterization made sense in the overall context of the movie. I hope WB make more movies for the DCEU. Overall, this was a near- perfect movie for me. Certainly, the best comic book adaptation in recent times.

title: The crappiest and most disappointing movie in a long time.

Weird and totally uninteresting dream scenes, what the f... did the writer smoke? If they wanted to pad the movie it a) was a crappy way of doing it and b) why? With over three hours (Ultimate Edition) it is way to long for such a crappy movie anyway.

title: Ultimate Edition makes up for the disappointing Theatrical Cut
review: First thing first. I like superhero movies & I am not biased towards either DC or Marvel. Now Coming to the review, Batman v Superman has big, bold, breathtaking action in a story propelled by character conflicts on a mythic scale. The result is visually stunning, with powerful emotional storytelling and awe- inspiring action spectacle. Ben Affleck is pitch perfect as Bruce Wayne and Batman. Henry Cavill as superman is Okay. Wonder Woman is thrilling perfection. Gal Gadot delivers a performance that will make her the best female superhero on the big screen. Lex Luthor is different from anything you've seen of the character before in live action. The Theatrical cut pushed through a lot of plot and action but cut away too fast during scenes that would have allowed the movie to dig below the surface and deliver meaningful character development. The result was a movie that was packed with plot holes and underdeveloped arcs(Thanks to Warner Bros.) People & critics alike doubted the storytelling of Zack Snyder's(myself including) but I am all against after watching the Ultimate Edition. This movie makes sense! The Ultimate Edition doesn't just add back in key details to the plot, it also includes a number of extended scenes and subplots that (even in the most subtle instances) allow the audience to linger on interesting conversations longer than before while also clarifying entire story beats that, originally, made characters look stupid, careless & even making us doubting their integrity. The result is proof that Batman v Superman was meant to be more than the theatrical cut, and if most critics and audiences had a chance to see Snyder's intended vision back in March, then it probably would've had a better reception! Theatrical Cut- 6/10. Not recommended at all but Ultimate Cut-9/10 Highly Recommended(especially if you watched the theatrical Cut)

title: The word Underrated gets thrown around a lot these days!
review:
This film is the most underrated movie I have actually seen. Going into this film knowing about all the negative reviews, the Rotten Tomato score, etc... I still was excited to see my two favourite superheroes on the big screen for the first time. I left the theatre wondering how in God's name did the critics get this so wrong?

Everybody is entitled to their own opinion, but mine is this: this movie exceeded my expectations. Ben Affleck is honestly the best Batman I've ever seen (Keaton close second; also not including voice acting - the amazing Kevin Conroy). I loved every second of Bruce Wayne/Batman, and his dynamic with Jeremy Irons' Alfred. Everybody knows about the warehouse scene, which is the best Batman fighting scene ever put to screen.

Henry Cavill is a great Superman. I do feel like Batman may have taken the spotlight away from him, but I am looking forward to see where they go with him. The returning cast from Man of Steel was great, with a heart felt cameo appearance!

Gal Gadot was terrific as Wonder Woman, my only complaint with this has to do with the marketing. It would have been much better to have not known anything about Wonder Woman appearing in the film until release (would have made an epic entrance even better).

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex is... different. I wasn't a fan at first but then after repeat viewings he grew on me as I realized, this is a fresh take on the character (though I could not help but picture Michael Rosenbaum delivering those lines.... man that would have been special).

One of the best characters in this film was the score by Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL. "The Beautiful Lie" is the most powerful song in the film, appearing at the beginning- the Wayne murder (which by the way was probably the best interpretation of it to date), and the famous "MARTHA" scene (which is one of the most powerful scenes in the film with Affleck's line delivery partnered with the music). Wonder Woman's theme also kicks some major arse and all the returning music from Man of Steel was great!

To date I have seen this film 3 times, and each time I enjoyed it more and more. Is it perfect? No, no film is. I rated this a 10 because that is simply how much I enjoyed it.

title: "Superman" Jesus, "Batman" Paul and the pinnacle of Zack Snyder's audio-visual mythmaking
review:
Snyder in the "Batman v Superman", perhaps, reached the pinnacle of his mythmaking work. In the "300" he has mostly stylized the "West-East" mythical dichotomy. In the "Watchmen" he has deconstructed modern mythological pantheon of comics' pseudo-pagan "deities". However in the "Man of Steel", and in the "300"sequel Zack has not simply played with a myths, but has tried to turn a myths into effective tool to represent to mass audience real political problems and the genuine myth.

Mythology, long driven underground by rationalism and forced to act using guerrilla methods, appearing in popular culture in the forms of a "scientific" evolutionism, a "scientific" communism and racism, pacifism, humanism and democracy, nihilism and relativism, religious rites, is now boldly enters the scene through the comic book heroes, reviving the pagan pantheon.

Zack has used this modern manifestation of mythology as means to achieve something bigger. Although Christian symbolism was quite timid in the "Man of Steel", pulled into the myth by smuggling, the question of price of democracy in the sequel of "300" sounds quite vocally. But the new "Superman" audio-visually claims to be a complete mythological picture of the world - stunning spectacle with "grim realism" connected with excellent music and an explicitly referenced to the passion of Christ. Here we can see theodicy - "if God is all powerful, why does he allow evil?" - and allusions to rejection of Christ, His sacrifice, perversion of good and evil in today's world, demons putted in the place of angels, the fall of the world, which declared that "God is dead" and summoned demons under the guise of humanitarianism, to an unprecedented evil, hope for good and resurrection, and even the new Saul - Paul - embodied in Batman. Politics is not circumvented in the movie too: here is your "useful idiot" depicted by Holly Hunter, who believes in stuff like that good and evil are determined through dialogue, and here is degeneration of democracy into the rule of mob, regulated like a stream of water at the tap by mass media.

So, we have a full-grown modern myth, and it is pointless to try to criticize a myth from the standpoint of logic - a myth is not based on logical constructs, but on facts and imagination. A myth is a holistic view of reality, not its analytical description. Thus negative critical reviews looks ridiculous - whether those critics are furious because of Christian symbolism, or because of satirizing depicture of the left-liberal useful idiots - they are trying to deconstruct an audiovisual concept on words and letters which are not there, claiming a violation of rules of construction of non-existent sentences. Myths are immune to such kind of criticism, and the critics only expose themselves to be fools, set out to chop up the wind.

Snyder was able to deliver what he wanted to with his myth - he took advantage of modern mythology to undermine its own pagan foundations, dragging in it and actualizing Christianity with its complex ontological questions and insisting on the absolute good and evil, contrary to the beliefs in "dialogue" by left-liberal useful idiots. All these are contained in a beautiful, fascinating mythological form, realistic, gloomy, dynamic and visually stunning. With great score and a wonderful selection of actors - cynical Affleck, ironic Irons, detached Cavill, natural Adams, convinced Eisenberg and antic cold Gadot - all are in their due places.

title: Better than most critics would have you believe
review: I've watched this movie 10 times and it gets better with each viewing. The opening sequence was awesome, the score was awesome and the acting was awesome (even Jesse Eisenberg). There was dark humor, which i prefer to corny jokes. I loved the lack of audience hand holding. One had to use their imagination to figure out the missing parts. I do wish there were more chase scenes with the bat-mobile though. Hopefully the extended cut will smoothen the plot and have more chase scenes. Otherwise this was a worthy addition to Man of Steel which i will always defend. This movie should be appreciated for what it is and not what someone expected it to be. I was thoroughly entertained by it. Now we wait for Captain America Civil War. Gonna watch it several times too because we have to support the superhero genre.

title: It's good but...
review:
...it's quite flawed. I gave it a 10 because I loved the spectacle that this movie provided but realistically, I'd give it a 7.5/10. Before I continue, I would like to address that I am a comic book fan. Although I prefer DC over Marvel, my reviews aim to be fair to both sides.

Cast/Characters: The cast from the previous movie returns to give good performances, but the best part is the new cast. Jeremy Irons is a great Alfred, Gal Gadot brought awe to the film as Wonder Woman, and Ben Affleck is the best live-action Batman to date. Jesse Eisenberg plays a good villain, and plays into the plot quite interestingly, but if someone told me that this great villain is actually Lex Luthor, I would be flabbergasted. Now Doomsday *sigh*. Look, I don't mind him being the big villain for the trinity to fight, but he could have looked better and not give him this weird energy blast or whatever that is.

Story: Critics are a bit rough on this movie for one thing that's reasonable, the story. It's quite incoherent, with Snyder trying to throw in all these comic book plot lines/references, and also trying to set up the Justice League. It's also takes itself a bit too seriously than it should. Although I'm kinda sick of Marvel's dumb jokes, one wouldn't hurt here. It's not boring, but it's quite a bit of political drama. It kinda works, but would be better with a better script. Either way, the Dawn of Justice part is awesome, but the whole Batman vs Superman part could have been better. And some scenes could have been removed.

Action: One dumb thing Marvel fans try to hate on this movie for is the action. The main criticism they face is that the fights are like mashing your action figures together. I don't know if they saw the wrong movie or what but wow, were they wrong! The fight scenes involving Batman are beautiful, truly demonstrating that Batman is a martial arts expert. The fight with the Trinity (Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman) vs Doomsday is so cool. The CGI in the fight is a bit crazy but it's not unbearable. And the fight between Batman and Superman is amazing! My only issue with it is for a movie called Batman v Superman, a 10 minute fight scene is really short.

FAQ:

Should I see this movie in theaters?

Sure, but I don't think it'll be as enjoyable as Captain America: Civil War

Are the critics wrong?

To a certain extent, yes. They attack this movie for its flaws and don't even bother to praise it for the amazing things it offers (Ben Affleck's Batman). And a 29% on Rotten Tomatoes in absolutely insane.

Does Zack Snyder (the director) need to be fired?

Well, that's a toughie. Snyder placed some great scenes in this movie and some meaningful imagery, but considering his track record and the critics consensus, that might be a sign that Snyder shouldn't direct anymore DC projects. I recommend that if they keep Snyder on board, that they have a much better director co-direct.

Was it disappointing?

Kinda. I was pumped for this movie from the moment it was announced. And I waited 3 years for it, so it was a bit saddening but a I still really enjoyed it.

Justice League? I'm a bit worried, but hopefully it would be great. BvS kinda shoehorns the cameos of Aquaman, the Flash, and Cyborg in.

title: Amongst the worst movies I've seen
review:
Warning: this review contains some spoilers.

I enjoy movies dominated by special effects, being a no-frills distraction. I enjoy super-hero movies more, because in addition to the special effects you've got a certain depth to the main character and/or the villain, that was built in a long series of comic books before the movie. Really, the screenplay writers have it easy. And in many cases you've got atmosphere. For example the Batman universe is dark and filled with criminals and lunatics, Batman the hero being cool because he's just a simple man that's helped by technology, fighting skills and his own craziness.

Batman v Superman ruins everything.

The special effects are boring. There's an interesting opening act showing what Superman's fight with general Zod might look like from the eyes of pedestrians and that was interesting, but it was over fast and from then on the action scenes felt very cartoonish. Oh, there's Batman and Superman fighting, in a deserted building, hitting each through walls. Oh great. Kryptonite is involved, as you can't have Superman without Kryptonite. How unpredictable. Then there's a monster that explodes with energy and of course, it happens to be on a deserted island with nothing interesting in sight and then they move to an abandoned dock. Yawn. I've seen zombie movies from the eighties more interesting than this.

Then there's the matter that the 2 universes of Batman v Superman don't mix. It might be fun to think about it, when your six years old maybe. And yes, they are completely ruining Batman's universe. But you know, I'm not conservative, I keep an open mind. I certainly wasn't expecting another Dark Night.

But I cannot forgive that the evil character, Lex Luthor, lacks any kind of motivation for his evil deeds, at the start of the movie he's presented as a rational evil genius that has money, technology and commands an army of mercenaries and then at the end he's presented as a pathetic, possibly schizophrenic mad man. Except he's not a believable evil genius and he's not a believable lunatic.

Of course, no character from this movie has depth and nobody is believable. Even worse, because Batman and Superman weren't enough, the Avengers needs competition, so now we've got Wonder Woman coming out of nowhere with an indestructible shield and with a fire whip that she was probably keeping in her purse, appearing just in the nick of time to fight the monster. You only need to look at the picture with all 3 of them to realize just how bad this movie is.

But wait, there's more. Superman dies in the end, but nobody believes it. I mean, just 10 minutes before that he's being hit by an atomic bomb and survives. Somebody in the audience actually yelled "let him stay in the sun a little". And then Batman tells Wonder Woman that she should gather other super-humans (there's more of them) to prepare for the coming fight, because, get this, Batman has a hunch. Then dust starts rising from Superman's coffin, leaving hope that he's not dead. Of course he's not, this character is so freaking indestructible that he's boring and Batman's hunches don't help in making me want a part two.

title: My childhood dreams come true
review:
A highly stylistic director's vision; dark and complicated writer's storyline; an ambivalent and torn editor's pace; a thunderous, yet bland composer's musical score; a passionate and unhinged puppeteer of a villain...

Batman v Superman is a complicated film; it is a film not for everyone, and nor should it.

First off, I can only praise Snyder's visual take on the conflict between these two mammoths. Everything you see, from a visual standpoint, is truly eye candy in its purest and most novel form, though I must admit that Luthor's hair style choice was nothing to be proud of, neither is that vile representation of Doomsday (which does not at all take away the menace or monstrosity he emits). In this perspective, the result is a prime reflection of comicbook's darkest moments.

The story, perhaps one of the most criticized aspects of the film, is one of the bigger reasons why I mentioned "it is a film not for everyone". The story is definitely a looker from a superficial perspective, though it does fall flat when it comes to certain character's motivations after thorough analysis. It is not exactly a burdensome story to follow, but neither is it a walk in the park, especially to those unfamiliar to comics. Dialogue is splendid most of the times, leaning on themes that will leave some food for thought, but I must admit it does get arduous at moments, undermining what could have been a very, very vigorous and all around excellent display of language.

The pace does fall short, which leads me to determine that there is some questionable editing, though I think both the writing and the editing share some responsibility for this complaint. Pacing is sluggish at moments, more explicitly at the beginning of the film with, but nevertheless picks up steam and establishes the grounds for a stunning climax that most comic fans will definitely enjoy.

The soundtrack has some very intriguing moments, some of them borderline Machiavellian in nature, displaying a daring application of exotic composing, but there are definitely not many true "memorable" moments, as say, Lord of The Rings, or Star Wars could offer.

As you may have noticed, there are many "this and this, but" moments, which I believe describes perfectly the film; it is not a flawless gemstone, but it is far from being what many describe as a colossal flop. See? There it is again.

The film quickly escalated to the top positions of my top 5 of comicbook pieces, up there with The Dark Knight and Watchmen (the latter being the closest I can think of to being similar in the comicbook realm.) In a 1 to 10 scale, I have no problem awarding this film an 8. Why? Because despite its flaws, its positive attributes and its daring gifts to me and many of its many fans, in my opinion, far outweigh the shortcomings, and I would have no regrets in choosing Snyder to direct again if I had the chance to go back in time and do so.

title: Good Movie
review:
Lets not all jump on the "its a bad movie" bandwagon. This movie is a good movie and don't be afraid to say it.

This film had a great BATMAN. The suit looked awesome, he can fight like batman should be able to fight (finally) and he had a believable relationship with Alfred. SUPERMAN seems like an actual super man in this film. people know his power and know he can ultimately kill anyone if he wanted to. He was shows to have emotions like a human and he was actually a cool superman. WONDER WOMAN was totally bas ass. She is strong like in the comics, she is sexy and she can fight. Her theme tune is also a nice touch. LEX LUTHER is.... not fleshed out enough for the general public who don't really know who he is and the actions he takes in this movie seem rash and weird. The cinematography was good, angles were fine, camera movement was well done and the music was OK... ALL OF THE ABOVE MAKES A GOOD FILM.

However, the plot was this movies downfall (not much of a downfall for me). The story was very simple and the plot was sort of confusing at times. An extremely simple story + a confusing plot = a confusing film. Things happen in this movie and people were confused as to why they happened, but the answer was so simple that people overlooked it, making the story seem like it was rubbish. Granted, a very simple story may be a rubbish one in many peoples eyes.

The majority of the general public didn't even know about this movie until about 3 weeks before it came out, which created a buzz and a over-hyped preconception. People thought this movie was going to be a huge fight between Bats and Sups, but got an introduction to a new universe. If a film is 2hrs 30min, do you really thing its just going to be a huge fight?

All in all, people thought one thing and got another. People wanted a deeper story such as Batman Begins or Man of Steel and got a simple one. Critics didn't like that and neither did some other people, but now EVERYONE hates this movie. See it for yourself, take it as it is and have your own opinion.

title: See it at the theater in 3D
review: It is not your regular big explosions action movie with some drama sprinkled over it. It tells large story with paying attention to whys. And this is a big epic visually striking movie and I suggest you to see it at a theater in 3D. Today I have seen it second time and it gets better and better. The first time I saw it, I left the theater with mixed feelings actually, loved it definitely, but I thought they were telling multiple stories from different directions and I was not ready for it, I wanted the superheros fight right away, cause I have watched the trailers like twenty times, No, the movie doesn't have any urgency at all, a striking start and a striking end, and it builds up the story slowly, it lets you digest, it builds the expectations slowly up and high and it serves as a big visual feast as it goes. I consider Zack Snyder as the best director out there with the best visual style, with the best comic book interpretations. And he makes these two superheros fight, the result is a big epic visually stunning movie, and some scenes you will see will stick in your mind for quite some time.

title: Thinking Man's Superhero movie
review:
The problem with Zack Snyder films is either you like him and his style or you don't.

He doesn't try to be a mainstream popular-ist director say like say "JJAbrams" who has a formulaic approach to film making.

Zack Snyder pushes the boat out and tries different things and you'll either love them or hate them. I personally love them, and this dark brooding version of the Batman V Superman story hits the mark.

The only reason why I haven't scored it 10 is because I think there will be an even better Directors cut when it goes to Blu-ray.

If you're expecting the humour and light touches of the Marvel series then you're in for a shock. This film is the Ying to Deadpool's Yang.

You have to engage fully throughout the film or you will miss key subtleties unlike Deadpool (which I also liked) where you could afford to switch off.

I don't know why the critics didn't get it, maybe they're too old or from a generation that doesn't get DC Universe.

title: Dawn of something great but flawed (Spoilers)
review:
I have been waiting for this film ever since it was announced. That's about 3 years. But believe it or not, as hyped as I was for this film, I walked in with an open mind and with low expectations. I didn't walk in over-excited nor did I walk in riding on the "hate WB/DC" bandwagon (one which many critics were on).

Let's begin with the negatives, and get that out of the way.

Biggest problem was the pacing, film was awfully slow at some points and edited poorly. Especially the first 45-60 minutes, was just back and forth of so many sub-plots that the viewer was forced to constantly recall and keep track of. Film also suffered from a lack of a base story. Because it wasn't a Batman v Superman film, wasn't a Justice League film, wasn't a Darkseid film, it was just a big cluster of everything. Of course, as a film itself, that is bad, but I can say for sure, as more DCEU films come out, BvS will make more sense and will be more appreciated. Something else that bugged me was how heart-less this film was at times, unlike Man of Steel, which was a film filled with heart and moments where the viewer really connected with characters, BvS didn't offer much of that, except for a couple of scenes. Best one being where Superman spoke with the ghost of Pa Kent and the brilliant score of Man of Steel was used, that was beautiful. Now let's speak of characters and the actors. Lois Lane was there, just for the sake of being there. I would be okay with less of her. Now, I love Henry Cavill, but he was overshadowed by all the other brilliant performances and needs to work on being more attention grabbing on camera. Superman had so much screen time and dialogue, but I feel like he was barely in the film. Couple more minor issues, bad dialogue here and there, but otherwise these are the only major issues I had with the film. Would like to mention, before we move on, this isn't a film for children or for people who enjoy constant action and having plot spoon-fed to them.

Now for the positive aspects of this film, where do I start? Oh man.

Will begin with the best part of this film, you guessed it, Ben Affleck's Batman. Brutal, ruthless, smart and just awesome. His Bruce Wayne was perfection. Batman combat was glorious and will make you jump in your seat. Almost every scene with him was great. We get to see a lot of detective skills from him, something that was lacking from Nolan's version of the The Caped Crusader. So many amazing performances, Jeremy Irons, Diane Lane, Jesse Eisenberg, Laurence Fishburne, all great. I wasn't taking Eisenberg's Luthor seriously, at first, but after that Courtroom scene where he kept that cup filled with "Granny's peach tea", I really started liking him. War in Metrolopis from Bruce Wayne's POV was interesting and gave us a view of how humans dealt with those two gods fighting above them. Wonder Woman was easily one of my favourite parts of this film, especially that little moment where she had this smile on her face while fighting, so very awesome. Everyone worked great with the dialogue, of course, except Cavill as I mentioned earlier. Also, I need to talk about that opening intro, did not see it coming from Snyder, and I really liked it. The score fit in perfectly, the opening credits looked good, and it was one of the few moments of the film that had heart. Seeing the trinity fight together was glorious, could not have been more perfect (maybe they shouldn't have revealed it in the trailer though). The cameos from the members of the Justice League was really well done,I was afraid it may interfere too much in the already over-stuffed film, but it worked perfectly. Knightmare sequence was terrifying and almost some of the darkest stuff I've seen from DC in film. Score was great for the most part, but not something you would listen on its own, unlike the Man of Steel score. But Zimmer and Junkie XL killed it with that opening, need to mention that again.

Overall, it was really solid. Film was great but flawed. This isn't your typical superhero film, it is VERY different. Snyder is a visual storyteller and is VERY ambitious, and I admire what he was attempting with Dawn of Justice. But it needed a good structure and not just slow motion shots (which were beautiful) every 5 minutes.

Torn between a final rating, but is somewhere around 7.8/10. Just rounding it up, for now.

  • Olie

title: Surprisingly, I really liked it
review:
Let me start by saying, unequivocally, I LIKED this film.

I know, I'm as surprised as you are.

Now, I'm trying to figure out why. Sometimes, when you watch a movie, you catch the mood and internal thinking of the film from the start. In BvS, I understood what was going on during some head scratching moments early on and had a theory as to the reasons behind some of these scenes. That understanding helped me get through the slow, grim first part of this film, I sensed there was a greater whole and it paid off for me later on.

The surprise to me is that BATMAN vs SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE is really two movies. There is the first hour and a half - BATMAN vs SUPERMAN and then there is the last hour DAWN OF JUSTICE (League).

The 2nd movie is the better of the two.

Picking up at the tail end of the grim MAN OF STEEL, BvS shows us the aftermath of that film through the eyes of Bruce Wayne/Batman - and boy is he angry. Ben Affleck ably dons the scowl (of Bruce Wayne) and the cowl (of Batman) and grimly picks up the pieces. Affleck is a good choice for Batman (and future JUSTICE LEAGUE films) as Batman needs to be less of a loner and more of "team player. Meanwhile, Henry Cavill's Superman (a portrayal of the Man of Steel that I like) is trying to make sense of his new world and his relationship with Lois Lane (a strong Amy Adams).

Not coincidentally, this film really picked up upon the arrival of Wonder Woman (a perfectly cast Gal Gadot), she brought an energy that helped lift the last hour of this film. When we finally got Batman, Superman AND Wonder Woman on the screen, I kept thinking "now THIS is how a Comicbook Superhero should be".

Director Zach Snyder toned down the endless carnage that was overdone in MAN OF STEEL. Don't get me wrong, there is still PLENTY of carnage, but it is only a fraction of what was in MOS. I would have preferred this film to be less dark and moody, but Snyder has a strong vision that he had the nerve to stick with, so "good for him".

Snyder does benefit from a strong cast. In addition to Affleck, Cavill, Gadot and Adams, BvS also includes stalwarts Lawrence Fishburne (Perry White), Holly Hunter (Senator Finch) and Diane Lane (Martha Kent). The highlight for me was Jeremy Irons' portrayal of Alfred, he was a breathe of fresh air. Only Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor didn't work for me - though I blame the writing more than I blame Eisenberg's performance.

Did this movie earn it's 2 1/2 hour run-time? Well...no. I could tell director Snyder where he could trim some time out of the first hour and a half. HOWEVER, to speak out of the other side of my mouth, I'm looking forward to the 3 hour DIRECTOR'S CUT where some scenes that seemed chopped up will be fleshed out.

The action in this film works well. The fight scenes are well choreographed and the motivations and actions and goals of the characters during the action scenes were clear. I didn't once wonder why someone was doing something nor did I ever tell myself "I have no idea what is going on, so I'm justing going to roll with it".

It is with great surprise that I recommend this film to you. 7 (out of 10) stars and you can take to the Bank (of Marquis).

title: It's Really Not A Bad Movie Guys.
review:
Batman Vs Superman Dawn of Justice is an interesting spectacle. It's this year's biggest opening so far and was dismissed by critics and a few people in the audience. But also, it's a film that's been wildly anticipated and is now doing slowly at the box office as we close in on it's second week.

It's seriously not a bad movie guys.

I mean, I see why people hate it but I really found this to be a breath of fresh air after The Dark Knight Trilogy. My main reason?

It's mindless entertainment.

It was hard for me to pick flaws for this movie, I was just so immersed in Ben Affleck's Batman that I just couldn't pick out flaws. But I think there is one gripe I have with this movie and that is Lex Luthor. He is the son of Lex Senior I guess? We don't really know his father's name. But I'm really mixed about Jesse Eisenberg's performance of him in this. Sometimes he can be really scary, sometimes he can be really really annoying.

But that was the only big flaw I found for me. Other than that, Batman Vs Superman is a blast. Ben Affleck's Batman is one of the great superhero performances I have ever seen. He is different than the other Batman's I have seen and I really enjoyed the new take on him. Wonder Woman was not bad for her first film appearance, Cyborg, Aquaman and The Flash make important cameo roles that are a big part of the story.

On the thing about Mindless Entertainment. I like movies that make you think, don't get me wrong. I like movies with smart and good messages. But as a film critic, you just need a break from those movies sometimes and this movie helped me get away from that for two and a half hours. Like with Man Of Steel, this movie made me feel more relaxed and didn't care about what flaws there were.

Overall...

This new superhero film in the DC Cinematic Universe has pitch perfect acting from Affleck and Henry Cavill, visually impressive action scenes, great grim cinematography, a standard but absolutely fun plot and a climax that will surely make you cheer for the heroes to win. Batman Vs Superman is a real winner and Zack Snyder in my opinion is going the right direction with the DC Universe.

86/100 B+

title: 5 Reasons Why BvS is a Really Good Movie *Minimal Spoilers*
review:
Critics are like complainers at an event: "Well, the music wasn't very good", or "Did you try the watered down sour mash?" - there's one in every crowd. And in Zack Snyder's latest superhero tentpole, I have to admit that I had big expectations (and when one does, it's easy to be let down). But I REALLY liked this film (and then again, I really liked "Man of Steel", Zack' first Superman event, and I really liked Chris Nolan's "Dark Knight" trilogy, too). When Batman v. Superman began, I was relieved when I saw that Chris Nolan was one of the exec producers - plus, I liked what I saw on the trailers. So here are 5 Reasons why I REALLY liked this film:

1. The Talent

With all the grumblings about Ben Affleck as the Caped Crusader, I thought it was an excellent choice - his acting has really matured, and I was curious to see how he'd pull it off. And boy, did he! He was REALLY REALLY good - different than Christian Bale's Batman of course, but played even darker. And he got 'the voice' right! That was one thing I disliked about the Bale-Nolan version. Also,

I LOVE Henry Cavill as Superman. He's the BEST By FAR!! He has the dorky Clark Kent part down, and his Superman is really a perfect blend of strength, valor, and good guy heroics. I'm not gonna spoil the film, but let's say, he'd better star in the next one!!

Jesse Eisenberg got slammed by some for his Lex Luthor, but again, I really liked his portrayal. He played the insane genius very, very well. Amy Adams is quite sexy and all (loved the bath scene!), but she didn't have that much to do in this film, although what she did was typically good. Jeremy Irons was a very unique and capable Alfred, and I really want to see him and Affleck together in a film!!! PLEASE, guys, do another Batman Film!!!! I wish they'd had a really good Jimmy Olsen!!! Gal Gadot is an interesting choice for Wonder Woman, and I'll reserve judgment until her film comes out. She certainly looks the part when in costume, but I was less convinced when she was in street clothes. Of course, no one can ever beat Linda Carter's WW - my personal fav. Notable mentions to Diane Lane, Costner's cameo, and Lawrence Fishburn - all under-utilized.

2. The Writing

The writing in this film was generally exceptional, and the theme was clear and almost perfect. Zack knows his craft, and I really, really, really liked the dialogue when Lex talks about God and Good and Evil. There were many tasty quotes (Affleck's "freaks dressed like clowns" and Eisenberg's "three syllable word to big for little minds" comes to mind). The fight scene between Bat of Gotham and Son of Krypton was EPIC! The outcome was totally unexpected, as was the film's ending... but all the little pieces in-between really drove the film well. I Do think these films would be even better without as much fighting, and at least Zack showed some restrain here. He should have shown more, though.

3. Production Design

Without getting too technical (I worked in Hollywood for 7 years), I wanted to highlight how well this was done, because when films get it right, you get a masterpiece, otherwise, you get a stinker. First off, of course Zach got the Suoerman stuff right, and the crashed ship of general Zod was sound. The Bat suit - all versions, from the standard fighting suit, to the hardened Supe-buster, to the desert warfare cover, was a home run. And the Batcar, while no 'tumbler', was exotic sports car-like, and the Bat plane - all done to perfection. The Bat lair was especially cool! So hats off on this - I'd give them an Oscar nom for the effort.

4. The Music

A GREAT score is one you don't notice, and in BvS, I can't even remember the score, which means it fit into the background as UNDERSCORE IS MEANT TO!! Music should serve the film, the film is not meant to be an ego-vehicle for the composer (which is why I have an issue with John Williams - his scores are more instantly recognizable on their own, like a hit song). The sound effects blended in nicely, and together, created the perfect atmosphere for this epic match.

5. Gestalt

The whole is definitely greater than the sum of its parts, and that's why I expect this film to continue making money for some time. I plan on seeing it again this weekend, because it works so well on the big screen. You should see it too, even if you've seen it already. I'm no shill for the business, nor this film, but when I honestly like a film, I want others to see it. The 2+ hours went by too quick, and the ending was the PERFECT cliffhanger that will ensure I come back to see the next film. Everything in the film fit together so well (my one criticism was with the 'Boss' - from video game terminology - the bad guy, who should have been more closely resembling Michael Shannon's Zod). So pay no attention to those critic fools, and see this film. Twice. If ANY film is worth your $10, this one CERTAINLY IS!

title: Mindblowing!!!
review:
I don't understand the critical backlash to the movie Dawn of Justice. May be they can't love DC works. May be they wanted to debunk such a cinematic spectacle. Only they know.

The movie is best not to be approached as the Man of Steel sequel. This is a stand alone justice league movie. We have a morally confused Superman, which Mr. Cavil portrays well. We have a Bruce Wayne who is hell-bent to make things right. Ben Affleck hits the spot perfectly. And then we have the most famous female superhero ever on the screen for the first time. We also get teasing seconds of Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg. The Aquaman moment was pure awesomeness. We can safely say that Jason Momoa can deliver.

Now, regarding the plot... Its not all hits. There are some misses too. But the set up was awesome. The Death of Superman arc was well adapted to include Lex Luthor and Doomsday. The Doomsday graphics were really really good. And Snyder delivered again. Great visual spectacle. 3D enhances the experience.

Performance wise, Afleck and Gal Gadot were the best choices for DCEU. Ms. Gadot's entry as the Wonder Woman was one of the best moments in the movie. There were large applause in cinemas for both of them. It is safe to say that Ben Affleck is everyone's favorite new Batman. Jesse Eisenberg deserves special praise for portrayal of Luthor as Maniacal. Henry Cavil conveyed his doubt in himself really well. Amy Adams and Mr. Fishburne were adequate. Jeremy Iron's Albert is truthful to the comics.

All in all, Dawn Of Justice is a thrill ride not to be missed. If you are to listen to critics who gives stupid reviews (remember Watchmen?), you will miss this visual grandeur that Mr. Snyder and Co. delivered.

This movie takes its place among all time greatest superhero movies, with the likes of Dark Knight trilogy, Captain America 2, Watchmen, X men: First Class and Guardians Of the Galaxy.

title: What movie did the critics and haters watch, because that was awesome!!!

I understood that these two characters are a reflection of the real world, therefore their character traits have been adjusted for that. title: A Movie too BIG for little Minds (Spoiler Free Review)
review:
A long wait was over as i stepped into the cinema hall where people of every age were rushing over to get in. Almost every one was wearing the Batman/Superman shirts and there were few guys who actually showed up doing a Cosplay.

Let me start with the pacing of the movie, it was brilliant. The movie gave one of the best opening montage for a comic book movie as we expected from Zack Snyder. With the opening title 'Metropolis: The day the world is introduced to Superman' we get to see Bruce's perspective of the battle between Superman and Zod in metropolis. This brilliant sequence itself sells us Bruce's grudge and fear of Superman. It was all presented in a pretty decent and detailed view for the people who haven't watched the Man of Steel. When we first saw Ben Affleck as Batman, trust me it was like straight out of comics. He was Dark, He was Gritty and it actually gave me goosebumps about how terrific he looked in that particular scene. There are no shaky cams or quick cuts between the sequences it was well shot and well paced. The fight sequence are amazing and better than i expected. Deep down i was kind of skeptical about Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor but to be honest he blew every one's expectations through the roof. His performance is insanely accurate and he did a really great job. Henry Cavill is the best superman ever, hands down. The spectacles really took off his facade of superman away as well as his portrayal of Clark Kent as well as the Superman persona. There's one particular scene at courtroom where he was just standing there and his face was expressing the million expressions, that gave me goosebumps. He really embodies the role of Superman. The changes in suit are something fresh and gives the vibe of an alien being walking among us. For me; when it comes to the expressions i think Henry Cavill overshadows every one in the movie.

Ben Affleck as Batman is a breath of fresh air. Entire time he really sunk into the role and WOW i was amazed as it was really difficult to find Ben Affleck in the movie,because there was only Bruce Wayne. The Bat-Suits are awesome, the fight scenes are generic and realistic as hell. Also Zack Snyder directs the 'Batman' not only as a cape crusader but as a Normal Human being, who feels pain, have feelings and can go towards any lengths to achieve whatever he sets his mind to. We see the glimpse of every aspect of his mindset as Bruce Wayne in the movie. His physique looked amazing, Ben is already huge but here as a Batman, we finally gets what we needed on the screen. The Armored suit really looks great as well as the Knightmare Sequence. The Batmobile is phenomenal and action regarding it is very much real and believable. The CGI of the suit is better than i expected and the voice modulation is perfect and audience were able to grasp every syllable out of his mouth. I don't think Batman steals the show as its equally Superman's film and he gets to shine in places.

I was astonished when i saw Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. The way she walked, fought and talked i was mesmerized and i was amazed. Specially her entrance sent the chills down my spine. Although she wasn't there for a long time but plays a vital role in BvS story-line.

Amy Adams plays the role of Lois Lane, the confident and risk taker reporter of Daily Planet. She played the role so good that she stands among the performance of Trinity. Her devotion to her character really improved from the Man of Steel and took her to the new heights.

The movie ties in with the other solo movies about to release in upcoming years. The cameos of other JL members are sequenced perfectly and the Hans Zimmer & Junkie XL's music ties the audiences with it and bonds them with movie phenomenally.

Whoever said prior to the release that Zack Snyder gave away too much in the trailers and TV Spots, well guess what, YOU'RE WRONG. The Movie projects itself in terms of story line and trust me you haven't seen the 'Awesomeness' and key points of this movie in the trailers.

As the other roles are concerned, Diane Lane did a great job as Martha Kent, Jeremy Irons as Alfred, Laurence Fishburne as Perry White nails their specific characters. There's unbelievable Action scenes that kicks the adrenaline in you, There's humor, There's sadness, There are scenes that will push you to the edge of Seat, There are deep conversations that will make you think and question the moral actions of the characters, There are scenes that will make you Cry. The script is really strong and the story went perfect along with it. The Final act will make you go in Awe. There are unexpected twists in the end which will really shock you. It takes itself quite seriously with an operatic grandeur that makes a good change from your typical comic book over-hyped movies.

The Movie is purely for the DC fans who understands the references and can pin point the Easter eggs, but if you're not the comic book fan and have no prior knowledge of what's going on, Don't worry. This movie will take you to the journey of awesomeness. Don't listen to the paid critics who bash this movie just because Snyder's name is attached to it. As a hardcore comic book fan, this is what we were waiting for.

My Ratings: Cinematography: 10/10 Music Score: 9/10 CGI: 10/10 Acting: 11/10 Comic Book Accuracy: 9.5/10 Direction: 11/10

In the end if you're wondering Who Will Win? Well the Answer is: Fans.

title: Defiant, Dark and Glorious
review:
*** This Review Contains Spoilers ***

Very soon everyone will know what happens at the end of the movie, but if you do not yet, stop reading now and go and watch the film soon.

Initial reviews have claimed that Batman is out of character because he kills people and that 'too much happens', or that Lex Luthor is a poor villain. None of this seems true to me at all. The film is a powerful one and had many people crying by the end.

Some waited till the final roll of the credits, perhaps hoping for a Marvel-like scene. A few waited because they were not ready to leave. The emotional impact was that great.

Flipping the original comic book so that Superman gets buried instead of Batman was brilliance, even down to the heartbeat heard at the close of the film. The Jesus imagery is totally appropriate and links in with Lex's paranoia and discovery of what are in effect 'ancient aliens' who have probably spawned religions throughout time. Brilliant. Yes, the imagery is heavy, but many will not see it otherwise.

Anyone complaining that Superman dies should know that this also took place in the comics years ago in 1992.

'Too much happens' is simply an odd complaint perhaps, with the caveat that lay-viewers may struggle to follow some elements, such as the identity of Johnathan and Martha Kent, or even the Batman origin story. However, compared to the glorious mess of 'Avengers 2', with heroes popping up all over the place, this was tight and controlled.

I think many of the professional critics are making foolish complaints. One objected to 'Justice League' being too-obviously set up in the scene where Wonder Woman opens the LuthorCorp files. Come on! EVERYONE wanted to click on those as soon as Batman opened them! It was great.

Complaining that there is 'no humour' is untrue. There are a number of moments that raise a smile, but it seems that some critics just want to see more Marvel movies and Tony Stark-like quips. Such levity is great in those films, but this is not such a movie: it is a Batman film and here both he and Superman come to grips with inner and outer demons. It is defiant, dark and glorious.

Lex developed from an autistic-savant-type dotcom billionaire (ironically starting in his 'Social Network' persona, as we all I think dreaded seeing) into a genuinely terrifying being, seeming inhuman himself. The scene where he has the sass to threaten Superman on the roof was tension-to-the maximum.

Wonder Woman was less fully drawn but featured far more than expected and seemed strong, defiant and independent. In particular, I could believe she was almost-immortal, because she seemed so distant.

Finally, yesBatman does shoot people, not just in his dream but surely with his vehicles and definitely during the chase scene for the kryptonite. This only seems realistic in out post 9/11 world, some may say, but artistically it positions him nicely against Superman. One kills criminals when he has to: the other kills innocents through collateral damage when he has to. Brilliant.

We are very lucky to be living in a time when these films are being made. I can't wait for what is next.

title: A jaw dropping masterpiece.
review:
Zack Snyder has delivered his best film yet, and arguably, one of the greatest comic book movies of the last decade, making for an astounding accomplishment in filmmaking. I left the theatre trembling and overwhelmed. I literally was at a loss for words.

This is not your typical popcorn flick. It completely alleviates from the "status quo" of modern superhero cinema. It's long, dense, violent, thematic and is certainly is not a "feel good" movie, nor is it a children's one. I do believe, that as brainless as this movie might be at times, it will stand the test of time as a real intellectual game changer. This is where I believe the critics to be dead wrong. Instead of embracing this movie and what it's trying to accomplish, they have pitted it against their apparent "golden standard." Just like Snyder's Watchmen, this movie is ahead of its time, and a lot of people will refuse to understand it.

Ben Affleck has delivered the quintessential Bruce Wayne/Batman. From here on out, there is no turning back..he IS the Batman. Jesse Eisenberg is menacing, crazy, and pure evil. His performance will send shivers down your spine. Henry Cavill shines brighter here than in Man of Steel, albeit still delivering some lines rather wooden. Amy Adams's Lois Lane is given more to work with in this film, allowing us to cozy up to her character. Jeremy Irons plays a great Alfred. He's witty, smart, and plays more of a hands on role than what we've seen before. Gal Gadot has a minor role, but she has unmistakably left a great impression. I can't wait to see more of her.

Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL have composed a phenomenal score. Listening to the soundtrack without the film may leave you feeling underwhelmed. But paired with the film it's breathtaking. I rarely fall so in love with movie scores. It's more thematic than bombast.

As expected, the action is over the top and incredible. The fight scenes are epic and brutal. The film has finally done justice to Batman's fighting style. The special effects are mind blowing. The visuals in this movie are unlike anything we have ever seen before. Whether or not you like Snyder, there is no denying he is a visual genius. It's as if they are coming right off a comic book page. On that topic, I really have to give props to Zack Snyder. He has evolved tremendously as a filmmaker. His direction has greatly improved. I personally always felt as if he had a hard time getting those great performances from his cast, but he has really gotten some great performances here.

More good news: Compared to Man of Steel, there are not nearly as many cringe-worthy moments in both dialogue and story. Chris Terrio and David Goyer have crafted both a great script and story that will leave your brain wired leaving the theatre.

Some bad news: Unfortunately, I believe WB marketed this movie to make it look like something that its not, which may also have something to do with the negative reviews. Heck, even calling it Batman v Superman I think was a bad idea. This movie is so much more while also being so much less than that, and ultimately I believe this will only hurt the film. This is not a family film, nor is it a children's one, nor is it a Batman fighting Superman film. The kids in my theatre were having a hard time sitting still, their parents were telling them to shut up more than anything. it is not 100 minutes of light-hearted comedy and soft-core family oriented action. It's a long, epic, and violent drama. Also, there are some liberties that were taken with Batman's character, that some people may not be cool with.

Anyways, huge props to WB and Snyder for pulling this off. It's such a unique movie that I think puts the DC universe in an interesting spot. It's risky, grand, operatic, and plays out more like a political thriller than an Avengers movie. It's a crowd pleaser all while not being one at the same time. Go see the movie and judge it for yourself. Just don't let the old guys who loved The Artist tell you how to watch this movie. Bring on a Snyder helmed Justice League, can't wait!
