title: Great way to start the DC Saga of movies
review: When getting ready to watch a movie, I no longer look at advance reviews, because most people are ridiculously negative. I went into this movie with an open mind, and came out loving it. Despite the earlier worries from comic book nerds, Ben Affleck was terrific as Batman and Bruce Wayne. He really got into the psychology of the character. He definitely looked the part. I also liked that they showed him being a detective, and doing undercover work. In the hand-to-hand combat scenes, he also fought like Batman should fight. We also got to see some character development from Lois and Clark. Clark struggles with having these great powers, but not understanding why people don't trust him, and see that his intentions are honorable. Amy Adams may be the best Lois ever (Sorry Teri and Erica). The only misfire for me was in casting Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. It's not that he did bad job. He was actually quite good from an acting standpoint. The problem was I just wasn't buying him as Lex. One of the things that got on my nerves was that he was laughing too much. Lex doesn't laugh, he just kind of smirks. He also didn't really convey that sinister side of him. I saw in the news that they had considered Bryan Cranston for Lex. That would have been the better choice. I think Jesse would have been better suited playing a different villain. He would have made a great Riddler, or even the Scarecrow or the Toyman. The movie was well written, and sets up nicely for The Justice League. Don't let the fan-boys or the critics get in your head. Sit back relax and enjoy the two and a half hour ride. I watched the movie with an audience of regular everyday people, and they enjoyed it so much that they stood up, cheered, and applauded the movie after it was over.

title: Can't agree with the critics
review:
At its core the movie is great and as a comic fan I was really delighted to see them going all out on the material. Affleck's Batman is the kind I hoped he'd be and now I hope they go for a few stand alone movies, because it was that good and left me wanting more. Same goes for Gadot and her Wonder Woman and luckily her movie is around the corner.

Though, it wasn't all roses and rainbows. Snyder, with his pacing problems came out in full force again. And that's what I think made most critics pan it. Focus and streamlined story telling isn't his strong suit and if you have no idea about the source material, I can see how the experience might be more frustrating than enjoyable.

bottom line. if you like comics and DC animated movies then I can highly recommend this one.

title: See it twice!
review:
Okay, I'm an adult and have been collecting Comic Book memorabilia (mainly Superman) but also Captain America, and others for 25 years. I lived in San Diego for many years and attended Comic Con religiously. The Death of Superman was what got me reading and collecting again in the early '90's. I thought MOS was good despite some of the popular criticism.

I took off work two hours early today with the intent of seeing the movie a couple times today and maybe again tomorrow. I promised my friends no spoilers but the first thing I did after seeing it the first time was text and basically say that the movie sucked. I also said a few choice things about WB execs.

Particularly I was irritated at the origin and appearance of Doomsday. Bad enough they screwed him up in the comics over the years, and don't even get me going on how bad he was represented in both the JLU animated series and that terrible DCU Movie! I felt Snyder's version was just rushed and terrible, I won't say more.

I also hated the fact that at the end Superman was "dead." Sure the dirt rose and he'll be back. The issue with this is that if they think people had an issue with an omnipotent MOS running around imagine how they'll feel when he returns from the dead! Seriously, won't people be a bit freaked out?!

So, I walked out the first time really disappointed. Having already committed to sitting through it again I did so. When watching it the second time it was actually much more enjoyable. I'm not sure what it was but it was just better the second time around. Maybe it's just the Superman fan in me wanting a good Supes movie, or the fact that I would really like to see DC movies do well. I'm not sure.

I decided to forgive them for the ridiculous version of Doomsday with the red EMP and tearing his skin off, or that he was somehow Zod and Luthor's love child. I let it go, this wasn't THE Doomsday that I loved seeing thrown into the end of time (how perfect) in Hunter Prey #3, this was just something cooked up for the movie that slightly resembled him. I also forgave the "death."

Some good stuff - this was the best Batman in my opinion. It wasn't Affleck, it was just Batman. I enjoyed the twists I didn't see coming like the Kryptonite coming from the world engine, and that the Senator was a Superman fan and not plotting with Luthor. I enjoyed the scene at the Capitol and didn't see that coming. I loved how Superman found out Batman's identity. The movie was a series of very short special moments all placed one after the other. I think that Gal Gadot was a great WW, even though she could use a little more meat on her lower half - kinda scrawny legs for a "Wonder Woman." Eisenberg was as good as they let him be although I wish Lex could have stayed focused a little more instead of sometimes seeming like a babbling idiot - he should have had moments of clarity where he just come across straight, focused, and evil instead of seeming like his mind was eighteen other places all the time (also messed up that he literally knows everyone's "secret" identity!). I did not think Batman was too violent and I don't think Superman acted too out of character. I enjoyed the interaction between Martha and Batman even though it was sort of cheesy how Batman stopped fighting when Superman mentioned the name. I think the entire cast was superb. Lawrence Fishburn was awesome reading Clark the riot act!

There were deeper moments that can be appreciated and that I feel will be important later, like Batman talking about how he "failed him in life." Pretty much Bruce realizes he had Superman all wrong and I am sure this will play into their future friendship. Evidently Superman had to literally die in order for people to believe he was a good guy.

So after seeing it once I was pretty disappointed but after my second viewing I got over the couple things I thought I had a problem with and see all of the really neat things that the movie has invested in. I'll see it again tomorrow after sleeping on it and am pretty sure it will be even more enjoyable.

As the title of this review says I think it is worth a second viewing if the first one really has you disappointed as I was. Or, read a few other reviews with spoilers so you can get used to all the things that will irritate you and go into it already with them in mind, or don't go at all.

title: Do not listen to the critics... listen to the fanboys!!!
review: This is stunning... its not a Marvel type film with laughs and nice bits, so stop expecting that... go see Antman if you want a simple story arch with chuckles! This is clever, dark, sad, and true to multiple comic story lines including the Death of superman, injustice league and Darkseid hints, (apart from doomsday, but still OK how he comes to be) Do not listen to the critics... some bloke who's just seen it and now off to watch My Big Fat Greek Wedding 2, this film is for the fans, the true fans, who loves the books, the mythology and who have read the links that hold this story together... the ending now sets things up for a multitude of other things, justice league obviously being one of them, however, after Superman died in the comics, it lead to two of the best Superhero books being written... "A world without superman, then the "Return of Superman" Sod the Critics, fanboys... go and see it!!!! NOW!

title: WOW this was BAD!!!!!
review: So much expectations, so little fulfilled. I have rarely seen such incoherent movie, jumping from one thing to another with no connection at all. Some background of Batman and Superman is given but nothing about Wonderwoman, who is she, where does she come from, anything about her superpowers....nothing!!!!! She just flies in the movie from nowhere... Acting is OK from Gal Gadot and Jesse Eisenberg, Henry Cavill is already well placed in his Superman role but Ben Affleck, man he is BAD!!! Please DC Comics, change him before another fiasco. All in all, interesting special effects but nothing special. I am utterly disasppointed. I give 3 out of 10 stars.

title: Work of Art
review:
I was so afraid that this movie would be like a Marvel movie. Don't get me wrong, I love the Marvel movies, but I don't want to see a DC movie that is done that way. Luckily it did not. This movie is DC comic books and DC anime's coming to life on the big screen, done the right way. The story telling combined with the music is something that has never been seen or done before with super heroes on the big screen.

This movie addresses the dark side of dealing with these type of humans/aliens very well. It shows the political and emotional issues from all perspectives.

As a comic books and anime fan I really appreciate the story and how they make this movie their own but keeping true to the comic books.

Ben Affleck is definitely now the one and only Batman for me. He doesn't play Batman or Bruce Wayne, he makes you believe he is Batman and Bruce Wayne. Henry Cavill was superb and convinced me this is how Superman would react and would handle these different difficult situations. Henry Cavill showing Superman's emotions was overwhelming. Gal Gadot is an awesome Wonder woman. Jesse Eissenberg was a whole different Lex Luthor, but he managed to show this dark soul of Lex Luthor, which I found refreshing and modernized. The rest of the cast was magnificent but I have to say that Holly Hunter's performance owned the screen every time she was on.

For the people who do not read comic books, it will still be a very good movie unless you expect it to be a Marvel Movie.

DC story telling is darker, and how strangely it may sound, it is a more realistic take on superheroes. The story is told "comic book style" in the movie, so it will jump back and forth, from character to character in the movie. I read some reviews that said the story was all over the place, but I can reassure you it's not. It is a comic book way of story telling. There are 3 story lines. 1) Superman/Clark Kent, 2) Batman/Bruce Wayne and 3) Lex Luthor. The thread in the story is Wonder Woman. The movie will jump from one story line to the other and all will come together.

If you are going to see this movie and compare it with the Marvel movies, don't. Go see this movie with an open mind. Don't expect a buddy movie, or a feel good movie or an all action movie with a lot of humor. This movie comes close to reality as it can get concerning superheroes comic books.

I've seen this movie 2 times already and the second time I saw it, I enjoyed it even so much more than the first time. I'm going to see this movie for a third time and I'll definitely will go a couple times more.

I love this movie, it's a work of art..

title: Don't pretend to be a hipster critic.
review:
Here's the thing. As an everyday movie goer who watched all the super hero movies and TV shows lately, this was a superb movie. The VFX were second to none, and I can safely say that this movie is many miles better than the marvel movies I've watched lately.

Ant-Man - Terrible waste of time. The latest avengers - Felt like i was watching some Disney channel animated series. Captain America - I got reminded of mickey mouse all over again.

The point is, it felt more grown up. You read around and you notice some critics even giving it a 10/100. Comon mate, don't exaggerate till that point. That's too much. 10? That's like hipster level hate right there.

So to keep it short and simple, It's an awesome movie. Just go watch it. Whatever you feel afterwards, I'm extremely confident you won't leave the cinema saying, "The plot line for this movie is a definite 10/100. I'm going to be a movie critic now."

title: The critics are lying to us.
review: The movie did not have any problems like previous Snyder films regarding pacing or whatever. The thing is that the reviews of the critics are very harsh and uncalled for(fan boys are another issue). There weren't as many problems with pacing and editing as man of steel. In fact, the only reason that it could get a bad reviews should be being too dark for some. The movie was perfectly FINE and a good treat to the fan boys of DC. The movie is going to do fine at the box office and we will have a much needed larger DC universe. Frankly i am sick of watching one tone funny one liners from marvel and it is just a needed change of pace. Some may not like it as much as the others but "bad movie" or "worst movie ever' comments are from bonkers haters and snobby nitpickers. It is not the best movie ever and it is not even a 10/10 movie but for a DC fan it is great and much needed. All the problems that the critics though it had, were simply not there. The story is not complicated and the visuals are incredible. The acting is great and there aren't many cringe worthy dialogs or forced events. It felt natural and not even as dark as people are making it out to be(there are far far far darker films out there).

title: Blew Past my Expectations!
review: First, let me begin by saying I am a huge Batman fan. With that being said, I absolutely loved this movie. Ben Affleck was phenomenal as both Bruce Wayne and Batman. The movie is two and a half hours long, but I personally felt like the time flew by. The trailers were cut in such a way that did not give away any spoilers, which was a wonderful surprise. Overall, the movie was well paced, action packed, and the dialogue was much improved from Man of Steel (which I enjoyed as well). Just be warned, this is NOT a Marvel movie. The story is much darker, which reflects a lot of the Batman comics of the past thirty years. Zack Snyder did an excellent job making the Batman a true vigilante that was feared by the criminals of Gotham. I will say this, however, Lex Luthor (played by Jesse Eisenberg) was a completely different Lex Luthor relative to the comic books. I found the performance refreshing but wishing the role was cast with a slightly more serious actor. With that being said, he still performed well above my expectations. One of the top performances was Gal Gadot. She was stunning, powerful (both as a female character and as Wonder Woman), and dynamic. I highly recommend this movie to everyone! Well done Mr. Snyder. I cannot wait until the next wave of movies comes out.

review:
I went to the theater tonight to see the worst superhero movie of 2016 and I glad I did. This movie is great, the tone is different, Batman is different to what we have seen to date, which is good.

title: A bit slow... but great!
review:
Wow. Just wow. I have been an IMDb user for 5 years now and I have been waiting for a film so great to review. I finally got it. BvS starts out slow, but it builds up to an epic battle between Batman and Superman. Jesse Eisenburg did great as a crazy, maniacal, and psychotic Lex Luthor. I was really upset when Bruce Wayne got cast as Batman, and he did okay, but not great. I guess I had way too high expectations for him. His fight scenes were a bit too slow as well. Alfred was great and funny like always.

The Battle between Batman and Superman was intense. I won't spoil it for you guys, but still it was great.

This movie is a must watch!

title: Onee superhero movie that will please the hardcore DC fans!!
review:
Right,I don't write reviews very often, but after seeing the bad reviews out there, I had to write one. I wont go on about the storyline...etc For the fans that grew up on dc comic's batman, superman and justice league, this movie will have all the bits we loved about those comics and story arcs. Because it's setting up the platform for what's to come, i.e aquaman, cyborg, flash, justice league part 1 and 2, this movie had to incorporate a lot of story lines. Although it might seem that it is incoherent when you watch it, people who have read the comics will know exactly where the movie is heading. It's got elements from flashpoint paradox, justice league war, the dark knight returns, a nod to sons of batman, some bits from vigilante registration acts...etc SO they have stayed mostly true to the source material.Personally I loved it!!! It's different from movies that need to set you up bit by bit for each character. review: Those of us who loved it, really, really do. We have to. Critics ripping the flick to shreds, all the annoying (not-comic-book-geeks who didn't understand a thing of the story) reviews - we have to beat all this. You may argue with me, hate me, troll me - I'll never change my mind. BVS is the most fan-service accurate and comic-booky movie ever since the Watchmen. Those who say that DC can't set Up a Universe like Marvel does it, well that's just trash. It's not true. Marvel, with all it's "references" and absolutely pointless humor and plain dialogues feels cheap to me. Sorry all the Marvel fans. But that's how it is to me. Back to the BVS movie. It does not need approval or judgment as if it is or it isn't a movie picture (plot drama, depth etc.) - just stop it already. It's a great experience for the comic book nerds, it has all the ties and references (those by the way don't lead to just nothing, they are there for a reason). This is A COMIC BOOK movie - which literally means that it's not supposed to bring super accurate literature-quality story. It just has to be comic-booky. Understand it in any way you like. All that said, this is the moment when all of us, comic-book geeks, we finally got our prize - the universe where you actually MUST read at least some books to get the understanding of the narrative, and not some attractions-like stupid kids-oriented theater like Marvel films after Iron Man 2. This is the moment we must save the DC Universe on the screen. We need to defend it, support it. I know, this all sounds like another stupidity of a geeks "holywar", but please, I you liked, it, go and see It twice. We need to support DC and Waner Bros with a coin, because lately, after I came home from the cinema (being exited) and started to read all the reviews on the web.... I got worried about the future of the cinematic DC. Thank you.

title: THIS IS THE DC COMICS MOVIE WE NEED! Dark, gritty, and a Batman/Bruce, we finally acknowledged from the comics. Ben Affleck you finessed it!
review: This is my first time going to a comic based movie on its first night of release and I was amazed. First, the trailers deceived us in a great way and this movie is what I needed to see from a DC Comic Universe. I am just not understanding the harsh criticism from professional critics, trust me their opinions matters to a certain extent; yet, it is a must-see if you're a fan. Ben Affleck!! So many people doubted you; but, you were the best as Batman/Bruce W. and I am a dedicated comic book Frank Miller fan of Batman. I watched Batman since 1992 Animated Series, Adam West, comics, animations and all the movies since a kid (I'm 25) and Ben hands down is the Best Batman to hit the big screen. Nolan in my view placed Batman into a realistic world, great; however, overall was not the original Batman from the Batmobile to the hockey costume. Sorry, Bale, it's been great. Synder, bring on the Justice League, P.S (spoiler alert) instead of waiting until the end of credits like marvel movies, Synder did courtesy and provides you what's to come from within the context of the film; therefore, go see it and prepare for a Dawn of Justice. Darkseid is coming!!!!! Leave when the film is over, I saved you time. Critics lighten up its a movie made for the true comic fans. Great job to all the cast, the director, and DC Comics.

title: A Spoiler-Free Review
review:
I'm gonna get straight to the point here, because all you really wanna know is if Batman v Superman is a movie worthy of its titular characters, and in my opinion, it totally is. While some might be thrown off by the notion of Batman and Superman fighting one another the first time they're actually in a movie together, director Zack Snyder and writers David Goyer and Chris Terrio, make it believable.

The whole notion of this series of DC Comics movies is that these are what-ifs. What if these superheroes actually existed in our real world? In this movie, Superman has to deal with the political ramifications of his actions in a way that is not too dissimilar than the political debates we find in our day-to-day. Superman can't win for losing and Batman's distrust of him only exacerbates the problem. Of course what makes this movie such a joy is not the depth of the material, but it's seeing these classic characters -- Batman, Superman, and yes, Wonder Woman -- fighting alongside one another for the very first time in live action.

If you were like me and did not like Man of Steel as much as you wanted to, this movie might rectify a lot of the issues you had with that movie. With that said, this movie certainly wont please everyone. I can already tell you Batman v Superman is going to go down as one of those love it or hate it movies with very little in-betweeners. The movie often has a slower pace than most will be expecting, and it also doesn't like to always spell everything out for the audience. Every now and then a scene transpires and it's not till after its completion do you even know what the scene was. There are a fair few dream sequences in this movie, almost all of them belonging to Bruce Wayne's nightmares and are setting up future sequels. Sure, the movie could have done with a little less teasing of the upcoming Justice League movie and been a tighter affair because of it, but the movie that exists is a good one that I found myself invested in, both emotionally and cerebrally.

The action sequences are top notch and exciting, and the drama, in particular the finale, is executed very powerfully. While I know there will be other fan boys complaining about Batman or Superman doing this or that that they never did in the comic books, both of these characters go on a journey in this movie, and if you hang with it, you'll see the two of them evolve into their traditional comic book counterparts by the time the credits roll. And rest assured, Ben Affleck is really, really good as Batman, while Henry Cavill continues to prove his chops as Superman. As for Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, she certainly holds her own alongside the other two and left me wanting more. All in all, I just wish the Justice League was already out so I can see what happens next! Yeah, I liked this one that much.

I give Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice an 8 out of 10!

title: Amazing! WOW
review:
What in the world are people whining about?? This movie is amazing!! Zack did a great job in telling the story and everything was on point. I don't even think many people who are writing on here, have even seen the movie. I can't wait to go back and see this again! The DC Universe is going to be awesome, and what a way to start it. title: Simply embarrassing. Wait for it to come out on video.
review:
Batman V Superman is a lot like an exaggerated Man of Steel; which means, that it takes all the things I didn't like about Man of Steel, and makes them even worse. It is like Zack Snyder didn't learn his lesson from Man of Steel. Batman v Superman is very palaverous and boring when you're not watching action, or the main characters interact with each other. It is dark in both story and literally film color palette. People complained about the dark and grainy filters in Man of steel, why would Snyder pull the same sh*t here" Next, the film has a lot of unnecessary moving parts, it was like someone threw in a bunch of random chunks of whatever into the movie. Basically, the movie is bloated because it has to introduce Batman, talk about what happened in Metropolis at the end of Man of steel, introduce Lex Luthor, Doomsday, Wonder Woman, a bunch of other people I can not tell you about because this is a spoiler free review, you see what I'm getting at. The movie does a lot of world building at the cost of making a watchable movie. It isn't really a big secret that Warner Brothers and DC is trying to rush out a whole cinematic universe, in hopes of being as successful as Marvel's many cash cow series of films. And that is the problem with this movie. It is rushed, bloated and choppy. It basically gives us an introduction to the Justice League while spending a lot of time setting up the Batman universe to the point of showing us the freaking Batman origin story all over again. How many times do I need to watch Batman's origin. Why didn't they just save it for a solo Batman film?

I'll tell you why, because Zack Snyder shouldn't be allowed behind a camera.

Zack Snyder is an overrated special effects producer, who should have never been promoted to director level status. His slow-mo bull got old with watchmen, and was annoying in man of steel, but now it is just rage inducing.

It is like he likes to slow sh*t down, or speed it up, why can't he just stop playing around with the funking speed button. Anyway, the film is dark, both literally and figuratively.

I'm not sure why Zack Snyder loves to use a darker filter when he is editing his films but it makes the movie feel dull, which isn't a good thing.

This movie isn't all bad but it isn't all good. But the bad things outweigh the good things and the mistakes are noticeable. The good news is that I was wrong about Ben Affleck, he makes a great Batman and Bruce Wayne. I have a newfound respect for Ben Affleck and I want to see him in a solo Batman movie.

Jessie Eisenberg does an okay job. If I had to watch him for 5 more minutes, he would start annoying me.

Gal Godot's Wonder Woman is overrated. She isn't in the movie long enough to really justify me even talking about her. They're basically still hiding her, because she can't act. I'm sorry, but I'm just being real. Henry Cavill does a fine job, and this time we get to see more of him as Clark Kent. The action in this movie is both good and bad. The actual fight between Batman and Superman is good, however shorter than I would have liked. Why would they call the movie Batman V Superman when they fight for about 4 or 5 minutes. Anyway. The fight between what I'm going to call Justice league one point o, and Doomsday, is embarrassing. The CGI is awful and they literally try to hide it was dust and dark lighting, and a bunch of other bull, but Doomsday looks like dog crap. What a waste, what a freaking waste. They shoehorned in like 20 different plots from various iconic comics just to give us and underwhelming movie that, I fear, will hurt comic book movies in general.

As a DC fan, I am genuinely worried. Do yourself a favor and just rent Batman V Superman. How can they spend so much money making this and not even give us good CGI. I can not even recommend this for the action. The Batman Superman fight was okay but short as hell and the reason they fight and resolution will pi$$ you off. This movie has a ton of easter eggs but what the hell. Please, stop just stop with all the easter eggs and give me a watchable movie. Yes, I see that funking easter egg and I get that stupid reference because I read the comic but damn, remember that you are making a movie for general movie goers, and not for a bunch of comic book fanboys on a stupid little easter egg hunt.

This movie has the potential to hurt all of the upcoming superhero films. Christopher Nolan and Joss Whedon worked so hard to make superhero movies respectable, and now, Zack Snyder pulls this crap and jeopardizes everything. This movie is disrespectful to the characters of Batman and Superman but I'm ignoring all that, I'm just reviewing this piece of crap of a film for whether it is entertaining or not and it is damn. I'm going to stop now.

title: Full power but some lengths
review:
I'll try to be as short as I can. There's a lot of stuff to say about this movie though.

All cast does a great job playing its characters, the Battfleck is great, Jesse Eisenberg too.

First of all, when you see this movie you have to forget about Marvel movies. This ain't gonna be like them. This is a new approach, BvS has its own style.

Every action scene is worth it but during the movie there's some lengths that make people uncomfortable. Lots of references that not everyone can understand. But in the head it's a sweet experience that can grasp the quality of the best Marvel movies (like Guardians of The Galaxy, Iron Man 1).

title: Just like the Comic books!
review:
If you know the DC Comics Universe, read the comic books and watched the old animated series, this is the film made for yo. If you don't follow it, and use the old films of these two iconic superheroes as your source, then you will probably not enjoy it.

It doesn't have to be like Marvel's universe or tone setting, it handles it well on it's own feet. Batman is straight from the comic books and to an extent like the Arkham Video game series, Dark and menacing that strikes fear in those he faces.

Sure the film has flaws, but there are far too many enjoyable scenes to let the little things bother you.

Overall, I walked out of the cinemas very happy with what I got. The beginning of a new Comic book universe for all of us to experience in the near future!

title: Do not pay attention to the movie reviews
review: Batman v Superman is not the best superhero movie ever and is really far far away from being it, but is awesome, the action scenes, the new characters, the performances and the soundtrack are the best from this movie. It is darker than many other superhero films and it does explain many things but you never feel it boring or saturated. Ben Affleck nailed it as Batman, and it's the best Batman we have seen to the date and I'm not joking, I was pleasantly surprised in that sense. Jesse Eissenberg was my biggest fear but overall he is OK as Lex Luthor. Wonder Woman was amazingly beautiful and epic in this movie even though that he is in just a couple of scenes. It has some flaws like the third act that has too much C.G.I that sometimes it seems really artificial and that some subplots didn't work but overall this was a very good movie, so go and check it out.

title: this movie is for batman fans only
review:

One has to wonder why has not invented a time machine to stop his parents from being killed, maybe he likes the fortune he inherited.

Anyway, if you are a batman fan then you will love the movie, just give yourself enough prep time.

title: Pretty disappointing
review:
This film, having Ben Affleck as Batman felt quite disappointing.

I personally really don't like this Batman. Here he felt like a very selfish, self-proclaimed judge / executioner. In the Dark Knight trilogy he didn't feel like this at all, which is why I loved Batman there. But Superman is just Superman, so that was alright.

Besides that, there was not much of an intense or interesting plot, it all felt really bare. It was quite boring and nothing special. The appearance of Wonder Woman was a welcome one, because if even she wasn't here, the film would've been rated lower for me.

All in all I wouldn't watch this film, because there is just nothing you will really miss.

title: Kind of pathetic
review:

It has some good ideas and performances, but the execution is poor and the writing doesn't make the actors any favors.

review:

title: What a mess
review:
I heard about how about this film but decided to watch anyway. If Man of Steel (2013) had any promise of being a decent start to the Justice League franchise, then this movie just took that and destroyed it!!!!!

To get it out of the way, there were a few good things about the film. I did enjoy the visuals, the fight scene between Batman and Superman was pretty good, and many the actors were chosen well for their roles like Affleck as Batman and Jeremy Irons as Alfred. But they are outweighed by bad points of the film.

First off, Batman being one of the great superheroes is also a great detective! He's able to figure out anything and yet he wasn't able to determine that Superman wasn't the enemy and Lex Luthor was manipulating everyone. Next, Lex Luthor's portrayal by Jesse Eisenberg was embarrassing to the character. This has always been a cool character being diabolical, sophisticated, and charming and yet this guy is like an over the top cartoon villain. Additionally, doomsday was pointless to the film other being bait for fans to see the movie.

My other problems with the film involve its structure. There are so many subplots that are trying to build up to the next films that it does nothing to the narrative going on the film. Then there's the three acts of the film where the first act (the build up) seems to take up so much time before the actual fight and they quickly run through the last two (the last 30 minutes).

All and all, it's an irritating film that ruins the Justice League for me especially having grown up with the cartoon. If you enjoy it then cool with you, but I can never.

title: Batman vs. Superman vs. The Audience
review:
This is the first time I've ever blamed the failure of a film on the editing. The movie jumps randomly and disconnectedly from scene to scene leaving the viewer in a state of constant bewilderment.

First of all, you have to figure out why Batman has it in for Superman. Apparently, in a misguided attempt to save his unremarkable girlfriend, Lois Lane, Superman manages to inadvertently kill several hundred people. Well, mistakes happen. Unfortunately, among these victims is Batman's father. What are the odds! Then come a series of flashbacks interwoven with a number of story lines that try, and often succeed, in baffling the viewer. The actors themselves seem vaguely confused with their roles and look as if they're not sure what emotions are required in certain scenes.

The movie is, unsurprisingly, targeted at teens, so I watched it with my 14-year-old son. When he frequently asked me what was happening, I could only respond with the look of a dog having the principles of the door knob explained to him. I told him that artistic films frequently had no discernible plot. He didn't buy it.

When the audience is finally on the ropes, the filmmakers tighten the screws by concocting an unending series of false endings. It becomes a battle of wills between the audience and the filmmakers. Who will break first? The deathblow comes when the filmmakers have an ending that threatens the audience with Batman vs Superman 2.

If you want to watch this film, it might be best to try to re-edit it yourself. The good news is that no matter how you put the scenes together, you won't do worse than the original version. You may even produce Batman vs. Superman 2 in the process.

title: Updated and dumbed down: 'I've killed monsters from other worlds before.'
review:
Someday we will run out of interest in the revisions of Marvel Comics, but for now yet another mind-blowing CGI monstrosity comes out – fine actors attempting to make this thin line of story work. Entertaining? Yes, it did well in the box office, but at over three hours in length and the introduction of yet another enormous hulky beast destroying everything in sight it just gets dreary.

The plot, though minimal is as follows: Society is fearing there should be no Superman because of his alien like actions and Batman is the one who agrees and will also take Superman down. While Superman fears that Batman's actions are wreckless and fearing others, owner of Lex Corp, Lex Luthor is plotting something that will destroy mankind. Will one of the heroes fall or will Lex Luthor take over Metropolis? Ben Affleck is Bruce Wayne/Batman (his supporting helper Alfred is Jeremy Irons), Henry Cavill is Clark Kent/Superman and Amy Adams is his Lois Lane while Diane Lane is his mother. Jesse Eisenberg is the evil Lex Luther, Gal Gadot is Diana Prince/Wonder Woman (yes, they did that), while Lawrence Fishburne and Holly Hunter play significant roles. Of course Krpytonite plays a major role but now as huge as the comically ugly beastie that likes to destroy everything – including Superman.

We may ask 'why don't they just leave the comic book heroes alone?' But obviously there is a paying audience for this. And after all, it is a chance to seem some popular actors play!

title: Great Movie don't let the Critics sway you away from seeing.
review:
I will begin spoiler free but later we will have more meat and potatoes. Batman V Superman is a solid 8-9 Stars. BVS Ultimate Cut is a solid 9-10 Stars. I will openly admit that I prefer DC, and Superman is my favorite superhero of all time so I am biased. However there is a meme floating around that sums my feelings up perfectly. It says "if you're a comic book reader it's a great awesome movie, if you're a casual it's a pretty nice movie, if you're looking for the marvel fun+childish formula maybe it ain't for you." The dark more serious tones truly do represent DC comics. With the entry of this film DC has placed themselves nicely for the future. Go watch it for yourself and get your own opinion. Just remember this is not your typical superhero movie. As far as acting goes I was decently impressed. No one should be concerned any more about Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne. Even though I am one of the people who would of loved to see Christian Bale put the cape on for this story arch, Afflecks performance was great and surpassed my expectations. Same thing with Jesse Eisenburg's Lex Luthor. While I think the role still could of be cast better, can I get a shout out for Bryan Cranston, Eisenburg was just the perfect level of crazy and jerk to make me believe he was Lex Luthor. But as much as I hate to admit it, the weakest performance came from Clark Kent/Superman. Henry Cavill played a similar cold dark confused boy as seen in "Man of Steel." I truly want to believe that this is because we are still trying to develop a Superman that knows his place in the world and is proud of it. I however am fearing that with each film we will realize that Henry Cavill has no acting chops and is only useful as a muscular handsome man. Visually the movie was strikingly beautiful, and as per usual Hans Zimmer knocked the soundtrack out of the park. It is important to note that Zimmer actually co-wrote the score with Junkie XL. This may be because as of now Zimmer has declared he is retired from scoring superhero films and Junkie XL could be taking the new lead in scoring for DC films. I can not really say much more without giving Spoilers so do not read past this point if you want to stay spoiler free.

Now for the section with spoilers.

Probably the biggest complaints I have heard about the movie can be answered if you have knowledge of the comics. One of said biggest issues people have is the dream sequences that Bruce Wayne "Batman" has at several points of the film. People found this to be very confusing and difficult to understand. I however thought they were really well made and exhilarated me for the future films. In the dreams that are about himself they are laying the foundation to show how this older Bruce has taken a mental toll from years of crime fighting. In the dreams that focus on external events like the man in a portal warning him of the future "aka the flash" or when Batman is leading a rogue group of soldiers vs flying demons and superman foot soldiers, Snyder is foreshadowing for to story lines in future films. Story lines such as Darkseid and Apokolips, Flashpoint Paradox, and possibly Injustice. If you are not familiar with any of these stories then you need to go get some reading done. Some people take real objection to the fact that Superman is killed at the end. I think the only reason this is an issue is because previous superhero films both DC and Marvel has illustrated this style of hero death as a no-no. But yet again go read the comics. Specifically the 1992 "The Death of Superman" Story-arc. Basically this a direct inspiration for BVS, and as such I fill BVS did good justice for the comic. Now a more in depth look at the characters. We really only have one time we see the free loving/spirited Clark Kent/ Superman. That one moment is when he is with Louis Lane after the rescue and she is in her bath tube. The sad thing is it seemed more like he was a horny teenager just trying to get some then an honorable man with the women he loves. Just as I previously stated I hope we are just dealing with a young inexperienced boy that is trying to find his place in the world and not stuck with a perversion of the man who stands for "truth, justice, and the American way." I have similar concerns with Gal Gadots portrayal of Diana Prince/ Wonder Woman. I can get over the fact that she is smaller then my perceived perception of Wonder Woman, especially because she is still just a beautiful as I would expect. Also the action she delivers when she enters the fight with Doomsday is phenomenal. However with limited screen time and relativity no important dialogue her character had a weak entrance to the universe. Perhaps my feelings will change in 2017 when the solo Wonder Woman film hits theaters and we get to see her shine in the light instead of sharing it with two other major heroes. Speaking of sharing the light let's talk about the 3 other members of the Justice League hinted at in the film. At one point we are introduced to video footage revealing Aquaman, The Flash, and Cyborg, also the flash shows up briefly at an earlier point of the film. While it was good that the movie did not try to shove a million characters down my throat like a similar Superhero film did this summer, **cough cough** Civil War **cough cough** I would of liked to see more of these characters then what we saw.

title: Ultimate version is the best option
review: In a few words, I can say that BATMAN V SUPERMAN is the best picture from DC Expanded Universe. It need a few of details for being at the level of THE DARK KNIGHT TRILOGY, but it's better developed and worked than MAN OF STEEL. I didn't go to the theater to see this movie, but I decided to discover the experience of the Ultimate version, and it's possible saw a better quality between this cut and the original cut (I saw 30 minutes of the Theatrical version). Great part of the actions are explained correctly, I could see an important component on character development (most notoriously for Bruce Wayne) and a clean edition. In the first version this situations aren't well. In other things, the score from Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL is powerful, the acting of Ben Affleck makes the sensation of darkness of Batman perfectly, the dark tones and seriousness are important elements for create the style of DC in films (Marvel has charisma and strong colors), and Zack Synder made a great job for this ambitious project. Unfortunately, in this film the screenplay has some details which are sometimes confused and not understandable (for example, the motivations of Lex Luthor aren't well explained and the scene of Flash appears with no reasons). However, BVS is a good superhero film. But the best option is try to watch the Ultimate version, because a lot of people said that the Theatrical version is bad. May be some people will thing that the long cut is better. Try to find the 3 hours of tension and fight, and then talk about this film.

title: BVS in 10 points (Spoiler alert)
review:
MY 10 POINTS ON BATMAN V SUPERMAN

------Spoiler Alert------------

1. Jimmy Olsen: He's jimmy Olsen, clack's friend and Sup's best friend and that guy that you can't just treat anyway you like. So don't put him at all in the movie if you are not going to use him. Sup told this guy about his secret identity, what what that about!

2. About Lois: Lane's sole purpose was to put herself in trouble to have Sup save her. OK! it's mostly what Lois does, but this is not a Sup's movie, it's a B&S movie so keep to what is important. BTW Lois' could never figure out who Sup is even when he's in front of her face (so major bust on MoS)

3. About Superman: Sup spent the entire movie confused about his purpose, not doing anything and saving only Lois. Sup is the most just, the most human loving-sacrificing everything for them kind of superheroes (unless he's been affected by some thing like red kryptonite, jokers' gas, Darkseid, apocalypse's hellfire, death of Lois or whatever), the sun in the sky for everyone, the truth teller. I don't know who that character wearing the S was in that movie. I do agree though on why he doesn't like Batman. And BTW he would never kill like that, another major bust on MoS. Give the actor something to work with here.

4. About Batman: Bat spent the entire movie clueless about everything, killing people, and dreaming about prophecies.prophecies seriously! He's the world's smartest detective (after that monkey in a hat guy), the most determined, the most authentic to his cause, the most organized strategist, the most knowledgeable about everything superhero ever ( only Mobius' chair knows more than Bruce, OK I might have gone a little too far with that but you get the point) with one rule: no killing no matter what, no matter what, that is the batman, that is Bruce. Bruce could be brutal, but can never be a straight up murderer. What's the point on fighting Sup if he's going to murder like that? Batman would've known about WW, Flash, AM,CB or even GL for that matter somehow. Lex's videos could have been the definite proof he needed. Bruce would also have done more than driving in the city with a car when Aliens are invading the Earth. Batman in the street in the Batmobile or actually in the Batwing saving people would have been more likely even when he couldn't save the Wayne's tower. The Bat would have been able to decode the weird video from Zod to see his face unlike the rest of the world and know his intentions. BTW putting the indication that he actually helped Lois tracked down Sup could have cleared out this mess. Great Batman performance though, just wrong story telling.

6. About Wonder Woman: WW spent the entire movie popping up in weird places for no reason at all. She's a warrior; she's not about spying on Lex Luther, or been cleverer than Batman. She should have been convinced by Batman to join the fight, though I like the line: "Is she with you? No I thought she was with you? Good one. Great choice of WW, she's awesome in the movie.

7. About Lex Luther (which is actually Lex Luther's son): Lex spent the entire movie doing Dr. Frankenstein things. What is it about Lex that you don't get? Since this is not Lex i have only one thing to say: He created Bizzaro not Doomsday. The real Lex would have been better but I can deal with the son assuming there's another story cooking for the future.

8. About Doomsday: Doomsdays gets the most ridiculous origin ever. Doomsday is the experimental kryptonian product of evolution. He was submitted to the worst scenarios, battling all kind of things including beasts, nature and so on until he evolved into this monster. Doomsday's story should have been kept for MoS2 (The death of Superman anyone). The fight scenes were too messy, too CGI for us to see wth was going on. Wrong choice of villain (Bizzaro could have worked fine), underdeveloped story and wrong ending (totally busted the death of superman story line which is why no one felt any emotion whatsoever when Sup died).

9. About reason for the heroes to join forces: Bat joined Sup because their moms have the same name? Seriously, the same name (something the Bat would already have known by discovering who Sup is immediately if not before, because ....wait for it...HE'S BATMAN!). Not because, the Bat found out about Lex's plan and convinced Sup and WW to join? Not because they realized only their perspectives and methods are different but not their objectives? Not because they both have respect for each other? I can't keep on going with this.

10. Finally, WB should reassess the Zack Snyder approach, adopt the Nolan and Affleck type approach and apologize to every one who watched the movie, especially true comic book fans. This was as close as a disappointment than M. Night Shyamalan' s "Last Air Bender". Zack should reflect deeply on the mess he has given us and rise back to better story telling (outside of the world of DC comics please). And before I'm asked who are you to say this? Let just say that I'm a disappointed movie fan with comic book knowledge.

This is my first review ever, I just couldn't keep it to myself anymore. Now cross fingers for JL. Zack, since you are already leading that project, can you do us a favor and not mess this up for us again please. Thank you.

title: Hot mess of a film
review:
This film could have been so much more; that's the reoccurring theme. There was a ton of things going on and it felt rushed, crowded and confusing. The tone of the film was so dark, at times it felt more like a horror flick. There were a few clumsy attempts to lighten it, but they were at best half-baked and shoehorned in. There was just no fun, no joy to be had here.

Cliche's! Why does Snyder rely on cliche's in a film of this magnitude? Two different times a damsel was held at gunpoint by a bad guy, threatening to "off" her if the hero didn't back down. Why, oh why do directors continue with this worn out trope?

On a good note, I will say that most of the action sequences were well choreographed and staged and the CGI was very good. But then again, there was just so much of it that I felt as if I was the one getting pounded by the end of the film. There was one particular scene in which so much firepower was used to protect an object that it would challenge a small army, but there was no real justification for this use of firepower and later in the film that same object was left barely protected.

The reliance on themes of gods and power were just overdone to the point of obsession. And Holly Hunter cast as a Kentucky Senator was laughable, except that it wasn't supposed to be funny.

The motivations used in this story were also flimsy, sometimes changing the very nature of the character we know. We got too much detail when we needed less and too little when we needed more. All in all, this was yet another misfire by DC and WB and it has me wondering if they understand or even care about their characters.

title: A long pointless tale to establish DCCU.
review:
The movie has promise, and while I favor Marvel, I can't say I would not anticipate DCCU. However, unless the producers gets their stuff together - DC will forever be "number two".

I don't get what do people like about Batfleck. I really don't. Not that I didn't like his acting, he did fine. But the way he was represented - is laughable. He, the genius vigilante - gets TROLLED. Trolled into fighting a near-godlike creature. I don't care that he shot people, murder is always involved in such stuff, direct or indirect. I don't care that he was "jedi mind tricked" by the word Martha. I've seen more stupid stuff on screen(even if Flash said "Lois is the key"). But when Nolan established Batman as a caring human character, perhaps too caring sometimes, all Znyder established was some angry dude who is angry and rude and goes all Punisher and has Iron Man tech and is very emotional... Bottom line - this Batman was a joke. A joke that I couldn't care for less. He didn't make sense, his over-over-over-over establishment didn't make sense. His actions regarding first movie didn't make sense. It's like they've just sucked him out of a thumb to insert into a Superman movie, but make him able to fight the Supe for 10 minutes.

As for the fight itself - laughable. I mean, come on, they sold this cr*p like apple pies for years, and this is what we get? A fake fight, originated from nothing, and resolvable by something called "communication". It's like that legendary yet stupid scene from Interstellar, where instead of "don't do that", the character could say "you'll blow the **** up, and take the station with you". Had Supe nothing better to say, than these "You don't understand, Lex is fooling you". He had to move, he had to trigger all the traps, he had to shove Batman and... bah, make it physical. Seriously, the whole FIGHT was one of the weakest parts of the movie. From the beginning to the end.

Lex Luthor was a bit of a bright spot, but he felt sort of... out of place. Not nearly enough to be a Joker, kind of a weaker, sillier Bane. Nothing he did made any sense. What did he expect when he created DD? The only reason he is alive is because Supe stopped DD's punch. So what if Supe was dead. The whole world would be dead too, including him.

WW\LL were there for the t*ts. Lois Lane was established right away, at which point I didn't know if I'm watching a romantic comedy or a dark superhero movie. And Wonder Woman... well, they needed the third of the DC trinity, but everything she did was pretty secondary. Appears out of nowhere, has no motive, comes very handy, survives the final fight. And damn, she is powerful. While Supe can't really do anything to DD, she actually manages to restrain him, cuts off his hand with... some magic sword(definitely not kryptonite-forged), and nearly finishes him off, if he didn't just spit some laser. And she might be strong and stuff, but last time I checked - she isn't remotely Superman. In fact, she is more like Batman with just some meta-human strength. But her attire is more durable than Supe's caped swimsuit. And she herself is clearly immune to any harm, being absolutely unflinching about fighting something that overpowers\kills Superman. She is as close to some Supergirl as it gets...

Ultimately, compared to the first movie, this is an improvement. Because it at least attempts to present a long, complex story, instead of boredom, followed by Super Sayian. But the fact that no effort has come to the writing\adaptation of the story, no attempt to make it comprehensive or believable... I hope, for the sake of DCCU - that they will change their direction.

title: A Let-down of expectations
review:
I was waiting for about a year to view this movie and was expecting a superbly written, well directed movie with a strong story line.

Boy was I disappointed! The story line was weak to put it politely, script was average and the only saving grace was the superbly taken action sequences. The title was Superman V Batman, the movie makes both of them fight for almost no reason at all! I would have expected a deep well defined reason for their fight, but there is none of it! Characters are rushed, there is no buildup for anything, and Lex Luthor is another let-down. Ben Afleck, despite all the negatives prior to the release, does the role well, and Henry Cavill (superman) does an OK job too.

I would have given it a 6/10, but love Batman and Superman too much for that, hence a 7/10.

title: Enjoyable movie
review:
First of all, I want to say I know this movie wasn't amazing, but I wanted so badly to give it 10/10 anyway to make up for all the unnecessarily harsh ratings I've seen on various sites. I don't know if I saw the same movie as some of these other people, because although it wasn't amazing, it was certainly not awful either. There were for sure some plot holes, and lazy introductions of various characters, but it also has some redeeming qualities too.

I for one never really bought lex luthor's motives and I wasn't sure what they were trying to sell either. I also wish that the other 'meta humans' weren't introduced via email lol but honesty it was still exciting to see these characters on screen.

The action scenes were exciting, and the movie was just visually very pretty. The casting worked for me. I understand why people were unhappy with lex Luthor, because some of his lines just took me out of the movie and made me cringe. But I went into the movie having no prior knowledge of the character or expectations about how he's "supposed" to be portrayed so it wasn't horrible for me. I loved Henry cavill, he is pretty effortlessly superman. Batman worked well too. I was invested in his character even though I was on team superman. I liked the fight scenes, I liked the emotions near the end, and I enjoyed all the political buildup the first half of the movie.

I hear people complaining about how it's "joyless" or too dark, but I don't understand why it has to have a lot of humor to balance out the dark. I mean obviously marvel has been more lighthearted so far, but I don't think all other comic book movies have to follow the same formula. In this case, I thought different is good.

The only part of the move that really made it lose some points for me, was the dialogue and some of the lines. I feel like hey cared less about superman, and gave him some cheesy and lazy ass lines. Hahaha I think Henry cavill did the best he could with those lines, but better writing definitely would have made him shine more. Even so, I liked batman v superman, and I believe it's being unfairly rated. It wasn't horrible and it wasn't outstanding. It was fun, and I think people should go into it with an open mind, instead of thinking about how it's going to be bad, and consequently only seeing the down side of the movie.

title: Confusing, yet intriguing plot, great casting and acting, amazing action and special effects
review: Plot: The biggest gripe I and most moviegoers have is the confusing and disjointed plot. That is a legitimate concern, but if you just sit back and watch, the plot is bearable, even enjoyable. This is not the kind of movie you watch for the plot. The plot masterfully conveys the theme of the movie and provides a break from the intense and beautiful action scenes. The plot is carried by the compelling theme and refreshing new look at the two most popular superheroes, else it would be rated lower. Any number with a 6 in it does not do it justice, but 7 seems too high.(7/10) Acting and Casting: The casting for this movie was fantastic. I especially liked Ben Affleck as Batman and the casting of Lex Luthor. If you are like me and enjoy flawed and multi-dimensional characters you are in for a treat. The acting was also very good, and it is easy to understand and sometimes empathize with the character's emotions. (9/10) Action and Special Effects: This is a staple of any superhero movie, and this one did not disappoint. There is no shortage of fight scenes, explosions, and destruction. The non human beings look very real. The settings for the movie are also very realistic and diverse. Save a major advance in technology, it is hard to imagine the special effects being much better. (10/10) Conclusion: This movie is an amazing experience I would recommend to anyone. Do not get top hung up on the plot which can be all over the place. Just go with the flow and it will be much more enjoyable. The acting is amazing, along with the fight scenes and special effects. A must see movie that leaves a bit to be desired. (8/10)

title: Great spectacle- good performances. but the story
review:
It was impossible for me, to not eagerly await this movie. Well - I like Superman; yet would like to see a "great" adaptation. But I love Batman - and we had already a couple of good "Bats" (Tim Burton's Batman - and "Batman begins") - though there was room for improvement.

After I seen now this flick once - I went again to the movies - and to my surprise, I actually enjoyed it more than the first time.

First to the great points: The mood of the movie is about right. It is dark, and the atmosphere is changing between the main characters. Heroic and epic on Supermans side - dark and almost sociopath on Batmans side. Wonderwoman is a real highlight! Especially the fighting scene is just a the high point of any feminist movement - she is not the one, who need to be saved - but she is also clearly feminine. Alfred is well presented by Jeremy Irons, he brings the "mothers arguments" to Bruce Wayne, which is pretty funny - but he is also totally in their enterprise - which is a bit better than the ever wining Michael Caine. Jesse Eisenberg was a bit of surprise. I really hated him, when I have seen the movie first, but was surprised, that I actually was more investing in his character, when I seen it the second time. Well... maybe the "ding, ding, ding, ding" might become the new Darth Vader "Noooooooooo"...

The shots were also made beautiful and most of the CGI and special effects were done beautifully.

So why haven't I rated it better? Because of following points:

1) Nobody wants to see Bruce Wayne's parents die again. Ever! Ever! The movie is long enough... i simply cannot understand, that they again showed a sequence of Batman's tragic childhood experience. Further "the bat dream" is also pretty useless.

2) Talking about dreams - there are too many of them in the movie. And some of them don't even make remotely sense (think about the Flash sequence).

3) Product placement: it has to be said, it should be forbidden to make obvious product placements in good movies. OK - let's think about it - a multimillionaire (probably billionaire) is leaving his helicopter and stepping into a... Jeep Renegade??? Really? With flashing lights - but without any markings (e.g. Security etc)? Why should he has this type of car?

4) Maybe this should be on number one: the overall story. Is. No. Good. Really. It seems, that the main story is as old as "stories themselves". It doesn't really imply any surprises. But for what it is, it is unnecessary complicated, confusing, and intertwined. It is obvious, that they wanted to set the stage for the next movie, but just screwed it really up!

5) Batmans tech Why is BvS disregarding the successful Batman trilogy? It was well established, that Batman got its tech from the military branch of Wayne Tech. And it made sense. Now you have a "superbullet proof" bat mobile - and a crazy bat plane - made with a couple of wrenches of Alfred... yeah right.

6) The Bruce training montage So Batman is obviously keeping himself fit. But when he decides to fight against Superman, he is doing some extra pull-ups (with a laughable big steel ball), pulling a truck tire and hammers on it. Yeah right... make sense, to do some extra workout, against an individual, who can fly and who pulls an icebreaker by himself...

7) Physics and realism Can we come to a point, where movies at least try to stay with physics? Heavy wood boxes are flying through the air as they were made from balsa wood - but also are not breaking. Superman seems to have trouble to lift Batman (with his armored suit), but then throws him through several walls. The armored suit itself...pathetic. And yeah - Supermans application of his powers, is also made in fantasy land. Also Superman seems to have the ability to appear instantly anywhere he wants... I thought that this is not one of his powers (even if he would fly extremely fast, he would need at least several seconds or even minutes to come to a remote place).

8) Armoured suit If we are already at the armored suit - if the story invest into it, why isn't it at least partly explained? Yeah - the voice modulation is mentioned... but if the suit should take a beating, how it was shown in the film, and keep Bruce Wayne alive, it should have been at least a bit explained.

9) Aquaman and the Flash No explanation needed :(

10) Many more stupid points... For example, that it is said, that Batman works with the Police, but there is no other evidence than the statement of Clark Kent.

title: Almost a great movie, almost
review:
I went into this with the standard doubts, "Batman v superman, hmm, Superman every time?" this total blows that question out of the water, on the right day Batman will kick Superman into tomorrow.

Ben Affleck plays an older, world weary and cynical Batman (and plays him VERY well) who stands as the voice of doubt against the new messiah, Superman. title: Some good parts, but also flaws
review:
As far as the positives go , I thought that the roles of Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman were played quite well. There were some great eye candy scenes, which were quite well done.

The believability factor was almost non-existent, however. For example, how can bats levitate young Bruce Wayne out of a hole? How can Superman and Doomsday survive a direct hit from a hydrogen bomb? How can Superman "breathe" in outer space? There's no scientific explanations behind those things and other things. Also, Gotham City and Metropolis are fictitious cities even though they originated in the comic books. The movie, to have a bit more realism, could have used cities such as St. Paul and Minneapolis if they're so close together as indicated by the movie. Otherwise, it's pure fantasy even though it's a superhero movie. Although superhero movies are in part fantasy, some scientific basis should be included in those movies to make it better.

The plot was OK in some ways, but it was quite fragmented, which made for an "uneven" movie. Lex Luther may as well have been the Joker, for he looked more that part. And, for there to be a Justice League movie, the Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg are going to have to be much more developed character-wise before that movie comes out. Wonder Woman was in herself not really well-developed as a character. Perhaps the upcoming Wonder Woman movie will bridge that gap.

All in all, it may have been OK as a popcorn movie, but otherwise, don't set your expectations too high IMO.

title: Battle of the Butt Chins
review:
Batman and Superman, two of the greatest superheroes of all time squaring off in toe to toe. It's going to be epic... Until you actually see it that is. This film had the making and source material to be one of the greatest superhero films but this film just isn't a good film period.

The film opens with the Wayne family tragedy which everyone and their grandma knows all too well, coupled with narration from Batfleck himself going for the most unoriginal movie opening sequence imaginable.

This is then followed by Bruce Wayne driving into a collapsing Metropolis as Superman and Zod fight at the close of Man of Steel. Although being a kick ass scene I cannot help but say to myself "Wouldn't he be of actual use and actually be able to save someone if he was in the bat suit flying the bat wing?" You could argue the lack of time on his part but when has movie magic stopped you from doing anything. In fact I would argue if he was in the bat suit it would actually establish why the two hate each other...

... Which brings me to my next point. Why do they hate each other? I can understand why Bruce Wayne hates Superman because he killed that one employee he liked in the opening, but it is not explained as to why Superman hates Batman. Clark Kent does talk about Batman being a vigilante being the reason, but hello, superman is a vigilante too in fact that is basically the basis of the film for the majority. The film really did fail in being clear in its motives.

There is a continual lack of logic and continuity as the film progresses and becomes so apparent that it leaves you scratching you head thinking "WTF???". I have no idea what the dream within a dream sequence about a post apocalyptic Batman and a weird dude crawling out a light portal to tell Bruce something was all about, and the latter isn't even followed up on. This even reaches the point of being laughable when Wonder Woman watches a live news broadcast on a TV located on the back of a air plane passenger seat. The filmmakers must know that those TV's don't do that right?

Which again brings me swiftly on to my next point of Wonder Women. What was the point of her? She was literally pointless. This leaves me to conclude her inclusion in this film to be purely economic rather than serving any real purpose to this particular film. Her only saving grace is her involvement in future films being made perfectly clear but she really could have been placed in the film the same way that the Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg where.

I enjoyed the action sequences for the most part. That I will admit, but the final fight against Doomsday takes the mick. The film becomes more of a Lazar light show which if you are lucky you may be able to work out what is going on. Also add to that the slightly rushed feel of the final act of the film and that the kryptonite spear is placed in water for some reason and not retrieved by Aquaman creating a missed opportunity that I'm sure many where expecting and exited to see happen but didn't. And you got yourself a rather less than satisfactory showdown on your hands.

Overall Batman vs Superman is crushed by hype and is sadly a deeply disappointing movie. Constant cuts to black and white as well as confusing plot development, lack of logic, CGI overkill, unclear or unexplained plot points etc etc etc. The film is a massive waste of potential which disappointed me even when I had average expectations. This is the start of the DC universe calendar and I sure hope they get better. Plus I'm not looking forward to seeing that annoying little not-Kevin-Spacey Lex Luther again that's for sure. Fingers crossed Suicide Squad is good.

title: Confusing and Boring
review: I have always been a huge Batman and Superman fan. I have read the comics, seen the movies, and pretty much done every nerdy thing you can think of that relates to the two super heroes. I was looking forward to this move for months and to say that I was underwhelmed is an understatement. The movie overall was very confusing because the movie was shot from different perspectives and often times in these completely different perspectives there would be a flashback or a dream that would just blur the plot, cause the true purpose of the movie to get lost, and overall it would just confuse the movie watcher. The confusion wouldn't have been so bad though if the movie was jam packed with action and fight scenes like the comic books or previous movies, but an hour and a half into the movie and Batman and Superman had never even really confronted one another. This movie lacked so much and overall was a huge disappointment. I left the movie theater thinking of ways I could easily have made the movie better, and anytime I leave a movie doing that, I know the movie I just saw was awful.

title: It starts off so perfectly right, and then goes so perfectly wrong!
review:
I gave this film the exact same rating as I gave Revenge of the Sith! I have a valid reason why. In Star Wars: Episode III, there were some beautiful and cool scenes. Some acting was believable. John Williams's soundtrack made the film watchable. Then there were parts of the movie that made me so angry at the wasted potential. The same can be said for Dawn of Justice. BEWARE: MANY SPOILERS AHEAD!!

The beginning was so beautiful and perfect, then became a comic book fan's worst nightmare. Doomsday, Lex Luthor, Batman, Lois Lane, and Superman are all disappointments. Every character that wasn't Wonder Woman was a moron. Lex Luthor has no clear motive for being such an ******* except that he's crazy. He seems like a lame attempt of Heath Ledger's Joker. Batman is a moron instead of being the detective that he's supposed to be. Superman is so slow and dumb. As Angry Joe said, after Lex captured his mom and told Superman to kill Batman, Superman could flown to Batman and said "WHOA WHOA, WAIT. Lex Luthor has my mom! Help me out." Instead, Superman knocks around Batman while saying "You have to understand!" *punches Bruce* "Listen to me!" *flies him through a building* Batman stops short of impaling Superman with spear after learning that their mothers share the same first name: Martha. After that, they became best friends. =_=. They team up to fight Lex and his goons, then Lex unleashes Doomsday. Doomsday almost immediately tries to kill Luthor but Superman stupidly saved him even though Luthor is a murderer and almost had Martha Kent burned to death. Doomsday looks like a cave troll from Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring. He looks nothing like his comic book self. Later, he evolves every couple of minutes. The comics made him evolve and get stronger any time he was defeated, making him unable to beat the same way twice. Then Doomsday killed Superman. That's it. This movie was The horrible Death of Superman that I and many other comic book fans had been waiting for for years. This effectively ruins Superman, his lore, and Man of Steel sequels. If Braniac, Mongul or Darkseid fight Superman now, there's no threat. Superman has already died once. He's not going to die again. That's why they should have waited to use Doomsday until the third or fourth Man of Steel movie, not the direct sequel to the newest reboot of Superman. Batman mourns the loss of Superman even though he was just trying to kill him 20 minutes before. He visits Luthor in prison, scares him, then leaves even though he kills criminals and Lex knows who Batman is. This movie is so self-contradicting it's insane. It's a ruination of what could have been great. The acting of Ben Affleck, Jeremy Irons, the soundtrack, the improved cinematography, and the incredible CGI is what keeps the rating at a 4/10. The rest of the movie took off the other 6 points.

title: Spectacle and atmosphere abound... but at the cost of all else...
review:
It was never going to be easy to re-introduce Batman onto the big screen after Nolan's fabulous "Dark Knight" trilogy, but Ben Affleck quells all doubt in a superb performance.

That said, it's worth beginning with the movie's good points. Firstly, the effects are amazing, as one would expect from a modern big- budget superhero flick. Superman's on-screen presence in particular is mesmerizing, and the combat towards the film's climax is grandiose in both its brutality and its spectacle. The casting itself seems spot- on, with stand-out performances from Ben Affleck's older, blooded portrayal of Batman to Jesse Eisenberg's young Lex Luthor. Eisenberg steals the scenes in which he features, perfectly defining Luthor on the cusp of becoming the cold, measured DC villain we know and love.

Unfortunately, there isn't much more positive praise to be said. The narrative just doesn't seem justified and - especially in the first half - is just shameful. Those who haven't seen the previous "Man of Steel" are left in the dust at certain moments. Scenes are hastily stuck together without any explanation, and Superman's vendetta against Batman's "unchecked" status seems ridiculous given that Batman doesn't posses any of Superman's Godlike powers. The fight itself lasts a mere ten minutes in an over-long and drawn out picture. Though Ben Affleck's performance is strong, Batman's character in this film seems uncaring... overly brutal and violent. Despite Batman's iconic "anti-hero" personality, it is as though Zack Snyder didn't know where to draw the line between a hero with a troubled past and a plain thug. The writing is average at best. This shows most evidently between Henry Cavill's dialogue with Amy Adams... a missed opportunity, as while both are perfectly casted, their scenes seem contrived and clichéd by their lines. Their relationship doesn't develop at all and doesn't seem genuine, which detracts from Adams' presence in the film. A final issue is the lighting and camera work. Batman vs Superman is an undeniably dark film, but the lack of light contrast on display was a terribly over-contrived attempt at creating atmosphere. Some scenes are so unnecessarily dark that all on-screen coherence is blurred, and this isn't helped by the shaky camera styles employed in certain scenes, which blur and shake to the extent that the shots employed seem a messy attempt at editing together a scene.

Overall, Batman vs Superman isn't a terrible film. It's arguably much more emotive than "Man of Steel", with it being evident that Snyder and his crew wished to create something packed with energy and atmosphere. The problem is that this comes at the cost of everything else: narrative, plot, a good script... none of these are present. It's a shame given that the film's effects and casting render it a wasted chance to create something truly special. Like Marvel before this, this new generation of DC film-writers is going to have to choose between going for all out spectacle, or creating a more balanced picture worthy of viewing.

title: Slow start but explosive end
review:
I agree with most critics that the movie starts too slow. There is too much explaining and not enough action. On the other hand, the climax is everything I hoped for.

It seems that the director had to cut a lot in the movie as at some moments the story does not make any sense. Hopefully the Director's cut will make this right.

I think that not all bad reviews are justifiable. Some critics just did not pay enough attention as a lot of their complaints are explained in the story. Maybe they should see it again (if they can bring themselves to that of course).

title: A new type of Comic Book film
review:
Zack Snyder's "Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice" is a different style of Comic Book movie than we have seen in the past. To some viewers who have gotten used to the "Marvel" style of Superhero movie, than this film will disappoint. But if you go into the theater with optimism, you will surely enjoy.

Pros: - Incredible visuals - Incredible score from Hans Zimmer - Acting is good from the entire cast - Some entertaining scenes - Well written script - Scenes will excite people for future DC films

Cons: - Drags on in some scenes - Jesse Eisenberg, while not terrible, would have been better suited to play "The Riddler" - Some scenes rushed or sloppily edited (I believe this will be fixed in the 3 hour directors cut) - The first part of the title "Batman V Superman" is a bit misleading - Forces a lot into this film - Some scenes will confuse non-hard-core DC fans

Overall, this is a great start to DC's Cinematic Universe. The only real problem with this film is the fact that some scenes become boring as they drag on, but other than that, it is a great film. I'm giving it an 8.

title: Most ambitious comic book film of all time.
review: Let start off by saying I enjoyed this film. Yes it's not a great film but it's not the worst either. It's a decent film. To me it's good. Now that I said that let me give more details into my rating for this film. Batman V Superman: Dawn Of Justice is one of the most ambitious comic book film I've seen since Watchmen. Unfortunately it comes up short on my expectations, as I'm sure does the same with yours, but still doesn't mean that I didn't enjoy it. I did not like the way this film was edited, Zack Snyder tried the same editing style he did in Watchmen with BVS but doesn't work out well. The story could've been more powerful but it lacks substance.
