title: If you like cool action with several loose and incoherent plots, this movie is for you
review: To begin with, I'm not a fan of comic books, I don't know the DC background lore, I am however a fan of comic book movies. I felt excluded from certain sections of the plot and as a result I feel frustrated. The story seems like it needs background information, this shouldn't be the case with a big budget blockbuster aimed at the masses. The actual movie falls way below par in several key areas. Firstly, the editing is terrible. There are several story lines crammed into this movie and it constantly flits between them. As you start to feel engaged with a particular story it all of a sudden jumps off on a non-linear nor coherent tangent into a completely different story. What is even more frustrating is that several of these stories actually don't make much sense nor do they add to the overarching (and might I add, thin) plot. One of the elements which actually disappointed me the most was the Hans Zimmer score. Whilst usually Hans Zimmer is amazing, and there are several sections where the score is excellent and really adds to the movie, I was not impressed. During the movies climactic scene, his score is based around electric guitars which seem to unpleasantly clash with the scene, it is not his finest work. I felt the characters were a mix bag. I really liked Ben Affleck's take on batman. It was aggressive and dark and unlike what we are used to. But that said, I felt the character required a little bit more exposition as to why he fell into such a dark place. Gal Gadot's Wonder Women disappointed me and it was nothing to do with her performance. You can't put an actress in pretty dresses and call that character development. The writing for her character seems to spit in the faces of your Jennifer Lawrence's, your Daisy Ridley's and your Charlize Theron's of the world. For most the movie she is given very little dialogue or job to do and I truly feel her sole role was as 'eye-candy' and to make the fan boys happy that she appears in it. Would the movie have suffered had she not been in it? Henry Caville's superman, whom I liked in man of steel was agonisingly boring. All he did was mope around and look stern and brooding. The movie seemed to set up a very interesting debate as to whether the world needs him and for a bizarre directorial choice decides to include the question in lot of scenes but never actually tackle it, it should have been an interesting question in the aftermath of MoS. And finally Lex Luther, he was just plain annoying! I never understood his motivation for his actions nor really his end game, I like Jesse Eisenberg, I didn't like him here. He wanted to come across as being a smart and high brow villain but name dropping myths and philosophers and pointing at art did not strike me as being particularly intelligent, merely that the screenwriter likes wikipedia. That said, Snyder does get action scenes and there were two outstanding fights, both with marvellous choreography and cinematography. This movie promised a clash of titans, what it delivered was an incoherent mess, where the full philosophical debate between Batman and Superman was never realised. The plot requires you to abandon reality and believe that these characters would really respond to certain situations in the way the movie would have you believe. The tone of the movie was dank and lacking in fun to the point that when a joke was inserted it felt more like an accident then by design. I enjoyed the visuals, I enjoyed the fights but no I did not really enjoy the movie.

title: Not Perfect...But a Good CBM Film Nonetheless!
review:
First of all. Don't believe the over the top ridiculous and rather unsubstantiated poisonous criticism that some "professional critics" have bestowed. I do use the term professional critics lightly because I consider them more hypo critics more than anything. Always talking out of both sides of there mouths when it comes to films and contradicting themselves from film to film. No credibility whatsoever.

BvS is not a carbon copy of the over the top, cheesy forced dialogue of the Marvel films and nor should it be. This film deals a little more with real world issues and anxieties and makes you think a little more.

It's also a film that upon first viewing is mind blowing and engrossing and entertaining superhero film. Affleck as Batman is simply bad ass. He is jaded and an older Bruce Wayne in his early 40's who has seen and been through horrible things while fighting the war that never ends for 20 years. Affleck is a beast as Batman and we the best action and fight scenes of Batman out of all the previous films and the Batsuit is the best overall as well. The Batcave is a mix between Nolans and Burtons films and is a nice upgrade from those films.

Cavill is fine as Superman and Clark Kent and is basically the heart and soul of the film.

Gadot is a highlight as mysterious Diana Prince and when we see her as Wonder Woman it is just one big tease to how great it will be to her in her solo origin film in Summer 2017. Note: Here is hoping WB's changes her release date from a crowded June to late March early April or early August date to set her film up for success financially.

Eisenbergs Lex is a younger, yet brilliant and twisted paranoid version of Lex who is out to destroy the "god" who will eventually destroy and take over humanity. Eisenberg adds some quirky humor to Lex and does solid work. I personally was worried about over acting from him, but he keeps himself in check just fine.

The rest of the supporting cast ie Adams, Fishburne, Lane and Irons are fine.

The pacing is up and down and becomes a little choppy in the 2nd half, but this is a 2 hr and 20 min film (not including end credits) that does not drag and keeps you engrossed with a good, surprising ending that leaves you wanting more. This film also does a nice job of teasing the Justice League that certainly does not ruin the flow of the film and also teases a potentially bigger legendary threat for the future of the DC films and the Justice League.

This film is quite easy to follow and if anything I do think Snyder could have added more humor in the 1st half of the film or maybe even bit more superhero action. The story and script is fine, but the editing could have been better. Regardless, the film keeps you engaged.

Watch the movie and enjoy. Don't try and pick it apart like the hypo critics. It's still a mind blowing and engrossing CBM film from start to finish. Despite it's flaws, this film has definite re watch value on the big screen. I look forward to seeing the improvements for the Justice League films!

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is a great movie.
review:
Batman V Superman was epic.

I only vaguely understand the massive hate that this film has been receiving. Not only is it visually STUNNING, but it also deals with themes that no other superhero movie has even briefly touched on, save for Zach Snyder's other epic superhero film The Watchmen. Maybe people are too use to Marvel's clean cut approach to superhero films, or maybe it's just too easy to fall into the 'mob' mentality, but this movie is great. It isn't perfect by a long shot, but it is a great film.

First off, the casting was spot on. Ben Affleck is without a shred of doubt the greatest on screen Batman that has ever appeared. He's brooding, angry, brutal, and at times charming as hell. And to match that perfect casting decision, Snyder cast the outstanding Jeremy Irons, who gave us one hell of an Alfred, perfectly matching Affleck's Bruce Wayne. Honestly the chemistry between the two was fantastic. Henry Cavill delivers as Superman/Clark Kent, but I do wish they had explored his mindset a little more throughout the movie to make some of the later dramatic scenes hold a bit more weight, but that isn't really Cavill's fault. Even Jesse Eisenberg, who people have attacked viciously online, gave a really good performance. It was quirky, menacing, uncomfortable, and made me feel like this Lex Luthor was a genuine threat within the context of the movie.

Now where the movie really shines is with the actions scenes. Never have I felt such a feeling of grandiose as when I watched Superman and Batman duke it out, it was like I was a kid again sitting on my bedroom floor playing action figures, and I mean that in a good way. When Batman is taking on thugs however is when I found the movie riveting. This Batman does not hold back at all and it is goddamn beautiful. I'm so happy they decided to go a different direction with their take on this character because it really pays off, and works wonderfully within the movie and to aid the overall themes on display.

All in all, a very impressive film. At times the editing was jarring, and there were perhaps one too man "dream sequences", but the major issues with the movie are generally nit picky. Honestly if you tore apart The Dark Knight as much as critics are tearing this apart you would see just as many holes, well maybe not just as many, but there would be holes nonetheless!

I think the best any of us can do when faced with a massive movie like this with such a divisive response from fans and critics, is to see it for yourself and decide whether you think its as much of a triumph as I do, or the crap that Rotten Tomatoes would have you believe.

title: My (detailed and spoiler-free) review of BvS
review:
Despite being an IMDb member for well over a decade, I have never written a review on this site before. But in the case of this movie, I feel compelled to... because the critics have got this one so wrong! I'll start by saying it isn't perfect. It does give the impression that they've tried to cram too many major events into one movie, and thus it feels a bit choppy, somewhat rushed, and lacks some overall polish as a consequence. But it is still a well-acted, well-shot, emotionally impactful and visually compelling movie.

To see this movie taking the lambasting it is taking from the critics suggests to me that many of them have a heavy personal bias or agenda against its themes, or frankly lack the critical insight to even understand what this movie is trying to convey. For instance, how can one particular moment in the film resonate so well with with some critics that it reduces them to tears, while others merely scoff and say, "Really, is that it? I don't understand why he'd act that way. Did I miss something?" (Yes, you did!)

I'll give a piece of advice to those of you who haven't seen this movie yet, or those want to watch it again from a different perspective. Take all the preconceptions you have from Superman: the Movie, the Marvel cinematic universe, and every previous CBM you've ever seen, and put them all to one side. Just like you cannot watch Game of Thrones with the same wantonly naïve glasses you watch the Lord of the Rings with. This is not a family friendly movie – nor does it try to be. Don't go in with personal demands of what you want the story to be and then complain when this film doesn't meet them. This is altogether a fresh take on the genre.

Before this movie was even released, Zack Snyder announced there would be an R-rated extended edition when the DVD release came out. What does that tell you?

So, on to the movie itself. There are some powerful scenes right off the bat – no pun intended – introducing us to Bruce Wayne and lining this movie up with the events of Man of Steel. I have to say here that anyone, (including myself), who previously ragged on the idea of Ben Affleck as Batman will be eating their words right now, because I swear Affleck displays a greater range of emotions in these introductory scenes alone than he has in his entire career. Even the harshest critics of this movie have conceded that Ben is awesome in this movie, and most will tell you that his is the best on-screen Batman we have ever witnessed.

From here on the pace of the movie does not relent as we are re-introduced to Lois and Superman, and meet many new characters for the first time. This is where many start to have issues with the film; there is an awful lot of ground to cover. It is because of all these new and old characters, each with their own intrigues and personal machinations, that the film starts to appear disjointed. There is so much going on at the same time, we are often forced to jump from one pivotal scene to another completely unrelated one, just to keep each individual story up-to-date and moving along on the same continuity. Personally, although I didn't find it difficult to follow at all, it did seem a little jarring at times.

The people who are saying it's poorly written don't know what they're talking about. I would argue here that the writing does a fantastic job of integrating so many tangential story lines into a single narrative. The real problem lies with the sheer amount of content that the writers were forced to contend with. And this was a problem many of us foresaw long before the movie came out – the producers were attempting to introduce and pack too many major elements into one movie. It was simply TOO MUCH – an altogether impatient and heavy-handed approach, reeking of desperation to compete with a certain other company.

Despite the film's title, the actual physical confrontation between Batman and Superman is brief but superbly done. It also done in a way that is plausible, and most people should have no problem suspending their disbelief for.

As to the obligatory act 3 showdown... Well, it seems that they tried to make it bigger and badder than in Man of Steel, but instead demonstrated why less is often more. In my opinion, the battle sequences in Man of Steel were some of the most beautiful I'd ever seen in a movie - an epic back-and-forth conflict moving from location to location against a backdrop of city lights and stunning skyscapes. Unfortunately, in Batman v Superman they forego this atmosphere for a cacophony of stupendous explosions, dirt and dust. It seemed like they sacrificed atmospherics for grandiosity, and for me it just didn't have the same emotional impact. (Although, to be honest, it was still leagues over anything I've seen from other cinematic universes.)

Finally, I cannot leave this review without mentioning Gal Gadot. This is the bit where I'm gonna have to swallow some pride because I have been one of the biggest critics of her casting until now. Yet for the few scenes she was in this movie, she was faultless. She looked the part, acted the part, and demonstrated precisely why Wonder Woman is the most kick-ass female superhero there is. I have now officially jumped on the bandwagon for her solo movie.

Overall, I'd give Batman v Superman a 7.5 out of 10, rounded up to 8 because its critical rating seems so unfairly harsh. And as to its current rating 44 on Metacritic – please, just gtfo!

title: Terrific visuals, other great stuff, but the movie is very very flawed
review:
Following the massive destruction in Metropolis during the battle between Superman and General Zod's forces, Bruce Wayne, distraught at the deaths of his employees in his office block, decides that Superman is too dangerous to exist in our world and, in his alternate identity as vigilante Batman, determines to do something about it. Squillionaire businessman / scientist / weirdo Lex Luthor comes to a similar conclusion. Probably. There is a senator who is similarly concerned. Various battles ensue.

Man Of Steel, the predecessor to this movie, polarised opinions, and its sequel looks set to do the same thing. Let me make one thing clear before going on to other matters – Zack Snyder is without equal in bringing truly eye-dazzling visuals to the big screen (albeit the 3D version of this is pointless because the 3D is unnoticeable).

I come to this with a slight change in my mindset. I loved much of Man Of Steel, but I took profound issue with its portrayal of Superman and (primarily) Pa Kent. Pa Kent (who turns up for an utterly unnecessary cameo here) was simply fundamentally misconceived – instead of giving Clark the selfless values which are Superman's watchword, he taught him to put himself before others, leaving a long way for the character to travel if he was ever going to find the inner nobility which is (or should be) his main characteristic. And Superman was written into a situation where he had no alternative but to kill, a deliberate statement by the filmmakers about the character. And guess what? I bet you thought Batman hates guns and doesn't kill, didn't you? Well, think again.

I grew up with the Silver Age iterations of these characters, albeit the movement of Batman from camp to dark was a good one. And Ben Affleck's Bruce Wayne/Batman is fine work, notwithstanding his casual attitude towards the deaths of criminal henchmen and (possibly) innocent passers-by. But in oder not to despise this film and its predecessor, one has to not be imprisoned by that pre-existing view and, instead, look at these as alternate interpretations of the characters – easy in Batman's case, since he has been interpreted many ways of the years, not so easy with Superman where grim, depressing and joyless are all terms which are the antithesis of the fairly consistent interpretation of the character over its 75-year history. My son says it's a Superman for the 21st century, and maybe he is right. It's not MY Superman, that's for sure. And the single scene which tells me that is when Superman stands in the middle of a massive explosion and does nothing to minimise the explosion or save people. Instead, he just stands there rather sadly. Nope, that's not Superman.

Cavill does his best with a character who isn't written as the hero he should be. Affleck is terrific. Gal Gadot's short appearance as Wonder Women is galvanising and makes you wish her film had arrived already. Lex Luthor – well, I like Jesse Eisenberg enormously and think his talent and versatility has motored through his rather clichéd nerdy appearance very effectively, but this interpretation of Luthor isn't one which is obvious. For me, it didn't really work. Amy Adams still doesn't have any real chemistry with Henry Cavill – there is more chemistry between them when they're on chat shows. Jeremy Irons' Alfred is excellent. The action, effects, props, sets are all first rate – as noted, visuals aren't Snyder's problem.

The film itself is a problem. If you're not careful, you'll finish it with a bucketful of unanswered questions, not just those which will fall to be answered in future films, but questions about motivations, opportunities, why no-one spotted this or did nothing about that – there is a LOT of carelessness in the script, which seems engineered to always set up a cool visual rather than progress things logically. The film is over two and a half hours long, and contains little bits of plot which never really go anywhere, never get developed, and which could have been dropped with minimal re-writing, making the film tighter and with better narrative flow. In particular the lead-up to the Batman / Superman fight feels terribly artificially engineered, although the fight itself is splendid.

I enjoyed this – it's the nearest I'm going to get to a World's Finest movie in my lifetime – but to say it's flawed is an understatement. Let Snyder capture his visuals by all means, but get someone who knows what they're doing on the screen writing, please.

title: Great buildup to an epic fight
review: Wow, I was amazed of how the writers built the story for Batman and Superman. I am not a comic reader but there was enough lore for the heroes that kept me interested. In the first few minutes it was just storytelling but that is what makes a movie good. Then the last hour or so there was nothing but action. Great buildup to the fight & loved Ben Affleck as Batman. In my opinion he is a far better choice than Christian Bale. This Batman does not have the corny voice, his voice sounds more natural. Superman was a force of nature that was difficult to stop. Great movie, acting & story just go watch it don't listen to the other ratings!!!

title: Batman v Superman (Batman and Superman)
review:
Fearing that the actions of Superman are left unchecked, Batman takes on the Man of Steel, while the world wrestles with what kind of a hero it really needs.

Well, this film kind of disappointed me.. I mean, the new creation of batman is very astonishing and wonder woman's first theatrical appearance is very breath-taking. But what I am absolutely concerned about is the whole plot?

The film's title says in clear words "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" yet in only of the 2 hrs, we see the rivalry between the two iconic superheroes but for around 10-15 mins, we actually see them finally fight and that's towards the end. Yet, they decide to reconcile and team up when Clark says "Martha!", comprehending that Superman isn't the real threat because of him saying Martha? I can completely understand that both of their mothers are called Martha but why would that make batman come to his senses that Superman isn't the real threat to humanity?

The film is not bad but needs a lot of improvements over its characters (apart from Wonder Woman and Batman) and their true meaning of contributing to the film. Lex is not even scary neither showing his antagonistic behaviour properly. The bombing of the capitol which killed Senator Finch was really depressing but that doesn't show how menacing he is, it shows how stupid and corrupt he is to do that.

What I truly loved is the intro of Wonder Woman (in her costume), that gave me the chills completely. I think Gal Gadot is the perfect person to play her, she's also accurate of the character's background and life.

Overall, I would give the film 7 / 10, mainly because of its confusing plot but great visual effects and brilliant portrayal of Wonder Woman and Batman.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice (Should be called Batman and Superman: United for Justice), the film that creates perfect visual techniques but a weird plot that misleads the audiences' attention.

title: Speed of light through an asteroid belt
review:
I had high hopes going into this film, until 5 minutes in Ben Affleck started to scream Dad!? Dan!? Dad!?....I just couldn't make out, Im sure it was Dan cause his dad was shot not once but twice throughout the film, so it must of been Dan, right? I mean they could of used a different name. This just to name a few huh! moments throughout the film.

The film felt rushed, disorientated, and in my opinion the script was totally dumb to say the least, this should of been made into an animation instead.

With regards to the actors, Im sure the wax model of superman at Madame Tussaud's wax museum could of given a better performance, Ben was OK as Bruce Wayne, CGI Batman was OK at times, Jesse Eisenberg made every scene Superawkward and Amy Adams.... what did she do again?

Finally when it came down to what everyone was waiting to see, Batman vs Superman, I was not impressed, it was a repeat of Mayweather vs Pacquiao, just a sigh of boredom, and I wont even bother describing the Doomsday battle that just ended the film right there, talk about CGI overkill, I should of brought my controller with. the only battle I can say I enjoyed was Batman vs thugs near the end, that scene alone garnered my 3 stars for this film.

The only room for improvement will be to replace Zack and have an adult draft the next script....then maybe just maybe I will return to the cinema.

title: Dawn of darkness and hollowness
review:
First of all this movie should have went for the R rating because of how dark it is. I believe that the parents who go with their kids to this movie are irresponsible. Not only are the colours, skies, sets, clothes, time of day always very "dark", but the whole atmosphere and general feeling the movie also created by the actors just makes you feel downright uncomfortable and uneasy.

Second, I do not agree at all that the storytelling or editing or the multiple sub-plots are bad. What is bad is the content of those scenes, that is a big difference. Content is a general problem of this movie in the sense that it is totally lacking in it. If you scale down the whole plot of this "set of moving pictures" you are left with an advertising trailer for the next money-grabbing moving pictures, "a la Avengers style".

I do not agree that it is better than "Man of Steel". Even though that wasn't a great movie, it "made more sense" than Batman vs Superman. People who like this movie have just been fooled and schemed by the greedy con-artists at Hollywood. Why not make a realistic approach to the concept of Superman or Batman? Why not explore the real-life consequences of such ideas in a cinematic way? Nope, instead let's just make an extremely commercial brain-washing empty shell of a movie.

Regarding the acting, it is pointless to try and judge performances, because it just all seems unrealistic, unnatural and forced. It was as if I was seeing a theatrical performance done and directed by kids or teenagers.

Lois Lane's and Wonder Woman's story lines are completely irrelevant and unnecessary. However, Ben Afleck is a better choice for Bruce Wayne, giving the character that charm and personality it completely lacked with Christian Bale's version. Still, he was not believable as the ass-kicking Batman, he does not really seem like a tough guy. Jeremy Irons was completely wasted as he is a fantastic actor and unfortunately was not given enough screen time for development. Lex Luthor was an unbelievable joke, completely miscast. It was like the casting people or director said "hey you know how today many successful businessmen are like young and nerdy, let's go that way!" Cavill, once again a glorious plank with muscles, no charm, no personality, but way sadder and sometimes seeming evil or evil-looking.

I know optimism, lighter tones and even actually decent content in movies are outdated today and seem cheesy, but I miss the times when I left a movie theater without having such a bad feeling and a bad taste. Honestly, do you people actually like darkness and sadness, are we all emos and goth now? Why aren't we as the main sponsors of this industry not doing anything about the direction of movies today?

title: And the winner is ... Marvel.
review:
MY REVIEW OF Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice! ðŸŽ¬

From the beginning we all knew DC was playing catch up with Marvel and that this film HAD to be a success to rival Marvel. Marvel have had 8 years to create there universe. DC have had 2 hours and 30 mins and it shows. It seemed as if Zack Snyder filmed his scenes got to his mixing booth and just pressed "SHUFFLE." Zack Snyder crammed in 4 movies in 1. You had the solo Batman movie, the Superman sequel, Batman v Superman and the Prequel to "The Justice League."

Let's start with Superman. I actually enjoyed Henry Cavill's Superman in this film. He portrayed actual emotion which lacked in Man of Steel. I enjoyed the premise of this story and was invested throughout. Lois Lane being the damsel in distress was quite annoying again she just seems a nuisance really now.

Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal as Lex Luthor will split the viewers down the middle. Some will hate him, some will like him. If you liked what you saw in the trailer then you should like him however if you didn't like what you saw then unfortunately not much will change. I actually started off liking him. I could see what Jesse was trying to portray however as the film progressed he started to grate on me. This wasn't the Lex Luthor I wanted in the DC Universe however it's the one we got and you just learn to live with it.

Ben Affleck as Batman was BRILLIANT! I will also hold my hands up and say I was quite sceptical when they cast Ben Affleck however he was brilliant. Now some of you may not enjoy the character due to reasons you will find out if you watch the film however I enjoyed it and felt it suited the story.

Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman really intrigued me she should of been used so much more however what I saw in the 3rd act gets me very excited for next years solo Wonder Woman film.

The story started off really promising, we see Bruce Wayne's point of view and involvement in the fight between Zod and Superman in Man of Steel. I felt it was fast paced and gripped you straight away however the next 2 hours were slow and although I understand that it needed to be done due to the universe DC are trying to create, this could of been done in such a better way.

The third act however is brilliant but felt underwhelming due to the other 2 acts. Now don't get me wrong I did enjoy this film however there are moments that let this film down. If you are a casual movie goer you may get confused with some of what's going on. This film was created for the comic book fans and I respected that. This is why I feel the critics have been harsh because they don't understand some of what was going on.

Overall Batman v Superman is an enjoyable film to watch and I recommend you seeing it, however you feel that this was a missed opportunity from DC and Marvel still remains on top.

title: Batman v Superman was EPIC!!!
review: It seems like people aren't really understanding the plot. Negative reviews focus mostly on the superficial reasoning of the fight. Blah blah. #Superman is the ultimate good guy. He disagrees with how the #Batman resolve crimes. Pretty much how #Daredevil feels about #ThePunisher. (Just finished S2 of #Daredevil and I loved it). #Batman is a little xenophobic towards #Superman. He fears the unknown. And believes that #Superman is a powerful alien that will destroy the earth. !!!Spoiler Alert!!! He stops fighting Superman when he realizes that Superman is also human because of his ties to humanity. His mother 'Martha' and Lois. He loves. And that makes him weak. Makes him human. The pace in the beginning was slow. And the editing inconsistent. I have a feeling a lot of the beginning scenes got cut or trimmed for time. Can't wait so see an uncut version. The movie is shot the same way as #ManOfSteel. Where each scene lines up like a storyboard. Throughout you can see beautiful lined up shots slowed down, that gives the illusion of flipping through a comic book. Almost like a moving portrait. It is just beautiful. #BenAffleck was the perfect #Batman. His performance was outstanding. #HenryCavill is hot. And he can act. Only negative thing I can say is Mr #ZachSnyder please stop with the shaky cam. Especially in the beginning. And especially with 3D. Can't say the 3D was justified. Movie would have been just as great in 2D. Maybe save some money and stick to 2D in the future.

title: A well made, well told story about two imperfect heroes
review:
To tell a tale about a hero is tough. To tell a tale about two heroes and their egos, that's tougher.

I always go into any comic book adaptation movie with no expectations.

Whats great about this movie?

Soundtrack (I particularly love the Wonderwoman theme)

Action (when Batman was kicking asses to save a lady)

Graphics (Superman looks super, the costumes looked amazing) - Details (Cmon, Jokes on you Batman!, that's some hidden Easter bunny stuff)

I love how they use "dreams" to tell how Batman became Batman.

Batman suit makes sense! That's always tough to do when you blend in Super powers. Batman suit needed to be thick and yet has enough space for impact absorption. Batman v Superman! go watch!

title: Not great, but good, ignore the "critics" and go see it.
review: BvS did not disappoint. I guess everyone who panned it was upset that it wasn't 2.75 hours of two guys bashing it out, and are whining that they had to wait for the big duel. I could have done without some of the dream scenes, they tended to break the pace of the movie and I'm not a fan of this twitchy, spazzy "Lex" Luthor. Luthors motivation for hating Superman seems vague and muddled, but everything else felt pretty solid. The film is a mash up of Millers "Dark Knight" series and the "Doomsday" story arc from the Superman series. Enjoyed Jeremy Irons turn as Alfred, efficient but sarcastic (sardonic?)and I think Gal Gadot did just fine filling the Amazons bracelets. Just one complaint- could they juuuust put a laugh in once in awhile? Don't go all Marvel, but.... Also, were ALL the men required to to a scene with a 3 day stubble? Seems OK for kids 8 and up, but you know your kids better than I do. One curse word, but, IT WAS COMPLETELY CORRECT FOR THE CONTEXT AND I HAVE NO TROUBLE WITH IT. (I am also glad they took my suggestion (at least in my mind) and had Batman use and electronic voice changer, instead of having Affleck growl all his lines)

title: Good but not Super
review: This movie starts with seeing Bruces parents murdered again, which lengthens an already cramped movie. I feel as though it is here mainly to please comic book fans with some camera shots identical to the comics. I personally feel this isn't needed and the film should start with Bruce Wayne in Metropolis during the Superman vs Zod fight that took place in Man of Steel. This would have made the film ten minutes shorter and jumped straight into some of the best action in the film. We are then reintroduced to Superman who i would have thought become against killing after the death of Zod, nope. He straight up kills a guy who has Lois hostage. Now i quite enjoyed that he killed. I mean how can someone be so powerful and not kill. It fits in nicely with the darkness of the DC universe and adds a realistic touch. Over all this film started strongly with motives for both characters, Batman not trusting Superman for killing thousands in metropolis and feels superman should be held responsible and Superman not enjoying the fact Batman feels that he is above the law. Both are good motives for a Batman vs Superman movie. There is also the political section in this film with the population divided between supporting superman and going against him. This gave Superman problems and caused him confusion. "why am i helping people if they don't like me?" is what he is thinking. Great this is humanising the character. However after this the movie starts to lose track of whats going on. Lex is introduced and i think completely wrong casting choice. They should have gone for a more aged, darker actor who can be evil almost naturally. Bryan Cranston would be my personal opinion and was linked to the role originally. Jesse Eisenberg who i spent more time laughing at, it reminded me of the Riddler from one of the older batman films. Lex did have a good motive "we need a weapon in case Superman turns evil" fair enough, superman can destroy humanity so it makes sense to have a weapon in preparation. This is only mentioned once and then his motives just go out of the window. This is how simple the plot should have been. Instead We have Wonder Woman who feels forced, although she is played well, is she really necessary for this film, and the its the same for doomsday. Were these characters needed for the plot. Instead we get some over the top Lex Luthor plan that could have easily failed by Batman not finding out about kryptonite, and then Lex Luthor black mails superman to fight batman, for fun? The final fights in this film is brilliantly choreographed and shot. It shows of Batman's tactical and superior hand to hand combat over a weakened superman. Again this was realistic to what it would be like. The one thing that annoyed me was how they became buddies. Their moms have the same name and all of sudden their best friends. NO! Let them both realises Lex is the biggest threat and then they team up to take him down. Instead of Doomsday give Lex his armoured kryptonite suit (maybe made from left over krypton armor) and take them both on. To me this would have been a simpler less cramped plot with better pacing. This was not a bad movie, it was good and the acting was amazing. Batman had Badass one liners, unfortunately given away in the trailers but still cool. It would have been nice for superman to have some cool one liners. Lois was given more of a plot than she needed and the dream sequences weren't needed and just extended the film. The cameos of other heroes could have been kept for an end of credits scene. But as movie this wasn't bad, but as BATMAN VS SUPERMAN it wasn't what it could have been.

title: A movie for fans, not for critics
review:
My most anticipated movie of 2016 left me feeling disappointed. Some of the content was amazing and just how I expected it to be, the rest confirmed my initial fears.

Positives: Ben Afflecks take on Batman is the best we've ever gotten. I was invested in every second he was on screen. Wonder Woman is a bad ass. She fits in every scene she's in and will be great as the first major female superhero. Jesse Eisenbergs portrayal of Lex Luthor was much better than the trailers suggested. He turned into a really menacing villain once the movie got going. The fight scene between Batman and Superman will go down as one of the best fights in movie history. Seeing the two hero's finally go at it was mesmerizing. The dark tone of the movie is a great contrast to other superhero movies

Negatives: The film has so much going on at once. Some of it is very engaging, some is downright pointless. The major problem here is the film constantly cuts back and forth between plots, its very hard to get invested in the good parts. Lois Lane has no place in this movie, the sub-plot surrounding her just sucks the life out of this movie. The setup for the Justice League is very lazy ( I can't elaborate without spoiling anything). The end of this film has a "Spiderman 3" feel to it when it comes to shoehorning characters in at the last possible second. The trailers showed EVERYTHING. If you haven't seen the movie yet than stay away from the trailers.

If you are going to see this movie just to have a good time I think you will enjoy it. If you are going looking for flaws you will feel let down. This is definitely a movie for easygoing fans, not critics. Batman v Superman has moments of greatness but is so overly concerned with setting up the DC cinematic universe that it forgets to be a great standalone movie. 7/10

title: Not Terrific. Not Terrible.
review:
This movie is full of potential, but Snyder just didn't make it work. The biggest worry going into the film for me turned out to be it's biggest flaw too, it just had too much going on. DC are playing catchup with Marvel whether people like it or not, and that's clearly evident here. This movie was suffocated with so many different story lines that at times it became difficult to follow, I will say that the second half of the film was much superior as the narrative was narrowed down from various different story lines to just one. It felt like there was three films here, a Man of Steel sequel, a standalone Batman film, and of course a Batman v Superman film. I feel like DC should've waited at least another year before making this, that way they would've had time to develop certain characters further, mainly Batman and Superman, in their own respective films before putting them on screen together.

Despite this seemingly unorganised mess though I'm still hyped to see what DC has to offer. Seeing Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman team up on screen was really cool, so I can't wait to see how they fair in a film dedicated to them teaming up in the Justice League, I still feel like a 2017 release is too soon, but hyped nonetheless.

Speaking of Wonder Woman, I went in to the movie knowing nothing about her character and I came out intrigued, I want to get to know her, I want to see her origin story unfold on screen before me. I'm highly anticipating her 2017 movie more then any other comic movie at this point. Gal Dadot looks the part, she was good in the role so credit to her. Credit also to Ben Affleck, who many were worried about when initially cast as Batman. He did fantastic here and deserves all the praise he's getting.

I just hope now that DC can learn where they went wrong and build off it, they've got the potential to make a truly fascinating universe, and I look forward to seeing how they play it.

title: A breath of fresh air ...
review: First of all, I don't know what the hell is wrong with the so called professional critics. They praise Deadpool (a movie I thoroughly enjoyed)but dislike BvS because "it is not funny", it's too violent and dark. The movie easily outclasses MoS, both in action, special effects and overall story, and I say this from the point of view of someone who really enjoys superhero movies. I think I had enough of the Marvel formula, with very little violence despite the almighty heroes, no blood (we know they are meant for a younger audience), no real threat to the heroes (Ultron and pretty much every other villain), unidimensional characters and last but not least, the lack of seriousness (except for The Winter Soldier, best MCU film in my opinion), always filled with childish and stupid humor, and I seriously hope they will change the tone of the films when Infinity War arrives (and Thor Ragnarok, it's the damn Nordic apocalypse, come on). So overall the dark tone of the film is fitting, the battles are amazing, visual effects top notch, and some clever ideas to give us a glimpse for what is to come.

title: I am giving the score of 9 points based on these 10 reasons (9 in favor).
review:
1. Characters: The criteria to judge, how good the actors take on the role basically comes from comic world. They all did it really well.

2. Set Design: I didn't had any issues with set design of MOS, the movies does a great job in setting up the scenes.

3. VFX: Well it is a movie by Zack Snyder, the VFX are amazing. The criteria to judge will be obviously how well they are in sync with the story, momentum and thrill it provides. So it definitely delivers the result.

4. Sound Track: Junkie and Hans Zimmer, They have been world class before and doesn't disappoint in this one either.

5. Story: Story is decent, it will keep you engaging and you will be interested in watching this movie again for few times because a lot of things happen which will only become noticeable if you see it again. I loved the take on the story where Batman is actually inspired from "The Dark Knight Returns", the movie keeps the basic idea of that Animated Movie but still comes with a great story.

6. Wardrobe & Costumes: Costume Designer did an amazing work with everything, all the characters fitness into the dark world.

7. Action: Very good action sequence, both Batman and Superman have different style and different level strength and you will feel the different in their strength from music, vfx and cinematography. The movie have plenty of action.

8. Momentum: The pace of the movie is fast enough to keep you engaged for the whole time. Everything is synced really good. But this is the part where I agree with the negative critics, there are some areas which could have been improved by reducing the pace. I am not going to give away any spoilers but you will notice that something is a bit off when it comes to momentum of the movie.

9. Plot Holes: I personally think the plot holes could have been avoided by stretching the movie for more 15-20 mins because they seem to be due to the reason that the movie runtime was already decided.

10. Villain: Really good villain.

title: Good movie, worth watching.
review:
Just when the movie came out, it got a high score on IMDb. It began with a 9,5 and quickly sunk to 7,5 which is more suitable to this movie. Maybe people who worked on this movie rated it a 10 and people who hate the director or the cast members slowly rated it 1. So the discussion started whether IMDb rating is credible or not. Well it is, after a few weeks. Like people who worked on this movie, everyone is free to vote as they please. Why do people vote it as 1? If you just don't like superhero movies, or the director, or the cast, there is Always a choice not to watch the movie at all.

So some negative points I have about the movie: * Movie was way too long. Three hours! What were they thinking? Give the audience something worth for their money? Well, the movie was not that great. * There were some flaws. Maybe we should forget that part. It's a fictional movie to start with. * Nolan's / Bale's Batman got killed. And that's a waste. * Music was weird at time to time. Not suitable. * The movie did not have a real story. I got the feeling they just made this movie, to make a movie. * Weird ending. * Why that monster?

Some positive points: * Despite of what people say; good cast. * Awesome action sequences. * Exciting.

Isn't it because these few positive points why we watch this kind of movies? Well, at least I do.

title: Good movie much better than expected
review: To be honest, I was not expecting much from this movie. I am a big fan of DC comics and I did not agree at the time with the actor choices they made, however I must say Affleck did a good job and he turned out to be a very decent Batman. On the other hand Gadot was a bad choice and she was terrible, luckily for the movie she is not on the screen for more than 15 minutes. The worse thing about the movie is Lex Luthor, I do not know who thought Lex would be a maniac psychopath. I think someone wanted to recreate Heath Ledger Joker kind of roll and did not even bother to read a single comic of Superman. Good movie if you are a fan of DC if you are not it might be a bit confusing some times.

title: Almost perfection, brilliant.
review:
I have to say, that this movie, is not an ordinary movie, it has too many layers, deep questions, and reflections. Critics were wrong, giving poor scores to this movie, i can explain that, thinking in a deep ignorance about DC superhero Universe, or too simply minds.

Great action sequences, great performances, outstanding music, if you know what is the meaning of an adult oriented comic adaptation, this is your movie, but you need to know the basis of this superheroes. ( At least..you have to watch the man of steel..at least).

First of all, batman introduction to the story, was simply, flawless, The superman's inner reflections regarding his role in the world, the implications, remarkable.

The story develops in a multilayer story, where every character is very important, there is a perfect balance. Great work Mr. Snyder.

title: The Perfect Dawn....
review: The whole movie was shot in dark atmosphere which made it even better. With no unnecessary comedy scenes the movie focused on its plot and build up the momentum for justice league.The performances were up to the mark.However wonder woman was given very limited scenes.She was not introduced well. Hope Wonder Woman (2017) does it. I wished for some references to joker or robin though in the movie. Nightmares scenes of Bruce with batman using the machine gun was a treat to watch. And the best thing about the movie was bat of Gotham overpowering son of Krypton.The movie left some questions unanswered though....waiting for the DVD release.....

title: Best superhero film to date.
review:
*SPOILER ALERT*

People who gave this movie bad critics are so stupid. This is an INTRO movie. That's basically why you're following so many things in the movie. This is Zack Snyder's way of introducing how the new DC Universe is going to be throughout the movies. You guys asked for a glimpse of new characters etc. and he came through. In man of steel people hated it because there was too much destruction. That is the most bullshit complaint ever because that was Zack's plan. He made it with a lot of destruction so that Batman has a reason to hate him, because he sees how strong he is. He has the same plan for BvS. The story structure is a bit odd but once the next movies come out you will understand and love it. People who gave bad critics really need to pay attention to what Zack is actually planning for the DC Universe. It's amazing. The action was out of this world. The fights were amazing. The cast is amazing. Jesse played Lex sooo good. Batfleck rules and Gal Gadot is a great Wonder Woman. I have no idea why this movie got so much bad critics.

title: Worth it in the end
review:
*Contains Spoilers*

I have been looking forward to this film for many months now, but went into the cinema with low expectations given the mixed reactions and reviews.

The first 90 minutes wasn't great, and to be honest I wish I had a book to keep me company. Fortunately however, the last hour or so more than made up for this.

One of my main concerns going into the film was Ben Affleck. I like Affleck but couldn't see him as Batman. However I thought he played the part really well, especially given he didn't have the quality of scripts that Christian Bale had in the Christopher Nolan trilogy. I quite liked Lex Luthor and the rest of the cast done a good job, but to be honest I didn't expect nor did I watch the film for Oscar winning performances.

Little happened in the first 90 minutes that couldn't have been summarised in half an hour of film. It wasn't the premise of the set up but it just dragged on for what felt like the entire afternoon.

The world wasn't sure it wanted an all powerful hero like Superman. Batman irrationally blames Superman for the events of Man of Steel, managing to overlook that Zod would have otherwise destroy mankind without his intervention. There were a few other small side stories, but nothing that could justify the length of time the film took is setting the scene for the upcoming confrontation between Batman and Superman and the introduction of Wonder Woman.

I can only summarise the Batman v Superman fight as stupid. I don't have issue with how Batman can actually fight Superman or the fight scene itself, and this was illustrated quite well in the film, but the whole premise of the fight.

Batman and Superman knew each other were Bruce Wayne and Clark Kent respectively (maybe I missed how, but they greeted each other by these names), so why on Earth wouldn't two seemingly intelligent people have a rational conversation to resolve their differences, which aren't really all that different. But no, they decide the best way to tackle this is to try and kill each other on their first or second encounter, leaving a trail of destruction in the process.

With Batman and Superman finally realising that they have bigger problems than disagreeing with each others methods of doing the pretty much the same thing, the film started to get going.

The fight with Doomsday was amazing. The portrayal of both Batman and Superman was well executed and I enjoyed the introduction of Wonder Woman. While slightly clichÃ©, I also enjoyed the ending of the film.

There isn't really need for me to go into detail, but if you can put up with the slow and at times unnecessary pacing of the film, you will be deeply rewarded with what most of us went to the cinema to see.

title: Excellent!! but...
review: In my opinion the movie is awesome, the cameos (Flash, Aquaman, Cyborg) were incredible, but the first hour is a little bit slow, superman isn't good enough for the movie (I think that he is the weak part of the movie), I though:"Really?, a Superman with no idea of his place on the world again?,that stuff should have been left in MOS". The rest of the movie is pure gold, the battles (batman vs superman and batman,superman,WW vs doomsday) were great and Lex Luthor is such an asshole (good point).For me, it's the best superhero movie since CATWS. Also the Ost is awesome, that WW theme is such a masterpiece, all the Soundtrack of the movie is in the right place in the right moment. I know this is just the beginning of a brand new universe, I can't wait to see WW movie next year.

title: Great Movie, Don't Be Dissuaded
review:
I gave this movie a 7 out of 10 because I expected more action. Also think the fight with Doomsday was really downplayed because the movie was so long. I think it could have been tens times better. Unfortunately they went a different route.

I liked the movie because it told a compelling story. I sat there and got most of the answers I was looking for, and really wasn't left in the dark. The movie does have some plots that are really sketchy. There is a scene where they accuse Superman of killing people who were obviously shot to death? Really? People in that world must be really stupid to believe Superman uses guns, and shoots people. :/

On another note, they did a great job with Ben Affleck as Batman. I think by far, he is the best Batman I've seen. He is smart, caring, and tough as nails. The new Alfred was a refreshing touch, and I'm happy with the direction they took.

They are really setting the tone for the Justice League in this movie and obviously Darkseid is going to be the next big bad. I hope there is more action in the Justice League, Dawn of Justice just felt lacking in that department.

All in all, a good movie. I hope they keep up the good work. Looking forward to it.

title: A good movie, but not without flaws
review:
I've been a comic fan all my life. I used to watch the old Adam West Batman in reruns with my dad. The Christopher Reeve Superman was also a staple of my childhood. To finally see the two Superheroes of my youth on the big screen guaranteed my ass would be in the seats opening day.

For comic fans, especially DC fans, this is a must see. For the average film-goer, people who are only familiar with what has been on screen before, it'll be hard to swallow. It wasn't made for the average viewer, so I can understand the critical reaction. As a Batman Fanatic, I enjoyed seeing a more comic faithful Caped Crusader, but it suffered from poor editing. The individual scenes were great, but the transitions sucked. Scenes feel like moving comic panels, leaving a feeling that the writers and director just wanted to get to THE EVENT. For a comic, that's fine, but it's a bit jarring on screen.

The cast is superb. Ben Affleck IS Batman. Jesse Eisenberg feels right to play Alexander Luthor II. But the real treat is Gal Gadot as Princess Diana of Themyscira. Her early scenes are mysterious, and when she finally makes her appearance in full costume, it is worth the wait. She is believable as a 5,000 year old warrior. She was definitely the highlight. My wife was so giddy when she appeared in her uniform she shook the entire row.

The Flash cameo and the "Knightmare" were interesting teases for the Justice League film. The second appearance of Barry Allen, as well as the appearances for Aquaman feel forced and out of place. The icing on the cake, however, is that Snyder and Company had the chutzpah not to waste Doomsday.

title: Intense and Bombastic Superhero Blockbuster
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. It's the moment many comic book fans have been waiting for- myself included -and while it's far from perfection, it was a good, intense and bombastic ride that I won't forget, with a battle between two iconic superheroes that was actually quite outstanding in itself.

I thought Ben Affleck as Batman/Bruce Wayne was superb. He brought a different kind of gravitas to the role, where in this universe he's more broken, hardened and brutal in his skills, mind-set and personality. He also shows that tragic side we saw with Christian Bale's Batman, but I don't think one did it better than the other (and I do personally think Bale is still #1 for being Batman, but Affleck can be better with more time in the role). Cavill's Superman was good, but I felt he was more a supporting role before the big battle of the movie, which I didn't mind, but felt a little underwhelming, considering this is technically supposed to be the "Man of Steel" pseudo-sequel. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor, honestly, I thought was really cartoonish and, while not a complete disservice to the character, wasn't good enough; Kevin Spacey's was better in Superman Returns. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman, on the other hand, was pure brilliance in her short screen time, and I'm dying to see her solo film. Zack Snyder's direction, I personally felt was better here than Man of Steel, but it felt incomplete, which makes sense since there is a Director's Cut coming later this year. The script, too, co-written by Chris Terrio, was solid, but showcased too much content. For instance, Doomsday. The inclusion of this monstrosity was completely unnecessary, as he was wasted in the final act of the movie, being "cannon fodder" for the fight, prolonging the epic conflict. Instead, what should have happened is they should have ended the film with his creation, showing that there will be an even more diabolical and insidious threat on the horizon (even though there still is one, subtly hinted at).

Batman v Superman was a solid action film with some great visuals, stunning musical score to accompany the disastrous destruction and sweeping fight that's gorgeously filmed, and boasts a few great performances amidst a few other decent to mediocre performances. I also have to say, to end my review, critics are being quite foolish and ignorant by comparing this to Marvel's MCU, being too grim and dark instead of "fun" and a little more heart. They aren't movies, but have critics forgotten Daredevil and Jessica Jones? Marvel can do grim, dark and violent, but that's what separated DC from Marvel, the penchant to stick with the truly awful and horrifying forces in the dark. I just hope they can continue an uphill climb, because this is a marathon, not a sprint.

title: Batman vs Superman Review - Not bad but not great.
review:
After just getting out from watching the new Batman vs Superman movie yesterday, here are my initial thoughts. The movie is not bad. Does that mean the movie is good? I'm not entirely sure. Probably. I would say I'd recommend people to watch it, more than I would not. I would also say I'd like to watch it again (maybe not in 3D) in case anything was missed, but I'll wait for the video release. It is interesting taken as a whole.

The Bad -

1. The pacing for the first 2/3 to 3/4 of the movie, going from scene to scene, character to character, motivation to motivation, with lack of any real action was almost a killer for me. It was just boring, and while I appreciate the topics being brought up, the way they were and how slowly things moved was draining. You never knew if it was a flashback scene, a dream sequence, anything. Obviously, you can figure it out, but the movie really was trying hard to be a Batman movie, no a Superman movie, no a Batman vs Superman movie, no a Batman and Superman vs Lex Luthor movie.

2. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. He didn't portray Lex Luthor. He portrayed some bizarre Riddler / Joker amalgam on Prozac that was indeed intelligent (he reminded me of Jim Carrey from Batman Forerver at times) and did put plans together, but the plans were a bit silly and not thought through. He wanted to kill Superman. But why? There was no motivation provided for that and why he acted so nutty other than he's nutty. Also, if his plan was to kill Superman, he could have found a much easier way to do so then planning to get Batman to fight Superman. Heck, lure Superman in by capturing Lois. Hit him with the kryptonite, and bam, nail him. Why did he need Batman? Well, because the movie is called Batman vs Superman. Plus, he created Doomsday with no plan on how to take him down after he killed Superman. In fact, Doomsday was going to kill him right away. Again, either that's just stupidity or he's crazy. Either way, it's not Lex Luthor. He is supposed to be the smartest guy in the DC Universe. He reminds me of a combination of the Kingpin and Doctor Doom. Cool, Calculating and not prone to error. Jesse Eisenberg was not Lex Luthor.

3. Henry Cavill as Superman. To no fault of the actor, but too often it seemed the only thing they had him do with look stoic and grim and hover. No humor, expressions. Nothing. He is a good actor. I know he is. Use him. I did like the final scene with him and Doomsday and his willingness to sacrifice himself.

4. The Batman vs Superman fight. The fight was cool. Short but cool, but totally not needed other than to fulfill the title. As soon as Lex told Superman he had Martha Kent and he wanted Superman to kill Batman to save her life, all Superman had to do was tell Batman right away he needed his help. Instead he tried one time in a half- hearted way, and then they both wasted so much time hitting each other. It was just a waste of time and energy. I thought a much better way to have Batman and Superman really fight would be for Lex to use either mind control or Red Kryptonite on Superman so Batman would be forced to tackle him. That I could believe. The motivations of Batman to fight here seemed petty, and Superman just as much.

The Good

1. Ben Affleck as Batman. I really liked him in this movie. I liked the Batsuit, him as Bruce Wayne and I thought his fighting style was good. Yes, he used guns, but it wasn't in some horrific fashion like the Punisher. Not exactly what I'd want but good. They just needed more of it. In fact, I'd have rather the three heroes not fought at all and just teamed up. More awesome Trinity action. I'd really like to see what he (Ben Affleck) could do if he wrote and directed his own standalone film.

2. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. I thought she did a fantastic job in the limited amount of time she had. Really, there was not a huge reason for her to be there other than to interact with the other two, and help fight, but her passion for the part was apparent, and makes me happy to see the standalone movie for her coming out.

3. Doomsday and the last 1/3 to 1/4 of the movie. Apart from the reasons why he was created, which for me didn't make a lot of sense since Lex couldn't control the thing, I liked the character and the fighting at the end. The way they had things leading to other things was cool.

4. The music. It was loud, but like Man Of Steel, I really thought it did well from scene to scene.

5. The Batman vs Superman fight . The fight was not needed as I stated but to review the actual fight, it was a lot of fun.

6. The showings of The Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg. While I wish they'd do standalone movies for all the characters first and then a Justice League movie for character development, it was cool to see them being shown.

The indifferent

1. Zach Synder's direction. I loved 300 and Watchmen. I am not a huge Man Of Steel fan, but the consistent thing is his movies feel the same, love it or hate it.

Overall Rating â€“ 6 out of 10

title: Mass media critics are WRONG.
review: First things first; dear producers, NO ONE wants to watch Martha and Thomas Wayne die AGAIN. We KNOW that little Brucey fell into the proverbial"Lassie's well" and became traumatised by bats. We've seen it countless times. HOWEVER; despite being reminded of all of that REPEATEDLY, these first few little details were fantastically and vividly detailed, to the point where pearls dropping were singularly focused upon. You actually SEE the light go out in Martha's eye.I was a little confused by the bats lifting Bruce into the 'light' as though they were somehow saving him. On reflection, I understand now that it was a metaphor explained away by the simple Affleck one liner "in the dream" which foreshadows a later confusion I had concerning another dream sequence(in an apparent post-apocalyptic future by the way), which given the lack of warning did not make much sense until after Bruce woke up at his computer. Someone needs to stop drinking coffee and fueling their traumatised, insomnia driven anxiety. In all, I came out of the movie massively impressed. The last time I had come out of a movie so stunned by the magic of cinematography, CGI and acting was when I went to see 300. I was blown away then, and I was blown away by this. This was a new level of superhero action movie. Having expected to have to 'switch off' my brain as I generally feel I need to with mindless action films and superhero movies, I was pleasantly surprised to be fully engaged throughout. There wasn't one point where I got fidgety and restless; because I was so visually captivated, and in a few instances actually on the edge of my seat. Doomsday; When Lord of the Rings showed us the creation of Uruk-Hai, they probably didn't imagine it being done better, or on a larger scale; but Doomsday squashed that belief with ease. It was easy to understand why they needed two superheroes and a very well trained, gadget loving vigilante to defeat him. Making something powerful and believable enough to be a match for Superman alone can be a difficult task, but this was wonderfully well executed. It made the CGI cave trolls from LOTR look like Ardman creations. When I first heard that Jesse Eisenberg was portraying Lex Luthor, I laughed. Previously, I had only ever seen him play those silly geeky roles like Columbus in Zombieland. After being forced to see The Social Network under duress however, I could kind of see it was a good choice, but was still a little dubious. Eisenberg's portrayal of Luthor was nothing short of brilliant. ANYONE who merely suggests that the character Jesse manages somehow to channel is not a maniacal psychopath needs to re-read the definition of those two perfectly descriptive words. It. Was. Genius. From the little twitches in his facial features, to the almost struggled attempt to mask his insanity from speeches given throughout; from the hand gestures representing a man who is struggling to organise the thoughts in his mind; therefore must use outlandish and physically accentuated visualisation techniques, to the downright rage glistening in his eyes in the last few moments you see him behind bars it is the only portrayal of such a notorious villain I believe I have EVER seen in a Superman movie (Sorry Spacey, you're a brilliant actor, but you've just been replaced in the role for best Luthor). Ben Affleck. The world who HATED him for ruining Daredevil was skeptical about him portraying yet another superhero; in the same way the world who HATED Ryan Reynolds for destroying Green Lantern was skeptical about him as Deadpool. In both instances, the world was wrong to be skeptical. We have never seen Batman so accurately dark, gritty and brooding. This was the polar opposite of the campness seen in 1966 and 1997 The fight sequences were fantastically choreographed. Never have we seen Batman fight like that. AND we could hear and see the effort it took him to take those infamous steel punches. He got battered around like a dog's favourite rag doll and was appropriately vocal about it. No one would get beaten like that and not grunt and groan and not have their toys get broken. Gal Gadot's FIRST appearance, actually dressed as Wonder Woman, as what critics are panning as a knock off Xena Warrior Princess, lacks the red, white and blue Americana influenced costume she's known for. But that doesn't make her any less beautiful, strong and confident. Anyone concerned that she's not a good choice as a representative of the feminist movement cannot fail to notice that her first act as Wonder Woman is to SAVE A MAN. And not just any man. She saves Batman. So she's not built like an Amazonian princess. Neither is Hugh Jackman 5'3, squat and occasionally running on all fours throughout any of his portrayals as Wolverine. No one is going to look like the illustrations of Wonder Woman without a lot of cosmetic surgery to enhance their breasts and waistline and without basically destroying their spinal cord in the process. She does appear as somewhat of a bit character, but despite this, I was impressed by the equality portrayed, showing that she's just as strong as Superman and just as intelligent as Batman, and doesn't need a man to 'rescue her' like Lois Lane frequently does. Move over Xena, there's a new girl in town.

title: Why Zach Synder Needs a Co director (Spoiler Alert) and the Pros and Cons of Batman vs Superman
review:
A lot of people say Zach Synder should be fired from directing the batman vs superman movie and the upcoming future DC movies. I don't believe that.

No other director could have made this movie look straight out of comic books like the way Zach did and that is why he should still be a director for the DC comic movies. But.....he needs help on telling the story and that is why Warner Brothers should have hired two directors.

Zach is great at creating action sequences, set designs, and picking the right costumes but he is NOT good at telling the story. This is where a second director could come in handy for having the responsibility of creating the storyline.

What Zach did that met my Expectations: 1. The movie showed the consequence of superman and zod's fight from the "man of steel". This served as a valid motivation for Batman wanting to fight Superman.

2. The live action fight sequence between batman and superman was just as epic as the fight in the DC Animated movie - Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Part 2 (2013).

3. The fight sequence between superman and doomsday looked just as good as the fight in the DC animated movie Superman: Doomsday (2007).

4. Ben Affleck is the best overall batman. He embodied Bruce Wayne and has the best fight scenes i have ever seen from any of the batman movies so far.

5. They get right to the point in showing that Lois Lane and Superman are in a relationship instead of making it long and drawn out for them to get together like they did in the 1980 superman movies 6. Superman is killed. Some people will be upset with this part, but it was done in the comics. Kudos to Zach for having the balls to actually kill superman in the movie. In the end however you can tell superman will be back because they show the dirt rise above his coffin indicating he may be alive.

With that being said, the direction of the story is where Zach fell flat and below is a list of items where a second director to work alongside of Zach could have improved the story: 1. The Batman vs Superman movie did not explain why Lex Luthor hated superman in this movie.

2. Jesse Eisenberg was incorrectly cast for the part of Lex Luthor and Zach missed the mark in realizing that Jesse would have been perfect in acting the part of the Riddler in a future batman movie. During the movie, Jesse sounded and walked like the Riddler.

3. Batmans parents being shot was a waste of movie time. This sequence should not have done as we all know how batman's parents died. If that scene was cut, more screen time could have been created and used to explain why Lex Luthor hated batman.

4. Superman agrees to meet with the senator to discuss the casualties that occurred in a scene where he rescued Lois Lane. There are people that clearly hate superman for the lives lost and buildings destroyed in the fight between him and zod. The movie shows people doubt superman's character. After superman dies from the doomsday fight, a funeral is given for him and magically the public changes their opinion of him. I think they rushed the public changing opinion and could have thought of something more creative.

5. Despite liking gal gadot as wonder woman, i believe she and several scenes in the movie should have been used as an after credit scene once the movie ended. Wonder Woman's character was forced into this movie because a video of her and separate videos for each of the members of the justice league were found by batman from Lex Luthors lab. Wonder woman should not have been used in the doomsday fight sequence even tho she did look cool in it.

The flash has a scene in the movie where he briefly appears to batman showing superman turning evil in the future because Lois died. I think this scene would have been better if it was slightly changed and put as a post credit after the movie ended.

The scenes i mentioned for point 5, should have been used for after credits once the movie ended in the following manner: Batman finds the pictures of the justice league on lex luthor's computer. Just as batman finds the justice league pictures, the flash appears to him showing dark seid with his back to the camera so we cant see how dark seid looks and an evil superman appears with red eyes(5 seconds), then a very short 40 second sequence where wonder woman leads the charge of the other justice league members fighting evil superman and some of them get wounded from superman's eye lasers and punches leaving uncertainty if the wounded justice league members die at superman's hand because the scene cuts off. If that would have been created as a post credit, so much hype would have been created for the upcoming wonder woman and justice league movie

Maybe this movie doesn't deserve a 10 and more of an 8 but I give this movie a high rating because overall i enjoyed it, it accomplished to me what the title of the movie is, and the things i mentioned that could have been fixed do not take away from the fact its still a good movie. Everyone is entitled to a opinion but its sad that some people are giving this movie a one when it does not deserve a one and you can tell zach put a lot of heart into making this movie have the comic book feel and the actors did a great job.

title: Epic movie that needs it's Extended Cut to live up to its own high standards
review:
So, I got around to seeing Batman v Superman last night and what I can say for sure is that this is a movie that will benefit greatly from its extended three-hour Director's Cut. My first impressions (I plan on seeing it again soon) are that not unexpectedly adapting a Batman/Superman story to the big screen was a monumental task, and, quite honestly, the very fact that it's here is something to be marvelled at. (no pun intended)

This is a very untradtitional film in that it does not have a central character or point of view to cling to; instead we follow two story lines, with two main characters and their own supporting cast. We have a Batman detective story with a side serving of Wonder Woman and Alfred, and a Superman story about his struggle to cope with his very existence, prominently featuring Lois Lane. Intersecting throughout and finally converging towards the final act of the movie, these story lines could serve their own separate movies, and so, hard as he tries, Snyder is only mildly successful in making everything work in the end. Such a colossal undertaking naturally deserves a massive run time as well, perhaps enough even for two movies, but what we have is the trimmed down Theatrical Cut, which feels like there's parts missing.

Despite all this, the direction and cinematogrpahy is stellar, with Zack Snyder's iconic style of filmmaking bringing us another comic book movie that not only has comic book characters in it but also looks and feels like a comic book come to life. The casting is stellar, with Ben Affleck chewing scenery as Batman, and, in my personal opinion, Henry Cavill truly coming into his own as this generation's Superman, and also Gal Gadot who is serviceable as Wonder Woman (it helps that she's tall). The soundtrack by crowd-pleasers Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL is top-notch but the sound-editing felt all over the place (especially with Wonder Woman's and Batman's theme) with abrupt starts and stops which tried to follow the flow of the action but just felt out of place at times.

And finally, massive props for the Batman origin story which was done with quickly and absolutely beautifully early-on in the movie. It was perhaps my favorite scene of the whole film. I'm majorly excited to see it again, and am eagerly anticipating the Extended Cut as well.
