title: Complex, grand and ultimately satisfying follow up to MAN OF STEEL
review:
A title is a powerful thing. In a few words, it shapes audiences expectations for a movie, tells them the subject of said movie and attempts to entice viewership. BATMAN V SUPERMAN: DAWN OF JUSTICE (BVS) is a mouthful of a title that at once teases a titanic showdown between two comic book icons and hints at the formation of the world famous Justice League superhero team. No doubt many are going to cry foul when they find out that BVS is not referring to an actual physical bout as it the conflict and contrast of the two titular characters' background, world views, motivations and beliefs. It is a movie that is more likely to make you think rather than cheer, more likely to make you question reality rather than be drawn into a fantasy.

We start with many subplots. So many subplots that the initial hour of the movie feels bloated. What seems like a meandering mess slowly comes together like branches in a pie chart. As the pieces fit and perceived chaos comes into order, viewers sharp enough would have noticed the foreshadowing of plot elements to come. Though it manages to hold our intrigue without splitting at the seams, this jigsaw style, non linear plot development may not appeal to everyone, especially those who are more used to traditional chronological arrangement of plot beats or the modern "right into the action" blockbusters.

What comes next is.......actually less epic than I thought it would be. It is less the super powered death match of the century but a more intimate examination of ideologies and philosophies surrounding the superhero mythos and how those philosophies relate and intertwine in a very real and familiar world. The fallible and corruptible nature of man, the benevolent god debate, the burden of responsibility, doing the "right" thing in a world where right and wrong is subjective, BVS explores all these. The prize bout of batman beating superman draws parallels to real life hate crimes against minorities or migrants with superman as the ultimate migrant.

Juxtaposed against the differing ideologies embodied by the conflicting trinity of Batman, Lex Luthor and Superman is the theme of how ones past shapes the present. We have three surprisingly well developed characters dealing with past trauma in wholly different ways in accordance with their personalities. The main attraction here is Ben Affleck's Batman. He oozes a restrained intensity with a volcano of emotions boiling beneath the surface, hidden behind a stoic mask. The world weary Wayne has channeled his loss into an unrelenting force against crime but unknowingly projects his past failures onto his current ones.

Similarly for Lex Luthor, he is the opposite reflection of Bruce Wayne. This young, sports shoe and t-shirt wearing eccentric tech mogul is full of energy in contrast to Wayne's older, mellowed portrayal. A phrase he quotes during a speech about having all the knowledge without the power, and the frustrated way he spits it out in contempt underpins his motivations perfectly. He is hilarious without losing his menace, a smidgen of humour in the otherwise serious film.

Superman on the other hand.......is less of a character and more of a concept. He acts best as the subject that fuels the debate, if he acts at all. For starters, there is little contrast in Henry Cavill's portrayal of the superman/Clark Kent dichotomy. One is just Superman with a costume, the other is superman in civvies and glasses. Exact same tone of voice, exact same facial expressions that only alternate between morose and angry. Wooden performance aside, BVS elaborates, addresses and brings to closure many of the themes first brought up in its predecessor MAN OF STEEL.

Perhaps the experience would be a complete one when this is viewed in tandem with the former? Surprisingly, the movie does not go full on dark and gritty like MAN OF STEEL did. As mentioned, Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor is like a devious bugs bunny full of dark ironic humour (Granny's Peach Tea). Laurence Fishburne as Perry White never fails to bring a chuckle. And the witty banter and strong chemistry between Affleck's Wayne and Gal Gadot's mysterious Diana Prince is absolutely charming.

Even the colour palette seems more vivid with clear distinct shades, most evident in the black and grey of batman's costume, quite unlike the washed out muted tones in MAN OF STEEL. Zack Snyder alternates between slow motion scenes of a surreal, almost otherworldly, feel, and the hyperkinetic shaky cam going full on "Michael Bay" for the action. His collaborator Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL returns for the music providing a heavy grandiose score full of percussion and choir chanting as if the movie were an operatic epic.

Like its titular heroes, BATMAN V SUPERMAN has divided people in opinion. It tries to do a lot and in doing so may be a challenge for simpler minded audiences to comprehend and follow. This is a complex movie delving into complex themes but maybe people have grown accustomed to something friendlier.

Filled with subtle but powerful emotional moments, equally powerful fight scenes, and strong underlying themes and real life allegory, BVS is loud, grand and an easily misunderstood creature. It is different from the more light hearted superhero movies of recent years and in that respect it will get shoehorned into the expectations of what a superhero movie should be rather than be appreciated for what it is and what it could be.

All this on account of a misleading title.

title: Hack Snyder Strikes Again
review:
First of all, if you saw it and enjoyed it, good for you. Don't let me ruin your enjoyment of the film with the extremely negative review I'm about to lay down. If you're one of the lucky few who haven't seen it by now, I'm telling you, it's a trap. There are lots of better movies out right now that deserve your attention more than this title

I'm gonna try to avoid major spoilers, but I'll likely get into some minor spoilers just so I can talk about a few specific scenes that truly irked my soul. So if you're actually still reading this then consider this your spoiler warning.

Let's get some positives out of the way first and foremost. I really enjoyed the first 10-ish minutes of the film. The opening scene was beautifully shot and edited, and would've been a lot more effective had we not seen the death of Batman's parents (spoiler?) in like, a hundred movies before this. That being said, this sequence on its own, was excellent. Simple, effective visual storytelling, with a beautiful score to back it up. I was instantly reminded of the opening credits sequence from Zack Snyder's Watchmen, which was the best part of that film too. Maybe he should just stick to making title sequences.

We then move to the climax of Man of Steel, but from the perspective of all of the helpless people on the ground while these two all- powerful aliens destroy the entire city of Metropolis. Bruce Wayne shows up to check out the scene, and to try to save some dude named Jack (who might be the most oblivious character in cinematic history, as he fails to notice the giant alien spacecraft blasting a hole into the middle of Metropolis until Bruce Wayne mentions said spacecraft). Look at that, I'm trying to talk about the positives and I keep running into negatives. Jack's stupidity aside, this scene was well-executed. It felt grounded and had some legitimate emotional weight to it, making it more than just a loud, obnoxious action setpiece for the sake of having one. It does a nice job of setting up Batman's motivation to go kick Superman's ass.

The performances across the board were pretty solid. Ben Affleck completely proved the nay-sayers wrong and delivered a terrific Bruce Wayne/Batman performance. Surprisingly, I actually really enjoyed Jesse Eisenberg's take on Lex Luthor. I've noticed most people giving him flak for his work here, but he seemed like the only one who was actually having fun in this movie. He played a fun, over-the-top, comic book villain, and that was enough for me. I understand if it rubs people the wrong way, but I quite liked it.

Finally, I dug the music. The score was probably the best part of this whole thing (and the entire soundtrack is available for free on YouTube so check that out if you're interested). There was a specific piece that played during some of the Batman sequences that felt like a mix of Fury Road's drums with an awesome synth sample that felt like it was right out of a cheesy 80s action movie, and I adored it.

Okay so the rest of it was garbage. I feel bad for the thousands of people who worked hard on this film, ultimately for jerks on the internet like me to crap all over their final product. The fact is, the man in charge, Zack Snyder, is the one who must take most of the blame. Now, I understand he had a lot on his plate, he had to include all the Justice League tie-ins and balance like a thousand different plot lines that were all going on in this overcrowded mess. At the end of the day, Snyder and Warner Bros. should've focused on making ONE good, coherent film, rather than a thousand short films stuffed into an awful one.

I have to talk about the scene where I pretty much gave up. Lois Lane (who is legitimately the stupidest person of all time next to that Jack dude) decides to go up to a man cleaning the floors of the Daily Planet, because she thinks they've met. Well, they have, because he was a terrorist at the beginning of the film who nearly killed her. WHY? Why did she go up to a man who reminded her of a terrorist who almost killed her a few months prior? Why didn't they just have a bunch of goons grab her and take her to Luthor? This isn't rocket science, this is screen writing 101.

The last act of the movie seemed to go on forever. The actual fight that literally ALL of the marketing for this film is built around is pretty entertaining while it lasts, but is cut short when the screenwriters decide they need to team up now (and it's very fortunate that Bruce and Clark's moms shared the same name, otherwise Supes would've found out the answer to #WhoWillWin). This climax just goes on and on and on. At this point, I'm not convinced of anything I'm seeing on the screen, all I can see is hundreds of computer animators working away; a fireball here, a laser beam there, etc. Then all the mind-numbing action finally ends, and we get what feels like another two hours of boring, drawn-out, depressing epilogue. Not depressing in the way that the film intends to be (it's supposed to have a "tragic" ending that is ruined by the fact that everyone knows which movies they have coming up on their slate, so no one is buying this one specific character's "death"), but depressing because the audience is just sitting there regretting their recent life choices.

title: Nowhere near a bad as the vocal minority claim.

title: This was the perfect movie and here is why....
review: This movie was done, exactly the way it was supposed to been done. Let me ask you a question, how many Marvel movies, since the beginning of the new Marvel Universe that created the Avengers, has there been? Can you even count them? I know for a fact that there's been 3 Iron Man, 2 Hulk, 2 Thor, 2 Spider Man (Im counting Garfields because his was in the time frame of the Avenges), 3 Captain America (with the new one coming out), 1 Guardians, 1 Deadpool, 5 or so X-Men (including origins) and I am pretty sure I'm missing some. Now lets count how many DC Comics Movies has there been? 3 Dark Knight, 1 Superman, 1 Green Lantern (Yes, it was trash) and that's it I believe, I'm sure I am missing some but can't be as many as Marvel. My point is that everyone thinks that Superhero movies should be like Marvel's, and don't get me wrong, Marvel did an amazing job at making their movies but what is there appeal? Families, Kids, funny, fun, quirky, corny and filled with dad-jokes (with the exception of Deadpool) and that's all nice and stuff but they never created something legendary, a vision, and if I dare to say, a Shakespearean Tragedy. Let's be honest now, we all have been brain-washed by Marvel, enough to expect all super hero movies to be like theirs, and that was genius. But what DC just did was set up the next movies perfectly. Now we get to have a Wonder Woman movie, an Aquaman movie, maybe even a Flash or Cyborg movie, and if we are lucky, a new Batman movie, with also the in between such as Suicide Squad and many others. But the way that DC is making these movies is in a total different approach from Marvels. A lot of people complain that Bat vs Sup is not "fun" and not "funny", why the hell does it have to be either of those things, who thought that a Comic Superhero movie can turn into a beautiful artistic Shakespearean Tragedy!! That is exactly what Snyder did in this one, and if you don't understand the way its filmed than just she The Watchmen and you'll understand, that movie is probably one of the greatest underrated superhero films ever. This movie had everything that DC is; love, sin, death, action, tragedy, sinister, dark, seriousness, artistic notion, it was freaking renaissance!! People need to be open minded and not judge this movie as a Marvel movie but as something completely different. Just look at the perfect boys that Marvel has in their movies. Now look at DC's actors and do they not look like freaking men and not a perfect skin, perfect face boy like Marvel's actors, have you seen the new Spider Man?. Feel the seriousness and the sin nester tone that Snyder brought, it was so artistic and beautiful. Everything about this movie was perfect. Snyder did not just make another superhero movie, he made a film that will not be known as the 3 installment in a franchise but a Vision of how Superhero films can be transformed into a realistic world that is full of loathing, lust, deception and death. Basically, Marvel does movies for kids, DC makes movies for adults.

In five minutes your emotional and intellectual investments are erased in the favor of a weird horror-like hyper-dystopian scenes+ A "disney" style ending where nobody dies and there are no consequences. This mix of cartoon-logic and horrid graphics & noise almost induces vomit. just count the times you hear that sound of 50 chalks-scraping-board-sounding-like-an-aeroplane- flying-in-your-ears. title: Let's be realistic.
review:
Firstly i would like to apologize for any fact that indicates misuse of the English language. There will not be any specific reference from the movie, but this review will include some facts that are going to make you understand what you are about to watch or what you have already watched.

Zack Snyder portrays Batman as a dark, brutal and cruel instrument of justice. This happens after Batman has faced many harsh circumstances during his years fighting crime being against demented and fierce opponents.Watching this character taking lives of criminals without hesitation makes me feel moderately ambivalent. Αfter being quite thoughtful i decided to be realistic. Let's face it, the director has merged the fictional universe with reality in such an ingenious way, that violence is inevitable. This is pointed out in every punch every gunshot and every conflicting statement.So Ben Affleck's Batman became, struggling all this time with injustice, from fair to cold-blooded because even if he is smart, methodic and a person with spine, he has after all went to pieces by the time his morality was corrupted.

Henry Cavill on the other hand has already introduced himself as Superman, who's having a stand-off with the constitution between the suitable and the legitimate measures that have to be taken while facing strong inhuman enemies.There is nothing new to add about this character, all we can say is that he is still new at being a hero and he still misunderstands the difference between right affected by ego and just. Which is obvious because he is a person with Personality, super strength and nο proper motivation, more of being 'his destiny' kind of motivation. So i would not like to see a superman that comes, saves the world from the biggest and worst enemy, and goes back to his monotonous life like nothing happened, good movie ending , a nice ending song and everything OK. NO! there were casualties, so we watched them, there was pain and anger, so we watched it. That's OK, being realistic it's not the same like being dark. It is what it is, nothing more nothing less.

The movie itself does not display good guys that lose a fistfight versus the bad guys, and then, after internal conflict, they find the courage to fight back and defeat evil for ever or for now. The main villain which is obviously Lex Luthor does not hit a punch in the whole movie ( as i remember ). Ηe is just playing mind games or else a chess match without an opponent for more than an hour in the movie. Which makes him the unsung villain that misleads the superheroes and controls the situations as he pleases. He wants to defeat the 'muscles' cause the 'brains' are already under his control. He is a good(meaning really bad) villain but still he can't handle the outcome while facing the united protagonists.

Lastly i would like to mention that i like the fact that we see other future superheroes, even for a couple of seconds each one. Being in a movie that does not include them as main characters makes me understand that they exist, they might know what's happening already, they just don't care or are afraid to act right now, BUT they exist.To sum up i liked the movie a lot, it gets a 8 from me cause i can't vote 8,5.The plot flows a bit too fast but it's OK i think, We have seen those heroes in many movies through years with various but small differences but overall same origin stories so we don't have to catch up with something. title: A masterpiece !
review: I think the story is very well thought-out, even though the critics are complaining about an "incoherent screenplay". I really don't get the negative ratings. Take for example the incident in the Sahara that was planned by Luthor to frame Superman. The critics complain that this storyline doesn't make any sense at all since the villagers were killed with bullets, so how can Superman be framed for it ? What the critics missed is that the surviving villagers testified against superman for being responsible, since they didn't eye-witness the mass killing by Luthor's men. The homeland security didn't disclose all evidence since they are secretly financing the rebels with American weapons produced by Luthor. Hence, they cleaned the crime scene and left superman to take the blame. Lois however, continue her investigation concerning the bullet she found in her notebook, trying to prove Superman's innocence, which leads her to Luthor. After collecting some evidence with the help of General Swanwick, Luthor is finally arrested and imprisoned for this incident and for creating Doomsday. I guess it was too complex for the critics to figure it out !! Another example is the training montage where Bruce is seen dragging a truck tire across the floor and hitting it with a sledgehammer. Some cynical critics considered this scene as being stupid and pointless, since "dragging a tire across a room" can in no way prepare a human to fight a demigod. Well, what they missed is that this training wasn't intended to physically prepare Bruce to actually fight Superman, but just to make him fit enough to wear his heavy iron/armored bat-suit, and move around with it !! As for the fight itself, Bruce prepared for it by simply weaponizing the Kryptonite he stole from Luthor. As for the Martha scene, I found it very logical due to its oedipal subtext: Bruce was about to kill a man saying the same words as his dying father. He was also sacrificing superman's potentially kidnapped mother. Hence, he was participating in the recreation of this whole circle of violence. Add to that the fact that Lois came and begged him to stop, which had a huge impact especially after the Flash clearly told him that Lois is the key to all of this. So all he did was to stop, and took a minute to rethink everything, and being the paranoid guy he is, he concluded he may have been manipulated from the start to fight Superman. Hence, he decided to believe Lois and give this "potentially dangerous alien" a chance, at least until he figure out the entire truth. Of course after Superman's death, Bruce is completely converted as he say: "I failed him in life, I won't fail him in death". Anyway, Henry Cavill is great as Superman here, way better than MOS. Ben Affleck is incredible as Bruce Wayne/Batman. Gal Gadot is OK as WW even though we don't see her a lot. The build up to the fight between our heroes is carefully done. The only thing I didn't like was the introduction of the other members of the JL, which felt pretty rushed. I think they should have just introduced WW in this film, which was more than enough, considering the amount of screen time they got to tell this complex story. I really liked Jesse Eisenberg as Luthor's son (yes, he's not Lex, but Alexander Luthor: his father built LexCorp). So, all in all, great film, great performances by all of the actors and supporting actors (Jeremy Irons is great), a decent script, and breathtaking visuals. Now, I don't think that we r ready for a JL movie yet. I think that MOS 2 should be shot first, at least to cover the Resurrection of Superman, and to introduce other JL members correctly. Also, I would like to have a Batfleck movie in 2017, along with WW, and then JL in 2018 or something. I would also pay to watch a post apocalyptic/alternate universe/Mad-Max style Batman movie directed by Zack Snyder, since the Knightmare sequence was very raw and very powerful. I guess basic raw human emotions can be easily explored in that kind of post apocalyptic setting. It would also be a good opportunity to introduce the Cyborg in this post-apocalyptic world/alternate universe. We shall wait and see how future projects will be developed. Until then, go see Batman v Superman, preferably in IMAX.

title: Best Comic-Book Movie Ever!
review:
First, the negatives:

1. Jesse Eisenberg / Lex Luthor. This was the one casting decision that I didn't like. And after seeing the movie, I still don't like it. This version of Lex Luthor just didn't work for me.

2. The Knightmare sequence. The Knightmare just suddenly came out of nowhere; it wasn't clear what triggered the Knightmare; and it didn't seem to be explained or referenced afterward.

Now the positives:

1. Gal Gadot / Wonder Woman. Many people didn't like the casting of Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman when it was announced, but I liked it. I thought Henry Cavill and Ben Affleck had good performances, but Gal Gadot was definitely one of the best things about the movie. Avengers director Joss Whedon was hired to make a Wonder Woman movie in 2007, but failed to do so. BvS director Zack Snyder not only brought Wonder Woman to the big screen for the 1st time ever, but also made Wonder Woman a real bad-ass warrior. We see Wonder Woman use her bracelets, her shield, her sword, and her magic lasso. I can't wait to see the Wonder Woman movie in 2017.

2. The Batman vs Superman fight. Not just the fight, but seeing Batman's meticulous and brilliant planning prior to the fight. And then the fight itself was one of the best mano a mano fights in comic-book movie (CBM) history. Batman's brilliant strategic moves during the fight demonstrate why Batman is the best strategist among superheroes and is always prepared (unlike dumb-ass Tony Stark who was so dumb in Iron Man 3 that he not only went on TV and announced his home address to the whole world so that the bad guys could attack his home, but also wasn't prepared for the attack from the bad guys and also didn't warn his girlfriend to stay away from the house so that she wouldn't get in danger when the bad guys fire a missile at his house).

3. Doomsday. A hero isn't much of a hero unless there's a formidable villain to challenge the hero and push the hero to the limit. Without Darth Vader, Luke Skywalker is just a farmer and not a Jedi Knight who helped defeat the Galactic Empire. Without Medusa and the Kraken, Perseus doesn't get a constellation named after him. A good hero needs a formidable villain to challenge him/her and push him/her to the limit.

As I mentioned in the negatives above, this version of Lex Luthor just didn't work for me. But Doomsday was a great villain because he's one of the most formidable villains in CBM history. That's what makes DC/WB movies in general far superior to Marvel Studios movies. Marvel Studios movies don't have any formidable villains. When watching The Avengers and Avengers: Age of Ultron, I never felt that the weak Chitauri (who had no superpowers at all) or even Ultron and his army of robots were ever any danger to the Avengers. But when watching BvS, Doomsday was clearly a danger to the Trinity. In The Avengers, all it took was 1 nuclear missile fired by a U.S. military jet to defeat 100s of Chitauri. Doomsday was hit with a nuclear missile and still couldn't be stopped!

4. The Trinity. The scene of the Trinity, 3 of the 4 most popular and most iconic superheroes in American comics history, standing together side-by-side ready for battle is the most iconic shot ever in a CBM. Even though I've seen that scene many times in the trailers, it was still awesome to see it happening for the 1st time in the movie. And that scene got 1 of the loudest applause in the theater.

5. The Flash, Aquaman, and Cyborg cameos. Unlike the stupid and useless Stan Lee cameos or the lame post-credit scenes that have no purpose other than to tease the next movie in Marvel Studios movies, Zack Snyder cleverly integrated the Flash, Aquaman, and Cyborg cameos into BvS in a way that not only made sense but also didn't clutter up the movie (like many detractors had claimed it would). It was a brilliant way by Snyder to set up the Justice League without resorting to a lame post-credit scene.

6. When Superman was asked by Senator Finch to appear at the hearing, he does so voluntarily even though they had no power to force him to do so (just like he had voluntarily surrendered himself to the U.S. military in Man of Steel even though they had no power to force him to). That demonstrates once again that Superman respects the authority of the people and is willing to answer to the people.

Overall:

The critics who gave BvS a low rating definitely got it wrong. Despite its flaws, BvS is still definitely better than any of the Marvel Studios movies that most critics always get an orgasm over. BvS presents a thought-provoking analysis of justice, absolute power, accountability, and the actions of and reaction to superheroes in a real-world environment. The 1st CBM I ever saw was Superman: The Movie in 1978. Since then, I've seen over 50 CBMs and I have to say that BvS is 1 of the best CBMs ever made.

After seeing BvS, I can understand why many critics gave the movie a low rating. Those critics are used to seeing the light-hearted, kiddie movies that Marvel Studios makes and aren't used to seeing CBMs that are mature and thought-provoking. Basically, Marvel Studios movies are like live-action cartoons (similar to The Flintstones or Scooby-Doo movies) while BvS is like a live-action graphic novel. Zack Snyder effectively took parts of The Dark Knight Returns and The Death of Superman stories from the comics and brought them to life on the big screen.

title: Very Entertaining (possibly minor spoilers)
review:
I've been a casual observer on IMDb since the early 2000's and have never posted a review or opinion of a film. However, this movie has so many polarizing views, I would like to offer somewhat of a fair assessment.

DISCLAIMER: Let me tell you that I don't read many comic books, but I am a huge Batman fan from his appearances in other media, such as the Arkham Games, Dark Knight Trilogy, and Animated Series. I feel Superman is an important character, but I have never been a huge follower of his. You could consider me a "DC fan" (mostly because of Batman). That doesn't mean that I don't enjoy Marvel movies. There is room in my life for bothas long as they are entertaining.

With that said, Batman v. Superman was very entertaining to me. The first 30 minutes are incredible (Batman's setup). After that, the movie does bounce around a bit for the next 45 minutes, but it doesn't require too many brain cells to follow along. If you have a basic understanding of the DC Universe, you can probably follow along easier than someone who doesn't. During this time, the main focus is on dialogue, rather than action. The last hour or so is just pure adrenaline.

As a Batman fan, I was pleased with Affleck's portrayal. We not only saw the bad@ss crime fighter, but we also saw the detective aspect that often gets overlooked in mainstream media. His fight scenes (against criminals) were brutal, as in Arkham Series brutal. Very pleasing. Also, I got more Alfred than I was expecting, and that was a good thing.

As far as Superman goes, again, I have never been a huge fan/follower of his. He was OK, but the Batman parts were by far my favorites. Ironically, I did find myself pulling for Superman during the fight with Batman. (I won't spoil it, but you probably will to)

What I didn't like so much: Doomsday was a neat idea, but I felt his appearance could have been more. Lex Luthor was menacing and dangerous, but I didn't like the goofiness that came from Eisenberg. It was sort of like he wanted to be a more restrained version of the Joker. Lois Lane was better this time, but she still kind of annoys me. Wonder Woman had nothing more than a glorified cameo.

I don't want to make this too long, so I will wrap it up here. If The Dark Knight (the Holy Grail of comic book movies) is a 10, I would be comfortable giving this movie a 7.5-8 rating. If you already made your mind up that you will hate this movie, then you probably will. If you are going in looking to have fun, you will.

I'm pulling for "Capt. America: Civil War" to be just as fun. Competition is a great thing Just ask WWE fans from the 90's.

title: Why All The Hate? It's Not That Bad
review:
Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is directed by Zack Snyder and stars Ben Affleck and Henry Cavill as Batman and Superman. This movie mostly follows Bruce Wayne as he begins to feel uneasy about Superman, and what he may be capable of when it comes to the existence of the human race. Bruce feels that if this "alien" wanted to, he could wipe out the Earth's population, and nobody could stop him. Due to this disagreement between the two, they end up in physical quarrel that could level monuments...literally.

Now, since this film hit theaters, I have heard nothing good about it, besides the praise around Ben Affleck's Batman. Although Ben Affleck does extremely well, I feel that Batman V Superman is actually a very good film, and a fun superhero movie. Like said earlier, everybody has been praising Affleck's Batman, and for such good reason. Ben Affleck plays one of the, if not the, best live action Batmans we have ever seen. Everything Affleck does in his portrayal as the caped crusader is fantastic, and he plays this character near perfectly. However great the performance, I do have a complaint with the character.

Now, anyone who has seen a former Batman movie, read the comics, or watched any of the animated series' then you know that Batman has a single rule when it comes to crime fighting...he doesn't kill. Not in Dawn of Justice. This dude just mows people down. He uses machine guns, grenade launchers, you name it. He kills people left and right, and it doesn't exactly do the legendary character justice; no pun intended. It does add affect to the character himself, but it doesn't stay true to the comics like it should. As a casual movie goer, it won't do harm, but as a comic book fan, it's a bit hard to swallow, in seeing the abrupt change in Batman's moral code.

Henry Cavill's performance as Superman didn't really change since Man of Steel (2013); he's fine. He doesn't do bad, but he definitely isn't Christopher Reeve. I personally like him better as Clark Kent than I do as Superman, but, like I said, he doesn't do bad. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was a really good casting choice. Although she doesn't have the biggest part in the film, she does pretty good. As far as the character goes, she seemed to just pop up randomly throughout the film, as if the filmmakers tried to keep her character bobbing above water, that way she didn't sink under, but she didn't exactly stay afloat either, if that analogy makes any sense.

Now, Amy Adams does good as Lois Lane, and I still stand by that casting choice. However, when it comes to Lois' actual character, it doesn't work. Throughout the entire film, Lois is on a wild goose chase, trying to figure out some dirty deed that Lex Luthor may or may not have had a hand in (more on him in a minute). Once her mindless subplot is finally over with, she gets involved with the final fight, and basically becomes a damsel in distress. It's at this point in which I realized that the filmmakers really just didn't know what to do with her character. They had her go on some unwarranted quest, just to occupy her character in one way or another. This upset me, because this whole factor took away from the film majorly.

A big controversial topic about Dawn of Justice is Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. He's been getting a lot of hate recently, and I can see why. He's a bit over the top, and crazy at times, and I really can understand why this doesn't work for some people. However, this was not the case for my personal experience. I really enjoyed Eisenberg as Lex, despite him being nothing like Lex Luthor from the comic books. This didn't bother me, however, because he actually isn't Lex Luthor, he's Lex Luthor Jr. He's the original Lex's son, and that's why he's so different from Lex in the comics, so it works for me. I like the wackyness to him, even though it's a little over the top at specific moments.

The action in this film is absolutely amazing. Every moment of the battle between Batman and Superman is gut wrenchingly exciting. All of the directing was also top notch. Many people know Zack Snyder for his style over substance, and that applies to Batman V Superman. Although the script is lacking a lot, the direction and action look beautiful, as true with most Snyder films.

Doomsday. Just like everybody speculated, he looks stupid. He looks like a Michael Bay ninja turtle mixed with the character of Abomination from The Incredible Hulk (2008). He also causes too much destruction in the city, and basically cancels out what this film tried to make up for with the destruction caused in Man of Steel (2013). His battle with the three heroes doesn't work out too much, considering he was created to "kill Superman." I say this because he also tries to kill Batman and Wonder Woman as well, which doesn't make too much sense.

The last topic I'll hit is really hard to discuss. All I'll say is that the film made a very ballsy choice towards the end of the movie, but then repeals the decision. It's hard to say without spoilers, but once you see the movie you'll know what I mean. The ballsy decision should have either stayed in effect up until the end, or not have happened at all. If either of this two outcomes would have been, the ending would have been better by a whole lot.

In conclusion, Batman V Superman isn't a bad film, and was very fun to watch on the big screen.

title: In a word?
review:
Fantastic. This movie delivers on nearly every level. As a comic book fan and lover of cinema, I feel that Chris Terrio and Zack Snyder have done exceptionally well in delivering an engaging, intellectually stimulating and aesthetically pleasing film that does justice to the characters, capturing their complexity and depth. The balance of dialogue and action is perfectly executed, with noteworthy performances all around. Ben Affleck stands out and embodies everything I love about Batman, putting to rest any fears that surfaced upon his casting. Jesse Eisenberg gives us a memorable portrayal as Lex Luthor that showcases both his genius and insanity. Henry Cavill0 takes somewhat of a backseat to Affleck through no fault of his own, but with Superman's introduction in MoS this movie demanded a bigger focus on Batman. What we do get from Cavill is consistently brilliant, even if it does leave you wanting more.

The cinematography is beautifully done, and the pacing mastered to perfection for a movie of this length. The set up for the Justice League is done wonderfully in a way that introduces the characters without ever giving the movie a feeling of being overloaded. The titular fight and climax are brilliant, making up for the action sequences in MoS that missed the mark at times, and leaving the audience wanting more, particularly from Wonder Woman, who steals the show.

I can only fault the movie on two things: 1. The lack of Clark Kent, especially as reporter, and 2. the final look of Doomsday (it certainly wasn't bad but I would have preferred a design more closely resembling that of the source material). All in all, a thrilling experience that proved to be worth the wait, leaving us with possibly the best superhero movie ever made and setting up for further greatness to come.

Oh, and screw the critics :-)

title: A Highly Enjoyable Flick that Starts a New Promising Franchise
review:
"Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" isn't the best name they could have given, but I have to admit, I didn't have very high expectations but it sure didn't disappoint. It's a long movie with a task, and that is to develop all the characters they could fit in one movie. Some characters didn't get the attention they needed, but I'm sure they want to save origin stories for standalone and "Justice League" movies.

Let's start with Batman. Never understood why so many people got mad with Affleck doing the role. He actually looks like Bruce Wayne and his performance was a big plus. It won't be hard to enjoy this Batman as much as we liked The Dark Knight. Affleck fits perfectly in the suit and all the fight scenes were better than ever. They perfectly recaptured the tone that fans so much praise and wanted to see. I wouldn't say it's fan service but I'm glad with where they're going to with this. And then there's Superman. It's nothing completely new, although they brought the man of steel to a deeper layer in character development. Even though Snyder doesn't go with the approach of the comics, where the tones are much lighter and colors are much brighter, this approach makes it more coherent as the movie goes on. Other surprising new characters came into the picture as well like Jeremy Irons as Alfred clearly was one, and of course, Eisenberg as Lex Luther was a completely different yet awesome approach to Superman's most popular enemy. Even though, Kevin Spacey was closer to the original in "Superman Returns", this was a performance that stood out and got us all intrigued.

The movie in general is filled with awesome action sequences that satisfy our needs and expectations. Let's not forget it's a 2 hour and a half movie but still, with so many big characters to develop I felt like some parts were rushed, and they could have used that time for more character development and richer side plots instead of long over the top dream sequences where we don't really know what's going on.

To be honest, I'm kinda tired of the superhero movie genre, but I feel like this one is well above average, with CGI filled non-stop action and a budget that can make anything possible.

The critics were pretty harsh in their evaluation, and if you haven't seen the movie, don't let those awful reviews decide whether it's good or bad. I found it to be highly enjoyable.

Visually it is indeed stunning, although the color grading made it way too dark. Sometimes you don't really know what's happening. Nolan didn't have to dim the lights to bring a darker tone in his trilogy, but Snyder likes to darken the colors overall, and that's something present in most of his movies. Visual effects were made by Weta Digital, the same company who brought the revolutionary effects in The Lord of The Rings and Avatar, so it's guaranteed it looks breathtaking. Doomsday looks pretty great, and its a full CG monster with tons of detail.

As a fan of The Walking Dead, I was really glad to see "Maggie" and "Negan" as Bruce Wayne's parents, it's definitely one of the best moments in the movie.

Since I saw the poster in apocalyptic Times Square on "I am Legend", I've been waiting for this movie, I'd say DC and Warner Brothers might have a new promising franchise on the way. I consider myself a fan of both Batman and Superman but I don't read the comics nor watch the animated series, so I'm rating this movie based on what I saw, not what I wanted to see or should have seen.

title: The Big Three Together at Last
review:
This may be the most unfairly maligned film in history.

Clearly made for DC fans who have been reading the books for a long time, BATMAN v SUPERMAN examines dark themes of the human (and perhaps not human) heart while giving us a story that evokes elements from some of the noisiest, grandest, disturbing crossover events in the company's history. (Think: INFINITE CRISIS and such.)

The plot is complex; not full of holes. The film is dark; but, what else would you expect from a story that features Doomsday, a discouraged and perhaps publicly scorned Superman, and a dangerously desperate and perplexed Bruce Wayne, seen here at a very dark period of his life. This Bruce is more Frank Miller and less Christian Bale, even. This Clark is more OMAC PROJECT Superman and less Christopher Reeve. The film is dark, but so are the most compelling moments in DC history.

Casual viewers who are less familiar with the DCU will not understand large segments of this movie. This is a film made for DC fans. For those of you, like me, who have followed the Big Three since their days on the animated SUPERFRIENDS TV show--seeing them together on that screen will truly make you feel like a kid again.

title: Flash
review:
My take on Batman vs Superman. Spoiler has been marked and is at the end of this review. Just going to single out the issues I had with it. Critics gonna nag. I would giveit a 7.5 out of 10.

The Positive - I felt Ben Affleck's dark performance of the Bat was well done. Henry Cavill, again in my opinion, is the best thing to happen to the Superman. Of course, I liked his first Superman movie more than most...Lex Luthor's character is delightfully Jokerish. He is the best thing to happen to Lex Luthor. The decade's long anticipated fight scenes between the Bat and Sup didn't disappoint me, it seemed to disappoint many others. Brains vs brawn is the main entrée. Luthor's thug-like play to make the Superman go after the Batman belonged in another decade though. Granted, the setup for the Barman wanting Superman was psychotic.The fight with Doomsday could have been more technical. Sarcasm alert - why were there no childhood memories of Doomsday(via Luthor's DNA)? I'd want to see how the little beast/Luthor became so evil. Okay, sarcasm off. We had way too much backstory in the movie as it is. I loved how Wonder Woman seemed to actually enjoy the battle vs Doomsday. Not as single minded determined like Superman or grim like Batman. I can't see many not liking that one aspect of her character. **Minor spoiler**Several future Justice League members are given 15-60 seconds of screen time via Bruce Wayne's decryption of Lex Luthor's files on the "Meta-Human Project.". Aside from Diana Prince(Wonder Woman) we "briefly" see Barry Allen (The Flash) but he has an important 2nd scene, Arthur Curry (Aquaman), and Vic Stone (Cyborg). Cyborg's spot was the longest but I had to look it up to even know it was him for sure. People always love to poke fun at Aquaman and his powers being useless outside of being in water(unless he summons a can of sardines). By the looks of it, he's going to be a real harda** when Justice League premiers.

The negative - Disappointed in a few spots such as starting the movie with a 5+ minute montage of young Bruce Wayne seeing his parents killed, pearls hitting the ground, running and falling in a cave the same thing several Batman movies have already done. If you miss the first 5 minutes or so you miss nothing. Except for maybe the line "Martha" you miss nothing. Several big scenes in the trailer are misleading as they are no more than visions or dreams and had no business being in the trailer, let alone the movie - The BIG one is Superman marching up to a captured Batman with determined hatred in his face and unmasking him. Based on another observation, these visions given to Batman, "Knightmares" if you will excuse the pun, may be hints of a dark parallel universe tied into Flash for a flash of a scene giving Bat a warning. Wonder Woman's character has no real direction or even explanation. She has her own movie next year(or year after) so maybe that's it. But her indecision and even walking away from the crisis at first sucked and do not show strength or resolve. Her character has always been written stronger than that. She has maybe 10 lines in the entire movie. Weak. I enjoy long movies with long sub plots most of the time but there are several minor scenes and plots that had no real purpose to either enhance the story or give character fill-in. It's almost as if they were taken off the cutting room floor. The ending is not strong. See below... ***Potential BIG BIG spoiler*** - Anyone who is familiar with the Superman vs Doomsday comic encounter knows how it must end. Movie sticks to that. It leaves the Bat and Wonder Woman in an awkward scene talking about gathering the others like them. But there is hope in the last 2 seconds of the film. I saw it coming. I think it is tied to the ring Lois was given.

In conclusion, Superman vs Batman was an action-packed movie with at least as many misses as hits. I feel it is worth the ticket. Purists will not be very satisfied and haters were always going to hate anyways, if for no other reason than to pick on the 2nd big hit of the year(Deadpool being the 1st) in an attempt to be part of a counterculture sticking it to the mainstream from their Apple device in their Mommy's basement. Nuff said.

title: Enjoyed it!
review:
This film was getting bogged down ever since its name surfaced. I don't know why all those hate was around. But after finally watching it, I have to say it was just what I was expecting from a superhero movie, nothing too gimmick nor too farce just a perfect blend of story and action. Granted there could have been more to the story but no movie is perfect-10, so we can cut some slack.

Casting of Ben Affleck as Batman was masterstroke from Z. Synder and so was Gal Gadot as WW. Prior to watching the movie I had some serious doubt about them but now all is done and dusted, they truly nailed it, now I cannot wait for Wonder Woman to hit the screen. Having said that, I have a mixed feeling towards Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, maybe the demeanor?

Well, all in all this is a good movie where you get to see your superheros in the action. What more could you ask?

title: Loved it
review:
Well done Zach and everyone connected to the film, It took some big ones to bring it to the screen and stay as true to the comic with risk of critical fallout. Awesome job, Affleck rocked as well, he is a great Batman, Darker, Cynical and just broke. "We are Criminals Alfred we always have been" summed him up.

Superman being more vulnerable than we saw in MOS totally worked, Wonder Woman rocked as well, The Bat looked weak in comparison to the Amazonian and the Kriptonian. Nice intro of the Justice League as well, I have my doubts that that movie will work and I think Snyder does as well Hence the talk of a new Batman Trilogy. I did feel the film was a bit unbalanced toward Superman and that kind of gave me the feeling Snyder has only got to make the film if he used Superman.

So we got the foundation film with a good story from DC without lots of fluff which works for me.DC using Snyder to create a darker and more grown up world of hero's.

I have read some reviews saying it was messy, I think there was one scene that will no doubt get meated out on the Director's cut but apart from that considering the different stories within the film it was put together very well.

It was a Mixture of Watchmen and MOS for me, Good job Snyder.

K

title: A Bloated Mess
review:
Just back from it and honestly, it's not great. The reason Batman starts to hate Superman is too weak, make it more personal like if his wife or Robin was killed. Plus he comes across as an angry idiot, I mean he's supposed to be an amazing detective and can't even figure out what Lex Luther is up to... like why is Lex stealing alien technology? There is only one scene between Clark Kent and Bruce Wayne with a bit of tension and you've seen it in the trailer, no character or tension build up to justify the fight. Oh and what's with Robin's suit and the Joker's message? Nothing explained there, Suicide Squad I suppose.

The reason Batman and Superman stop fighting is just ridiculous.

Everyone is blaming Superman for the destruction of Metropolis but seem to forget about Zod's army and the threat of transforming the earth and wiping out the human race, that was really stupid.

Wonder Woman has no reason for being in this other than looking for a photo Lex Luther has of her... really? She just turns up out of nowhere and joins the fight, OK she's an Amazon warrior and fights for justice but she has no real connection to the characters, lazy writing. Plus other Justice League characters are thrown into it in one scene just because you know DC need to make more money than Marvel... like really fast.

Doomsday, oh my God that was a colossal mess, a GCI mess that can't even talk, this is one of Superman's worst enemies. He just goes on the rampage for no apparent reason, we get wishy washy GCI non stop explosions to the point of boredom.

Recycling the murder of Bruce's parents..... again.

Government heads of state are complete morons and are easily bought.

So that was the bad, on the up side Cavill is excellent as Superman again and you really feel for him with all the grief he is getting. He's relationship with Louis is stronger and there's great chemistry in the acting, so you care about the characters, you don't really care about Batman. Aflik stand over there with Clooney. Keaton, Kilmer and bale, stand tall. Jeremy irons is pretty good as Alfred. Eisenberg is

excellent as Luther, he's the only intelligent thing about this film, he's manic and manipulative and didn't get enough screen time.

A let down after all the excitement and build up, Marvel are laughing their heads off.

title: A film that can't escape the shadow of its great predecessors
review:
OK ... I have been waiting, like every other male on planet earth for this movie since I'm 12..so this review hurts to write, but it must be done. lol.

Maybe it's the fact the this movie can't escape the shadow of "The Dark Knight" and "The Avengers", maybe it's the over exposure to so many super hero films that we're already exhausted, maybe it's too much of a high expectation, maybe it's the simple fact that the film began with bad credit... or maybe it's that the film positioned itself as a mere financial juggernaut wannabe for DC, but regardless of all the 'maybe's", one thing is clear, the film unfortunately can't escape the shadow of its great predecessors.

That being said, I need to proceed based on my own opinion and quite simply that is: I was dissatisfied with the film.

The final battle was so CG'I that it sucked out the potential for related realism, it was too much spectacle and not enough substance. The first half of the film spends too much time in dialogue and establishing characters that we all know by heart, and for the record... I found superman, or just Henry C. to be very unlikeable.

The film lacks an element of fun, it lacks humor, and lacks psychological dexterity. It's cinematography is not really that unique and the story is muddled by a messy arc.

Finally the only thing that saves this film is Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. WOW! Beautiful, sexy, bad ass and having fun as the only hero not psychologically messed up and able to lighten things up. She's presented as strong, fierce and I am for sure going to be in theaters for her solo film. She brought the action to the film and the attitude we expected from the guys. Given she's the first female here to be presented, even if in short version, they got her character right. The intro or preview of the Justice League was decent enough, but could have been better, especially the Aquaman scene.. I mean come one you have everything you need for a killer scene and they still got it wrong.

Ben as a new batman is not terrible, actually he was good... but the story could have benefited from a different approach than the ones we've always seen. As for Lex Luther, he was unbearable to watch, annoying and over the top.

All in all, the film disappoints in many levels, and does not live up to the hype, and for the future, maybe they can hold back on not showing the best scenes in the trailer because as I was watching I remembered "already saw this in the trailer".

The beginning was good, the ending was good. The entire remainder of the film was not, and for something that lasted 2 and a half hours the expectation was that somewhere down the line we could have maybe fall in love a movie we all want to love.

Final Grade C-

title: An exceptional...yet flawed movie:
review: I found myself extremely excited when this film was announced- even as someone who loves Marvel movies. Having watched previous DC movies, directed by Snyder (Watchmen and Man of Steel) I found them very enjoyable as they use a darker and more adult tone- especially Watchmen- than what I have seen many call 'childish' Marvel movies. I was happy to see Snyder return to work on what I see as a monumental task, pitting two of the most loved and recognisable heroes against each other. When the casting choices were announced, unlike others I did not take to the internet to complain about Ben Affleck portraying Batman. Instead, I wanted to see Affleck deliver a new Batman. Having watched the movie, I was not disappointed: Affleck delivered as both Batman and Bruce Wayne giving in my opinion, a portrayal that is comparable to that of Christian Bale's Batman. I was glad to see Henry Cavill return as Superman- for me he delivered a great permanence in MoS and in this film as well. I was sceptical about Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor yet, I feel he delivered a brilliant portrayal of Luthor and it generally scared me in some parts of the movie, with the craziness he was exerting. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman was also fantastic and I look forward to seeing Wonder Woman in 2017. Jeremy Iron's also portrayed a different version of Alfred than what we saw in the Nolan trilogy and I thoroughly enjoyed his performance. Aside from the cast, the movie itself was great but flawed. I feel the main issue was the editing. There was simply too much packed into the film and it jumped around a lot. To cite one critic it was "incoherent," yet I feel that many are too quick to blame Snyder for this issue. During the film my friend (who is not a big fan of Superhero films) turned to me and said 'this movie is s**t.' I ignored his comment. I for one did not feel like listening to movie criticisms from someone who believes no movie will ever come close to the SWTFA, and who thought Olympus has fallen was a quote 'brilliant' film. Yet I saw where he was coming from the first half of the film was all over the place, largely in my opinion because there was simply too much going on in the build up to the fight. Unlike many, I enjoyed the dream sequences and politics in the first half. However, there was so much going on and due to the way it was edited it made the film hard to follow yet I managed. Moving on the action was impeccable, the Kryptonite chase scene was a thrill to watch- yes I know Batman kills people, but again this a different version of Batman. The fight itself was a spectacle; it was awesome to watch these two legends battle it out. Contrary to others I understand (at least I thing I do) why the fight was stopped with the mention of Martha Clarke. I feel that here Batman realised that although Superman is this titan, he also has human emotions and this allowed Batman to see that Superman has a human- side to him, hence why he helped. Wonder Woman's entrance was amazing (even though the second trailer did give it away) and I reiterate that I cannot wait to see 2017s Wonder Woman. My last issue with the film is that the introduction of the Justice League was very forced and I really feel it could have been done better. I also found the ending to the film to be too dragged out. It should have ended in my opinion with the Superman symbol on the floor, instead of being dragged on further. Batman v Superman was an exceptional yet flawed film. The cast was great, yet this was let down by the movie being crammed- similar to that of Age of Ultron. The action and CGI is what one would expect from Snyder. Granted all of the criticisms I have made, I would find myself happy to watch this film again. I also encourage you to watch it in the cinema, because in doing this I think Warner Bros and Snyder will learn from this film and produce an awesome Justice League.

title: Is it perfect? No. Is it good? I think so.
review:
-SPOILER FREE-

Before I went in to this film I was aware of the largely negative reviews critics had been laying on to this film. I heard the plot was a mess, that the characters were all over the place, that the pacing was off and there was just lazy script writing in some place. So, were all of these true? Kind of.

Let me start off by saying I really REALLY enjoyed this film. As a fan of the DC Universe and the comics I really enjoyed the many nods to characters and the comics and the character interactions. This film had to shoulder a lot coming in, it needed to introduce a new Batman, Lex Luthor and hint at the upcoming Justice League. It ALSO needed to have a fight between Batman and Superman, an established motive for Batman and Superman, expand the DC Universe and still try and be a good movie overall, which I think it accomplished rather well.

Ben Affleck's new Batman is great. We got a good insight to our new Batman and saw that it's not a simple Dark Knight copy. This Batman is older, more calculating, and more prepared to make difficult decisions. A warning that Batman probably DOES kill people in this film, if you don't like that you won't like this Batman probably. Most of the Batman stuff is stellar, very well done, and has maybe one of the greatest Batman moments ever. I am very excited to see more from this. Cavil's Superman is passable but there is a feeling it was slightly pushed aside in order to introduce other plots and devices. It's not awfully done, and Superman does have a real ordeal to get through morally, but it feels like it could have been given a bit more attention. The fight between these two characters is great, every second of it, but for me it felt only slightly short, I feel I should have got a bit more considering the title of the film.

The portrayal of Lex Luthor may not be your cup of tea. It's kind of a more insane and jerky character than the cold calculating one viewers might be familiar with. If you didn't like the look of him in the trailers I doubt the film will curve your opinion. For me, he was fine. Not amazing but certainly not awful.

I feel I need to talk about the problem other critics have highlighted, which is largely the plot. It is a slight mess. The problem is the film is trying to tell five stories at once and as a result it can feel rather clunky and disjointed. Despite this, I didn't ever feel lost or confused, I feel it was still fairly basically well explained. I feel there's a lot of need for the audience to 'read between the lines' here when thinking about character motivation. I admit that I was very confused about any of Lex Luthor's motivations until I intentionally started theorising ideas in my head myself and then I understood. It requires a bit more independent thinking and I enjoy that, even if others don't.

The film, visually, is amazing. It's actually a really amazing looking movie. The very beginning of the film is great and I find little criticism online regarding it. I was extremely impressed with just how sleek and atmospheric the film looked and it totally drew me in early.

I feel there needs to be mention of the trailer. And yes, if you've watched the trailer you pretty much know most of the plot of the film. Not all of it, but the vast majority. AND if you've seen these trailers, you know of the other character in the film who I haven't mentioned thus far. I won't name the character, but I was worried about his inclusion in to the film prior to watching it. But having watched it I was pleasantly surprised. He felt a little shoehorned in, but not ridiculously done and I actually rather enjoyed his inclusion.

Overall, the film for me is extremely enjoyable. IT IS NOT perfect, there are things that I think some people are justified for disliking the movie for. The plot does feel quite clunky and if that's what breaks a movie for you, you won't like this. It does feel more like a Batman centred movie than a Superman one, he is addressed but it feels Batman just gets more. Go see it yourself and make your own decision.

title: As Deep As Comic Books Are
review:
This is the first superhero movie that joins action, philosophy and nostalgia -- three elements that were always present in classic comics, especially in Batman's. It's deep narrative combined with the amazing sequence of action -- always artistic! -- makes an incredible aesthetics experience to the spectator who enters in the atmosphere rooted in a tense drama. It demands not only disposition to face tragedy and contradiction, but also surrender to the act of the superheroes. It is all about power, fighting and transcendence; sarcastically funny, powerfully strong, incredibly human.

It should be noted the importance of women role. In most superheroes movies, women are confined to the second plan of the plot; whereas, in this movie, in spite of its title, the female characters are as important as male heroes.

In time, I've heard professional film critics around the world aren't appreciating this movie as the fans. Maybe because [1] they aren't comic books readers and/or [2] they expect superheroes movies to be just like Marvel's movies. Batman V Superman is a complete different world -- with a very own language, which seems film critics aren't able to speak of.

In my opinion, the best superhero movie ever made.

title: Go in with an open mind and leave amazed!!!
review:
First of all I'm going to leave out as much spoilers as I can but I'm only giving a warning just in case I say something that I consider not to be a spoiler but you might see it as one.

THIS MOVIE DOES NOT 100% FOLLOW THE COMICS OR ORIGINAL CHARACTERS AND THAT IS NOT A BAD THING! I'm certain if you go in with an absolute open mind that you will enjoy this movie.

I was skeptical about this movie because of all the terrible ratings and reviews from critics. I would now like to say screw the critics. This movie was amazing. Watched it with my brothers, one who is a huge DC fan and the other who is a huge Marvel fan (they argue a lot on which is better) and they both enjoyed this movie. I myself liked it so much I'm going to watch it again. This time with friends.

I must warn you that this Batman is very different from the other Batman characters we've seen. That being said, Ben Affleck is bar none the best live action Batman/Bruce Wayne. At the end of the day you should watch this movie and judge for yourself.

To save you guys some time I'll let you know there are no scenes at the end of the movie credits.

title: Great follow-up to Man of Steel
review: The only problem I had with this movie is that the trailers gave away too much! It's Batman V. Superman....people were going to see it. Why reveal Wonder Woman's entrance and the presence of Doomsday? The element of surprise would have made the film much more enjoyable. Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, and Gal Gadot (who I initially thought was too skinny, but she looked great) all acted very well. The opening perfectly connected this film to MoS, and I thought it was an excellent sequel. I absolutely loved Batman's fighting scenes, especially when he takes out 2 dozen thugs in a warehouse. Lex Luthor had to grow on me, but by the end I was sold on his psychosis. The action at the end of the movie was off the charts.

title: This is an amazing movie for comic book fans
review: I think people should stop bitching about this film, especially those who say this movie is not fun. This movie is the best movie I've seen this year, and for me easily far better than the Dark Knight Trilogy.Batman killing dudes should not be a shock to someone who has read multiple versions of batman and especially early Batman comics. Superman in this movie was amazing and in spite of not liking Superman, this movie made me like him. The story in the movie was pretty solid if you are paying attention and not knowing certain things doesn't mean it has plot holes. Many things will be explained in the future. The movie has solid action and as someone who has worked closely with CGI and VFX artists I know this movie has top of the line visual effects. Doomsday was pretty much what he was LIKE IN THE CARTOONS AND COMICS AND DON"T BITCH THAT HE DIDN'T HAVE SPIKES! HE GETS THOSE AFTER COMING BACK AGAIN AND AGAIN! What we saw was just the initial form of Doomsday. Batfleck is easily the best Batman in Batman's cinematic history. And about Lex, he's a new take on the character and I know people will find him hard to digest, but what this film did with Lex was the same what "Sherlock" did with Sherlock Holmes; that is taking out all the gentlemanly characteristics and portraying the character as more sociopathic, and Jesse nailed it. This movie is an amazing movie and a must-watch for comic book fans.

title: Zack Snyder is the Iceberg that hit the Titanic
review:
You might feel that I'm exaggerating here but the fact remains. I expected Batman vs Superman to be an epic, a masterpiece but it fell on all facets of becoming a masterpiece. The story was so incoherent and unbecoming for Batman especially after Christopher Nolan's epic Batman trilogy. There was no 'Dawn of Justice' here it should be just 'Batman vs Superman'.

Questions answered: 1. Why was Luthor so obsessed with the destruction of Metahumans? 2. Why was Batman so dumb as to fall for Luthor's trick? 3. Wonder Woman just appears! Yes, she practically just appears from nowhere for no reason at all. 4. The dreams rather the many dreams of Batman, Superman they had no connection at least to this story what so ever, it might be a build up for the upcoming movies but did it serve any purpose to understand the characters or the turmoil of our Superheros? None.

Zack Snyder is literally the iceberg that hit the titanic and caused it's doom. I was so heartbroken after watching my favorite heros fighting so aimlessly in such a mediocre story which could not even arouse a wow moment in it's entirety that I've decided to not watch any Zack Synder movies in the hall going forward.

The depth that each character here needed was completely amiss. You ask yourself and you'll know that just the Hulk and the Ironman fight in 'Avengers 2' had more eye-catching, jaw-dropping moments than the 151 mins of Batman vs Superman.

title: A Review for Non-Comic-Book Geeks
review:
For an all-out, no expectations, leave-your-brain-at-home action-fest, you will not be disappointed by 'Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice'. With an engaging plot-line that maintains your interest throughout, this movie delivered what I expected to see.

The comic-book geeks have torn this movie to shreds, and some of what they are saying is correct, in that there are multiple comic books rolled into one in this movie, and they are deeply offended by the mish-mashing of those story lines. But, then, which book/comic-book movie adaptation hasn't? Even the monstrously successful Lord of the Rings trilogy departed from Tolkien's books! However, for us pure movie-goers, it was a thoroughly enjoyable romp!

A couple of negative points - sorry, have to! 1) The Lex Luthor character was terribly miscast, and I didn't get what he was about at all. I only accepted the Lex Luthor character due to his presence in many other Superman-based films/series/books/comics. But he was pretty pointless, and poorly acted. What was wrong with Kevin Spacey? He played a pretty decent maniac in Superman Returns. Bring Mr. Spacey back in the next one; no-one will mind. 2) There were scenes that didn't make sense to a non-comic-book geek, like me, but did to my comic-book-geek friend. After hearing from him what these scenes actually meant, the Director could have done a far better job in setting such things up for us who have no prior knowledge of this subject matter, without much strain or effort.

In summary: Go see it, and have fun - I did!

title: Marvel fan turned to DC believer
review:
I'm not even sure where to start. I'm not a fan of DC, except for the Nolan Dark Knight movies. I've always been a big Marvel fan. Here goes:

--Slight spoilers ahead--

This movie was so good I decided to make an account to review it. I'm not sure where all the hate is coming from.

The first 40 min or so feel like a jumbled mess, which is why this movie wasn't a perfect 10. But I think this chaotic blend came together nicely to form a perfect middle and end.

I had my doubts about Affleck as Batman, but he became what I thought was the best Batman ever. His hate, judgment, everything was what I pictured Batman to be like. He proves himself a very proficient tactician when fighting Superman. His deduction skills were amazing as well. I kind of liked their approach to Lex, having an awkward looking tech genius be the bad guy, but I see where hardcore fans were disappointed. I appreciated his madness and psychotic ticks, it made him more believable in a way. Wonderwoman made a perfect entrance, although ruined by the trailer. I feel that they really got her right, even with the small smiles while being challenged in combat. Her personality is what I envisioned an Amazonian warrior would have. The reveals of the other meta-humans was awesome, definitely teases.

Tl;dr: This movie went from chaotic start to beautiful finish with an amazing take on each character. Batman 10/10, Wonderwoman 10/10, Superman 8/10, Lex Luthor 8/10.

title: Moving and thrilling - for what's a very complex film
review:
I went to see this film in 3D IMAX, having not read any reviews so as to not bias my assessment. I honestly was so pumped and excited after this film. It even moved me to tears at points, which is more than I can say for any other superhero film. People don't seem to appreciate that DC films are difficult to make. The Dark Knight film set a precedent for both gritty fantasy, but still realism and not shying away from difficult moral choices the hero needs to make. This has pleased the general public. At the same time, lots of these characters carry huge baggage from the comic book narrative arcs - and the comic fans cannot be offended either. Well this film achieves pleasing both - homage is paid to Frank Miller's comic The Dark Knight Returns, where Bats and Supes face off, and to the comics featuring Doomsday. Yet there's no pandering. A new, inventive story line has been written that twists and turns when you least expect it. This is why the feature length will not leave you bored once.

Are there problems? Yes. Lex Luthor lacks a full exposition of why they just hate everyone, and his total crazy twist on the character won't be every fan's cup of tea (instead of the very calm, collected cleverest man on earth traditional take). The sci-fi element towards the end won't be to everyone's liking, in contrast to the first half's realism. Yet with Man of Steel, that choice was already made. There are, as with any film, minor plot holes, such as: why doesn't superman use his super hearing more to rescue a particular person. I'm also not so convinced by the Daily Planet's stereotypical editor.

title: A terrible mistake has been made here
review: No one on the DC side of things has seemed to have learned they're lesson. The big problem with DC is that they refuse to adapt a proved comic into a film. I know that the executives were very nervous after Watchmen came out because it was an R-rated adaptation that was as philosophical as it was violent, and unfortunately it didn't do well at the box office. Having said that, fans are rediscovering the film version of Watchmen and they are realizing that it is in fact an amazing movie. The reason the film was so good is that it was not an off-shoot adaptation of the Watchmen graphic novel, in fact, it was nearly an exact replica of it's original source material. The same was done with 300, but how quickly we forget that adapting a comic exactly as it was shown in it's original comic and onto film is a proved method. So instead of taking on a direct adaptation of Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns, Zack Snyder and the writers decided to take elements from a masterpiece and add those elements into something really crappy. So what exactly was so crappy about the film? The story began, and then consistently lost itself in it's own abyss. We know that Batman and Superman must fight, but we also know that they can't kill each other because they must form the justice league together. So we are given a valid reason in the beginning of the film of why Bruce Wayne despises the threat that Superman poses. We are then giving a somewhat lame reason of why Superman disagrees with Batman's methods of fighting crime, even though Superman is partially responsible for destroying half of Metropolis, which resulted in countless deaths. So Superman takes it upon himself to confront Batman and give him a warning that he should stop doing what he's been doing. We should feel a build up to the fight to come. We should feel the hatred within both heroes bones, to the point that we want them to fight so badly, and not only that, but we take sides. None of these things happened. At least not for me. Instead of fighting on their own accord, Superman and Batman fight because Lex Luthor Jr. pulls off the most clichéd kidnapping known to cinema when he hold's Superman's mother hostage, all the while holding an egg timer to emphasize the amount of time Clark has to kill Batman. Let's stop here, and talk about Lex Luthor Jr. played by Jesse Eisenberg. Remember when we first heard the news that Jessie Eisenberg would be playing Lex? Remember when you felt like there was no possible way that it could end up being a good decision.? Well my friends, our greatest fears were realized when Jesse Eisenberg gave us a performance that wouldn't have even been suitable for one of those god forsaken Shumacher movies. It wasn't just bad, it was abysmal. I remember when everyone thought the worst decision in the history of the world was casting Ben Affleck as Batman. That apparently wasn't true, it was giving Zack Snyder the reins to the DC universe. If this didn't happen, Jesse Eisenberg wouldn't have been cast as Lex Luthor and we wouldn't have had to sit through this travesty and lost opportunity of fandom. I know it's a bit contradictory to sight Watchmen as a lost and newly found gem, given that Snyder was the one that directed it. But that was also back in 2009, before Legend of the Guardians, Sucker Punch and Man of Steel, which all sucked. Below is a series of reasons of the good, the bad and the ugly decisions that were made to make this...Abomination. The good: Ben Affleck was fine as Batman. That's pretty much it for the good. The bad: Doomsday is not only an unnecessary character addition to this movie, but he was also an unnecessary cartoon character in a live action film. Not to mention the play station one effects that were created to show zombie Superman recuperating after being blown up by a nuke. How does that happen in a film that's budget is over $250 million? Batman kills people in this movie. I guess the filmmakers decided to neglect the fact that we've been watching the Dark Knight trilogy for over a decade in which Batman made it a unmitigated point not to kill anyone, no matter how evil they are. Batman's decision making skills are on level of being mentally retarded. Batman severely under utilizes a small boulder of kryptonite and turns it into some gas pellets and a spear. Bruce Wayne also couldn't talk himself out of a paper bag when he gets caught trying to hack files from Lex Luthor's hard drives at a party, and not only this, but his hack is a failure after Wonder Woman steals it from him. Not Ben Affleck's fault. That's the fault of the film makers. The ugly: Jesse Eisenberg. Zack Snyder as the director and overseer of the DC cinematic universe.
