title: Mess of a film with amazing action sequences
review:
SPOILER-FILLED REVIEW OF BATMAN VS SUPERMAN:

So what can I say about Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice? Well first and foremost, it's a mess. That's the bottom line. Cool or not, the way the film was constructed made it seem as if they just threw certain scenes together effortlessly. But this said, it does have elements that make-up for the lack of value in the storytelling, at least to an extent.

Man of Steel was very mixed in the responses, though I was luckily one of the moviegoers who actually appreciated it. And after seeing the Rotten Tomatoes rating for BvS drop to sub-35, I knew something was up. Yet I still remained excited and optimistic about seeing it. The film has flaws, and a lot of them. They are especially prominent in the method by which the story is told: the piecing-together of scenes is barely sequential until the final act, and it quickly stoops to the level of inducing boredom. You try to acknowledge the fact that these were still moments complimenting the story, and you do your best to enjoy them, but all of this wishful thinking ultimately fails. The writers beat the "Superman = bad" idea to a pulp, and you could barely care about it until our two main heroes (later becoming three) confront one-another. Oh, and the "Batman fighting Superman" premise is merely a sort of "debate" until a small but sweet sequence prior to the climax.

Another issue with the film is that it was very difficult to become invested in any of the characters save for Lex Luther, as great as the acting was in general. Bruce Wayne and Alfred had a few neat moments, but otherwise nothing stood-out. They were just... bland; nothing more, nothing less. Clark and Lois were thrown to the side and did not feel significant in the least for the former two acts of the film. When taking the role of civilians, there was next to nothing intriguing about the primary protagonists in the plot; this said though, their roles as individual, separate superheroes was developed very well and was immensely satisfying.

Mentioned earlier was Lex Luther, who was actually a generally more exciting antagonist than what he has been given credit for, actually receiving loads of criticism in regards to his performance and dialogue. To be honest, this couldn't be further from the truth: rather, he is the only character that I actually cared about in non-action moments, and his plan overall just oozed of anticipation. His use of General Zod's lifeless body to concoct a biological weapon, Doomsday, was a fantastic plot point. Doomsday's design was neat, though his face looked very troll-ish and awkward; but all this information known, he was still an excellent addition to the film, and he was a tremendously terrifying creature that was also accurately-portrayed as reeking of raw power. Something else that is noteworthy is the sheer fact that this film did everything in its power to set-up the Justice League arc later in the DCCU, through both brief glimpses of the other heroes and, more importantly, references of Darkseid (which even Luther himself alludes to at the end).

Now to the film's expense, there is a scarcity of action, well at least this holds true up until the massive third act. But in the scenes that did involve fighting, the film just boomed with amazement. With a solid conjunction of great choreography and beautiful effects, this would make sense. Batman's fighting was crisp and satisfying, as did the suit look stunning, and his use of his gadgets was, from recollection, neatly-written. And the penultimate fight with Superman was small in-scale but sweet: it wasn't particularly a spectacle to watch, but it was decently-choreographed, despite being slow. But the final fight against Doomsday was downright gorgeous, both visually and physically. This was hands-down one of the coolest climactic battles I have ever witnessed in a film! Marvel needs to step their game up in their future films to stand-up to this sequence!

In the realm of action sequences, this film really did it! It did not fail to excite me more for the future of the DCCU. But in the department of editing and the overall composition of the film, it is an uneventful collage of scenes that could have been reworked to create a better movie. Awesome, but very flawed. 6/10

title: Expected a Lot More From This One
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is finally here after the many years of anticipation. I liked Man of Steel and was very much looking forward to this one. Batman v Superman follows the question of whether Superman's actions are justified and how Batman, Lex Luthor, and others react to him. So, is it a good movie? Well there are some things that are good and other things that are not so good.

Let's start with what's good first. The performances are great. Ben Affleck proved all the haters wrong and absolutely owned the role of Bruce Wayne and Batman. Batman was definitely the best part of this movie. He was very fun to watch in the action scenes and also his character is pretty well realized. Henry Cavill is once again solid as Clark Kent/Superman. He definitely gives a better performance than Man of Steel and you can really feel what he's actually going through when he's not in the suit. Gal Gadot is good as Wonder Woman in the limited time she has. Jesse Eisenburg is an interesting Lex Luthor and I guess it was decent. He didn't bother me as much as others are saying. Supporting characters were fine as well, especially Jeremy Irons as Alfred.

The visuals are very beautiful. Zack Snyder is a master in visuals and once again he creates a magnificently looking picture. The action and effects are good for the most part. Any action scene involving Batman was awesome. Ben Affleck blew me away in everything he did in this movie. The big fight between the Dark Knight and the Man of Steel is very fun to watch but it was kind of pointless when you think about it afterwards. Lastly, Hans Zimmer's score was fantastic as always. That's about it for the good.

Zack Snyder makes beautiful films but struggles with pretty much everything else while making movies. And it clearly shows here. The story is a huge mess. There are just way too many stories being told in this one movie. You've got Batman vs Superman, Lex's evil plan, references to future films, and the whole controversy surrounding Superman in this one movie. It was way too much. The movie brushes by some of these stories so fast that you get this feeling of incompleteness by the end. The movie, especially in the first half, has very choppy editing. The scenes switch and cut instantly and it's sometimes hard to connect the dots between certain scenes. I won't even talk about pacing because I think the director and writers completely forgot about it. Also there are a bunch of random dream sequences thrown in there but they make no sense and show up in the most bizarre places. They're interesting and fun to watch but it doesn't make sense why they're in the movie. The references to Justice League are very abundant and really not necessary... at all. Lois Lane is literally a damsel in distress in this movie. Almost every scene she's in, she has to rescued by Superman.

If you've seen the 2nd trailer of the film, you pretty much know the entire film. I feel like this movie would be much better received by critics and fans if we hadn't seen that trailer... but we did unfortunately. Doomsday is involved in a dumb way and he looks terrible. In Man of Steel, the end battle was ridiculous and caused a lot of destruction. And this movie is about whether Superman is to be held accountable for that. Well this movie actually has way more deaths and damage than Man of Steel ironically. I really wonder if Zack Snyder knows that.

Overall, I was disappointed walking out. Batman and Superman were very entertaining to watch but the rest of the film is a huge mess. The biggest problem with the film is that everything is just so rushed. I feel like the title shouldn't have even been Batman v Superman because that was only a fraction of what the movie is about. The movie really focused much more on the Dawn of Justice aspect than Batman v Superman. Honestly I don't know what to think about the future Justice League films after watching this. I really hope they find a new director for the future DC films because Zack Snyder really has a tough time with good storytelling, character development, and balance in a movie with so many important characters in one film. This movie isn't awful but there's as much good as there is bad.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice gets a C-.

title: Do the critics bleed? They will.
review:
I watched Batman v Superman yesterday and wanted to state my opinion on it in the midst of the mixed reactions and the huge difference between critics and user scores. This is my first review on this site so please go easy on me.

Story: 6/10 (NO SPOILERS, everything I mention can be seen in the trailers) After witnessing the power and destruction caused by Superman at the end of Man of Steel, Batman fears the actions of Superman are left unchecked and decides to take him on. Meanwhile the world is divided between people who really love Superman and people who really despise him and want him gone and Superman has become a wide spread controversial topic that is being debated all over the world. With Batman and Superman fighting each other, a new threat, Doomsday is created by Lex Luthor and it's up to Superman and Batman to set aside their differences along with Wonder Woman to stop Lex Luthor and Doomsday from destroying Metropolis. Basically if you seen the spoiler-filled second trailer, you pretty much know the main plot of this movie.

Characters: 7/10 Henry Cavil was good as Superman like he was in Man of Steel. I liked him more in this film as he was given more lines of dialogue to show and I really felt for his struggles and dilemmas that he had to face in this film which includes him having to deal with a world with people that have polar opposite views of him as mentioned above and judge him for everything he does. This made him feel more human which I liked. Ben Affleck stole the show as Batman. He was a great older and much more brutal Batman as seen in the no mercy way he deals with criminals and his fight with Superman. Gal Gadot was good as Wonder Woman and her brief appearance in the movie during the final showdown was awesome and many people including me in the cinema were rooting for her as she went up against Doomsday. My least favorite character in the film was Lex Luthor. Jessie Eisenburg was a decent villain but NOT a good Lex Luthor. It totally did not feel like Lex AT ALL. They made Lex a bit psychotic and over the top in the way he talks and acts for some odd reason and it DID NOT work for his character.

Action: 8/10 The Batman v Superman fight was AWESOME although it was quite short (8 min in a 2h30min film) and the final showdown with Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman against Doomsday was EPIC.

Enjoyment: 7/10 The first half which focused on world building and became a bit political was a bit boring at times. The movie was also fairly serious with little to no jokes in it (like in Man of Steel) However (as you can tell from what I mentioned above), the fights were EXTREMELY entertaining.

Overall: 7/10 It was a decent but disappointing film. The best part of the film was the fights and the worst part was the story and Lex. In my opinion, the film is on par with Man of Steel but I wanted it to be better and I'm pretty sure all of us including myself wanted this movie to be one of the best superhero movies of all time as it showed potential but I can say without hesitation that it is far from it. The DC cinematic universe is off to a rocky start and let's hope future films such as Suicide Squad, Wonder Woman and Justice League Part 1 will be better.

title: A dark and gritty take (100% spoiler free)
review:
Having been very much caught in the hype of this movie for the past 2 years or so, I was desperate to avoid spoilers at all costs, and thankfully the internet wasn't as spiteful as it had been on previous big releases (I'm looking at you Star Wars).

I was very ashamed at the bad press the movie instantly received when Ben Affleck was cast as Batman. People were quick to judge the movie and it's casting decisions before they even saw it, based on one bad role (Daredevil). I always remained optimistic that Ben would play the part well and was pleased to hear that it was met with standing ovations during an early screening, this further increased my enthusiasm for the movie.

On the day of release, bad reviews were starting to pour out and my expectations instantly dropped. I went into this movie suddenly expecting very little from it.

After seeing the movie, I can only assume that these reviews stem from people that were already sour about the casting of Ben Affleck as Batman, and wanted to maintain their dignity.

Granted the plot is shallow and some silly decisions are made throughout. I found myself thinking, why the hell doesn't he do this... on numerous occasions, but then I had to remember that this is a super hero movie, and a suspension of disbelief is absolutely imperative when watching a movie of this nature. We're not looking at a movie that is designed to show a deep and meaningful plot, we're looking at a movie, whereby the two most iconic characters in the history of movies have a scrap. That's what we're paying to see, and that is what you will see. Luckily, in my opinion it delivers this plus much more.

The majority of the movie is based around building the back stories of their hatred for one another, and in my opinion it successfully manages to give them both more than enough motivation to fight.

Ben Affleck's performance as Batman was on the mark. He deserves commendation for creating this dark and gritty character that is like nothing we've ever seen on screen before. He's clearly a hardened veteran that is not afraid of getting his hands dirty. I may get shot for this, but Ben has claimed the position as my favourite Batman.

Henry Cavill plays a fantastic and charming as always Superman. If you have seen MoS, you will already be aware that the Superman of this universe is not afraid of getting his hands dirty or taking morally questionable actions. He is not displayed as the passionate and loving Superman that we have grown to love all of these years. Many people hold this against him, but i think it is a complimentary and more believable take on the character whereby everything is not rosy coloured and rainbows.

For me, the stand out performance was Jesse Eisenberg as the absolutely deranged Lex Luther. He certainly has some of the most memorable quotes of the movie, and adds the necessary charisma to lighten up the relentlessly dark tone.

I would advise that anyone going to see this movie, expect it to be darker than any super hero movie before it. I have scored it 9 as opposed to 10 because I'd have liked to have seen more action scenes and the big fight was far too short. Considering the fight was what everyone really came to see, I feel that this particular section of the movie let it down.

I would recommend this movie to anyone, but I feel they really need to go into it with an open mind to get the most out of it. This is not a Marvel movie with tonnes of eye candy, but when it delivers on this front, it is wonderful to watch. I'm really looking forward to seeing what else Ben has to offer the character of Batman in future DC universe instalments.

title: I finally have a (clear) favorite superhero movie
review:
Most superhero movies have been giving me such a huge case of superhero movie fatigue. Not only did BvS not give me that at all, it made me realize why I felt that way with most other such movies. Most of them have a (a) origin story, (b) silly villain plot to destroy the world and no good motivation for doing so, (c) overall story does not relate to the real world at all, doesn't feel like something that would actually happen in the real world if there were actual supeheroes/villains. BvS has none of these and below are some of the reasons for why I love it:

1) First superhero movie (that I can think of) to really show scenes from the point of view of civilians.

2) One of the very few superhero movies (one of them being its predecessor: Man of Steel) to really make you feel like this is what it would be like if people with superpowers actually existed, it makes it relevant to us and not just a "for entertainment purposes only" movie. (The solo Batman movies don't count because Bats doesn't have superpowers.) From showing an actual terrorist bombing attack (like would happen in real life) and showing how even Superman can be totally helpless in such attacks if it isn't prevented from happening in the first place, to showing people wanting to destroy superheroes because they are afraid of them.

3) Best Batman EVER!!!!! He fights like a god and thinks like the world's greatest detective. This is the first time Batman fights like he should in action. Also, he is not afraid of anything (not even Superman) and does not let anything hold him back from doing what he needs to do. Example: there is a dream/flashforward scene with Batman fighting with guns (that's right, guns) because he absolutely has to in that scene and then showing how he deals with real world baddies currently (he is so efficient and experienced and such a bad-ass he doesn't need guns and not because he is personally against them).

4) Best Alfred ever. Doesn't look old or feeble, he's like an actual partner to Batman both physically and mentally, like he could go out into the field with Batman and only doesn't because Bats requires backend support.

5) Teasing of next movie the only way it should be done. If this were some other movie, you have to wait till end credits to watch some micro scene that takes places after the movie. In BvS, this happens within the movie in a scene that feels like an actual part of the movie and not just teasing the next movie.

6) Truly delivers on its title: Batman v Superman. They actually really fight in terms of ideals and there's a physical fight with a winner and and then there's aftermath. I've never really liked the idea of Batman existing in the same world as other superheroes (esp. Supeman), previously that is. Now I like this idea and accept it.

7) Properly deals with the issue of Superman being too powerful. In most other stories with Superman teaming with other heroes, they always, always dumb Superman down in terms of his superpowers! He just becomes physically weaker in their presence (with no explanation at all) and more powerful when he's alone. In BvS, the only point where Superman is weaken then he is is because of Kryptonite; they make his foes more powerful: Luthor and Batman are intellectually/ mentally more powerful than him, and Doomsday physically.

8) Lex Luthor. This is one of the few times I actually liked his character (previously he is either too goofy or totally unrelatable or felt too evil), him wanting to destroy Superman because of just powerful he is and that he is from another planet, all the evil he does in this movie is related and towards achieving that goal. This is how real world bad guys are, destroying what they are afraid of, think is a threat to them. Doing whatever they feel is necessary for their ideal/main motivation.

9) Wonder Woman. She looks hot (without looking like a slut) and physically imposing at the same time. I love how she's not just a cameo and feels like a small but vital part of the movie in terms of plot and action. They didn't overplay or underplay her in anyway at all.

I just loved BvS and can't wait for the r-rated bluray version with extra 30 minutes and the Wonder Woman movie!

title: Solid, Two-Part Plot
review:
Overall this was a fine film. It was nothing spectacular, but it certainly wasn't bad. The casting of Ben Affleck as Batman/ Bruce Wayne was brilliant, and he gave a fantastic performance, surpassing Christian Bale in my opinion. This movie felt like two movies combined into one, though, with the first half more of a political drama, and the second a paint-by-numbers, franchise superhero film.

I felt that the first half was extremely well done, and explored the moral conflicts of having a figure like Superman exist and act unchecked, as well as the comparison between Superman and Batman. A lot of Batman's story in particular was shown, not told, and what was told was extremely subtle. This version of Batman is different, and a lot of people will dislike how the character was portrayed, but I felt it worked very well and was a logical evolution of the masked vigilante. Where Batman's role was a welcome change of pace from the exposition-loaded superhero movies we've had the past few years, the same cannot be said for nearly any of the other characters. This movie is DC's attempt at a cinematic universe, so they had to shoe-horn in and introduce other characters they would later incorporate. Ergo, some characters felt very flat with superficial motives, and served simply to progress the plot. I give props to this movie, however, for several of its decisions in which to take the story, and for using as few tropes as possible in the process. Still, some of the tropes that were used were borderline painful to endure.

For people who are die-hard comic book fans with very rigid opinions about certain characters and their story-arcs, this is probably not a movie you'll enjoy. If you want a popcorn flick that requires little to no thought on the viewer's part, this is also not going to be a movie you enjoy. For those of you who disliked Man of Steel, however, I think you will like this movie if only because it explores the consequences of having a Superman. It had it flaws, but none of them broke the movie for me. Batman v Superman isn't necessarily "fun," but for the most part it is well executed, and deserves a 7/10.

title: Man of Steal x10, dramatic, longer, and with Batman.
review:
The moment has finally arrived, the day every nerd who asked their child friends, 'who would win in a fight between Batman and Superman' The first teaser caused us goosebumps, the first trailer made us excited, the next trailer made us sigh, but the next glimpses restored our faith. slightly.

The huge debate over the nerd web, is whether Batman V Superman is good. I can say it is really good to an extent. So, can we trust an alien form another planet to protect us, a rich disturbed billionaire doesn't think so, and will do what he can to stop him.

Firstly, the film is very good to an extent, but it's not perfect. What's great is the experience. Its mind blowingly stylised, with good cinematography (at moments) great score, and not too bad CGI. But the main issues are the narrative. Like others it does have a lot going on and there are things that can be taken out. I think there is a lot of context missing for some characters, but also parts of the story that are going on, and you sometimes just question what is happening but have to accept it. I could not really tell what directions some of the characters were going like Lex Luther.

Another problem was the structure. It starts off pulling you in and you're hooked but then it declines and loses its momentum, and then pulls it out of the bag in the final act. It is far too long for the basic story, but it does build up the tension.

I can agree that Ben Affleck was a great choice of casting for Batman, in my opinion Bale be better, but was great for this film. Henry Cavil reprises his role as the much darker version of Superman, but still with good will. Jessie Eisenberg plays the very crazy Lex Luther. I don't think he was bad but he was more Joker like than a subtle obsessed villain.

Overall, as Man of Steal was quite big and explosive, and Batman V Superman is more of this, but also much more loud, very dramatic, and has a very dark atmosphere. This makes me doubt the film's enjoyment for younger viewers. But I think in the future of the DC films, there is much more of this come.

So the first acts of the film are not so exciting and powerful, but the film really does explode an atomic bomb of cool and insane awesome in the last act. Dawn of Justice is an 8/10 but it is not perfect.

title: Honest Review From An Unbiased Superhero Movie Fan
review:
To begin, I'd like to notify you that I am not a Marvel or DC Fanboy. I have enjoyed and suffered through films from both sides and I have no bias. Also, don't listen to the critics on this one. It seems like they are all butt hurt Marvel fans hating on DC for mostly irrelevant reasons, and I'm a person who usually agrees with the critics.

Early this morning, I viewed the midnight premiere of Batman Superman: Dawn of Justice at my local theater. I have to say I had been eagerly awaiting this film for over a year and I was pretty excited. I tried to block all the bad reviews and the fact that the IMDb score had gone from 9.6 to 7.7 in a matter of two days from my head. Once the credits rolled I was questioning whether the critics had watched the same film that I had just had the privilege of watching.

I will now start breaking down why the critics and people who say this movie sucks are wrong. First, people keep saying this movie was boring. I completely disagree. Man of Steel was boring. This movie kept me intrigued and on the edge of my seat with anticipation the whole time. And I watched this 2 and a half hour movie at 12:30 AM. I have been known to fall asleep during movies when it's late but I never felt bored or tired in any part of this film. Next, one of their arguments is that their is no humor and it was too dark. One critic says, "...a few jokes wouldn't have gone amiss, either." I don't know if they were asleep or just not listening but there were at least three times a joke occurred and almost the entire audience laughed. Sure this movie is dark and sure there is barely any humor, but there were definitely "a few jokes." Also, DC is known for their dark movies and they proved a dark superhero movie can be amazing (i.e. The Dark Knight) just like Marvel proved a light and funny superhero movie can also be pretty good (i.e. Deadpool and Guardians of the Galaxy), so the absence of jokes should not have surprised viewers. Next, people were saying they were disappointed because they felt the whole movie was just a preview for the creation of the Justice League. Of course it is! The movie's fu(king subtitle is DAWN OF JUSTICE! Zach Snyder created an awesome, visually stunning, emotional, dark, gritty, and entertaining movie that introduced us to Lex Luthor and the Justice League. I do agree with the critics that said things like it was too "busy and overcrowded" and that "it's also cluttered and narratively wonky." But that doesn't stop it from being a pretty darn good film. Before the film premiered, people were worried about the casting choices of Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman, Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, and especially Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. First I will say that the acting in this movie was definitely it's high point for me, along with the soundtrack and visual effects. Henry Cavill did great again as the grim and tortured personification of the Man of Steel, Amy Adams did great as Lois Lane, and Laurence Fishburne's and Jeremy Irons' acting was stellar as well. But Ben Affleck "introduces an intriguing new Batman" that this franchise has never seen before and I really liked it, also his voice, thank God, doesn't sound like the victim of throat cancer anymore. Next, Gal Gadot showed us a newer and slimmer version of Wonder Woman and I think this film made her cool again. I fu(king loved her entrance and it gave me goosebumps (the soundtrack makes her entrance 600 times better, just watch it and you'll know what I mean). Lastly comes the highly controversial casting choice of Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. Critics saw him as annoying and it seemed like everyone hated him. I don't know if I'm weird but I do know I am in the minority here. I absolutely loved this new Lex Luthor. He was weird, crazy, psychotic, zany, smart, evil, and just plain fu(ked up... and I loved almost every moment of it. It was like watching the cross between the Joker, the Green Goblin, and Lex Luthor. Don't let the critics make up your mind, go watch it and decide for yourself. I do agree that their were times where he was annoying and the script was clunky but overall I loved him. To conclude, this movie isn't perfect, but it doesn't deserve the bashing it is getting from critics and people who haven't seen it. Please, do yourself a favor, stop reading reviews and go watch this movie, it is worth your money.

Pros: Visual Effects, Doomsday, Wonder Woman!!, awesome Justice League cameo (Cyborg, Aquaman, and the Flash), Soundtrack, New Batman, New Lex Luthor, Non-Throat Cancer Batman voice, Acting was stellar, awesome court room explosion scene (Granny's Peach Tea)!!!!, awesome superman and Lex Luthor confrontation on helipad, awesome foreshadowing

Cons: Doomsday seemed a little rushed and he died too soon in my opinion, soundtrack was 90% awesome but at times it felt unnecessary and it was just repeatedly bashing your head against the wall (you'll know what I mean), weird and unnecessary dream sequences (sigh, don't get me started with this), New Lex Luthor was too weird and annoying at times, Script was clunky and pacing was clunky as well, overcrowded and seemed like three movies in one, the fu(king trailer (sigh) revealed too much if you haven't watched the trailer DON"T FU(KING WATCH THEM you will enjoy the movie more believe me

Final rating for me: 7.3/10, barely better than Man of Steel, way better than Avengers: Age of Ultron, way worse than Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy though

GO WATCH IT!! Form your own opinion and ignore the biased critics and reviewers.

title: Gone in with high expectations - expectations met
review:
To those on the fence about watching this movie, given the poor Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic ratings - I'm staying up late to write this review for you. I have therefore deliberately kept it spoiler-free.

I am a Marvel fan boy. I've seen most of their properties so far, and they have only gotten better and better at honing their art. Kudos to them.

DC never really got my attention except for the recent Nolan movies. Burton piqued my interest. Man of Steel - though divisive - was entertaining in my book, though I had my fair share of issues with it.

Comics-wise, I've always been more interested in the DC series only because I think the plot lines were easier to follow, more consistent, and generally more interesting than Marvel's. Don't shoot me - I'm just speaking as a casual consumer in that regard.

I went in to BvS with high expectations, despite what I thought were pretty poorly edited trailers (which did not inspire me to watch this film, mind you), and not to mention the atrocious Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic scores. Suicide Squad looks much better by comparison, and is the Lego Batman movie. However, I decided to purchase 2 IMAX tickets (which were criminally expensive at my IMAX theater) because (i) it would be a good 'date night' with my wife and to have someone take care of our young daughter tonight; (ii) there are some actors and actresses in it that I have enjoyed in other movies (i.e. Ben Affleck, Amy Adams), and I respect most of their work so far though not all are critically acclaimed.

Zack Snyder wouldn't be the reason why I am watching this. Aside from Man of Steel, I have only seen his '300' which is strangely hailed as his best work. Personally, I detested it.

I walked away from BvS with a large smile on my face. The acting was good - Ben Affleck and Jesse Eisenberg were my personal highlights. I know some don't like his portrayal of Lex - but my wife found it to be the highlight. Teetering on the edge between that of a wealthy genius young entrepreneur and man obsessively manic over the morality of power -- man could Jesse Eisenberg act.

Ben Affleck is easily one of my favorite Batman depictions to date. Christian Bale's best take on the Dark Knight was in Batman Begins when Nolan had time to flesh out the character. But in none of Nolan's films was Batman thoroughly depicted as (i) a detective, and (ii) a fighter. Christian Bale's fight scene against Bane in TDKR was okay – a bit slow and I did not feel the weight of the punches/kicks (sometimes I wish that these action films would take note from the Ip Man series). In this film, I can see why, from the comics, he had the potential to lead the League of Assassins. Man, did the fight/action scenes deliver.

A side note is that this is easily one of the most visually splendid films I've had the pleasure to watch on IMAX. Don't know what it will be like on a smaller screen, but just on the level of cinematography alone, I was in awe. Much improved over Man of Steel. Larry Fong, well done.

Finally, plot. I have heard a lot of criticisms but given this is a spoiler-free, I can't say too much, but hear this:

1. It was not incoherent, but I can see why criticism is warranted. The editing, whilst an improvement from Man of Steel, still could do with some work. More time could be spent on certain plot lines before jumping to another. Personally, I found the different strands easy to follow.

2. I can see why Wonder Woman feels shoe-horned in, as also with the other Easter Eggs which seem to detract from the 'main story'. However, following the original Frank Miller comic which has a sub-text on the 'meta-human' controversy, I can also see why it makes sense to include another 'meta-human' (other than Superman) in this movie but not overcrowd it with anymore. This actually made a lot of sense to me, and feeds into Batman's story arc and character development.

3. This is not a Marvel film, which is riddled with humour to hide the fact that their properties, too, can be light on plot but nevertheless are great entertainment. I found the dark tone fitting, and the occasional levity appropriate. I left the cinema actually still pondering a lot of the serious theological-politico questions raised in the movie which I felt were cleanly and elegantly answered. The answers were not in my face but could be rewardingly reached with some work.

4. This movie has a lot of 'show, don't tell'. Many plots which, I suspect, would be explored in later movies. They are incorporated cleverly, fleeting, and not distracting. If you want distracting plots hammed in for sequels etc, go watch Iron Man 2 and Avengers 2.

5. My plot highlight was the reason why Batman and Superman eventually reconciles. Resonates a lot with me personally.

In brief DC has done a great job carving out their own identity with BvS, a tone that was set in motion since (flawed) Man of Steel. This deserves at least 80% on RT/Metacritic, and is not a 30% caliber film (I know what kind of films those are, and this is not one of them). This is perhaps why there is a surprising divide between the user review and critics' reviews.

Give this film a chance, bring a date if you will, and form your own view. Whatever it is, you cannot fault the makers for their excellent craft. On a plus side, my wife (who has no comic book b/g) enjoyed it immensely. A double win for me.

title: Expectations - do yourself a favor and set them outside the movie hall
review:
Welcome to Zack Snyder's first great movie.

His previous foray into the DC universe, Man of Steel failed to maintain a focus on its hero, instead succumbing to the comic book genre's fatal flaw of letting the villain's story take precedence, with fisticuffs being the protagonist's only response in the film's final fight scenes. The one thing it did accomplish was to return the Superman story to its science fiction roots. We got a first contact story, an intriguing premise that was let down by a badly structured script.

Snyder's experiment with the comic book movie genre didn't begin there however. 300 and Watchmen were fairly decent, albeit dark attempts and had some success as films. Watchmen's multiple character viewpoints where lines between hero and villain were blurred made it more watchable than Man of Steel.

And that's what Snyder brings to Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. Pitting hero against hero, he switches rapidly from torture interrogation scenes to the deceptions of a debonair playboy, from iconic hero shots to the condemnations of senate hearings.

Ben Affleck's Batman is as true to the character as comics and animation have presented him. An escape artist in his fleeting introduction, he is presented as a tenacious detective, brooding vigilante, fearless tactician and someone finally masterful at combat. There are few gadgets he doesn't employ here with the aid of Alfred, played true to form by Jeremy Irons. Batman is devastatingly versatile with a grappling hook, more than Spider-man was with webbing in Sony's last reboot. When he disappears behind smoke, you realize this is the definitive take on the iconic character.

Affleck's Bruce Wayne is just as versatile. A suave, drawling billionaire socialite who runs a business empire, rescues employees and spies on international mercenaries.

There's also Lex Luthor. A manic, creepy, genius level intellect whose possession of information puts him ahead of all the other characters. Played competently by Jesse Eisenberg, it's a departure from the source material but intriguing in its own way.

Wonder Woman's character was a joy to behold. Gal Gadot holds great promise for future installments. She conveys a spirited warrior with grace and her civilian identity of Diana Prince with elegance and poise.

Henry Cavill aided by Amy Adams provides the emotional core of this movie. They bring a vulnerability to their respective roles as Clark Kent aka Superman and Lois Lane. Cavill is given a more rounded arc in this sequel and the character has greater depth.

Snyder tempers the spectacle he is famous for with character building. The visuals convey conflict on scales that can only be described as Epic.

If you don't go into it with preconceived notions about what the movie, its story and its characters should be about, then you will find a very rewarding experience at the cinemas. Deserves to be seen on IMAX or equivalent for the full effect.

title: Just Another big budget superhero movie
review: Overall, this movie was bad. My expectations weren't very high, but somehow I still ended up disappointed. A horrible script lead to many cheesy one liners, and the actors who brought the lines to life made it even more cheesy. The ending fight sequence was overshadowed by a major overkill with the CGI and some sappy romance. There were a lot of irrelevant and confusing dream sequences, that Failed to relate to the plot of the film. The first act of the movie was very slow, and once it picked up, the film had already lost the interest of most people in the theater. Ben Affleck does a decent job playing Batman, but his performance of Bruce Wayne falls flat. Jessie Eisenberg was a horrible casting choice, and makes the menacing Lex Luther come off juvenile and not very intimidating. SPOILER ALERT: You're going to want your money back.

title: This Movie is AWESOME!
review:
First off, I want to state that I am by no means a film critic. I am simply a massive comic book and superhero fan. I love both DC and Marvel, and I am not just a DC fanboy. I also understand critics having problems with this movie. The plot does seem a bit jumbled at points, jumping back and forth between several different things. However, if you are a casual movie fan that loves superheroes, this is the movie we've been waiting for.

Ben Affleck is the best Batman I've ever seen on screen. I was not one of the initial haters, and I actually went into the film with high hopes for him. I was not disappointed. He exceeded my expectations. I will not give any spoilers, but he actually feels like a detective in this movie. His fight scenes are awesome. Zach Snyder truly does know how to film action. The batmobile and the batplane are also very cool. Henry Cavill returns as Superman. Now, I also loved Man of Steel. I think Superman is about as good as he was in Man of Steel. He does have a bit more emotional heft in this film, though. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman is one of the best things about this movie. She is strong, charming, and very powerful. Her entrance will have even the biggest skeptics cheering.

One of the biggest worries for this film was Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. I loved his character. His voice and gestures can get a bit annoying at times, but he is actually very creepy and I found his attitude to be hilarious. His personality contrasts well with the overall darker theme of the film. The supporting cast of Amy Adams, Laurence Fishburne, Holly Hunter, and Jeremy Irons all give great performances. The action is fantastic, and the fight scenes seem to have been pulled right from the comic books. This movie is not all action, and it pulls off non-action scenes quite well. I personally have never understood the hate for Zach Snyder. I loved Man of Steel, I really enjoyed Watchmen, and now I loved Batman v Superman.

One complaint I do have are the Justice League setup cameos. There is one that works really well, but the others seem very lazy and shoehorned into the movie. Besides that, I had a blast with this movie and I can't wait to see it again. I urge you not to listen to the critics, and just to go see the movie for yourself and form your own opinion. Because I was starting to get worried before I saw it, but actually seeing the movie completely changed my mind. 10/10 for me!

Oh yeah, and for the people saying that Batman shoots and murders people: it's not really like that. You'll see it for yourself when you see the movie, but don't worry! This movie makes me so excited for the future of the DC Cinematic Universe!

title: Affleck is good, story is weak, dialogue is bad. Wonder Woman impresses.
review:
Ben Affleck is good. Indeed, the cast is mostly good. But Affleck shines. The story is weak and doesn't really make any sense. It kinda fizzles out at the end. The narrative raises questions, or appears to, and then throws in some big action scenes to (hopefully) make us forget those questions. Much as Bruce basically forgets his desire to kill Clark and (inexplicably) refers to him as a friend!! The dialogue is often bad. Very bad. Bad enough to make you have to stifle chuckles from time to time. The film has an overly-serious, self-important tone. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex is terrible. He doesn't have one good scene. Zack Snyder seems to believe that the best way to tell a Superman story is to focus on politics, debate, morals, misery, regret and lots of destruction. It's like he read hundreds of comics and thought: This would be so much better with Senate hearings and sorrow. The result of all this is a dour character who does not resemble Superman. Snyder has a clear vision of who Superman is, but it's completely the wrong vision and it's one that nobody is likely to find all that interesting. Except Snyder, who is clearly fascinated by it. And by the idea that heroes should be punished. The Batman scenes are better than the Superman ones, and they always advance the story. Bruce is always doing stuff and getting closer to his goals. Clark, meanwhile, is always moping and saving Lois. Then moping some more. Clark is always miserable. So is Bruce, but at least Bruce is always moving forward. (Until the very end, when he just changes his mind. Because. Because he does.) The movie is too long, but still manages to be quite pacy because we are always jumping from Bruce to Clark to Lex and back again. It's well structured, just saddled with a script that is badly written. Every twist and turn is telegraphed far in advance. Nothing is subtle. Wonder Woman impresses, but doesn't get enough screen time.

5/10

title: Snyder Definitely Delivers!
review:
Dawn of Justice....... *Spoilers*

The movie that we've all been waiting for. Ever since I laid my eyes across that first Superman/Batman logo poster it's been more and more anticipation as the months have gone by. But was this all a big hype with huge advertisements everywhere from watches to airlines, Under Armour gear to the "well overdone" trailers worth it? Would Snyder be able to deliver?

First I'll say this, the movie is not bad, it is actually pretty good. It definitely lived up to the hype. The 2:33 running time was most certainly needed. The story was interesting and I was at the edge of my seat the whole movie. Yet, the way they edited the movie was confusing and didn't show me enough fight scenes between "Son of Krypton vs Bat of Gotham". The way Snyder set up Bruce's(Batman's) hatred was on point, fitting it in around Man of Steel's scenes. And then Bruce about to take Superman's life has a "moment" and decides "hay I'm not going to bother, we'll be best pals now." Would've wanted to see that scene play out a little better... There are a lot of critics giving the movie a bad review, the movie is not a masterpiece, and neither was Man of Steel. But it is jam packed full of action and comic book style moments, which is definitely what we needed. I loved Ben Affleck's batman, he felt a lot more based on the comic version as opposed to Bale's. Henry Cavill's superman was perfect as ever, Gal Gadot as wonder woman was amazing and Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor was damn crazy. The way Snyder introduced other justice league members felt a little rushed and then brushed under the table but that's just my thinking. Hans and Junkie XL delivered a perfect score for the entire film as they did for MoS, ohh the sound of the world engine constantly surrounding Bruce and fuelling his rage.

All in I'd give the movie a solid 8/10. I know it's certainly given me more anticipation for the up and coming Suicide Squad and Justice League movies. Has it for you?

title: **MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS**. A very good movie that will not let down Batman or Superman fans THAT KNOW THE BACKSTORY.
review:
This movie was a really good movie. Not great, but really good. It is a movie that can be enjoyed by everyone but will be appreciated by the fans who know that backstory of the characters. I watched this movie will high hopes and for the most part it delivered. I will start with some of the negatives: 1) The graphics were lacking in two scenes, but it did NOT ruin the movie for me. 2) The desert fight scene felt fake and forced. It was more of an acrobatic show rather than fighting, with fake punches totally visible and the enemies just running into Batmans wanted to be punched... 3) Some scenes felt rushed and could have been explored a little more. Considering the movie is already over 2:30, I totally get that. Some of the positive that caught my eye: 1) It is much more than just a movie. I know the characters and understood every single reference and why they acted like they did. My girlfriend whom which I watched the movie with needed to be filled in after the movie as to why they did what they did. After that she was fully on board and felt satisfied with the movie. 2) The end fight scenes were just awesome (shame the desert one wasn't as good). I can't describe how great it is to see all the characters in one movie. 3) Batmans new suit is great and looks really dark and menacing. 4) The ending of the movie fit perfectly with the whole feel of the movie.

I can't wait for the new JL movies as well as the stand alone Batman movie.

I understand that people might not like this movie but it does not deserve lower than 7.5 IMO. I gave it a 9 because I thought they paved the way to the new JL movies in a very good way. It was dark and full of hidden gems.

title: A Fresh Batman, A Fresh Story, Underrated, Misunderstood by Critics
review:
SPOILERS BELOW - WARNING.

I just got out of the theater. It was sold out. People had to sit all the way in the first row in the corner just to get a glimpse of the much-anticipated movie of early Spring 2016. I got my tickets ahead of time, front and center, and was it worth the wait? Yes.

As you can see I'm giving this movie a 7 out of 10. That doesn't mean it sucks. That doesn't mean it's the best Superman movie ever. It just means it's solid despite critics saying it's the worst Superman movie of all time. I'm going to break down some themes I've heard regarding complaints from this movie and end with quick conclusion and my opinion.

1. First, this isn't your Christopher Reeves Superman. If you are still living in the 1970s/1980s, don't bother watching. Comic books movies and specifically Superman and Batman have gone darker and taken on much more mature themes. This movie, IMO, connected great with Man of Steel. It was almost as if this movie was planned all along and links up perfectly with how Man of Steel ended. It gives Batman a purpose and a connection in this Superman/Batman universe.

2. Batman. This isn't TDK so don't compare. It's like comparing Curry to Jordan. It's a great version, it just isn't Christopher Nolan/Christian Bale good. Ben Affleck got bulked up for the role so this is by far the biggest Batman ever depicted. It didn't have the wow factor and didn't really show the brains behind Batman like TDK trilogy did, but this movie was already 150 minutes long as it is.

3. Wonder Woman. Not talked about much and when her character was fully introduced, it was starting to seem like Spiderman 3 - too many characters, too little time, not enough depth. That is what may be an issue with this movie. Imagine if Batman Begins and The Dark Knight were 1 movie. That would just be torture and make for 1 lousy movie instead of 2 epic movies.

4. Lex Luthor. People complaining need to get a grip. It was a fresh version. Not your TV version with the Adventures of Superman and not your Kevin Spacey version of Man of Steel. Something just didn't seem right here and not enough background was done. Was this version super rich? Or super crazy? Or something else? 5. Lois Lane. It's Amy Adams. You either like her or you don't.

6. Storyline. If you aren't familiar with the epic 1993 Death of Superman comic book, then don't bother with this movie. You will leave mad and whiny.

7. Doomsday. Decent, but again too many characters at this point.

Conclusion: 7/10. This movie comes up short to Man of Steel IMO. But it did have it's positives. I have a key issue with how they did Batman during the fight scenes. It was starting to seem too Ironman 2+ like if you know what I mean. Whereas Ironman 1 made the story and the hero much more realistic and TDK trilogy portrayed Batman as someone very vulnerable, they got Batman here doing something else entirely. I really liked Superman. I liked the ending. The pace at times seemed strange and the editing seemed like they had to cut a lot of the movie out during final takes. Definitely see in theaters.

title: A pleasant surprise
review:
I just got back from watching this movie. I must say that I liked it a lot better than the critics did. I don't think I've really liked a movie before that got panned this bad by the critics. The movie isn't perfect, but I found it to be thoroughly entertaining. Whether or not you like this movie is going to depend on your knowledge of D.C comics and on if you like gritty action movies. Zach Snyder seems to be a comic book nerd, and this film is an ode to fellow DC comic fanatics. Here's a breakdown of the characters: Batman/Bruce Wayne - This was easily my favorite character. I wish they had more scenes with him. This is not definitely Chis Nolan's Batman. This Batman is ripped right out of The Dark Knight Returns graphic novel. He's jaded, and brutal. This is a mature Batman who has endured too many loses. The idealism is gone, only the thirst to punish criminals/threats remains.

Superman/Clark Kent - Speaking of a loss of idealism, that describes Superman as well. The destruction from M.O.S has made many people distrustful of Superman, and it takes a toll on him. He doesn't lose all his values, but his sense of hope has dimmed.

Wonder Woman - She doesn't have a big role, but she's great in every scene she's in. I really like how they tied her into the story Lex Luthor - I was happy with this character. How much you like him is going to depend on your understanding of the character from the comics/T.V shows. Without that knowledge, you might be confused by his motivation. My biggest complaint about the character though is that he seemed to be almost omnipotent. They didn't seem to explain how he knew some of the stuff he knew.

Flash/Cyborg/Aquaman - Some might find their cameos ham fisted, but I got geek-ed up over it.

Overall, I can understand why people would be critical of this film. However, if you're big into DC Comics, and you like gritty movies, you'll really enjoy this flick.

title: Liking something doesn't mean its good (and vice versa)
review: I like super hero movies. I really don't care the brand behind. Marvel, DC, Legendary, Warner Bros, Disney, Sony, etc. All I care is to be entertained while I spend a couple hours at the theatre. Even more so if they go a step further in telling compelling stories in interesting ways. Zack Snyder is a film maker for the spectacle. His entire career has been built in bringing to life stories in the most shiny ways, and that's not a bad thing, but isn't necessarily what every movie needs. I went to see BvS knowing what I was getting into. I enjoyed MoS, I didn't care that much about the usual complaints the movie had and I thought that if BvS were more of that I wouldn't have much of an issue. The problem is that this movie is not. The screen writers of this movie went far into stuffing as much content as they could on a 2 and a half hour movie and the result is a puffy and shiny mess that can be entertaining at times but that fails to fulfill the promise behind the premise. For a movie that puts together on screen (for the first time) DC's holy trinity, it feels mostly bland and uninspired. I found myself, more times that I'd like to admit, rolling my eyes at some of the nonsense happening on screen and failing to enjoy at full 3 of the most iconic superheroes in pop-culture-lore kicking ass on screen, doing more fan-service than telling a good story for us to engage with. And to do so Snyder took almost 20 years worth of comics, threw them to a blender and arranged the pieces to get as many gasps from die-hard fans as he could. If the DC's cinematic universe it's gonna be all about shine and no substance, it's OK, this movie is exactly what they want and need. It's OK if you liked it, it's OK if you felt thrilled watching it, but I whole heartedly disagree that this is what all these years of great DC characters deserve to be portrayed on the big-screen.

title: For fans, it's not perfect (casting) but critics are inadequate to judge this
review:

title: Not the perfect gladiator match, but something close to it.
review:
Gonna start off by saying I could very well be biased, but I wanted to review this nonetheless. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a great way to kick off the DCEU (or whatever they choose to call it). Ben Affleck was fantastic, and gave the feeling that Frank Miller's Batman from TDKR was on screen. Henry Cavill continues to do a great job as Superman, and the dynamic between these two characters is exactly what the filmmakers intended; tense and opposing of one another. The supporting cast was great, but sometimes they felt like filler between big scenes, which is a shame. And as the title suggests, this is definitely a Dawn of Justice movie. The setup for future films was very prominent, which I felt I was going to get based on the trailers. If you're wanting a strict "Batman and Superman fight" movie, this isn't entirely it. And the biggest player in why that is is because of arguably the weakest link of the movie; Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. Yeah, if you watched the trailers and cringed when you saw him, then I can safely say you weren't lied to. Was he a... good villain? You could say so. He did have some very evil-genius moments that I can't deny were well put together, but he just isn't Lex Luthor. Not a modernized version or something similar, just simply an awkward, genius, rich scientist teenager. I hope that if/when he returns in a future film, he is much less Eisenberg and more Luthor (call me a comic purist if you want). But I don't know for sure.

Now, my last thing to point out is the amount of things crammed into this movie. While I can't say it felt like everything was happening at once and I felt uncomfortable with it all being there, I found plenty of moments that, had the editors taken out, would've helped the movie a little. I will say there were one too many scenes dedicated to "Dawn of Justice" When really the film could've focused more on the "Batman v Superman."

All in all, these issues didn't deter from what is otherwise a very good and fun experience. The atmosphere was great, the score was excellent (you've outdone yourself again, Mr. Zimmer), Batman and Superman were excellent on screen, especially together, and the overall storyline felt cohesive for the average movie goer, even more-so myself. If you want a good kick-start to the new DC movie franchise, this is your movie. And if you want to see Batman and Superman fight, you may have to trudge through "the red capes are coming" and some extra Justice League build-up, but the time is worth it. Give me a Batman v Superman 2 as soon as we've gotten through Justice League Part 2.

title: Could have been perfect.
review:
In a nutshell this movie is great. Not perfect in total but perfect in so many ways.

When Ben Affleck was cast I was not convinced he was a good choice even though I felt no one could fill Christian Bales shoes. I was wrong on both counts, Affleck is the best Batman so far.

Not to say I prefer this film to any of Nolan's but Batman looks like the seasoned professional. A fighter and a detective on a level we have not yet seen. Authentic in every way.

Henry Cavill was born to play Superman and you can feel the conflict that results from his rookie mistakes despite all of his power.

I thought Jesse Eisenberg came off as a clown in the trailers but believable in the movie as someone with a deep intellect and capable of great evil. Even when he lost control he was in control. Maybe the best developed villain of any superhero movie so far.

The opening sequence was simply beautiful.

The fight scene between Batman and Superman was epic. I wish I could find a better word as that is really the description we all hoped for and Snyder delivers in spades. You get a sense of that in the trailer and it really is only a hint compared to what is gifted to us here. Lets face it, as much as I also love Marvel, having all of their finest facing off in a parking lot for Civil War is more like the battle of the anchormen from Ron Burgundy 2. The setting and motives behind the battle between Superman and Batman on the other hand while there are greater things at stake has an intensity and gravitas that lends itself to the more grounded approach DC has decided to take on.

Batman sees Superman as a threat. Suddenly he is not in control, at least in the way he once was. So he reacts, it's human nature. I wonder if there is some parallel in some of the negative reviews of this film being a reaction to the overwhelming positive reviews by those who are not professional. Normal people who just see the movie and loved it. If all the professional critics just agreed with the majority of amateurs they become irrelevant. Dunning-Kruger usually makes an appearance in these circumstances.

Gal Gadot for the win. She is not in as much of the film as I expected but great presence when she is.

Amy Adams is always cool. Just great to watch on screen. She gets more character development here than she did in Man of Steel and it gives depth to the story.

There were some weaknesses and those in the last action scenes that to my mind could have easily been overcome. I'll address those in a spoiler discussion at some point. I wonder too if that had some impact on reviews. It's known that people remember how they felt at the beginning and the end of something. So if something is great in the middle but bad at the start and finish they remember it as bad but if flat in the middle but great at the start and the end they remember it as being great.

On last thing I should say. I love Marvel films and I love that we live at a time when it is possible to have comic books on the screen. But a point of difference in style is that Marvel are lighter in tone, described by some as more cartoon. There is nothing wrong with that. However don't expect that from this film, it's deep, the action comes but sometimes the film is not as fast paced because each scene means something that propels the story. If switching off and just enjoying the ride is your thing this may not be the film for you. If you like your mind stimulated as well as your other senses then get along, you won't be disappointed.

The film is a masterpiece right up till Doomsday is unleashed. There are some cool moments after, the arrival of Wonder Woman for example and the fight is good by any standards of other films but sub par based on the rest of this one.

At that point Batman who has been incredible all through really has nothing to do but bring his skills to survive being blasted. That is it.

What should have happened. Doomsday should not have been that gigantic, just powerful.

Batman should have had enough Kryptonite left over to do something but not enough to kill doomsday. He and WW should have worked well as a tag team with Batman giving her the ability to gain more ground.

Superman should have delivered the spear and the outcome the same except Doomsday survives. Batman should have then gone in and beaten doomsday to pulp and destroying the creature in the process. What was implied in the battle with Superman could now be finalized.

It would have been far more satisfying. As I point out because that last battle and the following scenes were just OK people around me that had been cheering and exclaiming delight scene after scene throughout the film up till the doomsday arrival shrugged as the credits rolled and exclaimed it was OK. People remember how they felt at the end and that needed to be better told.

Having said that I saw it twice in the same day and will see it again. Infinitely better than Age of Ultron.

title: Not great, not terrible.
review:
First off, yes, I have seen the film. I watched a screening last night. And I'm by no means trying to offend anyone on here. This is simply my opinion of the movie.

The good:

Ben Affleck was good, both as Batman and Bruce Wayne.

Gal Godot looked like Wonder Woman. Her presence was spot on and intensity was exactly what it should have been as WW.

The Bat/Sup fight scenes were pretty good, at least when they weren't cgi.

Fishburne's Parry White was fantastic

The Batmobile was a great hybrid of Burton and Nolan.

The bad:

Zero character development for Wonder Woman.

Jessie Eisenberg horribly miscast and annoying.

Doomsday was a bad cgi mess.

Far too much. All the Justice League inserts felt forced. No organic building of a team.

Batman kills and he's trying to keep Superman from possibly killing one day. Huh?

We see Batman's origin. Again. 3 times.

The dream sequences were very out of place. Really seemed like Nolan's input so he could "iInception" things up a bit.

title: Some movies are too big for little minds (especially critics)!
review:
This is a movie that does not hold back. Too many other recent franchise sequels played it too safe and, as fun as they were, let's admit, kinda underwhelmed as a result of not daring to do anything new and different (e.g., Age of Ultron, Jurassic World, Force Awakens). Movies deserve commendation when they go all out with their bold choices, even if not all of those choices work, rather than rehash the past. Batman V Superman is a movie that is not afraid of going all out crazy.

Action: Even if you dislike every other aspect of his films, you can't deny that Zack Snyder is a master-class level action director. His sense of timing, cinematography, and choreography, and his visual style have never failed to impress. Snyder always makes sure we see what's going on during the action and never subjects us to excessive shaky-cam & rapid-fire edits, like too many other modern action movies. His superb Watchmen fight scenes got me wishing: "If only Batman could fight like that," and sure enough that's what we're getting in BvS.

Past Batmen can't compete. Past stiff batsuits barely allowed movement, much less convincing fights. Nolan's Bale-man movies did many things well, but the Dark Knight trilogy fight scenes left a lot to be desired. From the disorienting rapid-edit can't-see-what's-going-on fights of Batman Begins & Dark Knight to the clumsy haymaker-heavy brawls of Dark Knight Rises, Batman hadn't really ever been allowed to truly fight like Batman... until now.

Pacing: This is a movie that recognizes that we already know these characters and does not waste any more than the bare minimum amount of time reintroducing them to you. Call it underdevelopment if you want, but I say that's absolutely the right choice. We've seen Batman and Superman before in other versions, so it's fine to dive right a world where Lois and Clark are already a couple, where Batman has been operating for years, & where Superman is already known to the world. This movie jumps right into the plot and the pace never gets slow or tedious.

Themes: Gods among us. How do we deal with them? These are deep concepts, with real world connections. For instance, how often do people with power get blamed for bad things, regardless of whether they are at fault? Can we leave power unchecked and simply hope and trust it doesn't turn on us? These are certainly bigger ideas than simple popcorn fluff such as "Ultron is an evil robot" on which to build a movie. Take that, Marvel :P Seriously though, the epic scale that the DC movie-verse is reaching for is nothing short of ambitious. Beyond simply guys in costume punching each other (yes, there's that too), this is a movie that gets us thinking about grand questions.

Fan Service: As a DC fan, I was pleased and surprised by all the straight-from-the-comics elements in BvS. In addition to the Dark Knight Returns, it also took inspiration from other DC sources, classic and new, such as, among others, from the old Crisis on Infinite Earths, to the new Injustice: Gods Among Us, and the Arkham Batman video games, as well as other notable classic DC series that I won't mention to avoid spoilers. This is definitely a movie for the fans, but what impresses me is that it was so willing to go full fan-service, even at the possible expense of casual audiences who may be not so fluent in the DC Universe lore. In fact, most of the complaints I've seen about how some parts were confusing, or incoherent (notably the dream-sequences), or plot holes, were really direct references to the comics that as a fan I can see what they're doing right away, but may be baffling to casual audiences. I'm sure these things will be explained in the upcoming sequels though. Keep in mind that there's a big difference between intentionally cryptic content that will probably be explained in the sequels and actual plot holes resulting from sloppy writing.

Cast/Characters: - Ben, Gal, and Henry: Awesome. - Mark Zuckerberg, oops, I mean Lex Luthor: This casting was the most perplexing one when it was first announced, but has turned out to be quite inspired. Of course, there could be no better modern interpretation of a diabolical businessman/mad-scientist than as an obnoxious young tech mogul as smart as he is smug. Who better to cast in this role than Facebook's CEO himself?! - Lois: a character who's traditionally been very annoying is not so in this version. No complaints here. - Perry White: Who says anything about no humor in this movie? Perry's hilarious. - Martha: Who says this movie has no heart? I dare you not to get emotional from her scenes. - Alfred: This Alfred is not a butler, but more of a partner. Bruce even brings Alfred coffee. That shows the respect between them. Alfred's constant quips remind me of the Alfred from the animated series (again, who said anything about no humor?), but minus the whole awkward master servant relationship. Great modern take on this classic relationship.

Music - Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL's score: Beautiful, haunting, and bad-ass all rolled into one. Love the lietmotifs. When Wonder Woman's electric cello kicks in, prepare for pure amazement to follow.

Highlights: - Batman vs. room full of bad guys: Holy $#! THIS is the Batman we've always wanted to see! - A single-take action scene in a desert setting that's as visually spectacular as it is bizarre. Some people call this moment confusing, but I say just sit back and enjoy the visuals, because it's awesome. - Seeing the DC Trinity together on screen... I'm in DC fan-heaven!

Final thoughts: I've never watched any movie more than once in theaters. But I'll definitely watch this one again. Good job, Snyder. Bring on the Justice League!

title: Awesome film...I loved it

title: How NOT to do a superhero movie
review:

title: Batman V Superman? V is for Vapid... Let me count the ways...
review:
If DC sought to be unlike Marvel in how to do an ensemble view, then they succeeded beyond their wildest nightmares. However, let's look at why and how it failed...

They tried cramming 40 years of comics into 20 minutes, this would have been better off as expanded into 3 segments - call them Trinity, but this means Continuity which DC is clearly a stranger to?

Lex Luthor - when Gene Hackman played him against Chris Reeve it was as a clown, and to a lesser extent with Kevin Spacey in the semi- worthy Brandon Routh revival. But Jesse Eisenberg as the child of an immigrant? As mentioned in a viral video, he did seem more of The Riddler a la Jim Carrey than Anthony LaPaglia's resolute yet twistedly noble villain in the animated All Star Superman. At no point in the picture did they give flesh to why he hated Bruce Wayne or Kal-El. The reason given at the end for his bald head was inadequate and implied he was about to get the Death Penalty, not just lounge about like Jeffrey Dahmer.

In the mid-80s, Elliott S! Maggin wrote 2 profound and ahead of their time treatises on the Kryptonian - the novels "Man Of Tomorrow" and "Miracle Monday" where he explored the Lex psychose in massive detail, and it was not just a throwaway point Supes made me lose my hair, in fact, that was the least of it... Luthor was doing a once in a Lifetime experiment to create Life without gametes and zygotes with his DNA as the lynchpin of the the descendant, but Superman destroyed it and Lex could not recreate the experiment and thus his friendship for the Kryptonian translated to enmity.

Then there was the Kryptonian ship which housed General Zod, it stated to Eisenberg it was 37% functional and when Lex was about to create Doomsday, the computer at first declined on the basis of the Kryptonian council, even if it knew (at 37% capacity mind you) that this arbiter was now extinct, could it not suggest a logic loop that it cannot break was that contravention of such genetics required a new decision or amendment from the same council - much like archaic Earth Programming a la Windows? Jesse should stick to "Now You See Me"!

How can Superman successfully fly holding a Kryptonite spear? How can he recover from Batman's Kryptonite dust so quickly without using the sun for recovery (clearly borrowed from Frank Miller's "The Dark Knight Returns"), there are too many inconsistencies.

Henry Cavill as Superman is competent, the portrayal of Lois Lane was Meh and never said how or why Supes loved her so, Fishburne as Perry White was a typical Editor/Publisher and Gal Godot as Wonder Woman was probably the best thing for for this sorry mess - she fought Doomsday better than Bats or Kal-El.

Ben Affleck was better and more Batman as Bruce Wayne than when he wore the bat-suit, his fight to save Martha Kent was brutal and again violated the original comics code of murder, yet when placed in reality can be understood if not ratified... It also ignored Batman's early shunning of firearms precisely for the way his parents died.

Luckily I won a ticket via my cell provider, I'd be very annoyed if I wasted my money for this dreck, please wait for Marvel's Civil War which demonstrates the art of plotting, continuity and character depth and motivation in the same time frame as a regular movie - maybe DC should pay Marvel to show them how?

title: Death of Justice
review:
I didn't want to buy in to the negative hype surrounding this movie. While the third act of Man of Steel was disappointing, I thought it was good overall. Batman v Superman on the other hand is a complete disaster.

The story and pacing is all over the place. At times you can be really invested in sequences that are very focused, then it drags and meanders, stringing along set-ups for The Justice League films that don't contribute to the conflict at hand. Some of the choices they made are completely baffling and it's clear they didn't have a unified vision.

Due to the fact that they're rebooting Batman, Superman and he compete for screen time and the set up for their eventual confrontation is like something out of a bad fan-fiction. It isn't clever or interesting and in the end it could have been resolved if they just talked to each other.

The biggest problem is that there isn't much contrast between Batman and Superman. They're both mopey muscle men. There is no grand conflict of ideology and method. The main thing they failed to set up in Man of Steel is Superman's idealism, optimism, and patriotism. This would have clashed perfectly with Batman's jaded outlook, but they hardly ever tap in to this.

I'm sure I'll get excited for the solo Batfleck film, but I don't know if they can pull it all together for the Justice League and quite frankly I don't really care right now. The way everything has to be so interconnected in these franchise films is getting really annoying. Can't a film just be self-contained anymore?
