title: Oh god, there's so much I could say about this movie...
review:
...But somehow I have to condense it into 1000 words, good lord. First off, I loved it. The story did a good job establishing the world our supers are in, and it's a new take on the world's opinion of superman. Unlike in comic books and cartoons, even previous reboots, the world does not universally love Superman. I think that's a much more realistic take on the character that mirrors the world we are in ourselves.

I liked the progression of the sub-plots as the movie went on, between Lois discovering what really happened in Nairomi with Lex Luthor's men and Bruce finding out who Diana really is, I just loved that they gave us little threads to latch onto. (Adding to this, Lois' subplot is the whole reason Luthor gets thrown into jail at all, and Diana's introduces the Justice League, plus Wonder Woman's solo movie).

I liked the psychological aspects of the film. Batman clearly suffers from PTSD, which manifests as disturbing nightmares and reliving his parents' deaths (which I don't think we've seen him have to deal with in life action Batman). I like (objectively) that we see similar haunting emotional turmoil in Lois Lane and Superman, after the events in Nairomi and the senate bombing. ("People died. It keeps me up at night," and "Do the nightmares ever stop?")

I like that they didn't ACTUALLY dwell on the fight between Superman and Batman all that much. I enjoy fight scenes, but I was glad when they finally communicated with each other to deal with the bigger threat -- Doomsday.

Wonder Woman was incredibly bad-ass, for the short amount of screen time she was given. I am so ready for her solo movie next year.

I liked Jeremy Irons as Alfred. He's everything a sassy British butler needs in life.

I especially liked Jesse Eisenberg as a wonderfully frightening portrayal of Lex Luthor Jr. He's clearly unhinged from the start, but he's very good at playing the game and manipulating the people around him. The puppet master pulling the strings behind the scenes, setting the stage for Batman and Superman to fight -- more than that, make them WANT to fight each other. ("You let your family die!" "Judge. Jury. Executioner. Justice?")

The visual effects were amazing, the costumes were equally awesome.

I loved the easter eggs hidden within the movie -- the Parademons, the omega symbol, the Flash, Jason Todd's robin costume. I'm wondering if that leads into Suicide Squad at all, if the Joker or Batman will make any references to Jason at all. I personally love to over-analyze everything with a fine-tooth comb, and I love that the movie left puzzle pieces for people to find.

I loved the interactions between the characters. Lois and Clark were adorable, Clark and Perry were... well, they really highlighted that Clark Kent isn't so meek as his previous incarnations pretended to be under the glasses. If anything, he's more aggressive as Clark than he is as Superman. Clark and Bruce, interacting as their alter- egos, was highly entertaining. Superman and Batman on the other hand, were full of a bit more angst. Lex is, well, Lex, and his dialogues with Senator Finch and Superman were disturbing.

More than anything, I like how the female figures in the heroes' lives weren't swept under the rug like they have been before. Martha Kent is clearly Superman's moral compass, and easily the most important woman in his life (sorry Lois). Martha Wayne was the indirect cause for the biggest turnaround in the showdown. Lois plays an important part in the latter as well, providing Superman with humanizing aspects as Batman is preparing to kill him. These are clearly important characters, not minimized for 'man-pain' reasons, but genuinely important.

All in all, I adore this movie and wish other people would just look a little closer to see what they're missing before they write it off as the "worst superhero movie ever". It's a lovely follow-up to Man of Steel, a great movie in its own right.

title: Big Batman fan... and it was better than I expected
review:
Let me give you a brief background of what kind of batman/superman fan I am-- I LOVE Batman. I don't particularly like Superman...at all. I grew up obsessing over Batman the Animated Series with Kevin Conroy. I adored Tim Burton's Batman, thought Val Kilmer was sexy, and dressed up as Alicia Silverstone's Batgirl for Halloween one year. I thought Christian Bale's interpretation of Batman was subpar, mainly because of his voice... but I won't even start that discussion. I play Batman Arkham Asylum and all that... so do not mess with Batman and if you are going to do a new interpretation of him, better do it right.

Overall, Ben Affleck surprised me with his portrayal of Batman/Bruce Wayne. Ben Affleck is one of those actors that when he is in a movie, I am not lost in whatever role he is playing... I am watching Ben Affleck play a role... if that makes sense. So, unfortunately, I was aware during the whole movie that Ben Affleck was Batman and not lost in the fantasy of the Dark Knight. However, Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman was the best interpretation of Batman/BW since Michael Keaton.

I want my Batman to be brooding but not so brooding that it's annoying. I want my Batman to be a freaking bad ass. I want his fighting skills to be shown off, his intellect unmatched, and gadgets showcased. Batman should be mysterious and be reluctant to a team. This Batman met all these requirements. Ben Affleck played the role of the traumatized orphan with a vendetta well. He means business, and he understands that Gotham City needs a hero/vigilante to get things done.

So Ben Affleck as Batman I give 8/10 I saw the movie in IMAX which made the movie 100x more enjoyable to watch because visually there were a lot of explosions and things of that nature. The action was good. The fight scenes' choreography were on point. Some chase/fight scenes dragged on for a bit. There were parts that could have been completely eliminated... the movie was a tad too long. But, they are trying to set the stage for the huge justice league franchise so I get it.

Jesse Eisenburg did a fantastic job as Lex Luthor. At first, I was like, "What the hell is a youngin' playing mastermind Lex Luthor for?!" But I quickly retracted all those thoughts when he appeared on screen.

Gal Gadot was a decent Wonder Woman-- better than I expected. I am anxious to see how she does when she gets a bigger role as wonder woman. Her costumes as Diana were drop dead gorgeous.

Disappointments of the Movie-- Lois Lane's Role-- she literally played the damsel in distress and gets saved by Superman like 5 times in a two and half hour movie... it started to get annoying.

The ending is overly dramatic when it is obvious that there is going to be more movies.

SPOILER They try and play off that superman is dead... c'mon... let's be real here.

END SPOILER Was the movie everything I had hoped for? No. Was it enjoyable and entertaining? Yes. Will I own it? Of course because it has freaking Batman in it! Go into the movie with realistic expectations, and you will be pleasantly surprised and highly entertained. Worth seeing it in a movie theater if you want to fully enjoy the action-y parts.

FYI-- there is no after credit scene...in case you're wondering.

Enjoy

title: Enjoyable? Totally. A good film? Not so much.
review:
Now before anything, I've been waiting for this movie since it was announced. I'm a DC fanboy and the darker the movie, the more it amuses my palette. Also, I ask everyone to go watch the movie without watching or reading anything even related to it. Getting to it, The movie was totally worth everything. This is the superhero movie we all deserve, the one we were waiting for. The first half feels like a good thriller. The script is tight, it keeps you on the edge of the seat as things get dark and intense. The second half, storytelling mostly goes for a toss, as everyone tightens their fists. I feel like I would have enjoyed it a lot more if I hadn't seen a single trailer. The pacing of the movie just doesn't work, don't know if the screenplay is to be blamed or the editing. Minutes have been wasted just pushing plots for future movies, though the fanboy in me was dancing, it wrecks BvS as a standalone movie. Now Zack Snyder, never lets you forget that he is the director of the movie. The movie is a Visual Treat, many a times a beautiful mess. You can count the number of times he chooses style over substance. I wouldn't have preferred any one else to bring all that action to life, but then the number of missed opportunities is too many. Ben Affleck is the best on screen batman. I couldn't have asked for anything more. He surpasses Keaton's Wayne as well. Henry Cavill was as good as the Man of Steel, and Gal Gadot nails Wonder Woman. Coming to the character with all my favorite scenes, Lex Luthor. Now this isn't your comic book Luthor. He is umm, Batshit crazy? Loved how all the characters were developed and treated, Superman's alienated god was really well done. Though Batman is overly sensitive to everything. Mainly because of all those little hints given throughout the first half. (Just to set up Batfleck's solo movie, everything will probably be explained then.) The soundtrack is on point (Loved wonder woman's theme), no complaints with cinematography too. Some shots were incredible. The IMAX is totally worth it. All the costumes look amazing, never mind the CGI character.

Overall, I loved the movie. I'm probably watching it in IMAX again.

title: Disjointed film; interesting Batman, bad plot
review: I was very excited about the movie but sorely disappointed after watching it tonight. I quickly realised that I would only watch the movie once. The plot is all over the show, some scenes are very odd, and Zach Snyder tries to do what only Christopher Nolan seems to be able to do well in a movie - develop concomitant related threads of a plot and join them up in an organised fashion. Except Zach Snyder fails miserably. Lex Luther is way over the top, and the idea of how the two main superheroes co-exist in this 'world' is scarcely believable (if one is to believe anything about superhero movies - but Nolan was able to do that with Batman, and Snyder did it well with the first Superman). Maybe the premise itself was always too far fetched. The positives are an interesting Batman, who has less scruples than the Nolan Batman; some nice one liners, some good action scenes, and a nice intro to the movie that connects us to the recent Superman movie. I don't know how the follow ups are going to lift the series. Disappointed.

title: Epic, spectacular, but one step below masterpiece
review:
Zack Snyder's Batman v Superman is epic and spectacular, and like his every other movie visually stunning. The fight sequences are well choreographed. The opening sequence is really great and serves as a reminder of what Batman is all about. It would have been a masterpiece, in superhero genre, if only it had the clarity and continuity of Nolan's Dark knight trilogy, especially The Dark Knight.

As far as the story and screenplay is concerned, I fully expected it to be something beyond expectations as David S. Goyer, one of the writers of Dark Knight trilogy, is also the co-writer of this film, but he along with Chris failed to deliver a great script with flawless continuity and they completely screwed up the way they handled some of the Easter eggs of the Justice League. I loved how the film sets up the premise for Justice League, but one scene in particular just doesn't make sense, and strictly speaking, it should never have made it in to the final cut of the film.

Now back to the topic of why this movie is great. I still remember the controversy during the casting of Ben Affleck, and Jesse Eisenberg, but they are most certainly two of the best things in the movie. Their portrayal of Batman and Lex Luthor is simply amazing. Affleck draws out the dark side of Batman while Eisenberg embraces the insanity of Lex.

Speaking of Batman, one thing I love the most is the way he uses his toys, and Batman v Superman surpasses any other Batman film till date in depicting this. If you are nuts about Batman kicking ass using all the gadgets in his arsenal, then this movie is definitely for you. When it comes to Superman, there is nothing much to say other that his character is well defined in this movie than in Man of Steel.

As for few other things, Gal Gadot is breathtakingly beautiful both as Diana Prince and Wonder Woman. Now, I am really looking forward to her movie. I never expected the film to have a bit of an emotional side to it, and it was a pleasant surprise as that part of the film delivers what it should deliver.

title: Makes Marvel movies look childish
review:

Overall, a great movie and as the title suggested this movie makes Marvel movies look childish and I meant no disrespect. Sure, Marvel movies are fun and entertaining too, but it's more dumbed down for little kids whereas this movie is dark. I loved it and it brought back memories of the Michael Keaton Batman days. I cannot wait for the Uncut/uncensored version that Zack Snyder is promising in the BluRay release in a few months. Go see this movie at the Cinemas, it's that good.

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn Of Justice
review:
The film follows the events after 2013's Man Of Steel and introduces Bruce Wayne in the story, which features a new incarnation to the character.

One aspect of the difference between Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy and this is that this is a darker imagination of Bruce Wayne, who is prepared to face Superman for the actions that happened during Man Of Steel. While the film focuses on Wayne's hatred for Superman, we're introduced to Lex Luthor and his plans on chaos. This is one of those films where knowing too much of the plot will affect the viewing process of this well written tale.

The film focuses on the characters very well, with Ben Affleck shining as his role as Bruce Wayne/Batman.

One important step in achieving a viewing is it's sound design. The sound is indeed loud and at times will give you the jumps. The brilliance of Hans Zimmer in the score has a mix of emotions, perfectly telling the tale.

A well written story, but could be a hindrance due to the long run time at 2 hours 40 mins (the original cut was to have been 3 hours).

title: Absolutely amazing!
review:
Even though the story has its problems, especially with pacing and explaining certain events - I can't quite understand the critics attitude towards this movie. It is absolutely stunning, both visual and story wise, not to mention it was a bold move to take on a story like this with so many things that could go wrong.

I must say that the cast delivered brilliantly, especially Affleck, considering the amount of hate received once he was announced as the new Batman.

For the first time ever we have a Batman as he really is, as he should be - brutal and led solely with desire for justice and safety for his city and man kind, using brute strength and intelligence in the process. Absolutely loved Ben's performance and Batman's character is a lot more like the original DC's Batman, as seen in comics or animated series rather than some improvised version.

I will see it again... And again... And yet again. And I would recommend it to... Anyone, really.

Hope to see a lot more from these guys!

title: I wanted it to be great but sadly its just okay
review:
First of all I have to write that I was a huge Man of Steel fan so I wanted BvS to be as good or even better! The movie has positives but also negatives and critics have been somewhat right on their reviews. From a fan point it has couple of truly great comicbook movie moments, looks great and action is very well shot. Sadly there is actually only a few action pieces in the movie considering its 2,5hour movie. The main fight between Batman and Superman is maybe 10mins if even that.

Casting wise they did a good job. Ben Affleck truly nails older battle weary Batman. Gadot is good Wonder Woman but she is on the screen so little that it could have been really anyone. Irons is great Alfred but Eisenbergs Luthor was... Well... different... Some people seem to hate him, so people seem to love him. I didn't really care much of him... Main problems with Lex are that his motivations and what drives him are never clear and people are left wondering why he did what he did.

The main problems of the movie are its focus and pacing. The first 90mins or so of the movie it keeps following 4-6 subplots at the same time and its jumping all over the place because of that. It can be tough to follow at the times. The world building for larger DCU is there and mostly it is done well with the exception of "dream sequences"... They are left way too vague and never talked again afterwards.

Also the ending is two edged sword. I personally felt that this was not the time or place for doomsday. I understand why they did it but in my opinion he was wasted here and he didn't seem like big thread enough to warrant the trinity nor the outcome where it all lead into.

Its worth seeing but sadly its not amazing...

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
review: This movie featuring the most famous DC Comics characters was hyped up so much before it's release, it initially started with a high gross, but suddenly dropped in figures, I knew I wanted to see it no matter what, from Razzie nominated Zack Snyder (300, Watchmen, Sucker Punch, Man of Steel). Basically in Metropolis it has been eighteen months since the destructive attack of General Zod (Michael Shannon), Superman (Razzie nominated Henry Cavill) has become a controversial figure, meanwhile, as his human alter ego Clark Kent, he has moved in with Lois Lane (Amy Adams). Meanwhile billionaire Bruce Wayne (Razzie nominated Ben Affleck) has operated in Gotham City as Batman for nearly two decades, he suffered the death of a friend in the destruction of Metropolis, he sees Superman as a threat to humanity, Superman views Batman as a threat learning of his activities. Wayne learns that LexCorp's mogul Lex Luthor (Razzie winning Jesse Eisenberg) has been in contact with Russian terrorist and weapon- trafficker Anatoli Knyazev (Callan Mulvey), meanwhile Luthor is trying to convince Senator Finch (Holly Hunter) to allow him to import a source of Kryptonite found in the Indian Ocean, claiming it is a deterrent against "Kryptonians", he also tries to gain access to Zod's body and the Kryptonian scout ship, Finch denies his request. Wayne attends a party at LexCorp, there he meets Kent, and he meets mysterious antiques dealer Diana Prince (Gal Gadot), before retrieving data from the company's mainframe, but Prince steals this, but unable to decrypt it she later returns it to Bruce. He begins the process to decrypt the data in the Batcave, whilst doing so he has a vision of a post-apocalyptic future, he leads a rebel force against Superman, a mysterious time traveller who urges him to find "the others", the data reveals what this figure was talking about. Wayne realises that Luthor is not experimenting with Kryptonite, he is investigating metahumans, one of them is Prince who is an immortal warrior, Wayne admits to his butler Alfred Pennyworth (Jeremy Irons) he plans to steal the Kryptonite to weaponize it against Superman, as Batman he pursues the convoy carrying the element, but Superman shows up and orders him to cease his activities. Superman is summoned by Senator Finch to stand before a congressional hearing to be questioned and justify his existence on earth, Finch and thousands of people are killed in a bombing by orchestrated Luthor s a bombing at the hearing, frustrated he did not save anyone Superman goes into self-imposed exile, Batman breaks into LexCorp and steals the Kryptonite, using it to create a Kryptonite grenade launcher and a Kryptonite-tipped spear, meanwhile Luthor enters the Kryptonian ship and learns recorded alien information. Luthor kidnaps and holds hostage Kent's adoptive mother Martha (Untraceable's Diane Lane), he reveals he has been sending messages to Batman and Superman to increase their animosity towards each other, Luthor forces Superman to fight Batman to spare Martha's life, Superman tries to reason with Batman, but a fight is initiated. After fighting Batman subdues Superman, before he can kill him with the Kryptonite spear Superman begs him to "save Martha", Wayne's late mother was also named Martha, Lane arrives and explains the situation, learning Luthor's plan Batman and Superman work together to save the city, also joined by Diana, aka Wonder Woman. Luthor unleashes a monstrous creature created by the splicing of his own DNA and Zod's body, the creature outmatches Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman with its ability to absorb energy, Superman realises it is vulnerable to Kryptonite, he sacrifices himself, retrieving the Kryptonite spear, impaling and destroying the creature, Superman is killed. Luthor is arrested and imprisoned, with his hair shaved off, he gloats to Batman who visits that earth is vulnerable to powerful alien threats, Metropolis hold a memorial for Superman, Clark is also declared dead, a private funeral is held in Smallville with Wayne, Lane and Diana attending. Martha reveals Clark to Lois that Clark had an engagement ring, Wayne tells Diana he plans to form a team of metahumans, starting with those identified in Luthor's files, to protect the world, but Superman may not be dead, as Clark's coffin stirs. Also starring Laurence Fishburne as Perry White, Tao Okamoto as Mercy Graves, Ray Fisher as Cyborg, Scoot McNairy as Wallace Keefe, Jason Momoa as Aquaman, Christina Wren as Major Farris, Harry Lennix as Swanwick, We Need to Talk About Kevin's Ezra Miller as The Flash, Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Thomas Wayne, Lauren Cohan as Martha Wayne, Kevin Costner as Jonathan Kent, Terminator 2: Judgement Day's Silas and Patrick Wilson as POTUS. Cavill is still just about bold and brave in the blue and red suit, Affleck was a controversial choice but proves fairly good as the Caped Crusader, Eisenberg is over the top at times but a reasonable manic villain, and there is alright support from Adams, Fishburne and Irons. This was one of the big dreams for superhero movie and comic book fans, the Man of Steel versus the Dark Knight, and the first big screen appearance of Wonder Woman is welcome, the majority of the movie however is boring, the actual fight is only relatively gripping, and it is a pointless story, all the budget is wasted on the special effects and no thought put into anything else, it is just an underwhelming, lacklustre and disappointing fantasy action film. It won the Razzies for Worst Screen Combo for Affleck & His BFF (Baddest Foe Forever) Cavill, Worst Screenplay and Worst Prequel, Remake, Rip-Off or Sequel. Adequate!

Secondly , Lex wasn't trying to say that superman used guns to shoot everyone , he was making implying that superman had something to do with the murders , not that he was directly the cause of it....you know...being in the right place at the wrong time , and of course, the media caught wind of the event and made up their own stories . doomsday was tolerable , not good , but tolerable ( the fight scene was cool though) and lex was a great villain, one of most terrifying incarnations of lex even though he didn't look that part . Bruce believed that superman brought the world engine and all this destruction here to earth and believing in that misconception plus the other factors from Lex caused him to wear the cowl once again and fight the man of steel . So agree with me or not , I just wanted to clear some misconceptions up about the movie to anyone who cares to listen I really like this movie and I can't wait for Civil War .ï»¿

title: Zack Snyder gets it right and I am sorry Ben Affleck.
review:
When it was first announced that Ben Affleck would be portraying the dark knight, I flipped a table over in rage. He does not appeal to me as an actor and I couldn't wrap my head around this choice. Needless to say, I spent many weeks bashing the movie and even refusing to go see it. Boy was I wrong...

As an avid comic book fan and one who is well versed in the DC universe, I was BLOWN AWAY! I was stunned. I was floored. Never was there a more perfect Batman in a film. They finally portrayed Batman THE WAY HE IS IN THE COMICS! He's shown grappling and using his gadgets and we also see Alfred as more than just a butler and confidant, but as an active participant in Bruce's crusade against the criminals of Gotham.

Some people compare Christopher Nolan's Batman franchise to Zack Snyder's version, but what they don't understand is that these are two entirely different versions. Nolan's Batman universe presents a "real-life" Batman, if Bruce Wayne was a present day individual. Snyder brings the comic books to life.

The movie got the visual aesthetics perfect, the only area that needed a little work was the plot. If you aren't acquainted with the graphic novels then the movie will confuse you, that's where I felt the issue was. They didn't give enough background info for those who don't know the graphic novels. For example, I was reading that a lot of people were confused about Superman's death, but if they knew about "Death of Superman" they would understand that there was a reason Amy Adams was on screen more than we would have liked, at least that's how I feel. Now, if you read the comics, the black and silver coffin might have made you pee your pants a little.

Another area I noticed people complaining about, was how dark and gloomy the movie was. If you know the DC universe it's actually quite violent and dark, so are some Marvel comics but Disney doesn't have the balls to go there in my humble opinion. How perfect was the death scene of Mr and Mrs Wayne? The way the gun takes hold of the pearl necklace, it's never been shown this way before. It was tragic and heart breaking but a perfect mini intro and refreshment to Bruce Wayne.

Another issue was the lack of comic relief. Why is that even necessary? Why do we have to fill movies with bad jokes and meager attempts to elicit humor. I laughed a few times in the movie, I didn't feel we needed more "jokes". This is not a kid's movie and it's not meant to be. Sorry parents, leave the kiddies at home for this one.

This is a movie for comic fans and not just "Batman" fans. Batman was created by Bob Kane in the 1930s, not a lot of people know this. They think Batman was created by the producers of the Adam West series or Tim Burton. A lot of the heat this movie faced is being spread by people, that I feel, have no idea about the history of Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, or DC.

Zack Snyder did an excellent job of bringing a comic book to life, hands down. The writing could have used a little work but did not take away from the overall experience. Ben Affleck was a phenomenal Batman (again, sir, well done!) and for the first time EVER we got to see Batman and Superman go head to head in IMAX 3D, what more could you ask for?

title: If You've seen the second trailer, you've seen everything
review:
First of all Batman and Superman are my childhood heroes but i'm not going to say this movie is amazing just for the sake of batman and superman being in one movie. Batman Vs Superman at times feels like an 2 and half hour extended trailer to promote the next movie.

The problem with the Batman Vs Superman is that it attempted to do what Marvel did, in only 2hrs and 30 min. The story is so discombobulated and messy and not to mention poorly structured at times. It tries to cram in too many things instead of taking its time. With that being said, the movie still has something that gets you through the whole thing and keeps you entertained despite some of the pacing problems and directorial issues.

Ben Affleck absolutely nails it as Batman and Bruce Wayne and i cant wait to see him in a solo film because he delivered the batman we have all been waiting for! I don't think Henry Cavil is better than Christopher Reeves but he works for Zack Snyder's world so i somewhat enjoyed his performance.

There was an annoying over abundance of Lois Lane scenes that were completely unnecessary and could of easily been replaced with scenes of batman.

I cannot believe that Zack Snyder was handed the property of Batman Vs Superman, a movie with two of the most iconic heroes in pop culture, and had the audacity to fill up the movie with so many flaws to the point it over shadowed the whole thing. I really hope DC get their sh*t together and stop being so concerned with catching up to Marvel.

If you've seen the second trailer for the movie, you really have seen the whole film. The second trailer to me it isn't a trailer, its a short film basically summarising a 2 and a half hour movie in only 2 minutes. The movie starts off good but then takes a turn and becomes a CGI fest.

You should still see the movie. Its not bad and there are great scenes it in it. Visually the movie looks amazing and the movie as a whole will keep you entertained but you will notice a lot of lazy writing and how messy the plot is. The movie is OKAY but there really isn't anymore surprises due to the over promotion of footage that was released.

review: The overall movie is enjoyable. but the 1st half of the movie hardly had any action scenes at all, which is not preferred (and kind of strange) for a superhero movie. particularly one featuring 2 major superheroes and especially when they were expected to fight with each other (from the title and trailers etc). to be fair, this part of the movie is not boring, just won't feel much like a superhero movie. the later about 1/3 rd of the movie has quite good action, but buy this time you would have waited a bit too long. title: Intense Action, Deplorable Storytelling
review: Soooo...hearing mixed opinions about this movie, I decided to go in with an open mind. And the more I watched, the more I really tried to see some light in the midst of this morbid portrayal of these comic hero's, but alas, the cacophony of absurdities dramatically overwhelmed my viewing experience. Suffice to say, if what you want to see in a movie is intense special effects, buildings falling, fires burning, fists bashing, and actors grimacing, then this movie is for you. But if you value any kind of reasonable plot flow, authentic character motivations, logistical actions, and at least a shred of an inspirational tone in a superhero movie, then you likely WILL NOT enjoy this movie. At least, this is my verdict on this one anyway.

title: DC can do better, they have to..
review: Opinions don't matter here; DC "fanboy" or Marvel, it doesn't which side you're rooting for or against, what matters are the facts. And the fact is when you have a movie that was such a mess on so many levels, where it had potential to be great, that it gave Ben Affleck Daredevil flashbacks and is causing Warner Bros. To reconsider their plans for a DC Cinematic Universe, things need to change. Fanboys for the movie will say it was perfect, when deep down even they know it was depressingly flawed. Fanboys against it won't give it any credit despite the movie having some good in it. Fanboying only hurts, it never helps. For me, it was disheartening to see characters and stories that I love be treated so poorly but it was just as sad to see so many dedicated actors and set makers in a movie this sub-par. Most of the rumors you've probably heard are true; the pacing was slow, some acting performances were better than others, but what really got me was the characterization, narrative direction, and lack of technical prowess that really bogged this movie down. While I applaud Ben Affleck's performance as Batman, more on that later, the motives of the Batman he portrayed were more inline with a petulant child overreacting, rather than the cold, calculating, brooding detective that values life. Jessie Eisenbeg is a fine actor,and he's shown us his skill before, but his depiction of Lex Luthor felt like a poorman's Joker. And Superman....I long for the day when we'll see a charismatic, inspiring Action Ace. I don't blame actors, for I know they can deliver better performances if allowed. Instead,I question the source of their direction. Zack Snyder is an artist when it comes to visual spectacle, but his ability to create a compelling, coherent narrative is almost none existent. In any film, the inability to forge a narrative is a problem, but with a movie that's supposed to serve as the launching point for an entire universe, bad storytelling is downright unacceptable. A major criticism I kept hearing was that this movie lacked heart. I think it did have heart but lacked direction and it suffered greatly for that reason. There's some hope for the future, Ben and Henry have potential to be great but they need better direction, the whole DCU needs it. Until they change things, DC will continue to achieve Pyyrhic victories with their films, raking in big bucks but tarnishing names and never fully realizing the potential their characters, stories, and storytellers have.

title: Amazing
review:
I cannot remember a movie this polarizing. Fans absolutely love it or hate it. After seeing it twice, I loved it. I know we all have different views on things, but here are a few of my thoughts:

Ben Affleck was great as Bruce Wayne/Batman. I never really had a doubt that he wouldn't be. He brought a unique take to the character that I enjoyed. Same can be said for Gal Gadot. Although her time on screen was limited, she was very captivating. So many things worked well together under the direction of Snyder. The score and cinematography were just epic. From the very first minute I was hooked.

This movie had its faults though. I was able to look past them, but I can understand why others refuse to. The movie just had so much it had to get in, the plot got a bit crazy. The justice league tie-ins would have been better as an after credit scene. Not right before the epic fight between Batman and Superman. And yeah some of the CGI made me laugh. But if you can't suspend your disbelief and enjoy this stuff, why are you at this movie to begin with? Overall, I think Snyder did a great job. He took the movie where a marvel movie would never go, which was refreshing to me. It felt real. It portrayed the fear I think we would all have of a man with the kind of power Superman has. Kudos to all involved. 9/10.

title: A big mess that shows that Marvel still rules the game.
review:
How do you go wrong with a title like Batman vs Superman? Apparently Zack Snyder has managed to do that with a movie that is full of interesting concepts but terrible plot and writing.

First and foremost I want to say that what bothers me the most is that I did neither really like or really hate this move. That is the biggest problem with the new DC universe in my opinion.

This was supposed to be DC's big movie. If this movie would have been good this would really put DC on map again. Sadly this was nothing special and nothing but a big "meh" for me.

The acting is pretty solid with an extraordinary good performance from Ben Affleck and Jeremy Irons but unfortunately a terrible performance from Jesse Eisenberg.

The worst thing about this movie is that it is so caught up in setting up its own sequel that it forgets to be good itself. Some characters don't get the proper big screen introduction they need witch could really confuse some viewers. This is a movie is a good example of what happens when you put style and quantity over substance and quality.

However I don't straight up hate it. The strengths with this movie is definitely in the first half. It plays with some interesting concepts and ideas but unfortunately never really dare to go there. I really liked the court scene but they never really used the full potential they could have got from that event.

In the beginning, the movie almost presents itself as a thinking mans war but as it goes on you start to realise hat it lacks the intelligence to accomplish that. The plot is full of unexplainable holes that is straight up stupid.

The last act of this movie is a big mess and does really drag the movie down. If I were you I would probably save my money for Civil War.

5/10 Interesting ideas but an unfocused plot that delivers very rarely.

title: Three syllable word too big for little minds.
review:
The other day, a friend posted how much they were looking forward to the TV Supergirl and Flash crossover; more than the cinematic version of their DC counterparts. I sat back in my chair, exhaled and thought, "Really?". Having seen this movie twice now, you have to really be in awe at the stupidity of very harsh reviews towards this movie. Everyone, and I mean everyone makes it sound like it's another Catwoman. No way BvS is on par, or even the 29% Rotten Tomatoes rating it makes it out to be.

Speaking of The Flash TV show, I sat through four episodes of the first season before I pressed the off button on the remote. And the only reason I sat through those four tiring and overly boring episodes was just to see Wentworth Miller's character, who was more remarkable in his role than Grant Gustin's awkwardly goofy Flash, in a show riddled with vomit-inducing teen drama that plays out like a superhero version of Sex and The City. And this is in such high praise?

Not only that, Kevin Smith recently remarked how much he loathed BvS, comparing a violent and brutal Affleck to that of Donald Trump, which he went as far as to label the character 'Bat-Trump'. Shame on Kevin Smith though, as a DC fan who was hyped up just as much as me about the film upon release, you have to wonder if he's an actual blithering idiot or just jumping on the hate bandwagon to appease his small fanbase.

Now for those lesser critics, who mind you, aren't really critics at all, said the film was an 'incoherent mess of a plot'. Granted, the movie wasn't spoon fed to us and a lot of scenes were open to interpretation. I kind of compare this to another underrated sequel that came out not so long ago called 'The Matrix Reloaded'. A film absolutely riddled with cryptic philosophy and Greek mythology, very much similar to Batman vs Superman, but at the time was also panned by the critics and called a 'flop'. It wasn't spelled out for us, and was not intended to be. You have to wonder if these so-called critics actually use a brain, or better yet, use the internet or Google for its intended purpose of researching what you don't understand!

But if we are to relate that to the movie, there's no comparison, as what was said by Luthor in the movie, a film 'too big for little minds'. Batman vs Superman is, by far, every comic book fan's dream come true. From the get-go, we are introduced to the Wayne murder, a story we all know but played out beautifully in two scenes juxtaposed of Bruce finding the bat cave. The track by the wonderful Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL really shines here by their track 'Beautiful Lie', which I've listened to countless times over already. Apart of what captivated me about Batman v Superman was not just the mind blowing action scenes, but the religious mythology.

Not being a religious man myself, it's something I appreciate very subtly in movies. The opening sequence of Bruce finding the bat cave is very reminiscent to Lucifer's fall from grace. Affleck plays the role remarkably. He's already played Batman in Gotham for 20 years now, he knows the ins and outs of crime fighting. Later scenes when he talks to Cavill including the infamous 'first meeting' as shown in the trailer, really compares the two. With Cavill being more of the boy scout. Whereas Batman really showed in his frightfulness , the scene where the women in cages call the caped crusader a 'Devil', other characters such as Henry Cavill's Superman and Amy Adams' Louis Lane, captured the heart of the script. So much in a way, I shed tears of Superman's death in the end. It was like watching an older brother you saw through Man of Steel maturing in Batman vs Superman coming to the point where his heroic actions payed their ultimate price. And the fight itself made me really glad they payed homage to Frank Miller's comic and the kryptonite spear coming straight from the pages of "Who would Win: Batman/Superman Detective Comics #78."

I also loved the violent and brutal Batman in this film. I was even all for Batman using guns, which I also see some people complaining about on the boards here. I mean, hello? He uses freaking missiles and turret guns on the Batmobile, and yes, even uses a gun in the game Arkham Knight, innocents are bound to get in the way eventually. I think what captivated me the most of Batman's fighting style is that it comes straight from the games.

To wrap up this review nicely, the other stars such as Gal Gadot really surprised me with Wonder Woman. She came across as very alluring, sexy, mysterious, and mischievous. She nails the role as does Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor Jr. Let's be aware, this is not the original Lex Luthor but his son and even makes mentions to his father throughout the film. I can't say enough how much I adored his facial mannerisms, coming off as deliberately quirky, a role Eisenberg is renowned for, so it was intentionally deliberate that they chose him to play the lesser villain. The only one I thought underrated is Jeremy Irons as the new Alfred. Man, was he impressive. His relationship to Bruce; you know its been there for a while. He knows Bruce like the back of his hand, even mentioning his solitary lifestyle over a wine bottle, "There's not going to be anymore members of the Wayne family." Bruce knew this too, he wasn't your typical billionaire scoring with the ladies, but a sad and angry loner, which I relate to a lot. He was shattered by his past, in a way in which we all do.

title: Well, it left me speechless, I will give it that
review:
Wow....I mean WOW!!!! Well, it left me speechless, I'll give it that. In fact, I am beyond speech....

MINOR SPOILERS

Now, before I go on with my rant, there is a single thing that is good about this film that got it the 2 stars I gave it. The performances. Battfleck actually pulled it off & both he and Cavill deserve Oscars for nailing both of their characters with the material that was given to them. Everyone is fine and comes across quite competent in their roles. So that is why this movie gets a two star rating from me. That being said, it is a pity the actual film makers weren't quite as competent. Aside from these amazing actors who managed to make something out of pure raw sewage, this would have gotten a Zero from me. Period.

I physically recoiled in horror as I watched this movie. I literally sat there with my mouth wide open in shock as Snyder & his goons not only completely destroy whatever chances the up and coming DC Cinematic Universe had to succeed, not only wasted $410 Million on something that looks like a video game, but I also saw this guy and his cohorts single handedly beat the art of storytelling to death with one fail swoop, as well as slam its corpse through a buildings foundations, causing it to topple and fall on top of it. This is everything wrong with "The Amazing Spider Man 2," "Fant4stick" & "Catwoman" all mixed into one. Oh yeah, you heard that right, I said "Catwoman." Remember that film starring Halle Barry? Yep, this is the level of entertainment you should expect while seeing this movie.

But you know what, I don't think any words can describe this theatrical abomination in full without the necessity to describe the cinematic experience I had while watching "Batman v Superman"....There literally is no need for spoilers, as the trailers managed to spoil the film just fine. In fact, just go watch those and stay right the hell away from the finished product. Keep the wonder intact. But I digress.

I feel that in order to allow you the chance to avoid this 2 and a half hour travesty and not get suckered in by the hype is to tell you what actually happened at the cinema that I watched this movie in.

1) At the start, the cinema was full to capacity, by the end it was half empty....

2) At one point I started laughing out loud and I just could not stop for a good three minutes, I was getting weird looks by everyone. And let me tell you, it was not an attempt at humour on the big screen that made me break out into a maniacal cackle, not unlike the Joker....It's just that my brain could not even begin to fathom the abomination of cinema that was presented to me via the Snyder/Goyer hope destroying machine that is this, the DC Cinematic Universe. This was at the point in the film when the newsreader on some television playing nearby talked about how it was lucky that this time, no one was in the city because it was night time and no one was at work. The city mind you that Batman just lured the villain back to, even though there were countless other options available to him that did not necessitate him bringing the destructive force that is Doomsday BACK to a populated area. But nope, Snyder has got to have his destruction porn to masturbate too.

3) During a Superman movie, I personally witnessed kids being escorted out by their parents traumatized, crying and screaming....

Yes, you heard that right. Kids began crying & screaming in terror, begging to leave. Zack Snyder has gone and made Superman, the symbol for hope and everything that humanity should aspire to be, too terrifying for the kids to watch. And no, I am not talking about little kids. I am talking 10, 11, 12 year old children who all now have PTSD and went home with nightmares thanks to Zack Snyder's own superpower of zero subtly. And they weren't the only ones that left either. I saw a few fan boys and some couples leave too, shaking their heads in disgust. As they should. As we all should.

The fact that a review on here compared it to "The Dark Knight" convinces me that humanity's evolutionary peak has been passed and we are now on the decline. And if "Art Reflects Society" and this is the "art" that we produce nowadays, I say humanity's extinction is not only long overdue but well deserved.

I have to go watch "Batman & Robin" now for some cohesive story telling. And before I leave you with my final thought, I have to point out that I have no love for comics, have no care for their canon, don't care about which company is superior and as a movie buff, all I want is a film that is so important to pop culture to be at least semi competent or half good so I don't feel it necessary to write something like this. But, in regards to "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice".

THANK GOD FOR MARVEL!

title: A flawless superhero movie, that masterfully establishes the DC Extended Universe.
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice continues, where Man of Steel(2013) left off. Bruce Wayne/Batman(Ben Affleck) was present during the battle between Clark Kent/Superman(Henry Cavill) & Zod(Michael Shannon), that decimated Metropolis. Bruce Wayne suffered many personal losses, on that fateful day. Batman is wary of Superman's unlimited strength & immortality & feels that, Superman might turn on mankind someday. So, the Caped Crusader decides that he has to take on the Man of Steel. After another international incident involving Superman, the American government feels that Superman should be held accountable for his actions. Meanwhile, Lex Luthor(Jesse Eisenberg) has his own diabolical plans for Batman & Superman.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a mind blowing film. Director Zack Snyder, has superbly crafted another masterpiece after Man of Steel(2013). This film, improves upon all the tiny flaws in its predecessor. For one thing, our heroes are mindful of civilian casualties. Another major improvement from Superman's solo adventure, is the addition of humor. Unlike Man of Steel(2013) which was humorless for the most part, there are quite a few witty one- liners in this film. Don't worry though. The dark tone of Man of Steel(2013) has been retained. The visual effects are awe inspiring. The fight sequences between Batman & Superman & the climactic showdown involving Batman, Superman, Diana Prince/Wonder Woman(Gal Gadot) & Doomsday are jaw-dropping. The 3D provides immersion & eye-popping scenes, aplenty. The viewer feels like he is right in the middle of the action on screen. The background score by Hans Zimmer & Junkie XL is intense & unforgettable. The music definitely adds to the overall experience of the movie. The script by Chris Terrio & David S. Goyer is amazing & has organically brought together, the two most famous superheroes of all time. Terrio & Goyer have also beautifully set the stage, for the upcoming Wonder Woman movie, Justice League movies & all the other films on the schedule of the DC Extended Universe. The performances are incredible. Ben Affleck is perfect as Bruce Wayne/Batman. Affleck's take on this beloved character, is the best iteration of Batman on the big screen, yet. Henry Cavill is brilliant as Clark Kent/Superman. Cavill portrays more shades of his complex character, this time around. Amy Adams is great as Lois. Jesse Eisenberg is outstanding as Lex Luthor. Eisenberg's performance proves that, DC's villains are definitely more memorable than Marvel's. Diane Lane is amazing as Martha Kent. Laurence Fishburne is impressive as Perry White. Jeremy Irons is awesome as Alfred. Holly Hunter is good as Senator Finch. Gal Gadot is spectacular as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. I am so excited, that Wonder Woman finally made her big screen debut & Gadot portrays her, effortlessly. Scott McNairy, Tao Okamoto & Callan Mulvey are effective as Wallace Keefe, Mercy Graves & Anatoli Knyazev, respectively. Brandon Spink & Lauren Cohan are fantastic as Young Bruce Wayne & Martha Wayne, respectively. There are various references & cameos, that tease upcoming movies in the DC Extended Universe. The film ends on an emotional cliffhanger, that will leave you wanting more. Don't listen to the critics. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a must watch. A classic! Go for it. I can't wait for future movies from the DC Extended Universe.

title: Finally, DC gets their s*** together
review:
This is definitely up to the hype. They take two major comic events, one for Batman, one for Superman, and meld them into a single screenplay, while not slighting either.

Decent characterization, decent plot, decent balance of action and story. It's not as funny as the first Avengers, nor quite as good as the "first" X-Men (i.e., "First Class"), but it's as good as anything DC has put into a movie, including Dark Knight, and as good as any of the better Marvel movies.

Well worth your time, if you're a comic fan at all. You get to see glimpses of the other "JLA" heroes, too -- Flash, Cyborg, Aquaman.

title: Batman v Superman
review:
VERY, VERY MILD SPOILERS Although the story does change and is quite over the place at times, this film does far better at setting up the DC Cinematic Universe than Iron Man 2, Thor and Captain America 1 ever did. Those films were never as good as both the Avengers and their sequels (both Thor films were terrible anyway). Batman v Superman has: 1. Ben Affleck as the best Batman to date: Batman is more brutal than ever, and he does kill, however not directly. This of course changes at the end, and throughout the rest of the DCCU he will not be killing anyone. The Batsuit was amazing, his voice digitally altered by the cowl rather than Bale's low, devil scream. His Batman is scarred, and battle-weary, but he is more bad-ass than ever, even taking on Doomsday. 2. Superman: the Man of Steel is still very much in his early stages here, however by the end and by the time he appears in Justice League he will definitely be the hero who represents hope in the world. 3. Wonder-woman: Need I say more? 4. Lex Luthor: At first he seems not so great, but this man is definitely a two-faced character. He is very, very scary, almost as much as Batman is. He is very much Lex Luthor by the end, and who knows if (due to his predicament at the end of the film) he will actually bulk up in his current living environment.

BATMAN V SUPERMAN is the beginning of something great, and I can guarantee that as soon as Suicide Squad and Wonder Woman are released, the world will be very much accepting of DC. This movie has people talking about it,and has the internet very much divided. The fans, however, love it. They really do. Considering that SUICIDE SQUAD, with its fantastic cast, might be the film to launch DC movies into critically acclaimed territory again, there might be nothing to worry about after all. BATMAN V SUPERMAN has laid the groundwork, and now the DC universe is set. The solo films will no doubt really cement the DCCU.

BATMAN V SUPERMAN is big, emotional and heavy. It is quite messy at times, but every other second is pure joy. With JUSTICE LEAGUE looking to be lighter, more optimistic and more amazing, BATMAN V SUPERMAN is the "darkest before the dawn", as Harvey Dent said in THE DARK KNIGHT. These heroes had to overcome their darkness to enter the light, and become heroes. BATMAN is no longer someone struggling as much, and SUPERMAN has become a beloved hero, as he has been for all these years. Bring it on DC, it is going to be an amazing journey.

title: Masterpiece.... Almost
review: Come on people, why all the hate? why all the negative comments? personally I don't get it. Batman V Superman is probably the BEST superhero film ever made. Forget about the Marvel movies, this is serious, this is no Deadpool, no Wolverine, no Ant-man. Praise Zack Snyder for the adult take on superheroes, for all the homages paid to classic comics in the film, this is the closest you'll ever be to Frank Miller's Batman the dark knight returns turned into film. title: DC finally catches up to Marvel
review:
Right, so where to start. I'm poor at reviewing movies, so i'll just share some of my thoughts. I have not read any "critics" reviews, only the few posted on IMDb from viewers that managed to attend early screenings of this movie. I managed to catch this at one of the first screenings here in South Africa.

So far Marvel have pretty much had it their own way in the battle of WATCHABLE comics to screen. From a Marvel universe perspective, the X-Men series, Wolverine, 2 versions of Spiderman, Ironman, Avengers, Thor, Antman, Captain America, Guardians of the Galaxy and the recent Deadpool, to name a few, have all been pretty good. It was only the 2 Hulk movies that were Luke warm and Daredevil that was a complete disaster. DC on the other hand have been through quite a rough patch with lemons such as Green Lantern, Catwoman, Jonah Hex, Superman returns and some pretty bad Batman movies especially Batman vs Robin. Their only saving graces after the Reeve version of Superman in the 1980's were the Dark Night series (mostly thanks to Nolan), a semi decent Watchmen movie and a return to form for Superman in the Man of Steel - although this one generated many split opinions.

Batman v Superman - Dawn of Justice pits the "Alien" against the "Bat of Gotham" in a battle to the death all carefully planned and executed by Lex Luther. The movies starts off with a brief overview of Batman's' history all through a series of flashbacks and dream sequences. It introduces Bruce Wayne as a caring business man and employer and goes to great length to show that he really cares for the people of Gotham and that he is a war weary vigilante that has made peace with his alter ego. It then introduces him into the Superman Man of Steel time line at the exact time that the Krypton Terraforming Machine starts its destruction of earth and then shows the following events from his perspective. Meanwhile, the intro depicts how humanity is battling to digest Superman's superior powers and the possible threat that he poses should he abuse his powers. Lex Luther is then also thrown into the mix for good measure, an evil genius hungry to cause destruction. This "intro" takes up around 40 minutes of the movie and it makes use of a pretty strange movie making methodology. The story telling is not linear and it consists of, what feels like, independent segments all sewn together. Only once the scene is set, does the movie start to follow a more traditional linear time line. Oddly it works, and manages to portray a lot of history and story in a pretty concise manner. Once the story starts to take shape, it shows the battle between the 2 super powers and, without spilling the beans, the fight thereafter and the aftermath events .

One of the key successes for me of the Nolan directed Dark Night series was the dark and dreary tone of the movies. Well, B v S takes that and multiplies it exponentially. There are no jokes (even Luther's wise cracks have dark undertones) and no lighter moments. The only moments that give the viewers some time to unclench their sweaty fists are those that portray the love between Kent and Lois Lane. For rest of it, the tone is pretty depressing. The CGI, effects and fight scenes are fantastically done, although there is one scene where the bat mobile returns to the cave that is not that convincing.

Although the story, CGI and Hans Zimmer score are all superb, the standout in the movie is the acting. Affleck simply kills it as Batman. I've never been a big fan of his work, but my word the man is astonishing in this role. He underplays Batman and portrays him as a cool and calculating, but ultimately caring bloke. He is without a doubt, the best Batman to date. Then there is Jesse Eisenberg. His portrayal of Luther rivals that of the Ledger Joker and the psychosis drips from his pores. All the other actors were superb as well.

Sure, the movie is not perfect, but is well done, has a great and believable story to tell, has a great score (for the music lover) and the acting is first class. With a single movie DC has managed to claw back most of the ground on Marvel. It also introduces WonderWoman and has a quick reference to the other Justice League members. If B v S is anything to go by, I'm looking forward to many more superhero movies.

Well worth watching (forget about the critics).

title: Mesmerizing, dark and gritty!!
review:
Honestly I am a fan of any comic book movie and so I went to watch the movie without any hesitation. And boy I was surprised to see the movie. The characters were taken straight out of their animated versions.

Batman is a no-joke character. He is dark and reserved. If Bale had just managed to touch the surface, then Affleck has taken it out of the roof. His portrayal of the Batman is top notch. He is human and frightening.

The theme of Man of Steel had really made sense in 2013! How can we allow just any alien to settle among us? I don't know how the people of this earth would react if someday a real alien came down on earth. I don't think he would be accepted that easily. This theme was correctly captured in Man of Steel and further explored in BvS.

The portrayal of Wonder Woman was awesome. Frankly speaking, I didn't had high hopes on Gal Gadot. But after watching her in BvS, I think she will give BatFleck and SuperCavill a run for their money.

Jeremy Irons as Alfred was magnificent. In the comic books, Alfred had donned the Cape many a times in order to protect Bruce Wayne and Mr. Irons seems to me he wouldn't hesitate to do the same in the movie-verse as well.

Jesse Eisenberg just proved that how sinister he can be if given the right scenario. The final 'Ding, ding, ding..' was haunting. Jared Leto better watch out. You have got serious competition.

The only loose end I believe was the portrayal of Lois Lane by Amy Adams. If you so wanna follow the comic versions, then you need to make her more independent and strong.

Some of the memorable scenes from the movie (Spoilers ahead)

1. Flash warning Batman in a dream.

2. Aquaman looking straight back at you ready to strike.

3. The glimpse of the Flash. Although they could have cast Grant Gustin.

4. Wonder Woman!!

5. The fabled trinity fighting together.

title: Honest and fresh review
review:
This is a fresh review because I have just come after seeing the movie.RIGHT NOW. So the imprint of the movie is fresh in my mind and I am honestly going to say that this movie is a beautiful mess. I haven't seen any other review. I haven't seen any spoilers and I walked into the theater knowing only what the trailers had shown.

First, I am going to talk about the pros that are in this movie. The movie is shot beautifully. Every scene is breathtaking. The CGI is as expected of Zack Snyder. The actions scenes are awesome. If the Man of Steel action scenes were 8/10 then the action scenes in this movie is 10/10. Exhilarating, adrenaline pumping action scenes. All the haters of Batfleck can zip their mouths shut because Ben Affleck gave a towering performance as Bruce Wayne as well as Batman. I had a little problem with the Batman part but I'll come to that later. Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne shows his humane side because of the incident at Metropolis. He's Emotionally vulnerable because the loss of Metropolis is still fresh in his mind. Apparently the Bruce Wayne he is portraying has been through a lot so it is understandable.Jeremy Irons as the new Alfred is a breath of fresh air. He is more grounded and handy just like you see in the trailers. I remember one scene from the comics where Alfred takes a pill which enhances his strength and beats up Superman for hurting Bruce Wayne and I can totally see Jeremy Irons' Alfred doing that to Henry Cavill's Superman. Henry Cavill as Superman is the best we have got since Christopher Reeves. Does he surpass his performance? According to me, yes. As we haven't seen any recent renditions of Wonder Woman I think Gal Gadot is promising. As a DC universe is being created I think she will fit in very good. Human characters like Lois, Perry and Martha Kent have enough screen time and are good. There are cameos by the members who will be forming the JLA. Jonathan Kent also pays a visit.

Now for the cons. Considering the run-time the film was a tad bit lengthy because of the script. Apparently Hollywood is still suffering from the Spider-man syndrome. That is, they are so busy building up for the sequels that they do not concentrate on the current premise. There are too many things going on in this movie. At first it looks like they are setting up for the Batman vs Superman throw down but then you see the Doomsday part coming up which scared me right when I saw it. It proved to be right. The second half is just a big CGI mess. The Batman and Superman fight is awesome and according to me they should have built the story arc like that so that it would have ended with the fight BUT they had to bring the Dawn of bloody Justice.

Doomsday looks like Shrek on the juice that made Bane grow big in Batman and Robin. They took too many references. I think it is an amalgamation of The Dark Knight Returns and Death of Superman and it turned out to be not according to the expectations.

Now the thing about Batman. Dude was killing right and left! I mean you could say they were rubber bullets but he drove his car through the car which apparently had the bad guys in it. BATMAN DOESN'T KILL. I hope they have a explanation for that. Now you see I haven't put Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor in the pros because it wasn't. He was towering and menacing but those were very brief moments. Otherwise he just comes out as a mockery of many goofy characters. He just didn't come out of his comfort zone to do something different. All in all the movie was OK. Probably the wait and expectation had built too much hype.

title: Visually entertaining with plenty to think about.
review:
Just my opinion. I saw this movie today (Australia) and it is by far my favourite superhero movie. The director and writers have offered a brilliant view through the eyes of superheroes. Snyder is the master of cinematography and your eyes won't blink during some scenes.

Since man of steel Henry Cavill is our superman and you can't help but feel for the man of steel in this movie. Gal Gaddot will be our wonder women based on her great performance. title: Watchable - but "why"?
review:
It seems okay, but when asking for reasons the card tower just falls and falls. Why is Lex doing this? What's the matter with Batmans dreams? Even "who is Bruce sleeping with" comes up. Why rushing the whole Justice League stuff without really rushing it? And - *major spoiler* - why killing Superman when you show and the end of the movie that it did not matter because he'll live anyway? *spoiler ends*

Don't get me wrong.

I don't want this movie to explain everything. I just want a movie which does work with the material it offers. Also this movie's tone is so dark and depressing. Yeah, it is somehow fresh and differs it from other comic books movies these days. But there is NO HOPE whats-o-ever anywhere. No even drops of humor. In three hours!!! This is definitely not a world where I want to live in.

It is damn cool, it is nice to see these characters finally work together on screen and it seems fresh at first. I won't become a hater but I also won't become a DC-movie-fanboy. In times when superhero movies are at the top of their powers this one's stale and mediocre.

title: When worlds collide...
review:
Firstly to be fair, I did not enjoy neither Man of Steel nor The Dark Knight Rises. I found the former to be overblown and loud, and the latter to be slow and dull. This movie however seemed to put the better elements of both characters together in a fast paced, enjoyable film.

The thing I enjoyed most was the contrasts between the characters. You begin to understand the two different worlds these characters come from, their different purposes, their different methods, and their differing moral compasses. Thrown into the mix is the first big screen and long awaited introduction of Wonder Woman. Fortunately she doesn't derail the other two characters, and her scenes are always a welcome change.

The film is not without its faults though. There seemed to be some plot holes I haven't quite figured out, such as how Luthor figured out Superman's secret identity, or how Lois Lane seems to know where their battle was taking place. Also, I thought the introduction of The Flash, Cyborg and Aquaman was poorly done and should have been much more subtle. This scene really diverted greatly from what this film is meant to represent.

Otherwise, the good definitely outweighs the bad and I would definitely recommend this to all DC fans, superhero worshippers, and those who just love a good action flick. Unlike the last Avengers movie, if you're not familiar with these characters, it can be figured out without leaving you feeling lost and scratching your head figuring out the plot.

Overall, worth seeing.

title: Dull and Depressing
review:
Zack Snyder directed a movie that should be powerful and all commanding, and he did that without much help, as the movie-goers were keen enough to see 3 powerful superhero figures coming together - Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman.

What the movie-goers, like me, did not want to see was the depressing and dull tone Zack offered to us. What did it have to be so dark and unoriginal, a rip-off from Christopher Nolan's work, which was beginning to be irritating at Batman 3. Unlike the fight in Avengers 1 between Ironman and Thor, which were brief and exciting, Batman v Superman's fight was unnecessary, tiring and uncalled for. Even the punch from Hulk on Thor beat the fight between Superman and Batman. It shamed me that one of them became the crybaby at the end of the scene.

To a certain extend, I am grateful that X-men did not tear apart cities every time at any fight. Watching Batman v Superman was like watching Transformers going loose. It did not make sense to say that these superheroes were saving the day when buildings were collapsing all around. It was ridiculous to even hear one saying that the whole area had been evacuated. I could not believe such ability of the army to clear within a few hours.

Bruce Wayne gathered no dust as he ran through the falling debris. Superman's hair was sill perfectly combed after he dipped into water. Superman was floating in the air, instead of helping those 3 people on the roof (flood scene). What was Superman doing? Enjoying a display of himself to those he was helping?

Did I miss something about the scene at the desert? Seems like the village was affected but I missed that scene?

Bruce Wayne's and his dreams/nightmares. Gosh.. Could the story line be any duller?

And if I have to see one more scene of Bruce Wayne's parents got killed in a Batman's reboot or even Uncle Ben's death in Spidey, I could scream murder in the cinema.

The world needs Alfred. He is the superhero. Not only he is a butler, he can design, build and fix cars, gadgets and more.

title: WAAAAYYYYY Better Than it is Being Credited
review:
Okay, now we get down to the nitty and the gritty(BvS and CA:CW):

1st - BvS I really don't get all the hate this movie is getting. I think it is a very good movie, bordering on great. That said, this makes it a pretty significant disappointment. The trailers - IMO - really made this film look like it was going to be EPIC. And it simply isn't. That's not saying it's bad. it's just that is could and - more importantly - SHOULD have been better.

The flaws: 1. to a small degree I can understand the complaints about the dark tone. but I think this is a minor failing, not a biggie. You have to take note of what I believe is the most important part of the title - "Dawn". What happens just before the dawn?(rhetorical). This is the dark hour before the dawn. I get that. That said - yes - it could have used a few more key points of levity.(though it did have a few of those that most people are ignoring). 2. The long, slow build-up. This is probably, for me, the biggest problem. They could have done this more like TDK in mixing in the action with the plot build-up IMO 3. The confusing "dream" sequence. I know - now - that this was not a dream at all. It was some type of time/dimensional portal or "drift". Seems to me that the comic book fans mostly got that. I had to study up on it after seeing the first time. That said, when I did understand what was going on when I saw it the 2nd time, it was really good the 2nd time for me.

There are a lot of things done well that the anti-DC/Anti-Snyder brigade are ignoring: 1. They intro'ed the new Batman and Wonder Woman really well IMO. I am very excited to see more of both of those characters. 2. In doing a good job of not copying Marvel with mid/post credit scenes, they did a good job of leaving many DC easter eggs - especially with the intro's of the other JL members. I thought that was really well done. 3. I thought all the action sequences were fantastic. This is a Snyder staple - the guy knows how to do action. Even Sucker Punch, with admittedly a weaker story, has some of the all-time best action sequences ever. 4. After seeing this and CA:CW, sorry, I'll argue all day long with the Marvel guys. Lex Luthor was a WAYYYYY better utilized villain than Zemo. (more on that in my CA:CW review) 5. When I saw it the 2nd time, I really loved how they ended the film. I really get the sense that Supes ultimate sacrifice really inspired Batman(and - to a lesser degree - WW). I could feel him returning to his more idealistic ways. I think this movie sets up Justice league very nicely(though definitely not perfectly).

8.2

title: My Objective Review
review:
In short, this movie is not very good, especially if you actually care about the characters in the slightest. If you can get past the fact that these characters are nothing like how they have been represented in the past, and you just want action scenes, then you'll like this movie, but wont want to see it again.

The biggest issue with this movie is the fact that it is very poorly paced. For the entire first and second acts, the movie will bounce around, and attempt to juggle three, to four story arcs all at once, and fails miserably at it.

The entire rest of the movie suffers from a very drab, and joyless tone. Rarely do you see moments of joy in this movie, because its too busy basking in how important its message is for the majority of the movie, and it forgets to be a decent super hero movie. Honestly this makes this movie have a severe identity crisis, which detracts greatly from the overall experience.

Basically this movie was rushed to beat marvel and it shows. the characters are all over the place with their motivations, some plot points will seem to be too dumb to be true for most people, and if you like DC at all, this movie will feel like an insult because of the way they disregarded the source material.

If none of those points sound bad to you, then this is your movie, if not... lets just hope they don't do as poorly directing the other movies.

title: Great for the fans but boring, long & confusing for the general audience.
review:
Jesus, where to start? This film was terrible!

Now I myself Have never been a Marvel fan. I was abit half & half with a film with such a gimmicky title & well, the film was A LOT worse than I thought it was going to be! I do think these films have great effects but to be honest that doesn't make them any better & even still smothers what the heroes are meant to be about, saving lives & connecting to the real world! The main problem I've had with these films! They're simply not like the classic where the plot was simple & the effects & sci-fi crap were scarce & used sparingly! I mean is it too much to ask? Really?

title: The Worst Batman Movie Since Batman & Robin; The Worst Superman Movie Since Superman Returns
review:
Just how bad is "Batman V. Superman: Dawn of Justice?" "Batman & Robin" was a better Batman movie. "Superman Returns" was a better Superman movie. "Daredevil" was a better super hero movie starring Ben Affleck. "Waterworld" was a better movie featuring Kevin Costner.

Those movies were all misguided messes, but at least I found them entertaining the first time I watched them, which is more than I can say for the joyless two and a half hour drag that is BvS.

Can Ben Affleck pull off Batman? That's been one of the big questions on everyone's mind since he was cast. He can and he does. While I wouldn't call him the best actor to ever dawn the cowl, he's suitably intense and brooding. If the movie was cut down to just Affleck's scenes, it still wouldn't be good, but it would at least be watchable. As for another questionable casting choice that pays off, Jeremy Irons' performance as Batman's faithful butler Alfred Pennyworth is pitch-perfect. Despite normally being associated with villainous roles, Irons' Alfred is the film's biggest bright spot. But this is far from the only terrible movie Jeremy Irons has been the only bright spot in.

On the opposite end of the spectrum is Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. Great actors like Gene Hackman and Kevin Spacey have chewed their way through the scenery in the role before, but Jesse Eisenberg takes it to a whole new level of over the top. From adopting a Southern accent to quote "A Streetcar Named Desire," to sharing a Jolly Rancher with a hapless Senator, to a mumbling Paul Revere impersonation, Eisenberg seems to be channeling the Joker rather than Superman's cerebral foe. There's such a thing as a villain that audiences are supposed to love to hate, but Lex Luthor had me wanting to walk up to the movie screen and punch it for all the wrong reasons. And the explanation for how the character goes from flowing locks to his iconic chrome dome had me scratching my own scalp.

The other performances are about what you'd expect. Henry Cavill fares just as well as Superman as he did in Zack Snyder's "Man of Steel." Gal Gadot, Ray Fisher, Ezra Miller, and Jason Momoa get too little screen time to make much of an impression as the other members of the Justice League.

But the movie's flaws go much deeper than the casting. BvS seems like it's trying too hard to be the antithesis to Disney's breezy Marvel Cinematic Universe. While those movies make comic book adaptations fun and enjoyable for mainstream audiences, BvS sucks all the fun out of the room. That's not to say that the film shouldn't be dark and gritty. But even Frank Miller's "The Dark Knight Returns," the graphic novel BvS takes most of its plot cues from, had its own warped sense of humor, and Heath Ledger's Joker and Tom Hardy's Bane had audiences laughing at, and still quoting, their darkly humorous quips throughout Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy.

The plot finds Superman suspected of war crimes after once again flying heedlessly to the rescue of damsel in distress Lois Lane. Meanwhile, mild-mannered reporter Clark Kent is appalled that the vigilante Batman in Gotham City has taken to branding the criminals he takes down, marking them for prison justice. Even for an alien that has only been on Earth for two years, it seems crazy that he would think he can curb Batman's brutal methods twenty years after the Bat Signal's been installed.

The two characters spend two hours dramatically circling each other before finally throwing down in an anticlimactic fist fight. (Batman seriously punches Superman in the chin several times before realizing the Man of Steel won't flinch.) And even with the slow crawl to the battle, it seems like key scenes had to be edited for time. With all the plot holes, it's hard to understand why Bats and Supes are finally fighting, or why we should care who wins. Or why so much time that could have been spent developing the plot was wasted on dream sequences.
