title: It's not perfect, but it is not as bad as the critics have made it out to be
review:
Let's get this clear, this is not your typical superhero movie, this is not filled with humor and bright colors. This is a movie where you're shown that superheroes CAN go bad, that their actions do have consequences! The casting choices have really paid off in this movie and the actors have done a fantastic job!

Ben Affleck is perfect as Bruce Wayne and Batman! His batman is extremely brutal and you just know he has gone through some major crap in his 20 or so years in Gotham. Henry Cavill does a fantastic job as Superman. All I'm going to say is you're going to feel for superman due to all the controversy surrounding him, and Cavill portrays it brilliantly! Is he the bright and "hopeful" superman from the Christopher Reeve era? NO. But, do you get a feeling that he's getting there? Absolutely! Gal Gadot is PERFECT! I was one of those who did not believe she was good enough to play WW, but I was proved absolutely wrong the moment she entered the scene! She's managed to control her heavy accent, and her acting and physique has gone up ten folds since her previous roles! You WILL cheer for her when she shows up! This DC Trinity looks absolutely badass on the big screen!

Jesse Eisenberg is confusing to say the least. He plays the role of Lex Luthor JR. and I can see this character getting divided opinions. He is manipulative and has a lot of character depth, but he comes off as a tad immature. Lex is perhaps the only disappointing character in this movie for me.

There are multiple stories being told in this movie, and they're told at their own pace. This is exactly why I think the complaints about "inconsistent pacing" are really unnecessary. Each story gets just about enough time and it ties in fairly well

What I do agree with, however, is that there are certain scenes that could've just been cut to reduce the length of the movie, or use that added time to dvelve deeper into some of the characters' development. There are a few pointless scenes that you don't need to watch in order to understand what's going on, and especially during the end, you keep thinking the movie is going to end here but it just keeps dragging on, which is kinda disappointing..

So in my honest opinion, this movie is a must watch for any superhero fan out there, but it does have its issues, so don't go in expecting a TDK beater or a 10/10 movie. I have no idea why the critics have bashed this movie as hard as they have, but it's nowhere near bad. In fact, it's a solid 8/10!

title: A beautiful movie with great character developments for the upcoming movies from the franchise.

First of all Batman V Superman is not just a superhero movie. It is a Zack Snyder movie. So like all other Zack Snyder movies there was action, drama and everything in between. But also there were various plot holes and a lot of non-comic book fans did not get certain moments in the movie. Right from the start it was all serious. That does not go well with a lot of the fans and critics. Mainly because they are not friendly to all type of audience like Marvel movies. Marvel movies are the complete package. They have a strong character base and great connection between the superheroes. But in my opinion what the marvel movies lack is a sense of priority. They give priority to making it a friendly movie rather then the story line. That is where DC is so good.

Lets jump in with the staring. It was by far the best opening credits I have ever seen in any movie. The cinematography was brilliant. The best flashback to Batman's origin. Still not sure if Ben Affleck was the best Batman ever but he was surely the best Bruce Wayne. The worn out post Joker Bruce Wayne was the perfect role for Ben.

But in a movie with Batman, it was surprising that Superman was the one with the more complex issues, as he fought with his human existence in this planet throughout the whole movie. But that just made us realize more that he is a part of this world and no matter how much powerful he is, he is a man too. He has feelings and a family that he cares about more then anything. Which made me connect with him more on a personal level.

Now for the very few moments with Wonder Women. Gal Gadot stole the show. I was in a full house theater and everyone was in "aw" of the moments she was on camera. Made me that much excited for the solo Wonder Women movie.

Some moments that were small plugs to the future movies were great for the comic fans. Because the moment Flash came from the future and said, "Am I too soon!? I'm too soon! You were right about him! You were always right about him! Fear him! Fear him and find us. You have to come find us, Bruce!". This was the moment I jumped out of my seat and shouted, "Flash, that's Flash! He came from the future!". But some people didn't understand that plug and I feel sorry for them but that was a great plug.

Everything in the movie was awesome including Zack Snyder's camera work and the cinematic justice he did to the movie. Some people will find it too dark. But all those people that don't have a problem with the theme will love it.

title: A CGI Festival, SPLOSIONS! But Beyond That... Pretty Empty
review:
I tried to remain neutral about the selection of Ben Affleck to play the part of Batman, after all, how exactly do you follow up Christian Bale, who undoubtedly set the bar for superhero blockbusters so high that no one will ever surpass it, and who can forget Daredevil, an uninspiring yarn that should have never seen the light of day? But, interestingly enough, Affleck was decent in this movie, Henry Cavill even better in the role he has personified now for a decade. The real problem came down to the role of Lex Luther, and the strange way the Luther character was presented.

Luther is meant to be an ultra intelligent villain with an insatiable appetite for power. From the very beginning it seemed as though the director Zach Snyder strayed away from this, instead trying to recreate Heath Ledger's "Joker". Luther is presented as a loose cannon loony toons with major daddy issues, hell bent on the anarchic destruction of the planet, for no reason whatsoever. Sound a lot like The Joker? Yep, same here. And worse yet, Eisenberg just doesn't pull it off. He might be in his 30's, but he looks 15, and simply doesn't have the persona for the part. Rather than recreating Heath Ledgers role, they should have allowed Luther to more closely resemble the Kevin Spacey/Gene Hackman version.

It also appears they spent a good portion of the movie trying to set up sequels for a number of other superhero characters, including bringing Wonder Woman into the fray. Her fight with the Doomsday monster left a lot of questions. And that brings up the Doomsday villain himself. The movie entirely screwed up the origin of Doomsday, who in the comic was an ancient beast created long before Krypton itself supported Kryptonian life. And somehow Luther just interacts with the ship, which in its good graces allows him to do whatever he wants with it. Oh sure, no security features at all, it asks Luther questions, apparently knows it is breaking protocol, but it helps him create this crazy monster anyway. Made no sense.

So many other problems, Luther's interactions with the spaceship, Batman's relationship with Alfred came off as cold, Batman cattle prodding villains, could go on and on, but I digress. In conclusion, the movie is worth seeing in terms of CGI, but the plot is terrible, character presentation is muddled at best beyond the apparent hatred between Superman and Batman, and in the end you are left rolling your eyes at the idea they'd even make a sequel (which by the way, they set up at the end). If you saw this in the theater, my condolences.

title: Ultimate Edition is better
review:
Over the past few months I've heard all manner of comments about how 'Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice' is 'The Showgirls of Super-Hero movies'. Not so: as long as 'Green Lantern', 'The Spirit' and (Gods help us) 'Catwoman' live on in our cultural memory, the bar for truly dire hero-flicks will remain quite exceptionally low.

It's...not that bad.

It lacks the thoughtful aspect of 'Man of Steel', and the messianic allegory of that film is continued a little too heavy handedly, here - even down to the film's Easter release (sent from his Daddy in the sky and raised as one of us, he dies to save us from a baddie identified - albeit fleetingly - as 'the devil', only to inevitably return...in the sequel.)

That said, the performances are very good, and Ben Affleck's grizzled Batman/Bruce Wayne is excellent. Deserving of his own solo flick, I think. He does 'angry' very well.

For comic geeks like myself there are obvious nods to 'The Dark Knight Returns', 'Doomsday', 'Trinity', 'Public Enemies', 'Batman: Year One', 'Batman: Earth One' and a host of individual tales (including the dystopian Batman issue #666). Gadot makes an excellent Wonder Woman, and some of the fight scenes are quite beautifully staged.

Two things let it down...annoyingly, but not irredeemably. Firstly, there's the unsubtle teasers for the imminent movies featuring Aquaman, The Flash and Cyborg. This franchise-fest slows the narrative, when it needs to maintain momentum, and seems woefully contrived.

More annoying is writer David S. Goyer's inability to write a superhero script which DOESN'T involve the sudden third-act appearance of a monster/machine-which-will-end-everything. The Blade flicks, Batman Begins/Dark Knight Rises...all spend ages developing believable personalities and motivations...then throw it all away in an unnecessary effects-fest.

Grrr, Mr Goyer, Grrrrrrrrrrr!

Many of the plot issues, particularly with regard to the 'magic bullet' and Bruce Wayne's back-story are properly fleshed out in the 'Ultimate Edition'...which provides a more coherent narrative, and should have been released in cinemas.

title: Zach Snyder!!!
review:
It's hard to fathom how this movie was as disjointed as it was. None of the acting was bad, in fact the whole movie was acted superbly (I even liked eisenburg's lex, it felt like a welcome extension of the character he played in The Double).

Character motivations were extremely lacking, and the story was incredibly bare bones. If you saw the trailer, you basically saw the movie. There's not much more to it, and the editing is atrocious. It seems like some one was trying to kill the movie, and then accidentally spliced it back together.

Most of the characters don't have strong motivations, if any explanation is given to explain why they're doing anything at all. Superman is largely ignored as well, it's as if they weren't sure how to write the character, so they did as little as possible with him.

I don't know if I care that batman was killing people, but he was a little (a lot) irrational where supes was concerned. Here's a guy who's only ever helped people, but just in case he decides to kill every one we'd better kill him first. Makes no sense for a guy who's supposed to be super intelligent to jump to that conclusion.

Gal Gadot seems great as Wonder Woman, but she really just shows up for no reason. The rest of the justice league's introductions are far worse. Literally just a file stolen from Lex Luthor, who also for some reason designed their logos.

I don't know if they ever had a great script, or even a good one, but they managed to whittle whatever it started as down into a whole lot of nonsense that possibly should have been set in a non-canon universe for its ultra violence.

title: Badman vs Stupidman - Dawn of Darkness
review:
This film has no reason to exist.

There's just no moral reason for the characters to be doing anything and Snyder (dir.) can't get any kind of connection between what's happening on screen and what's going on in peoples heads, let alone establish an emotional tone.

The script has a good turn of phrase now and again, for sure, but the earnestness becomes unintentionally funny after a while, when you realize the entire film is preposterous.

A combination of slick military propaganda and simplistic storytelling, the movies main enemies are a) Snyder's inability to make, feel, or create story ideas with a camera and written concepts, and secondly, criminally bad color grading, ruining acres of superior film craft, all professionally paid for and generally ignored or hated by the Comic Book Adaptation audience. (as if they have any choice, as there's hardly ever anything else on).

Last point, to coin a clichÃ© - the film's dramatic power is often indexed by how effective or magnetic the bad guy is. Dark Knight had the excellent Heath Ledger. This movie has a smirking, shallow, annoying dick called Jesse Eisenberg, who should have had a bit part in the movie making sandwiches or something in the background of the films endless, grim and very adult fantasy settings of offices, mansions, cityscapes and war zones, all aimed at bored, disappointed kids wasting what little money they have anyway.

I'd give this film a negative rating if the IMDb webmasters will set up such a function.

title: Brilliant Moments and Visual Style Outweighs Its Poor Moments
review:
Movie has problems. But it's overruled by the majority of the film being quite good.

Firstly, Batfleck. Holy crap. I knew he was gonna be better than Bale, but not that brilliant. He is the best on-screen Batman and I've been saying he was going to be from the moment they announced it was going to be along the lines of Frank Miller's Dark Knight. All of Batman's scenes were phenomenal. He felt like Batman and he had great chemistry with Jeremy Irons' Alfred (who I wished we could have seen more of). All his scenes were exactly what I've pictured the real Batman to look like on the big screen. Now, the killing aspect. I thought it would bother me. It didn't. In the context of the cinematic universe they're creating, it makes sense for his character that has been Batman for a while and has a loose wire in his head - and honestly, it made him seem a lot more badass than usual.

Henry Cavill was once again...a good Superman. He provided enough acting for the character, giving Superman his good human qualities. Lois Lane was reduced to a damsel in distress in this movie but I didn't really care because it's not her damn movie....and also because Wonder Woman was in this and she was freaking badass (although, she kinda just dropped in and out, without too much screen-time sadly). Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. Oh boy, I don't like it. Way too eccentric. However, there were moments in the film where I thought to myself, "holy crap that is 100% Luthor". I'm hoping his character will change by future movies, to make him more like the serious minded business man. If that really was Jimmy Olsen in the film...I don't care. Perry White and Lois Lane are enough. Overall, the acting was really good, besides Luthor and the characters were done well enough, for most of them.

Besides Watchmen, this is the most visually pleasing Superhero movie I've seen. I say this because DC hasn't had a large slate of the same looking movies like Marvel has. It still feels visually unique, and there were a lot of moments in the film that I think were visually brilliant. They were the opening sequence of child Bruce, Metropolis, one-shot dream sequence, Batman fighting Superman, warehouse segment and a bunch more. Also besides Watchmen and Man of Steel, this movie has the most solid, meatiest, coolest action in a superhero movie and I loved every action segment. A lot of people thought the Batman and Superman fight was a let down, but I thought it was 8 minutes of pure awesomeness. If Zac Snyder can do anything brilliantly, it's action scenes. He will always be better at doing them then a lot of people, because he doesn't shake the camera excessively, he doesn't have an insane amount of quick cuts and he knows how he wants his fights to look and sound. The man can do visuals and action.

As for editing. You can tell where deleted scenes would go. Cameos didn't feel forced. Flash, Cyborg and Aquaman looked cool. As for putting Doomsday in, I don't mind. It was a good way to bring the trinity together. And to those complaining about him simply being a plot device...congratulations. You've figured out the entire point of Doomsday's existence. He's only ever there to destroy.

I'll just leave it to my biggest problem of the movie being Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. The mind of Luthor was there, just not the personality.

Let's wrap this up.

Overall, I enjoyed watching this movie. Critics were really harsh which pretty much reinforces why I don't ever look at critic opinions when I go and watch a film. It was visually brilliant. The action was top notch. Batfleck was awesome (probably the best thing). There were some plot points and editing moments that could have been done better - they felt really choppy and that's obviously because it's a studio cut. I liked the ideologies behind Batman and Superman and what they believe in. I understand what they were going for with "Martha!" but it could've been written better and did I mention that Batfleck was awesome? Okay. It's a big screen movie so it deserves to be watched on the big screen. Don't go in with unbelievable expectations (I honestly can't believe the expectations people had for this - are you demented? It's a superhero film, they're rarely anything past a 7/10). I enjoyed it. Well, the really awesome moments I did - which came in abundance. But so did questionable choices. Such as putting a certain comic story arc in towards the end that could've been held for future films. It felt crammed at times but you can still tell what was going on (unless you're 5). But most importantly, it felt like an epic film. I give it a 7/10. I think I enjoyed this more than Man of Steel, which I also really liked.

EDIT: Just watched Ultimate Cut. Fixes some of the plot holes and confirmed some of my own reasoning's to certain unexplained moments. Has more Clark Kent which is welcoming. A little more hardcore which I liked. Still can't save the Lex Luthor of the film universe. He is still the biggest problem of the movie. Martha scene still disappointing because I know what they were going for but it just wasn't written as well as it should have been. The scene that I'm split on was the court scene with Superman. It furthers the story but wastes some of the potential for further analysis of the need for a Superman.

Not a major boost in score, but it was a good incentive to watch it again and go over it. Once again shows that the studio cut will usually be inferior to the original, directors cut. Looking forward to future DC movies.

7.5/10

title: Mostly enjoyably but a couple of issues that detract from the experience
review: I'm going to start out by saying I enjoyed this movie, undoubtedly it has its flaws and by no means was it the best movie that I've seen, but it was still enjoyable mostly because of its phenomenal cast. I thoroughly enjoyed Henry Cavill as a 'grown up' version of superman. I consider his take on the role as a more intelligent and mature take on the character instead of the traditional 'truth, justice, and the American way' ideal. Ben Affleck's Batman takes on a more grizzled veteran type role that I found particularly refreshing. And Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman was suitably mysterious and enigmatic throughout the film. However Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luther was probably the thing I enjoyed most about the entire movie. I found this version of Luther an incredibly well written and intelligent interpretation of the character, with an amazing performance. Every time Jesse Eisenberg came on screen I got the creeps. I wouldn't be able to find any flaws in the cinematography and action sequences of the movie which were very well shot and integrated into the movie. The only thing that brings the movie down in my estimation was that the entire affair felt very forced and rushed throughout. For the entire movie Zack Snyder seemed to be trying to cram as many Easter eggs, and references to DC lore and the following movies as possible. This meant that some parts failed to move the story forward in any way, causing parts to drag, while others seemed rushed and ill-fitting to the scenario and movie as a whole. The result is that the movie comes across as slow and rushed at the same time. This is because all the irrelevant bits and pieces drag the movie out longer than is necessary, while some parts come across as skimmed over and rushed in order to fit everything in. this was not the only flaw but it was the most glaring that I could see when watching the film, and the only one that really detracted from my enjoyment of the film. In conclusion, the movie was enjoyable and I would recommend watching it at least once if for no other reason than to simply appreciate the performances of the cast. But it does have some fairly key flaws notably the sense of 'cramming' of ideas and hints throughout that detracts from the quality of the film.

title: Entretaining, but it's mistakes stop it from shinning.
review:
This is by no means a bad movie. If you haven't seen it and you enjoy comic book movies you should see it and you will enjoy it. This is probably the best Batman we have ever had on the big screen, the action is great, and the movie was beautifully shot as any other Snyder movie, but you will often find yourself with a sour taste in your mouth from scenes that feel completely out of place because the movie was trying so hard to set up an upcoming movie, or scenes that don't make any sense at all that make the movie feel like it was rushed or the writers just didn't know how to join the upcoming movie and all the subplots form this movie together. Some parts are amazing, but they are eclipsed by the mess the script and plot are. Entertaining, but a complete waisted potential.

For me this movie was as disappointing in it's depth as Man of Steel, but it still leaves me excited for the upcoming movies because this universe has a lot of potential.

title: Good

The flat out truth is, had you not seen Man of Steel or been a comic fan (with sustainable knowledge about the DCU) then you were probably going to be lost for most of the film. Nonstop action for the most part, and the acting couldn't of been better. Affleck is an amazing Batman, though Batman's morals do not mirror those from the comics. All I'm saying. Still amazing job. Cavill and Gadot did fantastic as their respective characters. And lastly, Jesse Eisenberg played a very convincing young, troubled Luthor. The movie was fast paced, and if you didn't have time to dig into details, it had already moved to the next scene. This was the only true problem I had with the movie itself. Other than that, the movie was spaced just like your normal comic books would be, skipping from one perspective to another, telling a partial story, that you as a viewer must complete using prior knowledge or good judgement. This movie all in all, is a comic book coming to the big screen, skipping all minor details to introduce the bigger picture. By skipping scenes, it also felt some characters were robbed of development, but Zack Snyder knows this, and has left room for upcoming films to explain. Easter eggs galore and fun references leave the biggest of fans craving the next installment in the DCEU. This truly was the DAWN OF JUSTICE for DC's upcoming theatrical films. I give this movie a thumbs up. A must see for any fan. Oh and bring some Kleenex. —

title: Had So Much Potential...
review:
As someone who really loves Superman, I'm really disappointed with this film. It's a visual feast, to be sure, but it doesn't deliver on what it promises. It promises to discuss philosophical and heady things, but also forgets to actually deliver the necessary weight to those moments. Too much of this film is devoted to tying into the rest of the DC Cinematic Universe that it feels as though it's fit to burst. There are a few scenes that do exactly this and stop the forward momentum of the film dead in its tracks.

In Avengers Age of Ultron, there was a similar problem. The side-stories distracted from the main plot thread and everything felt overstuffed, as though Marvel was using its Avenger movie as a "hub" so that the next phase of films can be set up or at least hinted at. Here we have that problem, but at a greater magnitude.

I didn't want to hate this movie, but this film was an overstuffed affair that tried to do so much that it failed at everything that it was trying to do. I wanted to feel like I saw something great, but I just left the theater disappointed. I can only hope Suicide Squad delivers a more focused story rather than one that is too busy doing too many different things. I don't mind a morally complicated superhero movie. I just want a focused story that doesn't shove in so many elements that we can't care about our characters.

title: A pointless and meandering mess
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a cynical, ugly, mean-spirited film that completely misunderstands the material that it is trying to adapt. But I could forgive that if the film had a compelling story. It doesn't. Trying to follow the movie's narrative is a nightmare.

Scenes are placed in a seemingly random order. There's never any indication that what you're seeing on screen correlates to any other earlier scenes. Characters will go into dream sequences only to wake up and have another dream sequence. Then the film will never bring up those dream sequences ever again. Characters will say that an event we saw a few scenes ago happened months in the past, but there's no visual cue to let the audience know this. As a result, the audience must question everything that is said and done, and the very basics of the story get lost in the shuffle.

Characters spend endless scenes talking about how much they dislike someone, but they never have any meaningful interaction with one another. For instance, Batman and Superman meet each other a grand total of 1 time in costume and 1 time out of costume (where it's unclear if they both know each other's identities) before they have the big showdown in the end. The rest of the time they just talk to their associates about how bad the other is. How are we supposed to empathize with their positions if they base their perceptions on absolutely nothing?

Lex Luthor is one of the worst villains put on screen in the last decade. His motivations are constantly changing, and the performance is as erratic as Eddie Redmayne's in Jupiter Ascending. His plan makes no sense, and it culminates in creating a creature (that he cannot control) that has the power to wipe out all mankind. Why? Because reasons.

The score is ear-bleedingly bad, too. Overwrought and pompous, the score wants you to notice how great it is, but it never concerns itself with matching the imagery.

With that said, the dialogue is the same way. Everyone talks about gods, demons, heaven, and hell, but the film doesn't actually have anything to say about that subject matter. Everyone has an important speech to give, but these speeches neither sounds like anything a real person would actually say, nor do they move the narrative forward. They exist for the sole purpose of sounding intelligent and padding out the run time. Don't bother trying to analyze this dialogue; the emperor has no clothes here.

The best thing in the movie is Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, but that's only because she's not in the film long enough to have her character ruined by this mess. She's not in it long enough to impact the proceedings either, but you could say that about most of the secondary characters, too. The other actors (Jesse Eisenberg excluded) do a fine job, too. It's just a shame they have nothing to work with.

As a fan of films in general, I'm annoyed, angry, and I want that two and a half hours of my life back. As a fan of superhero films, I'm baffled and vexed; I didn't even think that they were capable of making superhero films this bad anymore. As a fan of DC comics, I'm disgusted. Save your money and do something else instead of watching this.

title: This might be brilliant for the fans
review:
I admit it, I'm not very fund of all these superhero-movies they make these days. There are some exceptions though: films like The Dark Night (2008), Spiderman and Tim Burtons Batman I very much enjoyed. This one I didn't.

For starters I think one should be skeptical to titles with "vs" in it. To me it sounds somewhat cheap or amateurish. This shouldn't really matter, but it's after all the movie title. Come up with something a little more original.

In my opinion the story isn't very much intriguing. How many times haven't we seen the young Bruce Wayne lose his parents in the back alley behind the movie theatre? Or his never ending fall down the hole in the ground facing a million bats on the bottom. Again, the originality. Not to mention Batman and Superman's sudden realization that they need to work together to defeat the evil. Sound awfully familiar.

It seems to me that this film is just a show of from the wizards of visual effects. They have very much focused on the technical aspect of movie-making - with some brilliant slow motion scenes, but halfway through it kind of got a little ridiculous. A non stop bag of huge explosions and intense gunfire was a bit over the top for me, to say the least. Thank god I don't suffer from epilepsy. I would have been in trouble.

Taking all this into consideration this may just be perfect for the fans - and good for them. But for an "outsider" like my self it was a highly tiresome affair.

4/10

title: Enjoyable
review:
The negative critical reaction is way OTT. I suspect a good example of the phenomenon where critics and online posters have their pre-viewing opinions influenced by others. Similar to people being more likely to up-vote a web posting which already has positive votes. It's how riots start-the influence of the crowd. And also people, psychologically, prefer to go with the majority view. The film certainly has flaws, but not which justify the critical response.

So, going into it with very low expectations, I enjoyed it. It's a good Batman film and portrayal of Batman. The main fight is exactly what you'd hope it is. Not too long either. My main criticism is it is indeed overly serious throughout, even Alfred! It needed a bit more lightness to balance it out. Superman is too glum. This version of Superman, as with Man of Steel, is a valid attempt to do something new. But it's not what I want from the character. Similarly, the film, particularly at the outset is too stylised, adopting the Watchmen film style. Not sure about Luthor either! But overall, it's perfectly enjoyable.

title: Flawed Film But Wildly Entertaining
review:
First, I think this film was made far too early. A second Superman film should have been made focusing on the increasing apprehension and government scrutiny directed at him in the wake of the destruction caused by his battle with Zod. A first Batman film should have been made prior to this film, as well, and there's no reason that Batman's awareness of the danger and destruction presented by Superman couldn't have more slowly built up to this battle. Doomsday and the Death of Superman storyline should have been reserved for a Justice League film. There was simply too much packed into this movie too soon, and it left me wanting a solo Batman film WAY more than a Justice League film.

All of the actors were great except for the Social Network kid, who apparently thought he was playing the Joker instead of Luthor.

The venom directed at this film by fan boys who feel the DC movie universe is too dark is, in my opinion, off base. These films have to be engaging films, not simply lockstep reproductions of the comic books. Marvel has done a very good job of making very fun movies that reflect the colorfulness and tone of many of their comic books. If that's what I want (and I do), I can watch the Marvel films. It is entirely valid for DC to take a completely different approach and create a very dark alternate take that expands what these characters can be.

I loved Man of Steel and thought it was the most HUGE film I had ever seen. It was bigger than life. I personally like the seriousness and almost mythological/religious tone of Dawn of Justice. Why should DC be obligated to do the same thing Marvel does?

I just wish DC would slow down. They took some MAJOR stories from the comics that could have easily represented complete films by themselves, and really shortchanged them by hacking them down to plot points. Batman was ready to actually KILL Superman! That's a giant deal! Then 20 minutes later Superman gets killed anyway by someone else? Too much. WAY too much.

Have some patience, DC.

title: The Positives and Negatives
review:
First of all, I enjoyed the film. The 10 year-old came out in me and I got to see Superman and Batman together, pretty cool. The positives are that I really like the direction of two main characters. Superman,as in MoS, is stoically portrayed and is a somewhat gaudy figure, (very similar to Snyder's Dr. Manhattan), and is portrayed as the superhero I always imagined Superman to be. Cavill does a fine job, and also portrays Clark Kent nicely. I also enjoyed watching the new Batman, I like the roughness of his traits, the less Playboy more Vigilante aspects as well. Kudos to Affleck and Irons for making Wayne/Batman & Alfred their own after Bale and Caine set the bar so high.

Some negatives, I haven't read many DC comics and didn't know much about Lex Luther prior to this film so I won't judge too harshly. I liked how Eisenberg has some philosophical lines, but other lines came off as rambled and incoherent, a rather strange character if you don't know the back story of the comics. Another negative aspect is that the movie felt rushed, I understand that this is only the 2nd movie introducing the JL, while Marvel has introduced a lot of their main heroes and everyone has been familiar with them for several years now, I guess DC is trying to catch up with Marvel, but it will never work if they rush.

title: Very immotional and intense movie
review:
I went to see BvS yesterday so my impression and feelings about this movie is fresh and lasting.I rated it 10/10 because I view it as a movie that's main purpose is to entertain and hype for upcoming/next sequel, BvS did it's job right.

Video Quality: I watched in IMAX, the experience was really good, all 3D effects were consistent without lag, no extra(unnecessary) visuals that would ruin the overall atmosphere, the tone was dark/gray/yellow but it only complimented the theme.CGI was well done and really up to date.

Audio Quality: Really nice music and sound effects that set the mood right,not really memorable but it did its job.

Acting: very good acting from Superman(in some scenes you forget that you are watching a movie , it feels like he is really a superman that is shooting in a movie). Ben did a great job too playing Batman, but Superman really shines here. You will be impressed with Lex's and WW's performance, very natural.

10/10- This is good action movie with serious grim dark tone, acting ,visuals and sound is excellent.

title: The best "okay" superhero film I've seen
review:
I've seen a lot of "okay" superhero movies like Ant-Man, Thor: The Dark World, Man Of Steel, The Wolverine and more. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is an "okay" movie but this has to be my favorite among the "okay" superhero movie.

I'll start with the things I liked in this movie. Ben Affleck as Batman/Bruce Wayne is very good. The fight scene of Batman and Superman is great. The way the other Justice League characters like Aquaman, Cyborg and The Flash are shown is very interesting. The Knightmare scene is also pretty interesting too. The part where Superman's body is heavily damaged from the nuclear explosion is very similar to what happened in The Dark Knight Returns Part 2; it makes a very clever easter egg. That's about it for this movie's positives.

Second is the nitpicking parts in this movie. Bruce's parents died on a sidewalk rather than an alley (Crime Alley to be exact); in which I think they missed an important detail. The part where Bruce fell on a hole in the forest then levitating back up with the help of bats, still kinda confused with that to be honest. Well I guess that's all for here.

Third is the things I hated in this movie. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was an idiotic decision. Lex is not supposed to be super crazy; he may have been crazy in the comics but not as crazy as the movie suggests. Doomsday is not the appropriate villain; it should've been Bizzaro. Also Doomsday's origin is complete bullsh*t! He wasn't made by Lex, He was made by a Kryptonian scientist. I hope this Doomsday in the film would stay dead. That's about it for this movie's negatives.

In conclusion, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is an okay superhero movie. It's not great, it's not bad either. An easily recommendable movie.

title: Awesome, just awesome
review:
What's wrong with people bitching about this movie? It was a great film with an actual story from exposition to climax and so on. It was dark and not filled with childish jokes and scenes. Don't get me wrong, I love the marvel movies but I'm glad DC and the directors took this path. It's more mature and true humanity related. It sets the difference and a good change in super hero movies, it would be lame if it was the same style as other similar movies.

Comic fan boys, I'm well aware it didn't stay entirely true to the original story but it's pretty close, besides, what movie about our teenage heroes stays true to the exact originals? None

title: Batman v Superman Action Packed but Overwrought
review:
Batman v Superman: Action-Packed but Overwrought Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a sprawling, generally enjoyable mess. The film, directed by Zack Snyder (from a script by Chris Terrio and David S. Goyer), is the official follow-up to 2013's Man of Steel. It's also a setup for the soon-to-lense Justice League superhero team-up movie. The main plot of this feature is self-explanatory: It's a clash between DC Comics' biggest icons. The internal logic of the plot— much like many of the comics that inspired it— is kind of a moot point. Let's get ready to rumble.

The estimable Henry Cavill (2015's The Man from U.N.C.L.E.) returns as Superman, and here he's a much more polarizing figure in the world (and his home country) than in previous screen depictions. Forget the patriotic exemplar role models of George Reeves and Christopher Reeve. (Fans probably won't have much difficulty forgetting Brandon Routh.) An early sequence finds him intervening in an African warlord's regime; while some lives are immediately saved (read: Lois Lane), there is soon public testimony about how the regime's loyalists retaliated against locals. In drastic contrast to previous depictions of the Man of Steel, Superman's actions are seen as fraught with indirect human casualties. Cavill's Superman is ponderous, brooding, and increasingly concerned with the vigilantism of Batman in nearby Gotham City.

This Batman— here played by Academy Award-winner Ben Affleck— is middle-aged and bitter after apparently having waged a 20-year war on crime in Gotham by the time of Superman's first public outing in Man of Steel. In that film, the onslaught of criminals from Superman's home planet left much of Metropolis devastated (featuring plenty of thinly-veiled allegory to 9/11). Bruce Wayne owned an office building that was leveled during the chaos, and it is on Superman that Wayne places the blame. It's this angle that sets up Batman in a dual role— that of co-hero and as a secondary villain.

Lead villain Lex Luthor is portrayed by The Social Network's Jesse Eisenberg as a twitchy, candy-munching sociopath. That this Lex is also a Generation Y technology mogul means that he ditches Gene Hackman's tailored suit and ascot for casual jackets, cartoon-monkey T-shirts and sneakers. This Lex isn't content with being rich; he's an insecure xenophobe who sees Superman's presence, fairly or unfairly, as a living reminder of his comparative impotence. In true comic-book villain rationale, that means the alien has to go— and if it means manipulating Batman into doing the dirty work, then it's killing two birds with one kryptonite stone.

The leading women in this film offer mixed results. Wonder Woman, played by Gal Gadot (recently of The Fast & the Furious films), has little dialogue and less to do with the overall tale than viewers might assume. Still, she makes an impression in the film's climax. Meanwhile, Amy Adams' Lois Lane is more substantively interspersed in the story. Having long ago learned Clark Kent's secret identity, she now worries that his adventures as Superman— now facing serious scrutiny from the U.S. government— puts an untenable strain on their relationship. Adams continues to convincingly update the role of Superman's plucky girlfriend— but the filmmakers still can't resist putting her in traditional distressed-damsel scenarios.

Supporting characters get shortchanged in this narrative. Jeremy Irons as Batman's loyal butler Alfred gets to wax wise with his boss/surrogate son, while offering prescient warnings about the risk of obsessive vendettas. Meanwhile, Daily Planet editor Perry White (Laurence Fishburne) mostly gets to offer expository dialogue to reporters Clark and Lois about the woes of the newspaper industry. They're both kind of wasted here; hopefully there's more for them to do in the next installment.

The film suffers somewhat because of the need to foreshadow future events. A lengthy nightmare sequence (technically, one of two) will probably just confuse casual viewers unhip to Justice League lore. Presumed future members of said League also have cameos here. The writer seemed to notice at least two or three false endings by the time of the (really) last shot. A shocking development in the climax may confuse some viewers regarding sequel possibilities, but it's likely all part of a plan.

Batman v Superman is almost best viewed as "Justice League .5". The first-ever cinematic assembly of this superhero team (and the immediately pending Wonder Woman feature) is bound to continue the momentum of the recently inaugurated DC Entertainment slate of films from Warner Bros. Studios. Still, based on the themes of this film, it looks like Batman and company are inhabiting a distinctly depressing, catastrophe-prone, paranoia-driven world. It's going to take more than a team of adventurers to save it; it's going to need a team of counselors.

Rating: B

review:

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Awesome
review: When I first seen the movie, I was skeptical due to the early reviews. However, after leaving the cinema, I realized how idiotic and blind those so-called 'critics' are. I mean 44% on Metacritic. Come on. The performances were brilliant, the action sequences were spectacular and the villains were sinister and original. However, the only fault with the movie was that the first 40-50 minutes were slowly paced and a bit dull. I would give this movie between 7.5-8.0 out of 10. It was enjoyable to see Ben Affleck dressed as the Caped Crusader and Henry Cavill as the Man of Steel. This movie has been out for about a week and it is already underrated. Critics are outdated and redundant. As a final, go see the movie. I liked it.

title: Amazing and Beautiful : )
review: I read some negative reviews but I had been looking forward to this film for years. I went to see it on Wednesday and gladly...... I didn't have the same experience as the people who were disappointed. I love the Frank Miller Batman and although he is still really tough and scary, there are cheesy elements that I have had to overlook. As far as I am concerned this movie borrowed and paid homage to all of the best parts of the graphic novel minus the cheese. The updated story was skilfully done and wickedly compelling to tie in with Man of Steel. The costumes were legendary as was the attention to detail and the overall scenery. I found the dream sequences spectacular and I thought that it was a really clever element, in the same way that the last trilogy used trip sequences early on. I thought every actor was brilliantly cast and did a great job... the camp but truly terrifying Lex was the best portrayal of the character I have ever seen. This older Batman is totally awesome and Ben Affleck played it perfectly...... Everything from the dark knight trilogy could have happened to this guy years ago, and he fits brilliantly into Zack S's movie universe. I can't wait for the new stories and the planned sequels! I read a comment where someone complained that there is too much detail. I don't think that this the kind of movie that you watch just one time only... it has taken years of work to create and it has the budget to employ the best in the industry. It ticked every box for me and I gave it 10 only because I couldn't give it 12. To everyone involved in creating it... from the bottom of my heart, thank you! . . . I am so pleased I am over the moon : )

title: One of my favorite comic book arcs made into a good movie
review:
I disliked "Man of Steel", thought it was drawn out and rather boring. The story was not too interesting either. "Deadpool" was great. Other favorites are "Batman Begins", "Spider-Man 1 + 2", "Iron Man" and "The Avengers".

Entering "Superman v Batman: Dawn of Justice", a title I thought was horrendous, (and still think it's very bad), and we get a story told extremely well. Little is explained, since we are expected to know enough about the characters at the beginning, and I like that. Much is shown, little is told.

Reviewers have complained about the murder of Bruce Wayne's parents, but it is used as a great storytelling device that I did not see coming. There are not too many dream sequences, but those sequences were quite good.

Someone even complained about Batman using guns in this movie, probably not realizing that this only happened in his nightmare.

There have also been complains about the movie being like five different stories. I only saw one, and it was driven by the madness caused by the terrible "Man of Steel" and Lex Luther's devilish plot to bring down the alien.

The characters are well portrayed. It feels a lot like reading an excellent comic book. Even some scenes are touching, and others very exciting. I did not expect that after going into the movie knowing about a 29% Rotten Tomato score.

I had a great time, perhaps factors were low expectations due to critical reaction and the previous Man of Steel.

My final verdict: excellent story telling, fine acting and competent direction, an enjoyable movie to watch on the big screen.

title: Witness the Ultimate Clash! Just GO for It! You won't regret!
review:
"God vs Man...Day vs Night" these words were truly portrayed in this movie in an outstanding manner..really hats off to the director Zack Snyder..one of his best directed movies and undoubtedly one of the best action comic movies in decades...I mean WOW! That's what a true comic fan would want from a comic action movie...if you are a big fan of batman and superman and if you love to see your super heroes clashing, then this movie is not going to leave you unsatisfied. The new Batman is Amazing..the Bat Suit..the Bat Power Suit was totally awesome!! It's highly recommended for Batman, Superman fans along with all the comic lovers.

Lastly....Awesomeness is coming!!! Awesomeness is coming!!! :D

title: Mild.
review:
Both Batman and Superman have had troubled depictions on film; some were great, some were terrible, some were mild. "Dawn of Justice" as a sequel/ reboot/ re-imagining emulates just that: mildness. From its genesis, the film rampaged the internet first in anticipation, then awe, then complete and utter disappointment. Is it justified? It is not by any means a horrible film nor is it bad; it is a film that strives to be an epic touchstone and ends up as an all confusing stem of prequels/sequels, stand-alone and Avenger-style mash-ups that already has audiences fearful of the outcome.

All hail Zack Snyder, (1) a Nolan disciple and wannabe, that values style over substance; (2) that managed to assemble an array of fine/serviceable actors and turning them into autopilot versions of themselves that seem to never fully commit to the roles at hand; (3) and mustered the courage to ignore the best days of Batman (Nolan's). What are we left with? A lost cast, a convoluted script, characters' childish and messy motives worthy of Nickelodeon special, and Gadot the only introduction that widely promising.

title: Avengers and Snyder destroy Nolan!
review:
What a miss! Batman Vs Superman (B Vs S)...two most popular super heroes on Earth battled against each other for the first time in the history of movies, what to expect? Well, depends upon who made it...unfortunately Zack and not Nolan. Few Hits:

#1 First half is gripping, grand and promising. The anticipation of the duo's battle is well laid.

#2 Fresh sketching of the Batman's character.

#3 Crisp fighting scenes especially by Ben.

Many Misses for the movie: It is B Vs S...can it get bigger than this? Then, why the hell did the story writer had to get other characters?

#1 The movie should have painted the conflicting philosophies of justice from B and S's view points and should have explored how both are right in their own ways and yet find the other wrong.

#2 B n S sharing the space together to battle should have been the ultimate climax battle. However, the battle between B Vs S left me wanting for more and as it was just a minor part of the movie.

#3 Same old Krypton daggers since 1978? Common writers give Batman some more wit.

#4 A monster (as seen in the trailers)? After watching the Joker, Bane and Al Ghul, who would enjoy watching a monster on the loose.

Lex has always been a conniving and a mean character...in this movie Jesse looks creepy and eccentric but somehow fails to take off. His game plan was...wait was there one? Remember the Joker's seductive words, "Do I look like a guy with a plan". Dare Lex ask the same!

Because of the Nolan trilogy, a Batman movie is now expected to be classy, complex and mature. This movie takes Batman to pre-Nolan days as the plot is simple, predictable and the climax is all about superficial actions and visuals, which you would find in an Avenger movie (and Snyder movies). The Superman...well, is yet to do justice to its reboot and can be excused for now.

title: Superman is not broken...we are.
review:
First off, forget the critics. They are spoiled into thinking every super hero movie should look like the Marvel films. This is not one of those.

Story: This movie, while not over-powering, is a bit darker and heavier than the aforementioned fare. It does this while still being altogether enjoyable. It is bold enough to at least ask the question: If Superman were real, how would humanity cope with that?

Casting: I can stop holding my breath on how bad mall rat Affleck would cock up Batman. He did well all things considered. Same goes for Gal Gadot, though her role was a bit light. Jeremy Irons did great as well but that was to be expected. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luther was a bit more of a psychotic Steve Jobs as opposed to evil genius.

That said, his part helps capture the sad fact that when confronted with someone more powerful and more importantly more virtuous some people can truly become evil.

Semi-spoiler: Seeing the beginnings of Justice League and the hints at an over-arching Omega story is also totally cool.

I don't mean to knock the epically fun things Marvel is doing, but this movie is just a tad more adult (if one can say that sort of thing about super-hero movies).

Worth seeing.

To save some time the trailer is pretty much the whole movie I'm not kidding, so I saw this movie with low expectations. By the end of the movie I was very disappointed. It was not that great it was mediocre it should of been released straight to DVD. This is the reason why.

Adding in dream sequences some good and some unnecessary that feel like Snyder or the writers wanted to throw all their ideas all at once. This is the problem some of this can be saved in future films I don't understand why they had to catch up with Marvel stop it DC take your time. Most of the actors were fine, unfortunately they miscasted Luthor played by Jesse Eisenberg and he ruined the whole movie he was playing himself and sounded like a brat who had no ulterior motives, like a poor version of the joker.

There is only two fight scenes with Batman and Superman one is on the roof and one is helping to fight against Doomsday which is the worst looking CGI. These fight scenes were brief. Wonder Women was meh, just thrown in as a cameo I would of love to see her origins first but DC is doing this all backwards.

The only good thing in this movie is Batman I am surprised that Ben Affleck did a better version in its own right, although there is a lot of irrationality of the character almost like a bully. There was not enough of Superman dialogue. The Superman franchise will greatly suffer because of DC (no spoilers), they made Lois look like a damsel in distress and her side quest in Africa was stupid. They were trying so hard to make this movie serious, but it stopped being serious to me after the Grandma's Peach Jar scene.

Your better off saving your money and watch a different upcoming superhero movie.

title: Batman vs Superman - Not so much !! Is it good...HELL YEAH !!!!
review:
I was not so keen on watching this one because the first trailer with batman overseeing superman did not make any impression on me. Now, come on !!! how can Batman match up with Superman. We all know how powerful Superman is don't we ? ??

With that mindset I booked a ticket for a Sunday evening. I was blown away !!!!! All this movie took was first 10 minutes to convince me. title: Dark, Gloomy, a 180-degree about-face from the good ol' classics ....
review:
The start of the movie is a gloomy beginning, wished they'd written that into something different than a cemetery walk.

I do appreciate that it continues from the Man of Steel movie from 2013, which led me to understand the movie rifts compared of how we portrayed Superman standing up for the American way, but this movie made me re-think of the overall picture when collateral damage happens and people now with more cynicism's in mind are looking for accountability instead of appreciation of what Superman tried to do.

Did not like the part where Superman was portrayed as a god and soldiers bowed down to him- which was also in the preview.

There are other bad write-ups about this movie but I do want to acknowledge the talent, creativity and innovative thinking - which prevented me to rate this as a 5, but as a 6 - no more than 7.

For me, a 7 or higher would mean I should totally enjoyed it, but when I finished the movie, it led a sense of bad taste at the same time that I should have waited for the DVD release instead.... just my honest opinion.

title: Disappointing
review: I went into this movie with high hopes as I love both the characters, Batman and Superman. First, let me talk about what I liked about the movie. Ben Affleck nailed it as the batman. Absolutely amazing performance by him. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was good as well even though she was hardly in the movie. Unfortunately, there were too many problems with this movie. The arrangement of the plot was sloppy. Some of the scenes dragged on for too long. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was a disaster. He tried too hard to be a villain and failed miserably. I hate the fact that the director ruined Lois Lane's character. This movie succeeded in making her a complete damsel in distress and very irrelevant to the plot, which is an insult to both Lois Lane and Amy Adams.Finally, my biggest pet peeve about the movie was the fight itself between batman and superman. The whole movie, batman talks about absolutely hating superman, but the reason they stop fighting is absolutely ridiculous. Both their mothers have the same name!!! In conclusion, BVS was very disappointing for me. Zack Snyder ruined it and I hope he doesn't ruin the Justice League movie as well.

review:

title: An Under-appreciated Artistic Comic Book Film Unlike Any Other
review:
I LOVED it, but not in the way I thought I would. Yes, the cast was great -- especially Ben Affleck's Batman, which is the best and most accurate Batman to date -- but there's more to this film than what the trailers made it out to be. In all actuality, it's better to go in with zero expectations and see the story unravel on it's own because its surprisingly thought provoking... Listen, this film works really well for those who love to really look in depth behind the major and wonderful themes of whether power can be innocent and radical religious views in our modern society. But just because it has depth and requires a lot of thinking, does the film stand well on it's own? I believe very much so!

People today like to watch films and let everything about the story be handed to them, but some of the best films force the audience to thinker deeper (i.e. Blade Runner, The Shining, A Clockwork Orange, etc.) However, when a comic-inspired film does this, it's off putting to the audience because they expect the usual "easy" entertainment. This film is very dark and it's not your popcorn-entertainment -- and some fans of DC had problems with the direction this film took because of generally how much more brutal it was than the original source material at times. But at the end of the day, it's important to think about whether it worked or not... Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice challenges the audience to understand the characters by diving into their complex psychological profiles to explain why their motives and actions are the way they are. Without paying attention to the visual storytelling Snyder presents in his beautiful shots and the smart but quick dialogue, this film will fly over your head.

Am I say it's perfect? Not at all. Was it to me? In ways. A lot of the complaints though from critics generally are personal preferences rather than whether a choice within the film was functional. At times, I found the film to have odd transitions and cut some scenes with great potential too short. Yes, some scenes can confuse the audience because one or two of them relay too heavily on the sequel (the Justice League film) to explain it, but they still serve a great purpose for the film. At times too, though I loved Snyder's use of "compressed" dialogue and large visuals to tell the story, it would've been nice for some expansions on ideas or scenes to further show the audience what happened, how it happened, and why... I think because of these sometimes strange edits, some petty plot holes are left unexplained -- but are either not important, left open for future DC films to tackle, or may possibly have been cut and will be in the director's cut with 30 extra minutes of footage.

Though I think the film had weird cuts and a few scenes with wasted potential, everything the audience needs to understand about these characters and the story is all at hand -- especially when giving it deep thought. I wouldn't say these flaws though ruined the joyful experience for me or burdened the film too much. Instead, I firmly believe people's issues with this movie stand on their specific expectations not being met and preferences they had in mind. But a mindset like this is harmful to any film because then we'd never enjoy any of them... Like I said before, many will be disappointed because the film isn't really part of the title says. Rather, it was used more to bring people in to see the film, but I still think how it made sense and was true to the characters and their nature. (In case you didn't know what part of the title I'm talking about, I'll give you a hint: it's the first half of the title.) This upset a lot of people -- and so did having to think through the "why's" and "how's" of the film -- because it wasn't what some of them hoped to see, but it doesn't mean it didn't work. I honestly believe the criticism of this film lied mostly on preference.

Go see the film for yourself and be the judge. Don't let the critics or others influence your thinking. Like any other film, go in with a clear mind with no expectations and figure it out for yourself. In the end, liking or disliking a film is all about preference.

title: A good DC movie but not as good as the Dark Knight

title: Decent movie
review:
I had high hopes for this movie, being a huge marvel and batman fan only to be disappointed. Don't get me wrong, this movie isn't bad, nor is it good. It is decent at best. I feel as though there was too many things going on at the same time, so many subplots that the director did not focus on. Instead, he hinted on them slightly before moving on and this really irked me! It felt like a great mess. I also think that the motivations for the fight between Batman and Superman were not well backed up and could have been avoided. The role of Lois Lane seemed almost unnecessary as well, it feels as though she had been forced to be in the film.

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was disastrous! I have never met a character more annoying. Moreover, Lex Luthor isn't supposed to be portrayed this way as in the comics, he's almost like how Batman is, calm, collected and intelligent as well as cunning.

Batman had prepared for a long time before facing Superman, so why would he stop short of killing Superman so easily? That makes zero sense. Also, it seems hypocritical that Batman would accuse Superman of being a threat to humanity when Batman was driving his batmobile and using missiles to wipe out cars? Pretty sure he killed quite a number of people in the movie.

--------------------------------------------------------------- Although this movie is average and has many bad elements to it, there are good parts that I would like to acknowledge.

Great fight scenes that will put you on the edge of your seat. Zack Snyder is pretty talented at directing fight sequences!

Amazing music that adds to the feel of the movie, especially when (Spoiler alert) Wonder Woman appears clad in her outfit! Lex Luthor's theme (The Red capes are coming) is amazing too!

I enjoyed the Batman here, he's darker and more intimidating and is really more athletic and acrobatic when fighting. The "Mark of Death" is unnecessary though.

The first part of the movie was pretty good IMO.

title: BvS: A shallow brawl amongst a thousand dream sequences.
review:
In my opinion, it was a mediocre intermediate product used to set up a franchise of films. It wasted all that was done in the Dark Knight films or Man of Steel regarding plausibility. Eg.: It was cartoonish to see so many bullets fired and Batman always unharmed, in a unarmoured suit. (?!) The overuse of dream sequences shows the weakness of the actual plot.

CGI Doomsday was terrible. Cinematography lacked creativity and clarity (too close and unnecessarily shaky). Colour palette was horrible; costume design was sub-par. Sequences shifted without any logic (terrible editing, Brenner). Plot holes galore. Eg.: Jimmy Olsen 'terminated' for CIA involvement... where was that really explained?!

Gadot as Wonder Woman is a skinny Prada princess (gorgeous but miscast); Eisenberg playing a Lex via Hedger-Joker pastiche, not the best choice. Adams, Affleck and Cavill act very well, at least, but can't hold together a shallow script. Reference this (Darkseid), reference that (Flash, Aquaman...). No real commitment to the central story... which is? BvS! They fought and reconciled within a few minutes. Then they're new best friends. What depth of a quarrel, FFS! How could they mess up such a great potential of a film? The director, producers and screenwriters got lost in the material by privileging their commercial objectives (setting up the following films).

Overall, it's worth a watch but with low expectations.

title: A real disappointment.
review:
As a big Batman fan and while not a Superman fan I did enjoy Man of Steel, I was cautiously excited for this movie. My personal opinion was that Superman should have received another solo movie and maybe even a new Batman solo movie before they began to combine universes, and it is for the reasons that I wanted those solo movies first that Batman v Superman is a disaster. I really can't think of anything about this movie that was really impressive and far more that were frustrating. I don't want this review to turn into a list of reasons why this movie fails but with so little to praise it may seem that way.

First off none of the performances are not bad. Batfleck is doing all he can but there is such little time to truly develop Bruce Wayne the way he should be that the character really just lacks depth and becomes fundamentally flawed. Cavil is a fine Superman. He fits the look and has been able to bring his personality to the character. i was not a fan of the casting of Jessie Eisenberg initially but he also is not bad in this movie, but he like Batman is severely underdeveloped. Luthor seemed to just go through the regular steps without a real clear motive. Wonder Woman's introduction is probably the best part of the movie. I don't really enjoy her being some sort of covert spy, but once she dons her normal garb and starts getting into the fray she gives us one of the only positive things to look forward to.

The first half of this movie is a real mess. The pace shifts violently and throws the viewer off. I could not tell if we were in a totally different scene or just moving up a few minutes. We get another Batman origin story which just seems unnecessary at this point. The trailer shows the scene showing what Bruce Wayne was up to during the end of Man Of Steel, so one of the most exciting scenes in the movie we have basically already seen before. There are obviously big parts of this movie that were completely cut out, and sometimes it feels like they were making two different movies and then just combined them and threw in some shameless and really lame fan service foreshadowing future movies.

Zach Snyder has always been an impressive visual filmmaker. His final fight scene in Man of Steel may be the best superhero fight scene to date, which is why this movie is so visually disappointing. We get beaten over the head so often with bigger and bigger fight scenes that have no substance or real excitement to them and unfortunately this movie falls into that trap. Lots of stuff gets destroyed, things explode and more stuff gets destroyed. On a side note visually both the Batmobile and the Batplane look terrible. This may be the worst visual adaptation of Batman ever. The suit looks boring and his coolest gadget is a phone that can copy other phones when both are placed on a bar.

I wanted to like this movie, but at every turn it gave me more reasons to hate it. I have not even mentioned the length, at 2 hours and 20 minutes or so it is one of the worst forms of self punishment let alone the 3D which was a waste as usual and even sickening. It seems as though too many things were forced into this movie and not enough time was spent trying to make it the best it could possibly be. I don't know who's fault this is but i hope it is a lesson to future movie makers in the superhero, and frankly any genre. Quality is always better them quantity. Bigger is not always better, even for a superhero movie the characters have to be compelling and the time has to be taken to make the small things great rather than shove as much different crap into a movie as possible.

title: Angry bat meets sombre god
review:
BvS is rather a disappointment. Not entirely bad (it still looks great and there's some good performances and lovely action, you know), but definitely a letdown.

Maybe the cause of its shortcomings is its director, Zack Snyder. He's been known to favour heavy topics surrounding flawed, traumatized characters living in unpleasant worlds filled with violent death. Even though he usually flavours said realms with a visually appealing, grandiose style of filming and fabulous artistry and dressing. Man of Steel, the movie to kick off this new DC Cinematic Universe which is meant to deliver some heavy competition at Marvel's doorstep, fit that bill perfectly, making the generally colorful and optimistic Superman a brooding alien refugee given near omnipotent power over his new neighbours, the human race. I liked Man of Steel. It made this God like character that much more identifiable by focusing on his lacks rather than his strengths. In its many philosophical moments, Man of Steel felt less like a superhero movie and more like a character study of a God living among man and contemplating his relationship with those who in all respects are so obviously inferior to him. Of course, that relationship is still explored in BvS, as the world now needs to cope with the existence of this powerful presence, a potential saviour to man. However, another type of hero has already been active for decades, it turns out.

For in BvS, the DC universe is supposed to be up and running for decades already. No starting from scratch here, as was the case for Marvel. For every character introduced, there is a long backstory that is teased, which in many cases frustrates more than it intrigues. Ben Affleck's Batman has been fighting crime for twenty years, and it has only made him darker. Crime has not been reduced, while his war on bad guys preying on the everyman has cost him dearly. No wonder he's grown so angry he's not averse to maiming and even killing criminals left and right. The Batman we've grown accustomed to was never a true killer, but Snyder's Caped Crusader has no such moral qualms anymore. And now there's this all powerful extraterrestrial policing the planet. A being Batman holds responsible for the invasion that laid waste to Metropolis and cost him employees and real estate. Affleck does a fine job portraying the sombre, disillusioned vigilante, but it cannot be denied that his explicit aim of killing Superman, who has since amply demonstrated he's on the side of justice, just feels wholly unjustified.

Meanwhile, as if the lethal rivalry between both tormented good guys was't enough to fill a two hour movie, Snyder introduces a younger version of classic villain Lex Luthor to pester them both. This evil tycoon, too, is haunted by a trauma involving his father, which is not enough to fully explain his demonic machinations in this film. What's more, Jesse Eisenberg's performance in the role is devoid of the 'wow' factor we would have hoped for. Applying a typical neurotic hyperactivity, Eisenberg is basically playing a nefarious version of his own Mark Zuckerberg. It doesn't make for a convincing baddie. Nor does Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman leave a lasting impression, which is also due to a lack of screen time (though 151 minutes certainly makes for a long piece already). Again, a shady past is implied but not explored. And so she leaves us confused by her transformation from uncaring socialite to warrior princess fighting for good.

Of course, with a subtitle like 'Dawn of Justice', adding more spice to your duo of core characters for a broader context is expected. So we also get this evil genius and a strong female heroine. But wait, says BvS, there's much more yet. A number of other super heroes is teased. But for ow, we simply cannot care. Worse, the still fairly investing story line of the titular protagonists is hindered by awkward attempts to set up bigger things to come, including an Apocalyptic nightmare of Batman wherein he's plagued by visions of a ruined world ruled by Superman (including insect warriors, I kid you not). Succeeded by a scene in which that same Batman is confronted with a temporal vortex and a warning from the future to stop someone doing something, totally out of the blue. Pointless material, as we already knew Batman was out for Superman's blood and this doesn't motivate him any more. Despite all the useless interruptions provided by DC's self-advertisement for coming attractions (to which we simply are not attracted), it's amazing we still at least care about the two iconic superheroes battling each other.

And their fight proves quite spectacular. Brutal, despite a lack of blood (PG-13 rating and all). But oh so dark and serious. Even Nolan's Dark Knight films, also not particularly light, optimistic fare, never lost sight of the need for a bit of humour and witticism. But Snyder tells such a gritty tale, there's simply no space left for those elements. Unfortunately, after the epic Batman/Superman throwdown, he however feels there is space left for another half an hour of three good guys battling an ugly digital monster. But this climax never feels near as climactic as the fight we expected to see and at least felt somewhat gratifying. As is usual for his approach, Snyder goes over the top much further than we would like him to have gone. Maybe he's not fully to blame for BvS' many shortcomings, a fair bit of it can likely be chalked up to DC interference for setting up the future. But that future does involve Snyder to a great extent, as he's already working on Justice League. We better hope he takes the failures of BvS to heart and lightens up a bit. There's gotta be more to the DC universe than angry heroes beating each other up...

title: BatmanVSuperman was incredible but it was also a mess!
review:
This review may contain SPOILERS please read in your own safety.

BvS one of the most anticipated movies of the year was a spectacle to watch, it looked beautiful but well did it had some major problems. The movie looked and felt beautiful, the action sequences even though they were small they looked like they were taking out of a comic book panel and being played into the cinema screen. But the pacing of the movie felt wrong and the editing seemed somehow sloppy and bad and they were certain parts that felt rushed with no apparent reason or an explanation. This film tried something different, of introducing several major characters and stories into one single movie which not only made it bigger but had to follow at certain points.It tried to chew too much and at the end it forgot to have fun with it self. They are many good things in this but there are also many bad ones. There are several moments that you are seating at the edge of your seat and you go SHOW ME MORE YEAH and then it cuts to something else and you are left with a weird felling that WAIT WHY DID IT END THAT WAY! They say that it doesn't have an ounce of fun in it and I think not every movie like this one should have.

Performance wise. Ben Affleck as Batman/Bruce Wayne was phenomenal. One of the best adaptation in the silver screen. He is different from all the ones you have seen before and get ready to be shocked from both characters he plays. Henry Cavill as Superman/Clark Kent was better than it was in Man of Steel in my opinion. We did get to see more of him as his alter ego Clark which looked smart in certain of his choices and tried to make a difference through his work as a journalist(I liked that they used him more like that) Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman/Diana Prince Well there are certain parts that her delivery has the emotional range of a wooden plank but most of them are being delivered great, even better. She did a great job and I think she can be even better with the right guidance(I though she will sink the movie but well was I wrong). Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor If you like that kind of approach for a villain you will like him a lot. There are moments that you can see how evil he is and that he can be the mastermind behind everything that happens, but at other certain one he takes it too far and he becomes too gimmicky. All the supporting characters did their jobs to the full extent! Jeremy Irons was incredible as Alfred(at the end you want to see more of him). Amy Adams was again the the person that moved the plot when needed it to be, but she was fine again. And Diane Lane did a good job as Ma Kent once more.

Final thoughts. BatmanVSupeman: Was it the best comic book movie of all time? No. Was it the worst one? Not even close! It was a nice movie to watch that had problems that could have been avoided. Maybe with a different director that can sacrifice a little bit on the action sequences and how everything looks and add a little more focus on the story and character development. At the end of the movie I was entertain and left with a smile on my face, and I will see it again for sure. This movie had a lot to offer but as I said it try to chew too much. I liked the way they moved and it took balls to end the movie how it did. Now I want to see what the DCEU has to offer and to be honest I can't wait for it to come.
