title: A Different Type of Superhero Movie & Great Launching Pad for a Cinematic DC Universe!
review: SPOLER FREE REVIEW***********I just came from seeing BvS. I'm a mega superhero geek. I love the Marvel movies and I also loved MoS. I was blown away by BvS! It has a dark tone to it and doesn't integrate humor like a Marvel movie. If you go in expecting a DC version of a Marvel movie, you probably won't be happy. If you go in looking for a good superhero story playing with some pretty deep themes then this movie won't disappoint. It had a slow build up and then just simply exploded (in the best possible way)! I thought it had the best action set pieces I think I have ever seen in a superhero movie. I've never been a super big Wonder Woman fan but when she hits the scene as WW, she nails it! I wasn't sure how I would like Ben Affleck as Batman but I really liked his Frank Miller inspired Batman. Finally we have a cinematic batman who combines the super science, the world's greatest detective, and the world's greatest combatant into one version of the character. Henry Cavill (and his Superman) continue to grow and by the end of the movie, he truly is Superman, not just in name, but in deed and spirit. The easter eggs were awesome and exactly what I hoped for in a movie intent on launching a shared movie universe. I am going to watch it again just to try and discover all of them. Again, I love the Marvel movies but I have never had an emotional reaction to a Superhero movie like I did with the end of BvS. I'm not a very emotionally expressive person but I actually choked up!

title: Finally the Batman we deserve, this is the closest to comic books and the finest we've ever had.
review: I have waited 3 years for this movie. But I am not mentioning that to tell everyone I am a huge fan and I'd watch basically anything. I keep an open mind when i enter the cinema. Let me tell you, they have done a terrific job, they have an outstanding plot, and I already had few ideas what story line they would go with. They actually went ahead and showed us several ideas that we've only seen in the comics and animated movies. It is a damn big deal to come close and make it real. For some reason, destiny maybe, I was watching Injustice Gods Among Us Game sequence 2 days ago because I was pretty sure after watching the promos, that I know this from somewhere, maybe I have seen that while playing the game 2 years ago. Today, when I was watching the movie, I actually jumped out of my seat during the scene when does Flash appears from another universe, says to Bruce Wayne that he has to stop Superman, he is absolutely right about him and that Superman can destroy the whole world. And Lois is they key, and something similar when Superman says they took her(Lois) from me. I shouted I knew it, they had taken that sequence from Injustice Gods Among Us. Then the desert sequence, Batman( in a Nightmare or Alternate Universe) fighting Superman's Army and Darkseid's army. Him being tied up in a basement and several other sequences. I loved how they did it so close. Maybe that does happen, in some alternate universe, and Flash was travelling through time to tell Batman to stop Superman. One Word, Wow. They are setting up for a Big Universe and storyline. I am beyond excited. Now, I can go on and on about CGI, how brilliant each and every actor portrayed their characters. I actually prefer Ben Affleck because he is near perfect portrayal of Batman as we've read in comics and seen in animated movies. (Sorry, Christian Bale was brilliant, but he's nowhere close to a comicbook Batman, I love the trilogy but he's a different Batman.) I loved Gal Gadot as Princess Diana. I am very excited for Wonderwoman movie. The only thing I am shocked and disappointed is how critics are destroying the movie. I understand some people may not like because the movie is too heavy for every audience to digest. That's fine. But I can't imagine labelling it as absolute Trash. Really? One of the near perfect portrayal of Batman, Superman, Wonderwoman, great storyline, outstanding CGI. What else do you expect from it? 10/10. Go Snyder, Affleck, Cavil and Gal Gadot. Love from a huge fan.

title: A tribute to Zack !
review:
It is not very often a fan-base goes so far to defend the director of a movie - but when unholy slaughter becomes unnecessary beatings - it's time for a review by a non critic.

Set in a dark world of redemption, Zack Snyder attempts to extend the repercussions that transpired during Man Of Steel.

18 months later, Bruce Wayne drives through downtown Metropolis in order to reach his new head-office in order to save his workers at Wayne Enterprises, but ends up being witness to utter destruction and human suffering, while Kal-EL forces General Zod to his knees in the sky.

This is the premise.

From here on we follow Bruce Wayne as a detective, with aid of his quite funny Alfred - old and tired (well somewhat) of his looming master Wayne, though always ready and alert, about his whereabouts.

At the same time Kal-EL struggles hard as the upper class world / and or media are quick to question the actions of an Alien. So does the government.

The third storyline, being Lex Luthors (or dare i write the son of Luthor). This obsessed maniac has issues beyond reason, and his rise to power comes through the meanest of tricks. He is not interested in "land" - he wants dictatorship in every sense - as he sees himself.... One sick puppy!

Maybe this movie demands too much of the audience, but if you are able to follow story lines like Inception, you're also able to follow BvS. It's a composition of three different arcs.

Visually you haven't seen anything like this. Every frame perfectly shot, every scene meticulously constructed by Zack Snyder. It's pure eye-candy.

Ben Affleck IS the ultimate Batman. Mad, sinister, hellbent on revenge - twisted as you would expect from a Miller inspired Batman. This guy would not only do TDKR Bane harm, he would laugh at him hanging! As Bruce Wayne, he is if not greater, a calm Wayne, who IS Wayne, and not just a playboy. Secluded, yet wise and with wits.

Eisenberg strikes me as trying to convey the same type of emotions as Ledgers Joker. Difference here though, is that Ledgers Joker was a "funny" monster... Where Eisenbergs has nothing to laugh at. You really quickly get the sense, that this Lex, has so many psychological issues, that he would be better of in a cell. Creepy, is a good word to describe him.. Borderline insanity.

And then we have Cavill. Perhaps, the ONE actor with the highest pressure on his shoulders. And he does a very tragic Superman. In this dark world, his face, his choices are all about redemption - and Cavill conveys them with such emotion - it's heartbreaking to watch!

I however, did not like the forced JL introductions, but I'll accept it, but it does pull the movie a little down.

There are some truly haunting moments, some that surely will drop a tear and some good jokes make up a movie that will end up as being considered masterpiece or complete failure.

We're dealing with the worlds finest, so quite good can never be enough.

If you want pink lollies, go see a Marvel movie. If you want a profoundly deep story, for the grown up audience - you're in for a treat!

It is doing, what it promised! It's a brutal, heartbreaking story of redemption ! It's a serious film, with few laughs - and that's a BOLD STATEMENT in a SuperHero World, that deserves my 8/10 rating.

title: Watch it as a Sequel to Man of Steel and as a Prequel to Justice League. Forget everything that was promised to you.
review:
An Overview (NO SPOILERS) This Movie has been hovering and romancing the minds of the Batman: The Dark Knight Returns and The Dark Knight Trilogy Fans since the Dawn of its Inception. The Fans have watched every bit of the Trailers and read every Fan theory out there just to calm their Nerves. But Does the Movie do Justice to its Fan base ? Nope, Not at all. In fact the worst (For the Fans) and the best (For Marketing) act that Zack Snyder has pulled throughout these 3 years is to have a Straight Face and call it a Batman Versus Superman Movie. It was all a Marketing Strategy to Draw the Gigantic Fanbase of Nolan Trilogy towards this Movie. This is not a Batman Movie. This is not a Superman Movie. This definitely not a Batman V Superman Movie. This Movie is about the Rise of Lex Luthor and the Dawn of Justice League And i must say, DC and Snyder has done a Wonderful Job on this Movie and had built a beautiful foundation for the future of Justice League Movies that will easily Kick Ass of Marvel Avengers Universe. Jesse Eisenberg has acted Brilliantly. Although his Personality does not Resemble Lex Luthor's at any Level his deranged acting makes him watchable Ben Affleck acts really well but makes an OK Batman. Jeremy Irons for change is really different as Alfred. I had my doubt about Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman but to my surprise, She is the next best thing in the Movie after Lex.

Batman Fans will really enjoy this Movie if somehow they can erase the memory of Batman that has been Branded by the Nolan Trilogy.

All in all, the name is deceiving And the several trailers that have already been watched reveal too much about the Movie.

Watch it as a Sequel to Man of Steel and as a Prequel to Justice League

P.S: Henry Cavill, though Wooden faced, is the Best Superman so far.

title: Truly a fantastic movie!
review:
Last night I went to see the movie. I have been waiting years too see this, and guess what, I was not disappointed. However I am very confused and upset at all of the terrible reviews. So here goes my review.

Ben Affleck is Batman. Anyone who says he still is awful, must have some real personal grudge against him. In this film he is truly exceptional and makes me look forward to a solo Batman film. This Batman is not your grandmother's Batman. He is dark, tortured by nightmares, and is tired of what the world has become. As a Batman fan that is something that I truly appreciate seeing in the character. As for the brutality and fans saying what he's using a gun? His Batmobiles always have guns. Michael Keaton's Batman even stuffed a bomb in a goons pants and walked away. Trust me this is not a lot different that other Batman portrayals we have seen in the past. This Batman truly is the best.

The CGI that was used was used well...mostly. It's a comic book movie, of course they are going to use a pretty good amount of CGI. Guardians of the Galaxy was in space...that's a lot of CGI. Overall I think the CGI used was good. I really have no big complaints about that.

Wonder Woman is awesome. Gal Gadot does an amazing job in the role and makes a solo Wonder Woman even more exciting. Her accent was not a problem at all and her acting skill are definitely on par with the rest of the cast. I have seen other reviews saying that her role was not appropriate in the movie, but truly I think it was fantastic. Sure we don't get a full back story for her but we're getting a whole Wonder Woman movie soon. Be patient.

Lex Luthor is different. He's truly crazing. Jesse Eisenberg really did a phenomenal job with the character. Let's remember this was only the first appearance of Lex Luthor, and with the ending, and his finally shaved head I am sure he will be even better in his next appearance.

This movie is crammed with amazing DC things. DC is starting a whole world in one movie of course they may gloss over a few things but for a comic book fan those things that are glossed over are things you will already know. There are so many amazing references and cameos and it make me so excited for the DC cinematic universe. As a comic fan this is exactly what I wanted to see in the movie. I can say for a fact that DC just caught up to Marvel because they established a world in one movie, while Marvel had to do it in many movies.

So there is a true review from a comic book fan. I knew how to fill in the glossed over parts. Regular movie goers may not fully appreciate some of the plot points or even understand how some things are possible in the movie. This movie was truly made for the fans. As a fan of the characters and the comics I can say this was a great movie and my favorite comic book movie I have ever seen. It is truly comic book adapted.

title: BvS will live in the shadow of Civil War
review:
The hype is real. More hype than there ever was before given that it is arguably the two biggest names in the comic book universe. With that said, this is ultimately either too much of a set up to future DC cinematic universe films, Zac Snyder's failed attempt to bring together two of the highest regarded and well known story arcs (both of which have no business being in the same room together, let alone the same film), or both.

Although DC and Marvel have different views on how they tell their character's stories, DC fails to do here what Marvel can successfully do; make me care about the characters. Upon seeing Ant- Man for the first time, there was a likeness to Hank Pym and Scott Lang as characters that, even though we were seeing them for the first time on screen, made me feel like I had known them for a few movies.

Henry Cavill's portrayal of Superman/Clark Kent was on par with the one he had in Man of Steel (do with that what you will based on your opinion), Ben Affleck had probably the third best performance as Batman/Bruce Wayne behind Christian Bale and Michael Keaton (fourth best if you count Kevin Conroy in animated adventures), and Gal Gadot had a too short to judge part as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. The show stealer here was really Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, having the attitude where he acts like the smartest person in the room because he (Luthor) thinks he probably is.

As for the supporting cast, they're just kind of there. Amy Adams once again plays the beautiful Lois Lane, but offers little to the overall plot other than making Superman remember his human side. Most others like Lawrence Fishburne, Diane Lane, and Holly Hunter have somewhat forgettable performances especially given their limited screen time. Perhaps Snyder should rethink his stance on not having actors like Stephen Amell from Arrow, to really have characters fans have grown to love and would unquestionably remember their performance in the film.

I wanted to like this movie, but the too jammed packed nature that was brought across made me need to think about the next one before I even had time to finish processing this one. By all means, this is not a bad movie, but then again, it isn't a great one either. As far as the superhero team up films go in 2016 so far, its Marvel 1 and DC 0, and that is without Civil War even being released yet.

title: Dawn of Justice is the only motion picture that does true justice to the DC comics story line
review:
I think Dawn of Justice is the only motion picture that does true justice to the DC comics story line as in Comics. A DC Comics fan, like me, is going to love this movie. The movie lays a good foundation for Justice League movies and DC universe. This movie revealed various characters from DC Universe other than Bats and Supes, such as Wonder Woman, Lex Luthor, Doomsday, Flash, Aquaman, Cyborg and Firefly. They have even shown Firefly's origin story if I guessed it right.

I hope Justice League movies come out good, but I seriously want to see a movie based on the Alternate Timeline shown in this movie, specifically from Injustice series. If you have read Flash's comics or even watched Flash TV show, you will know about alternate timelines.

Movie is awesome. It's one of the best representation of DC universe and Batman (along with mask of phantasm), and visually very beautiful.

Ben Affleck is very convincing as Batman contrary to what people were speculating. Why he looks older than Superman? The movie is after the time Batman has faced Joker before and as suggested by Robin's costume with Joker's message, Robin is dead. So Batman has been around a while already, but Superman has just arrived on earth. His fight with Zod in "Man Of Steel" destroys Wayne enterprises and Batman considers him a danger.

There are some reasons why people are not liking or may not like this movie. First, this movie can be hard to understand for those who haven't read DC comics or played games such as Batman's Arkham series and Injustice: Gods amongst us. Also, one must watch "Man Of Steel" first before watching Batman Vs Superman. Or one can also read Injustice comics. Second, the sequences related to alternate timelines are not explained properly, so someone can think what the hell is going on. Lastly, I will blame Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy. The trilogy showed Nolan's version of Batman which was quite different from actual story, such as Batman learning from Ra's Al Ghul, Bane being the main villain and few other. And now most of us think that Nolan's Batman movies show the true Batman, and we find it hard to accept a different version.

According to me the movie is not bad at all, as being suggested by Rotten Tomatoes. Fight sequences are very good and I wish there was more of Wonder Woman, but the stage is already set for her, and foundation laid for Justice League.

title: Better brush up on your comics before buying a ticket.
review:
If DC set out to produce a movie that was completely different than the Marvel movies, then they succeeded. Batman v Superman leaves you feeling like you are watching a sequel without an original movie. And no, Man of Steel does not sufficiently set up this "sequel." Imagine if you will, opening a book and starting to read. You are a few pages in, and you realize that there are situations, characters, settings that are unfamiliar or seem out of step. Oh, duh, you started on chapter two by mistake. Just as you flip back to find chapter one, you discover that the pages are missing. DC's attempt to setup an entire comic universe (Justice League), in one movie, failed miserably. However, you will be hard pressed to find another superhero action movie that is more cinematic than this one. The sound and visual effects blew my mind–exponentially more impressive than anything that Marvel (Disney or Fox) has produced; but that's Zack Snyder for you. Unfortunately, the man should have assisted a director in crafting a visual story, not attempted to tell it himself. If DC was fighting a losing battle up a hill, now it is fighting that same battle up a mountainside.

Look! Up in the sky. It's a bird, it's a plane, it's a box-office bomb. Film is a visual medium. The only other more visual medium, one could argue, is comics. And, you better have studied your Justice League universe comics before buying your ticket to this attempt at a Springtime/Easter blockbuster. But unfortunately, that's all that this movie has going for it–it's unparalleled use of phenomenal visual and sound effects to create a fantastically stimulating experience. One problem: where's the story??? I thought that this was (to borrow from Star Wars: the Force Awakens) "supposed to make things right"? Ironic how Easter is a holiday and season which represents rebirth; and as hard as DC Comics and Zack Snyder tried to rebirth this struggling universe, it still remains in the ground. All the water and fertilizer in the world could not help this Easter lily, for the farmer forgot to plant the bulb. There is little to no exposition in the entire movie. If you are unfamiliar with the story from the comics, you will most certainly feel dazed and confused. DC really needed this movie to tell an excellent story in order to continue to compete with the Marvel movies that are coming from Disney and Fox. After this travesty, there is almost no competition any longer. One can only hope that the next installment fixes things. But, it's highly unlikely at this point.

Sometimes poor writing can be covered and masked by flashy graphics and stunning cinematography, other times, it can be assisted by an excellent cast. Well, fail once again. The casting only aided in highlighting the fallacies in the plot structure and nearly non-existent, poorly setup story. Before I negatively criticize the majority of the cast, I need to point out what worked for the film in terms of cast. Although I have been informed that he did not portray the Lex Luther from the comics, I firmly hold to that Jesse Eisenberg played the Lex Luther that this film needed and benefited from. The quirky, psychopathy, childlike, socially awkward, intellectual Lex Luther works for this universe. He was probably my favorite part of the whole movie. He was quite the juxtaposition to other villains that have been in Marvel and DC movies–a refreshing new take. Amy Adams also plays a great Lois Lane. Since I am not familiar with the comics, I am not going to try to compare and contrast her portrayal to that of past Lois Lanes or the ones from the comics. Still, Adams brought about a fantastic charm to the character and she fit in well with Henry Cavill's Superman.

Sadly, the rest of the principle cast was terrible. Since when did Alfred (Jeremy Irons) become nearly Bruce's age??? Maybe he is ten years his senior, but that's pushing it. Alfred is supposed to be a lovable and endearing old man, and Batman's Jiminy Cricket, so to speak. Neither does Irons fit the age or the personality traits of Alfred. I sure missed Michael Caine and Michael Gough's Alfreds. There was a lot of concern when Affleck was chosen to become the caped crusader; and as it turns out, these concerns were valid. He has demonstrated that he cannot fill the cape in the manner in which Michael Keaton and Christian Bale were so successfully able to do. It's entirely possible that Holly Hunter's Senator Finch and Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman/Diana Prince could have been the much-needed support that the film lacked, but their respective characters were severely under-developed. Also, not so much cast as he is character but where did the Kryptonian deformed creature come from??? I think the film tried to explain, but again, it failed. Who cares, though? He made the climax shocking and exciting. A solid match for Superman.

If you want to have your eyes and ears stimulated beyond what you have likely experienced in superhero action movies in the past, then this is the movie for you. Just don't expect much beyond the mesmerizing surface. Already having a 33% on Rotten Tomatoes, most likely the grade will continue to drop. That being said, I DO believe that if you are a follower of the comics and know your stuff, then you will most likely thoroughly enjoy this film. I warn you; be prepared to be your group's personal Wikipedia after the movie.

PS. Didn't realize Gotham and Metropolis were closer than Tampa and St. Petersburg are.

title: One of the worst movies I've ever seen
review:
Dawn of Justice is one of the worst movies I've ever seen. I can't believe I watched it in IMAX and spent so much money on it.

"Ban' Affleck's Batman reminded me of Donald Trump. He wants to kill Superman simply because he is powerful and that there could be 1 percent chance that Superman wants to destroy humanity. Batman hates Superman because a building belonging to Wayne enterprises got destroyed when Superman was battling General Zod. However, he himself destroys buildings and public properties when he is trying to catch the 'bad guys'. So he has a problem with destruction of public properties by an alien and not with the destruction itself.

Batman only has nightmares and cannot get over his mommy and daddy issues. The movie implies that Batman mainly hates Superman because Batman does not have superpowers like Superman does. I haven't read too many graphic novels but I am quite certain that Batman does not suffer from an inferiority complex.

The villain, Lex Luthor, is a bad version of the psychotic villain played by Shahrukh Khan in Baazigar. He only wants to see Batman fight with Superman and his motives simply do not make sense. He does not look believable as a brilliant, intelligent man. He is more of a character out of Cartoon Network.

It seems like Ben Affleck did not get any time to use the restroom while filming this movie because he looks heavily constipated. Perhaps he should try Indian food. He only has a single expression on his face the whole time and does not really care about expressing his emotions (if he has any).

The main story seemed to be inspired from some cheap 90s Bollywood Movie. The Villain kidnaps the mother of one of the heroes to make the two heroes fight with each other. The two heroes start fighting and when one is about to kill the other (for no good reason), he realizes that the other guy's mother has the same name as his own mother. So he spares his life and the become brothers from another mother.

It seems like the whole movie was shot in North Pole during 6 months of darkness as one cannot see Sunlight during the movie. I understand Batman's connection with bats but that does not mean you have to keep showing bats no matter where he goes. He is Batman not bat's man.

There is no plot, the characters don't look believable at all and the direction is uninspiring. It is utterly boring and does not make any sense most of the times. Don't waste your money or time on this.

title: Hollywood Ending
review:
Yesterday, I watched Hollywood Ending, a comedy film by Woody Allen in which he plays a blind film director who makes what may be the world's worst film. Apparently, Batman v. Superman is the film he directed.

The single most incredible thing is that the villain has information and resources that could only be possessed by someone else.

Hollywood's stupidest fight sequence ever.

There are a few talented actors who have nothing to work with and too many talentless people.

title: Super-Disaster (Predictable!)
review:
There is a list of reasons this movie was a horrendous disaster. I don't plan to sit here all night though.

Main Problems: 1. Batman killed many people and it was never explained why he broke the one conviction separating himself from the people he fights. The reason behind it was however hinted at, but if you're not familiar with Jason Todd you're left clueless.

2. Batman woke up one day and decided to kill Superman for no apparent reason. Bruce Wayne is seen watching the news then suddenly turning to Alfred and vaguely suggesting his plans to murder Superman. Batman, a victim himself of bad publicity, watching the news or has Batman just become someone completely different?

3. 30 minute funeral... Half an hour of my life was wasted witnessing a staged funeral for an alien nobody in the audience believed to be dead. It was a pointless portion of the movie that only contributed to how awfully boring it was overall. We knew he wasn't dead, this isn't even a spoiler. There are several films scheduled to come out starring Superman.

4. Batman is a detective, not a juggernaut. In the movie he tears up the city in a loud, brightly lit, tank equipped with a rocket launcher. Apparently instead of analyzing crime scenes Batman would rather just blow stuff up and kill random cops.

5. Batman is stupid in this movie, a blithering fool. I'm surprised he didn't drool.

6. Jesse Eisenberg needs to be fired before the next movie starts filming. I could be a better Lex Luther and I'm a woman (there's a serious problem here).

7. Batman and Superman fight in the movie (Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice" for approximately 15 minutes out of the near 3 hour span of movie. That's a big problem.

8. Batman and Superman stop fighting because they both have/had mothers with the same first names. After that, they were instantly best friends. Again, 15 or so minutes...

9. Tall, beautiful, exotic woman..."I wonder who that could be." Please, we knew who Wonder Woman was the moment she hit the screen, but it still took up to the last half hour for her to make her long awaited reveal.

10. "Doomsday" is now among the legion of potentially amazing characters subjected to "bestialising" (being portrayed as a mindless, rampaging animal) followed by a very quick demise undermining the sheer power such characters are often capable of. A tragic example that we'll never forget is that of Bane (Batman and Robin 1997).

11. Finally, it was just bad. Badly written. Badly scripted. Badly directed. Badly thought through. I got bored. I got up and went to bathroom, when I came back I'd missed nothing. It was just bad. Very bad movie...boring, predictable, uninteresting, unbelievable, bad.

On the bright side kids seemed to like it.

title: Epic!
review: I made the mistake of listening to the reviews and missed this one at the theater. I am so sorry I did. This film has it all! Plenty of action and a fantastic beginning to the formation of The Justice League. Those who are comparing this to The Avengers are comparing apples and oranges. It's like trying to compare Star Wars and Star Trek. Two completely different mythologies here folks. If you aren't ready to accept that, then get off the bus. From start to finish I enjoyed this film. They did a wonderful job of setting up each character in the time that was available, and have done it in such a way that makes sequels inevitable. For which I cannot wait. I won't give away any details in case anyone else was misled as I was into not seeing this at the theater, but I will say that my only gripe with this movie was Lex Luthor. They tried too hard to blend him with The Joker, which doesn't work. This is what I think may have actually turned a lot of people off. But over all what a movie! Don't believe the haters. Oh, and Ben Affleck, fantastic as Batman. (Never thought I'd hear myself say that.) Don't wait till everyone is in bed, you'll want to watch this at full volume!

title: A Flashy Mess
review:
Batman v Superman is a film so frustratingly close to being good that it somehow become significantly worse. There is likely a version of this movie that could rival the best of the genre, but that version is very far away from the one we see on the screen. To start with the good, Ben Affleck kills it as Batman, he is a darker, more brooding, and certainly more mentally conflicted Batman then we have ever seen before. His opening scene is on of the best in the film, mostly carried by his performance. Gal Gadot also does well with the material she's given, and I can't wait to see her solo outing. As I said the opening of this film is very good, rivaling the incredible title sequence from Watchmen. Jeremy Irons gives a good performance as Alfred, and its nice to see the character in a more active role. The aesthetic of the movie is pretty solid. While I'm close to through with the super dark, shadow aesthetic, here it works. One fight scene involving Batman really great, it's a standout of the film and it has me fairly excited to see what he can do when he gets his own movie.

Now for the bad. Firstly the story is bloated, the writers have tried to pack too much into one film and it is painfully apparent. Worse, the pacing of the film is hampered by drawn out and mostly useless dream sequences which completely pull the viewer out of the movie. The movie also wastes time on a subplot about limiting Superman's powers that basically just dead ends when Luther blows up Capitol Hill. Speaking of Luther, his character is unbearably annoying, which I think was the intent, but the writers attempt to frame his argument against Superman as possibly valid (it's basically the same opinion Batman holds), but its nigh on impossible to take him seriously because every word out of his mouth make you want to punch him. His motivation for hating is loosely defined at best, and non-existent at worst and his plot to get Batman to kill Superman is just plain dumb, and feels mostly like a contrivance. The actual fight between Batman and Superman is incredibly bland, you get a few seconds of the two characters punching each other before Batman uses a kryptonite grenade to render Superman useless. The rest of the fights consists mostly of Batman beating up an effectively unconscious man. Most of the fights in this movie boil down to punch-fests, with very little environmental adaptation or gadgetry. Wonder woman uses her powers in the final fight with doomsday, but her powers are so loosely defined that it feels a bit cheap. WW's entire character is, in fact under developed, she gets about 10-15 minutes of screen time, and very few lines. Henry Cavill remains completely uncharismatic as Superman, his performance isn't bad so much as it is just dull. Lois Lane gets the shortest stick here though. The writers try to develop her as a strong female character with a few lines at the beginning of the film, but undercut it with every future plot point.

Ultimately this film shows more promise than it's predecessor, but fails to deliver. Whether through the fault of the writers or the director the version of Batman v. Superman we saw in theaters was a bloated, incoherent mess carried mostly by the skill of one actor.

title: Not A Masterpiece, But An Important Post Modern Commentary Nonetheless
review:
Been meaning to talk more extensively about this one, because arguably the most divisive film of the decade deserves more than a few sentences.

I'll start off by saying that Batman v. Superman is no masterpiece. This isn't a case like the Star Wars prequels or The Wolfman (2010) or even Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom where I will die on a hill in defense of it being one of the greatest blockbusters of all time. There are big problems I have with it.

Eisenberg as Lex was an interesting experiment that I feel ultimately failed. I don't mind the more neurotic take on the character, but the script presents him as too unstable too fast. I feel the direction the film goes with Lex would only have worked as a slow descent into madness (which makes sense, given that Eisenberg's best acted scenes are near the end) It's hardly out of character for Lex to lose his mind on an increasingly obsessive quest to destroy Superman, but there doesn't seem to really be a journey with him as a villain.

Doomsday isn't handled very well here either, which is shocking given that he's so easy to get right. His entire character revolves around him being the enemy of all life, the antithesis to the preserver of life that is Superman. That point doesn't get across very well when most of the death he causes is done in self defense or confusion. He lacks weight, he lacks menace and, worst of all, he's just not intimidating.

Batman doesn't spare Superman because their mothers have the same name. I feel that's self evident at this point, but it's important to say. That's being said, the dreadful dialogue and awkward editing in that scene don't exactly paint a clear picture for Batman's motivations and definitely undermine some rich thematic material and really not-bad acting. Snyder had the right idea with Batman's redemption coming through a son pleading for his mother's life, but the execution is incredibly messy. Scenes like this are why I call Snyder an absent minded professor; he's an intelligent storyteller with smart ideas, but he lacks the wisdom and patience to execute them properly.

Being a cinematic universe film doesn't do this film very many favors either. It's hard for me to take this entirely seriously for the art house masterpiece it's trying to be, exploring deep themes like xenophobia, cultural fear and media irresponsibility, when it's also trying to sell Aquaman, Cyborg and Flash films in a movie that has nothing to do with them.

With all of that out of the way...This is still a good film.

I'm tempted to say that this is the perfect take on the Superman character. Turning him into an allegory for the plight of the American refugee, the victim of horrific prejudice, intolerance and cultural hatred from a race he truly loves unconditionally, gives pathos, vulnerability and cultural relevance to the character that we haven't seen on film before. Cavill gives an outstanding performance as Clark Kent and I had no problem believing the increasingly heavy emotional burden he had to carry in his nuanced, detailed facial acting.

On the other side, we have Affleck's Batman, easily the best performance of the character in live action. He's as intimidating, haunted and convincingly ruthless as any great supervillain and the more cruel and sinister take on the character is a fascinating departure from Bale's version of the character. This is what Batman would look like in the real world; a jaded, paranoid billionaire who spends a small fortune waging a futile war on crime sinking further and further into violent madness. Affleck's vulnerability and fragility keeps the character sympathetic without being truly empathetic, a tragic villain who only finds redemption when Superman shines a mirror on his bigoted, Right Wing jingoistic ways.

The musical score is absolutely outstanding, arguably the most iconic since Elfman's scores of the early 90s. It's epic, sweeping and does a lot of the heavy lifting in translating the film to the modern myth that Snyder is obviously trying to hard to achieve. You Are My World is a particularly moving and emotionally evocative track and easily the most memorable here.

While Batman v. Superman is far from perfect, Zack Snyder should still be proud of what he's accomplished in what's probably the best live action Batman film to date. Heartfelt, smart, grounded and more relevant today than ever, BvS is a remarkably post modern commentary in an era when superhero films rarely aspire to be anything more than repetitive diversions.

title: 8.3/10⭐ Pretentious... or is it?
review:
"...you will battle him to the death. Black and blue; fight night. The greatest gladiator match in the history of the world. God versus man; day versus night." - Alexander Luthor

I suppose I'm right in saying that this is a movie of much controversy; you either loved it, hated it or thought it was just meh. This can be credited to a common misunderstanding of the film's content. It has been said that the film does not establish the characters that well and that their agendas were difficult to understand. Maybe you WOULD think that. If you weren't paying full attention to the movie.

As it turns out, the characters were developed surprisingly well. Superman has already established his agenda of providing hope to the world and displays the exact character coherent with that goal throughout the entire movie.

BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE IS SAID! It is vitally important to understand the context of this film - the DC Extended Universe. This is a dark world. The infamous city of Gotham and all of its atrocities have taken their toll on Bruce/Batman. He is no longer the 'nicer' version of Batman with the no killing rule. Let's get something straight, though. Batman doesn't kill all the time. HE HAS ALMOST BECOME THE "HOLLOW SHELL" THAT IS ILLUSTRATED IN FRANK MILLER'S 'THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS' and was set in motion as inevitable by Heath Ledger's the Joker when he claimed "Batman has no jurisdiction". That said, it is likely that Batman may become more of a criminal eventually. People simply don't want to see this sort of Batman in films.



"In the dream, (the bats) took me to the light...









... a beautiful lie."





This powerful quote is saying that Bruce thought that becoming Batman would make his life and world better, but it didn't. It only made him sink further into his personal darkness. This is sad. A bit depressing, but sad. This is to be expected when "Batman has no jurisdiction". THAT'S RIGHT ALL YOU BALE-OBSESSED FANS! Batman is not perfect. Maybe not even good. Effective, but not always good. HE'S CALLED THE DARK KNIGHT FOR A REASON AND IT'S NOT BECAUSE HE WEARS BLACK! He plunges his "hands into the filth, so that you can keep yours clean", to quote Gordon from The Dark Knight Rises; he is like the dark knights from the Arthurian era: he works by this own methods to serve a kind of justice. Ladies and gentlemen, this... is the true Batman. Bruce, having spent "20 years in Gotham" fighting its crime and seeing "how many good guys are left... how many stay that way", is terrified that superman will become bad like everyone else (including Batman himself). Only this time no one will be able to stop him. It was important that Superman said "No one stays good in this world, Lois."

The dying humanity left in Bruce comes back to him when he is about to kill Superman and the last thing Superman thinks about before he almost died was his mother. That struck Bruce hard. It reminded him of his own mother and how much he cared for her. Bruce couldn't kill someone who had that kind of a bond in his life.

When Heath Ledger's the Joker's destructive agenda was mysteriously insinuated people were intrigued, but Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor made sense. He has grown up in an unfair home with a cruel father (hinted at in the 'Smallville' television series) and now does not want some other form of God to rule his life unfairly. Lex claims that God (or rather, anyone who is in a great position of power) is always evil. He says that "the world needs to see the holes in the holy" and since Superman is already being questioned by almost everyone for his reckless actions, Lex wants to seal the deal and make it official. He claims some kryptonite for himself, but has that stolen from him, so he continues his work in the kryptonian vessel. You could say that he used Doomsday as a last resort. I would like to mention that Lex's script had some excellent parts to it at times.

Is this movie pretentious? Maybe a little, but truthfully, this is a very serious concept. Something truly epic and truly dangerous is going to happen. I haven't seen the ultimate edition yet, but I heard that it is better than the theatrical release because it explains more, though it is 3 hours long.

This is undoubtedly an under-appreciated movie. But coming from a DCEU fan, Justice League could've used some work and Suicide Squad was trashy and boring at times.

title: Batman v Superman will likely always be highly divisive, and it is very much a Marmite film; you'll either love it or you'll hate it.
review: BvS is not the worst installment of the DC Extended Universe. It is also not the best. There is no way you can ignore the numerous flaws that the film possesses, but there are also a lot of enjoyable elements in the film as well. What I'm implying is that BvS is distinctly average. Much of the story feels tedious, but the spectacle nearing the end of the film is immense. The action is overly stylish, but the plot is practical and coherent. Zack Snyder has directed a film with positives and negatives in equal proportion. For example, the performances; Ben Affleck is surprisingly compelling as Batman, providing a layered portrayal of the caped crusader. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman is also immediately charming, and Jeremy Irons makes a decent Alfred. Contrastingly, Henry Cavill's Man of Steel is once again soulless and uninteresting; I find his Superman too dull and dark, much like the film's tone. Jesse Eisenberg is horrifically miscast as primary antagonist Lex Luthor-there haven't been many villains which induce less fear than Eisenberg's eccentric take on Superman's nemesis. Lois Lane is also very character deprived, as hard as Amy Adams tries to fix it. Snyder's direction is a mixed bag; sometimes it's too arty, other times too CGI filled, but other times well handled. Tone is a major problem, which I am pleased that the people at DC have attempted to correct with Justice League, because the film is just too gloomy. You go to see films to have a good time, and tonally BvS defies that purpose. The film is also overstuffed with potential plot lines; I believe the studio gave this movie too much to do. Overall, a little disappointing, but still full of great spectacle to enjoy.

Zack Snyder with his great visuals and direction along with Chris Terrio and David S. Goyer created an amazing comic book film that will be talked about for years. Like movies like Blade Runner and 2001 this movie will be looked back on years later and opinions will be changed because in time people will realize this is just simply a great film...and a comic film truly ahead of its time.

title: Not For Children!
review:
First of all. Spoiler Alert. Do Not Read if you need to be surprised to enjoy a film.

Superman Dies. Granted it takes almost two long hours but the man of steel kills himself in the midst of epileptic blinding cgi explosions (i think no less than three nuclear bombs go off) to kill a big green monster that's half Jesse Eisenberg and half Michael Shannon so I guess it's an Unbreakable Irish Jew. The movie which was already about 20 minutes too long added another 20 in the aftermath of an unnecessary and unearned death of the title character. For nearly the first hour I loved it and my internal comic geek and film buff were rapt. But while early on there were some intelligent and beautiful visuals that honored the legacy of the characters after the first 40 minutes or so (much like Zack Snyder's Man of Steel) you feel the horrible notes of the studio forcing video game-like unrealistic and overlong action sequences designed to supposedly feed the already jello brained screen addicts in the audience. I think they may literally have jumped several sharks in the Batmobile sequences. You get nods back to character and story in the second and third hours of the movie but none woven into real satisfaction. Much like Man of Steel the actual casting and acting plays very well in moments. There is decent chemistry between all the actors and the dialogue is nicely crafted with the unfortunate exception of the very talented but strangely misguided or ill written Lex Luthor. Unless it was Jesse Eisenberg who felt the need to play Lex as the Joker or rather a generic loon instead of a megalomaniac/narcissist which would have been much more interesting coming from this actor. Perhaps it's all Snyder's fault and yet he's paid millions and millions and the movie still grossed almost a billion dollars. What is wrong with the folks at Warners Film when across the way Greg Berlanti is doing a better job of creating a DC universe on TV for less money? Sadly, Snyder is not at all Christoper Nolan who did such an extraordinary job with the Dark Knight series or even a Tim Burton. If he has a vision it's either being screwed with by the studio or it is a Lex Luthor like sabotage of the legacy and a cruel let down to anyone who grew up loving these characters in the many incarnations they have been previously given (yes even Clooney's attempt at camp). Finally and to my first point do not take a child under 12 or even let your child see it if he or she is sensitive. Maybe if your kid is a video game addict he or she is already desensitized to life and death and will be fine. But more likely your kid will lose interest in the first hour which plays best for an audience of continuing education film students or comic geeks who haven't showered for a few days. If you have a child who loves Batman and Superman stick to the Lego movies.

title: Unexpectedly Enjoyable.
review: I missed this movie when it was out in the cinema. Sometimes I tend to let a blockbuster pass me by. Usually because i don't get the chance or sometimes because the slating it receives in the vultural media is off-putting. Not that i would trust the judgment of most critics, just that I might feel prejudiced and critical myself of a movie that I should simply sit down and enjoy. After picking this movie up recently on Blu Ray I did just that. I sat down and enjoyed it. I wasn't expecting a whole lot...but was pleasantly surprised nonetheless. Now I'm not a comic nerd and can't refer to any story line lineage and thus could not be offended as a puritan. However, the plot was straightforward and well acted. Personally I wasn't overjoyed with the choice of Affleck as Batman. Truth is, he pulls it off. He put's in a believable display of an older Batman a little angry at the world. It had action, humour...and wonder woman. Now Gal Gadot is no Linda Carter...but my word, that's a movie I shall be checking out next year regardless of plot line, and I don't even care if Ben Affleck is in it wearing a cocktail dress. In short, it was a good watch. On a par with the marvel movies for sure. The only personal gripe I had was with Lex Luthor being portrayed akin to Heath Ledger's joker. If only Gene Hackman was younger. Anyway, it was better than I thought and to be fair, should be declared a decent movie in its own right. If you haven't seen it, check it out.

title: What's Sup?
review:
What's Sup?

The problem with DC Comics compared to, say, Marvel is that their superheroes are mutually exclusive. Bringing them together is therefore a difficult task, to say the least. It just doesn't work in this instance. Also, DC is very late in the convergence business, when the other team, for all its on screen sins, has developed most of the Avengers characters into their own franchise, allowing for a passable team spirit with occasional bouts of dialogue brilliance. Nothing of the sort here.

The movie, already bloated at 150′, also exists in a 180′ minutes "full" version, the deleted scenes giving some screen cred to some of it most baffling scenes but doing nothing to improve pace or character development. If Zach Snyder remains gifted with this rarest of quality in action movie directing, i.e. spatial consciousness, allowing the audience to follow who is fighting who, where and sometimes even why, his writing crew, who already presided over Man of Steel and the Christopher Nolan- helmed Batman trilogy, attempts at mixing oil and water and trips until it crashes under the weight of their portentous project.

For a movie opposing an omnipotent flying boy scout and a sociopath multibillionnaire with all sorts of vehicles at his disposal, Batman v Superman is shockingly pedestrian. Worse, it respects road lights and zebra crossings. So, what is the heck happening in two and a half hours?

After we are treated to the umpteenth version of the scene in which Master Bruce is saved by a Batnado, he grows up into Bat Affleck (doing his best Christian Bale impersonation and appearing smug in the process), who fills Gotham's prison with criminals he brands with red iron, meaning "certain death" at the end of their fellow convicts. Not only this is an idiotic idea, but it subverts the League of Justice purpose by reintroducing death penalty through the back door, while the State looks the other way. Hollywood, you are going on a dangerous limb.

The State acts in the opposite way in Metropolis, where Superman's proclivity to bring home his Kriptonian buddies for urbicide and countless civilian casualties comes under scrutiny. A "Kentucky junior senator" (Holly Hunter) wants him to answer to a federal commission and be harnessed for the greater good, to which Sup (Henri Cavill, gloomy) reacts by sulking. No doubt she's a democrat and she wants more State intrusion into the American people's constitutional rights.

Under the pretense of caring for collateral victims – an interesting idea in itself, if possibly quite boring in its 'The State vs. Superman" execution – the movie succumbs to its own hubris, shared in equal measures by its producers and its characters. Lois Lane (Amy Adams, bland) has never been so stupid – she interviews yet another African warlord (why are they popping out in every blockbuster this year?) and her first question is "Are you a terrorist?". Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg, interestingly mannered) is obviously deranged but no one seems to mind. At some point he mates with General Zod's corpse in a red pool and gives birth to "an abomination" called Doomsday, which could be doing an internship from any Kaiju next door, since it's just a mass of pixels, unkillable until it's killed.

So the Gotham Bat, as they call him, and Superman fight for a while, kryptonite kriptonite kriptonite, Batman knocks Superman out with a bathroom sink. Appear briefly The Flash (unnamed) and Aquaman (Jason Momoa). Also, Wonder Woman (Gad Gadot, sleek) comes to the big boys' rescue, allowing a "Bruce, I am your brother" moment who does not only feel embarrassing but the mark of writers at the end of their tethers, unable to elevate the material to its God-like ambitions.

What else? There is a lot of tuning, Bruce Wayne sporting a bat logo on his civilian car and Superman his logo on the coffin he's beyond the shadow of a doubt not buried in. Lois Lane dies but not, as required by her character. The Army nukes Doomsday, misses and the charge – apparently a mild one – falls on an "inhabited" island in the middle of the bay separating Metropolis from Gotham (asking all sorts of questions about why an encounter between Supie and Bat Boy didn't occur before and cautiously not answering any of them). There is a bit of King Kong, a bit of Tarzan and whatnot. Best of all, there is Jeremy Irons as Alfred the Butler, a considerable step up from Sir Michael Caine.

Oh also, there is what one prefers to think is a touch of meta humour, by courtesy of a open jar of urine labeled "Granny's Peach Tea". As a metaphor for inspiration, it works rather well. Come on, get back to the writing table already. It's already absurd with two and a half superheroes, how could it possibly be better with five?

title: The meeting of two icons of DC Comics
review:
For those who watched the trilogy "Dark Knight" by Christopher Nolan and after the most recent adaptation of the Man of Steel, led by the talented Zack Snyder and having Nolan as a producer, saw clearly a high visual convergence between these two icons of comics. For those who saw the completion of The Man of Steel (2013), already imagined possible reasons for a meeting of super-heroes and before long it was announced the meeting of the two greatest exponents of comics.

The Oscar winner for Argo (2012), Chris Terrio wrote the screenplay alongside David S. Goyer. The option to Terrio and Goyer was to divide the movie into three major acts with a background story that seeks to link the events. The first part begins simultaneously to the final act of the Man of Steel and shows the consequences of the Metropolis of destruction and as the battle of Superman with General Zod affected people. In these early sequences are presented to the new Batman, now played by Ben Affleck, and there we already know the reasons for which he finds Superman as a threat and start to devote their time to fight it. The third act is more focused on the completion of all, bringing a lot of action, superior even to the end of the first Avengers (2012). At this point, Zack Snyder presents fans with scenes visually clean, in a show of visual effects team. The pace only grows in this final hour. There are many struggles with a high degree of realism in complex movements. Many thought like Batman could face Superman on equal terms, as Batman is a human very well trained and prepared, while Superman is simply the most powerful man the universe. When the Apocalypse - known to have been responsible for the death of Superman in the successful story "Superman's death" (Superman # 75 in the US) - enters the story is that in fact everything is raised to the tenth power. Another point to highlight is the soundtrack of Junkie XL and Hans Zimmer. The trail is urgent, shocking, and thunderous striking. special emphasis on the theme track of Wonder Woman. When the song ( "She Is With You?") Starts playing as soon as she first appears as the heroine, it is a unique moment.

title: The foundation of a franchise without being a standalone film.
review:
Regardless of subjective skepticism on various levels; the divisive reception of the previous installment "Man of Steel", the expansion of a franchise hinting at subsequent stand alone films,the initial reviews, consisting of mixed to negative from critics and a more favorable reception from general movie goers, in addition to the simplicity of being its on self contained narrative; I still had the intention of viewing this film from a rational and overall optimistic outlook before I made any generalisations.

But after watching the film and validating both good and flawed aspects, skepticism prior to the viewing is exactly what prevented it from being a disappointment, as on a basic verdict, it was exactly how I expected it to be, an incoherent, convoluted and forced attempt at setting the first steps of a larger universe without establishing intrigue or investment.

The movie is not without its redeeming qualities.

The representation of some of the comic book counterparts was done effectively. Ben Affleck's depiction of the titular role managed to prevail over the controversial casting decision to deliver a strong performance on both personas as Bruce Wayne and Batman.

With the origin less emphasised and more implied to interpretation, the characterisation of Batman was done well for the most part, but would have been more effective in a more coherent premise.

The MAJORITY of the supporting actors also manage to convey strong performances, notably Jeremy Iron's portrayal of Alfred and the feature length debut of Wonder Woman by Gal Gadot.

Their presence in the film, while few and far between in terms of adequate screen time and and character interactions, still provided for intrigue that hopefully will be depicted more in depth in the subsequent installments.

Unfortunately, aside from visually stunning cinematography, the unique stylistic look present in all of Zack Snyder's previous directorial efforts and the majority of the action sequences, at this point I am done elaborating on the positive aspects.

The few redeeming aspects in the film are hardly enough to compensate or for me to overlook a cluttered plot, disjointed pacing, underdeveloped character motives, lazily shoe-horned in Justice League set ups and overall a movie that feels dull, hollow and at its lowest moments the last term I want to describe a film- boring.

For the majority of the film's run-time, there are evident attempts at being dark and realistic, which would have worked if not for the tonally inconsistent moments.

The impact of a dark depiction of the source material was reduced significantly with the inclusion of Eiseberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor.

Not only did his on screen presence feel forced an out of place, not only was he an underwhelming and pathetic antagonist, but his comic relief hardly compensated for the absence of genuine humour and likability that the movie was seriously devoid of, ruining any sense of escapism.

As for Eisenberg's performance, while forced and at its worst making supposedly pivotal moments laughable and contrived, even a superior casting choice such as Bryan Cranston or Mark Strong wouldn't have made the humorous and insane depiction of Lex believable. They only would have benefited the role if the screen writing had portrayed how Lex was established in the comics and previous material, calculating and intelligent. (I am aware he is Lex Luthor Jr,but that was still an unnecessary approach for the character)

"Man of Steel" was flawed and inherited the same problems as this film, but at least it felt stand alone. There was no concern over further installments and had the intention of emphasising the perspective of just one character. This film prioritises the expansion of an entire franchise, ensuring installments for various pre-established characters of the DC mythos, and because of this the screen writing glosses over something as simplistic as a basic premise and coherent characterisation from the two titular characters.

The Justice League set ups via the email gave that very implication. There is no intrigue or anticipation for the next steps of the franchise when no appeal or reason to be invested have been illustrated sufficiently.

The political evaluation of Superman's actions was necessary, but gradually became overly emphasised with more focus on exposition and less emphasis on why the publicity and the world were against him.

Henry Cavill delivers a solid second on screen performance as Superman/Clark Kent, but his characterisation and interaction with Batman was weak and not fleshed out. He had no real reason to oppose Batman's ideals and his reason for the confrontation was cliché and lacked tension.

The brief fight sequence with Batman at the climax of the film was initially enthralling, but their overall confrontation was redundant.

With their lack of prior interaction, there was no emotional implication to be engaged with the outcome of the fight sequence.

The resolution of the fight, after the controversially cliché "MARTHA!" scene, felt rushed and forced.

Batman and Superman's lack of interaction was the most disappointing aspect of the film, with their eventual union feeling underdeveloped.

But the unnecessary climax of the film was the decision of killing Superman off. Had he been explored with more depth, there would have been some emotional weight to the scene.

But his supposed death seemed less like a bold decision and more like a plot device for setting up the Justice League.

In addition, the movie backs away from the concept with the final shot implying the dirt rising from the coffin. It was hardly subtle, as it couldn't be any more evident Superman is alive.

Overall, aside from its under-cooked narrative and forced approach to adapt the source material, this movie does not even feel like a genuinely entertaining popcorn flick.

As a final verdict, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a horrendous and boring 2 and a half hours.

title: DC Graphic Novel not Comic Book
review: As a continuing story for Man of Steel - this film is fascinating. We are leveled to Ground Zero and the United State's fixation on post-9/11 paranoia is fully explored. Batman is brutal & almost merciless as he battles the demons of his values and his position in the world. It's so good to see comic book character challenged. shifting and evolving into versions or amalgams of tropes we've seen on paper. The squeaky clean versions are not present here... instead the characters are bitter ... troubled to the point that Supe's "Hope" symbol is reduced to just a letter. ... And here's the difference -- Marvel (on the whole) seem to be stuck on making films for teenagers & kids ... DC are developing films that are growing up with their audience. Snyder is fluent in the medium of graphic Novel... this isn't comic book stuff ... & there is a big big difference. He coped a lot of backlash -- which was reactionary & childish. Hopefully this doesn't affect his vision... we'll see....

title: Much better than I hoped for (Ultimate edition)
review:
I'm not a fan of super-hero movies, I didn't really like the idea of Affleck portraying Batman/Bruce Wayne, I didn't like Man of steel, and yet, I really liked this movie ! First I must give my hat to Ben Affleck which gives a new force to the Wayne/Batman character. Previous portrayals by good actors led me to believe that the batman was some kind of James Bond with a spandex black suit. Not in a ridicule way but in the way they were moving, fighting and behaving on a daily basis : archetype of rich classy guys and perfectly choreographed and skilled fighting. Affleck gives it angrier, more "realistic" touch that I really appreciated. I liked the introduction of Wonder woman who gets this character out of the kitsch era with charm and strength.

The movie has some lengths of course but overall no really unnecessary scenes. I'm basing this review on the "Ultimate edition" (UHD BD) so can't comment on the theatrical version.

A little regret on Lois Lane who didn't keep the feminist iconic figure she had in Man of steel (she got replaced by Wonder woman in this thing) one of the rare aspects I liked in man of steel.

I'm not really into searching goofs in a superhero movie (for me, they are already goofs in a way) so this didn't bother me.

Overall a far from perfect yet very entertaining movie, a very good performance from Affleck. A dark superhero movie that's a little more interesting to watch than an Avenger-film

title: Disjointed and depressing
review:
Acting - good; special effects and action sequences - great; Wonder Woman - amazing. Plot and story line - horrible.

In spite of the horribly disjointed script and twisted story line, all of the actors provided good performances. Especially well portrayed were Diana Prince (Gal Gadot), Alfred (Jeremy Irons), and Clark Kent (Henry Cavill). Worthy of note were Amy Adams, Diane Lane, and even Ben Afflack--Laurence Fishburn was under-used and his Perry White unfortunately lacking in depth. Even more unfortunate was Jesse Eisenburg's villain, who was so over the top insane, one must wonder how his Lex Luthor ever managed to stay out of the psych unit, much less build a major corporation.

I realize that the DC "Universe" is darker than the Marvel "Universe" but really people, let's at least give the next film a plot that adheres to at least some of the elements of good story telling.

title: This movie is like a girlfriend that one has been dating for a short while and one begins to see a long-term relationship (DC Universe)
review: Not sure whether my taste buds are that far off the majority, but I really enjoyed both cuts of the movie, and it totally makes sense that only Bruce's love for his mother would break through his irrational vengeance and reawaken his humanity. title: Daft editing, sadly lacking in explanations, but with a few highlights
review:
I loved 'Man of Steel', and had high hopes for this film. I was not certain when I heard that Ben Affleck had been cast as Batman / Bruce Wayne, but he turned out to actually be a highlight of the film.

The beginning of the movie is excellent: the latest iteration of the Wayne family murder (what is this, the third generation of this in the last 25 years?), but nicely done... then a fantastic sequence of Wayne driving through Metropolis during the chaos that was the battle between Zod and Superman. Amazing. I was slack-jawed.

Then it all started to fall apart. Sequences with no explanations, very sloppy editing with jerky transitions between scenes... a comedic walk by Lex Luthor down a hallway paradoxically set to some super-serious Hans Zimmer music... stupid dream sequences that are way too long, out of place, not well explained... all silly and dreadfully stupid.

I was slack-jawed, but now for a different reason. This movie had gone from 'hero' to 'zero'.

What was worse was the ongoing use of bad CGI that did not obey the laws of physics. Not only was it easily identifiable as CGI (Chris Nolan would never have let that junk through, his CGI was always seamless), but the way things moved in reaction to the exertion of various forces never, ever looked right. Whoever did these effects had no clue how the laws of physics work. Again, I was horrified. Part of the allure of Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy was its incredible realism. Look as you might, nothing on screen really looked fake. Compare that with the car chase in the Batmobile, where nothing is moving the way it should when it gets hit by something else, and this just pales by comparison.

And then there is Lex Luthor, who is an absolute idiot until his very last scene. This take on the character is aberrant, bizarre, and stupid. They should just have brought in the guy from Smallville.

I thought that the bad blood between Batman and Superman was rather well explained; you could see their separate perspectives at least.

Now, on to a few positives: Wonder Woman was AMAZING. (Except, right before she comes on screen as Wonder Woman, she changes clothes and locations three times in about two minutes... again, bad, bad editing). Doomsday was also awesome, and when the three heroes take him on, it was spectacular.

Another positive was Ben Affleck in the role of Bruce Wayne / Batman. I know a lot of people just hate him; I've never actually hated him, I just take each performance on its own merits. I loved Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne / Batman. But this performance by Affleck was outstanding, in my opinion. There were a few moments when I actually thought he was better than Bale -- and that's something I never thought I'd say.

The positives, however, do not outweigh the negatives... I would have waited an extra year if it meant that the director and studio could put out something that was actually decent.

On top of everything else, there is very little 'fun' in the movie. It just comes off like it takes itself too seriously for its own bad CGI and bad editing. Almost as bad as a bad SNL 'spoof'.

Terrible job an what should have been an insanely awesome movie. Two stars. Change things up in the behind-the-scenes staff before the next installments in the series. Make the next ones more like 'Man of Steel', or the fun-loving, rather lighthearted Marvel movies will crush the DC franchise in its tracks.

title: Horrible from the comic fan perspective.
review:
I have wanted to write this for some time, but as everyone was busy bashing the film from a film perspective, or defending it from a comic fan perspective, I thought i'd wait until it died down to write an honest and opened critic of the film.

To begin with it looks amazing, and I enjoy the overall dark tone. With that out of the way, the movie was horrible. The problem's don't stem from Zack Snyder, as most would argue, but rather from the writers.

Lex Luthur didn't seem like any interpretation of the character that I have ever read.He was zany and wacky, came across as a genius, but was not by any means of the word a charismatic con artist. This is the biggest fumble in my opinion. That would be like watching a batman movie and they get Joker wrong. We would burn them at the stake.

Batman/Bruce Wayne was not the world's greatest detective, in this film adaptation. The worlds greatest detective would have to go to Lex Luthur who was able to find all the main players of the justice league. The math that Bruce Wayne used as well with his, 1% chance being taken as an absolute certainty, is just faulty. This interpretation of the character lacks logic, and the character is all logic in the comics. Logic and heart. They made this character all mania and brawn.

Lastly, comic book stories are character driven, hence why getting the characters wrong is a big problem, but in this story the characters aren't very interesting, nor are they even coherent in their own narrative. It jumps back and forth way too much and thus doesn't give you the chance to care about any character.

This is a big problem for the DCEU.

title: Some good elements but even more bad elements
review:
It's been a long time since I've seen such an uneven movie. There are some good elements, but mainly bad elements - and nothing adds up.

It's a mess and the plot goes to all different directions without aim. It's like they had some good elements and they threw it here and there; it feels like scenes don't have any connection between them. There are so many flaws to this movie that I wouldn't know where to start. The motivation of Batman, Superman and Lex are very unclear and unrealistic to me. 3/4 into the movie and Wonder Woman only had about 3 lines.

But the worst thing for me in this movie is that every time I think "Hey, this is kind of smart/cool and they did it well", the movie takes a sharp turn and ruins it with pumping bad elements.

The battle of Batman vs. Superman feels just awkward - the motivation is missing (I don't see any reason for them to actually fight, although the writers tried to find some excuses for that) and it feels like a battle written for fans, trailers and to justify the movie's title.

Here are some of the things I like about this movie: Jesse Eisenberg - I'm not a fan of him, but just like you see in the trailers, he's an interesting character and Eisenberg plays him rather well with his weird behavior. I think he's doing a good job in this role.

Jeremy Irons - Alfred is not just a mentor anymore, but an actual helper. His character is different from the previous versions and Irons played his well. How is he in comparison to Caine? You can't compare the two of them - their characters are just too different.

Ben Affleck - Again, I'm not a fan, but he's OK in his role. His character is written very flat IMHO, so he doesn't make a huge or memorable impact.

I like the approach of trying to make a "down to Earth" realistic movie. It feels like they were trying to say: What would really happen in today's world if characters like Superman and Batman actually existed.

I also like the way the writers took the previous movie and connected it to this one in several elements, mainly the reason for Batman to hate Superman. Again, it's a good idea and I like it, but it doesn't seem like a good explanation to explain it.

The religion references are very explicit here and for the first time I actually like them because they "realistically" discuss the implications of Superman being a semi-god.

The last quarter of the movie is pretty bad and it ends with the usual mess you're familiar with in these kind of movies.

With so much publicity for Wonder Woman, it's almost hard to believe that her part in the movie is more or less what you see in the trailers.

This is a 2.5 hours movie that feels like 5 hours.

title: Connecting "Superman II" to Doomsday
review:
I've been gone for a while, and this was one of the first films I have seen for a few months. As always, I rate not by my faulty sense of how good or bad a film is, but by how much I enjoyed it. And, despite some huge problems, I really did enjoy this.

As with Zack Snyder's "Watchmen", we have a painted canvas that tells a story - Not as well as he told Watchmen, but as well as he could make it, with the mess he was handed.

And by Mess I mean, why on earth was the "General Zod" story line from Superman II resurrected for Man of Steel? I don't think the Zod story ever was told in Classic Superman comics, and it was not a good story especially since Richard Donner was removed as Director for it - Simply so that Menaham Golan would not have to pay Marlon Brando another 10 million dollars.

But somehow Zod reappeared in Man of Steel. That was the worst part of that film as well.

I have been a fan of Superman and a reader of comics since I was 5 years old, all through the 60's, and there were some great stories told back then. But one thing about the Batman of that era, he never used a gun, he never even touched them. So in the 80's when a Machine-Gun toting Batman appears (even though they were only in his Batmobile), I was shocked. The Batman from Chris Nolan's latest trilogy did not use them, at least not that much.

But this Batman in Dawn of Justice, is an Angry Batman. And a Batman who will use guns, and even kill people with them.

This film starts mainly with the battle of Zod and Kal-El seen from Bruce Wayne's perspective, which gives us an interesting view of what was happening underneath. Ben Affleck did a great job, an aging, angry Batman. being manipulated by Lex Luthor, but not knowing it yet.

Many people have said this film lacked a narrative structure, and it is true. The story is told visually, much like Watchmen was, but lacking Watchmen's great Narration as heard from Rorshach and Dr Manhattan, two very different people telling the same story. In Dawn of Justice, it's much the same way: The story is shown from Clark's view as well as Bruce's and even Lois.

I highly encourage anyone who has not seen this to skip any theatrical versions and go straight to the extended version, which explains much more about the underlying Metahuman stories.

While Bruce is nodding off at one point, is he visited by a Metahuman? He sees a man, who says it is "too soon"- But is it a dream? I am very curious about that, Zack Snyder is very good with little hints like this. I don't know what that meant, but I suppose in Justice League we will find out.

But the breakout performance here is by Gal Godot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman, and neither Batman nor Superman know who she's with. She was by far the best Wonder Woman of any Film or TV show, an actress that did not have to go far to really look and act the part.

The one good thing Zack has done with this film is effortlessly merging one of the most popular Superman stories (The Doomsday saga) with the Zod story or Superman II. Zack always does well with films based on Graphic Novels or Comics, and this is no exception. And it stands up to multiple viewings.
