title: BvS is a DC fans dream and ignites a world of wonder
review:
Let's just get one thing straight.....all the people saying Batman v Superman sucks are wrong. All the critics giving it incredible hate are wrong. There's no way this film is as bad as everyone makes it out to be....and it's NOT. Regardless if it met your expectations or not, it still delivers a solid popcorn flick that is entertaining. So those saying it's terrible are wrong. It's not an opinion, it's fact. It's like saying Star Wars (the original) is terrible. That person would be considered an idiot and it's not an opinion because it's one of those films that can't be considered anything below "entertaining" and BvS fits into this category.

Now that the rant is over, time to talk about what was awesome in the film.

Batman: Ben Affleck, first hated upon the casting announcement, proves that he is the Dark Knight comic fans have been waiting for. He delivers a solid mix of the Batman we see in the comics, Arkham games and overall every Batman you could possibly think of (Adam West and earlier incarnations aside). He proves that he will become the best Batman once he gets his own film (Under the Red Hood please). Not only that, he balances Batman perfectly with Bruce Wayne, portraying the two with such ease you'd start to wonder that maybe he was born for this role.

Superman: I've read a lot of complaints saying how bland and boring Superman was, that he was given barely any screen time. I however found he was given equal screen time with Batman and I also found myself rooting for him in the final battle with Batman. He did what Superman needed to do and always has done.

Wonder Woman: The biggest surprise to me. Gal Gadot owns this role. You can still think she was miscast but ultimately she was bad ass in the role.

Oh and then there's Alfred! I wasn't really on board with Jeremy Irons as Alfred but he delivers something new to the role that escaped Michael Caine in The Dark Knight trilogy. Still Gotham's Sean Pertwee remains my favourite Alfred.

In regards to Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor....it's safe to say you'll either hate him or enjoy him thoroughly as the maniac. I enjoyed him as Lex. It was different but I kept thinking we could have had a better Lex Luthor.

The visuals in this film were stunning, the action incredible and the story was really good. A lot of people (and I mean everyone but me) complain that the film has poor pacing and feels like 5 films happening at once.....but I found that each and every character's story that they were going through tied effectively together with the overall story. The whole "feels like 5 films" thing bugs me. Think back to 2008 with a little Tarantino film call Inglourious Basterds. A film that at it's very core has multiple movies happening at once that tie together effectively to one main story. If you're going to use the argument that BvS feels like 5 films, then consider that this Tarantino film did essentially the same thing yet got acclaim from critics and audiences upon release. To me this renders the '5 films' opinion redundant.

Lastly, here's why I believe BvS got such bad reviews. Marvel has dominated the superhero film world, no doubt there. It created a standard for super hero films. The world of the MCU is kid friendly, light in tone, very different to the dark world of the DCEU. I believe critics and a lot of the audiences have been too wrapped up in Marvel films, the same formula executed every time (sure yes different stories but essentially the same styles) that when BvS hit.....the critics didn't know if they should say it's good or bad because it was completely different from a Marvel film so they decided to say it was bad. This happened with Man of Steel as well.

I am a die hard DC Comics fan, I read and bleed DC Comics. So when I say BvS is a DC Comics fan's dream you know I mean it.

This film is under rater, undeserved of the low ratings and ultimately delivers a new type of super hero film to see if you're sick of the same Marvel formula executed twice every year. It's time for change and it begins here.

title: Thank God for Wonder Woman.
review:
I have been a DC fan as well as a Marvel fan since the age of 7. I grew up watching the animated series of the DC Animated Universe (DCAU) controlled by Bruce Timm. What did the DCAU (1992-2006) have that the DC Extended Universe (2013-Present) does not have at the moment? I will tell you! The DC Extended Universe does not have meticulous planning or someone like Kevin Feige to implement the universe. In other words, FOOLS RUSH IN!!!

Batman: I don't understand why people were angry at the casting of Ben Affleck. One of the many things, I liked about this version of Bruce Wayne is that the character has gone through a rough and horrific time off screen before the events in this film.

Superman: All I am going to say is that this time he showed concern for humanity as well as the damage he caused in Man Of Steel (2013) when he was fighting General Zod.

Wonder Woman: The director could have chosen any actress to play the Princess of Themyscira, but I am over the moon Snyder chose Gal Gadot to play Wonder Woman because she is not just the perfect choice, but she has had previous military training as she has served in the Israeli Army for two years. The loyalist fans will be impressed by her scenes when she arrives for the showdown with Doomsday. In addition, she WILL not only prove the critics wrong 100 percent, she will also make the hypocritical fans look like fools for saying that she does not have the physique or the talent to portray such a heroic and pivotal character. Whoever said that Gal is a skinny Prada princess (gorgeous but miscast) needs their eyes & head examined.

Lois Lane: I am sure many - along with me - adore Amy Adams as Lois Lane in this film as well as Man Of Steel. She played a pivotal role in the first film as well as a very important role in Batman V Superman: Dawn Of Justice and I am sure she will even play a more important role in the upcoming film adaption of Justice League as well. Amy Adams plays the Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter in a resolute, tough and persistent manner - who always seeks the ultimate scoop and story. After being saved by Superman from a near-death experience at the hands of terrorist scum, she is shaken up and takes a bath to wash away her torment. However - I like a naked woman like the many millions of men and women in this world - I do not understand why she had to be naked? What was the thought process? Did the creative team come to a conclusion that a woman who is feeling vulnerable had to be naked? Did they think that a fantastic and gorgeous woman like Amy Adams had to be naked to show the vulnerability of Lois Lane or was it just to increase the popularity of the film? I might sound cynical, but I am afraid that is the truth I believe in. If you think about it, the film is rated 12A and the scene was featured in a trailer. My point being is that Amy Adams is a beautiful and fantastic actress. She does not need to be naked to show the vulnerability of Lois Lane. And if the Man Of Steel wants to pretty much get down with Lois, isn't it fair that they both strip off?

Lex Luthor: Where do I begin with Jesse Eisenberg? I gave him the benefit of the doubt. However, after watching the film, I came to the conclusion that his character was misused and made a mockery of. He was not intimidating as a villain and he came off as an annoying bug in the room like a mosquito. Also, there was no charisma of a natural leader or any hint of the education received he to take advantage of this trait. In my opinion, the BEST performance by any actor who played Lex Luthor to the book was John Shea on Lois & Clark: The New Adventures Of Superman (1993-1997) specifically Season 1. Eisenberg should have paid homage to John Shea instead of degenerating a quintessential megalomaniac. Jesse Eisenberg? Not the best choice!!!

Doomsday: Doomsday WAS TERRIBLE. He looked similar to something from The Lord Of The Rings. He didn't utter a single word like in the animated series/films. Considering Doomsday was unlocked via the corpse of General Zod...a few words would've been great to add character depth and interaction.

* Bad Points/Worst Points

1) Flashback to Man Of Steel (2013): Bruce running towards Wayne Financial Tower was ridiculous. Okay, I get that he was calling his best friend to get out with everyone, but when the building began to crumble, it reminded me of the dark day on 9/11 and to me using such tragedy for entertainment is not just wrong but also 100% distasteful. People run away from danger and not towards it. Stupid scene 100%!

2) The fight was manipulated by Eisenberg and it did no justice for the title. What were his motivations? Why did he want the Bat and Big Blue to fight one another? Was it perverse lust? Was it because he was bored or was it just written into the film because they couldn't find a suitable reason?!

I would have given this film 5/10, however the only good thing that came from the movie has to be the arrival of Wonder Woman to the rocking theme called Is She With You. Gal Gadot nailed the role of Wonde Woman and I thank Zack Snyder for casting her! Plus, 2017 is next year and we get to see origin of Wonder Woman via the directing skills of Patty Jenkins.

title: Loved it! Seriously loved it! - Don't listen the critics! Go and see this movie!
review:
So, just saw BvS in a packed IMAX cinema here in London (IMAX 70mm) and I loved it! Have been following this movie since it was first announced way back when. Admittedly I was disappointed to read the reviews on Tuesday and I ventured to the cinema this evening with a certain degree of trepidation.....could it be as bad as the critics have said it is? Is it as bad as some folks here on IMDb have said it is....and the simple answer is no! I'm not sure what all these people were expecting. Seriously!

Personally I think it was better than MoS. I think that Superman was spot on. Definitely an improvement on MoS - much more "heroic". Batman was portrayed brilliantly. Affleck did a fantastic job donning the cowl. Gal Gadot as Diana Prince was great - her intro as WW was awesome! Eissenberg as Lex was genius (an evil genius). The soundtrack was fantastic - fitted with the tone of the film perfectly. The action scenes incredible. The much maligned (by the critics) storyline was absolutely fine. I think it did what it needed to do to bring Batman, Superman and WW together on the big screen for the first time ever and set the scene for the introduction of the rest of the members of the Justice League!

I honestly don't understand everyone's gripes with this movie, well not everyone but those that are rating it as 1/10 etc. It's baffling to me!

If you haven't seen it, GO AND SEE IT! Don't listen to the critics reviews! I shall be seeing it again for sure.

title: A Stylized Visual Spectacle which Stands Out in the Genre
review:
Minor Spoilers!

I thoroughly enjoyed this movie and liked it for the very reasons that the critics disliked it!

BvS tells the story of superheroes in a different way than most others in the genre. This style isn't like the typical chapter-oriented type where one chapter follows another in a linear fashion. Instead, BvS tells multiple stories at the same time while adding something to each story throughout the movie. The multiple stories then converge into the finale which was a treat to watch in action and story.

I get how there can be a disconnect as most movies cover one chapter before moving on and leaving it behind; but BvS keeps everything going at the same time which juggles multiple plot points to reach the finale. This style is common in many philosophy and religious books which is why I enjoyed it thoroughly for being different!

I also didn't think the criticisms were negative points in the movie. For instance, people didn't like Lex Luthor as he was a little eccentric but considering this character, he is in his early years still with hair which was a different Luthor. I know that eventually he becomes a cold and calculating villain later on but perhaps this is more of a reflection of his mad genius before he becomes the Lex Luthor we all know (a friend told me this is how it is in the early comics but I myself haven't verified this fact). I at least know from Smallville that Lex Luthor had many eccentricities and was a different character but then later becomes a psychotic and ruthless villain.

I also didn't mind how a lot was 'crammed' into this movie. As we know from Marvel movies, Thanos in one movie simply sits on his throne and then he gets up and picks up the gauntlet in another movie. The increased content provides the opportunity to tell much more interesting stories in the near future rather than drag out things which eventually never get answered (remember the TV show Lost, while it was great, many things were so slowly paced that they weren't really addressed!).

I am also a fan of the highly stylized visuals that Snyder brings. The cackling sound of Superman coming from the distance makes it seem even more cool than the best professional wrestling entrance in history! I have never seen Superman in such a light where each one of his abilities were given the proper treatment he deserves (also the cool glowing effect in the eyes!). These subtle effects really flesh out the heroes as with the ground dirt rising when Superman is about to fly and the demon-like ambiance of Batman when he's around as well as the symbols on Wonder Woman.

I thought the fights were truly awesome as well where Batman does seem like truly Batman, a superhero who shows the pinnacle of what a human being can do. I admire these heroes and I look forward to seeing them again.

I don't consider myself a DC fan. I consume both Marvel and DC as I wish to enjoy a variety in the genres I like (in Marvel I enjoy Xmen (particularly Cyclops if he was done well!), Thor, Ant-man, Spiderman, and many more!). Hey, if we lost one of the two, we wouldn't have as many Superhero movies which is not such a good thing. Instead, I appreciate the high quality variety we have and I hope others do as well!

Cheers!

title: Better than MOS but i don't think it quite got the home run.
review:
Don't go into this movie expecting the family orientated "Avengers" style superhero movie. Its Batman its supposed to be dark and it delivered on being dark. And is clearly the first of many justice league movies to come out in the near future.

Jesse Eisenberg and Ben Affleck nailed it. I loved them, Affleck played the dark crime fighter to a T and Eisenberg sucked you right into the character of Lex Luthor. Between the pair they could have made there own movie, great acting!

But we must get to the movie, it started off with no plot to a messy plot to eventually finding its way. 2 and a half hours was a bit long but i understand it needed to tell a big story. title: Really wanted to love this movie ... but I only just liked it
review:
Now I should say that I dragged my wife a long to watch this movie, so I was absolutely pinning my hopes on really enjoying this movie because otherwise my wife would not allow me to do movie selection for at least 2 years.

Visually, the movie is absolutely stunning albeit a bit too dark at times, and I don't mean as in the ambiance of the movie being a dark world ... but the movie was literally too dark in some parts making aspects (at least at the 3D showing I attended) to be quite hard to make out what was going on. It was a bit like watching a dark movie at night, with sunglasses on.

What you should not expect from your 2.5 hours of sitting down before this movie is a rushed introduction to the world of Batman and Superman, in fact, it doesn't really introduce you to them. At least in the case of Superman, we've met this iteration before already. Batman aka Bruce Wayne, at least this version we haven't met before - so he's just kinda there all of a sudden. What's more, he has seemingly been "there" for a long time based on some of the dialogue.

Bruce Wayne's character caused me the most annoyance because there were flashback scenes or dream sequences which just kind of appeared mid movie and they weren't clear that they were dream sequences ... not immediately anyway. There is perhaps some Easter Eggs in some of these scenes, some which were left unexplained. For instance, Bruce wakes up from one of the dreams hearing "Lois Lane is the key" ... but no explanation as to how he managed to attain this information and/or where it was coming from - although speculation is rife about the possibility of it having been the Flash.

The movie crawls through building up the tension between SM and BM, CK and BW, focusing particularly on their values as to why they might be against each other, with BW's being much easier to understand given he was present in Metropolis when Superman and Zod were playing hide the sausage with sky scrapers.

By crawl I mean almost painstakingly so ... it is well into the second half of the movie before you get any real action.

Plot is important and I can understand that, but the issue with this movie is that it serves as an introduction to the future of the DCEU on the big screen and is thus not only an introduction to this movie, but an introduction to the rest of the franchise as well. Without wanting to make too many comparisons with the Marvel EU - where that differs is that Marvel introduced Captain America, Iron Man and Thor in their own movies but created a connection through all of them that made their coming together much easier - this connection was largely created by "Phil Coulson" and "Nick Fury". They cleverly used post credits as well but the movie itself stayed focus on it's key character - even when Hawkeye appeared in Thor, the movie stayed true to it's focus on Thor.

Dawn of Justice is all over the place by comparison. Trying to give us a story but also trying to introduce the wider DCEU within the movie itself. The watching of the videos for Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg clearly shows that - not to mention the lingering focus on their logos when they are first seen (how did Lex Luthor manage to work out their logos anyway?).

Suffice to say, for me, DOJ was a seriously muddled and confuzzled cluster muck. It was fantastic to look at, but you can stare all day at an attractive man or woman and still be bored to death.

In spite of this, I still gave it a 6, for its visual depiction. The last 45 mins of the movie and I actually thought that Affleck was pretty good. Hoping that the next movies make up for some of the failings in this one.

title: I guess trailer #1 set the hype too high, but overall I liked it.
review:
Finally my 3-years-wait is over...Suffice to say I liked it, I really liked as a fan but I didn't love it and that's a bittersweet feeling to be honest. It's a strong start for the DCEU and I can't wait for what's coming. Despite its flaws, if you're a comic book fan you'll geek out over it.

First I'll list what I believe are the Negative points of this movie:

  • Transition between scenes, it annoyed me a little because it didn't feel natural and maybe one of the reasons is that some scenes were really quick and jump from a point to another with a different tone and plot, so it takes the immersion away and doesn't let a plot progress fluidly.


  • Cutting 30min from it, did more harm than good, it felt like a Comic with missing pages. For example, we have a scene where Bruce tracks the kryptonite o LexCorp, next scene...They show LexCorp destroyed and the kryptonite stolen, so what happened there? That may be shown in those 30min.


  • Due to the amount of information they wanted to give us during the movie, a lot of scenes (not all of them) felt underdeveloped. 2h and 20min of movie is not enough to develop every plot correctly. Like for example, when Superman leaves Metropolis, it would've been nice to develop the outcome of it and maybe get the answer to: Does the world needs a Superman? But no, he left, next scene he talks to Jonathan, next scene he's back to save Lois, it all happened so fast.


Now the Points I have mixed feelings with:

  • Like I said, this movie is aimed at fans and I appreciate that, I could enjoy ever little reference and easter eggs. I think bringing 2 stories together was nice, they did a good job mixing them, BUT it felt underdeveloped too, I mean I understood the reasons behind everything, but it lacked a lot of development, the conflict between the main characters, there should've been more scenes between them to rise the tension and be more dynamic, this movie could've been split into 2 parts.


  • The way they ended the fight, it's not like I hated it, far from it, actually it was a good way. Bruce having memories of his mother's death, he didn't want the same thing to happen to another person, especially to someone who reminded him of his mother, it's like a way for him to save his mother, to redeem himself since he couldn't do anything when he was a kid. But the WAY it ended, could've been a bit better and more emotional, it felt so dry.


  • Doomsday, thing is I've never cared about Doomsday in all honesty, so I don't get the excitement over his character and people claiming that he was underdeveloped, actually the movie got him right, he's just a (Kryptonian) beast that wants to destroy everything, its only feeling is rage, and its origin is similar to the comics. But Doomsday has always been a Plot Device, I think people fail to see it, it was only created for one reason and that's to kill Superman (that's the only reason it's famous, because if he didn't do it, he would've been just another monster), that's it and he doesn't need a lot of screen time.


Now, everything else was awesome and these are some points I consider to be good to great:

  • The casting, it's perfect, Affleck is Bruce AND Batman, I wanted to see more of Gal Gadot, she was awesome. Cavill is still a great Superman, I don't think there's a better choice. I loved Jeremy's Alfred, he's the Alfred I wanted to see portrayed.


  • Jesse as Luthor, in front of the crowd he's quirky, but macabre when he's face to face with someone. The scene when he shows Superman the pics of Martha was really sinister.


  • The opening sequence is a masterpiece, it was filmed flawless. From Bruce's origin to the destruction of Metropolis from Bruce's POV, it was excellent, that was the level of storytelling I expected from the whole movie, it was exceptional.


  • I loved the montage they made when Superman is rescuing people around the world while you can listen some interviews in the background, it's really interesting what they say and the questions they bring to the table. Neil was a surprise and I liked it.


  • Every cameo, easter eggs and references made in the movie. It opens a door for great stories like Flashpoint Paradox, Under the Red Hood and (why not) Injustice. That nightmare sequence was great, but some scenes were cut, however watching the Parademons and the Omega symbol was a dream come true, HE'S HUNGRY AND HE'S COMING.


  • Bruce and Clark spent almost the same time on screen, it was really balanced.


  • Kryptonite spear!


  • Every nod to The Dark Knight Returns, from quotes to scenes, especially the one when Batman rescues Martha, it's almost the same as the scene in The Dark Knight Returns when he rescues the little kid.


Overall I enjoyed the film, but it's a bittersweet feeling since I didn't love it, maybe I was expecting a lot, trailer #1 set the bar too high I guess. I like the way Snyder takes inspiration from the source material, bringing scenes to life and it's like he took the characters from the comics and pasted them into the movie. But that's not enough, because the movie, especially what we, as fans, are expecting from WB/DC, is a flawless storytelling, on the same as the opening sequence. In my opinion, WB should hire a co-director for their next major events, it's too much to be handled by one guy, especially by one who excels at some stuff but is not so good at others.

title: I'm glad that this time I don't fully agree w/ the critics negative reviews
review: I'm so happy that this is one of those times I don't fully agree with the negative reviews from the critics. The movie is far from perfect but I honestly enjoyed it a lot. This is definitely the best version we've seen of Batman on the big screen. As much as I love the Nolan dark knight trilogy, Affleck is hands down the best Wayne and Batman we've gotten. He is physically a beast like Batman should be, he has the swag Wayne should have, he doesn't have a ridiculous Batman voice, he definitely did seem like a great detective and most importantly he is brutal. Those batman fight sequences are just freaking awesome, which they make me very excited for an Affleck directed solo batman movie. As for the Batman V Superman portion of the movie, I mean the way they made Batman be able to fight superman was perfect. You could see that once Batman was at the same physical level as Superman, Batman was the better trained fighter as he should be. I loved that the fact that Superman has done some damage and that he is all powerful had consequences with the government. That the government doesn't just trusts and bows down to Sups. As for Wonder Woman, for the little we got, I can say that she is freaking bad as* and that I cannot wait for her solo film. The Fight with the big bad was super cool. For me Wonder Woman was the one that shinned the most is that fight scene. And lastly, I liked Lex Luthor. He is, like Louis said on the trailer, just psychotic. The Easter eggs we got and the beginning of the formation of the Justice League was in my opinion very well laid out. Yes maybe the movie has some editing issues, or some dialogue that didn't quite work but for me the positives of this movie outweigh the negatives. A must see in theaters! And I cannot wait for what's to come from the DC cinematic universe.

title: How did the critics get this so wrong??!!
review:
I went into this movie expecting a disappointment given some of the critical reviews out there. Some of them downright condemned this movie as simply the worst.

Boy was I surprised and happy that they were wrong.

Story: Understandable and an appropriate follow on from 'Man of Steel'. With the level of destruction in that movie, this was a perfect 'other view' continuation and expression of the consequences from that story.

Batman: It's not Dark Knight. It's not meant to be. It's meant to be a world where he feels he's lost. And now stopping these aliens is going to be his legacy. I think it was played very well.

Wonder Woman: Wow. Really is Wonder Woman. She is everything you want her to be and there was clapping when she appeared. It was amazing. Again, a character who has given up, and now has found a reason to come out and play again.

Other Characters: Just glimpses. An acknowledgement that they exist and that people are tracking them (and now only because they have the technology to track and analyse everything) I loved every bit of it. Came out wanting to watch it again and excited for what was to come in the future.

Now I accept that I am a fan of Comic book heroes. So maybe my view is slightly skewed. My wife watched it to. She was never exposed to these characters or comic books. She likes it. So I got two perspectives and they are both positive.

Everyone coming out of the cinema looked happy.

So this begs the question: How did the critics get it so wrong? Or is it perhaps time to critique the critics and give them a score of 1/10, and a caption that reads : 'Please realise that a critic is giving an opinion. It is as valid as yours and mine, and sometimes completely out of touch with reality' or maybe it is time that IMDb, RT, and MetaC all focused on less on the so called 'Critics' and placed more importance on the opinions of the general public.

Do yourself a favour and go watch the movie. Just try and enjoy yourself. Stop looking for flaws. After all this is a movie about Superheroes.

title: A must see for fans...But moves fast past the magic.
review:
Overall, I liked MOS and thought it was a good starting point for the upcoming DCEU, and was excited to see Batman V Superman, with high expectations that they were taking things to the next level. I have to say i enjoyed the film and it was visually stunning. From a "distance" its a good movie worth seeing and watching over again. Really look forward to the directors cut.

That said..It left a lot to be desired. It almost feels like watching a 4 hour movie on 1.5 speed fast-forward.

Finally...we get to see detective Batman/Bruce Wayne in action at the party.. sneaking around avoiding security, stealing secrets and evidence,using awesome bat-gadgets etc to break into highly secure areas to extract confidential information. NOPE. NOT HOW IT HAPPENED

Okay. Well, finally we get to watch the court proceedings, and hear some heated debate how the government and people really feel about Superman, aliens, the destruction etc, and how Superman defends himself and his actions, and how he fits in society, politics, and the world. Perhaps a super-speech that helps us understand his motives and what makes him the great savior and hero we've come to know from the comics. SORRY, BUT NO, TRY AGAIN

Well, at least we get to witness Batman and Superman fight it out... then after-wards realize they are on the same side, find some real common ground, and eventually develop a deep friendship and bond which ultimately leads to the foundation of the Justice League. NOT HAPPENING

The movie is FILLED with great ideas and scenes that, if fully developed, could have been very intense, interesting, insightful, and inspiring. Instead, all the great ideas and scenes are crammed into the movie and cut short... and we're left with an awesome Wonderman we don't know, a brilliant Batman/Bruce thats under-utilized, a dead Superman nobody really cares about, and a literally insane Lex, that doesn't seem mentally stable enough to command respect or devise a brilliant plan. Not to mention another so-so looking CGI creature that blows up more stuff.

Hopefully the directors/ultimate cut fills in some of the blanks. They are on the right track, and have the right actors, ideas, tone, and visuals to create something amazing. Just need to work on making a standalone good movie, as opposed to rushing the plot and fast- forwarding to the Justice League.

Too many really good ideas seem to have gone to waste in this one. But the fact that the ideas are good, the visuals are great, the score is amazing, and the actors are (almost) all cast perfectly...make this a solid film worth checking out. Especially if you're a fan of the characters. 7/10

title: Don't Believe the Critics - See it for yourself
review:
Ignore the critics on this. Batman V Superman is a very enjoyable movie and worth the ticket price to see on a big screen. I was skeptical of this movie due to the premise of two superheroes beating each other up and the negative "professional" reviews. I saw this in IMAX 3D with a packed audience and there was quite a buzz of excitement and discussion leaving the theater. This is one of those movies you can't help but enjoy and talk about later. There is much to like in this movie; an intriguing and surprisingly believable premise and story, great acting and portrayal for the characters (even Ben Affleck...actually especially Ben Affleck); great action scenes and special effects, awesome music, and a glimpse into what looks to be even more interesting sequels.

As with any movie this ambitious, there are going to be things here and there that you can nitpick, but overall the movie lives up to the hype. I think those that are critical of this movie are judging this movie too harshly because it is not the movie they wanted to see or were expecting to see. I was surprised myself, but embraced the direction of the movie. Batman V Superman does not have a traditional story arc where every loose end is tied up. (Funny, When J.J. Abrams has loose ends, the movie is considered mysterious, but for this movie, critics are calling these plot holes.) Many of the so call-ed plot holes critics called out in this movie are actually not holes at all. They are either left open for future movies to explore or simply just not spelled out 100% to allow the audience to decide for themselves. This movie is told more like a comic book in the sense that you the reader are given many different scenes, but some of the commentary for the scenes are left for the you to fill in or possibly wait to the next installment.

If you are a normal fan of superhero movies in general, chances are you are going to really enjoy Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice.

title: Awesome 3D Movie Making, Very Well Written - Encore!
review:
I had mixed feelings walking into Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, 3D. The trailers were great, but I was skeptical about Affleck (DareDevil, I said it) and the last Man of Steel performance, which was sub-par, with the effects mostly carrying that movie, as it did for Avengers, and Xmen included.

Surprisingly, Batman v. Superman was better than the average movie. Don't think of this movie as replicating the comic book, if that's what you want, go read the comic book.

The writing was above par for a superhero movie. This movie showed the struggles of humankind, of life and death, it showed that man could not win with politics, hatred, warfare, or technology, but that love, understanding, and togetherness prevailed.

Each scene was well thought out, and executed almost to perfection. I didn't feel like there were any fillers, or that I couldn't wait for the action scenes to start, every scene had you on the edge of your seat, even to the ending, people stayed in their seats after sitting for more than 2 1/2 hours to go through ending credits.

I'm not a religious freak, but this movie does play on religion, god v. man, similar theme in Man of Steel, is that although Superman can intervene to change destiny, he chooses to let man have free will at times (his father dying), (the bomb in the court room, thousands to save an entire planet). Almost like how, every prayer cannot be answered.

Ben Affleck has saved his name with this performance! Carry on to League of Justice!!! P.S. - The critics are full of feces, Comic book lovers need to sit down and appreciate!!!

title: Scratched surface
review:
While everyone was pretty much concerned about Affleck's performance as Batman, no-one really thought to wonder about how the story would turn out (well at least I didn't). All the marketing hype around the film got me super excited for it. However, I did not have that same sense of excitement while watching the film, which was a little disappointing. This is primarily because the movie incorporates so many big characters which resulted in numerous and repetitive jump cuts across the individual narratives. This resulted in multiple anti-climaxes as the scene would change just as it was starting to get interesting. Then when the narratives came together, it wasn't for very long.

I am pleasantly surprised by Affleck's portrayal of Batman. He did a pretty good job and embodied the persona of Bruce Wayne well. Cavill reprises his role as Superman and does a consistent job since Man of Steel. Adams as well retains her character's persona well and her chemistry with Cavill is believable. Eisenberg shows off his acting talent ass Luthor, and his characteristic speech production fits the character well. Jeremy Irons who plays Alfred brings some comedic relief to the movie, but should have had more screen time. As well, Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman deserved more action, plus there were some scenes about her past that seemed very cheesy.

The visual effects and action scenes were nicely done. The atmosphere of the film throughout had a consistent intense and serious tone to it which was complemented by its dark setting. However, both Affleck and Cavill frequently had frowns on their faces which seemed too intense to me. I get that they have a lot of emotional baggage, but it went overboard. Also, too much masculine pride and ego going around. Use your words not fists, bro. Though the final battle at the end had great visual effects and was quite impressive.

Overall, though I did feel like the film could have been polished better by creating a narrative that flowed, I am still somewhat impressed by it. Can't wait to see the Justice League films! But in general, I feel like DC should stick with TV shows, as Marvel is better at making movies.

title: Batman VS Superman VS The Critics
review: I was absolutely blown away my the movie. I have no idea why the critics are blasting it the way they are. Maybe they were expecting something along the lines of a marvel movie, but whatever the reason, their spite is blown way out of proportion. The acting is great, with a phenomenal performance by Jessie Eisenberg, and Ben Affleck being the best batman we've had so far. Since you can read a lot of reviews on the movie, i'd like to highlight one thing that some might skip over. This is the most faithful to the comics adaption of batman we've ever gotten. He's brutal, he's dark, he's calculating, the way he moves and fights has the perfect flow for batman. The fight choreography is really impressive. I'm really excited for the new Ben Affleck stand-alone batman movies now, just to see his batman.

title: Ignore the negative comments - Its a good movie. Affleck Rules the Show
review:
Don't know what's wrong with people for giving it such bad reviews. This is a good movie. It has its flaws but it makes up for it with a solid comic book type action scenes and story line. Just enjoy it as a comic book movie and stop comparing it with a more conventional movie. The star of the show BEN AFFLECK hands down. He follows in the line of Michael Keaton in proving his critics wrong in portraying the bat. The best Batman I would say till date, Dark and arrogant as we have come to love him. Rest of the cast was OK however the character of Lex Luthor can be looked at again in the next installments. It looks very weak and lacks the charisma of a smart and strong villain we have come to love through the comics.

Ben Affleck is so good as Batman i cannot explain enough, even much better than Christian Bale of Nolan's Batman Trilogy (makes him look like Toby Maguire of the previous Spiderman series) and makes the Batman character tailor made for him and must say even the Batmobile is better than the predecessors i mean Batman steals the show.

Rest all is good apart from Batman being above all and Luthor being below all, Kudos Zac and rest of the cast for an entertainer of a movie.

title: Passably Mediocre... Would not watch again... EVER!
review: I was not impressed with this film at all. the first 1 1/2 hour includes shoddily written dialogue, along with tons of random scenes that were not relevant to the story at all... for instance, Bruce Wayne is at his mothers grave site, and he sees blood dripping from it, as he goes to touch it, a giant bat creature (terrible CGI at this spot too) jumps out and grabs him... for nor apparent reason. I like Jesse Eisenberg, but i did nit feel this role suited him, a actually laughed out loud in the theater when he tried to be "menacing" at one part... Henry Cavill's performance was OK. now i never really was a fan of superman, and i was not i pressed with MOS, so i didn't expect much, and thats exactly what i got... now i'm going to get to the one aspect of the film that kept me from giving this one star. BATMAN WAS AMAZING!!! Ben Affleck has given us the best live action version of batman to date. my only complaint is that they didn't show enough of him. in fact, i would say he only got about 1/2 the screen time as superman... to sum up my review, i did nit enjoy this movie enough to see it again, and for a movie called Batman v Superman, you only get to see literally about 3 minutes of fighting... do yourself a favor, don't waste your money, just spend as little money as you can and get it from a red box or something...

title: Trust me, this movie doesn't deserve all the hate
review: I am not going to show any spoilers or anything like that, but what I will say is that this movie doesn't deserve all the hate it's getting. 7.5 is the perfect rating for this good movie. The film is a brilliant sequel to the Man of Steel, first and foremost, that's for sure. Even though half the movie can be slow and maybe even a little confusing, there are scenes that keep you going and gives you the excitement you are looking for in a superhero movie. For the acting performance, I want to first mention Eisenberg. He surprised me entirely. To be frank, Jesse Eisenberg gives one of the greatest performances of his career as the Psycho genius, Lex Luthor. Gal Gadot gave an incredible performance as well, shocking me and my friends in the theater. Let me just say that her sexiness and her ass-kicking was evident. It actually truly excites me for the Wonder Woman movie coming soon. I also loved watching the experienced acting of Jeremy Irons. Even though he didn't have as much of a story as Michael Cain's Alfred, he went all out with every scene he was in. As for Ben Affleck, his performance was kind of disappointing. He usually IS a good actor. But I don't think he was the right choice for Batman, yet I think I am just used to the Christian Bales Batman. Hopefully Affleck will come back with a more fulfilling performance. All in all, I would say this was much better than Man of Steel (I gave Man of Steel 4/10), therefore I think we should be patient with Zack Snyder for the future to continue making these DC movies in his own way. I think there will be progress.

title: Awesome:Must Watch on IMax 3D
review:
I nearly gave this movie a miss after hearing some negative reviews and reading about how Ben Affleck looked sad when asked about this movie. I feared that this would be another Fantastic Four.

But then, I decided to watch it any. And it turned out that this movie is AWESOME.

I hope that Ben Affleck continues as Batman. His Batman is a big powerful guy who looked like a credible threat to Superman. I liked Wonder Woman and Superman too. The guy who did Lex Luthor was also good.

I am looking forward to watching the Justice League movie if and when it makes it to the big screen. And also the next Batman movie.

I think those who complained about the movie were not familiar with the DC Universe. Perhaps they could not figure out what was going on during the origin flashbacks and the interludes.

If you are a comic book fan, you will like this movie. Ignore the critics and watch this movie in IMAX 3D

title: All 3 of my boys (14, 10, & 6) LOVED it and so did I
review:
I took my three oldest boys to see Batman v Superman. We all loved it. Not sure why the critics were so harsh. Doesn't matter. All that matters is that we had a great outing at the movies and we can't wait till Justice League comes out.

It was great to finally see Batman and Superman on the silver screen together. I thought the screen writers did a great job exploring what Batman's initial views of Superman would have been. I was pleasantly surprised how different Ben Affleck's batman was from Christain Bale, who was a really had act to follow. Batman has been done so many times, I was pleasantly surprised that he was different in this one. Batman starts the movie almost as a broken spirit, after years of battles in Gotham. By the end of the movie, the character believes in what he's doing again. In the final scenes, you can see that he turned a corner and he sees what the Justic League could become. Joining up with Superman and Wonder Woman gives him a path back to being a hero.

Naturally, there are some plot holes that could have been fixed, but the 'sell' was seeing Batman face off against Superman. They had to get there in a way that also allowed them a way back. Some critics point at the use of common mother name of 'Martha' as a being goofy. It was a little, but if you think about the story of Bruce Wayne and the pain he carried about not being able to save his mother (parents). I actually thought it was clever. A way to bring him back from becoming a murder himself.

I felt bad for Henry Cavill, he's a good actor. But I think the director wanted to focus more on how humanity would react to a 'Super Alien'. I thought it was realistic that not everyone would trust Superman. Why would we? We can agree on much and we don't trust each other. Then you add in someone like Lex Luthor - situations and emotions get manipulated. The movie didn't have time/room to explore how Superman would react to the fear his presence would cause or Superman's reaction to being setup. I'm not sure I liked the death of Superman ending. That's really hard to pull off when everyone knows he's in the next movies. I've got to assume it's tied into the plot for justice league. Otherwise they 'played that card' and got no impact from it.

All in all, it was a great day at the movies and the critics need to "lighten up". Putting these two icons on the silver screen together isn't an easy task. With due respect, Ironman and Captain America are not Superman and Batman. I think the movie did a great job delivering a 'fantasy' battle between the two heroes, given the audience a chance to cheer them both in the end and setting up Justice League.

Wonder Women was great. Can't wait to see Aquaman and Flash in the next film. Then Green Lantern down the road.

title: This movie is fantastic!
review: First of all, I would like to say that "Batman V. Superman" is a great comic book movie. It has very tense scenes. With Michael Keaton, Val Kilmer, George Clooney and Christian Bale having played Batman in the Batman movies, Ben Affleck gives an excellent performance as Bruce Wayne/Batman. Same with Henry Cavill as Clark Kent/Superman, who has been portrayed by Christopher Reeve and Brandon Routh. As I saw "Man of Steel", Cavill had the resemblance of Reeve as Superman. Unlike Gene Hackman's Lex Luthor, Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor comes off as nerdy and annoying, but like Hackman's Luthor, Eisenberg's Luthor is still insane. Fine performances by Amy Adams as Lois Lane, Laurence Fishburne as Perry White, Diane Lane as Martha Kent, Holly Hunter as Senator June Finch, Kevin Costner as Jonathan Kent and Jeremy Irons as Alfred Pennyworth. The real standout in this film is Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. I recommend it.

title: Slow paced but improved towards the end
review: 27 January 2016 Film of Choice at The Plaza Dorchester Tonight - Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. Yet another chapter in yet another superhero movie. Ben Affleck as Batman pitted against Henry Cavill as Superman, both unwittingly being controlled by the malevolent being that is Lex Luthor, played spookily well by Jesse Eisenberg. At 2 hours 31 minutes this was at least 31 minutes too long, although the historical nature of the opening credits worked very well as a reminder of what had come before. The first two thirds of this film were bitty and in places a little turgid. The story hopped all over the place and even though all the pieces eventually slotted together, at times I was in danger of losing concentration, yes we were being set up for the grand finale....but it took forever. However, there are just as many good points........the special effects, fight scenes, jumps, falls, crashes were all outstanding. The cast worked well together and contrary to many opinions I heard voiced prior to the release of this film, Ben Affleck was a credible Batman. Film makers are being Increasingly challenged to bring us bigger and better and it does make me wonder how many more ways we can defend ourselves against the big bad, fight the unfightable and kill the unkillable. Just three more words to add.......WOW Wonder Woman!!!

title: Batman vs Superman - You've taken your (second?) step into a larger world
review:
BvS is a really ambitious movie from a Director (Snyder) who has proved that he can tackle very complex story-to-screen adaptations (Watchmen). The end result is a movie that I suspect will be very re-watchable and contains so many seeds that it will obviously be a linchpin of the new DC Universe. It has some warts, but its glory moments are in fact glorious.

Here's your 6-8 sliding scale of how you'll enjoy this film:

6/10 - I know nothing about comics. The action is OK, but WTF is going on? Who are some of these people? I need more info because the sudden jumps in story are really disorienting. Also, why is everyone so mad? Why is this movie so depressing? Comics aren't dramas guys. Why aren't Batman & Superman just like they always are? Also, turn down the damn music.

7/10 - I dig the DC films. Oh wow, Ben Affleck crushes it as Batman, Gail Gadot is so good as Wonder Woman, and this story is really interesting. I wish I knew more about some of the stuff they are hinting at, but maybe more is coming? The fights are really cool and I like how the characters mesh even though it feels a bit dark. It was really great to see Wayne doing some stuff outside of the cave. Just, maybe, turn down the music a little?

8/10 - Holy crap! Affleck didn't suck as Batman and is super jacked! That Batman fight scene against bad guys is amazing! Superman is so cool! That crazy dream/sequence that hints at (#$@#redacted@#$#) and maybe even (!@#classified) was nuts! Luthor was actually cool and man oh man Wonder Woman! I'm so psyched they laid the foundations for Justice League by showing (spoiler) and (spoiler) and even (spoiler)! My ears are bleeding from the music and sound effects but maybe just maybe DC is starting to figure it out!

So yeah, not nearly as bad as the critics are saying, not by a mile. This movie will stand the test of time and has some scenes that you will never forget, ever. Go in with an open mind and I think you can really enjoy it.

P.S. Nitpicks for Mr Snyder: The nigh-endless "insert Lois Lane at story point" moments. Amy Adams is fine, but man, there's got to be other ways to make Clark have moments. Also, do we need the smash into the ground every time Supes lands? Come on man, he doesn't need to crater on every landing, lol. How about a soft one? Maybe a touch less uber-loud music at points, take it off of 11 and put it on 9 brother.

-Gaussgoat

title: The Apex of (not only) comic-books adaptations.
review:
"How do you know when the film is great? You do not want it to end!"

This film was visionary, without a doubt. The way it presented the story, developed characters.. I like it, when my mind is challenged with deep philosophical questions about morality, humanity and divinity. And this flick made just that. It makes you THINK, question yourself, our standards and, ultimately, what it is to be a Hero.. No matter how hard you try, you end up being the bad guy/No matter how much justice you ACTUALLY do, people see you as Evil.

The build-up to an epic clash was pretty humane, and most of us can understand the motives of Bruce Wayne. I mean, his entire office house was annihilated, people died that day when Clark battled Zod. Obviously, he will see Superman as a threat. Batfleck was the BEST Batman to date. Grimm, brutal, ruthless, smart and overall BAD-ASS. This is the Batman I longed for.

Superman was just perfect. Divine, mighty, pure-hearted and just,.. y'know, "god-like". Top notch acting from Mr. Cavill right there.

The actual battle between the two was magnificent. The whole cinema was electrified. It really looked EPIC, no abuse of the meaning of the word.

Overall, I liked this film even more than Mad Max, which legitimately makes it my No. 1 film of all times. Do NOT believe the critics, go watch for yourself and judge for yourself. I don't have enough room here to express how much I love this film and how great it is. I'll just go see another screening.

Doubt someone will be able to top this.

title: Better than Man of Steel
review:
I was not a great fan of Man of Steel and I went into this film expecting to really hate it. Surpringsly the reasons I didn't like it were not as I first thought they would be. Despite my initial feelings about Ben Affleck playing Batman, he did a pretty good job and I'd watch a standalone film. Henry Caville isn't my favourite Superman but I liked his character more in this film. I was very pleased that Jesse Eisenberg was cast as Lex Luther but his performance was nearly enough to ruin the plot hole filled story.

There are moments in the film that really set DC apart from Marvel and we're brilliantly done. However these moments would not make up for a shaky story, some poor casting decisions and some absolutely absurd moments that just allowed the film to come apart at the seams. It was not as bad as I thought it would be and if some parts had been done differently it could have been great.

title: Impressive pilot for Justice League,explains it all.
review: Don't expect much of an Avengers like action or man of steel like action from this movie.This movie is a pilot for the upcoming sequel ' Justice league' at first I also thought while watching movie,that this is not what I expected from the movie title.But in the end all pieces were in their correct places.In order to enjoy justice League you will need to watch this movie.Wonder woman is just fabulous,she added the spice to the movie with her super cool fearless intro.Also this movie reveals the another characters of Justice league ''Cyborg,Flash,Wonder woman, and Aquaman'' . Acting of Jesse Eisenberg as ''Lex luthor'' is just awesome.We cant compare him to Legend JOKER but he did pretty well as villain.Rest of the movie is full of entertainment.

title: Not getting as much hype as it deserves
review: Reading critiques of movies these days can be so depressing. It's full of self entitled people looking for an excuse to use big words. I went into this movie expecting it to be terrible because of all the bad "critiques", and was pleasantly surprised. Although this movie jumped around in the beginning (understandably; it needed to preface a lot about Batman since this is our first time seeing Ben Affleck play him), it ended up being one of the best movies I've seen in a while. I've been way into the Avengers universe, but I would go as far as to say this beats them. The action and fighting scenes were incredibly well-done, Wonder Woman's entrance was insane, and I didn't mind the long runtime at all. By the end of the movie, I didn't want it to be over.

title: Went in with low expectations and was blown away
review:
I went to see this film with my brother after watching as many spoiler free reviews as possible. We both went in after having discussed the need for very low to no expectations.

We're both avid DC fans, not fans of Zack Snyder and extremely skeptical of casting choices. 5 Minutes in my brother was leaning forward in his seat and I was enjoying the well paced ramps of intensity.

The editing was extremely manic, so much so that I'd describe it as a flood of visual and plot points, and narratives, for the greater DC universe. It wasn't hard to keep track of what was happening, But the cohesiveness off the story was like trying to piece together an amazing night out the next day.

That being said, It was an amazing night out. They went to great lengths to bring the comics to the screen while taking artistic/else-world liberties with the characters.

Jessie Eisenberg remains a bad choice for Lex, buuuut in context of the license being taken by this telling, he's forgivable against the whole. Gal Gadot, pretty to look at, decent action, interesting set up for future installments as Wonder Woman. Henry Cavil is an ... interesting superman... lack luster as far as this telling of Superman goes, but also intriguing against the "Injustice" set up.

Ben Affleck won over a fan in me as the new batman I have to admit. The only way he could begin to compete with Bale's batman is by being the batman wee saw in this movie. I look forward to seeing him find his humanity and moral compass again.

As far as the comic story adaptions, Doomsday, Dark Knight Returns, Death in the family, Death of Superman, (Red Son Rising?), Injustice, Darkseid AND the Justice League. It just felt like a lot to keep track of and the writers better have a game plan for a wholly original escalation for this telling as they tapped some of the greatest most iconic stories of all time in DC.

That being said It's exciting to think that a new stand alone batman movie might draw from Death in the family!

In conclusion, I view this as being handled in the opposite way Marvel setup characters individually then deployed the collective.

We've been given an intense overview of the story, now we'll be taken into the various character developments. The whole thing is very D.C and despite it's many failings, this movie is solid 7.5 out of 10 for me. I give it an 8 on IMDb because if I have to round off, I'll gladly round up on this one.

title: Great Film
review: I'm sick of all these critics snubbing great movies. Batman v Superman was an all around comic book lovers dream. It was entertaining, exciting and emotional. One of the best movies I have seen all year. I think DC gets a lot of un-warranted crap from critics and reviewers alike after a couple mishaps (see green lantern and Man-of-Steel) But I think this movie exceeded expectations. Ben Afleck's performance of Batman might have been the best on-screen adaptation in a long time. He was broad enough to look like a realistic comic book style Bruce Wayne and his success as an A-list celebrity gave him the Bruce Wayne confidence and appearance the role needed. It was great seeing the tactical aspect of the batman and Alfred pennyworth team up. And Batman's fighting style was awesome. It was awesome seeing his planned out attacks and surprising the enemy with a level of pre thought out genius that is truly batman. The arguments and internal and external conflict was enough to make even a one sided thinker flip flop at least once. It was a deep movie with great action sequences and filled with Easter eggs and foreshadowing. I think that it went on too long. That's what i would change. I would have been more than thrilled if the movie ended once they caught Lex Luthor and maybe he had a secretly planted a bomb or something just to extend it by a few more minutes so we got a glimpse of the Bats-Supes team up but I felt doomsday deserved his own movie and Snyder laid it on a little thick by throwing him in at the end. Jesse Eisenbeg's Lex Luthor was so complex a character he has been compared to Heath Ledger's joker in The Dark Knight. I can not wait for more of these movies and will continue to fight the evil critics that screw good movies. Batman v Superman was all around an immediate buy and well worked piece of film.

title: Incoherent... bloated... and just plain dull
review:
The moment we've long been waiting for, two the biggest names in the DC Universe on-screen together for the first time in cinema history. Alas, it was not worth the wait. We are left with a meandering mess that is so haphazard, it felt like some dastardly projectionist had slyly cut scenes out and left them on the projection-booth floor.

We begin with Bruce Wayne as he watches his own building collapse following the battle at the conclusion of Man of Steel. This is then followed by scenes in the Indian Ocean and then in Africa, the latter being the first of many occasions where Lois Lane requires saving by her caped hero in increasingly contrived and implausible situations. The first hour in particular is the film's weakest, taking an absolute age to go from point A to B from a narrative aspect. The superfluous flash-forwards and dream sequences also add to the confusion, leading to a situation where you're never quite sure if a scene is "real" or happening in the mind of a character. The focus is all over the place, and frankly the overwhelming emotion that the film left me with for the most part was was boredom.

It is each of the heroes' distrust of the others unchecked power which drives them into opposing paths. However, their character arcs are never fully explored, leading to a clash that just feels contrived. Also adding to the woe is Jesse Eisenberg's version of Lex Luthor. It is almost as if director Zack Snyder told him to play the character like he played Mark Zuckerberg in "Social Network", but turned up to the absolute max. Lex Luthor is a power-hungry, meticulous, billionaire businessman but Eisenberg portrays him as a maniacal character more akin to Heath Ledger's Joker. There were also incredibly few jokes in a film that played it completely straight.

The film is neither saved by its conclusion: a chest-thumping, headache-inducing, seemingly never-ending punch-up. On the plus side, Ben Affleck was excellent in his portrayal of a more world-weary Batman and Jeremy Irons was impressive despite being under-used. Fans may enjoy the sheer scale of the spectacle, but all I left with the cinema with was crushing disappointment and a missed opportunity.

title: This is good
review: It's very hard to make a good Superman film and have us humans relate to him. In Man of Steel we had two invulnerable aliens fighting each other on earth and destroying everything around them, not easy to relate to at all. This movie manages to humanise Superman more and give us an opponent that is a challenge for him. Ben Affleck is excellent as Batman and he represents all of us and how we would feel if this were real life. Wonder Woman is good but not used till the end but she looks like she loves the fight and will be back for more. Jessie Eisenberg is a good choice for Lex Luther and you watch his character become more unhinged as the movie progresses. I think audiences will love this film and it will do very well, even if the critics do not.

title: A film for genuine comic fans! Beautifully done
review: Honestly, this film is the best and most accurate comic book movie to date. Obviously there are things wrong with it, but what film does not have problems? This film feels already like a classic, I hope more people realise that soon enough. The writing, acting, directing were all beautifully done. My favourite movie so far, cannot wait for justice league. As a DC fan, and as a comic book fan in general, this movie exceeded all my expectations. Ignore all the lazy critics trying to dishonour this film; fair enough if you do not like a film, not everyone has the same taste, but do not go out of your way to bash and try too ruin a film for genuine fans who have waited for this for three years. Go get a life! All you fans, go enjoy this film, definitely worth it.

title: An awesome movie worthy of DC comics
review:
This movie was excellent in every aspect. Zack Snyder has excelled in recreating and showing us the characters from DC in exactly the way they should be shown. It is an excellent sequel to "The Man Of Steel" and also sets the base for future movies, which include, the "Justice League". The action scenes were tremendous and loved the way Ben Affleck and Jesse Eisenberg lived their role. The music was terrific, and the opening scene with the " Beautiful lie by Hans Zimmer" killed it. The cameos from the other members of the Justice League was like the icing on top of a cake.

I have seen many criticism against this movie which is highly illogical considering that Zack Snyder created the DC comics. The criticism seems to be coming from those who haven't read or even don't have any knowledge of the characters from DC comics. As for being dark - the movie is supposed to be dark seeing that this movie is mainly centered around Batman. It may be dull and boring for many, but the sole reason for that is, the inability of the people to understand what was happening at every point in the movie. I don't blame them, as it is indeed difficult for people without knowledge of DC comics to understand it. This movie is not as easy to understand as movies made by Marvel. So it would be better to take a friend with you who is crazy about DC. The dreams and visions of Batman, far from being irrelevant, provides the fans a basis on which to come up with theories and also gives hints about the future movies.

My only complaint with the movie is this:- The arrangement of scenes. Their seems to be a serious problem with the narration of the story. The individual scenes, being excellent on its own, when put together, the way it has been done in the movie, ruined it. This is the sole reason why I rated it 9.

But I am confident that Zack is going to learn from his mistakes and the Justice League set to release in 2018, will be a masterpiece!

title: Saw it, loved it. Same with my kids and everyone else there
review:
I thought that Ben Affleck would suck as Batman. He's usually pretty lame in movies, but I'll be damned if he wasn't pretty awesome in this. A much darker Batman, and Ben played him amazingly. My opinion is that he was a better fit than Christian Bale.

If you're going in for a 2 hour fight scene don't bother. There's a lot of fighting, but also a lot of kickass story telling to give a nice background on what is going on (very much like the comics).

Not sure why the "professional" reviewers are crapping on DoJ, maybe they didn't like Batman actually killing people and using guns. Or the fact that the movie gives a few minor story bits and backgrounds but doesn't waste time on crap, instead they put everything pertinent into the movie and let it rip.

If you're a sissy and a bitch like the "pro" reviewers, sit at home and watch more 50 Shades of Gray. If you like the comics and want to see good old Batman and Superman kickin some major ass go see it.

title: Good dark superhero movie. Definitely worth seeing.
review: For conflict of interest: I am a Marvel fan, not a DC fan. Yeah BvS has its issues, but its goodness just outweighs its problems. If you like dark and realistic superhero movie, this one should be on your list. Like I said, I am a Marvel fan. I enjoyed most of Marvel comics, cartoons, and some of the movies. BUT I really want superhero movies to be a little darker and convey deeper themes, rather than the Marvel movies that look like products coming from an assembly line. I do believe that BvS can be better. Its incoherent story-telling just makes things a little confusing, but if you are really attentive during the first half of the movie, you won't feel at lost. I like Ben Affleck's Batman, I love Henry Cavill's Superman, and Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman just blew my mind off! I give this movie a 9 because I really hope JL will be better.

title: Why Batman v Superman is Now My Favorite Superhero Movie
review: I honestly believed this movie would fail viewers in some way or another. Some of the casting choices as well as my near dislike for Man of Steel made me very convinced that it would be an enormous flop. Over the years while waiting for its release, however, I learned a lot about the comics, and some of Zach Snyder's motivations when it came to the stories he was trying to tell. We went to see BvS on the day it came to our theaters, and I can say now that it had my attention the entire time, the music was incredible,and I came away feeling that Ben Affleck was the best Batman yet. The story was good, and though the movie had its flaws, I definitely have a new favorite! I would go see it again if I had the chance, and I would say that whatever people are saying toward BvS that is negative,it has so many more reasons to be approved by fans. Whether someone enjoys the comics or simply wants to be entertained, it is worth the money and time. When I heard of the new Mad Max movie I was very critical, but came away with an awesome experience. I would compare BvS to that movie-when it comes to a powerful performance. Zach Snyder created a Batman that a viewer can get behind. Awesome movie!

title: It's fine, but still a big mess
review:
Does a film called 'Batman v Superman' deliver on the promise of its title? No. Does it provide an exciting, unpredictable and enjoyable watch? No. Does it have a well-held together and consistent story? No. There are a lot of issues with this film, and it seemed that for everything it did right, something went wrong. That said, there is something there, beneath the chaotic result that it is, and for the most part, despite its many, many problems, I found some enjoyment in Batman v Superman. It's a huge disappointment given the legendary stature of its characters, and the negatives are numerous, but don't be too ready to completely dismiss this film yet.

The biggest issue with this film is that it's overstuffed with four or five stories that, in truth, deserved to have their own feature films to be fleshed out. Rather than providing a coherent, exciting superhero movie, Batman v Superman includes the versus match-up, the political side to the presence of superheroes in this world, the set-up to the Justice League movies coming in future, an independent Batman story, and an independent Superman story, and trying to put all of that into one movie, even if it is two and a half hours long, is never going to work.

And what's worse is that it's almost impossible to ignore that problem. Right from the opening sequence, we have this horribly jerky, clunky editing, where we see various events from around the world relating to all the separate stories, all separated by painfully awkward cuts to black. That's an issue that continues throughout the film, and it really got on my nerves, because it just meant that I couldn't enjoy a simple, exciting blockbuster story thanks to there being so many disjointed stories going on all around.

There are a whole lot of other big problems with Batman v Superman, including the fact that it takes effectively 90 minutes to see any fighting between the two titular characters (and that only lasts a few minutes anyway), the major issues that we had with Man Of Steel not being rectified as the first act suggests, the horrifically ugly CGI-fest that obliterates your eyeballs in the final act, and the bizarre performance given by Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, coming across more as a bumbling weirdo than an eccentric villain (which really clashes with the film's hugely dark tone) and even more.

However, despite all that, there are some positives to be drawn from this film.

Overall, I thought Batman v Superman was fine. I didn't love it, but there were some elements that I think really worked well. For one, Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman is great, as is Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman (even if she's not in the movie as much), but as for Batman/Bruce Wayne, he was a character that I could really get behind and understand, and I had a great time learning more and more about this incarnation of the Caped Crusader thanks to Affleck's performance.

What I liked most, however, about this film, was the first act. Yes, it was insanely slow-moving, and should have been considerably shortened, but the first act presented a really interesting political question. Playing out with pretty much no action for 90 minutes, the first half of Batman v Superman is almost like watching a political drama about the legality and morality of superheroes, which I was really interested by. Unfortunately, that drama was squandered by a dumb, lacklustre action finale, but it does prove that there are some bright minds working behind building the DCEU, and I'm still hopeful for the future.
