title: Lives up to expectations
review:
Does absolute power allow for absolute good? Or does it mean having to compromise for the Greater Good? Does absolute power put someone above the rest? Or does it call for an even stricter moral restraint? These fundamental questions about morality, heroism and more, are addressed in DC Comics' new epic film, Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice.

This movie is not just about a physical battle between two titans. If that were the case, they'd be pounding upon each other for two and a half hours. No. This is a clash of ideals, a battle of wills. On one hand, the Batman, a ruthless vigilante who brands his victims, after mercilessly attacking criminals as and when the job requires; and on the other hand, Superman, whose incorruptible sense of morality forever prevents him from operating as an agent of Fear like the Batman, but rather as an agent of Hope.

The best part about this film is the fact that director Zack Snyder learns from his mistakes, and as a consequence, so does Superman. When the prequel, "Man of Steel", portrayed the Last Son of Krypton as just another mindless weapon of destruction, die-hard fans assumed (and they turned out to be right) that this uncharacteristic blandness in Superman's otherwise rich moral fiber would be washed away once he got more practice and got used to the whole "hero thing". Critics and Superman purists, on the other hand, had already dismissed the rebooted Superman franchise as another failed experiment. Snyder, however, proved them wrong. Henry Cavill puts on a balanced but impressive performance as a god who has to make the tough choices, but at the same time as the traditional save-a-cat-out-of- a-tree Superman that long-time fans know and love. Although Cavill's portrayal wasn't as accurate in this "humane" aspect, it was still a huge improvement upon his one-dimensional Man of Steel portrayal, and still a work in progress. More is expected from him in The Justice League: Part One.

Ben Affleck is simply spectacular as the Batman. He has the ideal physique for the character, being slightly bulkier than Christian Bale's unnaturally-lean-Batman. The film has some superbly choreographed Batman fight scenes, all of which showcase a slightly rougher combat style of a hero who knows 27 martial arts, although his incessant passive use of guns takes a lot away from the core of the character (who hasn't touched a gun since the 1960's). This Batman is much older than the traditional Batman, and he's also that much more merciless. This major change in the personality of the Batman is the central plot point of the movie; the crux of the moral battle between Fear and Hope. Affleck pulls off a great Bruce Wayne as well, with the exception of having a much more depressed Alfred to help him out.

While Amy Adams does a decent job of Lois Lane, Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor is a very squeaky disappointment. One of the biggest mistakes of the movie was having someone with the personality of the Joker (minus the confidence), in Lex Luthor's shoes. The two characters are poles apart, and Snyder seemed to have forgotten this. This film was a guide on how NOT to be Lex Luthor, because this is the furthest the character has ever deviated from the original version. Luthor is extremely self- confident, and the lack of this important personality trait in the film, is a major setback. A squeaky voice, nervous tics, and stage fright, all backfire on the character, taking away from his brash arrogant genius instead of adding to it. He has been shown, however, to be quite resourceful and cunning, something which redeems Eisenberg's performance a notch.

Superman's suit has been given more color and vibrancy after Man of Steel (helping to brighten the character as well), deepening the blue and yellow and giving a softer feel to the cloth rather than the plastic feel in the prequel. The Bat-suit has finally been made out of cloth armor, rather than the Kevlar battle armor we have seen in all previous movie versions of the character. His mechanized suit is very similar to the suit in The Dark Knight Returns comic, and does great justice to the same.

This brilliance in costume design is a perfect supplement to the special effects spectacle that unfolds. Zack Snyder started out as a cinematographer, and his specialty lies in his attention to detail and hyper-realism. From the tiniest speck of dust to the cinders on Wonder Woman's shield, from the lightest breeze when Superman hovers, to the bang that resonates when he breaks the sound barrier, everything is perfectly done. The fight scenes are right out of a comic book, with great accuracy shown in the trademark manner in which each hero fights (The Trinity vs Doomsday is the perfect example). Even the way Superman flies is much smoother than the rough bursts of speed shown in Man of Steel, emphasizing the fact that he's gotten so much better at being himself.

Hans Zimmer does it once again. Currently the greatest music director in mainstream Hollywood, he has surpassed his work in Inception and The Dark Knight with his unique take to each character. Keeping the same Man of Steel theme for Superman, he has created a separate theme for each character, which is merged into their respective fight scenes wonderfully, and will also be used for each hero's individual films in the future. Director Zack Snyder has hit three birds with one stone with this film: 1: a reasonably improved Superman; 2: setting a stage of epic universal proportions (via the upcoming The Justice League) with new characters and story lines; and 3: providing a visual treat to audiences, both the average movie goer and the die hard comic fan alike. He has also provided DC Comics fans with the opportunity to see some landmark story lines and characters come to life on the big screen.

title: If You Seek His Monument Look Around You *spoilers*
review: Trepidation is the first emotion felt in my first viewing of Zack Snyder's Batman vs Superman. The second time not so much. I can describe the joy of seeing a spectacle of filmmaking like this pepper with great choreography, effects, and homages to not only comic book source material but great films and literature. It opens strongly with a familiar yet poignant retelling of Bruce Waynes two births- his parents deaths tinged with a little Citizen Kane and his introduction to the Superman giving rebirth to his newly unforgiving alter ego. This film cannot be discussed or analyzed without addressing the critical smear campaign surrounding it. In my first go round I feared that the film wouldn't be good. I was wrong to worry. However it does not mean the film is perfect. The reviews for this film are either mostly below a fair score or overblown to 10's from very protective fans. This film is so strongly divisive that I can say objectively they both are valid simultaneously. The editing, particularly one or two scenes out of place or unnecessary, characterizations, and tone are the film's real problems. Acting and visuals were far from it. From scenes of Perry White randomly asking where Clark Kent is, to Justice League post-credit scenes popping up in medias res, a lot more time in the editing room wouldn't be so bad. Manic Lex Luthor is hate it or love it but Eisenberg goes for it. Instead of explaining his every action he uses allegory and scripture. This will frustrate anyone who can't read between his complex motivation. As is with most of the film it won't hold your hand through any context and requires you to use clues sprinkled in not only this film but also Man of Steel. For example there is a strange cut back to Luthor spilling blood over general Zod, that will go over your head. However it hearkens back to the Macguffin codex from MoS, and Luthor using his own blood as such with Zod as the Doomsday clone's host. Kryptonian clones designed with singular purpose, remember? And that is less of a problem for fans but a huge issue for general audiences who may not get the film's many references, callbacks, and allegories it puts forth with very little exposition. That is the true flaw of the film. Upon second view, the ending and story choices toward the end don't improve but the overall themes when analyzed work really well. 75 percent of this film is a masterpiece of art cinema. Feeling more Birdman than Furious 7. Even if you dislike Snyder, you must acknowledge the cinematography, choreography, and his boldness to unflinchingly go for comic book adaptations no one has ever seen so vividly. Don't go in expecting the fight but oh wow the Batman highlights in this is are out of All-Star or other brutal interpretations. 7.5 is the perfect score for this. But for Affleck I will personally score 8 of ten. The fans will survive the public shaming of this film but we know. Look around we are it's monument.

title: DC Cinematic Universe successful launched
review:
I have been waiting for Batman V Superman : DOJ Since it was announced 3 years ago. & Movie did not disappoint at all. Watched it on IMAX & Enjoyed It Thoroughly.Everyone was cheering in the hall.. The movie is absolutely stunning piece of comic book movie.One needs to pay attention through for easter eggs & plot development.You can lose track. & It Had few not so good moments. But It does not kill the movie like Critics Claim it.To please everyone is impossible.Either they were hoping for light-toned humorous U.A movie or Maybe they were not given freebies.

A Straight Forward True To Sources, A Stylish Comic Book Movie...

GOOD :- Movie Starts with Bruce Wayne's Parents were murdered in the opening Credits As Credits Roll.( Just Like In Watchmen.) That scene sets the tone of the movie. Metropolis War Seen Through Eyes of Bruce Wayne.The Horror of Death & Destruction felt by people on The Ground Level.Surely Gives Goosebumps. This is how Comic Movie should be.Gritty, Brutal, No Nonsense.

Nightmares :- Well timed & reflecting how troubled Bruce Wayne is. ( Critics complained about this too without understanding.) Never felt this in Marvel Cinematic Universe,when Tony Stark had traumatic illusions,it was so thin. Bruce Wayne & Batman cannot be chirpy & funny...shooting one liners.

Metahumans :-Cameos of Other members.Very clever on how DC have handled the Introductions of Flash,Aquaman & Flash in the universe.( Differ themselves from Marvel)Team-ups leading to solo movies.Something big is brewing for DC Cinematic Universe.

BvS Showdown:- Encounter Between Superman & Batman was epic.It really gave the feel of Two Most Iconic Superheroes going against each other. One of the most awaited Gladiator match. It was choreographed beautifully with Batman & Superman having fair fight,but Batman gets better of Superman.

Doomsday Climax:- Though the Fight was completely CGI, it was completely amazing. Doomsday emerges & goes on Rampage.Too Much to follow in one glance.

NOT SO GOOD :-

Damsel In Distress Act. It is been used many times.It puts the audience off.

Cocky Villain. As Heroes should be Bad Arse, The Bad Guys should be Too..But Bad Guys are always been the weak point to develop in Comic Book movies.Thats why Joker was good..Because he loved to get his hands dirty & he can plan too. But Lex Luthor can be develop in future installments.

CGI Monsters. Agreed that Doomsday cannot be showed otherwise,but CGI monsters are always been boring to watch as they first destroy & then die.There is no soul.

CAST:-

Ben Affleck portrayal as Bruce Wayne & Batman is perfect.He has No Mercy & Brutal..& Human..His face-off with Doomsday was real showdown between Mortal Being & Evil Carnage Machine.He is aware that he is unmatched & never faced anything like this before.( Not Acting cool like Black Widow & Hawk-Eye facing Aliens & Robots).His Detective Skills have not been explored that much.But His Fighting Skills are top-notch.

Henry Cavill carries performance from MOS. He did not had the time span like MOS due to multiple characters involved.But His role had the worthy impact.The Moral Values,Sacrifice shows the Superman has grown a lot.

Gal Gadot blasted through her role like she meant it to be.Her Entry As Wonder Woman was Kick Ass.Completely knocks the audience off the seat.Simply Outstanding.Her smirk & confidence when fighting Doomsday says about her being Warrior who has seen too much.

Jesse Eisenberg is cocky & doesn't live up to the character of Lex Luthor. He is downright sadistic,shrewd tactical villain. His presence would have been felt if he would be meaner instead of being annoying.His plans to frame Superman,Turning Against Batman & Other Sinister Plans would have been better. But He Does All the Damage.

Jeremy Irons's Alfred is wise cracking butler.Jeremy Irons character has brought new leaf to Alfred.He not only serves Bruce Wayne but also knows to operate weapons & machines in Batcave.

Other Cast Members did a fair job.

Ratings : - 8.5 / 10

Verdict : An Honest Attempt, True to sources.Can be Better. DC Cinematic Universe successful launched.

title: Batman fans rejoice. Superman fans-prepare to be disappointed.
review:
It is really evident that the writer of Argo has also been involved in the script for this movie. He has given his pal a wonderful role. Batman is the only one who has a consistent and meaningful role in the entire movie. He gets to defeat Superman, save Clark's mom and also live to let the tale of the fight with Doomsday. What more could Batman ask for?

Superman on the other hand, flies around like an alien completely detached and lost in his own thoughts. The scene at the US Senate is hilarious. Superman flies in, does not say a single word, everything blows up and then Superman flies off.

Superman's first encounter with Batman is also incredibly stupid. Batman chasing Lex's truck with Kryptonite. Superman suddenly appears and wrecks his car and asks him to stand down. He does not stop to ask what was Batman chasing and why? He does not show any interest in the cargo itself (a 80% destroyed truck gunning it at full speed). Superman is truly made to appear as all brawn and no brains.

For me, the most unforgiven act is the fight with Doomsday. It is one of the all time highlights of Superman's career where he makes the ultimate sacrifice. In the comic books (and in the animated movie), it is made clear why that needs to be done. No one else could stop him. No green rock, nobody except Superman. This was never done in this movie. We are made to believe that Lex's blood is so toxic that it made General Zod into Doomsday. Only Zack could go with such nonsense. For the sake of the idea of Justice League, Wonder Woman and Batman were introduced into the fight and Superman spends about 50% of the time laying injured and down on the ground, without any one-to-one fighting with Doomsday

The fight sequence of Superman and Doomsday has too many disruptions. What was the point of introducing the nuclear missile? It beggars belief that action was interrupted time and time again. What was wrong with showing a live action version of what was in the comics or the animated movie (or as close to it as possible)? For 90% of the audience, they would be seeing it for the first time and for the rest, it would be a real thrill to watch it from a different perspective.

It is the same as Warner making a Harry Potter movie and the director insisting on changing a key scene in the movie to be different from the book.

The DC movie franchise is cursed. We are doomed to be disappointed again and again.

review:

Some people are complaining about the plot that there was the lack of it I found it quite obvious what the whole plot was, it's true the director didn't went all obvious with the plot thing, it was more like in the Man of Steel, the little pieces of the story were there but if you don't watch it with you head you're gonna get lost in the process. title: A good platform for better things to come
review:
I can't understand all the hate going around about this movie. There is no way that this can be compared to the Nolan's batman trilogy. In the era where comic book movies are delivered to us like factory products every year, Batman v Superman is no different but it is not bad either. Zack Snyder takes a slightly different approach compared to his previous Man of Steel and has made Batman v Superman a conventional comic book movie. Dawn of Justice is dark, loaded with extreme action and old school.

The movie picks up from the end of Man of Steel and pits the two protagonists Batman and Superman against one another in their approach towards justice. The introduction of the Batman is kept short but done neatly. The story is based mainly upon the remains from Krypton (Reference: Man of Steel) and their use for evil purposes by the maniac Lex Luthor. Superman is made to look guilty in the eyes of the world and is branded Alien. Billionaire Bruce Wayne a part time vigilante who stops crime and plans on stopping Superman to save the world privately investigates Lex Luthor and his evil plans. The plot is a tad illogical at times but that doesn't take anything away from superbly shot action sequences and crisp characterization of the lead characters.

Haters gonna hate but Ben Affleck has nailed it as Bruce Wayne/Batman. Here Batman is much older and is a no nonsense guy when it comes to fighting crime. Henry Cavill is probably the best Superman ever. Somehow Amy Adams as Lois Lane once again finds herself in important scenes and actions sequences. Jesse Eisenberg has delivered in making Lex Luthor look as psychotic as possible. Jeremy Irons as the butler Alfred is more than a butler here. Gal Gadot is super hot as Wonder Woman and fits well for the role. Laurence Fishburne, Diane Lane and Kevin Costner in a cameo amp up the star value of the cast.

The movie is thoroughly entertaining and brings justice (league) to the DC's present and future plans. Don't see the ratings and read negative reviews, go watch this epic battle!

title: Dostoevsky's Heroes
review:
There seems to be a sense of gleeful abandon in the hate piled on Batman v Superman, with fierce denunciations of incoherent storytelling, excessive morbidity, unclear character motivation, and - worst of all - a lack of faithfulness to the source material.

Now, I'll put this up front: I loved both Watchmen and Batman Returns, two films that get a lot of hate for being slow and dark.

Did Man of Steel earn dark? No. While I understand Snyder's conceit that it was a formative Superman story, it's implausible that someone who demonstrated such conscience in the middle act would have to murder someone to learn murder is never the answer, or realize that punching someone into a building might endanger innocent life.

For Batman v Superman, dark is earned. While Superman is still finding his feet, Batman has been at it for 20 years. He's tired. He's jaded. He's lost a Robin and Wayne Manor. This isn't the Batman of the mainstream comic - this is the Batman of The Dark Knight Returns. There are machine guns on the Batmobile. He's been killing for years. And those crying foul over liberties with Batman's principles would do well to read Frank Miller's dystopian masterpiece: here we have a Batman broken by the cost of two decades of battle with nothing to show for it but ongoing crime.

Then this guy shows up who could stop any crime in an instant, but doesn't. Yet he has so much power he can kill thousands by accident. How could a hero devoted to protecting the innocent possibly allow such a danger to exist?

That's the surface part of Batman's motivation. But as we see throughout the film, Superman's very existence can damage the human psyche. Some worship him. Some see him as a hero. But for Bruce Wayne, who's been frustrated by his own inability to end crime, he represents an invalidation of everything he is. With a veritable god around, is there even a point in being Batman? What were all his sacrifices for? Bruce Wayne turns to drink to quiet his constant existential demons, and his increasing brutality is just another inappropriate outlet. This is not a hero Batman anymore; this is one who must be reined in.

This film also addresses the question of whether Superman's power is too much for one person to hold. While the MCU has many super- powered beings, as of the start of this film, DC has only one. Superman could kill us all, and we simply need to have faith that he won't. Batman himself turned from a paragon of justice to someone who kills to get the job done. How could he be sure Superman wouldn't do the same? And if he did, who could stop him? As (seemingly) the only other hero around, he has a responsibility to ensure Superman is either contained or destroyed. And nowadays, "destroy" is his natural choice.

This is why the story hinges on Batman's faith in Superman's humanity. While it could be argued that the transition is too quick when it comes, we must also remember that Batman is, though he doesn't know it, seeking to reclaim his own humanity. The realization that he's about to slay a man - not a god, but a man - who fears for his mother just as he feared for his own drives a nail straight into his heart. It may be contrived (what superhero movie isn't?), but it's not without logic or motivation.

As for Luthor, he has a similar existential problem. He doesn't fear Superman thwarting some particular plan. The problem is, if Superman exists, what are his plans worth?

Luthor believes knowledge is power, and as one of the most knowledgeable people on earth, he's at the top. Then Superman arrives and tilts the scales forever against him: no matter Luthor's knowledge, Superman will always have more power.

You can see Luthor cracking during his library speech, as the thing that makes him feel useless stands there while he can do nothing. Nothing, except pour his mind into finding a way to destroy Superman, both eliminating the symbol of his inadequacy and proving that knowledge can defeat a god's power.

And what kind of plan does he hatch? One that manipulates two heroes into mutual destruction while he prepares an insurance plan. It's a complex scheme from a complex villain using only his intellect to destroy the most powerful thing on earth. It's hard to follow, and should be, as it creates a worthy opponent for the detective Batman.

We must also understand that while we have a fallen Batman, we also have an incomplete Superman, traumatized by the idea that, despite his power, he's unable to save his mother. That Batman refuses to help - and won't even listen - drives this not-yet-self-accepting Superman to act in rage. The first appearance of Kryptonite is another shock. While the reaction is foolish, it's set up by the story: only Superman's humanity holds him back from killing Batman, yet the very symbol of his humanity is at stake, and the contradiction makes him prey to emotion.

This is not a film about physical goals, where villains want to steal something or destroy something or gain control over something. This is Dostoevskian: The characters' actions have everything to do with their sense of who they are. For Batman and Luthor, Superman's existence invalidates everything they ever thought themselves to be. And for Wonder Woman - who is, yes, important here - his dogged sacrifice represents a reason to fight for humanity once more. Her presence gives significance to his actions, and finally brings us around to what Superman can be at his best: the guy who does the right thing even when it's the hardest thing to do.

title: The Beginning...
review:
SupermanVs.Batman: Dawn of Justice, well let me start by saying this title fits this film, perfect. Throughout history we've all loved a good match-up, whether it be our favorite sports teams, Cowboys vs. Giants, Bears vs. packers, Or fighters like boxing, Ali vs. Frazier, Holyfield vs.Tyson, or even wrestling Icons, Hulk Hogan vs. The Ultimate Warrior, more recently and it will date this review for sure, Trump vs. Hilary. I Am sure you could give me an iconic match-up but can we think of one that resonates with us all, generations past, present and future all have they're heroes, and your talking about the two most iconic heroes of it all, Superman, and Batman.

Through out the years we've seen these two heroes develop from mere drawings in a comic too on the grandest of stages, Film. The actors that have portrayed Batman, Adam West, George Clooney, Christain Bale, & my favorite, Micheal Keaton, made the character all they're own, bringing what they feel that Batman, Is. Superman a little harder to cast in my opinion, has been portrayed by the talents of George Reeves, Dean Cain, Brandon Routh, And Superman forever for me, Christopher Reeve, the actor had to give the sense of being the most humble guy, while being the most powerful. Here we stand with a great Trilogy of films all starring Christian Bale, I felt he gave a decent portrayal of Batman, and Bruce Wayne, And now we begin a new era as Ben Affleck has stepped into the role. And Superman after stand alone film Titled Man Of Steel, this was Henry Cavill's coming out party to his era.

Dawn of Justice, written by David S. Goyer, Chris Terrio And Directed by Zack Snyder, Chris Terrio worked on The Dark Knight trilogy, and Man Of Steel, so that helps in forming a story for your characters. Zack no stranger to Directing, They Bring you Superman Vs. Batman, Dawn of Justice, Dawn of Justice indeed. The film starts out right where Man of Steel had ended, so it will help in watching Man Of Steel to understand this film. Henry Cavill reprising his role as The Man Of Steel, Superman. We're introduced immediately to Ben Affleck, but as Bruce Wayne, right in the middle of Superman facing off against General Zod, there is an untold amount of destruction occurring around the city as Bruce tries to get to his building in the city, his tower collapsed. Killing friends and colleagues.

Superman Prevails in his fight against Zod, and kills him. The world is thrust into a different state upon knowing of alien life, knowing there is another galaxy and planet besides earth sustaining life, Holly Hunter leads the senate or congress through what the world would probably be doing if we had a real life, Superman. During this time you see Bruce Wayne's past, yes it is exactly the same every time, His parents were murdered right in front of him, scarring him for life, upon running through a wooded area, he falls into what we become to know as his Batcave. This film builds you up, almost in my opinion giving you a mini Superman movie, And Batman movie. We are introduced to Lex Luthor, played by Jesse Eisenburg, now I do like Eisenburg as an actor, I enjoyed Zombieland very much, but I can't help but now after seeing the film thinking he was poor choice of Lex Luthor, I can see what he tried to give the character but first off all, age, Eisenburg is too young, Lex Luthor Is iconic for being the Rich, Mastermind and Eisenburg just didn't give me that I'm sane and powerful guy, instead he seemed like a weird, rich kid in the middle of something he shouldn't be involved in.

This film does boast a pretty stellar all star cast from obviously Henry and Ben, Jesse, but also Holly Hunter, Diane Lane, and were introduced to the beautiful up and coming actress Gal Gadot, when we're introduced to yes, Wonder Woman. What a great feeling when she finally appeared to fight, an Iconic character that hasn't been seen in years. Gal Gadots role was semi-sweet and short, I will be expecting more from her in the Justice League film. She had good screen presence, and fits Wonder Woman well. The film gives s sub plot all orchestrated by Lex Luthor, leading up to the match-up of the millennia, Superman vs. Batman. History has taught us that Superman could kill Batman, he's merely a man, but Batman develops his own plan, learning what hurts Superman, and uses it on him. I must say I was satisfied with the clash between them, I liked the fact you got to see a darker version Superman, taking himself to a place where he had to go in order to face Batman. By the end your left wanting more, I won't spoil it past this but you get a Super Iconic fight between Superman, and ?. And Batman and Wonder Woman are there to help. Overall I thought Ben did a decent job as Batman, Henry makes a good Superman but in my opinion not so much a good Clark Kent, I'll leave that one for the one and only, Christopher Reeve. This film does give you the sense that our planet, our human way of life has a Super threat now, Meta Humans. Alien beings,and superior men, out to save the world? Out to conquer and rule? Or just simply doing everything in they're power to keep us, this world, safe? I give it an 8/10, I would recommend if your a true fan of Superman, or Batman, and who knew, Wonder Woman fans are cheering now too, till the next film, enjoy this one.

title: Not what was expected...

title: From a non-critic, regular moviegoer's point-of-view: GOOD MOVIE
review:
BvS was one of the most hyped movies of the year. I am so excited to see this on screen. I'm not a hard- core comic book reader but I did read a few comic books.

I was not a fan of Man of Steel, it just wasn't mt cup of tea. BvS on the other hand for me is a lot better than MoS. It had great moments like the first encounter of Superman and Batman, Wonder Woman's appearance and Batman's story during MoS.

Ben Affleck's Batman is great. He was definitely a good fit for the role. Henry Cavil IS Superman, Gal Gadot is perfect as Wonder Woman.

I do get why some people don't like the film. It was a bit slow and fast at the same time. There were parts where the film wasn't able to explain what was being set up. It had too much going on but there wasn't enough time to explain what was going on.

I felt like Jesse's Lex Luthor was too much. It was more of Joker-ish than Lex Luthor. I also didn't like how they made Lex know all of Justice League's identities. I think they could've just let it unfold one at a time than giving Lex all the information at once.

This movie is actually enjoyable despite its flaws. I was hooked from start to finish, since I'm not so much familiar with the comic books.

BvS is like AoU. The film is just a set up for what's in store for us.

You should still see this movie, it's different from other Comic Book films.

title: A big step up from Man of Steel
review:
There's still a lot of destruction here, but it's not as pointless and I really appreciated that Superman actually makes a major attempt to avoid any civilian casualties this time around, instead of just throwing his enemies into whatever building is nearest. The new cast members are really good too, especially Affleck, Irons, and Gadot (even though she has a fairly small role, what we see of her is great). Amy Adams also improved and Henry Cavill is as good as he ever was.

There's an excess of scattered subplots in the first hour or so, but it's still entertaining for the most part, and it picks up more as it continues. Hans Zimmer also did a surprisingly good score, given how much I had disliked his work on Man of Steel and the previous Batman films, though I suppose Junkie XL did it with him. Wonder Woman's theme in particular is awesome.

Action's fair for the most part, though Snyder just won't let go of his beloved slow mo... Still, there are good sequences, especially the warehouse sequence with Batman.

title: Batman V Superman Is a Film With Many Flaws But Some Incredible Pros
review:
(Introduction) I was pretty excited for this film even though I wasn't a huge fan of the trailers, my love for Batman sucked me into the anticipation. And the question is, Was it Worth the Wait? Is Batman V Superman A Good Movie? Well, I'm pretty mixed on all those questions. This is a film I really have multiple opinions on. There are so many aspects of the film I liked and so many aspects I just hated. There is just so many Pros and Cons of this film that the film just seems so mixed and variant but in a negative and positive way.

(Performances) Let's get right into the acting performances. Ben Affleck as Batman is "Phenomenal." I will most likely get a lot of hate for this, but Ben Affleck just might be my favorite Batman. I'm still mixed on this decision but it just tells you how much I loved Bruce Wayne/Ben Affleck in this film. Every scene with Batman in it is so perfect, Batman in this film is definitely my favorite aspect of this movie. Henry Cavill and Amy Adams did great in their roles and did solid performances. I also enjoyed Jeremy Irons performance as Alfred and I can't wait to see him in the next DC film. Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, really didn't work for me. His character just came off as very "Jokerish" which sounds like that's a positive thing but it just comes out as "Over the Top." I can tell he was very committed to his role which I can respect but his character as Lex Luthor was just not serious enough. His role was not something that speaks the character "Lex Luthor."

(Plot/Script Writing) The plot and pacing of this film is the hugest problem I have with this film. This films plot is so messy, everything is just all over the place. The first hour and a little more than a half is so unnecessarily long. The first hour and a half is just a bunch of random scenes that tie up into this huge bundle of bore. Like the first half of this film could have been condensed into 20 to 30 minutes and this film would have been way better. Nope, there's just a ton of unnecessary scenes that could have been just gotten rid of the film completely. The problem is there isn't enough links to the main event which is "Batman V Superman." The actual Batman VS Superman fighting doesn't happen until like almost 2 hours into the film which is disappointing because the lead up for them fighting is really lazily made. Also the tie-ins to the Justice League film is really lazy as well. It just feels like the script writers and plot developers of this film cared more about tie-ing in other future films than actually working on what should've been the main story which is Batman fighting Superman.

(Action Sequences) Now on to the positive, holy whatever, some of the action scenes in this film are absolutely perfect. Zack Snyder knows how to make a good-looking film, maybe not a well plotted one, but a good looking film. This film is amazing in action ways mainly having to do with Batman. Every scene with Batman in it, is perfect and I love it. The look of Batman in my opinion is the best looking Batman ever! The action scenes especially the hand to hand combat with Batman in it, is just pure entertainment. I cannot critique anything about most scenes with Batman in it. Also when Batman and Superman fight (Don't Worry No Spoilers) is absolutely worth it. When "Batman VS Superman" actually happens, it is epic. Also Wonder Woman in this film is pretty sick in most the scenes she is. I like Gal Gadot as Wonderwoman and it makes me pretty excited for her stand alone film. So what is pretty much keeping this film from being a complete fail is the action and Batman in this film. I couldn't ask anymore of Batman in this movie and I think the majority of the action is top notch. The only problem I have is that in the end (DON'T WORRY NO SPOILERS I PROMISE) there is a certain character (That is shown in the trailers so I assume you know who I'm talking about) is so poorly CGI'ed and introduced that it kind of took me out of the story. Also the final battle and 3rd act was absolutely horrific. Like the 3rd act of the film really just took everything downhill. The fight scenes in the last act are somewhat interesting to watch but it just comes off as an excuse to add more action and CGI. There is also a choice they make with a character in the end that was ballsy to make, but in the very end they totally dis that choice and it just comes off as unnecessary and stupid.

(The Overall Pros) Affleck is a Phenomenal Batman Batman is a Perfect Batman Action Sequences are Terrific Batman Fight With Superman is Very Entertaining Cavill and Irons Commit Great Performances

(The Overall Cons) Terrible Plotting Okay Script Writing Slow Pacing for the First Half Lazy Justice League Tie-Ins Some Very Lazily Exposited Motivations An Okay Lex Luthor (Jessie Eisenberg's Performance) The Final Act and Character Choices

(My Overall Rating and Thoughts) Overall I actually wasn't expecting that much of the film. I was more than happy with Batman in this film. Batman was way higher than my expectations could ever reach. The movie looks visually fantastic and has some fan service in it. The lazy plot and script writing though really took me out of the film. So overall I'm going to give Batman V Superman and overall rating ofÂ…

title: Amazingly good!!!!
review: First off let me state the fact that I am not a movie critic. I am a lover of movies especially superhero movies. I go to the movies to be entertained and to escape from this world for a few hours. If you want a review from a critic go somewhere else. If you want an honest opinion from a movie lover please continue reading. I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. I've been waiting for this movie for a long time. title: Shut up, eat your popcorn and enjoy the ride.
review:
The first 15 minutes of this movie is amazing, and really ties into Man of Steel.

Ben Affleck's Batman is amazing, I liked Wonder Woman, and didn't even hate Eisenberg's Lex which I was genuinely concerned about before the movie. Really not sure why all the hate from the critics on the movie.

Could it have been cut together better? Sure.

Was it a good story with beautiful visuals? Of course.

There are definitely some major issues like the weird cuts, and the argument that it feels like 5 different movies can be made. It kinda felt like Man of Steel 2 meets a solo Batman movie meets Dawn of Justice, meets a Lex Luthor solo movie, meets Batman vs. Superman, but in no way is that a bad thing.

Anyway enough rambling I thought it was great. I mean c'mon guys its Batman v. Superman and is the set up for a Justice League movie. Period. Don't read too much into it or you'll find enough to criticize. Shut up, eat your popcorn and enjoy the ride. 8/10.

title: Beat my Expectations - And I Don't Do a Plot Summary
review:
I looked forward to this movie and my expectations were exceeded - but I was still a little let down by the final third. Th initial build up - especially the opening was absolutely brilliant. The way they chose to introduce Batman/Bruce Wayne and weave the original Man of Steel into the plot of this movie simply worked exceedingly well.

It was the fact that with the long running time, the final act actually felt rushed. Spoiler - you know that Batman and Superman will end up fighting together but I just felt that Doomsday felt rushed - it was sort of Lex creates him - releases him and bang - the gang must deal with him right now.

But overall, Afleck was a great Bruce Wayne/Batman - the choice to play him as a guy twenty years into the job was smart and Although there was virtually no humor at all in the film, the movies beats were all tight and felt right - mostly.

It's hard to please everyone when you have source material that's been around forever and has been glommed onto by fan-boys (guess I used to be one) who expect the unattainable. All that in mind, It was a solid and mostly satisfying effort. One step better than Age of Ultron but not ass good ass Iron Man or the first Avengers. (And simply forget the X Men)

title: How Warner manages to screw this movie
review:
With an all-star cast, budget, and million dollar marketing plan- Warner Bros. manages to turn Batman v Superman into a cluttered fiasco. A non-existent script and story is a great deal of the problem- but castings like Jesse Eisenberg as Lex is not going to help either.

Gal Gadot manages to impress in her short moments as Wonder Woman, but once again this disastrous script lacked any depth and barely set the bar for the Justice League Franchise. A 2.5 hour movie could have been spent more productively on Flash / Aquaman's character- and less on a geeky Lex Luthor.

Ben Affleck performance as Batman was done decently, but the personal development with Superman's character was forced and rushed until the ending. How many times have we watched a Bruce Wayne origin story? Also thanks for the Joker easter egg, would have preferred an after- credits scene.

In short words Warner Bros attempt at a DC universe timeline will take years to develop- a foundation as weak as BvS will put its future into serious question.

review:

title: Definitely a Movie for the Fans
review:
I have seen this movie twice within it's opening weekend, and I can honestly tell you that I have no idea why there is so much hate for this movie from the critics. Sure it's got flaws, like every movie (I have never given a movie a 10), but I do not think it's as flawed as people say.

This movie is full of comic book content. It effectively combines more than one story from the comics, and if you have read the comics, you can point out what was taken from the comics. In fact, there are some lines that are exactly the same from the comics. I was really impressed.

I've heard the pacing was bad from other people, but I don't think it really is. The pacing is always setting up something later in the movie, or trying to get you to think. There were questions presented in the film that really made you ponder. The action was awesome, but it wasn't just pure action (like some people thought Man of Steel was). All the actors and actresses did such a great job with their part, and I loved seeing the brutal Batman that we haven't seen much of over the years.

Unfortunately I do have a couple of complaints. What it comes down to mostly is that if you don't know the comics, then scenes from the movie might confuse you, and may seem random. They're actually not if you knew the stories. This is why I say this movie is for the fans. Maybe the critics don't know the comics, so thought the movie was a mess when it really isn't? I dunno. But I know for sure some people have been confused because they don't know the comics. Yes the writers should have made it so that even people who aren't fans of the comics would understand, but they didn't. This has made people think the movie is a tad confusing, and made it so that I have had to explain to a lot of people what was going on. But other than that, I really don't have much to complain about. It's what comic book fans would want to see in a movie based off some of their favorite comic book characters, and I was very pleased with what I saw.

Overall, this movie is quite good, and really enjoyable. I don't quite understand all the hate, and I hope people don't let the critics think for them, and actually go see the movie to form their own opinion. Critics are there to help people in some ways, but a lot of the time they are not correct, and the audience thinks the opposite of what they do. So give this movie a chance, and maybe you'll like it just as much as me.

title: Brilliance in a Superpowered Batblender
review:
While we live in a time of two track minds where nuance is not allowed, this is a film fan boys will flaunt and critics will flop while audience members unbound by nonsensical corporate corroborated dedication to one comic company or another will see good and bad. Yes, the film has many flaws and yes, it has a lot of fun, but overall it's neither a disaster, nor a masterwork, it's a slightly above average popcorn flick with production quality and performances that show effort in the face of flimsy storytelling and a butchered 30 minutes of missing movie.

The film seemed content to linger in melodrama until its final third during which as much action and Justice League set up had to be slammed in as sloppily as directorially possible. As fans assumed from some of the many overlong trailers there wasn't much left to see, it was overly crowed struggling to sustain the balance between brooding and bombastic brain bashing. With possibly one of the worst casting decisions since Voldemort's brother as Michael Jackson, you simply can't make an awkward, nasally man child who has never played anyone other than himself act like a brilliant and menacing 50 year old Lex Corp CEO and criminal mastermind who sounds nothing like Michael Cera on Adderall.

All in all, the film is a hodgepodge of good dialogue and poor story structure, likely due to one half of the two man writing team. It features phenomenal fight choreography, emotionally investing performances with payoff that often seems to refund itself. For every step forward the film takes, it takes one back, Batfleck is brutally bad to the bone, Lexinberg is a wacky cartoon character, Wonder Woman is wonderful, Mercy was mercilessly wasted, Cavil-El carried the climax and then backpedaled into a fumble, the world-building was bafflingly ham handed but in the end it was worth a watch for its sparks of brilliance, though they usually douse themselves. Whatever you do, don't wait until after the credits, because the only scene you'll see is a groaning audience walking wearily out after a few wasted minutes.

title: An Extravaganza of a Superhero Film!
review:
The critics are wrong. This is not a terrible or even bad film. It.Is.Amazing. The concept of the two biggest superheroes of all time is breathtaking enough. But the execution of that concept is murderous.

Ben Affleck is surprisingly amazing as Bruce Wayne/Batman. Although the Dark Knight is the superior film, I have to say I prefer Ben Affleck as Bruce compared to Bale. The Batsuit is redesigned to look amazing, and it gives the dark knight a darker tone. Henry Cavill once again repeats his superman performance with style, and is great as Clark Kent/Superman. But the standout actor of this film is Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. Jessie gives a new spin on Luthor, making him more crazily smart like the joker, rather then just an intellectual bold middle age man.

As far as filmmaking goes, this film is good. The typical Zach Snyder Shots are present, as are his intense over the top awesome action sequences. The Story is loyal to the comics and also displays a lot of good messages- That no one is perfect. That sometimes our ego gets in the way of what is important. Or sacrifice is the most important thing. The Special FX are great, but unnoticeable(which is what they're supposed to be.)

This film holds up VERY well compared to films of late like The Force Awakens(which destroyed many peoples franchise, unlike BVS which does the opposites) and Age of Ultron. Marvel fans will not like this film. 50% because they are jealous of this film, and 50% because they don't know a good film when they see it.

Hopefully this film will receive some Oscar love. Ben Affleck and Jessie Eisiendberg(I'm not a fanboy, I'm a film critic. And they're acting is great) deserve a nomination but sadly won't receive a nom. Instead BVS will be nominated for best visual effects and best sound effects, and hopefully will win.

Go see this film before You don't have time. It's great.

title: Great Movie!!!
review: Much better than Man of Steel. Different style and feel from Marvel movies, which is not necessarily good or bad, just different. Critics who call the story incoherent were not paying enough attention or don't have the capacity for anything beyond simple, obvious plots. Plot makes perfect sense by the end of the movie. There is a lot packed into 2.5 hrs and I expect the 3-hr blu-ray version will be even better. The only thing I really didn't care for was Lex's theme music. Affleck plays Batman well, I like his even-grittier character. Wonder Woman is amazing and Cavill continues to be a solid Superman? Overall, I rate BvS as 2nd-best DC movie, second only to Dark Knight. Can't wait for Justice League!!!

title: I can't believe I am defending DC
review:
First off, I am a big Marvel fan, but that being said, I don't get the ugly reviews of this movie. Let me start by saying I know why Professional Critics might tear the movie apart, but fans.. thats another story. So let me breakdown by categories so it will be easier to understand my opinion. If you are a DC purist: You will probably not like the movie as it takes a bunch of different story lines and tries to make it all come together, in my opinion unsuccessfully. If you are Man of Steel fan: You probably will like this movie as it has some of the feel of the Man of Steel movie that I like. If you a Batman fan: You have to feel that Ben Affleck did not wreck this movie. He was pretty good in fact, SPOILER, in his future dream fight scene it was pretty good action sequence and Jeremy Irons played a great Alfred IMO. If you are looking for a good comic book movie: Well BvS is a long movie, that has some cool action sequences but can be dull at parts. But when it came to action scenes, they were pretty cool. Action Movie junkies: All action this movie is not, but if you have patience it picks up pretty good. All and All I was happy about the movie action, I just always want more. But I am an action junkie.

Look, there is a lot of mistakes, ways you can pick it apart, I saw this with my girl friend and grandson, and we all left entertained and satisfied with the outcome. Zach Synder did not make the best comic book movie, but hes far from made the worst. I can rattle off 3 or 4 modern comic book movies that had far less action, were more boring and less character development.

Give it a chance, you might like it. Don't listen to anyone else or especially critics. Have fun! I did. + Batman (Ben was good) + Wonder Woman did a great job + Alfred (Jeremy Irons) + Action Scenes - Long winded - Superman seemed like to many different Superman's, should have stuck to one. - Doomsday wish they just made him like the comics, new powers seemed weird, pacific rimmish - kinda confusing at parts

title: Deep. Dark. Yet so pleasing.
review: I just went to see the movie this evening. I had glimpses of some reviews of the movie and mostly they were negative so I walked into the cinema hall, hoping the movie wouldn't suck! Guess what?!!! Those reviews couldn't have been more misleading! I thought the movie was brilliant. It was dark. There was depth to it. The back story was long yet necessary! Ben and Henry were fantastic in it, not to mention the beautiful and perfect cast as Wonder Woman! If I were to be critical about anything, it would be the fact that the first 30 minutes could have been less sluggish. Anyway, I am going to see it again tomorrow! Job well done!

title: Better than a nap
review:
Got into this one early -- Thursday afternoon at my favorite matinée theatre with balcony seating. Naturally, I was excited to see two of my favorite comic heroes duke it out.

Highlights: Batman + guns = *dead* bad guys..! Superman + flaws = a priceless stupid look on his face! Not even Kevin Spacey or the legendary Gene Hackman's performance had such blatant disregard for human life as Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor!

There's good, there's bad and there's unexpected x2. Do yourself a favor and watch https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Y8iRvQdSGA to get prepared for what's coming! ;)

title: Thoroughly entertaining
review: All the rant this movie's getting, it doesn't deserve it. Yes , it had plot holes, most of the time you gotta fill the blanks, it's the bad story telling and editing. The plot's actually got a tremendous potential, which was quite ruined. But that doesn't make this film a boring one. though losing it's potential, it does keep you entertained most of the time. Ben Affleck was kick ass, Henry Cavill was good too. Gal Gadot was terrific in the action sequences, but there wasn't much of acting skills required for her role in the movie except for one scene(which she does pretty well). Jesse Eisenberg as luthor was not charismatic, we don't see him as a threat, but there's definitely more to his character. Action scenes were terrific , and the score was phenomenal.

title: Great movie! Stop comparing to marvel!
review:
I would like to start off by saying, firstly, to all of you haters who hate this movie because you have no idea what going on, and dint like the story telling: Go home, and read a book

This movie was very well made, I am a huge batman fan, i read the comics, and even i thought superman (Henry Cavill) was great. Superman is such a hard character to make a movie about. He's an all around good-guy and pretty much indestructible. I would like everyone else make a better movie for him. I think Lex (Jessie Eisenberg) Played a great villain. The fight scenes were done really well, except for the CG (but lets face it, what other way can you do a superman movie?)The relationship between Lois Lane (Amy Adams) was done a lot better then in MOS. And, i really liked the way the world started turning on Superman to make him not a god.

Now, the story dragged off a bit, but IMO it was for good reason, everything in the movie had a purpose and if you just waited a little bit, it would be explained.

I guess, the biggest controversy in this movie was the creation of a certain character. But, who said the movies have to be IDENTICAL to a comic book? That would defeat the whole purpose of doing the movie. As for the bats.....

BEN AFFLECK IS BATMAN PEOPLE!!!! Forget Keaton, Bale, Kilmer, West. (I'm just gonna assume everyone forgot about Clooney years ago!) The way Ben takes on the cowl is amazing! Super dark and gritty. You actually feel the pain he's in the entire movie. The way they explained his origin was perfect, the best job doing it too! I was really impressed with how Zac Snyder decided to do batman's fighting style. The most accurate to comic book/ Animated movie ever! After this movie i went and watched The Dark Knight, and was really upset my Bales fighting style, he fought like an out of shape heavyweight boxer! Affleck takes it to another level! Even with half a movie, I'm more interested in this film then i am in the other 3 Nolan Films. The only thing i didn't like was that in the movie Bruce Wayne is in his 40's, but when he put on the cowl, no-one calls him batman, they just call him a bat demon, like he just started doing this. This Batman, was a big tribute to the Frank Miller Dark knight Returns, His costume is awesome! and the Batmobile is amazing! I can't say enough about the batman side. So, to avid more rambling, Ill stop now.

Anyways, to wrap this up, Gal Gadot played an awesome Wonder Woman, she made everyone in the audience go crazy when she came out. Jeremy Irons, will make you think Michael Caine who? Finally, When you go watch this movie, go in there with an open mind. Don't go in there expecting to hate the movie, or else why go in at all? its a fun action packed movie, that sets up perfectly for the rest of the DCCU.

Last note, before going to watch it, i would watch/read/spark note The Dark Knight Returns comic book by Frank miller. And, i would also read the "Doomsday!" Superman storyline.

title: Unfairly treated
review:
I can understand that people don't like this movie because it's very dark compared to movies like "The Avengers". This is not a superhero movie for everyone.

The complaints I hear the most are that DC is trying to catch up with Marvel. That is true but it does not hurt the movie nearly as much as people make it out to be. The Justice League cameos are very brief compared to the useless Hawkeye cameo in Thor.

The good stuff: Ben Affleck is amazing as Batman. I believe he is the best live-action adaption of the character. People like to complain about how Batman is killing people in this movie but they are forgetting that he did so in the first movie in 1989. Michael Keaton Batman kills people, nobody panics. Ben Affleck Batman kills people and everyone loses their minds.

Henry Cavill did a great job as superman but we already knew he was going to. All the other actors were also good in their roles. Jesse Eisenberg did a great new version of Lex Luthor. No it's not the Lex Luthor you remember from the old superman movies and that is not a bad thing. Remember that Heath Ledger changed the joker a lot to make it his own character and that is what Eisenberg did.

My only major complaint is that it felt like the movie was too short. I think there should be more build up to the fight between the two heroes. Zack Snyder even said that he cut a lot of scenes from the movie and that they are going to be added in a "ultimate cut" on the blu-ray.

Don't listen to rotten tomatoes. See the movie and make your own opinion.

title: A Triumph
review: all the critics are ,of course, completely wrong. The film is 3 hours long but doesn't feel it. its jams an awful lot into each scene the two male leads and there relationships never feel short changed. The build up to the conflict feel inevitable, inescapable and is not a disappointment when it arrives. It is not however the heart of the film ,it's all about the heroes place in the world that only knows shades of grey. Being pulled in different directions by the forces of corruption and trying to save a humanity that seems far too petty and stupid to be worth saving. The film has a lot to say as well as being merely an action film. so go watch.

title: Dawn of Justice
review:
To start this review, Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is an amazing film, of course there are very minor flaws, but it should never of been called "Batman V Superman". It should of been simply named, "Dawn of Justice". Do not expect a "Versus" film, this film sets up The Justice League and it does it perfectly, I loved this film very much and I believe it's the best Batman comic adaptation we've had yet. (Excluding the realistic and phenomenal Dark Knight trilogy)

This Batman is dark and brutal, perfectly played by Ben Affleck, he is, in my opinion, the best Batman we've had. Henry Cavill as Superman is superb also. The controversial casting for Lex Luthor played by Jesse Eisenberg was huge, but I think it was a good choice, of course there are probably better choices, but he still did a good job at creating this uneasy character, at times I didn't like him, but most of the time, (his theme song is also mind blowing). The dark tone of the film is brilliant, as expected. This film is not for those expecting a fun-loving Marvel film, this is not exactly filled with humour nor fun, which is perfect for this film. Visually, this movie is stunning, I was amazed at the cinematography and the music which goes with it, especially the opening scene and also Lex entering the military site with the crashed ship.

The action scenes are fantastic and done brilliantly, especially the Batman fight scenes, it reminds me of the same style which the Arkham games had. Now I come to the bad points, there isn't a lot of them to be honest, some small parts could of gone into detail, like how Lex's blood onto Zods body could form Doomsday, it is slightly explained, but maybe a bit more explanation could of helped. Also, the "Martha" scene was very good and deep, but maybe if it went slower and not so rushed then it would of settled more, on my second viewing I felt it more. Some people seem to be picking extremely small parts which do not even seem worth the trouble.

There isn't much else to say about the bad points, the film overall was amazing and it exceeded my expectations. I don't understand the amount of hate this movie has, 30% of Rotten Tomatoes is ridiculous, Superman Returns and Furious 7 are much, much higher and they were both awful. The rating on RT should be around 85% and the IMDb rating should be around 7.9 - 8.2. Zack Snyder has done an excellent job, as I expected. If this is what future DC films are to be like, then I will surely love the upcoming universe.

title: People hate what they do not understand (one or two spoilers ahead)
review:
Just watched Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. One thing I want to say about that the poor reviews given to this movie..I won't. However Calling BvS boring, rushed, dark...Dark?! Are you kidding me?! Criticizing Batman v Superman for being too dark & serious is a little hypocritical, no? Batman is the Dark Knight... Do yourselves a favor and page through Frank Miller's TDKR graphic novel or simply watch the animated TDKR movie and Superman: Doomsday. There is no fluffing a story like this. Script? Well written. Characters? Beautifully played. From Watchmen to Sucker Punch to Man of Steel...BvS is a COLOSSUS of a movie that was amazingly directed and no doubt it will break records. I read that a lot of people were confused about the plot....please watch Man of Steel.

Personal favorite highlight: the Trinity standing together side by side and my favorite DC superhero...The Flash (cameo). Oh yeah..Ben Affleck is BATMAN 👏. Score: 9.5/10 (it wasn't long enough😂) #WhoWillWin? The fans do! THANK YOU ZACK SNYDER. ✌

title: Batman v Superman, DC HEAVEN
review:
Snyder has done it again. As a fan who liked Man Of steel, I can say that Batman v Superman: Dawn Of Justice takes it to the next level, full of surprises, new things falling into place, here and there, its just insane to even think about how they pulled it off sometimes, and once you watch it, you can't stop thinking about it (if you're a DC Fan), you are gonna talk about it and you'll not be satisfied as long as you don't see it for the second, third time. Its not a perfect movie, nothings perfect but its way more than what i had expected it to be.

Performances are great, Ben Affleck has KILLED it as Batman/Bruce Wayne, he's the best till date and there is no doubt about that. Henry Cavill, i think was great, many people won't agree with me on this but for me he was great, exactly what i wanted out of him, he delivers, Lex Luthor, actually its Alexander Luthor, his son and most of the people are really confused about that, i liked him, i didn't hate him as Luthor and Wonder Woman, one word, epic.

Overall, wasn't bored, script could've been a bit better but then again if we keep on talking about the possibilities, this could've have been better and that could've been better, we will end up with nothing, and as far as this movie is concerned, i'm just waiting for that Blu ray to come out! i'm that much excited.

Thank you Zack Snyder!

title: Batman v Superman: A tedious, mess of a franchise launcher
review: BvS Dawn of Justice exists primarily to live up to the second half of its title, to serve as a launching pad for a DC Comics film franchise to mirror the wildly profitable cinematic Marvel Studios universe and a desperate attempt of Warner to birth a new cash cow. 1 Hour and 45 minutes of, "Can we please get to it already, bored to DEATH," and 45 minutes of 'YES! Chant' and your inner child being pleased and giddy, minus stupid CGI Doomsday. All the plot holes and illogical pacing in the first hour and 45 minutes makes the movie so haphazardly assembled and a mess, i honestly wondered if a reel had gone missing from the projection booth... Lex Luthor. Jesse Eisenberg sucks as Lex Luthor in look and presence...he is so intensely annoying that, very early on, you wish Batman and Superman would just patch up their differences and join forces to put the squirrelly rascal out of his, and our, misery. On to Batman and Superman...can DC Films ever get a live action Superman right? I thought after Man of Steel, we were going in a good direction with Superman and it would continue on in BvS. WRONG! Cavill Superman is a cardboard expressionless, brooding, sour faced Superman who still questions helping humanity with anything and who seems like it's just not worth it to do so most of the time. What a poor way to frame Superman. Superman is supposed to be the absolute light in the dark. He is the hope, the beacon of the type of person we should all strive to be. Instead, we get the Diet Coke version of Batman with superpowers. Instead of the BvS fight being "Day versus Night" as Lex so eloquently put it, it's more like 'late evening versus slightly later evening.' Superman has to have that sort of boy scout feel to him, he doesn't have to be campy like Reeves or anything, but god, crack a smile man...wave to the crowd, kiss a couple babies, BE THE WHITE KNIGHT! Because you seemed more like Hancock than anything, who didn't give a damn, in this movie. Batfleck, I think he did great as being the overly paranoid Batman in so many variations of shows, comics, and animated movies. So I was happy there. He delivers. Is he better than Bale? I'm going to need more screen time to determine that. However, if you're the type of Batman fan where his 'One Rule' of never killing people should be upheld, you better throw that notion out the window because this Batman has absolutely no problem killing people. I think he might actually kill you for Jay-Walking, he's that into killing criminals (slight exaggeration, greatly maim and disfigure for sure, but you get the point). Remember in The Dark Knight where the Joker was like, "You're going to have to break your one rule..." Batfleck would have easily broken that one rule, no questions asked, Joker would have died and Gotham would be a safer place. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. Seems perfectly fine, will need more screen time though as she didn't get to act much, so I'm looking forward to seeing her in her own movie. There was a point where she's laughing and smiling as she's fighting, like she loves the thrill of combat, if they make her into that kind of Wonder Woman. I'm totally for it. And now, we get into the final 45 minutes of the film, the good stuff, the stuff that as a kid, I wanted to see on the big screen. It delivers and it doesn't. Batman and Superman fight for 10 to 15 minutes, cut out some of the lame crap in the first hour and 45 mins and give us more Bats and Supes going at it, the movie is called Batman v Superman, after all. Once this fight happens it's immediately off to fight Doomsday for 20 minutes or so and then wrap up job to set up the other movies and end this one. CGI Doomsday is stupid, they used that card WAAAAY too soon. Doomsday could have been the bad guy in the Man of Steel sequel, that would have been better than using him here in this movie. I'd rather Lex have created some humanoid-machine hybrid of Zod, than them use Doomsday, but I guess you needed some threat to bring Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman together. All in all, the last 45 minutes of pay off is barely worth the hour and 45 minutes of nonsense, bore and chore. But I can't deny that the last 45 minutes was some good cinema and what we should have had the whole time. I'm still waiting for the universally loved DC Film (not counting Nolan's Batman flicks) that will bring all fans together and finally give Marvel a run for its money, but it is not this day and it is not this movie. This day, I continue to wait for that to happen.

title: A visual spectacle, but not much else.
review: Zack Snyder's follow-up to 2013's divisive Man of Steel feels nothing more than a 150 minute visually striking trailer for DC's Justice League movie that spoilt it's climax in the trailers. Ben Affleck does make for an excellent Bruce Wayne/Batman, walking a fine line between billionaire playboy and justice crazed vigilante, and when Gal Gadot is on screen, she makes for an enigmatic Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. However, the film is smothered in a coat of brooding dark paint with no levity in sight. So many explosions occur that you could be mistaken for watching a Michael Bay movie. The film's main plot is about controlling Superman so he doesn't cause as much unintentional destruction as in Man of Steel, but it completely goes against that to deliver a finale with MORE destruction than Man of Steel. Not to mention, when the trailer back in December showed Doomsday, I thought "Superman is going to die". And I was completely right. There are no twists or turns and the film is a structural trainwreck. If DC want their own cinematic universe, then they'll need to do better than this.
