title: BvS Dawn of Justice
review: It's quite apparent now that BvS has been getting very negative reviews by critics, mainly on the site Rotten Tomatoes. However, as Henry Cavill himself put it, how the audience and the fans feel about the film is what really matters, and both will enjoy BvS despite what critics may lead you to believe. The film deals with the consequences of Superman's actions in MoS, with people all over the globe split on how they should view this god like character. Ben Affleck is a terrific Batman, easily the most brutal Bats we've ever seen on screen. The supporting characters like Amy Adams, Jeremy Irons, and Gal Gadot all do great in their respective roles. A lot of the disdain for the film comes from the tone of the film, it's constantly shifting. The first and second halves of the film feel completely different. There are several plots running throughout the movie, and while most resolve themselves by the end of the film, a few of them are just pointless and add nothing to the film or DCEU. The film looks great, the cinematography and fight scenes are well done, Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL composed a great soundtrack as well. To sum up, BvS is an enjoyable, emotional, entertaining ride that opens up several doors in the DCEU. While there may be a lot going on in the film, and there could have been more time to develop Batman and Superman, it doesn't hurt the film enough to ruin the movie.

title: Not the best DC movie, but still enjoyable
review:
Imagine creating a play list with different genres of music from different periods and play it in shuffle. A mess, right? Yes. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a mess. Too many subplots with no cohesion. About two-thirds of this movie, the first ones, is confusing and dull.

But enough with that and let's get to the good things. First off, the opening sequence. One of the best opening sequence of a movie that I have ever seen and man, that score is haunting. Yes, we've seen it before but this one's on a whole new level. Then, we are introduce to Ben Affleck's Bruce Wayne/Batman and I gotta say, the best live- action adaptation of Batman ever. Ben Affleck nailed it. Though some moral personality of the character's kinda lost. But as a DC fan, I can honestly say they anything Batman-related in this film is great. This also includes Jeremy Iron's Alfred. I love the interaction between the two. You really feel that this two have known each other for a long time now. Henry Cavill's Superman is still good as he was in Man of Steel. Amy Adams is OK. All of the cast did great except I think for Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor. Maybe it's the script or something but, for me, was just OK. He went from socially awkward to really really insane.

On the other hand, the fight sequences are great. This is a good looking film and it's expected from director Zack Snyder. The titular fight between the two heroes was awesome and also that battle with Doomsday. Though, if you have watched that one trailer, then you really have watched the whole film. But that Wonderwoman intro was insane. It was a crowd pleaser and I definitely love Gal Gadot's portrayal already and makes me excited for her solo film. Definitely added her to crush list. Yep. Added.

That soundtrack for her also was great. It has Mad Max feel to it. This film has a great soundtrack. It's thanks to Hans Zimmer who returns after composing the MOS's score and Junkie XL from Mad Max: Fury Road.

Overall, the film is great looking, has a great fight sequences, great visual effects, well acted and awesome soundtrack. Even has the most bad-ass portrayal of Batman on screen ever. But the first two-thirds of the film is a mess and suffers from non-cohesion of subplots. As a DC fan, I still enjoy it though and will be looking forward to all DC films in the future.

title: I really really wanted to love this movie, but just couldn't.
review:
After 3 years of waiting, did it live up to the hype? No, sadly. It isn't even possible not be to be excited to see The Caped Crusader and The Son of Krypton go head to head on the big screen, now is the fight amazing? HELL YEAH!! for a brief 15 minutes. The main problem with this blockbuster is that its slow in the beginning then rushed in the end, the pacing was horrible and the story telling could've been done better.

Basically this film is The Dark Knight Returns and The Death Of Superman put to screen. The overall performances were spectacular, Ben Affleck is the best Batman/Bruce Wayne on screen yet. Although she had only 16 lines, Gal Gadot kills it as Wonder Woman.. Henry Cavill is great as Superman and especially Clark Kent. Jeremy Irons nails it as Alfred. Amy is a great Lois Lane, although she was shoehorned into most of this movie just to get saved by Superman. You might think everyone nailed it in the film, well not exactly. Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor Jr. is bad, like really bad. In the scenes that he was supposed to be menacing in made me laugh harder than I laughed in the Deadpool movie. All of the lines he delivered were corny and made him look more like a fool than he already was with that stupid wig on his head that looked like a mop.

Now the action was phenomenal, Zack Snyder sure does know how to make beautiful fights, Batman's fighting style reminded me a lot of the Arkham games because of how brutal he was, the frustrating part is that I think Batman killed a dozen people, like this incarnation of Batman doesn't go by his moral code anymore. Wonder Woman's soundtrack is the best I've heard in years and she steals the show when she fights the monstrosity called Doomsday, ugh we'll get to that part later, now the sad thing in the beginning is that they kill off Jimmy Olsen and Kal-El practically murders a terrorist while saving Lois, like he literally bashes him through several walls!

Doomsday, not only was his creation rushed and dumb and that he was supposed to be the big surprise of the movie then was shown to us in the second trailer, his appearance was even worse!! He looked like a troll from The Hobbit or The Abomination from The Incredible Hulk.

To the biggest plot twist of the whole film that was directly ripped out of the pages of Dan Jurgens' The Death of Superman. Superman and Doomsday kill each other at the same time, showing the heroism of Superman. To be honest I was shocked they had the balls to do that but at his and Clark Kent's funeral, in the last shot of the movie we see the dirt on the the casket rise revealing superman is in fact alive, I hated that they didn't end it before that like we all knew he's coming back cause you cant have a Justice League without Superman but at least stretch his death a little bit longer.

Another thing that bothered me was that the Justice League members' cameos that were promised, were shown to us through surveillance footage!, like really?!?! that's the best Hollywood writers can do?! The other shoehorned cameo was in the thrilling yet confusing (for non-comic- book fans) nightmare sequence that Bruce Wayne has about an apocalyptic future, when Bruce 'wakes' up from the nightmare we see The Flash traveling back in time and warning Bruce about Superman and how Batman was right about him and that Lois lane is the key to everything and Batman has to find them. The scene was out of place and confusing for the majority, this is probably some sort of Flashpoint Paradox that we'll see in the future.

My finally thoughts about this film is that it could've have been better, hopefully the R-Rated three hours edition will be better. This movie had the same flaws as Avengers: Age of Ultron were in that movie it's main aim was to set up future MCU projects and in this case it tried to build up the future of the DC Cinematic Universe and introduce the Justice League, this film focused on the Dawn of Justice (League) more than it did on Batman v Superman.

title: Cautiously Optimistic for the franchise's future
review:
BvS is a mediocre thunder match that failed to meet the audience's expectations. Snyder; while without a doubt executes the action sequences, came up empty when attempting to connect us emotionally to the characters. 151 minutes of run time was a bit long in the tooth as well. As the audience we open up to a spectacular sequence seen through the eyes of Bruce Wayne (I won't lie, if the whole movie was shot with that kind of pace, I may have said it was the best movie I have watched). Then we go through a choppy journey that attempts to intertwine the stories of Kent, Wayne and Luthor. As a DC enthusiast, I understand what Snyder is trying to accomplish but he just doesn't have the right tools to make a coherent story line.It isn't until we see Prince, Kent, and Wayne in one room does this story start to come together and make for one hell of a ride out. The last part of our journey is equal to the opening sequence; A fan-boys dream. I could not imagine that confrontation going down any other way except for the use of Doomsday. He may not have been what the audience wanted to see but he was what the audience needed to pave the way for a justice league movie. Don't worry Superman fans, you still have Bizarro, Brainiac and Darkseid.

Pros: Afflecks Batman (dark, ruthless, relentless, a true detective). Introduction of Wonder Women Jeremy Irons as Alfred The glimpses of our new Batcave Snyder's action sequences The dream/vision shoots

Cons: Run time Choppy story line Post-Production editing Utilization of Doomsday (he would have been a great villain for a standalone Superman film)

On the fence: Eisenberg as Luthor. Unique and Interesting take. Would have made a much better Jervis Tetch. At times his giddy laugh reminded me of Rumplestiltskin from the hit TV show; Once Upon a Time.

DC Universe future outlook: Caution. Warner Brothers will certainly make their pockets heavier with this movie but will the conclusion of this film be enough to draw the same amount of attention towards future films, especially knowing Snyder is on the helm for Justice League. All eyes will certainly be on Suicide Squad to help alleviate the fans disappoint of this chapter. I am optimistic about Gadot's standalone film, but outside of the trinity, does DC have enough support behind stand alone films such as Aquaman and Flash. While they are great characters, I do not know if they have enough star power to push them to box office success. There is a reason why we have only had Warner's endorse Batman and Superman time and time again.

title: Like a graphic novel on film!
review:
Like a graphic novel on film! You could tell they were struggling to fit all the story arcs which heavily influences the movie. But the performances were good, the JLA teasers were well woven in and the story was twisted and interesting.

Batfleck is probably the best comic book portrayal of Bruce Wayne/Batman so far. Gal Gadot wasn't a terrible Wonder Women (although someone with Ronda Rousy's physique would have been more believable as an amazon warrior, but then again I am prejudiced :D), and Herny Cavil is the Superman!

What sweetened the deal for me is that they referenced seamlessly almost all major cookbook plots and visual styles (death of Superman, "Death in the Family", Flash's time travel arc, Frank Miller's contribution, etc.). The movie truly pays homage to the comics. Pure nerd cocaine!

!!!Spoiler alert!!!

And, the mother of all Easter-eggs, Darkseid!! We we're shown para-demons and the omega symbol! Lex rambles on about a great presence coming! Who else could it be?!

!!!End of spoiler!!!

Overall, I don't think the hate for this movie is well justified. Sorry, but The Avengers 2 suffered from the same issues as this movie does - too much happening, 2-3 different set-ups for different movies, as well as many characters and not enough time. Avengers 2 was campy and fun, but there wasn't enough time to feel emotionally invested in the new characters, not to mention the repetitive doomsday plot.. Yet, people lash out against this movie more? Why?

This, too, is a comic-book movie and as such it's like watching the action on paper, taking shape on the screen. BvS doesn't deserve such negative reactions.

title: In my opinion the critics are off the mark..I LOVE BVS...Here is why:
review:
Admittedly I have been a fan of DC Comics for nearly 40 years so..you might think i'm biased but i'm not..in that I don't think DC walks on water. In fact...I thought Man Of Steel was actually one of the top 5 worst Superhero films I had ever seen. I am shocked however, to see how critics are panning Dawn Of Justice so much. I'll give minor spoilers at the end of this review to the two flaws I found with this excellent film. However..let me start spoiler free:

First..it needs to be said that Ben Affleck is probably the best live action Bruce Wayne we have ever had. When Affleck was first announced, I, like so many others had serious doubts..but I was very wrong. He turns in a performance worthy of the best Batman comics in history. I won't get into comparing him to past actors to have played the role, or this review will end up being far too long. I'll just say..if you have read any Batman Comics..not just the Frank Miller story that the film seems loosely based on...Ben Affleck will make you very proud.

The returning cast from Man Of Steel give more of the same. Henry Cavill in conjunction with Zack Snyder seem to feel the need to make Superman as dark as Batman...a choice I will never understand but..Cavill does however have a few pitch perfect scenes that I will briefly address in spoilers later.

Jeremy Irons is great as Alfred, and I hope his role is expanded in future movies. Gal Gadot is absolutely perfect as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. A character that has never been on the big screen in her 75 year Life..is again done proud. Gal is beautiful, classy, and tough..she will do amazing things in her solo film!

Another performance I found myself shocked to love was Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. This seemed liked terrible casting to me but...somehow it ended up working..really well. At some points this version of Lex can be downright scary. Which I much prefer to the campy criminal we saw with Gene Hackman or Kevin Spacey. Just wait until you see exactly how deranged this Lex can be! And by the way..just hearing a live action Batman talk about Lex or Metropolis...will have a true fan giddy with excitement! In summary before spoilers...Don't let critics sway you...SEE THE FILM...I'm sure you'll be glad you did!

Now...below are spoilers..regarding the best and worst parts of the film. If you haven't yet seen it..you have been warned:

There were just two flaws I found with the film...both of which were not the fault of the actors. One was a ridiculous dream sequence in the middle of the film..that has been eluded to in the trailers involving Batman..in the desert..shooting people. It is so misplaced and silly..that I have absolutely no idea why it is there. Batman using guns to kill..just looks ridiculous. Thankfully the scene is short and only a dream. The good part of it is..that it leads into the first of two cameos by The Flash...and it sets up who the Justice League Villain might be. Omega Symbol anyone???? The other flaw is that the final battle..no not the actual Batman/Superman fight..but the OTHER Fight is far too long. That was one of the biggest problems Snyder had with MOS...the final fight dragged on forever! Other than those two things the film is fabulous.

As I said earlier..Cavill who plays The Man From Uncle way better than he plays Superman has two standout scenes...where he gives Superman the sympathetic side he should have. The first is...a beautiful scene where he sees a vision of his dead earth father Jonathan Kent, while he is in the arctic. Cavill and Kevin Costners interplay was the only bright spot of MOS..and it is again on display here. The other great Superman scene is when he says two key words at the end of his fight with Batman..."Save Martha"! Those two words change everything between the two icons....and they give this version of Superman one of his best moments over 2 films! Again...see the film and judge for yourself but..I loved it!! I wish Zack Snyder didn't feel the need to be quite so artsy..with comic book heroes..and I hope he will be less so with JLA but it doesn't change all the good in the film..that makes it worth it!

This is the true Dawn of Justice!!

title: The Most Philosophical Superhero Film Yet
review:
This is not a fun film. Nor is it funny. Nor is it meant to be either. Instead of taking the punches-and-punchlines Marvel approach, it opts for suspense and psychodrama. But it's still a superhero film, so it delivers on its promise of large- scale action, blockbuster spectacles, memorable dialogue, and villainous twists, despite a predictable plot overall and some inconsistencies.

But more importantly for a good narrative, it develops complex character psychologies and asks questions. It explores where power lies, and how the powerless try to handle it. Each character wields a unique power over the others, and there's no easy answer to which is the most righteous or corrupt. This is the most philosophical superhero film yet.

That said, if you don't want to think about that topic, you won't like it. If you expect it to stick to the comics, you won't like it. If you want a Justice League movie, you won't like it.

But the real flaw is how it handles women. They're mostly ignored or in need of rescue. Even when they save their male rescuers in return, it just feels like the writers covering their tracks. She and Wonder Woman have very little depth.

7.5 / 10

title: A new style of Superhero movies. Enjoyable to those who understand comic-book logic, and want the full world in one.
review:
Batman v Superman Dawn of Justice: It was like watching how you would piece together a comic book scene in your head. At times it was WOW, and then at parts I was like REALLY you did that? It was very Watchmen-y, which depending on your taste or film view 50/50. I thought the introduction of the heroes was unique, I also thought Lex is a absolute psycho in this movie, like Joker level (so what's Leto's Joker gonna be huh?) which depending on your taste is 50/50. I prefer Man of Steel, but I REALLY did enjoy this, but I can understand people not liking this; critics, I still think where overreacting. I think if you understand comic book logic -again depending on your taste-, Greek mythology, god to alien theory and my favorite 'the understanding of the human spectacle and psyche of politics and hope' then you'll enjoy this. The editing will throw you a bit, but again image that bubble you get in a panel of a comic, then picture that into the film, then you'll get it. By the by they're are so many references in that film it is insane, even some unusual ones. But there are two heavily inspired ones sewn into the story. Overall I'll probably be told it was garbage but I liked its difference from what we are used to, e.g. not just a straight line. Overall, its just Dawn of Justice, not so much Batman v Superman.

Go see it for yourself, that's all you can do with this movie. Its really unique that you HAVE to see it to get YOUR OWN view of this.

title: WOW...What a movie, certainly was not expecting that.
review:
Batman Vs Superman: Dawn of Justice, the birth of the Justice League. This is it, DC is finally coming to the party to show Marvel that there is a new man in town.

How wrong can one be, Batman Vs Superman is a total dud, the only reason I am giving is 4/10 is because I have seen worse, a lot worse. To even call it Batman Vs Superman in my opinion is a little misleading. So I can see that everyone has written their reviews of the movie, however I am going to jump straight to the point and ask the question everyone will be asking in a few weeks time "Who is fault is for creating such a poor movie?".

For me hands down Zack Snyder, I would have thought WB would have gone for another director after Man of Steel, but no they stuck with him. I have never been a fan of Zack's movies, average at best (apart from 300...part 1 that is, part 2 is one of those movies that come into the a lot worse than this movie bracket).

The movie has no sense of direction, there was nothing any actors could do to save this movie. The movie spent to much time trying to clever when it didn't need to be. I almost got the impression Zack was trying to compete with Chris Nolan and his Dark Knight Trilogy. For me it fails in every way.

Finally according to IMDb the estimated budget for the movie was $250,000,000, WHAT????? What on earth was that kind of money spent on exactly? If your a fan of Batman and Superman then stick to Chris Nolan's trilogy for the Dark Knight and the Superman movies from the 80's as they were much better.

PS: Wonder Woman, Why put here in the movie if she is to serve no purpose.

title: From the comics to the screen!
review:
After 3 years of waiting, I finally got to see this movie and it did not let me down.

Zack Snyder really delivers the pages of a DC comic book onto the big screen. The story was good, the characters were great and the set up for the JLA was perfect. The film is a true spectacle.

Don't read too many negative reviews from the critics. This is a Snyder film so if you're you've seen Man of Steel, you know this film won't be the DCEU version of the Avengers so don't walk into the cinema thinking that it will be.

Snyder has done something completely different to what's out there at the moment and I fully embrace it. I can't wait for JLA in 2017 and all of the stand alone movies we have to come.

Go see it guys, I highly recommend you do.

title: Not that great...
review:
While it doesn't deserve the hate it's getting from the critics, BvS isn't quite a great movie either. Too much talking and very little action. Snyder and Goyer are to blame certainly. We shouldn't compare this to any Marvel movie to date, because it tries to be different, but tries too hard, and it fails to deliver. While i'ts certainly an improvement over Man of Steel, it's not nearly as good nor entertaining as The Dark Knight, The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy and many other examples of GOOD superhero movies.

I have to say I enjoyed Ben Affleck, Jeremy Irons, Forrest Whitacker and Gal Gadot performances, but I practically hated everything else. Bad pacing, weak script, too much talking, little action, no humour, and many other things made this movie more like a chore to me, and the editing doesn't help. It may be good enough for some DC fans, but I'll keep waiting for a decent DCEU movie.

title: We need Real Story
review:
This is an open letter to - Director - Zack Snyder, Writers - Chris Terrio, David D. Goyer and DC Entertainment.

Dismayed is the word, I use to describe the story. Why I and many others will feel betrayed is because we love the Superhero's. We want the good to eventually win over the evil. Now, the question is which evil. Well, story after story, we find that the our beloved Superhero's (Batman, Superman and so on) are fighting an unknown evil from an alien planet or an evil made from Kryptonian Technology.

My suggestion, in the current scenario is that don't go to an alien world to create a superficial evil. The evil is not only in Metropolis and Gotham. The evil at the moment is real and staring right in our eyes. So who is that evil? To build a good story, the director and writers have to connect with the Audience. The current world existing in front of us is throwing known evil. The evil at the moment is the attackers of Brussels, the evil at the moment are the Boko Haram extremists who burnt alive more than 80 kids, the evil at the moment are the self-proclaimed vigilantes in a village in India, who lynched a 50 year man merely on rumors and the evil at the moment is the deadly dangerous ISIS. As the senator in the movie puts across very nicely - "The world has been so caught up with what he (Superman) can do that no one has asked what he should do" Now, why the audience or common man has to be depended on fake Superheros. The answer was in the movie itself when Lois Lane tells Superman touching the "S" shield on the chest - "This means something. It's all some people have, it's all that gives them hope". For millions of Superhero fans, this presents a Hope. A hope that, one day at Dawn, Justice will be delivered.

title: The Perfect Superhero Flick
review:
There's no need to put on a writer's hat when reviewing this film. Everything about it makes you want to speak so naturally. Big words can only get in the way here. So for the sake of summarising this movie, we'll use a small word: EPIC!

Everything about this film made me fall in love with DC all over again. The merger of so many of DC's animated story lines, the production value, the performances (Henry Cavill - broke my heart, good sir), the depiction of humanity for each hero and lastly, a villain who has no moral compass, no inner turmoil, no boundaries. (The characteristics you want in a mere mortal taking on the divine).

So many doors have been opened by this film. From a studio perspective, that's great news. From an audience perspective, even better. The only unhappy party is a certain overall-wearing mouse.

BvS was never going to open to mass positive reviews because it isn't as colourful or as childish as other hero flicks. It presents a dark world with sinister intentions that don't limit villains to those who are developing dangerous weaponry or are after mythical power gems. Rather, each character has their own objective that sticks true - everything else that pops up is just incidental in the overall scheme.

See it. Then see it again. Grab some more popcorn. Take a potty break. Then re-take your seat for another session. Mr Snyder - well done. 10/10.

title: Honest Feedback From Someone Who Loved It, But Admits It Has Flaws
review:
I just saw the film and I have to say, I enjoyed it a lot. But I'll be a grownup about it and admit that it has flaws. What film doesn't? You want my honest opinion on how to actually enjoy this film? - you have to treat it like you're reading a comic. Don't do what everyone always does and make such a big deal about how the film has to be some kind of ultimate adaptation. Like they have to get everything right or its going to be ruined.

There's thousands of different variations on the Superman/Batman story in the DC universe. They're not all universally beloved. This is no different. What we're seeing is one artists take on the story. If its not something you enjoyed, then thats fine. But don't go around saying its horrible and therefore nobody else should like it either. That's just childish. Its silly how some people will react to a movie like they've been cheated out of something they were owed.

I enjoyed this film a lot. It had plenty of "man, that was awesome" moments. Some parts were definitely rushed and could have been developed more instead of shoehorning in other story aspects. But rather than complain about its shortcomings I always tend to focus on the elements that I like.

Ben Affleck is phenomenal, both as Bruce Wayne and as Batman. The most brutal Batman ever put to screen. A Batman that I think a lot of people have been waiting to see.

Jeremy Irons is amazing as Alfred. Very refreshing to see a take on the character that is as involved in Batman's exploits as Bruce is.

Wonder Woman was only briefly on screen, but her scenes were enjoyable. I think her presence in this film is going to leave a lot of people wanting more of her. Perhaps not the best way to introduce a character to a film, but I think now that people have had a taste of her it will bode well for her in future films.

Jesse Eisenburg, IMO, was an enjoyable take on the Lex Luthor character. Yes, he was quirky and borderline annoying at times. But overall I preferred the fact that they tried to do something different with the character than previous incarnations. Lex Luthor has always been a character driven by greed and selfishness. This film seemed to insinuate that he was psychotic and driven by his inner turmoil.

Superman probably could have been developed more. People rip on the fact that its such a dark story, despite being about Superman. But I'm alright with it. Its something different. I would have liked to see more emotion out of Henry Cavill.

I'm giving the film a 9/10. Not because its a great film, but because I enjoyed it. And the rule of thumb is that a film doesn't have to be great, by filmmaking standards, to be enjoyable. IMO the critics are being too harsh with this film. If I were to rate it with the mindset of a film critic, I'd say it deserves a 6/10.

Please don't write this film off entirely just because of negative reviews. There are plenty of elements to be enjoyed.

title: Zack Snyder should consider a career making video games
review:
I really wanted to like this movie. Even though many hated Man of Steel (which I didn't watch), I liked Sucker Punch and thought Zack Snyder could bring something new and complex to the Justice League. I heard beforehand that this film was panned by critics and chose to dismiss them as Marvel fanboys, but I now see that I was very wrong. I love the DC heroes and was stoked to see this but over the course of the film, my optimism faded to disappointment and disbelief at how bad it was. There were a lot of problems but my biggest gripes were 1.) Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Lex Luthor, 2.) The overuse of the slow motion effect, 3.) pointless dream sequences, and worst of all 4.) Lois Lane.

Lex Luthor is supposed to be a charismatic, egotistical, genius-level intellect, but in this film, he comes across as a mentally-troubled savant who's more of an annoyance to our heroes than a serious threat. If Superman and Batman weren't so distracted with defeating one another, Luthor would be a lame duck. For me, he didn't come across as a villain, but someone to pity instead. I didn't like the direction Snyder took with a deranged Lex Luthor. It was like watching a bad impersonation of the Joker instead. The real Lex Luthor is a villain that can match Superman's brawn with intellect alone.

Next up is the ridiculous amount of slow motion shots of this film and the lazy action scenes. I know that Snyder relies on slow motion quite a bit in his films and it's something I like to see in moderation. He overdoes it here. We see pearls falling in slow motion five or six times in a row, Superman's figure in the distance slowly descending, Bruce falling into a trapdoor in the woods, and many other small details that bog down the pace.

The action scenes were pretty mediocre for a superhero movie. The only standout fight scene was Batman when rescuing Martha Kent. The other scenes were for the most part machine-guns buzzing non-stop, Michael Bay level explosions, or fist fights that would have looked fantastic if they weren't all in the dark. Seriously, all the fights are during the night time amid rain and lightning so you can hardly see a thing. It's as if the producers are trying to mask technical flaws as much as they can.

The dream sequences shouldn't be in this movie. They felt out of place and drawn out. They'd be good as deleted scenes though.

Finally, Lois Lane was banal in this movie. Snyder just fell back on the old damsel in distress trope. No matter where she is, this purportedly capable journalist needs rescuing no matter how simple the task at hand is. She can't even recover a javelin from the bottom of a pool without drowning. She meets Luthor on the top of a building, not even taking care to not get pushed off. He comes up behind her and she just kind of waits for him to do it. From this movie, you get the sense that Lois will always be a burden to Clark.

There were some bright spots throughout like Wonderwoman, Holly Hunter as Senator Finch, and Jeremy Irons as Alfred, but overall this movie was too serious, colorless, and lacked subtlety and substance. People complain about Marvel movies being campy, but as I was watching Ben Affleck's stoic face delivering lines in monotone, I realized camp was exactly what I wanted at that moment.

title: Could have been so much better
review:
I'm torn with this movie, I really am. I love it and I hate it, I've never been more frustrated about a movie than I am about this one. I think it'll be easier for this review if I just separate what I liked and didn't like.

Liked:

Affleck as Batman - he was fantastic, Batman is so much darker here and brutal and it worked for the movie. He was the best thing about this movie in my opinion.

Wonder Woman - She was great but I wish she had more development and screen time, having said that, I don't think she was really necessary in the movie.

Superman - Henry Cavill does a great job as Superman but the big problem is that the script doesn't allow him to really showcase it properly.

Action sequences - Synder knows how to film action, all of that is great.

Didn't like:

Lex Luthor - I didn't like what they did with the character and even if this is what they wanted to go with, he was miscast in my opinion.

Lack of character development - we never really get a sense of why anyone (other than Batman) is doing what they're doing, even then, Batman sometimes comes across as a moron.

Cameos - I didn't care for them to be honest, they felt forced.

Batman & Superman's relationship - I like it better when these guys are friends but this is called Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice so it sells itself as a versus movie only that's really just a small part of the movie, there's so many stories overlapping but never connecting cohesively which brings me to my next issue...

Pacing - this movie is kinda all over the place, it doesn't give you time to get invested, there are potentially great moments right there but we never get enough time to delve into it because the movie wants to achieve so much. It's too much, too soon.

Overall opinion:

I was entertained but heavily disappointed at the same time. It's very hard for me to rate this movie, I wanted to give it a 10/10 before watching it but after the first viewing I gave it an 8/10, after a second viewing I gave it a 6/10. I wanted to love this movie but I didn't. Now I'm finding myself somewhere in the middle, so I'm going to settle with a 7/10. There's great stuff in the movie, it's just mixed with a lot of unnecessary stuff. I wish the movie was more focused, I still enjoyed it but I think we deserved so much better.

title: It's supposed to be a comic book movie people !! Not Shakespeare! I enjoyed it.
review: Here is the bottom line of Dawn of Justice...It's the start of the Justice League in one of many alternate realities. Just go with it. Is it absolutely perfect; what is these days? Zach Snyder assumes (just like J.J Abrams in the Star Trek reboot) that you know the basic back story of the characters. But like in Trek, this is a slightly different reality. The story moves at a comic book pace with comic book twists. Is it Hamlet, The Godfather or Pride and Prejudice? No! Nor should it be judge as such. It's a comic book movie about comic book characters for crying out loud! So why these critics are whining so much beats the hell out of me. The same thing goes for the purist comic book haters. It's not a retro issue of D.C.! It is SUPPOSED TO BE DIFFERENT. GET OVER IT!! It is not an easy thing to introduce three of the strongest, most well known, characters of the Justice League, in a couple of hours and have everyone absolutely love it. JUST GO SEE IT with same open mindedness that you would have when you were introduced to the characters. You know, back before we were all turned into whiny cynics. The effects do the characters and the story justice and I applaud Zach Snyder and all of the cast (Yes, that means Ben too) for their efforts and my wife and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

title: Another DC film which shows Marvel does it better
review:
This commits the same sin as Iron Man 2 and Star Wars 1: for some reason the film-makers think we want to see congressional hearings and lots of talk, talk, talk. It's at least 45 minutes longer than it needs to be thanks to ponderous conversations and slow motion shots accompanied by swelling orchestral soundtracks. The Superman = God metaphor is belaboured and the plot has far too many "What the?" moments.

I saw this with my wife (who loved Man of Steel) and she was looking at her watch throughout. I couldn't blame her. The worst sin is that we really didn't care about the characters. *SPOILERS* I should not be thinking "Lex Luthor has a point." Batman and Superman are dangerous. Batman straight up murders people. With guns! He must have gotten over childhood trauma as his trademark code against killing is nowhere in evidence. I thought, okay, that was just a dream sequence, but they he later pulls out the heavy artillery and kills goons with their own weaponry. Why doesn't he just carry a sidearm? The prophetic dreams are obvious tie-ins to a sequel as well as clues here and there (a giant Omega symbol on the ground alluding to Darkseid for example), but there is no point setting up a sequel unless the current movie inspires viewers to see it.

title: Batman v Superman: A brilliant dawn of the DCEU
review:
I know I have not been the only one waiting for this movie, the hype was huge and that had me nervous. I was also afraid because hype tends to come hand to hand with disappointment; however, BvS is not a disappointment at all. In fact, BvS not only lived to my hype but also gave me more of what I was expecting.

BvS has most of the usual stuff that superhero movies have been giving us for some years: kind-hearted super beings that have to fight to save the world while dealing with some personal, or sometimes, moral issues. BvS takes all of this and takes it to another level. In the film Batman and Superman are kind-hearted but for them it is hard to be that way, it does not matter how hard their convictions drive them to be rightful and strong the world is always trying to bring them down and it is succeeding in doing so; in the DCEU it is never black or while when it comes to be more or when it comes to be a hero, sometimes as a hero their hand get dirty and that hurts them, they are human, they struggle with the same demons as us. Furthermore, all the other characters and citizen of that world deal with that to, they are also afraid of what the world will be, afraid of what they want, of what they happen because they cannot control heroes, but heroes cannot control them either. BvS talks about the consequences of what we do, expect and receive; the movie itself is a chain reaction of continuous decision made by every character, sometimes at the same moment, just like real life.

It is not a perfect movie tough, and some aspect were changed by Zack Snyder but it is a new DCEU and that is OK, sometimes things a little different do not hurt anybody.

There are a lot more thing to chat about this, but I do not wish to spoil so go watch it and to conclude let me say that BvS offer a new perspective of superhero movies, people will lose their time if they try to compare it to other movies or genres. This clash of titans has left a huge mark on cinematic history because from here on out, superhero movies will not be only for the laughs or the entertainment (which is good too) but also will be an opportunity to reflect what we are, what we believe, what our world has become and could become. title: This was a Masterpiece
review:
Batman vs. Superman - A Review of Justice

-minor spoilers-

I love movies. I figure I watch more than average, perhaps a lot more. Might as well do what you love. I'm working to become a costumer for BC Film and I do is reviews. Reviews don't change the movies but maybe you can influence people to go see them. I've looked forward to writing this review more than any other. I've made no secret of my dislike for Zack Snyder's Man of Steel and his darker Superman. I gave this movie a 25% chance of being a good and couldn't wait to rip it apart.

Ben Affleck as Batman never bothered me. The man has been trying to do that role for years. It's certainly how he acted as Daredevil. And the film certain has an all-star cast. As much as I didn't like the darker Superman, Henry Cavill suits the role of Superman. Jeremy Irons looks good as a younger, or rather less ancient, Alfred. Laurence Fishbourne fits as Perry White. I spent a good chunk of the movie trying to remember where I knew Holly Hunt (Senator Finch) and it was from her voice acting in the Incredibles as Elastigirl. We finish up the core cast with Amy Adams as Lois, Jesse Eisenberg as a very charismatic Lex Luthor and the big surprise appearance of Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. Of course, at this point, it was only a surprise if you've been living without Internet access for the last year.

I sat down to watch this movie pretending I had an open mind and realized I just wanted to be right, that it would be terrible. I've argued that if Superman was evil, and since Batman is always darker than Superman, Batman will have to be a downright mass murderer. And then I realized that people need the opportunity to change. If we don't allow that, our first mistake, our first failure, would define the best we could ever be. If I insist that all DC movies be judged by Man of Steel, well they better fold up shop right now. It was at that point, that I was actually able to have an open mind. If I didn't, then I could only be as good as my worst mistake. Maybe that mistake was how angry I was that Zack Snyder had changed Superman.

Halfway through Batman vs. Superman, I still didn't know if it was a good movie or not. It was well filmed. The effects were unbelievable. The acting was superb. They breezed through the prerequisite origins without making it feel like they were taking too long. I really appreciated that. But the big fight had not happened. Would Superman break some more necks in this movie? Would Batman? Or even Wonder Woman? I didn't know, and you won't either until you go see it, because I'm not going to tell you that.

But I am going to tell you why this movie was amazing.

Clark Kent hides his secret identity by dropping a curl of hair over his forehead and wearing glasses. People complain that this would not work. But it does. Henry Cavil was walking around downtown New York in a T-Shirt with a Superman logo on it and no one noticed. Yeah, it works. At the height of the struggle between Batman and Superman, Chris Terrio and/or David S Goyer, the writers, dug out a gem. It was something obvious about these two Superheroes that I did not notice after 32 years of comic collecting. They have something in common. If you want to know what it is, please, go see this movie. And if you know, please don't be mean, don't tell people. And my point is, that is when I knew the movie was fantastic. They took characters I thought I knew and surprised me.

What about all my complaints about civilian casualties I levied at Man of Steel? The problem is that we have CGI and it's really easy to show building blowing up now. It's also really exciting. It's like what happened with the Mortal Kombat fighting video game. They now have "x-ray" attacks where, in full Dr. House or CSI zoom in graphic gore, they show a punch that breaks almost every bone in the opponent's body but they keep fighting afterwards like nothing has happened. I love Mortal Kombat but when it gets that absurd, you've got to call them on it. All I want is an excuse to believe things are realistic. Just throw me a bone. After Man of Steel, the Avengers 2: Age of Ultron came out and the heroes in that movie went to great efforts to save civilians and were willing to stay and die to prevent casualties. And so were Wonder Woman, Batman and Superman.

As a final note, many comics, cartoons and films have borrowed from Frank Miller's epic Graphic Novel, The Dark Knight Returns, which re-defined Batman, and they have never done it justice until now. The only other exception is the animated film version of The Dark Knight Returns which is a direct adaptation and well worth the watching especially as a preparation film for Batman vs. Superman. In watching the credits, I smiled when I saw Frank Miller's credit.

title: So Much Better than the Critics Led Me to Believe
review:
I was extremely excited for this film for about three years now but I have to admit that I was getting a bit nervous when the reviews started dropping. The majority of reviewers really aren't feeling the hype on this one but I'm happy I went ahead and gave the movie a shot. I'll be honest, I straight up love this film. I was taken aback right at first from the weird editing but it actually gave the movie this stream of consciousness feel that made me think William Faulkner was directing my superhero movie. You can definitely tell the influence of a writer like Chris Terrio combined with the particular directing style of Zach Snyder has managed to create something that's obviously divisive but at the same time incredibly unique, especially in the comic book movie genre.

This movie is a sequel to the events depicted in Man of Steel and focuses on Superman (Henry Cavill) trying to find his role in the world while Batman (Ben Affleck) becomes increasingly unhinged after the destruction of Metropolis. Superman is being worshiped by some people as a God while others are accusing him of involving himself in situations that shouldn't concern him. Batman has gone on his own personal mission to find a way to take down Superman since he believes he's responsible for the deaths of people that were close to him in Metropolis. While these two are struggling with their own demons, Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) is manipulating the government and the public to further his own plans.

The acting is absolutely phenomenal in this film. Put any fears you had about Ben Affleck to rest because this is easily one of the best iterations of Batman we've ever had. It's also one of the most unhinged. There is something seriously wrong with this man and we actually see it pretty early on because of Bruce's bizarre dreams. Honestly, this man desperately needs help but he decides to beat the living hell out of criminals instead. Henry Cavill also does an excellent job as Clark Kent. Superman has always been a bit of a goody two shoes and that's true here as well but there's more to it than that. Clark is having a bit of an existential crisis because of all of the criticism he's receiving and it's causing him to question himself and his relationship with humanity. It's an interesting direction to take the character but it works well.

I honestly enjoyed everyone's roles in this movie but I want to mention at least two other people. Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor is easily one of the most divisive aspects of the film but I actually really enjoyed what they decided to do with the character. This guy doesn't seem like much right at first but we soon learn this man is just as unhinged and terrifying as Batman, just in a different kind of way. This man is pure evil and is willing to do anything and kill anyone to get what he wants, all while believing in his own twisted sense of morality. Finally, I need to mention Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. She absolutely nails this role and Diana ends up being one of the best parts of the movie. Her presence just automatically adds more excitement into what's happening and helps to set up the whole subplot of introducing us to the idea of a Justice League.

I have to admit, the tone of this film is incredibly dark. I went in expecting it to be dark and the movie still managed to impress me with how far they were willing to go with it. However, a lot of this dark tone can be directly traced back to the machinations of Luthor and Bruce's deteriorating mental state. I don't want to spoil anything but the way Clark and Bruce eventually find hope once again is done very uniquely and makes for a very different kind of superhero film.

If I had to nitpick I would say that little nods to the other characters that would make up the Justice League feel a bit forced and awkward, but to be perfectly honest I actually kind of enjoyed them. They were so weird but they all had their own little flavor that helped to show that these characters would all bring something different to the tone of the sequel. I'm going to go ahead and give this movie a recommendation simply because I really did come out of the theater loving it. I think it might be one of my favorite superhero films, and this is coming from someone that absolutely adores all of the Marvel movies. I can however see why it didn't work for some people but it's hard to tell how you'll react to it unless you watch it yourself.

title: A little bit too big for its britches
review:
Batman v. Superman is ultimately overblown, overwrought and overstuffed. It's packed tight with a bevy of characters, concepts and themes that never get fully fleshed out, due to some lackluster execution. The editing is quite frenetic, so the story feels very fractured and scattered at times. It jumps from location to location so frequently, it's easy to lose track of just what's going on, even if you're paying attention. On top of that, the plot unnecessarily overcomplicates itself. For example, Lex's plan to get the world to hate Superman involves framing him for an incident in the African desert and then implicating him in a bombing at an opening court hearing (what??).

Some of the issues Man of Steel suffered from still carry over. Superman, as a character, is as shallow as ever. Religious references aside, we don't really learn any more about Clark/Kal-El than we did in the previous installment. Snyder's penchant for rampant CGI destruction is still present, but, at least it mostly takes place at an abandoned harbor this time. If you had a problem with Zod's neck getting snapped, you probably won't be happy to know Batman is twice the killer here that Supes ever was. He wastes guys left and right. Lastly, it's yet another exercise in style over substance for Snyder. Even with tons of subplots and exposition, the film has very little heart.

There are a few homeruns, though. Ben Affleck's Batman is a monster. The type fear and dread the comic book and animated versions of the character inspires definitely resonates with Batfleck. The sequence of him taking out the goons featured in the final trailer is, by far, the film's best sequence when played out in full. Wonder Woman is heroic and charming in her extended cameo. The film's eponymous battle is mostly wicked and Jeremy Irons shines in his bits of screen time. All in all, BVS is an earnest attempt to kickstart the DCCU, but the film lacks the cohesion and focus to pull its many elements together. It's still worth a watch, if only to see DC's big three or the Batman wrecking havoc.

title: A Director's Fanciful Dreams Make for a Muddied & Fractured Batman vs Superman
review:
With so much hype behind one of the most anticipated movies, "Batman v Superman," one would think that it would surely deliver on its promise to entertain the masses. And it does deliver on its promise of entertaining, but it sure as hell confuses you, too. The audience gets introduced to Batman via a semi-flashback from the "Man of Steel." Bruce Wayne watches Superman battle General Zodd in the sky, and he's, let's say that Bruce Wayne is ticked by the destruction that Superman and General Zodd are doing to the city and to the people. And, he has a right to be angry. Well, it is that anger which drives Bruce Wayne to want to get rid of good old Superman. Psst! Bruce plotted for almost two years.

So, fast forward eighteen months or so, and by that time, our Superheroes are in their respective cities, and they conduct life normally; however, they are secretly hating on one another. Where does Superman's dislike of Batman come from you may ask? Superman doesn't care for Batman swinging and flying around town branding (pun intended) his own brand of justice.

Okay that kind of makes for a decent plot, but it really becomes the subplot when it was originally the main plot, and then I think that Lex Luthor has a plan that involves their dislike of one another, but, but he's peddling ammunition and... Uh, one becomes confused, as you can see, I surely did. Our Superheroes have a lot of dream sequences and flashbacks, and they see ghosts, and I think that I saw a unicorn eating purple Twinkies and, and...Whoa! I'm running off on a tangent. Oops! I'm suffering from the Zack Snyder effect-too much stuff on my mind. Hint! Hint!

There's a little too much running off into different story lines or either of the Superheroes thoughts (more Bruce's) which can confuse and probably will confuse the crap out of the viewers! I strongly believe that the dream sequences, or whatever you'd like to call them, could have been omitted. Huh! A lot of material could have been omitted from the movie such as the rehashing of Bruce's parents getting killed. Fans are already familiar with Bruce Wayne's/Batman's story; therefore, the going back down memory lane was pure filler material. Mr. Snyder uses too many moments to add filler material instead of useful material that could propel the storyline or make the movie a bit shorter. There are a few things wrong with the movie, but there are a few things right with it. I can't think of them right now, but believe me, there are some cool things to watch and enjoy.

Yes! I remember what went right in the film. It was Wonder Woman. Her entrance into the film was ridiculously convoluted. But when she mounted up to kick some a**, she was on it! And the Batmobile was cool. That's all I've got for now.

I am keeping my fingers crossed that the "Justice League" will fare much better than this second installment of "Superfriends." Oh yeah, it's time that Mr. Snyder be relinquished of his directing ability when it comes to anything DC related. He just keeps missing the mark.

title: Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice review
review:
Mild Spoilers:

I am one of those (few) people who actually loved Man of Steel. I thought Zack Snyder's vision for what a Christ like figure walking among us was excellently portrayed. Of course, the movie has it's many flaws, but that never bothered me. Every time I watch it, its positives always outweighed the negatives. That is exactly how I feel with Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice.

First of all, the movies entire title is false advertising. The fight between Batman and Superman goes by so quickly that it leaves you wanting more. You would think that a movie 3 years in the making would give the viewer an incredible physical battle with these titans, but no. Most of the fighting takes place after these two duke it out. The Justice League don't "Dawn" either. 3 of them make an appearance and the other 3 make subtle cameos in a forced set up scene that was placed poorly in the middle of a fight. Speaking of a fight, the last 3rd of this movie was a CGI powerhouse that was fun while it lasted and might have memorable for some, but overall not as "good" as the last 3rd act in Man of Steel. Doomsday was horrible to look at and his new "Dragon Ball Z Energy Shield" power was extremely stupid. This movie was delayed for almost a year and they really couldn't make him look any better?

The Zack Snyder-ism's of slow motion and flashbacks make a return as well, but this time he adds dream sequences, AND hallucinations. Besides one dream sequence that was ripped directly out of one of my favorite DC comics, and the Wayne family murder flashback, these were poorly executed and made little to no sense to the overall story. Speaking of story this movie really couldn't decided what it wanted to be. So many things were going on throughout and it may confuse casual audience members who have never read a DC comic. There are also 3 endings.

Now it may sound like I absolutely hated this movie but I didn't. The truth is besides it's flaws, this movie is DC heaven. It was everything I needed it to be in terms up set up for future films, and had perfect adaptations of some very classic Superman and Batman stories. What stood out the most to me was Bruce Wayne's motivation. I might be biased because I will always be #TeamBatman, but you could really feel for the guy. He is just trying to protect what he cares for most. On a side note, besides actually committing straight up murder for the entire film, Ben Affleck's Batman is the definitive on screen Batman. He is so brutal and menacing that he may end up frightening little children, and that is the Batman we have needed for years to be put on screen. There is a certain shot of Batman in this movie that is just "So Batman" It'll make grown men giddy like a school girl. Fans have been praising Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman when in reality, she barely got any screen time, and it is to soon for her to be judged. Jesse Eisenberg's take on Lex Luthor started off very cartoon-y, but as the film went along I loved him. His motivation was genius and without spoiling anything, how he becomes bald was extremely clever. The returning cast was just fine. Henry Cavill is a great Superman, Amy Adams is a great Lois LaneÂ… etc. This film is made for an IMAX viewing. I recommend seeing it in IMAX first before or instead of seeing it on a regular screen.

Overall this movie was what I needed it to be. Currently it is sitting at a 31% on Rotten Tomatoes and that is not a fair grade to judge it on. This is the movie DC fans have been waiting for since Batman and Superman first shared a comic together. It might not be perfect, but it sure as hell isn't a 31%. My grade for Man of Steel always changes between a 7 and an 8 and I feel this will too with each viewing. For now, I have only seen it once and as I left the theater I was thinking 8, but as I am writing this I am thinking 6.5-7. Whatever the grade I highly recommend you see this film and judge for yourself what you think of it. Either way I promise you will have a good time.

Lastly: Don't let anyone spoil this movie for you. It is full of surprises, Double Lastly: Granny's Peach Tea

title: Too much of anything, good for nothing??
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice: **SPOILER FREE REVIEW** The problem with this movie are multi-fold. On the outset, I was very apprehensive about this hastily planned amalgamation of two superheroes, because DC doesn't have a planned "Cinematic Universe" yet as Marvel has. People just came out of Nolan's Batman trilogy, and for many (esp me) Nolan's Batman was too perfect a creation, that whenever I think of Batman I can only think of him I can only think of a superhero so bent on seeing the good in people, a superhero so steadfast in his ideology of not killing people, we are only used to seeing an Alfred who preaches Bruce on what's right not an Alfred who creates Bruce, weapons for his Bat-suit. All these are jarring aberrations throughout the movie.

This is not a bad movie by any stretch of imagination, its just a badly placed movie. It doesn't have its origin stories in place... Superman had one, this version of Batman didn't. We have no idea who this Batman is, what he stands for, what made him like this.. (We have vague reference about Robin's past and that's about it..) and Wonder Woman although intrigued me, without knowing her, most of the audiences had no idea what she was doing in the movie.. (In comparison to Marvel's first Avengers, by the time it came we all knew who the characters were and what they stand for..)

I like the way the makers thought of showing what's going on inside the mind of the superheroes, the nightmares they face day and day out, but it just not shown right..

The biggest drawback of this movie is one, Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg plays the most immature cringe-worthy villain) and two, Lois Lane, she is that one irritating character that we don't want, yet keeps coming everywhere in the movie.

Plus points are, BGM (Beautiful amalgamation of Batman theme and Superman theme) and camera effects are just beautiful..

Finally I think it's time we peacefully retire, Zack Snyder from this universe. It's not working.. title: A film to transcend its expectations
review:
I'm going to leave this review spoiler free, but let me begin by saying that this movie is replete with emotional and passionate nods to its comic lineage. This being said, if one were not to possess knowledge of certain key comic histories, I can see people feeling indifferent or even indignant of the inclusions that made the film. Quite frankly, Batman vs Superman is a chaos of spectacle and power, emotion and triumph, and with any epic of this scale each moment lost to a viewer can become increasingly risky. But with that out of the way, I'm fresh from the premiere and I need more - this movie is astounding.

The first thirty minutes of the film may be some of the most beautiful and impactful filming I've seen from Snyder. It generates a gravitas for the events that proceed, and serves as an artful mirror to those that would come to witness such horror in life. There is a sense of mortality and rage in the eyes of Ben Affleck, an almost flagrant disregard to the shadows these otherworldly warriors force upon the world, a singular drive of someone that is mindful of their limit - and irreverent to consequence as emotion sets in. In that moment I felt myself looking at decades of a character. An entire life. I would have paid for this movie for these scenes alone, I finally had my Batman.

So why an 8 out of 10? I found parts of the movie charming and fun. The philosophical portions were a bit labored and inconsistent, but they were a vehicle for so much more. If I were a betting man, I'd say its in regards to a specific world of gods, and one very frightening adversary. I always felt that Lex has known so much more than what is truly revealed. That his deliberate choices, much like Batman's meticulously planned fights, have been made through a neurotic call to arms. In the presence of gods mans actions, mans motives, have changed - mans weapon becomes obsession. And in capable hands, that obsession can move mountains.

Aesthetically the movie is a symphony of mediums, a beautiful marriage of a thousand storytellers and artists painting conflict and battle. The music charges with adrenaline, and the action tears through bone. Most of the drama - the remorse of loss, the journey of those that are forced to be strong while bearing such deep and lasting wounds - is delivered well enough throughout the film. But some lines fall flat, the chronology of events are frenetically twisting throughout, and just general small misses plague an otherwise masterful film. Lex's story in particular, in the third arc, is one that is tolerable but distractingly subpar... part of it captures the genius of the character, and another part just seems disgustingly convenient. Needless to say, it's a Macintosh in the hands of Jeff Goldblum.

I'd also like to note that while I loved most of the soundtrack, one important and lengthy scene happened to be accompanied by a woefully grating song. A siren whose song pushes you out, not pulls you in.

In short, the movie doesn't need to be a perfect 10/10 to be stunning and remarkable. For me it is like an heirloom, not nearly as treasured by the world for its richness as it is by me - but priceless for what I experience when I behold it. 8/10, I'll be watching this for the rest of my life.

review:

However, after Batman v Superman and Suicide Squad I'm just about ready to give up on this line of movies, because they (and Suicide Squad in particular) were horrendous.

That said, I don't know who does the casting for the Justice League series, but they must be doing it on a dare and failing miserably at it, from Jared Leto and Viola Davis in Suicide Squad to Jesse Eisenberg and Gal Gadot in Batman v Superman.

Gadot is pretty to look at, but she's a horrible actress. First of all I can barely understand what she says, and when I do the delivery is so wooden and dull it makes Keanu Reeves seem like a master thespian in comparison.

I don't know what part they told Jesse Eisenberg he was playing, but surely it couldn't have been Lex Luthor. Considering the amount of scenery he was chewing, he must have the digestive system of a thousand goats.

The saving grace is Ben Affleck as Batman. He is fantastic in this picture.

The plot is nonsensical and only serves as a 2+ hour set up for gathering the other Pokemon in the Justice League, something which came off as tacked on and contrived.

I have only seen the extended version, but considering how disjointed that felt I can only imagine what a jumbled mess the theatrical version must have been. Just think of what this movie this could have been if they had ditched the obligatory franchise building and focused on telling a contained story. The callback to Man of Steel which explains the animosity between Batman and Superman is excellent and a great starting point. But after that they can't decide whether to tell this story or the beginning of a handful of other stories which will (maybe) pay off in later movies in the franchise.

title: justice is served... somewhat.
review:
Let me start by saying that I am a massive fan of Man of Steel. I think they did something really interesting and memorable with the origin story, emphasising Superman's alien origins, and by giving more prominence and context to Krypton's people and fate, and the military Kryptonian antagonists, they really bring Superman to life as an entity in a universe, rather then the heavily symbolic figurehead he has often been before.

That's not to slam past Superman movies or comics of course, but, for example, making Superman's suit a Kryptonian family suit, rather then something his human family made to symbolise him as a hero, makes it feel so much more appropriate and plausible. I really loved the exchange about the S between Kal and Lois, and I think it gives added meaning and impact to the already iconic outfit.

Of course, seeing how Marvel have brought their universe to life in their expanded MCU film series, it made perfect sense for DC to bring about the burgeoning DCU that they are establishing with these films. The way The Dark Knight Rises ended doesn't leave much room for Bale's Batman, so we get yet another actor and a fresh continuity. I think we're all desensitised to the rampant rebooting that Hollywood has embraced now anyway. Nevertheless, I was apprehensive about Ben Affleck as Batman; he is a vastly talented actor but has a chequered history of roles, and it didn't seem like he could exude the intelligence, intensity, and strength that defines Batman. I was wrong about this; I think Affleck was a terrific Batman, and I look forward to more from him. But on with the rest of the film, I've indulged in enough preamble -

I think dawn of justice doesn't really deserve the hate it gets, but something is missing... a bit of fun and energy. This is perhaps necessary and intended to deliver the tone of the plot; Snyder's films tend to have this kind of sombre reverence; the problem is, this film could surely have benefited from a little more levity and fun.

I don't mean Clooney-Batman fun, of course, but while Affleck's Batman was a compelling, engaging character, he did lack the sass of Bale's, if not the charisma which he had in abundance. Superman, meanwhile, has a lot on his mind following the devastation of Metropolis and the revelation that he is the last of his race after being forced to kill General Zod, but he has also just liberated his new home-world from that grievous threat, found acceptance of his true self on this world - tempered, of course, by the fear of his power that drives the plot of this film, but still, widespread acceptance and even worship of him nevertheless abounds, and is fairly deserved as well, in light of his defence of earth and his respect of his surrogate race in spite of his immense power in comparison to them - and he has a relationship with Lois and a job at the Daily Planet as well. He should be full of vigour, but instead, he is dampened into brooding depression by the cascading contrivances of this film's plot.

it seemed like they tried to inject that fun into the show with eisenberg's luthor, but he just didn't deliver in my opinion. he had a quizzical impishness about him, as he was cast as the bright young entrepreneurial caricature of the modern world's elite trailblazer, but he just coasts on that left-field eisenbergness and doesn't really assume the mantle of a proper Luthor, someone with ambition, confidence and buckets of menace.

It's not his age, he just doesn't fit with the preconception of Luthor, and while that's not necessarily a bad thing, his quirks just come off as odd, rather then memorable and entertaining. Heath Ledger's Joker was a one-of-a-kind performance, but there was a villain with true levity to go with his villainy. His own jaunty aspects complemented and reinforced his actions.

On the plus side, we get a compelling cameo by Wonder Woman, and briefer cameos by other Justice League members, offering hope for the upcoming films - aquaman's often a figure of fun but he seems like a hell of a character here, for example.

As for Doomsday, the fight between him and the heroes is a bit odd, as Wonder Woman and Superman seem as untouchable as he does, while Batman tries to help while avoiding being completely obliterated, before Superman and Doomsday seemingly finish each other. Thus, we get a pretty Snydery ending of gritty moroseness, with the hint at Superman's rise from the grave to bookend it after Luthor's ding ding warning, which just felt uncomfortable, seeming so forcedly kooky.

pros - the reaction of the world to Superman. debate, fear and differing attempts by people to hold him to account for his abilities, or just to take him down; I thought it was also interesting to see him try his best to respect the humans in these attempts, like when he enters congress and gently opens the wooden gate to his stand, and how his initial warning to Batman came off as arrogant.

cons - Their minuscule attempts at humour. Superman and Batman's exchange regarding Wonder woman - nothing wrong with it, but it was a tiny island in a sea of overt seriousness.

kryptonite: there was no mention or appearance of the iconic substance in Man of Steel. MoS attempted to create a new status-quo for the Superman story, and while Kryptonian material and environment did affect its people, it wasn't glowing green.

I think this film has many flaws, but also has it's own qualities, and works as a companion piece in the DCU that's being built. I hope this review adequately explains that and helps you to enjoy the film anew.

title: Like a ten ton hammer
review:
The first half of the movie feels like you have to carry that hammer, though. It is dark, heavy, slow and tedious. The story is cut into many single strands that don't connect and the movie seems to flip through scenes that don't explain much. Nevertheless, camera and scenery are great. The casting is...special. Ben Affleck gives a better Batman than Daredevil, yet I had a hard time accepting his acting. Cavill is a fitting superhuman, yet unexpectedly remote and rather cold. Wonder Woman had a perfect introduction - although Gadot is a bit on the thin side. Luthor is played very well, although I think the actor should have been a bit older, but maybe that was just in canon, don't know. At times it seemed, though, that director and actor tried to compete with the perfect Joker of the last Dark Knight installments, instead of trying to find it's own style.

The last hour or so of the movie is like mentioned hammer coming down on you. Pure world-shattering action. Especially the duel between Batman and Superman did set new standards.

Some dialogues and the rare jokes felt a bit awkward. The roles of mortal sidekicks and friends paled next to the god-like super- heroes. Especially Lois was kind of a setback when it comes to strong modern women - she reminded me of the white girl in the hand of King Kong - totally dependent on Superman. She was good for being thrown of roofs, being used as bait and sorts of that, the rest of her role was cheesy and naive romance. I wonder when superhero movies or comics are going to stop this.

After all a satisfying and entertaining movie, despite the fact that I am everything but a Superman fan - I always found him to be one of the most unimaginative superheroes and a boring character.

I want to see what DC will bring up next year now. Hopefully not again in a 2:31 hour format.

title: Gritty, brooding and atmospheric, though with a few gaping logic holes
review:
I do like this film. Despite the complaints of it being too dark and not enough levity, I disagree. There's no way of truly telling the story of two deeply troubled men without it being really dark.

Batman/Bruce Wayne is probably a sociopath, and Clark Kent has a massive identity crisis. The reality of these two characters would be monstrous and not a particularly jovial story.

All that aside, there are a few things about this film that left me scratching my head.

Early in the film we see a team of mercenaries try to frame Superman for the murder of a warring gang in Africa by shooting them with unique bullets. Clearly anyone with a brain in their head would know that Superman doesn't need bullets to kill anyone, yet it makes it to a government hearing on Capitol Hill.

To me, it really feels like Superman is actually a dimwit throughout the film and has no analytical skills or common sense whatsoever. He is so easily manipulated by Luthor at the third act that he forgets he's a superhuman.

After the wheelchair explodes in the hearing, Superman could very easily have identified the perpetrator and gone after him, pretty much solving all of the issues of the latter part of the film. Instead he goes in a sulk and into exile.

Despite his clear ability to hear that his mother was in distress from afar in Man of Steel, he is blissfully unaware of her kidnap, but is able to come to Lois Lane's rescue after Luthor chucks her off the building.

Lois Lane is a bit stupid too. After being kidnapped and flown in a helicopter to the roof, she blithely walks to the edge of the helipad rather than going to a safer part of the pad. It's not like Luthor was a particularly big guy so she could easily have fended him off.

Despite this murderous streak that is apparent, Superman quickly acquiesces to Luthor's will and goes off to fight Batman rather than standing up to him. He could very easily have "persuaded" Luthor to tell him where to find his mother, or just used some basic detective work, alongside his superhuman senses to locate her. He was willing to kill Zod to protect his mother in MoS...

Then, upon his arrival at the battle ground with Batman, he really doesn't try very hard to explain the situation to Batman. Yes, Batman is spoiling for a fight, but Superman could very easily have stayed further back and used his words. Instead, he gets annoyed and starts punching like a petulant teenager.

Of course, Batman is a bit of a dumbass in this too. Despite being known for his exceptional detective skills and using them to great effect throughout the story, he is unable to deduce that Luthor is behind it all. Or maybe he is but doesn't care? In that case that makes him quite unlikable.

Moreover, the montage of him preparing the kryptonite weaponry is all well and good, but if he really wanted to quickly take down Superman, why not just make the kryptonite spear a projectile? Of course a lot has been said about why the two reconcile. I think it's not executed well in the film, but I get that Batman suddenly remembers his humanity.

Then of course there's the climax of the movie when they kill Doomsday. Again, Superman doesn't think anything through and could easily have killed the monster from any other angle that kept him out of harm's way. Or he could have had Wonder Woman or Batman undertake it. Sigh.

I would be interested to see the director's cut to see if there's more explanation for a lot of these things that has been lost.

Still, despite this, with suspension of disbelief it is a great cinematic spectacle.
