title: There's a good film in here....underneath the rubble
review:
I followed this film throughout its development. I was not a fan of Man of Steel at all, but I had hoped that the filmmakers had learned their lesson and plus, if you add Batman to anything, you have my attention. So it was, with cautious optimism, that I eagerly awaited this film. Then the reviews came out. Oh....

I had planned to see it in theaters, but the bad reviews drove me away. Now that it's out on DVD, I've finally gotten around to seeing it and I must say that it's not as bad as critics make it out to be. In fact, I believe there's a great film hiding in here somewhere, but it was unfortunately smothered by the insistence of setting up other films, some bad editing decisions, unclear motivations and, worst of all, falling back on the Snyder crutch of green screen 'splosions and confusing fights.

First, the good:

1. Ben Affleck was a good Batman. I was seemingly one of the few people who gave him the benefit of the doubt when he was first announced and he delivered an interesting Batman/Bruce Wayne. He is certainly the most authentic looking Batman we've ever seen, but he also finally captures the detective element and the paranoid, possibly crazy element as well. Like most people, I'd be interested in seeing him in a stand alone film.

2. Gal Gadot was good as our first big screen representation of Wonder Woman. There's a grace and mystery there combined with her ability to kick-butt that leaves you wanting more.

3. On a technical level, minus the CGI and score, this film was very interesting. The cinematography was stunning at times and the costumes were amazing. It shows that Snyder is a master of bringing comics to life. Unfortunately, he doesn't know what to do with them once he brings them to life.

4. Finally, I do like that DC is trying to do something different with these films in examining the real-world ramifications and ethics involved.

The negatives:

1. This film is just too overstuffed. The attempts to set up future films bloats this film to the point of boredom. Many of these scenes are simply unnecessary and cutting them could have reduced the run-time by 30-45 minutes, or could have filled in some sorely missing plot points.

2. Lex Luthor's motivation is dubious at best and the lengths at which he is willing to go to so he can accomplish his goals border on self-damaging. Why is he willing to potentially destroy the world to destroy Superman? Why does he hate Superman in the first place? Daddy issues? Jealousy? The genuine fear of powerful beings? All of the above? Possibly! Because all are explored and none make sense.

3. Jessie Eisenberg's performance was just too manic and annoying, and not at all like the cold, smooth and calculating Lex Luthor we know and love.

4. Superman is mopey, depressed, dark and brooding. He is not who Superman should be at all. He is, by far, the weakest and least interesting of our three heroes. There is some attempt at tension and doubt with the world being very suspicious of Superman and he himself wondering if it's all worth it, but in the end, those interesting parts are smothered by all the brooding.

5. The film's editing decisions are questionable as you get the feeling that a lot of potentially important information was left out.

6. The CGI was awful. It was genuinely laughable for a film of this budget. Either get some better CGI, or don't be so over-dependent on CGI in the first place because it was truly unacceptable.

7. The music was awful. This is shocking coming from the great Hans Zimmer, but it was loud, obnoxious, crude and added nothing to the overall film. I guess Hans is burnt-out on all these superhero movies.

8. MARTHA: This makes no sense no matter any way I look at it. It's just a poor decision for what could have a very powerful scene a la "I'm with you to the end of the line" from Captain America: The Winter Soldier.

9. Finally, the final act seems tacked on as if Snyder & Co. had no idea how to finish it, or thought that audiences expected a final battle with lots of BIG 'SPLOSIONS! The resulting battle of Doomsday is a very muddled, confusing, headache inducing mess that hearkens back to the final battle with Man of Steel. The poor CGI, as you can guess, only adds to issues.

So as you can see, not a perfect film by any means. There are tons of issues, but it's not nearly as bad as some critics made it out to be. It certainly superposes Marvel films such as Thor and The Incredible Hulk. The real tragedy is that you CAN see a great film trying to get out, it was just smothered by bad creative choices and studio interference. If you love these characters, definitely give it a look. If not, you may want to give it a pass.

title: Not a Batman movie!
review:
Although my first thought was that the movie is not as bad as I expected it to be, probably the pseudo philosophical parts soothed me a bit, I became more and more disappointed while watching the movie. Zack Snyder seemed to completely have failed to understand the character of Batman Batman is neither stupid nor killing people and it is an insult to his creator to portray him in that way.

title: An honest look of superhero adaptations and then some
review:
Snooze Fest: Of Gods and Superheroes

I have recently adapted a very bad habit of falling asleep inside the movie house. Did I waste my money? Yes, I did. Did I waste my time? Definitely. This may be a consequence of watching too many superhero or CGI-laden special effects movies lately. I'm talking about movies that are supposedly "blockbusters" that came out in the last few months. But alas, what a disappointment.

First stop: Gods of Egypt

A story about the gods of Egypt, much like the gods of Greek Mythology, hoping it would be as interesting as the gods of Olympus. The idea of the gods maybe, but how the gods are being portrayed here was so disappointing. Even the impressive actors in it couldn't save this disaster of a movie. The CGI alone made the special effects too "cartooney" and because of it, the movie in my opinion downgraded into a B-movie. I love Gerard Butler and Jamie Lannister actor as the main characters, but really, did they actually signed up for this? I cried out when Geoffrey Rush portrayed Ra (what a waste of talent), I mean the producers must have obscenely paid these great actors just to star in this blah of a movie. Amidst all the fighting scenes with overloaded CGI special effects made me dizzy, then sleepy and eventually fell asleep. I woke up just before the movie ended when the mortal character became a a ruler in behalf of the good god with one eye to find his true love. Another forgettable popcorn movie that could not even come close to The Mummy's entertainment value (cheesy that movie maybe).

Next stop: Batman V. Superman

For this movie which was directed by Jack Snyder of 300 fame, it a bit disappointing. I love his work in Man of Steel, which in my opinion was the best superhero adaptation in that year. But for this movie, it left a sour taste in my mouth. I did not get it. I was confused convoluted dream sequences that I failed to separate the real from the dream scenes (this is the part where I fell asleep). The movie was like the style in another Jack Snyder flick Watchmen. It had its dark setting and confusing plot, and trying to make it as cerebral as Christopher Nolan's style, which I think only Nolan can pull off. The only saving grace is Gal Gadot playing Wonder Woman. She's a superhero who has been out of the scene for some time now, if some of the audience can still remember or have actually lived during Linda Carter's Wonder Woman days (LOL!). When she helped Batman and Superman fight the ugly alien mutant I actually applauded. She was fierce and Gal Gadot played it to a T. Despite her obvious beauty she was believable as a Superhero. I didn't get the drama between Batman and Superman though and it was just that, pure drama. One would think two screaming women in a girly fight were doing those scenes. And please what's with the pubescent Lex Luthor, really? Him following in the footsteps of Gene Hackman or even Kevin Spacey (despite that cheesy Superman flick a decade ago he was still brilliant). Jesse Eisenberg should have been another character like Lex Luthor's retarded grandson who could not live up to the villainous expectations of his predecessor. Evil he is not, but whiny, insecure with serious psychological fatherly issues he can be (LOL!) I hope that the next installment of the Justice League sequels will be better off than this one. It has its moments but overall it was not outstanding.

Last Stop: Captain America: Civil War

Now this movie should've been a sequel to Avengers, not Capt. America. What with almost all of the superheroes in Avengers present and then some (Antman and a new Spiderman, again, ugh!) It was meant to be a treat to the fans I think, but sadly it was not. Well for one thing there's an attempt to make the superhero theme color-blind with the introduction of Black Panther, a royalty from Africa, (that was cool!) Despite its attempt for political correctness in including an African and female superheroes (despite just being 2 girls among boys) at least they tried. Then due to the many characters and RDJ's star power as Tony Stark, Chris Evans' Capt. America took a back seat. He failed to shine in the movie. As the namesake of the movie title shouldn't be the movie mainly about him? Good thing he's prettier than the girls and has some serious biceps to boot, at least he's swoon-worthy (sigh). Well, if he is to be the leader of the Avengers, I think there's some serious competition there with Ironman, which the producers/director definitely highlighted in the movie (I guess with RDJ's talent fee, you should at least make the most out of him to get your money's worth, LOL!). I must be dense lately with all the Superhero movies because I expected the plot to be good vs. evil. But in this movie (and also in Batman V. Superman) the Superheroes are fighting against each other, Team Capt America vs. Team Ironman (what?!) I got loss there for a minute or two (this is where I fell asleep) with superheroes fighting, showing off their powers and super human abilities, etc. Then, another fight between Capt America and Ironman because the latter is jealous of Bucky as the new BFF of the former (whoa some serious Bromance there, what's going on here? Â…hmmm) Anyways, overall it was a tepid movie, with just enough entertain for the die-hard fans (not one of them I'm afraid).

My last stop should have been Independence Day Resurgence, but since I fell asleep with the entire movie (in a new movie house in a nearby mall with almost empty seats, heaven for a sleep deprived like me), what's the use, right? ('nuf said).

title: Zero Expectations
review:
The combination of pretty decent performances, casting (undecided on Eisenberg still), cinematography and CGI is not enough to salvage such a sloppy, lazy story.

The film lacks any real character development and reveals are awkward and fall flat, and I sometimes wonder how Metropolis or Gotham still even have a population. Adding to that, the story is full of convenient coincidences that make even less sense than Wonder Woman taking a commercial airline flight.

You should go see this film; if not for the cool explosions, then to remind you that while money can certainly help, it can't fix everything.

title: An entertaining and unwieldy mess
review:
What could I possibly say that thousands of people haven't already said? Probably not much, but I'll try. BATMAN V SUPERMAN was one of my most anticipated films this year, although the polarized reaction toward it certainly made me lower my expectations a little bit. One thing I noticed on first viewing was that the pacing was a little off, particularly in the first and last half hours. Early scenes seemed heavily edited, and it took way too long for the different narrative threads to come together. The central conflict, while built up satisfactorily, was almost anticlimactic and resolved way too quickly. To avoid spoilers, I won't divulge what happens afterwards, but it did feel very tacked on, almost an afterthought. Lastly, the action was over-CGI'ed and mind-numbing at times. It looked cool, but lacked heft and believability. Still, one has to admire the scope and ambition of Zack Snyder & Co. It touches upon some interesting philosophical themes, however lightly. It also has some great character moments/development, that build upon what MAN OF STEEL started. Ultimately, I look forward to seeing the story fleshed out more in the Extended Cut where, hopefully, the editing and pacing will be a little better. The only element I hated outright was Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. Lex Luthor in the Christopher Reeve movies was stupid, yes, but Eisenberg's rendition pushes it into extremely annoying territory. As for the score, it was appropriately epic and emotional when it needed to be. My favorite themes were, ironically, Lex's theme, and Wonder Woman's theme. All things considered, I liked the film despite its flaws, but it was undeniably messy and unwieldy.

ULTIMATE EDITION: This is the version I was waiting for. While it doesn't eliminate the flaws inherent in the theatrical cut, it features improved editing/pacing and provides much-needed connective tissue that fleshes out the story and makes it more comprehensible. The majority of the additional 30 minutes were placed before the title fight and expand upon the various investigations by Lois, Clark, and Bruce that lead up to the central brawl. Character motivations were made clearer (particularly Lex) and, more importantly, the narrative was able to breathe a little. I still think that Lex's plan was kind of stupid and ridiculously complex but, thanks to the extended running time, his role was diluted somewhat and made his presence a little more tolerable. There were also some additional shout-outs/fan service/references to the DC Universe, like Steppenwolf and Arkham Asylum. Overall, I still found myself cheering and tearing up at the same places, but this Ultimate Edition is definitely a step up from its theatrical counterpart and is a fuller, more satisfying story.

title: Dawn of Just-Give-It-Another-Chance
review:
I'm going to make this one short. Whether you've seen the theatrical cut or not, check out the uncut. While still imperfect and silly at points (Are you a terrorist, anyone?), the uncut edition does a better job developing the overall plot, namely the desert scenes in context with Luthor's overall scheme, and Bruce Wayne's motivation in relation to Superman's presence and perceived threat to Earth.

Yes, it's still average as far as special effects go and Wonder Woman still lacks screen time. It's (somehow) still rushed at a nearly 3 hour running time, but it is a decided improvement and a better interpretation of what Zack Snyder wanted.

Uncut gets 3 out of 4 stars.

title: Visually excellent, but a steaming mess in most other respects
review:
So I wanted to love Man of Steel. Visually, it was breathtaking, and it was high time, imho, to give superman another go, especially in the wake of Nolan's Batman films.

But I just couldn't get behind the character decisions. I didn't like Lois, I thought pa Kent was well-cast but terribly written, and Clark... I didn't know what to do with the mess that was his character.

So the bar wasn't... super high going into this.

Batman actually surprised me. I thought Affleck did an excellent job and I was significantly more interested in his character than in any of the crap Clark pulled. I super extra appreciated that they didn't give us his origin story as well, after all, everyone knows Batman.

But really and truly, this film, though, again, visually fabulous (seriously, it felt like I was watching the comics), felt like it was written/constructed by someone who knew the character names, and their costumes, and their power sets, but didn't actually have any idea who those characters were. Nor were they interested in finding out.

This was one of the most contradictory portrayals of Superman I've ever seen (and I watched Smallville, all the way through the end, so I know from bad), when it wasn't completely flat, and in an effort, I assume, to set up The Justice League (and compete with the MCU which, hey, is also why this became a 'civil war' movie, despite their being about ten minutes of actual batman V superman conflict, and that completely contrived).... the story was a mess. There was unexplained dream/vision/flashback/time travel crap, and Lex Luthor's motivations are anybody's guess, and the pacing was all over the place... it feels like they wanted to make a couple of different movies here, and didn't have time if they wanted to catch up to Marvel, so everybody picked their favorite bits and slapped them together.

But with no Superman in the next one, I feel like the franchise might turn a corner. As I say, whether or not he's a batman I recognize, Affleck's performance was actually way more decent than I expected, and I am super into the Wonder Woman casting. :)

title: Zack Snyder's R- rated superhero showdown!
review:
Let me just come out and say this, this movie is exclusively for two kinds of people: a) The ones who are well versed with the DC comics and characters, and b) Those who followed the movie's every news with bated breath ever since it's announcement including all the castings, etc.

The reason I point that out because of the experience I garnered while watching the movie multiple times with different people. The first time when I saw the movie, I wasn't able to make up a clear picture of the kind of movie that it really was, but I should admit that my excitement got the better of me and I liked the movie on my first watch. The second time I saw the movie with someone who is just the opposite of the first category of persons that I pointed out earlier and I came out with some interesting observations: 1) The flash cameo, was awesome no doubt, but it made no sense what so ever for a person who doesn't know about him (I'm talking about the one after the batman nightmare sequence). Even the people who knew about flash had trouble recognizing him! And that is a fact! 2) The nightmare sequence, again another cool sequence that just made no sense, so totally out of place for the movie. People felt like they were suddenly watching a totally different movie having aliens and all that, neither did it anyhow substantiated the plot of the movie. It was just there doing nothing except looking "COOL", a word that Snyder loves to use. 3) The Justice League cameos: In the cameos we get introduced with two of the lesser known members of the JLA viz, AQUAMAN & CYBORG. And anyone who doesn't know that Jason Momoa is playing Aquaman or the other hero is Cyborg would be utterly confused and frustrated about what's going on. Seriously! These are only some of the basic problems that I am pointing out, they aren't even the major ones. I was so excited for this movie and for Zack Snyder before it hit the theaters because I thought that this might be his Magnum Opus and he'll finally get the respect and recognition he deserves. Unfortunately it wasn't meant to be so. He is now making the Justice League and i sincerely hope that he nails it, otherwise, Snyder would see the end of his big budget movie making career and would forever be remembered as the guy who took control of the most iconic comic book properties and made a big mess. He won't be easily forgiven by the huge army of fans the DC comic book heroes have!

title: poor script
review: This movie has a poor script. It may be OK if you don't think much while watching the movie. I don't quite understand why superman and batman started hating each other. The fight between superman and batman is stupid. If you were superman and you know you're susceptible to kryptonite, wouldn't you take more precaution after you see your opponent started to use it, like moving the fight elsewhere or removing his weapon? And why did the fight ended when someone mentioned their mothers' name? What if the mothers' name was mentioned before the fight, would they still fight? Jesse Eisenberg as a bad guy is not convincing. He does not have the evil look to portray a villain. Perhaps he could be a Woody Allen imitator. And then there is the gratuitous semi nude scene of Amy Adams. It is not necessary in this type of movie. When I saw that scene I immediately knew there is not much else in the script. And by the way, Amy Adams complexion does not look very good in this movie. She seems sick or something, despite the makeup. I wouldn't pay to watch this movie.

title: Ambition failed
review: I am perhaps 30 minutes into this movie - somewhat early to be making a judgement but I am going to anyway. This is actually the second attempt to watch it with no expectations. I am still totally confused as none of the first scenes make any sense at all. It has the ambition of taking the subject material completely seriously which is a huge mistake. The main characters are superheroes - they cannot be taken as seriously as this film is trying to do. The very premise is flawed as Batman could not take on Superman and be successful. Batman is after all only a man with thousands of cool toys - Superman is, well, Superman - super strong, superfast, invulnerable (kryptonite aside), completely unbeatable. Snyder has made the whole thing far too dark for it to be really enjoyable - too many flaws in the premise. All that said the film looks great and has a quality for that . Affleck and Cavill acquit themselves as well as is possible but I can never see Am Adams as Lois Lane she is far too lightweight. Jesse Eisenberg is not the Lex Luthor we all know, he is much too young for a starter and he seems to inhabit a different sort of film - a lighter touch than this film requires. I always understood that he was supposed to be a contemporary of Superman. A very disappointing, mess of a movie. It has had lots of money thrown at it but that is just not enough.

title: Batman vs Superman, potential spoilers
review:
If you are over 45 you will leave this movie unhappy but for the price of a rental it's worth the money.

First the acting, great! Quality is it's own reward, no problems there. Each actor managed to pull out a specific intense emotion and let you live it all throughout the movie and that is hard to do.

Next, the special effects... sometimes too much is too much. The technology exists where good graphics don't have to look like a computer game, let the actors act. Overall, I liked the total production values of the shots but too many sliding into the camera shots became distracting.

Third, the story... good idea poorly executed. I liked least- the cheap introductions of the future characters... who were never in the movie. Why? The water scene with the spear is a good example, and one of many...I was waiting for one of the afore mentioned new hero's to show up... nothing... even when the music changed direction... nothing. Introduction implies usage. Even a first year script writing student knows how to look beyond one scene to the next and have it weave together. The new Justice League folks would have been better introduced last. It made me wonder if anyone read the entire story in one sitting before production or if anyone who knows the history and tradition of the characters was actually involved in green lighting anything about this film? I liked the best - Superman being the thoughtful guy all across the board and Batman looking like a Trump supporter (before Batman's "Martha" conversion brought him back home and making the world a better place). Very poignant.

Fourth the direction... direction is a lot of work, got it, but so is the paycheck. I expected more, way more, well a super a lot more. I had a hard time following the storytelling and it felt choppy, out of balance, and it made me wonder if more than one person had too much input.

So, would I watch it again? I don't know. But I do know that the next film needs to be better across the board and if the next one can't be marvel-ous... I suggest the next title to be "The Death of the Superman and Batman Franchise for the Next 30 Years."

I have watched Superman and Batman shows for more that 50 years, I was a DC comics kid growing up but this film really pushed my loyalty. Although I'm not in a youngsters demographic and I am just an old guy spouting off...but...I do pay for my kids movie tickets and I think they can see through most movie blunders.

title: Meh, a fun night out
review: I'm gonna wrap this up pretty fast. Zack Snyder is great when it comes to telling a darker story than we are used to. Though the plot aren't as good as man of steel. The whole Martha scene was kind of stupid and that's what you get when you mix a good director with a not so great writer. I'm not throwing shade at the writers for the whole movie, just that scene.That BvS vibe I got at the start left off when they teamed up to fight Doomsday, obviously.That is what brought down the whole movie to the low ratings it now has.For the first time we also get to see a dark and brutal Batman. Beefed up and...fine with using guns?? Okay,with the guns aside we know get to see Batman in the criminals and civilians eyes. In the previous movies we saw him in his own point of view. Heroic, protecting the public and battling supervillains for the greater good. Seeing him now he's kind of scary and a nightmare to some, he's even referred as "The Devil". Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor performance disappointed me. If he played The Riddler that would have been a perfect match. But once again Snyder succeeds with the action. Excellent fight scenes with Batman, all credit goes to the fight coordinator. Overall this movie is a great night out, solid at some points. It pretty much wraps up a 7.0/10

title: My expectations were met, in a "meh" kinda' way
review:
I'd say there was about 60-70% of the movie i could have skipped and not miss much of anything worthwhile. A lot of build-up for a major turn-around in the last part of the movie. Most the of "cool" stuff started happening when I was pondering whether continuing watching had a point so it ended in a both somber and expectant mood.

It was well shot, nothing negative to say there, enjoyed the 21:9 aspect ration on a monitor with that exact ratio in ultra-wide. The audio didn't feel that punchy though, even though i was wearing a good pair of large-diaphragm headphones.

Overall i'd say disappointing as a standalone film.

title: Glaring flaws
review:
Just so we're clear here, I am not a Marvel or DC fanboy (I think I've typed that at least 3 times now... huh). I just like superheroes. And this movie is no different. Issue is, instead of being an actual decent movie, it decides to be many things at once. It tries to be Batman v Superman, but it also tries to be a billion other things that distract from the point and just set up sequels, something that only Marvel movies have been able to do right so far in my eyes. At least when they did it they weren't forced in.

There's a lot of information thrown your way in this movie, making it feel more like an exposition dump than an actual movie. Scenes are very forgettable, and some are so unnecessary I forgot them in less than a week, only to get traumatic flashbacks of them a month later. Remember that scene in the beginning where people get a thing of kryptonite? Or how about that scene where Batman watches a fight? Or maybe that one scene where... you know I forgot what I was gonna say. See? You probably didn't even remember those scenes yourself until I reminded you that they did in fact exist (unless you're a die hard Batman v Superman fan and you've seen the movie a million times). And even then you'll probably forget I said those things exist. Sad world we live in, isn't it?

The setting up for sequels thing isn't good either. When Marvel movies do it, it's either after the credits, or it's integrated into the story very nicely. Like in Guardians of the Galaxy, you have the whole Infinity Stone plot-line integrated quite nicely. And that set up for sequels. Here, they try to be like that, but lose focus and set up 5 or so movies ahead. Something Marvel movies don't try to do. It doesn't work. Instead of building up to something, or doing a twist reveal at the end, it just cuts to something jarring or sequel-y. Like how security footage shows off other members of the Justice League doing unnatural things, such as Aquaman being Aquaman, Flash stopping robbers, and the birth of Cyborg. Again, it doesn't work.

While there is a bunch to hate, it wasn't the worst movie ever. There were parts that were good, such as the action, and some of the comedy was good. But if you ever see this movie, set the bar low. Not to the ground low, just low enough not to expect much.

title: Batman V Superman:"The Bell Can Not Be Unrung!"
review:
Rating: 7.0, Good Movie, But Very Disappointing, I Expected More

*I might be a MARVEL fan boy at heart, but my favourite movies consist of The Dark Knight Trilogy, and given that Director Zack Snyder made me like Superman in 2013's Man Of Steel(7.0) I felt rather disappointed with his 2016's Batman V Superman, Dawn Of Justice. The DC Movie has its peaks and trenches throughout the movie's characters, plot and themes however lacks the enjoyment of that a super hero movie usually delivers. I would advice that the 3 hour edition is much more improved however.

* Characters - Batman: Th Dark Knight movies are the best Batman films, but Ben Affleck who I know everyone hates is now the Batman. He has the look of Bruce Wayne and the Fighting Style like an Arkham game, I still love Christian Bale, but Bat-fleck Forever! Except for those guns... thats a non no...

* Superman: Henry Cavill however is the Superman and the heart of this story, his acting was rather well providing emotion throughout the movie.

* Lex Luthor: While Jessie Eisenberg's Luthor was not the Lex is knew, he was the only character to keep my engaged in the Movie, his quotes and plans were indeed clever and cunning until his bells in the end... I like Jessie Eisenberg I just don't like the way he played Lex.

* Other Characters: Snyder ruined Doomsday with poor design and screen time,Wonder Woman checked her email and fought a monster, Louis Lane was just kind of there and as for Alfred... OK but I miss Michael Caine.

* The movies plot is understandable, establishing that "people fear what they don't understand" however as it drags on with the political side of it the audience begins to feel lost and bored with little entertainment. Batman's motives change from justice to revenge and overallit begins to feel like a trailer for the Justice League. Even the fight was rather average. It was like slow punch, badass quote, slow kick, badass quote?

*Overall this movie had high hopes which has now given me lower expectations for Suicide Squad. The movie has emotion and darkness but no enjoyment which the Dark Knight ticks off. I just wish Christopher Nolan made his own DC Universe and that given there was three years between this and Man Of Steel they could have pumped out a Batman movie? MARVEL is not perfect, they lack the darkness and emotion that DC executes well. However MARVEL no how to set up their universe and make it more enjoyable. I don't want DC to be MARVEL, I want both COMIC Companies to follow in each others strengths. Its decent, just not amazing.

title: Zach doesn't have your back this time
review:
I feel like I'm one of the few people who actually likes Zach Synder. Yeah his movies have the depth of a puddle, but his sepia- looking visuals combined with (usually) very artistic CGI make for movies that are at least enjoyable to your eyeballs. But yeah man, I can't defend you on this one bud. I didn't even have really any expectations for this movie, and you still managed to disappoint me somehow.

This movie is book ended by sh!t. The opening voice over monologue is probably the worst movie speech I've ever heard. It's pretentious. It has nothing to do with the plot. Its.Just.Stupid! The ending is just as bad. Spoilers: Super Man dies!!!! Jk of course he isn't really dead how would we finance the sequels without trailers of superman and Ben Affleck homo erotically pushing each other around? Instead batman decides in a single scene that everything the movie has built so far about his complete hatred for superman has been completely irrelevant because superman yells out "Martha" like some BDSM masochistic safe word. Yeah talk about a big fvck you to any audience members still invested in this movie's characters. Look I could go on and on about the sh!ttacular plot. I could complain about how useless Lois Lane (or however it's spelled) is in just about every situation. Or how it's retarded for batman to put a tracking device on a car only to immediately get in his CGI death car and mow everyone down in his way (including an innocent oil tanker truck driver) even though that's the same exact reason he hates superman. I could say it's useless for Lex Facebook to carefully and precisely and slowly cut off General Zod's fingerprints when he could just cut off his whole hand. I'm not going to say any of that though, I'll just type it on an online message board instead. Look the plot and structure of this movie is terrible. There are no less than four dream/hallucination sequences and none of them make any fvcking sense whatsoever: in one the flash, a character who is never even introduced, goes back in time to communicate to batman in batman's dream (cause that's not retarded), in another batman sees his parents grave bleeding black goo only to have the Faun from Pan's Labyrinth jump out and kill him. Look overall the dream sequences are probably my favorite parts of the movie ( in one batman has a tracking shot fight scene against Nazi superman soldiers under a recent nuclear explosion.) but overall they make no sense and have no effect on the plot at all. They could have been taken out and the story would have remained the same: fvcking stupid.

Now the CGI in this movie is bad. Really bad. I mean the bat car looks like it was pulled out of a 1995 hot wheels video game made for kids whose parents didn't love them enough to play hide and go seek like jimmy's parents would always do (no I'm not bitter). Doomsday looks great. Everything else... not so much.

Finally the editing in this movie is pitiful. There's no tension (except for one scene that we don't understand why it's intense until a briefcase explodes), no establishing shots to allow us to take in the scenery or even know wtf is happening. Sure this is just like Zach's first attempt into the superhero genre, watchmen, but I actually like watchmen so you're not allowed to criticize it.

Overall: 5 or a 5.5/10. Why you do dis Zach. I love you bb pls.

review:

title: Uh...
review:
Oh boy, where to start?

I believe that two additional movies that needed to happen before BvS took place to make this story a little bit more... whole. Like a Wonder Woman movie and their own Batman movie (WITHOUT THE ORIGIN PART). That way we have a better idea as to why Wonder Woman is where she (because that reason she gave in the film was seriously weak. Needless to say I was very disappointed.) and a better reason for Batman to be more distasteful of Superman than this movie gave him permission to be.

I am fully aware that there will be a solo movie for Batman and Wonder Woman in the future, but I feel like it's a little late because the damage is done.

It gave me a disorienting feeling with each ticking minutes and it also gave me more questions than answers. Questions like, what was Lex Luthor's motives? What happen to Batman's great detective skills? What happen to Robin? (I know what happens, but it's Hollywood. Come on...) Why did it end the way it did? Did they seriously kill any chance of a friendship between these two heroes? THE FRIENDSHIP THAT ALMOST NEVER DIES!?! And lastly this: I am partially deaf, so why was I able to hear that 'whrrr' sound of something... dynamite and Superman wasn't?

But the last straw for me was Wonder Woman. I was so happy when DC finally cast a female superhero, and not an anti-hero. (Catwoman is an anti-hero.) However I was disappointed by not only the amount of screen time WW had, but WHO played her. I have NO problems with Gal Gadot, but I did not feel the wonder from her. I'm seriously tired of seeing someone small playing a powerhouse character, because that's what WW is. Someone who can bench-press her male counterparts and not break a sweat. A warrior princess from Themyscira who takes pride in forming her physic to match her strength. However I can say that Gal's portrayal of her is good, so I can give her that. At the same time, I also believe that she would have played roll of Zatanna (IF they ever give her any screen time) even better than WW. (Food for though Snyder...)

TL;DR: This movie has a lot of plot-holes, more questions than answers, and Wonder Woman isn't exactly... wonder. If you plan on watching this movie, set a low standard for it. Trust me, you won't be disappointed. And yes, Ben Affleck did a good job as Batman, and he was a better Bruce Wayne then his predecessors. So look forward to that at least. And lastly... try not too laugh too hard at the beginning. I know that was a horrible thing of me to say, but I could not take the film seriously after the first five minutes.

title: The film vs The preconceived negative opinion
review:
First of all I am a comic fan, I am a DC fan and I am a Marvel fan, but most importantly I am a film fan more than anything.

Now we've all heard and seen all the hatred and animosity surrounding this film and Zack Snyder. The reason why this exists is not entirely clear and is certainly not entirely rational. Maybe it is because of the advertising mess up with the second trailer, it was not a good trailer in hardly any aspect, and was undoubtedly a big blow. Maybe the negative opinions are do to the fact that people feel they need to take a side because it is Marvel and DC, however if you do choose a side you are only choosing a film company to be loyal to which is ridiculous!! Maybe all of the negativity simply comes from the media, The media will condemn any film they want to because this animosity is money for them, if you hear a big film is going to be terrible by a media or critic you get interested in why and at the end of the day everybody loses except the businesses in the media, people are easily influenced in this social networking era.

Batman V Superman Dawn of justice has been subjected to a pre-conceived idea that the movie is not good or for some strange reason shouldn't be good. I do not understand why people are hating this film before they have seen it or giving it a one star simply because it wasn't there cup of tea, by no stretch of the imagination is this film a one star. A one star film implies that it is worse than 'baby geniuses 2' or something.

This movie has some of the best action scenes I have ever witnessed it most definitely tops the leaderboard for superhero action scenes that is where Zack Sneijder deserves his Due. Batman, superman and wonder woman etc. all have amazing combat choreography and this is complimented beautifully by Snyders great direction, the imagery and of course hans Zimmer's and junkie XL's impending soundtrack. When it comes to action Dawn of Justice gets an easy 10/10 from me.

I feel sorry for Zack he is being bullied by the world in a unimaginably cruel way at the moment, people have even started petitions, the truth of the matter is the majority of these people are comic fans and know little about movie-making, once a superhero film reaches the big screen it is now a film no different to any other physically, people need to look of superhero movies as films and not something greater.

The performances in this film are wonderful, Ben afleck brings us a terrific Bruce Wayne/batman, gal godot is absolutely stellar!! as Wonder Woman (she stole the show for me) and Jesse eisenberg is very very good! His lex Luther is ruthless, estranged and very evil there is definitely a comparison to be made with Heath ledgers Joker, Jessie's Lex is not quite as crazy but is much stranger and more evil. The acting side of things is for the most part impressive however carvil and Amy Adams aren't as good as the rest of the cast in my opinion. I would of liked to have seen Matt Bommer as superman and someone else for Lois, nevertheless they were both better in Dawn... Than they were in man of steel so this is nothing major to complain about.

The movies pacing had its high and low moments, there were times where it was fantastic and there were times where it was jagged (for lack of a better word). The movie is a upward slope, from the very begging the "epicness" and speed increases as the movie goes along. It was actually very refreshing to see, too often do action and superhero films put a massive action scene towards the begging leaving the concluding action scenes less impactful. Dawn of justice works on our anticipation and builds us up nicely from moment to moment. However some of the scene transitions didn't work very well, some scenes feel like they need to be longer because there was a hell of a lot of scenes (in the first half mostly) and the music didn't seem to complement a cut from dark batman scenes to light superman ones. (The man of steel piano). Wonder woman's drums were my favourite part of the soundtrack! They gave me goosebumps in the cinema.

I really like this movie, the things I were lead to believe I wouldn't like I actually really loved (like Jessie Eisenberg and Doomsday). I would recommend it to any action lover or superhero fan. It is unpredictable I was surprised a number of times because of things I didn't see coming. It is more mature and more thought provoking than any of Disneys marvel films (which are more lighthearted fun). I can say for sure that I am more excited for the upcoming DC films than I am marvel, and Disney is the reason (I want something more dark if serious Disney!) regardless of this the upcoming marvel films do look great!! I'm not going to pick a side because if I do the only person who losses is me.

title: A Film I Liked Against My Better Judgement
review:
I think it's only fair that I elucidate this from the outset: I am now, have been, and always will be in love with Superman. Ever since my grandfather handed me a massive anthology of 40s, 50s, and 60s era Man of Steel comics while bored in second grade, I was hooked. I would force my mother to drive me out to Captain Comic in New Hyde Park to pick up whatever old story arcs were cheapest, I prized my Superman HeroClix above all else, I even had The Man of Tomorrow's logo emblazoned on cufflinks during my bar mitzvah. While watching the titular comic book icons duke it out, a battle raged on in my own mind between my inner child and the objective, wannabe film critic.

Two years after the events of Man of Steel Superman (Henry Cavill) faces criticism from the media due to collateral damage that seems to follow him wherever he goes. One of those critics, the upstart Gotham-based vigilante known as Batman (Ben Affleck), attempts to formulate a way to fight the otherworldly menace while combating his own inner demons. All the while, Metropolis magnate Alexander Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) hunts for kryptonite and tinkers with the remains of General Zod's decaying spaceship.

In all candor, that summary scratches the plot's surface as thoroughly as a raindrop scratches the surface of Mount Rushmore. The film is an unwieldy mess of converging and diverging story threads thrown together by David Goyer and Chris Terrio, oversaturated to the point of bursting, even at a healthy two-and-a-half-hour run time. Too many characters are hurled at us, apropos of nothing, with a minimum of introduction and backstory, and where would we be without Zack Snyder's famous use of unbearably heavy-handed Jesus imagery. The word "god" is used so much, I wasn't sure I hadn't stumbled into a theater playing Miracles from Heaven by mistake.

But who among us can say they didn't see any of that coming? I could have written the previous paragraph back in 2014, when the film was first announced. What I didn't expect was how much I was able to smile through all of the stupidity the movie threw at me.

You cough up fifteen dollars at the box office to see Batman fight Superman, and to see if Mr. Snyder's special effects team can deliver the action. They do so in spades. The movie looks remarkably good, and the fight sequences feel fresh and imaginative in a way that startled me, especially after the recent slew of Marvel movies I've seen. One Batman dream sequence in the desert is especially awe inspiring in its cinematography and choreography. Even when the movie isn't presenting you with ass-kicking visuals, the movie doesn't drag. You might groan at the dialogue, and a cut might confuse you, but you'll always find yourself engaged.

Despite the movie's best attempts to make me hate it, I couldn't. The movie awoke in me a sense of childlike wonder and amazement that not even "The Force Awakens" could evoke. Wonder Woman made me laugh with excitement, and the cameo clips of various Justice League members brought me back to elementary school, when I would pit my various superhero figurines against one another. This film is the tangible embodiment of those mythical daydreams we'd have as kids, staring out the window as our teachers droned on about long division. As a critic, I can't, in good conscience, recommend "Dawn of Justice," but as an unabashed DC fanboy I sure as hell can.

title: You'll love it more if you're die hard fan and love the action
review: Batman v superman overall is a good film a real upgrade from man of steel. It had the potential to be better though and you'd have to be a fan and love the whole cinematic universe thing to love it. I am going to lay out the pros and cons. Lets start with the pros. The performance of the actors overall is phenomenal especially Ben Affleck as batman, I've got to say he is my favorite on-screen batman no doubt. Every scene he was in was perfect for me and he really displayed how dark batman is. Henry Cavill once again gave a solid performance of superman, I love Gal Gadot's wonder woman even though she wasn't on screen a lot, but Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor is quite interesting, portraying him as this nervous, psychotic type of luthor. The costumes were on point as well. The next pro is the great action sequences. The action is really what you expect from "batman vs superman" i had a really good time watching them go at each other also wonder woman coming in to save batman gave me chills. The story is quite solid but has a few plot holes and that brings us to the cons. There were a few lazy script writes like how they introduce the rest of the justice league. They could of done something way better than Diana getting an e-mail from bruce. Also when lex goes in the kryptonian ship to create doomsday, i mean a voice pops out, he puts blood on zod floating on some water then bam. The voice says it is forbidden then lex asks if the council is still alive then they do it like cmon. Another con is the reason superman wants to end the bat. Batamn has a good enough reason but superman really doesn't. He just hears about him then stops him all of a sudden and says "the bat's dead. Bury it". I just don't really get why superman doesn't like batman that much well other than the fact bruce tried to kill him. The movie also felt like two different movies. The first half was this political thriller and the second was just filled up with so much super things happening. The dream sequences were also not very necessary and just came out of the blue. But the thing that bothers me the most is batman killing people. I mean we all know his code is no killing but we can see in the movie that he blows up things obviously killing people and that's just not batman. Overall this movie is great for me since i love the whole cinematic universe thing and these iconic heroes have been a huge part of my life and after all i'm a guy that loves Comic adaptations whether people like it or not. I highly recommend you go see batman v superman for it's a real audience pleaser.

title: Lots to like, a little to dislike.
review:
It's not perfect, but I found lots to like in this movie.

I liked the plot. Convoluted and a bit all over the place but that's preferable to pedestrian. No immersion breaking moments for me.

Good character introductions. Good back-story hints given the time available and numbers. Good balance between dark/gritty and cartoon-y for me.

Actors all do a solid job. Nothing stand-out like a Heath Ledger Joker but something new and nuanced brought to the table for all.

Twin Cities of Gotham and Metropolis are a nice touch. It wasn't just downtown generic skyscraper cities which are overdone recently.

Batplane and Batmobile were good. Sound effects distinctive and somewhat memorable which is difficult these days.

Comparison to other recent franchises:

  • I liked Batman Begins and I rate it on par with this. Dark Knight and Rises were terrible movies and only Health Ledger saved the former.


  • Better than Avengers 2, equal to Civil War for me.


  • Far FAR better than Star Wars VII, that movie had nothing to like, lots to dislike and immersion breaking stupidity throughout. This is a solid EU franchise starter, STVII killed its franchise for me.

title: The ultimate cut is the ONLY watchable version !
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice Ultimate Edition Review: The Ultimate edition of this year's controversial superhero Flick is now out. This film, released back in march divided a line between fan boys and critics. The critics HATED it, its rated 27% on RT which is way too low for such a mega budget flick. The fan boys rabidly defended the movie including giving death threats to critics who said they didn't like it.

Now a 30 min extended version is out and how does this affect the movie? One of my BIGGEST issue with the movie was, it felt it had been edited by amateurs on a Mac. The pacing was off, the scenes made no sense and in all it was quite a mess.

That whole issue is completely solved in this edit. The extra minutes actually make the film shorter in some ways. There are no huge logic leaps and plots are revealed intricately.

The tone of this edit is very much similar to this director's Watchmen. This also shows a much better directed film than was released in theaters. I don't know whose decision it was to cut out these 30 minutes, but that decision has not only backfired but will haunt them forever.

This 3-hour movie would not have gotten 27% on RT, I dare say it would have been a acceptable 75-78% Easily.

But make no mistake, the huge glaring issues with the movie, such as the Martha scene and Lex's bad acting are still all there, it's just that they are not so glaring anymore. They are much more forgivable due to the movie being quite well made.

In the theatrical cut, the plot flowed so badly, it was so tedious that by the time the ending came, people were just fed up and not in a forgiving or understanding mood.

Every single scene where footage has been added is benefited GREATLY. Some more sub plot is introduced and they balance the movie out.

But even then, this movie has some problems. Other than one scene, this movie doesn't have ANY good action set piece for the first 2 and half hours. It's all drama and setup for the ending. Which would have been fine, it's the same formula from Man of Steel, but this film is much longer and it needs some REALLY good action scenes in between which it doesn't have.

But this 3 hour cut is 100% worth a watch. If this was released theatrically, I would have rated this movie much higher despite the Martha scene and the Lois dong moronic things scene.

Rating: 7.5/10 Fans HAVE to see it, anyone else who hasn't seen the movie yet, this is the version to see.

P.S : Some small easter eggs were very nice additions, like the ending funeral scene has Pete Ross (also seen in Man of Steel) in a brief cameo, its not important, but its good film making.

title: Spectacular
review:
I will admit this up front, I was skeptical of this film going in. Ever since it started production, I have doubted it. From the title to the casting to the score, I judged every single thing.

I had the opportunity to attend a pre-screening earlier tonight. My review won't contain spoilers.

This film is not what I expected at all. From the trailers, it looked like it was going to a be massive CGI mess. And even though it heavily relied on CGI, it was not a mess. The opposite, actually. One of the strongest super-hero films produced.

I'll begin with the negatives:

CGI usually doesn't bother me, but the final battle in this film was a little overdone. So much destruction and mayhem that it pulled me out of the story for a few seconds. I was not convinced that Wonder Woman or even Superman could survive the damage Doomsday was causing.

And . . . that's it. Honestly my only complaint about the film.

Now for the positives:

I'll begin with the cast.

Jesse Eisenberg/Lex Luthor - Let's just say that Eisenberg drives this film. His psychotic attitude isn't overdone, and honestly, I found myself kinda liking the guy throughout the film. He's funny. His timing is brilliant. And he has some of the most chilling lines in the film. This is one of the biggest surprises I experienced.

Henry Cavill/Superman played Clark Kent perfectly. The emotions that Superman faces throughout this film are extreme, and yet Cavill doesn't overplay them. He doesn't use tears to show you he's upset. It's in the way he stands, in the way his face moves, in the way he looks at the world. There are two scenes that really blew me away with his acting. One time when he's in physical pain, and the second time when he's in emotional pain.

Amy Adams/Lois Lane did really well. Some of the lines she was given were a little cheesy, but she pulled it off. Surprisingly, I really connected with her character.

Gal Gadot/Wonder Woman - Holy crap. Fabulous. That's all.

Ben Affleck/Batman - He's a very different Batman and a very different Bruce Wayne than any we've seen before. He was definitely the casting choice I was most skeptical of, but Affleck pulls it off. More than once, he got me to hate Superman even when knowing Superman's side of things. This film focuses a lot on Batman. It's almost a Batman solo film, really, but that's besides the point. Affleck gets you to hate Superman when you know that Superman only means well. It's amazing and what makes this whole film work.

As for Cyborg, The Flash and Aquaman, well, their introductions are executed perfectly. It wasn't forced at all, and it doesn't bog down or overwhelm the rest of the film. Batman v Superman is a perfect, and I mean a *perfect*, setup for the Justice League films.

The Story - The trailers don't show you most of what the actual story is. I was blown away beginning with the opening scene. This is a deeply emotional story. There's a scene in this film between Batman and Superman that's the most powerful and emotional exchange I've ever witnessed in a superhero film before. It focuses a lot on Superman's and Batman's tragedies (but again, does not bog down the story). And there's a moment where both of their tragedies come together, and ultimately, I believe, it's what's going to be driving their friendship and teamwork for the rest of the DCEU.

The film's resolution is well done. Again, a smooth setup for the Justice League.

And the cliffhanger, though a little bit expected, is exciting.

Overall, the film probably deserves a 7/10 or an 8/10, but I'll give it a perfect 10, because never have I seen Batman and Superman portrayed so humanely. It's the first Superman film that I've loved, and a perfect and fresh execution of Batman as well.

Enthralling, action-packed, emotional, suspenseful, deep and a little bit ridiculous, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is the ultimate super-hero film.

title: Great actors are miscast. Incredibly complicated, tedious story. Too little action.
review:
I recently saw the original Superman movie from the eighties. Silly and outdated in parts, yet still very funny at moments and generally speaking still quite entertaining. Why not give the new Superman franchise a try, was my thinking.

The good: first looks were impressive, because the photography and action looked stunning. It has got numerous great actors in it, whom I all like very much (in other movies), BUT these very same good actors are terribly miscast.

The bad: Ben Aflleck is not believable in his role. Neither is Jesse Eisenberg or anyone else. It's just one long disappointing miscast of characters. Really annoying to watch these great actors make a fool out of themselves. A better casting could have delivered a much better picture. But there is more troublesome with this picture.

The most troublesome thing about this movie is the incredibly complicated story, which lasts over 3 hours! (2.5 hours for the theatrical version). I saw the 3 hour version. I cant imagine anyone not getting bored at certain moments. And I guarantee you that you will NOT understand the plot. Is there enough action at least to compensate for the messy, complicated story? No, there is way too little action. The few action scenes are good though, but they consist of mostly CGI explosions and I honestly get bored by those CGI explosions after a while. Seen it all before.

I need drama and believable characters in a good story first. And they are all missing big time! Anyone expecting a similar quality like The Dark Knight Trilogy or the original Superman better skip this movie...

title: Supe v Batty = Yawn of Justice
review:
What can I say? DC have done it again. Spent millions of unnecessary dollars on a couple of caped idiots fighting over nothing. Well done! I mean that. Well done me for not going to see 2+ hrs of yet more explosions with no storyline at the cinema. Trust me when I say I would have demanded every hard earned penny back. I learnt my lesson from the last time with Man of Steel and that was only slightly better than this dud. I really don't understand how a relatively simple original story can be taken to the planet of nowhere special. This was just yawnsville at its best. It's the usual. Two overblown male egos fighting for dominance, to rid the planet of baddies and destroying it in the process. Yeah, that makes perfect sense, what was I thinking? It's obviously me at fault here as we all know there's only 1 life in the whole city worth saving Superman, and that's your gal Lois Lane. Oh yeah! There was a random stranger trapped in a burning building, and when rescued, a crowd of delirious folk started fawning over him as they obviously weren't used to seeing someone other than Lois Lane being saved. Yeah, that must be it. Who thought of this so-called "story"?? Well, no formal warning needed. Just fire him/her and do us all a favour.

There was one comedy moment that our household laugh about even though it was supposed to be a pivotal scene. Batman has spent weeks pumping iron (and maybe a few steroids) his body's now buffed to perfection. He's just gotta kill Superman and has pulled out the stops to find his Achilles heel. Finally they meet. He's thrown old supe all over the place, battered him senseless, and was just about to give the fatal blow when.... wait for it... Superman utters the all important words: "Find...Martha!!!!" "Why did you say that name??!!" demands our batty friend repeatedly (camera cuts to the scene of mummy's death - AGAIN (yawn)). Lois saves her beloved by gushing "it's his mother's name!" so the batty one decides that he'll spare his life, and they are now lifelong friends. Just like that!!! Oh, how I laughed heartily!!! If only Superman knew the secret password was 'Martha' at the beginning it would have saved so much bother. The city would have been intact, the ozone less damaged and Lex Luthor's plans thwarted. Speaking of the bald-headed one. A raging psychopath? Really? Lex is supposed to be a white collared criminal genius, not a cold-blooded murderer. Just awful. But at least Batman got a chiselled bod out of it. So there's that I suppose

This rubbish takes itself far too seriously. I miss Chris Reeve's tongue in cheek Superhero. It's dated, with ropey special effects, but it's a classic that I still laugh at for the right reasons. Take a leaf out of Mavel's comic book DC and allow us a little light relief now and then I beg of you

I wanted to award this tripe with zilch, but as there is no nil point, 1 would have to suffice, but I'm loathed to give it believe me

Do yourself a favour. Give this piece of Kryptonian/Gotham/Metropolis nonsense a miss. Wish I did

title: A billion times better than the media made it out to be.
review:
This film, same as 99% of superhero films, is about the ethics and philosophy of 'doing the right thing'. A theme that has been beaten to death. Batman is the more favored hero, so it's very interesting to me that he is the one who is ultimately wrong. This is a genius conception as we know that when you kill or go to war, you are also creating terror. Not just in the people you are after, but everyone around you. Superman is still learning, and has the idealistic outlook that Batman clearly lost. This is a very common struggle between adults and children. This very struggle is why a lot of people don't understand this film. With a title Batman v Superman, audiences whom think they've grown in intelligence past their ancestors, fail to realize they are no smarter than the people who went to see King Kong vs Godzilla. That's what people want. Unfortunately stories with characters with so many flaws and superpowers with responsibilities on where humanity should go should not be handled so lightly. This film handles these themes with grace. At some point these heroes grow up. Superman has sex, Batman kills and so on. These are the things that go on between the panels. It's not about a word "Martha" freaking Batman out. It's about why does this guy put on the cowl. Why does Clark put on the cape. Why? It's that little idealistic ticker we all have. If you want to hate this film because it didn't sync up to your vision in your head, fine. But these guys not only went into the philosophy and beyond, they GAVE us classic and monumental moments of comic history we are so lucky to finally have on screen.

The performances by all of the actors were superb. Particularly Jesse Eisenberg and Ben Affleck. The score was also amazing. I was very surprised by the opening 'Batman origin'. We've seen that so many times, but this was the most entertaining I've seen.

Ben Affleck is Batman. There, I said it.

When you make art, you are taking a risk. I love that this film took so many risks, and I love that the people this film made angry are the people that need to learn these lessons the most and for that I thank you Zack Snyder. Seriously thank you.

title: A crowded, dark action movie that struggles to meet expectations
review:
Batman V Superman has an almost impossible weight on its shoulders: - it has to simultaneously present a worthy adaptation of a revered story, while acting as a springboard for DC to launch their own super-team to rival the 'Avengers'.

In the hands of anybody, it'd be an impossible task. It's undeniable that it falls down on the job. However, criticising it feels a bit like belittling a brilliant student for trying too hard, because it still contains fantastic entertainment.

The trailer shows that the story involves Batman's escalating beef with the collateral damage that follows Superman's battles, and Superman's belief that Batman is a dangerous thug. Lex Luthor is involved in stirring feelings against Superman, and a growing need for Government to step in and oversee their super-heroic guest. Wonder Woman pops up in the adverts, and a giant beastie appears to start trashing a city. The trailer correctly suggests a film that may be too full of plot-lines for its own good. Piling conspiracy on conspiracy, the film over-bakes a simple idea - that Batman wants to stop Superman. By over-complicating the plot, some of Wayne's conviction is undersold; he never feels angry enough to try to murder a super-being. Similarly, Superman's reason for the brawl feels badly constructed, an earlier scene makes it clear that he could locate and fix the issue with ease, and the title brawl feels like it could be stopped completely by one or two quick sentences of grown up dialogue.

But what about the titular smack-down? Well, they make the Dark Knight taking on a superhuman feel almost believable. Fists fly, a multitude of Batman toys are used, and Affleck gets to perform a wonderful "Oh hell, I'm in for it now..." moment where he half-raises his hand in semi-supplication as Superman closes in to land a punch, adding a personality that was all too often missing from 'Man of Steel's pivotal Zod v Supes battle.

However, it feels almost a side-event to the film. The movie's stand- out sequence is a stunningly executed Batmobile chase that gets the adrenaline roaring, and the real joy is often in the drama of the character interactions: Clark and Bruce verbally jousting at a Luthor party, Bruce and Wonder Woman trading verbal barbs.

Eisenberg is partially successful as Luthor. He's fun, but his eccentricity goes too far. A man who rambles insensibly like a madman during a speech at a major society party wouldn't be treated with the political and societal carte- blanche that he receives, and if he carved the ham of his performance any thicker audience members would need bread and mustard.

Affleck is extremely good as Wayne. As you'd expect, a film so overloaded with ideas doesn't give him much room, but he does fill you with confidence that his Batman solo venture would be thrilling. His Batman is bitter and dark - more like Keaton's semi-sociopath of 1989 than Bale's clearer thinker.

Cavill is great as Superman, embodying Clark with humour and romance, while his Superman gets to feel noble and exciting. As with Batman, the character's a little on the thin side, but for the same reasons.

Gadot is elegant and fun, performs with sparky chemistry and dialogue, and almost steals her scenes. Her first appearance as Wonder Woman starts to look like it's going to consist of posing and glowering, but they eventually let her perform some combat moves, and hopes should be high for the solo outing.

So will you come out of the cinema satisfied? Maybe. It's clear the film suffered by trying to juggle too many elements. One early scene of destruction cuts straight into another unrelated scene, leaving the audience briefly wondering if they're looking at the last location or not, and then realising they're looking at the aftermath of something that's happened off- screen. Later, key characters seem to majorly change mood toward each other with almost no time or dialogue passing between them that would believably cause such a change. It feels like swathes of film have been left on the cutting room floor. Set ideas about plot are likely to be confounded too - this delights in twisting and turning. In terms of tone, don't expect Marvel. There are several moments of bad language, threat, on-screen death and destruction, grudges, moodiness and moral agonizing. It's also very blatant that it exists to set up a franchise (almost to the point that it might as well have 'Merchandising Opportunity!' stamped prominently on its poster, which may justifiably irk some viewers). So: dark emotion tone, blatant moments of commercial-mindedness, messy plot lines, a big beastie that's probably pretty unnecessary, an iffy main bad guy...is it worth seeing? Yes. It's worth seeing in the way that all big, far-reaching dreams are worth seeing. It's fun, dramatic, and exciting. It isn't perfect, but nothing this complicated ever is.
