title: A win for comic book MOVIE fans. Don't miss your chance to witness history on screen.
review:
Feast your eyes on the plethora of harsh words written about BvS and its creators. Everywhere you look, there will be another worthless low-life trying to bring the film down to his level.

I've been an IMDb member for nearly a decade, and I've never written a review before -- but THIS...this is necessary.

FOR THOSE PEOPLE WHO HAVE NOT SEEN THE MOVIE: go see it. Wipe your brain clean of all the negativity you've consumed and subsequently fashioned your own, meaningless critique out of. I know it's nearly impossible, but forget about the reviews (as much as possible), sit back, and enjoy. It is dynamic, it is epic, and it is DIFFERENT. A carbon-copy of the Marvel Cinematic Universe is NOT what we want...film doesn't work like comic books.

Look at what you have in front of you. This is Batman V Superman, for better or worse, on the movie screen. Many people worked extremely, extremely hard to give you something worth watching, yet so many of you make it seem as if the 3 year + endeavor is completely void and a terrible film because of a confusingly loud critical response.

As you've probably already read, Batfleck is a force to be reckoned with. He disappears in the role, and completely succeeds in bringing a fresh version of Batman to the screen (which two years ago, seemed highly, highly unlikely). Honestly, there's no reason to go any further, go watch it for him alone, if you must. The real issue has always been Superman:

Superman is phenomenal. The circumstances of Cavill's Superman are grounded in the real world: what sort of limitations would have to be lain upon someone with SO much power? The subtlety of Cavill's performance really comes through when you realize how much he is constantly restraining himself to fit in our world: when he opens the gate to the podium in the court room, when he tries not-killing Batman, and when he's so down and out he's got no fight left in him (he knows, in a second, he could burn the entire world to the ground if he wanted, but he'd rather die to some a hero than a menace to the entire world).

Everything about this Superman stands up for the same things the comic version does -- however, this film is meant to take place in the real world...as such, the world is never so forgiving so as to replenish Superman's reserves of hope and faith. Sometimes, especially in the beginning of his "herodome," he loses his grasp with his faith in the notion that he was created for a reason (and, as the world seems to suggest, a very important one likened to the savior of the human race). Does this not make sense? This is a huge burden for a man born and raised in the Midwest. Also, this makes for an increasingly interesting dynamic between the two titular characters: a man who has completely lost hope, and a superman who has an idyllic sense of hope, one the audience presumes, is destined to fail in the real world -- but what about the power of Superman? May he overcome it?

Maybe. There is much unanswered in this film. Themes are explored, but they are not necessarily dealt with -- this gives many critics the inclination that the movie was unfinished, poorly written. YES, it does suffer minute issues due to it being a gateway to the Justice League...HOWEVER, the movie provides a complete experience for every viewer -- so long as your not utterly consumed with your preconceived notions and misconceptions about the material and how important your opinions and preferences actually are.

The supporting cast is excellent. Alfred and Perry White bring some much needed humor to the film and Diane Lane and Costner each have two excellent scenes. Lois Lane is, well, Lois Lane. Gadot as Wonder Woman is remarkable - - it is truly one of those examples of casting where you finally admit the casting director knows a LOT more than you do about the subject. Speaking of, you probably DON't know that much about the subject. And no, not comic book lore, but FILMMAKING. Not everything you read about when you were 8- years-old has made it into the film. Lex, to me, was excellent; to be honest, I hated the choice of Eisenberg but he really surprised me. While he's a long-shot from the Lex in the comics, the motivations are still there and he is still fascinating to watch and witness his genius.

Don't TRY to love or hate the movie. Just watch it and pay attention. You're bound to get a few tough lines and things you don't like. The score and the visuals? From the two of the best in their respective fields? You won't be disappointed. Truly, excellent filmmaking overall -- trying to determine what the fuss is about.

Never in my twenty four years have I seen a group of people respond so negatively to a film for no particular reason. Things didn't play out the way you expected? No way. Batman is too dark? LOL!

I will see it again, and I honestly prefer an empty theater. But if you consider yourself a fan of film and not a pretentious douche bag that follows critics' orders, give Batman v Superman a shot and go see it.

title: Unimaginative series of explosions
review: Hard to figure out what exactly made this two and half hour theatrical experience a waste of time. Was it the terrible performance of Jesse Eisenberg? Was it the lack of imagination characterizing the scenario? Was it the completely useless intervention of Wonder woman? Was it the extra-ugly, extra-bad, stinky breathed baddie that came out of nowhere at the very end of the movie? Was it the "let's kill superman, but in the last 0.1 second hint at his revival" ? Oh wait I've just figured it out. The whole film is particularly uncreative, and that's all you could expect from a movie that has for basis "let's make superman and batman fight each other". I am not saying Jesse Eisenberg is a bad actor, on the other hand I think he is an excellent one and has proved it repeatedly, but the role itself was totally inappropriate. An obvious attempt at walking in Heath Ledger's footsteps (from TDK), except it seemed awfully out of place: the Joker and Lex Luthor have almost nothing in common. Nevertheless Ben Affleck does a pretty good Batman, and performances from Gal Gadot and Henry Cavill were satisfying. The entire cast did a pretty great job really. At the end of the day I would say this was slightly better than Man of Steel, but definitely not by much.

title: What just happened?
review:
What did Bruce Wayne do for 18 months to keep the rage against Sups. Did he stay secluded in his "batcave" watching Youtube Clips of the destruction of Metropolis, drunk, chanting "I HATE SUPERMAN! I HATE...".

The main issue with this movie is the main plot. It doesn't make any sense. After an apparent 18 months of millions of lives saved by Superman, "everybody" starts to hate him?! Why? WHY? And BW, his motives for hating SM could have been at the best plausible during the weeks following the Zod incident. But as time goes by wouldn't he have discovered that Clark is just a man, not a GOD, that actually is doin good. No Batman, the world's greatest detective, hates the man who saved 7 billion people from total annihilation. IT*S SO STUPID! The "fight" between Batman and Superman is utter nonsense, so contrived. It pisses me off. IDIOTS!

The rest of the movie is OK-isch, except they are pissing on Superman. Batfleck is doin his best to portray a man, lets be honest, who must be a psychopath, or at least a very unstable person with clear paranoia in some form. He is not dark and gritty. He is a murdering revengeful billionaire.

What caused this perfect storm? The acting is good overall. I like Henry Cavill better than Ben Afflecks performance, why you say? Who cares. Wonderwoman, (A)Lex and Alfred are actually quite good, though Gal Gadot's screen time is sadly very limited.

The problem is the script and the editing. I don't know how much Zack Snyder was involved with those two things but he is not all to blame. The Doomsday fight and its conclusion also worked. But the actual movie itself feels like a Video game with its FMV's separated from the actual gameplay and then bunched together. Like a car crash filmed in slow motion, me unable to turn away. I started off at 5/10 its now closer to 4. Im so sad.﻿

There are some more good and bad things in the movie, but i am too upset to vocalize or serialize them.﻿

title: It just wasn't very good
review:
I am so disappointed by this film, even though my hopes were not high going in. I thought to myself before seeing it "how bad can it possibly be, It'll probably be dumb but at least the action should be fun". oh how wrong I was, this film is not fun at all, the action is some of the most boring and lifeless I have seen in a modern blockbuster film, it just was not engaging whatsoever and at times nearly incomprehensible.

What I enjoyed in the film starts and ends at the beginning, the film starts off pretty well we see Bruce's origin story once again, but thankfully it is short. followed by a bizarre dream sequence. We then see the destruction of Metropolis from Bruce's point of view. I enjoyed this scene quite a lot , it was fast, exciting and intense. Things sorely lacking from the rest of this film.

A major issue with the film is the pacing, it is all over the place, we jump from scene to scene at a break neck speed with little time to process any of what we have just seen. It feels like they packed three films into one and cut it down to 2.5 hours. none of the characters have time to develop, none of the themes have time to develop, it is just a complete mess from beginning to end.

title: Good but not quite great
review:
I enjoyed this movie for a number of reasons, especially the first hour and a half or so, but I felt it would be a better movie had it ended there. Some of the best special effects I have seen in any movie and the action and story are fast paced. That is until the monster Lex Luthor creates appears. It then becomes all rather silly. It should have ended with the Superman/Batman battle in my opinion. All the acting is top notch, Henry Cavill, Ben Aflek and Amy Adams are all brilliant and suit the roles better then many previously. Although Louis really should have had dark hair, it was Lana Lang who was a red head in the comics. Jesse Eisenberg is a great Lex Luthor with just the right hint of genius and madness. Laurence Fishburne is a bit flat as Perry White, as is Jeremy Irons as Alfred, but they aren't in many scenes.

But over all an enjoyable watch.

title: Complete waste of time & money!!!!
review: Anyone claiming that this movie was anything but a complete waste of time is LYING or DELUSIONAL. I was prepared to give Ben a fighting chance but it was pure torture watching him! Is it possible that he was having a bad day throughout the entire filming? I know Ben can act so is it that he can't take direction? I don't know but I will not be watching another Batman featured movie with him in it. Henry Cavill is a superb actor and delivered as usual. Amy Adams bored me to death as usual. I had high hopes for Jesse Eisenberg but he just came across like he was on too many ADHD meds. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was awesome and was the only redeeming thing about this movie. Still not worth spending 151 minutes of my life watching way too many flashbacks & Ben weight training, walking around & dreaming. I hope that Ben has the good grace to bow out after this travesty!

title: Batman v Superman is a classic tale of battle between two different beings whose sense of perceiving and living are suffering through immense pain and controversies
review: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is the wrong title. It should've been Dawn of Justice. It ain't always about substance. In this case, Zack Snyder remains as consistent as ever and true to form, delivering a visual spectacle whose grandiose action sequences rival the biggest blockbusters Hollywood can ever offer. I'm not angry but shaken that critics can't see past the marvel formula. The theme, mood and pace that Zack Snyder often likes to make has become my favorite as in i'd like to see much more movies with this much dark, strengthened, gloomy and over saturated colors. This movie is unsettling and incomplete as it proceeds to something much bigger than the greatest gladiator match in the history of the world, but it was the need of this film. For first time in my life I've seen perfect unsettlement and perfect incompleteness in any movie. Maybe people expected a Bat v Supes and got a platform for the Justice League. Why see it as a movie when the director and the makers of the film want you to get inspired by its characters, to think a little more on why not to lose hope, to make the practicality and reality out of Fantasy, to observe the beauty of slow paced visual narration and unreal world we're hallucinated to live in with hope coming back anyway. Hope may be Superman's symbol but today i saw Batman symbolizing hope in a different manner in this cruel atmosphere. I did not see a film with heroes fighting instead i lived in a sensation between fear, rage, powerlessness, and the thing that unites us- HOPE to start again at any moment of failure. ZACK man you're new Best. It's not a feel good colorful movie which promises on entertainment or philosophies but it's based on possibilities of gray shades in lives that stands with dullness in color and momentarily silence. Bruce Wayne's hope monologue made me cry. And I'm speaking my heart out on Dawn of justice as i was waiting for this movie for more than 2 years and also i wasn't a film intellect in my Dark Knight years. Why compare Nolan's philosophical representative to Zack's presentation. Well Zack has an edge over Nolan because of his clarity in visual interpretation. I'm not writing this for you to agree or not to agree but i'd like you to see this movie not to analyze narrative or film style but to have the feeling of powerlessness and extemporaneous. Don't be disappointed be moved be inspired. We kill, we betray, we war but one thing holds my back...we start again and again to make things fine.

review:

title: Not worth the hype whatsoever
review: Well, to start, the lead role, occupied by the titular character: Bruce Wayne being portrayed by Ben Affleck comes off as dull and uninteresting to say the least. We start with a retelling of a familiar tale of how his parents were killed. How could anyone think Superman is a bad guy? I have no idea. He's a clean cut, all American dude. Batman doesn't seem as intense in this portrayal, and you get the feeling that Ole Ben only appeared for the paycheck, nothing else. The movie follows it predecessor with too much product placement, this time in the form of new Chrysler Cars. Man of steel was endorsed by IHOP, so it makes sense that they would follow suit. Highlights of the film include Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, and Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. You know you have a problem when the most interesting characters aren't even mentioned in the title. I have no problem with Cavill's Superman, but Afflecks Batman leaves a lot more to be desired. The fight changes tides when both the hero's realize their mothers share the same first name. Wow, a little too convenient, don't you think? The ending is the death of superman, which we all know is a facade. Walking in, I knew there would be no winner, but the movie studios felt the need to title it this way to garner some attention to their fizzling DC film franchise. The movie comes off as nomadic in the way it jumps around from point to point, leaving the audience with a huh? expression when the credits role. I'd say a 4/10 was going easy on it.

title: It wasn't that bad actually...
review:
At the beginning of the movie, I thought I would be wasting money by watching a reboot of superheroes fighting each other. Actually it was not that bad! I thought Henry Cavill and Ben Affleck were good as playing Batman and Superman.

Even though you would miss the "original" Superman who is known as Christopher Reeves but Cavill did his best too. I was bummed that Superman got killed off in this, why couldn't they just left that part alone and continue with trying to save the world?! I wish the movie didn't have a cliff hanger so we would know that Superman isn't actually dead but alive like! They really should just stick with this movie and never mind the sequels that will happen later on, it does cheese you off a bit!

Gal Gadot did a good job playing as Wonderwoman. However, you would miss her original colors on her costume which were:- red, blue and yellow. I suppose Lynda Carter really does miss being Wonderwoman. Who could blame her? She was awesome as Wonderwoman! I kinda feel the same with reboots but Gadot was class too!

I do like Jeremy Irons as Alfred even though he doesn't have the original look in which, I would wish he had. He's much better then Michael Caine because he was such a whinger that you would think he wasn't acting as the Alfred we know at all! Ben Affleck is likable too even though, I think he acts a bit older than Christian Bale but at the same time, he's better. Not because he is a popular actor but because he got good skills baby! With Batman, he does have the enthusiasm of saving the world and that's what we want from a superhero!

Didn't anyone think Jesse Eisenberg looked cute with his long hair? I did! He really does make a perfect DC villain, he could've been the Joker, he would definitely fit the role in his best nerdy ways! Seriously, I'm glad they got him to be Lex Luthor, DC would definitely find it beneficial to get great stars in starring their superhero movies! It's definitely a good idea for them to be involved with the film industries about this type of stuff to put out there!

Its a good film I have to say, glad I watched it regardless if it was too long!

title: Great Movie! Great Batman! Maybe Spoilers!
review: I believe that BVS is a great movie. I don't understand why people think is a bad movie. This movie is the beginning of a new kind of super hero movie. Excellent! Afleck as Batman is amazing! remember me the batman of Arkham Asylum, the video game!. Only for that you must watch the movie!. title: Best Time To Be A DC Fan. Spoiler Free Review.
review: The film is genuinely awesome. The movie is ACTION PACKED. The fight between Batman and Superman was amazing. It has a dark story with Superman trying to find his place in the world after his reveal to the world and aged and more brutal Batman. The movie has a lot deep and dark story that everyone can relate to. Zack Snyder also did a really great job setting up DCCU. All in all, it's uniquely, freshly directed & one of it's own kind superhero movie. It's an excellent adaptation of the greatest superheroes on the planet.

title: Amazing, fascinating and over all a great movie..
review: I would just say to the critics who are giving it a bad review, they don't see the movie as the fans do. Henry Cavill is already perfect as Superman, and Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was just mesmerizing, she looked enough sexy and graceful to portray Wonder Woman perfectly. But truly who unexpectedly did a great job was Jesse Eisenberg, he as Lex Luthor was amazing, he really portrayed the psycho, mad genius Luthor perfectly. Over all its just a marvelous piece of work by Zack Snyder, and one thing I would just add is that, the sound track of this movie was just amazing. Loved the movie all the way, not a single moment I would miss and would see it again soon.

title: Severely Underrated
review:
There are a lot of negative reviews out there of Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice. And I almost believed them. Until I went and saw the movie for myself. I loved it. The biggest problem I saw was the pacing. There were times where some scenes would come and go before you had time to process what was going on. Which only lasts the first part of the movie. Once things really hit the fan, things are paced pretty nicely.

Let me start by saying Ben Affleck surprised me as Batman. I wanted to give him the benefit of the doubt but I was still worried he'd be terrible. But I can safely say he did a good job as Batman. As of right now he's my second favorite live-action Batman. I'll have to see more of him in his solo movie before I can say if he's as good or better than Christian Bale.

Superman was one of my issues with the first half of the movie. He seemed to be glossed over a lot. Where his scenes would zip by. Like a rescue of a girl trapped in a burning building. Instead of getting to see him save her, we see as he's returning her to her family. I would have liked to see him in action more than what he was in the earlier parts of the film.

Wonder Woman has a fairly small role. But people clapped when she first entered the final battle of the movie.

There is a conspiracy against Superman where he is framed to appear like he killed some terrorists that led to corrupt governments having villagers killed in retaliation. We see why Batman wants to beat Superman's brains in, which was evident in the trailers.

The fight between Batman and Superman was epic. Batman utilized Kryptonite to give him a fighting chance. Kryptonite came into play after some was recovered from the World Engine from Man of Steel that crashed in the Indian Ocean after Superman destroyed it. Lex got his hands on it, and Batman stole it from him so he could use it in his fight against Superman. No spoilers about who won the fight.

We all saw Doomsday in the trailer. And all I'll say here is that the fight is pretty awesome. Wonder Woman and Superman slug it out with Doomsday and Batman spawn camps him with a Kryptonite smoke grenade.

I don't want to give too much away. But all of the negative reviews are unwarranted. It seems like if something doesn't have Marvel Studios in the title it is already under extreme scrutiny. Since the movie has a dark tone and isn't full of knock-knock jokes and fart jokes like the Marvel Cinematic Universe movies (an exaggeration, but those movies do get carried away with the jokes), people seem to have a negative opinion. People had already written off the movie because of Affleck's casting, which isn't fair considering people gave wooden acting Chris Evans a chance as Captain America (which he gives a wooden performance there).

I have seen people whine about the plot holes. And there are a couple. How does Lex find out Clark is Superman? How did Clark find out Bruce was Batman? How did Lois know to get the Kryptonite spear? But I can look past those because they weren't as massive a plot hole as the end of Thor: The Dark World where Thor couldn't see through Loki's disguise after seeing through his illusions earlier in the same movie.

Frankly, this movie had the guts to do what Marvel doesn't. There is a death in this movie that shocked me. Don't want to give too much away, but people aren't going to be happy because he didn't have baseball cards on him and he didn't pop up peachy-keen in the next scene like every character killed in the Marvel Cinematic Universe movie except for Quicksilver in Age of Ultron.

As I said, my biggest issue with the movie was the pacing. There were rumors late 2014 and early 2015 that Batman v. Superman was going to be broken up into two movies. And I wish they had done that. Then the pacing wouldn't have been an issue. There were parts of this movie where it felt like two movies being played out in one movie. But what can you do? Seems they only break movies into two parters when it's a young adult novel series. So what can you do?

Give this movie a chance. Frankly, I don't trust professional critics anymore. Seeing as how they act like every Marvel Cinematic Universe movie is solid gold when most of them have 1 dimensional villains and always have to rely on a MaGuffin to move the plot along. People go into those movies with an automatic positive view just because critics give them all stellar reviews, even when they are complete garbage like Iron Man 3 and Thor: The Dark World. And people seem to only want to go into DC movies with a negative outlook these days. All I can say is watch the movie for yourself. The pacing is a little quick, but the action is great, Ben Affleck actually did a good job, and the movie has a shocking moment that I know I'll be talking about for a long time at the end.

And not to bash people who liked it, how can critics slam this movie while praising Star Wars Ep. VII which most of that was a rehash of A New Hope? And those same critics will no doubt sing the praise of that new Ghostbusters movie that everyone is throwing up about.

title: IGNORE THE CRITICS, The Bias is Real!
review:
Like many, I made the mistake of looking at 'critical' reviews before seeing this film for myself; and tbh, they destroyed my excitement. Never before has a single movie been attacked so much from the word 'go' (going as far back as its announcement at Comic- Con) So it's understandable why I and many other fans would get on the defence.

It's obvious there's a critical bias against DC in favour of Marvel, but even if you'd missed the 1st half of this movie, the 2nd half is enough pure entertainment to grant the film AT LEAST 50%! Anything less than that is sheer, blatant spite.

Honestly, this movie isn't perfect by any means, there are tonnes of different ways to have done certain parts of this...

I feel Batman/Bruce was portrayed entirely wrong. Bats has always been the knowledgeable, patient detective; and in this film, he's just murderous straight off the 'bat" - however - Affleck was born to play Batman and I couldn't imagine Bale or anyone else from now on.

The scenes in which Superman saves ppl should have been longer and shown his caring side (talking to them etc) Also would've liked to see more Clark / Lois reporting.

Lex was too wild, Billy Zane would've been my choice, or Eisenberg should've harnessed as much 'Clancy Brown' as he could in his performance.

The BvS fight should've been at least 5mins longer and NO BATHROOM SINK!

Things I LOVED...

Alfred is hilarious and even better than TDK version. Should've been a little more of him and Bruce.

Zack Snyder's grandeur, scale and attention to detail are impeccable. The recap Metropolis scene is AWESOME!

Batman's warehouse fight scene is an instant classic. THAT'S HOW ITS DONE!

I loved the new approach to Doomsday and am positive we're not done with him! (Doomsday doesn't die, he regenerates and evolves to be immune to the same afflictions) Remember, he's practically an infant version in this.

Wonder Woman is badass! Should've been a little more of her.

Nods to the comics and original material shows just how much Snyder knows and loves the characters.

I actually liked "Martha" as you forget they share the same name and it makes Bruce realise Clark is more human than alien and in the end, he loves his mother and she's in trouble. This gives Bruce a chance to save Clark's Martha and redeem himself for past guilt and a lifetime of personal demons. I thought it was very touching and handled very well. It also lead to possibly the best scene in the whole film!

The Score is by far one of the best in any comic book movie you'll ever hear... Ever!

Conclusion... Could've been done a tonne of different ways to make it better (Characterization is the key!) but still a good effort and plenty classic moments!

title: Best superhero film EVER
review: Well, just got in from watching Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. And it certainly is a new dawn. This film is beautifully shot scene to scene. It literally is like Zach Snyder ripped the shots straight from a comic book itself. Its a beautiful film. But, so much more. The story is engaging, the dialog tight and witty. I gotta say, this is the DC universe. Ya cant beat it....

title: Big, Clumsy Mess
review:
Man of Steel knew what it was, and it stuck to that vision. Plenty of people disliked it. I happen to have really enjoyed the Superman reboot, but I cannot say the same about this one. If ever a film has been more ambitious than capable, it is BvS, which is packed to the brim with characters, ideas and plot lines, but doesn't juggle them very well at all. This is like a worse version of Avengers: Age of Ultron, a film that should have been great collapsing under its own weight.

BvS is klutzy to the extreme, which is a shame considering many of the individual pieces being good. I appreciate darker superhero stories, but this one is just a slog, way too long and surprisingly boring. It's not well-put-together like the Nolan films were (for the most part), nor is it fun like some of the wackier takes of the past. Big fail, in my book. WB needs to clean house, creatively, starting with Snyder.

title: Wonderful film that does not patronize the audience
review:
In a word Batman V Superman is amazing. I don't throw that word around lightly when it comes to new "blockbuster" movies. However, BVS is!

It does not insult the intelligence of the viewer by going over the same point repeatedly. Something I think Critics just don't understand. The film has beautiful heart and depth to characters that have been looked over in past depictions.

I hated the thought of Ben Affleck as Batman, Now I can't imagine anyone else in the role. He brought the dark to both Bruce Wayne and Batman. Something that has been lacking in the Bruce Wayne on screen mythos. I was so surprised in the best way possible. Thank you Batfleck!

Also just want to say how much I enjoyed Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of Lex Luthor. I think he may get looked over by a lot of people, but I think he did a brilliant job of making the non threatening Luthor, threatening.

The cinematography is stunning and for me has the best telling of Bruce Wayne's past. I can't recommend it high enough, go see it

title: Chaotic, inconsistent, humorless and packaged with a powerful dose of boredom, deja-vu and an intrusive background score.
review:
Chaotic, inconsistent, humorless and packaged with a powerful dose of boredom, deja-vu and an intrusive background score.

Following the worn out retelling of the story about dangers of uncontrolled power, 'Dawn of Justice' pits in Batman against Superman in an attempt to boot-start the DC comics universe. Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) gets offended and affected by Superman's (Henry Cavill) unchecked actions which led to numerous deaths as collateral damage in Gotham city. While Mr. Wayne is busy locating the alleged tyrant, the government and general public too in Metropolis are getting restless for the same reason leading to confrontation. Lex Luther (Jesse Eisenberg) meanwhile has his own sinister plans in developing a weapon based on Kryptonite that can keep Superman in check.

While the 3D and special effects are on par with any other super-hero movie that's released in the last 10 years, the same cannot be said about other departments. The uninteresting screenplay, chaotic editing especially in the first hour, non-relevant dream sequences and unrelated character introductions - all played into making a poor movie watching experience. No actions by any character feels convincing leaving nothing to root for the leads. While Ben Affleck was in his auto-pilot mode, Henry Cavill has taken the steel reference too seriously and added it to his performance too. Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) is in just for an introduction to her spin-off movie, so refraining from commenting. Hans Zimmer is a seasoned composer but this time his background score is so intrusive and epic that actually belittles the on-going action on the screen.

Zack Snyder should revisit his spectacular 'Watchmen' and figure out what all could have gone wrong here.

title: Best DC movie yet
review:
I know its not easy to state this as the best DC movie yet but that is mainly cause its a collaboration of heroes.

First of all i hated MoS. It was a brainless action movie that didn't show any humanity at all. Everything went to fast and everything apparently had to be destroyed.

This one on the other-hand shows us a lot more humanity of all the characters involved.

The movie starts with what happened in MoS. Just some other PoVs. I liked how the movie build up from there and how u see why not everyone loves the man in the red cape.

The interaction between B and S are great and it doesn't take long to figure out where WW comes in to place. BvS also shows us Cyborg, Aquaman and the flash ready to be launched in to the JL movies. The bat got some ugly dreams that i couldn't figure out all as I'm not to familiar with the comics.

Lex Luthor and Doomsday are great villains in this movie. Doomsday was way more bad-ass then i thought he would be.

Everyone did his part very well and Ben did not disappoint as the Batman.

Thanks to this movie I'm looking forward to the future installments of DC.

I recommend this movie to all who loves the genre. You will not be disappointed.

title: Ignore the Marvel fan boys! This was a fantastic movie!
review:
Don't listen to the chirping of the critics! Don't listen to the Disney stooges, quaking in their boots! Don't listen to the Marvel fan boys! Don't listen to the Nolanverse nostalgic! Forget the trailers! This was a fantastic movie!

Sure, it's a bit disjointed and incoherent in the first 10-15 minutes, as threads are unravelled without any real purpose, but the threads are slowly wound up as the movie goes on. Each scene in the first 10-15 minutes begins to make sense as the plans of each of the protagonists is revealed.

The overall plot is very predictable (obvious if you've seen anything Batman and Superman in the animated world over the last few years) and the movie isn't as layered as it should be, but there are Easter eggs and premonitions to potential future story lines littered throughout the film.

There were some glaring omissions that was disappointed not to see; preparation was one of them.

Although it wasn't needed for the veteran Superhero genre fans, the back stories to the characters were a little dry to almost non-existent. However, with the stand alone movies coming, I don't think there was a pressing need. It would have been nice to see some character history.

Ben Affleck was a fantastic Batman. Cruel and mean. What Batman should be. Nolan got the original Batman so wrong, he might have knocked the ball out of the park with some fantastic movie making, but the essence of the trilogy, the dark knight, was very underwhelming. This Batman however is so far away from that one and a lot closer to the Batman we seen and loved as children in the animated series.

Superman was almost a bit part character in the first half of the movie and then the big fight begins and he really comes into his own. The final fight scene is where we really get to see Wonder Woman flex her muscles and that smile in the heat of battle with doomsday is the cherry on the cake.

There is a, "how do they get out of this one" feel to second half of the movie, something I have NEVER seen in a Marvel movie (except Days of Future Past). I have never felt like the heroes are in any danger or have any difficulty in beating their foe in a Marvel flick. This movie is very different in that sense and that is what really sets Marvel and DC apart. The former is for the popcorn lovers looking for a cheap thrill. The latter is for people who want some excitement.

So forget the naysayers, go see this movie. You will enjoy it and you will rate it 10/10!

title: For Comic Book Fans
review:
(Originally written March 2016, slightly edited for the Wonder Woman solo origin film June 2017)

Batman v Superman Dawn of Justice is made for Comic Book Fans. If you are new to the universe, it will certainly be harder to follow and piece together...which is why there is so much distaste toward the film. The film expects the audience to be well versed in how courageously DC plays with their stories, even if it is risky.

This is a comic book movie that looks and feels that way, this what Zack Synder does really well. It breaks away from the semi-campy, Disney Princess portrayals that was taking over the industry after The Dark Knight trilogy. Unfortunately, the majority doesn't understand or like this yet. Fortunately, with darkness comes light. These characters must come from something bleak. The opposite of the norm for big franchises.

BvS: Dawn of Justice captures Bruce Wayne/Batman in his elder years and Ben Affleck absolutely NAILS it. Ben Affleck has a phenomenal performance that previous live-action interpretations of Bruce Wayne/Batman were lacking.

The film also briefly debuted Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, which left most wanting more. You can tell how her character fit in a bit better after watching her origin film that was released June 2017.

Finally...Superman...well you're not going to get the campy boy scout anymore. Man of Steel portrayed Superman in a different light. You know he should be a boy scout, and he sees himself that way, but this movie is teaching him how the real world actually works and is why there is a conflict between him and Batman.

On top of all that, this movie is called 'DAWN OF JUSTICE' for a reason. Might be hard understand that. One would expect dozens of films to explain stuff that is already part of our culture for decades (almost a century now), but this universe started with Man of Steel, it's still early and it needs to start somewhere that is different.

A real comic book fan can appreciate this film, it's visually stunning and compelling. Any confusion is exactly what you'd feel when you read a comic book, you'll be itching for the next issue.

Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is arguably one of the better COMIC BOOK movies to date. Visually stunning and quite easy to follow for fans...but might not be for those used to Marvel movies.

If you grew up with DC comic books and are a fan of them, this movie is definitely for you. You don't need to swear your allegiances to anyone, a real comic book fan will undoubtedly enjoy this film and recognize DC is shaping their universe in their own way and is definitely setting another tone for their films.

title: Worse than the first.
review:
There is more to why this movie is horrible than the horrible acting and length. It is also the stupidity of the plot.

1. Lois tries to run a piece in a paper in the newspaper instead of just calling Clark on his cell phone, or screaming out that she needs his help (he'd hear her). Logic there? None.

2. Superman fails to react to an explosion fast enough to save a single person in the white house, while being in the same room. (Not the injured who survived on their own that he helped after, but before people were hurt. He's faster than the explosion, and would at least be able to save *one* person, if not several.) Also, he apparently just left the kryptonian ships in the hands of the government and the public. Never went to clean up the technology to keep it out of human hands. Something Superman *always* does, considering how dangerous kryptonian technology is and he doesn't want humans reverse engineering it.

3. Lex Luthor apparently can push candy into a high ranking government official's mouth like he's a child, and not in that arrogant way Lex would, but in the insane childish persona they gave him. Oh, and let it be noted that he had absolutely zero leverage on this guy. They were trying to enter a mutually beneficial agreement, but Lex had nothing to make the guy into a complete b****.

4. Batman is an unrepentant killer. Alfred knows this and does nothing about it. Can we not destroy the one thing about batman that means something? You know, the one thing that is core to their character? Oh, and apparently when he fell into the caves as a kid, the bats swirled around him and floated him out. More Jesus imagery pushed onto our Superheroes. Keep the religious stuff out of the films people. They ruin it. This isn't a Jesus movie. It's a superhero movie. Jesus doesn't have to be in every little thing.

5. The ship that has a kryptonian command key in it apparently talks in English instead of Kryptonian when asking Lex if he wants to assume command. It doesn't have a visual recognition system that can see that he's human, and the atmosphere in the ship is just fine for him. None of this makes any sense at all.

6. After superman's death, they go to the trouble of keeping his Clark Kent personality secret by releasing two obituaries in the newspaper, but apparently they have Clarks body for a military 21 gun salute funeral, while then burying said body in the graveyard with the rest of the Kent family instead of in a public monument. Also Lois and Martha are afforded places of honor following the body. The reason the comics always had Superman buried in a public monument after one of his many "deaths" is because you can't put him in the Kent plots, or have Martha and Lois get special positioning at the funeral without breaching his identity. Logic people. Use it.

7. Lex makes Doomsday out of a mixture of human and kryptonian DNA, but this doesn't make Doomsday weaker, no... It makes him stronger. Somehow.

These are just a few off the top of my head after watching. This is sheer idiocy. Stop with the religious imagery, stop with the religious undertones. Just make our freaking comics. Every time you introduce religious undertones and imagery, you introduce religious logic (or the lack of) as shown by the flaws that any child who is a fan could find.

It is the sheer lack of logic that makes this film the worst mainstream superhero movie in history. Yes, it is a fantastical world, no that doesn't mean all logic goes out the window.

title: Anyone who likes this is in severe denial.
review:

title: Its a different kind of film - Warning-Spoilers
review:
Film Noir is not for everybody and neither is this movie. If you like all of the components that go into a good Film Noire then you will find this a satisfying watch, Both of the heroes are right and both of the heroes are wrong in their perception of responsibility and power. Both heroes cross "the tracks," or in this case, the bay. Everyone has damaged characters and no one may unequivocally claim the moral high ground. In the end you are not provided with the answer--only, the seemingly unresolved question; this is the ear mark of a good Film Noir product. This movie was very well done and should be applauded for its execution of a provocative method of story telling that is its own brand of bittersweet tea.

The really well done noir aside, the action was over the top a little distracting towards the end of the movie. Every actor was well chosen for these parts.

title: A real movie based on DC Comics, not some drama that tries to use DC characters and butcher them
review: Ignore the critics on journalism and YouTube. Watch it without comparing it to the Marvel Cinematic Universe because the DC Extended Universe is a whole new breed of animal. Finally Warner Bros and DC has made a decent movie that is enjoyable. Batman and Superman in the big screen with Wonder Woman by their side. This movie is one things fans had been waiting for and finally got it. Unlike previous DC movies, this one actually has a DC Comics feel and is like watching the DC animated movies with a live-action cast. Ben Affleck was great as Batman. He has detective skills, a proper costume that does no look fake and a better voice. Christian Bale as Batman lacked detective skills and preferred to ask business partner Lucius Fox for gadgets fight villains, had an armored costume that looked fake and had a voice that sounded like a cross between a chain-smoker and an drunkard. He actually felt like Bruce Wayne out of costume, unlike Bale who felt like a male version of Veronica Lodge from Archie Comics. Gal Gadot was great as Wonder Woman and the costume looked perfect, despite not being the same colors as the comics. The plot is not as rushed as people think. The reason Batman hates Superman here is not because of the damage resulting in the death of many people, including the mother of a child that Bruce comforts at the beginning. That also explains that the Martha seen had more to do than their mothers sharing the same name. It was also bout how Batman realizes that Superman is also an average human being with family, not just a deity that would end up taking over the world. That would also explain the so-called "Knightmare" scene. It is how the two heroes fear their morality is at stake. That would explain Batman using guns and killing people and Superman having an army of followers. The death of Superman does not mean Superman is gone forever. The casket and grave shaking mean Superman is still alive as his Kryptonian anatomy makes it easy for his body to heal on Earth. A message to Lex Luthor haters, the one that appears in this movie is just the beginning. A lot of people complain that this Luthor felt less like Luthor and more like the Joker or Riddler. The cold and diabolical personality of Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor will be shown in later movies. That may also explain the shaved head at the end of the movie with Luthor having a more cold facial expression. Also saying that Lex Luthor here is totally butchered seem like hypocrisy because no one here says that Baron Zemo in Captain America Civil war or Penguin on Gotham is butchered, because they are different from the comics. The Doomsday here was very scary, scarier than any version used outside comics. A lot of people complain why The Flash's cameo was unnecessary and the movie is crowded with too many heroes. Other than Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman, the others were just cameos to set up for future films. Yet no one complains that Captain America Civil War is overcrowded, even though almost every hero who appears here plays a major role. They also do not seem to call Spiderman's cameo unnecessary, even though it is the same as the Flash. A lot of people complain it is too dark, it is too serious and lacks humor. BvS is based on some of the darkest DC graphic novels and DC cannot make a light movie aimed at solely entertaining children like Marvel due to failed attempts like Superman Returns and Green Lantern. Asp critic and Marvel fanboys should be careful what they wish for because the last time they complained a DC movie was dark, the result was Batman & Robin, which is one the worst movies ever made.

title: An epic battle
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice To be very honest, when the news of Ben Affleck as the new Batman first hit the papers, I was skeptical about the choice and the movie itself (more like cursing the person who casted him). But then again, being loosely adapted from Frank Millers classic comic, I eventually accepted it and thought I'll at least give the movie a chance.

With little to no expectation and sheer faith in the work of Snyder, I entered the theater with a fluctuating belief. The movie begins with a tragic opening sequence of Bruce's parents being killed and then cuts directly to the catastrophic and cataclysmically thrilling end sequence of Man of Steel. Only this time it's through the eyes of Bruce Wayne. What we see in this sequence, something which was ignored or missed out in the previous one is the consequences of Superman's actions.

Fearing his powers and his unknown intentions, Bruce decides to take on his formidable opponent. Meanwhile the people are struggling with the kind of hero it needs or requires. Zack intelligently uses the characters to move the story to an explosive end that will definitely blow your mind. He brilliantly manages to give us some subtle and some obvious references that will make your jaw drop on the floor.

Ben's portrayal of Batman was the one thing that I was very worried about. Not to question his acting skills, but will he be able to live up to the iconic portrayals of his predecessors was my one major concern. But to my surprise, he did manage to do a more than decent job (and by that I mean he manages to vindicate himself and does that with an aggressive flair). The main thing that works for him is the fact that he closely resembles Batman from the series. Zack does not waste much time in developing his character, as it has already been well established. But unfortunately for some who have not seen the character develop since its inception may not be able to relate to the tragic loss of his close friend (one of the subtle reference I was referring too). But I hope Ben's depiction of this damaged character will be enough for people to understand what he's been through. I'll leave the decision up to you.

Cavill's portrayal of a physically indestructible and emotionally frail character was already regarded as the finest by many critics. With the sequel he continues to play his role with the same honesty. The cast this time around also includes Jesse Eisenberg who plays the role of Lex Luther. Unfortunately for me, even after the movie ended, I could not possibly fathom why Zack offered him the role. He is a brilliant actor, no doubt, but he just did not fit into this role. Hopefully he'll prove me wrong in the later parts.

The person who surpassed my expectation was Gal Gadot. Surprisingly in a brawl which involves Superman, Batman and Doomsday, she enters with such a compelling charm and completely steals the show. Han Zimmer's score plays to stirring effects, and feels as epic as the movie it's attached to.

So to conclude, I really did enjoy watching this epic battle and the IMAX experience was just an added advantage. My advice to all those who are planning to watch it, please do not compare it to Nolan's trilogy. I have always advocated that nothing shall ever come close to being as brilliant and realistic as the version of the Batman depicted by him. And Bale shall always be the true Batman. But if you look at it as an individual, different from its predecessors, I'm sure you'll enjoy it.

title: Well I loved it
review:
I felt from the opening credits that the filmmakers were going for something a little more grounded in reality. In fact most of the movie feels as though it's more in the vein of multi-perspective stories like "Traffic," "Syriana," "Short Cuts," "Boogie Nights,"and "Magnolia." Despite jumping around from character to character and sub-plot to sub-plot, the scenes in those movies are all connected thematically and via the overall thesis of the plot. A lot of the criticism directed at BvS seems to be that it's somewhat of a mess, but I found it completely coherent, thoroughly entertaining, very well performed by all the actors, beautifully photographed, and Chris Terrio's script was imbued with wry humor throughout, which elevated this iteration well above the "on-the-nose dialogue" in much of "Man of Steel."

The film certainly takes a more adult sensibility in some of the points it wishes to convey: one particular scene came under critics fire because it shows Lois in the bath, then Clark hopping in and getting intimate with her... Not sure what planet these puritanical critics come from, but that's a perfectly natural scene when two people have strong feelings for each other. It seems they prefer the more infantile or asexual conveyance of love. The scene worked in immediately informing the audience of how far Lois and Clark's relationship had come since "Man of Steel." It also humanized Superman in a way that just a regular lovers kiss wouldn't convey.

Adding more to the adult nature of the film, is the bone-crunching violence, with Batman being portrayed with far more venom, and showing less mercy on criminals than in previous incarnations of the character; and just having the non-linear brand of storytelling trusts that the audience is mature enough to keep up... given some of the "mess" and "incoherent" criticisms, it seems a large percentage of them couldn't.

Overall, for me at least (and as someone who enjoys both Marvel and DC characters), Ben Affleck IS Batman, Henry Cavill IS Superman, Gal Gadot IS Wonder Woman, Amy Adams IS Lois Lane, Jesse Eisenbergh's tormented, unrecognized genius in Lex Luthor really worked for me, and Laurence Fishburne and Jeremy Irons really add some gravitas to their respective characters: Perry White and Alfred Pennyworth. Zack Snyder's visual style is stunning as always, and Hans Zimmers score really added to the brooding tension of the film.

I know I'm in the "out-group," but I really did love this film.

title: A great film that should of been called Batman And Superman: Dawn Of Justice
review:
First off, I just want to let people know that most people usually complained about usually such little things in the film that could of been easily ignored in their reviews, and it was a bit sad, because those little things were being used so the critics could rip the movie to shreds. However, if you ignore all the small flaws, you find that you will probably enjoy this movie a LOT. The action scenes are great, the plot was quite good too and the actors were a good choice (in my opinion). A lot of people will not agree with my opinion, but that doesn't mean that this review wasn't helpful to you, so please don't click that just because you disagree with this review. So, let's have a little talk about what other critics have been thinking about the film, and the negativity that I agree with, and the negativity that I (mostly) disagree with. Let's get started.

A few people thought that Wonder Woman was in the film for too long and that she didn't need to be in it that long. Myself, I completely disagree with that. She was barely in the film for 15 minutes (I think), and it wasn't really something to complain about. Wonder Woman may of not of been a necessary character, but she was pretty bad ass, and I actually kinda wanted her to be in it more. But, lots disagree with that. So, it's absolutely fine if you disagree. But anyway, Wonder Woman was a very good character in the film, and in my opinion I think she should of been in the movie for a bit longer.

Another silly thing that people complained about was that the movie was too dark. This is, in no way, a small flaw. It was also called "humorless" and "way too serious." Myself, I really like dark movies, and I really enjoyed this film because it was dark. No, it's not all bright and happy like most superhero movies, but it's at least as good as some. In my opinion, this is one of the best superhero movies I've ever seen, and most flaws could be easily ignored. However, a lot will disagree. But really, the film being too dark? That isn't a good enough reason to hate a movie, that's just a good enough reason to know how much of a wuss you are. You need to watch darker movies if you find this movie dark, because this is barely dark at all. Even if it is dark for a superhero movie, it's as dark as the trailers are. So, if you don't like the look of the trailers, don't go and watch this expecting a masterpiece. If you like dark movies, or if you can handle them, you'll then enjoy this movie. Still not sure? Keep reading.

Now here's one thing that people were complaining about in the film that should of been complained about: Batman didn't have a good enough reason to hate Superman. That is true, and it really did bug me in the film. Batman pretty much wanted to kill innocent people and then kill Superman just because he was saving the city and doing his job. Although I prefer Batman than Superman usually, I kind of rooted for Superman in this film, because Zack Snyder did a brilliant job of making us support Superman in the film. I mean, a great job. I think we were supposed to think of Superman as the good guy, because that's probably why Batman didn't have a good reason to be angry at Superman, and that would make us root for Superman. The film definitely made me root for Superman, and even if it wasn't a good enough reason to hate Superman, it was a great way to make us root for who Zack Snyder probably wanted us to root for.

Another thing that people complained about was because the film wasn't really a Batman VS Superman film. Yes, that is definitely correct. However, even if it isn't a Batman VS Superman film, it's a great Batman And Superman film, and it's a great prequel to the two Justice League films coming out soon. Also, if I haven't told you yet, this is a sequel to the film Man Of Steel, which was also a great film. The only flaw in the film Man Of Steel was that it could be a bit slower, but otherwise, I'd rate Man of Steel 8.1/10! But I am right now talking about this film, aren't I? Mhm, but do make sure you go watch Man Of Steel first before you go watch this movie, because this is basically a sequel. And I imagine the Justice League films will basically be sequels to this movie too. So, I guess what I am trying to say is that this film is criticized for stupid reasons. No, this isn't Batman VS Superman, but it is a great prequel to the upcoming Justice League films, and also a great sequel to Man Of Steel. I recommend you go watch Man Of Steel before you watch this film though, as it will explain a bit of the start of the film.

Overall, I think this film is very underrated review wise. Lots of reviews criticize this film for weird reasons, even though those reasons can be easily ignored. So far, the only flaws in my opinion in this film was that it could be a bit slower paced, and Batman could have a better reason to hate Superman. But that's pretty much the only things I dislike about this film. Overall, I rate this a 7.8/10!

title: Disappointing start to the series
review:
So before I saw this movie I read a few reviews and got the general sense that this wouldn't be good. Still I had some hope because it has Batman in it, and Batman is one of my favorite superheroes. I think for the most part this didn't come together as a movie to me. 75% of the movie was build and it was confusing because it wasn't done well. I can only describe this as a bunch of scenes, like ones that could have been in a trailer, but there was no tie-in from one scene to the next. The plot didn't all come together until just before the epic fight scene. The only good thing I can say about this part is that some of the scenes were pretty cool to watch, and the theme running through the movie was comprehensible and interesting.

This was the worst part of the movie I think. On the one hand, I could be sympathetic to Superman's dilemma, although not writing an article because you're bothered by Batman being mad at you looks suspicious. On the other hand I could only be so sympathetic to Batman's kill all aliens plight, and that sympathy ran out by the climax of the movie. During that epic fight scene, Batman looked really dumb. And as someone who loves Batman, I was not happy about this. Batman looked like a scared bro bully. I'd like to think that Batman was clever enough to see through Lex's setup, especially having met Clark Kent and then coming face to face with Superman and the fact that he hacked into Lex's stuff, but apparently he was not. Also while I saw the reveal of the mother's name thing coming, I thought it was a little too dramatic..

Finally the way the characters were portrayed were amazing. Wonder Woman was super awesome! I really hope they do a prequel movie with her, she was huge redeeming quality of the movie. Jesse Eisenberg was egotistical and awkward, but that's just the character he usually plays, and considering Lex Luthor's motives, it makes sense for him to be like that. I also really liked the way Alfred was portrayed in this movie, and that he had a bigger role. And Ben Affleck as Batman was pretty good. I don't think the way he played him made the movie worse off.

Lastly this really bothers me, but if a major character is going to die, like really kill him off. Don't have the last ten minutes sad and emotional only to elude to the fact that he'll be coming back in the next movie. It undoes all of the impact of that plot point.

Overall, I think as a superhero movie there's a higher expectation, and this movie just didn't meet it.

title: Big mess with pretty visuals
review: Batman v Superman is the long awaited movie starring Ben Affleck as Batman, Henry Cavill as Superman, and Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luther. Everyone has been expecting this movie for a really long time, even myself. The films plot revolves around Superman, and that many people are questioning if he is really a superhero or an alien that can destroy everything. And Batman is caught in the middle of this as in the beginning of the movie, superman was destroying buildings and basically the whole city (This was the ending of Man of Steel). I am not going to spoil a lot of you haven't seen the movie, but if you seen the trailers, you unfortunately know the whole plot and movie with some twists. Positively, Batman looks really good. I think Ben Affleck did a perfect job on portraying that character. His new suit look amazing, and he really did sold me as Bruce Wayne (Although I personally prefer Christian Bale). But i don't really know what the writers were thinking when Batman is seen as a killer and he steals. I really did not have a problem IF they explained why did he killed people and stole, but the movie did not really bother to tell the audience why Batman was doing this. The visuals are good, the CGI is great, and some of the battle sequences were great, no complaints there. Superman was fine, the actor made his role and he was kind off conflicted, the film does not really says much about that. All the actors were great with one exception. Lex Luthor is really annoying, everything he says does not make sense, he is trying to be the next Joker, but fails miserably. Jesse Eisenberg was a bad choice for him, and he was not an interesting character at all. The writing, the pacing and the overall plot is a gigantic mess. In the beginning of the film, it tells the back story of young Bruce Wayne, visuals aside, it was also really awkward as when Bruce falls to the hole with the bats, the bats start gravitating him??? I don't know what they were thinking, but it felt really dumb. Then the film puts the perspective of Ben Affleck and he starts seeing a city being destroyed and many die including a friend of him and his own building. Then the plot starts. It fells like there are WAY to many cuts. Like they made this film R rated but chopped down to be a PG-13 film. Then Lex Luther suddenly appears in his company, then Louis Lane, Perry White, etc. This is where the film starts falling apart completely to the ground. There is literally a 5 min little story for every character, Batman, then Superman, then Lex, then Louis Lane, Then Louise Lane, then the film becomes man of steel 2, kind of. It seems like they made Man of Steel 2, and then cut bits and pieces of the that film and put it in this film. The movie is so broken, that it feels like 4 movies at once and thats my biggest problem. It does not focus on one story, it focus on Batman with Alfred, then Superman and Louis, then Lex Luther (which in my opinion has one of the most awkward and uncomfortable moments I have ever seen in a movie), then some senate debate. It does not feel grounded, it fells broken and messy. Then the film does the very stupid thing (some) comic book movies do nowadays and Batman sends an Email to Wonder Woman, in which she opens certain files about the next movie Justice League. That was the most out of place and awkward scene in the entire movie. There another tie end scene with Flash telling him some information that does not make sense. The battle the movie advertises starts great, then good, then fine, to overdone, to really short. The fight last about 8-10 min. and it ends really stupid. The ending with the monster was really bad, there were like 3-4 moments in the entire final battle that felt bad-ass, and investing. When they beat it, it felt predictable and really corny. The inclusion of Wonder Woman was forced, I did not care at all when Superman died, and the final shot was so stupid and the most comic book movie thing to do to have senseless questions. There are some really good things but the bad things overcome the good and it feels broken, misleading. I loved the Batman scenes and the acting overall was good but it was so chopped up, i did not really know what was going on. 4/10

In this movie, just as in Man of Steel, Superman kept the fight in the city and caused ridiculous amounts of destruction, death, and suffering. He is just evil.

This movie is bad. Well, the stories are bad. The visual effects, special effects and stunts are awesome.

title: CGI Action V Quality Storytelling
review:
It's a shame this movie fails so profoundly at a storytelling level. It has a cast of good actors, although poorly directed, and some fantastic action moments, but the story, dialogue, and character arcs are so convoluted and disjointed it makes the action sequences nonsensical.

Before I criticize this movie's most basic cinematic failures further, I will say this, there are two awesome scenes in this movie. The first is Batman's infiltration of the enemy compound with choreography lifted straight from an "Arkham" video game. It gets close to some of the best Batman action on screen. Also, Superman's fight with Doomsday is nothing short of epic. In some moments it feels like a 90's Superman comic brought to life. Those two sequences were truly memorable moments on screen that I genuinely found enjoyable. It's just a shame that these moments are drowning in the sea of a poorly written, poorly directed movie.

At a very base level, this movie suffers from the same problem that Man of Steel did, which is character motivation. It's not clear why a lot of characters do what they do in that film or this. At times when character motivation glaringly needs to be addressed, a forceful beat will be thrown in that induces whiplash as it veers from the established narrative. This movie deals with misperceptions, manipulation, conspiracies, vengeance, and teamwork- all character driven concepts that are never established with much motivation at all. In fact the movie works hard to establish the motivation for the grudge match in between Batman and Superman, only for motivations to be switched, manipulated, and then discarded at the drop of a hat.

These terrible character arcs are done even more disservice by a disjointed, undeveloped plot. From start to finish this movie will have you scratching your head and even asking, "why did they put that in there?". There are countless misnomers, superfluous scenes, and straight up red herrings in the plot that are confusing and destructive to any semblance of a logical narrative. Jumps in time, dream sequences, subplot after subplot, and just random events with no exposition or explanation make this story as coherent as one of Jesse Eisenberg's speeches in the film. The existence of such bad plot and storytelling seems to be a product of the aforementioned flat character motivation. The plot tries hard to simultaneously create conflict and unity in between the two title characters, but it does so with the tact of a jackhammer, and the thoughtfulness of a goldfish. Add on top of that the countless other characters that are clawing for their own storyline and the mess just gets bigger and bigger.

The actors in this film do their best to make something out of nothing, that is make 3 dimensional characters out of 1 dimensional caricatures, but a bad script and poor directing leave all these actors out in the lurch. Jesse Eisenberg does make for an interesting performance as he combines a tad bit of Ledger's terroristic joker with an ADHD megalomaniac- but his performance becomes quickly tiresome as his actions continually beg the question of "why" and "what". Affleck is not the definitive Bruce or Batman as some may have buzzed. Instead he is a single note wrecking ball of vengeance that doesn't so much brood, but constantly boils with omnidirectional rage. Meanwhile, Cavil's Superman is a brick wall that, despite the brewing controversy over his god-like powers, is fixated only on Amy Adam's Lois Lane and an unrelated crime fighter named Batman in another city. At times Cavil's Superman addresses his public perception or the effectiveness of his heroism, but only as passing thoughts that almost seem out of place. Meanwhile Amy Adams is just bait for Superman, or at times convenient Superman apologist, and Gal Gadot's Wonderwoman is nothing more than a super-powered Deus ex Machina dropped from the sky that squashes any hope of this movie making sense.

At two and a half hours, this movie truly tests your patience as you try to follow the story, only to find that there isn't much a story at all to follow. The makers of this film were much more resigned to creating a seat-filling headlining bout and providing CGI spectacle than creating even the most basic of rational stories or characters. I once again can say, some of these action sequences are rewarding and greatly entertaining, but this enjoyment will quickly be pulled out from underneath you as the movie carries on and a character opens its mouth.

title: 3 hr Justice League Teaser Trailer
review:
The problem with BVS (batman v Superman) is not the dark tone nor the acting. The Problem came with few things like pacing, the constant back and forth from batman and superman scenes. These kept ruining the flow of the plot.

What failed this movie is the use of unnecessary dream sequences. Which did not make sense at all and there were too many of these, which slowed the pacing down a lot. Even Man of Steel felt like a better structured story than this.

What failed for this film is the build up content. What marvel did well is get the audience connected with certain characters by doing solo films then bringing in an ensemble film. Marvel did well by establishing its characters traits such as the rift between Tony Stark and Captain America through out their films which leads us to believing and understanding the nature of Civil War.

DC/Warner bros just tried to cram too much into one and expected the audience to connect straight away. Ended up being a 3 hour teaser for Justice League. Even the easter eggs felt forced upon rather than a tease.

Superman Felt Whiny and boring. Lex Luther felt like an annoying nerd getting revenge after being bullied in high school, Batman and Wonder Woman is where the film got it right. Ben Affleck perfectly executed the old aged war torn batman. Great action scenes showing him beat up thugs ruthlessly. i would love to see Ben Affleck as Batman again. Wonder Woman felt out of place in the trailers but when you watch the film she is one of the very few who does fit in the movie and leaves you wanting/pondering her place in this universe which gets you excited for the solo Wonder Woman movie.

Action: 6/10. (batman scenes were excellent, climax was visually great yet visually illiterate, CGI in some scenes was a let down, needed more Practical action)

Acting: 6/10. (0 for Jessie Eisenberg, 6 for Henry Cavil, 10 for Ben Affleck and 10 for Gal Gadot)

Theater Experience: 10/10. (watched it in Dolby Atmos Cinema, George St Sydney. The Surround Sound quality of Dolby Atmos really enhances the experience of the movie)

Value for Money: 5/10 (points only for the Dolby Atmos sound, the movie wasn't worth the money. Ticket price was $25).

Recommendation: Wait for the ultimate R-18+ DVD cut. Unless you really want to go and watch it on the big screen then go to a Dolby Atmos theater.

Overall Rating: 6.7/10

title: After watching the movie a second time..........
review: I had returned from my first viewing of Dawn of Justice, relatively satisfied with the movie, I thought the movie was great though I had minor issues with the pacing as well as editing during the first part of the move. However, I soon realized that my opinions were not the consensus, critics hated the movie, and while at that time I did not think the movie was perfect, I didn't understand why there was so much vitriol, especially since even among the critics there never was a clear idea on why they hated the movie. For example some said there was too much story others said too little. So when I went to watch it a second time, I took extra care to scrutinize the film, trying to understand the reason for the overwhelming negative reactions by critics. And I have to say I actually enjoyed my second viewing more than the first, what I thought to be sloppy and careless editing turned out to be deliberate. The story was not told in a linear fashion with the director choosing to switch between Lex, Bruce and Superman, their scenes are parallels of each other. The parallels are most pronounced after the bombing at Superman's trial. The scene where Bruce training in the bat cave is immediately followed by Luthor entering the birthing chamber. (They are preparing for war) After which these scenes are followed by Bruce and Clark both having conversations with their dead father/ father figure (mental preparation for the battle). Lex Luthor is a character I feel is wrongfully maligned, he might not be the Lex Luthor we remember from the old movies and the animated series, but I feel that he is still very much a compelling character. His actions are easily explained by two lines, "the greatest tragedy is to have knowledge without power, because that is paradoxical" this shows that Lex feels that he has all the knowledge in the world yet he lacks power, hence he resents the god-like superman. The second line "I have come to realize that God if all powerful cannot be good, and if God is all good he cannot exist" the latter statement is proved wrong, as Superman (a god-like entity) exist, however Lex can still prove the first statement, that if God is all powerful he cannot be good. Hence he forces Superman to bring him the head of the bat, to show the whole world that his view is right. I think it's interesting that Batman's line later in the movie "the only way the world would make sense, is if you force it to" also very much applies to Lex as a character. Another issue fans have with the movie is that the conflict between Batman and Superman was resolve to quickly. Except I don't think it has, Batman did not save Martha Kent for Superman, he saves her for himself, to right the wrongs of his past. When batman leaves, he states â€“ Martha would not die. He does not say your mother, or even Martha Kent. For a man haunted by the deaths of his family, perhaps this is just another way for him to find closure, and to save his mother, even if it's by proxy. At the end of the day, Superman v Batman, is by no means a bad film, all you need is to pay attention to the visual and verbal cues that would make the story make sense. I'm pretty sure if someone were to rearrange all the shots in the film, we could end up with a more conventional and less convoluted movie, but I rather like it the way it is. The movie forces you to think, the question certain choices and decisions, making the experience and engaging one. Additionally, the way the film is edited also makes it harder for us to predict what is going to happen next, several scenes in this movie genuinely surprised me (something that is pretty rare these days). The movie doesn't present everything to you in BLACK AND WHITE, but it's all there, you just need to observe and look closely.
