title: Disappointing, forgettable mess. Another Fantastic Four bore fest.
review:
The movie feels like watching a kid with ADD, rushing through setting up all the characters and jumping all over the place, and yet dragging on forever until we get to the fight scenes which I felt were too short.

Most of the conflicts in the movie can be resolved by opening their mouths and talking, but in a contrived plot device they don't. These 2 bad asses that should sympathize with each other are instead fighting each other without ever discussing anything. Everyone's motivation is either not developed or just outright dumb.

The other characters fall victim to the same problem. The US government sets off a nuke above the atmosphere with no casualties? I'm pretty sure the end of civilization as we know would produce some casualties. Perhaps it's one of those NON-EMP nukes of the alternate universe. Only takes the movie about 40 seconds to make that decision from order to launch. I'm not sure Armageddon can be started quite that quickly.

The other is moment that annoyed me was Batman taking 2 shots to the back of the head point blank and continuing to fight. Even if his outfit is bullet proof that doesn't prevent the kinetic energy of the bullet from hitting his head. The fool should be out cold, possibly dead.

Last point, Superman dying is undermined by the fact that he is an idiot, just give the cryptonite to wonderwoman or batman. Why on earth would he personally use it, basically reducing himself to Batman level and resulting in a pointless sacrifice.

The problem is that you aren't invested in any of these characters, they are so dumb it's hard to empathize with their actions. Without having a prior attachment to them as comic book fans may, I just didn't care.

I saw this in a private screening at IMAX with a full house of 500. There was no applause the audience was clearly disappointed, and only 8 people myself included stuck around through the credits to get the shaft.

My feeling on this one is 4/10.

title: Mixed feelings...
review: It's been almost half a decade since this movie came out, yet I'm still not exactly sure about how i feel about it. Unlike most i don't hate this movie. People are calling this the worst DCEU movie, but it's significantly better than both Suicide Squad and Justice League. First of all I actually like the casting in this movie with one HUGE exception that I'll mention later on. Aflec is fine as the caped crusader and Cavil is great too. The fight scenes are honestly good here. Directing and cinematography is ok (maybe a bit too dark at times but I'll allow it). I liked the Batman vs Superman fight (minus.. you know) and the warehouse fight scene with Batman was legitimately great and the highlight of the movie. I also thoroughly enjoyed the scene where Bruce Wayne tries to save as many people as possible in the Metropolis fight scene from Man of Steel. Love the perspective and it shows why Batman dislikes Superman rather convincingly! Also love how we got to see Batman actually do some detective work this time round and Wonder Woman fit into the scene nicely. However, there a ton of bad stuff as well, with the worst one being the plot which is honestly awful. Nothing makes sense! Lex Luthors plan is insane! So he creates Doomsday by combining his DNA with Zods... WHAT? Why would he do that? Why did the ship let him do that despite it being stricly forbidden? And how did he know that Doomsday would be the result? Also, when Lex framed Sups for blowing up the building... like how did people believe that? You think Superman needs to use a bomb to kill everyone? And Batman decided to team up with Superman cause their moms have the same names... The fight could have also easily been resolved if Superman just... told Batman that Lex had his mother hostage and that he and Batman had the same goal. The movie expects you to suspend your disbelief to a point where you might be permanently damaged in order to make Lexs plan work. Speaking of Lex Luthor! Jesse is a great actor but the way he portrays Lex is awful! That character has NO resemblance whatsoever with the actual Lex, in fact he's significantly closer to the Joker than he is to Lex Luthor (closer than Leto at least). The ending fight was also another meh CGI mess and only served to lay the groundwork for Justice League (and we all know how that came out). Supermans death was almost as believable as Black Panthers when he fell off the waterfall, everyone with a brain knew he'd come back as soon as possible. Lois Lane is also... there. They even brought Jimmy Olsen! Ofcource this movie is DARK and SERIOUS so ofcource he instantly died. And lastly Batman killing people is a no no. Batman does not kill, like that's his ONE rule! You can't disregard that! I like the attempt to make him be a dark characters, as that's what he's supposed to be. But he doesn't have to brand and kill people to prove that. All in all this movie is fun and has nice aspects to it, but the flaws are overwhelming! This is a movie people have been wanting to see for decades, and it deserved to be better. 4/10 from me.

title: Great action terrible storyline
review:
I really enjoyed Man of Steel when it came out in 2013 and when it was announced that Batman V Superman was being made I was hoping for the same level of action and destruction with a decent storyline that would connect the two characters together and form the DCU Justice League movie franchise with this as it's introduction and while it did kind of meet these expectations the end result was just a little bit off making it not the best movie or introduction to these characters working together and not the best introduction for Wonder Woman's character.

The movie tries way to hard to be cool and interesting with it's action and story and while yeah the action scene's when they actually start are cool and look visually stylish and impactful the story really let's it down with a ton of story plot holes that make it so the whole fight could of been avoided by just simply talking to each other but they never do because Batman just decides Superman has to die in a universe where he let's Joker live even after killing so many people and even Robin it's weak character building just to get them both to fight when in the comics they fight even when they have been allies for years.

The movies story is made up of a ton of different storylines from the comics and a few animated movies all glued together to make one unrecognisable mess with way too may sub plots it would of been fine if they just focused on the actual Batman V Superman part but instead it crams in Lex Luther, Doomsday, Wonder Woman, Lois Lane, a state senator and a storyline about people being afraid of Superman there's just so much going on in the movie that by the time Batman and Superman do fight your mentally exhausted from trying to keep up with the story.

Visually the movie looks amazing with great CGI and special effects the fight scenes are really fun to watch and are enjoyable but sadly it takes the movie forever to get to it.

Casting is almost perfect everyone expect Jessie Isenburg as Lex Luther because he just isn't the right person to play a character who's main traits are Technological genius, business tycoon, evil villain and is calm and confident nothing against Jessie Isenburg but he's a comedy actor not a dramatic actor and his performance alone makes this movie hard to watch.

I recommend watching this movie if your a fan of Superman, Batman and the DCU and the comics just don't expect the best interpretation of Batman V Superman because you will be let down.

title: Beautiful trash
review: A truly awful second film to continue the DCEU with. Zack Snyder is a visual director and the visuals in this film are truly beautiful surpassing Snyder's previous 'Man of Steel'. The effects mostly through the second half of the film are truly awful, as the final villain Doomsday looks like a failed ninja turtle. The story attempts to present itself as "Deep" but ultimately just doesn't make sense and is not executed well. Ben Affleck makes an excellent Batman and makes the character unique and his own in this interpretation, while Henry Cavill struggles as Superman to find good direction as his character barely says anything throughout the picture and is not an interesting hero to follow. The villain is extremely weak in that of Doomsday being a giant Cg mess and Jessie Eisenberg makes for an awful Lex Luthor channeling the character into a "Joker" type villain. Attempting to set up the entire Justice League into this movie makes it feel like another 'Iron Man 2' except it's not fun. The new sequel of Man Of Steel presents us with Batman v Superman:Dawn Of Justice. With Zack Synder once again at helm as director,the viewers are treated with what else? A visual spectacle and nothing more. Action fans will definitely be treated with 3D action sequences and a lot of violent scenes.Special effects are great and the appearance of Wonder Woman will definitely entice viewers in watching her own solo film.But that's all to it in this film.

Too bad that just like the first film,Batman vs Superman: Dawn Of Justice is once again style over substance. The screenplay is poorly written and the story is just too dark that Superman and Batman fans are treated to superheroes whose psychology are close to that of killers,psychopaths and people with personality disorder.That's right.Superman is still struggling into how much responsibility of doing good on planet Earth just like in the first film.He is still mixed up of either living a normal life with Lois Lane or being too altruistic in helping people that are in trouble.Meanwhile,Batman came out as a darker character which is far worse than the villains that he is up against like Joker,Riddler and the likes. Aren't these superheroes good and moral people who do good?Anyway,that's how they turn out here.The change on the character of Batman was definitely bizarre and outlandish that even many people would probably be surprised especially the long-time fans of the hero.And what about the logic in the story?How could Batman beat Superman?How absurd!!!!!The producers have to do it because Ben Affleck a bigger movie star compared than Henry Cavill. I hope not!!!LOL What's worse,the story is overlong and somewhat slow in its development.

Here is hoping that Zack Synder should start changing his approach on doing these superhero films and start doing things that would have the mainstream audience appreciate it.Or else,more fans would catch up with him especially if continues to turn superheroes into dark characters that are far worse than villains.

title: A hollow story presented in an explosion of special effects...
review:
This was a movie that had been long awaited by many. But I wasn't one of them, because I don't really care much about superhero movies and such. But still, I had the chance to sit down and watch "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice", so I decided to take out two and a half hours of my life to do so.

First of all, I must say that I was entertained by the sheer amount of action and destruction that there was in the 2016 Zack Snyder rendering of the two classic iconic superheroes. And it was presented to the audience in a myriad of impressive visual and sound effects. It looked so real, actually, and that was one of the most impressive things.

As for the story in "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice", well I can only say three words: are you kidding? This was one of the most shallow story lines I have ever had to sit through in a superhero movie. The story was so pointless and ridiculous that hadn't it been for the amazing CGI, then I would have gotten up and found something else to watch.

Essentially this was a movie about two self-centered and egotistical men who were crying to themselves and trying to show off who had the biggest... Well, you get the idea. And that was really a laughable storyline, and it surprised me that Zack Snyder was behind this movie after I saw how shallow the movie actually was.

The effects in "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" are off the charts. Literally, be prepared to be blown away. Especially if you have a good sound system. For me, then the visual and sounds in this movie was an overload of stimuli. It was amazing what the special effects and sound team had come up with here.

One thing that I had dreaded about the movie was Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman. I will say that he handled himself fairly well, although I can't really claim to be impressed. But still, he fared well enough and got the job done where it counted, but then again, he had very, very little to work with script-wise here.

While we are on actors, then I wasn't particularly impressed with the choice of Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. He just didn't strike me to be plausible enough for that role. It was like he was a spoof on the Lex Luthor character.

And as for this movie being the beginning of the Justice League, well, sure it was nice to see Wonder Woman back on the screen. But then again, that whole Justice League thing is wasted on me, as I don't really care much for superheroes.

But all in all, an entertaining enough movie for what it turned out to be. Just a shame that the storyline was as shallow and ridiculous as the sound and effects were impressive. "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" really could have been so much more with a better script.

title: Better than expected - don't believe all the critics
review:
This film has been unnecessarily panned, and is actually rather good - in parts. The dark, moody setting is atmospheric and otherworldly, and Ben Affleck's portrayal of Batman as a world weary warrior with PTSD is particularly good. I really think he should have been given more credit for his interpretation of the role, and it is easy to see how this is a development of the Christopher Nolan version, as the older Bat who has become scarred and sickened by the world he lives in. There are some good set pieces, and at times the film replicates a dark thriller rather than a fantasy adventure. There has been some criticism that there is a lack of humour, but I really don't think that matters as sometimes injected humour is just cheesy. On the negative side, apart from the BvS, the storyline is a bit scattergun. It feels as though it doesn't know what direction to take, is it a love story, a revenge thriller, an action film, a gods v monsters? As there are so many strands, the film lacks the depth that could have made it great, there are too many distractions and a thin main plot. The Wonder Woman character was good, but I wondered (haha) why she needed to be in it, other than as an advert for her forthcoming solo outing. Also, Lois Lane had little to do other than cast loving looks at Superman which is a shame as she is supposed to be a feisty character, and another blow against women in these films. I'd really rather they didn't bother creating a female role if all she does is look doe eyed and require saving most of the time. The inclusion of a LotR Uruk Hai as the boss enemy was lazy, even it's 'birth' was derivative, and Jesse Eiseberg's Lex Luther was just irritating and overdone to the point where he lacked menace.

Overall, a good film, if rather too long, which has been criticized undeservedly.

title: Messy storyline, and extremely dark and moody. 4/10
review:
Review: I made the big mistake by watching the ultimate edition of this movie, which was over 3 hours long, and the storyline was a right mess. There are numerous sketchy scenes, which just became annoying after a while, and the so-called superheroes, seemed completely useless. In the old movie, Christopher Reeves was able to rewind the world so he could save his loved one, Lois Lane but in this film, Superman just stood there while Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) blew up the court room, which caused loads of destruction. Also, was it just me or did Superman (Henry Cavill) and Batman (Ben Affleck) seem extremely miserable through the whole film? And why do these directors have to give Batman that awful voice. We don't get to see none of Batman's gadgets, which we have grown to love with the Nolan movies, because the whole movie is extremely dark, so the attention to detail isn't that great. Another negative aspect about the film is that the scenes seem to jump from one thing to the next, so the whole flow of the project was pretty bad. Doomsday also looked cheap and plastic, and the big question is, why the hell was Batman fighting Superman? There was a too many things wrong with this movie, and to top it all, who came up with the awful idea of Jesse Eisenberg to play Lex Luthor? Gal Gadot was great as Wonderwoman and we do get a glimpse of Aquaman, Cyborg and Flash, which is quite exciting in terms of the Justice League finally coming together but this movie is nowhere close to Nolan's brilliant Batman movies. I've never liked Henry Cavill as Superman, so the ending didn't really bother me and the chemistry between Jeremy Irons and Bruce Wayne didn't have depth, like Michael Caine and Christian Bale. Anyway, I won't go on about how bad this movie was, because this review will go on forever but on the plus side the franchise is left open for some special superheroes to take on the popularity of the Marvel movies, which are much better in my eyes. Disappointing!

Round-Up: With such a big budget, how the hell did Zack Snyder, 50, do such a bad job with this film. His first movie, Dawn of the Dead, came in 2004, and it made a big impact in the horror genre, and then he returned with the great 300 in 2006. In 2009 he brought the Watchmen to the big screen and then be turned to animation with Legends of the Guardians in 2010. Sucker Punch was his next project in 2011 and then he directed the Man Of Steel in 2013, which I really didn't enjoy. He's due to direct Justice League, which is in post-production at the moment, and there is even rumours of a Justice League 2, which he also will be directing. I just hope that he takes all of the criticisms of this movie on board, because if he makes the Justice League movies like this one, I've got a funny feeling that they also will be a right mess.

I recommend this movie to people who are into their action/adventure/sci-fi movies, starring Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg, Diane Lane, Laurence Fishburne, Jeremy Irons, Holly Hunter, Gal Gadot and Kevin Costner. 4/10

title: Misguided and unnecessarily dark.
review:
I was disappointed in the Theatrical cut of this movie. REALLY disappointed. But, I insist on having complete collections, so I bought it anyway. I was hoping the "Ultimate Cut", which is 30 minutes longer, would be better. But, I was not getting my hopes up. The following are my unedited thoughts.

SPOILERS AHEAD!

I actually like the whole prologue where Bruce is dealing with the assault on Metropolis firsthand. But, it begins to go astray as soon as "Jimmy Olsen" is introduced. I am a fan of Superman's Pal and I despise how he is treated in this.

Superman and Batman are supposed to be two sides of the same coin. Both fight for what is right, but one is bright and happy and full of life and color (Superman) and the other is dark and mysterious and remains in the shadows (Batman). In this , they are both figures of the darkness. There is no contrast. No distinction.

I like the interaction between Clark and Lois in the bathroom, mainly because Clark smiles, something he does not do as Superman.

I really wish Lex Luthor had been a self made man rather than a legacy. And how did he so easily convince the government to just give him access to the Kryptonian tech? He was not that charming.

Love Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman. She is charming and exotic and stunning. Because of her real life past in the Israeli Military, I know for a fact she could hold her own in a fight. I just wish she had more to do in the movie.

A big deal was made about actress Jena Malone being cut out of the Theatrical Version of the movie but being reinserted in the Ultimate Version. She had a few scenes and any other actress could have been cast and then cut and no deal would have been made.

Why does the Bat-Brand equal a death sentence? I would have thought that criminals would stand by each other over it rather than kill one another.

I do not understand Bruce's future dream. Was it a dream? Was it a premonition? Are they spoiling "Justice League"? Why was The Flash there before he was introduced as a character? The whole sequence makes no sense at all.

Batman does not use guns to kill. He uses them as a ballistics weapon, like a battering ram, not to put down criminals. He also does not run them over with the Batmobile.

I HATE that Superman did nothing during the Senate bombing. He could have at least been shown to try to save the people. He saw something was wrong but he did nothing but stand there looking sad. He is faster than a speeding bullet after all. He could have done more.

In the Theatrical Version, I wondered how Lex infiltrated the Kryptonian ship and used their tech so easily. In the Ultimate Version, they explain a bit more. I still don't like it, but now it at least makes more sense...kinda?

Why does LexCorps files on the other Meta Humans include their insignia? Some of them have yet to be active heroes let alone have Superhero Symbols. Also, even though we as an audience did not see it, Bruce had to have looked at the other files. When Bruce saw the file on Barry (The Flash), did he recognize him? Like, "Holy Crap! That is the dude from my dream!"

Kevin Costner did a better job as Jonathan Kent in one scene than he did in the entire run of "Man Of Steel".

I really don't get Lex's motivation to pit hero v. hero. Okay, he's a nutter, but there has to be more than that. To show Superman is an fraud? Why? What beef does he have with Batman?

"WHY DID YOU SAY THAT NAME?" So stupid. All is forgiven because their mothers are both named Martha. Ugh!

Doomsday. The character was created in the comics for one purpose, to kill Superman. It was also the first comic I read. So, the monster has a special place on my heart, because without him, I would probably never have gotten into this hobby. So, I am glad he is used in the movie for his intended purpose. But, in the second film? The audience had no real emotional connection to this version of Superman before he is killed. Big deal. And to be created by Luthor? Even worse.

Yeah, Superman dies. But so does Clark Kent. They show his funeral. This means, when Superman comes back, and we all know he will, he can never be Clark again. That, makes me sad. Because Clark is just as important as Superman.

What the heck was that thing standing before Lex when he gets arrested? I paused it, walked up to my television to get a good look at it and I still have no idea. Also, was Lex napping at that moment?

For the most part, I like the Batman scenes. They set the tone of the characters pretty well. It is the Superman scenes I have the most issues with. I kind of think that two directors would have been beneficial. One to film the dark and another to film the bright.

I am glad to hear that, because of the negativity around BvS, DC and Warner Bros. have changed direction on their films. Hopefully going forward they will be better. I mean, they can't get worse right? Right?

title: Please watch the Ultimate Edition!
review: This review contains spoilers! When I first saw the theatrical cut I felt the film was disjointed with several plot holes and insufficient character development. Then I learned that the version shown in theaters was not the entire cut of the film, that a half hour of the film was cut upon release. I decided to buy the Batman v Superman Ultimate Edition on blu ray and was pleasantly surprised. It was like night and day compared to the theatrical release. My opinion of the film changed drastically from being disappointed to loving the film. The ultimate edition makes the film flow so much more cohesively and allows for much more character development. It also fleshes out character motives so much better. For instance the Africa scene makes so much more sense where they were looking to frame superman for the murder and destruction that took place. Also Clark Kent does some reporting on batman and explores through Gotham discovering that batman has been labeled a "judge, jury and executioner" and brands his criminals with a bat symbol which ultimately is a death sentence while in prison. Clark also wrongfully discovers that batman has inmates murder these criminals while in prison. But this is a lie constructed by lex luthor in order to cause Clark/superman to hate batman for his seemingly cruel tactics. This whole aspect was cut out of the theatrical release which is a crime because it takes away from character motives. This also gives Clark Kent more screen time in the film. This edition shows how elaborate and planned out Luthors plan was and adds to his character. Another small part that was removed from the theatrical edition is when batman pays Luthor a visit in prison and says to him that he is having Luthor Transferred to Arkham asylum. There is no reason for cutting this it took maybe 30 seconds for him to say it and it adds more to the DC universe as well as appreciation for fans of the comics. Ben Affleck did a phenomenal job portraying an older angry and damaged batman which is the batman I have always wanted to see. Since this cut is rated R there are more violet scenes with more blood, heavier language and some nudity. Regardless of how great the ultimate edition is, there are still some problems I have with the film such as batmans motive to join superman. Ultimately I believe this film should have been broken up into two films. One called Batman V superman and the other being called Dawn of Justice. This Ultimate edition is really the only edition that should be seen by anyone who is a fan of these characters and the DC universe and it is a crime that it was not released in its entirety. Do yourself a favor and watch the Ultimate edition. I give the Ultimate edition an 8/10 and the theatrical edition a 6/10

title: It's for comic book fans
review:
Now this is a highly anticipated movie that got put down by a lot of critics. I personally thought it was a engaging movie that I appreciated the more I watched it. Now before giving a full review I was waiting for the Ultimate Edition of this movie to come out. Mainly because I wanted to give credit for this film in the fullest form. Since in the theatrical release, about 30 minutes was missing. Which made this movie look choppy in certain parts and lackluster because of the editing. And because bits and pieces that appeared to be missing that could have further explained things. Besides it showing Ben Affleck's butt cheeks, the Ultimate Edition shows more of Lois and Clark's journalism and investigative skills. With both of them trying to dig into what is really going on. With Lois trying to prove Superman's innocence and Clark trying to delve deeper into gaining information about Batman vigilante and what he does to some criminals. Which further explains why Superman was trying to stop Batman from what he does. Instead of it just seeming like it's just forced in there just to entertain and give the fans what they want to see. I however really liked the artistic imagery in this despite it having Zack Snyder's slow motion bits, but it didn't take away from this movie but was mostly used during the dramatic scenes. Mainly the dropping of bullets on the ground. The opening really got me pumped for what this movie was going to offer and for a movie that is around 2 and a half hours long, it flew by very quickly. I was also one of the guys that had doubts about Ben Affleck playing Batman, but the guy nailed it. Mainly because of his looks and built stature, it looked like he just walked straight out of the comic books. And the Batman fight scenes looked like it came straight out of the Arkham games. It was brutal and super entertaining to watch, it was simply badass. Christopher Nolan's Batman films did have phenomenal stories but it was the weakest when it came to Batman's hand to hand fighting. Especially in "Batman Begins" the action scenes is distracting and not well done at all. In this however the fight choreography is topnotch and Batman fights like I envisioned he would. Plus Jeremy Irons is awesome here as Alfred, he appeared to me more as a caretaker and a friend than just a loyal butler. Plus he doesn't take crap from Bruce Wayne and speaks his mind. I was so pumped for this film, mainly because it has two of the most iconic superheroes in one movie and they are going to fight each other. How can anyone not be pumped for that? Maybe, unless you don't like superhero movies at all. Anyways the extra 30 minutes does add to the story and makes things make more sense. However it does make it in a way where it takes quite awhile to get to the action scenes. I am pretty sure that is one of the reasons why 30 minutes of it was cut in the theatrical release. And because although it adds to explaining certain things and why certain characters act the way they did. It isn't all that engaging or entertaining to sit through. Overall I thoroughly enjoyed this movie and I wouldn't mind watching it again and again. This movie is basically a set up for the upcoming Justice League films and so they compacted certain elements for the set up. Which I thought didn't really take away from the whole experience. However if you are not a comic book fan and didn't read much of DC comics, you will be one of the audiences that will be sort of confused with certain characters and set ups. The superheroes really needed there own individual movies to add more value to the characters and to what was going on, besides "Man of Steel". Gosh, Lois Lane has to be the ultimate damsel in distress, she gets saved like 3 times by Superman. Lastly when it comes to Lex Luthor it is a mixed bag when it comes down to it. I personally was fine with it, Jesse Eisenberg acted in a very odd and uncomfortable kind of way. You know the type of person you would stay away from at work, except that he is a Billionaire with a lot of power at his disposal. His version of Lex worked, because most Billionaire tycoons that has a silver tongue is more interested in making money over delving into the whole Superman ordeal. Yeah, he did remind me more of the Riddler, but his very odd and uncomfortable facade for the most part worked in this movie. Because it made his drive and insanity more believable. So yeah, this is a engaging superheroes movie with some cool imagery that is worth checking out for sure.

8.8/10

title: Dawn of Justice League and nothing more
review:

The epic battle between the most Iconic superheroes ever, hopes were sky high till the critic reviews started showing up. Hopes fell from sky to the mud. Still unlike many others I believed in Zack Snyder who gave us Watchmen and Man of Steel ( For me Mos worked as a good action packed psychological drama). But from this I have to say Snyder's best comes out when he is adapting directly from an existing comics story line ( like Watchmen and 300).

As of BvS Batman is experienced and brutal who blames Superman for incidents in Mos and doesn't want such a power to go unchecked. Superman continues his services to the world while having relationship with Louis along with having lots of moral conflicts. Lex Luthor is basically a psycho who is rich and brilliant but a character that didn't create any impact.

Henry Cavill proved himself as the definitive Superman in MoS and now Ben Affleck shows that he is one hell of a Batman even though he was basically a Villain here.

The showstealer is obviously Wonder Women. Making her a mysterious character throughout and giving a mind-blowing entry in the last battle, even if you didn't like this movie you will be definitely waiting for the next Wonder Women solo movie.

The plot which basically everyone knows is made weaker by stuffing a lot in it without making it feel like having a connection with everything. If at-least there was some more action in the first half rather than stuffing it all together into the last hour the movie could have been more entertaining.

While BvS doesn't meet expectations it doesn't really give the upcoming movies in the DCEU a bad impression because one of the main problems of this movie was that it was making too much ground for the next movies without having its own.

From lot of glimpses we get from here regarding next installments, they are really hopeful. It's like they showed the complete story in the trailers and gave the movie which acts as trailer for a bunch of new movies.

title: A beautiful, unamitaged mess. But it is really beautiful
review:
Just a preface, I haven't seen Man Of Steel, mainly because I disagreed with the concept of making a dark Superman - not because Superman can't be in "dark stories the way Batman is", because a lot of the time he is - but because of Superman's super-powered boy scout personality makes him as dark seem inappropriate. Nevertheless, I saw this because I love Batman and I love his story lines, and I can say without a doubt that the Batman stuff in this movie is the best things in it.

There are three positives that I can truly get behind: Ben Affleck and his performance as both Bruce Wayne AND Batman, the music score, and the action scenes. Everything else is super mishandled.

The biggest problem with this movie is that it seems that Zack Snyder, David S. Goyer AND even Christopher Nolan came up with absolutely nothing close to the characters they were creating, and one particular character comes off REALLY bad: Lex Luthor, in this movie, is a F***ING JOKE! I know they were going for something different, but this feels like a really cynical attempt to be a Heath Ledger as The Joker type thing. However, whilst The Joker was a original take on the old classic character, he still retained the trademark characteristics and fitted in the Universe. Eisenberg's Lex doesn't, and it cripples the film. Is he a scheming genius? Kind of, but his plan is so contrived that doesn't fit. Is a charming man? Nowhere near. Is he bald? At the end of the film, yes, but the rest of the time his hair is even longer than normal. Is he confident? Actually they take this too far - this Lex is fearless as hell, but it borders on Joker levels of fearlessness, and that was also distracting. Does he think super far ahead for every outcome? NO; he makes Doomsday to kill Superman, without ANY plan for what would happen if Doomsday won. In fact, Doomsday's first thing is to attack Lex but Superman stops him. It's not totally Jesse's fault, as this is the character they were going for, but if so, an actor like Joseph Gordon-Levitt would've been someone who CAN portray charm, scheming and confidence.

Superman is also poorly handed, as Henry Cavill gives no charm or charisma to the character, who also acts totally outside of the Superman way. He has no reason to be angry that Batman kills, because in one scene, he flies a guy in jeans and a t-shirt through a brick wall to save Lois. Fact: that guy died.

This is a movie made for the fans, but it falls apart so quickly under analysis from even the passing viewer: it drags too much, characters aren't really the characters and the casting choices were so bizarre - but to be fair, two of those casting decisions worked well, one of them didn't. They mishandle so many thing about the film, including the ending, which didn't have the emotional weight behind it that it needed. But I am glad I saw it - I just wish I liked it more than I did.

title: Could have been better but still packing a punch
review:
I rather enjoyed "Man Of Steel" - the latest rebooting of the Superman franchise - so I was looking forward to the sequel but, by the time I was able to see it at the cinema after an extended period travelling abroad, the critics had given it harsh treatment, although audiences had been kinder and it had already managed to recoup its estimated budget of $250M.

When the sequel was first publicised, friends of mine queried how this would be a genuine contest of rival superheroes since Superman has all the powers in the world (OK, out of this world) whereas Batman has no actual special powers but, of course, the explanation was in the clip at the end of "Man Of Steel": it is kryptonite that levels the playing the field.

Again Zack Synder is director which means that visually the movie has lots of terrific- looking scenes. The problem is that the narrative zig-zags all over the place, providing back story for the two main characters and scene-setting for a range of future characters as well as the central story of a conflict between two men who are both misunderstood and misunderstanding. This is a work of excess: too noisy, too loud, too serious, and at 151 minutes way too long.

This is a pity because the movie opens strongly with a revisiting of the concluding battle of "Man Of Steel" seen from the ground's eye view of a Batman who is bitterly critical of Superman's God-like powers which cause so much death and destruction.

But then there are so many themes running into each other: the romance between Superman (Henry Cavill) and Lois Lane (Amy Adams), the relationship between Batman (Ben Affleck) and his butler (Jeremy Irons), the emergence of Wonder Woman (Israeli- born Gal Gadot), and not just one really bad guy but two, the underdeveloped character Lex Luther (Jesse Eisenberg) and his weird (unnecessary) creation who is a kind of super-giant King Kong without the fur or the sensitivity.

This may be a film that stands taller in the future: if you expect less and understand more, it may feel more satisfying and, if it turns out to be a platform for a Justice League franchise, then DC Comics will be happy.

title: Tried really, really hard to like it. I guess I finally did.
review:
There's a lot going on and a lot that I could write about but the big thing that has stayed with me is Affleck's performance. After the Dark Knight trilogy, this was a daunting role. I had read that Affleck was cast in part because of his physical stature. Christian Bale is a lean 6' tall. Affleck has a broader build and is nearly 6'4'. That may not sound like a big deal but it really is. Because this movie accomplished what I didn't think was possible - it made Bale's Batman look dated and underwhelming in hindsight.

My favorite element to the movie is the emotion brought to Bruce Wayne. In the Dark Knight trilogy we saw Wayne's dark past drive him to become Batman. In this version, we see Wayne as a haunted and tortured soul. Rather than "rising" up to be a hero, it feels like he is on a downward spiral and doing good while he still can.

Overall, there were lots of elements to the story that were really a stretch or predictable. We knew the characters would end up in a big fight. We knew Kryptonite would play a crucial part. We knew they would end up best buddies afterward. It's difficult to have a truly great story when so many elements are obvious going in. Snyder did well enough, but not great.

I was skeptical of Jessie Eisenberg. He's proved time and time again to be a great actor but I initially worried he was miscast. The first couple of scenes didn't alleviate my concerns but by the end I felt he really brought something new to the role and was one of the standouts.

It's one of those frustrating movies where it's easy pick it apart. I wished this and that had been better, or this element had been different. Still, I think it's a good movie and am excited to see where they go from here.

title: Too much too soon..

Batman Vs Superman

Okay.. I must break my silence.

Let's see..um.. Batman Vs Superman. Let me start off by saying awesome visuals. The initial build up of the film is so great. I had a feeling that the whole body of the film (Much like it's interpretation of Doomsday) wouldn't be as strong as it's head.

Many people have asked me how was Ben Affleck in the film? Did he drop the ball? Drop the ball??? First off Ben Affleck is a fine established actor and director and has been around longer than most of the cast except for maybe Laurence Fishburne and Jeremy Irons.

Besides..Batman isn't that far of a stretch from Daredevil. (That's right. This actor played both). Although it wasn't the best of superhero films, but this wasn't Ben's fault. It was Sony's, the director, producers, and whoever thought it was a great idea to cast Jennifer Garner as Electra's fault! (I love her though. Just not as Electra).

Alright, the other thing is I'm not sure why Batman is actually killing people. Maybe he's finally had enough and decided to become the Bat- Punisher and take people out for good.

The story started out well and ends up all over the place. It's hard to tell where it is going. I personally think they decided to cramp too much into one film. One of my buds said that he thinks that Doomsday looks perfect. I was like "What film were you watching?" I'm more of a Doomsday fan than Supes and I think they just wanted to put a monster in it that looked like Godzilla 2000 and one of the beasts from LOTR and said "Hey, let's call this Doomsday!"

His treatment to the big screen was equal to Spiderman 3's Venom and Monster Sandman as well as Amazing Spidey's Lizard! Hell the Krakken from Clash of the Titans remake looked more threatening than the film version of Doomsday (who happened to be missing the white hair and much spike detail by the way).

Wonder woman had some good cameo scenes but was under utilized. Here are two things that really bothered me. 1. How is it that the greatest detective in the world who studies all of his enemies before battle, not know the names of his enemies' parents.

Interesting enough, he somehow knows that kryptonite kills him? 2. If Clark Kent's body is in his wooden coffin, who's body is in the black Superman coffin?

I could ask how does Superman always know when and where to show up, but we've been saying this for years. Well, it's still a visually stunning film overall and worth a treat. Hope I didn't kill it for anyone. Agree or disagree. I've stated my piece. I await Captain America: Civil War now. "Please Don't f this up!!!"

title: ...if you like comic books
review:
...then imagine one being adapted to film and you will probably see what the director and writers aimed for with this one.

Translating Superman to the screen is not easy, we all know, but MoS was heading towards something promising. It wasn't perfect and fell out of hand in the 2nd act but it planted a direction worth exploring. Most of which was thanks to Nolan I think. BvS wishes to continue on that path, it just goes too fast, too flat from the start.

A few thoughts on the negatives..

Instead of going trough another Batman origin (should saved that for the stand alone), we should have experienced better character development. Instead of Batmans dreams/visions, again, more character/ plot development. Because the plot holes are many and the characters only seem to have agendas because the director told them.

Why was Lex Luthor so excited about C.Kent and B.Wayne meeting at his party? Wayne is a celeb yes but Kent? and why should their meet mean anything. A billionaire and a journalist. Would have liked to see Lex plot things a bit more,

B.Wayne wants to kill Super because of "thousands of lives lost"+ "Jack"? Yeah, but he kind of saved the world from total destruction. Suspect his power sure, but investigate the guy a little, not just "he must die" from the jump. And later on it's all good because our mothers share the same first name.

Superman does not seem to care who ends up as collateral damage, as long as it's not L.Lane. He is not thrilled about using his powers to save his mother, it's better to fight Batman. Best hour spent ever. He can't pick up a spear with kryptonite out of water, but he will fly with it when mad?

The other metahumans exist on earth without any explanation, (maybe saved for JL stand alone) but still, they simply exist for some reason (W.Woman) and B.Wayne reasons they are good guys he needs to team up with. Why does he not suspect them and their powers too?

J.Eisenberg's Lex Luthor, a great actor going 80mph the wrong way. His fault, the direction, writing, I do not know. It is over the top, feels no way evil menace, more, I want to try to create what Heath accomplished. Almost every scene is cringe apart from a few where he somehow manages to tone it down slightly.

OK.. more is to be found wrong in this pic, but let's look at the positives..

Batfleck works without hesitation! Ben does well as both Batman and Bruce. Solid!

Music, not sure who did what, Zimmer or Junkie, but, few times the music comes off fantastic! Last scene/ end credits and often when Batman is on.

Supporting cast in general, everyone delivers (except Eisenberg) and holds their part of the deal.

Shots, many shots and close ups are beautiful! Cinematography is stunning at times( when it's not overblown by effects)

Sum it up- as a straight comic book movie it succeeds, but as an intelligent and deep adaption of a comic book to film it fails miserably.

title: Good, not great
review:
Batman v Superman is a visual masterpiece. The first 10 minutes are in my opinion some of the best filmmaking ever created, although the feeling does not last.

Batman v Superman is a good movie, but not amazing by any stretch. There are obvious flaws later on in the movie, from an editorial/directorial standpoint.

The film looks fantastic, but the story lacks substance at various points. Critically, I understand why this movie is unsuccessful, neglecting the origins of the characters and watching it as the movie it is.

Now, I am a comic book fan. I am one of the people who really enjoyed Man of Steel, and I would say I enjoyed Batman v Superman less.

I feel a large portion of reviews displaying Batman v Superman as the "best superhero movie ever" are not accurate, due to the reviewers previous love or attachment to the characters clouding their judgement.

In my opinion, there were comic book story lines that were "wasted" in this movie, story lines that would have worked much better in an experienced universe set up with much more character development. I thought Batman and Superman are both mischaracterized by this film, whereas Wonder Woman is not prominent enough in this movie to develop a solidified opinion of her character traits, which will be explored further in her solo movie next year.

Overall, the film had exciting elements that had me jumping out of my seat at some points, although the flaws were strong enough to cause it to lose its spectacle.

I do recommend that everyone sees this movie and forms their own opinion, because it is a film that will divide critics and fans alike.

title: An Excellent,Thrilling And Gripping Superhero Film.
review:
Batman V Superman:Dawn Of Justice is an excellent,thrilling and gripping Superhero film that combines terrific direction,a wonderful cast,amazing Action and a memorable score. All of those elements make Batman V Superman:Dawn Of Justice Batman,Superman,Superhero films and Comic Book films at their best.

Set 18 months after the events in Man Of Steel,Batman V Superman tells the story of Batman/Bruce Wayne(Ben Affleck)who is angry about the destruction of Wayne enterprises and lives that were lost and blames Superman(Henry Cavill)for it. Now,Batman wants to destroy Superman at all costs.

Batman V Superman:Dawn Of Justice is a terrific and very entertaining Superhero movie that after many solo feature films we finally saw two of the most iconic and famous Superhero in Comic Books and Pop Culture in Batman and Superman in a once in a lifetime showdown between the two famous figures. This is a movie that has been sharply and very harshly panned by critics and has And I'll admit while the movie is far from perfect and will not be for everyone this film in my opinion is one of the best films with both Batman and Superman and if you are a fan of either one of the characters or both you will enjoy this film. Batman V Superman is an amazing film where it shows the two worlds of Batman and Superman colliding on an big scale that grabs you from start to finish giving viewers a dark comic Book movie,an Action movie and character study for 153 minutes. What director Zack Snyder has done with the the film is incredible because It's an epic movie in story and scope giving us basically a Man Of Steel sequel,a Batman movie and a set up for a Justice League movie all in one continuing the story line from Man Of Steel while giving us something new and introducing another famous and iconic Superhero and Comic Book character in their first feature appearance. We get everything in this movie the Batman signal,Superman flying,fight scenes,Action and other things In BvS there is never a dull moment throughout with Action and Drama happening and never stopping until the very end. This movie while about Batman facing off against Superman is also about the two dealing with themselves and what they do in a complex and psychological way. With Batman/Bruce Wayne we see a man who is still haunted by the death of his parents and the destruction of Wayne enterprises and the people inside of the building and having nightmares(which are used in the film very effectively)and trying to get back at Superman at all costs. With Superman/Clark Kent we see him dealing with the idea of being seen as a hero or a villain to the people as well as himself while trying to find out who he is. The film explores the gray area of what is a hero and what is not a hero in a fascinating way. When the two finally face off and fight it's easily one of the best if not the best moment in the whole movie and will have you cheering at the screen. The Action and fight scenes are dazzling and stunning whether it's the Batman V superman fight or other Action scenes which keep you glued to the screen. The ending of Batman V Superman:Dawn Of Justice is outstanding with tons of Action,thrills and surprises that is fitting for the movie. A solid conclusion.

The cast is great. Ben Affleck is excellent as Batman/Bruce Wayne,with Affleck being gritty,tough and intense. Henry Cavill is brilliant once again as Superman/Clark Kent,with Cavill bringing depth and power to the role. Amy Adams is terrific and beautiful once again as Lois Lane,Superman's love interest. Jesse Eisenberg is delightful as Lex Luthor,the evil villain. Gal Gadot is great and sexy as Dians Prince,a mysterious woman. Diane Lane(Martha Kent),Laurence Fishburne(Perry White),Jeremy Irons(Alfred)and Holly Hunter(Senator Finch)give good performances as well.

The direction by Zack Snyder is fantastic,with Snyder bringing and effective and gritty atmosphere to the film. Amazing direction,Snyder.

The score by Hans Zimmer is outstanding,intense and moody,going nicely with the tone of the movie. Great score,Zimmer.

In final word,if you love Batman,Superman,Comic Book films or Superhero films,I highly suggest you see Batman V Superman:Dawn Of Justice,an excellent,thrilling and gripping Superhero film that is worth your time. 9.5/10.

title: Expectation v Reality: Dawn of an exciting universe
review:
I was waiting for this movie for a long time. I would have caught it on the first day but I was traveling so I had to wait for almost a week. Meanwhile, the internet exploded with negative critical reviews and contradicting public reviews. I am glad that I chose to decide for myself. This is a good movie, not a perfect movie, but a good movie which never bored me for the entire two and half hours.

I loved the setup for the Justice league, that's something people should watch this movie for because Justice League is happening whether you like this movie or not. I also liked the score, it's brilliant. Most people seem to have enjoyed wonder woman, however I liked her as Diana Price more. Her wonder woman avatar needs more exploring and I am now convinced that Wonder Woman solo movie could be good. Gal Godot looked gorgeous but her acting skills didn't shine in the short time she was given. I hope she won't disappoint in her solo movie. The rest of the Justice League cameo were also great. I liked Ben Affleck as batman, however there wasn't much to chew on his role. The chat between him and Jeremy Irons' Alfred was very well written. Those who said there was no funny moments in the movie should listen to their conversation carefully. Henry was Superman was OK. He was paired with Amy Adams who is a fabulous actor and I wished their acting skills were equally matched. Jessy's interpretation of Lex Luthor isn't a subtle guy I remember from the animation but his character is developing to a darker shade, so it's too early to pass judgement on him. Finally, the story is simple, which I like if the focus is the characters rather than story itself. Absolutely no complaints there.

Moving on the the negatives, this movie isn't mind blowing in any way, it's entertaining but that's it. I guess people expected too much from this movie and that's why they were disappointed and hence the negative reviews. There's also the problem with Doomsday. One, he was CGI, so he didn't look menacing enough. Two, the context for creating Doomsday was not developed(may be it is, in extended cut) so you never know how dangerous he is and what's his motive. Same goes for Lex Luthor. Lex was evil, but why he was evil was not explored. I therefore consider the third act to be the weakest. The final showdown of trinity didn't have much stake. I feel pity for DC, when they had the final fight in the city(Man of Steel) people complained about too many casualties and now the fight is in such a way that there's isn't even much stake to it. DC need to find the right balance for creating good stakes.

I don't agree with people who said that there was editing and coherence issues. The story was non-linear but it's not difficult to understand, when things are happening in parallel and when there is a flashback. If you think Momento was an editing mess then this movie is probably too difficult for you to understand. It wasn't funny movie, but you could certainly admire some witty lines. I understand when people say it wasn't fun (they didn't mean haha funny but some cool moment that can bring joy, smile or tears) and I completely agree. DC need to work on creating those moments. Al though I don't think Marvel movies have those moment either anymore, but that's not how you decide quality of movie.

Batman V Superman is a good movie, an enjoyable movie but it's not "The Dark Knight". It doesn't move you emotionally, thought it tries hard. In my opinion, it's a better story than Deadpool which was just a compilation of funny dialogues. Looking back, I think DC should focus more on creating movies like 'Batman Begins' than the 'The Dark Knight'.

7.5/10

title: Spoilers and F-bombs

There are only a few things that save this movie: Wonder Woman's badassery, the cinematography, the fight scenes, the dark Batman, Jeremy Irons, and the casting of Superman. That's about it. I didn't hate this movie, but it was such a mess that I turned to my friends multiple times in the theater and was like "What the f* is going on?", and they asked me the same thing. I don't usually do that, because I like to wait until the movie can explain itself, and I consider myself an intelligent audience that can eventually catch on. But it's been a few days and I am still asking the same question.

Let's start from the beginning. The movie starts with a kind of montage of the murder of Bruce Wayne's parents. And then the dad falls down and whispers "Martha" in his last breath (addressing the dead mom). Then it shows the kid Bruce at the funeral, running and crying, until he falls into a hole in the ground with a cave (like in every Batman back story). I was okay with everything up until this point because EVERYONE knows the Batman origin story so there's really no need to spend a half hour on it. But then, kid Bruce sees a sh- ton of bats, which then start flying around him (like in every Batman back story), and then the kid STARTS TO F*** FLY. Yeah, I know it was a dream and I figured it was in the theater, but I was laughing; my friends were laughing; there was chuckling in the theater. THERE WAS NO NEED FOR THAT. Who wants a f*** dream sequence anyway? Who personally walks up to Hollywood directors and asks for more f*** dream sequences? Please tell me, I need to know. Who genuinely wants to see something that changes the plot or adds something interesting to the story, and then have it to all just be a dream? But, I digress. I would have preferred that the whole back story opening sequence was taken out; it set a really goofy tone for a serious movie. But nonetheless, the producers needed the sequence so that daddy Bruce can whisper "Martha" for a plot point at the end of the movie. There is a time jump to Metropolis, where Superman is fighting General Zod (it's during the same time line as Man of Steel), and they are destroying the city. And in all the chaos people are being crushed by falling buildings and cars and are dying. Bruce, now big Bruce, is upset at this because I guess all this death is Superman's fault (totally not the douche Zod who wanted to start a f*** intergalactic war, but I understand that Bruce could have misinterpreted the situation). title: Critics reviews do no justice
review:
For a start, let me say that although I am a vivid Batman fan, I can still see the movie's shortcomings and after all the hype, I felt let down a bit after 1st viewing (2nd viewing was more enjoyable) Yet, 28% on RT is absolutely out of touch with reality, putting the movie on par with My big fat Greek wedding 2 and London has fallen. Moreover, the movie was always doomed to suffer from Nolan's trilogy comparisons which do not make much sense as the two universes as vastly different. I've mostly enjoyed the movie and though I've listed a lot of cons, most of them did not bother me that much.

Pros

● Ben Affleck as Batman- nailed it 100%

● Darker batman, brutal, makes you wonder if he is a good person at all (even the killing part works for me)

● Superman vs Zod fight from human perspective

● Batman vs Superman fight (should have been longer though)

● Batman rescuing Marta K. - great fighting choreography

● Lex Luthor Jr. presentation let's not forget this is NOT Lex Luthor but his son

● Perry White - all of his lines were spot on and very well executed

● Alfred

● Wonder Woman - great introduction and short on screen time, we will get to see more of her in WW

● Knightmare

● The score- used quite appropriately on all places

● The cameos of Flash, Aquaman, Cyborg were awesome. It was NOT needed to see more of them in this movie.

● Last scene between Luthor and Batman was great with Luthor warning of an impending threat

● Many scenes/shots were taken directly from comics- and worked very well, particularly Superman's power literally sucked out of him after the nuclear bomb in space

Cons

● Thomas and Martha Wayne's deaths could have been omitted, we've seen that too many times, the nightmare with the giant bat was enough proof of Bruce's torment

● Superman stopping batman when the latter is chasing bad guys; the very scene would have worked much better during a different time of the movie

● Flash appearing to B. Wayne- unnecessary addition to an already convoluted plot

● L. Lane getting the spear to help the Trinity; she was not aware of its potential. Batman should have got that, his participation in the final fight was limited anyway

● Luthor outsmarted everyone far too easily but I can bite that as Wayne and Clark were going through a lot of emotions and had clouded judgments already

● The scene where sen. Finch visited Luthor to tell him about the restriction on the kryptonite import (though there were some great lines)- Luthor imported it anyway

● Should have built more towards Batman vs Superman, showing Bruce preparation more, maybe even building the exoskeleton

● Batman realizes Superman is not a threat far too quickly. We could have had a few moments/scenes earlier in the movie with Bruce genuinely wondering if he is right about Superman

● Doomsday fight (not that bad but just way too much for one movie) Should have had Batman vs Superman as climax

● Doomsday could have just been shown at the end (moving inside the cocoon) and have the fight as an opening/mid scene in JL1

● Forced ending, too many story lines in the last 40mins

Overall, the movie was quite enjoyable and though it did not live up to its immense hype, I am confident the next DCCU movies will fare better!

title: A super serious event thats big showdown will leave many wanting
review:
After the huge successes of Marvel's superhero heavy ensemble double hits of Avenger action, DC comics have finally joined the Box Office party with their long gestating Batman and Superman team up, only thing is this time it's hero v hero, so don't go in expecting any tea party's between these two cape clad gentleman.

After the relative disappointment of Zack Snyder's previous superhero event Man of Steel it wasn't surprising that despite the big battle between comic book legends being touted, B v S was subject to much debate from day dot with many fearing this event would be an overblown CGI spectacle like Man of Steel was and when Ben Affleck was officially announced as the one to fit into the capped crusaders suite the hate campaign towards this film really ramped up.

Days into the films official release worldwide it seems as though the hate campaign isn't going away any time soon and although the films struck gold at the Box Office the world over there seems to be a great divide between the fans and the haters with some critics tearing strips off the overblown superhero smackdown, whilst others have lapped up every minute of Snyder's unwaveringly serious take on a no doubt silly excuse to set up the Justice League period of the DC film cannon.

B v S is neither in my books a complete failure or a raging success, it's another frequently frustrating film from a filmmaker that gave us the brilliant Watchman and the terrifically entertaining 300 and Dawn of the Dead yet has delivered turkeys like Sucker Punch and the aforementioned mediocre Man of Steel and B v S feels like another half film from Snyder, who as a director remains visually strong yet has shown increasing weaknesses as a storyteller.

Working from a script that was co-written by Argo scribe Chris Terrio, even at 150 minutes or so in length, B v S finds Snyder on more than one occasion finding himself lost in a character loaded plot line that can at times bore us to tears and even the titular versus match that takes place (after one of the longest build ups in cinematic history) is a fairly disappointing affair and there are numerous times B v S is edited in a jarring and ineffective manner suggesting a struggle in the editing suite to get the tone right.

Looking past Synder and into B v S cast we have an improved performance from Henry Cavill who still leaves a little to be desired as Superman/Clark Kent and in his first official outing as Bruce Wayne/Batman the much maligned Ben Affleck does a commendable job even if he doesn't exactly steal the show. The show stealing is left up to Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Women who is used sparingly and to great effect and judged on this showing alone we should all be excited where she might take her career as the lasso using hero.

While Gadot naturally steals the limelight Jesse Eisenberg's incarnation of Lex Luther threatens at times to take the film completely off the rails in what is a turn that needed to be reigned in more than a couple notches by the directing team. Seemingly channeling his best scientific take on The Joker, Eisenberg has some great moments but eventually turns his performance into an incarnation that seems cut from another film entirely and sits at odds with Snyder's realism drenched and politically charged event.

Far from an action packed thrill ride that many would be hoping to get and undoubtedly in need of a tougher and tighter edit, B v S still asks some intriguing questions of the overcrowded genre and also culminates in a fashion that will take many by surprise, even if it's highly unlikely it will stick to its guns come the next round. With Synder delivering on the visuals and with some nice groundwork for the DC future, B v S is a nice yet forgettable aside to what will hopefully be an entertaining and original take on the Justice League.

3 questionable spear disposals out of 5

title: It's messy and long, but you'll not be bored.
review:
"Black and blue. Fight night. The greatest gladiator match in the history of the world. God versus man. Day versus night! Son of Krypton versus Bat of Gotham!" Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg)

Lex Luthor's description of the battle in Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is just about right: Way too much is expected thematically when director Zach Snyder and buddies lard this super-hero opera with special effects and colorful characters too many to do any one of them justice. The best of Lex's phrases is "God versus Man" because more than once do writers Chris Terrio and David Goyer interject ideas about the notions of infallibility and accountability for whatever god we worship, mostly represented by Superman.

Maybe I'm missing the point. Maybe this super clash is really about the villain, best represented by Lex. In that case, the story is a hot mess of colliding motives, paramount of which is the boyish fun of making things go wrong, much like an adolescent version of Iago, who ruined Othello because he could (or like Bill Clinton who played like a boy in the infamous White House tryst because he "could.") At any rate, I prefer a Zod (Michael Shannon), whose sole purpose was to protect Krypton.

However, B v S has some nice moments, mostly when Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) is around, as when the titular heroes ask each other if she was with him. When she tells Bruce Wayne, "I don't think you've ever known a woman like me," I was convinced she was right, and I could look forward to her own Justice League segment to come.

Those quips remind me of the singular DC Comics characteristic that disappoints me—no sustained sense of humor. While Lex Luthor is assuredly meant to supply it, Jess Eisenberg delivers his lines like a petulant boy pushing impotent jokes (think of Gene Hackman's classic sneer and irony dripping lines). Even when Eisenberg says, "The Red Capes are coming! The Red Capes are coming!" it's so lightly tossed off amid much louder noise that its wit is lost.

In other words, I'm a Deadpool critic, lusting after the acidic asides that capture the fantasy of this whole comic-book hero concept. When Lex says, "Boys! Mmm! Bruce Wayne meets Clark Kent. Ha! I love it! I love bringing people together! How are we?" I am reminded about how much I love the asides that smartly capture theme. I'm hoping DC will lighten up like Marvel for the next 10 installments through 2017—I may be inflating the number, but I'm into hyperbole as much as the next fan boy.

"You know, it's true what they say about little boys: born with no natural inclination to share." (Diana Prince aka Wonder Woman) I'm relaxing now that Wonder Woman is here to get to the skinny of comic book devotion: Boy and girl men just having fun in their dreams.

title: Dark, gritty, Watchmen like take on the most beloved characters in the American consciousness
review:
I loved this film. As a life long Batman fanatic, I was terrified Ben Affleck would ruin the film, but I came away believing I had watched an older, cynical, paranoid Batman try to kill the Man of Steel.

I hate spoilers so I'll avoid them here, but there is absolutely a lot happening. Having read the comics for decades, there are many references in the movie to a host of plot lines, which provide the basis for an on-going story. On my second viewing, I could not find a weak scene or anything that I would remove. I won't say it was perfect, but it so far exceeded my expectations that it might as well have been.

I will say the movie is demanding, requiring the viewer to both pay attention and have a significant knowledge of the DC Universe. As a die hard fan, this is remarkable. Unlike other recent superhero films I could mention, it is much darker and does not give the story short shrift to maintain a needlessly frenetic pace.

I was most reminded of The Watchmen if you need a comparison. If you really like The Watchmen or Man of Steel, this will not disappoint you.
