title: Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Disappointment
review:
Batman vs Superman has been anticipated for decades. We've always wanted to see Batman and Superman duke it out in a film. And now, we've finally got to see it. But is it any good?

I can see many DC fans be very disappointed in this film, including myself, but I can also see many fans loving it. Film is subjective and everyone has their own opinion. As of writing this review, the film has 30% Critic score on Rotten Tomatoes, yet it has 74% Audience score, so while it it's been getting relatively negative reviews from critics, the public seems to liking the film. I'm not going to be a DC fan boy when writing this review. I will try to look at it as critically as I can.

First off, this movie takes itself VERY seriously, which may bug some people, considering the film is called Batman vs Superman, which albeit sounds quite ridiculous. However, being a massive fan of the Nolan films, it didn't bother me all that much. The cinematography was decent. It was much the same as most superhero films, the same sort of angles etc, but I still thought he did a good job. Hans Zimmers score wasn't great, but it was better than his score for The Amazing Spider Man 2. Jesse Eisenberg was good at playing a super villain, but he just didn't do it for me as Lex Luthor. Ben Affleck was a lot better than I had hoped as Batman, as was Cavill as Superman. But we've seen his portrayal of Superman before this, so we already knew that he plays a good Superman. It's hard to write this review without spoilers, but I'm worried i'll let out a crucial plot point and will ruin the film for you AND get my account blacklisted. Which I don't want. But anyway, the film is filled with special effects. I'm not even joking, it uses so much flashing imagery and computer effects that it gave me a bit of a headache. Another complain I have is the films run-time. I'm fine with long movies, but when they actually FEEL long, and you notice that the film is long, it takes you out of the film and you start to check your watch to see what the time is.

So, to finish up, Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice is probably worth seeing if its a rainy day and you've got nothing else to do. I don't think you need to see it URGENTLY, but I still recommend it. And hey, all of this is just my opinion, and if you don't agree with me, that's fine! It's just my stupid opinion.

title: More miss than hit
review:
I really don't get it; the movie is about Batman vs Superman, so why not concentrate on that? Why wasting a good part of the 2.5 hours on not relevant side stories?

This could have been an amazing movie about the conflict between two superheroes with different origins, different interpretations of where the place of a superhero is in our society, different opinions of what's wrong and right. And I think Snyder wanted to do exactly this, but somehow he got lost on the way. The conflict between the two was not well written, at no point I was able to believe and understand why those two fight.

There are some positive things, like Ben Affleck as Batman, Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, the scene in the Capitol, the new interpretation of Alfred. But all the good aspects, same as the conflict between Batman and Superman, got lost in a totally overstuffed plot, teasers for the next installment, bad acting from some side actors and over the top CGI.

Overall: average entertainment, a wasted opportunity.

Btw. does the new Batmobile really have turn signals? WHY???

title: Expect a COMIC book movie, not a Christopher Nolan "Crime Drama"
review:
This follow up to Man of Steel is dark and gritty pitting two of the most iconic heroes against each other. Although it first seems crowded with back-story and introductions of characters, it eventually layers the various plot-lines into the primary narrative.

Ben Affleck's interpretation of Batman is much more flawed than the cool and calculated Christian Bale version. He is just as intelligent in planning, but is much more battered and vengeful than the "Dark Knight" which makes for much more passionate acting. Affleck's performance is fantastic and his fighting is much more like the comics when it comes to brutality and defying physics.

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor is a unique choice in the fact that he brings a completely fresh take on the legendary villain. DO NOT compare him to the previous versions or you will be disappointed, but I suggest keep an open mind. He may seem like a wanna-be Joker, but with a classic comic book vendetta for power as opposed to just doing things to cause chaos.

Ultimately, Batman v. Superman sets the stage for the next wave of DC Universe movies and it is good to keep that in mind while watching the film. Yes, it does show us the murder of Martha and Thomas Wayne AGAIN, as we have seen in the other Batman movies, so bear with it. Yes, the fight scenes drag on for a while. And yes, Alfred is awesome AGAIN. In the end, Zack Snyder did well. Home you all enjoy the movie as much as I did!

title: Don't believe the noise. This movie is great from beginning to end.
review:
After all the negative reviews I have read regarding Batman V Superman - I have seen the film, and I can give my own opinion on the matter:

I loved it. I was totally entertained and I thought the performances were great. Ben Affleck made for a great Bruce Wayne/Batman and makes me super excited to see more from him. I also loved that Zack Snyder pulled good plot points from various great comic books and graphic novels, including Frank Millers "The Dark Knight Returns".

That being said, it is definitely a comic book movie. It is not meant to be comparable to the Christopher Nolan "Dark Knight" trilogy. There are over the top moments, and at times can seem a bit bloated, as well as the occasional eye rolling bits here and there - but it is not supposed to be based in reality like Nolan's films were. The punches are huge, the explosions are gigantic, and the destruction is colossal.

My only real qualm with it was that they tried to cover A LOT of ground in such a short time. It easily could have been two movies with more depth into the parallel story lines. Some stuff was skimmed over to make a solid platform for the Justice League films quickly. I took it with a grain of salt. I'm a big nerd and could watch hours of detailed movies about every nuance in the characters, but I also understand that these movies are meant to appeal to the broad masses that may have never even read a comic book - so I can deal with the fact that some stuff was barely touched on.

It is not, in my opinion, deserving of the hate it's getting. I think before going into it you have to realize that you aren't walking into a theatre to see the next Godfather or Schindler's List - it's a movie about two orphans who wear costumes and fight monsters. Oh, and one of them happens to be from space.

Don't take it to seriously and you'll have a really good time.

title: Gripping!
review: Easily the greatest Superhero movie of all time! Never before have I been so emotionally effected and connected by a movie based on comics, let alone a movie at all. The heroes were who they were supposed to be and more, leaving nothing to be desired. From the choices of actors and actresses to the sets and costumes, I can't imagine another team of people putting together a more wonderful movie, that by its end leaves you eager and waiting for more. I have waited nearly two years to see this film and I hoped that I wouldn't be let down and I can tell you with the utmost sincerity that I have never been so pleased by a movie in my life. Bravo to all those involved in bringing this cinematic work of art to the masses! I for one cannot wait to see what is next to come in the DC universe.

title: Batman v Superman... Made by a comic book fan for comic book fans.
review: Please see a direct quote below from one of the critics on Rotten Tomatoes. Rob Hunter... "I'm going to admit something right up front and acknowledge that I, like most film critics, am on Walt Disney/Marvel's payroll" That quote certainly helps to explain the mauling that this very solid movie has unfairly received from the critics. Don't believe the negative reviews, go and see this great movie made by a comic book fan for comic book fans; You won't be disappointed. Ben Affleck is ferocious as The Dark Knight, Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman is a scene stealer (when she finally arrives) and Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL's film score is worth the price of admission alone. Thanks Zack Snyder and Warner Bros for daring to be different.

title: So much potential, but ultimately so disappointing
review:
I'm so sad to have to say this but unfortunately this is not a great movie it's not even a good movie, it's a passable movie and that is just not good enough for a story of this caliber.

Here is a summation of the best and worst things about the movie.

The good:

Affleck is great as Batman, and I look forward to seeing a sole batman film with him.

The scenes with Wonder Woman in civilian disguise are very intriguing

Henry Cavill is still well cast as Superman.

Jeromy Irons is a good Alfred.

The bad:

There are so many interesting story lines and ideas in the film, but none of them are seen to a satisfying conclusion, if they even receive one at all.

The doomsday fight is shallow, you have no emotional involvement in the scene and you don't care about the stakes. Unfortunately he seems completely unnecessary as he himself is not the actual threat, but the pulses he emits feel like the only real danger.

No of what Lex Luthor does makes sense. He actes like the Joker from the Dark Knight, just wanting to create chaos with no real point to it all. That's no the way Lex should act.

The Justice League stuff is just awful, it seems so cheesy and stupid especially Cyborg and Aquaman.

The movie wants to do so much, but ultimately does so little and what it does do ends up feeling unfulfilling and as a wasted opportunity.

title: I walked away a bit let down to be honest
review:
I don't know maybe I was expecting too much. I hands up confess I am not a massive fan of DC comics. But I have dipped in to Superman and Batman story arcs over the years. Simply put the film is way too long (2 hours 40 minutes) and for me it really seemed to drag. The story is simple, All is cosy and then Superman turns up with the kryptonians and General Zod etc (the film follows directly on from Man of Steel which I enjoyed) Essentially you see Batman having a certain distrust towards Superman and basically thinks he's a killer (all of this is orchestrated by Lex Luthor of course) and he essentially wants the Dark Knight and the last son of Krypton to do battle. It happens but takes most of the film to get there. Also Doomsday turns up but it is spliced from General Zod and Lex's blood. Lots of CGI (some of it terrible, you'll see). Also a small cameo for Wonder Woman amongst others who is barely used at all. I just think for what they spent on this movie it could have had more story and substance and been better. I'm going to sound like a hypocrite here but I am going to see this again with one of my best friends and see if maybe I enjoy it more this time around. Like I said I felt a bit let down.

No to be honest I still found this a little (lot) dragged out, and I still felt very unsatisfied by the whole experience. This movie will probably make it's money back simply because there is no competition now (no Star Wars etc) but the box office takings according to the online press have nose dived a drastic amount after the opening weekend. I'm trying not to be a nay sayer and doom and gloom here because i love and watch all types of movies but this one just feels over hyped.

title: Some Good, A Lot of Bad, And Very Ugly.
review:
There will be a lot of reviews for this film. Some will defend it to the death, others will claim they were disgusted and appalled.

It's a divisive movie. Not just because it's a DC film, (though many will say that those who hate are Marvel to the bone and can't/couldn't appreciate it) but because it's a bad film that is intriguing.

The good of this film comes from it's initial premise. Batman wants to find a way to fight back against an alien being so powerful that given a whim the planet could be destroyed and brought underneath his rule. Interesting concept, poor execution.

This will be another point of contention: Batman kills. Batman straight up murders a dozen or more henchmen, and his goal when it comes to Superman is not beat him so badly that Superman willingly leaves Earth, no, it's to murder him with a Kryptonite spear.

Gone are the days of Batman, sending men to jail, and although no mention of Commissioner Gordon is in this film, you have to wonder if in this universe, if these executions are state approved, or is Batman now a vigilante with the tech and resources of Iron Man, and the moral compass of The Punisher? There's also a shocking lack of focus on the details. You see the Batmobile and Batwing, not in the cave first as a moment of glory, or a treat for the audience to soak it in, no, it's boom straight into action, and you're left to piece it together as the action unfolds. Never getting a true look and Batman's tech is a folly that not even Schumacher or Burton dared to make.

There's not much to say about Superman unfortunately. He believes he has a no kill code now, but someone needs to let him know that human spines and skulls don't fare well when hurled through layers of concrete and rock.

Lex Luthor is a mess as well. I'm a fan of Eisenberg usually, but this iteration of Lex was poorly written and acted with the jittery energy one would be more comfortable associating with a Joker or Riddler character.

The Senate hearing which occupy a large chunk of the film's run time, eventually lead to nowhere. Holly Hunter was misused, as was Lois Lane, Martha Kent, and Wonder Woman.

There are plot holes aplenty, and after viewing the film you'll know what they are and why the last third, and the set up for the continuing DCEU makes no sense.

The plot grinds to a halt to introduce us to the next Justice League members, and Wonder Woman is in the film to flirt a little with Bruce Wayne, allude to a back story that is yet to be explored, and then do some generic action stuff at the end.

A lot of people complain about Doomsday, and most of those are valid, he was spotting in the cgi department, he was shoe horned in, and again, in terms of Luthor's ultimate plan, didn't make a whole lot of sense. What's the point of an unstoppable murder machine if you can't stop it? I personally was very bored by and found Batman's visions/dreams to be complete filler. They take up a good amount or screen time, and they lead to nothing other than easter eggs for comic fans and to tell everyone what we already know, Batman doesn't trust Superman, we get it. But wait, now Superman will have a vision too! It was completely over done, and ultimately pointless.

Then there's the reason why Batman and Superman stop fighting. It's very hackneyed and foreshadowed so much it felt like being hit over the head with hammer while the writers and director shout, "GET IT!? DO YOU GET IT YET!?" I didn't know what to expect, but this was a poor effort from the DC team, and it does not make me excited for the journey to continue. Lighter tone, darker tone, it doesn't matter, just make a better movie.

title: Comic book style!
review:
Very mixed reviews on Batman Vs. Superman! Here is my 10c..

The words incoherent and disjointed keep popping up, I felt the format was very comic book like, scene hopping & a little scattered at times, it didn't need to flow.

it's an origins story that was primarily used to introduce/reintroduce batman, touch on Wonder Woman and continue from the awesomeness that was MOS.

It's definitely a Marmite movie, you will love it or you will hate it, either way, kudos to Snyder & the cast, Batfleck & Gal Godot portrayed their characters perfectly, it was true to DC, true to the comic books & I loved every minute, not at all disappointed but hey, I'm a fanboy!

2nd viewing is definitely on the cards..

An understanding of the DC universe, it's fundamentals and some of its history will make a massive difference, forget everything you think you know about the Bat from the dark knight trilogy & start a fresh! He's dark, he's been through some rough times & Robin is dead (that's not a spoiler)...

Roll on the justice league!

Side note: the amount of people comparing Marvel to DC is astounding, it's like comparing chalk and cheese or day and Night, they are very different worlds.

title: The hype was real, but the movie was better
review:
First of all let me say I was one of those people who has been waiting three years for this movie. When I first heard the casting choices I was not super excited but I figured I would give them a chance. The hype was so big for this movie I was afraid I would go in expecting too much. I was not disappointed; Zack Snyder has done an amazing job. The movie is not only the best super hero movie I have ever seen but it stays true to the source material When I was walking out of the theater I heard people saying things like "how could they do that". I actually went over and asked them if they have every read the comics and they said "No, I haven't" so I told them about the source material and then they became very pleasant with the outcome of the movie.

I would explain the movie plot as a Superman movie with Batman featuring Wonder Woman. The story was very well written and the movie was packed with action. I had goose bumps during the final half hour of the movie. I was a little shocked by Batman at first but when you put him into a world where Superman is the guy who snapped Zod's neck he is all that expected.

This movie was better than any other superhero movie that has come out before. If you loved Man of Steel you will love this movie. Comic book fans will be over joyed with how well they did with this movie. Thank you Zack Snyder and WB for finally giving Comic book fans the movie we deserve

title: A great COMIC BOOK movie! Go see it, decide for yourself!
review: I LOVED it. This is a COMIC BOOK movie - it's like it is straight out of the comics - literally! Like turning the pages and so on... I adored the opening sequence, the Easter Eggs, the cast, the twists, the turns. I was captivated from the the first few seconds until the closing credits. Make sure to at least review Man of Steel sometime before you watch it, it's really helpful and helps you understand Superman. It must be said Gal Gadot is a truly INCREDIBLE Wonder Woman, and Ben Affleck is an amazing Batman. I loved Superman - he does not take a back seat in this movie for me at all, to me he is the heart of this movie... It has not gotten a fair shake critically. Period. Loved it. I am seeing it again, and I am so excited to experience it again. I so enjoyed this movie. This is how I wanted to feel leaving the movie theater. My heart pounded the whole 2.5 hours - from beginning to end. Go, go, go, go, go see it! Welcome DCEU!

title: Superb, with a lot of subsistence.
review: Snyder has created a masterpiece, a stunning epic in tribute to comic book lore. The visuals were stunning, the Bat brutal, Superman has been solidified, and Luthor was absolutely petrifyingly intelligent, teetering on a precipice between absolute insanity and overbearing brilliance. Snyder is a visionary when it comes to what the fans want to see, countless scenes were ripped directly from the pages of some of my favorite story lines, all I can say is thank God for Frank Miller. The lighting, the imagery, it's reminiscent of poetry. Affleck is the definitive Batman, he is the only actor to date, in my opinion, to bring home both the Caped Crusader and Bruce Wyane. His fighting style is evocative of DC's animated works, the way he moves is torn out of his print legacy. As for the movie itself, it's not perfect, it has some minor issues, but every movie does. The philosophical ideas, the lofty concepts that would never fit in the MCU, they're still lingering. That being said, I'm going to see it again, maybe even a third time, just to process everything. It's so filled with little Easter eggs, shout outs, and tributes, that I'm sure I missed a few. Who's going with me?

title: A proper DC adaptation for the fans
review: I went to see BvS on March 23rd with a slightly diminished anticipation due to the amount of bad critic reviews I've seen/read the past couple of days. Starting from the opening scene and until the final one, the movie left me in awe. Sure, it has some flaws, but hell, tons of movies these days are fails and nobody insulted them in these ways, but for a fan that knows what this movie is based upon (comics / cartoons) it will be a total delight. 6-7 times during the film I almost screamed at certain scenes. Snyder treated the DC universe in his own original perspective but without forgetting what these characters stand for. Affleck is great as the new Batman, Eisenberg's Lex was a pleasant surprise and Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman will easily become one of the most bad-ass female characters on screen for the years to come. Setting up the tone for the upcoming Justice League movie, I can't help but count the months remaining until these great characters will unite on the big screen for some more epic moments that every DC fan out there is waiting for! PS: please stop comparing this movie with Nolan's trilogy or, God forbid, Marvel's take on their universe. BvS is perfect in it's own way.

title: Forget The Reviews - Get Your Own Opinion.
review:
Batman Vs Superman Review:

One of the most anticipated film of the year has finally arrived and has brought with it tons of action,darkness but also a lot of wasted scenes.

The film starts from batman's point of view of what happened in the end of Man Of Steel, a scene that builds the suspense between Bruce Wayne(Batman/Ben Affleck) and Clark Kent(Superman/Henry Cavill).From the first scenes I've noticed that it's not only a battle between the most heroic characters in DC's universe,but also a comeback to this whole universe,and that is why this movie is so long,most of the first hour had a mix of scenes that were only been put to build up the entire universe again,it was interesting but too long.

After the universe has been built the tension got higher and the scenes got more exciting,Batman wears his suit and the scenes started to contain more action than the first hour,but I must say that the "real" scenes start way after I was waiting for,it felt like a gym that being too much chewed and right before the taste fades you buy a new one and thing are tasty again.

And finally the battle arrived - in fact, a 10 minutes fight...

Batman and Superman had a visually stunning fight that gave me chills....but,the main battle comes right after(with no spoils)the real exciting battle is when Gal Gadot arrives and I won't tell you why...(Watch Trailer 2 if you can't wait)

In summary:

Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman

The stunning comeback of DC's universe

Ben Affleck as Batman

Amazing Action Scenes(especially at the end)

The Bad:

Too long

Expected for more.

Overall: 8.5 -Ido Yam-

title: Terrific Movie
review: Full disclosure: I am a lifelong Superman and Batman fan. (And I go back to 1958). The critics who are down on this movie don't get it. Many of them are comparing it unfavorably to the "bright and colorful" Marvel movies. I love the Marvel movies, but this is a darker, grittier take on the superhero mythos. To those who understand: this is Frank Miller's "Dark Knight Returns" Batman comics meets Superman's "Doomsday" comics. It blew my mind. It is much better than Snyder's "Man of Steel" in that while the closing battle is intense, it isn't that far over the top.The movie touches on so many Superman and Batman themes that it is a great gift to the fan boys and girls.Plus an utterly amazing and believable take on Wonder Woman. I was enthralled the whole time. Go!

title: Like reading your first ever comic book.
review:
Going in to this movie i had crazy expectations. Ever since i heard about the production i have been eagerly waiting to watch it on the big screen. And on a lot of levels it did NOT disappoint.

Seeing 'Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice' i was rather afraid of it spoiling the new image batman has had in cinema and pop-culture after 'The Dark Knight'-trilogy, and i was afraid i would be biased by 'The Dark Knight' watching this movie and comparing them while watching.

I was wrong.

Ben Affleck as Batman in this new series of movies works out just fine, he has the empty glance of a man in hardship seeking redemption through trying to save a city beyond saving, coming up against his biggest challenge yet, a corrupt symbol of hope for all of man.. a false God.. Superman. Ben Affleck really plays his part in this movie adding a darker layer to the beloved Bat. The action and cinematography are just as you would expect from Zack Snyder. The movie really has the feel of reading a comic book, the imagery bursting from the screen, trapping you in a new world. Great fighting and setup of scenes. It's almost like being 13 years old and watching '300' for the first time, just gasping at the screen, having your inner child bursting there and again at the mind-blowing action and especially the fighting between our two heroes. *Nerdgasm*

However.. If you walk into the theater expecting an intelligent storyline, an emotional journey taking you up and down like on a roller-coaster with characters that we love, not because of the action they give us, but because of their intentions, thoughts and lines, like Christopher Nolan brought to the screens with 'The Dark Knight'-trilogy.. You will be disappointed. This movie is nothing like that, but it doesn't need to be. It's a independent storyline, bringing life to the epic Justice League that we all know from our earlier years.

This is a movie for everyone who enjoys comic books today, or enjoyed them as a little kid sitting tucked in bed with flashlight reading about batman, superman, wonder woman, aquaman, the flash or any of the other DC heroes after bedtime.

A Superhero movie with no equal, just like reading your first ever comic book.

8.5/10 (9 since IMDb won't let me.)

title: Amazing superhero movie!
review: This movie was truly amazing. The entire 150 minutes were mesmerizing, and not just because of the visual effects. Every character played a great part. Fans of the DC comics will love the references and scenes from some of the most iconic graphic novels/comics. I am a little bewildered about the reviews the critics are giving this movie. As an average person that enjoys all sorts of films, I can truly say that most of the stuff they are writing is overly exaggerated or is an over-analysis of the film. Go see it yourself and you will see what I mean. Some people wrote Ben Affleck was too serious and Batman had no clear motive for his actions. A clear false statement. Some said there was no cohesive story telling. False again. It is easy to follow along and understand what is going on in the movie. This movie is not for a critic to pick a part as a work of art or filmmaking. This movie is for enjoyment, especially for DC fans. I recommend reading The Dark Knight Returns. The movie is the best comic book film I have ever seen. The film was amazing in every aspect. Go enjoy it.

title: BvS. No spoilers!!!
review: Overall, I enjoyed the movies. Two ways to look at it. The movie could have been shorter and skipped some of the beginning or could've been two separate films. Either way, it was still pretty darn good. Affleck is amazing as Wayne/Batman. Cavill has improved since Man of Steel. Gadot is great for the Wonder Woman role. Eisenberg is the weak point for me. He isn't terrible but he just isn't too great either; very average. Once the action gets rolling though the movie is very good. The CGI isn't tremendous but it could be much worse. With no spoilers, the ending seemed to drag on too. I feel parts of the beginning and the end of the movie could have been dramatically cut down to save on time. In the end, great improvement to Man of Steel and I look forward to more Affleck as Batman.

title: Different but very good
review: I went to this Movie yesterday and was afraid to see another MARVEL like superhero movie. Afraid because these movies left me feeling bored. They are all very much the same, seen one and you have seen them all. Luckily this wasn't the case. This Movie takes a very dark and serious approach on the superhero-theme, even darker than the "Dark Knight movie-trilogy" I think. The primary focus of this movie is set on the emotions and motivations of its two main characters, leaving less time for classic comic book style superhero-action and the introduction of new superhero-characters. But when it comes to action, this action is pictured perfectly, able to compete (and maybe surpass) with every modern superhero movie. This rarity makes these action-scenes ever more precious. This is how I like movies, serious with character-depth and well placed action. But I can understand, that if you value primarily colorful comicbookstyle superhero-action, where ever hero has a joke on his lips while beating up bad guys, this movie may be not the right movie for you.

title: A must-see!
review: As a comic book fan I thought I knew what was going to happen. Generally action movies are pretty straight forward anyway, and I thought I knew what the plot would be since I know the DC comics universe and these characters pretty well. Plus all the footage that had been released in the trailers. I was dead wrong. There were so many twists and turns that were genuinely jaw-dropping for me, and the movie always had me on the edge of my seat. This movie was phenomenal, by far my favourite live action superhero movie ever. The entire cast was phenomenal, especially Affleck who I was kind of worried about but completely blew me away. As someone who knows the comics well I think they did an amazing portrayal of these characters, staying loyal to the comics while also giving it something new. The action is AMAZING. You thought it was good in the trailer? It only gets a million times better. I'm dying to say more, but that would be a spoiler. There was more humor than I thought there would be. I was worried that there wouldn't be any at all, but there is some great humor and it's very well timed and executed, so it doesn't clash with the dark themes of the movie. This movie is a must-see on the big screen! Go out and watch it already!

title: Have a smart open mind and you'll love it
review: Watching this movie after seeing so many negative reviews makes me realize there's something very wrong with society. This movie is not just for fans, it's for truly immerse and ingenious enthusiasts of the immensity of superhero and comic book brilliance.

title: Underrated in so many levels
review:
This is phenomenon. It's a matter of personal preference, background knowledge of references (biblical/ mythological) the story, together with the ability to interpret meanings!

Web Slinger has put a representative review on his page, saying that "Look opinions change with time and distance. RIGHT NOW, I'm sitting here trying to decide if this really is the best comic movie I've ever seen, because RIGHT NOW, that's kind of how I feel.

Right off the bat (PUN) I'll say this is not a marvel movie. And that's OK. That's refreshing.

I love the fun of Marvel, and I love the weight of DC. They Shouldn't be the same product.

I've said before I don't listen to many critics. Conversely those of you who know me from my posts know I myself can be incredibly critical. But i tend to love the very very VERY few movies out there that I don't hate.

This movie blew me away. Affleck is now the most perfect representation of both batman and Bruce Wayne we've ever had. Cavil has that aura of superman.

Godot is still maturing as an actor, her performance was solid. Her gravitas and beauty are off the charts. She carries herself as if she were a goddess, which comes natural to her because she looks like one, that's a learned behavior. She had a fierce dignity that made her wonder woman.

I even loved Luthor. Very different take, but where I was worried he'd be another ed enigma or electro, he was not. He was eccentric but with an alpha dog bravado and a lurking dark side. He was very sinister and menacing, and he was ruthless.

I also wanna add that Affleck played batman a little crazy, which I loved.

The action was fantastic, the plot was simple and the story was brilliantly woven.

Last thing I want to point out is that the script, and especially the Luthor character, had a tremendous reverence for literature, history, and the arts. If you are a truly educated human being, you will find a lot of subtle, scholarly references to appreciate.

I'm not saying film critics and film students aren't classically or properly educated... but I guess I kind of am.

It's a really smart well crafted film, and it's also a nonstop thrill ride. I f--- LOVED IT! "

-Web Slinger

title: Straight out of the comics to the big screen.
review:
First of all it is nothing like Nolan's trilogy, neither it is a remake for it. This movie has a great story, idea to discuss and a little bit of drama that gives the movie a darker theme outside actions scenes.

All actors were great choices, and although Ben Afflek was the greater doubt, he is the most accurate batman for sure. The movie crew made a great job to get the real batman to the big screen, starting from the custom, the emotional and mental appeal, to his power and skills.

One of the best things about this (beside breath-taking action scenes) is that it skipped the focus on the characters made in older movies (either man of steel or Nolan's trilogy), it doesn't go over how batman got his gadgets and his skills, or how he use them, and same for superman and wonder woman, it just tells a good story with a beautiful plot, with a touch of drama that makes this movie different from marvel's equivalents, and makes it darker.

This is not a reboot after Nolan's trilogy, it is more like a sequel-prequel.

title: It is surprisingly really good movie.
review: I went to the movie with the last memory of rottentomatoes.com consensus of 32% rotten. That was certainly nerve-racking. Most of us wanted the movie to be epic and huge success. The expectations were huge and I was afraid for the movie since in general I found rotten tomatoes consensus acceptable. But after watching Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice, rotten tomatoes could never so wrong and fans can chill and enjoy the movie. I am not sure why it received so much criticism but before going to that let me grind out why this movie is so big. Batman, Wonder woman and Snyder. I know later would come as surprise to many including myself. But his action sequences through the movie were brilliant and they were highlight of the movie. Batman vs. Superman action and later doomsday battle were epic. The second half went like rocket. I thought after trailer doomsday would spoil the movie. It did exactly opposite of that. Even the flashback scenes of Wayne parents which were criticized during trailer had a place in the story. More interestingly the movie had a proper script. It was not all action. The script played some good purpose in the end. I didn't know why there were lots of hype of movie not being funny like marvel. I don't know if DC comics were funny but I loved the grim tone in the movie. After all the entire mood and theme were suppose to be grim. Though wonder woman brought some life at her scenes. But grim is what I expected and grim is what I got. It went very well with overall theme. So good things in the movie were batman, wonder woman, direction and script. So what went so wrong that critics are crying doomsday for DC movies? I believe somewhere bad publicity due to trailers could share the major blame for it. And I actually could understand it since trailer did lot of wrong to the movie. Since entire plot has paradigm shift from the trailer we witness. Superman as a character has lost the fun and the movie couldn't rejuvenate him. Though Lex Luthor played by Jesse Eisenberg is disappointment. I don't think script was bad to him. It was good but he over acted as young enthusiastic villain. The script gave him big role to play maybe as important as batman / superman and he couldn't do justice to it. It was big miss. In terms of Box office, I don't think fans need to worry about it. At least in India, fans were appreciative of movie and went crazy with every action sequence and popular line. The movie ended with the claps. The movie would get a solid word of mouth and it would be great game to watch whether it would be enough to overcome the negative criticism it received. Normally pen's are mightier than sword but it time around word of mouth need to do that job. I am worried for my next action hero movie now. I am long being fan of marvel movies and the captain America: the civil war is next in the list. But it had great shoes to fill and I don't think any action movie at least in marvel series can match the level of emotion of action I have just witnessed. Rating: 9/10 PS: People are discussion lot regarding Batman's violation of his own code of not killing people. But for me it was always philosophical. You can't actually believe that Batman wouldn't be killing people when he was keeping city safe? When he goes all around destroying and fighting thugs? For me it was having option to kill but choosing not to kill is all about Batman's code. I though Batman begins make this theme quite clear.

title: The Definition of a Comic Book Movie!
review:
Saw this movie last night (3-24-16 @6PM).....one word: SPEECHLESS. I didn't walk into the theater with the mindset that I'm going to judge this movie as a random critic would. I didn't expect it to be anything like The Revenant or any of those other movies that have gotten high praises from these critics even though most of them were sleeper-fests for many of us. They tend to be very biased with certain types of movies... I mean, on Rotten Tomatoes, Spy kids has an average rating of 93% and yet this movie has a rating of about 34%... makes absolutely no sense!! The story is greatly developed and the second half of the movie just plain old kicks ass.. absolutely amazing job! title: Its not bad, critics are either paid off or biased
review:
Really, its a nice movie. Yes there are problems, which will be addressed, spoiler free, but the good points will be addressed too.

Story: There honestly is not much here which is not good. Subplots are weak, substance of the story is weak too. If there were better subplots, this movie would be as incredible as Nolan's Batman. Bruce Wayne is investigating an incoming threat, along with planning to take down Superman, while Lex also plans the same against Superman. That is all I will say. If they improved the investigation part, automatically the subplots in there would be excellent. The movie is more Batman for sure, his introduction in the superhero world, however another lack is the fact that Bruce was already Batman for a long time, and they way Batman reintroduces himself, comes out of retirement was so.. bland and a let down, unlike 'The Dark Knight Rises,' Batman's return was memorable. There should have been more Clark and Bruce confrontation before the actual battle takes place. There is definitely a hint of an alternate future/time, which is classic DC and exciting. Story and tone of the film is dark, which fits film, there is humor, but the dark tone really gives the movie its strength. There is light, which is what Superman brings, its fascinating you have such a dark environment and you one character who restores positive feelings in the movie again.

The story borrows from the comic 'The Dark Knight Returns,' 'Injustice Gods Among Us,' and one more comic which I cannot say because it is spoiling, but this comic is a very memorable one and you will know what it is when you see the ending of the movie, which by the way, I felt the ending was not the best decision story wise, but it did cover that part from its source material well.

There are cameos of other JL members, but only cameos unfortunately, to set up a proper JL film, they should have brought them all together in the end, instead of only discussing it.

Action: The action is top. Very violent, fun, and beautiful looking. The graphics are great. The Batman vs Superman fight is good, could have been better but good. The Batman action from his solo missions are very Batman; Batmobile, grapple gun, Batarang, Batplane, the punches, but there is something which will be addressed later. The final fight, Trinity vs Doomsday was honestly really amazing and a fan's dream come true. Very enjoyable.

Batman: Ben Affleck is A GREAT Batman, he portrayed him well. We see Bruce Wayne work on his toys, investigating, speak another language, having his good heart, being his playboy ego and working with Alfred in his missions. Batman is grizzly, dangerous, quite scary and just a monster. There are 2 things however about this Batman which CANNOT BE ACCEPTED at all, its 2 things which Batman would never do and I was not pleased by it at all. Its hard to over look at these 2 things but we have a new take on Batman. Personally I'm not a huge fan of the new suit but I guess it suits the grisly Frank Miller Batman.

Alfred: I dare say this is best Alfred, even better than Caine's Alfred who is untouchable. Iron's Alfred works with Batman more than Caine did. Iron's Alfred is maintaining and repairing equipment, advises Bruce, very smart and knowledgeable, helps Batman and communicates with him throughout his missions, he's actually a pretty dangerous Alfred which I love, surely my new favorite character. We see a new side of Alfred every comic fan reads, and its too good.

Superman: Pretty much the same as Man of Steel, humble, funny, brings light to the dark movie, strong in what he believes in. Only new thing is he is conflicted from the government and people who hate him, what I love is even with all the hate, he still does good no matter what, because he IS Superman, love him or hate him, he will still help you no matter what, and this is why I love Henry's Superman a lot.

Wonder Woman: You would think WW barely has a role in this movie and is just eye candy and kicking ass. Well that's a little true, WW's role was not as small as I predicted, she does get a good screen time, she speaks important things, she's actually useful, she's more than eye candy and kicking ass, she's a proper character. I was not happy with Gal Gadot being cast, but she did VERY good, I am happy with her WW, and I'm excited for her film. She's classic WW, lasso, sword, shield, flies, fights amazing, Greek background, amazing costume, smart, yeah we have a PROPER WW here, be happy and excited! Sure we only see her fight in the end, but really it was worth it.

Lex Luthor: Casting Jesse was HUGE mistake, bad Lex Luthor. However, Lex's evil plans in the movie is classic Lex, his dialogs are pretty Lex Luthor, its just Jesse's take and personality on the character is a big miss, its literally a spoiled brat billionaire over a charming evil genius. To sum it up, Lex was written well, the character was prepare, they just cast the wrong guy to play him.

All and all, good movie, but there are problems with it; some can be over looked, some cannot be at all, mainly the Batman and Lex Luthor part. If you liked 'Man of Steel' you may enjoy this movie. Don't go in expecting the greatest of all greatest ever, but you will be happy with the movie. Story was weak, but I'm looking at this as a set up movie, the future DC movies will probably be good.

title: Batman v Superman, cool.
review:
So, last night I watched the film and before the film started I was pretty nervous about whether this would suck, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it, sure I could easily see why others wouldn't but that's their opinion and in mine it was very enjoyable and there were more than enough moments that kept me on the edge of my seat. Now without giving anything away to do with the actual plot, these are some pros and cons to the films, and let me just say that these are based on how I feel a casual superhero fan would possibly think.

PROS: 1. The introduction of Batman and Alfred was very smooth and fitted well with the last movie.

2. Ben Affleck was incredible as Batman to the point where it sent chills down my spine and I often found that he was actually pretty scary which is something I don't feel we've seen in the live action films yet.

3. The fighting scenes were very fun and showed a much more comic style of action that we didn't really get before man of steel.

4. There are a lot of nice nods to various comics which I can't really name because of potential spoilers.

5. The fight between Batman and Superman was epic and flowed very nicely.

6. Zack Synder did some very bold things in this film which really worked.

Now the CONS:

1. There were a few scenes that could be considered confusing for the casual fan.

2. It's very dark and gritty, which is something that is not for everyone and one of the reasons why some people disliked man of steel.

3. Some casting, although they played their role very well, they are very different to what most people were probably expecting.

All in all, this was a very fun film, and I will be going to watch it a second time soon.

title: Don't listen to non fans of the comics
review:
If you are a person with no knowledge of at least somewhat of what the comics are about, then you might not like this movie the same as someone who is in tune with the comics. There are some hints of certain characters that are outstandingly sneaked into the story. Superman was outstanding once again showing the vulnerability to human kind. Batman is without a doubt the Batman that we have been waiting for. He is a good detective and overall an outstanding fighter. Wonder Woman shows up enough to make you smile with pleasure. Lex is the conniving, manipulative, arrogant loony that you would expect to be.

The visuals are fantastic. The story runs smooth and inter connects various easter eggs that suggest something bigger than doomsday yet to be seen in other installments in the future. I was giddy with pleasure throughout the whole movie. It was well worth the wait for many years for the Justice League to finally form in the big screen.

Yes we all know that the major complaint to "serious tone" movies such as this one is that 'it was not fun enough', 'there were very few jokes',,,blah blah blah. I'd rather film makers make such visual and dramatic masterpieces than "corny" movies. Those "poptart" kind of movies get annoying after a while.

Please don't listen to naysayers. It is after all only an opinion they have. Go enjoy the show and make your own opinion.

title: Go watch it!!!
review:
Regardless of how good or bad a comic book movie is, I usually have my own thoughts about what could've been done better or maybe differently. But just like everyone else, it will always be AN opinion. Batman v Superman, just like all the other ones from the genre, is not a literal translation of comic book characters to the big screen. It's "Art" and everyone will have their own 2ç to add when talking about it.

My 2çs are:

A) Do not compare it to a Marvel property! DC movies are their own thing. Late bloomers in Hollywood, but not campy or light hearted like Marvel. Man of Steel may have flaws, but I felt it was a step in the right direction. And this is coming from someone who has grown being surrounded by more Marvel > DC and has enjoyed a majority of the marvel movies! I feel Marvel doesn't stress enough on real world implications and tries to focus almost everything on 'fun'. DC does it but with in a less 'colorful' and more serious way. I like both.

B) Keep an open mind! I have to admit that I'm more Batman > Superman, any given day. Having said that, I loved this movie and left the cinema wanting more of Superman. This movie was meant to be a sequel to Man of Steel and feels just as much every time Henry Cavil is 'Superman'. The "Justice League" seeds are also enough to wet a fans appetite and maybe even to a regular movie goer. BUT...This movie is made for the fans (fortunately or unfortunately) and is a literal comic book jump to the screen (Which IMO, I very much appreciated). Every movie has its flaws and so does this, being that it's made FOR THE FANS. An average movie goer may have a hard time watching it and may complain about "incoherent structure" but anyone watching this movie needs to realize that this is not a cartoon, not a 3D animated Pixar joy-ride but a full fledged live-action comic book movie. It's not meant to "feel" like Shakespearean literature come to life. I felt like Zack Snyder may have taken a few liberties but probably made a mistake by assuming that people are smart enough to make certain connections themselves. Having said that, there is still is no excuse for critics calling it a horrible movie. Zack Snyder and his team have done a wonderful job at trying to make fictional characters come off as believable in the real world. This interpretation of their characters are more mature than their comic counter parts. This Batman is a brutal, seasoned veteran with a touch of sadistic and a life-time of exhaustive experiences with unending troubles still creeping up day by day (Excellently played by Ben Affleck). Early in the movie Bruce Wayne is heard telling Alfred (played well by Jeremy Irons), "We're criminals, Alfred". He's very much aware of how the world views him and his brand of Justice but he doesn't care because he does what he believes is the right thing, albeit in a very strict and absolute way. This movie is Batmans stepping stone into the new DC universe and certain moments may feel rushed but that's also why he'll (hopefully) be getting his own movie. Just enough to want more. Just enough to see him be introduced and kick ass! Superman is having a hard time trying to just BE, after the events of Man of Steel. He's watching himself and is slowly turning into the character most fans have grown up with. Still a little wet behind the ears but his comic book character elements are very much there. He's still trying to understand his own value and is having a hard time with it because of ideas that characters like Lex Luthor and Bruce Wayne/Batman summarize quite well. Henry Cavill could've done with more screen time, but does well with how much ever is given to him. I already liked him for making his 'Superman' more like his physical comic book counter part. I like his character even more now, especially when thinking back to his scenes from Man of Steel.

Jesse Eisenbergs fresh take on Lex Luthor is refreshing and definitely more chaotic (? psychotic) than his comic book counterpart. I liked how he's more brains than brawn but significantly so.

Gal Gadots 'Wonder-Woman', I DEF liked. I wasn't phased as much as the other public was when Gal Gadot was cast. "Different take, different characterization" was my initial thought. If Snyders aim was to leave anyone wanting for more, then that's exactly what you'll get and like me and almost everyone else, will be waiting for her solo debut next year.

The music and sound are bang on by Hans Zimmer & Junkie XL!

If it were my way, the movie could've spent a little more time on the actual Gladiator match and (maybe) a little less on Lois Lane.

All in all...

Go watch it. On IMax 3D. It's a very good, mature & realistic take for me; along the same lines as The Dark knight (Which I must add had mediocre/poor action but great characterization)

The critics may need to be fed with a silver spoon but Zack Snyder has delivered exactly what DC/WB said they had planned on doing all along and he's done it in a very stylish, thought-provoking manner. For what it's worth, I would've gladly sat for another 30mims because I was having a good time watching something that made me feel like these characters were REAL and had actual seriousness to their personal

title: A movie for the fans, not for the critics.
review:
I went into this movie with a considerable amount of expectation. But I knew that it won't match or exceed them. So here are a few brief notes, I have about the movie:

Ben Affleck is the best Batman to appear on screen. Henry Cavill is much better as Superman here than he was in Man Of Steel. Wonder Woman is just too cool. Steals every scene she is in. Even outshines Batman. Lex Luthor is surprisingly one of the best things about the movie. Action sequences are a spectacle to watch. Story is rushed, but is on point and very well told. There is SO much that wasn't shown in the trailers. They were very cleverly deceptive on some plot points.

But...

IMO, it's not comparable to The Dark Knight trilogy. Gets close to being as good if not better than Dark Knight Rises, but has similar issues to TDKR. Was it worth the wait? Yes it was.

It is a really good movie. Visually stunning. Just seeing the Justice League Trinity together on screen made the ticket worth it. Don't miss out on watching it in the cinema.

The critics will not like it because it changes how superhero movies have become more adult-friendly than children-friendly. But then again, this is one for the fans and Zack Snyder and Co. have not disappointed us.

title: Solid film and a must watch for Batman and Superman fans!
review:
I went into BatmanvSuperman 2016 expecting a hodge podge mess with DC Comics clumsily playing catch up with Marvel. DC has been for sometime trying to imitate Marvel's success with superhero team up movies like the Avengers, and at this point they are very, very late to the party.

After watching the 2 and half hour film, I came out of the cinema hall feeling excited! Why? Because DC pulled it off! Was the movie perfect? Not by any means. But it got A lot right and its managed to set up the DC universe for some really exciting stuff in the next few years.

First, let me get this out of the way - Ben Affleck killed it as Batman! Best Batman hands down, sorry Bale Fanboys (and girls), but ‪#‎Batffleck‬ takes the batcrown and places it firmly on his cowl! To me, this film was worth it just to see the most faithful rendition of Batman till date, with plenty of homages to satisfy die hard fans (my favourite being an iconic pose from Frank Miller's Batman: The Dark Knight Returns comic book cover).

Now, here's where my opinion will start to divert from others. In terms of direction, cinematography etc., BvsS is stylistically jarring. When I say that, I mean you're either going to love it or hate it. BvsS takes a lot of risks. Sometimes it pays off, and sometimes, not so much, but I appreciate Zack Snyder for being true to himself and his vision because he didn't play it safe (coughjjabramscough). Personally I love his art style, BvsS takes it's cues somewhere between Man of Steel and the 300 series, so a cross between gritty realism and comic book grandeur, and you know what? It works! Well, it did for me at least.

Sadly, the movie doesn't score a perfect 10 from me due to some narrative and pacing issues, but mostly because of the shoehorning in of Wonder Woman (although I enjoyed Gal Gadot's portrayal) and the annoying cameos of the rest of the Justice League Cast.

8/10 - Solid film and a must watch for Batman and Superman fans!

title: Innovative storytelling and finally seeing the true Batman brought to life!
review:
Batman v Superman tells multiple amazing stories from multiple characters each with their own great deal of substance. When these stories all fall together it turns into a story almost as epic as the characters involved.

I enjoyed Man of Steel but it had its flaws. Batman vs Superman corrects a lot of those issues and while it does jump around somewhat it keeps you on your toes as if you were reading comic book panels - which is just awesome.

Henry Cavill is still a good Superman, Gal Gadot is beautifully brutal, and Ben Affleck is freaking Batman. Never doubted him for a second!

Detective Comics has started something very good here and has no shortage of some of the best source material.

title: Exceeded my expectations! now without flaws but great overall. mild spoilers very few.
review:
I just went and saw a screening of this the day before it opens nationwide and loved almost every minute of it. Batman is back and is the closest adaptation to the comics that's every been portrayed on film. The action sequences are intense, but not so crazy you can't tell what's going on. I'll list the pros and cons below.

Pros: Batman Batman Batman.

  • Film had a good story with plenty of twists and turns


  • Cinematography was breathtaking. nearly every shot was epic.


  • Wonder woman drew cheers from the audience and kicks butt!


  • Enjoyed the subplot of Lois and Clark.


  • Batman fight scenes were top notch!


Cons: not too many cons but some.

  • Dream sequences we're a little choppy and didn't flow smooth


  • Some C.G.I shots we're a bit cheesy looking.


  • introduction of Justice League members felt a little forced.


But for me that's it. Loved the movie. I'll probably go and see it a couple more times while it's in the theaters. Don't OVER THINK IT! it's a movie about a man who can fly and shoot lasers out of his eyes and a Vigilante who dresses like a Bat and an amazonian warrior princess goddess fighting machine. Sure, the movie can take itself a little serious at times but sit back and enjoy, Alfred is also a nice highlight and adds some needed comic relief. But overall tone is serious. title: Good Film....
review: let me start by saying that i am a movie fan,i like movies in general. i don't discriminate movies because of studios (Marvel & DC). the movie is good, its not perfect but its good. i understand why critics don't like the film (mostly the editing, sometimes the story jumps here and there, for example, superman can be talking to Louis in one scene, and then it cuts to superman doing something else that has nothing to do with the current scene and then it cuts back to him talking to Louis) besides that the movie is good, the visuals are excellent, batman and wonder woman are good. don't believe those who say that the fight between superman and batman is boring or short. the fight its entertaining and enjoyable. those people who say that the film sucked its because they made their mind 2 years ago (and because Marvel is god to them), hey everyone has their own opinion and i respect that, but the movie is not bad like they say. i would suggest people go an see for themselves and the make up their own mind about it.

title: Moving the plot forward
review:
Every movie comes with it's ups and it's downs, and if you are a critic, you generally walk into a movie with your own expectations set high, or low even. If you want to consider this a new movie, meaning the first, by all means do so, but if you to consider this a sequel to Man of Steel you would not be far off. At times throughout this movie I felt like I was going from point A to Z and then to point R and then B. It was a little over the place and if you did not pay close attention you could easily get lost in the overall storyline. At times the music is what really cared the movie, beyond some of the corny and pun lines. The positives of this movie, it moved the Justice League story forward and showed the development of the essential relationships that we are sure to see in the future. Probably a one time watch, but definitely not a never watch again movie.

The fight scenes were better then expected. Definitely a dedicated team of CGI. Some of the camera angles were a lead never wretching, as if your head could not movie fast enough with your eyes. All around I would say that this is a must watch for 2016.

title: Dark, a little overstuffed, some good performances, but LOUD
review:
Just saw the opening showing in IMAX 3D. Some of my impressions have been described previously by others: It's a very dark movie, it's overstuffed with action -- which is, admittedly, pretty well- done - - and there are some really good performances. But our (mine and teenagers') primary impression is that it was OPPRESSIVELY loud when there was anything other than dialogue. Without exaggeration, I spent the majority of the movie with my fingers in my ears; it reminded me of the old Maxell commercial with the guy being literally blown away by the sound of "Ride of the Valkyries" coming out of his speakers...

Affleck does a really good job, particularly given the standard of Bale. I think Cavill is an excellent Superman, with an edge to his good guy. Amy Adams is, well, Amy Adams: When hasn't she been really excellent? Jesse Eisenberg is suitably creepy: more than I thought he would be, although also a little bit like a truly evil Zuckerberg.

My overall rating of 6 would best be explained this way: After the fact, I don't think I would have felt bad waiting to watch it at home on a good system, whereas "Age of Ultron," for example, was one I was glad I saw in the big format on opening Thursday.

title: Grande Movie, Tall Plot
review:
Batman v Superman: The Dawn of Justice is grand, I can assure you that. The screenplay is ama-zing. We are told (a lot, every time we got to the internet lately) that this is not just another superhero cliché, because this is Batman and Superman, and it can be anything but small.

I love Ben Affleck; I really do! He is doing great in big movies such as Gone Girl and Argo, and I kinda love him as a funny/charming situation individual too; but honestly? He's not exactly doing a very best job portraying The Bruce Wayne of Gotham. Affleck said he is doing a totally different Batman with Christian Bale's Batman, but the vibes are very similar you can't help but comparing. He is simply a more unstable, angry, and ambitious Batman, without actual good and believable explanations rather than yet again the scene of Mr & Mrs. Wayne's tragedy in the past. Shortly, I didn't see the pain; only anger. As a big Batman's fangirl, I'm really disappointed, because I know Batman is so much more than that. Superman is being Superman, and I do think that Henry Cavill looks like Superman, only that I will still favour him as Napoleon Solo of The Man from U.N.C.L.E. to date. Wonder Woman is someone to root for, though; Gal Gadot is effortlessly stunning just the way she is, and that way she gives Wonder Woman's femme fatale just like that. Funny because she is the one whose cast got so many critiques from public! To be fair, she is doing so little there's nothing to judge; even Lois Lane's rescues alone has more screen time, I guess.

But I do like the way they're doing a realistic aftermath post the Superman/Zod battle, which ruined Metropolis and killed thousands. You don't simply move on from that in even years, it will be remembered forever. If we do have a Superman in this world, I'd be more scared than in love; those "Does the world need a Superman?" situations are serving as the core theme of this movie. There are a lot solemnity of the nature of man and gods, all-good or all-powerful gimmick, and powers and its consequences. So yeah, Batman v Superman portrays the superheroes as emotionally drained individuals that does seem real, giving us a deep thought in process, but forget to give us an actual strong plot to root for. Most of us know that Batman and Superman will be friends in the end of the movie, even before having our seat. They do have a little surprise, but even that doesn't cover a long two hours of them being all rivalry without us screaming in our head like, "C'mon, just be friends already!"

More or less, I think it is still fair to say that Batman v Superman is captured beautifully and engaging. Wonder Woman's theme song is winning at everything. They do, however, have a fatal flaw in the frustating, boring conflict that served merely for the sake of The Justice League's upcoming movies. Much to my subjective love, I still do tolerate that and rooting for another DC movies, just because. I don't know what the real critics may say about the movie (so far they are pretty mixed up), but if they meant to tickle us to watch Justice League and Wonder Woman with Batman v Superman, I think it's a 100% goal, at least for me. It is indeed a grande movie, only with tall plot.

title: Amazing experience, but in no way a masterpiece. Score : 7.6/10
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is good. Just don't go into the cinema expecting a masterpiece.

First, the negatives: Quite some technical issues - the editing wasn't good; in the first half they jumped from scene to scene without context. Probably needs 20-30 minutes more, for a lot is crammed into it. Plot - a bit convoluted but it works. Some of the dialogue feels out of place, but it's a vast improvement over Man of Steel. They try to setup the Justice League but it feels VERY forced. Some may have issues with the fight at the end, primarily because of CGI. Also, there's an aspect to Batman's character that people may not like - although it is a characteristic present in all the Live Action Batman movies so far. Batsy's nightmares were sudden and unexplained and there is that issue with that one cameo - it was ... weird?

The overall experience, however, was amazing. The good parts outshone the flaws and it gelled together despite initial editing issues. Cinematography and score were excellent. The humour was on point. I loved the Batman v Superman part. Ben Affleck as Batman killed it, Superman was an improvement over MOS, and the theatre exploded when Wonder Woman was on screen. I personally loved the Final fight. Lex Luthor was good, as long as you know what to expect. The ending is controversial, but I liked it. As did the theatre I was watching it in.

Note: I saw the ultimate edition

title: Underrated and very misunderstood masterpiece
review:
I'm gonna start by saying that this review is of the Ultimate Edition, which contains 30 minutes of extra footage and is vastly superior. I do, however love the theatrical edition aswell but it isn't as good.

I absolutely adore this movie. Everything from Zimmer's and JunkieXL's bombastic score, to the deeply emotional and grounded character motivations, to the amazing portrayals of Batman and Superman.

Sure, some elements of the movie doesn't work all that well. For example, Doomsday is a very bland and uninteresting villain, and Jesse Eisenberg's portrayal of the iconic Lex Luthor is very strange. But even these odd/bad things do wonders for the story. Doomsday serves his purpose quite well and doesn't really need to be anything more, as he isn't a villain, but more of a tool to unity our heroes.

The reason I believe this movie is disliked as much as it is, is, apart from studio meddling, that people came into it expecting a very action-heavy brawl between Batman and Superman, and instead got a very character driven, somber story about the duties and responsibilites of being a hero. And I can't blame them, that's how it was marketed, but it's not the focus of this film.

Also, that warehouse fight-scene is the single best action scene of batman. ever.

review: Well, they couldn't have done it worse even if they would have wanted to. Forget rationality, forget depth, ergo forget immersion. Finally, I quite like the nightmare sequence,and wished we could of seen Snyder's full vision for his Justice League trilogy.

And the bad, there is a bit. First of all, as much as I like Eissenburg's character in this film, it is not a good Lex Luthor. His actions fit more of a riddler type, kind of mad, but clever as well. Overall my biggest problem with the film is Doomsday. This film did not need a CGI tadpole with teeth for a villain. Also, the death of Superman was stupid and emotionless. No one thought he was dead, and why couldn't Wonder Women stab him with the kryptonite spear.

Better then I remember, and better than people say, but not the masterpiece the JL trilogy could of been.

title: A deep and intriguing development of storyline and characters... to follow-up with a disappointing endfight
review:
After having watched "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" in the cinemas and just now having watched the Director's Cut, I can already say this: if you have 3 hours to spare, be sure to watch the extended version instead of the shortened one!

To start of with, the much surfacing critique on the movie concerning the 'dark and gritty tone' of Zack Snyder is absolutely nonsense. This because the tone is one of the reasons that make this film shine. You place the concept of a Superman in a modern day world, and what happens in the movie could be a real life scenario. The old and hardened Batman doesn't trust this guy. Very good set-up and this flows naturally from the events of the previous film.

Batman is introduced as he should be. I like the colour palette of this film a lot because it strengthens the pessimistic point of view of both the heroes throughout the movie. And also because of that's what a (partly) Batman movie colour palette should be. The movie builds up quite slow, but a sublime scenery and astounding camera shots still have the ability to make you sit on the edge of your chair while waiting for the big clash.

But a fairy tale doesn't last forever. After a long build-up and a magnificent fight between Batman and Superman, the whole movie goes to ****. A slimy troll tries to take down the trinity of superheroes and the fight is just over the top. I know you can't just flush this movie down the toilet for a crappy design of Doomsday, but hey, my eyes also want something I guess.

At least the Director's Cut gives us a good and satisfying ending following the death of Superman. It needs time to really have its impact.

I give this movie a 8 out of 10. I do not blame Zack Snyder for this, but with a little more effort this could have been a 9 out of 10. It's a shame the movie didn't fall into the likes of the general audience, although I don't get why this is. This surely was an enjoyable film.

title: A thorough and remarkable performance by Ben Affleck congested in an inconveniently slow paced movie
review: Make no mistake, batman v superman :dawn of justice is an astonishing picture , it proves conclusively that Zack Snyder is a visionary and a world class director, yet in spite of all the respect that I give for all his pictures, I contest deeply over one single small yet crucial detail : the excessive length. The movie was filled with unnecessary and annoyingly lengthy scenes. For example, all of superman's meaningless walks through the capitol building or the streets of New York were easily, and in my opinion harmlessly expendable. Those spare moments would have been creatively used by the director or the screen writer to shed more light on one of this movie's biggest triumphs: the batman. Ben Affleck's performance was by all means this movie's last and best hope. I hate to use one of this domain's most utilized expressions but his acting was incredible, and this was for him the ultimate challenge. Because before I watched BvS, I had seen the dark knight returns: one of the few animated movies that have deeply touched me. This old masterpiece was DC's last fascinating movie that had, unexpectedly, amazing voice acting. The resemblance between that movie and the one we are talking about is uncanny , it even follows the same story arc but with a few big changes that made the batman character more intriguing, because it is for the first time since Michael Keaton's unforgettable performance in Tim Burton 's dark fantasy, that we see batman killing without remorse, affirming that he is no longer the guardian that Gotham deserved. It seemed like the incorruptible knight has finally fallen to the temptations of taking a man's life and this in itself is extremely shocking, because something must of had shattered his values and I as everyone who have seen the movie are craving to know what forced this man to show such brutality and despair. That's why Alfred pennyworth ,played by Jeremy irons, is for me one of this movie's essential pillars: satirical though as he may seem Alfred is this time worried about the safety of his friend and master, because the world has gone crazy since the arrival of the man of steel, whose mere existence in this movie ruined it for me . Henry cavil had his glorious moments and will undoubtedly have even more, but this movie is by far not one of them. In the time when every single member of the cast had shown a spark of good acting, Henry cavil exhibited such coldness and passiveness that he turned to be unworthy of this movies time, unfortunately he was there in every moment and every scene to the point that I started to doubt his acting skills In a nutshell, this movie might have been this year's biggest disappointment as the majority of the critics had confirmed .And I approve with certainty that this movie was the victim of poor editing and rushed screen writing, but at least showed us the bright side: the future of the dark knight is in safe hands.

title: The marketing is what messed the movie up.....BIG TIME.
review:
Having seen the Ultimate Cut of the movie I have to say that this was the film that should've came to theaters. The story makes so much more sense and actually adds some weight to the plot. Why it couldn't have been that way well...I blame the marketing 100%.

First off let's take the title for instance. Yes the film includes Batman and Superman and their objectives, but the overall film really isn't about them fighting. Do they fight yes. For the reasons you think, absolutely not. Them having problems with each other I believe do move the story forward and add to what happened in the previous MOS. However the basis of the title 'Batman v Superman's for what it is trying to do is very inaccurate. Not only does the fight end just short of that epic oomph we all wanted, it does nothing to bring that weight of importance for the entire film. It's just sort of....is... Which is fine. But to call a film BvS as if that scene is central to the plot and it's entirety is just plain bait and gives audiences more of a reason to complain. Dawn of Justice would've sufficed and when you watch it you'll see why.

Second, the trailers. I unfortunately saw all 3 of the trailers before the film released and when I went to the theater I was hoping for something that would surprise me and leave me speechless....and I wasn't. The trailers sold all the big cool points of the movie and kills the euphoria of seeing the highlights of the film. Doomsday I think was a great choice for the story and final showdown. So why the hell would you put his entire presence and all his glory in the trailer for us to look at. If they kept him out of sight I would've been all around excited. Say what you will about his CGI but I believe had they used him as a major hidden character to sweep the rug from its viewers it possibly could've been forgiven. Instead they show him and the three heroes together ready for a final showdown. Which leads me to my next point...

Wonder woman. Now I'm not saying she shouldn't have been in the movie. Not at all. But in the film Gal Gadot's character steals the show without a doubt. Seeing WONDER WOMAN of all superheroes on the big screen and in action was not only a very pleasant surprise, but a dream come true. I can only imagine what I would've felt like if I DIDN'T know she was in the movie and revealed in as epic fashion as she was in the Ultimate Cut. But no, that hidden gem was all over the place. In the posters, trailers, Internet, even the Blu-ray box art. The FREAKING BOX ART. Why! The movie is called BVS for God's sake. They practically are telling me that instead of two heroes fighting, it's in fact 3. That does nothing but tell me what to expect and kills any chance of me giving it a standing ovation just like there was in a very early screening for the studios before trailers were even released. She's the best parts of the movie when the film isn't even ABOUT her. Whoever thought putting her face all over the marketing prints to be a selling point should be fired in my opinion. With respect to Civil War, there's a character that was revealed in one trailer for like 5 secs and that was it. When I saw the movie he stole that one whole major 15 min scene and I indeed was jumping for joy shamelessly in front of my friends because marvel did a terrific job keeping his presence under wraps. And the box art doesn't even show a lick of him keeping me oblivious the entire time.

The box art for BvS spoils the best part for the film which in my opinion is the dumbest idea EVER and embarrassing for the fans that have been wanting a Wonder woman forever. Showing her glory like a unwrapped Xmas gift would've have been epic to say the least and it's quite a shame.

Having said all that the movie was very entertaining and honestly not as bad as critics and some others are saying. There's great action, great casting, great characters and even a great story (given you watch the Ultimate Edition. Please do) and it definitely is better than MoS in almost all cases. I think Snyder did a great job and can't wait for the JL movie. The only thing disappointing is that the marketing spoiled it all and left me wanted more and didn't get it. I got what was given to me. Which isn't a good thing. I urge you that if you're excited or even a tad curious for what the JL movie could bring I'd will stay away from his trailers in the future for that one.
