title: Maybe you just don't get it...
review:
To me, the most perplexing thing about this movie is how a certain segment of the audience can't accept the Snyder/Batfleck version of Batman: older, more fanatical, hostile to the super powered alien who flattened Bruce Wayne's Metropolis business premises and killed members of his 'family', but who seem to have no issue with the Nolan/Bale interpretation of the character in 'Rises'; an imbecilic, mother-fixated physical wreck (and if you haven't even considered what the pearls might symbolise in that movie, please stop reading now!). For me, the BvS Batman is just another version of the iconic comic book hero; the director even appears to point this out by having 'his' Bruce Wayne witness a vision of a Batman in another reality; one in which the Man of Steel is very much an enemy, the 'point man' for an apocalyptic alien invasion. Personally, I appreciated the manner in which Snyder fuses the version of Arthurian legend from the 1981 movie 'Excalibur' with his Batman/Superman match up, even going so far as to set Bruce's batchelor pad on pretty much the same lakeside where Percival returns Excalibur to the water at the end of that movie(to the strains of 'Siegfried's Funeral March'). By paralleling Superman's death with that of King Arthur (both die fighting an 'abomination', Superman's demise mirroring Arthur's), we are left with the notion of Superman's 'return' when he will be most needed, setting up not only the coming JL movie, but also creating a repentant, redemptive character arc for Batman. The movie could have done with more inspired CGI, more widespread suspicion of Superman's motives in the background and more clarity on Luthor's exact motives (I personally think he was probably originally intended to be much more of a religious nut than a scheming billionaire, but I can see why that would have been toned down!). Also, I would have liked for the distinction between the liberal, elitist ultra-modern Metropolis and run-down, urban wasteland Gotham to have been more clearly defined. As for the 'Martha' moment, I didn't subscribe to the 'dumb and dumber' interpretation when I first saw the movie, and I still don't. Would the Batman of the reality of BvS have reacted to Superman's ultimatum (retire or you're dead) and Luthor's set-up the way he did? Certainly. Would he have relented when Superman's mention of his mother's name made sense of the 'bat-monster' dream, making him realise how far he'd fallen? Of course. And again, why was Snyder's treatment of Bruce Wayne's 'mother issues' pilloried by critics while Nolan's portrayal of a Bruce Wayne so mother-fixated that he: (a) ignores the danger of his stolen fingerprints while getting her pearls back and (b) forms no suspicion of 'Miranda' whatsoever despite the chain of coincidences that placed her in a position to hand over the fusion reactor to Bane? Would a dying man (even Superman) actually use his mother's name in that situation? No, but this is a movie. And isn't the use of 'the child of Ra's Al Ghul' to disguise 'Miranda's' true identity in 'Rises' just as contrived? Would Bruce Wayne seek to redeem himself by taking on the challenge of defending the Earth from the dangers to come? Definitely. That's my tuppence worth, anyway. Maybe I'm completely wrong or maybe, like the Nolanites who don't understand that 'Rises' is woefully written and plotted (or worse, blindly refuse to accept the fact) while levelling similar criticism at BvS, you just don't get it.

NB: This review is for the Ultimate Cut.

title: A Marvel fan's view.
review:
To fess up straight away I absolutely hated Man Of Steel. Henry Cavill was a plank in it and the film itself was one long smash-up fest. So I avoided this movie when it came out. Normally I watch DC films, too as I have no hatred or bias against them. Just didn't like Man Of Steel!

I watched with some trepidation the 3hr version of the film on blue-ray. The cinema cut was poorly reviewed by critics and disliked by many DC fans, so maybe this "ultimate" cut makes a difference. It has faults, sure, and some plot points that should have been dropped into the nearest waste disposal; but much of it is also entertaining and watchable, and this time I thought Cavill was much better.

Ben Affleck, too, was surprisingly good. He fit the role of a slightly older Bruce Wayne well, and his Batman was much better than I thought it was going to be. The warehouse scene is arguably the best Batman fight ever. Not happy with Batman branding criminals. He's a vigilante not a torturer...

Wonder Woman? Don't know much about the character, probably needed a bit more build up and development; but she was very impressive in the fight scenes.

I would have been quite happy to give the film a 7 if it were not for Jesse Eisenberg. C'mon DC fans; you've been decrying Marvel villains for years as generic but admit it - he was one of the worst bad guys ever seen in a superhero movie. Eisenberg was terrible, and his plan was ridiculous. For god sake re-cast the role!

However, overall this has somewhat restored my faith in the DC film universe. Haven't seen Suicide Squad yet but I'm certainly prepared to give that a fair crack of the whip. Justice League could be great...

title: Epic Potential, drawn to above average
review:
Let me state that I'm basing my review by watching the 3 hours Directors' cut not the 2.5 hours Theatrical one.

as the DC universe developed in recent years after the Nolan's Bat Trio and Man of Steel improvement, I hoped very high for the historic encounter between the Dark Knight and the Man of Steel, and it had all the potential, bold twists and innovation but unfortunately, with duo respect, Snyder managed to crash my expectations with poor final product that contained too many negative plot holes, irrational directions and poor editing and build.

First of all, I'm a fan of movies going beyond the 2 hours limitations, where I would watch a 2.5 or 3 hours movie and spend the same amount after to revisit and think about what happened in the movie and try to fill in the mysterious gaps. On the contrary, I spent the night trying to figure out how much it could have been screwed if it wasn't for few factors giving it a bit of hope.

I will try to point my views to summaries the crap in my mind:

1) Batman: I'm a Bale fan that thought Affleck would simply suck, boy am I glad I was wrong :) the twist for the character, to make him remorselessly kill and brutally torture serves the structure of a devastated, mentally disordered Batman that doesn't manage his powerless felling and concern for the world in the right way, becoming as Alfred said; cruel. Hands up, Affleck delivers the version of Batman needed and does it astonishingly and deep.

2) Superman: Cavill is the right guy, he's got the Reeve's look, broad shoulders and actually gives a decent act but, the idea of picturing him careless about the casualties, not caring about the public opinion and then to calm the rage go on rescuing individuals here and there? you can definitely introduce a new version of a hero but you CAN'T alter the concept of the hero!! that one is on the writers and director. Of course, its been always there that with his unprecedented powers that casualties are felt and seen but not in this way where it would happen and he doesn't give a shi* about it!

3) Wonder Woman: This was a nice edition, good character building, good acting and introduced in an exciting way. Also, how would you not like Gadot in a movie, talent + Beauty = Damn Yeah.

4) Alfred: Irons, a Brit of course, delivered pretty decent as Alfred no doubt, but its mentioned in the movie Batman has been fighting Gotham's scumbags for 20 years, which he did after being away for a while as we know, and Alfred was around long enough with the Wayne but still he is not that old ,, writers?!

5) Lex: Eisenberg was good, but in short, its still not what to expect as Lex Luthor.

6) Lois, Martha K., Perry and the support: Good enough.

7) Fighting: How can we not tip into fighting when its all these bad ass characters. I liked the fighting mechanism, especially with Bats, we can feel the Arkham Knight style which was great.

8) Cinematography: All is good, great cinematography and nice effects and CGI, except for the last fighting scenes but it was good enough, nothing is perfect.

9) Intro: I think it was good that we just got less than brief introduction to Aqua, Cyborg and Flash. The movie already had too many ideas that Snyder couldn't manage to fit all properly in 3 hours! Imagine having even more hahaha but it was a good move to leave the story for the independent movies, hoping for a better managing.

All in all, again, this movie was meant to be an epic, unfortunately it wasn't. title: Fans Love It. Critics Hate It. I'm Kinda In Between.
review:
So after several times of declaring that this movie is going to be garbage and how it's going to completely kill the relevance of the characters of Batman and Superman, I finally saw it and came to the conclusion that it was...............eh. Not as bad as the Rotten Tomatoes score has you to believe, but not as good as some of the DC fanboys have you believe.

Ben Afleck was surprisingly good as Batman, even though the his character was a goddamn psychopath who killed and branded his symbol on the survivors, but I digress. Gal Gadot was good as Wonder Woman, Henry Cavill was alright as Superman, but I have no idea what the hell they were thinking casting Jesse Eisenburg as Lex Luthor. I mean I think he can be a really good actor, but man, he was just so awful in this movie. It seems like he was trying to pull off what Heath Ledger did in the Dark Knight, but it just fails so miserably. Every time he was on screen, everything felt so awkward and uncomfortable. During some of his scenes I actually heard some of the people in the audience groan. Jesse, I love ya, but you really stunk up this performance.

The plot, like I expected looking at the trailers, was all over the place. The opening was strong and I was thinking to myself, "What are the critics talking about? This is awesome." But that moment of relief was short-lived. One minute we're focusing on the backlash Superman is getting for his actions in Man of Steel, the next we're focusing on Batman hunting a Russian arms dealer, the next we're focusing on Lex Luthor trying to create Doomsday, the next we're focusing on a drive containing information on other superheroes and yada yada yada. I felt like I was watching five movies all crammed into one.

Easily the best part of the movie was focusing on Superman dealing with the backlash from the destruction of Metropolis. It felt the most realistic and it's also addressing the biggest flaw a lot of people had with Man of Steel. But it doesn't go anywhere, nor does it change the characters or plot in anyway, so it's overall just pointless. It seemed more concerned with setting up the Justice League than actually telling a coherent story. Like I said earlier, I felt like I was watching multiple movie all crammed into one. Despite all of that, it was actually cool to see heroes like the Flash, Aquaman, Cyborg, and Wonder Woman on the big screen for the first time. So that's a plus.

The action was hit and miss. Some action sequences were just constant shaky cam and flashes of lightning and rain every five seconds. (What is it with Zack Snyder movies and rain? I mean does he have a really weird fetish for it? Like I'm surprised the entire city didn't completely flood by the end of Watchmen.) But some action sequences were pretty enjoyable, like when Batman and Superman finally went toe to toe, when Batman rescues Superman's mother and the final battle with the ninja turtle, I mean ninja turtle, I mean ninja turtle, I mean Doomsday.

So the movie's a bit of a mixed bag for me. I can't say I enjoyed it all the way through, but I can't say it gave me nothing to enjoy either. So I guess my advice is, if you want to see some good action and some of your favorite heroes kicking ass, you'll probably get your money's worth. But if you're expecting something that's a lot more focused and coherent, then I'd recommend skipping this one.

6/10

title: Not as bad as you've probably heard
review:
Okay, I know I'm a little late to the party here – 'Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice' has been out for a while now, so I was well aware of the split opinions when I finally got round to watching this on DVD. From what I gathered you either thought it was the greatest film ever made or a steaming pile of bat-kryptonite.

I come down somewhere in the middle. I'm no die-hard comic book fan, so I can't really tell you how well the main characters are represented, apart from how they compare to their various filmic incarnations. But I can tell you that, although it's no classic, it's probably not as bad as you've heard. But then that's not to say that it isn't without faults.

First of all, if you didn't know, the comic company behind Batman and Superman is DC and they're playing catch-up to rivals Marvel when it comes to recent big screen outings. Marvel created a 'shared universe' where they made a film about each superhero then combined them for an 'ensemble' movie. Now, DC is jumping on the bandwagon, but is going a little too far too fast. BVS is packed full of characters and sub-plots, many of which could have been taken out. It only really had the Man of Steel (aka Superman 1) before it, so it's trying to get too much information in, compared to Marvel's slow build up.

Then you have Jessie Eissenberg. Yes, he plays the main villain 'Lex Luthor' (or Luthor's son to be precise). However, as many feared, he's just not up to it. I like the actor, I just think that he was horribly miscast for this role – and it shows. You really needed a more threatening (and older!) actor to take on the role.

Then you have the trailer. If you were looking forward to this film then you probably saw the trailers. They basically ended up being a condensed version of the two and a half hour film, so you can probably work out everything that's going to happen. No surprises here then.

But, despite its faults, I actually enjoyed it. I was sceptical about Ben Affleck as Batman, but he was actually pretty okay (and that's high praise for Affleck from me!). Wonder Woman's inclusion wasn't as 'shoe-horned' in as I thought it would be and she'll probably have a reasonably successful stand-alone movie off the back of this. Plus the fight scene that we were all waiting for was well worth the wait (if cut short for many people's taste).

Overall, don't believe either the lovers or the haters. If you go into this film with your expectations suitably set to something that will pass the time and is actually worth it for seeing – arguably – two of the greatest superheroes ever knocking seven bells out of each other, then you'll just about get your money's worth. Probably one for DVD rather than paying full price in the cinema for.

I'm well up for the Justice League – expectations set low for that, too.

title: Call it a "beautiful lie" or "too big for little minds", BvS is just a fascinating piece of filmmaking
review:
Let me just start by saying that, in concept, the whole DC Extended Universe was built on what I believe to be a right choice in tone and storytelling.

I mostly enjoyed the first half of Man of Steel because it managed to show a humanized and conflicted Superman. The fact that papa Kent gave him some ambiguous advice and that his home-world father kept telling Clark he was meant to be something great is a small detail that I found quite interesting because it meant this would be a Superman we haven't seen before. And, honestly, I didn't want another impression of campy Christopher Reeve.

So I was fine with the Christopher Nolan kind of tone, and was looking forward to some universe building when the new movies were released.

Batman v Superman tries to do just that while delivering a proper MoS sequel, a establishing story for Batman, an introduction to Wonder Woman and the 'dawn' of the Justice League. Oh, and setting up the advent of Darkseid, Steppenwolf, the introduction of both Lex Luthor, Doomsday and the death of Superman.

To say that's a convoluted plan is an understatement. But, somehow and despite some glaring flaws, Zack Snyder pulled it off.

Dawn of Justice keeps the dark, gritty, grounded-to-reality tone of Man of Steel, so, people who didn't like the aforementioned movie won't like this one. This movie will remain as divisive as it always has been, but it is a fascinating piece of filmmaking. Mostly because it has so many little, compelling details; so many small references and a clear attempt at grandeur that even though sometimes fells flat, for the most part work in regards to the tone of the movie.

Now, the movie has glaring, big flaws that keep it from being perfect, namely, the extremely convoluted plan of Lex Luthor that left the impression he wasn't really in control of everything that needed to happen and was just lucky (for reference, Zemo's plan in Captain America Civil War is pretty much the same), the creation, introduction and battle of Doomsday, and the fact the main battle between 'day and night' ends because they share their mother's name. Truth be told, however, I believe the 'Martha' scene was on-point conceptually but the dialogue was poorly executed (I would have left it without spoken words, as its concept was for Bruce to see himself in Clark's humanity).

But in general the movie delivers some solid storytelling and narrative. I remember defending Zack Snyder at university because he took simple stories and made them interesting through narrative techniques and symbolic frames. He does a great job here doing just that in a movie this overstuffed. I hope, however, he's more surrounded by talented writers and producers the next time he directs, because he, while excelling and some aspects; lacks in others.

It should be noted that the score I'm giving is mainly for the Ultimate Edition. I found the theatrical cut inferior and I remember leaving the theater a little confused and slightly disappointed. That happened because the editing was poor and there were some cut scenes that developed important events on the movie later on. I like not being hand-hold through a movie, but there were some really confusing events that got a lot better by the additional content.

A clear example of the poor editing in the theatrical cut is the motivations for the two main characters. Batman's motivation is (masterfully) established in the first 10 minutes of the movie; but Superman's aren't. During the first encounter between Batman and Superman right after the Bat-mobile chase, in the theatrical cut, Superman seems absolutely angry at Batman for no reason at all, and it comes as off-putting how he threatened Batman the way he did. The ultimate edition on the other hand, had a series of additional content showing Clark Kent doing some reporter work and growing his disgust towards the Bat, thus giving more weight to how serious he was when he confronted the dark knight.

Speaking of Superman, I insist I like this deconstructed version of him; I personally didn't want a comic-book character who fights for peace, justice and an outdated 'american way' but was clearly into the conflicted, humanized, vulnerable character we got. The other main piece of the equation; Batman, is fascinating and even though we didn't get more character background on Suicide Squad like I was hoping for, I think this is, so far, the definite version of the caped crusader on the big screen.

As for Wonder Woman, she was perfectly cast, but her presence feels a little shoehorned. Still and interesting addition to the roster and reason to look forward for future installments in this universe.

This is a movie that I've seen once in the theater and 4 times on iTunes (watching the extended cut) and I still want to see it again. You can call it a bad movie, a mess, or as some fans have said: "too big for little minds". But the four-syllable word I'd use is 'fascinating'. Clearly designed for multiple viewing. In contrast, I also have the digital release of Civil War and with each viewing I find it more and more boring and uninteresting (though it's really fun).

As a final note, I hope they don't ditch completely the Snyder tone, because I believe it's a way to differentiate themselves that benefits both parts. If viewers want a fun, adventurous movie they go watch a Marvel one. If they want a dark, deconstructed, grand and lofty endeavor; they go to DC. And besides, this bleak world is interesting as it is; flaws and all.

Here's hoping they don't ever go the panicked, derivative road they took with something like Suicide Squad. Keep the unique visual language and personality, develop more fascinating characters and go with that all the way.

title: Explosive dumptruck of justice
review:
About 30 minutes into Batman v. Superman, I was thinking "Oh, come on, this isn't that bad. Maybe a 5 or a 6." Forty minutes later, it was definitely not a six, and near the end of the movie, I weighed whether it was a 3 or a 4.

The biggest problem is that the most critical part of the film, the conflict between Batman and Superman, was desperately contrived and clumsily engineered. To be fair, hero v. hero plots in comic books are typically weak, but the final product in BvS is an especially shoddy job. The core plot is convoluted and incoherent (see the Honest Trailers plot cliffnotes on youtube for an accurate description of the ludicrous plot).

The pacing is horrendous. Cuts are poorly managed, and there are simply way too many useless scenes. The tie-ins to future movies are too frequent and too long. Also, Snyder needs to work on sustaining a simple linear plot. Get that down, and then maybe he can try more "advanced" techniques like dreams and flashbacks.

The movie is oppressively dark and grim, even unnecessarily gory at times. The script is flat and lifeless; jokes are not readily identifiable as jokes.

Batman is a murderous psychopath. But I'm okay with that. Snyder and Affleck can make their own version of Batman. But unfortunately that's not the worst of it: Batman is also a complete idiot in this movie, which is unforgivable. There are a lot of idiots in this movie. Which is usually a sign of a lazy script.

The final fight with the ultimate badguy ("DD") feels empty and tedious because there was, once again, no development. The DD comic book was pretty simplistic in its build-up to the final battle, but BvS doesn't even come close to achieving that. Really this entire plot line should have been saved for one or two movies down the road.

As for Eisenberg's Lex Luthor, a villain's quirkiness can work on screen, as we saw with Heath Ledger, but only if there is substantive character development that the oddness builds on. There was no development at all of Lex Luthor, so Eisenberg's twitches and mumbles came off as slapped on and gimmicky.

Ultimately, I give BvS a 4 out of 10. I think that's a bit generous. But I recently gave Transformers Age of Extinction a 3 out of 10, and I don't think BvS was quite that bad.

title: BvS - Boredom versus Sleepy

The action was good in some parts just not all the way like you would expect from a "Superhero vs. Superhero" movie. The pacing of the story was a bit all over the place and the build-up to the confrontation between Batman and Superman could've been better. It was no where near exciting. The tension between Jason and Freddy Krueger was much better (Yes, I said it). I'd rather watch Freddy vs. Jason more than once than this. As a matter a fact, I have the DVD for it. But back to the flaws of Batman V. Superman. I think the franchise could've made more money if they saved the Doomsday villain for another movie. It seemed rushed and made Batman look like a coward for not helping Superman on time. It's like he was waiting for Superman to be destroyed by Doomsday which brings me to another flaw in the film. That other flaw is the scene where Batman finally realizes why he wants to help Superman - because they both have a mother who shares the same name. Didn't make sense to me and just like a lot of other people, I caught myself saying "Oh come on!" The focus should've solely been on why Superman and Batman are battling and how the World is torn by the two superheroes colliding. Instead, it carried this dark-depressing and uninteresting feel to the movie and tried to be something more than extraordinary. And don't let me get started on the portrayal of Lex Luthor. Wasn't he the dude on Superbad?

title: Expensive Lesson in More is Way Less.....
review:
There are films about the pitfalls of American Foreign Policy - this isn't one of them. There are films about the challenges of self-doubt to those who shape our world - this isn't one of them. There are films about super- heroes pummeling the be-jezus out of each other - this isn't one of them. Unfortunately, for the viewer, this film wants to be all of them and spends a long, long, long time in that attempt. Failing in it's quest at every stage without realising the reason why. And the reason is - the creatives have made two thirds of each of those films and simply moved on to the next before the previous was finished!

What of the performances? They're OK. Amy Adams tries her best with hollow political epithets and Jeremy Irons' ballsy, earthy butler is refreshing. But Jesse Eisenberg is ultimately wasted here (in every way imaginable) and Affleck and Cavill are both dwarfed by the gargantuan nonsense around them.

There is a story to be told about the constant, wasteful collateral damage caused by super-heroes 'saving the world'. It just needs a far better team than this.

title: Decent movie for a comic fan who wishes to follow DC !

So it sort of makes sense in the development that Gotham is adjacent to Metropolis. The movie compared to the earlier Batman series in terms of graphics and the action scenes was much better. But the story as a whole took a beating. There's this critical scene or what you may call a climax scene, where Batman is on the verge of killing Superman. He just doesn't do it, simply because his mother's first name is the same as Superman's mother's. This is the scene where the movie hit a low. Also, there are some scenes where we find Batman shooting bad guys. This completely changes the character developed for Batman in the earlier series where he makes sure that he doesn't kill anyone. The movie as a whole was sort of awkwardly paced and a bit dull and boring. but the part where wonder woman was introduced was exciting, as a comic fan. some scenes to build on the story, such as the scene involving " The Flash", made it quite interesting.

I really like Ben Affleck as Batman and Henry Cavill as Superman and they are backed up by a great supporting cast especially Amy Adams, Diane Lane and Laurence Fishbourne. I'm still undecided on Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor sometimes I thought his portrayal was great and in other scenes he was grating. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman is fabulous and I'm looking forward to her origin film. There are too many unanswered questions such as why Holly Hunter dislikes Superman so much, what are the CIA guys expecting to achieve in Africa and the real biggie why don't the staff of Wayne Enterprises evacuate until Bruce tell them to I know I wouldn't have hung around with all hell breaking loose. All in all I liked the terrific film slightly more than the terrible one.

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice The Winner: DC Comic Book Fans
review:
BvS had A LOT of Easter eggs, plots, sub plots and a lot of ground to cover in order to lay the foundation for Justice League: Part One, slated for 2017. First off, the Easter eggs were BEYOND amazing! Any hardcore DC fan would appreciate them and be left with wanting more!

Off the bat, pun intended, the introduction of Ben Afleck's Batman and the all but forgotten back story of Bruce Wayne was flawless and perfectly executed. Short and sweet, but just enough to get the ball rolling on his story arch. Jeremy Iron's as Alfred was spectacular, his portrayal of a "hands on" Alfred really brings out a part of the character only seen in the comics. Henry Cavill's Superman offered more of the same we saw in Man of Steel, but brought more depth in my opinion, than in the previous film. His character really made up for what we didn't get in Man of Steel. Jesse Eisenburg's Lex Luther was amazing, brought some of his comic book persona into the big screen, and made that transition albeit a little bumpy but still pretty well, all things considered. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman brought a mysterious and mystical presence when she was on screen; she played the Amazon Princess as if the role was written for her! She definitely has set the stage and anticipation for her Solo Film due early 2017.

The Movie as a whole was a very beautiful film, great cinematography, slight brash editing, and the soundtrack was amazing, it really helped when the characters came on screen and really made their presence felt.

Onto the bad, however amazing I thought this movie was, it's not without its flaws. The pacing of this movie was pretty bad at first, then picks up, and finally settles in the end. The story-line was PACKED and I mean PACKED, almost too much and at some points becoming too messy for the average moviegoer. In a strange twist, had the Ultimate Cut been released to theater's this movie would probably have had a much more different reception.

title: BvS: Dawn of meh
review:
Dark Knight Returns (the original Batman vs Superman) is my favorite comic ever and the movie disappoints.

Perhaps the worst things about this movie is the epic potential that it contains. Unfortunately, these characters (or at least there iterations) are entirely new to us - and it shows.

There is entirely too much exposition, entirely too many new characters and an entirely ridiculous story-line. The sad thing is that it may have worked - may have even been good - had we been introduced to these characters previously. While it would seem ridiculous to have yet another Batman movie - with yet another set of dead parents - I can see that perhaps another Superman movie introducing Lex Luthor and the public's conflict with Superman.

There are some great scenes - Mostly when Batman is on screen - especially the titular fight. Unfortunately, this fight lasts all of ten minutes and has a ridiculous ending.

Overall, Batman vs Superman is disappointing - especially given all the hype. You can practically see Warner Bros scrambling to fit the entirety of the justice league into this movie whilst also trying to make it seem like an epic movie. It has the potential to be good - if there had been a few movies running up to it - but it feels isolated and you have no existing love for the characters to get you invested.

title: Messy, pretentious but also entertaining and memorable.
review:
The best aspect of the movie is definitely the portrayal of Batman. Ben Affleck nails the role both as Bruce and as the caped crusader, by exuding a refined and mature charm as the former and a terrifying angst and urgency as the latter. What is more, his whole physicality and fighting style is as true to the source material as you could hope; it's like an Arkham video game brought to the screen! Brutal and methodic to the core, it will leave no Bat-fan unsatisfied.

Many viewers were disappointed by the fact that he kills in this movie and it would be nice if we got a bit of dialogue of why Batman finally broke his basic moral code, but at least we get a hint of what might have drove him to that point from the painted suit you can see during the trailer. Was it a sidekick's suit? Was it Batman's? Who painted that? The movie doesn't answer that, but you're free to speculate

Another good aspect of the film has to be the fast pacing. Truly, I cannot understand how someone can get bored by it. The movie throws so much at you that you can get bored at any minute! Just look at the trailer and tell me that not a million things happen in this film. It is undoubtedly overstuffed. And an overstuffed film can never get boring, at least not on the first viewing.

The last positive is definitely the action scenes. With the exception of the too-much-lens-flare-and-shaky-cam Batmobile sequence, the action scenes are great. The main fight between Bats and Supes is epic and seems like it's been torn out of a comic book, while the final fight with Doomsday might have an overabundance of CGI and EXPLOSIONS, but is nevertheless entertaining and enthralling.

As for the bad aspects, well, there's a whole list. The main problem has to be the weak motivations behind the characters' actions. Superman is basically against Batman because he is a violent vigilante. Well, so are you Supes! The Senator (and the government) is basically against Superman's actions, thanks mainly to an attack he did on South Africa(?) to save Lois Lane, ignoring the fact that the killed men would have bullets in them, something that shows Superman didn't kill them.

There are two ways in which Snyder could have shaped these characters better: a) create different, stronger motivations and reasons for their actions or, b) point out the irony in Superman's hatred for Bats, making Supes seem like a man who abuses his power AND actually make the whole "we built a statue for Superman after he damaged half the city, but now we hate him just because the script says so" plot play out like a political game rather than an actual disapproval of Superman's action.

Lex Luthor has some daddy issues and thinks Superman is a god-tyrant he must kill, because daddy used to obey to tyrants during parades and daddy used to beat him and now little Lex has to kill God.what? His motivation is truly muddled and doesn't help us, the audience, to understand him as a human. He supposedly is against God (Superman) because, if there was a God, he would help him when his dad abused him, but at no point do we see the struggle he has. He is just quirky and nerdy all the time, showing little of the pain and torment he supposedly goes through.

The only one with a strong motivation (that nevertheless needed more time to be fully fledged out) is Batman. He actually is the only one we can understand, since we see through his own eyes the destruction of Wayne Tower, his eventual anger and distrust of Superman. Should they have used more of that? Hell yes, but in a film where everyone else's motivations are as strong as a sponge, Batman's reasoning stands out with ease, thus making him the only character you will be able to root for.

On to the plot, Luthor's master plan is convoluted, making little sense (he wants Kryptonite, Batman steals it, he kidnaps Superman's mother to make them fight and kill each other, but it seems he had planned creating Doomsday from the beginning!). The stupidest thing has to be the reconciliation between the main heroes. They basically stop fighting because their mothers have the same name. I'm sure the intention was to make Batman realize that Superman has a mother too, and that by killing him, he would be another Joe Chill who separated a mother from her child, but the way they center around the fact that "Martha" is the name for both mothers is melodramatic at best. It seems like a soap-opera, sadly.

And that whole "I kidnapped your mom" plot point ruins the emotional weight of the whole clash and thus, the film itself. Batman and Superman aren't fighting because of different ideals. No, they're fighting because the latter wants to save his mom. Only Bats has an actual reason to defeat Superman, but after the reconciliation, the whole thing seems more like a minor misunderstanding rather than an ideological fight.

Also, Snyder should back off with the endless symbolism. No more shots of people touching Superman like lifeless robots, no pathetic cry- faces of women who point at him in the sky, no Bruce flying from the pit he fell with Bats surrounding him. Either make a symbolism somewhat subtle and clever or don't make any symbolism at all.

Another problem has to be the dream sequence of Batman; yes, it will play a role in the next films, but it is absolutely useless in the narrative body of the film. Maybe it's time for DC to learn how to make a great stand-alone film and then worry about the sequels.

title: Did not enjoy

Then it switches scenes and shows his parents being murdered, then back to the funeral. This is probably the least confusing part. And then, Bruce falls into a hole and is saved by a swarm of bats, yeah a bit more confusing, but now we know what inspired him!

Many years later, Superman (Henry Cavill) flies through the building that is Bruce's adopted father's office while battling some random alien invasion that is never explained and destroys the rest of the building with his laser vision. I think this might be part of why they fight, but I don't know. That was unclear. By this point in the movie, my brain started to not understand what is going on at all. I asked my dad what was going on and he told me that it would make sense soon, but it never does.

This movie is a disgrace to DC comics because there is almost no point. I will explain as best as I can why without spoiling it. First, I will answer a big question, "Why are two legendary heroes battling?" I don't even know. You might better understand why this movie is so completely confusing. Another reason that this movie's title is very misleading is the battle has no meaning. It is only what happens next that matters.

This movie left me with a bad taste in my mouth, but these are my favorites parts of this film: My favorite character was Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg). Even though his lines were not so good, he made everything sound like the good, well bad, Lex Luthor that I know. My favorite costume and props are most definitely Batman's super armor and his gadgets. But, Batman and Superman do something confusing just because they have a super random connection! Some of you may have seen the famous Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) in the trailer, but she practically has 2% as much of a role as she does in the trailer.

I recommend this movie for ages 15 to 18 due to the jump scares, blood, screaming, death, guns and bullets, and many more horrible and violent things. I give it 2 and a half stars out of five stars because it is confusing, has no moral lesson and does not even match its title. This film is in theaters now if you wish to check it out.

Reviewed by Nathaniel B., KIDS FIRST! Film Critic, age 10

title: Batman vs. Superman vs. a Terrible Script
review:
Wow. The script for "Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice" (2016) was really bad.

I hate to begin a review with a statement so negative, but it's true. I really think that I could have done better than this, and I know nothing about screen writing. Hell, parts of the movie were actually MSTy-worthy. I just can't believe that the gifted David S. Goyer had a hand in this.

Batman is flatly rendered and barely likable. Superman is capably played by Henry Cavill, but has little to say. Lex Luthor is portrayed as a cloying, verbose, flamboyant, attention-seeking manchild. He gets all the screen time in the world (and more dialogue than Superman, it seems), and he really come across as a whiny, rambling high school student playing at theologian, trying in vain to impress the girls. Luthor seems to want to ingratiate himself to every other character on screen. Strangely, this includes even those he is threatening or endeavoring to murder. He has weird vocal tics that quickly get on our nerves. "Mmm." He makes repeated references to god, who he hates, and  this makes him hate the godlike Superman, via Freudian transference. Or something.

He consequently wants to kill Superman. He has kryptonite and demonstrably capable mercenaries at his disposal. But, for some reason, he wants to employ unreliable, convoluted plans to prompt Batman to do it. His plans to motivate Batman include harassing him with newspaper clippings and nasty notes, like a deranged stalker.

He also has a photograph of Wonder Woman that she would like to keep secret. She goes ahead and mentions it to an ostensibly drunken Bruce Wayne at a party anyway.

Oh! Luthor also knows the secret identities for both Superman and Batman, and has known for some time. We don't find out how he knows, and he does far less to exploit this information than you would think. Couldn't he easily (and quite legally) cause problems for both men simply by exposing them? Superman knows Batman's identity too; I guess we can chalk that up to his x-ray vision? Batman is not in the know, and spends much of the movie trying to play catch-up, and is easily manipulated by Luthor. This is despite the fact that, in the comics, he is the world's greatest detective.

There is bad dialogue, weird science, and bad science. There are murky, vague plot points and unsupported character motivations. Some things are just plain dumb — Metropolis and Gotham City stand within sight of each other, just across a bay. Either hero could easily intervene in the other's city  but they apparently respect each other's nearly adjacent turf, even though they don't know or trust each other.

Even the premise is shaky — legions of people hate Superman because they blame him for the damage inflicted by Zod during the events of "Man of Steel" (2013). Couldn't he just exonerate himself by simply telling the truth — that Zod attacked earth and he rose to defend it? I'm willing to bet most people would get that.

There are  dream sequences  and/or visions  and/or messages from the future? And  conversations with the dead? Or  not? You tell me.

Why does Superman need a winter jacket?

Why does he refer to his mother as "Martha?" Do any of us refer to our mothers by their first name?

I could go on, but you get the idea. I actually found my attention wandering during this movie.

All of this is a shame, because there are hints of brilliance hiding among the mediocrity. The movie is ambitious. It seems to want to say a lot about weighty themes such as power, unlimited power, its ability to corrupt, and the unintended consequences of unilateral action. There seem to be visual references to real world horrors like 9/11 and ISIS' terrorism, which I found pretty bold. I've never been good with subtext. Were there allegories here that I missed, connected with U.S. foreign policy or the War on Terror?

I will say this — the film isn't quite as bad as the critics are making it out to be. It isn't all garbage, it's just a below average superhero film. And it appears worse because it's part of a genre characterized by a lot of really good films — Christopher Nolan's Batman movies were groundbreaking, and most of the Marvel Cinematic Universe's titles were quite good. So this ambitious misfire seems far worse in contrast. I myself would rate this movie a 5 out of 10 — even if I might be biased here by my lifelong love for these iconic characters.

title: Not so bad if you don't expect it too much !
review:
First, i don't like "Man of steel" at all, but surprisingly I found this movie to be better than its prequel, even better than "Avengers: Age of Ultron".

I'm neither a fan of Marvels nor DC Comics, or superhero movies as a whole. I watched this movie after having heard of so many negative critics about its plot, long-boring storytelling. But after watching it, i think the boringness most people complained is actually the movie trying to lay down everything for the future sequles, it's just that there are so many things to be introduced so it feels kinda rush sometimes. However, the consequence is that everything seems to be off the course of what should have been "The greatest gladiator match in the history of the world", but instead became "The greatest trailer for the next sequel in the history of world's cinema"! (Also,because of this, i think this movie should be re- titled as "Justice League"!).

What i like most about "Batman vs Superman" is that the movie introduces some elements that are missing in "Man of steel", while trying to cut down on excessive actions in the previous movie (maybe this is why i don't like "Man of steel", since for me the action sequence in that movie is a bit too overdone, too many CG, explosions and destruction stuff).

The cast's performance is OK: Ben Afflect gives us a darker, more brutal side of Batman; Henry Cavill's superman is more vulnerable and fragile than in "Man of steel", Gal Gadot's screen time is short, so there's not much to judge, but she still did a pretty good job.

Lastly, the movie is too dark! It was very difficult for me to know what is going on during the action scenes.

Overall, i'll give it 7.5 / 10. If you don't expect it too much, i think "Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice" will not be so bad.

title: Lots of things to like... but far from perfect
review:
Haters will hate and this movie is being a little too harshly criticized. It is severely flawed:

  • It is long; too long; mainly because it does have a lot of disposable scenes that do not contribute to the movie. Batman v. Superman doesn't deserve an extended version; it actually needs a better, more coherent compact version


  • Somewhat linked but Z.Snyder has thrown in too much stuff in this movie. It lacks structure and plot coherence.


  • Some pieces just don't work: the bat-mobile chase scene looks way too digital. The car lacks weight and the scene lacks realism.


But but it does have a lot to like too!

  • For the geeks & fans: it is so cool to see some scenes that are too the exact replica of shots in the comics. Whether it's Alex Ross' Superman coming from the sky to the end (no spoiler) it's something that is just cool to see when you are familiar with the source material.


  • It builds on the Superman movie and creates the Justice League in a way that is actually satisfying! When was the last time anybody was excited about the DC Movie universe? - I actually do like Batfleck and the cast in this movie. Ben Affleck grits his teeth a little too much but is credible as a battle worn Batman... and Gail Gadot is just perfect as Wonder Woman - No spoiler but the end was good and poignant.


  • the fight scenes are cool. Snyder knows how to do those.


Overall, comic book fans have to see it... for the rest, if you're willing to sit through a (too) long superhero movie; there is still some fun to be had.

title: A below average depiction of a theme that could have been extraordinary...
review:
Well, to start with, this was one of my most anticipated movies of this year. Naturally, I wanted it to be good if not perfect and at the same time keeping my expectations low as it was directed by Zack Snyder. But still the movie managed to disappoint me.It tries hard, but still falls flat on so many levels. It was a really sloppy attempt in setting up the DC universe.The movie was all over the place and fails in indulging the audience throughout. Sure BvS has plenty moments of greatness, some good dialogs, great action sequences and incredible performances by the star cast, but for every incredible scene there is some strange or unnecessary successive scene which is out of its place.

Now, what I don't understand is that what does Warner Bros. and other producers see in Zack Snyder. He is simply an average director.Sure, i admired his movie Watchmen. But he tends to use the same effects and techniques in each of his movies.The visuals worked in Watchmen but they don't work every time.It can be observed in Bvs that many slow- mo sequences are misused.Also,there are too many dream sequences which totally felt out of its place.

The premise of the movie is totally logical, about how the people see Superman as a threat and there boils a difference in opinion among Batman and Superman regarding their choice of justice. But what i could not digest was that Batman, who is known for making sensible decisions chose to fight Superman just like that without even bothering to have a conversation with Superman in order to understand his frame of mind. The Batman here seemed impatient and reckless.The character of Superman was sensible though.And Lex Luthor was another waste of character here.The Lex whom we know as a mastermind and a person of magnitude was not depicted in the film. The Lex Luthor here has no motivation and no farsightedness. He was simply a mess and Jesse Eisenberg who portrayed him was annoying.I also felt the creation of Doomsday by Lex, in the way as was shown in the film to be a bit strange and odd.

Apart from these there are plenty of great aspects in the film.Definitely a step up from Man of Steel.Ben Affleck was great as Batman. Even Gal Gadot, another questionable casting choice, was great as Wonder Woman.Few surprises in the film, like the tease for Justice League were awesome.

Go see the movie, just not with too much expectations and I hope you enjoy it. (In the meantime I will keep my fingers crossed for Civil War.Please don't suck!!!)

title: Not as bad as critics claim, but a decent movie not without its problems
review:
THE CRITICS I do think many of the critiques that came out this past week were unwarranted and often exaggerated: one critic claimed that the duel between the two heroes took-up half the film!! Amazing! Their duel was surprisingly short. The more common critique is probably the one about the plot. Critics are calling the plot a mess. It's true that the plot isn't the best we've seen in a superhero movie. But, this is definitely not a "Dark Knight" or "Superman" quality plot. The movie has areas leaving you with question-marks- sometimes I think they were intentional, but in other parts probably not. Overall, the Critics were just cynical about the film: perhaps it's because of all the build-up and hype. I think this movie has been anticipated for about 3 years!! I I think some of the disappointment is due to that. Also, I think the Previews are misleading (gee, what a surprise!!) THIS IS NOT AN MMA MATCH BETWEEN BATMAN AND SUPERMAN! This movie is not merely trying to offer a fight between these two great heroes. It is only the culmination of their contrasting personas. I believe Snyder's intention was to show that Batman versus Superman is a conflict between Personas, Ideologies, Methods and Environments. The fight is only a culmination of their inherent differences as heroes. Batman is Dark, Brooding but willing to bend the rules to defeat criminals. Superman is set in boundaries and codes and tries to maintain Absolute Morality. The film tries to set this up for about the first hour or so. The way it does this IS NOT POORLY DONE. It's fairly consistent and it keeps you fairly interested.

PROS AND CONS ABOUT THE FILM Snyder is smart in bringing the characters to life in the modern setting. He presents Superman in light of the questions about Alien-life. Snyder's Superman hits on the modern topic about ETs: what if we were visited? How would we respond? What trail of conflict would ETs bring with them? I actually gained appreciation for Superman after "Man of Steel". Isn't it possible that if we were visited by ETs that they would be good and not just evil trying to invade us? Snyder gives us both-- Good and Bad ETs (Zod and other Kryptonians) as opposed to many popular myths about ALL ETs being evil and trying to colonize the planet. ALMOST NOBODY APPRECIATES THIS PERSPECTIVE

Snyder's Batman is convoluted. Sometimes, I think Affleck's Batman is pretty cool and enticing. His costume is great; the voice- manipulator has a great effect; Affleck's acting was good. But--- then Batman starts picking up guns and also blowing other guys away from his Batmobile! Batman NEVER PICKS UP A GUN. Fans knows he maintains this code because of the death of his parents. He would never do this because he would never compromise on something pertaining to the death of his parents: THE WHOLE BASIS FOR WHY HE IS EVEN BEING BATMAN!!!

With that-- SNYDER DOES GET TOO LIBERAL WITH THE COMIC BOOK CHARACTERS.

Also, Superman's presence in the film is pretty limited. We get more of Batman than Superman. Superman seems to be a fleeting presence and can almost be regarded as a cameo presence. IT's almost a Batman Movie with Superman in it.

To Snyder's credit- I think his idea of Batman versus Superman was to show the CONTRAST of the two heroes and not merely some kind of fist-fight. It feels like most critics miss this point.

The dream sequences are bizarre. The first one with Bruce Wayne dreaming of his parents' death and his encounter with the swarm of bats is fairly understandable. It is very unrealistic up to the point we realize it's a dream ending with "the light being a beautiful lie"-- we get Batman's perspective here that he is, indeed, jaded.

The dream sequence with Clark Kent seeing his earthly father was pretty off. In fact, Kevin Costner's accent changed in contrast to the first film. In the first film Costner's character spoke with a standard Kansan "plain" accent. But for some reason, in this dream, Kent encounters his father having a Texan, southern accent. He seemed different-- more like a cowboy just off the range. Amazing that the director and others did not catch this flaw.

There's another dream Wayne has where he is Batman trying to finish a shady deal to acquire kryptonite from the Lex-cons. Why is it in the middle of some desert? What the hell are those weird creatures or flying cyborg things?? Then, some weird electrical guy jumps out of his monitor giving him some hidden knowledge about where the kryptonite is.It's like some kind of poltergeist struggling in some electrical vortex- he gets sucked back into the vortex... "whooaaa, you must go to the (won't say it here)....uuggh arrrgghhh..." and then Wayne wakes up. Supposedly it's the Flash. A weird way to present him though-- "help me from the electrical vortex.... rrarrrgghh... but I will still help you be a detective fighting crime from this electrical after-life vortex...whoaaa" just bizarre

Don't want to make you think that this movie is plagued by the dream sequences. They are just a few moments and can be forgiven or overlooked by the greater whole of the story.

Ultimately, there's a lot of cynicism in the world today. This is showing itself in the critiques of this film. This film has its flaws but they do not plague the film like we see in something like SPIDER-MAN 3 (HOLY Christ!! WHAT A BAD MOVIE!!). This IS NOT A SPIDER-MAN 3!!

title: Another blockbuster losing fans
review:
So DC wants to kick-start it's Justice League bandwagon very badly. They are much delayed as Marvel has already marched ahead with 2 Avenger movies raking in billions. So they rope in Zack Snyder again who barely did justice to 'Man of Steel'. And then they cast Ben Affleck as the Batman. (Few Spoilers ahead, which won't matter much)

I tried my best to watch the big budget beginning of Justice League, without any preconceived judgements. Yes, I loved Nolan's Batman, but to each director, his own. First, the good!

The movie begins with young Bruce trying to run away from his childhood tragedy, across the woods and falling into the old well. In much improved 3D, the makers have to be credited for the photography and slo-mo scenes which is as good as it was in 'The Watchmen'.The slow falling leaves, the voice-over accompanied by relatable music, (gives you hope). Also, the alternate view of the man in the street feeling helpless while the God in cape fights his enemy without a care for the collateral damage is well presented. Bruce even with his financial and technological prowess, stands biting his lips while holding a child, who just became an orphan. (Hope did rise again) 18 months later, Bruce is busy tracking criminals and we are introduced to the maverick Lex Luther playful with his words while malicious in intent. Oh, and there is a scene where batmobile crashlands after just brushing it into the kryptonian generating chuckles from the audience. And another where the dark Knight keeps punching Mr. Tight jaws's face and he suddenly realizes that he's hitting a Spartan shield with a rubber fist. Oh, the Wonder woman is a hoot! Tall, talking with her eyes and dressed in style, she steals her scenes. And then there are Batman's hallucinations (makes u wonder if scarecrow still has an impact), which have graphics akin to video games with good action and appearing randomly, which could confuse a novice audience. Also well shot are Man of Steel's adventures, including saving astronauts from an exploding rocket.

The sad part is that the movie doesn't make much sense. The question of humans over how to trust an alien with powers that could easily destroy a world, who on one hand endeavors to save humans, is merciless over others who have threatened him or his love, delivering his own definition of Justice, is raised so meekly that it doesn't shake your conscience, neither do you believe it disturbs Clark the way Henry portrays it. One is similarly surprised when Bruce's initial enmity grows up to a peak and suddenly vanishes because of a common mother's name. Lois loiters all around in the movie, first in a desert, then all over metropolis, about to get shot, fall and drown, so that Mr. Steel can keep saving her. Big disappointments are also the design of Batmobile and Batplane, which looked like toys when compared to the 'Tumbler' or ' The Bat'. Also the car chase sequences, hand to hand combat and the final fight appear very weak and offer no new excitements.

As to the cast, Henry Cavill as The Man of Steel only looks the part, but fails to emote / move people. Ben Affleck has also built up a good body, looks dapper in his business suits with the greying hair showing age (20 yrs experience as the nightcrawler, older than his dad ever was), but doesn't come across as the dark and cunning Knight we have come to know. Jeremy Irons as Alfred, behaves less like the Butler and more like Fox / Robin, gets very few non-witty one liners and is wasted. Jesse Eisenberg as the hereditary CEO of LexCorp's keeps remembering his father and puts on a good show. Gal Gadot as the Wonder woman also looks the part as the Amazonian princess, has wonderful body language, but doesn't get much action screen time with her ill-designed wardrobe.

Lastly and more importantly, it's not at all clear as to why Luther was tracking 'Metahumans' and also why Bruce asks Diana's help to find future league members, except for his 'feeling'.

Overall a failure, another Big budget film goes the way of Avengers (Ultron) / Star Wars, losing more fans everyday, which their predecessors earned the hard way.

title: Pleasantly Surprised
review: I'm 40+ years old. Full disclosure: I grew up idolizing Superman and the original I and II movies. I was a little disappointed with MOS. But, I went and watched it solo on the RPX anyway, while the kids were enjoying Easter with the ex. I was pleasantly surprised. It's not a 9.2 out of 10, but a solid 7.7 in my book. There are a few things that disappointed, such as Eisenberg's LL and a gun toting Dark Knight, but it was entertaining and fulfilling in many other ways. Love the new look Batman and surprised at how good Affleck was in the role. The action was incredible. The story, although a little muddled, was intriguing. I like where they're headed with it. Gadot is smoking hot (sorry, I'm a dude) and convincing as WW. I liked the more vulnerable Superman. And yes, it was dark. There were a few light moments, but definitely dark. Anyone expecting a Marvel production will be disappointed. It's not Marvel. It has it's own identity and unique approach, that clearly isn't for everyone. Overall, I was happy and surprised at how much I enjoyed it after the mixed reviews I'd read. Critics can say what they like, but I would easily recommend BvS to anyone looking for a temporary escape into a solid addition to the Justice League universe.

title: Critics are being harsh
review: Good film. Critics are being very harsh, but the story did not ever really stick for me; I was never really drawn in. The editing was a little off, and if you don't know the characters it could be hard to understand. Dark and witty. Third act had some problems. Felt so intensely like a comic book -- I can understand how some people wouldn't like that. At times, scenes posed more questions then it answered. Batfelck was the best part and the film introduced Justice League characters well. Wonder Woman was great, character done justice. Lex Luthor was brilliantly preformed. This is not a bad film, I think critics have some sort of bias, to DC or to CBM in general, I don't know. See it and judge for yourself - the batman is worth the price of admission even if you end up hating the film.

title: Not perfect, but certainly a great superhero movie
review: I do not understand why the critics and some fans destroyed this movie as if it was pure garbage. It certainly is not the best superhero movie for me, but even though I was skeptic about it from the beginning, I couldn't find all the huge flaws everyone is talking about. Sure, it has some flaws and I agree that it tries to cover a lot of stories and aspects of the DC Universe that could have had a better treatment, but still I think it has more good than bad. In the first place, Batman is awesome, the superhero and Bruce Wayne are excellent. A mix of TDKR and the Arkham videogames that just nails it. I can't wait to see more of this Dark Knight. Superman is better than in MOS, Lois is always awesome (I love Adams), Alfred is one of the best ever and the rest of the cast is great. Maybe Eisenberg's Luthor can be annoying, but at least it's a different take on that villain. I agree that this movie works better with fans that understand the references (my wife had no clue when The Flash had its cameo, and for me that was amazing). But still, I believe the movie is not a flaw. Of course it could have been great if Snyder and everyone involved would have taken their time to set up the DCCU, but given the conditions, I believe they did a great job. Maybe it's too soon to say that the DCCU will be a failure or a success, but right now I don't see a tragedy here. (Consider a year ago I thought that DC had no chance on taking on Marvel. I still think Marvel has done a better job building their Cinematic Universe, but BvS is better than I thought. And the good thing is that I didn't expect that, and I am very happy with it.)

title: Story V DC
review:
Spoilers at the end!

This movie is better than I thought it would be. I had low expectations because of Man of Steel and other Zack Snyder films, but this was enjoyable. If you'd have asked me five years ago how I felt about Ben Affleck being Batman, I would have went into a blind rage at the thought of it. But he's been working on his acting skills and is easily the best part of this movie. Bruce Wayne/Batman's motivations are clearly laid out and understandable. He gets the most screen time and development so his part of the story makes sense. Superman, while competently portrayed by Henry Cavill, just isn't nearly as developed and the movie, and future DC movies, suffer from this (more on that in spoilers below.) Lex Luthor is just a mess; it's never clear why he wants Superman and Batman dead. How these three relate is the movie and how they relate is the problem.

This is a slow movie, at the start. Kids likely won't like this movie because there just isn't a lot of action. Most of the fight between Batman and Superman is behind each other's backs, until the third act. I didn't mind the pace (slow movies can still be engaging) but I can see why others will. This movie is also a lot of setup for the Justice League. I suspect Zack Snyder wanted to make a different movie, but DC and Warner Bros wanted him to include the extended DC Universe.

When the action does pick up, it's really good. The visuals, just like all of Snyder's films, are very beautiful. The fight choreography is really good and every fight is exciting even when the end fight has a lot of CG that isn't very convincing.

Overall, I did enjoy the film, but not everything sold me. You might not want to bring the kids because the pacing and themes might be a bit much to hold their attention. I was thoroughly engaged, but not everyone will be.

MAJOR SPOILERS

At the very end, Superman makes the ultimate sacrifice, but since his motivations haven't been fully fleshed out, it not only lessens the impact, but we haven't seen Superman being good. The movie appears to be setting up the Injustice storyline. While that's fine, Superman's decent into evil will lose a lot of meaning, when he gets resurrected. It skipped a lot of steps to make that particular story happen.

title: Good start for DC Extended Universe
review:
Zack Snyder was brilliant, after Man of Steel this film was a great success. The action scenes are wonderful, each character with its own way of fighting. Watching Superman, Wonder Woman and Batman in action was soooo exciting. The actors and their characters are incredible... Jesse Eisenberg left me with my mouth wide opened, Gal Gadot had animposing presence, Ben Affleck showed us an amazing Batman haunted byhis past and Jeremy Irons... do i really need to say something abouthim? But Superman doesn't convince me, doesn't make me feel anything, and I think every character should make us feel something towards it, either love, hate, compassion, shame, anything! There is a moment in the middle where the movie loose its course (maybe because the are too many characters and stories) but then so many important things happen and there are so many references that kept me thinking about everything that had happened when the movie finished and what may happen in Justice League... P.S.: I need to say this: The music by Junkie XL and Zimmer is AWESOME and gives a special touch to the movie.

title: Sometimes struggling to stay off the ground
review:
The mere idea of the fact that this film has been made for modern audiences today is a delight. As we have seen time and time again a film like this is not able to get past the script stage. Therefore, moviegoers and die-hard DC Comics fans should really bask in the glory of the existence of this film.

Batman vs Superman: Dawn of justice is really a love letter to those die hard DC Comic fans, myself included. Generally being able to understand, without delving into their comic book collections or the internet for things they didn't, what was happening in the film at a certain time. However, that doesn't restrict the film from criticism. As the general moviegoer, without any real knowledge of superheroes or comic books, may fail to follow who is who or where the plot is leading to or what a certain character is hinting at in forthcoming movies. Although with the current popularity of superheroes and their subsequent films you could ask have you been living under a rock for the past few years? Though those people could be left as the sheer amount of things going on and the introduction of new characters, setting up for future films, can be quite alarming to those who are in the unknown.

My main criticism of the film is at the beginning and sometimes later on in the film it can feel disjointed. Leaving you with a sense of wonder, questioning why this has been put in the film. Such as: Why is superman suddenly on a mountain? Those types of questions. That may be due to the fact this film itself is trying to set up a whole universe, thus they are trying to cram in so much information that they will be able to do a particular story in forthcoming films. Other than that I believe the film delivers a great amount of action. Ben Affleck delivers a new, interesting, different version of Batman that is one of the highlights of the film. They also manage to introduce the characters of the justice league film that isn't in your face. Gal Gadot provides an action- packed Wonder Woman that entices you to see more. Henry Cavill provides another solid performance as superman, building on Man of Stee. Jesse Eisenberg also provides a new,interesting take but on Lex Luthor.

If you are a general moviegoer or just a superhero film fan, I'd recommend going to see this film. You may not be impressed by all of it, but there are definitely moments in there that have you clenched on the edge of your seat. At moments you may be confused, hence, why I believe it just needs more fluent editing for everyone to be able to understand. Batman vs Superman provides a solid superhero film with plenty of action for your own entertainment as well as some great performances by the actors. Mainly providing a foundation for what the DC Cinematic Universe is going to look like and how the forthcoming films may follow on from it.

title: A good-looking messy film in the end
review:
I am a big fan-boy,I have being waiting this movies for about 2 years, when I realized that it was not a joke. title: Potentially Spoilery so scroll past if you're not keen on seeing it right now. :)
review: So I placed a suspension on my strike against DC comics for two and a half hours to see Batman V Superman. Taking my niece to see the movie as well there we sat through the trailers when Suicide Squad came on and when my niece saw Harley Quinn and the Joker she let out a very audible "Boo" which made me laugh so hard. I'm so proud of my little niece knowing she doesn't like Harley Quinn or Joker as much as I do. The movie starts and with much clichÃ© to it once again killing Bruce Wayne's parents within the first ten minutes of the movie starting. Do we really need to be shown that whenever Batman is involved in a movie; he's seventy-six years old by now if you don't know how or what compelled him to become Batman there is ample amounts of stories that will catch you up to speed. I must say that I was one of the people who was really excited that Ben Affleck got cast as Bruce Wayne/ Batman. Sure he might have had a few flops but you really can't blame those flops on him when writers should write better and directors need to well direct better as well. He's really grown in the last 10 years both as an actor and a director in his own right. He was brilliant to watch the way he went from privileged billionaire to the world's greatest detective we all know and love. I was really glad to see that his batman actually did detective work Jeremy Irons as Alfred was brilliant he bore that classic Alfred sass when he talked to Bruce one line stuck out to me perhaps an alluding to what's to come. "I fear any future Wayne's won't have much of a wine cellar left" that line had me giggling and my niece leaned over and whispered to me "Damian" and I just nodded. Seeing The Flash though that scene gave me chills more so than the rest of the movie his words from the future despite being in a dream just hit me. Now I wasn't so sure as to where I stood where Ezra Miller was concerned playing The Flash, but I think I'm on the side that thinks he can pull it off given that one scene. I think he's got it. I'm pretty sure. Gal's Wonder Woman now this is the scene that had my niece kneeling on her seat to see it better. My niece loves Wonder Woman and she was enthralled by her and I who once thought that Gal couldn't pull it off was surprised that she did a decent job. Though I will admit I wasn't fond of how much snark she had going on, Wonder Woman was quick with a quip but not full on snarky. Jessie Eisenberg's Lex Luthor felt weird it was like one moment he was the egotistical megalomaniac that is Lex Luthor. The next moment it was like he was a Mexican jumping bean hopped up on too much coffee. He didn't have that confident arrogance that Lex classically has in him. It felt like he was playing the Riddler at certain points. I halfway expected to hear him say "Riddle me this". When Lex was in the Kryptonian Genesis Ship there should have been no way he was able to take control of it by voice alone. Kryptonian society was far more advanced than human society and their tech alone would be leaps and bounds ahead of whatever we have. Lex slicing off Zod's fingerprints and using the genetic key in the way that he did should have had the tech slamming into security mode keeping Lex from taking control of the ship. Now the fight between The Trinity and Doomsday did have some issues. 1. Batman hiding behind a car while the blasts of Doomsday's heat vision were going off around him. It should have incinerated him but it didn't. 2. Wonder Woman's shield should have melted and once again incinerated her. All the magic in the world can't stop heat from burning the hell out of flesh. 3. Superman being able to hear Lois banging on the concrete wall that was blocking the exit out of the water. With all the chaos going around them despite his hearing he shouldn't have been able to zone into where she was so quickly. But over all the movie was decent sure I could go on for even much longer and could but I think I'm going to stop before I go too over. Was it all they hyped it up to be? Maybe not. Did they try to be true to the characters in which they had available to them? I think they might have. I'll give it a B rating. They could have filled in the few plot holes a little bit more and gone less into exposition. It was decent. Now I return to the Strike of DC comics cause I refuse to go to Suicide Squad while my girl Talia Al Ghul is left to rot on some shelf because DC comics doesn't have the balls to give her a comic of her own.

title: Despite its flaws it was still better than Avengers:AoU
review: The writing/story was shaky, the direction, especially in the action scenes was sloppy at best, it took far too long for something relevant to actually happen and the introduction of Wonder Woman served no purpose other than to introduce her to DC's cinematic universe (the story would have remainder the same without her), but it did what you would expect from a blockbuster - it entertained. Although my allegiance lies with Marvel, for all it's flaws I still found this better than the latest Avengers movie. Affleck was surprisingly good as the caped crusader, loved Jeremy Irons as Alfred. Jesse Eisenberg did a great job as Lex Luthor.

title: No improvement at all.
review:
Hold the fingers of your hand so as if you are holding an egg. This is the size of what was important in the movie. Then hold your arms wide open. This represents the length of the film. So, i am not saying that it was a total waste of time, but it sure is near to it. You should not make a multi million budget film which is a sequel and not improve it. I see no difference. Batman by Ben Affleck was the most tolerable thing for me, also Hans Zimmer's score was good but when it isn't. The film has so many characters and it failed to build everyone of them.
