title: Near Perfect, Not A Train Wreck But Lost A Couple Of Carriages!
review:
Many would have you believe this movie is a train wreck, In my opinion it isn't but It did lose a few carriages along the way. It touches on plot points from numerous Comic Book story lines and ties them together in an enjoyable film. It is by no means perfect, It has a few things they could have executed better or have left out all together but it is far from the disaster critics claim it to be.

I felt Batman and Superman were both relatable and they did a great job humanizing Superman with his reactions to the ongoing debate about him and his actions in Man of Steel. Batman was justified with his hate against the Kryptonian but I wasn't a fan of the "Branding" plot device they used to build Superman's dislike towards the Bat, They could have easily gone with excessive force like the breaking of knees and other injuries that take a severely long time to recover from and can effect their quality of life which would have still had the same effect but kept more in line with the character without making him a torturer.

Ben Affleck was a great Batman and an even better Bruce Wayne, You get the real sense that he is tired of putting on the whole Playboy routine when he is forced to go into it and his face suddenly drops into a scowl once he is free of the charade. This was something that was missing in almost every other Batman on screen. His interactions with Jeremy Irons/Alfred had a lot of character to them and you could feel like they have been at this for a while (some of my favorite scenes.) And FINALLY!, Batman fought how I always imagined him to, They nailed his fighting style and I loved seeing him use gadgets to disarm the thugs before jumping into the fight just like an Arkham game, I only wish we saw more of this as they showed almost the whole sequence in the trailer.

Wonder Woman was a highlight of the movie, Gal did a great job as both sides of her character, She was a very seductive playful Diana and a ferocious Wonder Woman. She made me excited for her solo film.

The villains were the weakest part, Doomsday though a necessary threat to combine the Trinity was rather generic and Jessie's Lex seemed like he was trying to channel Heath Ledger's Joker. I do not know why they insist on making Lex a typical run of the mill Insane guy that is quirky and somewhat childish when this movie needed a more cold, calculating and menacing Luthor like Clancy Brown delivered in the animated series. Some of his lines in this movie were great but could have been amazing with a more seasoned actor with a much more restrained performance.

Now on to Spoilers...

Now I knew pretty much the whole film already thanks to the bad PR job of trailer 2 but one thing that did surprise me was The Flash's message from the future, the multiverse or other. I wondered how they were going to add in the Darkseid nightmare and make it make sense since Batman would have no knowledge of him. I expected perhaps a vision of things to come if Batman and Superman wouldn't stop fighting but I wasn't sure where it would come from and liked what they did.

Lex bombing the court I thought was a great decision, It was a perfect straw to break Batman's back, It helps fuel the fire of the controversy as I'm sure some would believe Superman was the one responsible and the pain Henry conveyed standing in the demolished building, the only survivor was powerful.

The cameos of Aquaman, Cyborg and the other Flash while cool to see I feel could have been left out. All we really needed to see was the files with their logos on them and leave the rest up to our imaginations, As taking that 5 minutes away from the main story slowed the pace down for me just as it should have been ramping up to the confrontation between Batman and Superman

I hate that they had Batman nonchalantly killing the gun men in the vehicles during the Batmobile and Batwing scenes, and then again with the Flamethrower thug holding Ma Kent hostage, Potentially more if the thugs in the previous room didn't get out of the way when he aimed the thug that was discharging his weapon at them. I hoped the killing I heard rumors of would be strictly in the Nightmare scenarios but the fact that they had him murder thugs without hesitation almost ruined the film for me. I think it would have had added a lot more weight to the moment where Batman has the Krytonite spear to Superman's throat if he had never taken a life before. It would have made the stakes higher as Batman knows a random cop could get lucky and kill the Joker or another villain that he plays one too many jokes on, He doesn't have to kill him for him to die... but he is the only one that has what is needed to take out Superman, an alien that could enslave the world and he has to make the hardest choice in his life at that point. It would have also made me like the fact that he didn't kill him was because he heard his mother's name which would remind him that all life is precious and that he nearly made a big mistake. I think Ben would have excelled in that situation if given to him

And finally, Who else thinks that the A.I in Zod's ship may evolve to become the DCMU Brainiac?

title: So badly wanted to like it... SPOILERS
review:
First of all I wasn't a big fan of MAN OF STEEL. I thought it focused on trying too hard to be real it lost the sense of the Superman mythology. This film was even worse. Affleck was great as Batman, it was a new take on the character and I responded well to that. However, the narrative was a mess. I was just in the cinema desperately waiting for something to happen. When the throw down finally happened, credit where credit is due the small fight scene was awesome, but for me they had terrible material. Henry Cavil in all honesty was nothing special as Superman. Its not like he brought anything unique to the role. Ben however provided us with a different character, he didn't try to be like Bale or Keaton. I haven't seen this Batman on film and I want more of that. There wasn't much action, the point out to the Justice League was beyond cheesy. The dialogue was beyond a joke. I mean seriously... Oh and btw he Lois are in a relationship when before they were just friends. I mean it was just a complete mess. It was rushed, and lets be honest it was a money cow.

Some how he magically knew he was Bruce Wayne, fair enough he could done his x ray vision thing, but we don't know. Some how he knew he was really Clark Kent but I don't remember that being explained. It just all sucked and I don't understand why its so hard to get the screenplay so very wrong when there are so many resources out there. Countless graphic novels, I mean just watch Smallville and that will tell you everything about Superman.

title: I really wanted to like it....
review:
But it was just terrible. I couldn't like it.

1. Overlong. I'm OK with a long movie, as long as it actually does useful stuff with this time. Batman vs Superman used this time for subplots, most of which were irrelevant. 2. Scene transitions were non-existent, they seemed to jump from scene to scene with no rhyme or reason. 3. Batman nightmares were impossible to distinguish from reality, and made the incoherently scrapped together movie even more all over the place. 4. Batman and Superman fight for 10 minutes of a movie called Batman vs Superman. 5. Justice League introduced through an e-mail. WHAT. 6. Batman and Superman become great friends and stop fighting because their mother's names are both Martha. 7. Script tried to be quote-worthy and epic, but fell on its face every time. 8. Batman and Wonder Woman introductions rushed. 9. Superman and Batman had no personality, they were just kinda there and did stuff. 10. Boring. I'm not saying it needed to have jokes, I have no problem with a serious superhero movie, but the first hour and a half were devoid of any entertainment value whatsoever. 11. Batman complains about Superman wiping cities, drags Doomsday into the middle of Gotham. 12. After the Capital blew up, people want Superman back but threaten him death if he comes back. 13. The Doomsday reveal in the trailer resulted in no stakes at all for the Batman and Superman fight. 14. Batman beats Superman with a sink. A sink.

Things it did right: 1. Wonder Woman was amazing, as well as Lex. 2. Effects, visuals, and action, while not groundbreaking, were good.

Overall grade: 3.5, rounded up to a 4. I still feel as though that's generous.

title: A film with a tremendous amount of potential, yet failed to say the least.
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice had a lot of potential to be a good film, I'm not denying that- but all the potential it had was discarded for the most part. Most, if not all of us in a younger age had imagined Batman and Superman fighting each other whether it was with Action Figures, Lego, etc. So, with that being said, the expectations were quite high as our childhood imagination was finally coming to the big screen in Live-Action form.

When I first heard that a Batman v Superman film was in the works, I was excited. Once the first trailer dropped for the film, my expectations were starting to grow quickly. Once the second trailer was released, all my expectations I had for the film slowly started to fade away. The second trailer basically showed the whole film in a matter of three minutes, yet I was still interested in seeing the film. When the reviews for the film started releasing, my expectations for the film were almost non-existent.

Going into Batman v Superman with little to no expectations was probably the smartest choice due to the fact that the film was entirely a major disappointment. The acting in the film was fine for the most part, there was no faults in the acting choices whether it was Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Jesse Eisenberg, etc. The action, the fight choreography, the cinematography, and the directing choices were also good- I'm not denying that. The main faults of the film come to the writing, the plot, and the character motivations. The writing was an utter mess, it didn't decide whether the plot wanted to be a "Political Thriller" or a "Sci-Fi extravaganza". Those two do not mesh well together as it became boring, tedious, and sometimes laughably bad. The film felt like it was five films chopped up and mashed all into one. Batman and Superman's decision to team up nearing the end of the film was so silly that I laughed out loud when it was mentioned. The fact that they had Oscar Winning Writer Chris Terrio, David S Goyer, and uncredited Ben Affleck to write the film says a lot as the film was not good at all.

If you're still interested in seeing the film, I implore you to go in with low expectations and hopefully you'll find it enjoyable.

title: Iconic DC heroes dual in a middling action thriller with significant flaws
review:
It's that time of the year again when superheroes make their way to the big screen and earn a killer receipt at the box office. This long awaited DC Comics based action thriller directed by Zack Snyder who left in good impression with the Superman reboot 'Man of Steel' in the summer of 2013, pits two of DC Comics' iconic heroes into a epic battle full of flashy visual effects and adrenaline-fueled action sequences. This movie takes place eighteen months after the events of Man of Steel when Clark Kent/Superman defeated General Zod. After the massive destruction and countless of innocent lives lost in Metropolis as a result of the battle, Superman (played by Henry Cavill) has become a victim of scrutiny by public who consider him more of a threat than a hero. Bruce Wayne/Batman believes Superman should pay for his reckless actions and the result is an epic rivalry between the two heroes. Meanwhile, evil scientist Lex Luther (played by Jesse Eisenberg) hatches up a diabolical plan that could be the world's worst nightmare.

This long awaited movie had so much potential, and was on its way to great start and getting the DC Cinematic Universe caught up with Marvel's popularity status. Sadly, this movie only succeeds in its moderate standards and fails to live up near its full potential. The major flaws come almost entirely from the first half when we are introduced to the premise of the aftermath of the battle between Superman and General Zod, and the controversy surrounding Superman. The plot takes the first hour diving deep into the politics of the wrangle on how Superman is believe to be a threat to society, and not only progresses at an unnecessarily slow pace but leaves many unanswered details that seem to be significant to the story. The movie spends way too much time developing its exposition and not enough time with the main plot that it becomes less interesting as the story progresses. Another flaw comes from the choppily edited scenes that seem to come non-stop, and the results is questions left unanswered. It is not until the second half when the movie gains its appeal of excitement, starting from the long anticipated battle between the two titular characters, to the dazzling introduction of Wonder Woman (played by Gal Cabot), to the intense climatic battle at the end. Filled with spectacular action and visual effects that pack a strong punch, the final hour manages to the deliver above its sluggish first hour with pure excitement along with some emotional investment.

Now lets get into the performances. Henry Cavill remains good as ever in the role of Superman/Clark Kent since his debut in the role in 'Man of Steel'. Ben Affleck makes a surprisingly good impression as the new Batman/Bruce Wayne with a nicely updated costume and good commitment to the role. While he certainly doesn't level up to what Christian Bale brought as Batman to the Dark Knight trilogy, he definitely doesn't fail to satisfy. Amy Adams makes her return as Clark Kent's love interest Lois Lane and does fine job, despite being little more than a constant damsel in distress frequently throughout the picture. Jesse Eisenberg playing Lex Luthor on the other hand, could really use some improvement. As Luthor is supposed to be the villain, he's expected to be portrayed in a dark, sinister. Instead, Eisenberg gives off a more over-the-top Joker vibe that works in some scenes, but comes off a bit silly in other scenes. I really don't think he's the best actor for this role, but for all I can say, his performance is at least fine.

Batman V. Superman: Dawn of Justice is a bit of a middling superhero action flick that manages to succeed in some parts, but fails significantly in other parts. This movie is not I was hoping and left me in somewhat disappointment. However, it is not to say that this film isn't worth watching but a film that is a bit go-for-broke and will satisfy only some fans, but disappoint others. And there is no doubt that this film will definitely succeed highly at the box office for its mass anticipation. This film is not awful, but it just doesn't live up near its potential.

title: Good, certainly not great
review:
Is this film worth seeing in the theater? YES! Should you rush to see it? NO! Critics have not been harsh at all. This film is underwhelming and abandons the ideology of Batman and Superman entirely.

The positives: Visually at times this film is stunning and is the best in it's class in terms of comic book based films.

Action. If you are an action junkie then you need to see this film. It is an adrenaline rush that last all 2.5 hours. Never a dull moment.

Ben Affleck. Outstanding as Batman. The direction of his character and the elements that make the character what it is, make this the best adapted version of Batman to screen. He was a detective, a technologist and a self sufficient monster that proved why he will be an important part of the Justice League. Be warned, he is violent and shows no mercy.

Gal Gadot. Outstanding! I was pleasantly surprised. The writing of the character was superb. There is the one part of her not having her own vehicle that bothered me, but other than that she was fantastic and there maybe hope that a Wonder Woman film series might just work. At this point, it will be the fault of DC is it doesn't, because Gal was outstanding.

Negatives: Best comic book movie of all time it is not. Hardly and my list of 'best ever' stays the same. A film can't take short cuts and this one does.

One has to have seen ever comic book adaptation ever made to even make that assessment and I have seen close to all of them, regardless of the language and this one falls short of being the best ever.

It's congested with elements that don't even resemble the comic books. So you'll be left wondering what was that. The plot was straight forward to me, it's just, many of the short cuts taken seem cheap and lazy in terms of writing.

As a film it is not cohesive and the plot holes are glaring.

Superman? Some very good moments and well directed by Zack Snyder, sadly however Henry is simply holding back too much and doesn't understand how to play Superman or he is just a limited actor that doesn't have the range to play such an iconic character.

Lex Luthor. Jesse Eisenberg was a great choice for Lex. The writing was bad for this character. DC can get Lex right in the comics, but not in live action. Terrible writing. All Star Superman was great because we see Lex beat Superman essentially without Kryptonite, however I never liked the idea of Lex being obsessed with him.

To me Lex finds out everything there is to know about Superman and just makes it hard for Superman to stop him from committing crime. Instead of one Doomsday, what if it was an army? Make Lex a powerful villain that is hard to stop and necessitate the reason why the League would be needed to stop such a villain. Just because a villain get's his birth in a solo series, doesn't mean that character has to stay in that series or even be defeated.

Mercy Graves. A race change that equals yet another wasted character. Just terrible. One of the best ideas. Lex has a henchmen that poses as his driver but is really an enforcer and because it's a woman, it throws people off and they don't expect her to be the one to be his muscle or to even be capable of anything a man can do. This would have been an opportunity to have her shine and it was wasted.

Everyone else was good.

The cameos. Okay at best, but not great and one was down right terrible. Again just short sighted.

Not a terrible film. It's good, just not great.

The thing is I blame the fans for this, not just DC. The fans can't figure out what they want. No one wants campy again, but this film series can work without the excessive violence. It is not gory. So rest easy, but it is violent.

To me 'Dark" equals death and suffering and if fans can't handle that then they need to stop asking for it. To me you can't have one without the other. Also, I'm tired of the complaints of story elements that come directly from the comic book.

So to me the fans are just to blame as DC. Go see the film, just don't rush to see it.

title: Has DC cracked the Marvel Formula?
review:
Since people are going to compare Marvel and DC even though they are different things why not break it down. Marvel has crafted a winning formula while DC is still far behind and there is no denying that.

Warner Bros. tried to take a page from Marvel but sadly they were reading the things that went wrong with Iron Man 2 page. The narrative follows it's own thing until they reach the impasse of studio mandates that read "hurry up we have things to set up here." I genuinely think that both studios confuse plot-holes with set-ups so they have to cram so much as possible and it takes away from the experience.

A major problem with this movie is the title "Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice". If it was called "Dawn of Justice: Batman V Superman" it would make more sense story wise. It is by no means a bad movie, for me those two and a half hours flew by, but it really does a disservice to itself as a whole.

With this kind of thing: if you like it you're a DC fanboy. If you hate it you're a Marvel fanboy. What if I like both, what then? They both have their merits and both have their faults. I recommend it because it's something different and I like variety.

title: So Much Potential
review:
+ Scenes with Batman portray the Dark Knight as we have never seen him before on the big screen. Ben Affleck steals the show as the brutal, ruthless vigilante.

-I have a feeling the writers were more confused over where the plot was going than the audience was. A collection of incoherent storytelling and weak character development hold the film back from achieving greatness.

+It has already been repeated countless times before, but Zack Snyder is great when it comes to visuals. Beautiful shots that jump right off the page of beloved comics such as The Dark Knight Returns truly provide a treat for the eyes.

-I feel that the film's title misrepresents the film itself. Yes, we do witness the two titans pummel each other in glorious detail, but this element of the story is smothered by secondary plot lines.

The film really had so much potential, but sadly it falls very short of what I anticipated as DC's masterpiece. Incoherent plot lines, some horrendous editing, and weak character development that do not do the heroes "justice" dishevel what could have been a truly amazing film. However, many amazing sequences, Ben Affleck's Batman (as well Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman), and the promise of future Justice League films still made for an enjoyable experience and left me hopeful for things to come.

title: Full of potential, but lost it at the end!
review:
For many people myself included this movie ticked the box of 'one of the most anticipated movies of the year', and quite rightly so. The Dark Knight stands as a masterpiece of comic book movies, and although Man Of Steel was hit with a whole host of mixed reviews, I for one put it as the pinnacle of movies starring Superman, I am careful to say that in my opinion it is not a Superman film, in fact it is a Kal-El film, Superman exists for a single day.

Batman V Superman is another beast entirely, whenever I do a review whether it be written or spoken I make sure to note down four points â€“ Story, Cast, Score and Resonance. The story does not develop much past what is offered in the 3 Trailers released over the last 12 months, Bruce Wayne witnessed the destruction of Metropolis (Man Of Steel) and as such has declared Superman as the biggest threat to life on Earth. Clark Kent as a reporter believes the Brutality shown by Batman is out of control. With help from the scheming antagonist Lex Luther the two become entangled in the greatest gladiator fight in history. Well at least that is the plot to Batman V Superman, however this movie has another section, the 'Dawn of Justice' and this is where the story for me falls apart.

When we talk of the Cast we have to discuss the most controversial casting since Heath Ledger was masterfully cast as the Joker, that is Ben Affleck's casting as Bruce Wayne/Batman. This casting for me is the single greatest part of this movie, if I may be so bold I would say that Ben Affleck is my favourite Batman to date. Henry Cavill is a perfect Superman. Jesse Eisenberg is a really interesting and eccentric antagonist but not my ideal Lex Luther. Laurence Fishbourne is always great and that is where the compliments end. I would like to know who is responsible for the casting of Gal Gadot, yes she is a very beautiful woman and looks great as Wonder Woman but let's get straight to the point, Gal Gadot is not the greatest actress, she's wooden and inexperienced. It's almost offensive that they would give the leading female superhero to a model when there are countless phenomenal and beautiful actresses just in Hollywood alone. Going from one extreme to the other Amy Adams is a multiple Academy Award nominee who is placed in the movie simply to be saved, what a waste of talent.

The score to me is the soul of the movie, it should pull our emotional core along with the movie and its worth noting this score was composed by the great Hans Zimmer (Dark Knight, Inception) but for me the score was a little distracting, for the most part the score serves its purpose but as the story enters ridiculous unfortunately so does the score.

And then we get to Resonance, how I resonated with the movie, this is the most subjective and personal part of the review. I loved this movie for the first 90-110 minutes, I was onboard, I was excited to see Batman again on the big screen, the portrayal of Bruce Wayne was for me perfection, however when a movie with a dark tone, that screams this is as close to real life as possible, then takes a turn for the silly i'm out. When style is chosen over substance, when city's are destroyed like its made of Lego with no real consequence then I can only say that I am left bitterly disappointed.

But the movie isn't terrible, however without giving anything away the ending is cheap, it's as though they had not planned an ending, only an action scene. If however you want to watch to Goliath's fight, a big monster and an abrupt ending then you will thoroughly enjoy this movie.

I give this a 6.5/10, and if the movie had just stayed Batman V Superman my rating would likely have been an 8 or a 9/10!

title: Wrong in so many levels
review:
First than all, the movie has a lot of enjoyable things, and the best of it is WonderWoman by far... but for the rest, it is not good.

Instead of take ONE story and develop it well, Snyder and his team decided to take a blender and mix Dark Knight Returns, Crisis of Infinity Earths, Death of Superman and Injustice, delivering a poor and difficult to digest product.

I think that the worst thing is Batman, The Punisher. I understand they tried to put a more aggressive and darker Batman, but even when in their statements they say that "all here is collateral damage, and no more dead people that Nolan's films" give me a break, here Batman FRONTALLY FIRES AND LOOKS FOR THE KILL in almost all his adversaries... and that is not Batman, is exactly its opposite indeed.

The second worst thing is the SuperBonding just because both mothers are named the same... That is, I do not know, incoherent maybe? You have 2 years with a justified grudge against a planetary menace like Superman and out of the blue you became his super pal because his mother is named Martha? And do not tell me that is because of the fractured psyche of Batman or something... It is just incoherent.

The third wost thing: Luthor. And not because of the acting, the acting is supreme, it was the concept development... A freaky lunatic Luthor? Seriously? With a coming insane Joker around the corner you want a similar villain for Superman? Wrong decision... Luthor is a mastermind, a sane one... Highly obsessed but a Bruce Wayne counterpart in so many ways, brilliant, scientist, a business man... Not this wacky-o character.

Fourth: The visions, the Flash, the metahuman files with Superheores Logos made by whom? Luthor? everything look... I do not know... glued? like something smashed and bad fixed... "Bruce, you have to save the Cheerleader" and never, NEVER even look at Lois Lane during the whole film? Incoherent... I know it is like a seed for future films, but quite wrongly planted.

And the fifth worst thing: Too soon for Doomsday and for the death of Superman... To freaking soon...

That movie made me feel that DC wanted to catch up with Marvel, and put a decade of movies in only one...

Sorry it is a bad movie, a one of the worst of superheroes ever... For me it has 5 of 10 just for WonderWoman, who was awesome.

title: The first half needed better story writers, the second half is AMAZING !!
review:
First; this is a very good movie. you need to not expect a great one and you will be very pleased. It is based on "The dark knight returns" comic by Frank miller so expect a very unusual dark Batman. title: The big fight is here or maybe not
review: Batman v Superman is directed by Zach Snyder and stars Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg, and Gal Gadot. First off I'll say that I'm a huge fan of man of steel and going into the movie I was super exited( even with the bad reviews) to see how they would set up this universe. I came out of this movie loving a lot of stuff but at the same time I had lots of problems with it too. I will start off with the things I loved about it. Ben Affleck as batman as was just fantastic. I believed him as Bruce Wayne and as batman. Definitely one the best on screen batman's yet. Wonder Woman was amazing. She wasn't in the movie a lot or speak a lot but when they showed her, her character was very interesting. Her theme music was also one of the best parts of this movie. Henry Cavill was good, he's a good superman. He didn't very bring anything special but still good. Now Jesse Eisenberg, I thought he was actually a good Lex Luthor at times. At time he would go crazy for no reason which just made his performance awkward. Now the problems I had with the movie, it mostly wasn't the performances but more the story and how it was told. Zach Snyder is great director for action scenes which were amazing. Every action scene just blew me away but he doesn't know how to drive a story. The movie seemed to change pace to much and near the end the editing was very strange doesn't make it confusing but more of the question why did that? title: Very Very Good
review:
Lets start from the beginning, literally. The opening sequence is a total stunner. It is the Death of Bruce's Parents sequence and with the Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL score in the background it really is a sight to behold. Especially the theme when young Bruce rises with the bats is really jaw dropping. I thought it would be quite tough to top TDK Batman themes but BvS really tops it. I cannot explain how great the music in this film is and how well it is orchestrated. Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL have to be commended.

This film has fantastic content, very close to the comic books. The good parts are really really good. The destruction of Metropolis from Bruce's perspective(again fantastic background music),The Batman Car chase(yet again phenomenal background music), The Batman/Superman fight, The Batman fight to save MARTHA, Trinity/Doomsday fight are of seriously great quality and and epic scale. Visually the film is as good as it gets. Zack Snyder has to be commended for portraying the Superheroes as they should be, Mythological characters.

The BvS Batman is how a Batman should be. Again Zack has to be commended on presenting the Batman as he should be. The fighting is choreographed fantastically. This is how Batman must fight. Ben Affleck does a fantastic job. This characterization of Batman is the best ever as far as live action films go, hands down.

The pacing of the film I have to admit is a little slow in the middle. This is where the Nolan movies are good. The non action scenes are really fast paced often in a single montage like the 'TDK rises' ending montage. This probably is the only thing off about this film. Like I wrote before the content is phenomenal. If one has seen Man of Steel in detail then everything in this film will make absolute sense. It really is a very good sequel.

This in my opinion is a great film. I think the first time we see it, we are expecting a really fast paced film like 'TDK rises' which it is not. But when you see it the second time after knowing what you are in for, you will enjoy the epic spectacle of a film it really is.

title: The stage is set for more epic stuffs to follow!
review:
With this sequel of Man Of Steel, Snyder stamps his authority as the show-runner for DCEU. He shows better control than MoS, and presents a very different class of comic-book movies.

BvS brings together the world's finest. I had my initial doubts on his take of the Batman, but I must say that this Batman is unlike anything we have seen before, and in a good sense. Like Nolan created his own definition of the caped crusader, Snyder took a very different route and gave us a Batman - far more formidable, fierce and flawed. This guy is a war- hardened crime-fighter. He has been traumatized by the killing joke, witnessed deaths in the family. Nolan's Batman was new; he struggled to fit in and find his place. He was much more ideological. Snyder's Batman knows his place and shows how intimidating and cruel the Dark Knight can be. And Affleck portrays this Batman perfectly. Bale would probably still be the best Bruce Wayne, but if the timeline advances, you will definitely get Affleck's Wayne. This shift was much needed to fit the character in this universe. Nolan's/Bale's version could not.

Gadot does a wonderful Wonder Woman. A few scenes between her and Bruce were reminiscent of Selina and Bruce's initial meetings (TDKR). She dons her warrior persona later and fights Doomsday better than our other two heroes.

If I talk about fights, I must mention the one between the Batman and Luthor's goons. I don't have words good enough to describe that. It was a pure bliss watching Arkham-Batman come alive on screen. Mr Snyder, sir, take a bow for that scene.

The fight between the heroes was truly the 'greatest gladiator match', and we are eternally grateful to Luthor for bringing them, well, 'together'!

Eisenberg was nice as a manipulating, conniving Luthor, though very different from his comic-book counterpart. I would love to see some more back-story for his character in the next movies.

I loved the way the JL mates made appearances. Makes me more eager to watch all of them in action.

I would not say BvS has a great story. This is merely setting the stage for what is to come. Snyder shows a lot of things, fast-paced (I personally would have preferred a little more ease and a little more runtime). In terms of character development, there wasn't much to see and understandably so, but all that will leave you brimming with anticipation for the future solo movies, as there's a lot to explore!

BvS nicely sets the tone for the upcoming DCEU movies with its grim, harsh, brutal and unforgiving world. It shows that there are no perfect superheroes, but some 'men' and 'gods' who have the courage to fight for what's just. They bleed, they fall, but rise again to stand together.

title: Welcome to the League of Justice
review:
This is my review of Batman V Superman (spoiler free).

Director: Zack Snyder

Cast: Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg, Gal Gadot, Jeremy Irons.

Plot: Fearing the actions of Superman are left unchecked, Batman takes on the man of steel, while the world wrestles with what kind of a hero it really needs.

Director Zack Snyder returns with the explosive sequel to Man of Steel (2013) and this time we see Batman and Superman fight to the death.

The film has a very dark vibe to it and certainly welcomes the new era of Batman in very action addition to DC Cinematic Universe. Here are some points on why I think this film is a must see: Action: Obviously this is a superhero and there is always one thing that makes a superhero film better and that is action and a lot of it. This film is exactly that it is explosive and among everything else it is loud and edge of your seat madness. One more thing the action has the use of momentum rarely seen in action movies.

Lighting Effects: The film has the same lighting effects as Man of Steel with gigantic lens flares it just makes the impact of the film look more real, it also has an amazing use of dark and light shading.

CGI: The CGI is mind-boggling and it makes the atmosphere of the whole feel like you are actually there alongside the two biggest heroes in comic book history. My favourite bit about the CGI is that Doomsday looks really scary and very convincing.

On the negative side the jokes and references are funny at the start but then they begin to feel a little too much and a few of them wouldn't have gone amiss. Gal Gadot's acting as the Amazonian Goddess Wonder Woman is beyond atrocious I mean it's the first time that she has appeared on the big screen but she could have been done better.

If you liked Man of Steel and you like Batman or you just want to see them try to kill each other then this film is worth, even though that Ben Affleck is mediocre as Batman.

I recommend this film to all DC fans.

Verdict: Action packed and a lot of fun it makes the wait worth while although some of the jokes shouldn't have been there. 8/10 explosive recommendation.

title: What Could Have Been
review:
Okay, so here's the rub. This isn't a bad movie, well...not 30% on Rotten Tomatoes bad. There are certainly moments of greatness here, but it is so often smothered beneath grandiose plot points that need not be included. We get it, you're trying to lay the groundwork for the Justice League, but if I keep having to lean over and explain things to my wife, aka the general audience, then you're losing viewers with your own "cleverness". Now, like I said, there are great things in this film. The imagery was iconic, provocative even, and I was pleasantly surprised by Ben Affleck's Batman (though, he does not, nor ever has had, the gift of prophecy...just watch the movie). Snyder really knows how to direct dark and gritty anti- heroes...which is why it baffles me as to how WB thought it was a good idea to give him Superman. This man *Snyder* doesn't seem to grasp what makes Batman and Superman the World's Finest (hint: it's not because they're the same person, just wearing different clothes). Superman is not meant to be the dour, brooding, dark, and doubtful character. He is the bright day to Batman's Dark Knight; he is the man of bygone morals, meant to show mankind that they are capable of greater good while Batman takes the world as it is, in shadow. DC, show Snyder the door and Superman will be better for it...he's killing your cinematic universe. I understand that you're trying to convey a sense of gravitas, but if everything is serious, nothing is.

Lastly, while it was awesome seeing the Trinity (Superman, Batman, & Wonder Woman) on screen together, it just doesn't inspire and thrill as I'm sure the film executives wanted it to. Trying to reproduce the moment from the Avengers where our heroes stand back to back to face a formidable foe without putting in the years of effort and build doesn't have the same effect. It's the fulfillment of a promise, a promise that Nick Fury made to Tony Stark and that Marvel made to movie-goers in 2008, that made that moment great...not a 3 minute, tell-all trailer. I genuinely enjoyed this movie, but I just wish it had been something more, something inspired, something...super.

title: Not-Batman versus Not-Superman
review:
Okay, Batman vs. Superman. I saw it and I really didn't care for it. In fact, there were some parts I just hated.

But, to start with... Ben Afleck did quite well as Bruce Wayne. A millionaire CEO who actually cares about people that work for him. Who knew? But then things turn to crap.

The bulk of the movie feels like a bunch of smaller vignettes mashed together in a haphazard way.And a lot of times the motivation either doesn't make sense or changes to promote the next violence-saturated conflict.

Speaking of violence:Batman is now a homicidal vigilante. Actually gunning down bad guys in cold blood. The whole lack of morals in a hero bothered me quite a bit. It used to be that Batman would dance on the line between good and evil, striking a balance of doing good work in dark ways. Now, he's solidly in the camp of ugly violent vengeance, not shadowy justice.

Superman is depicted as aloof, disaffected and as an outright jerk at times. He actually just stands around while people burn to death around him. Not even an attempt to save anyone or even help in the chaos afterward. Seems like the writers went out of their way to make the paragon of truth, justice and the American way unlikable. It's less character development and more character assassination.

Then there's Lex Luthor. Played as twitchy, spastic and downright obnoxious, he's quite difficult to take as the arch-enemy of Superman that we've seen for the last 50 years or so.

Characterizations aside, this a movie that's high of flash, low on substance. The worst aspects of psychotic violence fantasies applied to classic heroes who are supposed to embody the exact opposite of that. They're no longer symbols to look up to. I expected more out of my childhood heroes than this.

It's a CGI slug-fest that you have to treat as its own entity and try not to compare to Christopher Nolan's epics.

title: Insufferable
review:
It's hard to even know where to begin. . . .

If you liked this movie, good for you. You can enjoy it to your heart's desire, and I'm not here to stop you. BUT, I am here because the objective quality of this film is to me, insufferable in its entirety by nearly all criteria I can fathom. I can't possibly go into detail about every flaw in the movie with this cursed 1,000 word limit, but I'll do my best. It's fine to disagree, but please do try to understand where I'm coming from before you turn sour about it.

I'm sensing a lot of denial about this movie, much like with the Phantom Menace, which I consider Batman v Superman on par with (that's a bad thing). Everything in this movie is incoherent, boring and obnoxious, but for so many people this movie represents a dream come to reality, and the flaws are understandably hard to come to terms with. There are decent concepts dissolved within the movie, first of which being that inherent of the comic books, and second, the idea of the story building off of a court/trial structure (hence the "v" in the title). However, the overall execution misses the mark by a long shot.

This is the second directorial work I've seen from Zack Snyder, and is where I see his greatest flaws as a filmmaker manifest. Most prominently is the struggle he has between balancing scenes and moments (credit: Evan Puschak). The time spent with and establishing the characters and settings are so fleeting that when the movie tries to amalgamate to something, it falls completely flat. "Scenes" are traded in favor of "moments" as Snyder tries to constantly "wow" you. But the characters and themes aren't given room to breathe. Every moment feels unearned and completely underwhelming. This makes the film boring, and endlessly tedious. This was a minor setback in Man of Steel, but here it consumes nearly every frame of its two-and-a-half hour runtime.

Unlike in Man of Steel, Snyder's visual flair here comes off as far more obnoxious and aggressive. The ramping shots and slow-motion and snap-zooms not only look bizarre, but come off as an outright assault on the senses. It feels like something a child would do for the sake of mindless, fleeting entertainment. The action and battle scenes are completely overbearing as well, and hence become uninteresting and exhausting. Though Zack Snyder's direction is very poor on its own, a movie's basic quality comes down to its script.

The screenplay by returner David S. Goyer and newcomer Chris Terrio is very poor, and is no doubt a substantial detriment to this movie. There are multiple sub-plots that don't contribute anything to the film, but maybe would have with any semblance of focus or convicted direction. The writers simply just don't know what they're doing. The story doesn't feel impactful or important, and the plot is nearly non-existent outside of seemingly random occurrences. The showdown concept wasn't written with any thoughtfulness, but rather as a completely forced set-up for the Justice League in what is by far the worst sequel-baiting I've seen in any blockbuster franchise, ever. Wonder Woman by the way, has no semblance of a reason to be in this film besides marketing, and wastes your time on contrived, studio-bred subplots. Furthermore, the court/trial concept (which is the only interesting part of the movie), adds up to nothing of interest. The characters throughout not only lack basic, consistent personality traits, but are mere vectors that change as the plot needs them to, if there is any characterization happening in the first place, which I couldn't discern.

Now for something that needs mentioning: I'm not opposed to religious allegories so long as they have a reasonable level of self-awareness to them. However, the Jesus analogy is just plain insulting. It's nothing but a fallacious, self-indulgent, self- aggrandizing ego trip, and I spent the better part of an hour trying to find a more scathing way to say that but I gave up.

And let's talk about the "Martha" moment. Yes, I realize it's used as a device to undermine the dehumanization Batman feels for Superman. And no, it's still moronic and laughably bad. I'd call it anti-climactic, but the rest of the movie wasn't building up to anything anyway, so really it was just dumb.

I'll be glossing over the performances, which were functional considering what the actors were given. I can't even blame Jesse Eisenberg for his loathsome portrayal of Lex Luthor, considering that kind of performance could only fly if the director/script were completely incompetent in the first place.

The score by Tom Holkenborg, Hans Zimmer, four others without forefronted credit, and X additional ghostwriters. . . . is bad. At best, the score was minimally serviceable, bland and unmemorable (enough to fool some general audiences these days). At worst, it was abhorrent and distractingly poorly-spotted. For example: the over- presence of the choir was oblivious to the tone, and the Wonder Woman theme is obnoxious and bears no resemblance to her character whatsoever. I picked up thematic development on maybe two cues otherwise, both of which sounded like they were plagiarized from a bad temp score. This score is an abomination of a following act in the footsteps of John Williams and Danny Elfman.

The CGI looks like gameplay footage from a PS3, but even if it was passable by any measure it can't come close to making up for the films blatant incompetency.

Batman v Superman is one of the worst "films" I've ever seen. I went in with hopes that it wouldn't be as bad as I expected, and it actually turned out worse. Also, I'm going to ask you to consider not seeing Justice League. Same writers. Same director. Odds are it'll be the same mess all over again.

Score: 2/10

title: Like it was written by checklist
review:
This movie seems to be created by a checklist. It forgets that for a movie to be great it must be more than the sum of its parts. I like Jessie Eisenberg but his portrayal of Lex lacked power. Wonder Woman wanders around the movie seemly one step ahead of Batman but without any reason why she seeems to know more than she does.

title: Good. And bad. And Ugly. It could have been great.
review:
The movie felt like a comic book, there is no denying it, for whatever its flaws, the story lines comic book fanatics are nostalgically referring to when criticizing films are no better. The acting was good, the complexity of the story was rare for this time and age, the characters were developed, the music and direction and editing came together nicely.

The problems are those of common sense and if you are willing to let go of it, considering it is a comic book movie, you will enjoy it. However little things like an entire drama about piercing the skin of Doomsday when they had just done that a few minutes before, or why Lex hated Superman, or why people did what they did in the manner they did, then switched to a completely different register just seconds after. And of course, matters of physical measures they just play with mercilessly, like the difference between punches, bullets and atomic explosions or how things that have reached outer space fall down relatively in the same spot as from where they left.

What personally bothered me were the villains. Turning the smart egocentric genius into a lame psychotic madman and downgrading Doomsday - my favorite guy in the world - to a 3D printed henchman subtracted from what could have been a brilliant story.

Bottom line: if you ignore the details, the story is complex and entertaining and if you ignore reality you might even enjoy the lavishly violent action details. Somehow in the middle there is an ugly layer of neglect that just disconnects the experience of the viewer, explaining why some people liked it and some hated it with equal passion.

title: one of the few who love this movie!
review:
First thing first: this is not a fake review. Not a paid review. I am one of the genuine BvS defenders and lovers. I was shocked coming out knowing how negative the reviews were. All my family members thought it was awful, and my sister constantly teases me for loving this film. I wish I was in the majority here, but I have to be honest. I freaking love this movie.

CGI is Fantatsic for the most part, and this film really is just a joy to watch. I never came out feeling "depressed" like other reviews say. I came out in joy!

I think, personally, that this film is better than the avengers (sorry, please don't kill me), and my rating for the film is:

9.0/10

title: A good movie with a good build up but an anti climax
review: The beginning of the movie is very good and there is also a good build up for both the characters of superman as well as batman. But the only thing missing was the good climax. I personally felt that there could be more to this movie than just the fight between batman and superman. Also the character of Doomsday did not appeal to me much as I wanted to see more of it. Also the death of superman could have been kept a secret which would have brought more interest in the upcoming DC movies.But the revelation of the other league members to the world has been a good move. I would have given it more if the ending of the movie would have been a little better.

title: Rush to the Justice League
review:
My overall reaction to this movie can be summed up in one word: meh. I went in with high expectations as this film was campaigned like there was no tomorrow. I was ready to see the Man of Steel take on the Dark Knight. However, there was a lot less Batman vs Superman and a whole lot of setting up for future movies. Every character in the justice league shows up sometime in this film. That I found annoying. I wanted more fighting between the most iconic comic heroes of all time and instead I got aqua man floating around awkwardly for an uncomfortable amount of time. And I saw little to no reason behind the fact that superman and batman are fighting. Neither did I see a reason for Lex Luthor's son, Lex Luthor to instigate that fight.

Superman is dead. Way to go WB, you killed superman 2 movies into your attempt of an MCU-like franchise. I felt nothing at all when superman was killed. The doomsday fiasco should've been pushed back to the end of Justice League pt 2. And who didn't know that this was coming after doomsday appeared in the FIRST trailer for this film? Bad decision.

However, despite this film's many flaws, I loved the new Batman, killing and all. It's unlike any other batman I've ever seen and I'm really liking this new take on the caped crusader. Although he was a liability in the doomsday fight, I really enjoyed him fighting street thugs in a brutal fashion. I also liked the action sequences between batman and superman, for the 5 minutes that fight lasted.

I give this movie a 5 because although it did not live up to my expectations, the action and the new batman character almost made it up to me. I do think that Civil War is going to be the superior film because Marvel is so deep into their cinematic universe and I think it's more appropriate for them to take a stab at the whole hero vs hero featuring collateral damage theme. I am not a marvel fanboy, I just think Marvel knows what they're doing and it's better than DC so far.

title: Batman v Superman not really...more like Batman v Superman for only 10 minutes till they realize their mothers have the same name.
review: (Contains Spoilers) Let me start off by saying I had low expectations for this movie since the first trailer and actually watching the movie didn't change it. The movie in general is too long and I feel like Zach Snyder hates Superman. I hated every scene with Superman, Lex Luthor, and Doomsday because in my opinion they were the worse parts about the movie. This is coming from a huge Superman fan. Jesse Eisenberg was an awful Lex Luthor it's like he was trying to be more comical then a sophisticated evil genius play boy with daddy issues and a sense of humor. I didn't like that it was Lex who created Doomsday or how he found out the secret indentures of the soon to be "Justice Legaue". I'm not really sure why it's called Batman v Superman to begin with because while Bruce Wayne basically holds a grudge against Superman for the most part of the movie we only get one actual fight scene. Batman basically beats Superman by using Kryptonite against and as he's getting ready to finish him off it's not until he realizes that their mothers share the same name and lets him ago. I just want to say that all of my years as a DC comics fan I never once realized that both Bruce and Clark's mom share the name "Martha" so thanks I guess Zachary Snyder for pointing that out...Honestly I'm not going to give away everything about the movie like who dies or where Wonder Woman comes into play because in my opinion she was one the best things about the movie. I do think they over marketed Aquaman because he is only in one small scene. The Flas had a bigger role then he did. I will say I thought Bruce's nightmare was unnecessary and not sure why they showed it other then to clearly hinting that Darkseid is coming. Ben Affleck is probably the best Batman to date and that was a total shock but I loved his portrayal of him. Gal Gadot steals the spotlight as Wonder Woman and I can't wait for her solo movie. Honestly if the movie would've just been about Batman and Wonder Woman with a small dose of Superman then I would've loved this movie! Will I watch this movie again? yes, but when it's out on Blu-Ray. Over all I give this movie a 5 out of 10 mainly because of the Batman storyline and the last 10 minutes.

title: It felt broken and unfinished
review:
I've heard many mixed opinions about this movie, yesterday I had nothing else to really do, so me and a mate decided we'll just go see it for ourselves, I can understand now why people are very mixed about this movie.

When I heard Ben Affleck will be taking on the role as my favourite DC hero, I was very sceptical, but after seeing his performance, I actually really enjoyed him as Bruce Wayne/Batman, even more so than Christian Bale. Batman was by far the best thing about this movie, Affleck didn't have to put on a silly voice instead it was replaced with a vocal manipulator, his character also seemed very torn apart, especially with the struggle of losing his sidekick, it even got to the point where he's even started killing bad guys.

Knowing Zack Snyder and how much he loves his fight scenes, the battles in this film were done extremely well, especially in the dream sequence when Batman was in the desert, I don't know why but seeing Batman beating up bad guys in a duster jacket was just pure awesomeness.

As expected, I was very disappointed when it came to Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg), every time I see Luthor on the screen all I see is Jesse Eisenberg being...well...Jesse Eisenberg. I understand they're going for "oh it's not Lex Luthor, it's his son", but why couldn't they just make it the older Lex Luthor instead? I would have been very happy seeing someone like Bryan Cranston taking on the role.

The other villain of the film was, another disappointment, I felt it was way too soon to throw in a major villain such as Doomsday, whereas they could have just done something like Lex Luthor building his armour and trying to take on Superman.

Overall I felt the film felt quite broken, like there were some scenes that could have been left out, some scenes were so short they were only like 2 minutes! I felt Snyder wanted to try and stuff in as much information, back story and development as much as possible, instead of trying to focus on the current story. The visuals and CGI were very impressive (apart from the walking turd that is Doomsday) and really the only thing that made this film worth watching was Batman.

I still think Deadpool is the best superhero movie of 2016, so I give Batman V Superman a 6 or 7 out of 10, if you're a hardcore Batman and DC fan then it's worth checking out, but if you're just someone who wants to see a superhero movie, then best to see Deadpool or wait until Captain America: Civil War is released.

title: Disappointing!
review:
Having just come home from the cinema I've got to say that I was very disappointed with the movie! For starters the first hour of the movie was so boring that I actually nodded off 3 times! Now I don't know if I missed some important parts of the story during the few minutes I fell asleep each time but parts of it just didn't make any sense to me such as why Batman decided just as he was about to kill Superman to not kill him after all but to partner up to rescue Superman's mother. Then what was the point of introducing Aquaman??...I mean they just plonked a 30 second scene of Aquaman out of the blue for no apparent reason at all! Also are we expected to believe that Wonder Woman has been living in Gotham for all these years but never showed her face or suited up in the past?? The way she was introduced to the story just made no sense whatsoever! Then there was the scene of Superman hiking in Alaska or wherever it was it...I mean why would he be hiking and all wrapped up in warm clothing when he could've flown there and doesn't need all that warm clothing because he doesn't feel the cold!

Apart from the above holes and the boring first hour, when the action did start it was as good as you would expect. Ben Affleck did a good job as the new Batman although he did look quite old in some scenes. As a huge fan of the original Wonder Woman I was concerned with the choice of Gal Gadot to play her but she actually did a good job and Henry Cavill is definitely the best choice for Superman since Christopher Reeve.

I've rated the movie as a 6, being just above average but overall I was very disappointed with the movie and would personally recommend that you save your money and wait until it's available to rent rather than pay the extortionate cinema costs!

title: Most Anticipated Movie Of 2016
review:
I watched the new BVS movie in theaters and here is my opinion on the movie. Lets start off with the positives

1. Great performances and acting that makes you believe the characters are angry!

2. Creative and unique ways to show how each Hero was born.

3. Intense action and extreme peril to keep audience entertained.

4. Great special effects and amazing photography.

5. Awesome music and great sound for an action movie.

6. Takes to classic ideas and puts them together.

7. Excellent idea for a successful movie.

Now, time for the bad stuff.

1. You don't actually see the characters fight very often, they actually only fought for about 15 minutes of the 3 hour film.

2. Too long, some scenes could have been cut out to make the film shorter, and most of the scenes weren't that good either.

3. Why does Lex Luther look like a teen that just finished Special Needs school?

4. Batman and Superman just don't have their "hero" feelings in this movie.

5. Bad ending.

Overall I was pretty disappointed but it was still a good movie.

title: So great and So eh..
review:
I'll be the first one to admit that my knowledge of the DC Universe is not so comprehensive as I would like it to be. That being said I was a little worried about this movie coming out since i found out it was in production. Many cause of the fact that people making a movie about BvS is like making a movie about Star trek vs Star wars. All that being said I wanted to like this film far more then I did.

To start off seeing yet another replay of Batman's creation was a huge let down for me personally. All I could think of was..."who doesn't already know this and how many times do I have to watch something that is so established?" They could have cut that time and maybe added a little more time explaining who the hell the Bad Guy actually was. Like I said I don't know as much about the DC Universe as I would like but I actually had to read reviews to find out who the bad guy was.

The Cast - I thought Ben would be iffy but I got used to it really fast and it didn't bother me at all. The cast for the movie I loved, mostly. I feel like everyone fits their roles. Even the brief Aquaman scene. Though the Flash..I was like..who is that? With the Flash TV show out it is hard to see two different people playing the same character. Really just makes things fall flat when they do that.

I believe that Lex had character issues. Not really the actors fault but how he was portrayed. My fiancé who knows nothing of DC kept asking me if Lex was the Joker. At first I recoiled against this but as I watched Lex i could see easily where she was getting that idea from. Lex seemed to be quite mentally unhinged rather then the persona I'm used to associating with Lex Luther the Brilliant/Business man. Lex just seemed to be more of a Smart lunatic then anything else.

The action of the movie was really good and the main fights were pretty epic..just the story behind all the fights is were things fall apart for me. I mean 3/4 the movie is the build up of tension between Batman and Superman and right at the moment of truth when Batman wins (who could have guessed Batman was going to win...sigh), all that happens is "Martha.." and TADA they just clap hands and start skipping down the yellow brick road. What the...seriously. All the build up, the people superman has killed, the way batman treats criminals...all of this..gone..cause their mother's name is the same...*Epic Faceplam*.

That single moment for me makes the entire first half of the movie seem just utterly pointless and that for me is the reason why I just couldn't like this movie as much as I wanted. It wasn't the Actors, Special Effects, the Battles. It was the execution of the story, the flow of the story, and its overall production.

title: The Ultimate Movie Review! - http://tss5078.blogspot.com - @tss5078
review: Marvel's Avengers was written in such a way, that if you'd never read a comic or seen any of the lead in films, you could still follow what was happening, DC was not so forthcoming with Dawn of Justice. Batman v. Superman is a relaunch of the Batman series, taking place long after the events of The Dark Knight Rises, and it's a direct sequel to Superman: Man of Steel. It would be impossible to give an adequate plot description without spoilers, so let me just start by saying this. The beginning of this film, switches back and fourth between Gotham and Metropolis, shoveling in as much backstory as they possibly can on the two characters in an hour. It is this confusing mix of flashbacks, dreams, and current events, that just leaves your head spinning, after that the movie gets pretty enjoyable until the inevitable fight scene, which was just entirely too long, and shoots off in a direction you wouldn't expect it to. If you're not familiar with the characters from previous films and comics, I assure you that you will have no idea what's happening for most of this film. For those who are more familiar, you'll understand what's happening, but will you care? The way they bring these two franchises together is just an utter mess and the cast from Gotham, in particular, don't make things go smoothly. The cast of Superman has worked together before and Henry Cavill was fantastic, his counterpart however, Ben Affleck, was just as horrible as was expected. I've said it before and I'll say it again, he is a terrific Director, but a complete joke as an actor. Batman is a very difficult role for anyone to play, because it requires two personalities, Affleck barely has one, and I was just awestruck by how someone with his reputation actually may have been a worse Batman than Val Kilmer. On the flip side, Jesse Eisenberg, portraying Lex Luthor, was a revelation! Similar to how people felt when Heath Ledger was cast as the Joker, people laughed at Eisenberg's inclusion, but I found him to be the best part of the whole film. The bottom line here, DC saw how much money Marvel was raking in with the Avengers and wanted to jump on the bandwagon. They didn't want to go the same route as the Avengers did, but their way was far too confusing for the general audience, and only somewhat interesting to the fans of both series. In the end, I think the second film will clear up the mistakes of the first and will be much more enjoyable, but as far as this one goes, I could take it or leave it.

title: A very average, mis-shaped picture
review:
Irrespective of what film critics said about this film, I went into Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice with a level head. The first third of the movie was not too bad albeit a long winded explanation focusing on Batman's hatred towards Superman. From then on, the film became very mis-shaped and less clear in telling the overall story.

From an acting front, the spotlight was more fixed on Ben Affleck than the others in the film due to his quite frankly appalling acting as Daredevil in 2003. I always thought Ben Affleck could portray Bruce Wayne very well, which he did but the huge question was 'Did he play Batman well?'. Yes, yes he did. At the beginning of the film, I was hopeful Jesse Eisenberg could deliver as Lex Luthor but halfway through, I felt as if his character sort of fell apart into some psychotic, Joker- esque character which didn't quite fit the attributes one would normally associate with Lex Luthor. Henry Cavill played his part exactly the same as he did in Man of Steel, which is a much better, clearer and more professional film than this.

Also, the film makes a very rushed and vague attempt at referencing the Justice League. Given that the film had to reference the other Justice League members before Part 1 next year, Zack Snyder could have made a better and more satisfying attempt at referring to the other DC Multiverse characters.

Upon reflection, this is a very average film. From what was a very promising start, the film more or less lost its original plot halfway through to focus on a grudge match between two superheroes which, similar to Man of Steel, causes significant damage to Metropolis. This film left me frustrated, it lost its focus and rushed the events leading to this fight, which as you will see, becomes incredibly pointless. The only consolation i will give it is the acting. Ben Affleck and Jeremy Irons deserve credit in their respective roles. 7/10

title: More than a superhero action flic...
review:
I know it's only a Comic Book Superhero Action movie, but I'm going to have some critique fun with it. And why not? After forcing me to sit through 151 minutes of Comic Book Superhero Action of the dark kind, I'm entitled to draw my own conclusions to what the hell lies under the capes of this superhero spectacle. It was the only way I could entertain myself while watching this with a two-year-old child beside me who was more interested in his popcorn and dirtying his nappy! (Not my child, belonged to some inconsiderate parents.)

On the surface it's all about Good verses Evil, and the perception of what is good and what is evil. That is the comic book analysis in a nutshell. Now, in my little demented world of analysis, this deliciously dark film is about the current state of our crazy political world in total chaos. As I see it, Batman and Superman are symbols of political and religious factions. So here it goes---

Batman is politically to the Right. A rich boy who is subconsciously out to revenge his parents death through his battle with crime. He is angry, as the Right tend to be because of all this political correctness gone mad and other social issues that has given rise to dangerous deluded leaders of the wrong kind. (Hang in there, this rant is going somewhere!) Superman is a Lefty. Raised on a farm, but he is not from this planet (a refugee?), who is a do-gooder, mostly saving people of all race and persuasion. Batman does not like Superman, because Superman cannot be trusted after what he did in his last bloody battle (taking out thousands of innocent civilians in friendly fire). And Superman is not from this world, therefore this refugee cannot be trusted by the Right.

Between them is Lex Luther, a ruthless wealthy megalomaniac, out to get rid of the superheroes so as to control the world. So how does he do it? Get them to turn on each other. He wants to be more powerful than they are, and it irks him that these superheroes are seen as Gods (a very valid point made by my son). Like Lex said, "If man won't kill God, the Devil will do it!" Lex is the Devil, ready to take out the Godly superheroes. The wealth and control of his evil corporation gives him the power to achieve that by manipulating the superheroes. But who does Lex Luther represent (besides the Devil)? At first I thought he was a symbol of the Government. But democratic governments are not wealthy enough to achieve anything alone (not unless you are a very ruthless corrupt government that suppresses its own people). Then I saw him as the Media Empire, who manipulate both political factions for their own financial gain. And then it eventually dawned on me that Lex Luther is, Rupert Murdoch! (Have I lost you yet?)

Now how the hell did I come to this conclusion? The opening titles display the corporate logo from Warner Brothers. Now Rupert wanted to buy some of Warner's shares, but the board knew of his craziness and cried, "NO WAY, JOSE'!" And Warner Brothers allows their filmmakers to express their own opinion, and maybe are happy for them to take a swipe at the old Grinch. Another crazy notion I have is that Lex worked overtime to create a distraction for the superheroes to combat each other, just like Rupert has distracted the population with political keyboard warfare. So while the fools (the Left and the Right) are battling each other, Rupert is at work making billions. And at some lavish library fund raising function, Lex makes a speech about philanthropists and the like, adding that, "Books are knowledge and knowledge is power. The bittersweet pain among men is having knowledge with no power!" And there lies the problem when wanna-be politicians with plenty of money behind them spring up with crazy notions to make the World a better place with dangerous ideas, and fools jump in to give a helping hand. These fools don't have the knowledge, but those that do then don't have the power, and can only standby the muddy ocean banks watching the sinking ships. (The attack on the newspapers publishing fluffy pieces and leaving out the real juicy stories that matter was also a nice little sly attack.)

Thrown into the elements of political pandemonium is the Feminist touch in the guise of Wonder Woman. She was a late entry, but added that extra political punch, ready for the next installment in this series. She helped the male ego driven superheroes take on the ever so powerful Super monster created by Lex. The more you blasted this Monster, the powerful it got, thriving on every explosion thrown its way. Just like Rupert continues to feed misinformation to the monsters, trolls and every other angry mob who want to lap it up to justify their ideology. Lex's supreme evil power and his monster could only be destroyed when the superheroes joined forces. Same case scenario in the world of reality, if both the main political ideologies joined forces they could rid of the powers-that-be who manipulate and destroy society to benefit itself. Then only can a decent conversation be held without misinformation and shouting matches.

I can go on, but I'm sure I've already lost most of my readers after the first few paragraphs (maybe the first sentence). But my actual take on the movie? title: A film that starts off promising but turns into a Justice League commercial
review:
I'll start off by explaining what I liked about this film before dwelling into why I was so disappointed.

Many scenes in this film are visual masterpieces. The cinematography in this film, especially the first half, is nothing short of amazing. Snyder's unique style of directing fits well for what this film is trying to be and the camera-work shines in many parts of the movie and doesn't feel as overwhelming and exhausting as Man of Steel did. This movie, despite being dark and grim in tone like Man of Steel, is a bit more visually colorful than it's predecessor. The score wasn't very bad either, it wasn't quite memorable but it blended seamlessly in this movie.

I enjoyed Ben Affleck's performance as Batman. Although, there are things I didn't like about the character of Batman in this film, Ben did a good job with what he was given. He was way better than I expected him to be. I was one of those people who threw a giant hissy fit in 2013 when it was announced that he would play The Caped Crusader. I was proved wrong. I think Ben added more depth to his performance than any of the other actors in this film. Cavill did a great job as well, I think he did good with the lines he were given especially since some of the lines (Superman's especially) are just terribly written. I did not enjoy Eisenburg as Lex Luthor. I felt like he was over the top and ridiculous for a movie that's trying to keep a dark, dreary tone.

The main problem with this movie is the writing, the story structure. It felt like a mess. A lot of the scenes without action were just bland, boring, dreary and filled with dry dialogue. I was hoping to see Batman and Superman duel it out (they hardly trade blows). I wanted to see more than just two great heroes fighting but also the clash between two battling ideologies and philosophies held by these heroes being driven with a powerful story. The film tried, but it was handled so poorly. It felt like 2 stories crammed into what could have been one great story between Batman and Superman. This is because they are setting up the Justice League,but at this point it feels rushed and undeserved. I could have done without the Superman's death, Batman's nightmare sequences, Wonder Woman, many of the Lex scenes that took away from what could have been a great Batman and Superman centered movie.

Batman's turn around (the "Martha" scene) seemed rushed and out of place, it was a great idea with a terrible execution. The writers knew to get Batman to turn you would need to reach his heart and by doing that you pull the "parents death" card. It just felt so halfassed here and it made no sense at all. Made worse when Lois comes in with her pointless exposition explaining that Martha is his mother. The film's tone overall is dark and depressing which makes the (few) humor lines seem very out of place. The pacing doesn't do the film a favor either, there were some parts where the film felt like it was dragging.

Snyder seems to be under the impression that a dark and gritty tone means realistic but writing well developed characters with understandable motives and good dialogue is what makes stories seem real, Regardless of the type of universe they are in. Snyder and Co. didn't do this, so they compensate for their poor writing by making everything dark and grim; giving the visual impression of a realistic looking film. Realistic comes from developing a character to the point where the audience understands their values and beliefs, and the motivations for taking any action are well understood. But more often than not, the film focuses on too many other things when it should be focusing on the titular characters more.

title: Spoiler free review of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
review:
A lot has been written about Batman Vs Super: Dawn of justice in last few days. I finally got to watch this movie yesterday, And here's my two cents.

* It's a fantastic movie. *

I loved Snyder's adaptation of Watchmen(2009), it's one of my all- time favorite movies. And he has honestly done a fan-boy's justice to BvS. Yes, BvS:DoJ is dark, gritty and humorless, almost to a fault. But for me, this is a verbatim portrayal of what DC universe actually is. DC comics never shy away from putting their cynosure on a pedestal with his character flaws wide open for public viewing. Even Nolan's Batman trilogy was woven around a near neo-noir genre to which characters such as a brooding hero struggling to find his true purpose or a screenplay full of long, sullen silences and profound monologues are pretty much inveterate.

Now, any comparison of this movie with a Spiderman or Avengers would be unjust. Think of it this way, at one time DC writers made a possessed Superman kill a pregnant Lois lane before he became an evil tyrant and butchered half of the Justice League. On the other hand, Marvel's gore blockbuster Daredevil had a cheesy boy-meets- girl subplot pandering the movie to an even larger demographic. I don't intend to deduce that either DC or Marvel is better than the other. Both have had different executional strategies with their movies. And both have done really well to bring Superheroes' realm on screen. But expecting BvS to mellow down or metamorphose to a potboiler would be unfair.

Cinematography in this movie is remarkable. Every frame is a visual treat. You don't have to be a comic book fan to enjoy the battle of Man of steel against the Dark Knight. Both Cavill and Affleck fit perfectly in their respective roles. Casting for Lex Luthor could have been done better. Jesse Eisenberg feels too "zany" to play the loathed super-villain. Gal Gadot(<3) is absolutely gorgeous as Wonder Women. And the ugly science experiment, aka Doomsday, though seems an overkill, proves to a handy punching bag to introduce Wonder Women to the big screen. This movie also neatly sets up the plot for the upcoming Justice League film. I would give this movie a 9/10.
