title: Clumsy and obvious
review:
I saw BvS under protest, because a friend wanted to do it for his birthday weekend. I think I may have set a record for how many times I checked the time on my phone, wondering how much longer this movie was going to go.

This seemed to me like nothing more nor less than a clumsy attempt to catch up to Marvel's Avengers franchise and get a jump on Civil War. The problem is that, unlike the Marvel cinematic creative team, Snyder and the rest of DC's cinematic brain trust haven't done a thing to create the dichotomy between Superman and Batman that exists between Captain America and Iron Man. Superman, as he's been portrayed in the Snyderverse, is almost as dark and brooding as Batman, and when one character complains that "(Superman) answers to no one," she could just as easily be talking about Batman.

Three dream sequences in one movie is at least two too many, and three "is he really dead" moments for the same character is worse. I have to wonder if Snyder felt that the name recognition on the characters was high enough that he didn't need to delve too deeply into his bag of storytelling tricks, because he certainly didn't do so for this.

Ben Affleck is very good as Batman--which shouldn't have been a surprise to anyone, Daredevil notwithstanding. Henry Cavill is just as good as what passes for Superman in this movie. But whether because of his own choices or because of how he's been directed, Jesse Eisenberg as Luthor delivers the most toxic performance I've seen since Tori Spelling in Trick. It is bad enough that every DC hero these days is trying to out-grim Batman; I do not need every DC villain to start trying to out-psychotic Joker.

Another thing that bothers me is Wonder Woman--specifically, how she's been used in the DC Cinematic Universe. Gail Gadot is fierce as all hell as Diana, but I'm really not happy that Wonder Woman is in this movie.

Marvel, in setting up the first Avengers movies, first gave us solo movies for what they considered to be their big guns--Captain America, Iron Man, Thor, and the Hulk, the ones even non-comics readers would recognize. Hawkeye and Black Widow did not get such movies (although they both debuted in one of the aforementioned big guns' movies); they are considered to be secondary characters not on the level of the Big Four.

Wonder Woman has not yet had a solo movie; having her make her cinematic debut here, in my mind, demotes her to the Hawkeye-Black Widow level, and the character, as one of the handful of superheroes to survive the Great Implosion of the late 1940s (when most superhero comics were either cancelled or reformatted) and as the most iconic female protagonist in any form of literature, deserves far better than that.

title: This Wasn't Bad But It Really Could Have Been Better.
review: It seems as if DC's "Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice" was just quickly thrown together to try and catch up with Marvel comics and its "Avengers" franchise, in my opinion. Although it seems as if it were quickly thrown together it wasn't too sloppy. It was done just good enough to get the ball rolling for DC to start their franchise but when you're dealing with "Iron Man 1", "Iron Man 2", and "Captain America: Civil War" being just good enough isn't good enough. There were a few good action scenes but most of this film seemed like a lot of dialog. I expected to see tons of action and suspense in the film. Maybe that's how the writers planned it to set the viewers up for what's to come. I don't know. One thing that puzzled me about this film was Lex Luther (Jesse Eisenberg). I though Lex Luther (Jesse Eisenberg) would be older than what his character portrayed in this film. I'm used to seeing the more mature "gentleman", which Gene Hackman and Kevin Spacey played so well! I'm not complaining about the performance of Jesse Eisenberg, I think he did a good job it's just that I expected someone older and more sinister. I'm not a fan of comic books but I do enjoy some of the films made from them so I probably won't be the best judge of this film but compared to other films I've seen that were made from comic books, this one isn't the best. It really could have been better.

title: A Modern Staple of Pop Culture
review:
Soft piano resonates the humanity sandwiched between the psychopathic personas and puzzled slaves of the modern world...

A modern world vividly captured within the subtle ambient score of The Social Network, and so often casting the world of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice.

Despite clear skill by those involved in the production of this film, the lofty ambitions characterized in the creative risks of this film wind up let down by the dialogue pacing, which very well may be due to the horrible screenwriters translation.

Struggling dialogue pace may distract many, yet 'Doomsday, the Rise and Fall of Superman' exceeds in the quiet moments where comically contrasting cinematography helps paint the vague abstract sense of how the screenwriter perceived the comics.

For a Sin City esque film to become a pop culture staple is remarkable in and of itself, in my eyes this film offers a fresh entry into the comic book film noir.

title: Overwrought mess
review:
Vamping off Dostoevsky's comment on families, all good movies are the same, each failed movie is unique. This is why I love to watch failure unfold on the big screen.

Failure is fractal, it scales from the smallest detail to the largest concept. This movie does not need Mandelbrot mathematics to be bad, it has Ben Afflick. Ben is the fibromyalgia of bad, sending out little tendrils through the spine of a movie and making it suck everywhere. Jesse Eisenberg, more like a bad rash, helps with the disaster creation. I am surprised they didn't cast Adam Sandler.

Reverend Ike in Detroit used to shout, "Throw your money to the wall, that what sticks is for the Lord, that what falls is for the Church." Well this was throwing plot lines at a wall to see what would stick. When none of them did, they just included them all into an over-long mess.

What I love about the movie is that it depicts big corporate management failure at its best. First they hire a bunch of expensive actors. We all know expensive is not necessarily good. Gotta have plot, so they ordered a bunch up, and man oh man, did they get it. A bunch. And a bunch of sets, and a bunch of shooting locations, and a bunch of wire work, and a bunch of special effects.

Oh crap, Charlie Rose is in this-- I hope the theaters had barf bags tucked into every seat-back.

This movie is pretty much suited to its target-- Asperger fan boys. Talk about lack of synaptic pruning, this thing is all over the place. Lets see how far along I am--- 46 minutes in, 1:45 to go, gosh help me, the horror, the horror.

They didn't hire a director that understood kid fanboys, they hired a kid fanboy. And they were surprised when they got an infantile movie mess.

I was always surprised when I took probability and statistics, how a certain outcome could be foretold with such a small sample size. But the confidence interval tells no lies. I am sure the minute they came out of the focus groups the studio knew it had a flop. I like to pretend I am the Webster Wolfe fixer they call to patch up the mess. There is no fix for this, Ben Afflick is in it. Maybe they could hire Christian Bale and digitally map his face over Ben Afflick's, but there are probably a whole slew of contract issues. Note to big studios, be sure to put in a clause that you can replace the actor's face and voice in all contracts.

Now somebody is grabbing somebody's heart out, foretelling more senseless plot points. Oh crap, an hour and thirty five minutes to go, give me strength.

Dragging a car by a cable, I guess the laws of physics never mattered, so whey should they now. And Batman needn't stand on a crane shooting tracking arrows into the truck, he could just sit in the Bat Cave and reroute the damn truck with a hack and some Perl code.

I hated this move from the opening shot of Bat Boy levitating, when the whole beautiful premise of Batman is he had no super-human powers. Then it was a dream, and I hated it even more, lazy hack third-rate story telling hacks.

Big plus, Eisenberg just used the word "Junebug" which reminded me of "I'm Gonna Get You Sucka," which was on Bounce last night. I have the DVD, of course. 1:21 to go, please make it stop.

The Superman actor looks a tiny bit like John Travolta, around the mouth. 1:16 to go-- I know a movie sucks when I don't pause the DVD when I go make a sandwich, unlike Vera or even that Woody Allen Paris flick I watched last night.

OK, I am going to take a shower and get ready for bed, while this movie plays out. Pro-tip to the studios-- watch 5 contiguous episodes of NYPD Blue before green-lighting anything. All you need a 6 good guys, 2 bad guys, and Sipowicz slapping one of the bad guys in the back of the head. Anything more is excess. Oh dear deity- Wonder Woman, who's next, Wolverine? I hope he slashes them all to tiny chunks and puts them on a pizza.

Nooooo Kevin Costner-- nooooooooo. If you film it they won't come dude, and they sure won't pay. Time to shower. A new Simpsons on tonight.

Well I'm back, totally refreshed, as if the shower washed this bad movie off me. Thankfully I watched Total Recall 2012 two days ago, so I was prepared for bad. I can't believe I am saying this-- but I would rather watch a Bob's Burger episode then the end of this mess. See ya!

title: Okay movie; Don't have high expectations
review:
Overall: I am a huge Batman fan and all I want is to see the DCEU do well but this movie just failed. This movie is just poor with horrific ideas yet also stirring in some great ones.

Good: Gorgeous visuals, special effects and cinematography which appear to be Snyder's speciality. Batfleck is the scariest Batman yet which is a great thing and could make an amazing arc for his character. Cavil as Superman is okay but nothing career defining. Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman was pretty good and she didn't have too much of a heavy accent. Jeremy Irons IS Alfred with the the one-lining butler we've come to know and love. I don't absolutely despise Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor but can understand his criticism so I'll factor him out. Great score. Some very interesting plot points and ideas which were, sadly, poorly executed.

Bad: The Ending makes me angry. Doomsday makes me sad. SuperDead MAKES ME hate Snyder. I will not discuss the ending any longer as I like my computer. The hatred of Jesse Eisenberg's Luthor is 100% understandable but I am not that bothered. I wont let him affect the final verdict because I think they can do some interesting things for his character. I've declared Snyder's super skill now his failing flaw: storytelling. His ability to tell a story is abysmal. This is why I don't think he should be a director. His talents are needed in other areas such as visual effects. Leave the story telling to people who are good at such as: The Russo Brothers, Nolan, Burton, Donner, Favreu etc. I will get so much hate for this but I love the idea of the Martha scene and Granny's Peach Tea and believe they could have done great things for the movie. I've said they could have been great but alas they were not. A great idea is nothing if the execution is poor and that was the fate of Martha and a jar of pee. The setup for the Justice League is so annoying and misplaced.

Best Part: Batfleck V Cavil: 5 Minuetes of Awesome MVP: Ben Affleck as Batman 6/10

title: Appreciate
review: As I re watch this movie, the more this movie seems like a masterpiece, Zack Snyder has created one of those movies that is very beautiful too watch, it is filled with a lot of comic Easter eggs fans will enjoy, and one of the best comic book adaptations of batman to ever be seen on screen, lets not forget that Batman v Superman fight, although focusing more on the dawn of justice it is still enjoyable, and I believe it gets way to much hate that's why I give 10/10 The glaring issues that I see to get a lot of hate within this movie is that it does try way too hard too hard to be something that it is not, but what it lacks in some things, I do believe that it's faults are strongly out weighed by the things that it does so well.

title: A Flicker of Hope
review:
I loved everything about Man of Steel. From the casting to the script to the gritty visuals. I soared with Clark, felt the loss of Johnathan Kent, and cheered for Superman.

I headed into the sequel with an excited heart. As a story, the film failed in every way. The acting was wooden, the plot expected, and the climax far too clunky to justify the incomprehensible running time. The only positives are Gal Gadot's effortless sensual strength as Diana Prince and Jesse Eisenberg's spot-on neurosis as a truly demented Lex Luthor. It is a shame so much effort and money was wasted on this drab, gruesome effort that couldn't possibly please anyone.

title: Despite all those negative reviews I could say that Batman vs Superman is a good superhero movie with few flaws but still a lot better when compared to Man of Steel.
review:
Batman Vs Superman:Dawn of Justice (2016): Since the reboot of Batman franchise by Nolan,superheroes movies became more convincing and entertaining with less action and more content.He introduced characters' tortured backgrounds and unhappy responsibilities despite focusing on their heroic acts.Zack Synder followed Nolan's style in giving a dark feel to his new movie Batman Vs Superman.Its predecessor The Man of Steel is just average movie which has less content and unlimited tiresome action.So how is Batman Vs Superman??

Plot: The movie begins with the destruction of Metropolis from The Man of Steel.In the wake of the destruction of Metropolis, the people try to determine whether Superman (Henry Cavill) should be praised as a hero or if he should turn himself over to the authorities. Batman (Ben Affleck) on the other hand sees Superman as a danger to everyone and prepares to take on the Man of Steel himself. On a side note, Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) plots to destroy mankind by creating conflict between humans and Superman,while mysterious Diana Prince/Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) pursues her own plans. Will one triumph over the other? Or will the world face certain doom?

Plus points:

1)Story and Direction: Batman Vs Superman has some meaningful plot where people start getting against Superman for his destructive power.The way Superman/Clarke Kent faces these issues and Bruce Wayne's intention of destroying Superman forms a greatest conflict.Zack Synder improved a lot from his previous venture The Man of Steel which totally depended on VFX rather than content.Though mostly inspired from Nolan,Synder did good in handling this massive project.

2)Performances: Ben Affleck as Batman did good and he is successful in keeping Christian Bale out of our minds until the end of movie.Gal Gadot is special attraction for this movie.In her little screen presence she lit up the screen with her beauty and by kick ass style.Henry Cavill did average job.Amy Adams is good in her role despite her less screen presence.

3)VFX: VFX is very good and action scenes are done splendidly well.

4)Music: Hans Zimmer,the frequent collaborator of Nolan gave some wonderful music to Batman Vs Superman.His BGM helped in elevating a lot of scenes.

Minus Points:

1)Editing: Except the last 45mins,most of the movie has several jump scenes.There is literally no scene which lasts for more than 3 minutes.Editing could have done better.

2)Performances of Jesse Eisenberg and Jeremy Irons: They both gave irritating performances in this movie.I missed Michael Caine a lot in the role of Alfred.Jeremy Irons spoiled the fun in that role.Lex Luthor gave his worst performance as psychotic Lex Luthor.

3)Duration: Movie's special edition (which I have watched) lasts for 3hr 5 min.Well I am not saying that its boring,I could say that most of the time story didn't move at all.

4)Misleading Title: Well unlike its title we couldn't see much of a conflict between Batman and Superman.I think Civil War suits this movie well and Civil War could have named as Iron man Vs Captain America(which could be perfectly apt)

So,despite all those negative reviews I could say that Batman vs Superman is a good superhero movie with few flaws but still a lot better when compared to Man of Steel.

My rating 7/10

title: Great movie with clear flaws
review:
Contains some spoilers, if you don't care then proceed...

Look, I'm gonna be honest, this movie has it's flaws:

-3 hours long It is just too much for us, it will get boring, especially with the journalism.

-Too much material This movie is too long for a reason, that reason being: Catching up with Marvel. It's obvious that they were trying to catch up, so they stuffed a lot of material into one film. This is bad and they should've taken their time.

-Martha That was dumb. Not a lot of people get that part well. To put it simply, Bruce was about to take away a son away from his Martha, his mom, thus becoming the criminal who murdered his parents, Joe Chill.

BUT This movie is nowhere near the title of "bad movie" It is very underrated and it is being criticized too much. This is a movie for DC fans who wanted to see these iconic heroes on the big screen for decades, and they got it. Yet they complain because -The fight was too short. The thing is, Batman wouldn't last longer, not in a dozen years of prep time, with that little to work with. He is a mortal man fighting a God, he needed to end it as fast as possible. Snyder's incredible directing of the fight left the theater with jaws dropped and till this day it still makes me go nuts. This is truly our Batman.

The last battle silenced me, I was on the edge of my seat, cheering on Wonder Woman and Superman, while at the same time laughing at Batman's inability to help in a battle of gods.

The only people I'm disappointed in are the critics, who compare this to garbage like Green Lantern or Daredevil.

Watch the movie, I suggest the Ultimate Edition, it's long but worth it for any DC fan like myself. I'd watch it again with great pleasure. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice League 7.5/10

title: Greatest movie of all time: Not so much but surely a one time watch
review:
This movie was the most anticipated movie of 2016. The movie is directed by Zack Snyder, who is one of the best action movie director out there.

I'll break this review into three parts:

Firstly, the direction:

The movie is directed by Zack Snyder who in my opinion is the best action movie director. Yet again he has directed the ACTION scenes perfectly. Note that I've highlighted ACTION, and the reason is that other then those CGI fights the movie is not well organized the events have not taken place in the order as they should have (the part about batman's parents would've been much better had it been placed after Superman says that he needed to save Martha).Then there are errors like how the hell did Lex know that Clark Kent is Superman and Wayne is Batman. The slow pace of the movie in the first half is tiring. I guess the director did too much of character development of the wrong person ( Take for instance Lois's character which should have had less screen time then Lex's character). Moving on to the positives, well I liked the way the other members of Justice League were presented on screen. Their timing was just perfect. As always I loved the CGI. The final fight was damn too great. And it got the whole theater cheering. Also the "BATMAN V SUPERMAN" fight was superb. Another thing I personally liked was the way it ended. I guess it left all of us wondering how will Superman be presented in the upcoming project. Concluding, Snyder was good but could've been better ( I think Nolan could've directed the movie in a much better way then Snyder).

Moving on to Acting:

Ben Affleck (one of my all time favorite actor) portrayed Batman here. I had high expectations from him which were fulfilled as well. Talking about his character I personally think he was antagonist as well as the hero in the movie. I liked the way he was presented in the movie. I hated Henry Cavill's same expression throughout the movie ( It was necessary that his expression changed little as he was a god but still some events required a scary or the terrified expression, especially when Martha was in danger). Moving on I liked Jesse Eisenberg's acting but his role was not well written and neither was his evil character brought out (You never get that strange evil feeling during Lex's screen time). Well next is Amy Adams she was never too good or bad to be truthful, she was average and yes she was given some useless shi***y screen time ( I hated it ). Doomsday's character was awfully developed rest was CGI which was awesome. Well I saved the best for the last, Yes you guessed it right, its Gal Gadot who plays Wonder Woman. She is beautifully written though lacking some screen time. Gadot looks as stunning as ever in the movie. I liked her the most.

Last on the list is story:

To all those who think that the story is dark I'd say stop whining about it, its not some marvel movie with crap humour. I loved the dark tone of the story. Secondly, Batman's dark character was great, the way he becomes negative and positive is good. The first half is boring but I was awestruck with the way the story moves forward in second half. The parliament incident was well executed. Batman taking kryptonite was well presented and acted as well. Overall the story is good but is awfully presented by the director ( looks like he was only concentrating on CGI.

Talking about the bigger battle then BvS ( I mean CW vs BvS ):

Its like eating in two awful restaurant on different days and finding one of them to be better. Well here the better one is BvS. Why? Because the story is better, CGI is better, timing of fights is better and at least it doesn't end at the point where it started.

Ending here, the movie is not the best superhero movie ( my favorite is "The Dark Knight") but yes its a one time watch and more importantly the better movie of the two franchises.

P.S: You will enjoy the CGI if you watch it in IMAX 3D.

title: This is not a movie. It is a product.
review:
This is NOT a movie. It is a PRODUCT. The counter statement to this would be "almost all films are products", which is partially true. But the one thing that most well known/successful films have is: An artistic vision. Because in the end, that's what film is. An art form. Sure, a lot of artists worked on this film, but they are overshadowed by the enormous involvement from the studio.

I feel bad, because they'll be known for doing the visual effects, make up, any kind of contribution to this "film". Their work wasn't what brought this movie down. It was the writers, the director, & the studio who made this into the insult that it is.

Like with most films involved with pre-existing properties (especially comic book films & their cinematic universes), the studio that's in charge of funding attempts to change the vision of the filmmaker. This is something that happens regularly. I'm not a huge fan of them having such a big part in the decision making of the film, but I understand.

BUT, Warner Bros showed it's true colors with Zack Snyder. Zack, is known as a YES man. Agreeing to most things that a studio puts forward. So, Warner Bros tells Zack what they want in the film, no big deal. EXCEPT, Zach said yes. He said yes to a lot of it.

Showing that Warner Bros has absolutely no idea what they're doing. After recently seeing Suicide Squad, their input is also messing up the track record of directors. Regardless of their talents. Warner Bros should be ashamed of themselves.

title: What a Mess
review: I will admit- I went into this movie with medium expectations. I liked Man of Steel well enough, but was curious about most people's complaint- that Superman was turning into a mass murderer or something along those lines. He certainly caused more destruction than necessary and *spoiler*, in killing Zod, broke one of his basic rules. But it was a pretty good superhero movie, not necessarily falling into DC's pit of unfortunate flops (i.e., Green Lantern, Jonah Hex, etc.). But something began to creep into the back of my mind from the internet, and, perhaps being swayed by clever editorials and reviews, I began to grow cautious of Zach Snyder and his work, which has a habit of being both unique, and confused in itself, like Sucker Punch. Looking back, this caution was a bit unfounded and probably biased, so I tried to put it out of my mind as I watched Batman v Superman. Let's just say that by the end of my viewing, I considered my caution to be perfectly legitimate. Let's start with my biggest problem: the editing. This movie got so jumbled up in its own design that maybe was trying to be unique but came across as confusing and messy. The cinematography was decent but could have been better. My second biggest problem: Lois. She was much better in Man of Steel. In BvS, she makes some of the dumbest decisions and becomes a damsel in distress too often. My third biggest problem: "Martha!" Yes. The reason Batman and Superman decide to be friends mid-fight is because their mothers have the same name. My fourth biggest problem: Lex. I like Jesse Eisenberg, I do. And his performance was good, if he were, perhaps, playing the Joker. I know, I know "But he's Alexander Luthor!". Yes, I know. But it just feels so strange. It's almost like the movie wants you to think it's Lex, and then when you find him out-of-character, the movie comes back with "No no no! It's his son!" And maybe this is a legitimate excuse. I don't know. I could go on for days about what feels so wrong with this movie. The Flash cameo is so random and forced just so you can go "Look! It's the Flash!" Wonder Woman had no character, perhaps setting up for her own movie, but having such a bland character who hardly shows up in the movie makes her feel like another pointless cameo, which is a shame, considering she's such an iconic character. However, BvS had its high points. Ben Affleck, who was my biggest reservation towards this movie, proved to be its savior in my eyes. He, for me, captured the Batman persona we see in more of the comics. Not that his character was greatly explored, but from what you see, you almost want to know more about him. I know I'm being nitpicky but this movie just did not feel right. The editing was confusing and the plot was contrived and it was not the movie fans were promised. But it's a good action flick if that's what you're up for.

title: This movie was not bad like critics said. Just more for adults
review: The two super hero's everyone always wanted to see face each other is not a bad movie. It's just not for young children or people that just want action. This movie has more drama and story than your typical super hero movie. It is a movie for people who want to see more dimensions of the characters. I personally didn't like Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luther, he is just not the right fit for that character. He may be the biggest negative in the movie. But that does not justify the harsh reviews that the movie initially received. Also I was skeptical about Ben Affleck as Batman, but he really did a great job. title: In Zach Snyder I Trust!
review:
With this one, don't pay any attention to the critics. They don't understand the graphic novel complexity, and have done little research in the absolutely layered and nuanced film Mr. Snyder has created. every shot is precise, beautifully crafted by Snyder and Team. Now, I watched the "Ultimate Edition" Blu-Ray. I did not see this film in theatres, so have no idea what was cut out of the theatrical release.

At three hours plus, B v S, with its restored footage, soars above so-called "super hero" films, and ensconces itself into the ranks of science fiction, just as Snyder's previous work, Man of Steel, did. Snyder seems to be most in his element when he is leading a team of shared vision. Some of the sequences rival the original Matrix in their breath-taking originality.

I cannot recommend this film enough. Regardless of the critics who will no doubt pan the upcoming Wonder Woman, and showpiece Justice League, Snyder has unified a vision across a multitude of films. That vision is realism, but with the eye of a Renaissance master painter.

review: 4/10. DC continues to try and keep up with the Marvel films, and once again fails dismally. It's like they are trying to make bad movies, what is Zack Snyder doing? title: An excellent superhero movie
review:
I never really liked the Christopher Reeve Superman movies, especially because they had a comic book humor that I did not understand at my young age growing up in a country without comic books. The first Superman incarnation that I liked was that of Tom Welling in Smallville, because it was a more serious take on the character. That's why I loved Man of Steele. It was dark, gritty, and serious, like all the good Batman movies. If you like these versions of the characters you will love B v. S. If you go to see this movie, you have to expect a serious movie, with dramatic events that trigger a really cool plot, that leads to Wonder Woman (just kidding, but in a way she is the outstanding character of the third act of the movie). Even the problematic interpretation of Lex Luthor is fitting if you see the movie (not just the trailer).

The casting of the main characters is spot on, and deliver a really good performance. This Alfred is the best, serious, ironic and with a subtle dark humor. He is more of a sidekick than the usual servant, and that is really cool. Ben Affleck is the best Bruce Wayne/Batman, because in previous incarnations of the character, there were good Bruce Waynes or good Batmans, but never a combination of the two. So, Batfleck is really what I always imagined Bruce/Batman should be. The first time we see Diana Prince (Gal Gadot) she is a sensual, mysterious presence. The second time around she is flirty and with the right amount of humor. The third time around she owns the battle field.

The clash of the main characters is spectacular, real, powerful but a little short (maybe it is longer in the extended edition). The first part of the movie is a little slow, but never boring. The second part is full of action with spectacular special effects. The dream sequences seem to come out of nowhere, but as the producers say, they are important for the future of the Justice League movies, so watch and wait for the future films.

If you are a fan of the Marvel Cinematic Universe you probably will have a problem with this movie, because the newer DC Universe movies are serious, real life copying, and not so funny. And that is good. There is humor in B v. S, but it's never in your face, but ironic, subtle and flirty. Forget the bad reviews. See the movie and savour it. I saw it 2 times (once in theater and once on Blu-Ray) and it was a good movie every time.

title: That last battle worth it!
review:
*Spoilers*

Even though I love Doomsday a lot and that creature at the end is certainly no Doomsday at all, that final battle is one of the best I have ever seen. And therefore the vote.

Each actor plays their part perfectly. I had my doubts about Ben Affleck to play Batman, after Christian Bale, but after seeing the move I think he is very good, he IS Batman. I love Henry Cavill as superman and for me Gal Gadot plays Wonder Woman perfectly, even though she doesn't look as strong as Wonder Woman in comics.

What I certainly did not like about the movie is how they portrayed Lex Luthor. He acts like a lunatic for no reason, and his plans and Superman's reactions to them are so ridiculous. And finally, that thing is NOT Doomsday.

*End of Spoilers*

So the problem with the movie is with its script, and it is totally ridiculous from time to time, but the acting is really good and for me the final half an hour of the movie definitely, definitely worth watching it.

title: Could've been better, but better than Man of Steel
review:
I actually thought that this movie was better than I anticipated. I thought it was just going to be a lot of action and a lot of fighting, but it actually had a story line to it.

The world is trying to figure out whether Superman is a god, a hero, or a threat to humanity, while Batman considers Superman an enemy and must be stopped. At the same time, Lex Luthor can't handle superman being an all powerful-like god, so he fuels Batman's rage to get Batman to kill Superman, as well as try to get Superman to kill Batman to prove that Superman can't be all good. In case Batman or Superman are unable to kill the other, Lex decides to create Doomsday to end Superman.

What I also like about this movie is that it doesn't include as much language as it did in Man of Steel.

However, I didn't like how Jesse Eisenberg was picked to play Lex Luthor and his portrayal of Lex seemed more like the Joker. Also, I think it was premature to kill Superman in this film; I think Zack Snyder could've waited until the Justice League movies to do this, since Superman is one of the founding members of the Justice League. Finally, the animators could've done a better job with creating Doomsday.

With all of that, I still think this movie was an improvement from Man of Steel and I hope that future DC movies continue to do better, as well.

title: Good but not great. It is a movie that will entertain you.
review: Batman v Superman is a good and entertaining movie but does not live up to the amazing amount of hype it has gained for the past couple of years. So I will start with the positives of the movie. Ben Affleck is the best Batman ever on the big screen while Gal Gadot gives one of the best performances of the year so far in her role as Wonder Woman. The visuals are amazing and is capped off by the battle between the Batman and Man of Steel. The action scenes are some of the best you will see and gives you the real fighting style of Batman. Now I'm not asking for a marvel movie but some jokes from people like Superman, Alfred and Lois would not hurt. Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was a mess and way off the source material. Doomsday should have never been in the film and was a waste of time that could have been used for better development between Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman. With all that said I would still buy The ultimate cut of this movie for a better idea of what this film tries to do. Until then I give it a solid 7/10.

In general I think they have spent way too much time developing the whole realm of superhero comics into film & TV. Those types of works do work-but only from time to time. title: Basically What You Should Expect From The Man Of Steel Era DC Movies
review:
You've got to understand something, first of all, that if you look at this movie from an entirely cinematic standpoint, and wasn't all that good. On the other end of the spectrum lie the superhero fanatics, who probably don't think that this movie is quite so good either. And that is understandably so, considering we have a dark Superman with a God-complex, a Batman who kills people and uses automatic weapons, and a Wonder Woman who was only in the movie for the advertising.

HOWEVER- If you are anything like me- a casual movie-goer and just as casual a comic book fan -then this movie is exactly the movie that you would expect when you go to see it. You won't be bothered by the portrayals of the characters, because at least the acting was pretty darn good. You won't be bothered by the numerous plot-holes and un-sensible scenes. You went in to see Batman fight Superman, and that's what you got... plus about 2 hours of worthlessness.

Overall enjoyable, but not great.

To see what my colleague has to say of the movie, go to The Blog 42's blog post about it called "Batman vs. Superman vs. the Critics" - the42ndblog.blogspot.com/2016/04/batman-vs-superman-vs-critics.html

review: There are a lot of things to like in this movie, but unfortunately, a lot more to dislike. Ultimately I loved Affleck's portrayal of Batman(though he was written very oddly). The movie looks very good at times, and kind of dumb CG-fest at times. The plot has more plot holes than I' like to see in a movie that had this amount of hype and money going into it. It's as if the screenwriters didn't really care about these huge holes in this story and just went with the first draft. I wouldn't want anyone to miss this movie when it's out, but one will be thinking of all the moronic decisions the characters make in the movie, which is just plain distracting. Let's see how David Ayer handles things!

title: mind over matter
review:
Let us get the good things out of the way first: This film looks amazing and the director really knows his trade in terms of camera angles and pacing and the acting is very solid.

The real problem is that these super heroes and villains are all emotion and no brains. I don't know what it is with writers these days but apparently it's simply enough to draw characters as emotionally and morally conflicted to get your script approved. There simply isn't anything resembling a valid motivation behind the protagonists' actions here.

Why would Lex Luthor set free Doomsday? If his plan of killing Superman succeeds then he'd be stuck with a destructive creature which would wreck human civilization. Sure, he somehow equates Superman with God and he wants to kill God. He comes up with a convoluted plan to trick Batman into doing so and that sucker falls for it. At NO point does this Batman question the fact that somehow, somebody feeds him weird letters which are supposed to make him see Superman as a threat. That is until Superman says the name of his mother who by the biggest of coincidences has the same name as Mr. Wayne's dead mother. Aren't we lucky that Batman's mother wasn't named Helen?

Superman on the other hand ambles about with no idea what is happening around him. He stumbles into some sort of Luthor plot which makes him loose faith in humanity but aren't we lucky because he still has his main squeeze (Lois Lane) who uncovers a conspiracy which could be revealed by 10 minutes of CSI. Then there is Wonder Woman who does.....what exactly?

It is hard to remember any super hero movie which is so full of plot holes and features characters which lack any coherent motivation for their actions.

Maybe it's because this abomination is nothing but a big trailer for things to come. We have Wonder Woman, Aquaman, The Flash and a hinted Justice League movie. I'm so sorry but DC and WB missed a good opportunity to come up with a plausible story which could do justice to Superman and Batman in their own right. This film is so held back by its many flaws. They meant well but ultimately they fail.

title: Surpringly works thanks to the great casting but a poor third act.
review:
Criminal mastermind Lex Luthor, obsessed with defeating Superman, manipulates Batman into preemptively battling him.

Despite its short comings director Zack Snyder (Man of Steel and The Dawn of the Dead remake) offers a brooding thoughtful take on the seminal figures of our 20th century pop culture. Ben Affleck is surprising perfect as the aged Batman and Henry Cavill once again proves he is rightly another generations Superman. While slightly out of place Jesse Eisenberg does his best at putting a new spin on Lex Luthor. Diane Lane, Amy Adams, Laurence Fishburne and Kevin Costner return and Amy's Lois Lane gets more to do in this installment.

Jeremy Irons' limited screen time is welcomed but with its excessive running time both Holly Hunter and Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman are underused. DC fans will be pleased as Snyder and writers Chris Terrio and David S. Goyer slip in live-action portrayals of Aquaman, Cyborg and the Flash. The film's plot twists are interesting and include the killing off of some main characters, the plot also includes Man of Steels' Zod. However, disappointingly once again the hero's face off with the typical effects-driven, end level bad guy in the closing act, smothering a potentially powerful story. Its also crammed with overt man versus god references.

Snyder thankfully though offers a fittingly dark toned grim whirlwind with a visual grandeur thanks to Larry Fong's cinematography. Notable are a few edgy jarring dream sequences. Wonder Woman's untold story with a Belgium 1918 photograph peaks interest. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice pays tribute to the characters' roots, offering great modern incarnations of them but Dawn of Justice loses momentum by the end with a clichéd effects driven Doomsday battle.

title: Snyder's Frankenstein
review:
What to say about this that already hasn't been crowed? Most likely my opinion will be no different than you heard from previous--and much better--critics than myself.

But that I have finally finished watching BvS, both on the big screen and a second time here, I am left with a singular impression: Frankenstein. That's strange, I know, but bear with me.

It's clear Zack Snyder had a helluva task before him: Marry his distinct visual flair with the seed of a story that will blossom into DC's cinematic universe for the next umpteenth years. But here's the catch: When it comes to Zack, that commandment is both his strength and ultimate weakness.

Zack, of course, excels at inventing revolutionary cinematic scenes. And I will wager he's one of the few directors who can layer meaning upon hidden meaning on a single piece of celluloid. Anyone else catch the Passion allegory at the end of the film with the "cross" (wreckage from the building) in the background that was clearly meant to intone a scene from Calvary? I won't go into too much detail to avoid spoilers, but all three heroes are in that scene, and its a quick flash. But Zack clearly knew what he was doing to instill meaning behind Superman-- and it was either incredibly clever or offensive (depending on your point of view) especially in light that this movie was released on Easter weekend.

But that, again, is Zack's strength. He's a visual storyteller.

Where he fails is in being able to build a long-form original story that will have multiple movies. Zack's best movies are ones that are stand-alone features: 300, Dawn of the Dead and even Watchmen. First--they're not original stories. But Zack has an incredible talent for translating publications to the screen. He's just not an original storyteller. That's clear when we saw Sucker Punch, a noble, yet outright failure.

In this case, instead of an encapsulated existing story, Zack meshed together elements of some of Batman and Superman's more iconic story arcs--The Dark Knight Returns and Death of Superman--into what amounts to a mess. I know. That's been said, but it's true. Snyder's BvS is a mess. He's pieced together the stories from various comics and tries to make a cohesive single story to launch the larger DC universe like Dr Victor Frankenstein tried to piece together various body parts to create a new life form. The end result was a monster that ran amok.

The same can be said for BvS.

That's not to say I didn't enjoy it. I actually loved BvS, if for nothing else than the sheer audacity to take the hopes and dreams of geek fan boys everywhere onto the Silver Screen. And I personally feel Henry Cavill is one of the best screen Supermans we've seen. Ben Affleck is an excellent Bruce Wayne, but only a mediocre Batman. Gal Gadot is an ...interesting...Wonder Woman, and at times hard to understand through her accent. And less said about Eisenberg's Luthor, the better.

If this movie sinned in any big single away against the DC comics cannon is having Batman flat out kill bad guys. That was shocking, and goes against everything us fan boys know about the Dark Knight's moral code as the treads a thin line between good guy and bad guy.

So, I still look forward to the coming Justice League movies, but I do not hold out hope that Zack will be able to craft a compelling original story that will keep everyone happy.

title: Unbiased review ( Not Marvel or DC fan )
review:
Many people had different opinions on this movie but first we have to understand some hard truths before we dig into any review of any critics. Batman V Superman is the lone standing competition to Marvels Civil War and there is already many lobbies that want each other to fail. That includes the so called famous critics on the web. So My review is purely based on neutral grounds as I am neither a big fan of DC or Marvel. I have tried to see the movie just as a movie fan and not as a DC or Marvel supporter.

Now about the movie - Many people complained that the tone of the movie was wrong. Well I disagree. We have to understand that this movie is set on much darker times when people don,t cheer like crazy for superheroes nor they sing songs about them in the street with a guitar. People have seen collateral damage that these battles of good vs evil can bring. Even the heroes themselves have turned older and darker with time as they have evolved their own personalities. Bruce Wayne goes all guns against criminals and superman is not understanding when it comes to bat vigilante and refuses to reason with him first( he did threaten to kill him twice ). So the times are darker than they were before when you saw them in TV and the movie captures them very well. The fact is Superheroes can also be as dark as any villain when they are angry and that is the tone of the movie.Batman played by Ben Affleck was very good and the new intolerant Batman who spares no criminal was something that I liked a lot. This Batman is older mature and much more angry that shows how time has affected the superheroes and their thought process. He does not hesitate to kill or punish the criminals which I liked a lot. Batman of this kind will be feared by me if I was a criminal. Ben Affleck does a great job as Batman and suits well. The action scene in the warehouse was too good to describe and that was something that audience wanted to see from Batman for a long time as this time you could actually see all his moves. Superman's strength and silence was well portrayed by Henry Cavill. This God of strength was already fighting a battle of his own inside as there were so many opinions about his presence in the world. He was silent, angry and was trying his best not to be the monster that people and batman feared he would eventually be. Hence superman chose more of his time with Louise Lane as that is something most of the human beings do. When you are tired with the battle of the world you try to find peace in your loved ones.

Lex Luther however is a big issue for me as the evil genius was portrayed as a stubborn teen nerd who wanted to see batman and superman fight. The motive behind all his actions were not very clear and honestly, Lex Luther is expected to be a more mature and older man.You have made Batman older but forgot about Lex. WonderWoman had very less role in the first half of the movie and tried to be Ann Hathaway Catwoman stealing and deceiving Bruce but her action entrance where very good HOWEVER The plot was rushed and ended. The hatred that was brewing inside Batman could not have extinguished in one second as both their mothers had same name. Lex Luther kidnaps Superman's mother. You don't abduct the mother of a God like person with unimaginable powers in order to make him do your bidding, that is not evil genius Lex Luther, That is teen nerdy immature Lex Luther. Batman,s hatred towards Superman was because his battle with Zod had destroyed half of the city. But he forgot to realize that superman was fighting Zod to save the city and the planet that Zod wanted to destroy. That cannot be a reason for people to hate superman because his battles destroyed buildings. The same Batman damages public property with his own Bat-mobile when he chases bad guys. Is he too bat-retard to understand this simple logic?? How did Louise Lane know that Doomsday was created from Zod and could not resist Kryptonite for which she jumped back to get the same weapon that she threw herself.And what did Lex Luther gain in all of the Batman vs Superman conflict? Why he hated both? As i told the ending was rushed and story writers could have shown less and made a compact story instead of leaving small plots unanswered. This actually needed a part 2.

Honestly I did not hate the movie as few people are saying I think all should go and watch this but yes it could have been a masterpiece if the story writers had given a little more effort along with Zach.

title: I have waited, and now I've watched it
review:
This movie is...controversial. In my opinion it isn't great although has its redeeming factors, it is in fact quite mediocre. Which is personally a big let down because I have been so hyped up for this for so long. My biggest problem with this is its story, to be more precise there is too much story. Now what can I possibly mean by this? Isn't lots of story/plot development good? Well yes, but in the case of Batman V Superman we didn't get any dept instead we get literally a lot of stories.

I reckon there are about 6 or 7 different plot lines going on. Batman's revenge/hate towards superman, Lois Lane journalist stuff, the general public deciding whether they should accept superman, superman dealing with the post 'man of steel' problems, "The dawn of justice", Superman and Lois' love story and Lex Luthor tinkering with "________" and alien stuff(+doomsday). There is too much content. Now I would've settled with like a maximum of 3, the DCCU has bit off far too much than they could chew. It would've been good enough to have this actually being batman v superman, without all the other mumbo jumbo. But because they tried to fit so much in nothing worked, not even the 'main event'. Superman didn't really even have any motives to fight batman, I didn't really see any reason why they settled the feud. Both the motives to begin to fight and to stop fighting were sloppy and didn't make much sense at all.

Now, as a fan of DC and comics in general I could understand what was happening because I've got the background knowledge and I basically know what is going to go down. But my friends who went to watch it with me who weren't comic book fans struggled and was quite confused at the end of it as far as I could tell. Watching Batman V Superman was like watching a Game of Thrones episode without watching any other episodes. Where we cut around and jump around to each character, how are we the viewers supposed to know what on Earth is happening when every other shot we move on to another plot line and character with no build up to anything.

However like I said there are some redeeming factors, Batfleck was great, I like how they did this Batman. He kills, which puts of lots of fans but to me it's absolutely alright. Batman had cool fights scenes and looks great. Superman was decent, basically what we saw in Man of Steel. But the big break out was definitely Gal Gadot's Wonder woman, although most of the time she is Diana Prince when we finally get Wonder Woman it was amazing. From what I can see apparently she is more overpowered than Batman and Superman, single handedly holding off a certain someone that was hammering old Bats and Sups. Plus overall it had good visuals and action.

The reason why I still gave it a 7/10 is because of how much I liked Wonder woman and Batman in this movie and the convoluted plot was more of a cringe to me instead of a complete put off. I understood that they wanted to establish this universe and give us the basis of the DCCU which is why they tried to fit in so much which I can get behind if it means that we would get a great DCCU. So overall although it wasn't great I shall have faith that at least it has paved the path to a great DCCU.

title: A good film with some problems
review:
My expectations from Zack Snyder and Warner bros was just better than Man of Steel. Which I thought was a good film with some problems, it had mixed reactions from fans and critics alike, batman v superman had to improve the level of the DCCU. The big question is did it, well yes and no. The film starts with Thomas and Martha Wayne being murderedAGAIN. However I do think that Zack Snyder put a very nice and different style to it than anything done previously. It then picks up from the end of man of steel but in Bruce Wayne's perspective, which I thought was done absolutely brilliantly. Especially when he runs into the dust cloud caused by superman and Zod destroying his building. You really feel the "Darkseid" ( pun intended ) of the Superman/Zod fight and the human impact it has had. This also really made me support Bruce Wayne and he hatred of superman due to the destruction and loss of live in that whole opening. With that in mind the dream or nightmare sequences involving Bruce Wayne I thought were absolutely fantastic and cleverly made. The desert sequence with the omega symbol and Parademons, hinting at Darkseid, is absolute comic book film gold. Dark, gritty and visually stunning as well as fulfilling the dawn of justice part of the title in this film. The final dream sequence involved the Flash, which I was pleasantly surprised by, was again foreshadowing the future of the universe whilst introducing us the Ezra Miller as the flash. I thought it looked visually stunning and helped the story, and maybe not just for this film is Zack Snyder hinting at the Flashpoint comic. Finally after about 140 minutes into the film we get what wanted, Batman v Superman. Well is it really Batman v Superman or is it just Batman against superman, because from what I can see superman doesn't have as strong a dislike towards batman as batman does towards him. Especially considering that the only reason he has flown to Batman is so he can convince him to team up and fight Lex Luthor, so superman never really wanted to fight Batman that much. However the fight itself once again is pure comic book gold, it is dark and brutal and truly fantastic. Is it a little too short? Did we see too much of it in the trailers? The answer to those questions is probably, doesn't mean that I didn't have a smile from ear to ear whilst watching it. Throughout the film batman has had this clear hatred towards superman, which was handled brilliantly, and then with a flick of a switch they are best friends because there mothers share the same name. I would of been fine with it if they had batman and superman share a little bit a dialogue between each other explaining the situation that they are in, and superman convincing batman why he is not his enemy. This is probably one of if not this worst part of the film, and this is sad because the director and writers had such an opportunity to make a really good emotion filled scene with the audience really engaged with both characters. Instead they sped it up so they could team up to fight doomsday. Talking of Doomsday I thought it was strange to have in the film anyway, but i was ready and intrigued as to how and what they were going to do with him. I thought the creation of him was rather clever and looked really cool. The ensuing fight with doomsday is brilliant, although it maybe a CGI mash, as the fight went on and on I started to wonder if Zack Snyder was going to do something very very ballsy. That something was to kill off superman, which is straight from the death of superman comic. As soon as the kryptonite spire came back into the plot, it was there staring me in the face that they were going to it. Obviously they would bring him back to life just in time for Justice League Part one. Personally for me I think it did work although saying that it again probably didn't hit home as much as it should off because of the lack of build up it.

Finally the good parts of film manly are visual as well as Ben Affleck's performance which are both amazing. The bad parts concern the convoluted script and poorly developed characters. All in all the film is good with some problems, it takes a number of references from the Dark Knight Returns and Death of Superman comics, which is really cool to see.

title: Doesn't live up to expectations
review: The movie isn't too bad, but could have been much better. It always felt like it had a very slow pace or was rushed too much, especially in the Batman and Superman fight. The movie had a lot of Easter eggs which the fans of the comics would like, but not for the audience which doesn't have much knowledge of the comics. Make sure to lower your expectations when you watch the movie other wise you'll be highly disappointed. It is different than Man of Steel, in a good way. Also a good thing about the movie is that it will make you question your perspective and see if you are on Superman's or Batman's team. If you haven't watched Man of Steel you will most likely side with Batman, but even if you have watched it it'll still be interesting to see how the movie pans out. I wouldn't highly recommend it, but if you plan to watch the Justice League movies, this is a must watch.

title: I went in reading a ton of reviews; came out slightly agreeing with a majority of them
review:
This was a meh film. I don't think it is wise for Zack Snyder to direct the Justice League series - just admit there were some flaws and move on. There were some things I liked, and there were some things I didn't like.

First off, Ben Affleck did a good job as Wayne/Batman. I was on the bandwagon of "no, not him. anyone but him". but he was relatively impressive and kept a serious demeanor in this dark mood esq. of a film. He did what he could with what he had, and although he is written in as this quasi- antagonist/protagonist role, he maintained good character and actually impressed me.

Henry Cavill is, well. He's damn Superman; and he did just fine.

HOWEVER, I cannot believe Jesse Eisenberg is still being casted in major roles of big films. Why?!?!?! He is a cancer to good acting and is just taking up jobs that other great actors can do. I wasn't intimidated by him at all, he did not rival other villains from other films. He didn't seem smart or even psychotic, like Lois accuses him of. I just kept feeling throughout the movie that I would love to bash his head into concrete repeatedly. More and more of an annoyance than a menacing villain.

Did we really need to give lois lane that much screen time when Wonder Woman was in this movie. If Nolan's idea was to leave as many short glimpses of Diana Prince to seem more mysterious and have me craving more, great job. However, it did not contribute to the well-being of your movie to continue on this Lois Lane "damsel in distress" act. My oh my, have I grown sick of it.

There were so many times during this movie when I said, "What the hell is going on?" and it made me realize that either A) DC was on a short timeframe to compete with Marvel or B) Nolan has just really lost it as a writer, and Zack Snyder didn't help much; and that is coming from a self proclaimed Nolanoid.

All-in-all, will I see it again? No. Not voluntarily. I just think that the idea was great, most of the casting was good. But overall everything, including the writing could be better. The plot was amiss.

Last thing I'm going to say; how many times are we going to see Bruce Wayne's parents killed? At this rate, that's DC saying "we need to take up more time throughout the movie because we can't come up with original content."

title: Disappointing
review: The film really didn't live up to the hype. Ben Affleck is a decent Batman, but I expected much more since he singed a multi-film deal with Warner. Henry Cavill is good as always, and you can expect that from him being Superman, he's really consistent there. Jesse Eisenberg did some good acting, but that just wasn't Lex Luthor. It seemed more like some Joker ripoff. Gal Gadot did the macho acting here. But, if in a film called 'Batman vs Superman' the thing that's the coolest is Wonder Woman, I think you have a problem there, Zack... The only aspect of the film that can be really praised is music, but that's Hans Zimmer anyway, so you can expect that. Film doesn't make sense in various ways, like the desert scene (Superman fires lasers, not bullets, duh) or the Knightmare (how the f*ck did Darkseid get there) and immediately after that, a futuristic Flash tells some gibberish to Bruce, not Batman (comic lovers, correct me if Flash really knows Batman's identity) also, Superman should be omnipresent one here, but it seems like that title belongs to Lois Lane, that girl is going places... The Doomsday part is really not needed, and somehow feels forced into the film, like the producers actually realized that they made a horrible battle between two main characters, and they tried to make up for it with a bag CGI-ed monster. The ending is really cringe worthy, with that cliché ring scene or that ethically wrong one liners (I'm sure that an average person can make up something better that 'The darkness is coming' or 'We must unite', I mean, really?) That final scene with Lex Luthor made me feel embarrassed, like it was me who made it. Lex Luthor, in this movie is, a bad Joker ripoff with autism. Batman is a maniacal mountain of muscle, and Superman is a teenager who doesn't know what to do with his life, and at the end he goes 'YOLO'. So, basically we got a two and a half hour long Justice League trailer, and if you really love trailers, watch the one for Suicide Squad.

title: BvS is more like Us Vs Makers - We desperately seek to have fun and they don't let us
review:
First of all, since this is my first post/ review on IMDb, its a tad bit long but if you are an average moviegoer and want to enjoy this movie even a bit, do read on.

This movie FORCED me to come here and write something because 1) I am a big big superhero movie's fan (doesn't matter which studio is bringing it in) but this flick was the biggest disappointment EVER for me 2) Some of the comments from extreme defenders are misleading (reasons best known to them) 3) I want other average movie fans like me (not comic followers or hardcore studio fans) to enjoy this superhero flick at least a bit by toning down there expectations (which sadly I didn't do for myself)

Now coming to actual analysis, I want to say that i don't care if something is a sequel or a prequel or setting up anything for future. My sole purpose to be in a theater (making time and spending money) is to have fun. Now this is what I felt when I was watching this movie:

1) Every scene felt disjointed, it was like not a movie but a bunch of scenes from different episodes put together so that they can keep you sitting for 2 and half hours

2) Every character felt like he was doing certain things for the heck of it. They just didn't have a solid reason or motivation. Because of this none of the scenes were engaging or felt relatable. At times when there was a certain reasoning, it was so hurried that it felt like the characters were stupid to go so extreme. Scenes were there because director wanted to film them in a certain way without relating them to other scenes.

Now some have been defending this by saying - this is because people didn't 'get' it. First all this is such a straight forward superficial movie that there is nothing to get. There's nothing deep or profound about it. Second and more importantly when a movie is targeted to make billions, its not made for hard core analytics or comic fans. Even if someone doesn't 'get' it (which is not the case here), it has to be a fun ride and engaging and this fails in being both for an average moviegoer. No point in working hard to have fun. Remember 'The Matrix'. That's a true example of a movie which almost none 'get' on first viewing but enjoyed the ride/portrayal/actions so very much and was so engaging that everyone wanted to 'get' it therefore saw it multiple times. Another more relatable example but not as good as matrix from this director will be 'Sucker punch'.

3) My life was just perfect. While the comic fans were busy arguing whose studios are shelling out better movies, I was on one hand enjoying Marvel giving all light hearted fun rides and DC satiating my dark and intense movie cravings both making sensible, coherent , real fun movies. But with this movie I felt like we all have been taken for granted. You are making billions for god's sake. Don't get lazy. Put some heart into it. The movie felt soulless. I wanted to be immersed into the experience of seeing Batman and Superman in the same frame but they just made sure that I cringe or roll eyes or look at others in embarrassment.

4) One of the best experience of watching a dark intense film is a real engaging threat from an equally menacing villain/ character.

Who the hell is lex Luther and why the hell is he chasing superman like a leach.

No character development whatsoever (Do your homework, get familiar with characters before you come for movies, its not easy to enjoy a movie, work hard)

Why the hell batman wants to kill superman?

Why the hell Batman doesn't want to kill superman anymore?

(pay hard attention everywhere, its Zack Snyder,you need to work hard to understand and have fun)

I can go on and on with this heartbroken rant I guess. But then its just another superhero flick but not a well made one.

Some of the things I liked and enjoyed - 1) Ben Afleck as the brooding intense batman 2) 'SOME' of the action sequences (to be taken at face value) 3) Wonder Woman - mostly because the way character has been portrayed and the actress is hot ( How much I wished for her back story or increase in her role - by the way her entry in doomsday fight in trailers was much more exciting and for some reason made more sense) 4) Short introduction of other superheroes 5) Watching Batman and Superman in the same frame (wish I could mute the dialogs and it wouldn't have ruined the experience later on)

Now if you are anywhere close to choosing or enjoying a movie like me, just remember that its just another badly made commercial pot boiler and highly frustrating because of all the expectations. Go in for this movie with minimal expectations in a theater or later-on on TV and I assure you that you'll enjoy at least a bit. Sadly i didn't read or take reviews from regular/ average moviegoers before going in for this one and paid a hefty price.

Anyways, finally my urge to BvS makers is to please not take us so much for granted. I urge them to replace Zack Snyder if possible. I always found him more of a 'All Style No Substance' kind of a film maker which I occasionally enjoy with unknown characters. But here you have these already established, well known characters. Don't ruin them by treating them as stylized puppets.

title: A labored series pilot
review:
Spoilers, spoilers, spoilers! Don't read. ;)

Those who have been following the DC superheroes comics in the 1960s or earlier (before my time, i.e.) will no doubt recognize the titular reference to the Justice League of America (fondly known to us as JLA). They will also recall, possibly with a silent chuckle, the uniform of the trio (prominently featured in posters today) back then: Batman with a "mask" that was flimsier than The Phantom's, Superman with his silly red under-pant worn outside, and Wonder Woman in bright red, high heel pumps. How times have changed!

JLA pilot or not, it is not an easy task to pitch the two titular superheroes against each other because of the immense gap between their physical abilities. Even with all the gadgets, Batman would be hopelessly outmatched. The solution is all but predictable: krypton. An even higher hurdle is how to contrive a scenario that is convincing. My summary line says "labored", but it works. It is not entirely out of the realm of belief that, with human nature the way it is (forgive my pessimism), there is an innate hostility and distrust of the "immigrant" Superman. And then, although Batman is one of us Earthlings, the hero of dark Gotham City has a sufficiently matching dark side that has been so successfully manifested in the brilliant work of Mr. Nolan. For the catalyst, we only need a scheming villain, Lex Luthor in this case, well selected from a rich pageantry of candidates (the Joker may serve just as well but none dare touch this one again after the immortal, ironically, portray by the late Mr. Ledger). Warranting special mention is the brilliant initial confrontation, not physical, but verbal, between Clark Kent and Bruce Wayne.

Wonder Woman, I must confess, it actually what brings me into the cinema, through the aforementioned poster of the trio (reminding me immediately of the scene in King Arthur (2004) where Keira Knightley shot her first arrow, standing between Clive Owen and Ioan Gruffudd). It is actually Gal Gadot, to be exact, sorely missed after she died as Gisele in "Fast and Furious 6". An Oscar should go to casting her as The Amazing Amazon, although her appearance in this pilot is brief. There are a couple of scenes with Wonder Woman in evening dress playing a cat-and-mouse game with Bruce Wayne. The climatic battle brings her out in full costume, not the star-and-stripes swimsuit half a century ago, but something that can almost pass her off as Lady Sif in Thor. She is also instrumental to the only moment of humor in this movie, poising between the two superheroes battle-station style. "Is she with you?" one of them asked the other. "I thought she is with you", the other jabbed.

The rest of the cast is impressive. Henry Cavill brought over from his "Man of Steel" reboot of Superman Amy Adams (sweetheart), Diane Lane (adopted mother), Laurence Fishburne (boss) although not some others (Russell Crowe, Ayelet Zurer, Kevin Costner). The Batman side, carrying no Nolan heritage, is represented by Ben Affleck and Jeremy Irons (guess what character he plays). The most notable performance belongs to Jesse Eisenberg, with his unique interpretation of the above-mentioned villain Lex Luthor. Personally, the best delight is seeing long missed Holly Hunter, playing a no-nonsense Senator Finch. It is hard to believe that her Best Actress Oscar win in "The piano" was more than two decades ago.

I have not said a great deal about the plot to justify the opening triple warning. Here it is, very briefly. With details omitted, the titular confrontation is crafted by Luthor who, failing at the verge of success, brings out his final trump card, a monstrous being hailed as indestructible. That is where Wonder Woman drops out of the sky, literally, to trigger the "dawn of Justice". The plot device instrumental to the final cliffhanger is so silly that it threatens to turn the movie into a farcical comedy. The ending though, is anything but comic, as Superman dies a heroic death. Needless to say, he will be resurrected in the first full-fledged JLA next year, together with The Flash and Aquaman. Personally, I am disappointed in not seeing Green Lantern, whether Ryan Reynolds version or other.

This movie has several flaws, but I don't think that the critics are doing a good job on rating it, they are been harsh on it and nitpicking with so many little things only to try brining it down or that's what they look like they are doing. I really think is one of the highlights of this movie. To conclude, please don't get discouraged by the awful critics, this is a movie that you have to see, you have to understand it, it is a very intelligent movie and has a lot of deep meaning into it, if you are a superhero fan, a comic book reader you will get pumped for all the action, the dialog, the references and eastern eggs thrown to you during the whole movie and if you are not, you'll still have an awesome story, a political thriller, compelling characters and exciting action that no other movie has.

title: Batman vs Superman: Should have been a 2nd Man of Steel
review:
Batman vs. Superman is a movie that is ill named. It should have been a 2nd Man of Steel movie. I say this because this movie was absolutely about Clark Kent/Superman and very little to do with Bruce Wayne/Batman. But before I get on with any further cons, I'd like to start with what made the movie good.

Well, I gave one thing away: Superman. Superman is what made this movie good. And I really mean it. Henry Cavrill's performance as Superman was superb. They really gave the character the depth and readability that he was sorely lacking in Man of Steel. He's much more humanized, and his struggle with the world's perceptions of his attempt to be a good guy are believable and really tug on your strings. He's a good guy who doesn't want to be seen as bad or do bad things, but ultimately his power and god status clearly make people afraid of him, including the deuteragonist Batman and the antagonist Lex Luthor. He's a good example of people fearing what they do not understand, and when people come to realize he is good, it serves to show the hurdles Superman had to overcome to get there. The movie did an overall excellent job of this.

I also really like how they characterized Lex Luthor. He is a brilliant but crazy egomaniac who finds the idea of a person more superior than him to be both frightening and dangerous. His penchant for perfection has him conceiving an elaborate plan to kill Superman that almost worked, had Superman and Batman's mothers not had the exact same name (lol). Still, despite being a bit quirkier than the comic/cartoon Lex Luthor, he still manages to be charming when needed, and psychotic at the right times. The bald head at the end was perfect as well. A worthy villain who plays to his strengths.

Wonder Woman, for the short time she was on screen, sounded, moved, and enjoyed combat just like the real Wonder Woman. She could have used a bit more boldness to her voice out of the costume, but now that she's been introduced she'll have time to flesh the character out better in the future sequel. Lois Lane was also a much better credit in this movie than she was in Man of Steel, where she actually had a use other than being the Damsel in Distress, actually getting to the bottom of the conspiracy and aiding Superman emotionally.

Now. *sighs*, to get to where the movie really started breaking up Batman-Yes, I know most people who went to see the movie saw it for Batman, and if you take issue with this, you can officially go gargle a raw egg for all I care. Anyway, I feel whether or not he was the best Batman ever is a moot point. The best kind of bland is still just that: bland. I feel that he was in the movie simply as a catalyst for an epic fan boy fight (which feeds right into the fact that Batman has far more fans *coughs*).

His back-story is nothing I haven't seen done a dozen times, his motivations while fitting with the character are WAY too hasty without any real thought, and the fact that he was going to steal a dangerous weapon from Luthor just to use on Superman is utterly stupid. If this is supposed to be the movie's way of saying, "Batman is one step away from being Luthor.", congratulations, I knew that ever since I read the comics and watched the show. This isn't clever, it's just a ton of filler to show off Batman.

The "Tell me, do you bleed?" was corny as hell and made me face palm, and the dream sequence which got interrupted by a future vision where he saw a red armored stubbly Cyborg was utterly jarring (and I couldn't understand a damn word that Cyborg said in that scene either). Alfred is not endearing at all, being a bitter old man who's just there to sneer at Batman (which got old after the first 3 times). Other than saving Martha Kent, he was pretty much pointless in the movie, fan filler.

Also, a minor complaint. If Mercy is supposed to be Luthor's robot bodyguard, why the chuck is she NEVER in any scene where he needs protection? Luthor should have probably junked her for failing so hard.

So anyway, after all is said and done, I feel the movie deserves a 7.5/10, which in my book is "good". Not "great", not "meh", not "bad", not "OMG YOU SUXXORS!", just good. I feel the good elements of the movie held it together, but this movie really should have just been a Superman Sequel to Man of Steel, rather than having Batman's name in the title. Oh well, at least Superman was good in this movie, and that's what really counts.
