title: Good overall. Affleck was excellent as Batman.
review: I enjoyed this movie for the most part, and don't agree with the overly harsh critics. This Batman was more like the Batman of The Dark Knight Returns comic-book tetralogy, who had gotten darker, more gritty, and more brutal with age. Gal Gadot pulled off an awesome Wonder Woman, whose character showed that she was in the big leagues in terms of her power and abilities, despite the actress herself not being Amazonian in size and stature. Henry Cavill continues to do a good job as Superman, and stays true to what comic-book fans would expect. This movie had superb action and fight scenes, and amazing audio. Jesse Eisenberg did a decent Luthor, although his personality diverges from the traditional one you may be used to. He's a bit more zany and more high-strung, and I think that annoyed people who expected the traditional Lex Luthor, but I was okay with the creative license. The only two points on which I tend to agree with critics is that too much was revealed in the trailers(!), and the movie perhaps tried to cram too much in. This movie could have actually been three movies, although I understand that it is intended as a setup for the Justice League franchise. I felt that the movie could have developed the emotional struggles of the characters better if the producers didn't try to fit so much in, and some parts of the story had to be glossed over because of time constraints. However I was not disappointed with this movie on the whole, as some critics say they were. Definitely worth seeing if you love the DC universe. Maybe not a "home run" like *Deadpool*, but at least a solid "base hit" or a "double," and it opens up a huge amount of potential for follow-up movies.

title: good as usual but below expectations
review: Although I give this movie a 10, it did not meet my expectations too much. At early 30 minutes, I think it was boring because there was no full action. It is rare in a superhero movie. I don't understand and am a little bit disappointed why the battle must happen in the night. This makes the visual effects of this movie cannot be enjoyed maximally. What a pity! Although Henry Cavill and Ben Affleck' s acting are very good, their battle action could not make me scream "wow" when I was watching it. With a very big budget, this box-office movie should give more than Man of Steel and Marvel hero movies. Since I am a very big fan of Superman, I have to give it 10.

title: Spoiler-Free Review
review: For three years, I've waited impatiently for this movie. At first my expectations were not very high because I didn't have any faith in them following up the mess of Man of Steel with success however after watching every trailer, my expectations increased for the movie and I was really excited. Seeing the movie the day it released in Australia, my mind was blown away! This movie had a great storyline, great dialogue, action and including several small references to satisfy the DC Comics fans. In my opinion, all the stars really nailed their roles with originality. Props to Henry Cavil, Gal Gadot, Jesse Eisenburg and especially the show-stealing Ben Affleck for carrying this movie. While this movie is supposed to jump-start an exclusive DC Comics Universe, it really started off great with more interest in the future films such as Wonder Woman and especially Batman Stand alone films. The highlights of this film would have to be Ben Affleck's scenes as both Bruce Wayne and Batman especially the titanic confrontation with Superman who Henry Cavill improved upon following Man of Steel plus both Gadot's wonderful performance as Wonder Woman and Eisenburg as the villainous Lex Luthor. The only problems i had with this movie would be the pacing and editing issues in the start where they would jump-start from many scenes to the next. However as the movie progressed, it truly presented a great film which could satisfy the DC Comic Fans especially who should look forward to the upcoming films of DCU.

title: Is this justice, or is it just criminal?
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice promised so much but only partially delivered. This film had moments of greatness and the Batman scenes did not disappoint, but the Superman and Lois Lane scenes, for me, were rather prolonged and felt very forced. The acting was of an acceptable standard with Jesse Eisenburg's portrayal of Lex Luthor being intriguingly idiosyncratic. However, he was fairly one dimensional as an evil scientist.

Zack Snyder's direction was all over the place. At one point the story would focus on Bruce Wayne's origin, the next something completely different. When the film came to the inevitable climax with Batman fighting Superman, something still felt like it was missing. In my opinion, the dialogue and plot needed some reworking to improve the end product. However, the fight itself was visually pleasing.

The lack of respect for the source material was criminal. Batman is seen using guns and killing numerous people, neither of which is true to the character of Batman. Having said this, Batman's scenes make the film worth watching, and I really look forward to seeing Ben Affleck's Batman confront Jared Leto's Joker.

For me, this film had a lot of potential but was overcrowded with disparate plot lines and too many characters. Overall, I would give the film 7 out of 10 because it transported me to the world of comic book heroes which I have grown up enjoying.

title: "You're not a god, you were never even a man"
review: Since the first reviews hit this movie has been getting poor reception. Okay, that's putting it lightly...this movie has been almost universally panned by critics and the question on everybody's mind: does it deserve it? The short answer is 'no'. This movie isn't terrible, it isn't the worst comic book movie of all time however it's not exactly good either. First of all, the good: This movie starts out good, great in fact. As a long time comic book fan the opening scene felt straight out of The Dark Knight Returns, it was shot beautifully, which is definitely director Zach Snyder's strong point. For the most part the entire movie is well shot and looks visually stunning. The performances are decent as well. Affleck (we'll get to him in a minute) was great, Gadot had barely any screen time but hone in what little time she was given. Cavill ups his game from Man of Steel but still isn't given much to do. He still feels rather bland. Everyone else is fine but nothing special with the exception of Jesse Eisenberg. The best part of the movie, hands down, is Affleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman. He is utterly amazing! Every scene he is in he steals. You really get the sense of a damaged individual who believes he is doing the right thing. Many were sceptical about this casting but he absolutely nails it. That however, pretty much sums up the positives. Now the bad: First of all: the pacing.....or lack of it. For the first hour, maybe more, this movie is incredibly boring. The final hour is then jam packed with non stop action. While at first it was fun to see Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman fighting Doomsday it got old really fast. The entire third act ends up being one giant CGi fest. And on the subject of that CGi...remember when I said this movie was visually stunning "for the most part"? Well here's why. Doomsday looks like GARBAGE. The effects in no way look finished for the entire final battle scene. It bewilders me how a movie that has taken 3 years to make can have effects that look this bad in the final product. The main problem with this film however, is it's a mess. That is the best way to describe it. For the first 10 or 20 minutes it felt like every scene was introducing something new. Sub plot after sub plot and while the film made half-assed attempts to connect all these story lines it never really succeeded. That was then mixed with the fact that this was essentially one big trailer for the Justice League movie. It did feel eerily similar to films like Iron Man 2 and The Amazing Spider-Man 2. There are points in the movie when what little plot there is literally stops dead in its tracks to shove gratuitous cameos in your face - how did this get past editing? This would all be forgivable if the film was at least some what interesting. If its plot was enjoyable. But it isn't. The film really doesn't know what it wants to be. For the first half it is a political thriller that features questions about the need for Superman and weather or not he should answer to someone. This is all dropped in the second half and never brought up again. The whole reason for Batman and Superman fighting feels incredibly paper thin and the 5 minute long fight scene, as fun as it was, really doesn't warrant the movies title. Overall, don't listen to the critics saying this film is utterly terrible. Go see it for yourself and make up your own mind. That being said, don't listen to the mindless fan-boys on YouTube who had made their minds up long before the film was released, either. Keep in mind that I'm not a professional critic and I certainly don't have a "Marvel bias". While I like to consider myself a comic book fan in general if I was forced to choose between the two then I would choose DC every time. 5.5/10

title: When two worlds collide
review:
Batman v Superman is a highly ambitious movie. Two superheroes each in their own class meet in a common universe, Metropolis v Gotham City, day versus night, human versus alien. On one hand you have a human being whose intention of doing good is born from the loss of his parents as a child to crime and on the other is an alien being whose intention of doing good is to protect the people that gave him a home and accepted him among themselves as a primary mission of his existence and survival to the destruction of his home planet. Now we are put in a situation that the very people (including Batman) that accepted Superman in the first place start to worry about him endangering their kind. All makes perfect sense, people are afraid of what they can't control even if Superman is trying to protect them. But as the saying goes, with great power comes great responsibility, things get messy and opinions divided. Right? Well, here things go a little messy as well. Firstly, I think Zack has his occasional great inspirational moments when it comes to directing. One of my favorite superhero movies is Watchmen, not because is a superhero action movie but because is a movie that asks questions about what it means to be a superhero as seen from each one's perspective. Batman v Superman lacks these introspective questions like what's their purpose in a chaotic world. Why is that they have to share the same world, did the existence of one influenced the existence of the other or they just purely happen to coexist in the same place at the same time? What Christopher Nolan did in the Dark Knight was to show that the villain and the hero are one and the same substance in two different states, one can not exist without the other, as the Joker says: "You complete me" and "What will I do without you?". The Joker never intended to actually kill Batman as Batman also chose not to kill the Joker when he could have the chance.

And that's what doesn't add up here. The plot is centered around Superman and this could have as well been a movie about Superman only. Batman is only dragged into the story by an event that happened in Man of Steel and while I found that quite interesting at the beginning, I was expecting to see some more past interferences between the two characters to help with the story telling. Instead Batman is presented just as another representative of humanity who wants to stop Superman from producing more damage to the world. In a sense it is understandable as he is what he is, a human, with emotions and fears, although with good intentions. But for an intelligent human superhero he seems to think and act in a too foolish way, that is, he is not thinking that Superman is as emphatic as any other human and might have a mother and persons who love him closely, nor does he thinks that Superman may as well be the best hope they have to save humanity in case of a higher power treat. Superman sacrificed his own kind and his only connection left with his home in Man of Steel in order to protect the human kind and now the humanity raise against him. All said how could there even be an equal battle between the two, man vs god? Here is where Lex Luther comes on the stage. Superman has nothing against Batman but Lex, similar with the Joker, is the chaos creator; he is the one manipulating the characters bringing them to fight each other and doing this out of pleasure. He is the real treat and only when the two superheroes realize this is when they join powers.

The movie seemed a bit too fragmented, too many things happening that somehow come together in the end nor is it a movie about a real battle between two superheroes but a battle of two superheroes with themselves. Characters lack a bit of a background story and they seem to collide with each other only briefly without forming stronger connections. The dark mood of the movie was quite fitting and sound was extraordinary, the opening sequences were well done and reminded me of Suckerpunch and Watchmen opening. The end was totally unexpected and sad but this is what makes the difference in a blockbuster movie, to take risks and leave the audience in wonder.

title: Mishap with DC universe presentation
review:
Honestly, I think it was a brilliant effort to set up the mantle of justice league in just one movie. Zack Snyder eagerly tries to bring realistic view of the DC universe in his movies, however bleak it may be.

Over the years fans have created the persona of their favorite Superhero which is tough to break considering the recent efforts. Plus it is tough to fill in the shoes of brilliant retired actors such as Christian Bale. Cast for BvS is shallow as they fail to bring out that persona associated with the character not that they lack trying.

Graphics A1. No doubt, especially Doomsday. Actions were beautiful and realistic, not defying the laws of physics. Uh may be a little, but its fiction, so no complains.

The script, as has been repeatedly mentioned by the critics, is a disaster. Events occur in haphazard manner which often seem confusing. Extraneous scenes occur from time to time which have no relevance what so ever. Especially the character of Lois Lane, played by Amy Adams, who seem to be of no use in the script except she is vital to superman.

title: Hmm ... not as good as Man of Steel
review: Bit disappointed, but I did like the movie. It's a mixed bag of great and not so good. Ben Affleck did an excellent job of Batman. Gal Gadot was excellent as Wonder Woman ( and tough, I like it ). Some very good cinematography and the beginning sequence is very well done. The 2 big failures were casting Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor - he's a spot on cast for The Joker, not Lex. I blame the directing on this, Lex was portrayed as a Joker style character high up in Corporate America. Eisenberg's genius is that fast talk, fly by your head insults going too fast for you to catch it before he's on to his next sentence - very cool in so many of his movies/rolls, but in this movie he's making Lex to be mentally unstable, which is not Lex and not believable such a person could put together a massively powerful/wealthy corporation, just isn't plausible. Lex Luthor is a sociopath megalomaniac with a foot in psychopathy ( he doesn't enjoy mass murder as much as using it as a tool to wealth/power ). My comment isn't that Lex isn't authentic, but that the artistic license to match the character to the actor's strengths/charisma simply doesn't work in this film. The 2nd big letdown is the ending with the energy monster - this is simply lazy writing. Hulk tried it and sadly ended a very good movie with a simply stupid ending. The whole attacking him makes him stronger was poor. Writing for Superman is very challenging, hard to come up with compelling scenarios where his life is at risk. But this ending was just bad and a quick excuse to show off massive destruction special effects. What's interesting is I was expecting the Superman arc of the story to be the strongest given how good the director did with Man of Steel - but it was the opposite, Batman was much better. The Batman/Superman confrontation was too quick ( could've been more interesting/clever opposed to just a boxing match - the comics were much better in this regard ) and the ending fighting sequence was too long and too over the top. You're simply not going to pull that amount of destruction without massive casualties to be completely overlooked with the funeral of a single person ( god? ) - contradicts the beginning of the movie. Anyways, I loved 1/2 and felt let down by 1/2. Gave it a 7 given it's better than average compared to movies out today.

title: Good, but not the masterpiece it could've been.
review:
Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice is by far one of the weirdest movie going experiences I've ever had. First off, I did enjoy it, but it's a flawed film make no mistake about it. This was like watching Alien 3 all over again. I've never been to a movie that felt so dead but alive at the same time. If that makes sense?

The first hour and half is all build up and it's so depressing. But I think that was the point. The film felt a lot like David Fincher's horror classic "Seven" and I got the impression that Snyder was trying to get something off his chest here. For me it didn't come off to preachy like some critics have stated, but there's an underlying theme of frustration that runs constantly throughout the film, especially when Superman shows up.

And as much as everyone says that Snyder hates Superman I found that he was relating to that character the most. You can tell that Superman wants to smile and feel good, but he's stuck in a world that doesn't want him to. I can understand that and I found myself enjoying this part of the story.

The film's story though is its biggest problem. There's to much going on. A lot of the supporting characters suffer because of this. Lois Lane and Martha Clark being the main ones.

It also feels like this was a sequel to movie that was never made at times. Man of Steel should've had a stand alone sequel and then they should've done the team up. I wanted to see more scenes between Lois and Clark like at the beginning showing the audience how their relationship had blossomed over the past eighteen months. But it's just business as usual once these opening scenes are over. This is not an empty headed movie, far from it, but it just lacks some in the character department.

As for Batman? Affleck pulled it off like I knew he would. He puts the Nolan Batman to shame. I know that might upset some fans but that's how I saw it. This Batman is crazy for sure. This is the Batman I've always wanted. Its Frank Miller's version come to life. Another surprise was actor Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. I thought for sure that he would get on my nerves but he was a surprisingly effective villain. And he's interested in more than just real estate for a change.

I also enjoyed how the story brings Batman and Superman together. It's well thought out and makes sense. I was always concerned about this but I'm happy to say that it didn't feel awkward or forced. And it was cool to see Wonder Woman. I don't know much about that character but after seeing her in this movie I know I want to see her solo movie.

With Rey from "The Force Awakens" and now Wonder Woman, it's good to see stronger female characters appearing in films. Let's hope it continues.

But at the end of the day BvS could've been so much better. There are parts in this movie that promise a film that could've been a masterpiece. But with this story I think that Snyder bit off more than he could chew. 7.5/10

title: Not Great but Still Satisfactory
review:
I read lot of reviews before going to watch the movie and every single review said this was a disaster. I personally feel all those reviews are just wrong.

This may not be the best movie ever made or an amazing thriller but it is what a Batman vs Superman movie could be. The first half is all disconnected, seems like you are watching small stories instead of one single movie. The second half is much better and has some great action scenes.

This movie is just about bringing Batman and Superman together and will act as a launchpad for the next movie which definitely will be Bigger and Better.

title: Improved from Man of Steel; Not Epic but Decent to Expand into Justice League
review: The most anticipated sequel of Man of Steel has once again attempted to differentiate its own DC brand from those in Marvels through the return of the Dark Knight which continues to amplify a darker, grittier and sombre adventure of clashing heroes. Slightly overlong in term of running time, the film opens surprisingly beautiful with flashback of Wayne's disastrous childhood and further progresses into the reckless fight between Superman and Zod at the end of previous installment. The ambitious and potential major acts in the film - conflict between Batman and Superman, Lex Luthor's motives and the fight against villain at the climax; all seems to be underdeveloped and not well executed, leaving several questions of all the intentions behind. Ben Affleck as Batman is on par with Bale's version but a bit more brutal and stubborn, Cavill's Superman is fine but a bit depressed, Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman is definitely the gorgeous one and she manages to capture the attentions even with a limited screening time, Jeremy Iron's Alfred owns a great chemistry with Wayne but Eisenberg portrayal of Lex Luthor is over exaggerated. Although heavily CGIs, Snyder has delivered spectacular visual effects and intense actions among the superheroes while the collaboration between Zimmer and Junkie XL are just outstanding to produce different adrenaline driven theme scores for all the superheroes. While it might not be the best superheroes flick, lacks of humors and emotional depth compared to The Dark Knight trilogy, it is an overall improvement from Man of Steel and the Nolan style ending is still impressive enough to further expands into the universe of Justice League.

title: Unique experience obliterates superficial wrongs.
review:
Discussing this movie is nearly impossible. Yes, the movie is peppered with superficial wrongs throughout, like fake camera effects (the chromatic separation was a big offender here) and seemingly an action sequence that displayed stunt men humorously waiting for the "knock-out blow" instead of a fluid struggle. I suppose one can apologize for that fight with dream logic because it does have a subtle yet important role to play with interpreting some scenes beyond their obvious message and easy implications.

My friends all say it was such a bad movie but they loved it because no movie has been made like it before. I feel much the same way except I do not think it's a bad movie and I still love it. To be fair, I expected to hate it more than anyone for many of the same reasons that put so many off in the trailers, like casting lex or the missing tells of what is supposed to be epic exchange between iconic titans. Even with the most generic and offensive repeat of a pointless monster in doomsday, which is the shoe-in conflict for the most imagination deprived writers and handlers, still managed to create scenes of ferocity I have always wished could be shown but have only scene Marvel come somewhat close with Hulk (the only Marvel comparison I will make). Doomsday fight is terrible on paper, it was terrible on-screen, but I won't lie that it achieved something greater than anything else I have seen with supernatural battling sheer ferocity... and the audio played a significant role in pulling this off.

The movie is a mess, not a big mess, but filled with traces of genius and plenty of balls. The audacity alone sells the movie but it really is something you must make your own mind about because for the first time, the usual barometers of taste in which I trust now to be consistent and gain a composite expectation were almost all wrong and even though I can see why they arrive to their conclusions I still have to disagree. The movie is just that different and doesn't shy from the full range of symbol to the cheapness of sign. A discerning mind will enjoy these elements once they penetrate past the surface "christ" mode projected upon superman, because sign does go deeper and reviews criminally overlook this but that's all I care to say. Be warned, if you were prepared to absolutely hate this movie you might more likely to be thoroughly surprised and love it for all you don't see coming.

title: Don't read the reviews, go and see it
review:
When I heard Ben Affleck was playing Batman I was not happy at all. I was wrong. He's awesome as Bruce Wayne and as Batman. The film is great and after 2 and a half hours I could easily have watched more. The story is top notch, Affleck, Cavill and Gardot are great as the DC top three and mentions also have to go to Jeremy Irons as a brilliantly acerbic Alfred and Jesse Eisenberg as an excellent 21st century Lex Luthor.

I have gripes but they're minor, Superman's character still seems to be in a state of flux as if they don't know which way to go with him and the finale is a little CGI heavy so at points is does tend to resemble a video game (albeit a really good video game)rather than a movie but none of that detracted from what was one of the most enjoyable times I've spent at the cinema

Just go and see it and make up your own mind. A brilliant opener for the DC Cinematic Universe and I can't wait for the next installment.

title: Watchmen 2 - Dawn Of Justice
review:
I saw the film last night at BFI IMAX theatre in London, and I was so eager to stand up and get out as soon as the film finished. Not because of the film but my seat was extremely uncomfortable, get better chairs BFI!!!!

This film is good! Not perfect but also certainly not bad either, it's just a good film with many memorable moments. My main gripe with the film overall is it doesn't know what it wants to be, is it a political drama? is it a batman film? is it a superman film? or Justice League prologue? I say that because the two title characters are very different. Requiring different elements to really work properly on screen, but as they jump to the next character to quickly it feels the main characters are underdeveloped. There was a rumour a while back that it was going to split into two films and I wish that actually did happen. The first film could of been all Batman viewing Superman from a distance, then ending just before their battle. Then the second could be all Superman, they could have spent time with each character and learnt more about them.

So the cast, I was unsure of Ben Afleck as Bruce Wayne/Batman but he did a decent job. He's improved as a actor over the past few years, it was a solid performance. Henry Cavill was born to be Clark Kent/Superman, he was the heart and soul of the film. The supporting cast are all brilliant, Jemery Irons in particular who had some funny moments. Now Lex Luther, Jesse Eisenburg did a amazing job, I really enjoyed his take on the character. He was funny and sinister at the same time, a very memorable villain. Now I would like to mention the cameos, Diana Prince/Wonder Woman was very good but served no purpose to the plot or overall film. Barry Allen/The Flash, Victor Stone/Cyborg and Arther Curry/Aquaman cameos should have not been in the film at all, saving it for later films! As for the nightmare scenes they felt misplaced, and was only really there for the hardcore fans.

Everything else was absolutely fine, and being very enjoyable. Some batman scenes really reminded me of Batman Begins and Dark Knight. Also a lot of the film really reminded me of Watchmen (which I love) for some reason. The style and tone are very similar, and fight choreography is also similar. Actually I think it's because they killed Jeffery Dean Morgan in the opening scene and the villains plan is to blame the death and destruction of civilians on the industructable man when someone means to murder him. Sounds familiar right?

And finally I wish to address the director Zack Synder and the editing issues, the critical reviews have highlighted it as the films biggest problem. Now I really like Zack Synder, he has made some of my favourite films. I know he has the ability to tell great story's with multiple characters, but he didn't quite hit the mark this time. Was it studio intervention? Maybe but I admit I'm worried this could be his last film in DC universe, I hope that doesn't happen. The editing is not great but like I said this film doesn't know what it wants to be and tries to do much. But it is a good film and it's just one in a long line of DC films. If I remember correctly Iron Man 2 had the same issue and look how then films turned out.

The Ulitmate Edition with extra 30mins will probably correct my issues, so the film will probably become a 10/10

And finally for all the haters out there WB/DC will give the people a film to strive towards. They will race behind it, they will stumble, they will fall. But in time, they will join Marvel in the sun. In time, they will accomplish wonders. I believe, you should too!

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
review:
Well, after all these years, it has finally come to this; Day vs. Night, Black vs. Blue, the Son of Krypton vs. the Bat of Gotham, and so on. So, how does it hold up? Let me tell you:

Pretty damn good. I know a lot of critics have been slamming the crap out of this film; so, here is a change of pace with a positive one. The film is set 18 months after Metropolis and the rest of the World were introduced to Henry Cavill's Superman, and the Man of Steel has come under fire after the horrific tragedies that took place during the hero's battle with Michael Shannon's General Zod. The entirety of Superman's storyline revolves around the repercussions of his actions and his power, and Henry Cavill does a superb job as a defeated Superman coming to terms with his own powers that he doesn't fully understand, against power that he doesn't fully understand, and we are treated to a very interesting and thought- provoking political story that asks an important question; do we need a "Superman?" One of the best things about this film that makes it far superior to 2013's 'Man of Steel' is that it replaces irritating flashbacks (that, I thought were unnecessary and removed any chance of actual character development) with story. A pretty good one, too.

It's always good when movies like this ask questions and have the character's think about what they've done and what they can do to improve on themselves. And, yes, I know that this can make things seem very down and gloomy, but, hey, none of you were complaining when 'The Dark Knight' did it, so suck it! Anyway, yes, it is very gloomy. But, it's good to have adult conversations in comic- book movies that don't have any quirky joke interrupt the drama (Marvel Studios, anyone?) I guess what I'm trying to say isÂ… a bit of politics never hurt anyone. Holly Hunter appears in the film as US Senator Finch, who asks these questions about Superman and whether or not we really need him to solve our problems (after all, he does provide a lot of collateral damage) and she does a good job as the politics side of the fight against Supes, (we all know who does the actual fighting, but we'll save him for last). She acts as a good foil to Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor.

Speaking of Lex LuthorÂ… he's a mixed bag, a really, really mixed bag of a dangerous threat andÂ… some quirky kid. Are we ever going to get a cinematic Lex Luthor who is actually depicted how he is in the comic- books? Cold, dominant and downright evil? That's not to say that I didn't enjoy Eisenberg's performance, he really went for it, and I applaud him for that. He was a very good villain, I might add, and entertaining as all Hell. I got a "Rich Kids of Instagram" vibe from him who thinks he can do all this diabolical stuff because of Daddy. As I write this, I am warming to this version of the character more and more. I just wish he toned it down a little, but there is still room for improvement.

Speaking of improvement, this film has some of the best action scenes I've ever seen in a comic- book film, most of it coming from Batman and the Batmobile. However, towards the end of the film, it does go back to the CGI filled spectacle of 'Man of Steel'. My auditory and visual senses were both ringing when I left the theatre to get a burger.

The intense build up to the fight of the Century, I felt, was unnecessarily lengthy. The fight should have been somewhere in the middle of the film, and then one at the end. And their final fight should have been way longer. Having said that, it was quite a fight (albeit, VERY one sided)

Whilst we're here, let's talk about the Bat in the room. Ben Affleck may just be the best Batman we've ever seen on screen (sorry Clooney). He is a much angrier and cynical Batman than ever before, much like Kevin Conroy's Batman from the 'Arkham' series of games. He's still the great detective that we know and love, but also more of a 'break necks, ask questions later' kind of guy. As Bruce Wayne, he's smooth, cool and charming, and as BatmanÂ… he's a force to be reckoned with. I look forward to seeing more of him.

Gal Gadot is great as our first cinematic Wonder Woman, and actually outshines the rest of the supporting players. She isn't given much to do for most of the film (why would she? Ain't her movie), until the very end when she assists the boys in an intense and explosive battle against Doomsday, which I enjoyed watching.

The culmination of the climactic battle against Doomsday resulted in THE ballsiest of endings, and took a huge, huge risk that I was not expecting, and I say 'kudos' to the film- makers for doing what they did.

My Verdict: this was a historical epic of 'Ben Hur' proportions. A great story, fascinating questions, excellent performances, pulse racing actions and overall, a damn good time.

title: I was wrong, this movie didn't sucked.
review:
Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice review: Well like most people who have seen DC and Zack Snyder movie's, I went into this film with a grain of salt. I expected it to be a major suck fest with whining emotional heroes who hate themselves and lots of needless violence and explosions. I was prepared to waste 2 and a half hours of my life. I will admit, I was wrong. While this movie wasn't the Popcorn movie that Marvel puts out, it was very enjoyable. Yes, it was still dark in nature but not unbearably so, it melded the light and dark into something that makes you go Hmmmm.

Now first, the flaws: The movie is, as stated, really long. However, as long as it is, it still felt rushed in a way. Trying to cram too much into this little space. So, empty your bladders before the movie because, chances are, you will miss a key plot point if you get up for those few seconds. The first half was almost unbearably slow coupled by the fact that the editing of the movie was sub-par at best. It didn't have a natural flow and seemed really choppy at points. Be prepared to settle into a scene and then go WTF, what happened.

Now the highs: Let's get this out of the way first. The Internet's biggest OMG moment was casting Ben Affleck as Batman/Bruce Wayne. People cited Daredevil and said it was a mistake. As I have stated before, he did a good job in Daredevil, but was limited by the crapping writing of that movie. Here in BvS, he was an OUTSTANDING Batman/Bruce Wayne combo. He portrayed Batman like he should be. A great fighter who relies on his speed and agility as well as gadgets, not just a stand still guy who gets a lucky shot. Kudos Ben, you done good.

Second, and this was my biggest fear going into the movie. Man of Steel sucked. Superman was portrayed as a whining little "bitch" who hated himself and his powers. Not so much here. Superman acts like Superman and displays his powers in full force. Yes there are moments where he has self doubt, but considering what happened previously in this movie, this time they were understood.

Thirdly, Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was incredible. She played the classic Greek Goddess, beauty, brains, skill and a lot of acting talent. She lit up the screen in each of her scenes. Plus, she is not bad to look at.

Let's move on to Lex Luthor as played by Jesse Eisenburg. This isn't the Lex we all know and love. This one was something completely different but still a Wow factor. This one was straight evil and psychotic but with a genius still beneath. Go into the movie with an open mind on Lex and you may find his performance enjoyable.

I won't review plot as I don't want to spoil it for those who haven't seen it yet, but I will say this. 1st act, slow to buildup. 2nd act, fast paced and action packed. And let's face it, the first time you see the Trinity of Supes, Bats and WW on screen, it will make you feel all child-like and happy.

I say, go see it. And this is coming from a Marvel fan-boy

Frankly, this movie completely blew me away. The performances bear particular emphasis. Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot are so perfectly cast and give such strong performances that I am now wondering how I ever doubted them. I never doubted Jeremy Irons, and he lived up to my expectations. The returning cast also get a chance to stretch their acting muscles and more than live up to the task, in particular Henry Cavill who has a couple of scenes where we can truly see his talent. title: Boring, pretentious garbage
review:
...Where do I even begin. Absolutely nothing about this movie works. I somehow ended up watching the three hour long version, but decided to only subject myself to the torture of the 2.5 hours viewed by cinema-goers, and I tried desperately to keep my eyes pried open during that time frame. Despite sounding uncultured, this film's major flaw is that it's so...boring. If your movie is going to have the gall to be three hours long, you best believe that you have some intriguing characters, plot, and action to make me hold my pee in the theatre that long. The first sign we're going to be in for a long ride--we get a recreation of a scene that is literally the ONE THING everyone knows about Batman already. We get it, his modus operandi is avenging his parent's death! But then, the audience is expected to know everything about Batman, Alfred, and the Batcave; while ALSO having been expected to have seen Man of Steel. Funny, considering this movie's title isn't, in fact, "Man of Steel 2". So after some more of Snyder's snooze- worthy slo-mo shtick, we're thrust into the middle of a plot so incoherent that I'm still not entirely sure what exactly occurred. This 'film' feels more like a string of tangentially related clips than an actual movie. Trying to keep up with the logic of it is exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, the cinematography is so dull and dreary that it makes Watchmen look like Carebears in comparison. It's a perfect suit for the thudding, pretentious, grim script though. I don't think a single affable thing is uttered in the whole movie. I believe it exacerbated my clinical depression.

But moving on to the ostensibly fun part--the characters! Our attention is already taken because we know them; Batman, Superman, Lois Lane, even Wonder Woman shows up for a bit. These characters are iconic and we expect certain things from them. But the issue here is--who exactly are we rooting for again? Do we want Batman to kill Superman, or vice versa? This lack of a clear protagonist is a glaring error, because we have no stake in the action. Most DC fans aren't going to desire the death of one of their beloved superheroes, so...what's the point? Batman's quip that if we have a 1% suspicion of Superman being a threat, then we should annihilate him is painfully dumb. If I have a 1% chance of getting cancer, should I go ahead and begin chemo? So to further our lack of investment in the conflict, we have some woeful acting to accompany it. Henry Cavill's only asset is his sculpted body, Ben Affleck does yet another brooding Batman, and Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor is an impotent, sniveling recreation of Heath Ledger's Joker. It would be amusing, if literally anything at all in this movie was amusing.

By the infamous "Martha" point (and oh dear god is the logic employed there mind-numbingly baseless), I couldn't even maintain a semblance of interest in what was going on. If anyone who enjoyed this film could actually decipher the plot and wasn't just watching to see two beefcakes beat each other up, please let me know the ways of your immaculate intelligence. For this film fails to either entertain, or enlighten (its not-so-subtle motif of godliness is eye-rollingly tired and shallow)--so therefore, what's the point?

title: Tries to do everything and fails miserably because of it.

We see super man beat up some terrorist to save Lois (lane has been omitted from her name in the credits so I will too), after this a whole bunch of discussion about superman needing to be kept in check. Eventually we meet who who turns out to be Luthor the film, who played the role like he was confused with whether he was Lex Luthor or a precursor character to the Joker. His biggest issues include he isn't suave, he has no legitimate reason to have issues with superman (superman actually helped his business so yeah he should actually love him). He eventually introduces Bruce and Clark who make little comments about each other's alter egos.

Lex sets up a trap to get Superman blamed for blowing up a meeting of world powers, by convincing Senator Finch who he is inexplicably on friendly terms with for some reason. While no one believes Superman blew up the building, he still is blamed for not stopping it.

Lex seduces the military to let him see the Zod ship by using the most awkward product placement for Jolly Ranchers in history to convince him to let him see the ship. He convinces the ship he is the last living kryptonian and then proceeds to meddle with the cloning capabilities (The ship initially refuses as it goes against krytonian law, but agrees after he claims he is the last living kryptonian despite using his own dna with the ship, would have thought a civilization this advance could make a better security protocol for preventing this from happening) of the ship to mix his DNA with Zod.... which if we learned anything from superman 4 mixing Lex's code with kryptonian dna results in bad things that will hurt people.

Batman and Superman meet and Superman tell him to retire and Batman asks if he bleeds. Bat

Superman goes off to seek advice of Johnathan Kent, who is an illusion? a hologram from the fortress of solitude? I don't know.

Superman is then lured into a trap when Lois being useful by being kidnapped by Lex, he in the ultimate cliché pushes her off the building and superman catches her. He then give superman an ultimatum, kill batman or he'll have his mother killed (cause superman can't possibly with his vast array of powers come up with a way to find his mother before Luthor reacts... when Batman can) They have a titanic fight where Batman holds the upper hand much of the fight thanks to his Hulkbuster-clone and kryptonite gas (am I crazy or this seem like some type of gimmick Ceaser Romano Joker would have used if superman came after him?) Ultimately Superman tries to reason with this batman to no avail until he cries out Martha... and the fight literally ends because Batman realizes they both had mothers with the same name (This plot point literally is cringeworthy, dumbest reason for a pointless fight to end). Superman and Batman make peace and realize something else is coming that is vulnerable to kryptonite, right after Lois tosses the kryptonite spear batman had to finish off Supes (because this batman is cool with killing which is another problem I have with this movie) Batman goes off and rescues Martha, after shooting a bunch of people (because in the comics he never had any issues with guns or murder or anything) Finally Lois retrieve the staff get it to Superman, Wonderwoman inexplicably is there for the final battle with Doomsday.... Superman and Doomsday fight and he gets killed while killing doomsday.

Lex goes to prison, his head is shaved, batman sneaks in to mess with his head... he starts cackling (seriously he knew he was playing Lex Luthor right? ) As the films ending we get a hint Superman isn't dead.

In looking back.... this movies biggest problem is it tries too hard to tackle and stitch together stories that just don't connect... It doesn't spend any real time needed to tell any of its stories properly. It sticks in other members of the justice league as easter eggs. This fight between Superman and Batman was better portrayed in the direct to video movie The Dark Knight Returns part II (It made more sense and it had a reasonable reason for them to fight). Superman Doomsday better shows the fight between Superman and Doomsday. Justice League War did a much better job as the introduction of the justice league... something based on this would have been a much better storyline to follow then trying to force a fight between Superman and Batman at this point (it really feels this film was trying to get the drop on Civil War). The only really likable things in the movie were Alfred Pennyworth and Diane Prince/WonderWoman and they had about 12 minutes of time if you combine their appearances. The movie drags on for 2 hours (it seriously feels like 3) I can't recommend this movie. i'd have to rank this movie as in comic book movie disappointment between XMen Origins: Wolverine and XMen-First Class in terms of failing to be watchable.

title: My Thought on Batman vs. Superman
review: For as much hype as this film indicated I was going expecting a knockout. Was it? No. But was it a total disaster? No. However, people for a long time have been waiting to see Batman and Superman on screen together, it is finally here, so there's that. The long wait is over as Zack Snyder gives us a CGI filled 2 hour film with two of the most iconic heroes ever. First, lets talk about the cast who played the characters. Henry Cavill is still able to show us why he was chosen as the next Superman, but doesn't offer more then what he did in Man of Steel. Superman himself in this film really got the "super" knocked out of him, meaning he got beaten up pretty bad, first by Batman, then by Doomsday. And what is with the ending, talk about a gutsy, but head-scratching conclusion to the film. I never would've expected to witness this move, but when they went for it my jaw dropped. Next, Ben Affleck as Batman may be the best part of this movie. How ironic? People were saying what a bad choice it was but they miraculously pulled it off. Batman however I don't particularly like in this one. He is so unnecessarily violent to the point where I was thinking him as the villain. I felt he was more of a villain then either Lex Luthor, or Doomsday. Many times we see Batman killing folks, and annihilating Superman to a pulp. In the previous Batman films he's only violent when he has to. Here, he just wails on people when he doesn't really have to. And one more character/actor I really liked was Jeremy Irons as Alfred Pennyworth. I think he should have been Alfred the whole time, as far back as Batman with Michael Keaton. He owns this character and brings a new perspective we never saw before. So, that's it for the positives. What's wrong with this film? Well, like I said before Batman is really violent, and kills people. Last I checked he wasn't like that. The ending will stir some questions when Superman bits the dust, yes, you heard right. They killed Superman. Why? I don't know. But I must say, it did make the last bit of the movie interesting. That's about as much I can say of how interested I was in this film. Before that seen I was constantly looking back and forth between the screen and the clock. I knew I was in a long movie, but nothing kept me on the edge of my seat, or biting my nails, or even giving me goosebumps for that matter, a film like this should do that. But one of the biggest problems I have is Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. What was Zack Snyder thinking? I know he must have wanted a different approach, but my goodness, he is as out of place as a tomato in an apple bin, he just doesn't work for the character. Lex is meant to be someone like what Gene Hackman did, heck Jeremy Irons would've been a better choice. And Doomsday...lets move on. I also think the title should've been Batman and Superman, because there is only one fight between them, and it really isn't much of a fight as Batman pretty much kicks Superman's rear end to oblivion. Well, that's all I got to say about it, if you are a fan of either hero you may have a good time, but you need to be a die-hard, know-it-all fan or else it will fly under your radar. For my opinion I'd just wait until it comes out on DVD. Now to grade. title: The Good, The Bad, The Ugly
review:
The Good:

1. Batman-Although I consider Christian Bale to be the definite Batman (thanks to Nolan etc.) Ben Affleck did a good job as a older, bitter, jaded Batman. The fighting was on point as well. 2. Superman-Henry Cavill beefed up more for this movie and continues to be a pretty good version of Superman. If you liked him in Man of Steel, you'll like him here. 3. Out of all the new DC movies, her individual movie (set in WWI) is the only one that looks promising (as long as Zach Snyder doesn't have any input...). 4. Batman Superman fight-gritty, brutal, cool. Nuff said.

The Bad:

1. Batman-For most casual movie goers, they may not know who batman is. He is a man on the verge of becoming a criminal himself but what separates him is his moral code and the promise to his parents. Here? He uses a gun. And he kills. I've always liked Batman because he was smart enough to defeat his enemies without resorting to a gun or killing. If you've watched the dark knight, he says "I only have one rule". He was referring to him killing people. Joker wanted him to kill because that would cause him to be one of them. But despite the pain, Batman endured. Here? Nope. He kills with the same weapon his parents died to. Guess Joker won. 2. Batman superman fight-We all waited for it but superman fans will be a little irritated that the man of steel looks so mortal. So incompetent, So unprepared and so inadequate to deal with Batman. Also, this fight was under developed. They didn't have to fight each other 3. Justice league-although I like wonder woman, her character was forced in. She didn't need to be there. She didn't add anything to the story. The email message from Batman was forced too. First, how would Lex even know the symbols (Flash's lightning bolt etc.) of the justice league? Last, Batman has always been the loner/rogue member of the group. Doesn't make much sense that he'd be the one to bring them together.

The Ugly:

1. Doomsday-looked like a bad cgi lord of the rings troll. Final fight was a big cgi fest, fast pace and completely takes you out of the movie. 2. Lex Luthor-"the red capes are coming" "ding, ding, ding". Jesse Eisenberg was a idiot/mad scientist which is different than any other version of Lex who is a smart, calculating villain. This Lex was trying to be a semi joker rip off. 3. The storyline-confusing, convoluted, messy. Biggest thing is things DON'T MAKE SENSE. Don't believe me? Think about the following: a. Mercy follows Bruce down stairs. Bruce says, I was looking for the bathroom. She says OK. THAT'S IT. Wouldn't mercy instead show him where the bathroom is at? But for the sake of moving the story along, she leaves allowing Bruce to set up the device. b. Clark follows Bruce downstairs. Clark kept hearing a conversation going on between Bruce and Alfred. He follows, get's distracted by the television then leaves. OK I get it, he had to save a little girl. BUT a better story writer would have him confront Bruce to find out what he's doing, maybe find out about the device which would cause Clark to start investigating Luthor himself. BUT because it's Batman vs Superman they have to fight each other. I guess they can't work together first then maybe 2 movies later fight. It means more when you care about what the characters have gone through, grown together but come to a place where they disagree. c. Final point (believe me I can keep going) Superman goes underwater to get the kryptonite spear. He almost dies coming back come. Few scenes later? He flies full speed WITH the kryptonite spear towards doomsday. No effects whatsoever from the kryptonite. Overall the critics were right...which is sad.

This movie could have been more. In fact Zach Snyder didn't have to do much. WB as a whole didn't have to do anything. Why? Simple. If they've watched the Justice league cartoons, Batman superman movie "world's finest" it would have been great. They literally could have just transported that to the big screen and it'd be successful. The writers understood the characters which is why it worked. Zach and WB as a whole could have set up something great. It should have been a worlds finest adaptation. Simple, concise, easy to follow.

title: Single handedly destroyed my love of comics - nearly
review:
The only reason I didn't give this flop a 1 was the opening sequence. Viewing the carnage of Metropolis from Bruce's point of view was inspired. It really highlight the enormity of power at Superman's disposal. It reminded me of how I felt reading Alex Ross'"Marvels". As a lifelong comic (and specifically Superman) fan, I was always frustrated at how the cinema had never really captured his near omnipotence and the fact that every man and his dog had kryptonite was always annoying as hell.

BUT - after the intro sequence, I found myself bored stiff. The upside was Ben as Batman and the usual cast was the best part of the first movie. Luthor however, was a total failure. The dream sequences were disjointed and confusing and the action was ridiculously over the top even allowing for the usual suspension of disbelief required for super heroes. Ironically I find it easier to do so with Superman than I do with sequences like the Batmobile chase. I mean Jeez - please stay within some framework of physical possibility in a damn car chase - please. Doomsday looked like a cross between a cave troll and the Abomination. Surely portraying him like the comics would have been a better option. The destruction in the final battle was so immense it became a bore. The CGI was average too compared to Man of Steel. A tragedy that this wasn't better. I can see most reviews are kinder than mine and I'm gad others found something to like but I suspect the higher ratings come from fans of movies more than of comics. I'm just about over the genre to be honest and I wish that were otherwise.

title: How about killing Ben Affleck? That would be the dawn of justice!
review:
What a disappointment this movie turned out to be. I watched it after seeing X-Men Apocalypse, which was indescribably awful in every possible way, so my expectations were reasonably low.

Credit where it's due: the opening scenes were very powerful, and quickly established that the quality of Batman Vs Superman was going to be far ahead of Apocalypse. But by the time the first act was over I could tell it would be downhill all the way, and sure enough that's what happened.

Superman is now even more of an emo than Batman. Batman is still unable to overcome his fear of guns, and still refuses to kill people. He's also stuck with some kind of weird unresolved mummy issues.

Batman needs to wear a mask and speak in a silly voice to disguise his identity. Superman only needs to put on a pair of glasses that do absolutely nothing to disguise his identity but somehow make him completely unrecognisable.

Lex Luthor is now a giggling halfwit (I must be one of the very few people who thought Jesse Eisenberg actually made this work) yet still capable of running a vast high tech multinational corporation.

Wonder Woman is supposed to be a super-strong Amazonian warrior, but she's built like a stick insect with the body mass of a flea. She doesn't bother to disguise her identity at all, because nobody cares.

Batman wants to kill Superman because he's jealous and Gotham lost the football game against Metropolis.

Doomsday is indestructible, unstoppable, and more powerful than Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman put together. Despite this they manage to kill him because something something the power of friendship.

The only person who emerges from this dire performance with any shred of dignity intact is the magnificent Jeremy Irons, whose Alfred is far more credible and relatable than the grovelling cockney 'cheers-guv'nor-'av-a- good-'un-at-Wayne-Manor-tonight-you-won't-'ear-a dicky-bird-out-outta-me- if-you-bring-a-bit-o'-fluff-'ome-at-3am' cretin played by Michael Caine.

title: This movie should never have been made
review:
First the good. The actor that plays Lex Luthor is good. He does a very good job, easily the best thing in the movie, along with the beautiful girl that plays Wonder Woman.

Actually, if the movie had been about those two, it would have had a shot at being good, even with the same lousy direction.

But this movie? Those are 2.5 hours of my life that are never coming back.

The movie is boring, with no humor, no originality, with the same boring CGI shots we've seen countless times before in other recent action movies, so much so that they could have saved all the money spent on special effects by taking the footage from previous movies, and no one would have noticed the difference.

The greatest sin of this movie is that it's pretentious; it takes itself too seriously and attempts pseudo-philosophy by addressing the issues of positive and negative freedoms, the moral duties of super heroes and the consent of the masses, and the concept of good and evil, issues that are too deep for the director and the intended audience of this movie.

The second greatest sin of this movie is that it turns Batman into a moron, for only a moron would buy the silly idea put forward in this silly movie that Superman could be a menace to humanity, and only a super (bat)moron would buy into this silly idea so much that he's willing to fight and kill Superman over it.

The third sin of the movie is that it's unoriginally dark, along the recent decade-long trend in action movies. It's a postmodern view of good vs evil, where the boundaries are pushed and evil seems to be smarter and more interesting than evil, for Lex Luthor in this movie is certainly smarter and more interesting than both Superman and Batman combined.

Don't waste your time.

title: Boring, Predictable, Forgettable Marketing Ploy
review: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice can be summed up in a few simple words: Boring, Predictable and Forgettable. This film could have been the biggest movie in years but instead it went over the top with TOO MANY forced characters, too many sub-plots, a movie lacking a main story and too strong a reliance on CGI and was WAY TOO long. Instead of focusing on a story, most of the film is used as a marketing ploy for future stand alone films and the Justice League films. It was painful at how hard they were forcing the Justice League on us. Instead of one story this film was made up of a (1)Man of Steel Sequel, (2) a stand alone Batman movie, (3) a Justice League Teaser Film, (4) a Lex Luthor film, (5) and finally a Batman vs Superman movie. Henry Cavill was once again "eh" as Superman, Jessie Eisenberg was terrible as Lex Luthor; his performance seemed like a nervous high school presentation instead of a super villain. Gal Gadot, although good as Wonder Woman who was badass in the final battle, she wasn't necessary for the film, if they removed her entirely, it would have been the same film. Finally is Ben Affleck as Batman: possibly the only good thing in the film. He is possible the best Bruce Wayne/Batman we've had in a long time and Jeremy Irons as Alfred was interesting but was a very good choice. Many will consider this a spoiler but if you have seen the trailers, you have already seen about 90% of the film. The marketing of this film can be compared to Terminator Genisys and its trailers. Don't waste your money, it's not worth it. Final complaint: Yes Superman killed General Zod in Man of Steel, but he was forced to as there would be no way to contain him if captured. Throughout this film Batman MURDERED dozens of people. I'm talking about shooting people, stabbing them, killing them by blowing up their cars, snapping necks, and even set a man on fire and left him for dead. Zach Snyder does not know anything about the characters he's working with and has destroyed the two biggest characters of all time.

title: Not Very Super, and Threw Away the Greatest Superhero Story of All Time
review:
Let me start by saying that I am a Superman guy. Yeah I like Batman too. But Superman has been my guy since I was a child. DC could have had the movie of the century. They could have spent a few years developing the other heroes, and then gone for a Doomsday movie with an ensemble cast. Guaranteed blockbuster, which would have led to several spinoff films. Instead, they wasted a great opportunity to show the world what makes Superman super. Unlike the Marvel heroes, Superman isn't super because of his powers. DC, you failed. Again.

title: Audience vs. Studios: Dawn of Anger
review:
I once liked this film if not loved it. Maybe it was the fan of superheroes and comic books inside of me, because this movie is a pile of dog feces.It is only the 2nd film of the DCEU, and its critical failure resulted in fans of DC comics and other audiences to be conflicted upon the films that would come out, where their stories would occur in this fictional universe. Here are some why this movie is not a 100% misfire, as well as reasons why this movie is still awful.

Pros:
  • Some good and okay performances, with Ben Affleck being a pretty good Batman for the most part. Gal Gadot is an awful actress, but I thought she was a good choice for Wonder Woman.
  • Despite some problems with the CGI, the visual effects and action sequences are pretty good, with great choreography, decent visual effects, and massive spectacle.
  • It has some good philosophical ideas, such as when the film talks about the difference between god and man, and discusses about how it would be like to have god-like abilities and have society hate you, simply because they do not fully know you.


Cons:
  • Jesse Eisenberg is obviously a terrible choice to play Lex Luthor. He is goofy, annoying, and over-the-top. He is does not seem intelligent, diabolical, sophisticated, and criminally-charming like the Lex Luthor that many Dc fans love as a character.
  • Henry Cavill seems like a good choice for Superman, but he gives a bad performance filled with no charisma whatsoever. I feel like it is not his fault, because the script he is given to work with is awful, it seems impossible for Cavill to give a good performance.
  • There are characters who feel like they do not have enough screen time and they seem pointless to the story, such as Alfred, Perry White, and Martha. Wonder Woman is especially a very pointless character, and she serves no purpose in the story. I feel as if her inclusion in the film is only to make DC fans pay money to buy tickets to see this piece of garbage.
-There are many hilariously atrocious and logical inconsistencies. From Lex pissing in a jar and sending it to Senator Finch, to the infamous "Martha" moment, the film has it all.
  • Lois Lane is a partially intriguing character, trying to discover the truth about the massacre in Africa, and uncovering mysteries with the culprit being Lex. However, her character is completely useless in the third act, when she thows away a Kryptonite Spear, only to bring it back, resulting in her drowning, then get saved by Superman, which leads to him being knocked out by the radiation of the Spear.
  • The plot and execution of storytelling is really bad. The movie spends an unnecessary amount of time building up potential sequels and spin-offs, and it does it in the laziest way possible. An example would be the clips of Flash, Aquaman, and Cyborg that Bruce sends to Diana, which felt lazy and hilariously stupid. In other times, the film is very confusing when you try to analyse the plot, with moments like Batman's dream sequence of an post- apocalyptic world. It especially sucks that some scenes are eliminated from the final product, making the plot unorganized and confusing, and that you need to buy the ultimate edition in order to fully understand the story. Even then , there are unexplained plot points, such as how Lex knew that Bruce was Batman, and how Clark was Kal-El/Superman.
  • Its treatment of DC comics source material is awful. The movie burns through future films worth of good materials by rushing and misusing comic book stories such as The Dark Knight Returns and The Death of Superman. It is obvious that these guys are trying to play catch-up with Marvel. The characters that I adore are given awful alterations, where it does not feel like Zack Snyder and others involved in this film cared about them, and wrote them in a way that make them unlikable. Batman is a killer instead of a person who appears to be a brooding jerk, but also has compassion for others, and has a moral code to not kill anyone, like the original Batman. Superman, is a depressed man with no charming personalities, and he does not exhibit qualities of compassion, truth, and justice, like the original Superman. In addition, the film feels dark and gritty, leaving no sense of hope or existence of a joyful moment, which makes this world that the film has built even more uninteresting.

Ultimately I have to praise this films ambition to tell a complex story of how the world reacts to heroes and all the different perspectives of it. I really like Jesse Eisenberg but he easily gives the worst performance of his career in this film but that's ultimately due to the script which turns him into a laughable and cringeworthy character that dragged this film down every time he is on screen. title: Sluggish story, but realistic tone featuring the REAL Super-man (guest-starring Wonder Woman)
review:
Released in 2016 and directed by Zach Snyder, "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" pits Batman against Superman via the manipulations of Lex Luthor. Wonder Woman joins the Word's Finest duo to take on the "Hulk-on-Krytonian-steroids" Doomsday in the climatic battle.

I viewed the Ultimate edition, which runs three hours; the theatrical version is a half hour shorter.

This is an ambitious film, a superhero epic, touted by DC fans as the movie that would crush Marvel's supremacy in the superhero movie market, but it was a disappointment due to its sluggish story. It takes about half the film just to build up any drive; the first hour is the worst, although it's not without highlights. Thankfully, the second half is compelling to the end.

Despite the listlessness of the first half, this is an impressive film and worthwhile for several reasons. For one, this is the absolute best depiction of Superman, as far as driving home his alien super-ness. Not to mention Henry Cavill is, by far, the best actor to play the Kryptonian. Secondly, the gritty realistic tone establishes in no uncertain terms that this is a totally serious superhero flick, which is driven home in the first act by the shocking murder of an iconic Superman Family character. It's akin to the feel of Nolan's Batman trilogy or 2003's "Hulk," the latter of which people love to hate because, apparently, it was a thinking-person's superhero film and didn't have enough "Hulk smash" moments (even though the Hulk's 22-minute rampage that starts at the 92-minute mark is definitely one of the best action sequences put to film). (But, don't get me wrong, I agree with the main criticisms of "Hulk," I just don't let them prevent me from enjoying its good points).

Thirdly, Ben Affleck makes for a great Bruce Wayne/Batman, on par with George Clooney's underrated depiction in 1997's "Batman & Robin." He's just all-around better than Christian Bale. Fourthly, Jesse Eisenberg is charismatic as the eccentric, but genius Lex Luthor. For anyone who's upset that he has a full head of hair, stay around till the end. Fifthly, Gal Gadot is effective as Wonder Woman due to her good looks and all-around athleticism (she's too tall and thin for my personal tastes, but she's great for the role of the Amazonian warrior princess).

One annoying cavil is that CNN (Counterfeit News Network) obviously paid for constant advertising throughout the film. See "Iron Man 2" (2010) for a superhero flick that knows how to present the news of the comic book world.

BOTTOM LINE: This is a one-of-a-kind superhero film with numerous highlights, like the ultra-serious tone, the best depiction of Superman ever, an offbeat-but-magnetic Luthor, Affleck's great portrayal of Wayne/Batman and the inclusion of Wonder Woman. But the first half is bogged down by a lethargic story with too much fat. They coulda and shoulda stripped this down to a roughly two-hour flick. As it is, it can't compete with more kinetic superhero films like "Avengers: Age of Ultron" (2015) and "Captain America: Civil War" (2016).

ADDITIONAL CAST MEMBERS: Amy Adams plays Lois Lane, Diane Lane & Kevin Costner appear as Clark's parents, Laurence Fishburne is on hand as Perry White, Holly Hunter plays a senator, Jeremy Irons appears as Alfred and cutie Rebecca Buller is on hand as Jenny, an employee at the Daily Planet.

FILMING LOCATIONS: Detroit (Metropolis); Birmingham, Michigan; Chicago; Yorkville, Illinois (Smallville); East Los Angeles College, Monterey Park, California (Gotham vs Metropolis football game); Deming, New Mexico (Nairomi, Africa); and Washington DC.

GRADE: B- (6.5/10)
