title: The Tools Are All There...But What Happened To The Execution?
review:
I never through I say this but BvS was a chore.

It didn't pull me in as much as I'd love to.

While I'd like to say the actors did everything they could, the script and the direction let them down.

I thought Ben Affleck was okay for the most part as Bruce/Batman, he wasn't stellar. Gal Gadot was good as Wonder Woman, serviceable at best. Henry Cavill could've been better, but the script let him down big time—at least in my opinion. As for Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Junior, I found "Lex" rather annoying performance-wise and the fact he has more lines than any other character makes you wonder. BvS movie could do without him.

Now let looks at Luthor's purpose in this movie, in which they are many, and probably more (like; a surrogate Screenwriter which he is, sort-of). And one can make an argument that he is far more developed than the titular heroes. Okay (1) He discovered kryptonite, but how Lex knew what kryptonite is and what it does is never explained. (2) He pitted Batman against Superman, which could have worked better if Batman went against Superman at his own expense—and sadly enough there was a build-up to that event but collapsed under the weight of this movie's "fool's gold" ambitions. And (3) creating DOOMSDAY—which if you ask me I think deserved to be a villain in a stand-alone superman movie—but in BvS, Doomsday was just there to lend the movie an invincible-villain, which he's not—he's far much complex character in the comics—and anyone with (a) Kryptonite (Spear) could've defeat him since—he's a biosynthesis of Krytonian blood (and Lex's). And, he 's also responsible for the death of Superman. Some might call it ballsy, I call this dumb. This is a comic-book movie, everyone knows superheroes/villains don't stay dead.

Man, what about the goals and the motivations, and the inner-conflicts of Both Bruce/Batman and Clark/Superman? It started somewhat strong and waned like smoke-"screen" in the pouring rain of unnecessary/convoluted plot lines—of what could've been a whirlwind inferno of set-up, built-up, and momentum—became Lex's Luthor's playground—and the two juggernaut of heroes became toys to play with. I felt like Superman's story was pushed so much to the background, as a framing device for the plot, instead of being developed as a human character. And as for Batman's, we've seen his origin story in countless incarnations. This time around it's designed to thrust some emotional depth in Bruce. Someone say, "Martha"?

As for they dialogues; they are contrite, monotonous, and lacks clarity.

Saying Snyder doesn't have the chops to make a good movie is giving him a pass. Here, he doesn't even try to give us the thrilling and suspense factor. the movie is predictable at best. Even when Superman face off against Batman, while the action and set-pieces are great to look at, he added nothing for us to care about the heroes' conflicts.

I wouldn't say I hate the movie, but I tried so hard to find it entertaining, and it just--wasn't.

By the end of the movie I kind-of asked myself, "Why is it such a bad idea to pit two of the greatest American comic-book Icons against one another in a movie? The simple answer is that, "Hollywood just won't do it justice."

Note: Does anyone know why Batman needed those beams on his eyes when he was in the suit if armor? If so, could he see well during the fighting scenes?" Anyway, I'm surprised Superman didn't take advantage of that.

Nonetheless I'm looking forward to what the DC Extended Universe have to offer in the future.

title: Almost As Bad As Batman & Robin
review: Batman V Superman seemed promising, but unfortunately it is boring and empty. The film is set 18 months after the events of Man of Steel. Aparrently Batman is suspicious of what Superman may do and wants to eliminate him as a threat. The story is virtually nonexistent. There is no explanation for anything such as character background or story. In an action movie there has to be a point in the action. The characters need motivation. This is also a problem. There is no clear explanation to things. An example is the only scene with Flash. Flash says to Bruce that Lois is the key. This is one of many pointless scenes. Every scene feels pointless. I also don't like the grey color pallet. The grey pallet feels depressing. A superhero movie needs to look warm, fun, and inviting like a majority of the Marvel films. Jessie Eisenberg was concerning for maybe a few. Unfortunately he is a miscast. Even with proper casting, it would have been hard to make this Luther work because he has no motivation. The lone bright spots are in Ben Affleck, Gal Gadot, and Henry Cavil. All of them do a mostly decent job, except Affleck. Affleck's interpretation of Batman is hardcore which is fine, but unfortunately as I already mentioned, there is no point. Because I am limited here in length I am going to refer you to my review on Rotten Tomatoes. http://www.rottentomatoes.com/user/id/900037159/ratings

title: A marriage of Convenience
review:
The last Batman & Superman movies were quite good so with the added attraction of Wonder Women my anticipation was quite high.

This a long movie so I was expecting a lot of fireworks, unfortunately for most parts of this movie there wasn't any. The movie dragged on including re-hatching points about Batman we already knew before, which didn't add anything of significance to the story. My attention did pick up a little bit when I saw there might be a bit of nudity but then I remembered this is only a 12A movie.

Parts of the movie didn't make any sense. They wanted an older Batman hence Ben Affleck but it strange that Alfred now played by Jeremy Irons is a lot younger than Micheal Cane. The way both Batman and Luthor obtained and created their technology was unbelievable and inconsistent with the previous movie. Superman just seemed blazy or uninterested about it all, which again was inconsistent with the Man of Steel.

Godot is a pretty woman but unconvincing as Wonder Woman. Adrianne Palicki and Lynda Carter were more convincing. Batman & Superman had rippling muscles but Woman Woman had very little appeal. No reason was given as to why Wonder Woman was in the story.

Affleck & Cavill acting were quite good but the story tell was awful. There was a disconnection between the previous Superman movie even though directed by the same director. It seemed writers had borrowed the way of story telling from Iron Man 3 "just make it up as you go along".

If Marvel and DC continue to make movies of this low quality it wont be too long before the comic book super hero bubble bursting.

title: Studio Gimmick
review: Studio gimmick to make millions of dollars, Zack Snyder does a horrible job making us care about the characters. The film will confuse movie goers and disappoint REAL comic book fans. Although there are some great moments, like Ben's Batman and the frame by frame of "The Dark knight Returns" comic book and best of all Wonder Women. As a film it has horrible in editing, story and is more focused on starting something bigger then focusing on a story. I wanted to love this film but simply could not, as the films flaws were greater then it's strengths. Cgi is used more then it should have, and some of it looks incomplete. Im a fan of the comic books and animated movies but this was a huge disappointment, that I wrote my first review on IMDb. The film will still make millions because thats what the studio is aiming for, not to please fans.

title: Was this level of suffering really necessary?
review: Attention! There may be spoilers in my review. They destroy Superman literally, in every sense, physically, emotionally, is judged, humiliated, socially discriminated, lead the character to an end of unnecessary suffering. If I knew it would be so I stayed at home to watch The Passion (of the Christ). Why not crucified him too like Jesus? The film is unfair, sad, dark, and leaves you with a feeling of sorrow, the audience really need that level of tragedy and drama to say that a movie is good? A shame, and I understand that Superman must demonstrate capacity to sacrifice for the humankind, but I feel that the purpose of the writers is to generate hard and strong emotions, when the focus must be on to make a enjoyable film that leaves you with the feeling of hope instead of sadness, after all, that's Superman message. Dark movies are trendy these days, message is good people are fated to suffer. I don't like that. Positives: I like versions of Batman and Wonder Woman. You really feel the fear of criminals for Batman (not achieved in Nolan films) and his agility and strenght (as in the video game, his strokes really hurts). Then, gestures of Wonder Woman are sublime and her movements in combat too.

title: Graphic overkill by Zack Snyder!!
review:
I loved Zack Snyder's Legend of the Guardians and the BEAUTIFUL, STUNNING GRAPHICS in it. But BM vs SM, he went overboard with the graphics. Compare these graphics with the ones in KUNG FU PANDA 3 - which is a cool example of how far the technology has come. BM vs SM - not close.

They should have toned down on graphics a bit. When graphics keep popping again and again, you lose their effect and significance.

Instead, he should have teamed with another director and complemented his skills for a complete movie. Acting by Ben Affleck was perfect compared to Christian Bale.

title: Zack Snyder fails in making a serious movie without taking out the fun
review: Being a big Batman fan and having been frustrated of Marvel's cartoonish action packed movies that lack depth I was looking forward to Batman v Superman to save the superhero movies from being dull entertainment action movies. After the Dark Knight trilogy Marvel's Avengers and Guardians of the Galaxy took what was essential in good superhero movies and turned it into cartoons that are for children or action seekers who expect no depth in a movie. So, yes I was hoping that this movie could give back what Marvel took from The Dark Knight Trilogy. Having said so, I was disappointed when I saw the movie; granted it was a dark, serious movie but it lacked the complexity and the narrative that the dark serious movies entertain the viewer with. Furthermore, I believe I can say this about all of Zack Snyder's movies. Having seen Watchmen, Man of Steel and Batman v Superman I seriously think that he tries to and to an extend manages to make serious movies out of comic books like Christophar Nolan did but when doing so he lacks the actual complexity and captivatingess that Nolan was giving to the genre. On the other hand, I've seen 300 as well but have a vague memory of it so I'll give Snyder the benefit of the doubt on that one and not include it into one of his failures which Batman v Superman certainly is included in.

title: Ben Affleck IS Batman
review: First of all, ignore the critics! They must just live a miserable life. There's nothing you can't like about this movie. The different take on Batman was amazing. Ben Affleck played true to the comics! Great story, great action! It's right up there with the Dark Knight. Go see it for yourself! This started the DC universe off perfect. Zach Snyder directed this perfectly. You can't make this movie any better so I don't understand why the critics hate it so much. Seeing batman, superman, and Wonder Woman on the screen for the first time was just amazing. The music was perfect by Hans Zimmer once again. There was a lot they had to fit into a 2.5 hour movie but it was all paced perfectly and you get a full understanding of each character.

title: I don't like it but I save something
review:
I don't like Batman V Superman. It was very bad film, with bad screenplay, plot and dialogues. Even Lex Luthor character was terrible in "Jocker style" but I think that the character of Clark Kent/Superman is the best who we have ever seen and of course a great suit. Ben Affleck was also great! I was very unhappy when I heard that Ben Affleck will be new Batman but after I saw the film I have changed my mind. We have an older Batman and Affleck was great instead I don't like batman suits! I'm surprised about that! Really. Maybe I love Amy Adams, she is beautiful and she was great. Summary the film is bad but not the worst film on superhero moreover Batman V Superma is better than Superman the man of steel so there is a improvement. Of course we stay very far by Batman Dark Knight but this is another topic!

Sorry for my English but I wanted to say that and see what you think about it so if you think like me, click on YES, instead on NO.

title: Not bad, but not great either.
review:
This movie is a very weird one, Ill start with the good. The first half an hour is excellent and was exactly what i wanted from this movie, it sets up the world and introduces us to the new Batman- played by Ben Affleck, who does the role justice and is easily the best part of this movie.

The fight/action scene are also amazingly well done and are defiantly worth the wait. Jeremy Irons was also a great Alfred and also a bit of a different take on the character. All scenes with Batman/Bruce Wayne in were terrific. To my surprise Gal Gadot as Women Women was also great in the movies and looked bad ass.

But this is where the movies start to fall apart. Its not awful by any means but its all over the place, the editing is not good at all and it effects the flow of the movie because it doesn't give you time to understand whats going on in certain scenes.

The writing and directing isn't up to standard either(for this type of movies), there are a number of plot holes which could be easily explained if there was more care taken to address them. You could also easily make this movies 30 minutes shorter as most of the build is unnecessary. I never found myself getting bored but i did start to get annoyed in a few scenes which is a weird thing to say about a movie.

Not really sure about Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luther either if I'm honest. The first scene he was in i automatically disliked his portray of the character and thought he was awful, but as the movie went on and the logic of it all went out the window i started to change my mind, there's not really a motivation with him but thats what i liked with villains in movies, if i had to describe him best he's basically a way worse, wanna be, rip off version of the joker.

Id recommend this movie to anyone that is looking to kick back, relax and switch off for a few hours but if you're one of these people that likes to nitpick or if you're standard for movies are high then I'm afraid its not for you.

title: Batman Vs Superman, Bros because they had to
review: First up, this movie is high on style, I'll give it that. Where does it go wrong? Let me summarize: Dreams, Lex Luthor, Batman's sudden change of heart towards batman, unnecessary scenes pertaining to Batman's past and most of all the unnecessary death of Superman. The fight between Batman and Superman is left too late, the trailers had us thinking that sure Batman hates Superman but we can also see that Clark believes that Batman's brand of justice is just wrong. This should have been the sole reason for them to go head to head. Instead we get a lame ass reason for Superman to go after Batman, just because Lex has his mother. Funny thing is even before he goes to fight batman he tells Louis that he must try to convince Batman to help him. Why does he think that Batman would help him? And even if he does believe that Batman is one of the good guys, why not reach out to him earlier and talk about an alliance instead of crashing his car and threatening him with consequences. Lex blowing up the senate hearing was so retarded, he already had access to the Kryptonite and the genesis chamber. Also the way he tried to frame superman was stupid. Everyody knows Superman wouldn't need guns to kill. Yet in the incident, bullets are the one thing responsible for the deaths. So many flaws. Special mention to Jesse for hamming it up as Lex Luthor. He was clearly copying the acting style of an Indian superstar - Shah Rukh Khan. But I will overlook all of this for the following: 1. A satisfying throw down between Batman and Superman. Something I have been waiting to watch for ages. 2. Wonder Woman! 3. The final boss fight. 4. The dawn of the justice league 5. Darkseid is coming!

title: Watch The movie... Don't read the critics...
review: So I watched Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice yesterday and have been thinking about the movie... And to be honest I liked it.. I liked it a lot... This is not Marvel... Please don't go to the theater and expect it to be a Marvel flick... And this is honestly a movie which every comic fans were waiting for... About time they made a movie for the comic fans... Not the average movie lovers... If you don't know the comic facts, well you wouldn't understand some certain bits of the story... I'm not saying the movie couldn't be better... But it's not as bad as it is being told... And again.. It is such a treat for the comic lovers... And about the critic reviews... Well even Sharknado has 82% score in rotten tomatoes... And if you want to know what that means, just watch the Sharknado movie and you'll realize believing the reviews blindly is just stupid... And why the critics didn't like the movies, maybe because they set the gore dark tone for the movie... They showed stuffs that people usually don't want to see in films... That PG-13 rating for the movie is kinda the understatement of the year... The only negative aspect about the movie is maybe the screenplay... Some scenes seemed kinda rushed due to shortage of time... Well in the director's cut, there is supposed to be more than half an hour of extra scenes... Maybe there some scenes would get properly explained... And finally to everyone its a must see... It will surprise you, shock you, maybe disappoint you a bit and may surpass your expectations at times... Just don't enter the theater expecting Thor or Iron-man saving the earth whenever there's trouble...

title: It's a DC Film done great just like the rest. Much better than MoS. What more do you want?
review: I'm writing this only a few hours removed from seeing the film so bare with my excitement. Batman V Superman has been my most anticipated movie for this year since its final release date of March 25th was announced last year. I like MOST superhero/comic book flicks, won't say all.. Zack Snyder's "Watchmen" is already one of my favorites of this category with ease, and the opening to BvS was a reminder of what he excels at in making these films. Now I can't type this review and not combat all of the negative reviews I've seen, not that I cared about them I still went to a midnight showing. One of the main issues people had was the no sense of direction or "all over the place" this film was. The first 45 to an hour is where I guess the naysayers saw this "issue", in my eyes it was quite easy to follow though not "spoon fed" I guess you'd all like. In a movie like this you just CANT focus on one thing, it won't work. Bruce/Batman had his agenda when he was on screen the first hour, Clark/Supes had his and Lex had his upon which they all ran into each other which was easy to see. There wasn't 50 different plot points so I have the slightest clue where that came from. Yes you heard right, Ben Affleck should get a legal name change to Bruce Wayne and be Batman full time. His dialogue with Alfred was always impressive and as the Bat of Gotham he was LETHAL in every fight scene. Eisenberg, you ARE the weakest link. Cringe-worthy is an understatement for how it was watching him as Lex, an actor I enjoy in every other film. Enough with that. Gal Gadot, though with little to no dialogue impacted this film immensely with an astounding impact in her own aspects. Gal, you ARE Wonder Woman. Superman was well, the Man of Steel. If you saw him in that you've seen him in this, with a little more feelings this time round. The main event battle scene was everything I hoped for, what more can you want? Seeing Bat and Supes go at it is something to behold anytime anywhere. Though the latter was holding back he still kicked ass. Seeing the Trinity come full circle in the end on screen was a great payoff if you ask me. Yes the marketing team kinda screwed us with the trailers but there is still much more to behold with this film of epicness! :) The final battle had but one 'turd' for me if you catch my drift ;) DC has mastered the "serious tone" in these films with no fun needed. I don't recall much "fun" in TDK trilogy. So in my opinion The Justice League set up is a mission complete. I will be waiting as long as need be. It will be the great ass kicking scenes in this movie times 10! Batman v Superman gets an 8.7/10

title: Disappointed but eager for future stories to unfold
review:
Before I start I wanna say two things 1. Since I'm from India my grammar maybe bad so please bear with me , 2. I'm a Marvel fan boy, Having said that I always loved DC story arcs especially the ones by Geoff Johns. To summarize my review, BvS had so many chances to be an epic, but blew it all away.To list out few drawbacks, Most parts of the movie were not coherent. One scene we have Lois and Clark making love and the next one Bruce Wayne having nightmares. I wasn't able to figure out what was the point for each sequence because the next sequence would be completely different which made me confusing. Why were they killing superman if they are going to resurrect him, there has to be a point him being dead right?. Now some would say they did that so that the World would feel Superman no longer a threat, but doesn't resurrecting him would make those people feel cheated and more frightened because there is no way to kill him. Jesse bombed the role, No that isn't the Lex I grew up watching. And about the big showdown, the entire point of the movie being Batman taking Superman the single reason why I went to the movie, The action sequences are not the ones we were promised and It was very dull just few punches and scratches and splash the fight is over. Above all the fight had no compelling point, they seriously could have settled with words. Doomsday origins have been tampered with for which I'm not happy, they could have chose Bizarro instead.

Now speaking about the positive things the one sequence which surprised me and got me excited, The flash running through speed force to warn Bruce which could be set-up for crisis on Infinite Earth or Flashpoint or Injustice but I'm very much eager to find out. Overall the movie is just a half baked blend of The Dark Knight returns and The Death of Superman.

title: Don't listen to the critics - form your own opinion
review:
OK, so my verdict on Batman v. Superman: See it for yourself, don't listen to the critics, make your own decision. I for one liked it. I can see how a lot of people won't - it's not like the Marvel movies. Don't get me wrong, I completely enjoy the Marvel takes...but an average person can go in and watch one and it will lead you by the hand thru the story and throw in some snappy one liners. BvS is more for the actual readers of comics from the 80s and early 90s, when they were much better than they are now, and the movie makes assumptions that you are at least slightly familiar with the characters. Affleck did a good job as the Batman, brought both the physicality and the gravitas to the role that it needed (and nice to see some actual detective work by "the world's greatest detective"). Also the movie did a good job completely conveying the fact that Superman is really the persona that Kansas raised Clark Kent puts on...and Bruce Wayne is the persona that the Batman puts on. Completely got that from the movie. Not sure I got behind the portrayal of Lex Luthor as the twitchy damaged rich kid; sure it's a different take on the character, but it just didn't ring any bells for me. Again, would have liked to see Superman/Clark not quite so angsty, that's really not quite how I've ever seen Superman being. He should be very much the "Boy Scout" that the classic comics and Chris Reeve crystallized him as. And Gal Gadot - all kinds of yes as Wonder Woman. She gets the look just right, the attitude, and does not disappoint in the action department. Definitely will be seeing her solo film.

All in all, I'm pleased. Some stuff straight out of The Dark Knight Returns, some other stuff added on. I am NOT a fan of the editing in this film, I'll say. It was very choppy and abrupt in places, jarringly so. I know they had to cut a lot out to get it to a manageable theater playing time, so maybe it will be a smoother ride in the Bluray extended version release. It's not perfect, but it's not the train wreck that some critics are putting out there. Honestly, I think the old school comics readers will mostly be pleased, the comic book movie only fans will be more up in the air, but I found it fairly fun. Had some problems, but it's more Superman II than Superman III.

title: A Very Good movie but struggles with the plot
review: First of all, I encourage people to go see the movie and not be put off by some negative reviews. Reading some of the other reviews I am astonished at the reception of this movie. Some of the critics and user reviews have been a little harsh in my opinion. Ben Afflecks performance as Bruce Wayne/Batman is remarkable and to date the best and most accurate iteration of the character.The opening 15 minutes was tremendous, and the acting ability of Affleck really conveys the hatred and anger of Bruce Wayne. Gal Gadot as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman also is very good and those 2 characters are in my opinion the standout characters in this film. However, I must say that Zack Snyder must take a lot of the blame for the negative reception from some. He fails to tell a coherent plot and for the first hour we jump from subplot to another from scene to scene. However, I do not feel the lack of a clear and structured plot is deserving of such harsh criticism. The lack of plot is more than made up for with the actual Batman and Superman fight, the end fight and the performances from the cast. Another stand out point of this movie that I feel is not getting enough mention is the Batman car chase and the Batman fight scene against 20 men. Those two portions of the film were fantastic and left me in amazement. Overall, I would be more than happy to see this film again and I again encourage people not to be put off. This film really is a spectacle and the action sequences coupled with good CGI are a thrill to watch.

title: Batman Vs Superman:Dawn of Justice - A review of sorts. A course correct for the DCCU.
review:
SPOILERS TO FOLLOW! Overall, I honestly didn't see much wrong with it, and I'd say I liked it. It's by no means a great film, but it does just fine. It doesn't do what this film deserves, but it does the job. It doesn't stand apart form any other comic film as it doesn't do anything different, nothing we haven't seen before with other characters.

The biggest shock for me is a lot of the the things Zack Snyder has put out there in interviews, just plain lies Which is a rather odd stance from him I guess he's just trying to get people worked up, and I admit, I took the bait. Batman shoots nobody directly. Anybody that is or may be (not shown as) killed, as in any other Batman film that has preceded this, "die" by consequence of their own. A lot of the Batman stuff is ripped right out of DKR, and is done well. Affleck does well as Batman, as does Irons as Alfred. I'd watch a solo film with those guys any day. The costume, is also, hands down the best screen Bat costume to date.

Another thing that most reviews seem to be getting wrong for me, is the involvement of Lois Lane. She does her fair share, and has a lot of point being in this movie.

Cavill's Superman improves from his last outing. For starters, within minutes he's called Superman for the first time in his existence. Something shied away from in the last outing. He's still not as compassionate as you'd want a Superman, but he's getting there, and is again more so by the end of the film. He also has a nice moment with his Dad (None space variant), which is also a lot better than any time they shared in the last film. And more in line with what I'd expect from the characters.

The way the two heroes come together could have been done better. They essentially stop in the middle of a fight and make friends, because their mothers share the same name. Which I totally get. It's a way the human Batman, comes to realise, that this Alien is actually just as human as he is. It's just handled with ham fists.

Eisenberg's Luthor, isn't for me. He's just not my Luthor. However I will say he's nowhere as bad as I expected him to be. And the bald thing is also handled badly. Just comes off as silly. Though it does transpire that he's pulling everybody's strings, and his motives are more in line with what I like in a Luthor. Far better than the obsession with property and land.

Wonder Woman is the only thing that got me excited, and produced that feeling inside me that Marvel films have continuously done when I've seen these things realised on film for the first time. She does nothing spectacular, other than join the fight. It's just fantastic to finally see her do so. She also out detectives Batman at one point. Which is cool.

There are one too many dream sequences I guess, but they do foreshadow what is to come, so I guess they're justified.

Of the other JL members that are briefly used. I'd say Aquaman was the most convincing. No lines, but very cool visually, and he moves like Superman, but underwater. I think this Flash is going to take some time to convince me. And I've never really cared for Cyborg. I'd much rather Martian Manhunter.

If the film can be described as anything, it certainly is DKR, but with a lot more Death of Superman than I expected. Overall I think it's been marketed badly, most of the money shots and plot points are actually in the trailers. It's also kind of sad that kids can't really see this film, and it's possible a generation may grow up not really learning what I personally have learnt from these characters. Having said that, there were many kids in my screening. I just know that had that been me at their age I would have been bored and would have lost interest. And a lot of casual viewers probably will do so, it does take it's time to get going.

If I can say one thing, it'd be the same thing I say about any film. Ignore what has been said, go and see it, make your mind up for yourself. But that seems to make even more sense with this film. It's well worth at least one watch.

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice - Review: Not a Masterpiece
review:
Part 1: Opinions

My anticipation for BVS was not high to begin with. I didn't really care that Ben Affleck was going to play the iconic Batman. When Gal Gadot was cast as Wonder Women I didn't care. I've only seen Gadot in the Fast & Furious movies, she's capable in those types of movies. Jesse Eisenberg plays Lex Luthor. Eisenberg is a capable actor, however, my only problem with him is that he always acts the same in everything. Jeremy Irons plays Alfred, okay sign me up. Henry Cavill is good as the Man Of Steel. Honestly, I'm not a huge Superman fan to begin with. Batman is my number one superhero, so you already know who I wanted to win this fight. Zack Snyder is back in the director's chair for BVS. I've seen a few of Snyder's movies, 300 is my favorite, Man of Steel is fine, and I honestly don't care for the rest of his catalog. In my opinion, everyone single one of Snyder's movies are mostly style over substance. David S. Goyer is back again as the screenwriter for this project. In my honest opinion, I don't believe Goyer to be the best screenwriter, all of his projects seem to work when he's collaborating, and when he's writing solo I feel that a majority of his projects stink.

My anticipation for BVS suddenly skyrocketed When Warner Bros Pictures brought in Chris Terrio. Argo is one of my favorite movies, I don't know much about Terrio, but it sure seems that Warner Bros sure like him. Warner Bros wants Terrio back to write Justice League part 1 and 2.

Part 2: Views

Jesse Eisenberg gave a fantastic performance as Lex Luthor, however, I feel like the character kind of felt out of place. Honestly, I would've preferred a more methodical version of Lex Luthor. Amy Adams plays Louise Lane and she doesn't really need to be in the movie. Louise Lane is on a mission, her mission is pointless, and it bores me to sleep. The first act of this movie is tremendous, the second act is tedious, and the third act is a spiritless extravaganza. I like that this movie has a darker tone, it's darker than a majority of superhero movies, however, this having a darker tone doesn't make up for the fact that this movie feels over packed. The stories plot could've been trimmed tremendously. I believe that the story doesn't have a crucial focus on what it's trying to achieve. All the story had to do was focus on Batman Vs. Superman, showcase their conflicted ideologies throughout, but what I got was a bunch of unnecessary fullers instead of getting the real meat.

Part 3: Positives and Negatives

POSITIVES: 1. Ben Affleck is great as Batman: In my opinion, this is the best live action Batman that we've ever received. Affleck was the perfect choice for this new incarnation of Batman. Affleck's Batman is brutal, he's menacing, he takes no prisoners, and he holds no punches (literally). The fight scenes with Batfleck are truly amazing and they're something to behold; in my opinion, every fight scene with Batfleck is 10x better than what we got in The Dark Knight Trilogy, and I'm sorry but I just have to point out that Batfleck is better. Affleck's Bruce Wayne is also quite good; Bruce Wayne is tired, bleary- eyed, frustrated, sorrowful, and extremely angry; however, in certain scenes Mr. Wayne's public persona is still somewhat of a spoiled rich jackass, and so this Bruce Wayne has bravado. I don't believe Affleck is the best actor, however, I do believe that he is a capable one. Ben Affleck's Batman massively shines in this movie.

2. This movie has a serious tone: I like dramas, suspense, and thrillers because those are my favorite types of genres. BVS's story is dark, brutally dark. People die in this movie and that's the focus. This movie focuses on how death can linger over someones head and consciences. Does BVS have drama (check), suspense (check), and emotional scenes (check).

3. The action was good: Synder never really has a problem showcasing action. Certain action scenes stood out among others. The opening Metropolis sequence was suspenseful. Batman fighting Superman was entertaining. Batman's warehouse fight was exhilarating. The final battle was fun.

NEGATIVES: 1. The story line was tortuous: I believe that this movie's runtime is excessively long. I don't mind extremely long movies if they're good; I love TDK, BVS's runtime is similar to that of TDK, but BVS just had to many subplots, and once it hit that hour mark I became tired. I've seen BVS three times now, on two occasions it put me to sleep, I've fallen asleep during the exact same sequences, on the third viewing I managed to stay awake, and my opinion on the movie has only slightly changed. Honestly, I believe that there's just to much extra fluff in this movie, it's interesting, but it just goes on forever, and at a certain point I drift off because I'm bored.

Side Note: I believe that Batmobile chase sequence was unnecessary; It's a useless action sequence that really went nowhere.

Overall, The first half of this movie is interesting, but certain plot points overstay their welcome, and by the time I see Batman fighting Superman I feel fatigued. The first act starts off in a good place, but then the story adds more layers to it, and then after an hour I fall asleep because of pure boredom. The action and fight sequences keep me entertained, but that doesn't make up for what I have to endure. This movie is simply not engaging enough for me to keep my eyes open during its entire runtime. I wasn't expecting a masterpiece, I just wanted a good movie, and what I got was...

Final Grade: C+

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn Of Justice
review: It was a novel idea pitting Batman against Superman in a test to determine humanity's real superhero and champion. Both have a downside. Henry Cavill became this generation's Superman, while 43-year-old Ben Affleck assumed the role of an aging Batman. Batman is human, and it is his movie. Superman, although not a god, has godlike powers because he is from the the planet Krypton, where the chemistry and gravity differ greatly from those on Earth. It would seem that Batman would be no match for Superman. Lex Luthor, who is more Joker-like than previous Lexes, adds to the chaos. My real interest in this movie is Wonder Woman. Gal Gadot is skinny as a rail, although she does have a look. Lynda Carter is impossible to top, and I suppose Warner Brothers decided to take a different approach. The Amazon teams up with Batman and Superman to battle Doomsday and form the Justice League. Batman (Bruce Wayne) lives in Gotham. Superman (Clark Kent) lives in Metropolis. Both cities are really New York. Wonder Woman (Diana Prince) is from the island of Themyscira. Some say Paradise Island.

title: Doing too much too soon by laying the ground works for Justice League
review:
Following the announcement of this film back at Comic Con '13, I've been eagerly anticipating this film since. Keeping up to date with all the latest developments, pictures, trailers etc. As a big Batman/DC fan, this is the movie I have wanted to see for years.

*Spoilers ahead*

Soon as the credits started rolling I didn't know what to think. Ben Affleck for me, nailed it as Bruce Wayne and in my opinion was the best incarnation we've had of Batman. Cant wait for a solo Batman movie with Batfleck! I knew they were pulling a lot of material from the Dark Knight Returns comic and an Injustice style nightmare scenario with an evil Superman. The two surprises for me was the Flashpoint paradox style time travel and also the Death of Superman. I love the fact they are pulling these stories straight from the comics. This is what the fans want to see! The trouble is, having that many different stories in one single film. I think that's the reason I wasn't able to enjoy it as much as I would of liked to, because it was a busy film and you had to keep up with what was going on. I don't blame Synder for this though as his directors cut was a whole 30 minutes longer, which I believe would have helped to piece things together a lot better, and explained things more. I can understand the studio wanting to cut the film down, 1)Three hours would have been too long for some people and means less showings of the film each day in cinemas = less money. 2) Taking out some of the intense violence to keep it PG13 so a wider audience can see the film, kids will buy the toys = more money. Its just the way the film was edited felt rather choppy, cutting from one scene to another and parts missing. The biggest disappointment is the main fight between Batman and Superman. It didn't feel long enough although the directors cut on Blu Ray I believe will have an extended fight.

I also think Dc crammed so much into this movie purely to play catch up with Marvel, who are way ahead in the cinematic universe. I really feel they should have just stuck to Batman v Superman, and the whole Dawn of Justice could have literally been a 5 minute bit at the end, rather than half this movie. We all know Justice League is coming, but we just wanted to see Batman take on Superman! The original two trailers were awesome but it was the Doomsday trailer which gave away way too much. I think if the whole Doomsday and Wonder Woman stuff wasn't shown, we would have had even more to be surprised about. So much footage was release in the marketing campaign I felt like I had already seen the movie. Hopefully Warner Bros will learn for their future DCEU films.

Few more little mentions of things that bugged me... Lex Luthor having all the Heroes symbols on the Meta Human file. Cyborgs meta human file video wasn't the best. How quickly Batman and Superman become friends after finding out they both have mums called Martha (Although there may be more dialog etc. cut from theatrical version). Bruce Wayne's last line to Wonder Woman felt a little weak at the end ("I've just got a feeling').

I am going to see it a second time tomorrow and I think now I've had time for it all to sink in, I may enjoy it a whole load more.

I do want to just mention the positives too as it really wasn't as bad as what the critics say, but it is definitely a film for the fans. If you aren't familiar with the comics you may not have a clue what's going on for half the movie! As I've mentioned, for me, Ben Affleck was great. I especially liked the part when the cops go into the dark building and you see Batman in the top corner of the room. Felt almost like a horror! Batman's fighting style is very much like the Arkham games which was cool. By far the most brutal Batman we've seen, which I like. People may have a problem with Batman killing but there is compilation videos on YouTube of all the Batman kills in previous movies and its at about 50, Its just you don't always realize. I loved the nightmare scene as it was a cool look into what could be and Batman with his trench coat (again taken from comics). The Batmobile and Bat suit are both my favourite out of any previous movie. In fact all the costumes are great. Jeremy Irons is a cool more hands on version of Alfred. Hans Zimmer and his friend Junkie XL do a brilliant job with the score. I loved what Hans did for the Dark Knight films and also on Man Of Steel. Every time Wonder Woman was seen, her own music played which made her seem even more mysterious, and then once in action, the music ramped up!

Overall, I thought all the casting was great. I prefer the fact that Dc are darker than Marvel. I still believe in Zack Synder, I really liked Man Of Steel, i just think the studio wanted too much too soon with not enough time to do it all in. I think I probably went into it with expectations a little too high wanting the best superhero movie ever. Realising after it didn't quite meet those expectations, plus unfortunately seeing bad reviews after put a downer on what could have been so epic.

I still don't think its as bad as some reviews I have read, and urge people to still go see it. But just have an open mind and don't expect it to be a 10/10 movie. I give it a 7/10

title: BvS: DoJ - Definitely entertaining!
review:
Batman Vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice Not a perfect film by a long shot but I left the cinema feeling satisfied! Definitely better than Man of Steel and as a superhero movie I think in time the negative opinions will change! This film definitely deserves everyone to give it a chance! Influenced by great source material (The Dark Knight Returns and All-Star Superman) Yes it's dark and yes it's grim at times but it's acted well and progresses nicely to the end! Again, it's not perfect and adding Batman to this film so soon after the hugely successful Dark Knight Trilogy was always going to raise a few eyebrows! (Keep in mind this isn't Batman and Robin thankfully!)

7/10 from me👍 and looking forward to the sequels!😆

title: An under written film
review:
MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS

Batman V Superman is not as bad as it has been made out to be. However there are a number of issues I found with the film.

The film starts off with a fantastic opening following the events of MOS but from Batman's perspective which was a great way to fuel the characters actions in the movie and hate for Superman. The film overall deals with the ethics of Superman and his place in the world. Much like Dr Manhattan in Snyder's Watchmen. Can a man with all that power be trusted? The two people out to challenge and show him in a negative light are Lex Luthor and Batman. With the discovery of Kryptonite as a weakness to the Man of Steel, Lex and Bats fight for control of it. In my opinion the film would be better titled Batman Vs Lex Luthor: Superman caught in the middle. The plot of the movie doesn't ultimately fit with the title.

As we learn Batman has an issue with Superman's destruction and that is also mirrored through one of Bruce Wayne's employees which is a great subplot played out. But when it comes to Superman's reasoning for having an issue with the Bat it comes across as a simplistic "I don't like how you handle thugs" which adds no weight to the conflict. For a film that talks about Superman, there seems to be very little of him, or for him to do. Much like Lois Lane who shows up once in a while to give him a kiss and ensure everything will be OK.

Though Affleck gives a good turn as Batman it seems the film makers didn't quite know what to do with him and instead riddled him with visualised nightmares that in my mind felt out of place and pointless. Though one nightmare sequence was as cool as hell it felt heavily misplaced. As the trailers suggested this is a seasoned Batman with a troubled past that has seen him loose more than just his parents, which they should have played on more. To give us a fresh Batman. One that has failed, and sees his challenge with Superman as one last shot at writing his wrongs.

Now onto Lex, who surprisingly delivers a good turn as a villain and tries cause chaos where he can. The only issue taken with the characters arc is his random creation of "Doomsday" who equals to a poorly designed CG character. Think of a hairless ape with laser eyes. This element seems rushed and unexplained.

Things do improve in the final act but the ending has no weight or satisfaction to it. SPOILER AHEAD! Our hero Superman dies at the hands of Doomsday but with the announced Justice League we know he will return and in knowing he will return just seems pointless in having him killed, only to come up with a far fetched way of bringing him back, just for the sake of bringing him back.

I enjoy lengthy films but this movie was way too long and could have sped up at the beginning getting straight to the point.

Despite these issues there are a few scenes I mostly enjoyed and wished the rest of the film had been in the same vain. The opening, Court scene, Batman rescues Martha Kent, the Meta Humans and the Wayne employee subplot. Wonder Woman's introduction and the reveal of future Justice League members feels organic and that DC is playing in a much larger universe. Wonder Woman is beautifully weaved in and out of the story with her own agenda, setting her up for her solo feature.

An improvement on Man of Steel but a missed opportunity. Although Frank Miller's Dark Knight Returns has inspired this film visually, perhaps Snyder should have looked to the novels story and context for influence.

title: Gotham v Metropolis? The real winner is you...
review:
I'm going to go out on a limb here and say it, but this is a damn fine film. Prior to watching this I was wondering how this would work yet it does. Building on the dark environment feel as from the Nolan films and Man of Steel, we have our two leads out to challenge each other whilst Lex Luther, The Daily Planet and Wonder Woman stick their noses in.

It's a long movie but it thankfully isn't struggling to either fill in the time or overdo it with the number of characters, strikes a fair balance. Thankfully avoids the errors that the second Avengers movie made. Introduces some new characters too. Jeremy Irons steels the show for me in his brief roles in the film.

I've not gone thru the critics reviews but have heard they have been disparaging, which is disappointing to hear. I feel it might be partially to do that some were carrying over some grudges from before (e.g. there have been many who have criticised Ben Afflecks inclusion) and maybe there is superhero movie fatigue. I don't know, but on its own this is a good movie.

So don your capes and head down to the cinema, a fine film which I'm sure many of you will enjoy.

title: Well worth the wait! Action packed from start to finish. Snyder doesn't only succeed in bringing this epic duo to life, he smashes it!
review: Batman vs Superman continues on from the success of Man of Steel, and maintains a seamless continuation of the story from where Man of Steel ended, with with equally superb action scenes from start to finish. I must comment on the excellent casting for the film, which many people (including myself) were skeptical of. Most especially Ben Affleck really made Batman his own, and has developed an awesome take on the character, with his performance being both believable and exceptional. The storyline is solid, coherent, and the action scenes are especially good. I would urge everyone to go and see this at the CINEMA, as this is the ONLY way you are going to experience the true epic-ness of this film. An all-round success and well, WELL worth a watch!

title: Batman v Superman: A Film for the Fans
review:
This film made me realise that critics reviews do not always mean you will not enjoy a picture. Despite me agreeing with so many reviews for films such as Dallas Buyers Club and Silence of the Lambs to name a couple I do believe this film was harshly criticised. As a huge fan of both Batman and Superman I, like many others went into this film with high hopes and least to say I was not disappointed.

Ben Affleck IS Batman. I personally love this incarnation of the Dark Knight as it is very reminiscent of The Dark Knight Returns comic by Frank Miller. From the first time you see The Bat on screen you know he means business, branding a thug for a Gotham PD Officer to find and sticking to the shadows. Instant Badassery. The mission for Batman in this film reminds me of how the character should be, a protector of the greater good. He feels that Superman could one day become a threat to humanity therefore he must stop him. This is how Batman should be! Willing to take on an all powerful alien and possibly give his life to save countless others.

Continuing on the subject of Ben Affleck he also completely nails Bruce Wayne in a way not seen on screen before. He is a damaged human being as a result of living a double life for twenty years and losing people he loves (Jason Todd's suit on display in the Batcave?) thus you can see in the subtle micro expressions seen on his face when certain topics come up in the film such as the look of sorrow on his face at the aforementioned Robin suit as well as the proud and smug grin he gives Clark Kent when discussing 'The Bat Vigilante'.

Moving over to our other titular character, Superman. There is a massive improvement over Man of Steel here. Henry Cavil has settled into the role of the hero perfectly. In the film we find Clark Kent torn over if the world needs a Superman but wanting to protect those he loves. The feel of the fearful Superman is amazing as it shows he has humanity despite being from another world and that he is not this evil monster depicted by both Bruce Wayne and Lex Luthor therefore grounding the character as a honourable and almost human hero.

The supporting characters really flesh out this film when comparing other variants of the characters seen in DC films of the past 30 years. I have to say Jeremy Iron's Alfred is without a doubt a shining star in BvS stealing the show in every scene he is featured in. He sarcasm and wit of this incarnation of Alfred is so apparent and amazing it it almost makes you think he is reluctant to go along with Bruce's shenanigans for over twenty years as shown through certain lines throughout the film putting Bruce down or putting him in his place. This reminds me much of my Dad as he often put me down and told me not to do something I may have really wanted to do and if I went ahead anyway nine times out of ten I'd be disappointed or hurt by what I've done, Alfred in this film does this exact thing, he is stern and hard but does it to defend what he loves. A tea serving Batman if you will.

I am going to call Wonder Woman out as one of the best things about this movie yet wishing she had more of a purpose in the narrative. Her role is to assist in the climactic fight at the end of the film and not much else except perhaps to initiate the Justice League cameo's and this disappoints me. Gal Gadot is a total badass and I am left wanting more from her character and instead she feels more like an afterthought in terms of the narrative. Diana Price is after a photograph stolen by Lex Luthor of herself which she manages to steal back from him with the unknowing help of Bruce Wayne but that is pretty much it. I am looking forward to what 2017's Wonder Woman solo film will bring for the character but at the moment I am left wanting more from her appearance in BvS.

Jesse Eisenberg is a bit of a strange one. Watching his version of Lex Luthor was so peculiar as I felt like I was watching The Riddler more than Lex. The socially awkward nature this version of Lex has brought to the table somehow fits the tone of the film in my opinion as the cinematic universe being built seems to be full of psychotic villains that will fit for all members of the Justice League.

I will only briefly touch on the story due to spoilers but I now see that Zack Snyder has a thing for the three act narrative as seen with many of his other films. There is a few scenes scattered throughout the film that I think could have been removed as they did nothing for the film both visually and from a narrative standpoint. The dramatics of both the opening and ending will prove to you that this film is worth seeing. But as I stated at the beginning, this is a film for fans as it truly feels like you are watching a moving comic book and will hopefully raise excitement levels for what is to come.

title: Affleck proves to be Superhero franchise Kryptonite
review: In Batman V Superman, we join not long after Man of Steel (2013) left off. Batman played by Ben Affleck, has grown increasingly concerned with the massive casualties caused by Superman's epic battles. Just as Superman (Henry Cavilll) has concern with Batman's torturous vigilante behavior. Mix in Lex Luthor stirring the villainous pot in provoking them to kill off each other and there you have the plot. I have a number of problems with this very flawed all be it, very flashy movie. First and foremost it feels rushed. I felt like a girl on prom night getting rushed through the fore play to get to the sex that is the soon to follow Justice League movie. In an attempt for DC to catch up with Marvel with their already popular Avengers franchise. Only problem is Avengers had two already strong franchises with Iron Man and Captain America to anchor it off. With BvS you get a decent Superman franchise reboot then a Batman Reboot after what was arguably the best superhero franchise with Christopher Nolan's Batman series. And now to vent on Ben Affleck for a moment. He has always been a hit or miss actor. He is far too goofy and smug to play the Dark Knight, this film was a perfect example of that. I wanted more the Town (2010) Affleck and I got what I expected, Daredevil (2003) in different tights. Sci-Fi/Action hero you are not. Stick to directing and dramas. Although he wasn't the most unappealing thing about this film. There was all too much digital effects and not enough time taken to create a good script. No spoilers here, but there are several eye-rolling plot points. It felt like watching someone play a video game for 2 and a half hours. Snoozers BvS does have one shinning gem, Jesse Isenberg as Lex Luthor. Imagine Mark Zuckerberg as a convincing Bond villain. With the two main characters battling it out, he manages to steal the show from hours of mindless CG explosions. If this series wants to stay relevant they need more Jesse Isenberg and less Affleck. I was shocked with all the A list actors in this, (Lawrence Fishburne, Holly Hunter, Jeremy Irons, Kevin Costner, Diane Lane, Amy Adams) he was the only real acting standout. I think post Deadpool (2016) the superhero movie franchise makers need to reevaluate the some things. Much in the way Daniel Craig claims Austin Powers (1997) did damage to the Bond franchise, Deadpool poked fun at the genre while simultaneously reinventing it. I'm not saying they need to reinvent the wheel here, but gone are the days where you can show an audience 2 hours of CG action with and intelligence insulting script and weak plot. With all that being said. AFFLECK YOU DA BOMB IN PHANTOMS (1998) YO!!

title: Spectacular movie but with some flaws
review: Today I've seen this long awaiting movie.I know there are and will be lots of negative reviews for this movie.I congratulate the whole cast and crew and of course Mr. Zack Snyder for making these iconic characters alive on screen.I know this isn't a perfect film and it has its flaws.But I'm glad someone took some initiative to portrait such epic figures of DC Universe on screen unlike we have seen anything before.I loved Ben Affleck as Bruce Wayne and as Batman he nailed it ! Now, I am not going to compare Bale with this one because Nolan's trilogy is based on a different universe and has absolutely nothing to do it with this one. His fighting is undoubtedly the most fascinating part of the movie. His character and combat style is heavily influenced by Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns and Arkham Game Series.(If you are a fan of DC Universe and you haven't seen and played these, you definitely should). The Superman's God like stature is influenced from Injustice: Gods among Us.I loved Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman and would love to see more.For Jesse as Lex some people may not like it because his characteristics are not exactly like the animated/comic version of Lex. However, his insanity and manipulating skills have done justice to the character. I think they might have gone a little overboard with the Doomsday but otherwise I find the movie very enjoyable.

title: What did you expect?
review: Oh Zach Synder... Why does your love of destruction always get in the way of your films being great? I must say, the first 2/3 of this film I loved. Ben Affleck really delivered with his unique take on 'Batman' and with supporting actors such as Lawrence Fishburm and Jeremy Irons it's was pleasantly surprises having had low expectations from a film that had been faced with a lot of prejudices before it was even released. Despite all the actors giving great, heart filled performances; the story was too full of sub-plots and pointless explosions that end you giving you a headache. The other flaw is it tries to do what marvel did in 10 films in 1 film which doesn't really work in its favor. Howerevr to summaries, good acting, weak story. Would recommend to anyone looking to switch off for 3 hours.

title: Ben Affleck, the true Batman!
review: I really don't understand the bad reviews. I loved the movie. Sure, it has flaws, like the way they introduced the Justice League characters, the CGI of the villain and finally Jesse Eisenberg portrayal of Lex Luthor (sorry Jesse), but the rest of the movie... my God! It's amazing! Cavill and Affleck truly nailed it. They are exactly the characters from the comics. It was like seeing the comics come to life. Snyder did an amazing job, like he did with Watchmen. Truly faithful to the comics. It's like reading a comic book. Don't expect to go see jokes and funny moments, this is a very dark movie with a dark and serious tone, just like DC is supposed to be. I give it a 10, I would give it an 8, but with all the haters out there, some people might be influenced by the negative rating of the movie. If you're a comic book fan or a fan of these characters go see it. Ben Affleck really shines on this one! Truly amazing work!

title: Good movie with certain flaws. Many critics reviews prejudiced, watch for yourself and decide
review:
With all the hype surrounding BvS( thanks to marketing team for a 30 month plus long campaign, pun intended ), and certainly all the bashing being directed against it by critics all around the world( currently 31% at Rotten Tomatoes), even a DC fan in his right mind might get skeptical regarding the outcome of this DC Spectacle, which is supposed to tie up one DC standalone movie( at the time of production) , Man of Steel to several other DC properties slated for future release, and at the same time distinguish itself from Marvel Cinematic Universe, DC TV Multiverse, DC animated universe and what not. Getting to Review.

Director Zack Snyder does deliver in this regard.

Having already seen and read some reviews, some of which were unapologetically negative, to say the least, I revered the movie for its visual nature( a trademark of Zack Snyder style of film-making), weaving together the complex nature of storytelling into a 150 minute format, and lastly bringing together two most loved characters in DC together since days of Animated Justice League Series and giving me goosebumps while they were smashing each other on the screen.

Whenever the directer wanted me to feel invested , I did and loved every bit of it.

While some people like me will appreciate the CGI and even go as far as calling it visual poetry of sorts, its repercussions will definitely have on others, including a much the darker tone then Man of Steel and that reasoning will vary from person to person, and most likely then not people will jump to the side as many critics have, comparing it to fun and light Marvel Cinematic Universe(except including the Daredevil and Jessica Jones Series, where a dark color pallet stand out as a highlight). I am a fan of both.

title: The Ultimate DC Film!
review:
I went into this film with decent expectations. I wasn't too fond of Man of Steel with the origin told in flashbacks, the shaky cam overload, the CGI overload and the dark tone and I was a little confused when hearing the Affleck and Eisenberg casting but when I saw this movie, I was surprised. I'm a massive DC fan, have been my whole life and after seeing this movie, I can say I really really enjoyed it.

Many people don't like Spider-Man 3 and the Amazing Spider-Man 2 for being too crowded and this film has a lot in it but I loved that. Being a huge DC fan, I understand everything in it and why everything was there. It was an ultimate DC film. First of all, Ben Affleck was fantastic. My third favourite behind Keaton and Conroy. Absolutely believable and entertaining, enjoyed every minute of him. Although when playing Bruce Wayne, I saw more Ben Affleck but probably because I'm just not yet used to him as batman/Bruce Wayne. Gal Gadot was great but my only problem was her accent was a little difficult to understand at times. Jessie Eisenberg was......interesting. He came across as a disturbed young boy who had a monster trying every minute to break out of him. It was a new take on Lex Luthor but I don't think I would pick this take over the Lex we've all grown to know and love, however, I can get used to it. He did have great attacks and plans on Superman and how he pulled the strings from the beginning showed his potential as a villain and it was great.

Seeing the Justice league set up was great! I didn't think it was forced in at all, I was so pleased to see what we saw of the Flash, Cyborg and Aquaman. On to Doomsday. I personally did not feel like he was shoved into the movie. They were setting him up very early in the film but was unleashed upon Superman at the end and for a decent amount of time. I don't understand why everyone thinks he was shoved in and wasted. For those who know the comics, he's a big, bad monster made to fight Superman and for those who didn't know Doomsday, why would this even bother them at all?! My only complaint about Doomsday was not growing horns on his body to look like the original design of the character but that's only a minor complaint any way. I also did not like the way they handled Jimmy Olsen in this movie. A very sad mistake this movie made that you'll see early in the film.

This movie was ultimate, it had a lot to juggle with. Batman, Wayne murders, Alfred, Batcave, Wonder Woman, Cyborg, Aquaman, The Flash, Lex Luthor, Lois Lane, Kryptonite, Doomsday, Batman fighting Superman and character relationships etc. It was all a lot to juggle and I personally think they handled it very well making a very entertaining and ultimate film. It was like being in DC heaven. I feel like I'm in a very small group of people who liked this film but I hope that you enjoy it when you see it.

title: Yet another one, from Snyder, set to split views
review: Zack Snyder did again what he best does, intrigue moviegoers and critics, alike, into a never-ending war. The movie picks up from the penultimate of its predecessor, Man of Steel, and for most of its entire length, tries to build upon its prequel and setting up a platform for future DC films, compromising its own storyline in the process by giving it a little bit less attention than required. From the title, we'd get an impression of an epic narrative of a ideological and physical battle between Superman and Batman, and we do get to see them fight but only for 5% of the entire runtime of the movie, but it's worth it. The best part of the movie is Batman, played by Ben Affleck. It is a Batman we haven't seen previously on the big screen. He is battle-hardened and brutal to the wrong-doers. He believes that justice must be done, no matter if it includes killing. If you do bad, he is sure to brand you with a bat logo and snap your neck off. Henry Cavil does his job great, as Superman. Superman finds himself in a dilemma about what good is, exactly? What has he really achieved? Some see him as an harbinger of good, here to save them from calamities, while there are people who question his accountability and unlimited prowess, including Bruce Wayne. Wonderwoman (Gal Gadot) has a much bigger role than shown in the trailers and she looks really great in the outfit and in action (She even uses the lasso of truth, but not to its fullest). You may find Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg) funny but me, personally, found it difficult to interpret his dialog. Over all, the movie is great, I liked it as much as my anticipation was and I look forward to Wonderwoman and the Justice League movies. TELL ME, WOULD YOU LIKE THIS MOVIE? YOU WILL.

title: A deeply flawed start to a larger story.
review:
This review does contain spoilers regarding specific plot points.

I wonder if the longer version planned for the home release will fill in some of, what I felt, were massive glaring plot problems. How the hell did Luthor even escape the very first Doomsday explosion? About Doomsday, I really don't think he looked as good as the Hulk does in the Avengers stuff. In fact, a few sequences, like virtually every one of Diana's, consisted mostly of reaction shots and then what looked like pure cg, without the smoother blend you get in the more expensive MCU films. I need to study the home release to really see how clean that was, because on first pass it looked weak. Perhaps having a lot of this take place in the dark was a terrible idea.

My favorite sequence was the opening. Pretty sick, actually. I'm not sure how strong I felt the rehashed Batman background worked, but all of the stuff in Metropolis during the Man of Steel sequence was pretty scary. The film starts out fairly strong, but then meanders all over the place while simultaneously glossing over major shifts in character motivation along the way.

How Cavill was directed to act when he shows up to "kill" Batman was really cringe worthy, I felt. He was kind of gritting his lines, I felt like I was watching professional wrestling at times. Everything Batman says to him during that sequence is equally so as well. Truth to tell, I was having a hard time believing in any characters actual motivations throughout the entire film, the longer it went on. It's an occasionally bland and occasionally confusing film, with odd narrative choices.

I am supposed to believe that Alex Luthor was just nuts, and he got worse after he grabbed the Kryptonian archive. OK, fine, but I still find his scenes with the Senator extremely tedious. and a seeming waste of time in this story completely. What about Alex writing Batman all of these little notes, just to anger him?

Batman suddenly being contacted from the future, where he had this "vision" sequence, was very clumsily handled, I thought. It kind of comes out of nowhere, and while the sequence itself looks cool in the beginning (aka Apokolips furnaces and Parademons), the entire sequence just felt, off. Are they implying that Superman comes back as a Darkseid servant? The story has been done before, of course.

Here's some comedy, a number of people in the theater applauded. I certainly wouldn't go that far, but I didn't hate it. I find it flawed, more so even than Man of Steel, which maybe I liked better, but I don't know.

I wonder how many parents are going to regret bringing really young kids to see this.

title: Batman vs Superman
review: This movie was OK. It wasn't that great. Most of the actors weren't even that good. Ben Affleck was OK as Batman, but I still like Christian Bale better. Also I was not expecting the death of Superman in this. Also Jessie Eisenberg was trying to imitate the Joker in this film. Also if you look in the Batcave you can see one of Batman's old suits with the Jokers writing on it. Another thing Lex Luthor is nothing like the Joker. Both are evil, but the Joker is more psychotic then Lex is. Also this movie didn't have a whole lot of emotion in it cause I already know about Superman's death in the comics. Still this was an OK movie but not that great. I don't even think I'll be watching this again any time soon.

title: Too Many Sub-plots, Not Enough Batman v Superman
review:
For a movie that is seemingly about a face-off between two of the most iconic heroes in comic book history, it's surprising how little they actually interact. Their "fight" is delegated to passive aggressive arguments between Bruce Wayne and Alfred Pennyworth, and the occasional scowl at a television screen every time Batman does something illegal. Part of me wishes that there had been more between Clark Kent and Bruce Wayne, because the scene at the Luthor party was pretty incredible. Once the first half of the movie has sufficiently built up the conflict, the final act of the movie is a non-stop science fiction battle sequence. Honestly, it feels like two separate movies : a political drama and a superhero movie. Both "films" are good, but I do not think they work as a single cohesive piece. Wonky editing that is increasingly a trade-mark in Zack Snyder films makes the first half appear sloppy and awkward, while the second half is regulated to green-screen, over saturated fighting.

I will that Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot are amazing as Batman and Wonder Woman, and Henry Cavill's Superman continues to mature into the classic hero that we all know him to be. Affleck manages to bring a new light to the character of Bruce Wayne, a difficult feat considering how many times Batman has been rewritten for audiences. And Affleck looks incredible - I want to shake the hand of the costume designer for this film. Affleck, Cavill and Gadot all bring these iconic heroes to life in a visual spectacle that will delight comic book fans everywhere. Henry Cavill's Superman was fine, nothing special, but I believe that to be because just how poor the writing is in so many of Superman's key scenes. Some of the the lines are just atrocious. And when you couple it with Jesse Eisenberg's maniacal, unhinged Lex Luthor, it's an uncomfortable mix of superheroes that writers cannot seem to do justice. No pun intended. Luthor is classically a suave genius. Superman, a complex man striving to do good in a world in which he does not belong. But they are both written into crude stereotypes that detract from the complexity of the story they are attempting and create odd moments of conflict. Eisenberg's villain worked in this film; he was certainly evil. But he was not Alexander Luthor.

Batman v Superman is far from a perfect film. There is a lot going on, and I think that's where the film falls short. The dream sequences are clunky and strange, and leave the audience confused rather than excited for future films. And the Justice League cameos felt thrown in there last minute to satisfy a studio executive. A email from Bruce Wayne to Diana Price? Containing files about future Justice League members? And with their respective symbols conveniently marking each file? That has to be the laziest film set-up that I have ever seen.

The heart of this movie lies in the relationships between characters. Clark and Lois ground this film, and I only wish that we were given more of them being a normal, domestic couple. Clark's devotion to Lois, and her intense protection of him give the film needed bittersweet moments that make Superman's fatal sacrifice at the end all the more poignant. In the heat of the moment, Superman's death felt stale and cheap to me. But looking back on it, it creates an engaging conflict for the character, and it certainly is a ballsy choice.

This is a solid movie. The criticisms with pacing and confusing plots are certainly warranted, but I think the good far outweighs the bad. For this one, the critics are wrong. The acting is good, the characters are engaging, and there is lot of potential for a fantastically complex cinematic universe.

title: Great movie, you might not enjoy it if you are not a fan.
review:
Just got back from watching BvS and I am now writing this review. This review WILL contain some spoilers so please do not continue reading unless you have seen the movie, or you want to ruin it for yourself.

This movie was shot beautifully; the director and cinematographer did an amazing job with this. As well as the music! Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL never seem to disappoint. I had the pleasure of watching this in an IMAX theatre which made the movie really draw me in. As for the movie itself, it was a movie made BY a fan, FOR the fans! There are a plethora of negative reviews around the internet right now and they all seem to have one thing in common, the majority of these people are not fans of comic book movies, or even DC comics. I am far from a DC fanboy and at this moment in time I really do prefer Marvel by a LONG stretch but after this film I'm worried that this is going to change. I genuinely enjoyed watching the movie that was the most important thing to me.

Batman was played brilliantly by Ben Affleck, probably better than Christian Bale, this Batman was very close to the comics, the fighting was especially fluid and you could really see that batman was just a man who is very, very strong but also very, very angry. The fact Batman kills is quite justified, possibly due to the death of Robin, whichever one it is, he is also older and probably sick and tired of giving criminals mercy as he can clearly see that that method was not working. On top of all of this Batman's reasons for wanting Superman taken down really did make sense, especially with Lex Luthor's manipulation! The only negative thing I can say about Batman in this movie is that I wasn't really a fan of his costume, I just wasn't a fan of it - but this did not impact my enjoyment of the movie at all.

Henry Cavil as Superman not much to say really, pretty much the same as Man of Steel, probably a bit more muscular? I couldn't tell. Too focused on Batfleck. One complaint I guess is his accent, could do with a little more work, but yet again, a minor detail that did not intrude with my enjoyment of the movie. Overall, Cavil is a great Superman; he certainly has the looks for the character but as an overpowered character who isn't as complicated of a man as Batman is, there isn't much to say about him. Lois Lane as a whole I found quite annoying during the film, I'm not really enjoying how she is becoming such an important character and I found her just as irritating as she was in Man of Steel.

Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman, in my opinion she didn't get as much screen time as I hope she would have, her secret identity Diana Prince was seen more – but the fighting that was shown as Wonder Woman was spectacular, probably on par with Superman's fight scenes, I'm really looking forward to her movie and seeing her origin story.

I really did love Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, bearing in mind he is the son of another Lex Luthor, who was probably the Lex Luthor that we all know that's in the comics. This Lex was different, I really did enjoy seeing him on screen, he was psychotic and played stunningly by Eisenberg, he was probably the only character that had the slightest bit of humour in him, but it was not laugh out loud humour as Lex is a complete madman in this, and is not afraid to kill civilians to prove a point. Jeremy Irons as Alfred Pennyworth was wonderful, just like he should be, he cares about Bruce Wayne and is a very useful aide to him, this was a brilliant casting choice as was the rest of the cast.

As for the cameos, I feel as if they were executed almost perfectly, they got me extremely hyped up for Justice League, the Flash's cameo near the middle of the film as Bruce Wayne wakes up from a nightmare was a clear indication of him warning him of a future threat, stating that "Lois Lane" is the key . He also had a second cameo as Wonder Woman accesses the files Bruce sent her that Lex had on meta humans, this was not as exciting. Although right after this we see Cyborg as he is being tested on and then finally, Aquaman, he was shown staring into the camera for some reason, I was wondering what was going on until he points his trident and was off, seemingly as fast as Superman was in the sky.

Overall all of the acts were satisfying, we saw Batman given a risen to fight Superman, we saw them actually fighting, we saw the introduction to the Justice League, we saw Lex being evil as well as Doomsday getting more and more powerful as he tests the limits of our three heroes. Very minor flaws in this movie but the main thing is that it served its purpose of plotting Batman and Superman against each other, and introduced the Justice League. Right now I am going to give this a 7.5/10, it sure as hell wasn't perfect, but I am excited for the DC extended universe and its forthcoming movies. That is what counts.
