title: Ultimate Justice
review:
It may Dawn on some, that this is darker than your average Marvel movie (yes pun intended). And whomever watches this, can decide (be the Jury) and do this movie a justice of his or her own. But enough of the puns, because while the Suicide Squad at least looks like it will be funny (still dark hopefully), this has almost no fun at all. Unless you count a writing on the wall in Latin, where Snyder makes fun of the Watchmen (or rather his own take/movie of it, probably).

Of course that and some other things may go over the head of some. And if you haven't seen the extended cut, my understanding is that the movie will make less sense. So I did only watch the 3 hours cut. And it was OK. But while Batman (and Affleck is the best thing in this, period!) is brooding and he is supposed to be that way, Superman at least should be much more than a mope ... Also there is not enough Batman in here. But I am excited about the Batman standalone movie. Visually of course Gal Gadot is stunning. When she opens her mouth on the other hand ... well let's just say you'll either find her accent enticing or ridiculous. (Un)Fortunately she doesn't have that much to say.

Her training paid off though, and the action scenes are really good. But we didn't expect anything less from a Zack Snyder movie. The major issue here (apart from the missing lightness, it's just too heavy and too serious for its own good), is that it has major plot holes and major logical errors (why did you say that name ... really? First of all you would state the relationship rather than a name in a situation like this and not the first name of the person you're trying to save, second of all: Really?). While not funny, there are many moments that are clearly ridiculous to say the least ... I really wanted to like this more. Especially because of the beating it got by the critics ... but foreshadowing aside, if you watch the Honest Trailer for this, it will be an eye opener!

review: There is so much more to this movie than meets the eye. There are multiple themes played out through this movie which makes this movie a taste for a more educated and intellectual person. This movie is packed with extraordinary action scenes and the tone for this movie is spectacular. The acting is incredible! However, some of the flow of the movie near the beginning was not good, only because the rest of the movie needed a strong basis to go on, and there were so many subplots that needed a beginning, which I believe is the main reason the start of the movie may seem like it is jumping back and forth, but near the middle of the movie the pace becomes one of the best I have seen, like Scarface's! This movie really makes you think philosophically, and Neil deGrasse Tyson's cameo left me excited and very passionate about the thematic elements in the movie. There are scenes serving as themes for other scenes which is remarkable! Chris Terrio, A Harvard graduate in English literature, wrote the script alongside David S. Goyer, who wrote the script with Chris Nolan on The Dark Knight Triogy, did a fantastic job! In conclusion this movie brings so much more to the table than any other superhero movie, it is almost impeccable. One of the only bad parts are the CGI near he end of the movie. And how the climax scene occurred. It was dealt with an an acceptable manner, but not an epic one. After watching this movie I felt the same way as I have just watched Scarface or The Godfather Pt. 2. A truly intellectual film. Overall, a close to 10/10 film which will leave you ecstatic for another DC film!

title: The World's Finest - Ultimate Edition
review:
If you're looking for The Batman Superman Movie of the late 1990s, then this is not the film for you. I personally love The Batman Superman Movie, I grew up on it and it's how I began loving Batman & Superman, but Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is something for the more serious moviegoer and fan who wants something new.

What people don't seem to understand about DC Films versus Marvel Studios is that Marvel Comics characters are made to be relatable, they're made to me more like the every-day person. DC Comics characters are not. They're written as legends. This is why when DC took the Marvel approach with their characters in the Green Lantern film that it failed. DC characters are not meant to be in Marvel Studios-like films. They're meant to be legendary.

Batman V Superman takes the Batman/Superman story to a whole new level by starting off with our heroes as enemies. Bruce Wayne is after Superman because he believes Superman to be a threat. He has an argument. Meanwhile, Clark Kent is after Batman because he believes Batman is unjustly beating, torturing, and killing criminals. He has an argument. We come to find out that Lex Luthor has been pitting both heroes against each other this whole time out of hatred for Superman and everything he stands for.

Many complaints I read about this film included: Batman kills people, Superman is not Superman, Lex sucks, and "Martha!"

Batman killing: Every single Batman film features Batman killing someone, directly or indirectly. In the original Batman comics, Batman actually used bullets on his Batplane to kill when necessary. Even in modern day comics, Superman has willingly given Batman a piece of Kryptonite to use on him in case it becomes necessary, and Batman agrees to kill him if he has to. But even besides that, in the DCEU Batman has lost Robin to the Joker, has been fighting crime for 20 years, and is largely based off of Frank Miller's Batman who will kill. This is not a surprise.

Superman: Superman is most certainly Superman. He's having doubts about what he's doing, Superman has had these same feelings in the Silver Age, Bronze Age, and even in current Superman books. It doesn't define his character, but if you've watched Man of Steel or BVS you see that it doesn't define Clark here either.

Lex: Honestly, this Lex is just personal taste. I can see why some like him and why some don't. It's okay to have a differing opinion. What sold me on this version was his final scene with Batman.

Martha: I personally had no problem with this either. It was set up the entire movie and works just fine.

I thought the theatrical cut of this film was excellent, I really did, but I have to say that the Ultimate Edition is definitely worth the time and money and is by far the superior vision of the film. It expands on Lex's mastermind plan, dives deeper into Superman's life as Clark Kent, extends the battle scenes a little more, and really fills in some of the plot hole issues I was having initially.

The one thing that I'm not completely convinced works for the film is the future sequence that teases Justice League when the Flash shows up to warn Bruce about the future. To the average moviegoer this is very confusing and will not be paid off until the Justice League feature film.

Speaking of, the Justice League cameos were great (see Suicide Squad for more) and really hyped me up for the film. The final fight between the Trinity (Superman, Wonder Woman, and Batman) versus Doomsday was incredible and was definitely the way the Death of Superman should be handled on film. As someone who's favorite Superman story is the Death (and Return) of Superman, I was very pleased.

Overall, Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice does cram a lot in (a Man of Steel sequel, a Batman reboot, a JLA prequel, and a versus movie) and at times this hurts the film, but in the end it is honestly an underrated masterpiece bringing together the World's Finest superheroes.

title: Not sure why so much hate.
review:
The CLAW here, bringing you another, should you see it in theaters, or wait for the DVD. Here we go:

I'm honestly surprised the amount of hate that this film has been getting. I truly feel that it is unwarranted. Do I think this is the best film ever made, no, but I also feel that it is unique and a great addition to the DC movie Universe.

This movie pits Batman, played by Ben Affleck, against Superman, Henry Cavill. We also get shots of Wonder Woman, played by Gal Gadot. The evil mastermind Lex Luthor, Jesse Eisenberg manages and extremely intricate plot to make both of our heroes take each other out. Which, for a villain, actually isn't a bad idea, have a hero do your dirty work. Superman is going through an identity process, is he the hero he thinks he is, or is he a vigilant anti that people on metropolis are starting to think he is. Which is strange because he never seems to anything anti hero, like Batman. Batman on the other hand is roaming the streets of Gotham branding people with his throwing stars, embracing being the vigilant, knowing it gets things down without all the red tape. Lex uses this to convince each other that they should kill each other, pretty ingenious.

This movie had a fairly decent pace, always advancing the plot, however there are quite a few noticeable plot holes holes. They don't distract you, but enough to make you think, "Hey, how'd he know that?!" The fight scenes were top notch, and more violent then I thought. DC seems to be taking a darker, grittier approach compared to Marvels comedic, light heart-ed approach, which I actually appreciate, it makes them different. The final battle scene was pretty awesome, and a montage of Batman training was pretty awesome. Pay attention to his exercise routine as he uses them all in the fight, pretty cool!

There are however a few things I did not like about this movie. Starting off, we get another, how Bruce Wayne's parents were murdered scene. Enough with those already. Secondly, the villain mastermind himself, Lex Luther. Eisenberg was not suited to play him. His performance reminded me more of a Riddler type character. Outwardly psychotic, with tantrums, and bursts of rage. To me, Lex was always the calm, cool, and collected villain like Gene Hackman portrayed, and even Kevin Spacey did. It really was bothersome to watch. Second, without getting to spoiler-ish, was the second villain Doomsday. He never amounted to anything other than to advance the plot for the next justice league movie. He was an awesome villain, and hes pretty much wasted. Overall though, I have to say the pros outdo the cons, and even with some negatives, I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. Definitely worth the watch!

Recommendation: See in Theaters! Also, buy the extended edition on DVD!

title: If you are a comic book fan you will enjoy it

title: A refreshingly new take on the superhero genre
review: DC has re-imagined its cinematic universe, and it is a breath of fresh air. We've gotten so used to our superheroes being completely perfect in the Marvel universe - there is nothing remotely dark about the MCU - that when a movie tries to break that mold, we freak out. I was a huge fan of Nolans re-imagined Batman Trilogy. Dark and gritty. Makes sense. It's Batman. Batman v Superman is a visual masterpiece. I highly recommend that you watch the Ultimate edition, as the studio made a huge mistake by making the Theatrical movie much shorter and losing some key plot momentum. That being said - Marvel is a fine tuned machine. It sticks to its safe, clean comedy - and that sells. However, DC did a great job with this movie - showing us a darker side to our favorite superheroes and bringing together two of the most iconic figures ever. The action is great, the plot makes sense, and considering the introduction of Batfleck...it was seamless. Which, by the way, Affleck might be the best one yet. It's time for us to demand more from our heroes. Give the DCEU a chance.

review: After creating a Superman who doesn't behave as Superman for disappointing "Man of Steel", the franchise includes in its sequel a Lex Luthor who does not look like Lex Luthor (shaving his long hair is not enough as his psychological traits are also different) and an Aquaman who does not look like Aquaman (indeed, he reminds Marvel's Namor). title: The black soldier turns on the blue and red supermodel- and it's excellent.
review: I saw this movie twice in the theater- once with my friend and once with my family- both times were awesome, no doubt. Almost everything is on the top of totem pole of superhero movies- the acting, the script, the orchestral score, the character development, the effects, the list goes on. The backstory of Bruce Wayne is handled marvelously, with an already heart-wrenching scene at the very beginning of the movie that does more justice in the film later. Ben Affleck nails the character of Batman, providing loads of soul and tech-savvy goodness to boast likability from the audience. The rest of the cast shines here as well, from the witty performance of Jeremy Irons as Pennyworth to the charming character that Henry Cavill reprised from Man Of Steel. The visuals are outstanding, particularly the practical effects. How can Hollywood pull all this off, I have no clue, but they do a lot right, that's a surefire fact. Can't wait to see Suicide Squad pull many more practical stunts later on! Lastly, I saw the film at an IMAX theater in 3D 45 minutes away from my home and I've got to say, it was definitely worth the extra expensive price. Everything popped out of the screen like it should have, the crisp picture matched with the color schemes and the sound let out a mighty roar when it needed to. Overall, Batman v. Superman: Dawn Of Justice is definitely a winner for any DC fan or non-DC fan, whether you liked Man Of Steel or not. Every cast member shines as their characters, the visuals are beguiling as ever, and the heart is still present. It may not be for everyone, but it's a goldmine for me!

title: (Ultimate Edition Review) Five Word Review: Overlong, Sprawling Spectacle; Good Moments
review:
This is a review just of the 'Ultimate Edition', as I did not deign to watch it in the cinema. Apparently I dodged a bullet, as the theatrical edition was a lot less coherent without the removed scenes. In this form, BvS: DoJ is certainly overlong and overstuffed, with far too many subplots to keep track of. Acting as a sequel to Man of Steel, an introduction to the new Batman, an introduction to Wonder Woman, a setup to Justice League by teasing a bigger interplanetary threat, introducing Aquaman, Cyborg, and The Flash, and having previously opposed figures Batman and Superman bury the hatchet, being a setup for The Joker in Suicide Squad...there's a lot to cram in, causing even this three hour special edition film to feel like a breakneck pace. In parts, that is - at other times the pace is drastically different, causing the film to sometimes feel like a Frankenstein-ed version of several different films all stitched together.

Nevertheless, there are many good things in this film. First and foremost, Ben Affleck - reviled by many on the internet after the announcement of his casting - makes an excellent Batman, as does Jeremy Irons as erstwhile butler Alfred. In fact, one of the best and most underdeveloped facets of the film is the moral uncertainty and dilemmas. Batman and Superman each have valid and well-developed reasons for mistrusting each other and wanting to depose the other. However, this element is somewhat abandoned in favour of more flashy reasons for the two to fight later in the film. In Superman's parts of the film, some elements of the story feel a little stretched out - Amy Adams is a great actor but her story is markedly less interesting and ultimately serves little purpose as Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor, a megalomaniacal business type with more than a streak of the eccentric, formulates his master plan anyway. Eisenberg is fantastic as ever, and imbues his role with the same energetic, insane mania that classic comic book villains like The Riddler boast (even if some of his character's lines are truly uninspired and just plain bad writing). Gal Gadot serves her purpose as Wonder Woman, yet ultimately is needlessly shoehorned in (though this doesn't stop her from outshining both Superman and Batman in the final showdown).

This afore-mentioned showdown, however, is the film's lowest moment. Unnecessarily spoiled in the trailer, little is added in the final film. The fight is as seizure-inducing and destructive as something out of a Transformers film, and is more eye-rolling than exciting. Which is a shame, because there are some great sequences of action elsewhere, mostly from Batman. Notably, one sequence in a multi-storey building is a real highlight, feeling like something out of an Arkham game, and it will be exciting to see Affleck direct his own take on Batman in a few years time. Hopefully he will be given the freedom to display some of the moral complexity he oversaw in Gone Baby Gone.

Ultimately, BvS: DoJ is nowhere near as bad as some would have you believe. It's flawed, sure. But as the announcements and trailers came out and everyone realised how much material was going to be crammed into one film, it became apparent that there would be problems. This film had to be made to advance various plots so that the DC film franchise could move on to better projects, such as the new Batman and The Justice League. It's often enjoyable - who didn't want to see two of the most famous popular culture icons ever go head to head? - and there are hints of a truly great film lying underneath layers of murky subplots and rushed setup. Overall, Batman v Superman is worth watching if at least to witness the spectacle and get prepared for upcoming projects. The much-touted one word resolution of the titular battle, however, is catastrophically inexcusable. 59/100.

title: The Ultimate Edition is a truly great movie stained by a truncated theatrical edition.
review: Upon hearing of the 3 hour cut and 30 minutes cut mere weeks before release, I immediately grew suspicious. Upon viewing, while I enjoyed it to rate it a 6/10, the film noticeably lacked many parts in ways that compromised the end product. Upon the UC's release, I made my judgment on BvS. I loved it. While unorthodox in behavior, Lex is a truly scheming villain, and dangerous when he begins resorting to more twisted means. The political and personal dramas around Superman's existence, the toll it has on him, his take on Batman, Batman's vendetta and distrust of meta-humans, Lois Lane uncovering Luthor's scheme, and the action scenes. If I had to pick one thing that stands above the others, it would be the music. Not to discredit the rest of the movie, but just saying, bravo Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL. And to Hans, DC fans will dearly miss you. The only true gripes I have are nothing to do with the key story itself, just minor scenes that were more fan service if anything. The Knightmare sequence felt like it would have been better suited in the Justice League by what DC is building towards, and the JL intro videos may have been better served as an online release only in a viral marketing stunt. Wonder Woman seeing her old photo sent by Batman reawakening her memories would have sufficed. In my personal opinion, I feel this movie will be better appreciated as the DC universe expands, as we will see it as the beginning for many characters, such as Lex, Batman and more. And I hope WB learns their lesson from this. To keep the mystery in the marketing, which they seem to have with Suicide Squad and Wonder Woman. And to not butcher the movie out of a greedy possibility of more showings per day, especially by reports saying this version was the one they themselves gave a standing ovation to. No bad movie is too short, and no good movie is too long. And 3 hours of this was what we needed, not the 2.5 hours we got in theaters. I shall be throwing away my DVD disk from the Blu-ray set, as only the other two disks contain the extras and the Ultimate Cut. It nearly pained me to have a movie I genuinely loved being so harshly criticized, but I will defend this movie, the Ultimate Cut, as a truly great comic book movie. Bring on Justice League!

title: The movie is in the Roots
review: Listen, first off let me say that the movie COULD have been better. However that's not to take away what the movie actually gave us. I have noticed my fair share of nay-sayers because the movie wasn't what they had imagined. But can we take the movie for what it was? Yes. It was great action, a decent combined story line, & amazing effects with 2 of the most beloved super heroes in history. No spoilers; but everything happens for a reason in this movie and a lot of it has original batman comic background knowledge. Which unless you're a hardcore batman fan, you would never notice. title: When franchises collide
review:
I went to see this movie with very low expectations. I'm not a fan of Zack Snyder and the mix of Superman and Batman seemed more like a construction for the box office than anything else. And if Man of Steel was anything to go by I expected this film to be both boring and pretentious.

Like King Kong vs Godzilla, Freddy vs Jason or Alien vs Predator; Batman v Superman comes out behind a number of movies with the two icons involved. Usually, these death-match flicks are made when both franchises are too washed-out to hype the audience. The producers turns to fan fiction for some new commercial potential. And in the case of Batman the franchise so clearly peaked with the brilliant Dark Knight that it was always going to be a downward spiral from there.

The plot comes with the standard concepts and problems associated with these franchise collisions. The two parties meet, conflict occurs and the fight is on. But why? In this case it's Alexander Luthor that applies the old divide and conquer tactic. Superman clearly wasn't blessed with super intelligence as you might think. But who's rational when it comes to love and family? Eventually they unite against an common enemy. Lets just say it's all very standard stuff.

The casting is a mixed bag to say the least. Henry Cavill does the same Superman thing we've seen before. I think Superman is quite a dull character to begin with and Cavill does absolutely nothing to make him more interesting. Supermans alter ego Clark Kent is the exact same thing but with glasses. Or is Superman the Alter ego? Whatever.

Ben Affleck fits in well with Cavill. His Bruce Wayne lacks all the humor and charisma the character should have and his Batman is even worse. Ben Affleck looks like he's walking around in one of those early diving suits with iron boots and helmet. I guess you need quite heavy armor when you're fighting Superman. But he ends up looking like one of those Batman impersonators in Dark Knight more than he does the real thing. Maybe he's wearing hockey pads? I don't know.

Jesse Eisenberg plays the villain Alexander Luthor. His part is a bit more interesting but sadly even worse. Luthor jr wants to bring on Supermans doomsday and starts off as a young and nerdy corporate wizkid developing into this evil Willy Wonka character. Seeing Eisenberg trying to pull off these Johnny Depp-ish lines and moves is pure pain. He even cites Alice in Wonderland. Bad casting and bad acting.

Amy Adams does a good job as Lois. The job of trying to make up for Supermans total lack of character that is. And Jeremy Irons is perfect as Alfred. A part he could probably do in his sleep.

A lot of the criticism of the cast should probably be aimed at the director. Snyder isn't in my opinion a very good director and it shows with the actors. But Snyder is all about overly orchestrated action scenes in CGI and slow motion. He's throwing people through buildings, walls, ceilings and building material in general. And he loves those dream scenes that you suppose to think is really happening but ends with a scare. If that's what you're looking for, look no more.

Some of the action is good though. At least the fighting that only involves humans. Snyder has clearly seen Dark Knight a few times. The grim tone and washed-out color palette makes for a similar look. A lot of the drama in the buildup to the action is done in a similar style. Lex is shot with his back to the camera a few times in Joker style, dramatic opening of doors and there's even a bad guy with a big scar by his mouth.

title: The Start of Something
review:
Arguably one of the most anticipated blockbusters of the decade, Zack Snyder's Batman vs Superman (2016) had a lot to live up to, for fans and critics alike. The first two thirds of the film are strong which is mostly due to the interesting subplots involving Scoot McNairy's character - an ex-employee of Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) who lost his legs in the attack on Metropolis in Man of Steel (2013) - and Holly Hunter's Senator Finch. However, once these are wrapped up the film loses a lot of momentum and then seems to sacrifice any coherent, structured narrative. It seems blatantly clear that the film is missing an extra half hour, which won't be seen until the extended cut is released on DVD in the near future. There is a struggle to work out how some scenes relate, whereas a handful of scenes just don't make sense at all. For example, when Lex Luthor (a disappointing Jesse Eisenberg) enters the crashed Kryptonian spaceship, he seems to know exactly how to control everything, including how to build a giant CGI monster called Doomsday. In regards to the superheroes, Affleck and Cavill nailed their parts. Affleck is possibly the grittiest incarnation of the caped crusader seen on screen, which is epitomised in a scene where he takes on a building full of goons in order to rescue a vital character. Cavill has matured in the costume and is easily believable as Superman. Wonder Woman, however, didn't have a big enough chance to make an impression and almost felt unnecessary. Perhaps the film would've benefited more if Snyder had instead focused more on Gal Gadot as Diana Prince and left Wonder Woman for the upcoming Justice League movies. The Justice League itself was set up too much, which detracted from the narrative. There was a cameo from Ezra Miller's version of the Flash which worked effectively until Bruce discovered a file that had footage of all the metahumans on it, thus giving Snyder a chance to show off all his new superheroes in a ridiculous and unbelievable manner. More groundwork for the Justice League movies appear to be Bruce's grim visions, which may have been induced by another major DC villain, Darkseid. The vision at his parents grave was unsettling and shocking, but the desert sequence seemed to be forced and, again, it didn't make much sense. Although it didn't live up to everyone's expectations and was often needlessly confusing, the film still managed to have some good, entertaining moments.

7/10

title: What a Mess...But It's Kind of an Entertaining Mess
review:
Right...I'm going to start off by saying that I thought it was a pretty damn fun watch...without a doubt it was extremely flawed but it was kind of fun, whether I was entertained by some of the unintentionally funny dialogue or the actual intentional aspects of the film is up for debate but if someone was to ask 'was I entertained?' I would certainly reply yes.

The dark & brooding Affleck was very convincing as both Batman & Bruce Wayne, Jeremy Irons & Laurence Fishburne although fleeting in screen time had some very funny & memorable dialogue, Jesse Eisenberg...well I'm probably going to break the general consensus here & state that I thought it was a bold & worthy attempt at breathing new life into a villain that needed something new to offer, that's not to say that at times he was a testing experience & galloping over the acceptable edge but I liked small aspects of what Eisenberg was trying to bring to the character, you certainly feel Gal Gadot's screen presence & she's effective as Wonder Woman & my word her music theme was just fantastic as was the general scoring of the film, those are what I deemed the positives.

Now lets go to the negatives, it was always going to be difficult to get the complete job done that needed to be done to build up to what is to come from their own DC cinematic universe so it's no surprise that editing of scenes together certainly felt a bit awkward at times, it was like the director went 'right I need this scene to happen, then this scene to happen & then this scene to happen' without really a thought as to how to actually link them together seamlessly, so now we get to 'that scene' you know the scene where they try to do what Marvel did over the course of five films before they made The Avengers, a world building, super-team building segment, it certainly does feel forced, on another note why was there a need for two...that's right two fake out dream segments?! One is clichéd enough, two is truly unforgivable, also the inclusion of a literally 'recycled' foe/villain towards the films end was rather uninspiring, also as I've said previously in my positives I was entertained by the dialogue but my word is some of it utter nuts & bolts dialogue & there's certain lines that for me were truly laugh out loud but unintentionally funny from a scriptwriters point of view, examples of this are a certain Kryptonian spaceships computer & comments made by characters as Superman is taking Doomsday into space were moments I couldn't hold myself back with laughter.

So how to sum it up? Well it certainly isn't the complete disaster many critics would have you believe but on an equally important note it certainly isn't anywhere near any of Marvel's best, it's big dumb superhero fun, given what I'd read beforehand & the fact that my expectations were never high in seeing this film maybe has had an effect on how I've eventually come to this slightly more positive than expected opinion, like I said if you're in the right mood this is a film that can be fun...however there's is stuff that is unforgivable & it kind of depends how much you're willing to forgive the filmmakers for cramming so much in, so massively & extremely flawed but if you're in the forgiving mood it can be kind of fun & that is my final verdict...phew! title: A Sloppy Plot with Good Moments
review: Batman V Superman is a movie that wants to be great at certain moments, and definitely is, yet it doesn't care about the rest of its running time. The main selling point of the film is in the title: the fight between our two main protagonists, and yet their motivations are sloppily set up, making both of the heroes unable to root for. The actors portraying the heroes, however, do shine in their performances. Ben Affleck ranks high in the long line of actors who have had the honor of playing Batman, and Henry Cavil plays a convincing Superman. However, just because the performances were good doesn't mean the characters were. Superman has little time to develop and any transformation he goes through is repeated from Man of Steel, a surprisingly better film, and Batman performs questionable actions.

The film falls down greatly with a script that sounds like it has just been transferred from a comic book. Doomsday just wasn't needed. A big scary monster just seemed out of context with the rest of the gritty film. The inclusion of Doomsday was almost comic, returning to Christopher Reeve Superman. I thought Snyder did quite well with the idea of Superman not being a God. There were some good parts in this film. Ben Affleck as Batman/ Bruce Wayne was very good, a very interesting character and a good hope for the future in this 'DC Expanded Universe'. I was initially skeptical of the inclusion of Wonder Woman, however I thought Gal Gadot really added to the film. I wanted to learn and see more about her. The action sequences were well thought out, especially the Batman sequences. Despite some obvious holes in this film, there are some good parts. I wouldn't even consider abandoning the DC Expanded Universe like some have suggested. Underneath some of the terrible dialogue, not so brilliant story and some plain stupidity that this film is plagued by, there is a good film somewhere underneath all of it. I think perhaps a Ben Affleck Batman film, before this would have benefited, just so this DC Universe could have two independent films before going on this Avengers equivalent. I think the Marvel Cinemaic Universe had 5 films before introducing a cross-over film, I think DC could have benefited if they had followed a similar pattern, just so we didn't have to be introduced to so many different characters. title: Why Batman v Superman Disappointed
review:
I heard about the poor critic's reviews. I heard the MCU and DCEU fanboys argue their points as to which would be more successful. I heard it all, but I wanted to see it for myself and make my own assessment. I tire from the mundane argument of which is better, Marvel or DC. Both have characters that incite the nostalgia of reading comic books and watching Saturday morning cartoons as a kid. So I'm going to skip the comparisons and just tell what I praise about this movie and what I was disappointed about by this movie.

The movie paced really well up to a certain point. I didn't find the editing at all confusing as I understood the necessity to show the impact of Bruce's parents' deaths and his ascension to becoming Batman. I also like that they interwove the vision of Darkseid into the story line as he poses a very credible threat necessary for the Justice League to come together. The cameo of the Flash, Aquaman, and Cyborg were well placed - a nice sprinkle of a teaser for things to come.

I praise the fact that DC is going for a more mature audience in that they don't take time for the witty jokes and fun-natured combat scenes that Marvel has so successfully capitalized on. It's much more realistically grounded and a welcome direction for comic book movies, one that works quite well within the DCEU.

Wonder Woman is part of the Amazons of Greek Mythology, and I believe people have had a misconception for quite some time as to how she should be depicted. In my opinion, she actually coincides a lot more closely to how I would imagine a Greek Amazon to appear. Gal Gadot has the olive skin, the build, and the exotic eyes to fit the description of a Greek women and I believe she does a fantastic job in the role.

Ben Affleck nailed the role of Batman. He is perhaps the most true to the character of anyone I've seen. From his build, to his fighting style, and he is perhaps the most strategical Batman we've yet seen on screen. Cavill, as I thought in Man of Steel, is physically the perfect manifestation of Superman I've seen. I know this point is silly, but he should've definitely smiled a bit more or at least not had such a depressed/angry demeanor throughout the entirety of the movie. My only critique to his character.

Now for my disappointments. It all started with Clark Kent screaming "Martha!" I feel the point could've been made by simply telling Batman that Lex has his mother. The impact would've been the same as Bruce knows what it's like to lose his parents.

I didn't like the portrayal of Lex Luthor by Jesse Eisenberg. I love Jesse Eisenberg, don't get me wrong, but Kevin Spacey still holds the top spot in my opinion for best Lex Luthor depiction. I always imagined Lex Luthor as either the same age or quite a bit older than Clark and this seemed a much younger foe who aimlessly wanted to create conflict between Batman and Superman for the purpose of...? If his intent was to create Doomsday in the first place, why did he not just continue to secretly perfect him and then unleash him when the time was ready? I think Eisenberg's portrayal of Lex was a tad bit too high strung and hipster for my liking. Perhaps if he were bald from the beginning with a laid-back, calm and collected disposition I could've seen him as an intellectually equal foe to Batman and Superman but he comes across as childish and maniacal more so than a genius capable of bringing down arguably the two greatest heroes of comic book history.

To add to that, Batman and Superman's conflict honestly could've evolved on its own with no outside help from Lex Luthor. There was really no need for Lex's interference and he put himself on the map when, again, he could've been secretly perfecting his Doomsday plans, etc. Also, Doomsday came and went all too quickly. If he were going to be in the movie only to be destroyed, which I would've hoped he would be a Justice League foe, then he should've been introduced earlier. His appearance seemed very thrown together and rushed. It was sort of how Venom, one of Spiderman's greatest foes, just all of a sudden popped up in Spiderman 3 and was gone after about 20 minutes of screen time. In fact, I think they spent more time fighting Doomsday than they did fighting each other, which is kind of what everybody came to see.

It was overall a great movie. I just think it could've done better. I'd say the first 2/3rds of the movie was fantastic and then the last 1/3rd was just...eh. I don't think this by any means signals the death of the DCEU or has any bearing on future successes but it definitely could've been better. I'm still very pumped to see Suicide Squad and hopefully, Justice League will make amends and fill the void in the places lacking in Batman v Superman.

title: Superman V Batman.
review:
Talking to a family friend about them having seen Captain America: Civil War,I was surprised to hear,that despite only buying Marvel Comics,that they actually preferred the DC movie to the Marvel one.Putting my memories of the "mixed" reaction it got to one side,I got set to see the DC heroes take on each other.

The plot:

After leaving an entire city to waste,Superman is seen as a danger to mankind.Spending his life protecting the people, Bruce Wayne / Batman fears that Superman is a serious threat to the people.Learning of Bruce Wayne's feelings on Superman,Clark Kent/Superman starts to suspect that Wayne might be some kind of threat to his unknown superhero.Failing to get permission to import kryptonite,business man Lex Luthor starts making plans to make Batman and Superman fight to the death.

View on the film:

Putting their two biggest superheroes against each other,the screenplay by Chris Terrio & David S. Goyer finds the spectacle,but fails to locate the purpose of their heroes existence. Giving the duo monstrous baddies and tangled nightmares,the writers give Batman and Superman a vast canvas to flex their action muscles,whilst the movements for their motives remain vague,which goes from Lex Luthor's master plans feeling like the writers made it up as they went along,Superman switching from being seen as a villain to a hero in the blink of an eye,to the excuse used to get the heroes on the same side being hilariously poor.

Toning down his slo-mo trademark,director Zack Snyder and 300/Watchmen cinematographer Larry Fong give the action scenes a mighty crunch,by splashing a vast array of smashed buildings and fire across the ring.Aiming to keep the DC stars grounded,Snyder and Fong soak the film in earthy grey and brown.Although this style does give the fight scenes a good thump,it also takes the shine off its main stars,due to the dour,washed-out colours smashing any shining light of heroism to the ground.

Logging on as the main baddie, Jesse Eisenberg gives a grating performance as Lex Luthor,a character whose annoying tics and "quirky" manner make the "big bad" look like a dazed and confused Mark Zuckerberg.Kept on the side lines for most of the movie, Gal Gadot grips every scene she is in as Wonder Women,with Gadot striking the perfect balance of giving Wonder Women a tough action skin,whilst keeping her wrapped in a mythical superhero flame. Showing that he is not just the bomb in Phantoms Yo, Ben Affleck gives a terrific performance as Batman,thanks to Affleck grinding a rustic gravitas in Batman,as Bruce Wayne and Clark Kent face the dawn of justice.

title: The movie that met fan expectations, but left us wanting more.
review:
Batman v Superman was at best a messy but firm installment that is meant to set up the DC Extended Universe; however, at worst it can be considered a movie that doomed the Extended Universe. Here's why:

The crew: This movie was destined to be a powerhouse from the start. Not only did it have many Academy Awards winner but it also had comic book movie veterans. Zach Snyder, the critically acclaimed director of another comic book movie "Watchmen", helmed this movie with a good mindset. The pacing of the movie is, I dare say, trash but the action sequences and story was average for a comic book movie. The actors were spot on and gave worthy performances but there was one that stuck out like a sore thumb: Jesse Eisenberg. The problem with him was The Diabolical Lex Luthor

he was not the right person to play the character in the first place. Don't get me wrong, I love his work, it's just that there were so many others actor that could have played the character better. The reason for this is because Lex Luthor, the character the Eisenberg plays, is not a crazy maniac. He is a sleazy business man that will do anything to get his way. The comparison is like Steve Jobs to Heath Ledger's Joker. That is my main complaint about the actors. One thing I loved was Ben Affleck's performance as Batman. He nailed both Bruce Wayne and Batman and is really getting me excited for his solo movie.

The plot: The plot of almost every superhero movie is it's kryptonite (see what I did there) and this movie is no exception. The pacing and shortness of the scenes that don't have any action only damages the plot. There is also way to much lead up to the main action because there are so many minor subplots. The problem with multiple hero comic book movies

is that the plot has to accommodate to each character's subplot equally, which gives the audience what seems like 3 different movies going at once.Overall the sequences in this movie seems to jump from one different theme to another which explains the pacing problem. The plot is average at best but it's nothing compared to the crazy, but predictable action sequences.

The action: Like all blockbuster action movies with big budget the movies tend to go beyond what is necessary and realistic when it comes to action. For example, when you see one giant super powered being going toe to toe with another super powered being you've really seen them all. The logical course for a huge movie like this one is to invent new concepts that will dazzle (i.e. Deadpool) the audience enough that they will keep coming back to the theaters to watch the movies; however, this movie does the opposite.

.

Greatest Batman Ever!

It gives the audience the same action that we have seen dozens of times, completely goes over the top with almost every action sequence, and really makes you questions why it is worth spending 12-20 dollars seeing it on a big screen. I'll be the first to admit that I wasn't yawning throughout the entire movie but come on guys, give us something we haven't seen over a dozen times. One good action sequence that I especially enjoyed, however, is the Batman action sequences. This is another reason I am excited for the next solo Batman movie.

All in all, the movie is a dull addition to the overgrowing roster of superhero movies but I can only hope that the DC Extended Universe movies will only get better.

title: A decent effort, but not the great film I wanted.
review:
*Warning – Mild spoiler alert (Nothing that wasn't in the trailer though)

Having sat back and watched this film get savaged upon release by critics, and succeed exponentially at the box office, I finally had the opportunity to see one of this year's most anticipated releases. Directed by Man of Steel helmsman Zack Snyder the film chronicles the ideological battle between two of the most famous superheroes in the world, Batman and Superman.

It's been 18 months since the events of Man of Steel when Superman (Henry Cavill) pretty much totalled Metropolis in his fight against General Zod. Turns out Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) was there that day, and horrified by the destruction of Superman's altercation with his fellow alien Batman has made it his mission to find and "immobolize" this threat.

Superman has always been a difficult character to translate to screen. His earnest morality makes him troublesome to adapt to complex story lines, especially in a realistic setting such as Snyder's Metropolis. Cavill does his best to create a compelling character but I don't feel the script gives him much to work with and his arc seems repetitive and dull. He never seems to develop, and his characterisation is caught between his morality and Snyder's attempts to create a grittier Superman, resulting in an unclear blandness. On the other hand Affleck's portrayal of Bruce Wayne as a paranoid, grief stricken man on the edge is much more decisive and interesting. Snyder's tenacious, visceral; imagery seems to mesh better with Batman's naturally darker inclinations. This moulded with Affleck's Batman, who seems like he has worn the mask for so long it has clouded his morality and corrupted his judgement, is one of the films strongest aspects. I wouldn't call him the definitive Batman, yet, as Keaton, Bale and Conroy have all delivered interesting portrayals of the character in the past, but it's a very strong start. Jeremy Irons is effortlessly brilliant as Alfred, however his screen time is unjustly limited, while Jesse Eisenberg's in full scenery feasting mode as a megalomaniacal Lex Luthor. Unlike some I wasn't as irritated by Eisenberg's performance and I felt his motivations were one of the clearer threads in an otherwise tangled narrative. Amy Adam's doesn't have an opportunity to do much as Lois Lane, again not her fault, whilst Gal Gadot's small role as Wonder Woman was understandably enigmatic, but I am interested in seeing her in a starring role next year.

The film's opening two acts are quite strong, with the occasional foible, but things start to unravel following a rather underwhelming brawl between the two eponymous superheroes. The last act is a bloated mess, rather than a satisfying resolution. Superman's ultimate weakness in the film isn't kryptonite but just being boring. The film has to cobble together some giant creature (Yes I know he's Doomsday) for Superman to have an opponent who can match him, whilst Batman stands behind a wall shooting an occasional grenade like a renegade member of the Gotham SWAT team. The films best action sequence? It's not Batman v Superman, or the Doomsday fight. It's when Batman takes on a group of about thirty men in a warehouse. It's visceral, brilliantly choreographed, and one of the best directed sequences of the film. The character feels vulnerable, the hits feel real, and if Superman took on thirty guys in a warehouse it would be incredibly boring because he could do it without trying.

The film has an impressive style, and I think there are some promising signs in the future for the DC cinematic universe, but Batman v Superman does lack clarity and vision. The ideological battle of the two leads is discarded in favour of shoe horning in a CGI knock off of a LOTR cave troll for Superman, and Wonder Woman to duke it out with, whilst Batman occasionally swoops by on a grappling hook. The final act is a let-down, and may be why the film has received a generally negative reception, but the work up to that point was nicely constructed and investing enough to keep me interested for the future of the Justice League.

Review by Alex Halsall.

title: DC Strikes back?
review:
Warning - this review contains spoilers.

So we have had the latest superhero movie, this time from the DC universe.

Batman V Superman:Dawn of Justice is the start of what DC hopes will put them on the same footing as the current Marvel universe. DC comics began in the late 1930's featuring Batman as a detective outside of the law. This proved a success and other characters started to be introduced in their own spaces. Soon we had Superman, the man of steel from another planet.

In 1960, DC brought together its core of characters as the Justice League. This team consisted of Aquaman, Batman, the Flash, Green Lantern, the Martian Manhunter, Superman, and Wonder Woman. The comics were a success and in turn prompted Marvel to bring together its own team, the Avengers.

Moving forward to the digital age and the dawn of the superhero movie. For the past few years we have been treated to the carefully planned building of Marvel's team and it has been a stunning success. There are back stories, each major character having its own movie working towards the Avengers.

DC must have realised the success was something they had to follow. They had a number of poor reviews for some of their films, including the Green Lantern and Superman Returns. One film barely recovered its production costs, so DC had to come up with a new blockbuster.

Bringing together its core characters and introducing the non DC public to the Justice League was a clear option.

There is now an art to selling a movie to the public. Fans of whatever it might will clearly split into two camps; the hoping its great and the worried it's going to fail (again). For myself, being a Marvel fan, I was honestly hoping for a good movie to push Marvel to be better.

Batman V Superman had the right selling points, it looked good and it appeared brilliant. The trailers gave all the teasers. I don't often give spoilers about any new movie as a rule. My reviews tend to just review. However, I do want to comment about what I feel are the differences between the two universes.

This movie opens once more with how Bruce Wayne becomes Batman. Why? Do people forget this every time the last movie ends? Yet nothing on Superman. There is a darkness to this as there appears to be with many DC movies. Some of it is good, some is over played. We sort of recap the end of Man of Steel using it to feed into this movie. It is a clever idea but it takes a bit too long to get going. The movie drags from the starts. It has stunning visual effects, yet there was little noticeable music. I am not sure I could place any themes anywhere, was that good or bad?

The story itself is disjointed, while Batman was torturing bad guys looking for a certain someone, Superman was being setup. Bruce Wayne was also 'unhappy' at the destruction Superman caused yet being hailed a hero. It seemed to annoy him. Clark Kent for his part did not seem to like the vigilante dispensing justice. Yet both of them were doing something of a similar role. Plot hole? That is one of many but all films have them. It seems to me that the DC executives have watched so many other versions of Big X V Big Y and thought that's our movie!

Yet they have forgotten to build in the sub-elements of the plot. Batman uses guns, not just to scare but kill and he has dreams of killing. Superman appears bored almost trying to recoup his mantel in human eyes by saving a few people. He fails in a couple of places. Then there is Lex Luther. An attempt at a psychotic, match-maker who helps telegraph the plot in stunning fashion. That is one of the biggest disappointments of this movie. Not only are some elements telegraphed, they are pounded out time and time again.

The plot device to make the two fight is weak, how did Luther find out about a secret that no one else could find, Superman's mum. Did I miss that?

How did Batman know that Luther was planning to get Superman to make the two fight?

How did a supposed alien spaceship who clearly says you can't make this alien, let an alien make a bigger badder alien?

One good point (I think) was the introduction of Wonder Woman. However no back story unlike how Marvel handle the main characters. She just appears, trying to keep a photo private that shows her to a whole bunch of people while she is in costume. She seems to have half the powers of Superman with the strength of Batman and more brains. There is also the brief flash (pardon the pun) of Flash, Cyborg and Aquaman without knowing who they are. Lex however seems to know it all, maybe he read the comics.

The film is way over 2 hours, it dragged for me. There are times when you think they should have expanded on that point, explained more yet they miss it. Somehow DC keep missing the mark in the movie universe but in the TV they have the edge. As I said before, Green Lantern was an almost movie, Man of Steel lost the end and Superman sort of returned. There is no humour in this film and it lacks a little humanity for me. There are so many words one could describe this film and it has been by many both 'professional' critics and fans alike.

My rating for this movie is 6 out 10.

title: Psycho v God
review:
This isn't a review per se. I'll only attempt to communicate the feelings I had upon watching BvS. Seen the movie twice and there are times now that I find myself getting excited to watch Superman_and_Batman on the big screen together,..moments,..like this movie never happened..I'm not saying I wish it didn't happen -yet- I'm saying it was so shallow and unsatisfying,..all the anticipation and expectation built over the last three years has nowhere to go now..Batman had his time with a great classical and modern take..Being the lifelong Superman fan I am,I thought this might have given us that modern Superman we were all aching to see after Nolan's Batman..Then came Snyder..One might say that 'modern Superman' was Man of Steel..No,it wasn't,MoS was a nice sci-fi action movie featuring Superman,it was not a Superman movie..But MoS was a complete narrative,a whole movie;..BvS often feels like a mashup of several clips,or like a very long music video.

There are two main problems with Snyder and his DCU,first is all about himself;..he isn't a storyteller. I've no idea what his process is but I believe he visualizes every frame of the movie when reading a script then he jumps on to create those frames in front of the camera without giving any consideration to the narrative or performance..On the bts photos I saw,he is always looking through a lens as he's directing,..no doubt,..he has great talent in composing beautiful frames with great cinematography;..but movies aren't photography exhibitions,they are stories..Great story and characters can save bad looking films in terms of cinematography(Avengers)but great cinematography doesn't make a movie if your story cannot convey emotion...Obviously,Snyder is smart enough to realize his shortcomings and employs talented individuals around him to compensate,especially in big movies,and once he does I believe he turns his whole focus on the visuals,doesn't think of the other aspects as he already assigned them to others.

The second big problem with DCU;..others aren't as good as Snyder thinks..Nolan may be gracious enough to give DavidGoyer writing credit,..but looking closely at the 'making of'of that trilogy,Goyer is merely there as a comicbook consultant..Then we have ChrisTerrio who wrote Oscar winning Argo,great writer,not a comicbook man and I believe Terrio took over the script after Goyer left so there wasn't one talented comicbook man in the cooking room..Of course there's always the possibility that Terrio wrote a great script but all the story moments were scrapped in favor of action visuals.

Then there's HenryCavill,..carbon copy of the comic book character...He is physically Superman but Cavill isn't a very talented actor, he is not so bad that his performance takes you out of the movie but he is nowhere near his co-stars...Great actors can give great performances even with bad direction,not-so-great actors need direction which Snyder only provides behind a telephoto lens I assume..Its not possible to fault Henry too much though;..I think only directions they gave him are..'look like God'..and..'look tough'..I'm %100 sure Henry speaks more words in any 2minute Youtube interview than BvS in its entirety..Snyder's Superman has no character..In their quest to make him relatable first they made him a greenhorn who doesn't know what he is supposed to do in MoS,then when it came to the actual 'formed' character in BvS they decided to turn him into God,a passive,narcissist God at that.

It's baffling how people cannot understand Superman so I'll provide an analogy to explain him..Every one of us probably has a friend who we trust and count on,one person who we know -even if we do not admit to ourselves- is better than ourselves, always trying to help us and others, selfless..I'm not saying this friend is perfect, he may have his own flaws, he may get fed up helping,but he does it anyway,because he is a good guy, a best friend...Superman is that friend, but not only for you or me, for everyone..Snyder might say "Yeah but we can't make an all good character,that's boring",yes that's boring,.I'm not saying you build a two dimensional character that you only see when he is saving people,that wouldn't have much more depth than Henry's Superman who we only see when he is watching people from above...I'm saying that's what Superman does, without changing that-essence of the character-its possible to add hundreds of different character traits..You want him more relatable? Focus on the psychological aspects of the immense responsibility he has when he is saving people, he can't save everyone -he's not God Zack- tries to make the best choice,may obsess over other possible ways even when he makes the best choice.Many inner conflict stories can be drawn from that 'responsibility' theme that can fill a NickCassavetes drama...I read Snyder saying"People cling on Reeve's version but the real source character's from comicbook"..Hey Zack,..those filmmakers didn't pull Superman the Movie out of their bottom,..they just understood the character from those comics..That's why Reeve is still most fans' Superman,..because he was able to embody that 'friend'.

A director only concerned with visuals,a leading man without any lines and 100different story lines from comics crammed into one script..This is what we get for the meeting of two greatest characters of modern history on the big screen.

Oh,nearly forgot...Batman.Greatest detective and ninja,one of the smartest people on the planet..Despises guns because his parents were killed by one and even if he knows killing might be the best option sometimes,he never does it because he is always afraid if he crosses that line,he would become one of the criminals he fights so hard to clean Gotham from..Snyder's Bat shoots guns(dream or not)his car has a machine gun,kills people in cold blood(port chase)and gets manipulated by Lex(who himself doesn't show any sign of intelligence)into fighting with God..And also you can shut this psycho Batman down by saying 'Martha'..How do you mess Batman up too?..Hasn't even been 4years since they explained who he is amazingly well..At least we have those for Batman though.

Anyway. Thanks Zack! Good action.

title: Although flawed, BvS delivers plenty of action and excitement to satisfy fans
review:
Okay, I'll admit, at first I was skeptical, but after seeing the film yesterday I've got to say; the film isn't nearly as bad as the critics make it out to be. Sure, the film isn't perfect and there are definitely many flaws and plot holes but the positives outweigh the bad. Does the film live up to all the hype? Probably not, but there is enough action and excitement to satisfy fans.

One of the biggest issues I had with the film was the writing and pacing. The story was filled with too many subplots and too many characters were squeezed into the narrative for the sole purpose of building up excitement for the future 'Justice League' film. The pacing was slow and many of the plot lines were either dragged out or unnecessarily long. Although it is a very compelling and complex story, it could've easily be done in a shorter amount of time without the unnecessary characters and subplots. The editing was a bit of a mess but despite the sloppy editing and writing, the film is saved by the stunning visuals and action sequences, one of the many highlights of the film. The action sequences definitely lived up to its expectations, even if the anticipated fight between Batman and Superman lasted for a mere five minutes. Personally, I would've preferred if the focus of the story was on the conflict between Batman and Superman instead of a complex, overly-long introduction to the Justice League. Although I felt the addition of Wonder Woman was forced and unnecessary to the plot, Gal Gadot did deliver a lot of charisma and charm to the role and it was nice to see the character make her big-screen debut. The story, I believe, had a lot of potential, unfortunately, it wasn't well-executed and could've been better.

I thoroughly enjoyed Ben Affleck's rendition of Batman and I've got to say, he's the best on-screen Batman to date, hands-down. Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Lex Luthor, however, was a bit over-acted and felt like an impersonation of Heath Ledger's Joker from 'The Dark Knight'. Unfortunately, the popular villain was miscast. Jeremy Irons also steps into the role of Alfred and gives us a new rendition of the character that differs from previous on-screen portrayals in a positive way. Many of the cast members from the film's predecessor 'Man of Steel' return and although they put on good performances, they appear quite bland and perhaps under better direction and a well-written script, could put more life into the iconic roles.

The Batsuit worn by Affleck heavily resembles the one in Frank Miller's 'The Dark Knight Returns' and is a lot closer to the comics than previous adaptations. It feels as though you're watching the Arkham games, one of the things I admired about the film. There are some people whining about how Batman isn't supposed to kill people, but word has it that in the earlier comics, Batman killed criminals all the time. Thing is, this rendition of Batman differs from previous on-screen renditions of Batman, which I believe is a good thing as it gives us a fresh and intriguing take on the character.

Critics complained that the film was too 'dark' and 'gritty' and that it was 'humorless'. Well, sorry to burst your bubble but this isn't Marvel. It's not meant to be funny. It's not meant to be humorous. If anything, the darkness and grittiness support the film's atmosphere and narrative. It wouldn't have worked well with too much humor. If you want 'funny', then I suggest you watch the 1960s Adam West series or Joel Schumacher's 'Batman & Robin'.

Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed the film and thought it was a vast improvement over 'Man of Steel'. Although not great, I definitely recommend the film to fans and anyone with an open mind. Just don't see the film with high expectations because you may leave the theater feeling disappointed. Just enjoy the film for what it is.

My rating: 6/10

title: BvS: Beautiful and fun, but brought down by hype and empty plot
review:
Ever since 2013 when this movie was announced, people, including me, have been waiting for this one movie to come out. With trailers, news, and TV spots, the comic book audience was hyped up, ready to witness the beautiful hero versus hero sold in the marketing. Of course, if you were part of this very large group, you already know the pain of anticipation. So without further ado, here is one of the many reviews of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice.

Eighteen months after the events seen in Man of Steel, BvS is connected to MOS very well with an amazing scene connecting the stories of Bruce Wayne and Superman together. Zack Snyder addresses the controversy of Superman's battle with Zod by setting the viewer into Bruce Wayne's story during the time. However, after that scene, the lead up to the fight between Batman and Superman is way too complicated and prolonged. The two stories of Batman and Superman feel like two different movies that got edited together into the same movie. Like many people, I was waiting for the connection between the two to be mind-blowing and amazing. However, the connection was very anti-climatic and once it came, the fight was just thrown into the movie. The story behind "the greatest gladiator match in the history of the world" lacks charm and attractiveness, heavily bringing down the movie's plot and mood. However, given that this movie's storyline was more fit for a darker mood like it had in MOS, BvS gives heed to a more dismal cinematic universe, compared to the bright lights of the MCU.

After the heavily dragging lead into the fight, the fans finally get what they want: Batman versus Superman. What the trailers, TV spots, and anticipation fed them a sample of had now come to the big screen. Let me just say that what they had been fed with for years had really paid off. For I experienced the most spectacular fight between the two. Between Superman's underestimation of his opponent and Batman's ruthlessness, the two go at each other in a striking performance of pure action and excitement. However, one downside to the fight is that Superman never really feels fully engaged into the fight and more into fighting Luthor. Obviously, this had to be so because of the way that the plot was driven, which was to see Luthor as the enemy and not the two at each other. (Also, I find that Lex Luthor's reason for making them fight was very lacking and didn't show as a master plan as it should have). However, as the trailers had sold, I was let down by the amount of hatred for each other and instead felt a Superman calming down his younger brother Batman's tantrum. So, yes, the fight was well coordinated and aggressive, but it never felt aimed towards each other, but to someone else. While the art of fighting each other may have been beautiful, without pure reason of anger, the entire fight feels useless and just something to fish audiences into something a lot less amazing.

In my opinion, this movie's strongest point is it's action sequences, particularly the warehouse scene. The scene is just so Batman. It relates closely to the brutal fighting of the Arkham video games and the slender, fluid movements in the comics. The entire scene shows the hard of the entire crew and how much they put into making that scene. As awesome as it was to have Batman shred through that warehouse, I think letting Superman ripping apart the building and take out Martha would have been more logical and time-efficient.

One of the main things that people are talking about is Affleck as Batman. Personally, it's great to finally have a gritty Batman not new to the game, as most previous movies have shown the story of an angry Bruce Wayne wearing the suit of the caped crusader for the first time. The madness shown in his eyes, the old hatred towards criminals, and the feeling that Bruce's hope of a pure city of righteousness and justice is slowly fading away. This part is especially shown when Superman is shouting Martha's name and Batman shouts back, "Who's Martha?!" To me, this shows his madness and his insanity from the battle he's been through for years. Affleck offers these dark characteristics to the audience, something that none of the past portrayals have shown before. However, for a graphic Batman to be portrayed well, there has to be a fine line between Batman and a Batman that kills. Unfortunately, Zack Snyder crosses this line with the use of murder and guns. Even if Batman is killing people with a gun, this lacks the image of Batman and his desire for justice because of his desire to kill in a dream. Overall, I liked Affleck's performance because it gave a view into a differently darker Batman, but also straying away from the classic symbol.

Every scene that Wonder Woman was in gave me hope. It gave me hope that next year and the years to come, there will be an amazing universe led by portrayals like this. Gal Gadot's performance completely stole the show, and her final fight scene with Doomsday was phenomenal. The teases to other Justice League characters is also led well into the movie and soon into bigger appearances. Obviously, Superman's fate is going to play a key role in the Justice League movies, which led to the Flash's warning to Bruce.

Overall, Batman v Superman was a fun, good movie to watch, led highly by its effects and action, but falling short on plot. I think this was mainly a result of over anticipation, but it is a good lead into future DCEU films.

title: Dawn of Justice: Love, Labour, Lost (Spoiler Riddled Late Review)
review:
OK, got it off my chest finally. This is my late review of the film Batman V Superman. Before going to this movie, I had ample share of comments from friends who had watched it. Some of them were not well versed with the DC universe so I decided not to make up my mind until I've seen it myself. Even paused every video review that said there were spoilers and graciously left a comment telling – would revisit after watching the movie. One thing that bugged me was the massive difference between the critics rating and the fan rating. Well, It doesn't anymore. I see where the critics saw the fault in this movie.. Yes DC fan boys (of whom I consider myself to be one) Batman V Superman is a flawed movie and it pains me to say that. I'll have to live with the TV shows.

There are a few promises of future goodness in the franchise but unless there is a great deal of improvement in the next installment, the justice league will have challenges winning over the moviegoers. For the most part I agree with the points made by Bobby Burns in his review video. The character development is certainly compromised. Moreover, in an attempt to reinvent the superheroes, a lot of what make these characters great, disappeared. Also as a consequence the storytelling got jumbled. Just hiding Easter eggs is not enough. For example, we see an old timey picture of Wonder woman standing next to Steve Trevor. We know its a set up for the WW standalone movie but would I be interested enough to see her origin story, now that I've seen her enough and didn't get excited about her?
