title: It really isn't bad
review:
I wouldn't say it's very good, but it certainly ain't bad, as you might have thought if you read the critics reviews.

Yes, first half of the movie is full of scenes lasting less than a minute. That makes it look like a very long trailer. Which it kind of is: trailer for the DC "cinematic universe". There is way too much they wanted to "say" in that first half. The other option would be for someone to tell it, but in that case critics would jump and say "show, don't tell". It could have been done better, but, it's not done bad. The story itself is actually OK. I don't get why someone would say there is no story here.

The second half is basically a couple of big fights, which are OK. I mean, it's a super-hero fight, of course it's silly and defies logic and physics, but, it looks OK.

Yes, it's not funny. About the only joke is the "I thought she was with you", which you probably saw in the trailers. But, that was the intention. You may not like that, but you can't say it's bad just because it's not funny.

Compared to the critics' darling "Star Wars: The Force Awakens", I see one big difference that makes this a better movie: its pivotal moment actually works. While Han Solo dying feels forced, predictable and artificial, making no emotional impact, the pivotal moment here works. Maybe because Amy Adams does a very good job of playing her part in the moment. Even though it is predictable, it doesn't feel forced or artificial and does make an emotional impact. There are other things that make this a better movie, but this is the most important one.

Other than that, acting isn't very good, except for Amy Adams. Gal Gadot pretty much doesn't act but walks around to show that she trained hard for many months (which is fine by me, of course, but it's not acting). Jeremy Irons and Laurence Fishburne simply don't have enough screen time. Batman and Superman try hard to do their job. They don't do it very well, but not bad either, which can also be said for everybody else involved.

title: Overall a disappointment for what she be the greatest film in history
review:
It has taken me a little bit of thought to finally just mark my review of this film and get my thoughts about it and put them into words. Batman v Superman should of been a film I loved, but instead it was film that I kind of liked but not really because it had all of these big glaring issues. These issues aren't like with Star Wars: The Force Awakens were I could easily brush them off and say the film overall worked.

No!

These are really major issues. From top to bottom. There are writers and directors who can do a million things in a movie and make them all fit and work in a really good way. Films such as "The Avengers," "Serenity," and "Age of Ultron." All where films that had to balance a lot of story and managed to do it in a fun and engaging way.

However Zack Snyder can't do that. Yes he did it sort of with Watchmen, but that was just right off the comic book page type of film with already and story built in. Batman v Superman is basically a original idea that takes from a million comic book storyline, and tries to mash them all together why also being both a Superman and Batman movie while also being a build up to Justice League. And Snyder just can't balance it all in this film.

But even bigger than that the issue this film really had was changing the motivation for the fight. I won't spoil it, but let me tell you it is one of the dumbest things that this movie did and it just failed on every level.

Jeese Eisenberg as Lex Luthor also turned me off big time. In the trailers I liked his lines because they were good lines and very symbolic, but the way he delivered them made him seem like a silly mad man over a human being. He seemed just psychotic all the way around, and I hate a Lex Luthor who is like that.

Now that all my anger towards this film is gone let me talk about why I am still able to give this film a fresh score in the end.

Although this isn't a story Snyder, David Goyer and Chris Terrio weren't able to balance it is still a stunning film you gotta see. I love Snyder's films. All of them and while this may be his weakest one there is still some fun to be had here.

The cinematography of this film is amazing. It is just stunning. If Snyder can do anything it is how to shoot a film. Every scene you see looks like this gorgeous art painting. And it looks just great. The fights look great, the way the camera zooms when people talk is great. All around the cinematography is well done. Larry Fong should get a high pay check for managing all of this beauty. And it should be scene in Imax too. This film looks best on a Imax screen, but be prepared to be completely blown away by it as well.

The acting is actually pretty decent. With the exception of Jesse Eisenberg none of the actors really made me cringe when the spoke or made me bored. I feel like with the lines they had they all were delivered well and made for some great and powerful scenes between some of these titans.

The fight despite the poor reason for it is still a pretty fun fight. I loved watching Superman get taken down by Batman then in turn Superman tries to do the same thing with Batman. It was a pretty cool thing to see.

The nightmare sequence is probably the best part of the film. Watching a evil Superman face off with Batman and all the solders trying to capture Batman was great too see and it was just a really well done scene that I liked to watch Batman in doing battle with all these Superman lovers.

Did I mention Batman and Superman were great. Ben Affleck and Henry Cavil are both great in there roles as Batman or Superman. And deserve a lot of praise for becoming these might titans that go into battle as well.

I also didn't mind Gal Godot as Wonder Woman either, In many ways she stole the show, but I am not giving the actress to much praise till her stand alone movie. It does make it seem like there is a good chance that Wonder Woman film will be a really good film overall in moving the DC universe forward.

Overall Batman v Superman had some good in it and some bad. It should at least be as good as Star Wars, but it can't even get close. This film is just okay in many ways. I didn't leave this film hating it, but I didn't leave this film in love with it and praising it either. Still go out and see it for yourself and tell your thoughts on this film, and then perhaps you may love it or hate it, but give it a shot, and see what happens.

title: Why was Batman v Superman such a bad movie?
review:
Batman, Superman & Wonder Woman on the big screen all at once is something comic book, and everyday movie fans alike have all been waiting for. This movie will end up being a box-office success and Warner Bros. will continue moving forward with the franchise. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice overall was a fun and enjoyable movie. It gives comic-book fans exactly what they've wanted and casual moviegoers the chance to become invested. It isn't without flaw, but contrary to popular belief, the good outweighs the bad. But why are the critical reviews so negative? Ultimately because the tone is untraditional dark, the ratio of story to action was unbalanced, and most importantly, people just don't know what they want when it comes to superhero movies.

The movie begins with a civilian's view of the destructive battle scene between Superman and General Zod in 2013's Man of Steel. The viewer is then taken into Bruce Wayne's point of view watching a local Wayne Enterprise building get demolished, as he tries to save them. Early on, this movie establishes the conflict between the two titular characters, and the tone of the film. The two heroes clash while Superman's character & actions are brought into question. We see a physically and emotionally battle-scarred Batman whose sole motive is protecting everyone from the threat that is a rogue Superman. The two join sides, team up with Wonder Woman, and lay the foundation for DC's Justice League franchise.

If this were a Batman solo movie, the overall reception would be more positive because he's a character that can get away with this darker, more grounded tone that Zack Snyder decided to go with. But Superman is the boy scout of superheroes, which gives viewers a very different version of Superman. The film's dark tone gives the viewers an interesting take on the Boy in Blue. Snyder and co. made a character with unbelievably, god-like abilities more human than viewers have seen since the CW's Smallville. The dark tone however, did work for Ben Affleck's Batman.

His portrayal of the Dark Knight exceeded expectations. Every scene with Batman/Bruce Wayne is one to remember. Affleck's acting, the camera movement and cinematography coupled with Hans Zimmer's score made for a mysterious, and downright scary interpretation of Batman. An idea that could have been fleshed out more was the foiling of Batman and Superman. Snyder attempted to use Batman's savage crime fighting methods and gruesome reputation, as a way to highlight Superman's supposed-to-be wholesomeness, which fell flat. Seeing Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman brought to life was exciting, but a bit of a let down in the movie. She was fun to watch, but her portrayal fell short of expectations because it wasn't as believable as her cast mates. Her role was small, but just enough doses for us to keep interest in what's to come in her own solo movie. Wonder Woman mainly acts as the bridge from Batman to the "metahuman" world, and setting up as one of the founding members of the Justice League.

Jesse Eisenberg's Lex Luthor was interesting to watch. He brought a very different vibe to the character while still giving viewers the murderous masterminded villain that we know him to be. Like Henry Cavill's Superman, Eisenberg's Luthor is young and inexperienced in what he does. What ultimately drives Lex in this film is what has always driven him, knowledge and power. Those expecting Lex and Superman to be fully developed characters when this is the 2nd movie of a growing franchise are the one's who were let down by Dawn of Justice.

Man of Steel sparked debates that the true Superman wouldn't have fought so carelessly and end up destroying a big city, let alone kill an enemy. This Superman isn't one that fans are familiar with yet, and if Batman v Superman doesn't do anything for you, it should at least give answers as to why that route was taken. To build this hero up into one that Superman fans are conversant with. It poses the question that will linger on within these films; where do we as humans fit in this world filled with aliens and godly beings? The idea of gods amongst men and a very particular scene with Bruce Wayne teases that DC is going in the route of the video-game/comic book series story line, Injustice: Gods Among Us. Holly Hunter plays the front runner of the political subplot in the film as Senator Finch, who also, gives us the hopeful connection to Amanda Waller and the upcoming film Suicide Squad. This also gives the DC universe that grounded feeling they're trying so hard to achieve, which can be challenging when there are characters like Superman, Green Lantern, and Martian Manhunter that exists in this world. Hunter acts as the voice of reason and concern that most people would have when it comes to idea of a Superman.

A key reason people are let down is because fans and critics alike aren't sure what they wanted from this movie. People are forgetting that this isn't the seasoned Superman we know from the comics & TV shows. He's a new hero who is still unsure of himself and unsure of how he is supposed to help the world. I'm not saying this film is without flaw. There is indeed a lot going on in this film. The actual fight between Batman and Superman should have definitely lasted longer and the scenes of Aquaman, Flash, and Cyborg screams, "Hey, Justice League is coming! Look Marvel we can do it too!" The story did move a bit fast for the average person to follow. However, I saw this movie with two people with no prior knowledge and was still able to follow the movie fluently. But if you go in this movie expecting what the title promises and take it for what it is, you'll enjoy this experience.

title: It's what it's supposed to be (sort of), and that's always good in my book.
review:
Note: this is an edited review, which lowered the score by one, since I've now have a better understanding of why people seem to hate this.

Usually when I review a movie/game/book/whatever, I review it; but, this time, I will just write a simple, stream-of-consciousness-esque opinion, moments after leaving the cinema - something that I do for the first time. The reason? While I avoid almost everything that can spoil/affect my opinion, a couple of days before going to see this movie, I was surprised to see so much HATE towards it, especially from (the scum of the earth) "professional" critics, who expected Lars von Trier, and got a superhero movie instead. Is it perfect? No. Will it become an iconic classic like The Dark Knight? No. Could the plot, the acting, and the overall direction be better? Sure but a bad movie?

Read the title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice. It wasn't supposed to be a colorful, funny, and fast-paced Marvel flick it's supposed to be a clash between two gods in a far darker setting, it's supposed to have a villain who can actually trick these gods, and it's supposed to introduce the Justice League. Has this film achieve all this? HELL YEAH. In many ways it reminded me of the hate that Man of Steel received, which, to this day, I don't understand why and this comes from someone who isn't exactly very fond of Superman.

There are indeed some major flaws here, though. I won't go in detail about some, such as why Lex behaves more like Joker, or how some characters have been reduced to cardboard ones like Lois Lane, amongst others, so I'll only mention the three big ones. #1: The rivalry between Sups and Batman is insanely forced, and the way things turn around is, admittedly, silly. #2: Doomsday looks bad, and should not be here so soon. Every comic book fan know that this dude is an extremely important part of Superman's lore, so it should get its own separate movie. #3: the biggest mistake IMO is that DC tried to do a lot of things to soon it tried to pit Batman against Superman, tried to introduce the Justice League, and tried to include Doomsday.

To keep it short (too late), here is my quick rundown:

The good: fantastic music, a great, dark mood, the best action sequences in recent comic book movie history, solid-to-good acting (even from good 'ol Ben), and, finally, a decent, although, far from flawless, exploration of several themes; especially of how terrifying a "God amongst us" can be.

The bad: Batman's hate towards Superman is bit forced and silly; He should be smarter than the average Joe. Wonder Woman was cool, but her inclusion felt a bit forced. Doomsday should be 10 times more threatening - even general Zod and his team felt like far better team of villains.

In conclusion: Not bad, not fantastic, and not mediocre but, undoubtedly a very entertaining superhero movie, despite its MANY shortcomings.

title: The title and the story.
review: Batman Vs Superman. Man Vs God. Or as Lex Luthor puts it in every possible comparison to highlight how massively epic this whole fight is to be.The hopes of fan boys and enthusiasts alike have been instantly shot up to an ethereal level expecting to have see how DC follows up to establish their universe as well as how two of the most iconic characters from the paper world scale on to the big screens.DC have got some recent success on the big screen post Nolan and Man of steel, so take a shot at establishing the universe.But here lies the little trouble, One of the titular characters in the movie hasn't got an origin story yet to establish what kind of attributes his version of the character has. Sure,there is a back-story in bits and pieces, but yet it's definitely not sufficient enough to live up to the first half of the title of movie.Affleck's Bat is good and capable in the way Synder intended to.In fact he is the silver lining here and puts his best foot forward for his take of this icon, but then since the origin story isn't large enough to get the audience established to this Bat it seems like much is amiss somewhere.It's more Dawn of Trinity than Dawn of Justice. So neither does the second half of the title stand apt.Gal Gadot illuminates the screen like Wonder Woman is supposed to and the fight between her character and Doomsday is actually more memorable than the Titular fight.Eisenberg's Lex is very confusing,as at times his psychotic anger doesn't seem to get along with the e billionaire thing.Rest of the members aren't introduced much and are in cameos, which actually makes it more interesting to anticipate their origin stories especially The Flash.Jeremy's Alfred is surely more Jarvis,if ever Jarvis was an 60 odd butler with a great voice.Adams does the typical "Lola" as she is from Man of steel being the Damsel in distress.Just to specify how important her love to Supes is and how important it is to him.Obviously that has sidetracked how Superman saves the rest of the world or he does his job as his alter ego.The story seems to going the "Injustice" comic way for now and it is not bad.But the execution could have hopefully been a bit more rapid and hard hitting. Just the cross-fit Batman, Synder intended to.CGI gets a little fazed out a bit at a few scenes, like the team was really exhausted whilst making that.Finally Cavill as Superman carries his Man of steel act and doesn't stand out much at places, which is actually a good thing because that spares us some time to understand the rest of the characters a bit more. BvS isn't a bad movie.But then it isn't as great as it was expected.Or maybe it was just the hype.It should have come after having at least a Batman origin movie like MoS,even possible a Wonder Woman one. Basically it is large teaser to what is coming in the DC universe and also ends in a "first book in the series" style.Imagine to go and watch the greatest fight between two gladiators, like Ali Vs Tyson, the only problem being here, is that you don't know,that well who one of them is.

title: umm....not that bad, yo!
review:
Okay, okay.....we already have a lifetime of negative reviews for this movie so I'm going to play the contrarian here and say it wasn't as bad as all that and in some ways, even a decent film. The thing I think we should all consider is that your characters in this flick are rather unique interpretations of extremely familiar , iconic entities and I think thats what makes it all so jarring when they don't act the way we think they should. Don't get me wrong, some elements did feel really off but generally if you go into this thing thinking "Snyderverse" Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, etc. it goes down a heck of a lot easier for both fanboys and casual viewers, I think. What- Supes can't be a depressed jerkass? He has as much right to as any of us, maybe more. Bats can't be an aggressive self-righteous sociopath with trust issues after all he's been through? Wonder Woman can't be....Awesome? My Theory is that what this film is trying to do can be encapsulated in the infamous "Martha" scene: Its trying to show us how human our heroes are! Superman is an alien who could hurl the Chrysler building into the sun but he also has a MOM! He is one of us. So is Batman. So is Lex. So is Doom....wait, no, never mind. Anyway it all comes off pretty ham-fisted but I'm actually kind of okay with that.

Anyway I'm gonna make a bold move and say that I think most of us already know Batmans origin so I will take off points for that because I've seen enough of his dying parents to have my own recurring PTSD nightmares about that particular aspect of Bruce Waynes life plus can you say filler? My goodness! PLEASE STOP SHOOTING BRUCE WAYNES PARENTS! I'm afraid to go to the movies now! Who the @#%# shoots two people leaving the movies on what, a busy Saturday night? What the fudge? We all know it happened! Perry White said it best...and in other news...water is wet!

Alright,alright, look.....The title fight was awesome as far as I'm concerned and lasted about as long as it should have in my opinion, plus it went the way ummm.....50% of you guys wanted it to so there's that. All in all I guess I would say that it feels maybe like it could have been maybe 30-45 minutes shorter and probably was before Joe Movie exec decided we should:

(a) Be spoonfed a bunch of stuff we should already know from like everything ever made containing even a passing reference to the origins of arguably the two most popular characters in the history of comics without actually adding anything new to said origin stories (They actually could have just lifted BMs from just about any BatMan movie- just the way it was and dropped it right there in the film.Coulda used a scene from Gotham even. Bruces parents deaths must be the most filmed scene ever!They may as well have him get bitten by a radioactive spider, too)

(b) Have Lex be Sort of Lex, The Joker plus Riddler plus sorta Pengunish, if you think about it , sprinkled it with some Bond villain Lets have a side of Ozymondias as well.....Willy Wonka...The Mad Hatter....Then let him smoke crack? Like Amadeus Cho meets Woody Harrelson hooked up to a car battery or something like that but with a Doctor Whovian Monologue powered character shield.....SNYDER!WHY! Why not just have him be smart, evil and hate supes.....What was all that crap? I mean, okay, you can be all "lets try this out" without keeping it! Was that like the last roll of film you had? I bet it looked great live.

(C)Stick the post credits scene in the middle of the @W#$%#$% Movie!Go ahead, naw, it'll go over really well when , you know, yeah...nothing happens.

(d)Have everybody do it for the evulz? Like seriously, this only make sense sometimes if they really are doing it for the evulz

(e)Find out the answer to the question "Why don't you just shoot him?" (Which I thought we already knew.)Then answer that question by not asking it at all...hmmmm

(f) All of you. Lets stretch this bad boy out to 151 minutes!

(g) Make Lois Lane into Carl Grimes

So, in closing Most of what Batman does on a certain level makes complete sense if you factor in that he's actually "Snyder-Bat" and Most of what "Snyder-Supes"(cough-Sentry-cough!) does makes sense in that context as well . Aside from it being maybe (totally) a little a lot!) too long it was worth a movie ticket. Batman fought Superman. Who cares why or how really? Still better than any transformers flick, right? Nerd rage aside, I really can't fault this movie for trying to be its own thing but I can fault it for essentially being an epic youtube video once all the filler is taken out. Affleck was not as bad as I thought he would be (impossible to be that bad, I'm sure) and actually pulled it off pretty good. I feel like too many of the reviews here were written too soon after seeing the movie-It may age better than you think.

title: Not the greatest superhero movie ever but I felt very satisfied with this film as three of the greatest superheroes team up in their first movie together.
review: I think film critics and even some fan boys/fan girls were to hard on this movie. I've read/heard a lot of people say it's another Zack Snyder movie full of overblown action and sloppy storytelling. However I felt it was the exact opposite. I thought the story was well told and not as much action as I thought it would be. I didn't walk out the theatre feeling that it was the greatest superhero movie ever but I walked out feeling very satisfied with what I saw. However I the biggest problem with the movie was it's story. It was a lot more complicated then it needed be and at times it felt too confusing and a lot of things were not well explained.. I thought it did a really good job fitting all these characters in one movie. Batman, superman, wonder woman, Lex Luthor and Lois Lane all fit well into the plot. Even smaller characters like Perry White, Martha Kent and Alfred fit well into the movie. I was surprised with how much screen time Perry White got but Lawerence Fishborne was so good in the role. Dian Lane was great in her part and had a good part in the movie. I really like Amy Adams as Lois Lane, I think she dose a god job at being tough without being annoying as the character sometime is. I like that they show that she's a really good reporter and we know Lois always has to be in danger for superman to save her but I feel like this might be the best use of Lois Lane I've ever seen in a movie. For the first time it feels like Lois Lane has a real purpose to be in this movie other then it's a superman movie. I love the first half of the movie because it felt like a drama and not a comic book movie. In fact I like how realistic the movie felt despite dealing with sci-fi elements. I think it's hard to say what's the single best thing about the movie but maybe I'll go with batman. I supported the casting of Ben Affleck as batman from the start and he didn't disappoint. Part of me feels like I would've liked to get more information about his past. They talked about his parents being killed but we don't know much about his years of fighting crime as batman. The trailers made it looked like he retired batman but put on the suit again to fight superman but it's hard to tell if he ever stopped. I like that he feels very different from other batmans. I like how he's just called "The Bat". I like that he's a very smart batman who is clearly a detective. I love the look of his batcave, batmobile and batplane. It looked realistic but still comic book. He has the 2nd best batsuit after Keaton. His bat voice is great too. I love the reference to the "death in the family" comic where the joker killed Robin with the burned robin suit hanging up. I think Zack Snyder found the perfect balance for batman between comic book and gritty realism. I love his Bruce Wayne and the fight scene between batman and a gang of thugs is the best batman fight I've ever seen. I love how he brands his victims. While Keaton is still my favorite batman, Affleck might be tied with Bale as the best Bruce Wayne. I love Jeremy Irons as Alfred I like how snarky he is. I also like that he's less of a butler and more of a shadow partner. I also love Gal Gadot as wonder woman, I was impressed with her acting abilities. She did much better then I thought. Her costume looked great and her accent fit perfectly. I wish we got to see more of her fighting. I think Henry Cavil is the 2nd best superman after Reeves. I think in this movie they made it plausible that no one knew Clark Kent and superman were the same because it seems like he tries to keep a low profile either way. I thought Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was the most interesting character in the movie but I felt he wasn't given enough backstory. I felt like I never understood him, yeah he hated superman but why? He was mentally unbalanced but why?However I think Jesse gave a great performance. I didn't find him annoying but I was intrigued by his character and I wish they explored his backstory a little more. I liked his assistant Mercy but I wish they didn't kill her(or so it seemed). I thought the future-Justice League cameos were really good. I think the fight between superman and batman was well done and satisfying. I though it was clever how they used the fact that both of their mothers were named Martha. I thought Doomsday worked well into the story and the fight at the end was great. I would have to say the best thing about this movie is that it makes me interested and excited about seeing future D.C. movies. I would love to see more of Ben Affleck's batman. I can't wait to see the wonder woman solo movie and I wonder how the upcoming suicide squad movie will fit into all this. I also liked that they killed superman at the end making us wait for justice league to see how he would come back. So I thought they did a great job of bringing all the characters together and making it feel like a natural fit and I want to see more of these characters. So it's a good movie but it could've been a great movie with a better plot.

title: Low expectations = a good time
review:
Disclaimer: Spoiler box ticked but know that I will be going into a lot of spoiler related detail. I went to see this movie after the first wave of reviews/opinions came through; there was a lot of negatives being used in both contexts so I wasn't expecting much from BvS (Batman vs Superman). What I found was a movie that had so many good things, or potential for so many good things, that I couldn't help but enjoy the experience.

The opening sequence was riveting and compelling, seeing the end of Man of Steel from Bruce Wayne's perspective added a level of emotion to the character while we simultaneously see his origins for becoming the Batman. Where the movie get slightly off track is when it starts establishing the other narrative elements of the story (Daily Planet/Louis Lane, Superman, disaster victim(s), Lex Luther). There are so many which the film tries to jump between whilst pushing the story towards the movie's name sake (Batman fighting Superman) that it loses out on engaging the audience with 1 of the 2 central characters (Superman).Bruce Wayne/Batman is fleshed out in a way which the audience can focus on, you know what his next move is and you understand the reasons behind his actions; Superman is left on the side-lines in terms of story progression. Stuff that happens with Lois Lane and Lex Luthor is choppy and you can't connect with their stories at all. What I'm getting at is the film loses focus when it jumps to any of the characters other than Batman.

I'm not gonna go into much detail about the acting because it was fine for the most part with Ben Affleck standing out (as Batman) as well as his on-screen counterpart Jeremy Irons (as Alfred). Jesse Eisenberg give a unique performance as Lex Luthor. I say unique because some people are going to like it and others are going to find it odd and annoying; I am in the former category however as I said before his sections of story are choppy so you can't engage with the character no matter how much you liked the actor's performance.

The main fight. Slightly annoying. You reach that part of the film and you know the fight is taking place (some plot holes but I'll get to that in my nagging section at the end) and it's heating up. Someone's going to get messed up. Then the fight ends, talk about anti- climaxes. It was kind of a wake- up call for me really, these are two characters that are essentially a force for good in their respective fashions so why would they fight? This is what I consider to be the movie's greatest mistake. It wants to be Batman taking on Superman but in the end all the motivation it tries to give the respective characters disappears (or gets re-directed). You ask yourself "well what was the point in all that build up?" The answer comes quickly, "oh that's right Lex Luthor was doing something in that spaceship". So now we come to what the film was really building to. Lex trying everything in his power to kill Superman because he didn't get much attention as a child? As you can tell from my poor exposition that this movie really is all over the place; great elements presented in the incorrect order or when they shouldn't have been presented at all (looking at you random Bruce Wayne e-mail).

Some quick positives before the nagging section. Visually a spectacular movie which really captures its environments and action beautifully (slightly too many cuts for my taste but never really to a point that it was distracting). Costume/set design on freaking point. Dream sequences (I always like the unexplained elements of a movie) although some random dude in a portal yelling something about Louis Lane was kind of crazy, like I get Batman having nightmares about Superman and all that but random portal guy was intense. Batman being brutal and accepting he's a criminal for justice; best fight in the movie is actually Batman vs warehouse goons after the BvS fight. Wonder Woman is bad-ass and beautiful (ticking all the Wonder Woman criteria) and I can't wait for her own movie.

Nagging section. We Brits love a good nag but I won't go on for too much longer. Plot hole the size of the Grand Canyon. Lex Luthor claims to be the one who helped push Batman to wanna take out Superman but already started making Doomsday before Batman v Superman actually takes place. Did he know Batman would fail? Louis Lane, love Amy Adams so I blame the script. Some of her lines feel forced and mostly she just feels useless in the movie, her side story is something I feel could have been left out for a more cohesive plot. The freaking e-mail. Like I know that end credits scenes are a Marvel thing but having something like that in the middle of a movie is nonsensical, have it right at the end after everything's gone down. Finally if you're going to kill a character, kill them. Don't fake it or something, that doesn't work and people don't like it (looking at you Dark Knight Rises).

Conclusion: I thoroughly enjoyed BvS even though there are some story elements that are choppy and others which are out of place. I know that I've focused in on negatives for the film but you can't ignore that kind of stuff in a review, just know that I felt a lot of positives came from this film and you can definitely have a good time watching it. Just don't expect the second coming of superhero movies. 68/100 (rounded up to 7 for the IMDb rating system).

title: Autistic Reviwers Opinion Of This Movie.
review:
As you have probably heard or read over social media, Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice has both gained negative reviews from critics while earning $420 million within its first days of opening. The critics 'say' have placed much attention on the film's value (even making Ben Affleck sad in a notable video interview) but after seeing this film, I can honestly admit that the critics are wrong on this one. BVS was a much anticipated film among comic book fans and audiences, brining to live the much famous face-off of Batman and Superman as we've read in its comic's series.

The plot for the film will not be said in my review, but I will state that the plot itself does run smoothly and does establish sources that will play out further in not only its films coming in years but sticks There are several points that made BVS a strong film compared to what critics have said;

 It reintroduces Batman (once again) but it's the best Batman role and adaptation to have surfaced in the last couple of years.  Sticks to the DC source material closely, having more serious and further established universe compared to Marvel's films from the MCU.  The performances of Affleck, Cavill, Gadot, Eisenberg, Adams, Irons and supporting cast are all spot on, with high appraisal going to Gadot, Affleck and Eisenberg for their character roles.  Zack Snyder's direction and vision for the film.  The face-off between the heroes and the climactic battle are both epic and engaging, along with exciting and well choreographed action sequences and character development

The music score composed by the great Hans Zimmer and rising composer Junkie XL is a sound for the ears and soundtrack lovers. Carrying the previous tones in MOS but establishing further dramatic, epic and soaring scores for its action set-pieces and character moments, this soundtrack is bound to win you over and make the purchase for the official album of the score.

Overall, BVS is a strong start to DC's revival of its movie universe with an epic tone, close to the source material and backed with solid performances and visuals. Ignore what critics have said of the film and embrace your inner geek for what will be labeled as underrated or misunderstood film for 2016.

5 / 5 – Nick

This film has copped very negative criticism, mainly by movie critics. With Nicholas (the other Autistic Reviewer) walked out loving this film, I must admit I was very disappointed.

The plot is very simple, and it doesn't go into background information on Batman or Superman. It just expects you to know already the background information on them. The plot leaves off exactly where "Man Of Steel" leaves you. And the government/the people are questioning whether or not if Superman and Batman are abusing their power and are a threat to society.

The plot takes too long. It's all talk, talk talk, and then after about 90 minutes some action happens. And the action wasn't even that good. The CGI was pretty bad and then after a 2 minute action scene then BACK TO TALKING! And the fight scene between Batman and Superman only goes for 6 minutes. So it was a waste of time, if you ask me.

The acting was good, both by Ben Affleck and Henry Cavill. Affleck makes a really good Bruce Wayne and Batman. He's better than Christian Bale. But, again, he doesn't get much screen time as Batman. We needed more. Jesse Eisenberg playing Lex Luthor was a joke in my opinion. He reminded me of Heath Ledger's joker and a spoiled brat, and it just didn't fit!

Overall, I would give this 2/5 stars. I hope Suicide Squad will be better!

Jay

title: Batman v Superman is a good movie, nothing more and nothing less
review: Batman v Superman is a good movie. Nothing more and nothing less. It's not awful and it's not great. It's somewhere in the middle. Why I say it's just simply good. This is because of the movie lacking in so many fronts. Let's take the first one, Ben Affleck as Batman. While his portrayal delivered, the script didn't. This is an established Batman fighting crime for over 20 years. Why is it necessary to go over his origin story again? The script fails in dialogue and story. These areas were weak in justifying why these two characters fight in the first place. The story just wasn't there for the build up to this fight, actual fight and the reason for them to cease fighting and joint forces. The reasons just didn't make sense or just wasn't epic enough. The actual fight was kind of a disappointment. To me the fight was one sided. This was a man of steel sequel and the character of Batman just took over the story. The biggest disappointments were Lois Lane in terms of story and Lex Luthur who was a catastrophic disaster both in story and portrayal. I always wanted to see corporate Lex Luthur in the big screen. This young and overly erratic version was not appealing at all. It wasn't a character that you would want to see in future installments. This movie ends up being just like man of steel, a good movie but not a great one mainly because of the special effects and overall look of the movie which were the best thing about this movie.

title: Just,.... OK...
review:
As many other people did when first hearing about this movie, I was skeptical about the title (superman would kick the bejesus out of batman), but I decided to watch the movie and see what all of the fuss was about, I have to say that I'm a fan of the marvel movies and I was hoping for some sort of rivalry between DC and Marvel,. Sadly this will not be the case of DC keep banging out movies like this, although this is the best one that they have done so far and I've rated it as a 6...

OK, so onto the main movie,. Pros Ben Afleck actually makes an interesting Batman, I think I speak for the majority of us when I say that casting Afleck seemed like a bad idea, but he actually does a pretty good job, Henry cavil as superman is a good casting choice too, and Jesse Eisenberg did a pretty good job at being a crazy lex luthor, Jeremy irons again fits the bill (as with all of his roles, and the new Wonder Woman seemed cool too The overall movie is good to watch and doesn't really seem like 2:30 hours worth in the end, it manages to stay pretty interesting throughout (I'll explain why in the 'cons'), the bat suit looks more bulky like Afleck has had some boosts, and the overall movie is worth a watch.

Cons The story line is,.. Well,.. Ridiculous... First of all superman looks like a wimp, I think I could Slap the lad around,. Batman is too big and seems to now have super strength! I liked batman as a mere mortal but for some reason he is stronger than our average Joe, also he likes to grapple a car and drag it around I case he might need to ramp it up a container and land it perfectly on top of a car full of gun men,... Yes that actually happened.. Now I know that an alien in a blue suit and an immortal chick with a sword and shield is a little 'unrealistic',. But movies with action scenes that defy logic just grinds my gears. Which brings us to the story line,.. Sorry.. 'Story line' It's just awful, hard to follow which keeps your brain ticking over making you concentrate harder than you thought was possible,. And to no prevail as the plot seems to give you no answers really, also, I have no idea why lex hates superman, or why batman does really, sure he killed a few people trying to save his own muscular rump from zod but when everyone is questioning superman it clearly shows the guy helping people all over the world,. I'm pretty sure that the majority of people would see him as a good guy...?

Now, time for some SPOILERS,. I will attack these in the form of questions and WTF's 1) why does superman only hear what Lou's is getting up to? And why is this woman running around and getting into mischief when her fella is busy saving the world,. Attention seeker if you ask me.. 2) how come with all of the technology that the cryptonites have, a guy that just wanders in can just create a monster which was banned from being made?!? That computer lady needs sacking! 3) when batman amazingly beats up superman, why does he change his mind and become his blood brother after learning that their mothers have the same name!? 'You killed thousands of people in your last movie and I hate everything about you!! I'm going too.. Oh wait,. Your mum is called Martha too!?? Well why didn't you say so!? Give me a hug brother!' 4) why did the big angry slimy monster thing fall back to Earth after being in space,..? I'm pretty sure that wouldn't happen (and I've watched a couple of space programs on the telebox) superman took the creature to outer space and the government think 'hey, good chance to see if our nukes work' 5) how did lex know to put some blood on zods face in the water? Did he read a manual or is this common knowledge in metropolis,...? 6) why do mercenaries with machine guns insist on running up to guys without guns? YOU HAVE A GUN! It's like fishing with a rod and jumping in the water when you see a fish! 7) I'm bored of myself now :/

Conclusion This movie could have been incredible, I like DC because of how dark they make their movies and characters, however in this portrayal they seem to be whining more than have real issues. I hope that this movie was just a taste of better things to come, they have all of the elements but seem to lack a great storyline, also, they should take some notes from bigger and better movies like the dark night and minimalise the use of CGI rather that using it in EVERY scene Note to directors everywhere : we like relatable and realistic movies

title: honest unbiased opinion

title: Don't believe what they tell you. Go see it and judge for yourself. And there are Spoilers
review:
So I went to see the most awaited and anticipated movie since the making of cinema. Sorry star wars fans, I know you think this spot is for you , but there were many star wars movies, but no other feature film with the most 2 iconic superheroes of all time.

title: The People Vs Hollywood Studios
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn Of Justice was a film surrounded by criticism from the very beginning. With the controversial casting of Ben Affleck as Batman, it had many people in an uproar as to how the final product would turn out.

Then came the horrendous reviews from the critics, including a pitiful 29% critics rating on Rotten Tomatoes. As much as the action-packed trailer had me excited to watch this film, I couldn't shake the niggling doubt that had infiltrated my mind.

Honestly, this film delivered in what I had expected from it. That's not to say it is an Oscar-worthy film but people need to remember that it's not what it set out to be. Two gorgeous leads playing superhero heavyweights, not to mention the introduction of Wonder Woman, played by the stunning Israeli actress Gal Gadot. There were two major things that did bother me: the lengthy duration of the film (which seemed quite unnecessary) and the fact that the title implies a heavy battle between Superman and Batman however this was quite short-lived and was poorly explored.

Having said that, the special effects were phenomenal and the cinematography by Larry Fong stayed true to Zack Snyder's video game/comic book style. The major thing to note was that despite the negative criticism attached to this film, this did not deter the regular cinema-goers from flocking to theatres worldwide to view this blockbuster on the big screen. Raking in a whopping $170.1 million at the U.S. box office during opening weekend, this is a shining example of the ever- increasing gap between the industry's professional opinions and the expectations and desires of the general population.

title: A Beautiful Mess
review:
(warning: mild spoilers)

If you are someone who liked Man of Steel, you will be entertained. If you are someone who is a fan of the comics, you will be pleased. But if you fan of film, you will be disappointed.

If you thought this film was about the ideological differences between two heroes and their physical fight to sort out these differences, you will be invested in the first half of the movie, as I was. And I must say, Snyder did make a visually stunning film, which is what I have come to expect from him. It is filmed fine, graded fine (maybe too unsaturated for some) and it is acted well generally. Also the score is great, especially with each hero and villain getting their own theme- props to Zimmer and Junkie XL.

The plot has the potential to be good, but it is too convoluted. The writing is okay, it is very true to the comics but it almost tries to pick so much from the comics that it is an overload of ideas. While the ideas are interesting and good individually, none of them are developed or explored in the detail required to do them justice. My main problem with the film is how it is executed, the editing is poor, the pacing is almost not considered when trying to fit what they intended into one film, and then there is the franchising!

In world flooded with superhero films, franchising is now all the producers care about. I am appalled at the audacity of the studio to introduce certain heroes in the way they did, and am also appalled at how much time the studio have spent in trying to create a justice league in this film. They should have used this time to make this film good. But now I feel studios are more interested in planning the next sequel before they make a film. And if franchising isn't bad enough, the marketing might be even worse. Dear Studio, please stop showing your film in the trailer.

The film begins very well, showing the events of man of steel from Bruce Wayne's perspective. I actually was invested in this duel of differences between Clark and Bruce, and the whole concept of Batman V Superman. Cavill still pulls off the role of Superman to me, and his performance is just fine. For me it was Ben Affleck who stole the show. He has the physical presence to be Batman, but he is also a brilliant Bruce Wayne. We learn a lot about his character in this film, who he is, what he has become and why he has become this way. Batman is dark, brooding, intelligent and the crime fighting vigilant detective we all love. Also Jeremy Irons is a fantastic Alfred, and Alfred's relationship with Bruce is very well portrayed, it is fresh and unique. Rather than being a just a butler, he is a partner to Bruce. Gal Gadot was good as Diana Prince/Wonder Woman but was really not needed in this film at all. As for the fights. They were great, especially the Batman V Superman fight. As for the final fight, while it was entertaining to watch, it belonged in another film, it felt out of place, and Doomsday was handled very badly. I just want to add that the nightmare sequence was brave, original and brilliant.

While there were those aspects that worked, the film as a whole, did not. This film is a mess. There are four different stories being told and two different movies being shown. There is the man of steel sequel, the origin of the new batman, the actual Batman V Superman and the 'Dawn of Justice'. There is not enough time and care spent on any of these stories which is a shame as they all showed such great potential. Certain scenes and subplots are not even needed, especially the attempted courtroom build up. Amy Adams fulfills her role as Lois Lane but her character is written poorly. They have tried to incorporate her into the story to give her importance and this comes across very forced. The scenes with Lois take away from the film, they are not needed, and really she should not have been given as big of a role as she has got. Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luther will either work for you or will not. For me, it did not work. They went down the crazy route and while the sinister side was portrayed well, I found his character overall very annoying, over- the-top, and like a two dimensional cartoon character. Now, in a film filled with destruction I expect a fair dose of CGI, but there are a few occasions in the long run time where the CGI is laugh worthy. The scenes are also baldy put together, with lazy editing, inefficient pacing and lack of the grandness needed in such a film. The scenes just jump so incessantly from sub plot to sub plot, the the plot becomes disjointed and disjunctive.

I watch to films to be told a story. And the story wasn't told well. It fell flat for me, with the ending not packing the emotional punch it was aiming to do. Parts really worked but I am reviewing the film as a whole so I cannot say this is a good film. I am disappointed as I wanted this film to be good, I wanted to love it. And I could deny its flaws but it would feel wrong. Overall, the movie is entertaining, original and fairly epic on scale. However it is also cluttered and narratively messy. It does the job, but only just about. Yet optimistically going forth, it sets up and has now built a world for a justice league to exist so I look forward to seeing what they do next.

title: Batman V Superman Dawn of Justice Non Spoiler Review
review: So I saw Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice last week Friday (release day) and I would just like to give my take on the movie coming from a comic book fan standpoint. I think it's worth noting that Batman is my favorite superhero so this movie automatically sparked my interest since Man Of Steel was a movie I wasn't particularly a fan of. Anyways, the Dark Knight Returns is my favorite animated film and my favorite batman story, so when this movie was announced, I was optimistic we would get a movie similar to that.Fast forward and I saw the second trailer (doomsday one), my expectations lowered but then rose after the final trailer. I was still hyped for this movie but then I saw the reviews and realized I had to see the movie myself and make my own opinion, well, they were right. This is a 2 and half hour film thats title holds no significance to the movie. And not only that, but this movie has so many more problems than just my disappointment. The first hour or so of the film includes a bunch of random scenes organized in a choppy, sloppy order that you have no idea what's going on. There is literally no plot to this movie. Lex Luthor and Supermans motivations in the movie make 0 sense, and Batmans motivation hold no significance after his battle with superman which, while looks great, is way too short for a movie with a title BATMAN V SUPERMAN and has an outcome that is so ridiculous I couldn't even believe it. Lois Lane is so annoying in this movie as Snyder and crew are continually finding ways to interject her into the main plot that you get so tiresome of seeing her on screen. I literally groaned Every time she showed up. The Justice league cameos were so forced. If you saw the doomsday trailer there's no surprises left for you. I will say Ben Affleck was good as batman/Bruce Wayne and him and Jeremy Irons as Alfred make me excited for solo batman films. Wonder Woman was great even though she didn't have to be in the movie and it was definitely cool when she showed up in costume. The action sequences were cool as well, but overall this movie is actually pretty boring and failed to meet my expectations. It sloppily sets up the DCCU but excites me for solo batman and wonder woman films.

title: Not a great movie,but not bad either.
review:
Batman v Superman for me is a complex movie but there is some enjoyment to be had in this movie.

First off the performances,Ben Affleck as Batman was a very good choice,he was just entertaining to watch. Affleck was also equally entertaining as Bruce Wayne as you get to understand why he hates Superman and what he is willing to do take him down. Wonder Woman was one of the best parts in this movie she doesn't have a big role but she just fits into the movie and i wish she could have been in the movie more as Gal Gadot does a good job at portraying Wonder Woman.Now Superman, i think Henry Cavill did the best he could do because Superman is in and out of this movie.At first the world is still struggling on whether Superman is a good guy or not and you get to see Superman struggle to get people on his side,but as the movie goes on the plot of him against the world dies down as the matter of Superman doesn't come to a conclusion.

For a movie called Batman v Superman, the focus on the fight is really focused on Batman's side as he goes on a brutal rampage to take Superman down but Superman himself isn't interested in fighting batman sure there are some signs that he is not a fan of Batman but Superman's side of the story is vague until the actual fight happens.Speaking of the fight, the build up to the fight is too quick and vague, though there is some tension,when the actual fight comes along it just happens with no real build up.The fight was entertaining but rather short,but when Doomsday comes into the picture the action is amped with Batman,Superman and Wonder Woman fight Doomsday and that fight is more entertaining than the Batman v Superman fight which is slightly disappointing for a movie called Batman v Superman.

Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor was a mixed bag for me, if your a fan of Jesse Eisenbrg then you won't be disappointed but for me Jesse as Lex Luthor was too wacky for me, he turned out to be menacing as the movie ends but he didn't have a real motive in this movie, he influences the Batman and Superman fight in some way but doesn't actually have a real agenda and his wackiness sometimes takes you out of the movie a bit.

I didn't really mind the tone of this movie it was dark and that's the way it should have been.Critics say there is no or little humor but not every superhero movie is a Marvel Movie that's what they fail to understand.There are a few chuckles in the movie and thats fine with me and Zack Synder does a good job at delivering some dramatic moments with the dark tone of the movie.

Now my biggest problem with Batman v Superman is that during the movie there are these totally unnecessary scenes, like Justice league set up the title 'Dawn Of Justice' suggested that the movie was going to touch on some justice league stuff and one one hand the introduction of the justice league was cool as you get to see other characters that could be involved in the justice league including Wonder Women,but there are some scenes that are confusing as hell and that have nothing to to with the movie like a certain dream sequence that confused me and took me out of the movie as it is never explained and you remain scratching your head on what just happened,Especially and the very end.

The action is good and entertaining especially the Batman and Wonder Woman action sequences.The Batman action sequences are brutal and fun with is unlike any other thing batman has done on screen and Wonder Woman's powers were equally entertaining.The romance between Superman and Lois lane is super vague, their relationship is never really explored and developed and when they showed deep feelings for each other you just didn't buy it.

So Batman v superman is just a mixed bag,somethings i enjoyed but some things were bad,this film could have done a lot better but there are is some fun to be had in this movie if you keep your expectations low.

title: LET ME DEFEND THE CRITICS  but with an 8/10 rating!
review:
I'll try not to deal with the usual stuff that critics or fans are talking about. Mostly on how one should understand BvS.

I've practically read MOST (if not all) the critics review incldg youtube vids & have also read almost a thousand FAN reviews before I came to watch it last night.

Believe me, I am by far one of the MOST excited to see BvS Too excited to have bought & GIVEN away 15 tickets to treat my friends & I'm willing to bet most haven't even done half of what I did.

Here's a comic film I've waited for 30 LONG years & have watched the 3 main trailers almost 100x & I was destined to prove the critics wrong but now... I understand.

& I hope you do too. But it doesn't mean that I didn't like the film.. & If you won't take it TOO seriously & literally, most will enjoy it too. Box Office figures WON'T LIE.

All the while I thought that It's just simple, either you get it or you don't get it.. but in this case, I'm afraid I got caught up right smack in the middle.

I understood the critics well when they complained about the Plot, Editing, Character build up, Seriousness & tone, etc etc.

Zack's DIRECTION as a Director is different compared to the likes of Chris Nolan, James Cameron, Ron Howard, Robert Zemeckis, to name a few.

Zack is of a different league, admittedly being a COMIC FREAK as he is, most esp working with Geoff Johns (iconic comic writer) & David Goyer on BvS, they set this film miles apart from the typical standard Oscar AWARD type of how a film should be presented.

There were inconsistencies in the way the story was told & the only way to understand these is to wait for the release of the much awaited DVD release and though we are still 3&1/2 months away from it, the addtl. 30min R-rated bonus scenes may IRON OUT these flaws but then again, this should be long fixed in the theatrical cut.

For the BvS plot was almost loosely based on how it would be presented in the COMICS. Again, the Zack, Goyer & Geoff tandem.

If you've watched MOS recently, (I just did) , this is MOSTLY an MOS sequel so It's the tone that began with MOS (dark) and now with Batman in it, quoting Zack, "It is what it is" It's supposed to be dark! Again, for a regular movie goer, if you're not so familiar with DC characters (villains & heroes) you will certainly GET LOST and ALIENATED watching BvS because the film tends to show visions/dreams of some revelations from certain DC characters & at times its presented QUICKLY that many tend to miss..

To appreciate this film more, one should be Acquainted & FAMILIAR with some DC characters or one would be surprised to see IRRELEVANT characters popping up every now & then. IRRELEVANT FOR NOW that is To many who find it hard to relate and connect to BvS, we should understand that DC has its OWN WORLD. Marvel's characters are mostly based in FACTUAL cities (e.g - Spiderman & Fantastic 4 are based in NewYork). The feeling of what it's like having these heroes in OUR OWN universe.

Whereas DC characters have Metropolis, Gotham City, Themyscara (W.Woman), Central City (Flash), Atlantis (Aquaman). FICTIONAL UNIVERSE so better not take it too heavily.

Dialogues & script were not bad. To me almost every movie has at least a few lines that will STAND OUT & be remembered & it was mostly uttered by the genius Luthor.

As for the actors, well to each his own.. I personally thought there were no subpar actors. All have finely executed their JOB. Their JOB, get it? Why an 8/10 rating? The reality of the most scenes, the fight sequences, Batman himself, and most of the effects is mostly what makes up for a popcorn COMIC movie that would click & though it is NOWHERE near as rich & deep as Chris Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy, it still deserves at least a SOLID 8 rating for a GUTSY movie. The Production team for BvS certainly has the BALLS to create one of this kind, combining at least 3 comic stories all rolled up into one film is a very BOLD & AMBITIOUS move.

I admit, I NEED to see this film maybe a couple more times coz I know i've missed some infos. I know many have coz there were so much going on in there. I have already read some 50 ANSWERS from other credible sites though I'd still rather see it for myself & enjoy some revelations.

I feel the NEED to watch it again so the more I'll understand it. Then the more ill WANT it. I NEED to WANT this film! Does is sound mildly pathetic? BvS should DEFINITELY be watched by MOST comic fans & movie fans alike. Is it an Epic? Most say it is & even if it receives the title say.. the most criticized comic movie of all time, it still belongs undeniably among the FUTURE of comic movie CLASSIC & should definitely be on everyone's DVD collection.

title: The Movie We Needed, But Not the One We Deserved
review:
The expectations were high. Perhaps too high for its own good. Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, in a nutshell, was promised to be the beginning of a greater age in its respective superhero genre, and finally deliver a worthy franchise to rival that of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The result? A dark, horribly messy, poorly edited attempt at creating the roots of an entire movie universe within the boundaries of one film, deprived of a meaningful narrative, with some highly entertaining action scenes sprinkled around occasionally great characters.

Warner Bros. decided to try and play catch up with their Marvel counterparts by saying, "they do A, B, and C, we do X, Y, and Z". Unfortunately, this is the major issue revolving around the superhero showdown. The attempt to create a large and rich extended universe practically in one film paves way for unbalanced disorder, with horrible pacing that leaves most of the movie dragging its feet in the sand. Director Zack Snyder's vision for this film was overall a defective one, with the entirety of the movie feeling like a contest started by Warner Bros. to try and one-up everything Marvel has done thus far. One thing this did prove, is that the film and its respective franchise, in its current state, are worlds behind what's happening at Marvel Studios.

There are times during the 2.5 hour film that feel like you're watching 3 or 4 different movies, and with deficient editing, the film also, at times, feels like a 151 minute trailer, devoid of any proper pacing as formerly stated. It is far too jumbled to coherently tell one single engaging story, it's an overloaded blur and a failed venture into making what should have been 3 or 4 movies into one. It's all flash and no finish, a mansion with no foundation.

When a new actor is cast into the role of an iconic character that people have loved across generations, it's usually met with skepticism from a large and passionate fan base. Maybe no casting in superhero film history was met with more skepticism than Ben Affleck landing the role as the legendary Batman. Minus one colossal flaw in the writing of the character (a MAJOR turn-off towards the film as a die hard Batman fan), Aflleck delivers a solid performance as the Caped Crusader, and an even better Bruce Wayne. Batman is fearsome and brooding, and overall I enjoyed this Batman more than any other character in the film, aside from the enormous previously mentioned flaw.

Henry Cavill returns as the Man of Steel, his character now in a much different position than before. The story leads Superman into exciting new dangers, but that same story strips the Man of Tomorrow from becoming something greater, no thanks to the horrible narrative cluster. Cavill's Superman isn't exceptional, but for the mood of the film, it was done well enough to get the stamp of approval. Gal Gadot proves any doubters wrong with an epic showcasing as Wonder Woman. Aided by stellar effects, the Amazon Princess's silver screen debut did not disappoint, even if her involvement felt forced.

While the Golden Trinity delivered a solid performance, the portrayal of Lex Luthor by Jesse Eisenberg is an absolute disaster. Whether you believe in taking age-long characters in a new direction or not, Eisenberg's Luthor was a tremendously annoying and painful thorn in the side of the film, giving off the complete wrong sense of what the iconic villain should be about. Easily one of the greatest downfalls of the movie, Eisenberg, along with more poor writing, sadly ruin one of comic book's all-time greatest villains.

Not all is lost in this film, with many high notes to reflect upon. Along with the portrayals of Batman, Wonder Woman and occasionally Superman, the initial cameo from The Flash was pretty awesome, and although it could be confusing for some viewers, any legitimate comic fan will know what's going on. Add to that a couple other cameos from Cyborg and Aquaman, and while they felt hopelessly forced, they were fun to see on screen for the first time, even if it was for a handful of seconds.

When it's not bogged down by poor editing, the movie's action is entertaining on a grand scale. God-like characters soar into battle and when he's in action, Batman is fun to watch. Add to that the phenomenal score composed by Hans Zimmer, who doesn't disappoint with the epic tone he musically sets for the movie. Although I have been harsh on the overall narrative, the immediate story set up between Batman and Superman is not a bad one by any means, and occasionally is wonderful. It's a shame that not only did the climax of our two heroes disappoint overall, but that there was again to much of an uncoordinated rhythm to keep any intensity flowing smoothly. BvS lives up to its subtitle by setting the stage for the upcoming Justice League film, but it took a lot of agonizing and unnecessary time to get there.

It's difficult to be so excited for a film and its characters and end up riddling it with negative criticism. I wanted desperately to walk out of the theater with nothing but positives, but no matter how much money this film makes, regardless of the different steps the DC Extended Universe is taking to succeed, the cold hard truth is this; Batman v Superman is collaborative chaos, weighed down by atrocious pacing, disjointed editing, overloaded storytelling, or a lack thereof, and some poorly written and developed characters. I truly believe this film collapsed under the weight of its own shoulders, too big for its own good. I have hope for the future of the DC movie world, but in its current state, with Zack Snyder at the helm, it's hard to see a brighter future through the dark, dark void that is Batman v Superman.

4.5/10

title: Not as bad as I expected, but still not great.
review:
After seeing the trailers for this movie I was ready to be disappointed. Not only did they give away huge spoilers for the movie, the spoilers they gave were also a dead giveaway that the movie was going to end up being more of a set up for the Justice League, which was not what I wanted out of Batman v Superman. While this did end up happening, it actually wasn't that awful.

The biggest issue I had with this movie is that it often felt like it was dragging on. I kept waiting for things to happen, and then when they did, it wasn't as exciting as it should've been, especially considering how long it took to get there. The Batman v Superman fight was a tiny part of the movie, and like much of the fighting in Man of Steel, and in the rest of BvS, it all felt so inconsequential. Although the fighting and special effects were cool at times, I just wasn't interested in many of the fights because it didn't feel like much was at stake. The intense fight *should've* been the BvS fight, but thanks to some great trailer work by DC, that was ruined for me too.

I think the plot needed work. The fights would've felt more intense if I was more invested in the story, but I really wasn't. The characters were cool (Batman looks sick in the movie, I really liked the power armor), and the acting was great by all of the stars, but the story wasn't there. I do have one complaint about a character though. Wonder Woman - she was really cool! Until the fight with Doomsday... It wasn't the way they portrayed her, it was that weird, cheesy guitar riff that came in with every shot of her. It really ruined the moment.

Oh, one more little complaint, the adult Bruce Wayne dream sequences were really weird. In a bad way. The first one wasn't awful (even with the jump scare) but the second one was just dumb. I won't go into detail, but yeah, not so great.

As far as things they did right, I thought that the cinematography was actually really good for a Superhero movie despite some grainy shots. The composition was always on point, and in general the shots were nice to look at. The scene towards the beginning of the movie with Bruce Wayne driving around the city trying seeing all the stuff that went down in Man of Steel was actually pretty good, and set up the the whole political/moral debate side of the movie effectively. Speaking of which, I thought they did that side of the movie pretty well. I found myself on both sides of the conflict at different times through the movie ultimately siding with Batman in the end, but that might not be the same for everyone. The friend I watched the movie with said he stuck on Superman's side.

My friend also made really good point - this movie is his favorite portrayal of Batman from an aesthetic and fighting standpoint. As in, the way he moved and acted through the film felt like a good comic book-y Batman, not like the super realistic version of Batman that Nolan gave us (not that the Nolan version was bad - it was good for what he was going for, but this Batman was more true to the fighting style of Batman). On the other side of the coin though, Batman did not feel like a master detective/planner in this film. He didn't think much at all actually. It seemed like he just acted on impulse, which didn't feel very Batman-esque. To conclude this Batman paragraph - he was cooler in fights, and lamer in person.

All things considered I give this movie a 6.5/10. It wasn't amazing by any means, but it didn't disappoint me completely.

title: Batman v Superman: The Most Highly Anticipated Comic Book Movie of the Year
review:
RATING: B-

This is possibly the most highly anticipated movie of the year. So how does it stack up? Did the producers create a good film? How does it compare to other comic book movies?

I will give you the comparisons first. In my opinion this film is better than Iron Man 3, because it has a better story. In my opinion this movie is better than the 2nd Avengers movie, because although the story in the Batman v Superman film has serious problems and serious plot holes, the 2nd Avengers movie has more serious problems in this regard. This film (Batman v Superman) is better than both XMen 3 (The Last Stand)and The Dark Knight Rises, both of which were dreadful abominations.

In my opinion Batman v Superman is not as good as the following comic book movies, which had good stories, good scripts and/or good character development: Iron Man (the 1st Iron Man film), XMen (the 1st film), XMen 2- XMen United, Batman Begins, The Dark Knight, and Captain America -The Winter Soldier.

The producers of Batman v. Superman try very hard to produce a very good quality film (or even a great film). The final product is entertaining to a certain extent, but to be honest, it misses the mark. To me the film is worth about 7 out of 10 largely because the picture/ cinematography is very good, the action scenes are good, and most of the actors do a very good job (the one exception being Jesse Eisenberg). Also every DC comic book fan is going to love seeing Batman, Superman and Wonderwoman on the big screen. This film excels in using references from other DC movies or referring to other DC characters. The casting (with the exception of Jesse Eisenberg) is very good. Also the movie manages to achieve good diversity in casting because even though none of the major 3 or 4 characters are visible minorities, there are several visible minorities, with speaking parts in this movie.

The major problems with this movie have to do with: (1) the story, (2) a failure to capitalize on the emotional moments in the story, (3) a poorly conceived Lex Luther character, which is poorly explained and (4) the casting of Lex Luther.

(1) The Story

The story is not intelligent enough. The story needed to make sense. Many things could have been better explained or better written. For example: Batman and Superman are both supposed to be the good guys. In order to get these guys hating each other you should have a really plausible explanation. The explanation provided in the movie is not plausible. Batman's hatred of Superman in the movie comes across as petty, jealous, egocentric, and maybe even a little childish.

Another thing that does not make sense: how can Superman hear one of his close associates in danger, but someone else (another associate for example) is in danger and Superman does not hear this.

They needed to come up with a better explanation as to how Lex Luther creates that thing that he creates.

There should have been a better explanation in the movie as to why Lex Luther was opposed to Superman and/or Batman.

(2) A Failure to Capitalize on the Emotional Moments in the Story

For example, there is a catastrophic scene (I am not going to spoil it for you). The director and story writers should have milked this scene so that audience would experience the following: shock, awe, crying, for a prolonged period of several minutes. Instead the audience experiences a very brief moment of shock.

(3) A Poorly Conceived Lex Luther Character, which is Poorly Explained

Lex Luther is presented as a pathological character whose personality is extremely similar to that of the Joker as played by Heat Ledger in the 2nd Chris Nolan Batman movie. Nobody needed to see Lex Luther pretend to be the Joker, which is what we got. (In that Chris Nolan movie, the Joker is a well written Character. When he speaks the audience almost finds itself agreeing with him 75 % percent of the time because he accurately points out some of the flaws in modern society and he artfully mixes lies with the truth.) Lex Luther needed to have a different personality. He needed to have his own personality, not the Joker's.

The Lex Luther character would have made more sense as a Machiavellian, psychological manipulator with political ambitions (think of Kevin Spacey's character in House of Cards, but played by a younger actor).

We never get a good explanation of what Lex Luthor plans to do once he gets rid of Superman and/or Batman.

(4) The Casting of Lex Luthor

As mentioned above, the Lex Luthor character presented in this movie is essentially the same personality as the Joker character from the second Chris Nolan Batman movie. No one needed to see Jesse Eisenberg play this character. Jesse Eisenberg is really not good in this role. Perhaps it is too much type-casting on the part of those who did the casting, but this was a really bad choice.

Overall the writers of these movies need to always keep in mind that they are writing these movies for intelligent adults and not just for 4 year olds.
