title: Super not so friendly ***SPOILERS SPOILERS SPOILERS***
review:
After two years of rumors disappointing casting decisions and teaser trailers that gradually began to give away the whole plot the day had arrived to finally see DC comics heavy hitters come together on film. I did feel it was a poor decision to show Wonder Woman in the final trailers she should've been introduced to audiences in the movie and this is the case with Batman v Superman Dawn of Justice, giving away so much before the film's release.

This movie while far from perfect is an enjoyable flick for comic book fans because it does embrace the comic book side of these characters Batman especially. A lot of people weren't happy with Ben Affleck's casting however I found myself actually liking his Bruce Wayne. His back story is of course rehashed although traditionally so no complaints there. I wish some other aspects of Batman's story were fleshed out like why is Wayne Manor in ruins? What happened to Robin exactly although it's obvious the Joker killed him it seems. This is an older Dark Knight Returns style of Batman who no longer resides in Wayne Manor but in a glass lake house where he has access to the Batcave from. Jeremy Irons plays a cynical but tech savvy Alfred Pennyworth who drinks a bit. If was refreshing to not have an Alfred who is lecturing Bruce on giving up the Batman and settling down with the right woman.

Superman is in a bit of a political pickle because of the destruction of most of Metropolis in Man of Steel. He does his usual soul searching from talking to Lois then his Mom and of course to the North pole to talk to his Dad. Not Jor El but the ghost of Johnathan Kent at the North Pole where he back packs to it! Your Superman FLY! This part of the movie I found redundant because we've all seen this before in the Christopher Reeve movies several times and in Man of Steel. I guess Zach Snyder felt this was an important aspect of Superman's character that he seek council with those closest to him before he acts. Hey Lex Luthor's egg timer is ticking, yes he use's an egg timer in this movie.

The third player in this film is Wonder Woman played by Gal Gadot who mysteriously emerges in this film at Lex's big gala event and we only see glimpses of until of course the final act. She is of course an ancient warrior princess from Paradise island although there is no mention of that in her back story. Bruce digs for info on her & other details emerge about other well known future members of the Justice League that were encrypted in Lex's hard drive. I really liked her as Wonder Woman she actually added to the film rather then just being inserted superfluously. She's of course sexy but she was Wonder Woman not just someone in a Halloween costume.

The showdown between Batman and Superman plays like a Godzilla movie which is actually kinda cool. You can't take this movie too seriously and enjoy it even if the movie does take itself too seriously throughout. Batman hate's Superman for causing so much destruction during his battle with Zod & Jessie Eisenburg's Lex has plotted to pit them against one another in a battle royal. Lois talks Batman from stabbing Superman in the chest with a Kryptonian spear he's made. Just like that they are unified in stopping Lex and his giant retarded monster he created with Zod's DNA know as DOOMSDAY!

At long last Wonder Woman arrives blocking rays coming from Doomsday's eyes with her super bracelets. The rest of the film is a bombastic loud battle between the founding members of the Superfriends. Ultimately Doomsday is only defeated upon Superman stabbing him with the Kryptonite tipped spear killing both of them. That's right Superman is dead folks as there was no other way to shoot Doomsday with a shard of green death rock. I could think of a few I'm sure Batman could've but it's what happened in the comics so um yeah. Superman of course will come back to life as will his alter ego Clark Kent who's death was staged so they don't have make some lame excuse as to where & what happened to him.

The Martin Shkreli of this film Lex Luthor is incarcerated at the end with a brief terrifying visit from the Dark Knight who is brandishing a searing hot bat brander, kinda like a car cigarette lighter shape like the bat logo. Words are exchanged Batsy vanishes in his usual form and the melancholy funeral denouement portion of the film plays out.

In conclusion kicking back to this movie with some popcorn is what this movie is about. It felt the same way with Star Wars the Force Awakens enjoyable although the story telling was lacking in places. They could take more chances with these kinda block buster comic book flicks by respecting that the audience does have an intellect that deserves a story that serves that.

title: A mesh of comic book galore!!
review: Everyone has high expectations for Batman and Superman flicks, depending on how much you take in from the comics. For most people, explaining the origin stories is not rocket science, it's common knowledge. I always like going into the theater with a movie like this with little to no expectations because if I do, that might spoil the movie for me. This movie is eye candy. With Zack Snyder directing, it's going to have good visual effects based on his previous work, which does include Man of Steel. I'm more of a Batman fan, but I do know enough of Superman's origins to follow along with what was happening on-screen. This DOES stick to the comic books/graphic novels. Okay, it does seem like half way though that it starts to look like a film adaption of The Dark Knight Returns, only with two extra characters in the mix. title: Not that great, but not terrible either
review:
I LOVE Man of Steel. I will put this out there right now. I LOVE Man of Steel. It's a re-imagining that I like, and I really like the original Christopher Reeve superman movies. So, it's a real shame that I have to admit that this movie left me very underwhelmed. Not because it didn't have as much action, but because the action, and most of the movie, was all over the place. Even by this point I can tell that I have a lot to say.

In 2013, we were promised a Man of Steel "sequel" with Batman, a movie that would focus on the clash of ideologies and strengths these two characters have had. The stuff we've seen in countless DC comics and shows. The moment I began feeling a wave of uncertainty for this kind of movie was when the second trailer was released, and we saw doomsday, and Wonder Woman. This split me into two trains of thought. One was thinking that Wonder Woman would only appear at the very end in an end credits scene and that Doomsday would be a vision that one of the characters would see. The other was thinking exactly what plays out in the movie.

I want to give my quick thoughts on what did work and what didn't. For me, Ben Affleck was great as both Bruce Wayne and Batman. I like his suits and his fight scenes. Even though the film was a mess, and it's really surprising to know that Affleck helped to direct it, he was still great as the Bat of Gotham. And Henry Cavill is still very good at Superman. I like the first half of the movie focusing on Bruce Wayne's preparation for fighting superman. I like that the first half of the film focuses on the politics of having a super-powered being on earth; an entire society living in fear at what he can do. That stuff was very well done.

The first thing I didn't like was the script. There are parts that are very good. But again, I wan't to get back to my main gripe with the movie. This movie is more concerned with forming the Justice League than it is telling a compelling story. Batman and Superman fight for less than 10 minutes, in a film called BATMAN V SUPERMAN. It was so bloody cheap that their entire conflict, the thing we've been looking forward to for 3 years, comes straight to an end so that they can fight another villain.

Now, Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. I have no idea what Zach Snyder was thinking when he casted Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. Apparently he's Lex Luthor Jr in the movie, but that doesn't excuse the fact that Eisenberg is a terrible actor in the movie. He isn't intimidating as a villain, he's not scary, and he just comes off as annoying. Also, he isn't given a motivation for why he wants to defeat superman, or batman, or wants to create doomsday. I don't know what Snyder saw in him, but this will go down as one of the most miscast roles since Megan Fox was cast as April O'Neal in TMNT.

Now moving on to Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman. I actually liked her as Wonder Woman. I have yet to see the solo Wonder Woman movie, but I think she's capable enough to lead a movie about the princess of Themiscyra. I also like that they chose a foreign actress, with an Mediterranean accent that would at least make sense since the amazons are about the Greek gods and ancient Greece. My problem with her in the movie is the fact that she's in it at all, since this is BATMAN V SUPERMAN, not BATMAN, SUPERMAN, WONDER WOMAN V DOOMSDAY.

I don't understand how hard it is to focus on the conflict between Batman and Superman in a movie called BATMAN V SUPERMAN. This film was so concerned with building up the justice league and setting up sequels that it forgot to focus on what the fans were waiting for in the first place, a clash of ideology and strength from the titular characters. There was so much wasted potential and nonsensical moments in this movie. And honestly, I don't think many fans will be that excited for the next movie once they see this mess.

title: Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice is a beautiful mess.
review:
As a huge fan of Batman and DC, I desperately wanted this movie to be amazing. Even with my low expectations, I was disappointed by this movie. What disappointed me the most was the potential that I saw in this movie that was wasted thanks to Warner Bros. and the director Zack Snyder, who I believe is the man to blame for the failure of this movie.

I may have been disappointed by the movie but I have to say that it still has some positive factors in it. First of all, the movie did a great job with showing the consequences of the events of Man of Steel and the destruction it created. This also meant that it did a great job with explaining the Batman and Superman conflict. Everything about Batman vs Superman was so awesome that its awesomeness only made my disappointment bigger. If these two conflicts were all this movie was about, I can assure you that it would have been a spectacular film. We also got to see a new Batman with his new suit and a slightly different personality. This new Batman is played by Ben Affleck, who I thought was the best part of the movie. I would say that he is the best Bruce Wayne we had so far in cinema and also a pretty good Batman. Jeremy Irons was very suitable casting for Alfred and he showed it with his performance in the movie, I loved him. This new Batman has a lot of promise and I love it already. Another casting choice that proved the doubters wrong was Gal Gadot, as I thought she did a really good job as Wonder Woman and her character looks very promising. The only problem with Wonder Woman was that her role was too unnecessarily big in Batman V Superman. The action and cinematography in this film was mind-blowing, hence why it gets the adjective beautiful. Zack Snyder might not be the best storyteller but it has to be said that he knows how to make a fantastic looking movie. The last positive of this movie is the way Justice League was set up in the very end of the film, but only the very end!

After I took the pros off my chest, I can finally talk about the cons. To pick off where I left off, Warner Bros. trying to set- up the Justice League movie degraded this movie as a whole. This made the movie only a set-up for Justice League. The fundamental issue of this film was how overcrowded it was. It had too many stories in it: a Batman vs Superman fight, the consequences of Man of Steel, a Justice League set-up and Lex Luthor's huge evil plan. Because it had too many story lines, none of them could be given adequate time and all of them fell flat other than the Justice League set-up, which didn't need to be there at all. Lex Luthor's evil plan should have been saved for the Justice League movie, so should have been Doomsday who was totally wasted in this story. A movie like this shouldn't have had a real villain. Speaking of a villain, Lex Luthor was by far the worst character in the movie. In hindsight, his presence should have been kept to a minimum and only as a setup for the future. What really happened was that they made him a character as important as both Batman and Superman, and it was extremely annoying. Luthor was totally out of character and it seemed as though Jesse Eisenberg was playing the super-villain version of Mark Zuckerberg. Everything about Lex Luthor in this movie was the true description of disappointing. Another extremely annoying character was Lois Lane. Her contributions to this movie were far exceeded by the annoyance she created. It is obvious that Superman needs Lois Lane, however this movie made her the girl that constantly created unnecessary drama and got herself in peril every single second. She shouldn't have had so much screen time if she wasn't going to have any real contribution to the story. Superman in Batman vs Superman was not so interesting at all. The biggest problem with Superman was that the controversy regarding him and the catastrophic resolution of Man of Steel made me want Batman to put him in his place. Even though I generally loved this new Batman, I still had a few problems with it. His dream sequences felt weird, his past was pretty blank and most importantly Batman kills! The fact that Batman kills does no favors to his character. The film also had a tough time reaching the realism levels set by The Dark Knight trilogy. After seeing how real Batman could be in those movies, this one didn't feel realistic at all. The only technical error in this technically superb film was the interruptions of the soundtrack from time to time. Even though I liked the score a lot, I thought it was a bit overused and too loud at times. The last big problem I had with this movie was the ending. The ending dragged so long that I ended up begging for it to end. The concluding action scene was somewhat uninteresting, had a hard time following the Batman vs Superman fight scene and couldn't learn from the mistakes Man of Steel made. We would have thought that they understood, but this movie ended in a very similar way to that movie; the only difference was that it was in the dark, thanks to Batman.

All in all, this movie was a false advertisement that took Batman vs Superman and changed it to "Dawn of Justice" with a little bit of Batman and Superman fighting peppered into it. In the end, Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice was a movie that had a huge chance at greatness, but ended up disappointing thanks to Warner Brothers' greed and Zack Snyder's fantasies.

title: Lots of missed opportunities (6/10)
review:
Conflicted is the word I would use to describe my feelings towards the movie. On one hand, there are so many things that I absolutely loved about this movie. But, some of the things didn't work at all. Though, I feel the good outweighed the bad, but just by a tiny margin.

Things I liked:

1.The new Batman/Batfleck: This Batman is the one I had always wanted. He was a culmination of Frank Miller's older Batman from Dark Knight Returns and the one from the Arkham Games. Not a bad way to start things at all. Ben Affleck is a Batman we have never seen before, and he knocks it out of the park as a vicious, menacing, intimidating, poignant and brutal vigilante.

2. Visuals: This is a fantastic looking movie. Some of the scenes are like orgasm for the eyes. But, that's something that we can all expect from a Zack Snyder movie.

3. Wonder Woman: I thought Gal Gadot did a good job. She added her own touch and small nuances to a few scenes. She is set up as a mystical woman, who even outsmarts Bruce Wayne. The next is her appearance as Wonder Woman, which was really cool. She looked like a well balanced combination of power and elegance. Needless to say, I'm excited to see Wonder Woman in her own solo movie, releasing in 2017.

4. Dark and Dreary Tone: They are trying to mirror real some of the real world issues and add a political thriller aspect to their movies, so the dark tone meshes well with this particular universe.

5. Final Showdown: The showdown between Batman and Superman is spectacular and I'm glad they nailed it.

6.Justice League Setup: Now, I don't have a huge problem with the way these characters were introduced, but it seemed to convenient and even a little lazy. I feel it could have been handled better.

Things I didn't like:

1.Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor: Many people would be surprised to know that Lex Luthor isn't actually playing Lex Luthor, he is portraying his son. However, that doesn't excuse that fact that Jesse Eisenberg didn't fit the bill at all. Jesse is a really good actor, but he was one of the most glaring failures of the movie. He was borderline autistic and insane whose motivation for killing Suerman aren't well explained. Luthor is supposed to be one of the most intelligent men in the DC universe. He is dark, vindictive, arrogant and egotistical. Also, he is the arch nemesis of Superman. But, I didn't get that feeling from portrayal. He is spontaneous quirkiness was unintentionally annoying.

2. Character Motivations: Some of the character motivations didn't make sense at all. Why does Lex want to fight Superman? They needed to delve deeper into that. Why is Batman so outraged by Superman? He has a personal vendetta against him. But, he goes crazy to do whatever it takes to destroy him. Some of his motivation was shown in the opening sequence, but Batman is called the "World's greatest detective". He analyzes each an every step and doesn't pick a fight unless he actually has to. Over here, Batman seemed to have an ego issue, out for the blood of Superman. Given his intellectual prowess and intuition, can't he see that despite the destruction of Metropolis, Superman is actually doing a lot of good for the world. I'm sorry, but again, his motivation to go against Superman was really lazy. He just picked the fight, so we could have an overblown visual spectacle.

3. Incoherent Presentation: This is another huge flaw of this movie. They were trying to juggle too many things in this movie. Batman's arc, Suerpman's arc, Batman and Superman conflict, Lex's evil schemes, Justice League setup, Doomsday, Lois Lane side plot, after effects of Man of Steel. It was a bit too much for just one movie, and boy did it bring the movie down.

4. Doomsday: Doomsday is another villain in the movie. You could call him a henchman of Lex Luthor, and I was really disappointed by this character. Here is a just a screaming maniac causing havoc on Metropolis, just used as a convenient tool to make Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman team up. Sad.

TLDR............... All in all, BvS is a mixed bag. There is greatness somewhere in this movie, but it doesn't live up to its full potential. After teasing this movie for all these years, the audience, especially a superhero nerd like me had higher expectations. Inconsistent is a word that can aptly describe this movie. Editing of the movie really holds it back. However, from a summer action stand point it is light years ahead of most the movies releasing at its time. The opening sequence and the Batman v Superman showdown is worth the admission price alone, so I feel it's certainly a movie you should check out cause there is a lot of enjoyment you will find in it. But, I like my movies to be deeper than just a 10 minute action scene. I wanted them to delve into the ideological difference between Batman and Superman. It's full of missed opportunities. But, it's full of great elements as well. Let's score is, shall we?

**Final Verdict: 7.2/10**

title: Movie is good:) Neither depressing nor amazing
review:
First off, I am a huge DC fan, but this review is certainly not biased.The movie is great in some aspects, and is disappointing in some others. However, overall, it delivers. The movie had the potential to be a lot more, and on that premise, it was disappointing. Nonetheless, it was good.

The first few minutes of the movie are absolutely brilliant. The first 2 minutes in particular are so brilliantly shot and I have never seen anything like it. The way they show Martha being shot is amazing. The movie starts off with the death of Bruce's parents, followed by Ben affleck going to Metropolis during the end of Man of Steel. From his perspective, the entire sequence looks amazing. The movie began to go a bit downhill from here. Overall, the plot of the movie is good, and the messages that Snyder wanted to convey are brilliant. However, the film does not do it very effectively. One major flaw of the film is its flow and sequencing. If the movie had just rearranged the scenes, it would have easily been better. The cast is amazing. Some might hate Jesse Eisenberg, but I felt he was really good as Lex Luthor. Affleck is my favourite batman to date and Henry delivers as well. Amy's acting is a bit sloppy at times, but overall, she did fine.

Ignore comments that say the movie feels packed BECAUSE OF THE JUSTICE LEAGUE INTRO. The movie did feel packed, but it certainly wasn't because of the justice league. The cameos were really short and yet effective. The action scenes are very well choreographed and will make fans go crazy. However, the fight between Batman and Superman was more because of Lex Luthor rather than what the movie had been trying to build up the entire time. Superman is merely trying to fight batman because he wants to save his mum, but the film tried to build up that Superman is going to Batman because he Batman thinks he is above the law. The idea of Batman viewing superman as a threat and superman viewing batman as a criminal is really great, but the film failed to convey that. This was a disappointing aspect. Wonder woman was really good and the trinity was amazing. It would have been better if the film flowed better.

I felt that the entire Doomsday part could have been avoided, not because the cgi was bad or it didn't make sense, but rather because they could've used the time to build on the existing characters. Superman dies and is hinted to be alive at the end and while some may find this a stupid idea, I feel that it's a really good intro to Justice League.

Overall, the film is way better than what critics have been saying, and is not as good as what fanboys are saying.

+ Cast + Action Sequences + The Trinity - Sequencing - Conveying of Batman and Superman's views of each other - Too packed

title: Not as bad as people say, not as good as we expected either
review:
So I will make this review as short as possible because I would like to keep it spoiler free while touching on major subjects. Now to begin, Batman V Superman is a well-executed film, with rather creative ideas behind it. However, DC did a gigantic mistake by not having more movies around all 3 characters so it would make sense.

Why is Batman the way he is here ? Sure us comic fans can assume and probably make sense, but what about the casual audience ? Yeah we needed a movie about this batman first

Why should I care so much about Superman ? We didn't see him adjust later on and weren't able to make sense after the first movie, so yes we needed another one from him as well.

Why on earth will I like this Wonderwomen ? for the very same reasons, we needed a movie.

Look at Marvel, despite being far inferior in content creation and quality, they did movies about their superheroes before so we can actually be hyped about what they offer. Instead of jamming everything in. Not to mention the multiple plot holes and stupid decisions.

That all being said, every character except Alex (Lex's son) delivered. Ben was a surprisingly good Batman and whatever shortcomings that were there came in with the writing and not his ability as an actor, on his end he was Solid. Overall decent movie, but feels rushed and doesn't have enough reason for us to care enough about the characters. The world building went wrong for DC

title: Overall Decent Film, do not go in thinking it will blow your mind.
review:
I just got back from seeing Batman V Superman earlier this afternoon. I've been anticipating it for about 3 years now ever since it was announce at SDCC 2013. I enjoyed it overall, but here are the pros and cons of this film

Pros: - As I'm sure you've heard, Ben Affleck IS BATMAN, he did an absolutely fantastic job as the dark knight and I hope his solo film pans out in the near future.

  • Visuals, being Snyder's forte, were reliably good as well. Very flashy and polished.


  • Cameos of other Justice League members are handled well


  • Gal Gadot is a superb wonder woman even though her screen time is relatively short


-Finally, this movie sets up the Justice League in an interesting way, while slightly rushed, it gets the job done and leaves you wanting more

Cons: - Editing, especially in the beginning of the movie is horrendous. The movie skips from scene to scene about every 5 minutes or so and is very disorienting

  • Doomsday battle in the third act is just a straight up CGI fest, nothing that hasn't been seen before.


  • Henry Cavill as Superman is nothing impressive, he does what he has to but his acting could definitely use improvement.


  • The dream sequences/knightmare sequences are just placed randomly and while a true DC comics fan as myself understood them, casual fans we'll be confused as hell when they pop up.


Overall, this film did what it needed to, to play catch up with Marvel a film this massive was the only way to accomplish that. I will recommend it on a entertainment level, but anything deeper than that I am a little iffy. Worth the price of admission but nothing to write home about. Psyched about justice league though. Enjoy the film for what it is!

title: A genuinely well-executed bad idea.
review:
To sum it all up: a lot of very talented artists did their very best to execute a very bad idea. I found it fun to watch, but it could have been so much more.

First the positive... Like I said this production was full of great artists, and they definitely were not phoning it in. Everyone involved in this movie gave it their all, and it shows with great photography, music, visual effects... And acting. Affleck in particular- his Batman is possibly the best live-action one yet. He's awesome, and I kinda feel bad for ever doubting him. I think a LOT of people will, if they approach his role in the movie with an open mind. Even Eisenberg's Luthor was the picture of an actor giving it everything he had, as much as it wasn't a Luthor I expected.

The thing is... This should have been a Batman movie instead of the ensemble piece it was. Or maybe Superman's second. Or Wonder Woman's first. There was plenty of characterization and concept to support any of those. That's the huge failing of this film- it tried to do way, WAY too much before it was time. That made it seem disjointed and cluttered and makes it really hard to get the motivations of the characters straight. It was kind of the opposite of The Hobbit, where a movie worth of material got inexplicably drawn out into three. This could have been a GREAT three movies, or maybe even four- but instead it was a jumbled one, especially with a terribly ill-advised climactic battle that felt like every major decision was made based on some kind of bland studio formula.

You can feel the fingerprints of the studio all over the film. This was an executive-built movie, born in a boardroom, I think, instead of a writer's room or a director's head. The writers, the director (who is going to be called to task on this, I am sure, but maybe not deservedly so), the actors, EVERYONE involved seemed like they gave it their all and tried to make the movie work... But it wasn't enough. You can't hide that it was a bad idea. You can't make something unearned seem earned. It just doesn't all work together, jumping into it cold like this.

It was a genuinely well-executed bad idea.

I'm torn on whether to say "see it and enjoy it for what it is, and hopefully we'll get a great Affleck Batman-only movie out of it later" or "don't see it, because studio executives need to learn that their over-involvement has consequences, don't reward them."

So I'm going to have to leave this one up to you. Overall, though, I enjoyed seeing so many people do their jobs so well and I think everyone involved in the movie deserves a lot of praise, even if their apparently weirdly disconnected bosses up on high may not entirely deserve theirs.

title: Watch this for Affleck's Batman
review:
I'd like to start out by blasting the editing team. You did an awful job! Plain awful! Alfred's dialogues in the first half sound like a kid reciting dialogues for a school play. I assume he had more lines which were edited out to fit the two and a half hour mark. A lot of scenes felt out of place, one in particular baffled me. We're watching Lex Luther on the screen and suddenly the scene transitions to Batman's dream which is emotional and in slow motion. It's like jumping from Star wars to Ben Hur in a flash and expecting the viewer to indulge in the scene instantaneously. I'm assuming again that this was editing team's stupidity.

Jesse eisenberg's performance was underwhelming. This part should've been played by someone who could appear imposing. I just couldn't take Jesse seriously in this one. I'm not a fan of Ben Affleck, but I've to agree that he did a very good job(Hear the resentment in my words? Yes, I'm a Bale fan. But this chap played the older Batman really well. Kudos to finding the new Batman!). Henry Cavill's Superman is just OK in my view, there's nothing spectacular about him in this movie either. His role and "performance" is just a continuation of man of steel. Wonder woman didn't have a huge role(hardly 10 lines), but Gal Gadot pulled it off. You can totally picture her as Wonder woman. Amy Adams' and Diane Lane's cameos were good too.

Although the action sequences were a lot gritty than any previous Batman series, I have a few gripes. There's an action sequence in Batman's dream where he fights soldiers (or mercenaries?) while looking for kryptonite. It was dismal! They had more than 2 years to make this movie and nobody saw that stupid fight sequence before releasing the movie? The soldiers attacking Batman have guns, but most of them forgot to use them. It was a close combat fist fight scene where everybody was like 15 feet away from each other. After Batman beats up one soldier, the next dazed soldier standing 15 feet away who has apparently forgotten he's holding a gun runs to Batman to get beaten up. And this continues till he beats up 3 more guys. Such things are unacceptable when you're making a big budget movie with so much time at your hands! The last big fight between doomsday and Batman, Superman and Wonder woman was reminiscent of the final fight from man of steel. There were barely any emotions to the whole scene. Just mindless action (some transformers inspiration!). In contrast, Batman vs Superman fight was enjoyable, it felt like the Bat really wanted to hurt Superman in that one. The fight scene following that was amazing! Batman gets shot multiple times wearing the bullet proof suit. It was Arkham Knight gritty.

The cinematography was commendable. With all the budget and cgi at their disposal, Hollywood is getting really good at transcending it's thoughts into a beautiful scene. Bat cave, the batmobile chase, Batman's high rise building shots, all looked really good.

I felt the story was good enough to set up the Justice league. Minus the stupid editing, Lex Luther and mindless action, it would've been an 8 rating movie. Watch this one for Affleck's Batman.

title: No one wanted this to be great more than me...
review:
Believe me, no one wanted this movie to be amazing more than me. I have never written a review before but I felt compelled to after seeing this movie. I am a huge DC fan, Superman is my favorite superhero, and I actually loved Man of Steel, but I was disappointed with this. This wasn't actually fully Zak Snyder's fault, the tone and acting in this movie was actually pretty good, and the fight scenes are beautiful. The problem was that DC and WB have gotten scared of Marvel's success and tried to rush a Justice League movie by making this movie a pre-JL jammed-packed mess. This is really 3-4 movie plot lines in a single movie. The fight scenes in this movie are really good, but we know Snyder can do that. There is just no meat here. As much as I loved Wonder Woman in the fight scene, every other scene with her out of costume seemed useless and the only purpose was to propel the JL angle. If this movie was purely about Batman and Superman and their fight, it would have been an excellent movie (besides Lex). Don't get me started on Lex... I like Jesse Eisenberg but the jittery psychopath take just didn't work for me. Besides all the JL stuff, there are a few script issues too. The way they revealed the other JL members was awful, so lazy. I loved the casting of Amy Adams as Louis Lane and loved her in MoS, but her character seemed lost in this movie, like they tried to find stuff for her to do. She was just annoying and Superman had to constantly go out of his way to save her, even in the middle of a fight! One of the best parts of this movie though was Affleck as batman. He killed it (and everyone else I guess ha). I'm actually excited for some solo movies with him as the Bat.

I know I gave this a 7, mostly out of nostalgia and how beautiful the movie looks. The problems with this movie are DC's fault in trying to rush Justice League and a messy script. They just forgot to make a good movie I guess.

title: Not bad, not great. Good superhero movie.
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is not as terrible as critics make it out to be. That being said, it isn't great either; it's just good.

Firstly, the cinematography in the movie is phenomenal. Zack Snyder has razor-sharp visuals that look beautiful. The score is fantastic. Batman's score really accentuates the type of Batman this is, brutal and terrifying. Superman's theme is a bit more uplifting and poignant. Wonder Woman's theme music when she arrives is just bad-ass.

The cast really stands out in this film. Particularly for me, Ben Affleck as the best Batman on screen, and Jeremy Irons as Alfred. They own their roles as though they've been playing the characters for a while.

Now, for the actual movie review: the movie is messy. The cast executes their scenes very well. But Zack Snyder's editing of the film makes the build-up to the Batman vs Superman battle lackluster. The dream sequences and the forced Justice League easter eggs take away from the build-up as well. In the end the actual battle ended up being very underdeveloped. While the action itself was awesome and exciting to watch, there wasn't as much substance to them. Because of the lack of setup, the fight didn't carry as much emotional weight. This effectively brings the movie down and keeps it from being great, as it could have been. A lot of potential was lost. The storytelling is also very rushed, as though there are 2-3 movies compacted into one.

Batman's character in the movie will be controversial as he breaks his rule many times and drops many bodies in the course of the movie. This new incarnation of Batman didn't really hurt the movie for me, but it may affect the opinions of many who expected something else.

While the characters are very well developed, the conflict between them is not as near as good as it could have been, once again, due to the lack of setup. The third act is explosive and may bother many due to the amount of CGI involved; I found it to be very awesome, but not everyone will like it. Wonder Woman's entrance is excellent and she serves a great role in the final battle, though her appearance in the movie before this was a bit forced and out of place.

The movie serves well as a springboard into a larger DC cinematic universe but at the expense of the quality of this movie. All in all, not as near as bad as critics are making it out to seem. It will be very under-appreciated, for now at least. This movie has me excited to see more of Wonder Woman and a standalone Batman film, and ultimately prepared me for Justice League.

"You're not brave. Men are brave."

6.5/10 is the final verdict. I can be talked up to a 7/10 or down to a 6/10.

title: "Greatest superhero movie ever" fan-boys need to calm down.
review:
POTENTIAL SPOILERS AHEAD:

First of all it's important to say that I really liked Man of Steel. I own the DVD/Blu-Ray, thought the movie laid out the origin story really well and it is a movie that is on my list of movies that I can re-watch whenever, irregardless if I've seen it recently.

Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice will not join MoS on that "rewatchable" list.

First of all, the film spends way too much time on the origin story of Batman. I understand that the "Dark Knight" trilogy is different interpretation of the DC character, but did the filmmakers of DvS really think the audience would forget how Batman "came to be"? (after a bunch of Batman movies in 90s and the more recent Dark Knight trilogy) This film which was a continuation of the MoS story line, had way too many flashbacks and dream- sequences about Batman. The Batman origin story in this film seemed rushed, it was really repetitive and crammed into a plot where it never truly fit.

Second, I am not sure if Ben Affleck wasn't a good Batman or that he wasn't a good fit for this style of Batman. He certainly lacked the Bruce Wayne swagger of previous Batman films (which I always thought should be an essential part to the overall character) and the film never created a relationship with Gotham but rather just vaguely alluded to Batman's presence in Gotham.

Third, the film needed MORE Wonder Woman. BvS teased her character really well throughout the movie, and she was awesome to watch in one of the main action sequences. But where Batman's background was dull, overbearing and repetitive, Wonder Woman's was sparse and indistinct.

With regards to the action/fight sequences, I thought they were done pretty well. These were comparable to MoS, a lot of CGI, but they really showed off the talents/strengths of the super-characters.

Overall I rate this a 6.7, 6.8 or 6.9 (7 rounded up). The movie was "alright"; I will continue to watch the upcoming DC Universe films, but this film should not be quoted as "one of the greatest superhero movies of all time" as I believe MoS and/or any of the Dark Knight trilogy films were better.

title: Not As Bad Or As Good As You've Probably Heard, I'm A Little Worried About The Justice League
review:
This is one of those movies that you just have to go see. If you read comic books or are a fan of super hero movies, it's almost like a rite of passage. You can't talk about it or give your opinion until you've seen it. I was definitely interested in seeing it, not only because it's the biggest movie of the year so far but because of the large disparity between the critical hatred and the fan love. I wanted to see which side I would fall on. I ended up disliking it more than I liked it but it's something that you need to see and decide for yourself.

*Minor Spoilers Ahead* The movie begins at the funeral for Thomas and Martha Wayne, their bodies are being carried to their graves. Young Bruce is being escorted by his butler Alfred (Jeremy Irons) but becomes upset and runs into the woods. While he's running away, we flashback to the unfortunate mugging with Thomas (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), Martha (Lauren Cohan) and Bruce leaving the theatre. The mugging happens with Thomas and Martha being shot and killed. Bruce continues to run away from the funeral and falls down a well disturbing some bats. He gets attacked by them but when it looks hopeless he starts to levitate out of the well (it's a dream sequence).

We then move years in the future when the epic battle between Superman (Henry Cavill) and General Zod (Michael Shannon). Entire office buildings are being destroyed and Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) lands in Metropolis via helicopter. He tries to drive to ground zero while talking to the man in charge of his building to evacuate the staff. He gets there but it's too late, the building collapses. Bruce tries to help out the victims including lifting a steel girder off an employee named Wallace Keefe (Scoot McNairy) and saving a little girl who was about to be crushed by falling concrete. He looks up to the sky, watching the battle of titans, full of rage.

Normally I start out with the positives but since most of what I didn't like was in the first half of the movie, I'll start with some negatives. I didn't like most of the plotting or characterization in Batman v Superman. There's a bunch of dream sequences put in that look cool but don't really fit (there are too many of them and they come in and out randomly). Looking past how awful Jesse Eisenberg is, there's almost no exploration of Lex's motivation for playing Batman and Superman against each other (they do say something but it's just tossed in there). There's almost no progression from Superman as a character (he now loves Lois and doesn't like Batman..... that's kind of it) and some of the dialogue is really groan worthy. Considering who this was written by, it's really disappointing (I took issue with most of Lex's dialogue, it's pretentious and besides the point). Don't take this as me just sitting there being impatient for the fight, it's just if the movie was going to take so long getting to it, I just wanted something substantial to hold my interest and I felt like I didn't get it.

Now at the same time, I thought the two standouts in the movie when it came to the characters were the new Batman and Wonder Woman. The fact that Batman is older and less restrained because of his anger is engaging and while a lot of people complained that he kills the bad guys, it fit for me considering his attitude. Wonder Woman was cool too. I wasn't sure at first but Gal Gadot was great and their inclusion of Wonder Woman was well done and well deserved. I actually enjoyed all the small clips that were there to lead up to the Justice League. They were also well done and they were a welcome distraction from other aspects of the movie.

When it comes to the acting, it's really uneven. I thought the best acting jobs from the main cast were Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot. Ben Affleck ended up being a good choice, I'm excited for his solo Batman movie and Gal Gadot was a good mix of being strong and yet mysterious enough that you wanted to know more about her character. A lot of the supporting parts were well performed and I liked Jeremy Irons, Amy Adams, Laurence Fishburne and Diane Lane. They're all great. Henry Cavill was decent but he's even more emotionless in this one. Jesse Eisenberg on the other hand was just terrible. He's normally a great actor (he was great in Zombieland) but he was so skittish and off key with the rest of the movie, when he appeared I was always covering my eyes or just wishing he would go away.

So I really didn't like the first half of the movie but in defense of Batman v Superman, the actual fight between them and the climactic battle with Doomsday were both pretty good. While Zack Snyder has made both good and bad movies, he does always seem to know his large scale action and this movie is no exception. Although Doomsday wasn't visually interesting and his appearance is really sudden, the actual battle is pretty sound. All the characters get something to do and while I question some things about it (how did Lois know they needed that spear again when no one told her how important it was?) it was a satisfying payoff.

I'm not a DC hater (I liked Man of Steel) but this movie was disappointing. I can see why opinions are so different from person to person. I'm still psyched for Suicide Squad but considering all the hype around this film, the fact the same people are in charge of the Justice League may not be a good thing. This movie should have been something epic but it fell short.

title: Awesome set up for the Justice League
review: So I just finished watching BvS for the second time, so here's my non spoilery review. Oh and be easy, it's my first IMDb review. Here goes. So I saw Batman V Superman Dawn of Justice for the second time today. The first time around watching it, I honestly just left the cinema in a state of awe. I couldn't sum up my feelings for it, did I just witness one of the best depictions of comic book to big screen?! Or did it fall short of being an Epic, all out battle between the 2 most iconic DC characters of all time!? And I have to say, it's a bit of both really. That's not just me sitting on the bench. This is me really trying to sum up my feelings in a way where it takes everything into consideration. Not just what happens in this movie, but what is to be expected from future projects. I will say this though, Snyder had a near impossible task of using one movie to literally set up the whole of the Justice League, and that is where I have to give him credit. The set up is very very good. Now that I've seen it a second time, I'm able to really process everything I've seen and truly understand what we have in store for us. We were pretty much given a glimpse of Wonderwoman and her powers (btw is she going to be able to fly?) and the other character cameos, not to mention that Flash sequence. All for the bigger role at play, what it is we're going to get from the solo Wonderwoman/ Batman/ Flash/ Aquaman/ Cyborg movies and not to mention the Justice League movies. We all know what's coming and it was done in a way that we have to really pull all of the pieces together. If you're a comic book fan, then doing that is easy, but I can imagine for someone who isn't necessarily a comic book fan, not finding it as easy to connect the dots. The movie is essentially an Introduction for the rest of the Justice League rather than just a self contained Batman V Superman movie. I do think that if Snyder focused on the movie as being just that one movie, I really think we would have had something a lot more special, and I mean that in the sense of just really focusing on introducing Batman, Superman and Wonderwoman, leaving out the Justice League aspects. I can totally understand why people might feel that the movie may not have gelled well and the fact that it raises a lot of unanswered questions. But I think that was the purpose of it, to have questions that need to be answered in Justice League Part 1 and 2. The movie had stunning visuals and an amazing score. The depiction of Batman, Superman and Wonderwoman was nigh on perfect, creating the dream Trinity on the big screen with Ben Affleck and Gal Gadot doing a really great job at bringing those characters to life like we've never seen them before! Affleck really made it his own and with the short glimpse we saw of Gal's Wonderwoman really making me look forward to the Wonderwoman movie that much more! I will stick to my initial guns from seeing the trailers, there was way too many spoilery moments, which in a way, ruined the whole experience. It left a lot of OMG moments quite stale, like the introduction of Wonderwoman and the Batman fight scene. However, this is not an issue at all seeing it the second time around. I've deliberately left out Lex Luthor because I really don't know how to sum up Snyder's vision for this character. I honestly think they miscast-ed for that role, but that's all I'm going to say. Doomsday was beast mode, but really could have been made to look a lot better, more in line with the comic book version. Although his powers and strength and abilities were very much in line with the comics. I do think though there was so much story to tell and literally no more time to tell it, which is why I guess we're having an extra 30 minutes added on to the R-rated Blu-Ray Ultimate Cut coming in July. All in all, I thought the movie brought the characters to life in a really great way, which would make any comic book lover proud. And it paves the way for the rest of the DCEU, really making you think about and get excited for what is yet to come. If you've gone into this movie with the Marvel formula expectation then you will definitely be disappointed. Snyder and Co. are doing things very differently to Marvel and that is not a bad thing. Things will start to make more sense as the movies release and we start to realise why things were set up the way they were. It was definitely entertaining to watch and a true Cinematic experience and I will be seeing it again.

title: Not as bad as the Critcs are saying...
review:
OK! Just ahead of me doing an Audio Only review on YouTube on my 'Just Another Review Show' Channel - Still in its infancy, I thought I would do my usual and share a few thoughts - Relatively spoiler free - on Batman Vs Superman...

And I am going to be brutal and honest IT WAS... Actually quite good! Criticisms first! How many bloody times do we need to see the Batman Origin Story? His parents were murdered in front of him as a child... We get it! The first 10 or 15 minutes is the same story AGAIN! ENOUGH ALREADY! Secondly, If you are one of the many people who has watched the Trailer expecting an all action set piece - FORGET IT! YOU WILL NOT LIKE THIS MOVIE!!! The Trailers are very misleading! This film is all about atmosphere and build up... It takes time to get to the meat of the story, hence many critics saying its Boring and Too Long...

NO! Actually its not, Thats GOOD STORY TELLING! I have to be honest, much as I tried to avoid the hype train, Even I went in expecting things to happen a lot sooner than they did... So I am giving you fair warning - DON'T TRUST THE TRAILERS! The film is all about Build up and pay off!!! If you go in expecting that, you will enjoy the film a lot more...

Finally, BaGhoul Scares!Yes, this movie has a freaking Jumpscare!!! For crying out loud Hollywood - Has this clichÃ© not done its rounds enough? Bruce Wayne having a nightmare and a bloody Jumpscare? OK! Credit where it's due.. It did make me jump - Even though its so damn obvious that its coming... But it was NOT NEEDED!!! END OF! So, That's the bad out of the way... Whats good about it? The Build up, Its atmospheric - Emotional, Maybe the more cynical and the young will not get affected by that but for me as a father, there are many points that really tug at the heart...

A lot of people seem to be moaning about Ben Affleck's Batman as well... Personally, I liked him! He looks the part, and plays it damn well...

Henry Cavill as Superman - If you hated Man Of Steel then you are NOT going to be on board for this film, so don't bother but again - I think he puts in a perfect performance.

The shocking castings, Amy Adams returns as Lois Lane - And she once again portrays her really well... So no shock there! I am just finding hard to get used to her in serious roles after seeing her in The Muppets... But yeah she is good! And Jessie Eisenberg as Lex Luthor... Possibly the one casting EVERYONE was worried about!!! He comes across to me as Jon Simms as 'The Master' In Doctor Who (If you have not seen them, Check them out AFTER you have seen the ORIGINAL Master in The Classic Episodes with tom Baker and Peter Davidson)...

He walks a really fine line of being slightly camp to overly maniacal... And he walks that line well! Very Well! It was the one casting choice I actually thought would fall flat on its backside, but instead I was enthralled!!! It was sad not to see more from him and the diabolical plot - Well they are far better than Gene Hackman's Real Estate plans in the 1978 Superman!!! Unsung Heroes so far - Wonder Woman's appearance - Yeah! You can already see the reviews out there - She REALLY IS BAD ASS! If I was worried about a Wonder Woman Movie before, I am not now... I can really see it working but will want to see a Prequel before anything else! Obvious clues for the future - I should warn of Spoilers but we have the Internet and we all know its coming... The first glimpses of Aquaman, The Flash and Cyborg...

There is no avoiding it - We all knew a Justice League Movie was on the way so I do not really think its a spoiler... Disappointments here - NOT Linking The Flash into their already established show (Why not? Its done no harm to MARVEL with Agents of Shield!)...

Plus Points - A Cyborg Origin Story is definitely going to happen in my view - Or needs to... And Jason Samoa as Aquaman - It is only a brief glimpse but again I am ACTUALLY LOOKING FORWARD to the movie even though I have NEVER LIKED AQUAMAN! So, Long and the short - The hype train has done its worst and the film due to that is going to be VERY polarising... If you are after an all action epic, Avoid it as you will be plain ANNOYED! But if you want a slow build up to a good pay off (I want to say great pay off, but I didn't really care much for the final battle... Except for seeing Wonder Woman!) then go in with open eyes and I am sure you will like it.

Overall, 6 out of 10 from me - Mainly due to the Hype train....Would have been a easy 7 or even 8 had it not been built up for a fall!

title: An Honest Opinion on BvS: Dawn of Justice
review:
To start, I might alienate some viewers by saying that I actually really enjoyed Man of Steel. Growing up as a kid, I always disliked Superman because I related to him the least compared to other superheroes. Even my elementary school self could realize that a "man" (well, alien) who was the symbol of good and justice was an ideal too good to be true. As Lex Luthor says in BvS, "If God is all-powerful, he cannot be all-good. If he is all-good, then he cannot be all-powerful." Therefore, it was refreshing to see that both Man of Steel and BvS portray Superman in a more human light. Is this portrayal truthful? I don't know; I haven't read the comic books or explored enough of Superman's backstory to judge its validity. But for an outsider who enjoys superhero movies, I liked Superman in Man of Steel and Batman vs. Superman.

While we're talking about superheroes, I'm a bit more conflicted about Batman. Ever since Nolan's masterpiece of a trilogy, it seems like both Marvel and DC are trying to one-up each other on who can make a darker superhero and story. Batman here is the same thing; Ben Affleck brings a Batman even darker than the one Christian Bale brought to life. And this is both good and bad; while Ben Affleck does a wonderful job portraying the brooding rage behind the handsome face of Bruce Wayne and the down-to-earth bone-breaking fighting Batman is so loved for (if you see the warehouse fight scene, you know what I mean), that is all Affleck does. Yet AGAIN, we see the famous origin scene where Bruce's parents are shot and killed, and we see Bruce's fear of bats in the scene right after, but then the story skips ahead. Out of nowhere, Batman appears. No motive, no reason, no sense. One more complaint I have about this Batman is that he is too one- dimensional. Yes, Batman is angry; yes, Bruce Wayne is angry. The problem is, that is the one emotion they have. What makes Batman interesting is not only the fact that he is badass, but also that he must go through a spectrum of emotion as a vigilante. Pain. Fear. Anger. The few moments of lightheartedness. These variations made the Batman in the Dark Knight Trilogy so interesting. Ben Affleck does a wonderful job of being angry, but that's it. No other emotion whatsoever. That made me alienate Batman in BvS.

Stepping back to look at the movie as a whole, the only thing I have to say is that I'm upset. So much wasted potential in this movie. The plot COULD have been engaging and relevant; after all, Superman's fight with Zod has consequences that must be answered to. Instead, the movie drops the whole issue after the court case bombing. After that, the movie becomes a CGI punch-fest, between Batman and Superman and the Justice League Trio against Doomsday, who was an awful villain. Speaking of villains, Jesse Eisenberg was simply the wrong choice for Lex Luthor. A lot of people think he acted poorly in this movie; I disagree. Eisenberg did a wonderful job portraying his character, which was an AWFUL interpretation of Lex Luthor. Eisenberg plays not the cold, calculating nemesis of Superman but instead an unwatchable, cringeworthy imitation of the Joker. And Doomsday was a nightmare (not in a good way). Jesus, the CGI explosions from Doomsday are enough to give Michael Bay a run for his money. Zach Snyder legitimately hurt my teenage eyes during the movie. Wonder Women was cool and fairly well-done, but just like Batman, there is no back story on her character. She just...appears. The new Wonder Women movie better explain a lot of things.

If you're still reading this, I'll leave with one final message. If you love Batman, Superman, CGI, and an unhealthy amount of set-up for the Justice League, you will like this movie. While the explosions may tell you otherwise, Zach Snyder is no Michael Bay, and his movie has all the pieces for a solid movie. BvS is watchable. It's by no means bad. But if you are a moderate superhero fan (like me) or an outsider, you will struggle to like this movie. At the end of the day, BvS had the impossible task of setting up a whole Cinematic Universe over the course of 2 hours and 30 minutes, and it both succeeds and fails at this goal. If you watch it with that in mind, you won't be as upset when you walk out of the theater.

title: Good Movie with Some Things Off
review:
WARNING: This review contains SPOILERS. If you don't want to know the stuff occurring in the movie in advance, or the movie ruined for you, skip this review now.

"Batman Vs. Superman" is a good action movie. With respect to the story, the story's one of two things where the movie shined on the most... the second being the action scenes, of course.

It's a revamp of Batman's story, since they retold his origin that differs from that of "Batman Begins". After that, they then showed that Bruce Wayne was in Metropolis during the events of "Man of Steel", and deaths and destruction under Superman's watch that made Bruce's blood boiled for up to eighteen months, leading up to the confrontation between Batman and Superman.

As for Superman, "Batman Vs. Superman" is a sort of "Man of Steel 2", since it continues from where Superman/Clark Kent left off. Being a super-powered superhero, and some events here and there in the world, people question if Superman should continue being a vigilante, and some recent deaths by bullets in Africa were his fault. It's made worse when Lex Luther showed interest in portraying him as a "devil" to the public, and a fellow senator. He'd even gone as far as discovering Kryptonite, intending to use it on Superman.

The movie is also a sort of prequel to "Justice League", as the title "Dawn of Justice" implies. It introduces us to the other members of the group, starting with Wonder Woman who had the most, and most important, presence throughout the film. Bruce Wayne managed to steal, and decrypt, files from Lex Corp, revealing details of the other heroes like Flash, Cyborg, and Aquaman. Bruce's/Batman's goal is to reach out to these other members, and create new means of delivering "justice", especially with the scrutiny both he and Superman faced by the public.

And, of course, the action scenes, and the dark moments like Lex framing Superman by blowing up his Capitol Hill hearing, were other examples of what kept viewers glued to their seats.

But, that doesn't mean that the movie's perfect.

Firstly, Lex Luther, or "Alexander", doesn't sound like what you expect Lex, both comics and TV, to sound like. He sounded like a troubled teenager taking over a company at age nineteen, and he has hair... till he was thrown to jail. How he twists things around in his favor, and plants the bomb in Capitol Hill, the actor should have been reserved as the Joker for a new Batman movie... since he was a lot like Heath Ledger's Joker in "The Dark Knight".

Another thing they did wrong was introducing Doomsday way too early, and a lot of us who'd seen the newer trailers had that same sentiment. In the comics, and the animated movie after them, Doomsday showed up when the Justice League was already in existence. In this film, that hadn't happened yet. This kills off potential, and epic, Superman trilogy, or the chance of seeing Superman's black-and-white uniform. It's good to have "Justice League", but I'd also like Batman and Superman to have their separate movies showing more of the said characters at the same time. With Marvel, we have "The Avengers", but we also have "Iron Man" and "Captain America", both of which show more of the said characters and their respective worlds and enemies. (Did I mention that Batman got revamped from the originals?)

And finally, the movie's more like "Lex Luther Vs. Superman" more than "Batman Vs. Superman". The movie focuses more on Lex defaming Superman to engineering Doomsday to kill him off. For some reason, probably to buy time to finish engineering Doomsday, or as a payback for Batman stealing his Kryptonite, he talked Superman into killing off Batman, in exchange for his mother's freedom. Batman fighting Superman, although cool that Batman armed himself with the Kryptonite he stole, and the armor suit, only occurred this one night... excluding the prophetic dream Bruce Wayne had while decrypting Lex Corp's files.

To conclude, the movie's story, although with some details off, from Lex to Doomsdays, was great as a Justice League origin film, along with the action and dark scenes here and there. The acting and soundtracks were great too. Hence, if you want a superhero movie, this is one of my personal recommendations.

title: Batman v Superman: my (spoiler-free) review
review:
Maybe the deluge of bad reviews sufficiently lowered my expectations, or maybe I'm just not enough of a fanboy to feel too outraged by Snyder's interpretation of these iconic heroes, but I did thoroughly enjoy the movie. Enough so that I would watch it again in the cinemas.

It was always going to be an uphill battle for Snyder to bring this "clash of the titans" to the big screen. Both Batman and Superman have such a huge fan base that a certain amount of expectation will permeate the audience. Add to that the mountain of hype surrounding its release and you get a summit that even Batman would find daunting to surmount.

In this case, perhaps all the negative reviews actually worked in the movie's favor. I went in expecting to be disappointed and came away feeling, if not 'blown away', then pleasantly surprised.

Ben Affleck did a good job holding up the torch that Christian Bale passed on, presenting a more mature and disenfranchised Bruce. Gal Gadot was likable as Wonder Woman, if a little two dimensional. Henry Cavill was Henry Cavill. But the supporting characters weren't given enough to work with. Laurence Fishburne felt unnecessary and Michael Caine was just better as Alfred.

There were moments I had to roll my eyes. I won't spoil anything but if you've seen the movie you know what I'm talking about. Too many clichÃ©s and lackluster character development. Luthor was basically Superman's Joker. The characters sometimes behave in incredulous ways. But there were also moments that were just gleefully fun to watch.

Finally, at roughly two and a half hours I still left the cinema feeling the movie was too short for what they wanted to do. Parts felt rushed and conflicts arose and ended too abruptly for the sake of pacing that if felt like the film could have benefited from another 30 minutes or so. However, the purpose of a movie of this type is first and foremost to entertain and, for me at least, I'd say it achieved its purpose. If you're on the fence because of all the naysayers out there I'd say go ahead and give it a try anyway. If you go in with an open mind and a light heart you might just be surprised.

title: Could have been better
review: Though not a comic book fan, a lot of us has put a lot of expectations in Batman vs Superman. I think the producers did a good job in presenting the world seeing Superman as a powerful being, a god to many, and yet, as an alien, not being totally sure of his intentions. He shows kindness towards humanity, not just locally, but everywhere. Still, to most people, it is not clear why he is helping humans. People don't know about his childhood in this planet. So we have this powerful alien among us doing this acts of god out of the blue? No agenda? So governments do have the right to question that. Then Bruce Wayne is entangled in this story. Writers could have done a better job actually taking it to an emotional level. But Bruce seems more concerned about his financial tower going down in rubles than about the people who works there for him. Batman at no time shows that he is actually caring for people. Quite opposite, he is depicted as a cruel vigilante troubled by his own nightmares and taking revenge on bandits. So you have Batman planning on taking Superman out of action because of the collateral damage during that battle? He, of all, being who he is, should understand there is always going to be tough choices and good people would die fighting evil. But he chooses to obsess over the idea and totally get played by Lex. So its very strange when after having Superman at his feet, merciless as he is, he totally gives up on the idea of killing him just because Clarks mother is in danger? So Superman shouldn't be checked anymore? Very bad script here. And at last, wonder woman has no story what so ever and you have no clue why she is there, why she leaves, and then comes back. So, good action and good story, but could have been told better.

title: BATMAN vs. SUPERMAN / Boring vs Satisfying?
review: f you have elected to see this movie for the intense fight between Batman and Superman and the action scenes, you will get it! Now if you are a movie goer looking for more than the kick butt action, like me, it will not deliver. The movie was long with terrible pacing; jumping from scene to scene which created nothing but confusion. The amount of endless dream scenes, even though understanding their purpose, were not needed in my opinion. The actors on a whole were not bad and offered an adequate portrayal of the characters in the film, but fell victim to some average writing and poor directing. Ben Affleck portrayed the ominous character of Batman, but his screen presence was mediocre at best. Him as Bruce Wayne,the secret identity of Batman, was fine. When Batman was first introduced in this film he was true to his character, operating in the shadows, hearing only screams, and making a quick escape. This did not hold true as he transitioned into a loud, running with weapons ablaze, and just having all-out brawls.Though a lot of fans praised the new darker portrayal of Batman who has no problem taking lives I wasn't that impressed. Jesse Eisenberg, I feel may get the "short end of the stick" for his Lex Luther role, because he displayed the character in different demeanor, as he portrayed more of a psychotic genius having a joker type feel to it. I will admit I was skeptical at the beginning of the film, but as it progressed Lex Luther became likable. Gal Godat as Wonder Woman didn't have enough screen time to deem her good or bad for the role but I didn't dislike what I saw. Overall the movie was below average and probably slightly better than "Man of Steel."

title: Not bad... but not good
review:
Simply put, this film was OK. Affleck and Gadot portray Batman and Wonder Woman well, but to be honest Wonder Womans inclusion in the film felt forced - as did all references to future JL characters. The film opens well but then starts chopping and changing the scenes so rapidly it felt like only half the story was being told. Because of the editing the audience doesn't get a chance to really develop a relationship with the characters - they are just delivering 10 second snippets of information to progress the plot. Lois and Alfred are good examples of this - despite what should be intricate roles in any Superman or Batman movie both characters scenes were clipped to the point of irrelevance and neither of the superb actors playing the parts had a chance to shine. Cavill as Superman was much the same as he was in MoS - average. You don't really feel for the character at all.

For me the worst part of the movie was Lex Luthor. Not because of Eisenbergs acting - he gave it his all, but because the Lex character just didn't work. His character development was non-existent and everybody I saw the movie with agreed the character was more like the Riddler or Joker (albeit a tame one), but it just was not Lex Luthor.

The CGI was great in places, poor in others. The fight scenes were epic as promised and the action was very fast paced and visually impressive. Fight scenes with Batman felt more fluid than Bales batman who always looked really stiff in battle, although Afflecks bulky bat took a bit of getting used to.

It really was a hit-and-miss movie. I wanted it to be better, but didn't feel stiffed for my ticket price. If they had just focused on the bat vs supes and not had to force the JL stuff the film would have been much better and a more reasonable running time, and we might have had a chance to love the new versions of these characters instead of just follow them.

Slow down DC and let your characters live to their fullest!

title: Aversive ! Juiceless ! Stony !

title: A missed opportunity
review: This was a film that I was very excited about seeing, I thought the casting of Ben Affleck in the role of Batman was a good one, he is an interesting and talented actor and I thought he would bring a new dimension to the role following on from Christian Bale. It is shame that whilst he is good in the film he is never given the opportunity to shine and that is down to the films shoddy narrative and structure. You go to a superhero film to be thrilled not to be overwrought by the heroes constantly moping about their actions and what has happened in their past. In this film not only do you see the death of Bruce Wayne's parents once but at least three to four times. Even during the middle of one of the major fights in the film, it pauses to show his parents' death - again!. This constant brooding of the main characters is the films major plot for over an hour of the first part of the film. You end up wanting to scream, yes his parents died now go and kick the hell out of superman!!!! Even Superman is not immune to this brooding (at one point he inexplicably ends up taking to his dead father on a mountain). So for the first hour its brooding, then we get the best part of the film, the showdown between the two main characters. This is handled extremely well and if you're a fan of the comic A Dark Night Returns, you're going to love the nod to its battle between the two. The final 40 minutes of the film are good but there is absolutely no reason for the character of Doomsday in the film. It really comes across as a way of adding another bout of city destruction which kinda ruins the whole plot of why Batman hates Superman in the first place. The structure of the film would have been much stronger if they had used Wonder Woman to calm the situation between the two rather than Lois Lane. The other weak point is that they are relying too much on people knowing the characters and their DC counterparts. If you don't know them then you are going to miss a lot and end up even more confused by the plot. Thirty minutes could have easily been cut from this film to give it a much tighter structure. It's worth seeing and there are some good parts to it. But Warner and DC need a lesson from Marvel on how to make superhero films that are fun to watch.

title: Special effects are awesome but the film's story is not up to the mark
review: The film's special effects are one of the best that we have seen this year. The fight sequences are amazing and well thought of. But the main problem of this film is the story. The story lacks a spine and is too simple for characters like batman, superman and lex luthor. Wonder woman's role is neglected and is given less time to be explored. The character of batman cannot be compared to Nolan's batman simply because of the more complexity and nuances of the latter. Superman's role is good and he is seen to be reevaluating his principles and his purpose. Ben Affleck's acting is deplorable. He is drab, emotionless and looks lost in the film. A better casting for batman should have been done. Overall, the film delivers on the big studio tag . With adrenaline pumping fight sequences, great special effects and good acting by Jesse Eisenberg and Amy Adams it is an above average film. The things that don't take it to a higher level is the quite poor story, simple plot line and poor acting of Ben Affleck .

This movie does a lot of thing very right but unfortunately it does more than few things wrong. Let's start with what I loved Ben Affleck is in my opinion the best live action Batman yet and I am happy to say he proved all the neighsayers wrong. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman was amazing she stole every scene she was in and I am incredibly excited to see her movie. Henry Cavill and Amy Adams continue to be amazing in the roles of Superman and Lois Lane respectively. Jesse Eisenburg as Lex Luthor Jr was really interesting. Let's just say that he doesn't play Lex Luthor but the son of Lex Luthor and I could write an entire review of just Jesse Eisenburg,and over all this film makes me really excited to see what else DC has in store for us, also before I move on to the bad I just want to add the the action sequences were amazing and visually the movie was stunning. But this movie does have its problems for one the pacing at times is a bit wonky and the writing and editing could have been a lot better. This movie also tries to pack a lot in 2 hours and 33 minutes a lot of the Justice League stuff felt really shoehorned in despite the fact that I did enjoy the cameos from Flash,Aquaman, and Cyborg. Overall, despite the movie not living up to it full potential I felt that it was extremely entertaining and I recommend this movie

title: Could have been better!
review:
Starting on a slightly frustrating note. I don't have to spoil anything for you. They already did with those three trailers. They really need to re-think their strategy next time. The success value of such super hero films (where there are more than one central character) is particularly based on certain 'moments' in the film, unless of course you have a super brilliant script at your disposal.

Now if you kill those beautiful moments - a couple of months even before the release of the movie - then that literally kills the movie upon release.

The script is ordinary in many ways. Some really 'fantasy' stuff happens (Luthor creating Doomsday was easier than someone stirring up a lemon shake).

Clichéd and predictable ending didn't help either. I felt both the central characters had very little 'motivation' to hate the other one.

But everything said .. it is Superman Vs Batman .. If you like either or both of them then the film is worth a watch. I felt the film is more Batman oriented though Superman saves the day ultimately.

The actors fit well in their roles. Ben Affleck exceeded expectations easily. WonderWoman has been gracefully incorporated into the scheme of things (her backstory pending)

Lex Luthor - acted well but was different from the Luthor that I know - Dark Knight's Joker invariably crept in - and eventually ended up a lunatic instead of that serious villain that we all know - who had a reason (however childish that may be) to hate Superman in the comics.

The BG Scores were good. The action and the CGI was good. Still many things lacked clarity (unlike Avengers where we could 'see the fight')

To summarize - I enjoyed the film but left with a dropping head. Had there been NO TRAILERS it would have been a 7.5 movie. Now it's just a 7 for me.
