title: Not as bad as the press makes it out to be, but certainly flawed
review:
I saw Batman Vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice on opening day in Beijing (where I currently work). I didn't have particularly high expectations going as, as I couldn't help but notice that it has been universally panned in the press. However, after having seen it, I personally don't think it's entirely awful. Certainly, the movie has a few notable problems. A few moments would have been better off cut out of the script. Really, in my opinion, the movie's main fault was simply that it was too ambitious. It set out to do too much all at once, leaving much of it feeling rather rushed and half-baked.

The movie gives the impression of being the product of a team of writers who banged out a first draft in a weekend and tried to throw as many ideas (and characters) in as they could, then didn't think to revise, instead immediately heading to the studio to shoot what they had. That's probably not far from the truth.

BvS could have been a very good movie, and there are a few enjoyable moments in it, to be sure. But the problem is, there were enough ideas and characters in this movie to set up a proper trilogy, which, I feel, is what they should have done. Instead, the studio tried to cram everything into one two and half hour clip show, which leaves the whole affair feeling overstuffed and, at times, completely incoherent.

This feeling of incoherence becomes especially apparent through a blatant non-sequitur which is neither explained nor even referenced at any time after it transpires. It just happens. End of story. If you see the movie, you'll probably understand what I'm writing about it. Obviously, DC is hoping to use this movie as a springboard for a series of movies in a shared universe, similar to what Marvel has accomplished. What I find refreshing about the movie is that it doesn't tap into the by now very familiar Marvel movie aesthetic. In recent Marvel movies, the productions are all very similar. They're rather banal affairs which seem to have emerged from the same playbook. Cookie cutter film making. No risks are taken, everyone is friends, and live happily together and don't think too much in their delightful PG-13 world. DC's movie is darker, and certainly more philosophical. The only philosophy to be found in a Marvel movie is that evil must be destroyed. Cue explosions. DC's movie motions to question the definition of evil and dabbles in moral ambiguity. And then it cues explosions.

My impression is that a Marvel movies delivers a narrative which goes, in essence, "Evil? Well, I got a gun! Boom Boom Boom! Good job, guys. High five!" End of story.

In contrast, DC movies, if BvS is any indication for the future, seem to be delivering a message more so akin to, "Evil? Well, I got a gun! ... But wait...er... What is evil? I mean, really... ah... ah, hell. Boom Boom Boom! ... Okay... er... good job? ... Ah, er... Well, uh, yes. Good job. Yes. Er, good job. I feel like I need to shower..."

I wonder somewhat if the reason the movie has been receiving so much bad press is simply because it doesn't follow along the mindless action train format set by the recent Marvel movies.

Honestly, this is hardly the worst Batman film on record, thanks largely to Joel Schumacher's earlier, abysmal, efforts in the franchise. It's not even the worst Superman film. Not by a long shot. Remember Superman IV? Pray that you don't.

One thing I find very interesting is that Snyder's Batman is not afraid of using guns and getting dirty. This is not the idealistic Dark Knight which we have seen in more recent films. In Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight, Batman goes to extraordinarily lengths to defeat the Joker without killing him. This idealism is gone in the new Bat. I feel the new take on the character would rather just have him blow a hole in the Joker's skull and be done with it.

This also leads me to ask, then, is this really Batman? Because Batman, to me, is not just a character, but a way of thinking. That is, defeating the darkness in humanity without succumbing to it one's self. That was one of the primary lessons in the Nolan's trilogy, at the very least. Perhaps this thematic change is just a reflection of a changing America. Out with the idealistic times of the Obama presidency and its message of hope and change, in with Trump and his message of ... well... "f*** you!"

Is it, perhaps, just a sign of the times; the product of a fatigued America which has given up on hope? Perhaps. Batman Vs Superman is not a bad film. But it could have been a much better one.

My personal rating: 7.9 out of 10

title: Batman v Superman (minor spoilers)
review:
First of all, sorry for my bad English.

We live in a time where comicbookmovies pop up a couple of times every year with characters I've read about since I was a kid.

Never would I have though I'd see wonderwoman, ant-man, aquaman or even captain America or iron man on the big screen, but now I have and I love it.

It's hard to see a movie being taken over by CGI and impossible camera angels when they could've just used practical effects and a camerarig.

I must admit I was skeptical entering the cinema after films like Jurassic World and The force awakens ruined so much from my childhood and avengers: age of ultron and Ant-man were kinda weak and all over the place. But this was really something else. It's a dark and beautiful story about fear of the unknown. I loved the story, from Superman and Batman's point of view. I loved how they handled WonderWoman and the small Aquaman, Cyborg and Flash cameos. I loved the pace, even though it could've been longer and the music was perfect all way through. Louise Lane and Alfred where great in smaller roles and Jessie Eisenberg was good as Lex Luthor, even though he was a little to much from time to time.

The real star of the movie was Ben Afflecks Batman, the best Batman yet, perhaps the first really good Batman on the big screen even though I thought Christian Bale did a good job too.

Henry Cavill is the best Superman yet and gets a lot of room even though, sometimes, especially the first hour of the movie, it feels like a Batman movie.

As I mentioned before I don't like the overuse of CGI (The Hobbit, Avengers, Jurassic World.) It looks bad, especially in daylight, but here, everything is dark and gritty, which is the perfect way to use it, that's how Jurassic Park used it and that's why people still think those effects holds up today.

I feel like Zack Snyder didn't listen to the critique from Man of steel (another great movie) and that's a good thing. He didn't change direction, he just did the same routine with more characters. Its the same dark tone and the heroes still kill people - or at least Batman does and that gives him more deep. It feels like he has given up a bit, like he is the judge, jury and executioner.

When they introduced Doomsday it felt a little to much, but he grew on me, like everything else in this movie. Perhaps they should have waited to introduce him till' the next movie, but the way it all happens work so well that I accept it.

I don't understand the bad critique for this movie, but I don't care, this is a masterpiece from beginning to end and perhaps the best movie in this genre I've ever seen - I can't wait for Justice League to see more of Zack Snyders dark and gritty DC universe. I give it a nine, not because im a fanboy, but because it deserves it, it's almost a perfect movie in a time when comicbookmovies start to feel a little repetitive.

title: Batman v Superman is one for the fans.
review:
Fearing the actions of Superman are being left unchecked, The Dark Knight takes on the Man of Steel, while the world wrestles with what kind of a hero it really needs. With a new threat arising, it's up to Superman and Batman to set aside their differences and stop the destruction of the world, their home. With a new cast of heroes and villains joining the universe that was setup brilliantly in Man of Steel, Batman v Superman cranks it up to 11, and as enjoyable as it may be, if falters along the way.

Dawn of Justice sees a new Bruce Wayne / Batman introduced for this universe, and i'm happy to say Ben Affleck nails this role as an older, more aggressive vigilante. His side of the story is well developed, there's a solid foundation on why he doesn't trust Superman and how he goes about planning his downfall. It may take a solo film to show how he became this way, but for now Affleck may be the best Batman yet. The new Alfred in Jeremy Irons and the returning Laurence Fishburn as Perry White are the older, wiser characters that provide much needed words of advice for our heroes. Superman himself Henry Cavill has a slightly lesser time of progressing his character this time round, and actually looks rather stoic in some key scenes. Yet him and Amy Adams' Lois Lane are the real heart of this story, and the closing scenes may get you a bit teary eyed. Gal Gadot as Wonder Woman is very good, even though she only has a dozen lines in the whole film. To see her in action during the last act is probably the best vindication for her casting. The inclusion of minor roles for Holly Hunter and Scoot McNairy give the sense of a more realized Metropolis. And finally there is Lex Luthor, an eccentric and manic take on the famous villain played by Jesse Eisenberg. This performance will either rub you the wrong way or you won't mind it much. In my opinion it works, with all his ticks and dark turns. Although different from previous incarnations, he embodies the qualities of Luthor, but only just.

The plot and subplots are engaging but uneven in presentation, so there's a lot of potential that feels squandered. For a film titled Batman v Superman, we never really see the two of them at odds enough. The motivation for them to fight is more down to misunderstanding. The introduction (or tease) of other Justice League members during one scene in particular, although interesting, felt rushed. In fact the film just tries to include too many ideas from sources like The Dark Knight Returns, Red Son and another that surprised me, which was my big worry going in. And despite all that, without doubt the most geeky, fan-boy moment was the Knightmare Batman scene, weird and bizarre in all it's glory, a huge tease for what's to come in the franchise.

The film has a more comic book style than most, it never drags and gets to the point quickly, moving along like a breeze. Yet annoyingly the structure of certain scenes felt jarring, like it's about to reach greatness but then diverts to subplots that are either uninteresting or take too long to resolve. The last act is the biggest victim of this.

For whatever problems the film has, I feel it's dark and grim tone is not one of them.. The DC comics have always been known for their psychological and political themes, so i'm fully on board with the direction taken for this new universe. There are moments of humour from Perry White, Alfred and others several times throughout the film to break up the tension, so any accusations of this being joyless are just plain false. Definitely not the 'wink wink at the audience' kind of jokes that some comic book films offer, but enough to make these characters memorable. In saying that, there are moments of horror and brutality that may be too much for younger children.

The action scenes, when they finally arrive, are superbly shot. Batman's hand to hand combat against thugs is fast and fierce, while his showdown with Superman is the spectacle you would expect. The bat mobile and bat wing make appearances, they look and sound as frightening as ever. The final battle is given the 'everything including the kitchen sink' treatment, an explosion of CGI that some will love and others may hate.

Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL once again have produced a fantastic score to accompany this film. The standout tracks for me are the epic 'Their War Here' and the emotional 'Men Are Still Good'. And of course the Wonder Woman theme 'Is She With You' is ideal for the Amazonian heroine's grand appearance. Oddly, there are scenes where the music becomes intruding and loud when a more subtle approach was required.

As much as i loved watching these iconic characters finally on screen together, i feel it's a step back from the more focused Man of Steel. Whether it's the direction under Zack Snyder or the writing by Chris Terrio, Warner Bros will need to make a few changes to hit a home run next time round. The critics have made their feelings known, but Batman v Superman feels like one for the fans.

And WARNER BROS was so busy in promoting the upcoming movies that it faltered in making this movie a good one.

When ZACK SNYDER made MAN OF STEEL , many people didn't liked it , because of its dark tone and too much seriousness in it. But i find it great . It both DARK KNIGHT series and MAN OF STEEL , we get to know about the inner life of BATMAN and SUPERMAN . We get to see different prospective to see superheroes. Guess what DAWN OF JUSTICE is not that kind of movie. DAWN OF JUSTICE want to swallow so much things that it doesn't have time for character development , or psychological fighting in brain. In an early scene Superman ended on and unknown place while saving Louis Len and some how it creates and international dispute situation that SUPERMAN is dangerous to human kind. You have to understand it by yourself that there must have been some destruction of mankind , but why nit show it. title: Over all it seems a little under-cooked but it has its moments of glory!
review:
The ultimate fantasy of every superhero comics fan of seeing two of the most popular superheroes crossing paths finally bore roots with Zack Snyder's Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice. A 'loose' sequel to Man of Steel, DOJ has undoubtedly been one of the most talked about and anticipated films ever since its announcement. And as it goes with every superhero movie, comic book nerds had a field time panning out theories- one more absurd than the other. For starters, and to put the outrageous fan theories to rest, Batman is Batman and not Deathstroke. Ben Affleck is Bruce Wayne and not Slade Wilson. So all that moolah in coming up with such a complex theory accounts to nothing. I mean common what were you expecting really?! This isn't Church and the Illuminati. Its just comics.

Coming to the movie itself, Zack Snyder had millions of hopes riding upon him. After all, he was bringing the caped crusader and the man of steel to share screen space for an ultimate showdown. It doesn't get any bigger. Since its opening, the film has got pretty mixed reviews. To put it straight, it could have been bettera lot, lot better. There are a plentiful of plot holes, lots of unconvincing sub-plots, multiple cliché filled sequences and almost nothing innovative. But then it is not entirely bad either. A few boxes checked rightly and the film manages to save itself from drowning. With all its weaknesses and shortcomings, there are moments when you just can't help whistling, clapping and cheering like it were the 'El Clásico'.

The film begins with the millionth portrayal of Bruce Wayne's back story. By now we all know it but we're shown it again nevertheless. Snyder looks hugely inspired by Christopher Nolan's formula of storytelling, as he builds it all slowly and patiently. So if you go expecting a fist fight between the two super heroes from the word go, you'd be disappointed and how. Interestingly, there are various instances in the film which suggest that Gotham and Metropolis are almost neighboring cities. Wonder why and how did the two big guys not cross path anytime earlier in that case. Anyway, when they finally do, it is when Bruce Wayne witnesses Superman battling it out with Zod, destructing every building, car and human that comes into their paths. (Remember the climax from Man of Steel, yes Bruce Wayne was at the scene). One such building that bites the dust happens to be a Wayne enterprises office, thereby killing many of Bruce's friends and colleagues. That is when the hero of Gotham becomes wary of the son of Krypton considering the amount of damage he can cause lest he turn to the dark side (Don't mind the Star Wars reference, you get the point).

Meanwhile, Mark Zuckerbergerr, Jesse Eisenberg in his unconventional portrayal of Lex Luthor is busy negotiating with senator Finch to create a scheme that will help neutralize Superman if need be, just in case. That the young billionaire psychotic character with God complex has more sinister intentions is any ones guess. Quite predictably, he also is the catalyst that gets the two superheroes warring. How he does it is the least innovative and most over used ploy in movie history. They fight for what could have been easily avoided, but with their big superhero egos they fight it out before they talk it out. It is as unconvincing as it gets, but who caresthis is what we paid to see. The build up  is amazing and the fight, for as long as it lasts is enjoyable. "Do you bleed?" is what Batman asks his nemesis during an earlier confrontation and he doesn't disappoint when they do clash. I'll leave it there and keep the rest for you to watch.

The other major character in the movie and surprisingly the most convincing one is Gal Gadot's Diana Prince aka the Wonder Woman. Right from her first introduction to the eerie revelation of hers being a meta human and finally her grand entrance in the climax, she is a delightful surprise. Fans would have surely loved to see a lot more of the Wonder Woman than what they get. Coming to Ben Affleck's portrayal of the dark knight, it takes us a little while to get adjusted to seeing him as Bruce Wayne and un-see the epic and memorable image of Christian Bale from Nolanverse. But once the transformation happens, he is an absolute treat to watch. You need a powerful actor to portray a character as intense and popular as that and Affleck does fine justice to the role.

Eisenberg is believable as Lex Luthor and shines more and more as the film goes by. The director has managed to portray him as an evil entity strong enough to challenge both super heroes. Predictably, Luthor creates the almost 'undefeatable' mega villain Doomsday to set up a grand show down in the climax and a somewhat shocking ending.  The ever reliable Amy Adams has much more to do this time around that her previous outing and she keeps the charm of Lois Lane intact.

As far as extra freebies go, we get a glimpse of preview of the other meta humans in form of video files on Lex corps hard drives. This, naturally in the quest towards building up the DC version of a superhero multi-starrer-The Justice League. We thus, for the first time see the introduction of Flash, Aquaman and Cyborg.

To wrap it up, Dawn of Justice as a stand alone film seems a little under cooked considering the significance of bringing the two mighty superheroes in the same cinematic universe for the very first time. That said, it has its moments of glory and does its job of driving the DC verse towards an eventual assembly of heroes.

title: One Fatal Flaw
review:
I wasn't sure what to expect going to the theaters. Man of Steel had many, many issues. Too many, I thought, to be fixed in just one movie. Not to mention the fact that it was painfully boring and dry. So, I didn't have overly high hopes. I wasn't disappointed or surprised.

Honestly, this movie takes a lot of risks. Batman is totally and completely different from any version I've seen and Lex Luthor is much different than you would expect. Affleck's performance, whether you like his rendition of the Bat or not, is solid. He makes a very strong and convincing Bruce Wayne. I prefer a lighter and more traditional version of the Caped Crusader, but I respect Affleck's showing. I look forward to seeing where they take the Bat moving forward. Eisenberg's performance is much more polarizing. It's not for everybody, but you have to respect how much he committed. It was a risk. And it definitely made him stand out as a villain.

Cinematographically, this movie is surprisingly brilliant. The opening of the movie contains many varied and interesting shots, even poetic at times. The dark colors work much more beautifully with the introduction of Batman. The score is very well written and very evidently varies from character to character, hero to hero.

There is one major thing which kills this movie. The script is a mess. Act 1 is brilliant and act 3 is solid. However, it falls apart in act 2. It feels as if we have five different movies in one. It is sloppy and hard to follow through the middle. I think they tried to accomplish to much in this one film. Rather than being just a Batman vs Superman plot, it is that plus many other various major plot lines. This movie should've accomplished one goal, but rather tried to move the universe five steps ahead instead of one. You will see what I mean when you watch it. It isn't the individual moments or the dialogue. In fact, other than a few stray scenes, most dialogue and action is solid. In acts 1 and 3 there are even some great and powerful moments. It is how the story is told that makes it feel sloppy.

Overall, this movie was good and worth watching. It felt difficult and sloppy at times, but the action was great. What it did well, it did really well. What it did poorly, it did really poorly. It will suffice for what it meant to accomplish. I just don't know that I can sit through 5 or 10 more DC movies like that.

title: Catered to Purely Comic Fan Boy
review:
I being this huge fan of DC comics was waiting with bated breaths for the film to release for 3 years at least. A joy ride it was, giving all the thrills typically etched for a comic fan I'd say, if not everyone BvS starts off giving the usual introduction of Bruce Wayne's parents' demise without adding much to it. And then it also goes about explaining how it ignited the spark in the Batman to fight Superman. Though it clearly sways away from the comics, it gets us warmed up of what we can expect. I wouldn't go into the plot so much, virtually everything should be kept away from the readers to avoid the spoilers.

Zack did not do such a bad job with Man of Steel, though not even coming close to the expectations everyone had for the film especially knowing Nolan is at the helm as an executive producer. Without Nolan present for any creative decisions (not at least as much as he was involved in Man of Steel), Zack has slipped into his indulgence for clean Comic like taste he likes to keep for his films (read 300, Watchmen, Sucker Punch). The cinematography particularly is spotless and erodes all ideas of the real world gritty feel Nolan generally gave with Wally Pfister. He goes for a dark bluish tinge whenever Batman is around and sometimes uses a bright yellow to its addition (Nolan kept Orange as the second color). Every frame seems to be sprayed with water paints, constantly reminding us of the graphics we have been reading. I loved the use of strong close ups and his trademark usual slow mo's in certain scenes.

But having 2 superheroes and also touching Wonder Woman arch is a tricky business. Unlike Avengers, you don't always have these super heroes together, with completely different cities and tones they carry, it is rather tough to have a story develop in parallel to the development of the characters. And Zack doesn't completely manage that either, one can actually notice the choppy editing (a word I also used for Man of Steel review). The lack of fluidity to the scenes keep us floating without generating much interest for the film, at least in the first half. As the film advances the plot lines coincide which also proportionally keeps getting us more hooked. Subsequently they merge and the comic fan boy, in all scenes later, is thoroughly tickled.

Acting isn't exactly the best, which means Ben doesn't surprise! Henry and Gal have done well enough with the limited scenes both were squeezed into to accommodate Batman. Jeremy Irons (Alfred) would have done much better had he been offered more screen time while Jesse as Lex goes clearly over board, but again no complaints as such. Amy was highly credible and so was Holly as senator Finch, my picks among the caste.

The film very smartly gives glimpses of DC characters for the expansion of its universe, never feeling too forced, though with 2 and a half hour length, those could have been edited, conveniently avoiding the distraction. The action choreography is a huge improvement from Nolan's much rebuked such scenes, but it also serves as a reminder in one of the Batman dream sequence where Ben clearly looks like waiting to get hit when watched closely, slow and pretentious. The music is more towards the entertaining part than what Zimmer uses for Nolan's films, the famous escalating music with arrests. Here, each character has its own signature, I specifically loved Wonder Woman's and Batman's theme, also the music used towards the end for Lex is cheekily sweet.

The plot is heavily stuffed, if worked on details could have easily been turned into a good two films. But it still delights never losing the grip once it takes off, which almost is in the second half. Zack also over comes his drawback of making "humorless" films, subtly entertaining with a few one liners here and there.

In all, this film is nowhere close to what I have been reading in the reviews (31% Rotten Tomatoes score, are you kidding me? Lower than Daredevil?). It's a fantastic entertainer, worthy of letting Zack direct the Justice League.

title: Generally good, but critically bad

title: It was more Dawn of Justice than Batman v Superman
review: As a big fan of DC's animated movies, comic books and characters I went into the theater hyped up and ended up disappointed. Ben Affleck's Batman was the best part of this movie, Gal Gadot and Henry Cavill were great in their roles also. The odd one out was Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor, a far different take from the Luthor I know and love, but I respect the decision to do something different with the character. title: A highly entertaining yet imperfect film, that provides a great Batman.
review:
Firstly, Ben Affleck as Batman. There was a lot of controversy when he was first announced to play the role, however, all those worries have been laid to rest. Ben Affleck is THE Batman. He killed it in the role. I was immediately sold on his performance. He nailed the look of Batman, the voice, the personality and that solemnness and severity the character has been known for since his inception. Every scene with Batman are the best scenes in the entire movie, especially the opening scene, the car chase, the warehouse fight and the actual fight with Superman. In fact, all the Batman aspects of the films are great. Jeremy Irons' portrayal of Alfred was solid, as he offered many humorous comments when conversing with Batman. I also liked the new Batmobile and Batwing. I can't wait to see this Batman again, and his own solo movie.

Most of the Superman aspects are done very well. Henry Cavill delivers once again as Superman, further developing his character. I especially like the divided opinion the general public has toward Superman that is presented in the film, as I think this is how the real-world would receive a god- like being, which makes it all- the- more intriguing. Amy Adams as Lois Lane, Laurence Fishburne as Perry White and Diane Lane as Martha Kent all do a fine job as the supporting cast returning from the previous film.

Gal Gadot killed it as Wonder Woman. She wasn't in it a lot and didn't play a big role until the third act. But when she finally shows up in full garment, she steals the spotlight and becomes a major highlight of the film, and is overall just awesome. I look forward to seeing more of her in her solo movie next year.

The fight between Batman and Superman was astounding, and a remarkable thing to witness on the big screen. The build-up for it takes a long time, but when it finally happens, it's worth the wait. It's very realistic and aggressive, definitely the best scene in the entire film. My only problem is it goes for about 10-15 minutes, and that's very short compared to the rest of the film and its long running time. The film should have been called 'Batman & Superman', rather than 'Batman v Superman'.

The villains of this movie are a bit underwhelming. I have spoken very highly of the cast, with the exception of one; Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor. He didn't seem like the type of actor who would play such a villainous character, so I have been cautious toward this casting since the beginning. And how was he in the role? He was just okay. His performance was a very quirky, eccentric and geeky take, instead of the more stern, calculative and manipulative megalomaniac-genius from the comics. I admit, Eisenberg's portrayal works well for the character established in the movie, and most of the time, he delivers solidly in that role, with the exception of two scenes where he was like a villain out of Schumacher's Batman films. However, as an adaptation of the classic character from the comics, it falls flat, which is a shame.

As for Doomsday. Doomsday looked like utter garbage in the movie, and to me, didn't pose as much of a threat, but instead a big colossal CGI mess utilized just for the Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman to team up and lay the groundwork for the Justice League. However, I did thoroughly enjoyed seeing the Trinity finally appear together on the same screen. I wish Doomsday would have looked more like he did in the comics and of been saved later on for a solo Superman film so he could have gone through characterization and have a much bigger impact.

Speaking of the Justice League, this film tries too hard to setup the extended universe, as I feel like DC is just playing catchup with Marvel, and putting too much into one single film. There's two scenes that spend too much time on references to the Justice League, and it just presents itself as a distraction. It is an example of more is less. The film spends more time on DC's side players, when it should be solely focused on what the audience has come to see; Batman and Superman duking it out, and the development of their relationship, with just a few small references to what's to come next.

The main aspect of the film critics have been complaining about is the storyline. I actually found the story easy to follow, yet I have two problems with it; the pacing and the ending. The pacing is weird and all over the shop. It feels like an episode of Game of Thrones, focusing on various characters' ongoings in each different scene. Also, the first hour of the movie doesn't really have much action, and instead a lot of talking about politics and ethics, whilst the last half hour is almost nothing but destructive mayhem. I really didn't like the ending, it felt unnecessary, but I feel like it's the resolution that had to be used because of how the climax was set out. And it took a very long time to wrap it all up, it felt like 4 endings in one, making it feel quite tedious. If you have seen the movie, you'll understand what I mean, and you know it'll be undone in Justice League, which makes it all the more pointless.

Overall, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is like Superman in the film; a very divisive topic in the public's eye. Personally, I think it is an imperfect and flawed film, but that did not get in the way of my overall enjoyment of it, as I found more good things in it than things I disliked. 7/10

title: All the right ingredients, let down by poor editing
review:
Batman v Superman had everything it needed to be a 9/10 movie. Casting was generally very good - Affleck's Batman was easily the most believable to date, for example. Cinematography was excellent, CGI was (mostly) very high quality, and even the script itself was solid.

Unfortunately, despite being delayed by a year, editing seemed rushed. The origin stories are all intermixed in a non-chronological mess, broken up with a series of perplexing and irrelevant dream sequences. Almost the entire first hour to hour and a half could be cut without detrimental effect to the plot. Confusingly selective backstory was present throughout - for example, Bruce's childhood tragedy is conveyed, however other details such as who Alfred is were left out. Lex has pretty much no origin story whatsoever, making his motives as the primary villain a bit shaky. Why bother doing origins at all if you're going to pull the "fans will get it" card for most aspects of the character backgrounds?

At the end of the day, the movie is worth seeing, and its flaws are not beyond repair. Hopefully a more coherent cut will make it to home release down the line.

title: Pretty good, even if it falls short of expectations
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is a mixed bag, yes. Yes, it is bloated and unnecessarily loud at times. Yes, the first half of the movie feels disjointed. But this is certainly not a bad movie. It is not popcorn fluff. It does raise a lot of real questions on how the world would react to superheroes. This brings me to a common thread among most of the reviews I have seen. That Superman is not 'cheerful'. That batman is 'brutal'. Lex Luthor is too 'eccentric'. And these characters are not 'supposed' to be this way. This is what has irritated me the most. The real question to be asked when looking for character motivation is not 'what would Superman do?' The real question to be asked is 'How would an alien, who is feeling responsible for getting thousands of people killed on another planet, feel like?' I doubt he'll be cheerful. Ditto for Batman who's so disillusioned with criminals and crime that he just doesn't care anymore.

I really liked the movie. It's gorgeous and edge-of-the-seat stuff. It's generally well-acted. The conflict between Batman and Superman is well set up. The cameos are awesome! It feels real and high-stakes.

I guess it comes down to the minor judgment about a movie before we go watch it. I went in with the thought that this one will be awesome. It turned out to be pretty good. Even if you go expecting a crime against superhero movies, I'm sure you'll come out feeling it was not that bad. Anyway, I'm really excited for the other DC films.

title: Keep your Mind at home, do not expect a classic and Enjoy this Entertainer.

Actually i feel we can easily skip first half and watch movie from its 2nd half. Film's Runtime is long 153 mins and we get entertainment for 40 mins only and here film fails to impress. Story also looked confusing, took pace after 100 mins passed and then all the massy elements like Visual effects, action, fight scenes, destruction scenes which made the film to end on a positive note. Acting- i really never cared about acting field for any Superhero movie except TDK so its better to not talk about it. Music- really, do we get something called music from movies like this? Only Background Music is something for which we looks forward and even that is not so great in this film. You can call me mad but don't know why, my fanship level towards TDK is so high that whenever Batman's fighting scenes were going on, TDK Background music was playing in my mind. Story- It looked confusing till 1st half, but then 2nd half recovered all the failure of 1st half. They ended the movie with an interesting note that The Sequel is Coming, yes you read it right Sequel is Coming. Screenplay- as i mentioned earlier Dull 1st half, good 2nd half. Screenplay had too much to improve. They could have easily reduce Runtime to 120 mins. Direction- i don't know previous work of Snyder so i didn't expect Nolan's classic from him. Whatever he has done was not satisfying for me. Still his focus was good. I loved his vision cause he gave the much needed importance to Batman's character despite knowing he's human not an alien or a man with super powers. Batman almost killed Superman without any super powers. He didn't forget to keep Batman our favorite Superhero. Visual effect- its good but nothing great. I went to watch it in 3D and now i am questioning myself that why did i watch it in 3D, i mean 3D Effects were good for nothing i could have certainly watch this movie in 2D. Batman's get up & fight scenes, Superman's effects, Wonder woman's power scenes in her cameo and the Devil in the Climax etc. These scenes are something to appreciate for their technical work. Final words- Overall a good massy entertainer which you should watch at least once. If i compare this one with other superhero flicks then it is similar to Avengers and other superhero flicks except TDK series. If you loved money making entertainers of Marvel then you will definitely like this one. Go for it and enjoy 2 of your favorite superheroes at the same time, sorry its 3 actually. I would give 6 stars to the film but giving 1 star extra for my Favourite superhero Batman. 7/10 stars by me

title: Mediocre at best *Spoilers*
review:
I went to see this movie with high expectations. Being a hardcore DC fan, I had to. I couldn't wait to be amazed by Mr. Snyder and flame those Marvel fans and DC haters right in their faces. But it was all a lie. A decent first half followed by a travesty.

The biggest doubt before the release was if Affleck is going to be THE hero we need AND deserve. To be honest, he was. It was good to see a Frank Miller version of Batman. Old, gritty, bitter, violent, with a drinking problem. And Ben Affleck was spot on. And what they showed next was perfect. Alfred, the character so true to the actual source, I felt the need to thank Jeremy Irons in person. However, that was the end of one's dream.

Jesse Eisenberg was nowhere near the mastermind and charming villainy, he so fondly called himself, LEX LUTHOR. I cringed every time he tried too hard at being LEX and failed miserably.

As a comic book fan, I knew there would be some moments where Snyder would abuse his liberty to use his own imagination which would make every comic nerd a bit uncomfortable. But Mr. Snyder surpassed Shane Black's record and totally p-i-s-s-e-d over one of the best back stories of one of THE biggest villains of DCU. Doomsday was made a joke. His appearances, his abilities, and his back story, all went down the gutter.

Another big fail was the climax to BnS's supposed war. The only thing that had good development was Batman and Superman's hatred towards each other and I was excited about the conclusion of their rivalry. Alas, that was the dumbest moment of the 2 hours 30 minutes Snyder- rampage. Bruce had all the enthusiasm for killing Clark, so much that he even argues with Alfred about it, kills/injures people and is okay with being a criminal as long as he ends up killing Clark. Till the moment, he finds out that Clark's mother's name is Martha as was his mother's following which he throws the Kryptonite spear and joins hands with Clark. I lost it at that point really. There was hardly anything to salvage from.

Clarke's "Super Hearing" was only meant for Lois and not for Martha. She got kidnapped and Clarke didn't know. Superman's super hearing is supposed to be so good that he could hear a person's heartbeat on the other end of the globe and he can't find his mother? Clarke "heard" Bruce's plan to steal Lex's data but was oblivious to the entire Kryptonite plan?

Also, the introduction to other league members was so random and stupid. Basically, Batman shows you teaser trailers of 4 other members on his Bat-Laptop.

Honestly, if the movie was any good, I would have defended it at any cost. I would have shut those haters down with all the witty remarks and the comic book knowledge I have gathered all these years.

BUT I CAN NOT LIE

It felt like a Michael Bay movie.

There were two-three references to the incoming threat in the upcoming sequel. The para-demons and the omega sign in the dream sequence. And the last few words from LUTHOR about "he's seen us and he's hungry". But honestly, I'm not too sure if even Darkseid can save it.

*Tries not to cry*

*Cries a lot*

title: Don't listen to the fans OR the critics
review: Batman v Superman is finally out, and so far it has been creating some pretty mixed reactions. Fans love it, critics hate it, and I personally believe that it's somewhere in between those 2 extremes. For the 3 of you who don't know, the plot centers around a fight between the two heroes. After witnessing the destruction of Metropolis (as seen in the end of Man of Steel and the beginning of BvS), Batman swears to avenge Jack (a character who isn't mentioned beyond the first five minutes of the movie) and the rest of the city. And it seems like the rest of the world feels the same way, putting Superman on trial. These tensions reach a climax when the titular fight happens, which lasts about 5-10 minutes before they're forced to put aside their differences to fight Doomsday, the evil creation of Lex Luther. There's also Wonder Woman and terrorists and a guy in a wheelchair and whole bunch of other things cram packed into this movie. And this is where the main problem with the movie arises; the movie is all over the place. The first half of the movie is sort of political thriller, while the last half is a CGI explosion-fest. If the these 2 parts of the movie were inter-woven nicely (as they should've been), it might have made the movie that much better. But this is Zack Snyder we're talking about. There's also very little character development, cramming the entire story of Batman into the opening credits sequence. There's also very little exposition for Clark Kent's character, which you could say was done in Man of Steel. But sequels aren't supposed to entirely rely on their predecessors, they should also work as stand alone movies. As previously mentioned, there's way too much going on in the movie. One second Clark and Lois are having bath tub sex, the next Bruce is having a dream sequence, and then after that we see Lex Luther forcing a jolly rancher into someone's mouth. It also tries way to hard to set up the rest of the DC Cinematic Universe, with cameos from many of DC's biggest character's being crammed into a one minute sequence that doesn't benefit the story in any way. And yet, despite the constant events and plot that won't slow down, the movie somehow seems drawn out and often boring, something only Zack Snyder could pull off. Also, the ending was kind of unnecessary. I won't give anything away, but I will say it feels kind of tacked on and pointless. Aside from that, this movie has some things that really worked, namely the acting. Although not phenomenal, Ben Affleck does a pretty good job as Batman. He's everything the character should be: bruiting, emotionally unstable, and intimidating. He also has a better "Bat" voice than The Dark Knight trilogy's Christian Bale (which isn't saying much). Gal Gadot does a pretty good job, too, playing the mysterious Diana Prince, who later turns out to be Wonder Woman. Although she's barely in the movie, she still is one of the cast's better members. Henry Cavil also does a decent job as the Man of Steel, considering how bland of a character Superman actually is. I, as well as many others, believe that there should've been another stand-alone Man of Steel movie released before BvS to further develop the character of Kal El, but what can you do when DC is desperately trying to catch up to what Disney has done with Marvel. The rest of the cast does pretty well: Jesse Eisenberg offers a different, if sometimes hysterically-bad, portrayal of Lex Luther. Jeremy Irons does a great job as Alfred in the 10 minutes he has on screen. Diana Lane does a great job as Martha Kent. Overall, some very solid performances. Other positives include the pretty stellar visual effects, Hans Zimmer and Junkie XL's amazing score, and (of course) the fight between Batman and Superman. And, while the execution might have been weak, the plot is a very enthralling one, and it makes sense within the context of Man of Steel. While Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice is without a doubt a flawed movie due to it's poor pacing, lack of character development, and jumbled story, it's acting and visuals make the movie a fun ride. If you go into the movie with low expectations, you'll probably find yourself enjoying it. Depending on how big of a fan you are, I would recommend seeing this movie at either matinée price or on Blu Ray when the R-Rated "Ultimate Edition" comes out.

title: Very Well Done Action, but Crowded and Rushed Story
review:
Batman v. Superman is finally here, and it's now official that DC is trying to match Marvel, but lacks the skillfulness. Batman v. Superman is probably one of, if not the most, hyped films of the year, where 2 of the most iconic comic-book characters finally come together on the big screen. Batman v. Superman is action packed, crowded, and rushed making it a true mixed bag. For those who want to enjoy a great action film, and don't care about some of the finer details, this will probably live up to expectations.

As with it's predecessor Man of Steel, Batman v. Superman handles the action sequences really well. The film's special effects are also very good, and the character designs are very well done. It seems with this film most of the positives revolve around Ben Affleck and Batman, as he seems to be the main focus of the film. Batman's characterization seems to be the not just a shining spot in the cloud of carnage that is this film, but possibly one of the best Batman characterizations ever.

On that note Batman saves this film, because the rest of the film is in a word, a mess. The film tries to do too much, which seems odd since Marvel's The Avengers was able to handle the same task perfectly. When looking at it Superman, Lois Lane, Wonder-Woman, Lex Luthor, and other various characters are underdeveloped simply because they aren't given enough screen time. Not only are they not given enough screen time, but the writers rush through shoddy plot points simply to get back to Batman, as if they know the only thing they were getting right was Batman.

The issue with that is if the focus is Batman, then they made the wrong film here, and the film comes across as a wasted opportunity. The problem is the objective of the film, which was to do too much, and therefore rush through the underdeveloped story. Looking at it they either should have done a Batman standalone film or a smaller version of this, which focuses on Batman and Superman, not Wonder-Woman, Lois Lane, Perry White, and countless other throwaway characters. This is where Marvel gets it right and DC still hasn't figured it out.

In the end Batman v. Superman is a decent popcorn flick, that contains amazing visuals and action sequences. The film isn't really bad, it just isn't great, when it really could have and therefore should have been. It should be said that while the film is rushed, crowded, paper-thin, and a little repetitive Ben Affleck and Zack Snyder did do a pretty good job getting Batman right, and that leaves potential for this franchise, but it's hanging on a thread. In the end if you're on the edge about seeing this film, it depends on what you want, if you want great action and visuals this is your film, if you want great story and characters, this is a weaker film.

title: Much better than I thought it would be, but still not fantastic
review:
While reading this review, keep in mind that I have seen this movie, and that I will discuss some spoilers.

In this comic book adaptation, we see, like the title suggests, Batman and Superman fighting... for like five minutes. Seriously. They fight for five minutes. But everything builds up to this, but they don't only build up to the fight. No, also other things, which brings me to my first problem with the movie. But as always I will discuss this in my last paragraph.

Let's start of with the directing. You could have easily guessed that this movie is directed by Zack Snyder; Slow Motion? Check. Muscular men? Check. References to previously made movies by him? Check... I could go on, but I only have my 1000-words limit, and it would be not entertaining to read, if anyone actually reads these reviews, except from me. I was a little suspicious when they said that Zack Snyder would be directing the movie, and I guess I was right. I never really enjoyed watching Zacks movies, so I was also going to expect a not so fun movie. The movie was fun, though, but not to great. Snyder did create a very beautiful movie. I didn't really have a comment on his camera choices. But again, a trademark for Snyder, is the dark filter put over the movie. There are movies that come of great with it (Gone Girl, Fury...) But in this movie it looked like everything was night all the time. Or just really clouded. Snyders directing isn't the knockdown argument. He actually did a fine job, so congrats Snyder. The bad part lays in the script/screenplay. This, again will be discussed in the end of my review. The cinematography was as well very pretty to look at. This was done by Larry Fong.

I didn't hate the movie, so there are also some things, except from the acting directing and writing, that I will discuss in the paragraph. The first thing is the violence, which also brings a negative, but let's first start of with the positive. The fight- scenes were choreographed well, and so was the directing at those times. No real shaky cam, and no obnoxious editing, in my opinion. But the negative aspect is the choice they made for the Batman character. He kills people. This was really annoying for me, as a fan. You can't say that I don't know with certainly that he kills them, because I am pretty sure that people die from explosions, and by getting shot at... Well at least last time I checked. The CGI was a bit less good. It was like in the trailers. The only good Cgi thing was Superman flying, etc. The cape of Batman was also made of Cgi, and you could easily see that. The editing overall was kind of good, nothing really fantastic. The 3D doesn't add anything to the movie, except for the five extra euros.

Now the acting and characters. Batman was played by Ben Affleck. I really liked his version of the character, except for the killing part. His Bruce was damaged and you could see that, due to the acting. He has a lot of stares, but you can see the emotion in them. I also understand his idea why Superman has to be stopped, on the contrary of a other characters motivation. Superman was played by Henry Cavill. He was good, but not as good as Affleck. Cavills Superman isn't my favorite, he does do his best, but it's just not enough for me. He played with not so much emotion, when I think that he should have showed emotion. The antagonist, well the main antagonist, was Lex Luthor. I really didn't like his character in the movie. He had no motivation for wanting Batman dead, or they just don't tell it in the movie. Luthor was played by Jesse Eisenderg. He is a good actor, but he overacted a lot of the scenes. A helper of Superman is the well know Lois Lane. She is a character that I very much like, she is independent, yet she brags with it. Amy Adams did a fantastic job at portraying her. Wonder Woman also has a role in the movie, just a small one. She is there to just be there. But I liked the incarnation of her. Gal Gadot was good, for the scenes that she was in. Jermey Irons as Alfred was the most surprising for me. I absolutely loved him. The chemistry between Affleck and him was great, and they builded on it. The supporting cast was fine, some better than others.

The screenplay was the worst part of the movie. The dialogue between characters was a bit dull at times, but that is not the worst part. What I wonder is why no one has decided to tell them that a lot of the lines felt forced. Like the 'Do You Bleed' scene. It is a cool line etc. But someone probably came up with it, and suggested it. The others probably went like: 'Yeah, sure, we'll get in in there...' there are a lot of forced, cool lines, that feel out of place. But also just moments without dialogue are sometimes dull. But the story overall is, like I predicted, a total mess. If you would ask me to sum up the plot in a understandable way, I would have to think a long time... Also they tried to put in as many characters in the movie, which didn't work out well. There is also to much set up, if you have seen the movie, you know what I mean. (the e-mails). They really want to get you excited for the next movie, but this just didn't make me want to see it, eventhouh I probably will.

That's all I can say, due to the limit. But thank you for reading this review.

6.75/10

title: The Knight of Gotham vs The Reedemer from Krypton: Birth of the League
review:
Like all Nolan movies, the title is sufficient to summarize it.

It is indeed a 'Batman VS Superman' movie, where there is a clash of ideals that leads to (somewhat 'pointless') fight, which is certainly the most enjoyable scene there is. Also the story's end is basically the launch of other DC heroes to form the Justice league, hence the 'Dawn of Justice' part.

The pace is fast, holding the attention of audience throughout.

The story is simple without much surprises or flair.

Ben Affleck presented a different view of Batman unlike its predecessors. He is more Humanly, full of emotions, fearing for his people. A hero, who has suffered,is more experienced and is preparing for something dreadful to come. Kudos to Ben!

Whereas Superman is still finding his identity in our World. Branded as "Saviour" by some or "False God" by others, Henry Cavil showed how vulnerable Superman is. He got some serious ass-kicking in this movie.

The movie has got many 'jaw-dropping' action scenes with our Heroes showing new moves and weapons.

Wonder-woman is smoking Hot. High hopes from Gal Gadot.

The movie needs no brainer, so just go watch and enjoy. ;)

P.S.- Do NOT wait for any post-credit scenes. (DC isn't following that much from Marvel. Phew :P )

title: A great start for DC's Cinematic Extended Universe (No Spoilers)
review:
Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice picks up from where Man of Steel ended. First of all, is the movie good? Well, I think it's brilliant. Of course there is so much going on, and much details to take in, but if you concentrate on the movie, I bet you all will like it.

A lot of people will think that Ben Affleck's Batman is much more brutal than the other versions/performances, and yes it is, but I personally think that Affleck was a bad-ass. Before Affleck we've seen 5 other actors who've portrayed the caped crusader, but none of them could do justice to both roles as Batman and Bruce Wayne equally, in this case, I think Affleck has nailed it. The suit is on point, and so is his chin too. The other thing I loved about Batfleck was the combat style. The fighting technique is not as lame as Keaton's or Bale's, but it's absolutely fantastic. Affleck uses the same combat style which is used in the Arkham Games. Shortly said, I think Ben Affleck is the best actor to portray Batman/Bruce Wayne till date.

Henry Cavill in the other hand, wasn't as great as Ben Affleck performance-wise, but he has improved a bit. He is still a bit stiff, and doesn't have that much charisma in him. The beautiful-looking Gal Gadot was great as Wonder Woman even though we only see her as Wonder Woman in the final battle.

Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Lex Luthor made me questioning his portrayal. The character is supposed to be hungry for power, but instead the director made him to be psychotic. Eisenberg is a good performer, but he was exaggerating a bit at times.

The storytelling has improved a lot since Man of Steel, and I think the credit should go to Chris Terrio. David S. Goyer, who was also a co-writer has sharpened up his writing since Man of Steel (which wasn't as great as expected). Larry Fong's cinematography and David Brenner's editing was excellent. The scenes in the movie would have had a different, but better atmosphere if the production team had let Hans Zimmer do all the film scores by himself. The collaboration with Junkie XL wasn't as great as Zimmer's previous works (The Dark Knight Trilogy, Interstellar, The Amazing Spider- Man 2). The few things that I would criticize are Snyder's directing, the design of Doomsday (he looks awful) and the screenplay. As many of you already know, there are a few dream sequences here and there, which I think were placed wrongly, and the fact that Batman is using guns is actually a bit devastating for the fans. Another thing that I personally feel is that they gave too much of the movie away in the trailers and TV-Spots. Other than that the movie is great, but I suggest DC and Warner Bros. to replace Snyder for the Justice League films.

title: Still waiting for the real thing
review: Another missed opportunity to do justice to the greatest superhero of all time. I can understand - it is not easy to get a grip on this complex character. Superman is a supernatural alien without any weakness (if you do it right, you leave it there - but again and again in the movies kryptonite is used to overcome this strength, instead of developing the indestructible side of Superman). It is this indestructible side, paired with the feelings and weaknesses of a normal guy, without being one. The longing to be part of a world, a human world reflects our own longings. Superman must have the feeling to be with power without limits - only then the problems arise: the fear of outliving all the loved ones, fear never to be understand by another person, fear to have no shining example for the own living. A fear that is also in our souls - but he knows, these fears will be fulfilled. In the 90's Superman DC comic books developed one of the greatest stories ever written. For over one year in multiple comic book series the death of Superman and his rebirth did catch the readers by surprise. What a story that was. And in this movie it was wasted during several minutes only! A shame, since this cast is gorgeous. Every character, especially Henry Cavill, Amy Adams and Jesse Eisenberg (as Luthor) are spot on. Two thirds of the movie are wasted on a silly plot. Already in the comic books an enmity between Superman and Batman never worked out. Because it doesn't fit to the basic characters of Batman and Superman. In this movie the plot construction to give reason for hate between them is mostly senseless. Only, after the enmity changes to friendship the movie can go on - but only 35 minutes left! Here the movie goes into action. Doomsday is introduced by an obscure twist. No development of Doomsday. Doomsday is wonderfully drawn (by computers). And killed after 15 minutes. What a waste! Get Superman away from the DC Extended Universe. He and his friends at the Daily Planet needs all the time they can get. Justice League never worked out in the comic books. It will never work out in the movies.

title: It's Batman v Superman...but we all loose...
review:
My God, I wanted to love this movie. I needed to love this movie. I hope it gets better on a second viewing but I don't think it will. It's a mess. A big, incoherent mess. There's some really good things going on here, but nothing that can save this movie. Ben Affleck as Batman is right on the money. So is Jeremy Iron's Alfred. But they're working from a script that couldn't save a cat from a tree. So is Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman. She looks the part and the set-up to her stand-alone movie is pretty obvious, but the script is just such a mess! There's no explanation for most of the things our heroes do. There's no real MacGuffin here. It's as if a future Justice league movie is the carrot and this movie is just the dumb donkey chasing after it. To me, it's obvious that Zack Snyder doesn't know what to do with Superman. Look, I've been a Superman collector for over 36 years now. Trust me, I love the character. I had no love for him in this movie whatsoever. I don't understand his motivation in this film. I also think that the reason he's going after Batman (as Clark as well as Superman) makes him a big hypocrite. Add to that, that most of the time when he's saving people, he does it with an expression on his face that is similar to my daughter's when I tell her to clean her room. No, I didn't like Superman in this movie! I did love the Loïs and Clark stuff. And of course the special effects are of the charts. But I needed so much more. This movie tries to do way too much and most of it fails miserably. This is a placeholder movie.... The real icing is the Justice League movie coming in 2 years. But I don't know if I still want that now.

*************EDIT AFTER SECOND VIEWING**************************

Saw it for the second time today. I liked it more this time. There isn't more coherence, it's just that I understand it a bit better now. I clearly LOVE the Batman and Wonder Woman stuff even more this time around. It's still too serious for me and I still don't like Lex Luthor and the way he's portrayed here. But all in all, I want to give DC the benefit of the doubt here. I've changed my vote from 6 to 7/10.

title: It's a great superhero movie.
review: I personally wanna say that this film is amazing. Though the casts are all great, from the leading Batman and Superman to The Flash, Cyborg and Aquaman who only appear for about a minute. But the story is lacking any character development. Wonder Woman just appear suddenly in the last fight is ridiculous. They should have done any important plot with her. The effect is great though not as great as Man of Steel, it's still great. Ben Affleck did an amazing job in this film, he saved the film alongside Jesse Eisenberg. It's a great superhero movie, but not a great movie overall. Lacking character development and story is the big problem in this film. But, it's still worth to watch if you just love film.
